kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: Tomas Lawry! Backbone of the Kourend Council!

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: Of course, it's a shame the Council are totally spineless.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Tomas Lawry
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: Hmm. What are you doing here Martin?

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: I'm here for a drink of course. This is a pub, you know. Lovely place to sit back and relax. You should try it some time.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Tomas Lawry
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: This would be easier if you told the truth.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: I am telling the truth. Is it illegal to go to the pub now?

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Tomas Lawry
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: For you, I'm afraid it is. Martin Holt, I am arresting you for inciting violence against the Kourend Council.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: Inciting violence? You must be joking! All I've done is express my valid concerns. There is no law against that!

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Tomas Lawry
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: You have encouraged people to take up arms against the rightful rulers of Kourend.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: I have given the people a voice! You cannot silence us all!

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Tomas Lawry
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: The people can express their concerns through the proper channels. Now, I must ask that you come with us at once.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Tomas Lawry
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: Come now, Martin. Let's not go there. You know how it ends.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.speaker: Martin Holt
kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.text: Fine! But the people will not stand for this. I will not be responsible for what happens now!
Martin is taken away; the cutscene ends.

kourend-s-last-princess-martin-s-arrest.player: Looks like I'm on my own now.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: A cutscene begins; the player enters the basement of a small shack.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Oh my.
Err... Hello.
Can you hear me?
Rose?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: A man appears from a cell gate further in the basement.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Man
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: What the... Who are you?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I could ask you the same question.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Man
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: This place is private! You're not welcome here!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Well here's the thing: I don't actually care.
I came here looking for someone, and I think this woman here might be that someone. If she is, you're in a whole different world of trouble.
So tell me, who are you?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Man
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: My god...

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Man
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: You're looking for Rose, aren't you?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Is this her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Man
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: It... Yes, this is her.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: And you are?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Man
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'm Councillor Liam Orson, of the Kourend Council. But please, you have to understand...

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Yes, I'd very much like to understand. Why are you here with Kourend's missing princess? And why is she just lying there like that?
I suggest you explain everything. You should probably do it fast, as well.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I don't know where to begin.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: How about with her father. How did he die?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: There was something wrong with him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: You expect me to believe that?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: It's the truth!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: He was always a fan of antiques. One day he bought some old flask from a stall in Lovakengj. He began drinking from the flask wherever he went, and it started to change him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Change him?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: The flask was cursed. Some dark magic. He stopped being himself. Started saying things. Things he would do to people. To the citizens!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: We did what we had to...

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: You killed him. You killed him and took his throne for yourselves.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: No... We never wanted the throne. The throne was always meant for Rose.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Well that clearly didn't happen.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: She was never meant to be involved. We were just going to look after things until she was ready. But she found out what we did.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: So you did this to her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: We didn't want to hurt her, but we couldn't risk her telling anyone. This was the only way.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Well, you failed. She got the word out. It took 20 years, but thanks to her, your rule is at an end.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: So, what happens now?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: That's not for me to decide. There's someone who needs to see this.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: The screen fades to black, and Commander Fullore arrives at the basement.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Is it... Is it really her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I think so.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: And you say she's not aware of... anything?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Doesn't look like it.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: What a mess.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: What of the Councillor? Where is he?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I locked him in the other room. Didn't want him running off. I'll get him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: The player opens the cell gates.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: You can come out now.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Councillor.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Commander.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Liam... tell me it isn't true.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'm sorry Lydia.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I defended you! I defended all of you! And all this time, you've been lying!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I swear to you, we did it for the people.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Don't give me that!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Look at her! Look at what you did to her! She was a child, Liam!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'm sorry.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: What did you do to her? Why is she like this?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: We didn't want to kill her. She didn't deserve that. The mage gave us a potion. He said it would stop her revealing the truth.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Mage? What mage?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: There was an Arceuus mage. He was an expert in curses, and he realised what was happening. He gave us the poison for the King.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Would have been nice for you to mention this earlier! Who was this mage?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: He never told us his name.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: And you trusted him? Are you serious? Some random mage comes along and tells you to poison the King and you just... do it?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Everything the mage said was true. The King was cursed. We could see it.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Did it ever cross your mind that maybe this mage was the one that cursed him in the first place? How do you know he wasn't just using you?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Of course it crossed our minds, but we didn't have a choice. The King was deteriorating by the hour.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: You could have gone to Lord Arceuus! You could have gone to Lord Shayzien! You could have gone to anyone apart from some random mage!

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: This mage. Have you met him since?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Yes. Rose's condition...

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: You mean the condition you gave her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Her condition has no cure, but it can be kept in check with regular treatment. He meets with me and gives me the potions she needs.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: How do you know it's not the potions that are doing this to her?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I've done my research. The potions are safe, and she can't live without them.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Where is this mage?

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: We meet outside Molch. I think he lives in the temple there, with the lizardmen.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: This mage. We need to find out who he is.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I'll go to Molch. If he's there, I'll find him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Cutscene ends.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Good luck out there. I'll keep an eye on this... I don't even have a word for him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Try not to kill him.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: I'll do my best.

steps.player: How are you doing?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: I'd rather not talk about it. We have work to focus on. There'll be plenty of time to contemplate later.

options.text: How are things back at the castle?

steps.player: How are things back at the castle?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Terrible. I take it you heard about Martin?

steps.player: The arrest? I was there.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Such a stupid move. I told Councillor Andrews not to do it, but he listened to Lawry instead. Now the protestors are even angrier.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: At this rate, it's only a matter of time before things get violent. I even had Councillor Unkar moved to the castle for his own safety.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Not that he deserves safety! What a mess this is.

steps.player: I'd better be off.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Councillor.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Councillor Orson
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: Oh, hello there.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: I have a question for you.

options.text: What do you know of this mage?

steps.player: What do you know of this mage?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Very little. It was David... Sorry, Councillor Andrews, who he contacted first. The rest of us didn't meet him until much later.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: He was an expert in old curses. He could see what was wrong with the King. He told Councillor Andrews and offered his help.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: By then, it was already too late. The King had deteriorated too much. There was only one solution.

steps.player: I don't know if that's true.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: You weren't there. You didn't see what was happening to him. There was no time to consider other options. We did what we had to do.

steps.player: If you say so. You said he lives in Molch?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: That's right. In the temple, I think.

steps.player: A mysterious mage with no name who lives with some lizardmen. He sure sounds like an upstanding citizen with nothing suspicious about him at all.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: You're not funny. Do you think we'd have worked with him if we knew all of that? We didn't find out about the lizardman connection until much later. By then, the deed had already been done.

steps.player: I'm suprised you'd even care about lizardman. They're pretty tame compared to demon summoning.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Sophia wasn't always like that. Before she joined that cult, she was just like the rest of us. The only difference was that she had other beliefs.

steps.player: Zamorakian beliefs aren't particularly welcome in most places.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: So what? People should be entitled to their beliefs!

steps.player: Sure, but I suspect being entitled to summon demons is more up for debate.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Like I said, she wasn't always like that.

steps.player: What happened with Rose?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: I know you probably don't believe it, but we always meant for her to take the throne.

steps.player: I guess I'd probably have an easier time believing that if she wasn't lying right here instead.

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: She overheard us talking about the King. We couldn't let her tell anyone.

steps.player: But why? If it was really all about her, why would it matter what happened to you?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: Because without us, who would have been left to rule? We had to do it for the good of Kourend.

steps.player: Did you? Or have you lied to yourself so much that you now actually believe it?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: She was like a daughter to me!

steps.player: So you poisoned her?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: And I have taken care of her every day since! Without me, she wouldn't even be alive.

steps.player: Is what she has now really much of a life at all?

steps.speaker: Councillor Orson
steps.text: You don't understand...

steps.player: To be honest, I don't know if I want to.
Actually, never mind.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.speaker: Commander Fullore
kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.text: You need to find out who this mage is.

kourend-s-last-princess-the-sleeping-pri.player: Don't worry. I'll work it out.

options.text: How are things back at the castle?
I have a question about that door over there.

steps.player: I have a question about that door over there.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Yesss? What about it?

steps.player: Not got any mages hiding behind it have you?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Magesss? You know of the Yo'kal ahk?

steps.player: Yo'kal ahk?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: It isss the name we ussse for the mage you ssspeak of. In your ssspeach, he hasss another name.

steps.player: This mage. Where did he come from?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: He hasss been here sssince our massster ssstill walked among usss. He wasss sssealed away before, but they releasssed him so he could guide usss.

steps.player: I need to see this mage. How do I get through the door?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: It is closssed, but there are keysss. We shhhamansss carry them.

steps.player: Well can I have your key?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Perhapsss. But why shhhould I help you?

steps.player: I could just kill you instead?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: And I could shhhout for help. Humansss are not meant to be in thisss temple. Do you think you can sssurvive usss all?

steps.player: Alright. What do you want in return?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: A trade? Yesss, that worksss well.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: The mage you ssspeak of. He sssends us to fight the humansss. He sssays we mussst do it for our massster, but he isss long gone.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: I am done with thisss fighting. I want to ssserve our massster in other waysss.

steps.player: I could help you escape?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: I am a shhhaman. I need no help from humansss.

steps.player: What, then?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: The hatching area in the ssswamp, to the sssouth wessst of here. My lassst egg isss there. If I go and it ssstays, it will die in thisss falssse war.

steps.player: So if I bring you this egg, you'll give me the key?

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Yesss. The egg isss marked with the sssymbol of our massster. Go fassst human.

options.text: So, about the key to that door...

steps.player: So, about the key to that door...

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Yesss. I can give you the key, but firssst I need my lassst egg. It'sss at the hatching area in the ssswamp, to the sssouth wessst of here.

steps.player: Alright. I'll bring you the egg.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: It isss marked with the sssymbol of our massster. Go fassst human.

options.text: So, about the key to that door...

steps.player: So, about the key to that door...

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Yesss. I can give you the key, but firssst I need my lassst egg.

steps.player: I have it here.

steps.text: You give the egg to Kaht B'alam.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Thank you, human. You have given usss a chance for a new ssstart. Here isss the key.
Kaht B'alam gives you a key.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Be cautiousss of the Yo'kal ahk human. He isss very dangerousss.

steps.player: I'll be careful.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Ye niauh, human. Perhapsss we will meet again.

options.text: So, about that door over there...

steps.player: So, about that door over there...

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Ussse the key I gave you. That will get you inssside. But be cautiousss of the Yo'kal ahk human. He isss very dangerousss.

steps.player: I'll be careful.

steps.speaker: Kaht B'alam
steps.text: Ye niauh, human. Perhapsss we will meet again.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: You hear a conversation taking place in the next room...

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: ...actually quite surprised. I thought you of all people would have made more of an effort to find me.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Your greatest achievement was my downfall, my lord. The lizardmen blamed me for your disappearance and sealed me away. I was trapped for centuries.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: And yet, here you are.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: I managed to convince their shamans I was on their side. They set me free. I have been trying to find you ever since.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Except you were beaten by a treasure hunter.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: With humble respect, my lord, this treasure hunter is not the one to thank.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: It was me. I was the one who worked out how to find you. I planted the seeds that eventually led him to you.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: A proxy? Interesting. I wouldn't have thought you would be one to hide away.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: The world has changed. Working from the shadows has served me well. And now it has reunited us once more.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Yes, the earthquake. That was a considerable amount of dark energy. Something I could not ignore. But to what end?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: The same end as always, my lord. Quidamortem has been lost to us, but there are other ways to harness the Dark Altar.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: I see. And tell me, what of this Council that now rules Kourend? I sense your work at play there.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Second Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: I needed access to the Altar. They were a means to an end.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: You installed some puppet rulers just to access the Altar? My my, Xamphur, you haven't lost your ambition.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Never, my lord. I also hoped that access to Kourend would have further uses, but I fear the Council is done.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: From what I hear, you are likely right. No matter, though. Kourend is of limited use to us.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: My lord?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: That kingdom was always a means to an end. A disappointing necessity while we were still shackled.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: But now, those shackles are gone. I have discovered a new way to achieve our goals, and this time, none will stand in our way.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Now, we have much time to make up. Unfortunate, but bearable. Soon time will be of little meaning to us.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Ah, but on that note, it seems this conversation is at an end, for we are no longer alone.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: First Mysterious Voice
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Deal with your guest Xamphur. We will meet again in the south.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: It will be done, my lord.
The player is forcefully teleported.
Veos teleports away.
Xamphur approaches the player.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.player: So I think I took a wrong turn somewhere. I'll just go now...

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Go? No I don't think so.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: You have heard too much. You have seen too much. You won't be going anywhere.

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.player: Ah. Well in that case... Xamphur, was it? How about you tell me what on Gielinor is going on here?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: Really? You think this is the part where I tell you everything?

the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-through-the-doorway.text: No, no, no. This is the part where you die.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: Xamphur
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: Really now? You actually thought you could defeat me?
The player is knocked out by a powerful lightning spell, and a cutscene begins.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: First Lizardman
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: What are we sssupposssed to be doing?

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: Second Lizardman
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: The Yo'kal ahk wantsss thisss corpssse removing.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.speaker: First Lizardman
the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.text: It'sss a zombie! Let'sss get out of here!
The lizardmen leave, and the cutscene ends.

the-mysterious-mage-knocked-out.player: I guess I should have a look around.

the-mysterious-mage-searching-the-table-.text: Among other things, the table is covered in books and notes. One note looks to have been written fairly recently. You decide to give it a read...

the-mysterious-mage-searching-the-table-.player: Hmm. I should tell Lydia about this.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: You're back.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I am. Where's the Councillor?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Don't worry, I didn't kill him. I was sick of looking at him, so I moved him somewhere safe. He won't be going anywhere.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Did you find the mage?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I did, but he got away. To be honest, he also left me with more questions than answers.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: What happened?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: His name is Xamphur. I overheard a conversation between him and someone else. They talked about the Council, among other things.
The weird thing is, the person he was talking to... I think it was Veos.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The treasure hunter?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Yes. He disappeared after that earthquake, but I saw him with this mage.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The conversation? What was it about?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Xamphur called Veos, or whoever it was, his master. It sounded like he had been seeking him out for a long time.
They talked about the Council and the Dark Altar. I couldn't make much sense of it, but I managed to look around after they left.
From what I found, it seems that Xamphur worked with Councillor Andrews to manipulate the other councillors into killing the King.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Councillor Andrews was in on it from the start? That monster.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: It seems he always wanted the throne. Xamphur offered it to him in return for access to the Dark Altar.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The Dark Altar? Why?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Xamphur has been redirecting power from the Altar, but I don't know why. It seems his work is what caused the recent issues in Arceuus.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The death? I heard about that.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Makes you wonder what else he's been responsible for.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I'm not sure what any of this means, but it can't be good. We need to do something. But first...

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: What?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Rose. What do we do with her?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I did some research while you were gone. Liam wasn't lying. The poison they gave her irreversibly destroyed her mind. There is no cure.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I suspect Xamphur won't be making her any more potions any time soon. Maybe someone in Arceuus could help?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Someone else could make the potions, but all they do is prolong her suffering.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: What are you saying?

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: This is no life for anyone. The truth is, Rose died long ago. All that's left now is an empty shell.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Oh... I think I understand.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I'm sorry, Rose.
A cutscene begins, with the player and Commander Fullore in front of Rose's grave.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Back when I was a girl, there was this Shayzien patrol that would go past our house each morning. Every day I would run out to wave at them as they went by.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: For as long as I can remember, I always wanted to join the army. 'Become a farmer or a chef,' my parents would say to me. 'The army isn't for you.'

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: But I knew what I wanted, and I knew nothing would stop me from getting it.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I saw some nasty things while serving the Council. I'd always tell myself that it was necessary.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Whenever I thought about giving up, I'd ask myself who I'd be replaced with. Even if things weren't perfect, I was in the best place to improve them.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: It was all a lie though, wasn't it? It's always been a lie.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I've spent most of my life serving a bunch of murderers; turning away from the truth because I was so scared of being wrong.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: To think it was Martin who was right all along!

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: We can still make this right. We can still stop the Council.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: We won't be able to do it alone. The Council still holds the power in Kourend.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: I'm not sure if that's true. The real power is held by the five houses of Kourend. Together, they could replace the Council and take over the kingdom.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: We'd need to get them all on board.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Leave that with me.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: Alright, you gather the five leaders. Convince them to meet us at Xeric's Lookout, south east of Shayzien.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: It's where I left Councillor Orson. We won't be disturbed there.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: Consider it done.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: It feels wrong, her being out here. She should have had a proper funeral.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: It's not so bad. It's nice and peaceful. She's finally free from the drama of Kourend.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: I guess you're right.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: We'd better get going. Good luck.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.player: You too.

the-mysterious-mage-returning-to-command.text: The cutscene ends.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Have you spoken with all the leaders yet?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Keep at it. We'll need all five of them on board. When you speak to them, tell them to meet us here.
The trapdoor is securely locked.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Councillor Orson is down there. I'm keeping it locked, just in case.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.player: Hello Lord Arceuus. There's something I need your help with.
We should discuss it in private. It involves the Kourend Council. It's also connected to the recent death here.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.text: I see. Then I will come at once. Where shall we meet?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.text: Very well. I will join you there soon.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-tr.text: I will join you at Xeric's Lookout soon.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.player: Lord Hosidius. I need to discuss something with you.
We can't talk about it here. I need you to meet me at Xeric's Lookout.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: Well you have helped me in the past. That said, I can't just go running off to Xeric's Lookout for no reason.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: Ah, I see. Then the day has finally come.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: There has been discontent with the Council since the day they took control of the kingdom. That was always going to come to a head at some point.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: It seems that point has now arrived. I will depart for Xeric's Lookout shortly.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.player: Will you be departing for Xeric's Lookout soon?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-ka.text: I will. But there are a few things I need to prepare first.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Oh look, it's the human. Hello human.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.player: Lady Lovakengj. I need you to join me at Xeric's Lookout. There's something urgent we need to discuss.
That's right. We can't discuss it here, but it involves the Kourend Council.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Oh. Well you really should speak to Councillor Unkar. He's part of the Council, you know.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.player: That's not quite what I meant. It's not something to discuss with the Council themselves. It's something I need the house leaders for.
To Xeric's Lookout. To discuss this Council business.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Ah yes, the Council business at Xeric's Lookout. I will come at once, but first...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Oh look, it's the human. Hello human.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.speaker: Lady Vulcana Lovakengj
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-vu.text: Yes, yes. Come to Xeric's Lookout. I'll be there as soon as I've finished this sherry.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: I need your help. It's about the Council.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Anything to do with that demon you summoned on my docks?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: That wasn't me! Besides, I'd have thought you'd be happy to see Sophia Hughes dealt with.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: I'd have preferred it be done without demons being involved. Idiots will be idiots, I suppose.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Come on then, tell me about this latest Council nonsense.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: We can't discuss it here. We need to be somewhere more private.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Oh I'm sorry. Is my secret hideout in the sewers not private enough for you now?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: Well... not really. Meet me at Xeric's Lookout. We can talk more there.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Fine. But if you waste my time you will seriously regret it.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.player: Will you be departing for Xeric's Lookout soon?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lady-sh.text: Do you want to get off my back? I already said I'll meet you there. Now clear off.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.player: There's something urgent I need your help with.
It involves the Kourend Council, but we can't really discuss it here. Come alone to Xeric's Lookout.
I appreciate it's an unusual request, but yes please. All of Kourend could be at stake here.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.text: Well I suppose you have been a friend to Shayzien in the past, and this does sound serious.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.text: Very well citizen. I will depart soon.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-lord-sh.text: I will depart for Xeric's Lookout soon, citizen. I have a few things I need to do first.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Well you did it. It's been a while since I've seen the leaders of all five houses together. They're downstairs waiting.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Is the Councillor there as well?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: He is. I told him about Rose.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: How do you think?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: We'd better keep a close eye on him.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Indeed. Now, let's get down there.
A cutscene begins, with the leaders of the five houses gathered.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: This is quite the group you've gathered here.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Indeed it is my lord, but I assure you, it's for a very good reason.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Liam.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: My lords and ladies, there is something I must make you aware of.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: It's regarding myself and my fellow councillors. We...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Yes?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: I can't...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Yes you can Liam, and you will.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Don't you lecture me! You have no right! You killed her!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: What on Gielinor are you fools on about? Killed who?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: They call me a murderer, but they killed Rose! I kept her safe!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: No. You killed Rose. You killed her 20 years ago. It's time to stop hiding and accept the truth.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Rose? You speak of the King's daughter. What happened?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: This coward here killed her, just like he killed her father.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: We did it for the good of the kingdom...

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: You did it for yourselves!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: The King was cursed!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: The King was cursed so that you had an excuse to kill him. It was never about the people, it was only about the throne.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: That's not true!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: I have seen proof with my own eyes. If you think overwise, then you have been fooled as well.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Could you idiots please stop arguing and give us an explanation!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Councillor Andrews plotted to kill the King with a mage called Xamphur. Xamphur cursed the King so that Councillor Andrews had an argument to get the others on board.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: And then they killed him?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Councillor Orson
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Rose was never meant to get hurt! She overheard us!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Rose was smart, but do you really think she just happened to overhear you? I've no doubt Councillor Andrews arranged for that to happen as well.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: So it's true! I always knew the Council was corrupt, and now we have the proof!

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: So what do we do with this proof?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: That's why we gathered you all here. The Council needs to be removed from power. You five can make that happen.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: If the Council are to be removed, they will also have to be replaced.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: Who should replace them?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.player: Could there be another member of the royal family still out there?

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Commander Fullore
the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.text: I doubt it. The Council's plan worked because Rose was the King's only heir.

the-houses-of-kourend-talking-to-command.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Come on now. If you do care for the people, this is the best option.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Fine. It's still a stupid move, but if there's to be a vote, I might be willing to support it.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Might?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Yes. First, there's something else we need to discuss.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Of course there is.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: While you've been running around chasing dead princesses and mad mages, you've forgotten what started all of this. You summoned a demon in my home!

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: No... I killed a demon that someone else summoned in your home. You should thank me.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Really? Thank you for being as useless as I feared.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: How about we skip over the insults this time and you just tell me what you want.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: The Disciples of Yama are a big problem. They need dealing with.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Tell Lord Shayzien to send the army in, then. They literally live right on his doorstep.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Exactly! They live on his doorstep and he cares more about stupid lizardmen. The man is clearly as incompetent as you.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Thanks. So it sounds like you want me to take on this cult singlehandedly? I feel like that won't go well.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Of course I don't expect you to take on an entire cult! What you need to do is cut the head off the snake. Remove the influence of their leader and they won't be a problem.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: So, what? Kill Yama?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: No. Yama has no presence among his followers. At least, not yet. If you remove their connection to him, he won't be able to communicate with them.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: I know of a mage in Arceuus who's hopefully not as useless as you or Lord Shayzien. Her name is Mori and she's been investigating the Disciples of Yama. She should be able to help.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Woah! Slow down there. How do you know all of this?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Because I did some digging. Oddly enough I wasn't going to ignore a corrupt councillor summoning a demon on my docks.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: You learnt all of this just with a bit of digging? There's something you're not telling me here. Besides, why would you care so much about this compared to everything else going on?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: This conversation is pointless. If you want my support, this is the price. Now go and talk to Mori. I hear she spends most of her time in the Arceuus Church.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Fine. I'll be back later.
Hello there.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: Have you spoken to Mori yet?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.player: Not yet.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.speaker: Lady Shauna Piscarilius
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-la.text: From what I hear, she spends most of her time in the Arceuus Church. Now clear off.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Ah, there you are citizen. There's something I need to discuss with you.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: The Royal Accord?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Correct, citizen. Once the Council are removed from power, we will need a new ruler. I for one think this Royal Accord is the perfect move.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: I think we can also agree that when the times comes, I will be a suitable candidate to rule. These are unstable times. My military leadership will put me in a good position to take over.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Do you think the other leaders will support that?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: I've no doubt they'll consider me a strong contender. That said, I expect Lord Hosidius will also be considered. On that note, there's a job I have that would be perfect for one with your skills.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: What is it?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Before we come to finalise this Royal Accord, we need to be sure that everyone is in a place where they can pick the right ruler.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: While Lord Hosidius seems like a good man for the job, I've recently obtained some intelligence that could suggest otherwise. I'd like you to look into this.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Lord Hosidius? Interesting... What is this intelligence?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Some of my best people have been looking into the disappearance of Phileas Rimor and King Shayzien VII's journal. We now believe we have located both.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Hang on... Phileas Rimor?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: That's right. Is there a problem, citizen?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Well... no. Sorry, carry on.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Very well... I will personally see to the rescue of Phileas. I need you to recover the journal.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Hang on... I thought this was about Lord Hosidius?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: That it is, citizen. If our intelligence is to be believed, Lord Hosidius is now in possession of the journal.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: That doesn't make sense! Why would Lord Hosidius want that journal?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: That I don't know, citizen. Lord Hosidius is meant to be an ally to Shayzien. After all, he's married to my sister.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Perhaps this is some plot of his to grow his influence. He may wish to use the journal to discredit my family. Regardless, I need you to retrieve it. Only then will we be able to determine the truth.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: This is all very odd. Do you know where he keeps the journal?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Apparently he has a private office hidden below the Hosidius Vinery. That will likely be where he's keeping it. You'll need to go there, find out how to enter this office and then recover the journal.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Okay. I'll let you know what I find.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: Hello there citizen. Have you found that journal?

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Not yet.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.text: It's critical that you do so, as soon as possible. It will likely be in Lord Hosidius' hidden office below the Hosidius Vinery.

convincing-the-five-houses-talking-to-lo.player: Okay. I'll let you know what I find.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: How do you know that?

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: It is our place to know.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: I was hoping you could take a look at this device and tell me more about the person that made it.
Why what?
Because this device is the thing that was redirecting power from the Dark Altar. The person who made it was also responsible for the trapped soul that needed freeing.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Xil-Dar
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: And so we shall help you.
You feel a strange sensation as the Tasakaal magically inspect the device.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Two others?
Darkness? That sounds like Xamphur. Can you tell how old he is?

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Xil-Dar
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: His body was born long ago.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: In the time of the great betrayer.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Great betrayer? Do you mean Xeric?
You know of him?
But is that who you speak of?
So Lord Arceuus was right. What of this other person, the one touched by fire?
A Pyromancer? Xamphur is working with a Pyromancer?
Hang on... I recently helped to repair some damage to the Doors of Dinh. What if this Pyromancer was the one responsible?
Well then what's to stop them doing it again? We have to do something!

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: We have no part in this.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Keeping the balance between life and death. That's your thing isn't it? If the Wintertodt escapes, it will destroy all life in Kourend. That doesn't seem very balanced!

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: The human makes a valid point.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Well it's been known to happen.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: The Dark Altar powers the Doors of Dinh.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: How?

options.text: Where can I get volcanic sulphur?

steps.player: Where can I get volcanic sulphur?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: It can be mined in Lovakengj.

steps.player: Got it. I'll be back soon.

options.text: Sulphur in a defence potion. Got it. I'll be back soon.

steps.player: Sulphur in a defence potion. Got it. I'll be back soon.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

options.text: Where can I get volcanic sulphur?

steps.player: Alright. I'll be back soon.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: I have the potion.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: You feel a strange sensation as the Tasakaal enchant the potion.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: Pour it on the Doors of Dinh.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Xil-Dar
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: And your work will be done.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Alright. I'll get it sorted.
What am I meant to be doing again?

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: Pour it on the Doors of Dinh.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Xil-Dar
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: And your work will be done.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Alright. I'll get it sorted.
I lost the potion.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Xil-Dar
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: We prepared for such an outcome.
You feel a strange sensation as the Tasakaal replace your potion.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: Pour it on the Doors of Dinh.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.speaker: Kaal-Xil-Dar
lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.text: And your work will be done.

lord-arceuus-favour-speaking-to-the-tasa.player: Okay. I'll get it sorted.

lord-arceuus-favour-pouring-the-shieldin.player: Well that's that done. I'd better get back to Lord Arceuus.

lord-arceuus-favour-pouring-the-shieldin.speaker: Ignisia
lord-arceuus-favour-pouring-the-shieldin.text: Hey! What are you doing with those doors?

lord-arceuus-favour-pouring-the-shieldin.speaker: Ignisia
lord-arceuus-favour-pouring-the-shieldin.text: Well you can either go through them or leave them alone.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: Hello there. Have you spoken with the Tasakaal?

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.player: I have. They confirmed that this Xamphur is the same one that served Xeric.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: So it's as I feared. This is not good.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.player: There's more. We discovered that Xamphur has been working with a Pyromancer. That means he may have been involved in the sabotage of the Doors of Dinh.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: A Pyromancer? Do you know who?

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: Are you sure about this? Had the Doors of Dinh fully failed, the Wintertodt would have destroyed Kourend. What would Xamphur gain from that?

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.player: I don't know, but the Tasakaal themselves confirmed it.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: I will have someone look into this. We'll also use this new knowledge to try and locate Xamphur.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.player: His master said they'd meet again in the south.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: Interesting. This is useful information that could help our search. I wonder... could they mean the southern Kingdom of Varlamore?

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: Ah, but that's one for another time. I believe we've learnt all we can about Xamphur for now. Until we can locate him, we must turn our focus towards the Council.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.player: So you'll support the new Royal Accord?

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: I will. While I have no desire to rule myself, I'll gladly support one of my fellow leaders in that role.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.player: Thank you. I'd better go and speak with the others.

lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.speaker: Lord Trobin Arceuus
lord-arceuus-favour-talking-to-lord-arce.text: Hello there. You have my support with the Royal Accord. You should speak with the others.

lord-hosidius-favour-the-barbarian-camp.speaker: Barbarian Warlord
lord-hosidius-favour-the-barbarian-camp.text: You shouldn't be here! Time to die!

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: You came for me! I knew you would!

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.player: I don't understand Phileas. Why are you here?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: These barbarians raided my home! They took me prisoner. I thought they were going to kill me!

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: I don't know. I heard one of them saying they'd been paid to do it. But who would pay to have me captured?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.player: Wait! What about that parcel? The one with King Shayzien VII's journal. Do you have it?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: No. They took it from me. You don't think that's what this was about, do you?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.player: I'm not sure, but I don't like this at all. I need to speak with Lord Hosidius.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: Lord Hosidius? What's he got to do with this? And what about me?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.player: There's too much to explain right now. Now, there are a lot of barbarians outside, so I can't free you at the moment. I'll go get help. Don't worry, you'll be safe soon.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: Alright. But please, don't take long.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: Is it safe to free me yet?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.player: Not yet. I need to go and speak to Lord Hosidius. Don't worry, you'll be safe soon.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.speaker: Phileas Rimor
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-phileas-.text: Alright. But please, don't take long.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: Hello there. Any luck with that barbarian camp?

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.player: We need to get some people down there urgently! The barbarians have Phileas Rimor prisoner.
He's a retired soldier from Shayzien. I helped him out with something a while ago, but he went missing. Turns out these barbarians were paid to take him.
I don't know for sure, but I doubt Lord Shayzien's visit was a coincidence.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: So, it's as I feared. Still, that doesn't explain why Lord Shayzien would pay for one of his own citizens to be captured.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.player: The thing I was helping Phileas with involved a mysterious parcel he'd received. The parcel contained King Shayzien VII's journal. When Phileas was captured, it was taken by the barbarians.
Before that happened, I followed some clues in the journal. They eventually led me to the discovery that King Shayzien VII may have been responsible for the creation of the lizardmen.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: Ah, the discovery at Quidamortem. This is all starting to make sense. It's long been believed that King Shayzien VII eventually became Xeric. That discovery did little to suggest otherwise.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: Lord Shayzien wouldn't have been too happy of further evidence that Xeric was part of his family. He must have made arrangements to hide as much of that evidence as possible.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: Thank you, friend. I think we have all the information we need. I'll have some of my people head to this camp. They'll ensure Phileas is safe.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: It's probably best he disappear for a while, for his own safety. I'll make the arrangements.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: For now, nothing. We should keep this information to ourselves, until the time is right. As for the Royal Accord, I am ready to finalise things when you are.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.player: Okay. I guess I'd better go and speak with the others.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.text: Hello there. Thank you for your help earlier. You'll be pleased to know that Phileas is now safe.

lord-hosidius-favour-talking-to-lord-hos.player: That's good to hear. Thank you for taking care of him. I'd better go and speak with the others.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-comma.text: Keep at it. We need to find a solution that they all agree on.

options.text: I need some help with Lady Lovakengj.

steps.player: I need some help with Lady Lovakengj.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: What do you need?

steps.player: She doesn't believe that Councillor Unkar has anything to do with this. She wants proof he's involved before she signs the new Royal Accord.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: That's not too suprising. The two of them are old friends. I've got nothing on him, but I can think of one person who might be able to help.

steps.player: Martin?

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Exactly. His group has no doubt kept tabs on all of the councillors.

steps.player: But he's been arrested. I can't just go and break him out.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: No, but you can still talk to him. You've helped the Council enough that no one would think much of it if you paid him a visit.

steps.player: Fair point, I suppose. If anyone asks, I can claim I'm trying to round up more of his group.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Nice idea. They took him to the Shayzien Prison, just west of the city.

steps.player: Alright. I'll go and see what he knows.

options.text: I wanted to ask you something about the leaders.

steps.player: I wanted to ask you something about the leaders.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Go ahead.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-comma.speaker: Commander Fullore
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-comma.text: Keep at it. We need to find a solution that they all agree on.

options.text: I need some help with Lady Lovakengj.

steps.player: I need some help with Lady Lovakengj.

steps.speaker: Commander Fullore
steps.text: Have you spoken to Martin? He's in the Shayzien Prison, just west of the city.

steps.player: I'll go and see what he knows.

options.text: I wanted to ask you something about the leaders.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Guard
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Sorry, but I can't let you talk to the prisoners.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: But I'm here on Council business. I need to learn more about his group.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Guard
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Ah yes! You're the one that helped with Councillor Hughes. Carry on then.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Oh wonderful! There's free food and a bed! Can you believe it? Luxury compared to anything in Port Piscarilius!

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Well I'm glad you're keeping your spirits up. Now, I need your help with something.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Of course. Right down to business. As you can see, I'm a little indisposed right now. Apparently the right to protest isn't so much of a right after all.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Don't worry, it's just information I need. Things have progressed with the Council. I can't say any more here, but we're close. However, I need information on Councillor Unkar.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Excellent work my friend! From the moment I met you, I knew you were something special. Now, what information do you need on him?

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Anything that could prove his corruption.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: If I had information on his corruption, I might not be stood in a cell right now.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Of course, but you must have something on him. Anything could be helpful at this point.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: I see. Well, there's a member of the Royal Society who has close access to Councillor Unkar's dealings. He gives me regular reports, but there hasn't been anything of note yet.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Still, things have progressed fast recently. Maybe he's had more luck since my imprisonment. As I'm stuck in here, perhaps you should go on my behalf to our usual meeting.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Sounds like a plan. Where does this meeting take place?

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: In the Shayzien Graveyard of Heroes. Look for a dwarf. He'll speak with you if you say the passphrase: 'Evil only triumphs when the good do nothing.'

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Thanks for the help, Martin. We'll have you out of there soon.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Good luck friend. Finish this for all of us!

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: Hello again, Martin. Remind me, where is this meeting?

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: In the Shayzien Graveyard of Heroes. Look for a dwarf. He'll speak with you if you say the passphrase: 'Evil only triumphs when the good do nothing.'

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.player: That was it. Thanks for the help.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.speaker: Martin Holt
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-marti.text: Not a problem. Now get out there and finish this!

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-jorra.player: I know you! You're Jorra, Lady Lovakengj's assistant.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-jorra.speaker: Jorra
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-jorra.text: That's right. What brings you here, human?

options.text: The evening owl doesn't eat much pudding.

steps.player: The evening owl doesn't eat much pudding.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: What?

steps.player: I don't know.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Maybe you should go and lie down.

options.text: Evil only triumphs when the good do nothing.

steps.player: Evil only triumphs when the good do nothing.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Never have truer words been spoken. Martin sent you, right? I wasn't sure if anyone would come after he got arrested.

steps.player: That's right. So you're with the Royal Society? How come?

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Why wouldn't I be? The Council are nothing but trouble.

steps.player: But things don't seem too bad in Lovakengj with them in charge.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Lady Lovakengj is in charge of Lovakengj, not the Council. Sure, Councillor Unkar might act like he plays a big part, but it's all empty words.

steps.player: Do you not get sick of her asking for sherry?

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Not really. It's not like it's a hard job. Councillor Unkar would see us all work to death in the mines instead.

steps.player: I see. Well Councillor Unkar is why I'm here. I'm hoping you can give me something of note on him.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Any other day you'd be wasting your time, but today you're in luck. Due to the protests, Councillor Unkar has been staying at the castle for safety. I've had a chance to go through his private documents.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: I think you'll find...

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Wait! What was that?

steps.player: Oh no. Not again!

steps.speaker: Assassin
steps.text: Jorra Ashtar. You have been marked for death.

options.text: If tomorrow never comes, what is today?

steps.player: If tomorrow never comes, what is today?

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: What?

steps.player: I don't know.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Maybe you should go and lie down.

steps.player: Nothing.

steps.speaker: Jorra
steps.text: Huh... Fair enough.

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-jorra.speaker: Jorra
lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-jorra.text: That was close! Are you okay human?

lady-lovakengj-s-favour-talking-to-jorra.speaker: Jorra
