the-archaeological-dig-talking-to-tegdak.speaker: Tegdak
the-archaeological-dig-talking-to-tegdak.text: How are you getting on with extracting the artefacts?

the-archaeological-dig-talking-to-tegdak.player: I haven't got any more yet.

the-archaeological-dig-talking-to-tegdak.text: If the player doesn't have a trowel:
If the player doesn't have a specimen brush:

the-archaeological-dig-talking-to-tegdak.speaker: Tegdak
the-archaeological-dig-talking-to-tegdak.text: Thanks for your help. There's not much left for us to do here except pack everything up. Have you shown that mace to the scribe yet?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik.text: I've got a strange feeling about this mace, [player name]. Maybe when we find out about it, it will shed some light onto my destiny. Come on, let's show it to the scribe.

steps.player: Okay.

options.text: I need to do something else for a bit

steps.player: I need to do something else for a bit.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: All right. I'll go back and help finish the dig.
Zanik returns to the railway

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-picki.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-picki.text: Shall we go and talk to the scribe about this ancient mace now?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Let's go then!
Zanik starts following the player.

steps.player: No.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Oh well. Let me know when you're ready.

steps.player: Where is the mace?

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: I've got it! I'll hold onto it until we've shown it to the scribe. Shall we go?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-ambassador-.speaker: Ambassador Alvijar
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-ambassador-.text: Thank you for helping with the dig! Ur-tag tells me it will be finished soon, and then we will be able to resume work!

options.text: What can I do in the city?
Why did you decide to open the city?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-oldak-with-.speaker: Oldak
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-oldak-with-.text: Ah, Zanik. Would you like to see the results of my experiment with nature runes?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-oldak-with-.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-oldak-with-.text: Not right now, Oldak. I'm helping [player name]!

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: Ah, hello Zanik, hello [player name]. How is the dig going?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: [player name] helped us to finish the dig! Look what she dug up!
Zanik shows the mace to the scribe.

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: Hmm... that is interesting. What do you think it is?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: [player name] says that's a kind of weapon.

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: I can see how. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit with it!

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: We think it's a magical weapon from the surface. Can you decipher the symbols on it?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: No, I'm afraid not. Our written language has developed so much since then that it's totally indecipherable to me.

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: Wait a moment. [player name], didn't you say you talked to some surface goblins when you were trying to find your way through our mines?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.player: Yes, I talked to the generals in the Goblin Village.

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: Perhaps you could talk to them again. They might know more about weapons than we do.

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: I'd rather not travel all that way over the surface, though. I wonder if Oldak could use magic to help us get there?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Goblin scribe
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: Hello, Zanik. Have you found out about that mace yet?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-the-goblin-.text: Not yet. Come on, [player name]! We should go and ask the goblin generals about it!

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-2.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-2.text: I can't believe we're going to the Goblin Village on the surface! I'm finally going to see how my distant relatives live!

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-2.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-2.text: Actually, I'm a little nervous about what I'll find there...

steps.player: Okay.

options.text: I need to do something else for a bit

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-picki.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-zanik-picki.text: Shall we go see Oldak now? I'm sure he'll have a way of getting us to the Goblin Village quickly!

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-tegdak.speaker: Tegdak
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-tegdak.text: Thanks for your help. There's not much left for us to do here except pack everything up. Have you shown that mace to the scribe yet?

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-tegdak.player: Yes! Now we're going to go to the Goblin Village to ask the surface goblins about it!

the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-tegdak.speaker: Tegdak
the-goblin-scribe-talking-to-tegdak.text: Good idea! Maybe Oldak can help you get there.

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
talking-to-oldak.text: Ah, Zanik. Would you like to see the results of my experiment with nature runes?

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak.text: Not right now, Oldak. We wanted to see if you could make Moving-Over-Distance Spheres to somewhere other than the city.

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
talking-to-oldak.text: Oh, yes. My research along those lines has been coming along very well. I think I could make a Moving-Over-Distance Sphere to anywhere you like, given a little work.

talking-to-oldak.player: We're trying to take this ancient goblin mace to the Goblin Village on the surface. Do you think you could help us to get there?

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
talking-to-oldak.text: Hmm. The Goblin Village, you say? Yes, I think I could do that. Just a moment.
Oldak carefully measures out some crushed runes and makes a glass sphere around them.

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
talking-to-oldak.text: There you go. I've made you each one to get you to the Goblin Village and one to bring you back here.

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak.text: Thanks Oldak! Okay, [player name], let's go!
The player and Zanik both break the glass spheres on the ground and begin to teleport. Start of cutscene in Goblin Village as it fades to black

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak.text: So this is the Goblin Village! It's so different from Dorgesh-Kaan, isn't it, [player name]?
The player finally teleports to Goblin Village

talking-to-oldak.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak.text: Sorry about that, [player name]! Oldak's calculations aren't always exact!

talking-to-oldak-talking-with-zanik-in-g.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak-talking-with-zanik-in-g.text: So this is how goblins on the surface live! Come on, [player name], lets talk to them!

options.text: I need to do something else for a bit

talking-to-oldak-leaving-goblin-village.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak-leaving-goblin-village.text: I'll meet you back in Dorgesh-Kaan, [player name].

talking-to-oldak-getting-zanik-from-the-.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak-getting-zanik-from-the-.text: Come on [player name], let's get back to the Goblin Village on the surface! Shall we go?

talking-to-oldak-talking-to-zanik-in-dor.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak-talking-to-zanik-in-dor.text: What are we doing here, [player name]? We should get to the Goblin Village!

options.text: I need to do something else for a bit

talking-to-oldak-returning-to-oldak-agai.speaker: Oldak
talking-to-oldak-returning-to-oldak-agai.text: Ah, Zanik. How did you get on at the Goblin Village?

talking-to-oldak-returning-to-oldak-agai.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak-returning-to-oldak-agai.text: We haven't finished there actually. Do you think you could teleport us there again?
The player and Zanik both break the glass spheres on the ground and begin to teleport.

talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.speaker: Zanik
talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.text: Yes! We're another tribe of goblins who live underground. We've been cut off from the surface for generations but now we're back.

talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.speaker: Goblin
talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.text: That General [Wartface/Bentnoze]. He live in big hut.

talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.speaker: Goblin
talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.text: He say [Bentnoze/Wartface] is leader but real leader is [Wartface/Bentnoze]!

talking-to-oldak-talking-to-goblins-arou.player: These goblins fight all the time, Zanik. Come on, Wartface and Bentnoze are both in the big hut.

the-goblin-generals.text: A cutscene of the generals meeting with Zanik and the player with Grubfoot in the background

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: Who you?

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: I'm Zanik of the Dorgeshuun!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: Lost tribe?

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: That's right! We've been cut off from the outside world for thousands of years but now we're back!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: So legend true!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: What you want?

the-goblin-generals.player: Can you tell us anything about this mace?

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: That holy mace of Big High War God.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: In time of great war, strongest goblin warriors carry maces like this.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: They use them to take favour of gods away from enemy. If another god protecting enemy, goblin warrior use this mace and favour of god is stolen away!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: Oh. A holy mace of the War God.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: You not look very happy.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: You should praise Big High War God for giving you holy mace!

the-goblin-generals.player: The Dorgeshuun don't have quite the same attitude to the gods as you on the surface do.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: All goblins worship Big High War God! Without him we nothing!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: You not real goblin! You filthy human!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: I am a goblin!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: You not even look like goblin! You have big eyes and wrong colour skin!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Grubfoot
the-goblin-generals.text: She is goblin!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: No let him speak.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Grubfoot
the-goblin-generals.text: She is goblin. And she more than that...

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Grubfoot
the-goblin-generals.text: Last night I have dream. I see this new goblin come into village, holding up holy mace.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Grubfoot
the-goblin-generals.text: All goblins gather around her. Not just from village, from all over world. She is Chosen Commander!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: That story from goblin holy book. We not had Commander of all goblins since time of great war.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: Holy book say someday Big High War God send Chosen Commander to lead us to victory over whole world.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Grubfoot
the-goblin-generals.text: That what I see in dream. It her destiny.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: My destiny...

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: That not true! She cannot be Chosen Commander! She not proper goblin! She not worship Big High War God!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: But what if she is? If we ignore her, Big High War God strike us down!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: All right. I not believe you Chosen Commander. But we let you talk to people in village.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: Grubfoot! Tell people in village to gather around! Dorgesh goblin will speak to us all!
Fade out to the generals addressing the goblins of Goblin Village

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: Goblins listen up! This Zanik, she from Dorgeshuun tribe!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: She say she Chosen Commander!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: No, I-

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: We not know what she have to say. But in case she Chosen Commander, we let her speak. Speak, Zanik!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: Help, [player name]! What should I say?

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: Goblins... goblins of the Goblin Village. I'm Zanik of the Dorgeshuun. You may know the legend of the Dorgeshuun, but let me tell you our own version.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: Thousands of years ago, the Big High War God forced all goblins to fight in a terrible war.
The goblins all raise their weapons and cheer.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Goblins
the-goblin-generals.text: Big High War God! Big High War God!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: No! Listen! The god commanded the Dorgeshuun to fight a battle they could not win!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Goblin
the-goblin-generals.text: You weak! You hide instead of fight!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: You don't need to think in those terms! We've lived for centuries without war, and without gods, and-
A goblin gets hit with a magical fire attack, scorching them to death.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Goblin
the-goblin-generals.text: Aaaargh!
Another goblin gets hit with a arrow and dies.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Goblin
the-goblin-generals.text: Unk!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Bentnoze
the-goblin-generals.text: We under attack!

the-goblin-generals.speaker: General Wartface
the-goblin-generals.text: Scatter!
The goblins scatter into buildings.
All the goblins are gone. Zanik and the player are hidden behind different buildings.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: The shots came from the top of that tower, [player name]! Can you see anything?

the-goblin-generals.player: There are two snipers up there.

the-goblin-generals.speaker: Zanik
the-goblin-generals.text: I can't get anywhere without coming into their line of fire, but I think you could get around the side of the buildings to the ladder.
end of cutscene

the-goblin-generals-walking-into-the-cen.text: An arrow thuds into the ground and forces you to jump back.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Sigmund attacks Zanik in the centre of Goblin Village

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Sigmund
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: You can never defeat me! I've been training my Combat by killing goblins around Lumbridge!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Zanik
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: You... you murderer!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Zanik
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Quick, [player name]! Shoot him while I have him distracted!
Sigmund throws a flashbang on the ground and bright white light flashes.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Zanik
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Aaaaah! My eyes!
Sigmund now has Zanik in front of him facing the player with his sword at her throat.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Sigmund
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Don't even think about it, [player name]! Make one move and I'll slit her throat!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Sigmund
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Your little goblin friend has a role in my plan! I'm taking her to the tunnel we've built from the Lumbridge Swamp Caves to the new dwarven train track.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Sigmund
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: When the cave goblins find that the dwarven train has killed their hero, there will be war between them! Saradomin's chosen children can watch as two vile underground races wipe each another out!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: Sigmund
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: A-ha-ha-ha-ha-haaa!
Sigmund turns and backs out of the village with Zanik

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Wartface
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Are they gone?

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Bentnoze
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: What happen?

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Wartface
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: He kidnap Chosen Commander? You must rescue her!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Bentnoze
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Human will need help. You take our best warrior, Sergeant Mossfists.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Wartface
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: No! Sergeant Slimetoes best warrior! Take him!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.player: We don't have time for this! Why don't I take both warriors?

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Bentnoze
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Okay.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Bentnoze
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: Grubfoot! Fetch Mossfists and Slimetoes and tell them to meet [player name] in Lumbridge Swamp!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Bentnoze
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: You take ancient goblin mace. Maybe it be useful.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.speaker: General Wartface
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members.text: You rescue Chosen Commander and she lead us all to glory!
end of cutscene

options.text: I've heard that one of your number has got hold of part of a map.

steps.player: How can I rescue Zanik?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Pink robe man say they digging tunnel under Lumbridge Swamp Caves. You go there to rescue Chosen Commander.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Sergeants wait for you at entrance to Lumbridge Swamp Caves.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: You take ancient goblin mace. Maybe it be useful.
If the player lost the ancient mace:

steps.player: I lost the mace.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: We know! Some goblin find it, give it back here.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Me tell you human not clever enough! He lose mace.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: You want mace, you give us 1,000 coins. Maybe you not lose it again if you have to pay!

steps.player: Fair enough. Here you go.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have 1,000 coins:

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: You stupid human! You not have enough money!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: When come back, bring 1,000 coins.
If the player has 1,000 coins:
1,000 coins
ancient mace

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: You take ancient goblin mace now and rescue Chosen Commander!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Remember, mace has power to rob enemy of power of Prayer!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Pink robe man say they digging tunnel under Lumbridge Swamp Caves. You go there to rescue Chosen Commander.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Sergeants wait for you at entrance to Lumbridge Swamp Caves.

steps.player: No way!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Well then, human no get mace.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: But me not think you able to kill Sigmund with no mace.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: So if you care about big-eyed friend, you find 1,000 coins!

options.text: So how is life for the goblins?

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members-tal.speaker: Ambassador Alvijar
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members-tal.text: Thank you for helping with the dig! I hear that the work on the tunnel is now complete and the first train will be making the journey very soon!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members-tal.player: You've got to stop the train! Sigmund is planning something terrible down there!

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members-tal.speaker: Ambassador Alvijar
upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members-tal.text: What are you babbling about? Everyone was cleared out of the tunnel when we completed work. There's no reason to stop the train.

upon-defeating-the-two-h-a-m-members-att.text: The staircase is closed while the train station is being completed. You will have to find another way down there.

talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists
talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.text: Generals say we help you rescue Chosen Commander.

talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.text: It too important for puny human to do on own. You just get killed.

talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists
talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.text: So we come to look after you so you not die.

talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.text: Grubfoot say pink robe man take Chosen Commander down this hole into new tunnel.

talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists/Slimetoes
talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.text: Look, there new hole with ladder just next to climby-out rope. We go down there.

talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists/Slimetoes
talking-to-the-sergeants-in-the-lumbridg.text: What we waiting for? We must go down into tunnel and rescue Chosen Commander!

the-under-underground.text: Shoulder view from the guard to the player and goblin sergeants
Fade out as the guard runs off

the-under-underground.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists
the-under-underground.text: Ha ha! Puny human scared of me!

the-under-underground.player: He's probably just gone to get reinforcements. He'll be back in a few moments with more guards.

steps.player: Both of you follow me.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
steps.text: Okay.

steps.player: One of you wait here.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
steps.text: Okay.

steps.player: Both of you wait here.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
steps.text: Okay.

steps.player: Wait here.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
steps.text: Okay.

steps.player: Follow me.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Slimetoes
steps.text: Okay.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists/Slimetoes
steps.text: Quick! Me keep human busy!

steps.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists/Slimetoes
steps.text: Ha ha ha!

steps.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists/Slimetoes
steps.text: Take that!

the-distraction-if-the-guards-spot-the-p.text: You are caught and thrown out of the tunnel.

the-distraction-if-the-guard-at-the-end-.text: You are caught and thrown out of the tunnel.

the-distraction-talking-to-either-of-the.speaker: Sergeant Mossfists/Slimetoes
the-distraction-talking-to-either-of-the.text: You go quick! I keep guard busy!

climbing-down-to-the-railway.text: Sigmund has Zanik tied to the train tracks.

climbing-down-to-the-railway.speaker: Sigmund
climbing-down-to-the-railway.text: At last I have defeated you, you filthy goblin!

climbing-down-to-the-railway.speaker: Sigmund
climbing-down-to-the-railway.text: Any moment now the first dwarf train will come thundering down this tunnel and crush you! And then the goblins and the dwarves will go to war!

climbing-down-to-the-railway.speaker: Sigmund
climbing-down-to-the-railway.text: No, YOU'RE the monster! That's why you and all your filthy species must die!

climbing-down-to-the-railway.speaker: Sigmund
climbing-down-to-the-railway.text: This time your goblin friend cannot help you. You are on your own and have no way to overcome my prayers!
The cutscene ends and the fight starts

climbing-down-to-the-railway-attempting-.text: You cannot untie Zanik until you have defeated Sigmund!

attacking-him-with-the-ancient-mace-spec.speaker: Sigmund
attacking-him-with-the-ancient-mace-spec.text: What's happening? That weapon is overcoming Saradomin's protection! You've taken away the last of my prayer energy!

defeating-sigmund.speaker: Sigmund
defeating-sigmund.text: Bah! You win again, [player name]! But someday, somehow, I will have my revenge!

defeating-sigmund.speaker: Zanik
defeating-sigmund.text: Quick, [player name]! Untie me before the train comes!
The player unties Zanik from the railway and they both jump out of the way as the train goes by
~ The grand opening of the Dorgesh-Kaan - Keldagrim train line ~
Dwarves and goblins are cheering in the crowd faving Ur-tag, Zanik, and the player

defeating-sigmund.speaker: Ur-tag
defeating-sigmund.text: It gives me great pleasure to declare this new train link open!

defeating-sigmund.speaker: Ur-tag
defeating-sigmund.text: [player name], Zanik has told me about your exploits. It seems that all the Dorgeshuun owe you our lives once again.

defeating-sigmund.player: All in a day's work for an adventurer like me!

defeating-sigmund.speaker: Ur-tag
defeating-sigmund.text: As a reward, I suggest you keep the ancient goblin mace that you helped to excavate.

defeating-sigmund.speaker: Ur-tag
defeating-sigmund.text: Most of the Dorgeshuun would be happy if such a war-like artefact was kept outside the city, and I am sure you will keep it in safe hands.

standard-dialogue.npc: Ahhh, hello there. How can I help?

standard-dialogue.player: Looks like you have a good selection of weapons around here...

standard-dialogue.npc: Indeed so, specially imported from the finest smiths around the lands, take a look at my wares.

steps.npc: A fine selection of blades for you to peruse, come take a look!
Armours and axes to suit your needs.
Imported weapons from the finest smithys around the lands!

steps.npc: Welcome to the Moonrise Brewery and Winery, the oldest and largest producer of alcohol in all of Varlamore.

steps.player: Could I buy some wine?

steps.npc: Certainly!

options.text: Could you tell me more about this place?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about this place?

steps.npc: Of course! The Moonrise Winery was originally opened over 400 years ago by Bracus Ramio.
While we originally started off as just a winery, the brewing side of the business was established by Bracus' grandson, Ludovic, when he created the now famous sunbeam ale!

steps.player: So it was a family business? Do the family still own it today?

steps.npc: Unfortunately not. Ludovic found himself in a tragic and unexpected wine-related incident before ever having children himself. After his death, the business was taken over by a collective.

steps.player: A collective?

steps.npc: That's right. Some of the most influential people all across Varlamore have a stake in the Moonrise Brewery and Winery these days, though most prefer to stay anonymous.

steps.player: Anonymous? How come?

steps.npc: Ah, well their reasoning is something only they know.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Not at all. Now, is there anything else I can do for you?

options.text: I'd better be on my way.

steps.player: I'd better be on my way.

steps.npc: Do come back soon!
Nilsal, iknami. Thank you for saving my life in that cave.

steps.player: It's my pleasure.

steps.npc: After what happened, I've decided to make some changes in my life. First up is less work. Next is more drinking!

steps.player: More drinking?

steps.npc: Well, not too much more. I wouldn't want to become known for it. I just plan to relax and enjoy myself a bit more.

steps.player: Well, I can't blame you for that. All the best.

steps.npc: And to you, iknami.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.npc: Cleaning, cleaning, always cleaning. This apprenticeship isn't all that it was cracked up to be.
Oh, Aadeela, the sorceress upstairs, said she'd teach me magic, she did. And here I am scrubbing floors without a spell to help me.

options.text: I could cast a Water Blast or a Wind Blast spell?

steps.player: I could cast a Water Blast or a Wind Blast spell to hurry things along if you'd like?

steps.npc: No, no, she'd kill me or worse if she knew I was using Magic to do chores. Her last apprentice - well I'd rather not say.

steps.player: Oh go on, what happened to them?

steps.npc: They say she turned them into little spiders.

steps.player: Oh, that's too bad. I had better leave you to it.

options.text: Surely there must be upsides to the task?

steps.player: Surely there must be upsides to the task?

steps.npc: Nope. Clean this, clean that. When I'm finished cleaning here I have to go help out in the garden.

steps.player: What garden?

steps.npc: Oh, I shouldn't have told you.

steps.player: You're right, you shouldn't have.

steps.npc: Well, if you don't mind then, I'm busy and have to get back to work.

steps.player: Don't let me keep you.

options.text: Oh, you can talk to me. I can see you're having a bad day.

steps.player: Oh, you can talk to me. I can see you're having a bad day.

steps.npc: You know you're right. Nobody listens to me.

options.text: I can't blame them, all you do is whine.

steps.player: I can't blame them, all you do is whine.

steps.text: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

options.text: A sympathetic ear can do wonders.

steps.player: A sympathetic ear can do wonders.

steps.npc: Yes, if I just let my frustrations out, I'd feel a lot better. Now what was I saying?

options.text: I don't know. You were whining about something or other.

steps.player: I don't know. You were whining about something or other. To tell you the truth, I wasn't really listening.

steps.text: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

options.text: To tell you the truth, I wasn't really listening.

steps.player: To tell you the truth, I wasn't really listening.

steps.text: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

options.text: You mentioned something about the garden.

steps.player: You mentioned something about the garden.

steps.npc: Oh yeah, that dreadful garden of hers.

steps.player: Where is it?

steps.npc: Oh, it's nowhere.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: Well it's here, but not really. You see the sorceress is trying out some new type of compression magic.

steps.player: Oh, that sounds interesting - so how does it work?

steps.npc: It would take too long to explain and, to be honest, I don't really understand how it works.

steps.player: Fair enough, but tell me, how do you get to the garden?

steps.npc: By magic! The sorceress did teach me one spell.

options.text: Wow, cast the spell on me. It will be good Magic training for you.

steps.player: Wow, cast the spell on me. It will be good Magic training for you.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello friend. I wish to slay evil and avail them of their loot! Take me to Burgh de Rott!

options.text: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.player: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.npc: I think so? At least my heart knows courage and that should be sufficient for the meantime. I expect that when we get to Burgh de Rott, we'll be able to purchase suitable provisions.

steps.player: But you do realise that the vampyres in Morytania are immune to everything except silver?

steps.npc: Er...well, I've not heard mention of that fact, but I have faith that Saradomin will provide the means to furnish me with suitable weapons when I reach Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: And if we happen to run into some vampyres on the journey down there?

steps.npc: I trust that you will help us to avoid them. You are a guide after all, aren't you? Anyway, you look like you can handle yourself. I presume you've fought such creatures before and won? How hard can it be?

steps.player: It can be pretty difficult, actually. But you're right, I'll be your guide so I should be able to handle the situation.

options.text: Why do you want to go to Burgh de Rott?

steps.player: Why do you want to go to Burgh de Rott?

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I'm going down there to teach those vampyres a lesson or two. I've heard about the terrible conditions down there and I intend to put a stop to it.

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I want to have a go at this Theatre of Blood everyone keeps talking about!

options.text: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies...?

steps.player: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies on the route to Burgh de Rott?

steps.npc: Let's just say that I'm somewhat experienced and I'm happy to take on my fair share of enemies. You don't need to worry about that.

options.text: I can take you to Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: I can take you to Burgh de Rott.

steps.text: If the player has a follower:

steps.npc: Hmmm, it seems that you have a follower. I think it may get lost on this journey if it's left to wander on its own. Let's leave when your follower is safe.
Oh really? That would be great! I'll give you a small reward once we reach our destination.

steps.npc: This place is a bit grim. How can people live here?
Do you visit Burgh de Rott often? You seem to know the route well.
When are we going to get to Burgh de Rott?
We don't have all day to stand around chatting; let's press on. I have loot to get.
Oh, I hate this trip, but it's better than the opulet life styles forced on us adventurer types. I'd much rather be up to my eyes in mud and having a good fight!

We need shield barriers up before anything comes through that rift!
We need to protect the Great Guardian!
We need to power up the Great Guardian!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey, [player name]. Got any abyssal pearls you want to trade?

steps.player: Let's see what you have.

steps.npc: I have my general store, but I also have a small collection of lanterns available, if that interests you?

options.text: Can I see your general items?

steps.player: Lanterns, you say?

steps.npc: Yes, powerful artefacts of The Abyss. We have accumulated a small collection of them from all of the fighting.

steps.player: Do the wizards not use them in the fight against the abyss?

steps.npc: Absolutely not. We know how powerful they are, yet their magic is too unknown to us to risk using.

steps.player: Could I have one to aid in the fight?

steps.npc: I'm afraid I can't just give you one. We're under strict instructions to only provide lanterns to people who prove themselves as committed to the cause.

steps.player: How committed does one have to be?

steps.npc: If you've fought the abyss enough to amass 1,500 abyssal pearls, that would be enough.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough abyssal pearls in their inventory:

steps.player: Ah, I don't have enough on me right now.

steps.npc: That's alright. Feel free to come back when you have more pearls on you.

steps.text: If the player has at least 1,500 abyssal pearls in their inventory:

steps.npc: As long as you are aware of how powerful they are, and that I can trust you won't lost it.

options.text: I understand how powerful these are, I'd like to buy one.
I'm not sure I'm ready to buy one yet.
What's that rift guardian doing over there?

steps.player: What's that rift guardian doing over there?

steps.npc: They're great, aren't they? I don't know their name, if they even have one, so I just call them Rifty.
That rift they have is a folded-space storage rift, just like the ones Traiborn uses! Small on the outside, but big on the inside!

steps.player: But what's the rift for?

steps.npc: The guardians use it to store things. If you help hold back the Abyss, they'll let you take things from the rift in return.
Anyway, did you want to trade?

options.text: Why are you selling things here?

steps.player: Why are you selling things here?

steps.npc: Sedridor told us to make sure there was plenty of incentive for people to help us. He also wants us to gather abyssal pearls for research purposes. I thought this would be a good way of doing both!

steps.player: So you sell things in exchange for abyssal pearls?

steps.npc: Exactly! I've got some interesting things from the Wizards' Tower, along with some cool stuff the Guardians of the Rift gave us. Want to take a look?

options.text: Could you tell me more about this place.

steps.player: Could you tell me more about this place.

steps.npc: Well, I only really know what the Great Guardian told us. This is the Temple of the Eye, or at least, what's left of it. It was built long ago to house the Eye, a powerful Saradominist artefact.
Apparently, servants of some 'Fallen Empire' desired this artefact. However, in their attempt to steal it, they accidently opened a rift into a deadly area of the Abyss called the Scar.
Were it not for the Justiciar of the Lion, the rift would have endangered all of Gielinor. She used the Eye to close it and then created the Guardians of the Rift to protect this temple.
Of course, the rift is open again now, but with our help, the Guardians of the Rift are keeping it under control.
Anyway, did you want to trade?

options.text: I found this dye in the rewards rift...
options.condition: If the player is holding a dye:

steps.player: I found this dye in the rewards rift...

steps.npc: And you want me to change it to a different one?

options.text: Yes, but how did you know?

steps.npc: You'd be surprised at how often this happens. Lots of adventurers have been pulling bottles of dye out of that rift, only to wish they'd got a different one. I've ended up with plenty of spares.
So on that note, would you like me to swap your dye for you?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: Well, you have stymphikes, bloodwood trees, leechfin, venators, and of course, the Maggot King.

steps.player: Tell me more about stymphikes.

steps.npc: They are birds that prey upon many of the other creatures here. However, their population is so great that they have been causing issues for Father Sugadinti's research.
As such, we'd be grateful if you could help us control their numbers.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.npc: There are some stymphike trees just east of Sangvesti. The trees are named for the birds themselves, for they like to use the spiked branches to impale their prey, giving them easy access to the blood within.
Go to those trees and bait them with something that will attract the stymphikes. We have found that letvek work best. They are small insects that you can catch across the river south of Sangvesti.

steps.player: And once I've baited the tree?

steps.npc: Find somewhere to hide nearby so the stymphikes can't see you, then strike when they come for the bait.

options.text: Tell me more about bloodwood trees.

steps.player: Tell me more about bloodwood trees.

steps.npc: Well, Father Sugadinti has been using their sap in his research, but it also has other benefits that you might appreciate.

steps.player: Those being?

steps.npc: We have found that when applied to arrows, the sap makes them more powerful.

steps.player: Interesting... And how do I get this sap?

steps.npc: You will need to cut through the trunk of the tree until the sap begins to seep out. Be warned, the trees are tough, so it will take a bit more work than the trees you're probably used to.
Before you start cutting them though, make sure to put a bucket down. You'll need it to collect the sap in. Some of my fellow disciples keep buckets on hand. Seek them out if needed.

steps.player: Tell me more about leechfin.

steps.npc: As you've no doubt realised by now, blood is quite the commodity here in Vampyrium, and leechfin have more blood than creatures twice their size.
You can fish them in the river to the far east. Catch enough of them, and you'll be able to collect up their blood in a vial.
I believe that vials of blood are quite useful in potion making. Unsurprisingly, they are also of great use to Father Sugadinti.

steps.player: Tell me more about venators.

steps.npc: Father Sugadinti believes they are the closest living relative to vampyres, making them very useful indeed. However, their population has diminished significantly. We are working to address that.

steps.player: And is that something I can help with?

steps.npc: Quite possibly. While we need to restore their numbers, it is also important we ensure only the strongest are able to breed. As such, with a Slayer Master's permission, we will allow you to slay them.
Alternatively, if you bring some stymphike feathers to either myself or one of my fellow disciples, we will allow you to kill some venators in return.

options.text: Tell me more about the Maggot King.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Maggot King.

steps.npc: Ah, yes. A Maggot King is the final form of one of Vampyrium's most disgusting creatures, the ur-maggot. They are thankfully very rare, but very destructive.
Dealing with it is unfortunately beyond our abilities, but if you feel you are able, it would be highly beneficial to our work here for you to do so instead.

steps.player: Where do I find it?

steps.npc: If you take the path north east of Sangvesti, that should lead you right to it.

steps.npc: Until next time, my friend.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the old Wizards' Tower?

steps.npc: Of course. The first Wizards' Tower was built at the same time the Order of Wizards was founded. It was at the dawn of the Fifth Age, when the secrets of runecrafting were rediscovered.
For years, the tower was a hub of magical research. Wizards of all races and religions were welcomed into our order.
Alas, that openness is what ultimately led to disaster. The wizards who served Zamorak, the evil god of chaos, tried to claim our magical discoveries in his name.
They failed, but in retaliation, they burnt the entire tower to the ground. Years of work was destroyed.
The tower was soon rebuilt of course, but even now we are still trying to regain knowledge that was lost.
That's why I spend my time down here, in fact. This basement is all that is left of the old tower, and I believe there are still some secrets to discover here.
Of course, one secret I am no longer looking for is the teleportation incantation to the Rune Essence Mine. We have you to thank for that.

steps.player: I've heard a different take on how the tower burnt down. Something about a ritual gone wrong?

steps.npc: Nothing more than Zamorakian hearsay! They burnt the tower down and are now too cowardly to even admit it!

steps.player: Fair enough.

options.text: Nothing thanks, I'm just looking around.

steps.player: Nothing thanks, I'm just looking around.

steps.npc: Well, take care. You stand on the ruins of the old destroyed Wizards' Tower. Strange and powerful magicks lurk here.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Me? I am the Archpriest who was responsible for the running of this place! I am impressed that you managed to reach my resting place on the lowest level.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Well it wasn't easy for sure. You wouldn't believe how difficult it was to overcome some of those traps.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: The intention was that they should've been impossible to pass. I should know. After all, it was I who was responsible for overseeing the safeguarding of this place.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Why did you need the safeguards? Surely they made it more difficult to do your work down here?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I'm not sure if I should say... I wouldn't want to compromise the trust that the Justiciar of the Unicorn has in me. Afterall, we did what we did for the safety of Hallowvale.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: So... about that. Hallowvale no longer exists. The Hallowed Sepulchre is now beneath the vampyre capital of Darkmeyer within the lands of Morytania.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I see... So we lost then? In that case, I suppose it doesn't hurt to tell you after all.
One day the justiciar sent word to me that I should begin work on securing the Sepulchre. He feared an invasion from the followers of the Dark Lord.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Do you mean Zamorak?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Yes, I do. The justiciar said he was going to confront these forces but that I should stay to protect the secrets within this place. I wish I could have joined him on the battlefield. I carried out my duties though.
I never told the others what was really happening. Day by day we worked our way down to the final floor.
As we progressed further, we became more experienced at creating the traps. Each one was more deadly than the last.
Eventually, when our work was done, I performed the last rites for each of my followers and sealed them within the coffins on the final floor.
Finally, I did the same for myself. The knowledge of how to disarm the traps died with us.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: You buried yourselves alive? That's... horrible!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: No, I think at that point most of us were already dead. We died knowing that we sacrificed ourselves for the good of holy Saradomin and the justiciars who follow him.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Well, at the very least you succeeded at keeping the vampyres out of the Sepulchre. From what I have seen, none of them have been able to enter.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I am glad adventurer. Perhaps that information will allow my spirit to pass on peacefully soon.

upon-opening-the-grand-hallowed-coffin-i.npc: What are you doing in my coffin? Leave this holy place at once!

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.text: If the ring of endurance is uncharged:

steps.text: You show the Archpriest the Ring of endurance (uncharged).

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.text: If the ring of endurance is charged:

steps.text: You show the Archpriest the Ring of endurance.

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.npc: That... That's my ring! I thought I destroyed it!

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.player: Oh, it's your ring? I didn't know.

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.npc: The Justiciar of the Unicorn bestowed it upon me to help with my work within this place.
I had to work for many hours each day to ensure that everything ran smoothly. As I got older, I found it more and more difficult.
This ring allowed me to continue my work without feeling the effects that aging was having on my body. I suppose I have no use for it now. I guess you can keep it.

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.player: Why did you try to destroy it?

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.npc: When I got word that we had to protect this place from the Zamorakian invaders, I was worried that the ring would fall into the wrong hands.
You don't seem to be too bad though. I hope you put the ring to good use!

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is the Emir's Arena. Fighters come from far and wide to arrange fights against their friends and rivals. They can fight in 1v1 Tournaments or Duels.

steps.text: The Arena is open only on PvP Arena worlds. Switch to one of those game worlds to play in the Arena.

steps.npc: Head over to the hospital north of the Arena, and speak to the Guides. They'll help you sign up to a fight. Now, can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: The Emir of Al Kharid has decreed that his Arena should be guarded, to stop ruffians like the Calamity Coven from returning. But is there something I can do for you?

options.text: Tell me about the Calamity Coven.

steps.player: Tell me about the Calamity Coven.

steps.npc: The Calamity Coven were three brigands, followers of an ancient and derelict religion. Through their foul arts, they turned this Arena into a hotbed of corruption.
Maoma was a captain of the Emir's guard, but she abused her authority to rig fights so that the Coven would get rich at the people's expense.
Saika was the brains behind their operation, forging the Arena's accounts so that the Coven could keep all the profits, starving the Emir's public works of all funding.
Koriff used her charms to act as a gracious hostess, whipping up the crowds' excitement so that they'd gamble more and more unwisely, enriching the Coven.
The Calamity Coven are long gone now; some of their old possessions are even being sold as rewards. Now, we are here to prevent a resurgence in such crime. But is there something I can do for you?

options.text: Tell me again about the Calamity Coven.

steps.player: Do you have any tips on how to win duels?

steps.npc: The easiest way to win is to knock your opponent out in one blow!

steps.player: But I can't hit that hard!

steps.npc: Don't stop believing.

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

standard-dialogue.npc: Respect the souls, traveller.

options.text: Why are all these souls here?

steps.player: Why are all these souls here?

steps.npc: A corporeal body is a mere flesh-temple in which the soul dwells. As the body fails, the soul loses its home. Without guidance, it would drift into oblivion.
However, the Soul Altar provides a beacon, drawing the souls to this place where they may join the River.
The River leads the souls through unchartable realms, transcending the plane of the world as you see it, but the three-headed Guardian keeps them safe.
The souls are the dead of Kourend - ensure you respect the souls.

steps.player: Why are you here?

steps.npc: I am here to salute the dead of Kourend whose souls are joining the River. Ensure you respect the souls.

options.condition: If the player has not yet found the Soul bearer:

steps.player: I've been reading your book: 'The Journey of Souls'

steps.npc: Let me guess, traveller... did you come to ask me where the soul bearer was buried? Every mortal who reads my book seems to want to get their hands on it.
Mortals are so predictable. This is the kind of thinking that led that adventurer to break into the Guardian's cave and damage the soul bearer in the first place.
It occurs to me, though, that even if you dig it up, the artefact is damaged. Although the Elders of Arceuus never had the knowledge to repair it, there is one who may be able to help.
I speak of the Key Master, he who watches over the cave of the three-headed Guardian of the River. He has been there for countless years, and will have absorbed power from the River in that time.

Now, we buried the artefact in the crypt of the Arceuus church. As I have revealed this secret to you, you will no longer be affected by the spells that prevent unwary explorers from stumbling across it.

steps.player: Thanks! I'll be off now.

options.text: No, I don't want your smelly soul bearer.

steps.player: No, I don't want your smelly soul bearer.

steps.npc: Hmmph! So what do you want? I trust you will respect the souls while you are in this hallowed place.

options.condition: If the player has started/completed the Bear Your Soul miniquest:

steps.player: About the soul bearer again... I got it repaired by the Key Master. Thanks for your help.

steps.npc: Use it carefully, traveller, and respect the souls.

steps.player: Okay, I'm respecting the souls.

steps.player: What brings you out here?

steps.npc: This is my home for the moment. I'll probably move on at some point, but I'm in no rush. Humans like yourself stop off to do a bit of fishing or woodcutting from time to time, but it's otherwise nice and peaceful here.

steps.npc: I believe that puts us at mayor [# of replaced mayors + 27] now. Long live the mayor.

options.text: Where abouts do you make deliveries to?

steps.player: What are beginner clues?

steps.text: Arthur's eyes light up.

steps.npc: Beginner clues are the lowest tier of clue scroll and as such only require a couple of steps to solve.
Beginner clues are gained through various activities. Those activities are as follows.
Slaying monsters for a chance at a clue being dropped. I hear goblins are sneaky, maybe they have some clue scrolls on them ripe for the taking.
Maybe someone left one in the cow field, who knows where you could obtain them.
Beginner clues have also been known to be left in geodes while mining, as well as sometimes in bottles that you may fish up from time to time and from nests which fall out of trees.
Although this is a much rarer occurrence.
Unlike more advanced clues, you should not expect to get very valuable items from completing a beginner clue.

steps.player: What are more advanced clues?

steps.npc: Advanced clues have tiers between easy and master.
You can gain advanced clues the same way you would get a beginner clue. But to get higher tier scrolls you will need to defeat more powerful foes.

The chance to get a higher tier clue from geodes, bottles and nests is lower the higher the tier. But if you chop down higher-level trees you will have a higher chance of receiving a nest which contains a clue. Same with fishing and mining.
The only exception to this is master clue scrolls.
Master clues can only be obtained as a rare chance when opening your casket or by handing in one of every type of clue, apart from beginner, to Watson who resides in Hosidius.
But with more advanced tiers of clue, come better loot.

options.text: Ask about the types of clues.

steps.npc: This type of clue has you talk to someone around Gielinor. Although the clue does not tell you exactly who to talk to.
You will see a couple of words that may or may not make sense together. You will have to rearrange the letter to make the name of the person you need to talk to.
This type of clue has you work out a logical problem for the person you need to talk to. This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium, hard and elite.
There are also challenges that will involve you gathering an item or crafting an item for a certain person.
This type of clue has you talk to someone around Gielinor. Although the clue does not tell you exactly who to talk to. This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium, hard and elite.
A cipher is a string of letters that have been scrambled using the shift cipher method.
An example of this would be ZCZL which, shifted forward by one, would be Adam.
This type of clue will have you use a sextant, chart and a watch to find out the place you will need to dig. This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium and above.
After you find the place you need to dig, you may find a casket or another scroll.
This type of clue can be as simple as talk to the specified person or searching a crate in a specified location.
But the higher the tier of clue, the more steps you will have to do beforehand. An example of this would be needing to find a key before opening a chest.
This type of clue will give you a location that you will need to visit, along with some items you will need.
At this location you will need to perform an emote, as well as wear the items that you had to bring along.
Some clues may have you wear nothing at all.
But please don't do that in public!
This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium and above.
Depending on the tier of clue, you will need to obtain a strange device from either Reldo, located in Varrock, or Jorral, located south of Tree Gnome Stronghold.
You will then need to use this device to find the location you will need to dig.
There are many different puzzles that you can come across while doing clues. These range from light boxes to puzzle boxes.
Puzzle boxes are puzzles that will have you complete a slider puzzle that, when complete, will look like an image in game.
Light boxes are a puzzle which contains a 5 by 5 grid of lights with some lights on and some lights off.
The puzzle will have you click the buttons below to turn on or off some of the lights with the end goal being, having all the lights turned on.
This type of clue will show you a map of an area.
This map will show you where you will need to dig, or what you will need to search to get the next clue.
This type of clue will show you which fairy ring code you will need to use to get to the right place to dig.
You will then need to use the numbers to figure our where you will need to dig after arriving to your destination.

before-desert-treasure-i.npc: Howdy stranger. What brings you out to these parts?

steps.player: Nothing much - What are you doing here? It doesn't seem like there's much to do out here in the desert!

steps.npc: Well, that's where you'd be wrong. I work for the Archaeological Society of Varrock, and have been excavating around here recently.
Was there something you specifically wanted?

steps.player: Do you have any quests? Call it a hunch, but you look like the type of man who might...

steps.npc: Well, it's funny you should say that. I'm not sure if I would really call it a quest as such, but I found this ancient stone tablet in one of my excavations, and it would really help me out if you
could go and take it back to the digsite for me and get it examined.
It's very old, and I don't recognise any of the inscriptions on it.

steps.prompt: Start the Desert Treasure I quest?

steps.text: Continues in Transcript:Desert Treasure I

steps.player: No thanks. Playing delivery boy doesn't really sound much like fun to me.

steps.npc: Well, okay. Can't say as I blame you for thinking that. I'll go take it there myself later I guess.

steps.player: Who are you, anyway?

steps.npc: You don't recognise me??? I am the world famous Asgarnia Smith, Archaeologist extraordinaire!
I am the one who discovered the long forgotten Temple of Ikov! The one who unearthed the strange trap filled arena in Brimhaven!
I'm the leading archaeological expert of our time! I was voted archaeologist of the year four years running by the Varrock Herald! Are you REALLY sure you've never heard of me?

steps.player: No, I really haven't.

steps.npc: Well then, I'm confused. Why did you come over and speak to me if you don't know who I am? What do you want?

steps.player: Nothing really. I'm just wandering around for no good reason.

steps.npc: Uh-huh. Well, if you'll excuse me, I have a lot more work to do before I can bed down for the night.

after-desert-treasure-i.npc: Hello again. You find any signs of that treasure yet?

after-desert-treasure-i.player: Well... not as such, but I unleashed a powerful demon from its tomb in return for unbelievable magical power.
Not as such, no. Sorry about that.

after-desert-treasure-i.npc: Aw... I was hoping to go abroad on holiday this year.
Maybe I'll go check out Karamja next, I hear there's treasure to be found there...

steps.player: I was wondering...
As you are a big famous archaeologist, maybe you could spare the time to tell me a couple of tales of your exploits?

steps.npc: Hey, sure thing kid! Well, this one time I found this spooky old temple in the middle of the jungle.
The entrance was hidden from sight by all these vines and stuff, and it was full of zombies and crazy tribesmen and stuff.
That wasn't the worst thing though! There were all these crazy traps that were hidden around the place too!
Well anyway, I found the secret entrance, fought my way in through the zombies and tribesmen, and came to a big pedestal with a statue of solid gold sat on top of it!

steps.player: Solid gold, huh? Wow.

steps.npc: That's right! It was a cunning trap though! As soon as I picked up the statue, a trapdoor opened up underneath me, and I fell into a darkened room, full of
bones, and the biggest meanest tribesman you ever did see!
Huge he was, and real ugly looking! He had this huge sword too, and he came running towards me screaming something in some language I didn't understand!

steps.player: What did you do?

steps.npc: Well, while he was screaming at me, and swinging his sword around in front of me, trying to intimidate me before attacking, I cooly and calmly...

steps.player: Yes?

steps.npc: All the while, knowing that if I died in this spot nobody would even know where I was...

steps.player: What then?

steps.npc: I knew, if this tribesman killed me, that would be the end of Asgarnia Smith, and all of his treasure hunting...

steps.player: SO WHAT DID YOU DO?!?!

steps.npc: Well, while he was screaming and waving his sword around, I stood behind a nearby stalactite, then shot him with my shortbow.
And that was how I recovered the Golden Monkey of Tee-Ta-Toh.

options.text: Tell me how you became an Archaeologist

steps.player: So... How exactly did you get into this line of work anyway?
It seems an odd choice of career for a man like yourself.

steps.npc: Thinking of joining your pal Asgarnia in the wonderful world of treasure hun- um, archaeology, huh?
Well, it all started the day I was fishing in catherby, funnily enough.
Ah yes, I remember it well... I was just sat there, hoping to catch a bass or two, when I made the most amazing discovery!
In my fishing nets, I had found an ancient casket, marred and worn by centuries underwater!
With trembling hands, I slowly and cautiously opened it, wondering what ancient secret may have been kept inside...
What valuable heirloom may have been dredged up by my nets that had not decayed underwater long ago...
And you know what I found inside?

steps.player: No, what?

steps.npc: I found 320 coins! Just like that! Just by fishing I had found 320 coins! 320 coins! Can you believe it?

steps.player: Um... Yes, yes I can.

steps.npc: Well, it might not seem much to us now kid, but back then, it was a revelation!
Why waste my time fishing when there were secret treasures from long ago hidden around the world?
I immediately applied to the Museum of Varrock as a field agent, and the rest is history!

steps.player: Nice hat!

steps.npc: Hey, thanks kid. Looking snazzy is an important part of being a treasure hunter!

steps.player: Well, I'll see you again sometime maybe. Sorry I couldn't get you any treasure...

steps.npc: Ah, don't sweat it kid. I'll be honest with ya - I'm already rich many times over, and its more the kicks of being a treasure hunter I do it for than the actual cash!

right-click-check-approval.player: Can you tell me how the kingdom approves of me?

steps.npc: Hello, [player name].

steps.player: Tell me more about Nex.

steps.npc: Long ago, these lands were dominated by a great empire, ruled over by an ancient god. The Empty Lord is what they often called him, but his true name was Zaros.

steps.player: Zaros? I've heard of him.

steps.npc: At the height of his power, Zaros seemed untouchable, but he was eventually defeated by those he trusted the most. With him gone, the empire collapsed. War broke out soon after.
Although their god was gone, many Zarosians fought to keep his empire alive. Among them was Nex. She was Zaros' most powerful weapon, and she led a great army to try and restore his empire.
Not that she needed an army of course. Nex alone was powerful enough to hold back hundreds of lesser beings.

steps.player: So how did she end up here?

steps.npc: The forces of Saradomin knew that Nex needed to be dealt with. They were able to lure her into these caverns.
After great effort and sacrifice, they managed to place Nex and her followers into a frozen, enchanted sleep.
Once Nex was no longer an immediate threat, they built the Temple of Lost Ancients around her. Most of the temple has since fallen to ruin, but you can still see some of the remains.

steps.player: But she wasn't frozen forever, was she? You said you were fooled into freeing her.

steps.npc: Yes. Later in the war, a great battle broke out in the Temple of Lost Ancients. I was a Saradominist soldier at the time, and I was among those who fought for him in that battle.

By then, many of us had grown tired of war. One of our priests discovered this. He came to us and revealed that he felt the same way, and that he had secretly converted to Guthix. He encouraged us to join him.
We abandoned the cause of Saradomin and became followers of Guthix. Our new leader taught us the ways of the druids, including an ancient ritual that had the power to awaken Guthix himself.
We believed this ritual to be the only way to end the war.

steps.player: But I'm guessing that's not how things went?

steps.npc: No... When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. The ritual also destroyed the protective enchantments on their prison.

steps.player: And that was exactly what your leader wanted?

steps.npc: It was. He had never been a follower of Guthix, or Saradomin. His real goal had always been to free Nex.

The rest is as I already told you. Nex posed such a danger, that the four armies temporarily joined forces to drive her back into the prison. They resealed it, but were unable to fix the enchantments we destroyed.

As for me, I was one of the first to fall after Nex was freed, but I didn't truly die. Something about our ritual tied me to this place. I've been trapped here ever since. Not dead, but not really alive either.

steps.player: I'm sorry.

steps.npc: Don't be. This is the punishment for my sins.

steps.player: What of the one that led the ritual. What came of him?

steps.npc: He'd achieved his goal, so he left. I never saw him again.

steps.player: But who was he really?

steps.npc: He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him.

steps.player: She knew him?

steps.npc: It seemed that way. I heard little of what they said, but I did hear what she called him.

steps.player: What was it?

steps.npc: Sliske.
Forgive me, but this conversation has brought back many memories. Let us speak no more of this.
