Or, if that doesn't interest you, then maybe you have something else to offer? I'm always on the look out for interesting or unusual new materials.

options.text: Okay, lets see what you've got then.

steps.player: Okay, let's see what you've got then.

options.text: Do you have a spare Priest Gown?
options.condition: During Biohazard:

steps.player: Do you have a spare Priest Gown?

steps.npc: Well I do sell them. I don't hand them out for free though. This is a shop not a charity.

steps.player: Please! It's really important.

steps.npc: Well I suppose you can have this old one. It's not in good enough condition to sell.

steps.text: You are given a Priest Gown.

steps.player: Thank you.

options.text: Could you make another bird costume for me?

steps.player: Could you make another eagle costume for me?

steps.npc: Certainly, if you can supply the materials. I'll need appropriate feathers, swamp tar and some yellow dye. It'll also cost you 25 gold pieces.

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.

options.text: I think I might just leave the perusing for now thanks.

steps.player: I think I might just leave the perusing for now, thanks.

options.text: Can you make clothing suitable for hunting in?

steps.player: Can you make clothing suitable for hunting?

steps.npc: Certainly. Take a look at my range of made-to-order items. If you can supply the furs, I'll gladly make any of these for you.

options.text: What sort of unusual materials did you have in mind?

steps.player: What sort of unusual materials did you have in mind?

steps.npc: Well, some more colourful feathers might be useful. For some surreal reason, all I normally seem to get offered are large quantities of rather beaten-up looking chicken feathers.
People must have some very strange pastimes around these parts, that's all I can say.

steps.player: Ok, let's see what you've got then.

on-a-non-members-world.npc: Sorry, we're closed at the moment.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guildmaster-apa.text: If the player does not meet the quest's requirements:

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Sorry, but you need to be a better hunter before we can help you out.
You need 46 Hunter to access Hunter Guild amenities.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guildmaster-apa.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guildmaster-apa.text: Oh, you're a new face around here, aren't you?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guildmaster-apa.player: I am indeed. Just exploring the savannah.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guildmaster-apa.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guildmaster-apa.text: Well, I'm Apatura. Let me welcome you to our small corner of Varlamore.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: We're mostly here to keep an eye on the local animal populations, and provide animal parts to the city.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: As for me personally, I'm the current master of this guild.

steps.player: Current master?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: A hunter's work is dangerous. We tend to go through members faster than other guilds. That said, I'm usually too busy with politics and paperwork to go out hunting these days.

steps.player: Could I hunt with the guild?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Absolutely! There's always more work to be done. Head down into the Burrow and talk to the other hunters to get an idea of what we need help with.

options.text: Can I help you with anything?

steps.player: Can I help you with anything?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: I'm not sure if you have the time or the patience, iknami, but a little birdy told me that our esteemed scribe Verity may require some assistance.

steps.player: What sort of assistance?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: If I had to guess, she needs someone to find something for her.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: She's a wonderful scribe, but can lose some strange things here and there.

steps.prompt: Start the At First Light quest?

steps.player: Great! Point me in her direction and I'll get cracking!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: She's behind the bar in the Burrow. Just look for the stressed woman trying to wrangle a bunch of barely- bathed hunters.

steps.player: I'm not sure I have the time for that right now.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Tetamo... Well, hopefully it's not too important.

steps.player: I'd better be off.

options.text: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.player: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Absolutely. Have you spoken to Verity yet?

steps.player: No, not quite yet.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: If you're having a hard time finding her, she's behind the bar in the Burrow. Head down the stairs in the big tree. You can't miss it, and if you can, maybe you're not cut out for the Hunter Guild.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: If the player has never talked to Guild Scribe Verity:

steps.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
steps.text: Oh, hello there newcomer. I'm Guild Scribe Verity. Do you need me to explain the work we do here?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
steps.text: So it's nice and simple. Just chat to any of the hunters in here to help them out. They're all following reports that I've split up amongst them.

steps.player: Reports?

steps.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
steps.text: Indeed. There are all sorts of interesting creatures to hunt out there. Sometimes we get reports of a particularly unique example. When that happens, one of the hunters will set out to find it.

steps.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
steps.text: If you do decide to take a job from any of the hunters, they'll tell you what type of creature they're looking into. Hunt that creature until you encounter the unique specimen.

steps.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
steps.text: Once you've caught it, bring some proof back to the hunter that sent you out in the first place. I'm sure they'll reward you for your time.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
steps.text: Now, what else can I do for you.

steps.player: Well actually, I heard there might be something I could help you with?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: If the player has previously talked to Guild Scribe Verity:

steps.player: Hi Verity. I heard there might be something I could help you with?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: You'll have to be slightly more specific. There's always something that needs doing down here!

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.player: Something a little birdy may have told Apatura?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: Tetamo... Pitri needs to stop twittering with the birds. Yes, Gilman and I are concerned about Fox. He left quietly in the night, but we have no record of what he was doing.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.player: Do you normally keep track of the hunters here?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: We try to, but it's like herding cats! We at least like to keep an eye on what they're hunting and point them in the right direction. It prevents us from losing track of too many creatures... or people.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.player: Could anyone else have put Fox onto a hunt?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: If anyone did, it would've been Wolf. She's always getting Fox into some kind of trouble.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.player: I'll follow up with her then.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.text: Have you spoken to Wolf yet?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-scribe-ve.player: Not yet. I'll have a chat to her now.

options.text: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.player: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Absolutely. So was our little birdy right about Verity needing a hand?

steps.player: They were... It wasn't an actual bird was it?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Of course not. Only Pitri talks to the birds.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: So, here to ask me what trouble I've gotten Fox into, are you?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.player: That's not quite how I'd word it... but how did you know?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: I've honed my instincts over the years.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: Well, that and the fact you had that whole conversation within earshot.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.player: Right... So did you send Fox out to do something?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: Sort of. He's on some very unofficial business for me.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: If I told you... I'd have to kill you!

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: Your face! Don't worry, I'm just pulling your leg.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: I asked him to look into making some repairs to Kiko's bed. It's been getting tatty lately. I'm guessing he didn't end up having the materials needed. That'll be why he headed out.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.player: Well then I guess the first step is to work out what he went to get. Could I take a look at Kiko's bed?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: You're welcome to try, but you'll need to convince Kiko to let you. He's just by the table there.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: He's very easy to distract. We have a little fake mouse we use sometimes.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.player: Could I borrow it when I have a free hand to take it?

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
steps.text: Sure thing.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.player: Could I borrow it to have a go at distracting him?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: Wolf hands you a small toy mouse.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: Have you checked Kiko's bed yet? It's just to the side of this table.
If the player has inventory space and has not yet gotten the mouse:

steps.player: Not yet. Could I grab that mouse to distract him with?

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
steps.text: Absolutely.
Wolf hands you a small toy mouse.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: If the player has the toy mouse in their inventory:

steps.player: Not yet. I'll get to it now.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-guild-hunter-wo.text: If the player lost the toy mouse:

steps.player: Not yet. Do you happen to have that mouse to distract him with?

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
steps.text: I already gave it to you. If you've lost it, you'll need to get another for yourself. I'd do so quickly if I were you. Kiko won't be happy if he finds out it's gone.

a-missing-fox-petting-kiko.text: If the player doesn't have a catspeak amulet or Dragon Slayer II completed:

steps.text: You pet the cat, who leans into your hand in return.

a-missing-fox-petting-kiko.speaker: Guild Hunter Kiko
a-missing-fox-petting-kiko.text: Can you scratch my belly next? It's perfectly safe.

a-missing-fox-using-an-unwound-toy-mouse.speaker: Guild Hunter Kiko
a-missing-fox-using-an-unwound-toy-mouse.text: Are you not going to wind it up first? Come on now, put some effort in.

a-missing-fox-checking-the-cat-bed.speaker: Guild Hunter Kiko
a-missing-fox-checking-the-cat-bed.text: Do you mind? I'm trying to sleep here.
If the player has a toy mouse (wound):

steps.player: Here you go, little guy.

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Kiko
steps.text: A mouse? Fantastic!

You check the cat's bed. It sure could use a little bit of love... and a lot of repairs. It's made of a luxurious fluffy fur that you don't recognise. It looks like someone has intentionally cut off a small bit of it.

a-missing-fox-using-a-wound-toy-mouse-on.text: Kiko happily starts playing with the toy mouse.
You see that the cat's bed is unsurprisingly still in need of repairs.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.player: I managed to have a look at that bed. I've never seen such luxury material for a cat bed before.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.text: Only the best for our Kiko.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.player: I'm guessing it's the actual fur itself that Fox will be looking to replace. It looks like he cut a small bit off. I don't suppose you know where he'd have gone to get that.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.text: We have a contact who lives in Outer Fortis. She stocks the best of the best when it comes to fabrics. That'll be where he went, but knowing Fox, he won't have gone directly there.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.text: He'll have stopped off for a bit of hunting first. There are some pyre foxes about halfway between here and the Locus Oasis that he was eyeing up. I bet that's where you'll find him.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.player: In that case, I'd better get out there then.
I haven't yet. You said he might be hunting pyre foxes, right?

a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
a-missing-fox-talking-to-wolf-after-insp.text: That's right. They're about halfway between here and the Locus Oasis.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-verity-after-sp.player: It seems like Fox is trying to find something to repair Kiko's bed with.

a-missing-fox-talking-to-verity-after-sp.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
a-missing-fox-talking-to-verity-after-sp.text: Why does that not surprise me? There's two things that man loves: that cat, and not filing in his reports correctly.

options.text: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.player: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.player: I checked in with Verity and apparently Fox has gone missing.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Ha, that certainly sounds like Fox! What errand has Wolf got him running this time?

steps.player: How did you know Wolf was involved?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Let's just say you don't run things around here without good instincts. Let me guess - it's also got something to do with Kiko.

steps.player: That's spot on! How did you know?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: It's an open secret how much Fox and Wolf care about that cat. We all do of course, but those two don't half spoil him rotten.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.player: Are you Fox? Everyone's worried about you.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: Something attacked me in the dark... I can't move much...

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.player: Can I help you? Maybe patch you up?

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: That would be much appreciated! There should be a couple of plants around to make a poultice... Hold it together with an embertailed jerboa tail, and...

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: There should be a couple of plants around to make a... make a...

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.player: Stay with me, Fox! Where are these plants?

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: It's a bit fuzzy... I've lost a lot of blood! One should be around here... the other may be near the oasis... with the capybabas... haha, capybaras...

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.player: And what am I making with them?

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: A poultice! And hold it together with the tail from an embertailed jerboa.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: Don't forget... your traps for the jerboa... they're boxy...

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-fox.text: How's that poul... pool... poultice... Did you find the plants?

options.text: I think I've got them both.

steps.player: I think I've got them both.

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: It doesn't look like you do... Who's the one with the head wound again?

steps.player: Where can I find them?

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: It's a bit fuzzy... I've lost a lot of blood! One should be around here... the other may be near the oasis... with the capybabas... haha, capybaras...

options.text: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.player: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.player: Fox has been injured out in the savannah!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Well, that is impressive. How has he managed that?

steps.player: He said he was attacked by an unknown assailant.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Well as you're not offering your condolences, I can only assume he's survived the encounter?

steps.player: He should be fine once I help him make a poultice for the wound.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Excellent. A final question - was his hand injured?

steps.player: No?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Wonderful! Then I look foward to reading his report.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.player: I've found Fox. He's been injured by something out in the savannah.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.text: Oh no... I should've offered to go with him. It's never sensible to be out after dark alone...

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.player: I'm going to do what I can to make sure he's okay.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.text: Well thanks for checking in at least. He's still breathing and that's all Fox needs to come out on top.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-scribe-ver.player: He's been injured out in the savannah, but I'll do my best to make sure he makes it back.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-scribe-ver.speaker: Guild Scribe Verity
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-scribe-ver.text: Tetamo! Only he could get injured on an errand for a cat!

steps.text: You pull a smooth leaf off the bush.

fox-tracking-picking-the-leafy-bush.text: If the player already has a smooth leaf:

steps.player: I don't think I need any more leaves from this bush.

steps.text: You pull a sticky leaf off the bush.

fox-tracking-picking-the-rough-looking-b.text: If the player already has a sticky leaf:

steps.player: I don't think I need any more leaves from this bush.

fox-tracking-using-two-poultice-ingredie.text: You need leaves from two different plants along with an embertailed jerboa tail to make the poultice Fox asked for.
You craft a makeshift poultice. It looks like it should just about do the job.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.player: I have that poultice here for you.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: You give the poultice to Fox.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: Kuani! That's making a difference already.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.player: Happy to help. Now, how did you get on finding what you needed to fix Kiko's bed?

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: I thought a little detour wouldn't hurt. I'd caught a glimpse of the most stunning pelt ever seen!

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: As I was tracking it, I was attacked and knocked out. When I came to, it was gone.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: Without a trace, as well as most of my hunting equipment.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.player: Do you think someone attacked you for it, or was it just an opportunist looting you?

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: You've already done me a huge favour, but I don't suppose I could ask for one more small one?

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.player: I suppose I could. Especially if it goes towards repairing that cat's bed and getting you back to the guild.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: Well it's your lucky day! Make some room and I'll give you the sample needed to fix the bed.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: Well it's your lucky day! Take this sample to a woman called Atza in Outer Fortis. She'll have exactly what we need.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.player: Where in the outskirts can I find her? And... what exactly do we need, again?

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-with-the-mak.text: She lives by the south western gate of the city. She'll be able to give us the matching fur to repair the cat's bed with.
Fox gives you a fur sample.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-after-giving.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-after-giving.text: I thought a little detour wouldn't hurt. I'd caught a glimpse of the most stunning pelt ever seen!

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-before-getti.text: Fox gives you a fur sample.
If the player still has the fur sample or has a full inventory and not yet received the sample:

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: Any success with Atza yet?

steps.player: Not quite.

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: If you're struggling to find her, she's in Outer Fortis, near the south western gate.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-before-getti.text: If the player lost the fur sample and has a full inventory:

steps.player: I appear to have lost the sample you gave me...

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: Luckily, I always come prepared. Here's a spare.

steps.player: Ah. It seems I don't have room for it.

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: Well I'm not going anywhere. Let me know when you do have room.

fox-tracking-talking-to-fox-before-getti.text: If the player lost the fur sample:

steps.player: I don't suppose you've got another sample of Kiko's bed for me to take to Atza?

steps.speaker: Guild Hunter Fox
steps.text: Fortunately for you, I'm always prepared... And our thief clearly didn't care for fine fur samples.

steps.player: That's convenient! Usually I'm the one that's always ready for these situations.

steps.text: Fox gives you a fur sample.

options.text: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.player: Are you free to talk about my quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster Apatura
steps.text: Absolutely. How's it going, iknami?

steps.player: We're getting there. I should have everything sorted very soon.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.player: He's doing well. He's got me doing a few things for him whilst he recuperates.

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.speaker: Guild Hunter Wolf (Master)
fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-hunter-wol.text: Ha! Now that's the Fox I know. I'll have to give him some odd jobs once he's back to make up for ones you're covering!

fox-tracking-talking-to-guild-scribe-ver.player: I'm still working on it, but I'm getting there.

fox-tracking-talking-to-atza.player: Hi there. You must be Atza. I heard you're the person to talk to about getting some material to match a sample?

fox-tracking-talking-to-atza.speaker: Atza
fox-tracking-talking-to-atza.text: I might be. Depends who's asking... and what you're looking for, of course.

fox-tracking-talking-to-atza.player: Your friend Fox was going to bring this sample to you, but he's been a little... waylaid.

fox-tracking-talking-to-atza.speaker: Atza
fox-tracking-talking-to-atza.text: Well, this wouldn't be the first time! Let's take a look.
If the player lost the sample:

steps.player: I don't seem to have it with me.

steps.speaker: Atza

steps.npc: Hello there, [player name]. What can I do for you?

steps.player: How are things?

steps.npc: Now that the situation in the ruins is under control, things are nice and quiet, which is just what we need. That whole business down there got a lot of dwarves riled up.
Naturally, most blame you humans.

steps.player: Of course. Have you tried explaining to them that we actually helped?

steps.npc: Ha! Good one. You think I'm going to make a laughing stock of myself by daring to claim a human did something positive? Keep dreaming!

options.text: So how long has Cam Torum been around?

steps.player: So how long has Cam Torum been around?

steps.npc: What am I, a historian?

steps.player: No, but you're the only dwarf here that might be willing to share that sort of information with me.

steps.npc: Hmph. Very well. The Varlamorians won't mention this, but we were the first to settle here. Our ancestors saw the writing on the wall when Xeric came to power in Kourend. They chose not to stick around.

steps.player: Must have been a big thing for them, leaving their home.

steps.npc: Doubtful. My people are all too familiar with that sort of thing. The Lovakengj dwarves have mostly forgotten their history, but we Dwarves of Cam Torum remember it all too well.

steps.player: Remember what?

steps.npc: Before Lovakengj, there was Imcandoria. Our ancestors there were forced to abandon their home, just as we were forced to leave Kourend.
If you humans had had your way, we might have had to abandon Cam Torum by now as well.

steps.player: You don't know that.

steps.npc: But I do know that. As I said, we remember our history, and we know that those who don't are doomed to repeat it.
The Varlamorians nearly destroyed themselves in their War of Betrayal, but it was not them who were betrayed, it was us.
I was a young dwarf when their war risked destroying our home. I saw the results of their pride. Meanwhile, they've all but forgotten it.

steps.player: Sorry. I didn't mean to dig up old wounds.

steps.npc: Hmph. It's fine. Your intentions are good, [player name], which is more than can be said for most of your kind. Who knows, maybe one or two dwarves here might even grow to tolerate you.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

steps.npc: That patch is diseased - you should cure it before asking me to be responsible for it!

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in
the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Hops are good for brewing ales. There's a brewery over on Aldarin if you fancy trying it.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

steps.player: I'd like information, please.

steps.npc: Just a few bits of information before you run away to persecute rock crabs or cows.
Firstly, your new device won't work if you are wearing certain metallic chest armours.
The magnetic attraction required for operation would cause feedback, so the device does not allow such incompatible item equip page.
Secondly, although the device is calibrated to attract only arrow heads, there is a chance that other magnetically active items will be attracted.

The arrow recovery function of the devices is slightly different and relies upon a harmonic bond between your arrows and the chicken's magnet. You'll thus only recover arrows which you have fired rather than those
fired by nearby folks.
You'll also need to move about if you want to collect arrows since the gathering of long-lost arrowheads can't work otherwise.
Finally, the device will only work when worn. It automatically deactivates in other circumstances.
I was worried about what would happen if you were to place it in a bank in its active state, so I've made sure it only works when it's on your back.

steps.player: Okay, I don't mind hearing sto-

steps.npc: Wonderful!
Well, I was going through some ancient documents recently, expanding my knowledge of our great ancestors...
Hmm, actually, I think I had better go further back, so you will understand.
You know of our ancient war with the Fremennik that you recently healed?

steps.player: Of course! I am a great diplomat, aren't I?

steps.npc: Some diplomat. Did you even discover WHY we were at war for so long?

steps.player: Errr... You couldn't see eye to eye about magic, or something like that.

steps.npc: Not too far off; it goes deeper than that.
The Fremennik were actually the first to discover how to make runes, but there was disagreement within the tribe about the implications of making such powerful objects.

Most Fremennik felt we were stealing power from the gods. They could not see past that to the great things we could do with such power, so we split from them and became the Moon Clan. Our ancient leader, who first

discovered the rune essence mine here on Lunar Isle, travelled far and wide searching for more places of power. He and his followers built altars all over Gielinor - which you use today to create runes - and at their

height they made runes by the crateful. They had perfected the process and even advanced it, creating altars that could create any type of rune regardless of the crafter's ability. But the strife between the Moon

Clan and the Fremennik heightened. The Fremennik had grown strong in body, while our clan had grown stong in mind. They overpowered our tribe and we retreated to Lunar Isle, where we had lived ever since.
The Fremennik then swept over Gielinor destroying the altars we had made, in an attempt to remove all trace of magic from the land.

steps.player: That's all very interesting, but what's it got to do with this spell?

steps.npc: I'm getting to that!

The Fremennik were not as thorough as they thought. They destroyed only the entrances to the altars, for the altars themselves were on a different plane, but they were successful in wiping out our ability to create
runes. That ability has only recently been rediscovered on the mainland, so I hear.

Our people were left isolated on Lunar Isle but we used it to our advantage. Our control over Magic advanced beyond the need for runes and all knowledge of the altar locations passed from memory. Fortunately,

some records survived... The manuscript I discovered contains the teleportation spell to an advanced altar called Ourania. It's an altar that allows the user, regardless of their Runecrafting ability, to craft any
type of rune upon it. Ourania is a powerful altar indeed. What state it is in after so many millennia, I know not, but it's interesting all the same.

steps.player: So, will you teach me the spell?

steps.npc: Certainly.
*Baby Yaga whispers in your ear*

steps.player: I believe I understand now.

steps.npc: Oh? Do tell.

steps.player: Well, while us adventurers have been doing our best to fight against the Devourer's corruption, we've been neglecting what has been lost to achieve that goal. Namely, the four guardians we defeated along the way.
Ba-Ba was a proud baboon who wished for her troop to flourish. To honour her, I made sure that they won't be forgotten by telling their story to the monkeys of Ape Atoll.
Akkha was cruelly denied death by the Devourer, so I gave his ashes to the High Priest of Icthlarin to give him a proper send-off.
Zebak was fooled into leaving his home and confined within the tomb, so I took his fang and buried it on an island surrounded by crocodiles.
Kephri was promised a future for her race, but it was all a lie. I found a scarab egg within some of her dung, and I gave it to the High Priest of Scabaras to try and nurture it.

steps.npc: Well well, colour me impressed adventurer. It seems that you do care after all.
It's a shame that much of the damage cannot truly be undone, but I know that Het, Apmeken, Crondis and even Scabaras will be grateful for your actions.

options.text: How do I use the bank?

steps.player: Using the bank itself. I'm not sure how....?

steps.npc: Speak to any banker and ask to see your bank account. If you have set a PIN you will be asked for it, then all the belongings you have placed in the bank will appear in the window. To withdraw one item, left-
click on it once.

To withdraw many, right-click on the item and select from the menu. The same for depositing, left-click on the item in your inventory to deposit it in the bank. Right-click on it to deposit many of the same items.

To move things around in your bank: firstly select Swap or Insert as your default moving mode, you can find these buttons on the bank window itself. Then click and drag an item to where you want it to appear.
You may withdraw 'notes' or 'certificates' when the items you are trying to withdraw do not stack in your inventory. This will only work for items which are tradable.

For instance, if you wanted to sell 100 logs to another player, they would not fit in one inventory and you would need to do multiple trades. Instead, click the Note button to do withdraw the logs as 'certs' or 'notes',
then withdraw the items you need.

steps.player: Using Bank deposit boxes.... what are they?

steps.npc: They look like grey pillars, there's one just over there, near the desk. Bank deposit boxes save so much time. If you're simply wanting to deposit a single item, 'Use' it on the deposit box.
Otherwise, simply click once on the box and it will give you a choice of what to deposit in an interface very similar to the bank itself. Very quick for when you're simply fishing or mining etc.

options.text: What's this PIN thing that people keep talking about?

steps.player: What's this PIN thing that people keep talking about?

steps.npc: The PIN - Personal Identification Number - can be set on your bank account to protect the items there in case someone finds out your account password. It consists of four numbers that you remember and tell
no one.
So if someone did manage to get your password they couldn't steal your items if they were in the bank.

options.text: How do I set my PIN?

steps.player: How do I set my PIN?

steps.npc: You can set your PIN by talking to any banker, they will allow you to access your bank pin settings. Here you can choose to set your pin and recovery delay. Remember not to set it to anything personal such as
your real life bank PIN or birthday.

The recovery delay is to protect your banked items from account thieves. If someone stole your account and asked to have the PIN deleted, they would have to wait a few days before accessing your bank account to
steal your items. This will give you time to recover your account.
There will also be a delay in actually setting the PIN to be used, this is so that if your account is stolen and a PIN set, you can cancel it before it comes into use!

options.text: How do I remove my PIN?

steps.player: How do I remove my PIN?

steps.npc: Talking to any banker will enable you to access your PIN settings. There you can cancel or change your PIN, but you will need to wait for your recovery delay to expire to be able to access your bank. This
can be set in the settings page and will protect your items should your account be stolen.

options.text: What happens if I forget my PIN?

steps.player: What happens if I forget my PIN?

steps.npc: If you find yourself faced with the PIN keypad and you don't know the PIN, just look on the right-hand side for a button marked 'I don't know it'. Click this button. Your PIN will be deleted (after a delay of a
few days) and you'll be able to use your bank as before. You may still use the bank deposit box without your PIN.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: To learn more of such as tool, you must first focus your studies on those fish that the tool is used to catch.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: You must catch fish which are usually harpooned, without a harpoon. You will be using your skill and strength.

steps.player: How do you expect me to do that?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Use your arm as bait. Wriggle your fingers as if they are a tasty snack and hungry tuna and swordfish will throng to be caught by you.

steps.player: That sounds rather insanely dangerous. I'm glad you didn't mention shark too.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Oh, my mind slipped for a moment, this method does indeed work with shark - though in this case the action must be more of a frenzied thrashing of the arm than a wriggle.

steps.player: ... and I thought fishing was a safe way to pass the time.
I seek more knowledge.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.

steps.player: I have no more questions at this time.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: In that case, farewell.

options.text: What can I learn about the use of a fishing rod?

steps.player: What can I learn about the use of a fishing rod?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: While you civilised folk use small, weak fishing rods, we barbarians are skilled with heavier tackle. We fish in the lake nearby.

steps.player: So can you teach me of your methods?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Certainly. Take the rod from under my bed and fish in the lake. When you have caught a few fish, I am sure you will be ready to talk more with me.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: You will know when you are ready, since inspiration will fill your mind.

steps.player: So I can obtain new foods from these fishing spots?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: We do not use these fish quite as you might expect. When you return we can speak more of this matter.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
I'm ready for your firemaking wisdom. Please instruct me.

steps.player: I'm ready for your firemaking wisdom. Please instruct me.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The first point in your progression is that of lighting fires without a tinderbox.

steps.player: That sounds pretty useful. Tell me more.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: For this process you will require a strung bow. You use the bow to quickly rotate pieces of wood against one another. As you rub the wood, it becomes hot, eventually springing into flame.

steps.player: No more secret details?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The spirits will aid you. The power they supply will guide your hands. Go and benefit from their guidance upon oak logs.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
How can I use my strength in the ways of agriculture?

steps.player: How can I use my strength in the ways of agriculture?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Ah, so you wish to get your hands dirty? I can teach you how to plant seeds without the use of a seed dibber.

steps.player: I can handle a little bit of muck. How does this work?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The difficulty in this method is providing enough force to deeply root the seed in the ground, yet with enough care so that the the seed itself is not damaged.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Practice this. You might fail at first, especially if like many a barbarian, you are not used to holding back. Indeed, it may be wise to avoid using seeds you are not willing to lose.

steps.player: I'll do my best.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Remember to be calm, and good luck.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

starting-off-after-speaking-to-him-once-.speaker: Otto Godblessed
starting-off-after-speaking-to-him-once-.text: Good day to you, hearty warrior! May the spirits guide you.

options.text: Please teach me of your cunning with harpoons.

steps.player: Please teach me of your cunning with harpoons.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I see you need encouragement in learning the ways of fishing without a harpoon.

steps.player: It's not the most safe-sounding task I have ever been given.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Neither is it the most deadly. Go now and return when you have drawn a fish from the sea, with sheer strength and knowledge of our scaled prey.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
What can I learn about the use of a fishing rod?

steps.player: What can I learn about the use of a fishing rod?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Alas, I do not sense that you have been successful in your fishing yet. The look in your eyes is not that of the osprey.

steps.player: Osprey?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Legendary birds, which the ignorant call eagles. They prey upon fish. Do as they do to gain inspiration.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
I'm ready for your firemaking wisdom. Please instruct me.

steps.player: I'm ready for your firemaking wisdom. Please instruct me.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: By now you know my response.

steps.player: Go and light some oak logs using a strung bow?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Exactly.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
How can I use my strength in the ways of agriculture?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I see you have yet to be successful in planting a seed with your fists.

steps.player: It's definitely one of the more delicate tasks you have provided me.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Remember to be calm, and good luck.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

starting-off-speaking-to-otto-after-lear.speaker: Otto Godblessed
starting-off-speaking-to-otto-after-lear.text: Good day to you, hearty warrior! May the spirits guide you.

steps.player: Let's talk about my training.

options.text: Do you have anything for me?

steps.player: Do you have anything for me?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I see you have free space and no way to record any information you may recover from the caverns. Please take this book as a record of your researches.
my notes

steps.player: What kind of information are you thinking of?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Those who have previously entered the cavern have not all returned. Some of them seemed intent upon research and discovery as much as loot and daring deeds.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: It would be a shame if you were to recover any of their notes and be unable to record them handily. I hope the new book will give you space for such discoveries.

options.text: Could you tell me more of these spirits you continually refer to?

steps.player: Could you tell me more of these spirits you continually refer to?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Certainly, though it is quite simple - they are the barbarians of the past who have died in the passing of the years. There are three categories which learned sages claim may describe all spirits encountered.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The majority are at peace, having died with their ambitions sated, even if this ambition was as simple as a glorious death. They can contact those in our world in order to spur us on to glory.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Of course, they cannot or will not contact all inhabitants of these lands, for not all are worthy.

steps.player: So those are the spirits who give us guidance. What of the other sorts?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: A second category of spirit is made up of those who are not yet at peace. However, all that is needed is for their mortal remains to be laid to rest and they will join the peaceful majority.

steps.player: I can see the pyres serve this purpose. The final category is also restless?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Alas, there is a small minority who will never be at rest. These have been slain in moments of insanity by their brothers or by adventurers.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: They are not at rest and will attack those they blame for their tortured state. They are not known, however, for being able to determine this blame with any great accuracy, so should be considered dangerous to all.

steps.player: Thank you Otto. It makes a bit more sense now.
I'd better get going.

fishing.speaker: Otto Godblessed
fishing.text: Good day to you, hearty warrior! May the spirits guide you.

steps.player: I've fished with my hands!

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I sense you have more understanding of harpoons through your studies.

steps.player: Well it was interesting, can I move on to more sane hobbies now?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Nothing is sane when one is born knowing only certain death. The spirits approve of you however, so death is on your side.

steps.player: What is that supposed to mean?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I mean that when you eventually die and find peace, at least the spirits you encounter will be your friends. Alas for you adventurous sort, the natural ways of passing are close to impossible.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
I've fished with a barbarian rod!

steps.player: I've fished with a barbarian rod!

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Your mind is as clear as the waters you have fished. This is good.

steps.player: So what do I do with these fish? They are all bloated and so nasty looking that even a starving vulture wouldn't eat one.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Patience young one. These are fish which are fat with eggs rather than fat of flesh. It is these eggs that are the thing to make use of.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
I'm ready for your firemaking wisdom. Please instruct me.
How can I use my strength in the ways of agriculture?

firemaking.speaker: Otto Godblessed
firemaking.text: Good day to you, hearty warrior! May the spirits guide you.

options.text: I've fished with a barbarian rod!
I've set fire to logs with a bow!

steps.player: I've set fire to logs with a bow!

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Fine news indeed!

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
I have completed firemaking with a bow. What follows this?
options.condition: If the player had already selected the option above

steps.player: I have completed firemaking with a bow. What follows this?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The next stage is quite complex, so listen well. In order to send our ancestors into the spirit world, their mortal remains must be burned with due ceremony.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: This can only be done close to the water on the shore of the lake, just to our north-east. You will recognise the correct places by the ashes to be seen there.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: You will need to construct a small ship by using an axe upon logs in this area, then add the bones of a long dead barbarian hero.

steps.player: Where do I obtain these bones?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: From the caverns beneath this lake. Many of our ancestors travelled to these caverns in order to hunt for glory, but found only death. Their bones must still lie inside, their spirits trapped in torment.

steps.player: So I make sure I am in the right place, then throw these bones on a ceremonial ship before I set light to it?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Correct. The spirit will ascend to glory while the pyre will send the earthly remains to the depths. You will also obtain a closer link to the spirit world.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: During this heightened contact, any bones you bury will have increased importance to the gods. The number of bones that may be buried before the link fades will depend on the wood used.

steps.player: Is there anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I have little knowledge of the caverns - they are blocked from the sight of the spirits with whom I commune. I can only suspect that whatever slew the barbarian heroes is indeed mighty.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I also suspect that the bones you seek might well be very uncommon, since heroes are not found in vast numbers.

steps.player: How do I enter the caverns?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Dive into the whirlpool in the lake to the east. The spirits will use their abilities to ensure you arrive in the correct location. Be warned, their influence fades, so you must find your own way out.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
How can I use my strength in the ways of agriculture?

firemaking-speaking-to-otto-after-creati.text: Good day to you, hearty warrior! May the spirits guide you.

I've created a pyre ship!

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Hail to you, saviour of my ancestors. The spirits herald your presence with a spectral fanfare.

steps.player: It's good to be appreciated.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: On this great day you have my eternal thanks. May you find riches while rescuing my spiritual ancestors in the caverns for many moons to come.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: And with that, your training is done. You have gone from apprentice, to master. Seek to inspire all with your daring deeds and legendary feats.

options.text: Tell me more about the use of spears.

steps.player: Tell me more about the use of spears.

steps.text: If Tai Bwo Wannai Trio has not been completed:

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The next step is to manufacture a spear, suitable for combat. To do so, you must speak with our distant cousins on Karamja, in the village of Tai Bwo Wannai.

steps.player: Couldn't you just take a bribe or something? I am sure you could do with some cash.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: I am afraid this is a vital step. The spirits foresee that your understanding of spears will increase through your journey there. You may not progress in the use of spears until you have completed this mission.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.

steps.text: If Tai Bwo Wannai Trio has been completed:

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Many warriors complain that spears are difficult to find, we barbarians thus forge our own.

steps.player: Can I just use some metal on an anvil, or is there something else involved?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: If you use our special barbarian anvil here, you will find it ideal. Other anvils are not sturdy enough or shaped appropriately for the forging work involved. Make any of our spears and return.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Note well that you will require wood for the spear shafts; the quality of wood must be similar to that of the metal involved.

options.text: I have no more questions at this time.
What of the one-handed spears of which you spoke?
options.condition: If the player has learnt how to make spears

steps.player: What of the one handed spears of which you spoke?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The next step is to manufacture a one-handed version of a spear, suitable for combat. Such a spear is known to us as a hasta.

steps.player: Can't I just pick one up and use it in one hand?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: As you might suspect, our ways require greater understanding than is gained by simply looking at a weapon. It is also the case that the process involves a differently

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: balanced spear. Before you may use such a weapon in anger, you must make an example. Only then will you fully understand the poise and techniques involved.

steps.player: So I must manufacture one? I see. This makes sense.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Indeed. You may use our special anvil for this spear type too. The ways of black and dragon spears are beyond our knowledge, however; these spears may not be created.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The secret is linked to the fish in the lake nearby. If you use your knife upon them, several new fishy items will be produced. Fish parts can be used as bait, but the roe and caviar is more useful for us.

steps.player: Do I cook them?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Certainly not. Mixing these items with two dose potions is what should be done. This results in a nutritious slop, perfect for healing as well as imparting the effect of the potion.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Roe can only be used for some of the more easily combined mixes, while caviar may be used for any of the mixes of which I am aware.

steps.player: What if I only have four dose potions?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: You are able to decant a four dose potion into an empty vial, thus giving two potions of two doses. This will aid you in the process.

steps.player: I guess you just want me to go away and make one of these potions?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Have I become so predictable? But yes, I do indeed require a potion. It is of the highest importance that you bring me a lesser attack potion combined with fish roe.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: This technique fully embraces your strength as a barbarian. Nuance is not required here. It's about the fine art of smashing pots.

steps.player: Smashing pots? That doesn't sound overly difficult.

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: The secret is how to smash them in a way that doesn't leave debris on the ground, for that would not be of benefit to the environment.

steps.player: That makes sense. I wouldn't want to be littering shards of pot everywhere. What's the trick?

steps.speaker: Otto Godblessed
steps.text: Planting a tree is strenuous work. You need to channel this energy into pure anger. Release all that anger on the pot that contained it, shattering it into dust!

steps.player: I'm good at getting angry. I'll give it a try.

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-gr.player: Hey there. What are you lot doing out here?

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-gr.npc: We're from the College of Bards in Tempestus. We thought we'd set up camp here to do some performances for anyone travelling through the savannah.
With the kingdom now open to tourists, we've had plenty of new fans!

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-tr.npc: Thanks! I made it myself. The College of Bards insist that we all have the ability to create and maintain our own instruments. I'm quite proud of what I came up with!

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-tr.player: Well I hope it serves you well.

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-ma.npc: Think you've got what it takes to join the College of Bards?
Well it only takes a lifetime of practice, so maybe give it a go one day.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.player: Hi there. Are you enjoying the view?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: I am, though I do wish it would be blocked by the ferry to Tempestus.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.player: The ferry? Is there something wrong with it?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: I'm not sure exactly. All I know is that it's not running at the moment.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.player: How urgently do you need to get there?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: We should be back at the College of Bards already, but I'm sure they'll understand why we got delayed.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.player: Oh, you're a bard? Could you sing for me?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: Maybe. Can you take us to Temptestus?
Then I'm afraid you don't get any singing this time.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Nilsal! Have you come to hear a song from the Sister Songstresses of the College of Bards?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: Sister Songstresses? So you're a group of sisters who sing together?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Don't be silly! Of course we aren't!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: Oh... The name did suggest otherwise...

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Well, we realised when we met that we were all very similar, so we've been using it as a selling point! Everyone loves Snappy Sister, Stormy Sister, and of course me, Spirited Sister!
People love a nice story about a trio of sisters coming together! So yes, it works rather well.
It's all storytelling! Songs, appearance, history. We're telling a story and people want to hear it!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: I'm not sure if people wanting to hear it makes it entirely ethical.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Is it made better if our songs are good?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: Now that you mention it... no of course it isn't.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Well, you're just no fun, iknami.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.player: You seem a little down. What's up?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.npc: I just want to get back to the College of Bards. It's like my spark has gone out being away from such a creative environment.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.player: I'm sure you'll be back there before long.
It doesn't hurt to be hopeful, does it? Not to mention, hope can be a great inspiration!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.npc: Hope can be a great inspiration... Perfect! I'll use that!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.player: Oh... Well, I'm happy to have helped.

before-starting-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Ah! Outerlander! Do not interrupt me in my business! I must cull these fiends!

before-starting-the-fremennik-trials.player: What are you doing down here?

before-starting-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Only an outerlander would ask such a question! Is it not obvious what I am doing?
I kill the daggermouths for glory and for sport! When I have had my fill, I move on to the daggermouths' lair!

before-starting-the-fremennik-trials.player: Erm... okay then. I'll leave you to it.

before-starting-the-fremennik-trials-usi.npc: I do not trust you outerlander, I will not accept your gifts, no matter what your intention...

My sword arm grows weary, and the blood of my foes hangs heavy upon my clothing!

after-completing-the-fremennik-trials.player: Can you tell me anything about the caves down here?

after-completing-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Aye, that I can [Fremennik name]! Yonder lies the lair of the daggermouth kings, the three beasts of legend!
I train my skills upon its foul brood, to prepare myself for the fight ahead!

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Oh! Hello there.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Ex Sea Captain Barfy Bill.

steps.player: Ex sea captain?

steps.npc: Yeah, I bought a lovely ship and was planning to make a fortune running her as a merchant vessel.

steps.player: Why are you not still sailing?

steps.npc: Chronic sea sickness. My first, and only, voyage was spent dry heaving over the rails.
If I had known about the sea sickness I could have saved myself a lot of money.

steps.player: What are you up to now then?

steps.npc: Well my ship had a little fire related problem. Fortunately it was well insured.
Anyway, I don't have to work anymore so I've taken to canoeing on the river.
I don't get river sick!
Would you like to know how to make a canoe?

steps.player: Could you teach me about canoes?

steps.text: If the player has 1-11 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Well, you don't look like you have the skill to make a canoe.
You need to have at least level 12 woodcutting.
Once you are able to make a canoe it makes travel along the river much quicker!

steps.text: If the player has 12-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: It's really quite simple. Just walk down to that tree on the bank and chop it down.
When you have done that you can shape the log further with your axe to make a canoe.

steps.text: If the player has 12-26 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Hah! I can tell just by looking that you lack talent in woodcutting.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: No Callouses! No Splinters! No camp fires littering the trail behind you.
Anyway, the only 'canoe' you can make is a log. You'll be able to travel 1 stop along the river with a log canoe.

steps.text: If the player has 27-41 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: With your skill in woodcutting you could make my favourite canoe, the Dugout. They might not be the best canoe on the river, but they get you where you're going.

steps.player: How far will I be able to go in a Dugout canoe?

steps.npc: You will be able to travel 2 stops on the river.

steps.text: If the player has 42-56 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: The best canoe you can make is a Stable Dugout, one step beyond a normal Dugout.
With a Stable Dugout you can travel to any place on the river.

steps.player: Even into the Wilderness?

steps.npc: Not likely! I've heard tell of a man up near Edgeville who claims he can use a Waka to get up into the Wilderness.
I can't think why anyone would wish to venture into that hellish landscape though.

steps.text: If the player has 57-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Hoo! You look like you know which end of an axe is which!
You can easily build one of those Wakas. Be careful if you travel into the Wilderness though.
I've heard tell of great evil in that blasted wasteland.

steps.npc: Like I said, this is Nemus Retreat. Back during the War of Betrayal, this was a military camp for Imafore's army, run by none other than General Nemus himself!
General Nemus is something of a hero in these parts. Towards the end of the war, the forces of Kourend had mostly taken the Auburn Valley.
As a result, Imafore ordered General Nemus to burn the entire valley to the ground to stop the Kourend advance. Many would have died on both sides, but Nemus refused the order.
Imafore had him executed as a traitor, but in doing so he lost the support of all of Nemus' troops.

steps.player: Sounds like a bit of a shortsighted decision.

options.text: I just wanted to check that you're okay

steps.player: I just wanted to check that you're okay.

steps.speaker: Basilisk
steps.text: Apart from being dead and stuffed and hanging on a wall, you mean?

steps.player: Uh... yeah, apart from that are you okay?

steps.speaker: Basilisk
steps.text: Actually there's something blocking my view of the far wall.

steps.player: I don't see anything.

steps.speaker: Basilisk
steps.text: Perhaps if you were to move to one side of me.
You walk to the side of the basilisk head...

steps.player: I still don't see anything.

steps.speaker: Basilisk
steps.text: Oh, it's moved away. I can see now.

steps.player: Nothing.

steps.speaker: Basilisk
steps.text: Leave me alone.

steps.npc: What can I do for you, traveller?

steps.player: I'll have a pint.

steps.npc: That'll be 4 gold pieces.

steps.text: If the player does not have 4 coins:

steps.player: I don't have enough coin.

steps.npc: I can't just be handing out free beers...

steps.player: Couldn't I just take one off those tables?

steps.npc: ...I suppose, if that's the kind of person you are.

steps.text: If the player has 4 coins:
Beer

steps.player: Thanks, Bast.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Sorry, you don't seem to have room to hold it.

steps.player: Oops!
What is this place?

steps.npc: My pub's called The Legless Faun. It's where all the newcomers find themselves after the long voyage from the east. A good drink takes the edge off, y'know? So, fancy a pint?

options.text: Have you heard any rumours here?

steps.player: Have you heard any rumours here?

steps.text: If Client of Kourend has not been started:

steps.npc: Apparently Veos is looking for some help with something. He hangs around the docks of Port Piscarilius.

steps.text: If The Queen of Thieves has not been started:

steps.npc: They say there's trouble in Port Piscarilius. Something about gangs uniting. Might be worth looking into.

steps.text: If The Depths of Despair has not been started:

steps.npc: I hear that Lord Hosidius has misplaced one of his sons. The Hosidius family might pay a lot to see him returned safely.

steps.text: If Tale of the Righteous has not been started:

steps.npc: Phileas Rimor has supposedly been looking for some assistance with something in Shayzien. Maybe worth investigating.

steps.text: If The Forsaken Tower has not been started:

steps.npc: I hear that the rulers of Lovakengj have some work available. You'll find them in the Lovakengj Assembly.

steps.text: If The Ascent of Arceuus has not been started:

steps.npc: Apparently there's been some commotion in the middle of Arceuus. Might be worth checking out.

steps.text: If A Kingdom Divided has not been started:

steps.npc: That protest outside Kourend Castle is starting to attract some attention. Could be worth taking a look.

steps.text: If all quests above have been completed:

steps.npc: No, it hasn't been very busy lately.

options.text: Could I get something to eat?
options.condition: During Trailblazer Reloaded League:

steps.player: Could I get something to eat?

steps.npc: Sure, we sell stew made at The Golden Field pub for 25 gold pieces.
Would you like a bowl?

steps.player: Yes please, sounds great.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough money:

steps.npc: Are you sure you have enough money?

steps.player: Oh... You're right, I don't have enough money.

steps.npc: That's ok, come back when you have enough money.

steps.text: If the player has enough money:
Stew
Bast gives you a bowl of stew.

steps.player: Thanks, Bast.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Sorry, you don't seem to have room to hold it.

steps.player: Oops!
No thanks.

steps.npc: Suit yourself. More delicious stew for everyone else.

steps.player: I'm afraid not as I've something to attend to.

steps.npc: A wise man once told me to never fear a drink... But perhaps I'm a little bias.

steps.speaker: Battle mage (Zamorak)
