the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: The spirit looks at you for a moment, before you suddenly hear a voice echoing in your head.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Spirit
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Curious... It has been a long time since I've spoken to another. The last time was when my body still had form. Tell me, stranger, what brings you to my tomb?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: I was looking for some scabarites.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Spirit
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Ah, yes. The fallen remnants of my once great sect. You will find plenty of them here. Why do you seek them?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: Do you know of Amascut, the Devourer?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Spirit
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: All too well.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: There's an old tomb south of here. Amascut has been excavating the entrance, and the scabarites have been helping her. She's looking for something inside, but I don't know what.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: I see. If you are an enemy of the Devourer and her corrupt scabarites, then you are a friend to me. I am Mehhar, and I can help you.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: You can help? Do you know of this tomb?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Even when I still lived, the desert hid many secrets. Now, centuries later, it hides even more. Of all those secrets, few are greater than the ones hidden in that tomb.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: It is the resting place of my father, Osmumten. He was once Pharaoh of these lands. My destiny was to succeed him, but the usurpers saw an end to that.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: And what are the secrets in his tomb?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Being a Pharaoh offers many luxuries, both in life and in death. Many strive only for these luxuries. They forget that being a Pharaoh also comes with responsibility.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: My father had a responsibility greater than most. At the time of his rule, our people were locked in a great war. To hold back the Ruinous Powers, our gods granted us immensely powerful weapons.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: When the war was over, my father was tasked with hiding those weapons, lest they fall into nefarious hands. Two of them were buried with him. They will be what the Devourer seeks.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: I trust you are aware of what the Devourer desires?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Yes. When the war ended and the Devourer rose from the ashes, she did so with only one goal. She will not stop until every soul, living or dead, has been destroyed.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: And these weapons can help her?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Many would call the Devourer a god, but they speak only half truths. She is a demi-goddess of limited power, and does not possess the means to devour souls on a mass scale.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: The weapons in my father's tomb can be used to drain a being of divine energy and transfer that energy to another. If used correctly, they would grant the Devourer true godhood.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: Then I need to get into that tomb and stop her.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Before you leave, I ask that you remember your original purpose here.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Yes. They have made their home here in my tomb, disturbing my rest. From the chamber above, the High Priest of Scabaras commands them.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: He believes he does so in the name of Scabaras. He does not realise that he is actually a puppet of the Devourer.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Free him of her control, and the Devourer will be without a powerful resource. It will also allow me to rest once more.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: He might also know more about what Amascut is planning. I did free a guard from Amascut's control through combat. I could try that again.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: When the Devourer first emerged, Icthlarin himself taught us an incantation to free an individual from her control. I would suggest you use it, rather than risking harm to the High Priest.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: Ah, that seems wise. What's this incantation?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: 'Majaan, Manand, Almuk.' Be warned, while it will work on those she has hypnotised, it will have no effect on her corrupted akhs. They are sadly beyond saving.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: You will find a key to the upper chamber in an urn to the back of this room. Now go, with the blessing of Scabaras.

steps.player: Tell me more about yourself.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: In life I was Mehhar, son of Osmumten. To me, my death was mere moments ago. To you on the other hand, I am surely considered ancient.

steps.player: How ancient?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: I sense that the gods have long since departed this world, but when I lived, they still walked among us.

steps.player: And your father, Osmumten? You said he was the Pharaoh. What happened?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: My father ruled during the great war. While the war was eventually won, many considered the cost too great. My father led us with the support of the gods, yet he was the one people blamed.

steps.player: So they killed him?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: Him, and the rest of my family. I would have died as well, were it not for the bravery of my father's servants. They gave their lives, so that I might live.

steps.player: And then you came here?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: To Ullek? Yes. I found solace here with a group dedicated to Scabaras. In time, I became their leader, and the Sect of Scabaras was formed.

steps.player: There's not much left of Ullek now, or the sect.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: That is no surprise. Such is the fate of all things. Still, while the sect would have eventually decayed, it was the Devourer's corruption that quickened its demise.

steps.player: I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: Don't be. You have a chance to free the High Priest of Scabaras. If you do, the sect may yet be reborn.

options.text: What do you know about Amascut?

steps.player: What do you know about Amascut?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: The one you call Amascut died long ago. In her place, the Devourer was born.

steps.player: How did it happen?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: Only Icthlarin himself knows the true answer to that question.

steps.player: Okay... but you must have some idea?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: During the great war, our forces were decimated by the servants of the Ruinous Powers. To turn the tide, Icthlarin and Amascut sought powerful allies to aid us.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: They found them far from here, in a place beyond this world. A powerful race of faceless ones. They became Icthlarin's Stern Judges.

steps.player: What's that got to do with Amascut?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: Upon her return, Amascut vanished. She played no further part in the war. Only when the fighting was over did she reappear, but it wasn't really her at all.

steps.player: So you think it had something to do with the Stern Judges?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: It seems highly likely.

options.text: Tell me more about the war you mentioned.

steps.player: Tell me more about the war you mentioned.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: It started during the rule of my grandmother. An ever-expanding empire to the north set their sights on our lands. War soon broke out.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: The armies of the Ruinous Powers were far stronger than our own. That was until Icthlarin's Stern Judges joined the fray. Thanks to them, the war was seemingly won.

steps.player: It wasn't really though, was it?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: No. Among the Stern Judges, there was a serpent. After my father became Pharaoh, this serpent convinced the others to abandon us.

steps.player: They joined the enemy?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: They did. We were powerless against a force of that might. Nothing could stop their advance.

steps.player: So how did the war end?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: It was Tumeken himself. He sacrificed himself to annihilate the enemy. The cost was great, but the war was won.

steps.player: So Tumeken died?

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: That's a matter of perspective. I died long ago, and yet we are still having this conversation.

steps.player: That doesn't really answer my question.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: While Tumeken himself may be gone, he lives on through his four avatars. While they walk among us, Tumeken will always be at our side.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

steps.speaker: Mehhar
steps.text: Scabaras be with you.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: You can help? Do you know of this tomb?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Even when I still lived, the desert hid many secrets. Now, centuries later, it hides even more. Of all those secrets, few are greater than the ones hidden in that tomb.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: I need to get into your father's tomb and stop Amascut.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: Before you leave, I ask that you remember your original purpose here.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.player: Hello again. How do I access the upper chamber?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-spirit.text: You will find a key in an urn at the back of this room. May Scabaras guide you to success.

options.text: What do you know about Amascut?
Tell me more about the war you mentioned.

the-ruins-of-ullek-searching-the-urn-by-.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You search the urn and find a rusty key, but you don't have enough room to take it.

the-ruins-of-ullek-searching-the-urn-by-.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: You search the urn and find a rusty key.

the-ruins-of-ullek-the-champion-of-scaba.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-the-champion-of-scaba.text: Intruder! You are not welcome here!

the-ruins-of-ullek-the-champion-of-scaba.player: Fear not! I am here to rescue you!

the-ruins-of-ullek-the-champion-of-scaba.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-the-champion-of-scaba.text: Silence! Champion, protect your High Priest!

the-ruins-of-ullek-the-champion-of-scaba.player: Fine. We'll do it your way.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.text: Have you freed the High Priest of Scabaras yet?

options.text: What do you know about Amascut?
Tell me more about the war you mentioned.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Stay back!

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Argh!

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: What... What happened?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: It's alright. You were being controlled by Amascut, but you're free now.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: I... I don't remember.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: I've been in your position. Don't worry, your memories will come back in time. Familiar places and objects can help them come back faster.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: This room is familiar... as I look around, I feel something stirring...

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Yes, I can see it now! There are a few gaps, but it's all coming back to me. Thank you, adventurer.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: There is much for me to set right. We have made some terrible mistakes.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: I know the feeling. What did she have you do?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Many things. I have been under her control my whole life. It was the same for my predecessor, and her predecessor as well. We were all slaves to the Devourer, even our lord himself.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Yes. She used him as her puppet for centuries, but now she has a new plan for him.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: I don't know. She took him into some tomb, along with the others.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: Osmumten's tomb. Who are these others you speak of?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Apmeken, Crondis and Het. The other avatars of Tumeken.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: She does. We helped her capture them. It took many lifetimes, but she was able to fool them all.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: This isn't good. There're weapons in that tomb that can transfer divine power between beings. She must be planning to use them on the lesser deities.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: The four of them all came from Tumeken himself. Their power is his power. If she claims that power as her own, she will become a true goddess...

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: Don't worry, I'll make sure that doesn't happen.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: How can you hope to withstand her power?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: I'll find a way. Do you have any other information that can help me?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: We were not the only ones to fall to the Devourer. She has control over Pharaoh Kemesis of Menaphos.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: We feared as much. Do you know what she wants with him?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: She needed control over the city, but she kept the reason a secret. She even had us release locusts and frogs into Sophanem so she could have Menaphos locked down.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: You caused the plagues? The cows and the pox as well?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: We did also poison the cows. I know nothing of this pox, though.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: Hmm... what will you do now?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: I fear many of my people are forever lost, but I will save as many as I can. Together, we will reform the Sect of Scabaras, and right the wrongs of the Devourer.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: So you'll help me fight her?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: In our own way. Before the Devourer, we were an isolated people, just as Scabaras taught us to be. We will go back to that way of life.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: We may go unseen, but we will be there, fighting the forces of the Devourer wherever they appear.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: Good to hear. Now, I'd better head over to Nardah. I have a friend there who needs to hear about all of this.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Good luck in your fight, adventurer. May Scabaras guide you.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.player: Do you have any other information about Amascut that could help me?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: We were not the only ones to fall to the Devourer. She has control over Pharaoh Kemesis of Menaphos.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: What... What happened?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.speaker: High Priest of Scabaras
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-the-high-p.text: Hello, adventurer. Thank you for freeing me from the Devourer. I would be alone now. Scabaras teaches us to remain isolated, and I have much to think about.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.text: I sense that the Devourer's corruption has been lessened. I trust you were successful?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.player: Does this mean you can rest now?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.text: That was my hope, but while the High Priest is free, many scabarites have been lost to the Devourer. I sense that they will soon descend on my tomb, hoping to reclaim it.

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.speaker: Mehhar
the-ruins-of-ullek-talking-to-mehhar-aft.text: Continue your fight against the Devourer. Only with her defeat, will we finally find freedom.

options.text: What do you know about Amascut?
Tell me more about the war you mentioned.
What do you know about Amascut?
Tell me more about the war you mentioned.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Ah, there you are. Any luck in those ruins?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: Plenty. I discovered all sorts of things. How about you?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: I filled Zahur in on our discoveries and obtained a blood sample from one of Sophanem's citizens for her. Don't ask me how. She's looked over it, and thinks the pox should be easily curable.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Yes, it's a very interesting one this. Do you know of the cadava bush?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: Yes! One time I used some to help this young couple. I gave one of them a cadava potion to appear dead.
It all went a bit wrong though, and he ended up with her cousin instead...

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Right...
If the player has completed Making Friends with My Arm:

steps.player: Oh, and I used one another time when I was helping My Arm!

steps.speaker: Zahur
steps.text: You were helping your arm? I'm not sure I need to know about your private life...

steps.player: No, not my arm. My Arm! He's a troll! He needed to kill an old man, so we used a potion to fake it.
It all went a bit wrong though... again. That seems to happen quite often for some reason...

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: What on Gielinor are you on about?

steps.speaker: Zahur
steps.text: Maybe we should get back to what I was saying...

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: As most people know, cadava berries are quite poisonous. When used in the right quantity, they can put someone into a deep sleep. Use the wrong amount...

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: ... and you're not going to be waking up again. Cadava potions are standard issue for Al Kharid spies for that very reason. In fact, they're what I used to get myself and those citizens out of Menaphos.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Well, the thing about cadava berries is that they're not the only part of the bush that's dangerous. If you're not careful, the bark can have quite a nasty effect on the skin.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: Like the spots from the pox! Are you saying that's what caused all the trouble? A rogue cadava bush?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Maybe, but you won't find any of those bushes this far south. It's quite unexpected. I don't think anyone in Sophanem would even recognise cadava bark, let alone figure out it caused the pox.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: To be honest, I probably wouldn't have suspected it myself either. I only realised because of the time I spent training with the Apothecary in Varrock.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: It sounds like someone could have caused the pox on purpose.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: Well that leads on to what I discovered in those ruins. I found the High Priest of Scabaras there, under Amascut's control. Turns out she had him and the scabarites cause the plagues in Sophanem.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: They caused the plagues? Why?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: Amascut wanted an excuse to have Menaphos locked down. She's up to something there, but the High Priest of Scabaras didn't know what. However, he did confirm that Pharaoh Kemesis is under her control as well.
The thing is, now that I think about it, the High Priest of Scabaras didn't actually seem to be aware of the pox. I doubt he'd have been able to get hold of cadava bark either.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: So there's other forces at play. That's not good. What else did you find out?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: The next bit is worse, I'm afraid. I found out what Amascut is looking for in that tomb. Apparently, there are two weapons in there that could grant her true godhood.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: True godhood? You can't be serious!

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: I'm afraid so. She's managed to capture all four of the lesser gods. It's likely that her plan is to use the weapons to claim their power.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: The lesser gods? It can't be!

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Are you really sure about all of this?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Do not doubt the will of the Devourer, Maisa. She is a force of pure evil.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: It wasn't that long ago that I didn't even think she was still around. Now I'm hearing she's trying to become a true goddess! It's a lot to get used to.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: I do have one bit of good news. I know an incantation that can free a person from her mind control. We can use it to free the people at the necropolis.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Right, well we'd better get to work then. First, let's finish off this cure. Once that's done, we can free the citizens.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: Anything you need me to do?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Maisa has already obtained most of what I need. All that's left now is some scarab venom and a Lily of the Elid.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: Okay, let's split up. I'll get the scarab venom.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.player: And I guess that leaves the Lily of the Elid for me. From the name, I assume they grow near the river?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: That's right. I know of a small island just west of here where you can find some.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur.text: As will I.
Maisa departs.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur-ta.speaker: Maisa
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur-ta.text: So what did you find in those ruins?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur-ta.player: I found the High Priest of Scabaras there, under Amascut's control. Turns out she had him and the scabarites cause the plagues in Sophanem.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur-ta.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-talking-to-maisa-or-zahur-ta.text: Hello again. Do you need anything?

options.text: Where can I get a Lily of the Elid?

steps.player: Where can I get a Lily of the Elid?

steps.speaker: Zahur
steps.text: There's a small island just west of here where you should be able to find some.

steps.player: Okay.

cure-me-pox-crossing-the-river-to-the-is.player: Hello there crocodile. I think I'll call you Roger. You're looking very hungry, Roger.
I think I'd better find something to distract you with before I try getting any closer.

steps.text: (Continues with meat dialogue.)

cure-me-pox-crossing-the-river-to-the-is.text: You'll need to distract Roger before you can cross.

steps.text: If the player uses raw beef:
You give Roger some meat. He happily takes it before swimming away. You feel that you have connected with Roger on a deep level. The two of you are now firm friends.
If the player user cooked meat:
You give Roger some meat. He happily takes it before swimming away. You feel that you have connected with Roger on a deep level. The two of you are now firm friends.

cure-me-pox-crossing-the-river-to-the-is.text: If the player has enough inventory space:

steps.text: You pick the lily.

cure-me-pox-crossing-the-river-to-the-is.text: If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.text: You don't have enough room to take the lily.

cure-me-pox-crossing-the-river-to-the-is.text: If the player already picked the lily:

steps.text: You've already picked the lily that was growing here.

cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.text: Welcome back. Do you have a Lily of the Elid?
If the player does not have the lily:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Zahur
steps.text: Well, there's a small island just west of here where you can find some.

steps.player: Okay. I'll be back soon.

cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.text: I think I have everything I need to make the cure now.

cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.player: Can I help with anything else?

cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.text: Actually, I think you can. To make the cure, I'll need to get the ingredients to just the right temperature. While I get them prepared, could you get my equipment heated up?

cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur.text: Just adjust the individual heats until the overall temperature is at the marked level. Be warned, the equipment can be a bit temperamental sometimes.

cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur-talking-t.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-returning-to-zahur-talking-t.text: I think I have everything I need to make the cure now.

cure-me-pox-warming-up-the-equipment.text: Excellent! I think I have it!

cure-me-pox-warming-up-the-equipment.speaker: Zahur
cure-me-pox-warming-up-the-equipment.text: Now, it's going to take a few batches of this to cure everyone in Sophanem. I'll get started on those right away. In the meantime, I can give you the first batch to take down there now.

cure-me-pox-warming-up-the-equipment.player: Okay. I can deliver it to the High Priest of Icthlarin.

cure-me-pox-warming-up-the-equipment.speaker: Maisa

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.player: Hello. How are things going here?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: We're making progress on those plagues. With our citizens back, we had enough people to finally drive out the frogs and locusts that were filling the town up.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: We worried they'd just come back, but perhaps we have managed to appease whichever god sent them.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: The infected cows have been dealt with as well. The only plague left now is this infuriating pox. Still, at least it isn't contagious.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.player: Well, I think I might be able to help with that.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: If the player does not have the crate:

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: How?

steps.player: Oh... I was meant to bring you something, but it seems I've forgotten it. I'll be right back.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.player: If all goes well, the potions in there should cure the pox. Sophanem will finally be free of the plagues. This is just the first batch. More will come soon.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: Free of the plagues? How is this possible? We tried everything!

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.player: Well I just found a good herbalist. What did you try?

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: Er... mostly I prayed to Icthlarin and hoped for the best.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.player: Right... Well I have some things to do down at the necropolis. I'll be back to see how the potions are working once I'm done.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: Thank you, friend. You are once again our saviour!

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.speaker: High Priest
cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.text: Thank you for bringing us that cure. We will hopefully start seeing the effects soon.

cure-me-pox-talking-to-the-high-priest-o.player: I'm sure it won't take long. I'll be back to see for myself once I'm done at the necropolis.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Hey there. Everything go okay with the High Priest?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: I think so. I guess we'll see for sure soon.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Well in the meantime, do you think this incantation will work?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: It did when I used it on the High Priest of Scabaras, so we shouldn't have any issues here.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Let's not waste any more time then.
A cutscene starts. The player and Maisa walk towards the citizens and Menaphite Guards.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Looks like we have a welcome party.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Guard
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: You have been warned before... leave, now...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Amascut's hold on you all is at an end. Majaan, Manand, Almuk.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: My... my head...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What happened?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: You were all enthralled by the Devourer, but you're free now. Things will be confusing at the moment, but your memories will return in time.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The Devourer? It can't be!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: I'm afraid so.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: You've all been through a lot, but unfortunately you won't be able to return to Menaphos. The city remains locked down.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: You should seek refuge in Sophanem or one of the other nearby settlements. Hopefully you'll be able to go home soon.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: You saved us!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Thank you!
The scene pans to the Jaltevas Pyramid entrance.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Well... that's quite the blockage.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Clearing it is going to take work. A lot of work.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: And time isn't on our side. Amascut is already in there looking for those weapons.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Two citizens approach the player and Maisa.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Excuse me...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Sorry to interrupt, but we can help.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What do you mean?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: We can mine away the blockage for you.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Are you sure? You've already been out here so long.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The Devourer made us her slaves. We want to help you stop her.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Thank you.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Citizen
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: We'll get to work at once.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: It's still going to be a bit longer before the cure starts to work. I guess we should head back to my camp for now.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Alright.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The scene pans to Maisa's camp.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Stop!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: What is it?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Stay quiet!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: What's going on?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Impressive, Maisa.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Osman! You've been spying on us!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: That is the job of a spy, Maisa. I remember that, but it seems you do not.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What's that supposed to mean?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: We had a plan, Maisa. You were ordered to stay in Menaphos. Now your recklessness has cost us dearly.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Don't lecture me on cost. I know exactly how much this little game of yours has cost.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Yes... Kaleef. Did you think I wasn't aware of your little romance?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Did you take me for a fool? I've been dealing in deception since before you were born. Yours was not hard to spot.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I made the mistake of letting it slide. A poor move on my part. Kaleef's death has clearly impacted your ability to think rationally.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Or maybe it just made me see the truth! You're a monster, Osman! You'd see us all dead to get what you want!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I serve Al Kharid, Maisa, just as you once did.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I'll never stop serving Al Kharid. I've just stopped serving you!
Maisa walks away.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Soooo...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I hope you don't believe yourself innocent in all of this. You have been meddling in affairs that are not your concern.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: I've only been trying to help.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: By curing the pox? Tell me, who does that help? Al Kharid or Menaphos?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: You know, despite all your spying, Al Kharid and Menaphos aren't actually enemies.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: On paper perhaps, but our two cities were at war for years. Signing a few treaties does not stop us from being enemies.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Even if that's true, I don't see why the pox being cured is a problem.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: It will surely lead to the end of the Menaphos quarantine. That is not to our benefit. We wanted that city isolated.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: There are larger forces at play here, Osman. That quarantine was helping them far more than it benefitted you.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What are you on about?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Amascut. She has control over Pharaoh Kemesis. She arranged the quarantine to keep her actions in Menaphos a secret.
That's why we made the cure. We need to get in there and find out what she's up to.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The Devourer? You speak of legends and fairy tales.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: You don't believe the gods exist?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Maybe once, but that was a long time ago.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: You're wrong, Osman. The Devourer's behind everything that's been happening down here, and the worst is yet to come. She's looking for some weapons. Ones that could grant her true godhood.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: And these weapons are in Menaphos?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: No. She's after something else in Menaphos. We don't know what... yet. The weapons are in a tomb to the south, and she's already in there. She could be using them right now.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Pharaoh Kemesis has you fooled. This is clearly some ploy of his to keep us confused and divided. He is our true foe.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Osman, you can't...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The ground shakes. Lightning strikes the sand and scarlet flames begin to burn.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: What the...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Time to go...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Osman! Don't you dare!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Menaphite Akh
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The mistress has tired of your interference...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Menaphite Akh
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Pray to your false gods... your end comes now...

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Great! Here we go again.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The cutscene ends, and the fight against the Menaphite Akh begins.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Looks like we have a welcome party.
The entrance is completely blocked. The citizens are slowly mining a way through, but it will take some time.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Let's head back to my camp.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Stop!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.prompt: Are you sure you want to leave?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.text: You had it all in hand. I must say, this has been an interesting development.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.player: So do you believe Amascut is involved now?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.text: No. I believe what my eyes tell me, and I am yet to see any true evidence that this is the work of an ancient goddess.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.text: But I will admit that there is more going on here than I first thought. Dark magic is clearly at play. This may require us to reconsider our approach.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.text: For now, nothing. I need to go and think on this. I suggest you seek out Maisa and see what results your meddling has caused. I'm sure I'll be in touch at some point.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.player: Dare I ask for a 'thank you' this time?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.speaker: Osman
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.text: I imagine Maisa will have gone to Sophanem to check on this cure. She will be waiting for you. Goodbye.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-defeating-t.player: That's what I thought. Thanks, Osman.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Sorry for leaving you back there. How was your chat with Osman?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: He seems to have been somewhat enlightened.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What do you mean?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: After you left, we were attacked by one of Amascut's servants. I think they convinced Osman that there's more to all of this than he realised.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Maybe he'll finally get his head out of the sand. We don't need him, though. Look at what we've managed on our own.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Yes, the cure. Is it working?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I'll let the High Priest answer that one.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: High Priest
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Hello again, friend. Your cure has worked wonderfully. Not a single citizen is infected any more. We're finally free of the plagues!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: And Menaphos?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: High Priest
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: We sent word to them earlier. They have agreed to meet with us at the bridge. If all goes well, this quarantine will soon be behind us.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Let's hope so.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: High Priest
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Please do join us for the meeting. After all, none of this would have been possible without you.
A cutscene plays. The player and Maisa are with the priests of Sophanem, waiting at the bridge.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: How long do you think we'll need to wait?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I don't know. This has probably put Pharaoh Kemesis in an awkward spot. He'll have much to consider.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: If the quarantine benefits the Devourer, he won't want to end it. Problem is, if he doesn't, it will draw a lot of suspicion.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Makes you wonder how much control he actually has left. Does he make any decisions for himself now, or is it all just Amascut?
How are you doing, by the way?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What do you mean?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: You know, the stuff Osman said about you and Kaleef.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: What happened between Kaleef and I is none of your business.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: If you're sure.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Speaking of Osman, that reminds me.
Maisa shows you a spear with a keris on the end.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: He left this for you. I'll leave it in the tent at my camp for you to pick up.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: He left this for you.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: His way of saying 'thank you' perhaps?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Doubt it. He's probably just trying to keep on your good side.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Do you think he's here?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: If not him, one of his minions will be. He'll want to know what happens at this meeting.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Anyway, he wasn't the only one with something for you. This is from the High Priest.
Maisa shows you an enchanted circlet.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: You can pick it up from him once we're done here.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: I'm sure I'll be able to put it to good use.
Ah, looks like something's happening.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Hang on... is that...?
The scene pans to the bridge. Pharaoh Kemesis, Jabari, Coenus, and several Menaphite Guards can be seen. The Pharaoh walks towards the middle of the bridge.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: High Priest
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Pharaoh Kemesis! I did not expect you to attend to this personally.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: High Priest
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Pharaoh Kemesis?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Pharaoh Kemesis
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The city of Menaphos will begin preparations to end the quarantine. It will take some time for these preparations to be complete. Good day.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Well that was anticlimactic.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: That's one way of putting it. Still, I wasn't expecting Kemesis himself to make the announcement. It's very unusual for him to appear in public.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: What do you think it means?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: I don't know. Until we can get into Menaphos, I doubt we'll find out.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: He said it would take some time for the city to open.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Stalling for as long as possible, no doubt.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: So what now?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The citizens should hopefully be nearly done unblocking the entrance to Osmumten's Tomb. I'm going to head down there.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: Maisa
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: As for you, I'd say you've earnt a small break. Take whatever time you need to prepare, then meet me at the tomb once you're ready.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Alright, I'll see you soon. Good luck.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Congratulations! Quest complete!

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: How long do you think we'll need to wait?

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.speaker: High Priest
fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: Hello again! Please take this as a thank you for all your help.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: The High Priest tries to hand you a Circlet of Water, but you don't have enough room for it.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: The High Priest hands you a Circlet of Water.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.player: Thanks.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You find a Keris partisan in the tent, but you don't have enough room to take it.

fight-with-the-menaphite-akh-talking-to-.text: You find a Keris partisan in the tent.

historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.speaker: Maisa
historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.text: I think we've done all we can for the moment. Menaphos is preparing to reopen, and the citizens are unblocking the entrance to Osmumten's Tomb.

historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.speaker: Maisa
historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.text: Until we see some progress in one of those areas, we'll just have to wait. Hopefully it won't be too long.

historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.speaker: Maisa
historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.text: In the meantime, I'll be helping out at the excavation. I think you'll agree that's our top priority.

historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.speaker: Maisa
historical-dialogue-quest-ending-before-.text: Look after yourself. You'll need to be well prepared for what's to come. I'll send word once the entry is cleared.

BCKuPh.player: I need to do something first.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.npc: Thanks so much for saving me from being a vampyre. Here, take this certificate, I'm sorry but it's all I can offer as a reward.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.text: You're handed a certificate of treasure as a reward.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-them-again.npc: Thanks for changing me back, it must have been hard for you. I must be off now.

options.text: Can I have a newspaper, please?

steps.player: Can I have a newspaper, please?

steps.npc: Certainly, Guv. That'll be 50 coins, please.

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 50 coins:

steps.player: Maybe when I've got more money on me.

steps.npc: Well, no cash, no paper. Live in ignorance.

steps.text: If the player has at least 50 coins:

steps.player: Sure, here you go...

steps.text: Newspaper

steps.npc: Okay, suit yourself. Plenty more fish in the sea.

options.text: How much does a paper cost?

steps.player: How much does a paper cost?

steps.npc: Just 50 coins! An absolute bargain! Want one?

options.text: Varrock Herald? Never heard of it.

steps.player: Varrock Herald? Never heard of it.

steps.npc: For the illiterate amongst us, I shall elucidate. The Varrock Herald is a new newspaper. It is edited, printed and published by myself, Benny Gutenberg, and each edition promises to enthrall the reader with
captivating material! Now, can I interest you in buying one for a mere 50 coins?

steps.player: Anything interesting in there?

steps.npc: Of course there is, mate. Packed full of thought provoking insights, contentious interviews and celebrity scandalmongering! An excellent read and all for just 50 coins! Want one?
Read all about it!
Extra! Extra! Read all about it!
Buy your Varrock Herald now!
Varrock Herald, now only 50 coins!
Get you Varrock Herald here!
Varrock Herald, on sale here!
Do you mind? You're in my home.

steps.player: I'm sorry, should I have knocked?

steps.npc: Very funny, human.
We can't all live in plush houses, you know. But that doesn't mean us mining dwarves don't work hard.

steps.player: Where do you do your mining?

steps.npc: Normally the coal mine to the north. We need a lot of coal to keep our steam engines going, you know.

steps.player: Can I do a bit of mining there as well?

steps.npc: I'm not sure, but as long as no one notices I don't think anyone is going to care.

before-garden-of-tranquillity.npc: Do you know anything about grapevine diseases?
Oh that's a shame. I hope I find someone soon, otherwise I could lose all this year's crops.

standard-dialogue.player: How are your grapes coming along?

standard-dialogue.npc: Marvellously, thanks to your help, [player name]!

steps.player: Hey there, I can take you somewhere safe if you'd like?

steps.npc: Arf arf!

steps.text: The Bernese Mountain Dog heads to the dog shelter.

standard-dialogue.npc: Good day, adventurer. If you have any questions, I'm sure Lars will be more than happy to answer them. He's in the building to the south.
Also don't forget to visit my sister's axe shop. She works in the same building as Lars.

when-entering-the-woodcutting-guild.npc: Welcome to the Woodcutting Guild, adventurer.

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.player: They arrested Sandy for the murder of a wizard and the sand pit now refills itself!

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.npc: ME JOB! I'VE LOSTED ME JOB! 'ow c'n yer say tha' be good news?? Me wife'll tear me limb fr'm limb!

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.player: Don't worry, the Wizards are going to pay you a large pension so that you can retire...

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.npc: Bu' wha'll I be doin' wit' me day now! I be lovin' tha sand.

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.player: What will you do with your day? Well....You could build sand castles with your own two hands!

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.npc: I din't think so... bu' iffen yer ever need someone ta haul buckets o'sand 'round, ye be lettin' me know [player name], I's can help yer!

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.player: Wow! That would be great, buckets of sand direct to bank everday you say? That's great!

after-the-hand-in-the-sand.text: Once per day you may ask Bert to help you by carrying 84 buckets of sand to your bank. Just talk to him!

options.text: Can you deliver my sand to my bank, please?

steps.player: Can you deliver my sand to my bank, please?

steps.text: If the player has space for the sand in their bank:

steps.npc: Aye, give me a minute cause I be rushed off me feet!

steps.text: Bert delivers the sand to your bank.

steps.player: Hello Bert, could I have my sand today please?

steps.npc: Aye, give me a minute cause I be rushed off me feet!

steps.player: Thanks for the sand Bert!

steps.npc: 'Ello there [player name]!

steps.player: Hope you're having a good day!

steps.npc: Oh arr, no' too bad, though sometoimes, I could do wi' a second pair o' hands! I'll be gettin' on movin' them there buckets o' sand to yer bank!

steps.player: Thanks Bert, see you tomorrow!

steps.text: Bert delivers the sand to your bank.

steps.npc: I'll ge' on wi' movin' it. Thankee fer makin' sure Sandy go' it in t'neck fer 'is double dealin's!

steps.text: Bert delivers the sand to your bank.
If the player has no space for the sand in their bank, or is an Ultimate Ironman:

steps.npc: Eeee, ye've go' no free space in yon bank [player name]. Make some room 'tween the fishes 'n boots fore ye come back ta me.

steps.player: Ok, I'll make some more space in my bank and come back!

options.text: Did you already give me some sand today?
options.condition: If the player has already claimed their sand for the day:

steps.player: Did you already give me some sand today?

steps.npc: Yep, I dropped it off a while ago. Mebbe come back tomorrow fer some more.

options.text: Please don't notify me when you deliver sand
options.condition: If the player has completed the Elite Ardougne Diary:

steps.player: Please don't notify me when you deliver sand.

steps.npc: Aye, when I take yer bucket o' sand to yer bank each day, I'll not bother ye wi' any messages 'bout it. Ye'll just find yer sand in there.

options.text: Can you notify me when you deliver sand?
options.condition: If the player has completed the Elite Ardougne Diary:

steps.player: Can you notify me when you deliver sand?

steps.npc: Aye, when I takes yer bucket o' sand to yer bank each day, I'll drop ye a message ter tell yer 'bout it, so ye knows I been workin'!

options.text: I no longer want daily sand deliveries.

steps.player: I no longer want sand deliveries.

steps.npc: Suits me, [player name]! I be a wee bi' busy, an' I'll happily stop takin' sand to  yer bank for ye. Come an' see me if ye changes yer mind.

options.text: Did you already give me some sand today?
I'd like daily sand deliveries again

steps.player: I'd like daily sand deliveries again.

steps.npc: Aye, ye bin a big help to me, an I'll be 'appy to take yer sand to yer bank.

steps.player: I'll see you another time.

standard-dialogue-in-free-to-play.npc: Hello there. Welcome to my magic emporium.

steps.player: Can I see your wares?

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.player: Sorry, I'm not into magic.

steps.npc: Well, if you see anyone who is, please send them my way.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello again. What can I do for you?

steps.player: Can I see your wares?

steps.npc: Of course.

options.text: I managed to decipher those notes.
options.condition: One time after Ethically Acquired Antiquities:

steps.player: I managed to decipher those notes.

steps.npc: Oh really? Please do tell. It's been driving me crazy!

steps.player: It seems like he was trying to find the runes for the Varrock teleport spell.

steps.npc: Ah, of course. I'm not sure how I didn't figure that out!

options.text: Could I buy some more pink dye?
options.condition: After The Hand in the Sand:

steps.player: Could I buy some more pink dye?

steps.npc: Of course. It's 20 coins per bottle.

steps.text: If the player has 20 coins and open inventory space:

steps.player: Sounds good.

steps.text: Betty sells you some pink dye in exchange for 20 coins.

steps.player: Actually, I'll pass.

steps.npc: Fair enough.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have 20 coins:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have free inventory space:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have enough room for any.
I'm good, thanks.

crack-the-clue-iii.npc: Good job. I have new information to share with you.

crack-the-clue-iii.text: You've found a new special clue! However, a magical force prevents you from putting this item in your inventory!
Interface showing the next clue opens.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Why, I'm Dondakan, of course!

options.text: Why are you firing a cannon at a wall?

steps.player: Why are you firing a cannon at a wall?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: It's not a wall! It's a rock!

steps.player: What's the difference?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: It's a very special rock!

steps.player: I still don't quite follow...

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Oh, for Guthix' sake, it's perfectly simple! See, that rock over there, it's impenetrable!

steps.player: Have you tried taking a pickaxe to it?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Of course I have, I'm holding this rune pickaxe, aren't I? We've been trying to mine through it for years!

steps.player: We? I don't see anyone else.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Well, I'm the only one left... all the others gave up. Said it wasn't worth their while anymore. Wouldn't have a good return profit on their time investment.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: At first we thought there might be a huge treasure behind the rock, you see.

steps.player: Isn't there?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Until we had a look further down the stream, around the rock... no, there's no treasure there, just a dead end.

steps.player: Okay... so why were you trying to get through the rock again?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Because obviously there are vast deposits of minerals inside the rock! And if not, I want to harness the extreme hardness of the rock itself!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: The only problem is that I have run out of ideas on how to do it.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Perhaps a young adventurer like you is willing to help out an old dwarf like me? Want to find out what's inside the rock?

steps.prompt: Start the Between a Rock... quest?

steps.player: Sure, sounds interesting!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Welcome aboard then!

steps.player: No thanks, I do enough mining on my own.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Suit yourself, I don't need any help from a human anyway!

steps.player: Bit noisy here, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Cozy? No, not really, it's damp and cold!

steps.player: No! I said it's noisy!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Then stop shouting!

steps.player: Goodbye!
Any idea on what's inside the rock?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: No, but that's where you come in!

steps.player: How so?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I want you to find out some more information on the rock.

steps.player: Now where would I do that?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I don't know! Wish I knew!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: But we have to get some better understanding of what this thing actually is. Maybe then we can find a way to break it open.

steps.player: And what are you going to do while I go running across half of Gielinor, I'll wager?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I'll guard my cannon and fire more cannonballs at it, of course! Wish I had your job, mine's a tough one!

steps.player: Want to trade places?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: My legs are too old and worn to do much running around anymore, I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Well, off you go now! Start running, start talking!

steps.player: But I still don't know where!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Oh, why so difficult?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Look, try the city, further down the stream here. There's bound to be someone there who knows something. If you still can't find anyone, go to the librarian, he knows a lot.

options.text: What did you need me to do?

steps.player: What did you need me to do?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I want you to find out some more information on the rock.

steps.player: Now where would I do that?
I'll be back later.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: See Miodvetnir, Derni, and Dernu#Subsequent dialogue

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-knowledge-o.speaker: Librarian
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-knowledge-o.text: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!

options.text: Can you tell me more about the library?
What do you know about impenetrable rocks?

steps.player: What do you know about impenetrable rocks?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: You're confusing me, what rock exactly are you talking about?

steps.player: The big one in the mines south of the city. Dondakan's big rock.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I see, I see.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: But I don't know much about that rock, I'm afraid. It's baffled us for many generations.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: There is a dwarf in the mechanics shop, though, who I believe has some connections with a certain scholar.

steps.player: Where can I find him exactly?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: Go south to the palace, the shop is called Wemund's Wrench Warehouse. He should be working there somewhere.

steps.player: Thanks!

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.player: Do you know anything about this rock in the mines?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.speaker: Dwarven Engineer
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.text: Now what rock would that be, exactly?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.player: The big rock in the mines to the south, with an old dwarf standing beside it..?
Er, yes, I think so. Do you know what it's made of?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.speaker: Dwarven Engineer
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.text: No, no one knows. No one here, anyway. The only one I can think of is Rolad, a renowned scholar. He was part of Dondakan's team once, many years ago.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.player: So where can I find this Rolad?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.speaker: Dwarven Engineer
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.text: He left to explore the world. Learning by experience, or so he said. Me, I prefer a cold stout at home, but it takes all sorts.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.speaker: Dwarven Engineer
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-engineer-i-.text: I think he's currently with the Black Guard at Ice Mountain.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.player: Excuse me... would you happen to be Rolad the scholar?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: Why, yes, I think so... who's asking?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.player: [player name], and I've come to ask you about a rock.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: You're awfully tall for a dwarf, you know, [player name]. And a rock you say? I suppose I know a fair bit about rocks, yes.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.player: It's this rock that Dondakan is trying to break open. You know Dondakan, right?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: Oh, old Dondakan, sure I know him. And I know his rock too. It's that unbreakable one, isn't it?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.player: Yes, that's the one. What can you tell me about it?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: Well, as a matter of fact, I picked up an interesting book on one of my travels, from a quite out of the way dwarven outpost.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: I'm not entirely sure, but it seems to describe this very rock, and how it came to be placed in that cavern. I tore out the most interesting pages for more detailed perusal. Let me get them for you.
There is a slight pause, as Rolad realizes something is wrong.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: I seem to have misplaced the pages... a pity, I had wanted to study them some more. Oh well...

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.player: What? No! I need that book!

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: Oh, well, if it's that important to you, perhaps you can go and look for the pages? There should be three of them.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: I probably lost them in the mines below. I don't have them up here in any case.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.text: No no, I never go there, I'm not a member you know. But I sometimes go down to the regular mines to study the conditions of the working dwarf.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-rolad-the-s.player: Okay, thanks, I'll go and look for the pages then.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.player: Rolad has a book that might help us!

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: A book? How's a book going to help? What's in it?

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.player: Well, that's the problem... the most important pages are missing.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: Then run along and find them!

steps.text: You turn over the corpse of the scorpion and find a missing page of Rolad's book! Unfortunately, you can't carry it and are forced to drop it on the ground.
At the bottom of the cart you find a missing page of Rolad's book! Unfortunately, you can't carry it and are forced to drop it on the ground.
You see something lying just behind the rock you just mined... it's a missing page of Rolad's book!
Unfortunately, you can't carry it and are forced to drop it on the ground.
You turn over the corpse of the scorpion and find a missing page of Rolad's book!
At the bottom of the cart you find a missing page of Rolad's book!
You see something lying just behind the rock you just mined... it's a missing page of Rolad's book!

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-hi-ho-hi-ho.text: You've found all three of Rolad's missing pages. Return them to him so he can put them back in his book.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.speaker: Rolad
an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: How are you getting on with finding those missing pages?
If the player is yet to find any pages:

steps.player: I haven't found a single one yet, I have no idea where I should be looking.

steps.speaker: Rolad
steps.text: Down in the mines below, that'd be my best bet. I don't know where though, they could be anywhere down there.

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: If the player has found only one page:

steps.player: Well, I found the first page, but I still have two to go.

steps.speaker: Rolad
steps.text: That's splendid, keep going and you'll find them all, I'm sure!

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: If the player has found only two pages:

steps.player: I found two of the pages! But I haven't found the last one yet.

steps.speaker: Rolad
steps.text: Marvelous! I'm sure it's only a matter of time before you find the final page!

an-unbreakable-rock-or-stone-talking-to-.text: If the player has found all of the pages:

steps.player: Look, I found all of your missing pages!

steps.speaker: Rolad
steps.text: Missing pages..?

steps.player: Yes, the missing pages of that book we were talking about earlier?

steps.speaker: Rolad
steps.text: Oh yes, quite right... let me see them, please, and I'll put the book back together for you.
Player hands over the pages to Rolad.

steps.speaker: Rolad

going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.text: Gold! I knew it! I struck gold! I'm set for life!

going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf

going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.player: Sorry, the book doesn't say... it doesn't seem to be particularly concerned with actually breaking open the rock. You see, the demonic spirit is being kept inside it.

going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf

going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
going-for-the-gold-returning-to-dondakan.text: Well, we're not very much closer to a solution then, are we?

options.text: What have you tried so far?

steps.player: What have you tried so far?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Well, let's see...

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: At one time, we had a hundred dwarves in here, all picking away at the rock. Didn't do a thing.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Then there was the time when we set fire to this whole section of the cave. What a smell that made!

steps.player: Any effect?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Apart from coating the rock with soot? Not really, no.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I was able to borrow a cannon from the Black Guard, my son was able to pull some strings you know.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Of course, steel cannonballs didn't make a dent. But then ol' Donnie had a clever idea.

steps.player: Oh really?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I made this adamantite cannonball, you see! Cost me quite a pile of coins too!

steps.player: Wow! That must have made quite an impact!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Well, yes, it did... when it bounced back onto the ground it did.

steps.player: What else did you try?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Well, then I had an even more clever idea!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I put an even bigger pile of coins together to get some rune cannonballs! Good idea, right?

steps.player: Yeah, great!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: No, it wasn't. Didn't do anything! Nothing at all!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Latest thing I've tried are these boots.

steps.player: Nice boots... but what about them?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: They're made out of granite! I don't have enough money left to make granite cannonballs though. But see!
Dondakan walks up the passage, kicks it, and walks back.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Did you see? Did you?

steps.player: I er... didn't see anything.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: That's because there wasn't anything to see! Even granite doesn't do anything to it!

steps.player: And now I have to come up with a material that will affect it somehow?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: You got it!

steps.player: Some kind of new material that no one has ever found before but which I am supposed to accidentally stumble upon, perhaps?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Don't be silly, I'm sure there must be some known material that will affect it.

steps.player: I'm tired of these stories.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Go on then... leave an old dwarf to his work.

options.text: Maybe we need to set up another cannon?

steps.player: Maybe we should set up another cannon?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Another cannon? How will that help?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: No, no, what we need is a different material of cannonballs. The hardest, toughest you can find.

steps.player: How do you mean, that I can find? What are you doing then?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: I'm guarding the cannon. Won't do us much good if it were stolen, would it?

steps.player: I'll be back later.

going-for-the-gold-using-gold-ore-bar-on.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf

going-for-the-gold-using-gold-ore-bar-on.text: Tell you what, if you make a golden cannonball and give it to me, I'll fire it at the rock.

steps.text: Very simple. I'll have to make a few modifications to my cannon so that it can fire a human, and you'll need a golden helmet of course.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Then I'll fire you at the rock so you can do a little reconnaissance. Don't worry, you should land safely on the other side of the rock.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Might want to pick up that cannonball again while you're at it!

steps.player: But... what if I bump into that demon, the one from the book?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Don't be silly now. It's just a rock... just a rock with lots of gold in it!
