steps.player: So you want to... fire me into the rock?

steps.text: Yes, just to see what's inside... to see if all that gold is really embedded inside it.

options.text: Find someone else for your bizarre experiment!

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf

steps.player: Won't a gold plated helmet do?

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: No, it has to be a helmet made out of solid gold. Gold plated helmets contain so little actual gold, it'd be a bit dangerous.

steps.speaker: Dondakan the Dwarf
steps.text: Unless you want to die when I shoot you at the rock?

steps.player: No no, I'll get you a helmet made out of solid gold.

post-quest-hugi-the-librarian.text: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!

options.text: Can you tell me more about the library?
What do you know about impenetrable rocks?

steps.player: What do you know about impenetrable rocks?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: You're confusing me, what rock exactly are you talking about?

steps.player: The big one in the mines south of the city. Dondakan's big rock.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I see, I see.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I heard there was a demon inside there that you banished.

steps.player: Yes, what exactly does that mean anyway?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: There are some demons that we cannot see properly as mortals. They also cannot be fought with normal weapons.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: But sometimes these creatures manifest themselves in a solid form in our world. Their avatar.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: When you defeat an avatar, you defeat the actual demon behind it. But they don't die, they are banished to where they came from originally.

steps.player: Does that mean I will have to deal with this demon again some time?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: Doubtful. He will grow stronger and stronger over time, but that's a process that will take a thousand years at least.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: Even dwarves don't live so long.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: No, we won't see him again and the mines are safe to dig for gold now. Of course, that might lead to other problems eventually...

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: The name is Big Mo. I was a travelling salesman and businessman, passing through the towns to see what wares I could get my hands on.
I turned up a few years ago, selling clue scrolls to encourage people to explore. I'd only sell each person one clue scroll per day, of course.

steps.player: Where were you from originally?

steps.npc: HA HA HA! I deliberately didn't tell people where I was from. Mostly they assumed me to be from Zeah.
That may or may not be true, though - no-one else in Zeah looks much like me. I'll leave it as a mystery...

steps.player: Goodbye.

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: Oh, hello there. Welcome to the Drumstick Kingdom. King Biles is the name. I am the ruler of this land.
That's right. Once I was a banknote exchange merchant, but after becoming stranded here, I decided to make the best of it.

options.text: Can you exchange some banknotes for me?

steps.player: Can you exchange some banknotes for me?

steps.npc: Well, it's not something I do as much now that I'm a king, but I suppose I can. Just hand me the banknotes you wish me to exchange. It will cost you 5 coins for each banknote.

steps.player: The Drumstick Kingdom?

steps.npc: Yes, I wanted to call this place Drumstick Isle because I thought it looked like a chicken drumstick, but apparently that name was taken. I settled for Drumstick Kingdom instead.

steps.player: So that's the name of this island?

steps.npc: No, just the kingdom. This island already had a name as well, so I can't change it. It all seems stupid to me. It's not like there's some central authority in charge of naming islands!
Besides, I'm a king! I should get to name whatever I want, just like Sleve does. He gets to name everything. He even named me! Before all this, my name was Friedrich Henglebert!

steps.player: Right... Well, good luck with... the kingdom.
I need to get going.

steps.npc: Very well.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: Oh, hello again. Welcome back to the Drumstick Kingdom.

standard-dialogue-before-cabin-fever.npc: What right have ye to be so happy, landlubber?

standard-dialogue-before-cabin-fever.player: Well it is quite a nice day.

standard-dialogue-before-cabin-fever.npc: Will ye forgive an old sailor his temper [lad/lass/kid]? I'm in dire straits indeed.

standard-dialogue-before-cabin-fever.player: What's the problem? I may be able to help.

standard-dialogue-before-cabin-fever.npc: I dunno, [lad/lass/kid], I need a pirate to help me with my problem, but none will sail with me.
Well, ye look like ye might have the right stuff, tell me would ye like te be a pirate?

options.text: Yes, I've always wanted to be a pirate!

steps.player: Aye Cap'n!

steps.npc: Then here, have this other copy I dug up.

steps.text: Book o' Piracy

standard-dialogue.text: Billy isn't interested in talking.

getting-started-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
getting-started-talking-to-elena.text: You too, thanks for freeing me.

getting-started-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
getting-started-talking-to-elena.text: It's just a shame the mourners confiscated my equipment.

getting-started-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
getting-started-talking-to-elena.text: My distillator. I can't test any plague samples without it. They're holding it in the Mourner Headquarters in West Ardougne.

getting-started-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
getting-started-talking-to-elena.text: I must somehow retrieve that distillator if I am to find a cure for this awful affliction. Do you think you could help me?

steps.player: Of course I can help. Where do we start?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I was hoping you would say that. Unfortunately they discovered the tunnel and filled it in. We need another way over the wall.

steps.player: Any ideas?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: My father's friend Jerico is in communication with West Ardougne. He might be able to help us. He lives in a house south east of here, north of the chapel.

steps.player: I'm busy at the moment, I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Fair enough.

getting-started-talking-to-elena-trying-.text: The ground's been filled in and packed hard.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico.text: Hello, I've been expecting you. Elena tells me you need to cross the wall.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico.text: My messenger pigeons help me communicate with friends over the wall.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico.text: I have arranged for two of them to aid you with a rope ladder. Omart is waiting for you at the southern end of the wall.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico.text: But be careful, if the mourners catch you, the punishment will be severe.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-again.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico-again.text: Hello again. Have you spoken to Omart yet?

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-again.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico-again.text: You'll find him at the southern end of the wall. Keep an eye out for them mourners.

getting-started-searching-the-cupboard.text: The cupboard is full of bird feed.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You find some bird feed in the cupboard but you don't have enough room to take it.

getting-started-searching-the-cupboard.text: If the player already has bird feed:

steps.player: I don't need any more bird feed.

getting-started-searching-the-cupboard.player: Mmm, bird feed! Now what could I do with that?

getting-started-talking-to-omart.player: Omart, Jerico said you might be able to help me.

getting-started-talking-to-omart.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart.text: He informed me of your problem traveller. I would be glad to help, I have a rope ladder and my associate, Kilron, is waiting on the other side.

getting-started-talking-to-omart.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart.text: Unfortunately we can't risk it with the watchtower so close. So first we need to distract the guards in the tower.

getting-started-talking-to-omart.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart.text: I reckon some of Jerico's pigeons might help us out here. Chuck some bird feed at the tower and then release some pigeons nearby. They should provide a nice distraction.

getting-started-talking-to-omart.player: Where do I get the bird feed and the pigeons?

getting-started-talking-to-omart.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart.text: I'm sure Jerico can help you out with that if you ask him nicely.

getting-started-talking-to-omart-talking.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart-talking.text: Hello. Have you sorted that distraction yet?

getting-started-talking-to-omart-talking.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart-talking.text: Try using some of Jerico's pigeons. Chuck some bird feed at the tower and then release some pigeons nearby. Jerico should be able to help you out.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.text: Hello again. Have you spoken to Omart yet?

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.player: I have. He told me to ask you about some pigeons.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.text: Pigeons? What do you need my pigeons for?

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.player: Omart thought they'd make a good distraction for the guards.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.text: Ahh, very clever. Well I'm sure I can let you borrow some, as long as you look after them. Just grab one of the cages from behind my house. You'll want some bird feed as well. I should have some in my cupboard.

getting-started-throwing-bird-feed.text: If the player is not near the watchtower fence:

steps.player: I probably shouldn't waste it by throwing it here.

getting-started-throwing-bird-feed.text: If the player is near the fence:

steps.text: You throw a handful of seeds onto the watchtower. The mourners do not seem to notice.

getting-started-opening-pigeon-cage.text: If the player is in the wrong place or has not thrown the bird feed:

steps.text: The pigeons don't want to leave.

getting-started-opening-pigeon-cage.text: If the player has thrown the bird feed and is near the watchtower fence:

steps.text: The pigeons fly towards the watchtower. The mourners frantically try to scare them away.

getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.speaker: Jerico
getting-started-talking-to-jerico-after-.text: The guards are distracted by the birds, you must go now, quickly traveller.

getting-started-talking-to-omart-after-f.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart-after-f.text: Well done, the guards are having real trouble with those birds. You must go now traveller, it's your only chance.

steps.player: Okay, lets do it.

steps.text: If the player is not wearing a gas mask:

steps.speaker: Omart
steps.text: I'd recommend you wear a gas mask before entering West Ardougne. You don't want to risk catching the plague.

steps.player: That would be wise. Thanks Omart.

steps.text: Omart throws a rope ladder over the wall.
You climb up the rope ladder...
...and drop down on the other side.

steps.speaker: Kilron
steps.text: Welcome to West Ardougne friend. I'm Kilron. Let me know if you want to go back over the wall.

steps.player: Thanks Kilron. Do you know where to find the Mourner Headquarters?

steps.speaker: Kilron
steps.text: It's the most north eastern building in the city. Be careful around there.

steps.player: I'll be back soon.

steps.speaker: Omart
steps.text: Don't take too long, those mourners will soon be rid of those birds.

getting-started-talking-to-omart-after-e.speaker: Omart
getting-started-talking-to-omart-after-e.text: Hello traveller. Do you wish to cross the wall?

steps.player: Okay, lets do it.

steps.text: Omart throws a rope ladder over the wall.
You climb up the rope ladder...
...and drop down on the other side.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-attempting-t.text: You should leave your gas mask on while you're in West Ardougne

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-k.speaker: Kilron
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-k.text: Hello traveller. Do you need to go back over?

steps.player: Yes I do.

steps.speaker: Kilron
steps.text: Okay, quickly now!
Kilron throws a rope ladder over the wall.
You climb up the rope ladder...
...and drop down on the other side.

options.text: Do you know where to find the Mourner Headquarters?

steps.player: Do you know where to find the Mourner Headquarters?

steps.speaker: Kilron
steps.text: It's the most north eastern building in the city. Be careful around there.

steps.player: Not yet Kilron.

steps.speaker: Kilron
steps.text: Okay, just give me the word.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-j.speaker: Jerico
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-j.text: So you've returned traveller. Did you get what you wanted?

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-j.speaker: Jerico
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-j.text: Omart will be waiting by the wall, in case you need to cross again.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: Back away citizen. Only mourners are allowed inside the headquarters.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.player: Hmm. I wonder if there's another way in.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-inspecting-c.player: Looks like a nice stew is being prepared. This must be to feed all of the mourners.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.speaker: Nurse Sarah
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.text: I don't know how much longer I can cope here.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.player: What? Is the plague getting to you?

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.speaker: Nurse Sarah
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.text: No, strangely enough the people here don't seem to be affected. It's just the awful living conditions that is making people ill.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.player: I was under the impression that everyone here was affected.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.speaker: Nurse Sarah
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-n.text: Me too, but that doesn't seem to be the case.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-using-rotten.text: You place the rotten apple in the pot. It quickly dissolves into the stew.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-using-rotten.player: Anyone who eats this stew is going to have a bad time now.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-opening-back.player: Eugh, locked. There must be a way for me to get in. Maybe there's something around here that will help me.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: Back away citizen. Several mourners are ill with food poisoning.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.player: Is there a doctor nearby? Maybe I can go fetch them.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: There are no doctors in West Ardougne, just that nurse south west of the chapel. You don't need to worry though, we'll soon have it sorted.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-searching-cu.text: If the player has not yet poisoned the stew or already has a medical gown:

steps.text: You search the cupboard but you find nothing of interest.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-searching-cu.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You find a medical gown in the cupboard but you don't have enough room to take it.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-searching-cu.text: You find a medical gown in the cupboard.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: A doctor? I didn't think there were any left around here.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.player: I heard there was some trouble with food poisoning here.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: You heard right. Head on in and see what you can do.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-attempting-t.text: You should leave your medical gown on while you're in the Mourner Headquarters.
The trapdoor is bolted on the other side.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: Oh dear oh dear. I feel terrible, I think it was the stew.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.player: You should be more careful with your ingredients.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: There is one mourner who's really sick. They're resting upstairs. You should see to them first.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.player: Okay, I'll see what I can do.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.text: A doctor? At last! I don't know what I've eaten but I feel like I'm on death's door.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.player: Hmm... interesting, sounds like food poisoning.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.text: Yes, I'd figured that out already. What can you give me to help.

options.text: Just hold your breath and count to ten.

steps.player: Just hold your breath and count to ten.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: What? How will that help? What kind of doctor are you?

steps.player: Erm... I'm new, I just started.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: You're no doctor!
(Mourner attacks the player.)

options.text: The best I can do is pray for you.

steps.player: The best I can do is pray for you.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Pray for me? You're no doctor... You're an imposter!
(Mourner attacks the player.)

options.text: There's nothing I can do, it's fatal.

steps.player: There's nothing I can do, it's fatal.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: No, I'm too young to die! I've never even had a girlfriend.

steps.player: That's life for you.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Wait a minute, where's your equipment?

steps.player: It's erm... at home.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: You're no doctor!
(Mourner attacks the player.)

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-s.text: Sorry, I'd like to be left in peace.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-opening-the-.text: If the player has the key:

steps.text: You use the key to open the gate.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-opening-the-.text: If the player does not have the key:

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-searching-th.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You search the crate and find Elena's distillator but you don't have enough room to take it.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-searching-th.text: If the player already has the distillator:

steps.text: You search the crate but find nothing of interest.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-searching-th.text: You search the crate and find Elena's distillator.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.speaker: Mourner
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.text: Oh dear oh dear. I feel terrible, I think it was the stew.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-m.player: You should be more careful with your ingredients.

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-e.speaker: Elena
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-e.text: You're back, did you find the distillator?

infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-e.speaker: Elena
infiltrating-the-mourner-hq-talking-to-e.text: I can't test the samples without the distillator. Please don't give up until you find it.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: You're back, did you find the distillator?

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: Great! Now I can finally run these tests.
Elena uses the distillator to test some samples.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: I don't understand... the touch paper hasn't changed colour at all...

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: I'm not sure. My old mentor in Varrock, Guidor, might know though. Could you take these to him and see what he thinks? You'll need to drop by the chemist in Rimmington first to pick up some more touch paper.
Elena gives you a plague sample along with three vials.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: Now, last time I went to see Guidor, some one told the guards I was carrying some plague samples. Annoyingly, that means they've started searching everyone going to that part of the city.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: Ironically, the guards won't be smart enough to recognise the sample itself, so you should be able to get that in just fine. They'll probably confiscate the rest though.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: Well I know the chemist has still been managing to get chemicals to Guidor. Maybe he can help you smuggle the things in.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.player: Great, I'll see if he can help. See you soon.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.speaker: Elena
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-elena-.text: What are you doing back here?

options.text: I just find it hard to say goodbye sometimes.

steps.player: I just find it hard to say goodbye sometimes.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I see... I understand what you mean... But let's discuss that later.

options.text: I'm afraid I've lost some of the stuff that you gave me...

steps.player: I'm afraid I've lost some of the stuff that you gave me...

steps.text: If the player has all the items:

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Are you sure? Looks like you have everything to me.
If the player is missing items:

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: That's alright, I've got plenty.
If the player has no inventory space:
Elena tries to give you some items but you don't have enough room for them.
Elena replaces your lost items.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: There you go. That should be everything.

steps.player: Great, I'll be on my way.

options.text: I've forgotten what I need to do.

steps.player: I've forgotten what I need to do.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Go to Rimmington and get some touch paper from the chemist. Once you've done that, you'll need to take those things to Guidor in Varrock.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: You'll probably need to smuggle some of the items in to stop them getting confiscated. If you need help moving them discreetly, the chemist might be able to assist you.

steps.player: Okay, I'll get to it.
Nothing.

delivering-the-samples-talking-to-omart-.speaker: Omart
delivering-the-samples-talking-to-omart-.text: Hello adventurer. I'm afraid it's too risky to use the ladder again. You'll have to find another way into the city.

visiting-the-chemist-house-in-rimmington.speaker: Chancy
visiting-the-chemist-house-in-rimmington.text: Hush - I'm trying to perfect the art of dealing off the bottom of the deck.

visiting-the-chemist-house-in-rimmington.prompt: What do you want to talk about?

steps.speaker: Chemist
steps.text: Sorry, I'm afraid we're just closing now. You'll have to come back another time.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-c.speaker: Chancy

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-c.speaker: Chancy

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-c.speaker: Chancy

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-d.text: Absolutely. It's just not stored in a vial anymore.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-d.speaker: Da Vinci

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-d.player: That's great. Thanks to you I'll have to walk back to East Ardougne to get another vial.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-d.speaker: Da Vinci

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-h.player: Thanks, I'll let you get your drink now.

visiting-south-east-varrock-exiting-sout.player: I should probably talk to Guidor before leaving the area. Otherwise I'll need to get my vials smuggled in again.

visiting-south-east-varrock-entering-gui.player: That's someone's bedroom. I'm not going in there without a reason.

visiting-south-east-varrock-entering-gui.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-entering-gui.text: Please leave my husband alone. He's very sick, and I don't want anyone bothering him.

visiting-south-east-varrock-entering-gui.player: I'm sorry to hear that. Is there anything I can do?

visiting-south-east-varrock-entering-gui.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-entering-gui.text: Thank you, but I just want him to see a priest.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.text: Oh dear! Oh dear! I don't have time to chat!

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.player: Hello. I'm a friend of Elena, here to see Guidor.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.text: I'm afraid that Guidor is not long for this world! So I'm not letting people see him now.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.player: I'm really sorry to hear about Guidor.
But I do have some very important business to attend to!

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.text: You heartless rogue! What could be more important than Guidor's life? A life spent well, if not always wisely... I just hope that Saradomin shows mercy on his soul!

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.text: Oh goodness no! But I am! If only I could get him to see a priest!

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-a.speaker: Asyff
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-a.text: Now you look like someone who goes to a lot of fancy dress parties.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-a.speaker: Asyff
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-a.text: I'm just saying that perhaps you would like to peruse my selection of garments.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-a.speaker: Asyff
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-a.text: Or, if that doesn't interest you, then maybe you have something else to offer? I'm always on the look out for interesting or unusual new materials.

options.text: Okay, let's see what you've got then.
Do you have a spare Priest Gown?

steps.player: Do you have a spare Priest Gown?

steps.speaker: Asyff
steps.text: Well I do sell them. I don't hand them out for free though. This is a shop not a charity.

steps.player: Please! It's really important.

steps.speaker: Asyff
steps.text: Well I suppose you can have this old one. It's not in good enough condition to sell.
You are given a Priest Gown.

steps.player: Thank you.

options.text: I think I might just leave the perusing for now, thanks.
Can you make clothing suitable for hunting?
What sort of unusual materials did you have in mind?

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.text: A priest! thank goodness! My husband is very ill! Perhaps you could read him his last rites?

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.player: I'll see what I can do.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.player: Hello, you must be Guidor. I understand that you are unwell.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.speaker: Guidor
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.text: Is my wife asking priests to visit me now? I'm a man of science for god's sake. I know she means well but it's only a little cough!

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.player: She made out it was something more serious.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.speaker: Guidor
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.text: Well it's not killed me yet. So what do you want?

options.text: I've come to ask your assistance in stopping a plague.

steps.player: I've come to ask your assistance in stopping a plague.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: You mean the plague of West Ardougne?

steps.player: That's the one. I have a sample here from your former student, Elena.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Elena eh?

steps.player: Yes, she wants you to analyse it. You might be the only one who can help.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Right then, sounds like we'd better get to work!

steps.player: I have the plague sample.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Now I'll be needing some liquid honey, some sulphuric broline, and then...

steps.player: ... some ethenea?

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Indeed!
If the player does not have all three vials:

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Look, I need all three reagents to test the plague sample. Come back when you've got them.
If the player does not have touch paper:

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Oh. You don't have any touch paper. I won't be able to help after all.
If the player does not have the plague sample:

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Seems like you don't actually have the plague sample. It's a long way to come empty handed... and quite a long way back too.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Now I'll just apply these to the sample and... I don't get it... the touch paper has remained the same.

steps.player: That's why Elena wanted you to do it, because she wasn't sure what was happening.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Well that's just it, nothing has happened. I don't know what this sample is, but it certainly isn't toxic.

steps.player: So what about the plague?

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: This result can only mean one thing... there is no plague. It seems that someone has been lying about all of it. The only question is... why?

steps.player: Well this is worrying. I'd better go and tell Elena right away.

options.text: I was just going to bless your room and I've done that now.

steps.player: I was just going to bless your room and I've done that now.

steps.speaker: Guidor
steps.text: Oh. Goodbye then.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.speaker: Guidor
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.text: Well, hello traveller. I still can't understand why they would lie about the plague.

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-g.player: It's strange, anyway how are you doing?

visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.speaker: Julie
visiting-south-east-varrock-talking-to-j.text: Hello there. I fear Guidor may not be long for this world!

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.speaker: Elena
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.text: You're back! So what did Guidor say?

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.player: He ran his tests and discovered nothing. The plague... it doesn't exist.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.speaker: Elena
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.text: Doesn't exist? But I don't understand... why?

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.player: I don't know, but I think we're about to uncover something huge.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.speaker: Elena
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.text: Well I think there's only one thing for it. The king must be confronted!

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.speaker: Elena
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.text: Yes. King Lathas of East Ardougne. He was the one that had the wall built. He was the one who called the mourners in. He must know what's really going on here.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.player: Well I'd better go and speak to the king then.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.speaker: Elena
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.text: Be quick. You should find him in the castle.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.speaker: Elena
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-elena-afte.text: You must go and see King Lathas immediately!

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.player: I assume that you are King Lathas of East Ardougne?

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: You assume correctly, but where do you get such impertinence.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.player: I get it from finding out that the plague is a hoax.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: A hoax? I've never heard such a ridiculous thing...

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.player: I have evidence, from Guidor of Varrock.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: Ah... I see. Well then you are right about the plague. But I did it for the good of my people.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.player: When is it ever good to lie to people like that?

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: When it protects them from a far greater danger, a fear too big to fathom.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: When my father was king, he ruled over a united Ardougne. But on his deathbed, he could not decide which of his sons should succeed him, so he had the city split into two.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: I became king of East Ardougne while my brother, Tyras, ruled over West Ardougne. My brother was a good man and was great at many things. Being a king was not one of them.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: Rather than looking after his people, he went on numerous expeditions to the lands west of here. On one of these expeditions, he was captured by the forces of the Dark Lord.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: The Dark Lord agreed to spare his life, but only on one condition... That he would drink from the Chalice of Eternity.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: The chalice corrupted him. He joined forces with the Dark Lord, the embodiment of pure evil...

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: And so I erected the wall, not just to protect my people, but to protect all the people of Gielinor. Tyras is king of West Ardougne, sealing off the city was the only way to stop him and the Dark Lord.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: I knew people would never believe the truth, so I had the plague made up as an excuse for the cordon. I'm not proud of it, but it was the only way to keep people safe.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.player: I see. Well at least I know now.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: While my brother is still at large, I must ask that you keep this secret. We can't bring the wall down until we know he is no longer a danger.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.player: But how do we stop him?

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: You're willing to help? Gods be praised!

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: My brother is currently gathering strength in the lands to the west. If we are to stop him, we must find a way through the mountains. There is an underground pass that should lead through but it is full of danger.

return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.speaker: King Lathas
return-to-ardougne-talking-to-king-latha.text: Return to me when you are ready to face this peril. Until then, I give you permission to use my training area. It's located just to the north west of the city.

steps.player: How do I brew ales?

steps.npc: Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.player: What's the blast furnace?

steps.npc: The blast furnace is the pinnacle of dwarven metal- processing! Ore goes in the top and comes out as metal bars almost at once! And it's so efficient it only takes half as much coal to purify it as a regular furnace.
But we've got a bit of a labour shortage at the moment, which is why I have to rely on immigrant workers to keep the furnace going. So, are you here to start work?

How can I help work the blast furnace?

steps.player: How can I help work the blast furnace?

steps.npc: The blast furnace will only work if there is a group of people keeping it going. Let me explain...

steps.text: (The Blast Furnace Plan interface opens, with the X next to the stove flashing.)

steps.npc: Firstly, the stove needs to be kept filled with coal. If this runs out the furnace will not work.

steps.text: (The X next to the Air Pump starts flashing.)

steps.npc: Secondly, someone needs to operate the pump that keeps the hot air blast circulating through the furnace.

steps.text: (The X next to the Temp Gauge starts flashing.)

steps.npc: Thirdly, someone needs to keep an eye on the temperature gauge. They should tell the pumper to start or stop so that the temperature stays in the right range.

steps.text: (The X next to the Cogs starts flashing.)

steps.npc: Lastly, someone needs to be on the pedals to power the conveyor belt that puts ore into the furnace.
Someone will also need to be on standby with a hammer in case the machine breaks!
While that's going, anyone else can put their ore on the conveyor belt to have it smelted.

steps.text: (The Blast Furnace Plan interface closes.)

options.text: So what do I get out of it?

steps.player: So what do I get out of it?

steps.npc: Keeping the furnace going is valuable experience in itself!
Keeping the stove alight will train your Firemaking, working the pump will train your Strength, pedalling the conveyor belt will train your Agility and repairing the furnace will train Crafting.
Plus, everyone working the furnace will get a bit of experience in Smithing whenever anyone smelts ore in it.

steps.player: So I don't actually get paid then?

steps.npc: I offer you the privilege of working on the greatest example of dwarven engineering and you want to be PAID?

standard-dialogue-after-murder-mystery.npc: Apparently you aren't as stupid as you look.

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.npc: Hmm... Wish I had a cat to talk to.
Erm, hello? Can you understand me?

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.player: I certainly can. I am wearing this amulet I got in Sophanem!

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.npc: Ah so you've met some of the local felines. Wise and confusing, those Sphinges.

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.player: Wow!! You know the plural of Sphinx!! What else do you know?

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.npc: All sorts of stuff! I pick up no end of comments on my travels. Want to hear one?

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.player: I certainly do. Share your wisdom Bob!

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-a-catspe.text: Bob then says a tidbit of wisdom.

steps.player: Hi Bob, how's tricks?

steps.npc: Tricks? Dogs are for tricks! Cats are for admiring and fussing over.

steps.player: OK then, how about a joke instead?

steps.npc: Woof woof. Yip yip!

steps.player: Excuse me?

steps.npc: Ah, don't mind me. I am learning a second language!

steps.player: No, you don't understand. I wanted to hear a joke.

steps.npc: Sigh... OK. Did you hear about the cat who drank 10 bowls of milk? He set a new lap record.

steps.player: Did he? Wow. What about this joke then?

steps.npc: Are you trying to be funny?

steps.player: No, that's your job isn't it?

steps.npc: Grrrowl. OK, last try. What do you call a cat that lives in an igloo?.... An Eskimew!

steps.player: An Eskimew... That's not funny. I waited all this time for that? Sheesh.

steps.npc: You know, sometimes I wonder why I still bother with this place. It's just not the same since the humans arrived.

options.text: Speak to me, Bob! Give me some wise words of advice!

steps.player: Speak to me, Bob! Give me some wise words of advice!

steps.npc: Advice you want eh? Well, I could just enlighten you with a snippet of my vast knowledge.

steps.player: That would be fantastic! I heard you were very very wise indeed.

steps.npc: Well, I think I will let you decide that.

steps.player: OK, bamboozle me with your intelligence!

steps.text: Bob then says a tidbit of wisdom.

standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.player: Do you two know each other?

standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.npc: Yes you do. Dive deep, search your feelings.
If only you knew the power of Bob. Your master never told you who your real father was, did he?

standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.speaker: Cat
standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.text: No, but what's that got to do with... no, nooooooo! It cannot be!!

standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.npc: You can destroy Zamorak. He has foreseen this. It is your destiny. Join me, and together we can rule this place as father and son.

standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.speaker: Cat
standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.text: OK dad, maybe later, you're scaring me!

standard-dialogue-while-having-a-cat-fol.player: I think that's about enough of that. I'm off.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-ca.npc: [player name], why do you keep your cat in the bank?

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-ca.player: I thought it was too dangerous to bring it out with me.
Or, I could let the poor thing get butchered! Is that what you want?

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-ca.npc: Butchered!!! I think not. Cats are easily as tough as sheep. Cats were the second thing Guthix brought here, after sheep of course.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-ca.player: Weird. I thought Gnomes and the Dwarves were the first ones. Oh well back to school for me.

location-specific-falador.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-falador.npc: Yes I guess so. But I've been asked to get some coal for Dunstan. He ran out, you see.

location-specific-falador.player: Anything I can do to help?

location-specific-falador.npc: No thanks. I'm on my way back now.

location-specific-lumbridge.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-lumbridge.npc: Yes, but the fish round here are oh so tasty! And there's nobody who can make a good old fashioned seafood gumbo like the Lumbridge cook!
Oh yes, an old recipe passed down from generation to generation of cooks. But this might be the last generation since the Duke's current cook doesn't have any children.

location-specific-lumbridge.player: Ah, I will have to ask him for the recipe then.

location-specific-lumbridge.npc: Oh, I wouldn't do that if I were you, he's very sensitive about his gumbo responsibilities. I'm sure that if you're a good enough fisherman and cook the knowledge will reach you one day.

location-specific-lumbridge.player: OK, I shan't bring it up with him. Cheers for the chat Bob.

location-specific-lumbridge.npc: No problem. Just make sure you bring me some of you ever get the chance to make it. I love that gumbo!

location-specific-taverley.player: Hi Bob. What are you doing here?

location-specific-taverley.npc: Ah, another person who thinks I want to talk to them just because they can understand me.
OK, you asked what I'm doing here.

I'm here to study the druids. They're boring, but they know how to treat animals, and they don't go around bothering you just because they've got a silly gadget that lets them understand what you say!

location-specific-varrock.player: Hi Bob. What are you doing hanging around Varrock?

location-specific-varrock.npc: Not much. Just came to see how things are going. Not visited here in a while you see. Me and Roald used to talk all the time.
Well, those white knights are far more complicated than you might imagine. Not the ‘goodie goodies' they claim to be. Just watch your back.

location-specific-seers-village.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-seers-village.npc: Yikes!! Where did you pop up from?

location-specific-seers-village.player: Oh sorry Bob, didn't mean to make you jump.

location-specific-seers-village.npc: Noooooo. Now that mouse I was chasing has got away. Can you be a bit more sneaky next time? You know, sneaky sneaky stick da chompy as my old friend Rantz often says.

location-specific-ardougne.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-ardougne.npc: Argh! My thumbs have gone weird!

location-specific-ardougne.player: But Bob, you don't have any thumbs!

location-specific-ardougne.npc: Exactly!! Clearly I must go home, the sky's beginning to bruise, night must fall and I shall be forced to camp.
No, not really. I've just had a severe disappointment.

location-specific-ardougne.player: Whats up Bob, lost your favorite toy?

location-specific-ardougne.npc: No, it's just that there comes a time in every cats life where he realises how much time he has wasted just.... playing with rats.

location-specific-ardougne.player: Doesn't sound like a waste of time to me! They deserve it!

location-specific-ardougne.npc: Ahh, I guess your right. Thanks!

location-specific-port-sarim.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-port-sarim.npc: Actually no. I come from round here originally. Back then all this was just fields.

location-specific-port-sarim.player: Back then? How old are you Bob?

location-specific-port-sarim.npc: Ha! How old indeed. How old are the trees? How old are the waves that crash against the shore? How old is the stone we walk on?

location-specific-port-sarim.player: I see. Cryptic as ever. Cheers Bob.... I think.

steps.npc: If a player falls down in a forest and nobody is there, do they make any noise?
Now, where did the rest of my PK clan go?
Be wery, wery quiet... I'm hunting pwayers.
Ah, don't mind me. I'm just looting bodies.
Look out!! He's over there!! Run!!
You know, my feet are knackered. This walking lark isn't all it's cracked up to be. Give me a nice monitor to sleep on any day.
In this place it's not HOW you die that matters. It's who you take with you.
Those who live by the sword, die by the mage.
Did you see that? Someone with a big shiny new halberd hiding behind that rock. I thought only rangers acted as cowardly as that.

steps.player: Are you really just a cat Bob?

steps.npc: Apparently so yes. Well, that's what they told me after the experiment.

steps.player: What experiment?

steps.npc: Yes. There was this professor called 'Oddenstein' I think. He must have tricked me into that machine of his, then the next thing I knew I was feline!

steps.player: Oddenstein? I am sure I have heard that name...

steps.npc: Yes. Once the authorities found out about his experiments he ran away. Lucky for him or I would scratch his eyes out.

steps.player: Is this really all true? Sounds a bit suspicious to me.

steps.npc: Never question the logic of a cat, however flawed.

steps.player: Flawed? So it isn't true... so, erm, eh?

steps.npc: Perhaps one day you will learn the truth. Until then, the Oddenstein story is what we will tell the 'others'. Understood?

steps.player: OK. Your secrets safe with me Bob.
This is a long way from Burthorpe. What you doing out here?

steps.npc: I am drawing a picture of that thing over there.

steps.player: Really? What thing?

steps.npc: That gullible thing over there. Next to that tree where that man sometimes stands.

steps.player: Wow. Could you be any more vague and sarcastic?

steps.npc: Probably. It's just no challenge these days.

steps.player: It's not safe here Bob. You should leave.

steps.npc: No way. I am here catching mice.

steps.player: But there aren't any mice in the Wilderness.

steps.npc: Ahh, the human shows signs of a brain. Why do you think that is?

steps.player: Because you caught them all?

steps.npc: Exactly. Well done!

wisdom.player: Hey Bob. Got any wisdom to share?

steps.npc: If a player falls down in a forest and nobody is there, do they make any noise?
Sorry, I am far too busy marking my territory.

steps.player: Your territory? This place is ruled by the Grand Highmage Gower and his minions.

steps.npc: I think not. They are my minions, and I let him think that he's in charge. I'm the real power behind the throne.

steps.player: I knew it!!

steps.npc: Yeah, it keeps them happy that way, but don't tell anyone!

steps.player: Hee hee. OK Bob.

steps.npc: Dogs believe they are human. Cats believe they are Guthix!

steps.player: What do you believe, Bob?

steps.npc: Well, I don't believe much really since I know I am Zar... erm, well, no, I erm, meow?

steps.player: Hee hee. OK Bob.

steps.npc: Don't get distracted so easily! See, I'm distracting you right now!
Sorry, I'm far too busy calculating thermal vectors.

steps.player: Eh?

steps.npc: Oh, sorry... I meant, erm, meow?
Nothing interesting happens.

steps.player: Eh? That's hardly useful.

steps.npc: Ahh, but it is you see. It does all sorts of wonderous things.

steps.player: Like what?

steps.npc: Well, it's more to do with what happens when you hear that being said. You see, something interesting happens somewhere else.

steps.player: So what you're saying is that if nothing interesting happens to me, then something interesting is happening for someone else somewhere that IS interesting?

steps.npc: Yes, that's about it.

steps.player: OK... I see.... I think.

steps.npc: Cats are rather delicate creatures and they are subject to a good many ailments, but I never heard of one who suffered from insomnia.
So, you want to know how us cats keep so clean all day?

steps.player: Must be all that washing you do.

steps.npc: You would think so wouldn't you. But is being covered in spit really clean?

steps.player: Eeeww. Gross.

steps.npc: Anything not nailed down is a cat toy.
If at first you don't succeed, take a short nap.
Yeah, I could tell you something really useful, but then I would have to '1-hit you' to death.

steps.player: Bob, you couldn't 1-hit a noob.

steps.npc: Care to place a wager on that? Sorry, hang on, I've got no pockets. Maybe next time.

steps.player: I'll be waiting.

steps.npc: Dogs have owners, cats have staff.
I have studied many philosophers and many cats. The wisdom of cats is infinitely superior.
There are many intelligent species in the universe. They are all owned by cats.
Cats and teleporting just don't mix well. That's why I walk everywhere. Messes my hair up terribly.
Cats are smarter than dogs. You can't get eight cats to pull a sled through snow.
Sorry, no time for chat. Still got mouse bones stuck in my teeth. How awkward.
You know, cats are the first species to fully evolve. We're perfect.
Preserve nature. Pickle a dog!
Do you like dogs?

steps.player: Yes!

steps.npc: Me too. Care to swap recipes? I have a rather unique hotdog sauce.

steps.player: Bob, you're a bit messed up really aren't you.

steps.npc: No, I just know what I like. Besides, it was a joke.

steps.player: A joke? I doubt the dogs are laughing.

steps.npc: What dogs? I have already rid this place of dogs. Have you ever seen one?

steps.player: Yes actually. I heard there are a few wild dogs about here somewhere.

steps.npc: Right!! Fellow cats, prepare for war!!
Mmm. Maybe another time.
Cat Rule number 1: Always act afraid when near dogs, especially if you're near a human. They will pick you up and fuss you, then shout at the dog. Most amusing!
Cat Rule number 2: When assisting a human at work, make sure you sit behind its right leg. You stand a much better chance of getting picked up and stroked. Also, it's very amusing
Cat Rule number 3: If you ever make a mistake, which is rare and probably involves a dog, make sure you wash yourself immediately. This will give everyone the impression that
it was done on purpose.
Cat Rule number 4: Beware the bag monster. These things live in small bags and under newspapers, sometimes even hidden in shoes if they are very clever. They will be very small and
take on the same colour as the hiding place. Attack these things on sight - stop at nothing. If you see a bag or shoe you have not inspected recently, pounce!!

steps.player: Do you like all the monsters around here?

steps.npc: No, not really. I'm actually signed up with all those HAM fanatics. Kill the whole lot of 'em!!

steps.player: That's a bit cruel isn't it?

steps.npc: Yeah, that's one of my best qualities. Just behind sneaky and vicious. Besides, after a few doses of catnip, they all look like mice to me!

steps.npc: My cow of a sister kicked me out of her bar. Said I was getting the place a bad name. So I'm staying here until I'm old enough to get my own place.

steps.npc: Yeah, you're in the biggest dumpster of Dumpsterville. Now you know. Anyway, do you want something?

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: Yeah, alright...
I am Bologa Gricoller, seeker of forbidden wisdom, wanderer of the dark pathways, thinker of the unthinkable. I can do bartending too.
I used to work at The Golden Field. That's my sister's bar. It's mostly farmhands drinking there, but you get some interesting people as well.
See, most Hosidius people are Saradominists. My sister, she's always listening to Father Jean at the church with his goodie-goodie sermons.
But some of us in the bar thought we'd give Zamorak a try. Like, you gotta be open-minded, right? What did Saradomin ever do for us anyway?
So we'd meet in the bar, sharing books that the Piscarilius smugglers would bring us, learning what the Saradominists don't want us to know.
Anyway, my sister - she's a right cow, by the way - she fired me and kicked me out. Said I was bringing bad sorts to her bar.
Bad sorts, she said! Like, morality is totally subjective, right? So who's she to call us bad sorts just 'cos we're not afraid to think differently?
Anyway, I've learnt all this cool stuff about Zamorak, and being stuck in a fruit farm doesn't stop me being his loyal servant, right?
In fact I've invented a Zamorakian blessing that works on fruit! You can use it to make Zamorak's wine out of grapes from the Vinery.

steps.text: Well, you may be aware of the previous attempts at this expedition?

steps.player: No, what happened?

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: Well, the first barge had some serious design flaws... it didn't float.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: The second barge suffered from 'feature creep'. Senior museum staff stuck their oar in and added unnecessary features: 'go-faster stripes', a portable fossil centrifuge and a walk-on mini-museum.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: Needless to say, it had... buoyancy issues.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: The third barge made it out to sea, but a special sealant was used that attracted sea monsters. They didn't make it very far.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: The fourth also used a special sealant, this one attracted icebergs.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: The fifth barge crashed into the sixth.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: We lost the seventh one.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: The eighth barge is still here, we think. An accident involving a magical explosion and some talking anchovies means that it is now believed to reside 12 seconds out of phase.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: The ninth version was built using magic logs. The barge gained some form of rudimentary sentience. It developed serious depression and ran itself aground near Crandor.

steps.speaker: Lead Navigator
steps.text: So, now do you understand why we need your help?

options.text: I'm aware, no need to tell me about them.

steps.text: Well, [player name], whether you believe it or not, know that none of my men will be going on this expedition unless you can ensure our safety from the curse.

steps.text: Aye, 'tis a matter we take very seriously. Luckily, there are ways ye can avoid a curse.

steps.text: Well that all depends on the nature of yer travels!

steps.speaker: Jack Seagull

steps.player: Well... I guess so.

steps.text: Then the way I be seein' it, ye be needin' a lucky charm to do with that!

steps.player: What does this seed pod do?

steps.npc: Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not
very pleasant...

It is rumoured that this place used to be of religious significance to druidic followers of both Ralos and Ranul.

steps.npc: According to religious texts, Ralos is the god of the sun and Ranul, his brother, is the god of the moon.
If you find any artifacts or relics from within this temple, I would be very interested in seeing them.

I worship Ralos, a common practice where I am from. However, I found out that our order may have originated from this temple. If you find anything of interest, please let me know.

options.text: Tell me of the finding of Koschei

steps.player: I'm interested in finding out about that mysterious warrior I fought as part of Thorvalds' combat trial. His name is Koschei I believe.

steps.npc: Ah... the deathless one... We do not even know if Koschei is his name, when we found him he had no memory, he was simply repeating that single word.
Whatever happened to him must have rattled his soul so hard that his memory ran away from him, and he has not yet found it's hiding place.

steps.player: So how exactly did you find him?

steps.npc: Well, it was a raiding party like any other. We had just struck one of the smaller northern islands to harvest supplies by combat, as our laws allow,
when we saw a figure in the icey waters. As we were at least a 3 week sail from any port, and saw no other ships nearby, he must have been there some time.
We could not leave someone to the cold death of the ocean, even an outerlander, so we fished him aboard. He muttered continually, but his words made no sense.
He had no clothes or possessions with him, and seemed to have been burnt somehow before he had landed in the water.
I cannot help but wonder what burnt him, for as you may have seen, he is incredibly powerful and resistant to damage by any means I know of!
Anyway, we decided to bring him back to Rellekka, for he did not seem of good health or sound mind, and simply repeated the word Koschei over and over.
Yrsa tended to him for many weeks, until one day it was as though a new soul had entered his burnt and broken body.
He suddenly left her house one day, fully healed, and able to speak to us as though nothing had happened to him.
He still had no recollection of how he had come to be in the icey ocean, or of who he was, or where he had come from, but this did not matter to us or him.
He took his trials of adulthood, as you did, and has been a boon to our clan ever since. Someday I fear he may regain his memory, and leave us for his past...
But I will always respect any decision he decides to make should that day ever come upon us. Until then, he is more than welcome to stay here.
So, [Fremennik name]. Was there anything more you wished to hear?

steps.npc: Well, I think the best thing for you would be to go to the docks and ask to join one of our longboats on a journey.
My affairs are concentrated mostly on Rellekka, so my knowledge is not great, but I will happily share what I do know with you [Fremennik name].
North of this town the atmosphere becomes bitterly cold. There are a number of small inhabited islands that we have sea routes with.
The largest of these is possibly Miscellania, although I hear that there has been some recent incident with their monarch, but I don't know the details.
There is also of course the island of the moon clan, who change with the tides. They are our bitterest enemies, and we are currently at war with them.
They are an evil people, equally cursed and blessed by the magic in their blood. Beyond those islands, there is the large frozen wasteland we call Acheron.
It is an inhospitable land, and you will need an agile and sturdy body just to keep alive in it's perils.
As I say, my knowledge outside of this town is rather limited, and I know no more than this. Was there anything else you wished to hear tell of?

steps.player: I would like to hear a little of the history between the Fremenniks and the outerlanders.

steps.npc: Ah, now that is something I know a great deal about. Believe it or not, all outerlanders were once orginally Fremenniks.
When first man came to these lands all were Fremenniks, and followed our ways. We lived a happy life, and never settled in one place for long.
We travelled by boat along the coastlines, never taking more from the land than could be regrown by the same time in the following year.
However, many moons past, some of our tribesmen were weary of constantly travelling the lands, and decided to build themselves permanent homes.
Unfortunately, the other races that had also migrated here did not like this. They waged war against us at every opportunity.
We were driven mostly to the coastlines, where we could escape by boat when attacked. Remember, at this time we had no real way to defend against constant attack.
Then one day one of our Seers, whose name has been lost in the telling of this tale, discovered a cave full of strange rocks.
This rock would never be consumed, no matter how much we took, and sparkled at its peak, and broke off in small and regular sized chunks when mined.
Stranger than this, we found that these rocks would become filled with power when taken to certain places across this land!
There was a terrible argument in our tribe! Some said that we should take as many of these rocks as we could, and use them in defending against our enemies attacks!
Others said that we had found a place that belonged only to the gods, and that should we steal what was not ours we would find only torment and misery.
We voted on this, and decided that it was in the best interests of the tribe to leave these strange rocks where they lay, for the gods can be spiteful and cruel,
especially to those who do not treat them with the respect they desire. Some of our number refused to accept this ruling by our council however.
They began to mine these rocks, and set up transport systems to the various places of power that enchanted them.
They even created temples at each of these places! This was going too far! We had no choice, but to expel them from our tribe forever!
We turned our backs upon them, and let them know they would never be welcome back to our tribes until they had released themselves from the rocks.
This is the tale of how the outerlanders came about; through stealing from the gods, and from betraying our ideals. This is why we show them no trust.
Was there something else you wished to hear?

steps.player: Actually, history isn't really my thing.

steps.npc: Well let me know should you wish to hear our lore and histories. We value them highly.

options.text: Could you explain this place to me again?

steps.player: Could you explain this place to me again?

steps.npc: This here is the Gauntlet, the finest creation of the Amlodd clan. It was built years ago to help train Prifddinas' finest warriors and survivalists.

steps.player: Train?

steps.npc: That's right. The Gauntlet contains a range of deadly creatures formed from crystal. Defeating them is the key to victory, but it is no easy task.
This is because all participants start with nothing at hand beyond a few basic tools.

steps.player: But how do people fight without their gear?

steps.npc: Resources can be gathered throughout the dungeon. These can be used to create the weapons, armour, food and potions needed to survive.
Without any armour, those crystalline creatures can be real nasty. Any armour that you make down there will greatly reduce the damage they do to you.

steps.player: Okay, I think I follow... But I thought this was all about combat, not just gathering my own equipment.

steps.npc: That's right. Once you feel you're ready, or once we decide that you've spent long enough down there, you'll have to face the fearsome Crystalline Hunllef.

steps.player: And what makes it so dangerous, if it's just for training?

steps.npc: Once you go down there, there are only two ways out... You can make a break for the exit, or if you're bested in combat we'll send someone in for you.

steps.text: The Gauntlet is not a safe environment, and teleports are blocked inside! If you die in there, any items stored at a gravestone will be lost!

steps.npc: Things can be a little unstable down there at times, too... Everything gets corrupted, and it might be a little frightening, but it makes for a good challenge.

steps.text: The Corrupted Gauntlet can be accessed by rightclicking the entrance.

steps.npc: I think that covers it... Everything else, you'll have to work out for yourself while you're in there.

steps.player: Okay... I think I've got it.

steps.npc: You can always come back and ask me to go over things again.

before-starting-perilous-moons.speaker: Builder 1
before-starting-perilous-moons.text: It's a bit rude of 'em to take up the whole bridge with their conversation, isn't it, mate?

before-starting-perilous-moons.speaker: Builder 2
before-starting-perilous-moons.text: Aye, mate, but wouldn't it be just as rude for us to interrupt?

before-starting-perilous-moons.speaker: Builder 1
before-starting-perilous-moons.text: A good point well made, mate. Who are we to decide that the dig is more impor'ant than a personal disagreement between two people?

before-starting-perilous-moons.speaker: Builder 2
before-starting-perilous-moons.text: You're not wrong, mate. We often place matters of industry above those of people, and it's chippin' away at our ability to relate to each other on a human level.

steps.player: What's going on here?

steps.text: We're part of a dig into some ruins beneath Cam Torum, but the way's blocked by these folks.

steps.player: Have you tried asking them to move?

steps.speaker: Builder 2

steps.player: Are you two philosophers?

steps.speaker: Builder 1
steps.text: No mate, builders.

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: But thinking, talking, discussing, it's what makes us human, mate.

steps.player: It's not just humans that do those things.

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: Fair play, mate. I guess we're reflecting more on the condition of sen'ience in general then.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Builder 2
steps.text: Have a good one, mate.

after-perilous-moons.speaker: Builder 1

2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.npc: Hello sir, are you going to make a snowman?

2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.player: Maybe, I'm not sure I'd be very good at it!

2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.npc: I want to make a snowman, but I can't reach high enough to stack the snowballs properly.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Hello Buoy and Gurl!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Hello sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: How do you know our names?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I had a chat with your dad. He's super busy, so he's asked me to help you build a snowman!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Really? We get to make a snowman?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes! And I'm going to build whatever snowman you want!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Yay! Can it be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: But I want it to be five tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Five is a bad number, it should be three tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You're a bad number. Five is so much better.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait a second. Why don't we meet in the middle. How about four snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl think for a second.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Fine, it can be four tall.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Yes, four tall is okay.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Great. Now, we need to pick what size snowballs we want for each tier. Why don't you take it in turns? You can do two each.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The bottom one should be a huge snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: The next one should be big!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: This is working nicely, we're half way! What about the top two parts?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The next one should be a small snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: No, it should be little!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: But it needs to be small, little would look bad.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: It wouldn't look bad. Small is better for decorations.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: My decorations will fit on a little one.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Why do you always ruin everything?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You ruin everything with your silly ideas!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait. This clearly isn't working, and I don't want you two to fall out. It's Christmas, we shouldn't be arguing!
How about I make you both a snowman? It can be whatever height and size you like. One each!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: So mine can be five snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: And mine can be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes, I'll make you both whatever snowman you like!
What would you both like?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: I'd like mine to be three snowballs tall please! And I want the bottom one to be small, the middle one big, and the top one huge!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I'd like mine to be five snowballs tall please! I want the bottom one to be humongous, then large, then normal, then big, and then a little one for the top!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: That's two very different snowmen, I see why this didn't work before!
What do all these different sizes mean? Humongous? Normal? Little? How big are those?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You silly billy! Humongous is the biggest snowball of course!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Normal is the normal size that you get when you make a snowball normally. It's easy!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Right, thank you for clearing that up. I'll figure something out.
What are you two going to do for decorations?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: I already know what I want mine to look like!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Me too!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Why don't you guys find some decorations while I build the snowmen? Then you can add them once I'm done.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Okay sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: We will do that!
Buoy and Gurl go back to playing in the snow.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, that seems sorted. I should speak to Larry again, and see if he has any advice about building the snowmen.
Hello there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Have you started making the snowmen yet?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You should talk to dad if you need some help, he knows how to make snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Yeah, he always used to make really big ones with us!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Maybe I'll go talk to him and see what advice he has.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: He'll say, make them really tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: He'll say make them shorter, because that's better!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl wander off, arguing about what size snowman is the best.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I should go and speak to Larry. I'm sure he has some handy advice for me!

2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.speaker: Buoy/Gurl
2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.text: That looks good! It needs a [size] snowball next!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Yay! Can we decorate them now?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.npc: Yes! Can we decorate them now please [player name]?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: Of course you can. Are they what you wanted?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.npc: Mine too. It's just how I wanted it.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I am happy to hear that. It was harder work than I thought.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: You did a good job. Thank you very much [sir/madam].

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: It was no problem. Merry Christmas to you both!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Buoy and Gurl go to their snowmen to start decorating.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I should go and speak to Larry. Hopefully he has that festive white wine ready for me.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Those snowmen look amazing!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Thank you! Decorating them was quite hard!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yeah, they took ages to do! Do you like mine?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: It's really good! Reminds me of something actually.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: What about mine? Do you like it?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I like yours too. They both remind me of something!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Mine is Thermy! My favourite monster! She's so big and scary, makes me go woah!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Mine is Tempy! My favourite monster! He lives in the water, a huge mass of angry wet!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: They're both amazing! I didn't know you guys would be so good at decorating.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Dad lets us decorate every year. We get a lot of practice!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Last year we made them into the Fragment of Seren and the King Black Dragon!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: What... really??? I'd like to have seen that. Those sound even more difficult than these two!
How do you know all these monsters anyway? There is no way your dad would let you anywhere near them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Dad reads us lots of stories, and we hear about them from passing adventurers, like you.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: You must meet some interesting and cool adventurers!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Not as cool as you though; none of them helped us make our snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Yes, you're the first to help us make them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, you're welcome. I really enjoyed it. What are you guys going to do now you're finished?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: We're going to go and play! And maybe visit the festival. Will you be there?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I sure will be. Maybe see you there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Bye sir, Merry Christmas.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Merry Christmas, have fun!
