during-the-depths-of-despair.player: Hello. I'm helping Lord Hosidius find his missing son. I was wondering if you could help me.

during-the-depths-of-despair.npc: I'm afraid I know not where Artur has gone. I do not speak to him much. He keeps himself to himself.
However, I've noticed him speaking to Olivia before. Maybe she can help.

during-the-depths-of-despair-after-talki.npc: Good day [sir/madam]. I hope your quest is going well.

after-completing-the-depths-of-despair.npc: Good day [sir/madam]. On behalf of the Hosidius family, I thank you for bringing Artur home.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.npc: Good day [sir/madam]. I'm afraid I can't stop to talk. The new Lord Hosidius has plenty of work for me.

after-hazeel-cult.npc: It's an honour to be in your presence again, adventurer. I hope things are well?
Unfortunately, I am still forced to deal with this insufferable family. Many generations have passed, but they are still the enemy. As such, they must be kept a close eye on.
Still, I have no doubt that the time will soon come for me to leave this place. Our lord will certainly have need of me elsewhere once his current work is complete.

after-hazeel-cult.player: I see. Well good luck with it all.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Not much to say. Came to Weiss with other trolls when we got kicked out of caves further south, but I was just young troll then.
Mostly been enjoying living round Weiss, 'cos wildlife is interesting here.

steps.player: Tell me about this place.

steps.npc: This here is Weiss. Trolls built it years ago, after we got kicked out from caves further south. Now Weiss is our home.
It great here, now Snowflake an' her husband troll taught us goutweed farming. Food so much better now.

steps.player: Do you like it here?

steps.npc: Eh, it kinda rough, but it getting better. Snowflake, she taught us goutweed farming. Goat, wolf, human all taste so much nicer with goutweed in.
So yeah, Weiss is good place to live, now Snowflake in charge. All trolls like Snowflake. Her husband troll kinda weird, but that not our problem.

steps.player: I'll be off.

standard-dialogue.npc: Urgh, it just happened again! Every time I almost have it my hand slips.

standard-dialogue.player: Oh, that's unfortunate. Are you using a lockpick?

standard-dialogue.npc: Yes. Well actually, I'm using a Strange old lockpick. I found it while looting one of these coffins and I typically have better luck with it.

standard-dialogue.player: Oh, that's interesting. I'll keep my eyes out for one.

standard-dialogue.npc: I've found a few of them while raiding this place. There appear to be more of them on this floor than the floors above.

standard-dialogue.player: I see. If you don't mind me asking, you already have dark graceful so why are you still looking for hallowed marks?

standard-dialogue.npc: Oh, it's because of this little fellow following me. I've heard that the Dark acorn sold by the guy upstairs will transform him into a Dark Squirrel.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player does not have a Dark squirrel following them:

steps.player: Wow, I didn't know that! That sounds pretty cool.

steps.npc: Yeah, that's what I thought but that mysterious stranger is asking for 3,000 Hallowed marks for it.

steps.player: 3,000? That sounds extortionate!

steps.npc: Yeah, that's what I thought. Feels like he set the price just to keep me down here for longer. Still, it's not like I have anything better to do.

steps.player: I see, well best of luck. Hopefully you survive long enough to finish your goal.

steps.npc: I'm sure I'll be fine.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has a Dark squirrel following them:

steps.player: Yeah, I ended up buying one myself and fed it to my Giant Squirrel. It took a while but it was definitely worth it.

steps.npc: Wow, I'm impressed! How long did it take you to get the 3,000 marks?

steps.player: Long enough... Still, at least I feel much more agile now than when I started.

steps.npc: I don't think I'm going to get any more agile while looking for it myself. I'm glad you received some benefit from the grind though.

steps.player: I see, well best of luck. Hopefully you survive long enough to finish your goal.

steps.npc: I'm sure I'll be fine.

steps.npc: Who cares about that? If it doesn't work then I should just wear the full graceful outfit since that would be much more efficient.

steps.player: Each to their own I suppose.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Bill Teach
starting-the-quest.text: Mumblelandlubbermumblemumble...

starting-the-quest.speaker: Bill Teach
starting-the-quest.text: What right have ye to be so happy, landlubber?

starting-the-quest.player: Well it is quite a nice day.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Bill Teach
starting-the-quest.text: Aye, that it is.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Bill Teach
starting-the-quest.text: Will ye forgive an old sailor his temper [lad/lass/kid]? I'm in dire straits indeed.

starting-the-quest.player: What's the problem? I may be able to help.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Bill Teach
starting-the-quest.text: I dunno, [lad/lass/kid], I need a pirate to help me with my problem, but none will sail with me.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Bill Teach
starting-the-quest.text: Well, ye look like ye might have the right stuff, tell me would ye like te be a pirate?

options.text: Yes, I've always wanted to be a pirate!

steps.player: Yes, I've always wanted to be a pirate!

steps.text: If the player does not have all quest requirements:

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: It takes more grit than most have te be a pirate, and I don't think ye've got what it takes [lad/lass/kid].
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Cabin Fever quest.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Well [lad/lass/kid], I don't think ye could pirate yer way out of a chest full of piracy.

steps.player: Awww...

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: But since nobody else will risk the trip ye'll do!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Well [lad/lass/kid], I be Bill Teach, the Captain of the Adventurous, one of the finest ships ever to sail these waters.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: I'm in port doin' some legitimate tradin' before headin' back to Mos Le'Harmless.

steps.player: Mos Le'Harmless? Where is that?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: It's a pirate stronghold off the southern coast of Morytania. Been in existence for years it has and I reckon it's the best place for pirates to relax!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Well, one of the best... A lot be liking the Pandemonium these days, and Brimhaven does have that fancy Agility Arena...

steps.player: Will it be OK for me to go there if I am not a pirate?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Of course [lad/lass/kid], once we make landfall ye'll have worked as a sailor on a pirate vessel, which is one of the easiest ways to become a true pirate.
If the player has completed The Pandemonium:

steps.player: Worked as a sailor? Do I really need to do that? I've already got some sailing experience.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Of course ye do, [lad/lass/kid]! Plenty be claiming they've got what it takes to be a pirate, but I can't be takin' ye word 'till I see it for myself.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: This brings me back to the reason I'm stuck here of course, and the reason I need your help.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Last night I got into a war o' words with another Cap'n, and he has vowed to sink my ship and put all of my crew to the sword.

steps.player: How horrible! How did your crew react?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: By desertin'.

steps.player: All of them?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Every last one!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: The second I leave port I'll come under attack. I think I'll be able te make it if I have another person helpin' out, but I wouldn't stand a chance by me self.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Ye said ye would help me out [lad/lass/kid], will ye stand by yer word?

options.text: Yes, I am a man of my word.

steps.player: Yes, I am a [man/woman] of my word.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Arr! Ye struck me as a [man/woman] of integrity!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: My ship is the Adventurous, and she's at the east dock.

steps.player: You won't...err...I mean ye'll not regret it Cap'n!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: I'm sure I won't.

options.text: No, if it's so dangerous your crew left, count me out.

steps.player: No, if it's so dangerous your crew left, count me out.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Well, that doesn't surprise me much.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: On yer way [lad/lass/kid], leave me be.

options.text: No thanks, it sounds quite dangerous.

steps.player: No thanks, it sounds quite dangerous.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Aye, that it be. Come back when yer liver ain't so lily-like, [lad/lass/kid].

starting-the-quest-trying-to-board-the-a.player: I don't think that whoever owns this ship will be happy with me wandering all over it.

speaking-to-bill-teach-again-at-the-pub.speaker: Bill Teach
speaking-to-bill-teach-again-at-the-pub.text: If ye ain't up te scratch as a pirate I may not get another one.

speaking-to-bill-teach-on-the-ship.player: Don't ye worry about me, Cap'n! I'm the scurviest, throat-cuttinest pirate to ever walk the mainplank! Arr!

speaking-to-bill-teach-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
speaking-to-bill-teach-on-the-ship.text: Aye, I should have remembered ye was eager.

steps.player: Let's go Cap'n!

options.text: Can I just go grab something?

steps.text: Aye [lad/lass], take yer time, I'm not goin' anywhere without ye.

options.text: Can I just go grab something?

cutscene-on-the-ship.player: Well, it looks like they've found us Cap'n.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: Well, without anyone else te help ye'll have te do some hard work if we don't want to end up walkin' home on the sea bed.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: Well if their first shot hadn't taken out the cannon I'd be firing that at them.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: Arr! They seek te hole the ship! Go and take care of their cannon.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: If ye grab some fuse from the gun locker, and a rope from the repair locker, then ye can use the rope on the sails to swing over and deal with their cannon.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: Just take the fuse, use it on the barrel of gunpowder next to the cannon, and then light it with something.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: A lantern, a tinderbox, it doesn't matter.

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: They have masts as well don't they?

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: Just do the same trick using some rope on their sails and swing over.

cutscene-on-the-ship.player: Arr! I'll hop to it Cap'n!

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: Ye ain't a pirate yet by a long shot!

cutscene-on-the-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
cutscene-on-the-ship.text: I'll be on deck if ye need me.

cutscene-on-the-ship.player: Now to take care of that cannon!

cutscene-on-the-ship-teleporting-out-of-.text: It will probably not take Bill long to notice you have left the battle.

dealing-with-the-cannon-trying-to-fill-t.text: Urgent as this looks, if I haven't taken out that cannon they will just hole the ship again.

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.player: Just to clear everything up, what is it you want me to do?

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.speaker: Bill Teach
dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.text: Well, ye'll need to silence their cannon before it sinks us. Before ye do that though, ye'll need to swing over to their ship.

options.text: How do I make a rope swing?

steps.player: How do I make a rope swing?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Yer not much of a pirate are ye lad?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Ye climb up the mast and use a rope on the sails up there.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Then ye climb down and ye swing on the rope.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: If I have te explain how ye do THAT then I might as well just send out some biscuit weevles to do the job instead.

steps.player: Aye aye Cap'n! One rope swing coming right up!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Egad...

options.text: How can I blow up their cannon?

steps.player: How can I blow up their cannon?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Well, ye'll need some fuse from the cannon locker below decks.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Swing over to the enemy ship and put the fuse in the barrel of gunpowder they'll have next to the cannon to speed up their firin'.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Then, use something on the fuse te get it lit.  A tinderbox, candle or any sort of flame will do.

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: After that ye just step back and let it burn by its self.

steps.player: Arr! I'll blow that cannon sky high, sez I!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Give me strength...

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: That's the spirit!

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.speaker: Bill Teach
dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.text: Well, as much as this is an interestin' break, why don't ye head back to the ship and we'll see if we can beat them this time?

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.speaker: Bill Teach
dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.text: All right, lad let's try this again. This time, try not te run away!

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.speaker: Bill Teach
dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-.text: Ye all ready to go lad?

options.text: Can I just go grab something?

dealing-with-the-cannon-the-enemy-reappe.speaker: Bill Teach
dealing-with-the-cannon-the-enemy-reappe.text: One look at the enemy and ye run away.

dealing-with-the-cannon-the-enemy-reappe.speaker: Bill Teach
dealing-with-the-cannon-the-enemy-reappe.text: Get over there and take out their cannon before I throw ye there me self.

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-enemy.speaker: Pirate
dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-enemy.text: I'll have ye guts fer garters!

dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-enemy.speaker: Pirate
dealing-with-the-cannon-talking-to-enemy.text: Arr! Run him through sez I!

dealing-with-the-cannon-trying-to-plunde.text: I don't have time to search that.

dealing-with-the-cannon-using-a-rope-swi.text: The rope falls off the mast! Clearly your knots are sub-sailor standard.
You fall in the water with a splash!
You have to swim across; which puts a considerable drain on your energy.

dealing-with-the-cannon-using-fuse-on-th.text: You attach the fuse to the barrel.
You are a little too close. Try lighting the end of the fuse.
The fuse refuses to light. Try again.
You cannot get the flame close enough to the fuse to use that to light it.

dealing-with-the-cannon-the-fuse-is-lit.text: ...and destroy the barrel and the cannon.
(The barrel blows up, taking out the cannon in the process.)

sort-out-the-leaks.player: Arr! I've blown their cannon to smithereens Cap'n!

sort-out-the-leaks.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks.text: Yer not a pirate yet [lad/lass], so stop talkin' like that!

sort-out-the-leaks.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks.text: Well, ye've sorted out their cannon, but we're takin' on water.

sort-out-the-leaks.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks.text: Go below deck and sort out the leaks.

sort-out-the-leaks.player: Will smearing swamp paste on the holes do?

sort-out-the-leaks.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks.text: No [lad/lass], these holes were made by cannon fire.

sort-out-the-leaks.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks.text: Ye'll need to get some planks from the repair locker and tack them in place. Then ye smear swamp paste over the planks to seal the hole.

sort-out-the-leaks.player: Arr! I'll have this ship ship-shape in no time! Arr!

sort-out-the-leaks.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks.text: Wait 'till we make landfall before ye start actin' like a pirate!

sort-out-the-leaks-talking-to-bill-teach.player: Errr...I may well have been caught up in the whole 'pirate' thing, and I can't seem to remember what I need to do now...

sort-out-the-leaks-talking-to-bill-teach.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-talking-to-bill-teach.text: Ye'll need to get some planks from the repair locker and tack them in place. Then ye smear swamp paste over the planks to seal the hole.

sort-out-the-leaks-talking-to-bill-teach.player: Arr! I be rememberin' now Cap'n!

sort-out-the-leaks-talking-to-bill-teach.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-talking-to-bill-teach.text: This is what I get when I ask random strangers for help...

sort-out-the-leaks-returning-to-battle-a.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-returning-to-battle-a.text: Looks like they haven't been back to port to get that cannon fixed, which is lucky.

sort-out-the-leaks-returning-to-battle-a.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-returning-to-battle-a.text: Get below and fix the holes in the hull pronto, or we'll sink before they have a chance te kill us!
You need 2 repair planks to repair this hole.
You need 10 tacks to repair this hole.
You need a Hammer to repair this hole.

sort-out-the-leaks-planking-up-a-hole.text: You nail the Planks over the the hole!

sort-out-the-leaks-planking-up-a-hole-tr.text: You need Swamp Paste to waterproof this hole.

sort-out-the-leaks-patching-up-a-hole.text: You smear the Swamp Paste over the hole!

sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.text: Why not pay them a visit and go plunder their hold?

sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.player: Arr! I'll plunder their booty and no mistake!

sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.text: Come back here and drop it in the chest in the hold.

sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.player: Aye aye Cap'n! One plunderin' comin' right up!

sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.speaker: Bill Teach
sort-out-the-leaks-after-all-the-holes-h.text: I've been a pirate all me life and I've never heard anyone keep harpin' on like that!

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.player: So...how many loads of plunder did you want me to get?

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.speaker: Bill Teach
time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.text: Ten! Can't ye count that high?

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.player: What happens if I take all the plunder I find and there is less than ten loads?

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.speaker: Bill Teach
time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.text: Then ye wait for the pirates to stash some more in the hold. Since they are under attack they'll be dumpin' their gold and stuff in there every chance they get.

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.speaker: Bill Teach
time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.text: Just give it a minute and head back!

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.player: Arr! I'll keep plunderin' till the hold be full of booty!

time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.speaker: Bill Teach
time-to-plunder-talking-to-bill-teach-be.text: Yer not making any friends here [lad/lass], just go and do it.

time-to-plunder-returning-to-plunder-fro.speaker: Bill Teach
time-to-plunder-returning-to-plunder-fro.text: When yer quite done runnin' away lad ye've got a load of plunder to be grabbin'!

time-to-plunder-plundering-the-chest.text: If the player has recently plundered the chest:

steps.text: This chest has been recently plundered.

time-to-plunder-looting-the-crate.text: If the player has recently looted the crate:

steps.text: This crate has been recently looted.

time-to-plunder-looting-the-crate.text: (The player finds two loads of plunder.)

time-to-plunder-ransacking-the-barrel.text: If the player has recently ransacked the barrel:

steps.text: This barrel has been recently ransacked.

time-to-plunder-ransacking-the-barrel.text: (The player finds one load of plunder.)

time-to-plunder-storing-the-loot-in-the-.text: If the player has no plunder to store

steps.text: You have plunder to deposit.

time-to-plunder-storing-the-loot-in-the-.text: You deposit [X] loads of plunder in the chest.
You deposit as much plunder as you can.

time-to-plunder-counting-the-plunder-in-.text: If the storage is filled with 10 plunder

steps.text: This chest is full of plunder.

time-to-plunder-counting-the-plunder-in-.text: This chest has [X] loads of plunder inside.
I seem to have taken all the plunder.

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: I warn ye, [lad/lass], if the first word out of yer mouth is 'Arr' I'll be wearing yer spleen as a novelty hat before ye reach the second 'r'!

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: I should have seen that comin'

fixing-up-the-cannon.player: Cap'n! I've put ten loads of plunder in the chest, in the hold!

fixing-up-the-cannon.text: If the player has extra plunder on them:

steps.player: I even had some left over!

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Let me see that.

steps.player: Can I have those back?

steps.speaker: Bill Teach
steps.text: Have what back?

steps.player: Nothing...

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: Not yet! Let's give em a blast with the cannon before we leave!

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: Alright [lad/lass], try and stay with me on this one.

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: See, there is a secret technique for making things that be broken right again.

fixing-up-the-cannon.player: How do I repair the cannon?

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: Ye need to remove the old barrel, then replace it with a new one from the gun locker downstairs.

fixing-up-the-cannon.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon.text: I don't want to overload ye with too many details right now. Come tell me when the cannon is ready again.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: If ye know what is good for ye, yer off to fix the cannon!

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.player: How was I going to do that again?

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: By replacing the broken barrel with a new one! Hop to it [lad/lass], the salt air is clearly eatin' into yer brains!

fixing-up-the-cannon-returning-to-fix-th.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-returning-to-fix-th.text: Have ye sorted out the cannon yet?

fixing-up-the-cannon-taking-a-new-barrel.text: You don't need [a Ramrod/a cannon ball/a canister/any Fuse] right now.

fixing-up-the-cannon-using-a-new-barrel-.text: You attach the new barrel to the cannon.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Have ye fixed the cannon yet, yes or no.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Now ye can give those pirates a good shot across their bows.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Ye'll need to load the cannon, and if ye get it wrong the barrel will blow, and ye'll need to start again.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: First, ye take some powder from the powder keg.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Then ye use a ramrod from the gun locker on the powder to tamp the charge.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Then ye use a canister round on the cannon.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Finally ye use some fuse on the cannon, and light it like ye did the fuse on the barrel earlier.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: Then, ye'll need to use the ramrod on the cannon to clean it out for the next shot.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.player: Yes, but if I forget I'll come and ask you.

fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.speaker: Bill Teach
fixing-up-the-cannon-talking-to-bill-tea.text: And te think this was all I could get te help...

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: I can guess from the lack of an explosion that ye haven't fired the cannon yet, correct?

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: And I'll bet ye want a quick recap of how to do it, correct?

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.player: That would help to be honest.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Ye'll need to load the cannon, and if ye get it wrong the barrel will blow, and ye'll need to start again.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: First, ye take some powder from the powder keg.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Then ye use a ramrod from the gun locker on the powder to tamp the charge.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Then ye use a canister round on the cannon.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Finally ye use some fuse on the cannon, and light it like ye did the fuse on the barrel earlier.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Then, ye'll need to use the ramrod on the cannon to clean it out for the next shot.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Ye got all that this time?

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Yer still not a pirate, so cut that out!

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: We were on the home stretch lad why did we turn back?

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.speaker: Bill Teach
talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: Never mind, just go shoot the pirates and let's press on.
You pour the powder into the cannon.
You shove the Ramrod into the cannon barrel.
You roll the canister round into the cannon.
You ready the cannon for firing.
You take some gunpowder
The cannon blows up!
(The player takes 5 damage and the barrel is destroyed.)
You inspect the cannon...

steps.text: The cannon has not been cleaned out after firing:
The cannon has been fired, but not cleaned with a Ramrod.

The cannon has had powder added.

The cannon has been loaded with ammunition.

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: This cannonball is far too big.
You clean out the cannon.
(The cannon is emptied.)
You fire the cannon at the crew!
If the player hits the enemy:

steps.text: You hit them!
(The enemy takes 52 damage and dies.)

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: If the player misses the enemy:

steps.text: You missed!
Try waiting for there to be pirates in front of the cannon next time you fire!

talking-to-bill-teach-again-before-firin.text: There is no powder in this cannon, you will need to start again.
(The cannon is emptied.)
Looks like you forgot to load it, you will need to start again.
(The cannon is emptied.)

sinking-the-enemy-ship.player: Well, that seems to have showed them Cap'n!

sinking-the-enemy-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship.text: Great! This ordeal will soon be over!

sinking-the-enemy-ship.player: Aye Cap'n, we'll beat these pirates yet!

sinking-the-enemy-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship.text: Now [lad/lass], we'll send them to the bottom of the sea.

sinking-the-enemy-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship.text: Well, ye'll shoot holes in their hull with the cannon.

sinking-the-enemy-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship.text: Essentially ye do what ye just did, but use a cannonball from the gun locker in the hold instead of the canister rounds.

sinking-the-enemy-ship.player: Arr! I'll sink them scurvy dogs!

sinking-the-enemy-ship.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship.text: Give it three tries and see if they sink, that many holes should do it.

sinking-the-enemy-ship-talking-to-bill-t.player: Cap'n, I know I need to load and fire the cannon at the enemy ship...
and I know I do this by adding powder to the cannon, tamping the charge with a ramrod, adding a cannonball, adding some fuse and then lighting it...
And I also remembered your warning about cleaning the barrel after every shot to avoid the cannon exploding...
But I've forgotten how many times I'm supposed to shoot the enemy ship...

sinking-the-enemy-ship-talking-to-bill-t.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship-talking-to-bill-t.text: Three! Three times [lad/lass]! Three! One more than two, one less than four! Got it!

sinking-the-enemy-ship-talking-to-bill-t.player: There is no need to shout...

sinking-the-enemy-ship-returning-to-sink.speaker: Bill Teach
sinking-the-enemy-ship-returning-to-sink.text: Were almost there! Just hole their hull and we'll be able to make it past. Get to it!

sinking-the-enemy-ship-fire-at-will.text: You shoot the cannon ball at the enemy ship!
If the player hits their shot:

steps.text: You put a hole in the hull!

sinking-the-enemy-ship-fire-at-will.text: If the player misses their shot:

steps.text: You fail to damage the hull.

sinking-the-enemy-ship-shooting-at-the-h.text: You shoot the cannon ball at the enemy ship!
You put another hole in the hull!

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Ye've done it [lad/lass]! They're sunk now!

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Let's head to the island!

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Mama
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Bill? You look like you've been to Davey Jones' locker and back.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Oh, Miss La'Fiette, if only I were that lucky.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: My crew deserted and I was stuck with an adventurer mannin' me ship.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: [He/She] was as piratical as a bunch of Dwellberries...

end-of-quest-cutscene.player: I am still here you know...

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Aye [lad/lass], I remember.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Mama
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: I'll leave you two alone.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: All right...

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Ok [player name], yer now a pirate, but...

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: BUT ye can't just go around talking like some pirate in a fancy play.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: No self-respectin' pirate says 'Arr' that much!

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Well, except for Fancy Dan, but that be another story.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Here, have this book. It'll learn ye how to be a pirate.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Or at least learn ye te talk proper like one.

end-of-quest-cutscene.player: So all I have to do is read this book and I'm a pirate?

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Aye...that be all ye need te do.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Ye'll need that book if ye want te trade with some of the pirates round here.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Outsiders tend not te understand them if ye catch me drift.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Anyway, I'd have been shark bait without ye.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: If ye get a moment come see me fer yer share of the loot.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: I'm sure as soon as ye stop yellin' 'Arr!' ye'll make a great pirate.

end-of-quest-cutscene.speaker: Bill Teach
end-of-quest-cutscene.text: Thanks [player name]. If ye need a lift back, just come see me.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

end-of-quest-cutscene-claiming-the-loot-.player: Can I have that gold now?

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-does-not.npc: I bet you're after another lens!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-does-not.player: How could you possibly know that?

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-does-not.npc: Hey, I think I'm learning a thing or two from these Moon Clan ladies.

steps.player: Oi! I need another lens, boy.

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.npc: But you don't have space.

steps.player: Good point.

steps.npc: Huh, oh ok, I suppose I owe you one.

steps.player: I think I'll pass. But thanks..

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-already-.player: So you've plucked up the courage to come and confront that girl!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-already-.npc: That I did, that I did!
She turned out to be really nice! She's joining us to become a pirate!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-already-.player: Really? And you're not sceptical about this? You know, after what she did last time?
Huh? Why are you talking like that?
Like someone else was talking for you. Are you sure she hasn't put a spell on you again? Did she wave a watch in front of your face? You know, tell you to look deep into her eyes?
I think you've been hypnotised. I wonder what happens if I click my fingers?
Oh dear. Oh well, I'm sure you'll learn one day.

steps.npc: Hello there; I see you're qualified. Come to help us out?
Hello! You're that student who recently finished all three Earth Sciences exams, aren't you? Come to help us out?
Greetings, my dear [sir/madam]. Have you come to give us a hand?

options.text: Yes, how can I help out?

steps.player: Yes, how can I help out?

steps.text: If the player doesn't meet of the following criteria: a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory; leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: Well, you'll need to get your equipment first - it's all there on the tool rack. Use what you learned from your Earth Sciences exams. You'll need to be wearing your leather gloves and boots as well as have access to
your trowel, rock pick and specimen brush.

steps.text: If the player has a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory and also have leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: I see you have your equipment - well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.

steps.player: I found something interesting.

steps.npc: Oh? Let's take a look...

steps.text: If the player has a Clean necklace in their inventory:

steps.player: I found this pretty necklace.

steps.npc: Interesting...yes...yes...hmmm.... It looks like it's enchanted.

steps.player: With what?

steps.npc: Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

How do you make lanterns?

steps.npc: Out of glass.  The more advanced lanterns have a metal component as well.
Firstly you can make a simple candle lantern out of glass.  It's just like a candle, but the flame isn't exposed, so it's safer.
Then you can make an oil lamp, which is brighter but has an exposed flame.  But if you make an iron frame for it you can turn it into an oil lantern.
Finally there's the bullseye lantern.  You'll need to make a frame out of steel and add a glass lens.
Once you've made your lamp or lantern, you'll need to make lamp oil for it.  The chemist near Rimmington has a machine for that.
For any light source, you'll need a tinderbox to light it. Keep your tinderbox handy in case it goes out!

options.text: What do I do in the arena?

Ye receive tickets for tagging more than one pillar in a row. So ye won't get a ticket from the first pillar but ye will for every platform ye tag in a row after that.
If ye miss a platform ye will miss out on the next ticket so try and get every platform you can! When ye be done, take the tickets to Jackie over there and she'll exchange them for more stuff!

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Tag when green light means tickets! Tag when red light means green light!

steps.player: Thanks!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello there, I'm Captain Bruce. Do you want to serve in the Shayzien Army and defend our kingdom?

steps.player: Yes, I'd love to join.

steps.npc: Wonderful! To get started, you need to answer a few questions.
Are you a resident of Kourend?

steps.player: Errrr... Not really.

steps.npc: Ah. Then you cannot join I'm afraid.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: It's in the rules I'm afraid. Only citizens of Kourend are allowed to join the Shayzien Army.

steps.player: Is that not too restrictive?

steps.npc: Well at one time only citizens of Shayzien could join the army. It wasn't until the reign of King Byrne I that people from other parts of the kingdom were allowed to enlist.
Of course, many people in Kourend still like to stick to tradition. After all, the five cities of Kourend have always had very defined roles within the kingdom.

steps.player: Interesting. So most people in the army are still from Shayzien?

steps.npc: Indeed. While the Shayzien Army is by far the largest military force in Kourend, the other cities still have some form of militia, apart from Arceuus of course.
Even if someone from elsewhere in the kingdom wants to become a soldier, they're far more likely to join their local city force than come to us.
Still, times are slowly changing. Every year we see more people from outside Shayzien enlist.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: My pleasure.

steps.player: No, I'm not interested.

steps.npc: That's alright. Come back if you change your mind.

steps.player: Sir, yes sir!

steps.npc: Then listen closely.

steps.text: If the player is carrying any disallowed items:

steps.npc: Wait a minute! I'm not giving a tutorial to someone carrying that stuff. Use that bank chest over there first!

steps.text: If the player is carrying food items or a coloured satchel:
You can't enter the game with any food; the Healer will cure you.
If the player is carrying any Barbarian mixes or leaping fish:
You can't enter the game with any brutal potions or ingredients; the Healer will cure you.
If the player is carrying any Phoenix necklaces:
There is no reason to take a phoenix necklace into the arena, as you won't lose any items if you die in the minigame.
If the player is carrying runes or a rune pouch:
You can't enter the game with any runes - there are free ones in there.
If the player is carrying arrows:
You can't take arrows into a game - there are free ones in there.
If the player is carrying a pet:
The barbarians don't want you to take your follower in.
If the player is carrying logs:
You can't take your own logs with you - you have to use the ones the barbarians provide.
If the player is carrying parts of the Dwarven multicannon:
The barbarians don't want you using artillery down there.
If the player is carrying a looting bag:
The barbarians don't trust whatever you may have stored in your looting bag. They won't let you in with it.
If the player is carrying Saradomin brews:
The barbarians don't want you using Saradomin brews down there. You will have to restore your health as they intend.

steps.npc: My ship! The front fell off!

steps.player: The front fell off?

steps.npc: Yes! That's not very typical, I'd like to make that point!

steps.player: Well, how is it untypical?

steps.npc: Well, there are a lot of ships going around the world all the time, and very seldom does anything like this happen!

steps.npc: Because of that meteorologist! He didn't provide the usual weather report and we sailed right into a storm!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello there. What do you need?

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is one of the lairs of those foul Lizardmen. We've managed to corner these ones so they can't escape.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Cleive. Captain Cleive. Captain in the Shayzien Guard and renowned slayer.

steps.player: Renowned?

steps.npc: Absolutely. I'm part of a great family of slayers. You've probably met a few of them over on the mainland.

steps.player: Why are you here?

steps.npc: We learnt of a group of Lizardman Shamans causing trouble on the surface. I led a taskforce out to drive them back into their lair.
We suffered many losses but we've now managed to trap them in this cave.
We've lost too many men to be able to finish them off but I'm happy for someone else to do it if I feel they're worthy of the challenge.

steps.player: Can I fight these Lizardmen?

steps.npc: Perhaps. I've lost too many men to be able to kill them myself but I'm happy for someone else to do it if I feel they're worthy of the challenge.

steps.player: What do you define as worthy?

steps.npc: You'll need to be favoured by the people of Shayzien. You'll also need to be on a Lizardman Slayer task.

at-tempoross-cove.npc: What do you need, adventurer? There is a battle to fight!

steps.player: How do I help?

steps.npc: Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

steps.player: Aye aye!

options.text: What should I watch out for?

steps.player: What should I watch out for?

steps.npc: If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

steps.player: Aye aye!
I want to leave.

steps.npc: Really? You will receive no reward if you do.

options.text: Yes, I really want to leave.
No, I don't want to leave.
I'll get on with the fighting.

steps.player: I'll get on with the fighting.

at-tempoross-cove-after-subduing-temporo.npc: We did it! Tempoross has been sudbued once again. Well done!
Take a well deserved rest but don't get too comfy, it'll regain its energy soon enough!

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.npc: We usually find some debris washed up near the docks back at Unkah. Feel free t' have a look. Ya might find somethin' useful!
It won't be long before Tempoross regains enough energy to be a problem and we'll have to wrangle it again. Hopefully we can count on you to 'elp!

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.npc: Ahoy! I'm Cap'n Pudi, currently assisting the Spirit Anglers in their effort against Tempoross.

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.player: Tempoross? Spirit Anglers? Who are they?

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.npc: You 'aven't heard?! The freak storms? Sailors running into trouble? Ye really must be a landlubber!
Tempoross is some kind o' great sea spirit that's been spookin' sailors and causing crazy storms!
Taiman and his crew were one of the first t' run into it. Washed up outside Al Kharid amongst piles of debris, they did. 'Tis a troublin' time to be a cap'n!

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.player: Oh that doesn't sound good at all!

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.npc: It isn't, but worry not. The Spirit Anglers 'ave been formed t' tackle this beastie! We're recruiting all skilled sailors and fisherfolk t' help us.

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.text: If the player does not have the required Fishing level:

steps.npc: Are you sure? It's pretty rough out there and you look like you could do with more experience.

steps.text: You need a Fishing level of 35 to fight Tempoross.

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has the required Fishing level:

steps.npc: Excellent!
The ships on the dock regularly embark to Tempoross Cove. Once there, you'll need to keep the cannons loaded with Harpoonfish t' weaken the Spirit. You can fish 'em on the island.
When Tempoross submerges, get up close and clear the fish from its whirlpools; they're how it gets its energy.

steps.player: Well, that sounds easy enough!

steps.npc: Aye, that be the easy part!
The storm of Tempoross will rage around you, so you better be ready to deal with lightning strikes and avoid getting zapped when Tempoross attacks the cannons.
Also, watch out for those mighty waves! You'll want t' tether yourself t' something solid so you don't find yourself lost in the deep blue when they come crashing down!

steps.player: Oh... Well, I suppose I can do that.
Will I need any special equipment?

steps.npc: Everythin' you need can be found on-board. Though if you have a favourite harpoon, you can always bring that!
The complete Spirit Anglers outfit also has an 'andy harness built-in, so you won't need a rope if you're wearin' it. You can speak t' Gita about getting one.
Ye can find Gita just east of 'ere, next t' some fishin' equipment.
When you're ready, just board the ship and we'll set sail soon!

steps.player: Aye aye cap'n!

options.text: Are there any benefits to helping the Spirit Anglers?

steps.player: Are there any benefits to helping the Spirit Anglers?

steps.speaker: Captain Pudi:
steps.text: Other than maintainin' safe passage and savin' lives?!

steps.player: Well...

steps.text: The captain laughs.

steps.npc: I'm just messin' with ye! Of course there are benefits!
We find all sorts washed up by the storms. Aside from the usual junk, we often find old chests from merchant supply ships, as well as the odd artefact here and there.
If it's not needed for the Spirit Anglers' research, it's yours to keep!
Some of the more resourceful Spirit Anglers also discovered a fishing use for the spirit energised scales shed by the fish within Tempoross. You're free t' keep any you find.

options.text: Can you remind me what to do on the island?

steps.player: Can you remind me what to do on the island?

steps.npc: The ships on the dock regularly embark to Tempoross Cove. Once there, you'll need to keep the cannons loaded with Harpoonfish t' weaken the Spirit. You can fish 'em on the island.

options.text: Are there any benefits to helping the Spirit Anglers?
Can you tell me more about the Spirit Anglers?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Spirit Anglers?

steps.npc: Well, as I mentioned before, Taiman and his fishing crew from Al Kharid 'ad a tussle with Tempoross. They barely made it back.
I was sitting down by the shore enjoying one of Karim's kebabs at the time, when suddenly the crew washed up amongst a pile of debris. Looked like they'd just seen a ghost!
As soon as they could talk sense they went to the Chancellor and within days more shockin' tales of the Sea Spirit's wrath came in.
The Chancellor called a meeting for all us local seafarin' folk and we agreed action must be taken!
Ain't nothin' goin' t' take the seas from me, even if it is a powerful spirit!
Anyway, it was decided that we'd setup a base 'ere amongst these ruins, and so the Spirit Anglers was formed!
Don't ask me what the ruins used to be. And it's not like Menaphos can 'ave a say!
Whatever they are, they make a fine base for the Spirit Anglers!
Since moving in, we've been recruiting fisherfolk from all over, and some of the readin' types 'ave been studyin' Tempoross durin' our trips to subdue it.
I like t' get stuck in, me-self; face off toe t' toe with the beastie. I'll be right by your side when you go out there!

steps.player: Well that's encouraging, I think...

steps.npc: I'm still 'ere, ain't I?
Anyway, there's plenty o' research going on, so maybe you can find some notes lyin' around if ye want to know more.

options.text: Can you remind me what to do on the island?
Are there any benefits to helping the Spirit Anglers?

steps.player: Goodbye.

at-tempoross-cove.npc: What do you need, adventurer? There is a battle to fight!

steps.player: How do I help?

steps.npc: Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

steps.player: Aye aye!

options.text: What should I watch out for?

steps.player: What should I watch out for?

steps.npc: If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

steps.player: Aye aye!
I want to leave.

steps.npc: Really? You will receive no reward if you do.

options.text: Yes, I really want to leave.

steps.player: Yes, I really want to leave.

at-tempoross-cove-after-subduing-temporo.npc: We did it! Tempoross has been sudbued once again. Well done!
Take a well deserved rest but don't get too comfy, it'll regain its energy soon enough!

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.npc: We usually find some debris washed up near the docks back at Unkah. Feel free t' have a look. Ya might find somethin' useful!
It won't be long before Tempoross regains enough energy to be a problem and we'll have to wrangle it again. Hopefully we can count on you to 'elp!

steps.player: I'm ready to leave.

standard-dialogue.npc: Beyond this wall you'll find the Kebos Lowlands. Most of the region is lizardman territory. We're here to keep them from entering Kourend.
We used to keep this passage properly barricaded shut, but then the fancy historians from the Arceuus Library wanted to go do some research out there.
Soon the farmers joined them, and before you knew it, everyone wanted to go explore. Some of them have even started living out there.
I can see it all ending badly, but that's the problem with intellectuals - they always think they know better.
Anyway, maybe they'll all get themselves killed. Then we can put the barricade back up.
If you go out there yourself, give the lizardmen a kicking from me. They've killed too many of my soldiers.

On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

steps.player: Nothing.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

steps.player: Hello there!

steps.npc: Hello! You're not from around here, are you? It's exciting to see that even people from outside of Varlamore are looking to join the Emissaries!

steps.player: Well after I heard about all the good work they were doing, I could hardly say no! What about you? What made you want to join them?

steps.npc: Well it's our duty of course! The Church of Ralos has become lost, but the Emissaries know the truth. Ximoua will not come to be unless we make it so!

steps.player: So you're quite eager to see the end of the world then?

steps.npc: End? Ximoua is no end! It is the beginning! We will all come together as one and bring about a new world! I can't wait!

steps.player: Well I'm glad to see you're so excited. Good luck with the tests.

steps.npc: And you!

steps.player: What ales are you serving?

steps.npc: We serve Crombwick's finest Bloody Bracer, that is all.

steps.player: Sounds rough, how much?

steps.npc: 99 of you finest coins.

options.text: Alright, one Bloody Bracer, if that's all you have.

steps.player: Alright, one Bloody Bracer, if that's all you have.

steps.text: If the player has less than 99 coins:

steps.npc: I said 99 coins! You haven't got 99 coins!

steps.player: Sorry, I'll come back another day.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99 coins:

steps.player: Thanks, Carl.
99 coins? That's ridiculous!

steps.npc: What can I say? The ingredients are locally sourced so it's high quality, I promise.

steps.player: Well, I guess I shouldn't shoot the messenger.

steps.npc: So...

options.text: What can you tell me about this town?

steps.player: What can you tell me about this town?

steps.npc: I've not been here long myself, so I'm afraid I may not be of much help.

steps.player: What happened to the previous barkeep?

steps.npc: Oh, he had to leave.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: Scared of turning.

steps.player: Turning?

steps.npc: Yes, into a sleeper.

steps.player: Oh right! You see, for a second there I thought you were talking about vampyres.

steps.npc: Ha ha! We, err, don't see many of those types around here. No, no, not at all.

steps.player: If you say so.

steps.npc: I do. So...

steps.player: Actually, I'm no longer thirsty.

steps.npc: Oh, the red thirst will be upon you soon.

steps.player: Excuse me?

steps.npc: Just a jest, traveller.

steps.player: Oh.

standard-dialogue-before-song-of-the-elv.npc: My son fell ill with the plague...
It would be easier to cope with if I could have spent his last few days with him.
Those mourners came and whisked him away. He didn't even seem that ill, I thought it was a common cold... But the mourners said that he was infected and had to be taken away.
Two days later the mourners returned and told me he had died.

standard-dialogue-before-song-of-the-elv.player: Again, I'm sorry. Life can be harsh.

options.text: Where did the plague come from?

steps.player: Where did the plague come from?

steps.npc: It's down to King Tyras. He and his men brought the plague here from the west, and then left us to suffer. One day he'll pay for what he's done!

options.text: Have there been many victims of the plague?

steps.player: Have there been many victims of the plague?

steps.npc: You could say that... I've heard reports that half of West Ardougne is infected! Many have lost friends and family...

steps.player: It sounds an awful way to live.

steps.npc: People are very depressed and scared. I've never met anyone fully infected though. I suppose we should be grateful to the mourners for that.

options.text: I hope things get easier for you.

steps.player: I hope things get easier for you.

steps.npc: Me too...

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.player: Hey Carla, how are you doing?

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.npc: I'm okay. The loss of my son is something that I'll never be over. At least no one else has to suffer at the hands of those mourners though.

standard-dialogue-after-murder-mystery.npc: Apparently you aren't as stupid as you look.

before-sea-slug.npc: Is there any chance you could help me?
It's my husband, he works on a fishing platform. Once a month he takes our son, Kennith, out with him.
They usually write to me regularly, but I've heard nothing all week. It's very strange.
Maybe, but no-one's heard from the other fishermen on the platform. Their families are becoming quite concerned.
Is there any chance you could visit the platform and find out what's going on?

steps.player: I suppose so, how do I get there?

steps.npc: That's very good of you [player name]. My friend Holgart will take you there.

steps.player: Ok, I'll go and see if they're ok.

steps.npc: I'll reward you for your time. It'll give me peace of mind to know Kennith and my husband, Kent, are safe.

steps.player: I'm sorry, I'm too busy.

steps.npc: That's a shame.

steps.player: Bye.

steps.npc: Bye.

after-sea-slug.npc: I'm good. Busy as always looking after Kent and Kennith but no complaints.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-icthla.player: Hey there. How're you holding up?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-icthla.npc: Not too bad. Still, I hope we can get rid of these spots soon.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-contac.player: Hey there. How're you holding up?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-contac.npc: Not too bad. Still, I hope we can get rid of these spots soon.
The embalmer has been importing a soothing balm from a merchant called Ali M. It's meant to stop the itching.
Not even remotely, but it sure does keep the flies away.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-beneat.player: Hey there. How're you holding up?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-beneat.npc: Much better now that we've finally got rid of those spots.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-beneat.player: That's great to hear! All the best.

using-a-potion-on-him.npc: What? You intolerable, insufferable idiot. That won't work! I would say get out of my sight but that's not far enough away!

using-a-potion-on-him.player: I was just trying to help.

using-a-potion-on-him.npc: Clear off before I give you something to feel sorry about!

standard-dialogue.npc: Greetings! I'm Cassim. Welcome to my home.

options.text: That's a big barrel of wine!

steps.player: That's a big barrel of wine!

steps.npc: Isn't it just! I'm a bit of a connoisseur.

steps.player: Do you make it yourself?

steps.npc: I've dabbled, but this is all imported. I have a connection in the far west who has the best vineyards.

steps.player: In the west?

steps.npc: Yes! A fine Hosidius grape, strong hints of plum and blackberry, very sweet.

steps.player: Sounds lovely!

options.condition: After talking to Ali the Tea Seller:

steps.player: How's the tea here?

steps.npc: It's fantastic! Ali really knows how to brew a fine tea!

steps.player: Which is your favourite?

steps.npc: Well I've supplied him with a small import of mine. I call the concoction 'Zamorak's Fire'.

steps.player: Sounds hot!

steps.npc: Yes, yes. It has a certain kick to it! Although, it'll keep you safe from fire for a short time after drinking!
Great for when dragons attack!

steps.player: Does that happen often here?

steps.npc: You never know... Dragons can be sneaky.

steps.player: I'd best be off.

steps.npc: May the flames of Zamorak light your path.

steps.player: Er... yeah...

standard-dialogue-subsequent-dialogue.npc: Welcome back.

options.text: That's a big barrel of wine!

options.condition: After talking to Ali the Tea Seller:

rescuing-the-castaway-man.npc: Oh, Saradomin's light! Rescue at last!

rescuing-the-castaway-man.player: Quick, climb aboard! We'll get you to solid ground.

rescuing-the-castaway-man.text: You help the castaway climb aboard.

rescuing-the-castaway-woman.npc: Oh, Saradomin's light! Rescue at last!

rescuing-the-castaway-woman.player: Quick, climb aboard! We'll get you to solid ground.

rescuing-the-castaway-woman.text: You help the castaway climb aboard.

rescuing-the-castaway-wilson.player: Quick, climb aboard! We'll get you to solid ground.

rescuing-the-castaway-dog.player: Quick, climb aboard! We'll get you to solid ground.

rescuing-the-castaway-dog.text: You help the castaway climb aboard.

talking-to-the-castaway-on-the-boat-wils.player: Don't worry, friend. I can get you back to dry land.

talking-to-the-castaway-on-the-boat-dog.player: There, there, buddy. We'll get you to a port!

dropping-the-castaway-off-man.npc: Thank you! And to think, this day could have been my last...

dropping-the-castaway-off-man.text: The castaway hurries off, with a new appreciation for life.

dropping-the-castaway-off-woman.npc: Thank you! And to think, this day could have been my last...

dropping-the-castaway-off-woman.text: The castaway hurries off, with a new appreciation for life.

dropping-the-castaway-off-wilson.text: The ball seems to be grateful at being returned to dry land.

dropping-the-castaway-off-dog.text: The dog jumps at you, licks your face, and scampers away.

P1pnMx.npc: You've saved my life! I thought I was done for...

P1pnMx.player: Well, I wasn't just going to sail on by! When I get the chance, I'll drop you off at a port.

when-petted-without-a-catspeak-amulet-eq.text: The cat softly purrs between snores.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: It's a desolate, sad place... The peoples here seldom feed me - take me with you!

steps.player: I'm sorry, I can't take you with me, but I will help if I can.
How are you doing?

steps.npc: Not well, I have to ssssssay, but you look healthy. I wish I were healthy like you.

steps.player: What's that awful smell?

steps.npc: Sniff, sniff* I don't think it's me. All I can smell is dirty vyrewatches tithing the poor humans.

options.text: How long have you been here?

steps.player: How long have you been here?

steps.npc: As long as I can remember. So far we've not found any way out of this place, and after all, we couldn't leave these poor humans to fend for themselves.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Hello there.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: All this work they're doing to fix this place up and they still barely feed me anything! It's an outrage!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: There's plenty of rats around. Maybe you could help out with the work by getting rid of a few.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hmm... Yes, very well.

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-amulet.text: If the player has no tuna in their inventory:

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Hmmmph.

standard-dialogue-with-catspeak-amulet.text: If the player does have tuna in their inventory:

steps.player: Why yes I do have some tuna.

steps.npc: Give! *purr*

options.text: Give a tuna to the cat.

steps.text: You give some tuna to the cat. It devours it and purrs loudly.

steps.npc: Catch toad for me.

steps.player: What? I think not...
Nah... my tuna.

steps.npc: Hissss...
Hey look it's the hero! It's great to have you around.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: The Great Guardian wants you to know that there has been a development in our fight against the Abyss.
A magical signal has been detected emerging from the rift. It is not of the Abyss.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.player: Hmm... I was actually hoping to enter the Scar myself. Perhaps I could investigate this signal while I'm in there.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: Nothing can survive the Scar. To enter would not be wise.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.player: But how do you know nothing can survive? Has anyone actually confirmed that?

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: There are a few who have entered the Scar in the past. None have returned.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.player: Well then give me a chance to be the first.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: If you wish to enter, it is not our place to stop you. In the likely event of your demise, you will be mourned.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.player: Thanks... I think. Anything I should know before entering?

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: The rift is unpredictable. Normally, you would not be able to control its destination. However, the magical signal coming from within could be of benefit. It could act as a guide.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.player: So you'd be able to send me right to the source?
Well I suppose that's the best I can ask for.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: Are you ready to enter the Scar?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Then may your death come quick, human. Good luck.

steps.text: Player is transported to the Scar.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Then speak to me once you are.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.npc: How unexpected. The Great Guardian will need to be informed.
In the meantime, do you wish to return to the Scar?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Very well. Good luck.

steps.text: Player is transported to the Scar.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Speak to me again if you do.

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-de.npc: Do you wish to return to the Scar?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Very well. Good luck.

steps.text: Player is transported to the Scar.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Speak to me again if you do.

before-starting-fallen-from-grace-or-aft.text: Catriona refuses to look at you.

after-completing-fallen-from-grace.npc: I hear you found Keenan. Shame about what happened, but not surprising. Hopefully this is the last time that sort of thing happens.
I suppose time will tell if you're right.

steps.npc: How can you see properly with such tiny little eyes?
Ooh! Are you [player name]?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Everyone's talking about how you helped Zanik save the city! You're a hero!
Have you visited the market? There are visitors selling foods from all over the surface there. It's so exotic!
Well, I suppose it wouldn't be exotic for you, since you're from the surface.
But you should check it out anyway. Maybe you could sell some of your food. Everyone's crazy about surface food at the moment.
So, what do you think of our city, surface-dweller?

steps.player: I like it!

steps.npc: That, surface-dweller, was the right answer.

steps.player: I think it's rubbish.

steps.npc: Well, it beats crawling around on the surface with nothing above your head!
What's it like on the surface? It sounds scary to me, having nothing above my head.

steps.player: It's alright.

steps.npc: I'm still not sure it would be for me, though.

steps.player: It's not all that great.

steps.npc: Never mind, you can stay down here now!
What do you think you're doing?

steps.text: Stuns the player, dealing 1 damage.

steps.npc: Help! A thief!

steps.text: Stuns the player, dealing 1 damage.

options.text: I'm not going to hurt you.

steps.player: I'm not going to hurt you.

options.text: I'm going to slay you all, you evil goblins!

steps.player: I'm going to slay you all, you evil goblins!

steps.text: Any nearby cave goblins will run away and say one of the following phrases:

steps.npc: Help!
Don't hurt us!
Nooo!
Eeek!
Don't tread on my feet!

steps.player: I'm not going to tread on your feet.

steps.npc: Beware of swamp gas! Look out for the warning marks!

steps.player: Um, thanks.
Hello, how are you?

steps.npc: I'm a bit worried about the increase of humans these days.
Present company excluded, of course!
Nice weather we're having!

steps.player: But you live underground. The weather is always the same!

steps.npc: Yes, it's always nice!
Where did you come from?

steps.player: From above ground.

steps.npc: Above ground? Where is that?

steps.player: You know, out of the caves, in the open air, with sunshine and wide open spaces!

steps.npc: Ick.  Sounds horrible.

options.condition: If The Lost Tribe has been completed:

steps.npc: You're the human who secured peace between the Dorgeshuun and Lumbridge, aren't you?

steps.player: Um, yes.

steps.npc: Thank you so much! I was worried it was a return to the times of war, but perhaps surface-dwellers are not so bad.

options.condition: When carrying a lit, open light source:

steps.npc: Watch out! You don't want to let a naked flame near swamp gas! Look out for the warning marks.

options.condition: When carrying light sources with a combined light level of 2 or more:

steps.npc: Don't shine that thing in my eyes!

options.condition: If not carrying a lit light source:

steps.npc: What are you doing down here without a lamp?
Here, I have a spare torch.

steps.text: a Lit torch

steps.npc: But be careful not to let it near swamp gas! Watch out for the warning marks.

steps.player: Er, thanks a lot.

steps.npc: You're welcome.

options.condition: If not carrying a tinderbox:

steps.npc: You haven't got a tinderbox! What if your light goes out?
Here, I have a spare.

steps.text: a Tinderbox

steps.player: Thanks.

unknown-condition.npc: Oh no! The surface-dwellers are coming to kill us all!

unknown-condition.text: The cave goblins are too scared to talk to you.
The goblin retreats away from the player

steps.npc: Oh dear, oh dear. I hope this dwarf train works properly!
Look, everyone! It's [player name]!
Everyone's talking about how you rescued Zanik! You're the city's hero again!
Visiting Keldagrim is so exciting! I never thought I'd be so far from Dorgesh-Kaan in my life!
These dwarves have so much more advanced technology than us. Look at this train! We could never build something like this.
Keldagrim's very nice to visit, but I don't think I'd want to live there.
Shh! Don't tell anyone!

steps.player: Don't tell anyone what?

steps.npc: SHHH!
Are you [player name]? Did you help Zanik save the city?

steps.player: Yes, that was me!

steps.npc: When I'm older I'm going to be an adventurer, just like Zanik!
Are you a surface-dweller?

steps.player: Yes...

steps.npc: Haha! You look funny! All tall and skinny with tiny eyes!
Help! Help! The surface people are attacking!

steps.player: It's alright, I'm friendly!

steps.npc: Sorry, I'm not meant to talk to strangers.

before-the-lost-tribe.npc: Surface-dweller! You should leave the mines now!

before-the-lost-tribe-attempting-to-ente.npc: Surface-dweller! You may not pass through that door!

steps.npc: Have a nice day!
I'm keeping an eye on you, surface-dweller.
Surface-dweller! You will never find your way into the city of Dorgesh-Kaan!

steps.player: Isn't it through that big door?

steps.npc: Well, yes, but you'll never find your way in!
Have a nice day!
I'm keeping an eye on you, surface-dweller.
Surface-dweller! You will never find your way into the city of Dorgesh-Kaan!

steps.player: But I thought I was allowed into the city now.

steps.npc: Oh yes, so you are. I'd better say something different.
Ahem*
Surface-dweller! You will easily find your way into the city of Dorgesh-Kaan!
How about that?

steps.player: Yes, that's much more appropiate.
How's the mining going?

steps.npc: I nearly got caught in a rockfall earlier!
Still, since humans started coming down here, the proportion of miners killed in rockfalls has fallen dramatically!
Oh, you know, can't complain.
It's going well. I find repeatedly hitting a piece of rock very therapeutic.
Well, don't tell Mistag...
...but actually I wasn't working very hard!
We're a bit behind schedule. If you lent us a hand, Mistag would pay you for your work.

options.text: Where do you take all this ore?

steps.player: Where do you take all this ore?

steps.npc: To the town of Dorgesh-Kaan, deep in the caves.

options.text: Why do you use bones to build with?

steps.player: Why do you use bones to build with?

steps.npc: Well, our legends say that on the surface there was a substance called 'wood', which grew out of the ground in towers.
But we cannot get wood here, so we can only build with stone, bone, and iron.

steps.player: Oh, right.
Giant frogs aren't fearsome!

steps.npc: Perhaps not for a mighty adventurer like you, but we think they're terrifying!

standard-dialogue.npc: Be careful going in there! You are unarmed, and there is much evilness lurking down there! The evilness seems to block off our contact with our gods,
so our prayers seem to have less effect down there. Oh, also, you won't be able to come back this way - This ladder only goes one way!
The only exit from the caves below is a portal which leads only to the deepest wilderness!

options.text: I don't think I'm strong enough to enter then.

steps.player: I don't think I'm strong enough to enter then.

options.text: Well that is a risk I will have to take.

standard-dialogue-without-witchwood-icon.npc: Be ye mad? There be Horrors in this cave!
Have ye ever heard of the sort of evil, flesh-eatin' horrors that dwell in the darkest pits of the world?
The sort of dark, sanity-breakin' THINGS that cause the livin' to drop to their knees and weep for the fate of all creation?

standard-dialogue-without-witchwood-icon.player: Yes, I think I've killed a few of them as well.

standard-dialogue-without-witchwood-icon.npc: But, ye'll need a Witchwood Icon from a slayer master if ye want te go in these caves and live.
Well, ye see them Jungle Horrors? Well down in the caves there be Cave Horrors.
They are bigger, badder, meaner, and have a howl that freezes the blood in yer veins.
Wearin' earmuffs or a helmet won't work, cos them masks they wear make the sound magical. Only thing that works is wearin' a Witchwood Icon.
That is, o'course, if ye can see them, cos if ye don't have any light down there then yer likely te be picked te bones by the insects before the Horrors get ye.

standard-dialogue-without-witchwood-icon.player: I see, thanks for the warning.

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-in.npc: Be ye some form of simpleton? Do ye not hear the howlin' of the Horrors?

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-in.player: Well, I can hear something now you mention it...

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-in.npc: That be them, howlin', always howlin'!
If ye value yer limbs ye'll put that Icon round yer neck, and hope they don't come out into the light!

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-in.player: Err, all right, I'll get right on that.

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-eq.npc: Be ye here te deal with the Horrors?

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-eq.player: I might well give it a shot.

standard-dialogue-with-witchwood-icon-eq.npc: Aye, well, keep yer Icon with ye if ye wants te walk out alive again.

We're exploring this island.

steps.npc: All right, [lad/lass], since yer so insistent, I'll tell ye.
See, I was clingin' onto a barrel, me ship havin' just had an encounter with this albatross.
The sea was thrashin' and wild, but not so wild that I didn't see the fins of some sharks closin' in on me.
I managed to yank a sliver of wood from the barrel just as one of them grabbed me from below, but I slipped down the things throat by about two feet before I managed te kill it.

steps.player: How did you survive?

steps.npc: A passin' ship saw the sharks and knew there would be survivors in the water. They sent a longboat and picked me up, but not before the sharks had taken off my legs.

steps.npc: Actually, now that you come to mention it, you might be able to help me.
A few weeks ago we had a delivery of a northern ferret. They're funny little creatures. Turns out they're tricksy little blighters too.
Whilst we were unloading him from the cart he managed to escape his cage. What's more he gave the driver a nasty nip on the way out too.
This was obviously a bit of a blow, you can't make a new attraction without any animals.
We got in contact with one of our associates, a huntsman called Nickolaus, who agreed to capture us another.
Funny thing is we haven't heard from him for some time now. I don't suppose you'd mind having a look for him?

options.text: Sure. Any idea where I should start looking?

steps.npc: Well the northern ferret is mostly found around the mountains just west of the Gnome Stronghold, so that would probably be as good a place as any to start looking.
