How do I go about charting the sea?

steps.player: How do I go about charting the sea?

steps.npc: Well, that very much depends. You see, when it comes to charting, there are quite a few different things you'll want to track. What you need to do is going to vary depending on what it is you're tracking.
That said, the starting point is always going to be your captain's log. I actually helped author the standard log that we give out around the Pandemonium.
I made sure to include some big hints in there about the things you might find on your sailing adventures.

steps.text: You get the distinct impression you were just winked at by a blindfolded eye.

steps.player: You say there are a few different things I might want to track. What are they?

steps.npc: Well, you have both big and small points of interest, water currents, sea depths, weather patterns, and then there's also drink crates. They're a curious one that Steve likes people to track.

options.text: Can you tell me about charting smaller points of interest?

steps.player: Can you tell me about charting smaller points of interest?

steps.npc: Well, you'll likely spot some interesting things in the sea and on some of the less explored islands that you find whilst out sailing.
Charting these things is simple. All you need to do is just make a note of them as you find them!

steps.text: Many points of interest don't require any tools to chart. Just interact with them from your boat or while on foot when close enough to them.

options.text: Can you tell me about charting larger points of interest?

steps.player: Can you tell me about charting larger points of interest?

steps.npc: Ah, for them, you'll want to find a good spot and use a spyglass to take it all in.

steps.player: But how do I know where a good spot is?

steps.npc: That can take a bit of practice, but if you pay close attention, you might find some very subtle, definitely not obvious signs of where the best places are...

steps.text: The spyglass can be used to chart larger points of interest. You can do so either from your boat or while on foot. Keep an eye out for the sparkly white circles that show where a spyglass can be used.

options.text: Can you tell me about drink crates?

steps.player: Can you tell me about drink crates?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Prying Times:

steps.npc: They're a bit of an interesting one. It's been argued that they're not actually completely essential for charting the sea, but Steve thinks otherwise. Probably best you talk to him if you want to know more.

steps.text: You need to complete the Prying Times quest to learn about drink crates.
If the player has completed Prying Times:

steps.npc: They're a bit of an interesting one. On your travels, you may spot some sealed crates floating in the sea.
Once you find one, just pry it open with your crowbar. If you're lucky, there will be a refreshing beverage inside for you to try.
Be careful though, as some of them can be a tinge on the ripe side...

steps.player: I must admit, I'm not totally sure what these crates have to do with charting...

steps.npc: Yes, that opinion has come up before. However, according to Steve, it's an unwritten rule in this world that alcohol is the key to solving all problems.
It's also been said that these crates add a bit of much needed danger to the whole charting effort.

steps.player: I see...

steps.text: Floating crates of drink can be found at sea and pried open with a crowbar. Once open, you can sample what you find inside. However, take care, for expired alcohol can be dangerous...

options.text: Can you tell me about tracking currents?

steps.player: Can you tell me about tracking currents?

steps.npc: Absolutely! Understanding the various currents around the seas is essential. As you sail around, you'll likely spot many currents of potential interest.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Current Affairs:

steps.player: But once I spot them, how do I track them?

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need the right tool. Well, I suppose in this case, it's less of a tool and more of a friend.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: To track them, you'll need to make use of your good friend, the current duck! Specifically, once you've found some currents you want to track, you'll want to let your current duck head out for a swim.

steps.player: Is this really the standard way of doing this?

steps.npc: Of course! I simply can't think of any alternatives!

steps.text: A current duck can be used to track currents. To do so, find an area of circularly expanding currents and release your duck there. Then just follow the duck with your boat and collect it again once it stops.

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need to go diving. Doing so will let you take a record of the sea depth, but it's also great for learning more about the local underwater flora and fauna.

steps.player: A puzzle?

steps.npc: Indeed, so get your thinking cap on... under your diving gear of course. It's very important you don't forget that.

steps.text: To check sea depths, you'll need to find a mermaid in the ocean, don some diving gear and then answer her puzzle. She'll then guide you down to the bottom of the sea for you to document your findings.

steps.text: If the player does not have 57 Sailing:

steps.npc: Well, all good captains need to have a strong understanding of the weather out at sea. However, it requires a fair bit of skill to do it well. I'd suggest you wait until you're more experienced.

steps.text: You require 57 Sailing to learn about tracking weather patterns.
If the player has 57 Sailing:

steps.npc: Of course! All good captains need to have a strong understanding of the weather out at sea. However, to do it well, you'll probably want to enlist the help of a meteorologist.

steps.player: Where can I find one of those?

steps.npc: Well, it's a bit of an odd one, but I've been told there's a troll who has started working as one recently.

steps.player: A troll?

steps.npc: Indeed. It's a bit unusual, but who am I to judge! Anyway, apparently she's aquired a portable weather station, a very fine piece of equipment for measuring weather data.
If you come across this troll, she'll hopefully allow you to use this weather station for yourself.

steps.player: And how is it used?

steps.npc: Well, what you'll find is that the wind typically blows in large circles. What you need to do is find the middle of this circle, or the eye as we often call it.

You can use the weather station to work out the wind direction. If you follow it for a bit, you should be able to work out which way the circle is curving, and from that, you should be able to find the eye.
Just remember not to keep following the wind forever, or you'll just keep going around in circles!
Anyway, once you reach the eye, you can use the weather station to take the readings you need. After that, just make sure to return the weather station to the troll.

steps.text: To track weather patterns, you'll need to find the troll meteorologist, take her portable weather station and use it to find the eye of a circular wind storm. Once there, you can use the weather station to record your data.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Mother says I shouldn't speak with strangers.

steps.player: Fair enough.
Hello there. How's it going?

steps.npc: I don't know you.
I don't want to talk to you.
I shouldn't be talking to you.
I shouldn't speak with strangers.
I'm not allowed to talk to strangers.

delegation-talking-to-noah-or-alina.speaker: Alina
delegation-talking-to-noah-or-alina.text: Yes! They call it Varlamore, the Shining Kingdom! It's meant to be one of the most beautiful places in the world!
If the player is on a free-to-play world:

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Oh, nothing you need to worry about.

delegation-talking-to-noah-or-alina.text: If the player is on a member's world:

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Oh, hello! Are you here to see the delegation?

steps.player: Delegation?

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: See! It's not just me who doesn't know what's happening.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: The delegation from Varlamore, of course! After all these years, they're finally opening up the kingdom for travel and trade! Isn't it exciting?

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: Why would I be excited about a place I never even knew existed?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: A whole land locked off for hundreds of years! Do you not want to be one of the first outsiders to step foot there? Think of the adventure!

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: Adventure? Sounds dangerous. I'll be staying right here, thank you very much!

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Bah! Boring! What about you, stranger?

steps.prompt: Start the Children of the Sun quest?

steps.player: Well I'm actually something of an adventurer myself.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: That's the spirit! I bet you'll want to be one of the first to head over to Varlamore!

options.text: What can you tell me about Varlamore?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: It's far across the western sea, over the mountains south of Great Kourend. Between the sea and the mountains, it's totally isolated! No one is allowed to come or go without good reason.

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: Sounds like a prison.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Quite the opposite! It's a beautiful and prosperous kingdom, ruled over by the Sun Queen!

steps.player: The Sun Queen?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Yes! She rules from her palace in their capital, Civitas illa Fortis. The sun plays an important role in Varlamorian life. In fact, they worship it!

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: What... the sun?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: That's right! They have their own religion over there dedicated to the sun and the moon. Isn't that fascinating?

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: I don't know... It all sounds a bit odd to me.

options.text: How come you know so much about Varlamore?

steps.player: How come you know so much about Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: A while back, a group of travellers came through here, on their way to the dark lands of Morytania. They said they were from the College of Bards!

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: College of Bards?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Yes! It's found in the floating city of Tempestus! Members of the College are some of the only people allowed to travel to and from Varlamore.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: They stayed the night in the Blue Moon Inn and spent hours telling us all about their homeland. I've been dying to visit ever since!

steps.player: When will this delegation arrive?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Well it should be any time now!

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: Hang on... what's going on over there?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Wait! That's them! They're here!

The scene begins with King Roald, Aeonisig Raispher, and two Varrock guards standing beside the square fountain. On the far side, the delegation can be seen approaching the king, which consists of Prince Itzla Arkan, Servius, Teokan of Ralos, Furia Tullus, Ennius Tullus, and six Knights of Varlamore.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: There they are: The children of the sun! That's Itzla Arkan, heir to the throne of Varlamore! And there's Servius, the Teokan of Ralos!

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: Teokan? What's a Teokan?

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: It means High Priest. He's the religious leader in Varlamore.

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: Huh...
A guard with a big bag walks out of Varrock Castle.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: What are you doing with that bag?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh... Er... Just delivering some supplies to the guards at the gates.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: Well hurry back. We need everyone at their posts.
The guard walks past Alina, Noah, and the player.

steps.speaker: Noah
steps.text: That's an unusually big bag he's carrying.

steps.player: Hmm... Now where might you be going with that...?

steps.text: (Player begins tailing the guard.)

options.text: Sorry, but I need to head off.

steps.player: Sorry, but I need to head off.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Fair enough.

steps.player: I'm not sure. Doesn't really sound like my kind of thing.

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Well... suit yourself, I guess.

delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.speaker: Alina
delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.text: A whole land locked off for hundreds of years! Do you not want to be one of the first outsiders to step foot there? Think of the adventure!

delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.speaker: Noah
delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.text: Adventure? Sounds dangerous. I'll be staying right here, thank you very much!

delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.speaker: Alina
delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.text: Bah! Boring! What about you, stranger?

delegation-subsequent-dialogues-before-s.prompt: Start the Children of the Sun quest?

delegation-subsequent-dialogues-after-st.text: If the player is on a free-to-play world:

steps.speaker: [Noah/Alina]
steps.text: Sorry, I can't stop to talk right now.

delegation-subsequent-dialogues-after-st.text: If the player is on a member's world:

steps.speaker: Alina
steps.text: Hello again! So what do you think? Reckon you'll be one of the first to head over to Varlamore?

options.text: What can you tell me about Varlamore?
How come you know so much about Varlamore?
Sorry, but I need to head off.

investigation-tailing-the-guard.text: If the player is spotted by the guard:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Hey! What are you doing?
You failed to stay hidden from the guard.

investigation-tailing-the-guard.text: If the player is too far from the guard:

steps.text: You failed to stay close enough to the guard.

investigation-talking-to-noah-or-alina-a.speaker: Noah
investigation-talking-to-noah-or-alina-a.text: That was quite a large bag that guard was carrying. I wonder where he's taking it...

investigation-successfully-following-the.text: A cutscene begins. The player listens in on four bandits and the guard from a window outside the building.

investigation-successfully-following-the.player: What are you up to in there...?

investigation-successfully-following-the.speaker: Guard
investigation-successfully-following-the.text: I'm here aren't I? If you're not happy, maybe you should have been the one to steal the uniforms!

investigation-successfully-following-the.speaker: Bandit (woman)
investigation-successfully-following-the.text: Enough! We don't have much time. Do you have everything?

investigation-successfully-following-the.speaker: Bandit (bearded)
investigation-successfully-following-the.text: We're just going to have to make do. The delegation is already in the palace. We need to be ready to strike as they leave.

investigation-successfully-following-the.speaker: Bandit (tanned)
investigation-successfully-following-the.text: Indeed. You all know the target. Get changed quick and be ready to take your positions.

investigation-successfully-following-the.speaker: Guard
investigation-successfully-following-the.text: Good luck. You're going to need it.

investigation-successfully-following-the.speaker: Bandit (bearded)
investigation-successfully-following-the.text: You lot panic too much. It's going to be fine. Now, let's get going.

investigation-successfully-following-the.player: This doesn't sound good. I'd better let that sergeant know.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.player: Wait! I have some information that you need to hear.
There are some bandits disguising themselves as guards! I think they're planning to attack the delegation from Varlamore!
It's true! One of them infiltrated your guards and stole some uniforms. He came right through here earlier with them.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.text: The one with the large bag? I thought I didn't recognise him, but then it's so hard to keep up. We get through guards so quickly around here for some reason...

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.player: So what do we do? Should we warn the delegation?

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.text: And risk a panic? No. Better we deal with this now while they're safe in the palace. Do you know how many bandits there are?

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.text: Right, we can work with that. You get out there and point them out. With them being disguised, you'll need to keep a close eye out for any guard who looks or acts differently to the others.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.text: Don't go too far. If the bandits intend to attack the delegation, they'll either be here in the square or on the eastern road between the square and the bank.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn.text: Return to me once you've found all four and we'll take them all at the same time.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.text: Get out there and point out the four bandits. They're in disguise, so be sure to keep a close eye out for any guard who looks or acts differently to the others.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.text: Remember, if they intend to attack the delegation, they'll either be here in the square or on the eastern road between the square and the bank.

investigation-marking-a-guard.text: If four guards are already marked:

steps.text: You've already marked enough guards.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.player: Alright, I've pointed out all the bandits.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.text: If the player incorrectly marked any guards:

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: Are you sure? I definitely recognise at least one of them as one of my guards. Maybe you should try again.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.text: If the player correctly marked all four bandits:

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: Good work. I'll signal my guards to bring them in...
Sergeant Tobyn signals to his guards and the bandits are quickly arrested.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: That could have ended up quite nasty if not for you. Once again, good work.

steps.player: So what happens now?

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: The bandits will be interrogated. If all goes well, we'll get some useful information out of them.

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: Speaking of which... given it was you who found them in the first place, you might be able to offer some support. Would you be willing to help?

steps.player: Of course! Where do you need me?

steps.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
steps.text: Come with me. We'll use the cell on the palace roof for the interrogations. It's nice and out of the way.
Sergeant Tobyn escorts you to the palace roof.

investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
investigation-talking-to-sergeant-tobyn-.text: That could have ended up quite nasty if not for you. Once again, good work.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Ah, nilsal, sergeant.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Prince Itzla! I... I'm sorry, but I wasn't expecting you here.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well all that politics downstairs was getting a bit dry, but then I heard there'd been a bit of a commotion. I thought I'd come see what the fuss was all about. You don't mind, do you?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well no, it's just...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Wonderful! And you! Who are you?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: [player name]? Kuaini! Pleased to meet you. Crown Prince Itzla Arkan, heir to the Sun Throne, at your service.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Tell me, [player name], are you the one who caught these would-be assassins?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well then, why don't you and I ask this one a few little questions. You don't mind, do you, sergeant?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Not at all, but...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Excellent! Let's get started then.
The player and Prince Itzla enter one of the bandits' cells.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Nilsal to you, iknami. I hear you managed to get yourself into a spot of bother.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: I'm not telling you anything.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Ah, tetamo! Such a shame. No matter though! We'll have you talking in no time.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Now, you'll need to forgive me, but I'm a bit new around here, so your customs are not familiar to me. Tell me, iknami, what's the preferred method of interrogation in these parts?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: You're asking me how you should interrogate me?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well it just seemed polite to ask. We have all sorts of fun methods back home in Varlamore. We could give one or two of them a go if you want?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: If I want?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Absolutely! Now, what are your thoughts on chicken?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Chicken?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Oh, [player name], do you not have chickens here? Sorry, again, all this is quite new to me.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.player: Yes, we have chickens. The farms around here have loads.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well then, why the confusion? Have you never seen one before? Oh you poor sheltered thing. Did your parents never show you the wonders of the countryside?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: I know what a chicken is!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well why didn't you say so?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: I don't know what game you're playing, but it won't work on me!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: No game at all, iknami. The reason I ask is because one of our preferred methods in Varlamore involves just a small amount of fire, and you'd never believe it, but the smell of human flesh once it gets going...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: You're going to cook me?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Cook? No, not at all! That would imply I'm going to eat you, and I'm not a barbarian! Though, it would be interesting to know if it tastes like chicken as well...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Alright, enough! I'll tell you what you want!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Kuaini!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: So who are you working for?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: I don't know their name. They just paid us to attack the delegation. They didn't look to be from around here. I reckon it was one of your lot!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Why did they want you to attack the delegation?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: They didn't say, but that priest... he was the target!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: So a Varlamorian paid you to assassinate the Teokan? You're not giving me much to go on.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Bandit
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: That's all I know!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Hmm...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well I think we're done here. Come, [player name].
The player and Prince Itzla leave the cell.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: I think we got what we needed there.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: You're sure he told you everything?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Oh yes. The fear of being cooked will do that to a person. All total rubbish of course! Imagine burning someone alive! We're much more civilised over in Varlamore.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: We just cut out their heart while it's still beating instead.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.player: I can't tell if you're joking or not...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Anyway, sounds like there'll be some work to do when we get back home. An assassination attempt on the Teokan of Ralos... Concerning stuff. First up though, I'd better get back to the politics!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: [player name], once we've got these papers signed, you lot will be free to travel to Varlamore for the first time! No more needing explicit permission. You can come and go as you please!

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Now, it's entirely up to you of course, but given we have you to thank for stopping this plot, I'd be very keen if you'd join me in Varlamore to continue the investigation.
Before the release of Varlamore:

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: No need to decide now. It will take a bit longer for us to be ready for visitors anyway, but when the time comes, I'll have my people send word to you.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: After the release of Varlamore:

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: No need to decide now, but if you do wish to accept my offer, just speak to Regulus Cento outside the eastern gates of this city.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Now, they'll be missing me downstairs. Timoiva, and may the sun light your way!
Itzla departs.

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Well, that was interesting...

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.player: Not every day the heir to a far-off land comes and interrogates one of your prisoners?

interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.speaker: Sergeant Tobyn
interrogation-talking-to-the-prince-or-s.text: Oddly enough, no. This will be an interesting report to write. And on that note, I'd best get to it. All the best, adventurer. Thank you for your help.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

interrogation-talking-again-after-finish.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
interrogation-talking-again-after-finish.text: I think we got what we needed there.

messages-whack-da-chompy-wif-da-fisties.text: You'll need a weapon to try and attack this beast.

messages-stick-da-chompy-with-the-scratc.text: The Chompy Bird is too quick for your melee weapon.

messages-casting-da-creepy-splishy-splas.text: Magic simply won't affect this beast!

messages-stick-da-chompy-wif-da-uman-sta.text: Your ranged weapon isn't powerful enough to hurt the Chompy bird.

interacting-with-the-green-campfire-with.npc: Hmm... Such potential. Such a waste...
That helmet... Don't think it protects you... Don't think it hides the truth...

steps.npc: Nilsal, iknami. Would you like me to tan any hides for you?

steps.text: If player has no hides:

steps.player: No thanks. I don't have any hides.

steps.npc: No problem, iknami. Come back if you need me to tan any hides for you.

steps.text: If player has hides:

steps.player: Yes please.
No thanks.

steps.npc: No problem, iknami. Come back if you need me to tan any hides for you.

standard-dialogue-on-main-game-worlds.npc: Hello, I've got some wares in you might have lost. Care to take a look?

standard-dialogue-on-main-game-worlds.prompt: What would you like to say?

options.text: Who are you and what do you sell?

steps.player: Who are you and what do you sell?

steps.npc: I'm Chris, travelling repairman. If you need something repaired, I can do it for you if you've got the money for it.

I've also got a collection of items people end up losing a lot. Nothing fancy, and certainly nothing you couldn't get elsewhere, maybe for free. Still, I charge a convenience fee for having it right here. Interested?

steps.player: Show me what you've got.

options.text: About items that break when people kill me...

steps.player: About items that break when people kill me...

steps.npc: Yeah, some things will break if you get killed in the Wilderness. And if you die deep in the Wilderness, they can vanish altogether.

steps.player: Can you fix them?

steps.npc: For a fee, sure. Just show me the broken item.

options.text: Can you stop them vanishing in deep Wilderness?

steps.player: Can you stop them vanishing in deep Wilderness?

steps.npc: Well, if you bring me a Trouver Parchment and some coins, I can enchant some items so they won't disappear if you end up losing them deep in the Wilderness.

If you need a Trouver Parchment, there's a mage up in Ferox Enclave called Justine who sells them. I've also heard rumours there's a cave in the Wilderness with creatures that sometimes carry them as well.

steps.player: Why would wild creatures be carrying magic parchments?

steps.npc: Eh, some poor sap walks in carrying one, gets himself killed, and the creature just hangs on to it as a trophy? I can see it.

steps.player: No thanks.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Clerk. I work on gathering people together to form what we call clans.

steps.player: What is a clan?

steps.npc: Ah, clans. Where do I begin? Clans are groups of people gathered together for numerous reasons. Usually they have shared interests, like activities they enjoy together.
These activities could include improving certain skills, battling the same monsters, or even battling other clans!
Other clans form together because they just enjoy the company of other like-minded people. The clan community can be a great resource if you should ever need help with anything.

options.text: How do I join a clan?

steps.player: How do I join a clan?

steps.npc: You can either form your own clan with your friends, or apply to an already existing clan.
Should you choose to form your own clan you will need four friends to join you, and it is recommended that you have spent a good amount of time in this world first. Leadership is not for everyone.
However, fret not. There are plenty of interesting and exciting clans out there! Check out the clan recruitment board to see which clans are currently accepting applications.
You can either form your own clan with your friends, or apply to an already existing clan.

options.text: What can a clan offer me?

steps.player: What can a clan offer me?

steps.npc: Clans offer you the ability to have an official gathering of friends or like-minded individuals in a hierarchical structure.
In other words, you and your friends get an exclusive chat channel and a Clan Hall, as well as the ability to assign ranks to members.
Ranks can be assigned from custom pre-sets, which then determine what permissions that person has.
For example: One person may have the rank to kick players from the chat, while another has the rank to access the Clan Coffer.

steps.player: What is the Clan Coffer?

steps.npc: The Clan Coffer is a shared coin store, used by members of the clan. Highly ranked members can assign who has permission to deposit and withdraw coins.

steps.player: What is a Clan Hall?

steps.npc: A Clan Hall is a private area only accessible for the people with the permission to enter. High ranked members of the clan can restrict it to only allow certain ranks in, or open it up to even allow guests.

steps.player: Why would I need a Clan Hall? Can't I get a house instead?

steps.npc: The beauty of it is that you can have both. You can keep your house for private guests and your own personal use, but when you wish to see larger groups then the Clan Hall may be more fitting.

options.text: What is it that Piscarilius provides for Kourend?

steps.player: You're certainly a chirpy woman! What is it that Piscarilius house provides for Great Kourend?

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: Within the Piscarilius house, you'll find, great fisherman, traders, pirates and I. All lead, by our ruthless leader, Shauna Piscarilius, none yet to supersede her.

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: No surprise if you meet her, her tactics are ruthless. Her demeanour renders, all pirates toothless.

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: Our great shore and trading, have treasures to be found, providing export and fish, in quantities abound.

options.text: How do people start gaining favour in Piscarilius?

steps.player: How do people start gaining favour in Port Piscarilius?

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: Repairing net cranes, and gathering bait, newcomers to the port, well this is their fate... It's labour intensive, and dirty work, though stick to it friend, 'till your arms are inert.

options.text: Why should I gain favour in Piscarilius?

steps.player: Why should I gain favour in Piscarilius?

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: Our shore is brimming, with gold from the sea, the most loyal of our people, are handed the key. We'll let you stand on our shores and collect, the great anglerfish; other houses... covet?
If Leenz was not the last general store owner you talked to:
If Leenz was the last general store owner you talked to:

steps.player: Hang on a second... that last one didn't rhyme too well!

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: Listen here pal, you don't mess with people in Piscarilius. Do you want happy rhyming Leenz, or angry, gruff and pain-inflicting Leenz?

steps.player: Happy rhyming Leenz, please! Thanks for your help!

steps.speaker: Leenz
steps.text: Anytime, my adventuring friend, enjoy your time in Great Kourend!

jennifer-the-shayzien-general-store-owne.text: What're yer looking for, me luv'?

options.text: I don't need anything right now.
Can I ask you about the Shayzien house?

steps.player: Can I ask you about the Shayzien house?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Well I could give you some info if that's all yer wantin'. Gets lonely in 'ere while me mates are out there fightin' the good war!

options.text: What is it that Shayzien provides for Great Kourend?

steps.player: What is it that Shayzien provides for Great Kourend?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Phwoar, what don' we do? This 'ouse is filled with officers and the like. Lead by our rig'rous leader Shiro Shayzien, 'e ensures ultimate justice and safety for the entirety of Great Kourend.

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Our soldiers fight off the constant threat of the lizardman, while our 'ighly trained medics 'eal them from battle. Strict in combat trainin' and discipline. Law, order and defence. These are the words we live by!

options.text: How do people start gaining favour in Shayzien?

steps.player: How do people start gaining favour in Shayzien?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Don't get us wrong, me luv', it ain't all pretty. Those who're lookin' to gain favour within this household need to 'elp in 'ealing our fallen soldiers and tackling organised crime... It's 'ard work! That bein' said...

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: The rewards for the most loyal of this 'ouse are great. The 'onour to train alongside our elite guards and wear our prestigious armour, while also fightin' on the front line against the lizardman forces. The spoils of wars are

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: grand.

options.text: Why should I gain favour in Shayzien?

steps.player: Thanks for your help, Jennifer!

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: That's alright petal, you go'un and have fun.

returning-to-veos.speaker: Veos
returning-to-veos.text: Hello again, [player name]! What can I do for you?

options.text: Can you take me back to Port Sarim please?

steps.player: I have gathered information from all of the houses.
I could hear a voice, Veos... in my head! As if it whispered in my ear to return to you!

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: Yes, I heard it too... they mentioned that your task was complete.

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: Let me take those items off your hands.
Veos removes the items he gave you from your backpack.

steps.player: That reminds me, Veos! I didn't sign up to this with the knowledge that my mind would not only be entered but that there was a possibility of severely damaging my hand!

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: If it makes you feel any better, my client sends their apologies. It wasn't intentional. Needless to say, something you said provoked emotion...

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: Namely...

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: The Dark Altar...

steps.player: If I knew mentioning the Dark Altar would upset them so much, I'd have not written that bit of information down on the scroll!

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: Well that's just the thing, [player name]. My client is pleased you found such information. Tell me... Would you be willing to do one last thing for him?

steps.player: Well, I don't necessarily believe I have much of a choice!

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: I'm certainly glad you're able to assist once again.

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: My client will be most pleased.

steps.player: So what exactly is it your client now wants me to do?

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: My client requires... another simple task. He assures me that it will be the last. Take this orb. You must activate it beside the Dark Altar.
Player receives a mysterious orb.

steps.player: Can I ask why I would do that?

steps.speaker: Veos
steps.text: It's best you don't.

steps.player: Well, can't argue with that! I'll return when I'm done!

activating-the-orb.text: Player using the "Activate" option on the mysterious orb by the Dark Altar

activating-the-orb.player: I really wish I would be warned about these things earlier...

finishing-up.speaker: Veos

options.text: Can you take me back to Port Sarim please?

steps.player: Veos, enough is enough! I've suffered through enough. Exploding orbs and burning quills...

steps.speaker: Xeric

starting-out.speaker: Brother Kojo
starting-out.text: Hello adventurer. My name is Brother Kojo. Do you happen to know the time?

starting-out.speaker: Brother Kojo
starting-out.text: Exactly! This clock tower has recently broken down, and without it nobody can tell the correct time. I must fix it before the town people become too angry!

starting-out.speaker: Brother Kojo
starting-out.text: I don't suppose you could assist me in the repairs? I'll pay you for your help.

steps.player: OK old monk, what can I do?

steps.speaker: Brother Kojo
steps.text: Oh, thank you kindly! In the cellar below, you'll find four cogs. They're too heavy for me, but you should be able to carry them one at a time.

steps.speaker: Brother Kojo
steps.text: I know one goes on each floor... but I can't exactly remember which goes where specifically. Oh well, I'm sure you can figure it out fairly easily.

steps.player: Well, I'll do my best.

steps.speaker: Brother Kojo
steps.text: Thank you again! And remember to be careful, the cellar is full of strange beasts!

steps.player: Not now old monk.

steps.speaker: Brother Kojo
steps.text: OK then. Come back and let me know if you change your mind.

starting-out-talking-to-brother-kojo-aga.speaker: Brother Kojo
starting-out-talking-to-brother-kojo-aga.text: Oh hello, are you having trouble? The cogs are in four rooms below us. Place one cog on a pole on each of the four tower levels.

starting-out-talking-to-brother-kojo-aga.player: Right, gotcha. I'll do that then.

black-cog.text: If the player does not have a bucket of water or ice gloves equipped:

steps.text: The cog is red hot from the flames. You cannot pick it up.

black-cog.text: If the player has a bucket of water or ice gloves equipped:

steps.text: You pour water over the cog. It quickly cools down enough to take.
a black cog

white-cog.text: Trying to open the door before the rats have been poisoned:

steps.text: This door does not seem to be openable.

white-cog.text: Using the poison on the food trough:

steps.text: The rats swarm towards the poisoned food...
... and devour it hungrily.
You see them smashing against the gates in a panic.
They seem to be dying.

white-cog.text: Opening the door after poisoning the rats:

steps.text: The death throes of the rats seem to have shaken the door loose its hinges. You pick it up and go through.

placing-the-cogs-after-placing-a-cog.speaker: Brother Kojo
placing-the-cogs-after-placing-a-cog.text: That's great. Come see me when you've done the other three.

finishing-up.player: I have replaced all the cogs!

finishing-up.speaker: Brother Kojo
finishing-up.text: Really..? Wait, listen! Well done, well done! Yes yes yes, you've done it! You ARE clever!

finishing-up.speaker: Brother Kojo
finishing-up.text: The townsfolk will all be able to know the correct time now! Thank you so much for all of your help! And as promised, here is your reward!
Congratulations! Quest complete!

steps.npc: Welcome to Cobado's Groceries. Feeling hungry?

steps.player: Let's see what you have.

options.text: Why do you have an orange on your head?

steps.player: Why do you have an orange on your head?

steps.text: If the player does not have an orange on their head:

steps.npc: Why don't you have an orange on your head?

steps.player: Er... Because it's not an item of clothing?

steps.npc: Not for you perhaps, but it is for me.

steps.player: Right...

steps.npc: So anyway, looking to buy some food.

steps.text: If the player has an orange on their head:

steps.npc: You know you've got one on your head as well, right? Why have you done it?

steps.player: Er... I guess it's fun?

steps.npc: Exactly! Now we've cleared that up, looking to buy some food.

steps.text: If the player has an orange on their head, the purple token but not all of the other tokens, and has not received the blueberry muffin:

steps.npc: Why? I think you're well on the path to working that out yourself!

steps.player: I am?

steps.npc: That token you have! That's what it's all about! The capybaras left them for us, to test if we were worthy!

steps.player: Okay... But what do I do with it?

steps.npc: You need to find the others! The nice ones and the nasty ones! That's how you pass the test!

steps.player: Okay...

steps.text: If the player hasn't received the one coin yet:

steps.npc: Here! I shouldn't really do this, but let me give you a little hand! Take this!

steps.text: Cobado gives you a singular coin.

steps.player: Thanks...

steps.text: If the player has an orange on their head and all of the Varlamore tokens, and has not received the reward yet:

steps.npc: Why? I think you've worked that out yourself now!

steps.player: I have?

steps.npc: The tokens! It's always been about the tokens! The capybaras left them for us, to test if we were worthy! Now you finally have them all!

steps.player: Okay... But what do I do with them all now?

steps.npc: Do with them? Well... nothing. You've already passed the test!

steps.player: So there isn't some big reward?

steps.npc: Reward? Of course not! That was part of the test! They wanted to see how far you'd go!

steps.player: So I literally get nothing for this?

steps.npc: Hmm... I'll tell you what, because you worked so hard, I'll give you a little something!

steps.text: Cobado gives you some coins along with something extra nice.

steps.player: Wow, this is extra nice.
I'm good.

steps.npc: Well come back when you're hungry.

finding-the-outpost-not-getting-the-phra.text: I once had to clean all the penguins feet, back when I had a job.

finding-the-outpost-not-getting-the-phra.speaker: Larry

finding-the-outpost-not-getting-the-phra.player: I don't think I ever want to be a Zoo keeper.

finding-the-outpost-not-getting-the-phra.speaker: Larry
finding-the-outpost-not-getting-the-phra.text: Or perhaps there's some sort of magic that could persuade the penguin? An object of power or the like?

steps.player: I need that phrase! Isn't there anything you can do?

steps.text: (See 'Asking the Zoo penguin the phrase' section above)
(See 'Asking the Zoo penguin the phrase' section above)

finding-the-outpost-after-obtaining-the-.player: I got the phrase! These penguins are so weird. It's something about a walrus.

finding-the-outpost-after-obtaining-the-.speaker: Larry
finding-the-outpost-after-obtaining-the-.text: You aren't taking this seriously! They are dangerous!

finding-the-outpost-after-obtaining-the-.speaker: Larry
finding-the-outpost-after-obtaining-the-.text: Oh, just go talk to the sheep.

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.player: The penguin at the Zoo told me to see if you had any news.

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.text: We can't get any news in this field! All these humans keep trying to shear us!

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.text: We think the Farmer may be an agent for the other side, trying to have us assassinated by all these foolish humans. If you investigate him for us, we can finish our mission report and you can go on your way.

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.player: You want me to disguise myself as a human and talk to the Farmer? Seems like a tough request. I'll only do it if you tell me how to get to the outpost.

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.text: What do you mean 'How to get to the outpost'? Any intelligent penguin knows that.

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.player: Are you calling me dumb? Fine. You can talk to the Farmer yourself, and compromise your mission.

finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-returning-to-the-she.text: No, no, we'll tell you. You just deal with the Farmer.

finding-the-outpost-speaking-with-fred.speaker: Fred the Farmer
finding-the-outpost-speaking-with-fred.text: What are you doing on my land?

options.text: I'm looking for something to kill.
I need to talk to you about penguins.

steps.player: I need to talk to you about penguins.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: About what now? What do penguins have to do with anything?

steps.player: Hey Fred! You've been messing with the wrong people. You better leave the penguins alone... OR ELSE!

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: What are you shouting about? Don't you come into my house shouting at me.

steps.player: I mean it Fred, I don't know whose side you're working for, but assassinating the penguin operatives is going to get you in trouble. To think you'd even stoop to sending others to try and 'shear' them. Be careful, or you might find you've been shorn.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Is this some kind of joke? I'm a SHEEP farmer. That means I need to shear sheep. What are these penguins you keep talking about?

steps.player: Don't play neutral with me, Fred. I see right through you. You're probably working for the squirrels, aren't you? I'll be watching Fred. I'm always watching.
You know that 'Thing' out in your field? It's two penguins in disguise.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Like I haven't heard that before.

steps.player: No really, it is! They're trying to observe humans to learn our weaknesses.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Then why are they disguised as sheep?

steps.player: They probably thought they'd blend in better. Anyway, I came to warn you to not annoy them too much. They're funny little guys but they seem to have a grudge against you.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: You talk to these penguins?

steps.player: Yes, I have a penguin suit and I know the secret greeting. I'm infiltrating them because this crazy guy Larry is convinced they are trying to take over the world or something.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Look, when these voices in your head start talking to you again, you might want to ignore them.

steps.player: HEY! I'm not crazy! Larry's a little left of centre, but I'm just helping him out. The penguins really can talk.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Right, right. I believe you, sure. Maybe on your way out you could ask the sheep to herd themselves for me.

steps.player: Fine. Don't believe me. Larry and I will prove you wrong. Just don't go near the penguins, Fred, not if you value your life.

finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.text: Is the Farmer an agent for the other side?

options.text: The farmer is definitely an enemy.

steps.player: The Farmer is definitely an enemy. High ranking too, I think. He might even be the King of Lumbridge in disguise!

steps.speaker: Sheep
steps.text: King? I thought there was a duke, not a king.

steps.player: Well, that's why he's in disguise. Duh.

steps.speaker: Sheep
steps.text: This is an amazing revelation. We must include it in our report. Thank you, we'll mention your bravery.

steps.player: The Farmer is harmless. The sheep, however...now they seem pretty crafty.

steps.speaker: Sheep
steps.text: The sheep? But...They just wander around in this field all day. Trust us, we know.

steps.player: Exactly! So you don't suspect them! That's why they are so cunning. Watch your backs.

steps.speaker: Sheep
steps.text: You have a good point. Yes, we must warn Pescaling Pax of this new threat. We'll put it in the report and you can give it to them.

finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.player: Hey wait, you said you'd tell me where the outpost is!

finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.text: You are one clueless penguin. The outpost is the iceberg to the North. The entrance is concealed by what looks like an avalanche.

finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.text: When you try and go through a guard will stop you and ask for the password.

finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.speaker: Sheep
finding-the-outpost-reporting-back-to-th.text: The password is cabbage. Don't forget it.

finding-the-outpost-after-finding-the-ou.text: If the player told the penguins that Fred is a threat:

steps.player: I just convinced them Fred the Farmer was the King of Lumbridge!

steps.speaker: Larry
steps.text: But there is no King of Lumbridge.

steps.player: Exactly! They are so gullible. Even if they are organised.

steps.speaker: Larry
steps.text: Don't take this so lightly. You might put Fred in danger because you were having a laugh.

steps.player: Sorry. It was just a bit of fun.

finding-the-outpost-after-finding-the-ou.text: If the player told the penguins that Fred is harmless:

steps.speaker: Larry
steps.text: They are?

steps.player: No! They're just sheep. But I wanted to confuse the penguins. Put them off our scent.

steps.speaker: Larry
steps.text: What a good plan! I just hope the sheep aren't working for the other side.

steps.player: Larry, we need to get you to hang out with people, not animals.

finding-the-outpost-after-finding-the-ou.player: I know where their outpost is! The entrance is on the iceberg. It's concealed by an avalanche.

finding-the-outpost-after-finding-the-ou.speaker: Larry
finding-the-outpost-after-finding-the-ou.text: Great. Let's go back to the iceberg, I'll put you in your suit and we'll really see what these penguins are up to.

entering-the-outpost-speaking-to-larry.player: It's fun for you! You're not risking your neck.

entering-the-outpost-speaking-to-larry.speaker: Larry
entering-the-outpost-speaking-to-larry.text: But you don't think penguins are dangerous anyway. So there's no danger is there? Or are you coming around to my thinking that they are dangerous?

entering-the-outpost-speaking-to-larry.player: No...I mean...yes. Oh never mind. Just do the spell. Wait, won't the spell wear off once I'm inside? You'll be too far away.

entering-the-outpost-speaking-to-larry.speaker: Larry
entering-the-outpost-speaking-to-larry.text: Oh, no. The ice magnifies this spell, so it will allow you to go greater distances.

entering-the-outpost-asking-larry-about-.speaker: Larry

inside-the-outpost-debriefing.player: Yes, and I have my mission report. I also have the mission reports from the operatives in the Ardougne Zoo and the Lumbridge sheep field.

inside-the-outpost-debriefing.speaker: KGP Agent

inside-the-outpost-finishing-the-agility.speaker: Agility Instructor

inside-the-outpost-finishing-the-agility.speaker: Army Commander
inside-the-outpost-finishing-the-agility.text: Ah, they are doing drills! Getting ready for the invasion. What a glorious day that will be!

inside-the-outpost-finishing-the-agility.speaker: Army Commander
inside-the-outpost-finishing-the-agility.text: Yes, yes, I know we all get excited. But, I need you to get out of the way. Move along!

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.player: Larry, you were right! There's an entire army of them, and they're drilling and... Larry, they're ORGANISED!

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.speaker: Larry
inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.text: That's what I've been saying from the start! But an entire army? This is just an outpost, so it can't be an entire army.

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.player: I know what I saw! They were doing drills and everything.

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.speaker: Larry
inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.text: Still, it must only be an invasion party. The main force is on...well, it doesn't matter right now.

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.speaker: Larry
inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.text: I've been doing some research of my own, and I think I know what our next step should be. There's a secret room, deep in the glacier. I think that is where they are making their war plans.

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.player: War plans! Who are they going to war with?

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.speaker: Larry
inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.text: With us, you dolt! They are trying to take over the world. Have you not grasped this yet? You need to find that room. Our future depends on it.

inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.speaker: Larry
inside-the-outpost-reporting-to-larry-af.text: It's probably the most well guarded room in the place. You'll need to find a way to get into it without arousing suspicion.

searching-for-the-secret-room-speaking-t.speaker: Larry
searching-for-the-secret-room-speaking-t.text: What are you doing out here! You need to get in there and find the secret room.

searching-for-the-secret-room-speaking-t.player: Keep your shorts on; I'm working on it.

searching-for-the-secret-room-talking-to.player: You there, let me through those doors.

searching-for-the-secret-room-talking-to.text: I'm sorry comrade, you do not have the clearance to go through these doors.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: You look like...knowledgeable...penguins. What's through those doors at the end of the hall?

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Hey man, don't stress. Those doors open new worlds, man. Like, new rooms too.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: Yes, well, I would like to know what rooms.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Ping
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Like, the War Room and stuff like that, dude. Wicked stuff. Too bad only 'the man' gets to go through.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: No, man. He just means the authority. The MAN, you know?

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: Who are you? You don't really look like KGP agents.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Ping
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Dude, we are bards. We sing of the glories of the common penguin. We are also supposed to record history, but man, it is so HIS story. Like, the MAN's story.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Ping
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Totally, dude. You want to hear one of our songs?

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: Sure, I haven't got anything to lose, except my eardrums.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Well, like, we can't play it in THIS now. Maybe at a later now. We don't have any instruments to accompany our great song.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: But this room is filled with instruments.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Yeah man, but they come from the south, where humans have thumbs to play them with. We don't have thumbs. Also, the Pescaling had our old ones confiscated for being too loud.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Ping
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: But dude, I was reading, and there are instruments we could play. I read about one called bongos. They just need to be hit.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: But we need two instruments, man. Like, to make it harmonious with the vibes.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: What about a cowbell? You don't need thumbs for that.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Righteous man. So you'll get a cowbell and bongos for us and we'll rock out. We'll be so harmonious, no Pescallion could complain.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: Wait, why am I getting these instruments?

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Because your aura says you should.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.player: I think I have a lead. These two penguin bards seem to know a lot of the history of the iceberg. I think they might know a way into the War Room.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Larry
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: I'm not even going to ask why.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Larry
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: I think dairy cows have bells, you could steal one from it. Bongos... I suppose you could make them? Mahogany is good for bending, and then just use soft leather for the drum.

searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.speaker: Pong
searching-for-the-secret-room-asking-pen.text: Man, did you bring the instruments to us?

steps.npc: I'm Commissioner Anwar. I'm in charge of the Shayzien Constabulary. With Lord Shayzien currently busy with the war efforts, I'm also assisting him with his duties here in the city.

steps.player: What's the Shayzien Constabulary?

steps.npc: The Shayzien Army is split into six regiments plus the Shayzien Constabulary. While the six regiments are jointly responsible for protecting Kourend from external threats, we deal with issues closer to home.

steps.player: What are the six regiments?

steps.npc: The Intelligence Corps, the Medical Corps, the Engineering Corps, the Logistics Corps, the Rangers and of course, the Infantry. Each regiment is led by a general who reports directly to Lord Shayzien.

steps.player: It feels like there must be a bit of overlap between the Constabulary and the regiments, especially the Intelligence Corps.

steps.npc: On paper we're totally separate from the regiments. However, in reality you are correct. The distinction between internal and external threats grows murkier by the day.
More and more we find ourselves working alongside the Intelligence Corps and the other regiments. In particular, they've been supporting us in combating the rising gang threat in Port Piscarilius.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is the Shayzien Administration. The city of Shayzien is run from here.

steps.player: It seems very quiet.

steps.npc: A lot of focus right now is on the war with the lizardmen. Most senior members of the Shayzien Army, including Lord Shayzien himself, are working out of the Shayzien Encampment instead.

steps.player: So the Shayzien Army are also responsible for running the city?

steps.npc: Indeed. There's more of a separation between the city of Shayzien and the Shayzien Army now than there used to be, but this will likely always be a military settlement.
