starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: If continuing from Icthlarin's Little Helper:

steps.player: So what do you plan to do now?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well now that we've sorted out this business with Klenter, we can properly focus on dealing with these plagues.

steps.player: And how's that looking?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Not great. However, we do have one bit of good news in that area, thanks to you.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: If coming back to the High Priest:

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Good day.

steps.player: Hello there. How goes things?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Better now that we've sorted out that business with Klenter. Still, we're no closer to dealing with these plagues.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: However, we do have one bit of good news in that area, thanks to you.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: Yes. You've shown us that the pox we're all infected with can't be contagious. If it was, you'd be covered in spots by now.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.player: That's a very good point. Does this mean you can reopen the city?

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: It does indeed. The decision to lock things down was made very quickly, so we were forced to trap many of our citizens outside the walls. We'll be able to let them all back in now.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: It is, but there is a problem.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: When the plague first started, Menaphos, our neighbouring city, closed their gates as well. Many of our citizens became trapped there when they did.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.player: But if there's no risk of them becoming infected, can't they open up again as well?

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: You'd think so, but they believe that there is still a danger. It seems they're even willing to kill if it helps keep their city isolated.
If the player lacks the requirements for Contact!

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: The offer is appreciated, but I don't think there's anything you can do.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Contact! quest.

starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-the-high-priest.text: You'd really be willing to help us again?

steps.player: Of course!

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I'm very grateful. To be honest though, I'm not really sure where to start with this.

steps.player: Well first up, why don't you tell me what happened with Menaphos? You said something about them being willing to kill?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Indeed. Earlier today, I led a delegation across the bridge between the two cities in the hope of convincing them to end the quarantine. It didn't go well...
(Cut scene 1 begins.)

steps.player: Actually, I have other things to do.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I see. Fair enough.

starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.text: That is an improper greeting. You address the High Priest of Icthlarin!

starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.speaker: Coenus
starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.text: Don't try my patience! I have been ordered to stop anyone attempting to cross this bridge!

starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.text: We have discovered that we are not contagious. You must let us pass!

starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.speaker: Coenus
starting-out-cut-scene-1-sophanem-and-me.text: Step back or we will open fire.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.player: So they just started firing arrows at you? They sound like cold-blooded thugs.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: It is often the way under Pharoah Kemesis. He leads the Menaphites in a more secular manner than we would like. Respect for the old ways is diminishing.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.player: By old ways, do you mean Icthlarin?

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: The whole Menaphite Pantheon really. Religion is starting to mean less and less in Menaphos.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: There was once a time when we would care for all of Menaphos' dead here. Now, many opt for less traditional burials.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: Anyway, I've let myself become distracted. My focus is often on the dead, but right now our main worry is the living.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: It's clear that the Pharaoh has no desire to open his city, so we need to find another way of getting our citizens home.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.player: Any ideas on how we do that?

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: Well... I don't know. I'm open to any ideas you have.

options.text: What if I disguised myself as a citizen or a guard?

steps.player: What if I disguised myself as a citizen or a guard?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: It would not work. Their quarantine is very strict, just as ours was. Even their own people are not allowed in or out of the city.

steps.player: So how do they get food and other supplies in?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: The port south of the main city is still open. Traders take their goods to the city gates and exchange them with the guards there. Everything is thoroughly checked.

steps.player: I see. Doesn't sound like we can make anything work there then.

options.text: Is there any way across the river?

steps.player: Is there any way across the river?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: You'd want to swim across? If the current doesn't kill you, the crocodiles surely will.

steps.player: Ah... Maybe not then.

options.text: Perhaps I could fight my way in?

steps.player: Perhaps I could fight my way in?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Absolutely not! We here in Sophanem are still Menaphites and those guards are our brethren. Besides, I doubt you'd succeed against so many of them.

steps.player: Fair enough.

options.text: Is there any way into Menaphos from below?

steps.player: Is there any way into Menaphos from below?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

steps.player: Oh. So there aren't any tunnels under this city?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Beyond the homes of our dead? I can't imagine so. We are not ones for digging tunnels unnecessarily. We leave that nonsense to the Sect of Scabaras, and they're long gone.

steps.player: The Sect of Scabaras?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: They were a group dedicated to Scabaras, one of the lesser deities.

steps.player: What's a lesser deity?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: You already know of Icthlarin and the Devourer. They are the son and daughter of Tumeken and Elidinis. Together, they are the four main deities of the Menaphite Pantheon.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: However, the pantheon also has four lesser deities, or avatars as some call them. The Book of Light and Day says that Tumeken once fell into a deep sleep and dreamt for four days and four nights.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: With each night, his dreams took form. Those four forms became the lesser deities of the pantheon, with Scabaras being the last of them.

steps.player: And his followers liked to dig tunnels?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: That's right. Scabaras is the god of isolation. In keeping with his teachings, his followers mostly lived underground. As such, they were said to be great architects of the subterranean.

steps.player: So what happened to them?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: The Devourer was not the only member of the pantheon to wish ill upon our people. It is said that many years ago, Scabaras and his sect tried to claim these lands as their own.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: They built great tunnels beneath the Elid and used them to attack our settlements. However, Elidinis stood against them. The sect was destroyed, and Scabaras was fittingly driven into isolation.

steps.player: And you don't think there's a chance they might have built some tunnels under Sophanem and Menaphos?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Er... I suppose I've never considered it before. I guess it's not impossible.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Maybe you should visit Jex at the Temple of the Lesser Gods in the north east corner of the city. He knows more about the Sect of Scabaras than I do.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: In fact, now that I think about it, I recall a rumour that the temple was actually once home to the sect.

steps.player: Interesting. I'll pay him a visit.

options.text: I'll have to think some more.

steps.player: I'll have to think some more.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-afte.text: Hello again. Have you had any thoughts on how we can get our citizens out of Menaphos?

options.text: What if I disguised myself as a citizen or a guard?
Is there any way across the river?
Perhaps I could fight my way in?
Is there any way into Menaphos from below?
I'll have a think about it.

steps.player: I'll have a think about it.

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-agai.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-agai.text: Hello again. Did you visit Jex at the Temple of the Lesser Gods?

starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-agai.speaker: High Priest
starting-out-talking-to-high-priest-agai.text: You'll find the temple in the north east corner of the city.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: That's right. What can I do for you?

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: I'm hoping to learn a bit more about the Sect of Scabaras. The High Priest said you'd be a good person to ask.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: Ah yes. To be honest, not much is known about them. The sect was destroyed long ago. However, it is said that this temple was once their home.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: Speaking of the temple, what happened here? The place isn't looking great.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: It was just before the plagues started! They burst up from under the cellar and trashed the place! It was late at night, so I couldn't see who they were, or if they were even human!

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: What? Why wasn't the High Priest aware of this?

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: The first of the plagues started that next morning. It didn't seem wise to bother him.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: I'm sure he'd have still liked to have been made aware. You say they came from beneath the cellar?

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: That's right. Turns out there's quite the network of tunnels down there.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: Well then I think this is just what I'm after. I'd like to investigate these tunnels.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: I wouldn't if I were you. It's incredibly dangerous down there. We had a quick look, but there are some fearsome traps and vicious monsters lurking in the darkness.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: I'm afraid it's essential that I go down there.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: Well then you're either very brave or very foolish. We covered the tunnel they made with a trapdoor. Just head down into the cellar and then down that trapdoor.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.text: Oh, it's also very dark down there. You should take some sort of light source and a tinderbox with you.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex.player: Thanks. You've been a great help.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.player: I'd better get down there.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex-a.player: I haven't made it down to the tunnels yet.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex-a.speaker: Jex
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex-a.text: Well don't forget to take a light source and a tinderbox with you.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-jex-a.player: I will. Thanks for the warning.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.player: I'd better get going.

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-high-.speaker: High Priest
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-high-.text: Hello again. Any luck with getting our people out of Menaphos?

the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-high-.speaker: High Priest
the-route-into-menaphos-talking-to-high-.text: Well just let me know if I can help in any way.

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.speaker: Sophanem Guard
the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.text: Hello. How can I help you?

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: We're here to guard this place. Until recently, this was a bank, but then something came from the tunnels below and trashed the place.

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: Now we're guarding the trapdoor down to the tunnels instead.

steps.player: Do you have a tinderbox?

steps.text: If the player has a tinderbox:

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: I do, but I'd like to hold on to it for now.

steps.player: That's okay, I have one with me anyway.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have a tinderbox:

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: I have one I could sell you for 50 coins.

steps.player: I'll take it.

steps.text: The guard hands you a tinderbox in exchange for 50 coins.

steps.player: Sorry, that's too expensive.

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: No problem. Come back if you change your mind.

steps.player: Do you have a torch?

steps.text: If the player has a lit or unlit torch:

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: I do, but I'd like to hold on to it for now.

steps.player: That's okay, I have one with me anyway.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have a lit or unlit torch:

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: I'll sell you an unlit one for 200 coins.

steps.player: I'll take it.

steps.text: The guard hands you an unlit torch in exchange for 200 coins.

steps.player: Sorry, that's too expensive.

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: No problem. Come back if you change your mind.

steps.player: How come you're not spotty?

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: Ah, the pox. We weren't here when the outbreak took place. We were out of town trying to catch an antiques thief called Simon Templeton. We've only just got back.

steps.player: Aren't you afraid you'll fall ill as well?

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: The only reason we've been let back into the city is because the High Priest believes the pox isn't contagious.

steps.speaker: Sophanem Guard
steps.text: Besides, Sophanem is my home. It will take a lot more than the threat of a few spots to keep me away.

options.condition: Before picking another dialogue option:

steps.player: You can't. I'd better go.

options.condition: After picking another dialogue option:

steps.player: I'd better go.

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.speaker: Bank Guard
the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.text: It really is incredibly dangerous down there!

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.speaker: Bank Guard
the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.text: You should take some food down with you in case you get hurt!

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.speaker: Bank Guard
the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.text: I wouldn't take many valuables down there, just in case something bad happens.

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.speaker: Bank Guard
the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.text: If you see a scarab on any of the walls, stay well away from it!

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.speaker: Bank Guard
the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.text: I saw one of the other guards disappear down a trapdoor when he approached it. We never saw him again!

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-sophanem.player: I'll look out for them then.

the-sect-of-scabaras-talking-to-jex-afte.player: Not bad. Hopefully I'll make some real progress soon.
Well good luck, and be careful in those tunnels.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: No, I'm not, I'm [player name]. As for Kaleef, I'm afraid I have some bad news about him.
I'm sorry, but Kaleef is dead.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: Dead? He can't be dead! You're lying!

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: It's true. It looks like some creature killed him as he was entering this cavern.
Were the two of you close?

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: No. I barely knew him. He was meant to relieve me of my posting up in Menaphos, but now I'm stuck.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: Not that it matters I suppose. Even if he had made it, he wouldn't have been able to get across this chasm. We'd hoped there would be a route between the two cities down here, but clearly not.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: To be honest, that's kind of what I was hoping as well. I came down here to try and find a way into Menaphos.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: Well good luck with that. If there was a way into the city, I'd have found it by now. This was my last hope.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: So you have no way to leave?

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: Oh I could leave. While I may not know of any way into the city, I do know of a way out. Problem is, I was ordered not to leave until I found a way for Kaleef to get in.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: Hmm... That gives me an idea.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: An idea? What are you talking about?

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: The reason I'm looking for a way into Menaphos is so that I can help the citizens of Sophanem trapped there return home. However, maybe I don't actually need to enter the city to help them.
You said you knew of a way out of the city. You could help the citizens escape.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: And why would I do that?

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: Because if you help me, I might be able to help you. You mentioned Osman, right? I'm guessing you work for him, which makes you a spy from Al Kharid.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: That's right... I'm Maisa. You know Osman?

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.player: Yes. I'm the one who helped him free Prince Ali. I'm sure I could convince him to reconsider your posting.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: Hmm... If you are who you say you are, tell me where the Prince was being kept.

steps.player: Pollnivneach.
Draynor Village.
Port Sarim.
Goblin Village.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa.text: Interesting. And who helped you free the Prince?

steps.player: Hassan.
Louie Legs.
Leela.
Ranael.

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: You're obviously an imposter. You answered both questions incorrectly!

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: You'll have to do better than that to convince me.

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: Fair enough. I'm sorry I doubted you. I will help the citizens of Sophanem for you, but first you must convince Osman to come here and meet with me.

steps.player: You want him to come here?

steps.speaker: Maisa
steps.text: Yes. No more secret messages or intermediaries. I want to speak to him, face to face.

steps.player: Alright. I'll go to Al Kharid and see what I can do.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa-again-a.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa-again-a.text: You again. If you are who you say you are, tell me where Prince Ali was being kept.

kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa-again-a.speaker: Maisa
kaleef-s-corpse-talking-to-maisa-again-a.text: Don't take too long. It's not safe for me to stay down here.

options.text: Is there anything I can help you with?
I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.player: I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Sophanem?

steps.player: Yes. Your help is needed urgently there.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: My help is needed all over the place. What makes you suggest that I'm more urgently needed in Sophanem?

steps.player: Maisa wants to speak with you.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Maisa? You are mistaken. She's in Menaphos, and that city is locked tight to everyone, thanks in no small part to me.

steps.player: What? What have you been up to there?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Nothing you need to concern yourself with.

steps.player: You don't need to be so secretive with me. Did I not prove myself by freeing Prince Ali?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Hmm... Very well. What do you know of the political landscape here in the Kharidian Desert?

steps.player: Not a lot.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Well unlike many other regions, the Kharidian Desert is not united under a single banner. Instead, there are multiple independent city states, along with various lawless collectives.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: While all of the city states are currently at peace with each other, between some you'll find certain... rivalries.

steps.player: Oh I see. So one of those rivalries is between Menaphos and Al Kharid?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Some would say so.

steps.player: Including you?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: We were at war with the Menaphites for a long time. As Spymaster for Al Kharid, I know that no war is ever truly over.

steps.player: Does the Emir agree with you on that?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: The Emir trusts me to protect the best interests of Al Kharid. So in answer to your original question, that's what I've been doing in Menaphos and Sophanem.

steps.player: Look, this is all very interesting, but one of your people, Kaleef, is dead. He was meant to relieve Maisa of her post in Menaphos, but now he can't.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Then I will send someone else down instead. Is that all?

steps.player: No. Maisa is insisting that you meet with her personally.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: That's not possible and she knows it. It would be tantamount to sticking one's head in a crocodile's mouth. If the Menaphites caught me, I'd be lynched on sight.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Now, return to her and tell her that I will send a replacement for Kaleef shortly.

steps.player: That's not going to work. There's a chasm blocking the way from Sophanem to Menaphos. Any agent you send won't be able to enter the city. That's why Maisa wants to speak with you.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: If there's no way for someone to relieve Maisa, then she will have to remain there herself. This is the job she signed up for.

steps.player: But I need Maisa to help me with something. She'll only do that if you go and speak to her.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: That is your problem, not mine.

steps.player: And Prince Ali was your problem, but I still helped you.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: And you were paid for your services. What do you need from Maisa anyway?

steps.player: When Menaphos was locked down, many citizens from Sophanem were trapped there. I need to try and get them out of the city, but I have no way of entering Menaphos myself.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: So, you've convinced Maisa to help them on your behalf? What makes you think I want any part in this? The citizens of Sophanem are still Menaphites.

steps.player: Hmm... Let's see...
It must be boring here.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You wish to charm me with the idea of getting my hands dirty? Well I'm perfectly happy here in Al Kharid. I did all the adventuring I ever wanted to do in my youth.

options.text: There might be treasures underneath Sophanem.

steps.player: There might be treasures underneath Sophanem.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: That there might be, but if so, those treasures belong to the dead. We have treasures aplenty here in Al Kharid.

options.text: It could drive a wedge between the Menaphite cities.

steps.player: It could drive a wedge between the Menaphite cities.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: How so?

steps.player: Menaphos wouldn't be happy if the citizens of Sophanem bypassed the quarantine. I imagine you'd be able to take advantage of that.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Hmm... Alright, you have my curiosity. Let's see where this trail takes us. Meet me outside the gates to Sophanem. I have one or two things to sort out here before I depart.

options.text: It would give you the chance to spy first hand.

steps.player: It would give you the chance to spy first hand.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I have Maisa and others in place to do that already.

options.condition: Before selecting an incorrect option:

steps.player: I don't know.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Perhaps because there is no suitable answer. Now, I must get on with my work.

options.condition: After selecting an incorrect option:

steps.player: Fine. I give up.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: So you've seen sense? Good. Now, I must get on with my work.

options.text: I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.player: I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: As I've already told you, I have little interest in this business of yours. Why should I help you?

options.text: There might be treasures underneath Sophanem.
It could drive a wedge between the Menaphite cities.
It would give you the chance to spy first hand.
I'd like to talk about sq'irks.
I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.player: I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Yes, yes. I have one or two things to sort here before I depart. I'll meet you outside the gates to Sophanem.

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.speaker: Osman
i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.text: Ah, you're here. Do you know of a good way into the city? I'm getting too old for scaling walls.

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.player: What's wrong with using the gates?

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.speaker: Osman
i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.text: What if I'm recognised? Do you not think they'd question the presence of Al Kharid's Spymaster?

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.player: Okay, so maybe it wasn't one of my better suggestions.
I know of a secret entrance to the north.
There's a tunnel in some rocks near a camp.

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.speaker: Osman
i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.text: Good. Now, wait for me here. There's no point in both of us risking our necks getting seen together.

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.player: What if you injure yourself down in the tunnels?

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.speaker: Osman
i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.text: Don't worry about me. I may be getting older, but I didn't become Spymaster without getting into a fight or two.

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.speaker: Osman
i-spy-with-my-little-eye-talking-to-osma.text: Give me two hours. If I'm not back by then, come and look for me.

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-cut-scene-2-osm.text: (After cut scene 2 ends, the player yawns outside Sophanem.)

i-spy-with-my-little-eye-cut-scene-2-osm.player: Osman's been gone for hours. I think I should have a look for him.

options.text: I'd like to talk about sq'irks
I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.player: I want to talk to you about Sophanem.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I've no idea what's going on there. It's all on a need-to-know basis, and I don't need to know.

options.text: Who are you? Osman can't possibly be here!

steps.player: Who are you? Osman can't possibly be here!

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You can call me Osman, even though I am the man who is not Osman.

steps.player: So... you're one of his agents then? But you look just like him?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Of course I look like him. I'm in disguise. What sort of spy would look like a spy?

steps.player: Well the last time I worked with Osman there was some business with really bad wigs.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Right... Let's change the subject to something Osman might talk about. I don't want to blow my cover.

steps.player: I need to go.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Until next time.

beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.text: Some degenerate clubbed me and gave me a lump the size of an egg on the back of my head.

beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.player: Oh no! I'll keep my eyes peeled for suspicious looking characters.

beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.text: I have a fairly good idea who did it.

beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex
beetle-battle-talking-to-jex.text: That linen merchant, Siamun. He's never liked me.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.text: ... and whatever you do, don't risk giving yourself away when you help the citizens return.

beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.speaker: Maisa
beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.text: I know what I'm doing Osman.

beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.speaker: Maisa
beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.text: Hang on... What's going on? What's that shaking?

beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-cut-scene-3-osman-and-mais.text: Get out of here quick! Before the cave collapses!
The Giant Scarab forms out of several scarab swarms and attacks the player.

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.text: I seem to recall telling you to wait for me. What are you doing down here?

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.player: Well your two hours ran out a long time ago. Anyway, where did you disappear off to during the fight?

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.text: I didn't go anywhere. I decided to blend into the shadows. It's one of the many tricks I've picked up over the years. Not every problem needs a blade to solve it.

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.player: Right... So are you going to say 'thank you' or anything?

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.text: That's not required. Once again, I had it all under control.

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.text: Anyway, you'll be pleased to know that before we were interrupted, I was able to convince Maisa to remain in Menaphos. As agreed, she will help the citizens of Sophanem return home.

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.player: That's good to hear. I guess I should let the High Priest know.

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.text: If the Keris dagger hasn't been picked up yet:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Before you leave, it seems that Kaleef was able to at least get one hit on that beast. I suggest you take his dagger. It's quite powerful, and he has no need for it now.

beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.speaker: Osman
beetle-battle-talking-to-osman-after-the.text: Well done. You did an alright job here.

steps.npc: Corkat quo Sihar. I am one of the mystics of the Kahlith. Are you here to serve the balance?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Then you should speak to Konar quo Maten. She will guide you.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: A shame. You are a bringer of death, you could be of great use to the balance.

steps.player: I'm not sure.

steps.npc: Then you should speak with Xorrah quo Sihar. He will show you the way.
[player name]! Good t' see you!

steps.player: Hi Cormac. How's the island?

steps.npc: We're learnin' to live a bit differently now that the Angel's gone... It feels a little odd, but we be makin' the best of it.
For example, thanks t' some notes that Keenan left behind, we've worked out how to make golems out o' sunstone. They do nay do much right now, but we reckon we can eventually make use of 'em.

steps.player: Interesting...

steps.npc: Aye. Feel free to give it a go yoursen if you fancy.

steps.text: If the player has the sunstone crystal, or if they have already built the bank chest with it:

steps.player: I might do that. Thanks.

steps.text: If the player has lost the sunstone crystal and has free inventory space:

steps.npc: Oh, by the way, one o' the others managed to find this sunstone crystal. 'ere, you can have it.

steps.text: Cormac hands you a sunstone crystal.

steps.npc: We weren't sure what t' do with it. Figured you'd have an inkling as you've been digging around the place.

steps.player: I can't say I've seen much reference to something like this, but I'll see what use I can make of it. Thanks, Cormac.

steps.text: If the player has lost the sunstone crystal, but does not have any inventory space:

steps.npc: Oh, by the way, one o' the others managed to find this sunstone crystal. Come back when you have space for it, and you can have it.

after-in-aid-of-the-myreque.npc: Hey it's the hero! Thank you so much for saving us from Gadderanks. And the town is looking lovely as well. You've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Cornelius. I run the bank now.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect. Thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really. We're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place.
Hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey across the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know. We have some basic amenities now which is so very useful and we're all incredibly grateful to you.
I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Cornelius. I run the bank now.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

standard-dialogue-entering-daimon-s-crat.npc: Excuse me! This area is different than the rest of the Wilderness, are you sure you understand the rules?
I can tell you everything you need to know, but if you're in a rush then be warned my overlords will NOT be happy if they find you to be fighting with no honour.
Just don't go doing anything silly like selling your soul to your opponent else there will be big trouble!

standard-dialogue-entering-daimon-s-crat.prompt: Buying or selling kills within Bounty Hunter is against the rules.

standard-dialogue-daimon-s-crater.npc: [How may I help you, sir/How may I help you, madam/How may I help you]?

options.text: I'd like to learn the rules of combat in this arena!

steps.player: I'd like to learn the rules of combat in this arena!

steps.npc: Sure. Which part do you want to learn?

steps.player: Let's talk about Targets.

steps.npc: Sure. Upon entering the arena, you will be assigned a Target based on your combat level, and if you wish to adjust the range of potential Targets, you may do so by speaking with the Trader.

If you wish to change your Target, you may skip your current one, but please note that if you skip three skulled Targets within 30 minutes, you will not be able to receive a new Target for the next 30 minutes.
Additionally, it's worth mentioning that killing a player who is not your Target will not reward you with any bonuses related to Emblem or Bounty Hunter Points.

options.text: Can you explain Bounty Hunter Points to me?
How do I get bounty crates?

steps.player: Goodbye.
Tell me about Emblems.

steps.npc: After defeating your Target, you may come across a tier one Emblem. Defeating another Target will level up the Emblem; the higher its tier, the greater its value.
If you die while carrying an Emblem, its tier will be reduced by one. If you die with a Tier 1 emblem, you will lose the emblem.
You may use Bounty Hunter Points to purchase a tier one Emblem from the Trader, or sell your own Emblem to him for Bounty Hunter Points. You can only have one Emblem at a time.

options.text: Can you explain Bounty Hunter Points to me?

steps.player: Can you explain Bounty Hunter Points to me?

steps.npc: You can earn Bounty Hunter Points by defeating your target or selling Emblems to the Trader. Once you have Bounty Hunter Points, you may use them to purchase rewards from the reward shop.

steps.player: What is the Coffer for?

steps.npc: To participate in Bounty Hunter, you must have a certain amount of coins in your Coffer, which varies based on your combat level. Currently you need at least [x] coins to participate.
If you are unskulled and another person kills you in Bounty Hunter, [x] coins will be deducted from your Coffer and given to your killer.
If you are skulled, 10,000 coins will be deducted from your Coffer and given to your killer. However, any surplus money in your Coffer will remain safe.
To manage your Coffer, talk to the Trader.

options.text: How do I get bounty crates?

steps.player: How do I get bounty crates?

steps.npc: Well, if you want crates, you'll need to be fighting a target in the arena while having a minimum value of risked items on you. Anything you can protect, we won't count.
If you meet these requirements, we'll keep track of how long you're in there for. We'll occasionally give you a bonus if you die as well.
When you kill a target, if you've been in long enough, you'll get a crate. If you've been in there longer, you'll get a higher value crate.
The crates don't contain anything special; just coins and supplies to help cover what you'll use in the crater.
If you keep killing your target, you probably won't get many high value crates, but you'll certainly get a lot more points and Emblems instead.

options.text: Can you corrupt my Ancient Warrior armour?

steps.player: Can you corrupt my Ancient Warrior armour?

steps.npc: Of course. Just show me the armour and I'll get it done.

steps.player: Do you know anything about Bounty Hunter hats?

steps.text: Without at least 1 target kill:

steps.npc: Ah yes, you'll be able to collect them from me, once you've got some targeted kills that is.

steps.text: With at least 1 target kill:

steps.npc: Ah yes! I've been told to hold onto some hats for you, for your uhm... deeds in the wilderness.

steps.player: Oh wonderful, can I take a look?

steps.text: (Hat selection interface opens.)
If the player picks a hat they are not eligible to receive:
You need [number] target kills to claim this hat. You currently have [number].
If the player picks Rogue's revenge or Hunter's honour while already having one:

steps.npc: I'm afraid you've already got one of those hats, I can't let you have another.

steps.text: If the player picks a hat they are eligible to receive with a full inventory:

steps.npc: I'm afraid you've got nowhere to put a hat if I gave one to you.

steps.text: If the player picks a hat they are eligible to receive:

steps.npc: Here you go, enjoy!

steps.player: Can you tell me my current EP value?

steps.npc: Of course. Your current EP value is [number]%.

standard-dialogue-ferox-enclave.npc: [How may I help you, sir/How may I help you, madam/How may I help you]?

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: Beyond this portal lies Daimon's Crater, a place where you'll fight other adventurers like yourself for glory and rewards.

steps.text: If the player is not on an official Bounty Hunter world:

steps.npc: Sadly, I can't let you into Daimon's Crater right now.

steps.text: Bounty Hunter is only available on specific Bounty Hunter worlds.
If the player is on an official Bounty Hunter world:

steps.npc: If you step through this portal, you'll be taken to Daimon's Crater, where we've set up a lobby area for you to ready yourself for combat.
If you'd like, I can explain the rules of Bounty Hunter to you.

options.text: Can you explain Bounty Hunter Points to me?
Can I access my Bounty Hunter coffer?

steps.player: Can I access my Bounty Hunter coffer?

steps.npc: Certainly. Would you like to add or remove coins from it?

steps.prompt: Current coffer: [number of coins]

overhead-dialogue.text: One of the following will be said while hitting him:

steps.npc: Ye'll pay!
Curse you!
Curse 'em all!
Arrr, land-lubber!

standard-dialogue.npc: Salutations traveller! It is unusual for one of the creatures called 'humans' to visit this plane. How can I assist you?

steps.player: I'm just looking around, thanks.

steps.npc: I hope the beauty of my world brings you great joy.

steps.text: A random universal mystery will be selected from the list below.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name, in your language, would be Bubrezankaldargarez'jk, but you can just call me Bub. This small plane is my home, here I study and ponder the mysteries of existence.

steps.player: Mysteries of existence, eh? Like what?

steps.text: A random universal mystery will be selected from the list below.

options.text: I'm looking for a Star Flower.
options.condition: During Fairytale II - Cure a Queen

steps.player: I'm looking for a Star Flower.

steps.npc: Then you've come to the right place. Star Flower, which is much prized for its magical properties, only grows on this plane. It has a very short life-span; plants grow, flower and die in the space of minutes! If you search
around you might find some growing somewhere.
Where do flies go at night?
Have you ever flicked through a dictionary and afterwards felt really depressed by how much you don't know?
Do other birds speak pigeon pidgin?
Political philosophy is an oxymoron.
Why are yawns contagious?
Do sick days include when you're sick of work?
To be is to be the value of a variable.
How do you know when you've run out of invisible ink?
Where does a snake's tail begin?
How long do fish wait to swim after they eat?
If you're halfway from here to there, which is which?

standard-dialogue.npc: You were very brave for going on stage to confront a killer. Looks like you did well to get her to surrender without damaging her costume.

standard-dialogue.player: It was very well made. Makes the job of not damaging it much easier!

standard-dialogue.npc: Why thank you! I credit my needles for the good work.

standard-dialogue.player: Would I be able to get one of them for my own purposes?

standard-dialogue.npc: I suppose I could part with one... If you're careful not to lose it.

standard-dialogue.text: The costumer gives you one of her special needles.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-co.npc: Have you still got that needle safe and secure?

when-petted-during-the-2022-christmas-ev.player: Aww, what a cute cat! I better not wake it up.

when-petted-during-the-2022-christmas-ev.text: If the player has not completed Plague City or is on a free-to-play world:
If the player has completed Plague City and is on a members world:

steps.player: I certainly wouldn't hand you over for any runes, you're too adorable.

standard-dialogue.npc: How do. You planning on crossing this here bridge and heading up to Rellekka then?

steps.player: Yes, actually I was.

steps.npc: Aye, 'tis a good thing we fixed this 'ere bridge, I reckon. You best be careful up there. Them Fremenniks are odd 'uns.

steps.player: So you fixed this bridge yourself?

steps.npc: Aye, that I did. 'Twas real thirsty work too. If only some kind stranger would buy us a bit of beer to sup, eh?
What with that inn at seers so close by and all, eh?

steps.text: The workman winks at you

steps.npc: Just make sure yer don't get me none of that non alcoholic rubbish from that poison salesman guy at the tavern!

steps.player: I wasn't planning on it, no.

steps.npc: Aye, that's what I told t'gaffer. Nobody wants to go up and hang out with a buncha dumb barbarians when there's a perfectly good inn to sup in, in t'seers village.
Ain't much better in life than having a nice cold beer to sup on a hot day like this, eh? Better'n fixing bridges, eh?

steps.text: The workman winks at you

steps.npc: Just make sure yer don't get me none of that non alcoholic rubbish from that poison salesman guy at the tavern!

standard-dialogue-when-using-a-beer-or-b.npc: A bit early in the day fer that ain't it?
Ta very much, like. That'll hit the spot nicely. Here, you can have this. I picked it up as a souvenir on me last hols.
I dunno rightly, but if you use a tinderbox on it, it don't half make a loud noise!

standard-dialogue-when-using-another-typ.npc: No ta, not my brand of beer.

standard-dialogue-when-using-a-jug-of-wi.npc: No ta, not a big wine fan, me.

standard-dialogue-when-using-a-bottled-d.npc: A bit early in the day fer that ain't it?

standard-dialogue.npc: Good day to you.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is David Andrews. I'm the Head Councillor of the Kourend Council.

options.text: Tell me about the Kourend Council.

steps.player: Tell me about the Kourend Council.

steps.npc: Kourend's last King, Kharedst IV, had only one child when he died. She was too young to take the throne, so the Kourend Council was formed to look after things until she came of age.
Alas, she was very close to her father and his sudden death drove her to insanity. With no suitable ruler, the Kourend Council was made permanent.

steps.player: How is the Council structured?

steps.npc: The Kourend Council is made up of four councillors. Every four years there is an election for the people to decide who the councillors should be.
One of the councillors holds the position of Head Councillor and this rotates every year. I am the current Head Councillor.

steps.text: If the player has not completed The Queen of Thieves:

steps.npc: The other councillors are Councillor Hughes, Councillor Unkar and Councillor Orson.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Queen of Thieves:

steps.npc: The other councillors are Councillor Unkar and Councillor Orson. The fourth seat on the Council is currently vacent after the recent arrest of Councillor Hughes.

steps.player: So where do the five houses fit in?

steps.npc: The five houses of Kourend each have their own leader who rules over their city. The leaders of the individual houses must enforce and obey the laws set out by the Kourend Council, but can otherwise rule as they see fit.
I hope that helps.

steps.player: Yes, thank you.
Time for me to go.

steps.npc: Good day citizen.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.player: Well I do enjoy it when people get what they deserve.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.npc: You'll never know what it's like to be on top of the world. The power I had was unconquerable. I'd do it all again without hesitation.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.player: You never had any power. You were just a puppet. You've always been nothing, and that's all you'll ever be.
Enjoy your cell, puppet. Won't be seeing you.

steps.npc: Welcome to the Catherby Council Office. Your views are important to us.

steps.player: That's good to hear...

steps.npc: Unfortunately, all of our operatives are too busy to help you today. Please try again soon.

steps.player: Delightful...
What's wrong?

steps.npc: You may or may not be aware, but a plague has spread across West Ardougne. Now, so far, our efforts to contain it have been largely successful, for the most part.
However, some sheep recently escaped from a farm near the city. When they were found, we noticed that they were strangely discoloured, so we asked the mourners to examine them.
They believe that the sheep have become infected with the plague.

steps.player: Are you sure it's the plague?

steps.npc: Well the mourners seemed convinced and they're the experts. Even if it's not though, the sheep are clearly diseased in some way.
As the councillor responsible for public health and safety here in East Ardougne, I am in charge of dealing with this problem.
We need someone to herd these sheep into a safe enclosure, kill them quickly and cleanly and then dispose of the remains hygienically in a special incinerator.
Unfortunately, nobody wants to risk catching the plague, and I am unable to find someone willing to undertake this mission for me.

steps.prompt: Start the Sheep Herder quest?

steps.player: I can do that for you.

steps.npc: You will? That is excellent news! Head to the enclosure we have set up on Farmer Brumty's land to the north of the city; the four infected sheep should still be somewhere in that vicinity.
Before you will be allowed to enter the enclosure, however, you must ensure you have some kind of protective clothing to prevent contagion.

steps.player: Where can I find some protective clothing then?

steps.npc: Doctor Orbon should have something suitable. You should be able to find him in the chapel just north of here.
Please also take this poisoned sheep feed; we believe poisoning the sheep will minimise the risk of airborne contamination, and is of course also more humane to the sheep.

steps.text: The councillor gives you some poisoned sheep feed.

steps.player: How will I know which sheep are infected?

steps.npc: The poor creatures have developed strangely discoloured wool and flesh. You should have no trouble spotting them. There should be four in total.

steps.player: That's not a job for me.

steps.npc: I do not blame you adventurer. It is not particularly pleasant work. My problem remains however. If you know of anyone suitable please send them this way; time is of the essence.

steps.player: That's life for you.

steps.npc: That's what concerns me... There might not be much life around here soon.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder.npc: Well hello again adventurer! How are you today?
I'm okay. Sadly some more diseased sheep have appeared so I have them to deal with.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder.player: Do you need me to help again?

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder.npc: Thank you for the kind offer. You've done enough though. We'll find someone else to deal with these ones.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder-whi.npc: Hello, is there any news about how our sheep keep getting infected with the plague?

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder-whi.player: Not that I know of, sorry.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder-whi.npc: I'd sure like to know why we can't contain it. Please raise the issue next time you see the Head Mourner.

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.npc: Well hello again adventurer! How are you today?
Not too bad, I've a lot to do though. King Lathas left plenty of things for us to clean up.

after-completing-the-forsaken-tower-ques.npc: Thank you for helping to repair the Doors of Dinh. Kourend is a safer place because of you.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm Councillor Unkar, one of the members of the Kourend Council. We are responsible for running the entire Kingdom of Great Kourend.

steps.player: What brings you to Lovakengj then?

steps.npc: It's important for the council to maintain a good relationship with the rulers of the five houses. Although it is the council that rules, we can only do so with their support.
I'm here to help Lady Lovakengj out and to make sure she has everything she needs to rule effectively.

options.text: What are the Doors of Dinh?

steps.player: What are the Doors of Dinh?

steps.npc: They are a great set of doors built by the legendary smith, Dinh, in the early days of Kourend. They were created to imprison a deadly beast known as the Wintertodt.
Unfortunately, the doors were recently damaged, putting Kourend at risk. The master smith Undor, managed to repair them though, something he couldn't have done without you.

steps.player: I'll get going.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.npc: A step down from what I'm used to.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.player: Well you'd better get used to it. This is where you'll spend the rest of your life, however long that ends up being.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.npc: Oh, I'm all too aware of that. Here, I will fade into obscurity as the world forgets my actions. I've accepted it. Besides, it's for the best that I not be remembered.
I only hope that the work I did for my home endures. Everything I did was to ensure that Lovakengj prospered.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.player: I'm sure they'll be just fine. If anything, I imagine they're better off without you.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.npc: Don't be so sure. I've no doubt the new king has good intent, but our intentions mean little compared to our actions.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.player: Something you're all too aware of, I'm sure.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.npc: Indeed. But I guess only time will tell. Farewell human.

standard-dialogue.npc: Ahahahaha! I am Count Check, the renowned security expert. Would you like me to check your account to see if it is secure?

steps.player: Check my account, Count Check!

steps.text: If the player's account has a Bank PIN and is attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: You have a Jagex Account, and you have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! As you've passed my check for the first time, I award you a prize.

steps.text: lamp
If the player's account has a Bank PIN and is attached to a Jagex Account, but has already received the lamp:

steps.npc: You have a Jagex Account, and you have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! As you've passed my check before, there's no prize now.

steps.text: If the player's account has a Bank PIN, but is not attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: You do not have a Jagex Account, so you fail my checks! You should upgrade before we meet again.

steps.text: If the player's account does not have a Bank PIN and is not attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: You do not have a Jagex Account, nor a Bank PIN, so so you fail my checks! Please upgrade before we meet again.

options.text: Can you give me any advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any advice?

steps.npc: I can! Count with the Count as I count the steps to securing your account:
ONE... unique password!
Never use the same password for different accounts, or on different websites. If it got leaked, all of your accounts would become vulnerable at once!
TWO... step verification for your email account!
Good email providers let you set up two-step verification, maybe by generating security codes on a second device, or by sending codes to your phone. Make sure you've enabled this.

steps.text: If the player's account is attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: THREE... Um... Use a Jagex Account. I can see you already do this.

steps.player: Carry on.

options.text: What's that got to do with THREE?

steps.player: What's that got to do with THREE?

steps.npc: Look, I'd got something for ONE, TWO and FOUR, and I like counting, okay? Don't interrupt my flow!

steps.text: If the player's account is not attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: THREE... Um... Use a Jagex Account.
Visit the RuneScape website and log in to update your Account settings.

options.text: What's that got to do with THREE?

steps.text: If the player has set up a bank PIN:

steps.npc: FOUR... digit Bank PIN! I can see you have set one.

steps.text: If the player has not set up a bank PIN:

steps.npc: FOUR... digit Bank PIN!
Next time you visit a bank, talk to a banker and ask to check your PIN settings.

steps.text: If the player is an Ultimate Ironman:

steps.npc: FOUR... digit Bank PIN! I can see you do not use banks, by the way.
Muhahahahhaa! Such fun it is to count!

steps.text: Lightning strikes the Count's square.

options.text: Where can I learn more about security?

steps.player: Where can I learn more about security?

steps.text: If the player has not visited the Stronghold of Security:

steps.npc: The Stronghold of Security, in Barbarian Village. I see you have not visited it. Would you like to? I can send you straight there - but only once.

steps.prompt: Teleport to the Stronghold of Security?

steps.text: The player is teleported to the entrance of the Stronghold of Security.

steps.npc: So may I check your account for you?

steps.text: If the player has visited the Stronghold of Security:

steps.npc: The Stronghold of Security, in Barbarian Village. There is much to learn there. But while you are here, may I check your account for you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: As you may see, I am a vampyre, from Morytania. I left there when I heard the terrible news and now I choose to spend my days warning others of the perils that lay in wait for them.

steps.player: The perils?

steps.npc: Yes, be warned! The travellers of these lands face danger from outside. Accounts can be stolen, and when that happens one can lose everything one has worked for.
I've left my vampyric ways behind me, and now I spend my days letting everyone know of this terrible danger.
In return for my dedication, I have been blessed with the ability to check if adventurers are ready to defend themselves against these account thieves.

options.text: If you're a vampyre, how did you cross the Salve?
options.condition: If the player has completed Priest in Peril:

steps.player: If you're a vampyre, how did you cross the Salve?

steps.npc: What do you mean? 'If' I am a vampyre? Of course I am a vampyre! See my pale complexion, my teeth, my outfit - how could anyone doubt I am a true vampyre?
I used to stalk the night drinking blood like vampyres do, and I am certainly not just a role-playing enthusiast in a costume! Never question that!

steps.player: Right.

steps.npc: So may I check your account for you?

options.text: Can you give me any advice?
Where can I learn more about security?

steps.player: I'll see you another time.

random-event-dialogue.text: If the player has a Jagex Account and a bank PIN:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You have a Jagex Account, and you have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! Enjoy your prize.

random-event-dialogue.text: If the player has a Jagex Account, but does not have a bank PIN:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You do not have a Bank PIN, so you fail my checks! Talk to a banker to set a PIN before we meet again.

random-event-dialogue.text: If the player does not have a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You do not have a Jagex Account, so you fail my checks! You should upgrade before we meet again.

steps.text: To upgrade your account, visit the RuneScape Website and log in to update your Account settings.

random-event-dialogue.text: If the player does not have a Jagex Account or a bank PIN:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You do not have a Jagex Account, nor a Bank PIN, so so you fail my checks! Please upgrade before we meet again.

steps.text: To upgrade your account, visit the RuneScape Website and log in to update your Account settings.
To set a Bank PIN, talk to a banker and ask to check your PIN settings.

random-event-dialogue-other-player-s-eve.npc: I came to check [player name], not you.

overhead-dialogue.text: Upon spawning in for the player:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha, [player name]!

overhead-dialogue.text: While waiting for a response by the player:

steps.npc: Please let me check you, [player name]!
I have come to check you, [player name]...

overhead-dialogue.text: If the player does not respond in time:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha, ONE more person ignored me...
Hello [player name] you look like you've seen a ghost.

steps.player: Well, not a ghost, but... well... you're a vampyre aren't you? Shouldn't you be in Morytania?

steps.npc: Ah yes, I miss that place. So lovely and dark. I left there when I heard the terrible news and now I choose to spend the rest of my days warning others of the perils that lay in wait for them.

steps.player: Terrible news? Peril? I don't like the sound of this. Is there something I should know?

steps.npc: Yes be warned! The travellers of these lands face danger from outside. Accounts that allow them access to this magical place can be stolen and when that happens they could lose everything they have worked so hard

for. I've left my Vampyre ways behind me and now spend my days letting everyone know of this terrible danger. In return for my dedication I have been blessed with a unique ability to be able to check if
adventurers who speak with me are ready to defend themselves against these account thieves.

steps.player: Can you check to see if my account is secure?

steps.npc: Ok let me check your account security, but before I do there are some things that even I can not see. Firstly you must have a unique password for your account and not share it with anyone else and secondly make
sure you have 2 step verification for your registered recovery email. I'll leave it with you to make sure both of those things are in place.

steps.player: A unique password that I don't share, and 2 step verification on my email... got it.

steps.npc: Now let me take a look at some of your other security settings for you...

steps.text: If the player has set up an authenticator:

steps.npc: You are using the authenticator! Excellent. This will help to keep your account secure.

steps.text: If the player has not set up an authenticator:

steps.npc: You aren't using the authenticator! This is a disaster. You should enable this to keep your account secure. Simply visit the support link on the oldschool.runescape.com website.

steps.text: If the player has set up a bank PIN:

steps.npc: You have a bank PIN. This is good, but make sure that it's one that can't be easily guessed.

steps.text: If the player has not set up a bank PIN:

steps.npc: You really should set a bank PIN. If your account does get stolen, your items in the bank and other places like the GE will be safe.

steps.player: Is there an easy way to remember all these account security things?

steps.npc: Yes there is. by counting. I am a count, who likes to count and check accounts. You can ask me to check your account at any time you like and if you want to remember my top tips for account security just ask me
to count for you. The count loves to count.
Count with the count to easily remember my top account security tips:
One... unique password.
Two... step email verification.
Free... authenticator.
Four... digit bank PIN!
Muhahahahhaa!

steps.text: Lightning strikes the Count's square.

steps.player: Is there somewhere I can learn more about account security?

steps.npc: Yes! The Stronghold of Security which can be accessed via Barbarian Village.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has a Jagex Account and a bank PIN:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You have a Jagex Account, and you have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! Enjoy your prize.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has a Jagex Account, but does not have a bank PIN:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You do not have a Bank PIN, so you fail my checks! Talk to a banker to set a PIN before we meet again.

steps.text: To set a Bank PIN, talk to a banker and ask to check your PIN settings.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player does not have a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You do not have a Jagex Account, so you fail my checks! You should upgrade before we meet again.

steps.text: To upgrade your account, visit the RuneScape Website and log in to update your Account settings.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player does not have a Jagex Account or a bank PIN:

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You do not have a Jagex Account, nor a Bank PIN, so so you fail my checks! Please upgrade before we meet again.

steps.text: To upgrade your account, visit the RuneScape Website and log in to update your Account settings.
To set a Bank PIN, talk to a banker and ask to check your PIN settings.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player does not have a Jagex Account, but has a bank PIN (only on worlds where the Jagex Account requirement is waived):

steps.npc: Ahahahaha! I, Count Check, have checked your account. You have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! Enjoy your prize.
