talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: Yes, I'm afraid it did, LogWarden - all too well.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: I tricked it into going up to the Tower, and there it remains, imprisoned.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.player: So the creature wasn't all you'd hoped, then?
Oh, I see, we're developing a sense of right and wrong now are we?
Bit late for that, I'd say.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: I have no control over it! It's coming to get me!

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.player: What do you want me to do about it?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: Destroy it!!! Take the key to the Tower and take back the life I never should have granted!!!

talking-to-the-gardener-ghost-after-usin.speaker: Gardener Ghost
talking-to-the-gardener-ghost-after-usin.text: Same as ever, mate, just getting' on with it regardless.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I am commanded to destroy you, creature!
You really don't know, do you? Have a look for yourself.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: The creature stumbles over towards the mirror, focuses upon his reflection and...
The creature becomes instantly sober, horror all too evident in his undead eyes.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I'm sorry. I suppose I'm partly to blame for this.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: No - it was him I wager - Fenkenstrain - wasn't it? He's brought me back to life!

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: I was Rologarth, Lord of the North Coast - this castle was once mine. Fenkenstrain was the castle doctor.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: So the castle wasn't really abandoned when he found it?

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: Is that what he told you? No, no, this castle was once full of people and life. Fenkenstrain advised me to sell them to the vampyres, which - I am sad to say - I did.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I found your brain in a jar in Canifis, so he must have sold you too.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: Of that I will not speak. There lie memories that should rest with the dead, the living unable to bear them.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: That's it - I'm leaving this dreadful place, whether I get paid or not. Is there anything I can do for you before I leave?

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: Only one - please stop Fenkenstrain from carrying on his experiments, once and for all, so that no other poor soul has to endure suffering such as that of my people and I.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.player: Do you know how I can stop Fenkenstrain's experiments?

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: Take the Ring of Charos from him.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: It was my birthright, passed down to me through the ages, its origin forgotten.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: The Ring of Charos has many powers, but Fenkenstrain has bent them to his own evil purposes. Without the power of the ring, he will not be able to raise the dead from their sleep.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: It has one other, extremely important use - it confuses the werewolves' senses, making them believe that they smell one of their own kind. Without the ring, Fenkenstrain will be at their mercy.

convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.player: Never, now that he has told me the truth!

convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.text: Oh my, oh my, this is exactly what I feared!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Nilsal to you, iknami. Welcome to the Grand Museum. I hope your visit is a pleasant one. If you have any questions about Varlamore, I'm happy to help.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Certainly! When it comes to the existence of Varlamore, it is Xeric we have to thank. During his Age of Strife, many refugees fled Kourend over the previously unexplored Custodia Mountains.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: There were three notable groups of these refugees. The first group, the Talkasti, settled in the Tlati Rainforest.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: While they initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The next group were the Pericans. They first settled right here, building the town of Fortis, or Civitas illa Fortis as it eventually became.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Finally we have the dwarves. These were refugees from Lovakengj who established a home beneath Ralos' Rise, becoming known as the Dwarves of Cam Torum.

steps.player: Was there any friction between these groups initially?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Oh yes, very much so. The dwarves, just as they do today, mostly kept to themselves. However, the Talkasti and Pericans came into regular conflict over various matters.

steps.player: But that's not the case now, right? What brought them together?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: As you may well have already guessed, it was religion. Long before leaving Kourend, the Talkasti had taken to secretly worshipping Ralos and Ranul.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: After arriving here, they were able to openly practice their religion for the first time. Over time, the Pericans started to adopt this religion as well.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: As the two groups came together, the population of the region started to rapidly expand. This eventually led to the construction of Tempestus, and with it, the founding of Varlamore.

steps.player: So are there still distinctions between the Talkasti and the Pericans now?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Yes and no. Those terms are no longer used to describe people today. Since we united, we have all been Varlamorians. However, you'll still find many traces of our previous divide.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: For example, here in Fortis, you'll find yourself surrounded by Perican architecture, whereas over in the Tlati Rainforest, the influence of the Talkasti remains clear.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Names are another good example. Indeed, look no further than our rulers. For most of our history, we were ruled by the Tullus dynasty, with Tullus very much being a name of Perican origin.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: However, we are now ruled by the Arkan dynasty, whose name can be traced back to early Talkasti nomads.

steps.player: I see. So where did the name Varlamore come from.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The name comes from the River Varla that separated Talkasti and Perican territory. What was once a symbol of our divide, became the symbol of our unification.

steps.player: That was all super interesting! Thanks for the information.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Not a problem, iknami!

options.text: Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?
Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?
I'd better get going. Thanks again.

steps.player: I'd better get going. Thanks again.

options.text: Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Of course! Whereas in other parts of the world you'll likely find followers of many gods, here in Varlamore, you'll only really find those dedicated to Ralos and Ranul.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Losanium is the official term for this religion, though it is not a term you'll find used very often.

steps.player: How come?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Losanium encompasses the worship of both Ralos and Ranul, and while they do indeed go hand in hand, it is rare to find individuals equally dedicated to both.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Instead, most people focus their worship on one of the two, with Ralos being by far the more popular. Something that isn't too surprising given Ranul's association with death.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Now that said, you might actually find a higher than normal number of Ranul worshippers right here in the museum.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Something that is easily forgotten is that while Ranul is indeed a god of death, he is also a god of learning and knowledge.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: If you wish to learn more, you may well want to seek out one of the teoki in the temple to the south. Though of course, they may well have somewhat biased takes on their religious practices.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind. Thanks.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Don't mention it.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: I can indeed! When it comes to recent events in the kingdom, the best place to start is with the War of Betrayal. It all started around 100 years ago when Imafore Tullus ascended to the throne.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: He soon reorganised the kingdom into the Varlamorian Empire, a controversial choice to say the least, though it soon became clear that controversial choices were quite popular with Imafore.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: While public opinion was always mixed, nothing he did resulted in outright conflict until his sudden and brutal murder of the Kourend Royal Family. War was quickly declared.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Until that day, Varlamore had successfully managed to avoid conflict since before the kingdom was officially established. To say the war was unpopular would be an understatement.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Imafore soon found himself facing as much resistance from within as he did from Kourend. The end result was predictable.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Imafore and his forces found themselves trapped between two armies at the Battle of the Proudspire. He was captured and executed, bringing an end to the Tullus dynasty.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: This brings us to a fun little fact. After his death, Imafore was succeeded by King Mezpah Arkan. One of his first acts was to call for the beheading of every statue of Imafore in the kingdom.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The statues remain to this day. It's actually a crime to try and remove them. They exist as a reminder of our history, and a warning to any who would try to follow in Imafore's footsteps.

steps.player: I'll have to keep an eye out for them.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Indeed. I often like to challenge people to try and find them all!

steps.player: So how has the kingdom changed since Imafore died?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The War of Betrayal was very much seen as a wake- up call. While Varlamore had once flourished under the traditions of the Tullus dynasty, by the end, it's fair to say we were stagnating.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: King Mezpah set to work on transforming the kingdom. His ambitions were high, to the point that much of what he desired never came to pass in his lifetime.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: One of his most notable goals was to see Varlamore open more widely to the outer world. A goal which thanks to his great-granddaughter, has now finally been achieved!

steps.player: Well then I should be very thankful. Without him, I might never have been allowed to visit!

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Indeed. We would often send our students on trips to the east prior to the opening of the borders. The amount of paperwork needed was astounding! Now we can just hop on a ship any time we like!

steps.player: That definitely sounds much more fun. Thanks for all the information.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: It's not a problem, iknami.

options.text: Thanks. If I have any questions, I'll be sure to ask.

steps.player: Thanks. If I have any questions, I'll be sure to ask.

steps.player: Hello mate. What are you up to now?

steps.npc: Well, I'm trying to fight TzTok-Jad at the moment.

steps.npc: Yes, he's level 702 in Combat.

steps.player: Enjoy!

steps.npc: Thanks. Arghhhh, death to you foul beast!

steps.player: Hello!

steps.npc: Oh, hi.

steps.player: What adventure are you now on?

steps.npc: Well, I just dispatched TzTok-Jad. Pretty tough! I'm now on my way to the desert. I'm going to see if I can hunt down this Kalphite Queen everyone's been telling me about.

steps.player: I should warn you, you'll need a team to take that beast on.

steps.npc: I've already thought of that. I've arranged for a couple of the Slayer masters to join me.

steps.player: Wow! I wish I could witness that!
Hello again!

steps.npc: That's funny, I was just talking about you.

steps.player: You were?

steps.npc: Yes, I've been arranging a meeting between various leaders of Gielinor to discuss some political issues. It seems you have certainly been around a bit!

steps.player: I suppose I have. What issues are you going to be discussing in this meeting? Who will be there?

steps.npc: Sorry, that's top secret information.

steps.player: That's fine, I understand.
Hey there, where are you now?

steps.npc: Well, I thought I'd try out this place called the Wilderness.

steps.player: Oh dear.

steps.npc: Quite a gloomy place.
Oh! I can see someone.
He seems to be coming this way.

steps.player: Be careful!

steps.npc: Yes, he's definitely looking at me.
He's wearing some impressive armour.

steps.player: Watch out! He's going to attack you!

steps.npc: Surely not. Oh, look, there's another two of them coming to meet me.

steps.player: They're in a clan, they're going to fight you!

steps.npc: I don't think so.
Hi there gentlemen! Nice day...
Woah, take it easy! Hey, stop that!

steps.player: Fight Cyrisus!

steps.npc: I'll teach you to hit me! Have this!
That'll teach them.

steps.player: You beat them?

steps.npc: Of course. Easy.

steps.player: Phew!

Maybe that loathsome vampyre wandering about knows something?

steps.npc: Hmm, you might be right. He'll be of no use...

steps.player: Well then, if you do find the missing notes, I'm always happy to help.

steps.npc: Yes? Oh, of course! Keep your eyes peeled when you're down here. If you see anything of interest, you know where to find me.

steps.player: See you later.

steps.npc: Yes... Good day!

steps.player: Hi there.

steps.npc: Hello, young one. What brings you to our humble dwelling?

steps.player: I was wondering what this place was?

steps.npc: These are the Tunnels of Chaos. They radiate with the energy of chaos magic. At the far end of the tunnel, you will find a portal to the Chaos Altar itself where chaos runes are crafted!

options.text: Why is the tunnel so short?

steps.player: Why is the tunnel so short?

steps.npc: The nature of chaos magic itself is mysterious and hard to understand.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: The tunnel is here, and yet it is not here. We also are here, where we should be, yet we are somewhere else. And so, the tunnel goes from one place to another, yet touches neither.

steps.player: I really don't understand.

steps.npc: I told you you wouldn't. The best way to think of it is that the tunnel is like a gateway that allows you to travel from one place in the world to another in a more safe and convenient way.

steps.player: Oh, I think I see. So it is like a magical alternate route?

steps.npc: Exactly! Well done! And at the end, there is a portal which will transport you to the Chaos Altar.

steps.player: Oh, ok.

options.text: Why are there only three of you?

steps.player: Why are there only three of you?

steps.npc: Our order is a secret one and those of us that remain and survive through the ages choose to hide ourselves away.

steps.player: Where are the rest of you now?

steps.npc: We have built or found many tunnels such as these. This is not the only one. Rest assured, there are many more of us around.

steps.player: Is the Wilderness above us?

steps.npc: Yes, I can understand you would expect it to be since the tunnel leads to the Chaos Altar. And yet, the tunnel does not enter the Wilderness, no.
Rest assured, you are safe here and should not come to harm.

steps.player: How do I get into the Sanguinesti region?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: The entire region is surrounded by a wall that you'll find impossible to get over.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: That said, you might be able to find a way around the wall at the point where it meets the sea. Perhaps there's something in Burgh de Rott that could help you.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Once you're in, try and establish contact with the Myreque there. I'm sure they'll have sympathisers amongst the citizens. Someone should be able to point you in the right direction.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: One last thing to be aware of is the vyrewatch. They're powerful vampyres that patrol the entire region. We haven't found any way of killing them. Even the Rod of Ivandis does nothing!

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: It's a large region to the east of here. The southern part is a city called Meiyerditch. Humans live there in ghettos and are regularly tithed by the vampyres.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: The northern part is the vampyre capital of Darkmeyer. It is from his castle there that Lowerniel Drakan rules over all of Morytania.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Sanguinesti Myreque?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Sanguinesti Myreque?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Certainly. The Myreque, or at least the resistance that has now become the Myreque, originated in the region. Previously there was nothing.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: It was many years ago that a small group, led by a man called Safalaan Hallow, managed to escape from the ghettos of Meiyerditch.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: They got information out about what was happening and helped to organise the resistance, which today is called the Myreque.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: The name was given to us by the locals, who named us after the place where we hid in Mort Myre.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

steps.text: Halt! Halt, I say!

steps.speaker: Vyrewatch
steps.text: Slurp! You look positively delicious - let me help you lose a bit of weight! Either I get a bite or you can be my combat practice; which is it to be, meat sack?

steps.speaker: Vyrewatch
steps.text: Hmm, you look like a tasty specimen - in fact I'm quite peckish right now. You can either give me a bite or I'll use you for combat practice; what do you say?

steps.speaker: Vyrewatch
steps.text: Ooh, a meat sack... I could just do with a snack. What's it to be: do I use you for combat practice or do I get a bite?

options.text: Okay, have a bite (Offer a blood tithe).

steps.player: Okay, have a bite.

steps.player: Give me your best shot, you evil bloodsucker!

steps.speaker: Vyrewatch
steps.text: Impressive. Not many of you have the spine for it these days!
(The vyrewatch attacks the player)

options.text: Hey, look over there! (Distract and sneak away).

steps.player: Hey, look over there!

steps.text: Ha! I'm not falling for that! Prepare to be tithed...

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-talk.player: Hey again. I've made my way into the Sanguinesti region, I think!

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-talk.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-talk.text: Good news. Presumably you took precautions not to be followed?

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-talk.player: Err... Well anyway, I have some questions.

options.text: What did you want me to do again?

steps.player: What did you want me to do again?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Now that you've made your way into the Sanguinesti region, we need you to try and make contact with the Myreque there.

steps.player: How should I do that?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: You may need to ask some of the citizens, but try to be discreet! Remember to avoid the vyrewatch at all costs!

options.text: Any tips you can give to help out a bit?

steps.player: Any tips you can give to help out a bit?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: You may get lost while in the city. It might be worth your while to invest in some teleportation devices to get yourself out.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-ente.text: These floorboards look a little weak near to the wall.

steps.text: The player kicks in the floorboards on a section of the wall, making it passable

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-atte.text: You try to open it, but it seems to be stuck fast.

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-atte.player: Interesting... It looks like this section of the wall has been tampered with.

contact-with-the-sanguinesti-region-atte.text: You're pretty sure you'll get lost if you start exploring like this. Perhaps you should first ask someone where to go.

options.text: (whisper) Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Child

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

steps.text: He-he-hello?

steps.player: Hello, I wondered if I could have a chat.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Well, I guess so.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Argghghhh!

steps.player: Hey, don't be scared, I just want to talk to you.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Well, I guess so.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Leave me alone!

steps.player: Sorry but I need to ask a couple of questions.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Well, I guess so.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Get off me! I haven't got anything!

steps.player: Hey, calm down, I'm not going to hurt you. I just want to ask a few questions.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Well, I guess so.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: I'm barely surviving...

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: When I'm not being drained of blood, the vyrewatch force me to repair the walls.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: When I'm not being drained of blood I'm fixing up the ghetto.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: I just try to make a living the best way I can. You haven't got some food have you?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Like everyone else, I just survive here. Just try to keep alive till after the next blood tithe. That's when they feed us.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Why do you wanna know?

steps.player: Just curious, that's all.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: I dunno. I don't know if I can trust you...

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.player: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Well, you're in sector one, but if you were hoping for any other help then I'm very sorry. I find it hard enough to help myself.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Life's so very hard here. Before too long they'll be wanting to have another blood tithing and then I'll feel just awful again.

steps.player: What's a blood tithing?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: You must be new here, else you'd know for sure. It's where we have to give a blood tithe to the vampyres. They do it on a weekly basis, a different sector each week so they don't kill us all off.

options.text: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: It's probably best not to talk about that, friend.

steps.player: I need to make contact with them. Please don't worry - I'm on their side.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: As are we all, but I really can't talk about them. It's not a subject easily broached here.

options.text: (whisper) Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Yes... but I really can't talk about them.

options.text: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Yep, that's where we are at the moment. This place, Meiyerditch, is just one large ghetto.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: The city is sectioned off so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill us all off in one go.

options.text: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.player: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: They're monsters, I know that much. I've never known anything else, but I have a feeling it might be nice to not have to live in fear the whole time. Worrying if I'm going to make the next blood tithe quota.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres. Apparently they were human once, converted by the vampyres.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Then you have juvinates. They're initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to get some powers.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: After that you have the vyres. They're nasty... really nasty.

options.text: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.player: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Drakan? Which one: Ranis or Vanescula?

steps.player: Well, I was referring to the main Drakan, you know, the overlord of Morytania.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Hmm, nothing has been seen of him for many years now. Some people say they occasionally see Ranis or Vanescula flying about, but it's not too often.

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: To do? Around here? Survive! Eke out an existence and just live for another day, that's it really.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: The juvinates organise work crews to mine the daeyalt, fix the walls, the castles and so on. If we refuse to do the work, they put us on double tithes and you can't do that for long before you dry up.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: If you want to escape, there's only one way. Anyone who survives in the theatre gets to leave. It's pointless though. No one survives.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: It's very nice of you to offer, my friend, but I shouldn't expect that you could do anything. The vampyres are just too powerful to overcome.

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: They say this place once had a Saradominist Queen. Even she could not withstand the vampyres. Anyone who has challenged their power in the past has come undone.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?
Do you know of the Myreque?
(whisper) I really need to meet the Myreque.

steps.player: I really need to meet the Myreque. If you can't talk to me about them, maybe you know someone who will?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: I understand, but you may not like what you find. Go and talk to Old Man Ral. He might help you. He lives in the centre of sector one.

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?
Can you introduce me to Old Man Ral?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: Well, I don't need to do that. Just tell him that a friend has recommended you to him. It makes him feel important.

options.text: How can Old Man Ral help me?

steps.player: How can Old Man Ral help me?

steps.speaker: Meiyerditch citizen
steps.text: He should be able to give you some background information on this place and perhaps put you in touch with people of the same way of thinking as yourself... Hope that helps. See you around.

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.player: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! What do I know about anything? I know nothing of you!

options.text: Do you know anything about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know anything about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! A simple man only knows simple truths, and what I know is my own business. I share that which is precious only to those who consider it valuable. Nothing will I share with those who are unknown to me.

options.text: I just want to help, what should I do?

steps.player: I just want to help, what should I do?

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! I am a simple man, what little do I know? In esteem, must a man be held, before he feels his efforts are truly appreciated?

steps.player: You're answering every question with a question!

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Am I?

options.text: Someone said you could help me.
options.condition: If the player has asked a citizen about Old Man Ral:

steps.player: Someone said you could help me.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! People say things they do not mean - many times this has been true.

steps.player: It's true. They said that you were very well informed. In fact they had a name for you!

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Oh yes, what was it?

options.text: Old Man Ral, he's a very good pal.

steps.player: Old Man Ral, he's a very good pal.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Nope, that's not me they're talking about, must be someone else.

steps.player: No, I'm sure they gave you a name, but it might have been something else.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Okay then, what was it?

options.text: Old Man Ral, the nefarious rascal.

steps.player: Old Man Ral, the nefarious rascal.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Nope, doesn't sound like me, you sure you've not got me confused with someone else?

steps.player: No, I'm pretty sure they directed me to you. What was that name they used to describe you?

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Yes indeed, what was the name?

options.text: Old Man Ral, the Meiyerditch snitch.

steps.player: Old Man Ral, the Meiyerditch snitch.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! A snitch! Are you trying to insult me? Get out! Go on!

steps.player: No, no, sorry, I do apologise. I'm sure that was someone else. My mistake entirely!

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! So no one actually referred you to me at all then?

steps.player: No they did, and they referred to you as...

options.text: Old Man Ral, the sage of Sanguinesti.

steps.player: Old Man Ral, the sage of Sanguinesti.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! Sage of Sanguinesti, eh?

steps.player: Yes, yes, saying you were the local font of knowledge.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph! So that's what they call me now is it?

steps.player: Oh yes, yes. All the time. And only in the most respectful way.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmmm. Sage of Sanguinesti. Has a nice ring to it. Yes, that sounds like they were referring to me. What else did they say about me?

steps.player: They said that you might be able to help me find some people... Some hidden people...

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmmmph. That depends. Did they hide themselves or did someone else hide them?

steps.player: Well, hopefully they hid themselves. I need to make contact with the Myreque.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: Hmph. Myreque, eh? Well, it'll take a lot to find them. It's not an easy route up to sector three, but that's where they are. You'll need to follow the symbols in order to get there.

steps.speaker: Old Man Ral
steps.text: And now you should leave. I have little tolerance for people and talking to you has tired me out.

steps.player: Okay, thanks very much.
Sorry to bother you.
Sorry to bother you.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.player: I'm [player name]. I'm a friend of the Myreque. I've come to help!

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.text: Oh, and I'm just supposed to believe you am I?

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.text: Veliaf? Is he still alive? Amazing! Well, you make a convincing story, so I guess I'll have to believe you, for now.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.text: So anyway, I'm Vertida, one of the Myreque here. What brings you to this miserable place?

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida.player: I was asked to make contact with the Myreque here.

steps.player: So what do you do here?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: I'm the second in command of the Myreque here in Meiyerditch. The others are all out on missions right now.

steps.player: Have you always lived here?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: Not always. I was originally from Lumbridge, perhaps much like yourself. I ended up here when I was captured by the vampyres while exploring Mort Myre. That was a long time ago.

steps.player: How have you survived this long?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: I found Safalaan, the leader of this group. Together we escaped from Meiyerditch and formed the Myreque out in Mort Myre.

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: We eventually came back here though. We knew we couldn't leave the people here to the vampyres.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: That's really up to you. That said, I imagine you'll probably want to get back to where you came from and deliver that message I gave you.

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: There you go.

options.text: So what do you do here?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-being-sent-to-the-.text: Your inventory is too full to hold any more ore.
If the cart has room and the player has enough ore to fill it:

steps.text: You deposit [1-15] ore(s) into the cart. The cart is now full.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-being-sent-to-the-.text: If the cart has room and the player has ore to deposit but not enough to fill it:

steps.text: You deposit [1-14] ore(s) into the cart. The cart can hold [1-14] more ore(s).

sanguinesti-diplomacy-being-sent-to-the-.text: If the cart has room but the player has no ore:

steps.text: The cart can hold [1-15] more ore(s).

sanguinesti-diplomacy-being-sent-to-the-.text: If the cart does not have room:

steps.text: The cart is now full.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.player: I have met with the Sanguinesti Myreque!
Yes! They gave me a message to give to you but I don't have it on me at the moment.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: Well, please bring it to me when you can. I'd be very interested to hear what they have to say.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.player: I have a message for you from the Sanguinesti Myreque!

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: Great! Please let me see it.
You hand over the message to Veliaf.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: Hmm, sounds like they're struggling just as much as we are. At least they still live though.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: I need some time to consider how we can best support the Sanguinesti Myreque. In the meantime, I have a new task for you.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.player: What do you want me to do?

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: I've had word from Drezel that there's something strange going on at Paterdomus. Head up there and see what support you can offer.

sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: Once you're done, press onwards to Varrock and seek an audience with King Roald. Express the desperate nature of the situation here and beg him to send troops.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Hey there. What should I do now?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: I've had word from Drezel that there's something strange going on at Paterdomus. Head up there and see what support you can offer.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: Once you're done, press onwards to Varrock and seek an audience with King Roald. Express the desperate nature of the situation here and beg him to send troops.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida-s.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida-s.text: Myreque prevail! What can I do for you?

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: I'm the second in command of the Myreque here in Meiyerditch. The others are all out on missions right now.

steps.player: Have you always lived here?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: Not always. I was originally from Lumbridge, perhaps much like yourself. I ended up here when I was captured by the vampyres while exploring Mort Myre. That was a long time ago.

steps.player: How have you survived this long?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: I found Safalaan, the leader of this group. Together we escaped from Meiyerditch and formed the Myreque out in Mort Myre.

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: We eventually came back here though. We knew we couldn't leave the people here to the vampyres.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?
I'm a bit lost... Can you help?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: Well, I've been with them for years now. We have multiple groups in Morytania but I only really know about those of us based here.

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: To be honest, things haven't been great for us. Our leader, Safalaan, keeps us going. We'd be nowhere without him.

options.text: I'm a bit lost... Can you help?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: I'm a bit lost... Can you help?

steps.player: I'm a bit lost... Can you help?

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: I'd like to help, I really would, but I can't leave the base right now. The others are all out on missions so someone needs to keep watch here.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.
Nothing, thanks.

options.text: Talk to the king about Morytania.

steps.player: I must speak with you on a matter of grave importance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I'm very sorry, but I'm currently rather busy. Apparently old Drezel is having a bit of bother near Paterdomus and I have to try and sort someone out to go and visit him.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I don't suppose you would fancy popping in and seeing him, would you?

steps.player: Oh, Veliaf asked me to pay him a visit, actually. I guess I could go and meet with him.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: That would be very good indeed. Your king commends you!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.player: Hey, Drezel. Veliaf sent me. Apparently there have been some strange goings on which you need me to investigate.
Actually, that's a bit odd isn't it? Because in Morytania, strange is the order of the day. I'd have been more surprised if there had been reports of things getting back to normal!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.text: I'm glad you're keeping your sense of humour. It will help you to maintain mental clarity while dealing with the tasks you've been given.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.player: Well there's no shortage of tasks for me. Once I'm done here I have to go and speak to King Roald, or rather, Roald. We've been on first name terms for quite a while now. Funny that, eh?
To think, a lowly adventurer like me having friends like you and the king. Still, at least I haven't lost my common touch.
But anyway, what do you need from me?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.text: Ivan mentioned that he heard some strange noises recently out in front of the temple. Could you have a look and make sure there's nothing funny going on?

options.text: When and where were these noises heard?

steps.player: When and where were these noises heard?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Ivan said he heard them throughout the day, but usually when things were very quiet. We both looked around near the temple but we didn't find anything.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: We were both a bit nervous about going any further west than the steps.

steps.player: Do you think the noises could have come from beyond the steps? I mean, from further west?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It's certainly possible and more than likely. I'd be grateful if you could extend your search as wide as you can.

options.text: Did you hear the noises as well?
Has anyone seen or reported anything unusual?
How is Ivan? Is he okay?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: Did you hear the noises as well?

steps.player: Did you hear the noises as well?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: I must confess, I have heard some strange things around here recently. Like hushed voices.

steps.player: So, maybe Ivan was whispering to you?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: They didn't sound human!

steps.player: Right! That's different! What did they sound like?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Very gruff. almost animal-like in fact.

steps.player: Hmmm, never fear, [player name] is here! I'll work this out Drezel, don't you worry!

options.text: When and where were these noises heard?
Has anyone seen or reported anything unusual?
How is Ivan? Is he okay?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: Has anyone seen or reported anything unusual?

steps.player: Has anyone seen or reported anything unusual?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Unfortunately, they have. Several people have gone missing from the local limestone mining area.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Other locals have reported seeing shadowy figures in the Silvaria pass. Could just be an enterprising, though perhaps ruthless, bunch of brigands. If it is, simply give them a taste of Misthalin law and order.

steps.player: And if it turns out to be more than that?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well then, my friend, I will pray that Saradomin's blessings be upon you and that he guides your actions and keeps you safe from harm.

steps.player: How incredibly reassuring!

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Don't take that tone with me! Saradomin's powers are not to be underestimated.

options.text: When and where were these noises heard?
Did you hear the noises as well?
How is Ivan? Is he okay?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: How is Ivan? Is he okay?

steps.player: How is Ivan? Is he okay?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: He's as well as can be expected considering the circumstances. He's a very confused young man at the moment what with the shadowy events that started his life.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Both his parents died in the Sanguinesti region, though he still holds hope that they may be found alive.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The death of Sani has really affected him as well. Like him, she was an orphan. They had a lot in common.

steps.player: It's all so tragic. I wish there was something I could do for him.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well, you brought him here, which was very brave. He's very grateful to you. It's remarkable, really. He has this inner calmness that I find so very affecting.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: His studies go well and he has Saradomin's blessings, it's clear to see. I would see him as a worthy successor as protector of Paterdomus. When all of his teachings are done, naturally.

options.text: When and where were these noises heard?
Did you hear the noises as well?
Has anyone seen or reported anything unusual?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.
Okay, will do.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-ag.player: Sorry, Drezel, what did you want me to do again?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-ag.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-ag.text: Ivan mentioned that he heard some strange noises recently out in front of the temple. Could you have a look and make sure there's nothing funny going on?

options.text: When and where were these noises heard?
Did you hear the noises as well?
Has anyone seen or reported anything unusual?
How is Ivan? Is he okay?

steps.player: Okay, will do.

misthalin-diplomacy-searching-the-bush-o.text: You search the bushes and find someone lying unconscious.
The player is knocked out by a werewolf (#1)
The two werewolves depart and the player wakes up

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Yes. And I have some news!
I was attacked near the temple! On the other side of the Salve!
By beasts! From Morytania, I believe. Perhaps werewolves.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: The vampyres must be behind this! Did you speak with Roald yet? We need his support if we are to end this suffering.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Not yet, I'm afraid. I thought you would want to know about the werewolves as soon as possible.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: It's good of you to return with this information, but we need to know Roald's answer before we can make any further plans.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [playername]. Did you find anything out nearby?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Not clearly, but I believe they could have been werewolves.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: This is terrible, terrible news! They have found a way to get across the Salve!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: I must make immediate preparations and meet with other members of my order. You must hurry directly to King Roald and impart this information to him.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Here, take these runes. They should help you to return to Varrock faster.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Very well, I'll make my way to Varrock and bid you good luck.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [playername]. Have you been to Varrock yet?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Not yet, sorry. What should I do again?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: You need to warn King Roald about possible incursions into Misthalin from Morytania.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Ah yes, quite right. Thanks for reminding me.

options.text: Talk to the king about Morytania.

steps.player: I must speak with you on a matter of grave importance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Certainly. What seems to be the problem?

steps.player: I've witnessed a great many terrible things happening in Morytania, some of which could be happening in Misthalin before long!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This sounds pretty grave, please go on.

steps.player: I have been helping a collection of brave freedom fighters called the Myreque for some time now. They've been fighting against the vampyres and their ruler, Lowerniel Drakan.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: We're all too aware of Drakan and his vampyres. What risk do they pose to Misthalin though?

steps.player: In Morytania, Drakan and his kin farm humans for their blood! People, my lord, like your own loyal subjects!
It's not just the citizens of Morytania at risk though. It seems that werewolves have been kidnapping people from this side of the Salve to be used as blood tithes for the vampyres!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This is awful! Yes, yes of course, we must do something!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: I would beg my lord not to give in so easily to his very compassionate nature. We know not if these people are loyal Saradomin supporters, my liege.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Oh yes, we need to consider that as well. You're right of course, Aeonisig. Do you know if these people follow Saradomin?

steps.player: I am not certain, but surely this isn't the issue? They are in dire need...

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: As are many, my young friend. Is the king meant to leave Misthalin unguarded on the whim of some errant adventurer?

steps.player: But you don't understand! It's not just about the people of Morytania. Like I say, there were werewolves in Misthalin!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I dare say you gave fight and slaughtered the foul beasts where they stood!

steps.player: I'm sad to say that I did not. I had no chance. I was knocked unconscious before I could properly react. Please, Misthalin must come to the aid of the people of Morytania.
The Myreque cannot fight this battle against the vampyres by themselves!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, yes! I will ready my army and prepare to enter Morytania via Paterdomus. Morytania has for too long threatened the borders of Misthalin.

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: My lord, this course of action will lead to very severe consequences! Your interference in Morytania will likely upset the balance and could send the world into another cataclysmic God War.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: But Drakan has invaded Misthalin! I must respond!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: There is no proof that Drakan has invaded Misthalin, my lord!

steps.player: Yes there is! I saw it with my own eyes!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Being knocked out by agents unknown does not constitute evidence. In fact, it's something that the most inexperienced of local folk could accomplish!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: But I can't just stand here and do nothing, Aeonisig! I must try to help if I can.

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: I am afraid with the Guthixian edicts regarding religious balance, there is little else we can do.

steps.player: Guthixian edicts?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Indeed. They were put in place by Guthix himself at the end of the God Wars. At least, so his followers claim. All of us must abide by them, lest the world fall into ruin again.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: What a load of tosh!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: An apt description, my lord. The edicts are likely to be little more than propaganda created by the followers of Guthix.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Well then what's the issue?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: The edicts need closer study before we can be sure.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: But that will take ages, we need to act now!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: As you say, it will take some time. We now pay the price for our lack of foresight in letting Guthixian edicts restrict the might of Saradomin's will.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, yes, but we can start to make amends for that now, can't we?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Yes sire, there are some papers to sign, but essentially we can start work on this right away.

steps.player: Signing papers! Is that the sum of the aid that Misthalin can provide to Morytania?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Hold your disrespectful tongue! How dare you address the king in that way? We should throw you in the stocks!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I am sorry, but Aeonisig is my advisor, and what he says, while it pains me, is the truth. However, I will enact a mercenary protocol.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This will allow all able-bodied men to fight in the defence of Misthalin for glory and spoils. You will find that many sword arms from Misthalin should soon join the resistance force.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: In the meantime, we will look into the Guthixian edicts and find a way to rid ourselves of Drakan for good.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: That is for you to decide, but I would assume that you'd want to report back to your comrades in Morytania.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: If they're relying on support from Misthalin, you'll need to let them know that it might take some time before that happens.

steps.player: So I came all this way for nothing?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Is it nothing then to have an audience with the king? Your lack of respect astonishes me. How you have survived so long with such disgraceful manners is nothing short of a miracle!

steps.player: Sorry. I had just hoped for so much more.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Well then, I must try to do something to satisfy you. I will have my advisor Aeonisig teleport you to Paterdomus so that you are more quickly on your way. Will you accept my offer?

options.text: Yes thanks. I'll accept the free teleport.

steps.player: Yes thanks. I'll accept the free teleport.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Very good. My advisor, Aeonisig, will teleport you back. The best of luck to you.

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Prepare yourself for teleport!
Aeonisig teleports you back to Paterdomus.

options.text: No thanks. I've other things to do here.
Why can't you send troops to Morytania?

steps.player: Why can't you send troops to Morytania?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: The Guthixian edicts supposedly exist to ensure a balance is kept when it comes to religious and spiritual beliefs in the world. At the moment, things are considered to be in balance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Misthalin is a Saradominist region, but Morytania is filled with creatures of Zamorak. A war between our two regions would be considered a war between Saradomin and Zamorak.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: If I send troops to Morytania, there is risk that the balance will be disrupted. Many followers of Guthix are apparently bound by oath to fight to keep the balance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: It is said that when all three sides are joined in war, Guthix will 'reawaken and remake the world without mercy for the pain of beast or man.'

steps.player: Is that really true?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Personally, I don't think so. However, Aeonisig does not feel we should risk it until we can do further research on the Guthixian edicts.

steps.player: What is a mercenary protocol?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: It means that people can fight with the blessings of the king in defence of the kingdom.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Normally, if a force is amassed, they may be considered a threat to Misthalin's national security. We'd have to send the army to disband them.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: However, a mercenary protocol allows a group to form a mercenary company. They are allowed certain rights so long as they operate within the law.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: The Guthixian edicts prevent us from doing too much at this point, but this situation in Morytania requires some action. Unfortunately, this is the best thing I can think of at the moment.

options.text: When can you send aid to Morytania?

steps.player: When can you send aid to Morytania?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: It depends on how long it takes the Church of Saradomin to read through the Guthixian edicts and return with an answer on how to proceed.

steps.player: What part does Guthix play in all this?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Guthixian edicts rule over those of all other religions. Many followers of Guthix claim that the edicts have largely controlled the peace that Misthalin has experienced for so many years.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Apparently, some followers of Guthix have sworn an oath to perform ceremonies to try and re-awaken Guthix if the edicts are broken.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: They say that peace and tolerance are needed to maintain the balance. I've no doubt it's all a load of rubbish, but we can't proceed until we are sure.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: Talk to the king about Morytania.
Does your offer of a teleport still stand?

steps.player: Does your offer of a teleport still stand?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Certainly, are you ready now?

options.text: Yes thanks. I'll accept the free teleport.

steps.player: Yes thanks. I'll accept the free teleport.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Very good. My advisor, Aeonisig, will teleport you back. The best of luck to you.

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Prepare yourself for teleport!
Aeonisig casts teleother on the player
The player arrives in the basement of Paterdomus Temple
Aeonisig teleports you back to Paterdomus.

options.text: No thanks. I've other things to do here.
I'd like to ask a few questions if I may?

steps.player: I'd like to ask a few questions if I may?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Certainly, go ahead.

options.text: Why can't you send troops to Morytania?
When can you send aid to Morytania?

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [player name]. Have you been to Varrock yet?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: I have. King Roald isn't able to send troops for our fight against the Drakans. Apparently, some Guthixian edicts need to be scrutinised in more detail or else the balance will be affected?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Oh dear! I once did some studying of the edicts. I can see why the king and his advisors are cautious.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The Myreque will need to know all that you have experienced so far. You should report to Veliaf when you can.

options.text: Can you explain a little about the Guthixian edicts?

steps.player: Can you explain a little about the Guthixian edicts?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well, only a little. The followers of Guthix make all sorts of wild claims where he is involved. Those of us who serve Saradomin know that these claims are mostly baseless.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: What we do know is that Guthix is a god of nature and balance. We believe him to be of average power. Enough to pay attention to, but nothing compared to the strength of Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It is said that long ago, back when the gods walked these lands with us, a great war was fought called the God Wars.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The stories say the war lasted for thousands of years and that the carnage saw the world forever changed.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The followers of Guthix claim that this war ended when Guthix awoke from his slumber and banished the other gods, leaving the world to mortals.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: This is likely not the true version of events. Guthixians also claim that it was Guthix himself who made the world. Obviously, that is not correct.

steps.player: So where do these edicts come in?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: They were apparently created at the end of the God Wars to ensure that the world never sees a conflict like that again.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The edicts state that no single god should be allowed to gain enough power to become dominant. Instead, a balance must be kept between the gods and their servants.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: If the balance is not kept, the followers of Guthix will try to intervene. If they are unable to restore balance, they will supposedly awaken Guthix from his slumber beneath the earth.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Once he awakens, they say he will remake the world, destroying civilisation as we know it.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It's just a story of course. All made up by the Guthixians to help them feel relevant.

steps.player: But if the edicts are just made up, what's the risk?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well when there's threats of the world being remade, you can't be too careful. It is wise to be cautious. After all, wisdom is one of Saradomin's greatest strengths.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: Of course. I plan to assist the forces of Saradomin who will come to our aid, and fight against the legions of vampyres that infest this foul place. These brave mercenaries shall need a guide.

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: When a guide arrives, I will aid the mercenary by holding their wealth for their eventual return. The mercenary will repay the guide by giving him a token for items which I am holding.

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: I shall give such items to the guide as payment for their services once I'm handed the token.

steps.player: What items will you hold?

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: Oh, the range of items is very varied. Mercenaries tend to hold raw materials in high esteem and so will deposit those with me. They also seem to be good bartering items.

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: Generally, things like uncooked lobsters, coal, silver bars, bow strings. Things which are useful! Plus the odd tome of experience, which are considered incredibly useful.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida-s.player: Hello there. What should I do now?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida-s.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-vertida-s.text: Myreque prevail, [player name]. You should have a chat with Safalaan. He may be able to help you.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Hello, Veliaf. I have some news for you.
I was attacked near the temple! On the other side of the Salve!
By beasts! From Morytania, I believe. Perhaps werewolves.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: The vampyres must be behind this! Did you speak with Roald yet? We need his support if we are to end this suffering.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: King Roald cannot send troops! I talked to him at great length and was unable to persuade him. His Saradominist advisor cited Guthixian edicts as the reason for not sending aid.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: Guthixian edicts? How do they prevent Roald from sending troops?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Apparently a war in Morytania will risk disturbing the balance between Saradomin and Zamorak so the Guthixians will need to intervene.
The Church of Saradomin is looking into it now to see if it's true.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: There has long been a desire by the Church of Saradomin to see Guthixian power eroded away. This stinks of politics. They're just using the situation here for their own gain!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Roald did agree to enact a mercenary protocol. He said it was the best he could offer for the moment without contravening the Guthixian edicts.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: Well that's something I guess. Not exactly what we were hoping for though.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: What should we do now? There must be someone else we can turn to?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: We must inform the Sanguinesti order of the Myreque of these events. Please go as fast as you can back to the Meiyerditch hideout and forward this information to them.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-ag.player: What do I need to do now?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-ag.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-ag.text: We must inform the Sanguinesti order of the Myreque of what we have learnt. Please go as fast as you can back to the Meiyerditch hideout and forward this information to them.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [player name]. How are things in Morytania?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Not as well as I'd hope, Drezel. I'm still working with the Myreque. I just hope that we can find a way to defeat those Drakans.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: You can be sure that a great many people hope for exactly the same thing, [player name]. Good luck to you, and Myreque prevail!

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Hello there.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Myreque prevail! What can I do for you?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: I have a message from Veliaf. It's bad news I'm afraid. I was sent on a mission to Misthalin to seek help from King Roald. Sadly, he isn't able to offer much support.
That's not all though. On my way to Varrock, I came across some beasts on the other side of the River Salve! I think they were werewolves working for the vampyres.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: This is disastrous! Things seem to go from bad to worse! You will have to communicate this information to our leader, Safalaan. He needs to know as soon as possible.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Where is Safalaan and what does he look like?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: He's out on a mission sketching Castle Drakan. He's taken the wall route so you'll need to do the same.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: There is a barricade that prevents further travel north. It's located under the wall. You'll need to search the wall southeast of the barricade to release the lock on the door.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Okay, great, that's helpful. Now, how can I recognise Safalaan?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: He's very distinctive. It shouldn't be a problem trying to find him if you know where to look, and you've got a good set of eyes on you!

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Anyway, I need to head towards the wall myself now, so you can come with me. It'll be quicker than going back on your own.

steps.player: Okay, lead the way.

steps.text: Vertida leads you through the ghetto.
The player is led through Meiyerditch to the building west of Trader Sven

steps.player: I'll make my own way.

steps.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
steps.text: I'll be here if you change your mind.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: You need to report to our leader, Safalaan. He's out on a mission sketching Castle Drakan. He's taken the wall route so you'll need to do the same.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: There is a barricade that prevents further travel north. It's located under the wall. You'll need to search the wall southeast of the barricade to release the lock on the door.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Okay, great, that's helpful. How can I recognise Safalaan?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: He's very distinctive. It shouldn't be a problem trying to find him if you know where to look, and you've got a good set of eyes on you!

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Vertida Sefalatis
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Anyway, I need to head towards the wall myself now, so you can come with me. It'll be quicker than going back on your own.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-starting.text: You try to open it, but it seems to be stuck fast. You seem to remember Vertida telling you something about nearby rocks?
You notice that the rocks seem to move. You push them in and hear a mechanical click.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: You must be Safalaan. My name is [player name]. I come with a very important message from Vertida.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Vertida, eh? What makes you think I know a Vertida?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: He's asked me to come and seek you out. I'm working with Veliaf in Burgh de Rott.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Ah, Veliaf! Myreque prevail! My friend, you're just the tonic for my otherwise dark mood. Tell me, what news comes from the west?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: I went to see King Roald to request support in our fight. Unfortunately, his advisor reminded him that the Guthixian edicts prevent his intervention.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Guthixian edicts? Sounds like excuses to me. I commend you on your efforts to rally support for our cause though.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: I'm afraid that's not all. I was attacked by beasts on the western side of the Salve, near to Paterdomus. I think they were werewolves working for the vampyres.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: This is terrible! Surely the magical influence of the Salve should be preventing that? What if the vampyres are able to cross as well? Drakan could start a full onslaught!

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: I must return to the base in order to discuss this information and work out what must be done.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Can I help in some way?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Yes, you certainly can, my friend. I was on a mission to scout out this castle. I have yet to start, but please could you take over for me?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: I can certainly try! Are there any specific details I should know?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Indeed there are. We need sketches of the northern, western, and southern sides of the castle.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: I've checked the vyrewatch flight patterns and I think you'll attract less attention if you make your way to the north and do that sketch first, then sketch the western side, and finally finish off here.
Safalaan gives you some charcoal and papyrus.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: One of the others has already marked the best spots to sketch from. If you need some more papyrus, you can get some off Old Man Ral. He's helped us out once or twice before.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Good luck, my friend. Return to the hideout when you have completed the sketches.

3 {{x}} papyrus

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Hello again!

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: Hello, Veliaf. I'm doing some work for the Sanguinesti Myreque.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Good. It seems like you're really proving your worth. Keep it up.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-attempti.text: You already have a sketch of the castle from this angle; you don't need a second one.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-attempti.player: I need to make a sketch of the western face of the castle.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: You start sketching...
The scene changes to a view of three vampyres talking over a tray of  blood tithe pouches

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: So yes, Lady Vanescula, we're getting maximum yield from the current rotation. And more tithes are coming in all the time.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanescula Drakan
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Good, good! You seem to be well in control.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: If I remember, madam, I had little choice. You were quite... 'persuasive' the last time we met.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanescula Drakan
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Ha, ha, ha. Vanstrom, you do make me laugh.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Perhaps a light refreshment m'lady? This is from the fresh batch.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanescula Drakan
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Why, with these blood tithes you're really spoiling us!

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Ranis Drakan
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Visciously efficient as ever, Vanstrom! You never fail to please us.
The vampyres devour some of their snack

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanescula Drakan
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Mmm, delicious! Well, it's been lovely as usual, Vanstrom.
Vanescula and Ranis transform to their vyre form

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanescula Drakan
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: But we really have to get on.
Vanstrom transforms to his vyre form

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanstrom Klause

The three fly off and the scene ends

Vanstrom Klause appears on the wall next to the player

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Ha! So we meet again, [player name]. Prepare to die!
(Vanstrom and the player fight, with the player unable to hit through Vanstrom's protection. The player is knocked out after taking five hits.)
Sarius Guile appears, overseeing Vanstrom and the downed player

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Sorry for the interruption, Lord Vanstrom, but Lady Vanescula 'requests' that this individual be questioned before being used as a punch bag.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: I take no orders from food sacks like you, Guile. Attend to this yourself. In any case, [he/she] wasn't much of a punch bag anyway.
Vanstrom departs

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Awaken! There are things for you to know.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Your life may be forfeit but for now you live. My mistress will understand my motives. She has an interest in the one called Safalaan.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: As a gesture for my intervening on your behalf, I'd take it as a kindness if you would deliver a message to him.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: The message you will find secreted behind tiles where smoke is carried away from the depiction of statuesque evil.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: And now be away, but forget not the task that Safalaan set you! For why else would you be here?
Sarius departs
