showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: The surface is a strange and wonderful place! We should embrace it, not shut ourselves off!

showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.speaker: Zanik
showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: And not all surface-dwellers are bad. Without [player name] the city would have been destroyed for sure!

showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.speaker: Ur-tag
showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: [player name], we are in your debt once again.

showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.speaker: Ur-tag
showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: The council has voted that, if Zanik's recommendation was positive, humans from Lumbridge should be allowed into the city. You may now enter Dorgesh-Kaan!

showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.speaker: Zanik
showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: This is brilliant! I'm sure you won't regret this!

showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.speaker: Zanik
showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: Thank you for taking me on that adventure, [player name]! I'll show you how to use the bone crossbow like I promised I would!
Zanik shows you how to use the bone crossbow's special attack.

showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.speaker: Zanik
showdown-with-sigmund-leaving-through-th.text: Come find me in the city if you ever want to chat, [player name]. I'm going to go and think about what Juna said about my destiny. I don't know what it will involve, but I have a feeling we will adventure together again!
If the player left the water mill cellar without a light source:

steps.text: Zanik gives you a torch so you can see.

pk0FnR.speaker: Zanik
pk0FnR.text: I'll wait for you back in the castle then.

standard-dialogue-before-completing-sins.npc: You don't seem very sure. We don't want any infected near the children. Be off with you!

standard-dialogue-after-completing-sins-.npc: Whatever it is you're selling, we ain't interested!

steps.npc: Sorry, reckon I won't be doing business with you. Not 'til Cormac trusts you, at least.

No thanks.

after-completing-fallen-from-grace.npc: Can I help you at all?

No thanks.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: If the player did not speak to Elias at the Uzer Oasis prior to 21 February 2024:

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Good day to you.

steps.player: What brings you here?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The eternal quest for knowledge, of course! The name's Elias White. I'm something of an explorer.

steps.player: Pleased to meet you. I'm [player name]. So you're searching for knowledge in an inn?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Not exactly. In fact, I was previously hunting down information on an ancient race deep within the desert.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: However, I received an interesting yet concerning tip- off from a contact of mine regarding some of my research. I came here to investigate for myself.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: If the player spoke to Elias at the Uzer Oasis before 21 February 2024:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Oh, hello there. You look familiar. Have we met before?

steps.player: I think so. The name's [player name]. You're Elias, right? You had a camp out near Uzer.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Ah, of course. You offered to help with my work, didn't you? I'm still very keen to take you up on that offer at some point, but a more pressing matter has delayed that somewhat.

steps.player: Is that what's brought you here?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed. I recived an interesting yet concerning tip-off from a contact of mine regarding some of my research. I came here to investigate for myself.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: If the player does not meet the quest's requirements:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: How kind of you to offer. I'm not in need of any extra help right now though.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: If the player meets the quest's requirements:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: How kind of you to offer. I definitely wouldn't complain about some extra support, if you're sure you're interested?

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.prompt: Start the Defender of Varrock quest?

steps.player: Absolutely! So what was this tip-off you received?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: It's nothing much, but apparently one of the patrons in here was ranting and raving about zombies. Most just dismissed him as having had one too many, but I'm not so sure.

steps.player: How come?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Varrock has an interesting history when it comes to zombies. Tell me, what do you know of Arrav?

steps.player: Arrav? As in the Shield of Arrav? I was the one who helped return it to the museum.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Ah, I heard about that. Excellent work! You may well know then that the former owner of that shield, Arrav himself, once defended Varrock against a zombie invasion led by a Mahjarrat named Zemouregal.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Arrav sacrificed himself to save his city, but Zemouregal survived.

steps.player: And you think these zombie sightings mean he's returned?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Apparently the zombies were seen forming ranks. Zombies don't naturally organise themselves, so someone must be organising them. I can think of worse candidates than Zemouregal.

steps.player: I can see why you think this is worth looking into. Where do we start?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Zombies are not particularly light on their feet, so my hope is we can pick up their trail. The sightings were apparently right outside the inn.

steps.player: Follow the tracks and see where they came from. Good plan.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Then shall we get started?

steps.player: Ready when you are.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Excellent! I'm right behind you.
(Elias begins to follow the player.)

steps.player: Let's get going.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Lead the way.

options.text: What can you tell me about Arrav and Zemouregal?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Arrav and Zemouregal?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: It's quite the tale and I doubt I'd be able to do it justice, but I can try and give you an overview.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Back in the Fourth Age, a group of travellers came upon an abandoned child. It is said the child was unusual for one so young. Dark eyes and a fierce countenance, yet fair hair and skin, with a kind smile.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The travellers saw this as an omen and set up camp where they found him. The camp soon grew into the town of Avarrocka, or Varrock as we now call it.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: As for the child, he grew to become a mighty hero. After defending the town from a goblin attack, he took on the name Arrav, a curse word in goblin tongue, for he had become the Curse of Goblins.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Arrav's heroic deeds continued, until he was granted a vision of the future. He saw the Mahjarrat Zemouregal claiming Avarrocka as his own.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Determined to stop Zemouregal in any way he could, Arrav set out to find a powerful weapon with which to best him. His journey took him to the Imcando Dwarves, who granted him a powerful shield.

steps.player: The Shield of Arrav?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Exactly. With the shield in hand, Arrav returned home and faced off against Zemouregal and his zombie horde. Thanks to him, the invasion was repelled, but at the cost of Arrav's life.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Zemouregal has not been seen since, but it is said that his last act before retreating was to claim Arrav's body, promising to turn him into an undead slave to one day return with.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Hundreds of years have now passed, and while there are few who haven't heard of Arrav, many have forgotten Zemouregal and his promise.

options.text: So what exactly is it you're researching?

steps.player: So what exactly is it you're researching?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The Mahjarrat. It's fair to say they are quite the subject of fascination for me. Many of them once held dominion over huge parts of the world. Zamorak himself was a Mahjarrat, and he managed to achieve godhood!

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: But now, they've all but vanished! Most will go through their whole lives without ever seeing one, and their most common appearance these days is in the spooky stories parents use to keep their children in line.

steps.player: And that's why you're so interested in Zemouregal?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed. An actual Mahjarrat, and a very dangerous one at that. Ancient tomes can only teach us so much. If I want to learn everything there is to know about their race, it's going to take some more hands on work.

steps.player: What about the danger?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Well that's just all the more reason for me to be here. If Zemouregal is planning a new attack on Varrock, an expert on his race might come in quite useful.

options.text: If you're an explorer, I'm guessing you travel a lot?

steps.player: If you're an explorer, I'm guessing you travel a lot?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed! From the frozen wastes of the north to the ancient tombs of the desert, I've seen it all.

steps.player: So where do you call home?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: I've lived in many places over the years, but I wouldn't really say I have a home. I guess here in Varrock would be the closest answer.

steps.player: Sounds like you have quite the history.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Oh yes! If nothing else, I've definitely lived a varied life.

steps.player: So you weren't always an explorer?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Not at all. I've done all sorts of things in my time. In fact, at one point I was an adventurer like you!

steps.player: What happened? Some sort of life-changing injury?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Thankfully not. I just found that when it came to my work, it was the history I discovered that interested me more than the treasure.

steps.player: Fair enough.

options.text: I need to do something else.

steps.player: I need to do something else.

options.text: I need to do something else first.

steps.player: I need to do something else first.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Very well. I'll be here when you're ready.

steps.player: Actually, I think I'll pass.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Very well. If you change your mind, I'll be here.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.player: Hello again. So what was this tip-off you received?

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: It's nothing much, but apparently one of the patrons in here was ranting and raving about zombies. Most just dismissed him as having had one too many, but I'm not so sure.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: Ready to get back to it? My hope is we can pick up the trail left by those zombies right outside the inn.

options.text: Do you have that key we found?
options.condition: If the player has given the grubby key to Elias:

steps.player: Do you have that key we found?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: I do indeed. Don't worry, I'll look after it until we need it.

options.text: I need to do something else.

steps.player: I need to do something else.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Very well. I'll meet you back at the Jolly Boar Inn.

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.text: I'll meet you back at the Jolly Boar Inn, [player name].

organised-zombies-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White

organised-zombies-inspecting-the-plant-n.text: Look! Footprints. Let's see where they lead us.

organised-zombies-inspecting-any-incorre.text: Nothing seems out of place here.

organised-zombies-inspecting-the-correct.text: The bush has been disturbed recently. Something came this way.

organised-zombies-inspecting-the-plant-w.speaker: Elias White
organised-zombies-inspecting-the-plant-w.text: A key? I wonder what it opens... Best we keep a hold of it and find out.

organised-zombies-destroying-the-grubby-.speaker: Elias White
organised-zombies-destroying-the-grubby-.text: Why are you trying to destroy that? We need it. I can look after it for you if you want?

organised-zombies-opening-the-trapdoor.player: Only one way to find out...

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-z.speaker: Elias White
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-z.text: Then let's look around and find out!

the-infamous-necromancer-talking-to-elia.speaker: Elias White

the-infamous-necromancer-killing-an-armo.text: A strange red mist rises from the dying zombie.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Sharathteerk
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Zemouregal, this magical mist feels like it's corroding my insides. This seems like a bad idea...

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Nonsense! The mist has no side effects. Besides, it's essential for the new security system. Everyone needs to be imbued with it if they wish to pass through any doors or gates in the base.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Now, what news do you bring from the north?

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Sharathteerk
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Your cousin grows unusually strong. We should consider allying ourselves to him, maybe even combine forces.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Combine forces? I won't hear of it! Lucien would never enter into such an arrangement unless he were the one in control, and I have no desire to serve at his behest.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Besides, Lucien isn't the only one with powerful resources...

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Elias White
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Arrav. So the stories are true. The legendary hero of Avarrocka, now the slave of a disgusting necromancer.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: After many long years, it is time for Arrav to take command of my zombie troops. And on that note, come, let us inspect the forces.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Elias White
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: I see it's just as I suspected. Zemouregal is the one responsible for our zombie gatherings. We should inform the authorities in Varrock at once.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.player: What about the rest of this place? There could be more useful information to uncover here.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Elias White
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: True. Perhaps it would be wise for us to split up.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.player: Sounds like a plan. You head to Varrock and let them know what we've found so far. I'll keep exploring.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Elias White
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Very well. I'll meet you in the palace once you're done. Be careful.
There doesn't seem to be a lot going on down there.

the-infamous-necromancer-opening-the-fir.text: If the player does not have any bottles of red mist:

steps.text: The gate is locked.

the-infamous-necromancer-opening-the-fir.text: If the player has less than three bottles of red mist:

steps.text: The gate seems to respond to the mist bottles you're carrying, but it remains locked. Perhaps more are needed.

the-infamous-necromancer-opening-the-fir.text: If the player has three bottles of red mist:

steps.text: The gate absorbs the mist from the bottles you're carrying, unlocking in the process.

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.speaker: Arrav
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.text: You... You must leave this place. It's too... urgh...

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.speaker: Arrav
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.text: ... too dangerous for the likes of you here.

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.player: Arrav? But how are you... Are you fighting Zemouregal's control?

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.speaker: Arrav
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.text: My body is... under his control. I can sometimes manage to speak when Zemouregal's concentration is elsewhere, but even then, it's... painful. My mind, however... gahh...

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.speaker: Arrav
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.text: ... is still intact. He left it that way. He wanted me to feel the horror when I... urgh...

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.player: I'm so sorry, Arrav. There must be some way I can help you. What can I do?

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.speaker: Arrav
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.text: My heart... He has it. That's how he... how he... arrgh...

the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.speaker: Arrav
the-infamous-necromancer-upon-entering-t.text: I'm sorry, he calls to me. I must go. Please, leave... Leave before you...

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Sharathteerk
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: I'm telling you, he may be close to finding it.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Enough! I don't have time to worry about fairy tales.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Sharathteerk
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: But think of the power...

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Do you not think that I am all too aware of the power? You couldn't begin to imagine what I'd do to have it for myself! But I am also all too aware of what happens to those who try to claim it.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: If that is the fate Lucien wishes for himself, then he is welcome to it. In the meantime, we will focus on more practical endeavours. This is our last chance before the time comes to head north.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Sharathteerk
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Your forces are ready, Zemouregal.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Then let us waste no more time. Begin the final preparations.

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.speaker: Zemouregal
the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.text: Soon, the Mahjarrat will hold dominion over these lands once more. Varrock will be mine. Arrav cannot save his people this time. He can only watch as he himself seals their fate!

the-infamous-necromancer-looking-over-th.player: This isn't good. I'd better get to Varrock right away!

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Ah, there you are. How did things go after I left you?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.player: Not good. Zemouregal is nearly ready to begin another attack on Varrock.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Then it's just as I feared. I've already reported our discovery to Captain Rovin. Come, let's fill him in on everything else you've learnt.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: About time, adventurer. Your companion here tells me we have a zombie army on our doorstep!

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: I'm afraid that's not all, Captain. [player name] has made some further discoveries.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.player: Indeed. Zemouregal plans to have Arrav lead the zombies in an attack on Varrock, and he plans to do so very soon.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Zemouregal attacking Varrock again is our greatest fear and worst nightmare. And to think he now has Arrav under his control as well... What a horrifying fate for our greatest hero.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.player: There may still be hope for Arrav. While spying on Zemouregal, I came face to face with him. He may serve Zemouregal, but not willingly. His mind is still his own.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: A zombie with his mind intact... Most zombies are mere husks, their souls having long departed their bodies. For one to still be sentient is highly unusual. Could it mean...

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Oh, nothing to worry about now. Still, we may be able to work with this. What did Arrav have to say to you?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.player: He told me that Zemouregal has his heart.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: His heart? Interesting... Could that be how Zemouregal is controlling him?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: What are you saying? Does this mean we might be able to save Arrav?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: In the long term, potentially. But this will require a fair amount of research. Something I fear we have little time for right now.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Well then what other options do we have?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Well thanks to our good friend here, we have the very shield that was used to stop Zemouregal the first time he attacked.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: The Shield of Arrav? But is it really any use? Despite our attempts, we've never been able to unlock its power. Could it be that the legends were exaggerated and that it's just an ordinary shield?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: To answer that, our best bet would likely be to seek out the creators of the shield: The Imcando Dwarves of Camdozaal.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Hmm... but are the Imcando not extinct now?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.player: Not quite. There are still a few out there, including one in Camdozaal. Ramarno is his name.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white.text: Well then what are we waiting for? [player name], speak to this Ramarno and seek his advice on how to use the shield to defend our city. In the meantime, we will prepare our defences.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.text: About time, adventurer. Your companion here tells me we have a zombie army on our doorstep!

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.speaker: Elias White
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.text: You'd better head over to Camdozaal, [player name]. Time is not on our side.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.text: Adventurer. Have you been to Camdozaal yet?

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-elias-white-.player: No, not yet. I'll be on my way shortly.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-ramarno.speaker: Ramarno
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-ramarno.text: Ah, [player name]. I'm sure you have plenty of questions. I will do my best to answer them.

options.text: I need your help with a shield.

steps.player: I need your help with a shield.

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: A shield? What kind of shield?

steps.player: The Shield of Arrav. We've discovered that Zemouregal intends to attack the city of Varrock with a zombie army. It was the shield that stopped him last time.

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: Ah, and you are hoping to use it to do so again. I wish I could help you, but I know little of the shield and its power. It was created far before my time.

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: Still, I may have a way for you to learn what you need.

steps.player: How?

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: The Sacred Forge of course!

steps.player: But how will a forge help me?

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: The Sacred Forge is far more than a mere furnace! It is a powerful relic from a time when the gods still walked these lands.

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: Before Camdozaal's ruin, our sages would use the forge to guide our people. It is said the forge granted them access to the Dream Theatre, a place where they were blessed with visions of the past, present and future.

steps.player: I see. So how do I access this Dream Theatre?

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: The Forge will need powering, but normal barronite won't work for this. You'll need to obtain some imbued barronite. With that, provided the forge deems you worthy, you will be able to enter the Dream Theatre.

steps.player: And how do I get imbued barronite?

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: Head to the mines and mine yourself a barronite deposit. Once you have that, imbue it using the core of a chaos golem from the golem workshop.

options.text: What happened to the other Imcando Dwarves?
Never mind, I have no questions for now.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-ramarno-talk.speaker: Ramarno
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-ramarno-talk.text: Ah, [player name]. I'm sure you have plenty of questions. I will do my best to answer them.

options.text: How do I access the Dream Theatre?

steps.player: How do I access the Dream Theatre?

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: You'll need to obtain some imbued barronite. Head to the mines and mine yourself a barronite deposit. Once you have that, imbue it using the core of a chaos golem from the golem workshop.

options.text: What happened to the other Imcando Dwarves?
Never mind, I have no questions for now.

the-sacred-forge-imbuing-the-barronite.text: You imbue the barronite deposit using the chaos core.

the-sacred-forge-talking-to-ramarno-afte.speaker: Ramarno
the-sacred-forge-talking-to-ramarno-afte.text: Ah, [player name]. I'm sure you have plenty of questions. I will do my best to answer them.

options.text: I have something I'd like you to examine.
How do I access the Dream Theatre?

steps.player: How do I access the Dream Theatre?

steps.speaker: Ramarno
steps.text: I see you've got the imbued barronite. Just place it into the Sacred Forge. Provided the forge deems you worthy, you'll then be able to enter the Dream Theatre.

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.speaker: Arrav
the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.text: What is this? I feel... free. I can speak without pain. How is this possible?

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.player: We don't have much time. I'm talking to you from the Imcando Dream Theatre. I need to know how to use your shield.

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.speaker: Arrav
the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.text: The shield... of course. What do you need to know?

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.player: You used the shield to defeat Zemouregal's army before. How can we do it again?

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.speaker: Arrav
the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.text: It was not I who used the shield. When I faced Zemouregal, I cast the shield to the son of Avarrocka's founder. Only then did the zombies meet their doom.

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.speaker: Arrav
the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.text: It was his blood. The shield is tied to Avarrocka. Only one with the blood of the founder can use it.

the-sacred-forge-inside-the-dream-theatr.player: So if I can find his descendant...

the-true-descendant-talking-to-diminthei.text: If the player has completed Family Pest:

steps.player: Hello Dimintheis.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: I will not forget what you did for my family, [player name]. Those 500,000 coins have allowed us to put food on the table.

steps.player: That's no problem.

options.text: Could I get another pair of gauntlets?
I need your help with the zombie invasion.
The gauntlets are a family heirloom?

the-true-descendant-talking-to-diminthei.text: If the player has not completed Family Pest:

options.text: Have you got any quests for me?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: You have my eternal gratitude for all you have done in saving my family's honour, adventurer. Perhaps some day my sons will overcome their differences.

options.text: Do you have any gauntlets for me?
I need your help with the zombie invasion.

steps.player: I need your help with the zombie invasion.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: You want me to use the shield? It seems to be responding to me in some way! Is this what you were expecting?

steps.player: I think so! Quick, let's get to the palace!

steps.text: (Cutscene begins.)

the-true-descendant-talking-to-diminthei.text: If the player has completed Family Pest:

steps.player: Hello Dimintheis.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis

the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.text: A cutscene begins in which Dimintheis, wielding the shield, arrives at Varrock Palace.
Dimintheis unleashes the shield's power, instantly killing the zombies in the vicinity. The scene then changes to the imprisoned Monk of Zamorak, who has broken out.
The shield's power destroys the zombies inside the palace.
The scene changes to the palace garden.

the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.text: Stay back! I won't let you eat me!
The shield's power destroys the zombies in the garden. The scene then changes to the broken wall north of the palace.

the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.speaker: Sharathteerk
the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.text: Zemouregal... The forces... What do we do?

the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.speaker: Zemouregal
the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.text: What do we do? We flee, you fool!

the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.speaker: Zemouregal
the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.text: Do you have a better suggestion? Are you hiding some secret to overcoming such an astounding disaster?

the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.speaker: Zemouregal
the-true-descendant-defeating-the-zombie.text: Then recall Arrav at once! There is nothing more to be gained here. It is time for us to head north.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: It seems the shield worked better than anyone could have hoped for. From what we can tell, not a single zombie remains! It was a close one, but thanks to you, Varrock is saved!

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.player: It wouldn't have been possible without Dimintheis.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: Indeed. I will ensure the King is made aware of his contribution.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.player: Any word on what happened to Zemouregal?

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: There's been no sign of him so far. We'll keep an eye out, but I suspect he'll have gone to ground.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.player: And he'll have Arrav with him.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Elias White
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: We may not have been able to save Arrav today, but thanks to your discoveries, we now have a lead to follow. It will take me some time, but once I have something on this heart business, I'll be in touch.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Elias White
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: And on that note, I intend to get started right away. Until we meet again.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: Well once again, adventurer, on behalf of Varrock, you have my thanks. Today's victory will go down in history.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-true-descendant-talking-to-elias-or-.text: Now, you'd best be on your way. I have lots of work to do, and I'm sure you have better places to be than here.

the-true-descendant-talking-to-captain-r.speaker: Captain Rovin
the-true-descendant-talking-to-captain-r.text: Well once again, adventurer, on behalf of Varrock, you have my thanks. Today's victory will go down in history.

post-quest-dialogue-captain-rovin.speaker: Captain Rovin
post-quest-dialogue-captain-rovin.text: Oh, it's you. Thank you again for your help in defeating the zombie army.

post-quest-dialogue-captain-rovin.speaker: Captain Rovin
post-quest-dialogue-captain-rovin.text: Now, you must excuse me. I have lots to do.

post-quest-dialogue-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
post-quest-dialogue-elias-white.text: Ah, hello there, [player name]. Good to see you.
If the player did not speak to Elias at the Uzer Oasis prior to 21 February 2024:

steps.player: And you, Elias. So what brings you all the way out here?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Well it turns out the desert was the best place to begin my research into Arrav and his heart. Not too surprising of course, given the burial practices here.

steps.player: And how's that going so far?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Pretty well. In fact, I think I'm getting close to something. It's related to that old mastaba up on the plateau. I reckon it might contain the knowledge we need to help old Arrav out.

post-quest-dialogue-elias-white.text: If the player spoke to Elias at the Uzer Oasis before 21 February 2024:

steps.player: And you, Elias. So you're back out here again?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed. Turns out the desert was the best place to begin my research into Arrav and his heart. Not too surprising of course, given the burial practices here.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: In fact, as you might recall, I was here before to look into that old mastaba up on the plateau.

steps.player: Yes, I remember. You said it might contain important information on the Mahjarrat.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed I did. And I reckon it might also contain the knowledge we need to help old Arrav out.

post-quest-dialogue-elias-white.speaker: Elias White
post-quest-dialogue-elias-white.text: Now, I still have quite a bit of preparatory work to do before we consider heading inside, but once that's done, I'll be in touch.

post-quest-dialogue-elias-white.player: Sounds good. I'd best leave you to your work.

JW6I-J.speaker: Elias White
JW6I-J.text: You're back. Have you managed to make any progress?

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello, no-fur. What are you doing in my mistress's garden?

steps.player: Looking for sq'irks.

steps.npc: If it's sq'irks you're after then you've come to the right place. We've got four seasons' worth of them.

steps.player: I've a couple of questions.

steps.npc: I'd be happy to help a friend of the feline.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: The Sphinx gave you that amulet, so she must hold you in high regard.

steps.player: If I remember correctly, it was the High Priest of Sophanem who gave it to me.

steps.npc: He and the Sphinx are as thick as thieves, but regardless, I think you've a bit of a cat feel about you.
Now what are these questions?

options.text: What are the creatures inside the gardens?

steps.player: What are the creatures inside the gardens?

steps.npc: Oh, you mean the gardeners?

steps.player: The strange, floaty creatures.

steps.npc: Yes, the gardeners. Don't let them see you or they'll teleport you out here. They're very protective of their crops.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.

options.text: How do you get into the seasonal gardens?

steps.player: How do you get into the seasonal gardens?

steps.npc: I get in through gaps in the hedge. You are a little too big to squeeze through. I think you'll have to use the gates.
I think the gates are locked, so you'll have to have good Thieving skills to get in.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.

options.text: How is it that the gardens are in different seasons?

steps.player: How is it that the gardens are in different seasons?

steps.npc: How did you get here?

steps.player: Magic?

steps.npc: Exactly. The Sorceress likes to have a good supply of in-season sq'irks and herbs at all times.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.

options.text: How do I get out of here?

steps.player: How do I get out of here?

steps.npc: Take a drink from the fountain.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.
Talking to cats.

steps.npc: A noble and rewarding past-time.

steps.player: How did you get here?

steps.npc: Every time I play with spiders in the Sorceress's house, her silly apprentice completely freaks out and teleports me here!

steps.player: So you've been stuck here since?

steps.npc: No, silly! I drink from the fountain whenever I want to leave.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.
What are you doing here?

steps.npc: I get this strange urge for sq'irks. It's quite peculiar. I think I may be addicted.

steps.player: I think I know someone else who may be in a similar position.

steps.npc: Don't tell me. Osman, right?

steps.player: You know him too?

steps.npc: Oh, he used to come here all the time. Then one day, he just stopped.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.
Who are you?

steps.npc: Del-Monty the cat, at your service.

steps.player: Are you a famous adventurer who was turned into a cat by a vindictive mage?

steps.npc: No; as I said, I'm Del-Monty the cat, connoisseur of exotic fruits.

steps.player: In that case, can you tell me anything about sq'irks?

steps.npc: But of course! Their juice is an excellent source of energy for runners, and in the riper varieties they are known to heighten one's Thieving abilities.

options.text: Thanks, I have another question though.

steps.player: Thanks, I have another question though.
Thanks for your help.
Nothing much.

steps.npc: Yawn! Nice talking to you then, no-fur.
You interested in buying some ores?

steps.player: Yes please.
No thanks.

steps.npc: Move along then please.

starting-demon-slayer.speaker: Aris
starting-demon-slayer.text: Hello young one. Cross my palm with silver and the future will be revealed to you.
If the player doesn't have any money with them:

steps.player: Oh dear. I don't have any money.
Okay, here you go.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Come closer, and listen carefully to what the future holds for you, as I peer into the swirling mists of the crystal ball.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I can see images forming. I can see you.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: You are holding a very impressive looking sword. I'm sure I recognise that sword...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: There is a big dark shadow appearing now.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Aaargh!

steps.player: Are you all right?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: It's Delrith! Delrith is coming!

steps.player: Who's Delrith?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Delrith...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Delrith is a powerful demon.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Oh! I really hope he didn't see me looking at him through my crystal ball!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: He tried to destroy this city 150 years ago. He was stopped just in time by the great hero Wally.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Using his magic sword Silverlight, Wally managed to trap the demon in the stone circle just south of this city.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ye gods! Silverlight was the sword you were holding in my vision! You are the one destined to stop the demon this time.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

options.text: How am I meant to fight a demon who can destroy cities?

steps.player: How am I meant to fight a demon who can destroy cities?!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: If you face Delrith while he is still weak from being summoned, and use the correct weapon, you will not find the task too arduous.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Do not fear. If you follow the path of the great hero Wally, then you are sure to defeat the demon.

options.text: Okay, where is he? I'll kill him for you!

steps.player: Okay, where is he? I'll kill him for you!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ah, the overconfidence of the young!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Delrith can't be harmed by ordinary weapons. You must face him using the same weapon that Wally used.

options.text: Wally doesn't sound like a very heroic name.

steps.player: Wally doesn't sound a very heroic name.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes I know. Maybe that is why history doesn't remember him. However he was a very great hero.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Who knows how much pain and suffering Delrith would have brought forth without Wally to stop him!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: It looks like you are going to need to perform similar heroics.

options.text: So how did Wally kill Delrith?

steps.player: So how did Wally kill Delrith?

steps.text: A cutscene showing Wally defeating Delrith plays.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Wally managed to arrive at the stone circle just as Delrith was summoned by a cult of chaos druids...

steps.speaker: Wally
steps.text: Die, foul demon!

steps.speaker: Wally
steps.text: Now, what was that incantation again?
The following five words are Aber, Gabindo, Purchai, Camerinthum, and Carlem. The order of the five words is random.

steps.speaker: Wally
steps.text: [word 1]... [word 2]... [word 3]... [word 4]... [word 5]!

steps.speaker: Wally
steps.text: I am the greatest demon slayer EVER!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: By reciting the correct magical incantation, and thrusting Silverlight into Delrith while he was newly summoned, Wally was able to imprison Delrith in the stone block in the centre of the circle.
Cutscene ends.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Delrith will come forth from the stone circle again.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I would imagine an evil sorcerer is already starting on the rituals to summon Delrith as we speak.

options.text: How am I meant to fight a demon who can destroy cities?
Okay, where is he? I'll kill him for you!

steps.player: What is the magical incantation?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Oh yes, let me think a second...
The following five words Aber, Gabindo, Purchai, Camerinthum, and Carlem

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Alright, I think I've got it now, it goes.... [word 1]... [word 2]... [word 3]... [word 4]... [word 5]. Have you got that?

steps.player: I think so, yes.
Where can I find Silverlight?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Silverlight has been passed down through Wally's descendants. I believe it is currently in the care of one of the King's knights called Sir Prysin.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: He shouldn't be too hard to find. He lives in the royal palace in this city. Tell him Aris sent you.

options.text: Okay, thanks. I'll do my best to stop the demon.

steps.player: Ok thanks. I'll do my best to stop the demon.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Good luck, and may Guthix be with you!
Demon Slayer is started.

steps.player: No, I don't believe in that stuff.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ok suit yourself.

starting-demon-slayer-aris-after-startin.speaker: Aris
starting-demon-slayer-aris-after-startin.text: Well if you need any advice I'm always here, young one.

steps.player: Stop calling me that!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: In the scheme of things you are very young.

options.text: Ok but how old are you?

steps.player: Ok, but how old are you?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Count the number of legs on the stools in the Blue Moon inn, and multiply that number by seven.

steps.player: Er, yeah, whatever.

options.text: Oh if it's in the scheme of things that's ok.

steps.player: Oh if it's in the scheme of things that's ok.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: You show wisdom for one so young.

options.text: Well I'd better press on with it.
I am a mighty adventurer. Who are you?

steps.player: I am a mighty adventurer, who are you?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I am Sir Prysin. A bold and famous knight of the realm.

options.text: I'm not sure, I was hoping you could tell me.

steps.player: I was hoping you could tell me.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Well I've never met you before.

options.text: Aris said I should come and talk to you.
options.condition: If Demon Slayer is started:

steps.player: Aris said I should come and talk to you.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Aris? Is she still alive? I remember her from when I was pretty young. Well what do you need to talk to me about?

steps.player: I need to find Silverlight.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: What do you need to find that for?

steps.player: I need it to fight Delrith.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Delrith? I thought the world was rid of him, thanks to my great-grandfather.

options.text: Well, Aris' crystal ball seems to think otherwise.

steps.player: Well Aris' crystal ball seems to think otherwise.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Well if the ball says so, I'd better help you.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: The problem is getting Silverlight.

steps.player: You mean you don't have it?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Oh I do have it, but it is so powerful that the king made me put it in a special box which needs three different keys to open it. That way it won't fall into the wrong hands.

steps.player: So give me the keys!

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Um, well, it's not so easy.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I kept one of the keys. I gave the other two to other people for safe keeping.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: One I gave to Rovin, the captain of the palace guard.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I gave the other to the wizard Traiborn.

options.text: Can you give me your key?

steps.player: Can you give me your key?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Well there's a problem there as well.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I managed to drop the key in the drain just outside the palace kitchen. It is just inside and I can't reach it.

options.text: So what does the drain lead to?

steps.player: So what does the drain connect to?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: It is the drain for the drainpipe running from the sink in the kitchen down to the palace sewers.

options.text: Where can I find Captain Rovin?
Well I'd better go key hunting.

steps.player: Well I'd better go key hunting.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Ok, goodbye.

options.text: Where can I find Captain Rovin?
Where can I find Captain Rovin?

steps.player: Where can I find Captain Rovin?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Captain Rovin lives at the top of the guards' quarters in the north-west wing of this palace.

options.text: Can you give me your key?
Well I'd better go key hunting.

steps.player: Where does the wizard live?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Wizard Traiborn?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: He is one of the wizards who lives in the tower on the little island just off the south coast. I believe his quarters are on the first floor of the tower.

options.text: Can you give me your key?
Where can I find Captain Rovin?
Well I'd better go key hunting.
And why is this a problem?

steps.player: And why is this a problem?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I kept one of the keys. I gave the other two to other people for safe keeping.

options.text: He's back and unfortunately I've got to deal with him.

steps.player: He's back and unfortunately I've got to deal with him.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: You don't look up to much. I suppose Silverlight may be good enough to carry you through though.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: The problem is getting Silverlight.

steps.player: You mean you don't have it?
Yes she is still alive. She lives right outside the castle!

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Oh, is that the same Aris? I would have thought she would have died by now. She was pretty old when I was a lad.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Anyway, what can I do for you?

steps.player: I need to find Silverlight.

sir-prysin-talking-to-sir-prysin-again-b.speaker: Sir Prysin
sir-prysin-talking-to-sir-prysin-again-b.text: So how are you doing with getting the keys?

sir-prysin-talking-to-sir-prysin-again-b.player: I haven't found any of them yet.

options.text: Can you remind me where all the keys were again?

steps.player: Can you remind me where all the keys were again?

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I kept one of the keys. I gave the other two to other people for safe keeping.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: One I gave to Rovin, the captain of the palace guard.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: I gave the other to the wizard Traiborn.

options.text: Can you give me your key?
Where can I find Captain Rovin?

steps.player: I'm still looking.

steps.speaker: Sir Prysin
steps.text: Ok, tell me when you've got them all.

sir-prysin-returning-to-sir-prysin-with-.speaker: Sir Prysin
sir-prysin-returning-to-sir-prysin-with-.text: So how are you doing with getting the keys?
If the player has the key from Captain Rovin:

steps.player: I've got the key from Captain Rovin.

sir-prysin-returning-to-sir-prysin-with-.text: If the player has the key from Wizard Traiborn:

steps.player: I've got the key from Wizard Traiborn.

sir-prysin-returning-to-sir-prysin-with-.text: If the player has the key from the drain:

steps.player: I've got the key which you dropped down the drain.

sir-prysin-talking-to-sir-prysin-with-tw.speaker: Sir Prysin
sir-prysin-talking-to-sir-prysin-with-tw.text: So how are you doing with getting the keys?
If the player has keys from Traiborn and Rovin:

steps.player: I've got the keys from Wizard Traiborn and Captain Rovin.

steps.player: I've got the key from Captain Rovin and the one that you dropped down the drain.

sir-prysin-talking-to-sir-prysin-with-tw.text: If the player has keys from Traiborn and the drain:

steps.player: I've got the key from Wizard Traiborn and the one that you dropped down the drain.

getting-the-key-from-captain-rovin.speaker: Captain Rovin
getting-the-key-from-captain-rovin.text: What are you doing up here? Only the palace guards are allowed up here.

options.text: I am one of the palace guards.
Yes I know, but this is important.

steps.player: Yes, I know, but this is important.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: Ok, I'm listening. Tell me what's so important.

options.text: There's a demon who wants to invade this city.

steps.player: There's a demon who wants to invade the city.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: Is it a powerful demon?

steps.player: Not really.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: Well, I'm sure the palace guards can deal with it, then. Thanks for the information.

steps.player: Yes, very.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: As good as the palace guards are, I don't know if they're up to taking on a very powerful demon.

options.text: Yeah, the palace guards are rubbish!

steps.player: Yeah, the palace guards are rubbish!

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: Yeah, they're--

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: Wait! How dare you insult the palace guards? Get out of my sight!

options.text: It's not them who are going to fight the demon, it's me.

steps.player: It's not them who are going to fight the demon, it's me.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: What, all by yourself? How are you going to do that?

steps.player: I'm going to use the powerful sword Silverlight, which I believe you have one of the keys for?

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: Yes, I do. But why should I give it to you?

options.text: Fortune-teller Aris said I was destined to kill the demon.

steps.player: Fortune-teller Aris said I was destined to kill the demon.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: A fortune-teller? Destiny? I don't believe in that stuff. I got where I am today by hard work, not by destiny! Why should I care what that mad old fortune-teller says?

options.text: Otherwise the demon will destroy the city!

steps.player: Otherwise the demon will destroy the city!

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin
steps.text: You can't fool me! How do I know you haven't just made that story up to get my key?

options.text: Sir Prysin said you would give me the key.

steps.player: Sir Prysin said you would give me the key.

steps.speaker: Captain Rovin

steps.player: What happens after? When you do take Callisto down that is.

steps.npc: Oh... uh... I never thought about that...
My whole life has been spent preparing to avenge my father, I never thought about anything else...

steps.player: You seem like you've got a lot to think about then. I'll leave you to it.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: He seems to be lost in his own thoughts...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Howdy stranger. What brings you out to these parts?

steps.player: Nothing much - What are you doing here? It doesn't seem like there's much to do out here in the desert!

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well, that's where you'd be wrong. I work for the Archaeological Society of Varrock, and have been excavating around here recently.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Was there something you specifically wanted?

steps.player: Do you have any quests? Call it a hunch, but you look like the type of man who might...

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well, it's funny you should say that. I'm not sure if I would really call it a quest as such, but I found this ancient stone tablet in one of my excavations, and it would really help me out if you could go and take it back to the digsite for me and get it examined.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: It's very old, and I don't recognise any of the inscriptions on it.
Without the required skill levels
Before starting this quest, be aware that one or more of your skill levels are lower than what is required to fully complete it.

steps.prompt: Start the Desert Treasure I quest?

steps.player: Sure, I was heading that way anyway. Any particular person at the digsite you want me to talk to?

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: His name's Terry Balando. Give it to nobody but him. I'm sorry, I can't entrust you with the actual tablet I found, it is far too valuable to give away, but I took these etchings - they should be enough for him to make

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: a preliminary translation on. Come back and let me know what he says, I would hate to waste my time excavating anything that isn't worth my time as a world famous archaeologist!
etchings

steps.player: No thanks. Playing delivery boy doesn't really sound much like fun to me.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well, okay. Can't say as I blame you for thinking that. I'll go take it there myself later I guess.

steps.player: Who are you, anyway?

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: You don't recognise me??? I am the world famous Asgarnia Smith, Archaeologist extraordinaire!

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: I am the one who discovered the long forgotten Temple of Ikov! The one who unearthed the strange trap filled arena in Brimhaven!

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: I'm the leading archaeological expert of our time! I was voted archaeologist of the year four years running by the Varrock Herald! Are you REALLY sure you've never heard of me?

steps.player: No, I really haven't.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well then, I'm confused. Why did you come over and speak to me if you don't know who I am? What do you want?

steps.player: Nothing really. I'm just wandering around for no good reason.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Uh-huh. Well, if you'll excuse me, I have a lot more work to do before I can bed down for the night.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: So what did Terry Balando say about those etchings? Did he give you a translation for me?
If the player has the etchings.

steps.player: Um... yeah... about that... I kind of didn't go and speak to him yet...

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well what are you waiting for? A written invitation? All I want you to do is take those etchings up to the digsite for me!

steps.player: Okay, I'll do that then.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: If the player lost the etchings.

steps.player: Um... yeah... about that... I kind of lost those etchings you gave me...

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well how in the world did you do that? (sigh) Okay, I'll make another set, but try not to lose these ones this time!
etchings

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry.text: That's right, who wants to know...?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry.text: Ah yes, I recognise you! You're the fellow who found that strange artefact about Zaros for the museum, aren't you? What can I do for you now?
If the player doesn't have the etchings.

steps.player: I had some etchings to deliver to you, but I don't have them on me...

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: Then... you better go get them for me?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry.text: If the player has the etchings.

steps.player: That's right. I was in the desert down by the Bedabin Camp, and I found an archaeologist who asked me to deliver this to you.

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: You spoke to the legendary Asgarnia Smith??? Quickly, let me see what he had to give you! He is always at the forefront of archaeological breakthroughs!

steps.player: So what does the inscription say? Anything interesting?

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: This... this is fascinating! These cuneiforms seem to predate even the settlement we are excavating here... Yes, yes, this is most interesting indeed!

steps.player: Can you translate it for me?

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: Well, I am not familiar with this particular language, but the similarities inherent in the pictographs seem to show a prevalent trend towards a syllabary consistent with the phonemes we have discovered in this excavation!

steps.player: Um... So, can you translate it for me or not?

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: Well, unfortunately this is the only example of this particular language I have ever seen, but I might be able to make a rough translation, of sorts...

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: It might be slightly obscure on the finer details, but it should be good enough to understand the rough meaning of what was originally written. Please, just wait a moment, I will write up what I can

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: translate into a journal for you. Then you can take it back to Asgarnia, I think he will be extremely interested in the translation!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.text: There you go, that book contains the sum of my translating ability. If you would be so kind as to take that back to Asgarnia, I think it will reassure him that he is on the

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.text: right track for a find of great archaeological importance

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.player: Wow! You write really quickly don't you?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.text: What can I say? It's a skill I picked up through my many years of taking field notes!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.text: Hello again. Was that translation any use to Asgarnia?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.player: I, uh, kind of didn't take it to him yet...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.text: Whyever not? You're the strangest delivery boy I've ever met!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.player: I lost that translation you gave me...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.speaker: Terry Balando
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.text: Oh, no matter, I mostly remember what it said anyway! Here you go!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: So what did Terry Balando say about those etchings? Did he give you a translation for me?
If the player doesn't have the translation.

steps.player: Yeah, he did. But I don't have it with me.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: I see.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Well could you go and get me that translation? It could be vital!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: If the player has the translation.

steps.player: Yeah, he did. I have it here in this book.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Did you take a ready of this? It will do you good to understand how this profession works. Here, have a read.

steps.player: Yeah, I did. Kind of boring really.

steps.text: translation

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Excellent. Just give me a moment to read this, and talk to me again in a second.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Hmmm. Interesting. It seems to me like there's some kind of treasure hidden out in the desert.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: So what do you say? Fancy being a treasure hunter like me?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Yeeees... An archaeologist...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: It's all this hot sun getting to me I think.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Well anyway, let's just assume there is a treasure hidden in the desert somewhere, and let's just say for the sake of argument that maybe if I found a big stash of gold and treasure I wouldn't necessarily just hand it

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: all over to the Museum of Varrock.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Let's also say, purely hypothetically, that if there were such a big stash of treasure and someone were to help me find it, then that hypothetical person might be entitled to, oh, let's say a purely for the sake of

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: argument thirty percent split...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: That's right!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: A purely for the sake of argument fifty-fifty split on this hypothetical treasure, should it exist...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Do you see where I'm going with this?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.player: You want me to help you find some treasure for a fifty percent share, as long as I don't tell anybody, and your reputation as an esteemed archaeologist with the Museum of Varrock remains intact, and nobody
discovers you're actually just a treasure hunter?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Uh... yes, but the way you said it makes it sound like I'm doing something wrong...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: So what do you say? Partners?

steps.player: Well... I guess nobody is really going to lose out on anything, and we don't even know if there is any treasure...
Aw, go on then. Count me in.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: That's what I like to hear! Now, if we split up we'll be able to find treasure quicker.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: I'll continue searching around here in this Bedabin Camp, you head due South to the Bandit Village. If either of us find anything, we'll come find each other and say what, okay?

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: You head due South, see what you can find out about this tablet.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.player: This all sounds very immoral, and I don't want any part of your seedy little schemes.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Aw, c'mon, cut me a break here! Look, nobody is really getting hurt, right? This treasure is either going to lie around in some underground ruin, or lie around in some museum for

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: people to look at!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: It makes sense for the people to go to all the risk to get a little payback for it, right? Besides, anything of real historical value we can hand over to the museum - we'll just keep the cash for

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: ourselves!

steps.player: I don't trust anything about your little scheme, including you! I want nothing to do with this!

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: Eh, you'll come running back when you realise just how much money we could be talking here.

steps.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
steps.text: I'll see you again when you come crawling back, begging to be cut in on the deal.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Hello again. You find any signs of that treasure yet?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Well, head south to that bandit camp. I bet if there's anything out here, they'll know about it.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.speaker: Asgarnia Smith
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-asgarn.text: Don't let on it might be valuable though! Those thieves will steal it as soon as look at you!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-terry-.prompt: What would you like to talk about?

options.text: Ask about the Desert Treasure quest.

steps.speaker: Terry Balando
steps.text: Hello again. Was that translation any use to Asgarnia?

steps.player: I think it was, thanks!

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-a-band.player: I'm here on an archaeological expedition for the Museum of Varrock.
I believe there may be some interesting artefacts in the area.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-a-band.speaker: Bandit
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-a-band.text: I have no interest in the world that betrayed my people. Search where you will, you will find nothing.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.player: Hello. I represent the Museum of Varrock, and I have reason to believe there may be some kinds of artefacts of historical significance in the nearby area...

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.speaker: Eblis
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.text: Ah yes. The only time people care about our existence is when they think they have something to gain from us.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.speaker: Eblis
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.text: I have nothing to say to you. You and your kind are not welcome here.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.player: Please, if I can just have a few minutes of your time to ask some questions...?

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.speaker: Eblis
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-eblis-.text: (sigh) I suppose I can spare you that. What do you wish to know about?

options.text: Why is this village so hostile?

steps.player: Why are all of the people here so hostile? You would think I was asking you for money instead of just for answers to a few questions...

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: It is a long story, and I doubt you have much interest in hearing it. Your sort never are, you just take what you can of ours, and then abandon us once more to the desert.

options.text: No, I want to hear this story.

steps.player: Actually, I'd be quite interested to hear what it is you have to say to excuse the attitude everybody in this village seems to have.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Ah, it all begun many generations ago, when our ancestors were the proud rulers of these lands...

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: My ancestors lived far to the North of here, and our lands stretched from the sea in the East to the river Lum, and the mountain of ice. From coast to coast, North to South, our domain was absolute.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Our god was kind to us, and blessed us with prosperity and happiness, and in return we were merciless to his enemies wherever we found them.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Then came the betrayal.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Our god was banished, leaving us helpless to our fates.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Without his protection, we were forced to fend for ourselves once more, against the enemies that sought to destroy us through their petty jealousies.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: But we did not succumb without fighting! The spiteful Saradomin and pathetic Zamorak warred with each other, but the hatred they had for each other was as nothing to the hatred they held towards us!

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: With each battle they waged, we lost more and more land, unable to fight on all fronts, and were pushed further and further South into this gods-forsaken desert.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Our greatest hero, Azzanadra, was finally trapped in a strange stone structure to the South of here, and bound within by terrible powers...

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: And with that our lands, our homes, our very lives were stolen from us! Too weak to reclaim what was rightfully ours, we made our homes here, knowing that someday Azzanadra will

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: return with his magnificent power, and bring us back to our former glory...

steps.player: So you're upset because of something that happened hundreds of years ago?
Seems to me like maybe you should find some closure, and let the past go...

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: The insults heaped upon my race will never be forgotten, will never be forgiven and will never again be overlooked.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Someday, a harsh wind will blow upon this land, uncovering the wrongs of the past, and we will get back what is rightfully ours. Until such a day we will bide our time here, and will

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: always be ready with our blades for our righteous vengeance.

options.text: I don't care about your story.

steps.player: I don't really care what your story is to be honest, there is no excuse for such rudeness or hostility.
I have done nothing wrong to you, but everybody here treats me like I have committed some great crime against the village.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: That is because, from our point of view, you have.

steps.player: What? Just because I entered your village?

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: You have no right to be here! You have no right to the life you have, for it was taken at our expense!

steps.player: Whatever... No wonder all you loonies live out here in the desert by yourselves.

options.text: Do you know anything about treasure near here?

steps.player: I was wondering if you knew anything about some treasure somewhere around here?
I have some evidence that there might be some kind of treasure hidden very close to this village...

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: If I knew of any treasure I would not choose to spend my life in this gods-forsaken desert.

options.text: Do you know anything about a fortress near here?

steps.player: Do you know anything about some kind of fortress nearby? I have reason to believe there is, or at least used to be, some kind of fortress very close to here...

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Nobody would build anything in this wasteland unless they were forced to, to survive.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: I know of no fortress, I know of no reason why anyone would ever bother doing anything out here in the desert.

steps.player: Actually, there was nothing I really wanted to ask you about.

steps.speaker: Eblis
steps.text: Yes, it is exactly like your sort to waste my time in such a way.

enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-the-ba.speaker: Bartender
enchanting-the-mirrors-talking-to-the-ba.text: If you're not buying anything, I have nothing to say to you.

steps.player: As I understand it there's some kind of hidden treasure in these parts...

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: Look around pal. Does it looks like there's any treasure near here?

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: If I were you I'd get lost before someone takes a dislike to your face and removes it for you.
If the player doesn't have 650 coins.

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: You ain't got the 650 coins it costs to buy it, and I'm glad 'cos I didn't want to serve you anyway.
If the player has 650 coins.

steps.text: What's that? You wanna buy a beer? It'll cost ya 650 coins.

650 coins
