steps.player: Ok, I will help you.

steps.npc: I thank you greatly adventurer! Also... if you find Caleb... please... let him know his father still loves him...

options.text: You're rich then? Can I have some money?

steps.player: You're rich then? Can I have some money?

steps.npc: Gah! Lousy beggar! Your sort is what's ruining this great land! Why don't you just go and get a job if you need money so badly?

options.text: Hi, I am a bold adventurer.

steps.player: Hi, I am a bold adventurer.

steps.npc: An adventurer hmmm? How lucky. I may have an adventure for you. I desperately need my family crest returning to me. It is of utmost importance.

options.text: Why are you so desperate for it?

steps.player: Why are you so desperate for it?

options.text: I'm not interested in that adventure right now.
Have you got any quests for me?

steps.player: Do you have any quests for me? I really want one. I really want to help out!

steps.text: You murmur under your breath something about how great the rewards were last time you did a quest for Dimintheis.

steps.npc: My family consider what you did for us a great service. We couldn't possibly trouble you further.

steps.player: There must be SOMETHING you need help with. I am a great adventurer after all.

steps.npc: There really isn't anything, I am very content with life right now.

options.text: I guess money does buy happiness.

steps.player: I guess money really does buy happiness.

steps.npc: What was that? I didn't quite catch that.

steps.player: Nothing...

options.text: Oh come on, however menial, I want to help!

steps.player: Oh come on, surely there's something I can help out with! I want to help, however menial it is.

steps.npc: Okay okay. Fine then. Whilst I don't have anything for you, how about you try my sons, they are always wanting something done.

steps.player: Fantastic! I'll get straight to it!

steps.text: You smell the sweet smell of the great rewards that may soon come.
If Defender of Varrock has not been completed:

steps.npc: You have my eternal gratitude for all you have done in saving my family's honour, adventurer. Perhaps some day my sons will overcome their differences.

steps.text: If Defender of Varrock has been completed:

steps.npc: Hello again, adventurer. I hope that Shield of Arrav business marks the start of something big for my family. Maybe it will help me finally get out of this hole!

steps.player: Do you have any gauntlets for me?

steps.text: If the player is missing their gauntlets:

steps.npc: Yes, your [steel/goldsmithing/cooking/chaos] gauntlets returned to me through their magic power recently. Would you like them back?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.npc: Here you go.

steps.text: Dimintheis returns your gauntlets.

steps.player: Not right now.

steps.npc: Well, come back if you change your mind any time. I owe you for your trouble.

steps.text: If the player has their gauntlets:

steps.npc: No, I don't think so. You must have them yourself somewhere.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-famil.npc: I will not forget what you did for my family, [player name]. Those 500,000 coins have allowed us to put food on the table.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-famil.text: If the player has completed Defender of Varrock:

steps.npc: Combine that with the whole Shield of Arrav business and things are really starting to look up for us!

options.text: Could I get some more gauntlets, please?

steps.player: Could I get some more gauntlets, please?

steps.npc: You may, but you'll have to ask my sons for them, unless you just want the plain steel gauntlets.

options.text: Yes, I do want some steel gauntlets, please.

steps.player: Yes, I do want some steel gauntlets, please.

steps.text: How many would you like to take?
Dimintheis hands you some steel gauntlets.

steps.npc: Here you go.

options.text: No thanks, I'll ask your sons instead.

steps.player: No thanks, I'll ask your sons instead.

options.text: The gauntlets are a family heirloom?

steps.player: I thought these gauntlets were a family heirloom. How do you have several of them?

steps.npc: I'm sorry for lying to you, [player name], it was just all part of the ploy to make our family seem wealthy.
They're not heirlooms at all, we have crates full of the things hidden away in the basement.

steps.player: And you still think that these are an acceptable reward for what I have done for your family?

steps.npc: It's all I have to give...

steps.player: Very well, I do admit, they are useful.

options.text: Could I get some more gauntlets, please?

steps.player: See you another time, Dimintheis.

standard-dialogue-by-the-entrance-of-the.npc: Welcome. Have you come to give your soul to the Chasm?

standard-dialogue-by-the-entrance-of-the.player: Uh, I believe I'm still using it.

standard-dialogue-by-the-entrance-of-the.npc: For now. Have you came to prove yourself in combat against the many demons within the Chasm?
My master prefers that his minions be killed with purpose.

standard-dialogue-by-the-entrance-of-the.text: If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I ask no questions of my master, I just inform.

standard-dialogue-by-the-entrance-of-the.text: If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided, but has not signed Yama's contract:

steps.npc: I am not worthy to explain on his behalf. Descend the Chasm and speak with him yourself if you wish for further details.

standard-dialogue-by-the-entrance-of-the.text: If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided and has signed Yama's contract:

steps.npc: As outlined in your contract, he wishes them slain in particular ways.

steps.player: Could you remind me what ways those were?

steps.npc: Death by two-handed melee weapons, heavy ranged weapons, magic spells, special attacks, and defeating them whilst bound.
Additionaly, he will request a specific method to be used. If you comply, your chances of obtaining a reward will be increased.

steps.text: If the player is currently required to kill a demon with a two-handed melee weapon:

steps.npc: Currently, my master wishes for you to use two handed melee weapons to kill his minions.

steps.text: If the player is currently required to kill a demon with a heavy ranged weapon:

steps.npc: Currently, my master wishes for you to use heavy ranged weapons to kill his minions.

steps.text: If the player is currently required to kill a demon with a magic spell:

steps.npc: Currently, my master wishes for you to use spells to kill his minions.

steps.player: Does that include powered staves?

steps.npc: No.

steps.text: If the player is currently required to kill a demon with a special attack:

steps.npc: Currently, my master wishes for you to use special attacks to kill his minions.

steps.text: If the player is currently required to kill a demon while it is bound:

steps.player: What kinds of rewards would I receive?

steps.npc: Special contracts, to be presented to my master for further discussion.

steps.player: Interesting. Thank you.

steps.npc: You are most welcome.

standard-dialogue-inside-the-chasm-of-fi.npc: Oh yes! Just praying to my new master. It's hot down here, isn't it?

options.text: Your new master, that would be...?

steps.player: Your new master, that would be...?

steps.npc: Yama! I sold my soul you see, well, I guess that Ox-headed guy down there forcibly removed it.

steps.player: That doesn't sound like a fair trade...

steps.npc: Oh, don't worry, I'm perfectly fine with the outcome. Sure, the loss of vision is a shame but it could be worse.

steps.player: Could it?

steps.npc: Underground there are no tall buildings, I'm awfully afraid of heights, you see.

steps.player: Perhaps it's a good thing you can't see...

steps.npc: What was that?

steps.player: Oh, nothing...
What happened to your eyes?

steps.npc: The ritual, there were some... adverse effects...

steps.player: The ritual?

steps.npc: Oh yes! Pretty basic really, head of an Ox, bruma roots, lots of fire and of course the human sacrifice.

steps.player: And at what point did that blind you?

steps.npc: The voice demanded that we stare into the fire until we saw enlightenment.

steps.player: I guess the fire was pretty bright.

steps.npc: Blindingly so.

steps.player: Wait! Did you say human sacrifice?

steps.npc: Why, of course! We're Zamorakians, we're evil...

steps.player: Yeah, I guess that's true.

options.text: Well, I'll leave you to it.

steps.player: Well, I'll leave you to it.

steps.npc: So soon?

steps.player: Yep, the demons won't slay themselves.

steps.npc: What demons?

I can't offer you any payment at the moment, but hard work doesn't go unnoticed around these parts.

standard-dialogue-before-song-of-the-elv.npc: How do you feel? No heavy flu, shivers, nausea or loss of appetite?
How about nightmares then? Are you experiencing any problems with especially scary nightmares?

standard-dialogue-before-song-of-the-elv.player: No... not since I was young.

standard-dialogue-before-song-of-the-elv.npc: Good, good, I had to make sure. This plague really has an incredibly fast contagion rate. It spreads faster than the common cold!

steps.player: The plague? Tell me more.

steps.npc: It came from the west somewhere. It is extremely quick spreading, and utterly deadly.

steps.player: What are the symptoms?

steps.npc: It varies slightly from case to case, but usually abnormal nightmares and flu-like symptoms, progressing as you succumb more. Eventually, it results in the presence of a thick black tar-like substance secreted
from the nose and eyes.
Unfortunately if you reach this stage of infection then no one can save you.

steps.player: Okay, I'll be careful.

steps.npc: You do that adventurer. You do not want to become infected by the plague.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-no-d.npc: Welcome to the Nightmare Zone! Would you like me to create a dream for you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name's Dominic Onion but you can call me Dom, or Mr Onion.

steps.player: Mr Oni...Dom, how did you get that name?

steps.npc: Well that's a long story...but I can tell you that it involved my parents, 3 blurberry specials, and a chinchompa.

steps.player: ...and a chinchompa?

steps.npc: Oh yes, Nigel played a crucial role in the whole debacle. It's all very amusing now that I think back to it.

steps.player: Right...

steps.npc: Good times...

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is the Nightmare Zone!

steps.player: Wwwwhat?!

steps.npc: Don't worry, it's not as bad as it sounds...most of the time.

steps.player: That's comforting.

steps.npc: Truth be told, that name wasn't my first choice, it's what the local folk have been calling it and so it sort of stuck.
My original plan came to me in a vivid dream when I was younger you see, I saw myself running a successful business from a great structure in a strange land.
Well, I say strange, but I'd never left Lunar Isle at the time and this place was very hot and dry, unlike anything I'd seen before.
When I told my father about the dream he laughed and said I should become a banker like him and his father before him but in that moment I knew that it wasn't the life for me.
I had to find out what this dream meant and if it was a vision of the future or not.
Growing up, I studied hard to find out more about magic, especially oneiromancy and the interpretation of dreams.
Having learned as much as I could on Lunar Isle I set out to find and learn from other great wizards I'd heard of in stories as a child.
I set off to travel the world, discovering more about dreams to enable me to understand the dream I'd had as a child.
I needed to know what this dream meant and if it was truly a vision of the future.
If so I knew I had to try and find this location and build the huge tower I saw.
I was going to call it 'Dom Onion's Tower', but I've not found this strange place or gathered enough money to build it just yet.
That's why I've setup this small business venture in the mean time selling dreams to people. I just need a big enough crowd to kickstart my business.
It's all part of my five year plan, and who knows, perhaps my dream will come true; I'll discover this place and build Dom Onion's Tower!

options.text: Can you tell me about the dreams?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the dreams?

steps.npc: Certainly. I can delve into your memories and search for the key events that have affected you on your adventures.
I then take the essence of these memories and put that in the vial you see on the plinth.
I imbue a bit of magic, then give the vial a bit of a shake, and when you drink it you'll be able to re-live an encounter close to the original.
Don't worry though, when you're in a dream, you're perfectly safe even if it does seem very real.
If you sucessfully overcome the dream or die trying, you'll leave the dream state and return to normal with your grey matter and appendages intact.

steps.player: Are all dreams the same or are there different options?

steps.npc: Oh no, they can vary wildly! You can choose from one of three main options.
Firstly, I can create a one-on-one encounter with an adversary you've defeated in your adventures. People like to practice in these dreams.
Then there's a sort of Endurance dream, where you face enemies in encounter after encounter, and try to survive to the end.
And finally there's something I like to call a Rumble, where you face multiple adversaries at the same time. I imbue a bit more magic and shake the vial harder to create that one!
You can invite friends to fight alongside you in a Rumble dream. Once I've set up the dream for you, step into the enclosure and invite up to 4 friends.
For the Endurance and Rumble dreams, I charge a fee for my work. I don't like handling the money directly, so instead I've set up a secure coffer.
After you've asked me to set up a dream, put some money in my coffer. I'll deduct the fee from the coffer when you start the dream.
There's a red vial on the other plinth. Your friends can drink from it to enter your dream as a spectator to observe your progress.
Finally here's one other option you get, and that's how difficult the encounters are. As well as the normal dreams, the bravest adventurers can choose a harder version*.

steps.player: What's the giant tree stump all about?

steps.npc: This stump is all that remains of the Great Auburn Redwood. It was, and in many ways still is, one of the key holy sites of Varlamore.

steps.player: What happened to it?

steps.npc: The tree was destroyed during the War of Betrayal many years ago. It was here in the Auburn Valley that the fighting was at its most fierce.
Both sides resorted to tactics that most would consider to be beyond horrifying. The tree was sadly a casualty of such tactics.

steps.player: Which side was responsible?

steps.npc: That has never been clear. Ranul teaches us to find and preserve the truth, but in war, the truth is sadly left behind.

steps.player: So the battles that took place here... Is that why all these animal spirits are here now?

steps.npc: Yes. They are the spirits of the animals that died here during the War of Betrayal. They did not pass on to Mictl, for they have unfinished business in these lands.

steps.player: What business?

steps.npc: That is beyond our understanding. We believe they are here to guide the ents that live in the valley so that they may one day regrow the Great Auburn Redwood.

steps.player: The ents can do that?

steps.npc: Much of the valley was destroyed during the war. Most of what you see around you was regrown by the ents.

steps.player: That's incredible!

steps.npc: Indeed it is, my child. That is why it is our duty to ensure the ents are protected. The events of the war cannot be repeated.

steps.npc: Then go in peace, my child.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Vampyre Slayer:

options.text: Small.. something small would be good.

steps.npc: Small? Small isn't really that dangerous though is it?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Imp Catcher:

steps.player: Thanks for your help.

steps.npc: Imps will be imps!

steps.player: Maybe another time.

options.text: Something easy please, I'm new here.

steps.player: Something easy please, I'm new here.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Rune Mysteries:

options.text: What's it like living so close to the wilderness?

steps.player: What's it like living so close to the wilderness?

steps.npc: Oh, it's not all that bad. It was a bit scary at first but as long as I don't go past the warning signs I'm all right.
It's actually pretty quiet here. I used to live in Lumbridge and, let me tell you, that's the dangerous place for people like me.
Thieves were picking people's pockets with impunity, and killing them on the streets in broad daylight!
And there weren't even any guards to protect us! Not that the guards in the other cities do much good to protect people from what I've heard.
I just thank goodness I haven't got an Attack option any more! I wouldn't last five minutes!

options.text: How did Dave come to be evil?

steps.player: How did Dave come to be evil?

steps.npc: Oh, I don't know really. He's always been evil, I think. Maybe growing up so close to the wilderness has affected him in some way.
When he was little he used to want to go into Edgeville dungeon. You know how kids are, always wanting to be dungeon adventurers! But he didn't want to be a hero, he wanted to be a monster!
And then he spent all summer building a tree-house. Except it wasn't a tree-house, of course, it was his Tower of Fear!
Of course I was hoping he'd have grown out of it by now and maybe even left home. But at least it keeps him happy.

standard-dialogue.npc: What, what do you want?

standard-dialogue.player: Why are you out here on your own?

standard-dialogue.npc: I was drawn here... I use to be a traveling doctor, until I arrived in Al Kharid.
Then I heard it call to me... I immediately gave up my profession and set up here.
I'm happy here... the voices tell me I'm happy here. I can continue my work.

standard-dialogue.player: Uhh... what voices? There is no one else here.

standard-dialogue.npc: Of course there isn't, the hole you idiot, the hole speaks to me and I listen... It says I will do great things, only if I listen...

standard-dialogue.player: Well... alright then, I think I'm just going to go and leave then.

options.text: What did you do before you worked here?

steps.player: What did you do before you worked here?

steps.npc: Oh, I used to be a travelling surgeon. Whenever I saw someone have an accident, I'd be there to check for concussion and offer treatment.
It was a worthy cause, but I didn't feel properly appreciated, so I retired. Then I got bored, so I came to work here.
So can I help you with something?

steps.player: Nothing, I'm fine.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: This is the Champions' Guild. Only adventurers who have proved themselves worthy by gaining influence from quests are allowed in here.

steps.player: Can I have a quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Aha!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Yes! A mighty and perilous quest fit only for the most powerful champions! And, at the end of it, you will earn the right to wear the legendary rune platebody!
If the player does not have 45 combat or 33 Magic:
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 45. One or more of your skill levels are also lower than recommended.

steps.prompt: Start the Dragon Slayer I quest?

steps.player: So, what is this quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: You'll have to speak to Oziach, the maker of rune armour. He sets the quests that champions must complete in order to wear it.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Oziach lives in a hut, by the cliffs to the west of Edgeville. He can be a little...odd...sometimes, though.

steps.player: Actually, I'll give it a miss.
Can I have a quest?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: You're already on a quest for me, if I recall correctly. Have you talked to Oziach yet?

steps.player: No, not yet.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Well, he's the only one who can grant you the right to wear rune platemail. He lives in a hut, by the cliffs west of Edgeville.

steps.player: Okay, I'll go and talk to him.

a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.speaker: Oziach
a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.text: Aye, 'tis a fair day my friend.

options.text: Can you sell me a rune platebody?

steps.player: Can you sell me a rune platebody?

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: So, how does thee know I 'ave some?

options.text: The Guildmaster of the Champions' Guild told me.

steps.player: The Guildmaster of the Champions' Guild told me.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Yes, I suppose he would, wouldn't he? He's always sending you fancy-pants 'heroes' up to bother me. Telling me I'll give them a quest or sommat like that.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Well, I'm not going to let just anyone wear my rune platemail. It's only for heroes. So, leave me alone.

options.text: I thought you were going to give me a quest.

steps.player: I thought you were going to give me a quest.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Sigh*

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: All right, I'll give ye a quest. I'll let ye wear my rune platemail if ye...

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Slay the dragon of Crandor!

options.text: A dragon, that sounds like fun.

steps.player: A dragon, that sounds like fun!

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Hah, yes, you are a typical reckless adventurer, aren't you? Now go kill the dragon and get out of my face.

steps.player: But how can I defeat the dragon?

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Go talk to the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild. He'll help ye out if yer so keen on doing a quest. I'm not going to be handholding any adventurers.

options.text: I may be a champion, but I don't think I'm up to dragon-killing yet.

steps.player: I may be a champion, but I don't think I'm up to dragon-killing yet.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Yes, I can understand that. Yer a coward.

options.text: That's a pity, I'm not a hero.

steps.player: That's a pity, I'm not a hero.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Aye, I ken tell!

steps.player: I am a master detective.

steps.text: If Murder Mystery has been completed:

steps.player: I solved the Sinclair murder mystery by myself!

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Never 'eard of yer.

steps.speaker: Oziach
steps.text: Well, however you found out about it, I'm not going to let just anyone wear my rune platemail. It's only for heroes. So leave me alone.

options.text: I thought you were going to give me a quest.
That's a pity, I'm not a hero.
Yes, it's a very nice day.

a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.speaker: Oziach
a-quest-for-the-rune-platebody-talking-t.text: Have ye slayed that dragon yet?

steps.player: I talked to Oziach and he gave me a quest.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Oh? What did he tell you to do?

steps.player: Defeat the dragon of Crandor.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: The dragon of Crandor?

steps.player: Um, yes...

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Goodness, he hasn't given you an easy job, has he?

steps.player: What's so special about this dragon?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Thirty years ago, Crandor was a thriving community with a great tradition of mages and adventurers. Many Crandorians even earned the right to be part of the Champions' Guild!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: One of their adventurers went too far, however. He descended into the volcano in the centre of Crandor and woke the dragon Elvarg.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: He must have fought valiantly against the dragon because they say that, to this day, she has a scar down her side,

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: but the dragon still won the fight. She emerged and laid waste to the whole of Crandor with her fire breath!

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Some refugees managed to escape in fishing boats. They landed on the coast, north of Rimmington, and set up camp but the dragon followed them and burned the camp to the ground.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Out of all the people of Crandor there were only three survivors: a trio of wizards who used magic to escape. Their names were Thalzar, Lozar and Melzar.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If you're serious about taking on Elvarg, first you'll need to get to Crandor, and to my knowledge, the only way to do that is by sea.

steps.player: So I just sail over there? Seems easy enough.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If only that were true. The island is surrounded by dangerous underwater reefs. You'll need a map to guide you through them and a ship capable of doing so.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: And then of course there's the dragon herself. Once you reach Crandor, you'll need some kind of protection against her breath.

options.text: Where can I find a map to Crandor?

steps.player: Where can I find a map to Crandor?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: After what happened, people were afraid of enraging the dragon. Most maps to the island were destroyed, but I have heard that one survived. It was held by Melzar, Thalzar and Lozar.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: However, the three apparently split the map into three pieces, which each of them taking one piece.

steps.player: Where is Melzar's map piece?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Melzar built a castle on the site of the Crandorian refugee camp, north of Rimmington. He's locked himself in there and no one's seen him for years.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: The inside of his castle is like a maze, and is populated by undead monsters. Maybe, if you could get all the way through the maze, you could find his piece of the map.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Adventurers sometimes go in there to prove themselves, so I can give you this key to Melzar's Maze.
The Guildmaster hands you a key.

steps.player: Where is Thalzar's map piece?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Thalzar was the most paranoid of the three wizards. He hid his map piece and took the secret of its location to his grave.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: I don't think you'd be able to find out where it is by ordinary means. You'll need to talk to the Oracle on Ice Mountain.

steps.player: Where is Lozar's map piece?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: A few weeks ago, I'd have told you to speak to Lozar herself, in her house across the river from Lumbridge.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Unfortunately, goblin raiders killed her and stole everything. One of the goblins from the Goblin Village probably has the map piece now.

options.text: What kind of ship do I need?

steps.player: What kind of ship do I need?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: Quite a specific one I'm afraid. Even with a map, very few ships will be able to navigate the reefs around the island. You're going to need one of Crandorian design.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: If there's still one in existence, it's probably in Port Sarim. However, a ship will also need a captain, and I'm not sure where you'd find one willing to sail to Crandor!
If the player has completed Pandemonium:

steps.player: Could I not just captain it myself? I have some experience in that area.

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: I suppose you could, but given you have a dragon to be dealing with, I'd suggest getting someone else to worry about the captaining for you.

options.text: How can I protect myself from the dragon's breath?

steps.player: How can I protect myself from the dragon's breath?

steps.speaker: Guildmaster
steps.text: That part shouldn't be too difficult, actually. I believe the Duke of Lumbridge has a special shield in his armoury that is enchanted against dragon's breath.

options.text: What's so special about this dragon?

steps.player: Okay, I'll get going!

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: By the power of custard!

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: Feel the wrath of my feet!

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: Let me drink my tea in peace.

steps.speaker: Melzar the Mad
steps.text: Leave me alone, I need to feed my pet rock.

melzar-s-map-piece-searching-the-chest.text: You find a map piece in the chest.

melzar-s-map-piece-studying-melzar-s-map.text: This is a piece of map that you found in Melzar's Maze. You will need to join it to the other two map pieces before you can see the route to Crandor.

options.text: I seek a piece of the map to the island of Crandor.

steps.player: I seek a piece of the map to the island of Crandor.

steps.speaker: Oracle
steps.text: The map's behind a door below, but entering is rather tough. This is what you need to know: You must use the following stuff.

steps.speaker: Oracle
steps.text: First, a drink used by a mage. Next, some worm string, changed to sheet. Then, a small crustacean cage. Last, a bowl that's not seen heat.

options.text: Can you impart your wise knowledge to me, O Oracle?

thalzar-s-map-piece-using-respective-ite.text: You put the silk into the opening in the door.
You put the Lobster pot into the opening in the door.
You put the unfired bowl into the opening in the door.
You pour the Wizard's Mind Bomb into the opening in the door.

thalzar-s-map-piece-searching-the-chest.text: As you open the chest, you notice an inscription on the lid:

Here I rest the map to my beloved home. To whoever finds it, I beg of you, let it be. I was honour-bound not to destroy the map piece, but I have used all my magical skill to keep it from being recovered.

This map leads to the lair of the beast that destroyed my home, devoured my family, and burned to a cinder all that I love. But revenge would not benefit me now, and to disturb this beast is to risk bringing its wrath down upon another land.
I cannot stop you from taking this map piece now, but think on this: if you can slay the Dragon of Crandor, you are a greater hero than my land ever produced. There is no shame in backing out now.
You find a map piece in the chest.

thalzar-s-map-piece-studying-thalzar-s-m.text: This is a piece of map that you found in a secret chest in the Dwarven Mine. You will need to join it to the other two map pieces before you can see the route to Crandor.

options.text: I've heard that one of your number has got hold of part of a map.

steps.player: I've heard that one of your number has got hold of part of a map.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Aha, that'd be Wormbrain.

steps.player: Where would he be?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Wormbrain steals too much. He got caught. Now he lives in Port Sarim town jail.

options.text: So how is life for the goblins?
I believe you've got a piece of map that I need.

steps.text: Me not stoopid, it worth at least 10,000 coins!

options.text: You must be joking! Forget it.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: But, by the time me get box open, other goblins gone. Then me not run fast enough and guards catch me.

steps.speaker: Wormbrain
steps.text: But now you want map piece so must be special! What you do for me to get it?

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Only the most worthy may access our guild and I'm afraid you are not quite there yet. Go out and hone your skills. Then you can return to us.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Dragon Slayer II quest.
If the player meets all the requirements:

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Only the most worthy are allowed access into the Myths' Guild. If you wish to enter, you'll need to prove yourself.

steps.player: How can I do that?

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: As time passes, that which was once fact, becomes myth. Some tales are just that, tales. However, some tales are something more.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Here at the Myths' Guild, we live to tell the difference between the two. If you wish to join us, you must do the same.

steps.player: So what myth would you like me to investigate?

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: For as long as history remembers, dragons have roamed these lands, but despite how long they've been here, much of their history remains hidden.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: There are tales of course, but tales are not enough for us. We want you to discover the truth. Where did the dragons come from? Why are they here? Who do they serve?

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Answer these questions for us. Help us fill our Library of Knowledge. In return, we will grant you access to the guild and you will reap the rewards within.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: So, do you feel up for the challenge?

steps.player: Yes. Where should I begin?

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Head to Karamja Wines, Spirits, and Beers at Musa Point. There you'll find Dallas Jones. We've heard that he is investigating the destruction of Crandor. This seems like a good place to start.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Good luck.

steps.player: No. This is too much for me.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: As you wish. If you change your mind, you know where we are.

starting-out-talking-to-alec-kincade-tal.speaker: Alec Kincade
starting-out-talking-to-alec-kincade-tal.text: Greetings, adventurer. Welcome to the Myths' Guild.

steps.player: Let's talk about my quest.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: How are things progressing?
Before reaching the Ancient Doors:

steps.player: I'm yet to discover anything.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Well return to us once you do. If you help us fill our Library of Knowledge, we shall grant you access to the guild.
Once the player reaches the point where they must find Bob the Cat:

steps.player: I'm investigating the origin of Elvarg. I've found some old doors on a ruined island, but they're locked. I think something important lies behind them.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Well keep at it. If you help us fill our Library of Knowledge, we shall grant you access to the guild.
Once the player recovers Bob's memories as Robert:

steps.player: I'm investigating the origin of Elvarg. I've found some old doors on a ruined island, but they're locked. I'm trying to find the key.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Well keep at it. If you help us fill our Library of Knowledge, we shall grant you access to the guild.
Once the player opens the Lithkren Vault:

steps.player: I'm investigating the origin of Elvarg. I've found an ancient vault beneath a ruined island. I think it contains something important.

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Well you'd better investigate it then. If you help us fill our Library of Knowledge, we shall grant you access to the guild.
Once Zorgoth and Galvek escape from the vault:

steps.player: I was investigating the origin of Elvarg but I accidently released a dragonkin!

steps.speaker: Alec Kincade
steps.text: Well that can't be good. You'd better sort that out.

steps.player: I'm working on it.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.player: Hello there. I'm [player name]. Are you Dallas Jones?

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.text: I am. Pleased to meet you. I'm assuming you're here because of my advert?

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.text: Excellent! Let me run you through the details.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.text: We're to head to Elvarg's lair beneath Crandor. There we will begin a research project on Elvarg and her attack on the island.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.text: I trust you know the tale of Elvarg?

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.player: Well I was the one who killed her in the first place.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.text: You're the Hero of Crandor? Amazing!

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-jones.text: I take it you know her story very well then?

steps.player: Remind me.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Thirty years ago, an adventurer descended into the caves beneath Crandor. There he discovered the dragon Elvarg.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Elvarg made short work of the adventurer. Once she was finished with him, she emerged from the caves and laid waste to the island.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: For the next thirty years, Elvarg remained on Crandor until she was finally defeated, by you.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Now that Elvarg is dead, we have the opportunity to perform research on the island and investigate her attack.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Meet me in Elvarg's Lair beneath Crandor when you're ready to begin.

steps.player: Sounds good. See you there.
Yes I know it well.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Wonderful. I won't waste your time with it then.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Now that Elvarg is dead, we have the opportunity to perform research on the island and investigate her attack.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Meet me in Elvarg's Lair beneath Crandor when you're ready to begin.

steps.player: Sounds good. See you there.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.player: Hello, Dallas. So what exactly are we researching here?

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.text: Elvarg's attack on Crandor is a bit of an anomaly. We're here to work out why.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.text: Elvarg is very unusual in that she is one of the few dragons to live alone. Most of her kind live in large groups.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.text: Not only that, she also displayed far greater aggression than most other dragons by directly attacking Crandor.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.text: Not like Elvarg was. Most dragons will only attack those who enter their territory. Elvarg strayed well outside of hers when she attacked the island.

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.player: I see. Where should we start?

starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-talking-to-dallas-in-elvarg.text: This is where Elvarg made her home. There must be something here to point us in the right direction. Have a look around and see what you can find.

steps.player: Let's talk about the investigation.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: How are things going?

steps.player: I've found a strange wall that looks like it might have something behind it. We might be able to mine through it.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Good work. I'm afraid you'll need to be the one to do the mining. My back isn't what it once was.

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Not much to tell really. My name is Dallas Jones and I'm a researcher for the Varrock Museum. Many of the researchers have an area of expertise. Mine is dragons.

steps.player: Why dragons?

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: My father used to live on Crandor before it was destroyed. He was one of the many who were killed by Elvarg.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: His death left me with a great interest in dragons and I've spent the last fifteen years trying to learn more about them.

steps.player: I see. Thanks, Dallas.
Let's talk about the investigation.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: How are things going?

steps.player: I've mined through a strange wall and found a tunnel behind it.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: I can see that. We could well be on to something here. You go through the tunnel and see if it's safe. I'll be right behind you.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.text: Goodness me! What is this place?

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.player: It looks like some sort of laboratory.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.text: Are the tales true? Could this mean?

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.text: There are ancient tales that tell of the origin of the dragons. They say they were created by a powerful race of creatures known as the dragonkin.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.text: Yes, you likely will have. We know for a fact that the dragonkin existed. They terrorised the world for many years during the early Fourth Age.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.text: The thing is, despite their similar names, no actual connection between the dragonkin and the dragons has ever been proven.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.player: Well maybe we'll be the ones to prove it.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory.text: We might just be. We should look around and see what we can uncover.

steps.player: Let's talk about the investigation.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: I just can't believe it. This place may not just hold the secrets of Elvarg, but of the whole dragon race!

steps.player: I'll look around and see what I can find.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: How strange. We should keep looking around.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-inspe.text: The mural has images of dragons and fungi along with the word 'Lithkren'.
You find some notes next to the machinery.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.player: I've found an old mural. It has lots of dragons and fungi on it along with some strange writing.
I don't know. It looked like a different language. It had odd words on it like 'Lithkren'.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: Lithkren? That name sounds familiar. Where have I seen it before?

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: Of course! Fossil Island! I was there recently as part of the research team investigating the differences between wyverns and dragons.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: There's an old settlement on the island with similar architecture to this place. It contains lots of books, many written in a strange language. One of the books mentioned a place called Lithkren.
If the player has read the ancient diary:

steps.player: You know, now that you mention it, I think I may have read that book as well.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Well that just confirms it! Not to mention that Fossil Island is also coated in various types of fungi. It must be connected!

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: If the player has not read the ancient diary:

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Fossil Island is also coated in various types of fungi. It must be connected!

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.player: In that case, we should probably go to Fossil Island.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: I agree. Head to the old settlement on the north side of the island. I'll meet you there once I've finished up here.

starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.speaker: Dallas Jones
starting-out-the-secret-laboratory-talki.text: It looks like we've found everything here. We should move on to Fossil Island. I'll meet you at the old settlement on the north side of the island.

the-house-on-the-hill-talking-to-dallas.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-talking-to-dallas.text: So while I was waiting for you, I had a look through these books again. One of them mentions a nearby island called Lithkren. Thing is, there are lots of islands around here. It doesn't say which one it is.
If the player has read the ancient diary:

steps.player: So how do we know which island to go to?

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Have a look at this grid on the floor. I think it might actually be a map. If you look at that tile in the middle, it looks like part of this island.

steps.player: Hmm... So this map could lead us to Lithkren. Most of the pieces are missing though.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: That they are. However, I had a look around and I managed to find some of the pieces.
Dallas shows you some of the map pieces.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: By my calculations, there are 24 pieces left to find. I suspect they'll either be in this building or very close by.

steps.player: Great! I'll have a look around and see if I can find them.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Good luck. Once you have all of the pieces, bring them here and we'll see about putting this map together.

the-house-on-the-hill-talking-to-dallas.text: If the player has not read the ancient diary:

options.text: So how do we know which island to go to?

steps.player: Which book was it?

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Check the pile behind the ladder. You should find it there.

steps.player: So how do we know which island to go to?
Let's talk about the investigation.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Have you managed to find those map pieces yet?
If the player does not have map pieces on them:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Well keep looking. We have [amount] pieces left to find. I suspect they'll either be in this building or very close by.

steps.player: Yes. I have some here.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Great. I'll look after them for you.
If there are more pieces to find:

steps.player: Is that all of them?

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Not yet. We have [amount] pieces left to find. I suspect they'll either be in this building or very close by.
If there are no more pieces to find:

steps.player: I think that's all of them.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: It looks like it is. Good job.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Now then, shall we see about finishing this map?

steps.player: Let's do it!
Not right now.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Fair enough. Let me know when you're ready.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.text: I do believe you've got it! Yes, we should be able to find Lithkren now.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.text: There's a strange symbol on the map in two places. One marks this building and the other marks an island. I bet that's Lithkren.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.player: I think you might be right. So now that we know where the island is, we need to find a way there. Do you think the museum can help us?

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.text: The museum? No that won't work. Any requisition of museum resources requires a mountain of paperwork and we simply don't have time.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.text: Of course not! Besides, I've spent years working towards this and I'm tired of waiting. It's time to discover the truth.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.player: Alright, alright. So what do we do instead?

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.text: We'll need a boat. Find a dwarf called Jardric. He should be somewhere on the island. He's an old friend who owes me a favour. He should be able to get a boat for us.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map.text: While you're doing that, I'm going to take a copy of this map.

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map-.player: What should I be doing again?

the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map-.speaker: Dallas Jones
the-house-on-the-hill-finishing-the-map-.text: We'll need a boat to get to Lithkren. Jardric should be able to help us. See if you can find him. He should be somewhere on the island.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: That I am. Former boatman and now a researcher for Keldagrim. What can I do for you?

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.player: I'm working with Dallas Jones on a research project. We're investigating the destruction of Crandor. We need a boat to get to one of the nearby islands. Dallas said you could help us.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: Did he now? Looking to cash in on that favour I bet. I'm afraid I can't help you. All the boats around here are owned by the museum and they won't just let you take them.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: Of course, Dallas works with the museum and he could easily put in a request for one, but he's not a fan of waiting around...

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.player: He said as much. So what can we do?

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: Well I suppose you could always build your own. If the island isn't far you'll only need a small rowboat.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: Mind you, you'll want to be quite good at building things, unless you fancy a trip to the bottom of the ocean.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.player: I'm not actually too bad when it comes to construction. What will I need?

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: Let's see... I'd say eight oak planks, ten swamp paste and 12 nails of any kind should do it. Obviously you'll need a hammer and a saw too.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: You'll probably be wanting someone to look after the boat as well. I guess I can do that. But this means that Dallas and I are even.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric.text: There should be a good spot to build the boat on the west side of the island, near the mushroom forest.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-talking-t.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-talking-t.text: Hello again. How's the boat coming along?

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-talking-t.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-talking-t.text: You'll need a saw, a hammer, eight oak planks, ten swamp paste and 12 nails of any kind. The best place to build the boat will be on the west side of the island, near the mushroom forest.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-at-the-ro.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-at-the-ro.text: Hello again. This should be a good place to build the boat.

to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-at-the-ro.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-jardric-at-the-ro.text: You'll need a saw, a hammer, eight oak planks, ten swamp paste and 12 nails of any kind.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.text: Hello again. How's the boat coming along?

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.text: Well talk to Jardric if you need some help. He'll know what to do.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.speaker: Jardric
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.text: And not a bad boat either. Good job.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-row.text: This is it. This is our chance to finally find some answers. To finally find out the truth behind Elvarg. Are you ready to go?

steps.player: I'm ready.

steps.text: Player is transported to Lithkren

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Look at this place! I'm going to explore and see what I can find.
Dallas departs to explore the island.

steps.player: Someone's in a hurry. I suppose I should look around as well.

steps.speaker: Jardric
steps.text: And I guess I'll stay here and look after the boat. Good luck.

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Well don't take too long. We've had to wait years for this. I don't want to wait much longer.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.player: Well those are some big doors.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.text: Look at them. Look at the markings on them.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.text: Exactly. This is it. This has to be the place.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.text: We can't. I already tried, but the doors are sealed. There's a circular indentation in the middle. Maybe it's a keyhole.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-at-the-anc.player: Well a keyhole isn't much good if there isn't a key. We should look around and see if there are any clues nearby.

to-lithkren-searching-the-charred-skelet.text: You find an old book next to the skeleton.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.text: If the player has not read Aivas' diary:

steps.player: I found an old diary nearby but I haven't read it yet.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Well read it and see what it says. It could well contain the information we need.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.text: If the player has read Aivas' diary:

steps.player: I found an old diary nearby but I haven't read it yet.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Well read it and see what it says. It could well contain the information we need.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Any luck?

steps.player: I found an old diary nearby. It mentioned a battle that took place here involving Robert the Strong.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Robert the Strong? He spent most of his life fighting the dragonkin. Does this mean it's true? Did they really create the dragons?

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: I guess we'll never know though. Robert the Strong is gone. We've reached a dead end.

steps.player: Not necessarily. Robert the Strong might not be as dead as you think.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.player: Robert the Strong is still alive. He's been reincarnated as a cat called Bob.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Just think once before you speak please.

steps.player: I'm serious! Why would I lie about this?

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: Well I'm definitely not convinced, but let's say you're telling the truth... how can a cat help us?

steps.player: I have an amulet that lets me talk to cats. I can use it to ask Bob what he knows.

steps.speaker: Dallas Jones
steps.text: This is all very confusing. You go find this cat of yours. I need to sit down and clear my head of all this weirdness.

steps.player: Very well. I shall return once I've learnt more.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.text: Hello. Have you found that cat yet?

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.player: Not yet I'm afraid. He likes to move around a lot.

to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.speaker: Dallas Jones
to-lithkren-talking-to-dallas-after-find.text: Well keep at it. We need to get through these doors.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.player: Not bad. I was wondering if you could help me with something.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.text: I guess that depends what it is.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.player: So you know how you're actually Robert the Strong?

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.text: So you and the Sphinx tell me.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.player: Long story, I'll keep it brief. I found an old dungeon with a large set of doors in it. There was a skeleton nearby with a diary that mentioned Robert the Strong.
I was hoping you could use your memories of Robert the Strong to help me open the doors.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.text: But I don't have any memories of Robert the Strong. It was only when the Sphinx hypnotised me that we learnt who I really was and I don't even remember that.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.player: Maybe the Sphinx can help us again.
That it did. Bob, would you mind meeting me in Sophanem?

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.text: Well I suppose I don't have anything better to do. Not unless Unferth has forgotten where he lives again.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.text: Oh fudge. Give me one moment, [player name].
Bob and Neite have a quiet conversation with each other.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob.text: Well that all sounds great to me, [player name]. I'll meet you in Sophanem.

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob-talking-to-bo.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob-talking-to-bo.text: Hello, [player name]. I'm on my way to Sophanem to see the Sphinx.

steps.player: Where's Bob?

steps.speaker: Neite
steps.text: He's meant to be with you. You haven't lost him have you?

steps.player: I don't think so.

steps.speaker: Neite
steps.text: Well keep an eye on him for me.

options.text: Do you talk to the Sphinx much?
Ask the Sphinx for help with Bob's memories.

steps.text: If the player is not wearing a catspeak amulet:

steps.player: I should probably wear my catspeak amulet before talking to Bob and the Sphinx.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a catspeak amulet:

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Hello, human. Bob was just telling me about your dungeon.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: That's right. Before we get into that though, about that thing I mentioned...

steps.player: Thing?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Ah yes. That amulet of yours is very useful, but it has limitations. I can use my power to grant you the ability to talk to cats even when you're not wearing it.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Very few humans are ever given this power, but you've proven yourself to be a friend to feline kind.

steps.player: I'm very honoured.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Excellent. Prepare yourself!
You feel a strange tingling as the Sphinx casts her enchantment upon you.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: All done. Now, what is it you need my help with?

steps.player: We were hoping you could hypnotise Bob again so we can learn more about his past.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: What is it you wish to learn?

steps.player: It's about that dungeon. I believe that it was once visited by Robert the Strong. I want to know what he did while he was there.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I'm afraid I will be of little help here. All I can do is hypnotise Bob. I can't enter his mind and choose which memory to view.

steps.player: Hmm... Enter his mind...

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: What are you thinking, [player name]?

steps.player: I once entered the mind of a guy called Cyrisus to confront some personal issues of his. The Oneiromancer on Lunar Isle helped me do it. Maybe she can help us now.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Okay, I'll join you there. That's going to be a long walk on these paws.
If the player has their pet cat with them:

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: More walking? Why don't we ever get a nice easy teleport for these things?

bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob-before-leavin.speaker: Bob
bob-the-cat-talking-to-bob-before-leavin.text: I'm not ready to set out yet. You go on ahead. I'll meet you on Lunar Isle and we'll ask the Oneiromancer to help us.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: Hello again, [player name]. The Oneiromancer and I were just discussing what our perfect Sunday would be.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.player: I didn't know you two knew each other. Also, how can you speak to cats?

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Oneiromancer
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: You know it's really not that hard. You just need a bit of magic on your side. Anyway, Bob and I go way back.
If the player has their pet cat with them:

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Seems like everyone knows everyone in these parts.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: If the player doesn't have their pet cat with them:

steps.player: Huh... small world.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Oneiromancer
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: So what was it you wanted?

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.player: We need to unlock Bob's memories from his old life as Robert the Strong. We were hoping that we could use a shared dream.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Oneiromancer
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: Well we've never actually done a shared dream between a human and a cat before, but it shouldn't be any different. You'll just need another Potion of Shared Dreaming.
If the player has their pet cat with them:

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Should we be worried here?

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Oneiromancer
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: Would you like me to remind you how they are made?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: I'll give you a vial. You'll need to fill it with water, followed by one ground astral rune and some goutweed.

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: Once you've done that, light the brazier in the middle of town. When you're ready to begin your dream, just use the potion on the brazier.
If the player does not have a free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: Here's a vial for your potion. Good luck.
a dream vial

steps.player: No thanks.

steps.text: If the player does not have a free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: Here's a vial for your potion. Good luck.
a dream vial

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: You should get to work on making that potion.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.player: Hi, Bob! I've finished the Potion of Shared Dreaming.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-on-luna.text: Good stuff. Take it to the brazier in the middle of town and we can begin the dream.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-the-oneirom.speaker: Oneiromancer
robert-the-strong-talking-to-the-oneirom.text: Hello there. What do you want to talk about?

steps.text: If the player already has a dream vial:

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: How are things going?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: Take the vial I gave you and fill it with water. After that, add one ground astral rune and some goutweed.
If the player does not have a free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: Here's a vial for your potion. Good luck.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-the-oneirom.speaker: Oneiromancer
robert-the-strong-talking-to-the-oneirom.text: Hello there. What do you want to talk about?

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: How are things going?

steps.player: I've made the Potion of Shared Dreaming.

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: In that case you should take it to the brazier in the middle of town.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-by-the-.player: Hi, Bob! I've finished the Potion of Shared Dreaming.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-by-the-.text: If the player has not lit up the Ceremonial Brazier:

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Good stuff. Light the brazier then add the potion.

robert-the-strong-talking-to-bob-by-the-.text: If the player has lit up the Ceremonial Brazier:

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Good stuff. Add the potion to the brazier and we can begin.

robert-the-strong-using-the-potion-on-th.prompt: Are you ready to enter the dream?

steps.text: Player and Bob enter the dream.

robert-the-strong-using-the-potion-on-th.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-using-the-potion-on-th.text: Hello, [player name]. Shall we go back into the dream again?

robert-the-strong-using-the-potion-on-th.prompt: Are you ready to enter the dream?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: Well one thing's for sure, I'm definitely Not Bob.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: Okay... so who are you then?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: I just told you, I'm Not Bob.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: So Not Bob, why are you here?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: You tell me. It's your mind we're in right now.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.player: We're here to recover Bob's lost memories from his life as Robert the Strong. Do you think you can help us?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: I suppose I can. This barrier represents the divide between Bob the Cat and Robert the Strong. The memories you seek are right here, on the other side of the barrier.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: So all we need to do is go through the barrier?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: Going through the barrier will give you access to Robert's memories, but only while you're in the dream. As soon as you leave, you'll forget them again.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.player: So how can we permanently unlock them?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: Destroying the barrier of course. Head through the barrier and defeat the guardian. That should do the trick.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: Defeat the guardian? I'm no good at combat... I'm a cat.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.text: Good job this is a shared dream then. It doesn't have to be you that defeats him.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream.player: Looks like it's up to me then. Wish me luck.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream-tal.player: What should I be doing again?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream-tal.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream-tal.text: Apparently you need to defeat the guardian on the other side of this barrier. Sounds odd to me, but what do I know.

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream-tal.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream-tal.speaker: Not Bob
robert-the-strong-inside-bob-s-dream-tal.text: Pass through the barrier and defeat the guardian. That should restore Bob's lost memories.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: I remember! Lithkren! The dragonkin! The vault!
Flashback starts

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Dragonkin
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Robert! I should have known that this would be your doing.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Robert the Strong
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: It's over dragonkin. The island is ours. You have lost.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Dragonkin
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Lost? This is no more than a minor setback. The work we have done here will see the end of your kind. You are too late to stop it.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Aivas
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: And what work might that be?

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Dragonkin
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Our new weapon. One that will bring a swift end to humanity. I'd love to be able to show you, but I'm afraid I have more pressing matters.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Camorra
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Like dying perhaps?

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Dragonkin
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: You'd like that, wouldn't you? Alas, I'm afraid that I won't be the one that dies today.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Tristan
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: We'll see about that.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Dragonkin
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Yes we will, for this is where it begins.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Robert the Strong
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: No. This is where it ends.
The heroes begin to fight the dragonkin. Aivas is killed instantly upon the dragonkin attacking him.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Tristan
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Aivas!

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Camorra
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: You'll pay for that!
The heroes continue the assault, eventually defeating the dragonkin, who drops a dragon key.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Tristan
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: What is that?

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Robert the Strong
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Looks like some sort of key. For these doors I assume.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Camorra
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Should we open them?

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Robert the Strong
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: No. That dragonkin mentioned a weapon. One that could destroy us all. Better something like that remains hidden... for now.
Robert picks up the key, and the flashback ends.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: I've got a lot to take in and understand, but I'm okay.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.player: So do you have all of your memories back now?

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Yes and no. I now have my old memories again, but there are so many of them. I can't quite piece them all together yet. I need time to properly work things out.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: However, one thing that I do remember clearly is that battle. I also remember what happened next.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: After the battle, myself, Tristan and Camorra split the key into four pieces. We vowed to ensure that the dragonkin would never recover them, and to only return once the war was won.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: No. In the end, we went our seperate ways. Of the four pieces, Camorra took one, Tristan took another and I took the final two.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Camorra eventually boarded a ship for lands to the far west, never to be seen again. She took her key piece with her.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: Tristan passed his piece on to his descendants. They lived in the city of Saranthium, where Varrock now stands. Perhaps the Varrock Library has some record of them.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: I hid one of my pieces in the most unlikely of places, an abandoned dragonkin fortress. You'll find the fortress on a snow covered island, north west of Rellekka.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: The final piece I took to Karamja. I hid it in an ancient temple on the south coast of the island.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.player: Sounds like I have a fair amount of work to do. Thanks, Bob.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: With the dragonkin long gone, the vault should be safe to open. That said, you should still be cautious, [player name].

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories.text: The scars of our war with the dragonkin remain to this day, and the weapon in that vault could still be very dangerous.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.player: Hi, Bob. Could you remind me where those key pieces are?

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.text: The key was split into four different pieces. Camorra took one piece, Tristan took another and I took the final two.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.text: Camorra boarded a ship for lands to the far west, never to be seen again. She took her key piece with her.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.text: Tristan passed his piece on to his descendants. They lived in the city of Saranthium, where Varrock now stands. Perhaps the Varrock Library has some record of them.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.text: I hid one of my pieces in the most unlikely of places, an abandoned dragonkin fortress. You'll find the fortress on a snow covered island, north west of Rellekka.

robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.speaker: Bob
robert-the-strong-robert-s-memories-talk.text: The final piece I took to Karamja. I hid it in an ancient temple on the south coast of the island.

steps.player: Hello. I was wondering if you could help me with something?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: What do you need?

steps.player: I'm looking for information on a Fourth Age hero. His name was Tristan and he fought alongside Robert the Strong.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Ah, you must mean Tristan Corvo. I can't remember anyone ever asking about him before. Most prefer to hear about the bigger heroes like Arrav or Robert.

steps.player: But you know about Tristan?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Oh yes. What was it you wanted to learn?

steps.player: I'd like to learn about his descendants. I know they lived in this area.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Well we do have census records which date back to when the city was still called Avarrocka, but I'm afraid we don't have anything from before that time.

steps.player: Hmm... It might still be worth a look. Where can I find this information?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I have a book around here somewhere with all of the details. Why don't you see if you can find it? It's red if I remember right.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Have you found that book yet?

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I know it's around here somewhere. It's red if I remember right.

tristan-s-key-piece-finding-the-book.text: You find an interesting looking book.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Have you found that book yet?

steps.player: I have it here.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Wonderful! Let's have a look.
You hand the book to Reldo.

steps.player: So what does the book say?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Okay let's see... The Corvo family... Here we are! According to this, there was a family by the name of Corvo living in Avarrocka for most of the Fourth Age.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: The last entry is from the year 1770 of the Fourth Age.

steps.player: What happened to them?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Impossible to say for sure, but it was around that time that many people left Misthalin to settle in Morytania. It's possible that the Corvo family was among them.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I'm afraid that's all the help I can provide. Port Phasmatys is where most of the Morytania settlers wound up. Perhaps you'll find what you're looking for there.

steps.player: Okay, thanks Reldo.
Hello.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Did you have any luck finding the Corvo family?

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Port Phasmatys might be a good place to look. It's where most of the Morytania settlers wound up.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-a-ghost-v.player: Hello. Do you know anyone with the name Corvo?

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-a-ghost-v.speaker: Ghost villager
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-a-ghost-v.text: Sarah Corvo? She lives in the house next to the bank.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.player: Hello. Do you know anyone with the name Corvo?

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.speaker: Sarah
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.text: Of course. I'm Sarah Corvo. Not many people interested in visiting me these days. What brings you here?

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.player: I'm on the hunt for the piece of a key. It was once in the possession of your ancestor, Tristan Corvo.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.speaker: Sarah
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.text: I see. I'm afraid I can't help you. The key piece is gone.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.speaker: Sarah
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.text: Yes gone. When my father passed the key piece down to me, he told me that I must keep it safe no matter what. When the vampyres came to Port Phasmatys, I buried it out in the swamps to stop them getting it.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.player: But how do I get it back?

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.speaker: Sarah
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.text: You don't. The key piece is gone and it's safer that way. I never liked looking after that red lump of metal anyway.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.player: Hmm... I think I might know just the scientist to help me out with this. Time for me to visit Draynor Manor.
Oh, nothing. I'd best be off. Thank you for your time.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.speaker: Sarah
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.text: You again. You're not still after that key piece are you?

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-sarah-cor.player: Nope. Just stopping by to say hello.
Well that was great. See you later.

tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-ava.speaker: Ava
tristan-s-key-piece-talking-to-ava.text: Hello again. Are you after another device, or some information, or would you like to see my goods for sale?

options.text: I need your help with a key piece.

steps.player: I need your help with a key piece.

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.text: A key piece?

steps.player: Yes. I'm looking for the piece of a key made out of red metal. I know it's buried somewhere in Mort Myre Swamp, but I don't know exactly where. I was thinking...

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.text: You were thinking that because I made you a metal attracting device before that I'd be able to do it again.

steps.player: Er... yeah, pretty much.
