finishing-up.player: Hello there.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: I have word from Sanfew that you have been very helpful in assisting him with his preparations for the purification ritual. As promised I will now teach you the ancient arts of Herblore.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Herblore is the skill of working with herbs and other ingredients, to make useful potions and poison.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: First you will need a vial, which can be found or made with the crafting skill.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Then you must gather the herbs needed to make the potion you want.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: You must fill your vial with water and add the ingredients you need. There are normally 2 ingredients to each type of potion.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Bear in mind, you must first clean each herb before you can use it.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: You may also have to grind some ingredients before you can use them. You will need a pestle and mortar in order to do this.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Herbs can be found on the ground, and are also dropped by some monsters when you kill them.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Let's try an example Attack potion: The first ingredient is Guam leaf; the next is Eye of Newt.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Mix these in your water-filled vial, and you will produce an Attack potion. Drink this potion to increase your Attack level.

finishing-up.speaker: Kaqemeex
finishing-up.text: Different potions also require different Herblore levels before you can make them.

Welcome to the Emir's Arena! Are you interested in Duels? We organise ranked Duels here, or alternatively you can organise your own unranked Duels.

steps.player: What's a Duel?

steps.npc: Two fighters are placed in a combat arena together, to battle to the death. The survivor wins the Duel.

options.text: Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?

steps.player: Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?

steps.npc: Everyone has a rank. It's meant to indicate how good they are at fighting, compared to other people.
In ranked fights, the winners gain rank and the losers lose rank. The Arena staff will decide who'll be fighting in each ranked Duel, and send the invitations.
But if you just want some casual fun, you can have an unranked Duel, where no-one gains or loses rank. You can organise your own unranked Duel against whoever you want to fight.
Only the ranked fights offer access to the other rewards of the Arena.

options.text: How do I get invited to a Duel?

steps.player: How do I get invited to a Duel?

steps.npc: For a ranked Duel, you'll need to sign up to the recruitment group...

steps.text: This is the icon for the Grouping tab. Within it you'll find the PvP Arena options.
There, you can click Find to seek the official group for ranked Duels.
Once you've found it, click Sign up to sign up to one, and you'll be considered for an invitation to a Duel, whenever one begins.

steps.npc: You can carry on with your adventures while you're waiting for a ranked Duel to begin, since it may be a while before suitable fighters are available.
For an unranked Duel, other people might challenge you while you're wandering around the PvP Arena, so keep an eye out for invitation messages.

steps.text: Click the Challenge option on other players to challenge them to an unranked Duel, and keep an eye on your chatbox for challenges.
You can have unranked Duels on any game world. However, the PvP Arena provides supplies only on its official game worlds, so please bring your own gear if you plan a Duel on other worlds.

options.text: I want to organise my own Duel.

steps.player: I want to organise my own Duel.

steps.npc: When you see other people wandering around the PvP Arena, you can challenge them directly, and they can challenge you. This would be an unranked Duel, so neither of you would gain rank or earn rewards.

steps.npc: Well, you're a braver [man/woman] than I!

steps.player: Why is everyone so scared of this dragon?

steps.npc: Back in my father's day, Crandor was an important city-state. Politically it was as important as Falador and Varrock and its ships traded with every port.
But, one day, when I was little, all contact was lost. The trading ships and the diplomatic envoys just stopped coming.
I remember my father being very scared. He posted lookouts on the roof to warn if the dragon was approaching. All the city rulers worried that Elvarg would devastate the whole continent.

options.text: I'd better leave that dragon alone.

steps.player: I'd better leave that dragon alone.

steps.npc: That's a relief. I would hate to see such a promising adventurer cut down in [his/her] prime.

options.text: So, are you going to give me the shield or not?

steps.npc: If you really think you're up to it then perhaps you are the one who can kill this dragon.

steps.player: Oh, no dragon in particular. I just feel like killing a dragon.

steps.npc: I hope the goblins are properly maintaining their stretch of track! I'd hate to see them spoil good Dwarven workmanship.
You're [player name], aren't you? It's a good job you did helping to get this train link open.
Y'know, at first I didn't like the idea of visiting a goblin city, but these cave goblins are alright.
These goblins have so much more advanced technology than us. Take a look at their magical lights! We could never create something like them.
Dorgesh-Kaan's very nice to visit, but I don't think I'd want to live there.

captain-lawgof.speaker: Captain Lawgof
captain-lawgof.text: Guthix be praised, the cavalry has arrived! Hero, how would you like to be made an honorary member of the Black Guard?

captain-lawgof.speaker: Captain Lawgof
captain-lawgof.text: Hawhaw! 'What's that' [he/she] asks, what a sense of humour! The Black Guard is the finest regiment in the dwarven army. Only the best of the best are allowed to join it and then they receive months of rigorous training.

captain-lawgof.speaker: Captain Lawgof
captain-lawgof.text: However, we are currently in need of a hero, so for a limited time only I'm offering you, a human, a chance to join this prestigious regiment. What do you say?

steps.player: Sure, I'd be honoured to join.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: That's the spirit! Now trooper, we have no time to waste - the goblins are attacking from the forests to the South. There are so many of them, they are overwhelming my men and breaking through our

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: perimeter defences; could you please try to fix the stockade by replacing the broken rails with these new ones?

steps.player: Sure, sounds easy enough...

steps.text: The Dwarf Captain gives you six railings.
If the player does not have a hammer:

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: You'll need this hammer too.
a hammer

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: Report back to me once you've fixed the railings.

steps.player: Yes Sir, Captain!
I'm sorry, I'm too busy mining.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: Well best make the most of it while you can, if the goblins over-run us they'll descend on the mines like a plague of locusts!

captain-lawgof-inspecting-the-broken-mul.text: The Black Guard sent Lawgof this cannon to help defend the mines against the goblins.

fixing-the-railings-trying-to-fix-a-rail.text: This railing is broken and needs to be replaced.
If the player does not have a railing:

steps.player: I'm not going to be able to fix this without a new railing. Lawgof should have some spare ones.

fixing-the-railings-trying-to-fix-a-rail.text: You attempt to repalce the broken railing...
If the player does not have a hammer:

steps.text: You will need a hammer to fix the railings.

fixing-the-railings-trying-to-fix-a-rail.text: If the player fails to repair the railing:

steps.text: Your arm is getting tired.
You cut yourself on the rusty old railing.
You accidentally crush your hand in the railing.
You wrench your back trying to handle the railings.
(The player is dealt 0-2 damage.)

steps.player: Oooch!
Ow!
Urrrgh!
Gah!

fixing-the-railings-trying-to-fix-a-rail.text: If the player successfully repairs the railing:

steps.text: This railing is now fixed.

fixing-the-railings-trying-to-fix-a-rail.text: If all the railing are fixed:

steps.player: I've fixed all these railings now.

fixing-the-railings-inspecting-a-fixed-r.player: I've fixed all these railings now.

fixing-the-railings-using-other-items-on.player: That's better, the goblins won't get past this piece of fencing now.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: Hello, trooper, how are you doing with those railings?

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: The goblins are still getting in, so there must still be some broken railings.
If the player has no railings:

steps.player: But I'm out of railings...

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: That's okay, we've got plenty, here you go.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: There's no room in your backpack, so I can't give you anymore.
The Dwarf Captain gives you another railing.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: If the player has at least 1 railing:

steps.player: Don't worry, I'll find them soon enough.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: Well done, trooper! The goblins seems to have stopped getting in. I think you've done the job!

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.player: Great, I'll be getting on then.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: What? I'll have you jailed for desertion!

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: Besides, I have another commission for you. Just before the goblins over-ran us we lost contact with our watch tower to the South, that's why the goblins managed to catch us unawares. I'd like you to perform

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: a covert operation into enemy territory, to check up on the guards we have stationed there.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: They should have reported in by now ...

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.player: Okay, I'll see what I can find out.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: Excellent! I have two men there, the dwarf-in-charge is called Gilob, find him and tell him that I'll send him a relief guard just as soon as we mop up these remaining goblins.

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: Hello, any news from the watchman?

fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-railings-talking-to-captain-l.text: Well, as quick as you can then.

finding-the-remains-picking-up-the-remai.text: If the player already has the remains:

steps.player: What? Carrying one set of Dwarf remains is enough...

finding-the-remains-picking-up-the-remai.player: I had better take these remains. {{^|Remains drop to ground with full inventory.}}

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.text: Have you been to the watch tower yet?

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.player: Yes, I went up but there was no one there.

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.text: That's strange, Gilob would never leave his post... His son was also with him, something doesn't smell right. Can you return and look for clues?

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.player: Of course, I'll do what I can.

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.text: Have you been to the watch tower yet?

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.player: I have some terrible news for you Captain, the goblins over ran the tower, your guards fought well but were overwhelmed.

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.text: You give the Dwarf Captain his subordinate's remains...

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.text: I can't believe it, Gilob was the finest lieutenant I had! We'll give him a fitting funeral, but what of his command? His son, Lollk, was with him. Did you find his body too?

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.player: No, there was only one body there, I searched pretty well.

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.speaker: Captain Lawgof
finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.text: The goblins must have taken him. Please traveler, seek out the goblins' hideout and return the lad to us. They always attack from the South-east, so they must be based down there.

finding-the-remains-talking-to-captain-l.player: Okay, I'll see if I can find their hideout.

the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.text: You search the crate but find nothing.
Inside you see a dwarf child, tied up!

the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.speaker: Lollk
the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.text: Thank the heavens, you saved me! I thought I'd be goblin lunch for sure!

the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.speaker: Lollk
the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.text: I think so, I'd better run off home.

the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.player: That's right, you get going, I'll catch up.

the-dwarf-child-searching-the-crate-cont.text: The dwarf child runs off into the caverns.

the-dwarf-child-talking-to-captain-lawgo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
the-dwarf-child-talking-to-captain-lawgo.text: He has, and I thank you from the bottom of my heart - without you he'd be a goblin barbecue!

the-dwarf-child-talking-to-captain-lawgo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
the-dwarf-child-talking-to-captain-lawgo.text: In that case could I ask one more favour of you...

the-dwarf-child-talking-to-captain-lawgo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
the-dwarf-child-talking-to-captain-lawgo.text: When the goblins attacked us some of them managed to slip past my guards and sabotage our cannon. I don't have anybody who understands how it works, could you have a look at it and see if you could get it working for

options.text: Okay, I'll see what I can do.

steps.player: Okay, I'll see what I can do.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: Thank you, take this toolkit, you'll need it...
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: You don't have room to take this, report back to me when you do.
The Dwarf Captain gives you a tool kit.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: Report back to me if you manage to fix it.

options.text: Sorry, I've done enough for today.

steps.player: Sorry, I've done enough for today.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: Fair enough, didn't think you'd be able to help anyway, not much chance for a human to be able to fix it when the best dwarven engineers have failed.

fixing-the-cannon-inspecting-the-broken-.player: I guess I'd better fix it with the toolkit I was given.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: How are you doing in there, trooper? We've been trying our best with that thing, but I just haven't got the patience.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.player: It's not an easy job, but I'm getting there.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: Good stuff, let me know if you have any luck. If we manage to get that thing working, those goblins will be no trouble at all.
If the player lost the toolkit:

steps.player: I'm afraid I lost the toolkit...

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: That was silly... never mind, I can give you another, but you'll have to free up some space in your backpack first.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: That was silly... never mind, here you go.
The Dwarf Captain gives you another toolkit.

fixing-the-cannon-fixing-the-cannon.text: Well done! You've fixed the cannon! Better go and tell Captain Lawgof.

fixing-the-cannon-fire-the-fixed-dwarf-m.player: This should work nicely now that I've fixed it.

fixing-the-cannon-pick-up-the-fixed-dwar.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-pick-up-the-fixed-dwar.text: What do you think you're doing, trooper! Did I give you orders to move that cannon? No! Well then don't!

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.player: Well, I think I've done it, take a look...

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: Well I don't believe it, it seems to be working perfectly! I seem to have underestimated you, trooper!

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.player: Not bad for an adventurer eh?

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: You give the toolkit back to Captain Lawgof.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: Not bad at all, your effort is appreciated, my friend. Now, if I could figure what the thing uses as ammo...

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: The Black Guard forgot to send instructions. I know I said that was the last favour, but...

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: I can't leave this post, could you go to the Black Guard base and find out what this thing actually shoots?

steps.player: Sorry, I've really done enough.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: Fair enough, fair enough.

steps.player: Okay then, just for you!

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: That's great, we were lucky you came along when you did. The base is located just South of the Ice Mountain.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: You'll need to speak to Nulodion, the Dwarf Cannon engineer. He's the Weapons Development Chief for the Black Guard, so if anyone knows how to fire this thing, it'll be him.

steps.player: Okay, I'll see what I can do.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: Hello trooper, any word from the Cannon Engineer?

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.speaker: Captain Lawgof
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-captain-law.text: The Black Guard camp is South of the Ice Mountain, the quicker we can get some ammo for this thing the quicker those Goblins will leave us be.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.player: Captain Lawgof sent me. He's having trouble with his cannon.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.speaker: Nulodion
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.text: Of course, we forgot to send the ammo mould!

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.speaker: Nulodion
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.text: Don't be silly - the ammo's made by using a mould. Here, take these to him. The instructions explain everything.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Nulodion
steps.text: You can't take these things unless you free up some space in your inventory. I suggest you visit a bank and then come back to talk to me.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.text: The Cannon Engineer gives you some notes and a mould.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.speaker: Nulodion
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion.text: Thank you, adventurer. The Dwarf Black Guard will remember this.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.text: If the player lost the notes:

steps.player: I've lost the notes.

steps.speaker: Nulodion
steps.text: Here, take these...

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.text: If the player lost the ammo mould:

steps.player: I've lost the cannonball mould.

steps.speaker: Nulodion
steps.text: Deary me, you are trouble. Here, take this one.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.speaker: Nulodion
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.text: So has the Captain figured out how to work the cannon yet?

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.player: Not yet, but I'm sure he will.

fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.speaker: Nulodion
fixing-the-cannon-talking-to-nulodion-ag.text: If you can get those items to him it'll be a great help.

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.text: Hello trooper, any word from the Cannon Engineer?

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.player: Yes, I have spoken to him.

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.text: If the player does not have the notes and ammo mould:

steps.player: He gave me some items to give you... but I seem to have lost something.

steps.speaker: Captain Lawgof
steps.text: If you could go back and get another, I'd appreciate it.

steps.player: Oh, okay then.

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.player: He gave me an ammo mould and some notes to give to you...

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.text: Aah, of course, we make the ammo! This is great, now we will be able to defend ourselves. I don't know how to thank you...

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.player: You could give me a cannon...

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.text: Hah! You'd be lucky, those things are worth a fortune.

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.text: I'll tell you what though, I'll write to the Cannon Engineer requesting him to sell you one. He controls production of the cannons.

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.speaker: Captain Lawgof
talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.text: He won't be able to give you one, but for the right price, I'm sure he'll sell one to you.

talking-to-lawgof-after-getting-the-ammo.player: Hmmm... sounds interesting, I might take you up on that.

steps.npc: Yeah...whada you want?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm nobody you need to worry about...who are you? Why are you asking so many questions? Are you with the Varrock guards?

steps.player: What're you doing here?

steps.npc: Well, as if it's any of your business, I'm an associate of Hammerspike. He's a great dwarf you know. You could learn a lot from a dwarf like him.

steps.player: Who do you work for?

steps.npc: I have an ongoing contract with Hammerspike, when he gives the word, the hammer starts flying.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

pre-quest-dialogue.npc: Ho there, [player name]! Want to take a ride with me?

pre-quest-dialogue.player: Where are you going? Across the river?

pre-quest-dialogue.npc: No no, that's what the ferryman is for! I'm going to Keldagrim, my home!

pre-quest-dialogue.player: How much will that cost me then?

pre-quest-dialogue.npc: For a human like you, I can do it for free!

steps.player: That's a deal!

steps.npc: Excellent! I'm just waiting for my ship to arrive and then we can go.
Mind, this trip could take a few minutes! Are you sure you're ready to go as well?

steps.text: If the player does not have the skills to complete The Giant Dwarf:
Before starting this quest, be aware that one or more of your skill levels are lower than what is required to fully complete it.

steps.prompt: Start The Giant Dwarf quest?

steps.text: Continues in Transcript:The Giant Dwarf

steps.player: No, I don't have time right now, I'll be back later.

steps.npc: Sure, sure! Come back when you need to!

options.text: I prefer the mines to the city.

steps.player: I prefer the mines to the city.

steps.npc: Well, suit yourself then!

standard-dialogue-mines.npc: Hello again, [player name]! Want to go back to Keldagrim?

steps.player: Yes, please take me.

options.text: What, on your ship? No way.

steps.player: What, on your ship? No way.

steps.npc: Hey, it was only a little accident! Calm down!

standard-dialogue-keldagrim.npc: Want me to take you back to the mines?

steps.player: Yes, please take me.

options.text: What, on your ship! No thanks!

steps.player: What, on your ship? No thanks! I don't want to crash into any more things!

steps.npc: Hey now, it was only a slight accident!

steps.text: During The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: A slight accident?? Thanks to you I have to rebuild this statue you so carelessly knocked over!

steps.text: After The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: A slight accident?? Have you any idea how much time I spent rebuilding that statue?

steps.npc: Calm down, calm down! You got what you paid for the trip, didn't you?
Do you have any gold ore that you want me to take to the bank in the city?

steps.text: If the player has no gold ore:

steps.player: I don't have any, I'm afraid.

steps.text: If the player has 1 gold ore:

steps.player: Well, I have this one piece of ore...

steps.npc: That wouldn't do you much good, I'm afraid. My minimum fee is one piece of gold ore, there wouldn't be anything left for you.

options.text: Yes, please take my gold to the city.

steps.player: Yes, please take my gold to the city. I've got [number] pieces of ore right here.

steps.text: If the player does not have sufficient bank space or is an Ultimate Ironman:

steps.npc: Are you sure you have enough space in your bank account for that?

steps.player: No, you're right actually, I don't.

steps.npc: Let's see, if I take that to the bank for you, I'd keep [number] for myself and bring [number] to the bank for you. Does that sound fair?

steps.player: Yes, it does.

steps.npc: Excellent, it's been good doing business with you! I'll take these to the city with my next shipment.

steps.player: No, that's far too expensive for me.

options.text: No, I'll hang on to these myself.

steps.player: No, I'll hang on to these myself, thanks.

options.text: [Charm] It all seems a bit expensive, really.
options.condition: If the player is wearing the Ring of Charos(a):

steps.player: It all seems a bit expensive, really.

steps.npc: I don't know... it's just what Dondakan told me, if someone wanted me to ship their gold.

steps.player: There's plenty of gold coming from that rock now, surely you can lower the price somewhat?

steps.npc: Alright. Tell you what, I'll only keep [number] for myself and bring [number] ores to the bank for you. Deal?

steps.player: Yes, much appreciated.

steps.npc: Excellent, it's been good doing business with you!

steps.player: No, I'll hang on to these myself, thanks.

steps.npc: I wish you'd just leave me alone.

steps.player: Why, what's wrong?

steps.npc: I was a great engineer once. Still am actually.
They just don't let me do the work I do best anymore.

steps.player: What do you do then?

steps.npc: I'm an assistant in this shop. I get all the lousy jobs too.

steps.player: Well, I'm sorry to hear that.

standard-dialogue-north-ferryman.npc: Want to cross the river? It's just 2 gold pieces!

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.text: If the player has 2 coins:
The dwarf ferries you across the river.
If the player doesn't have 2 coins:

steps.npc: You don't even have 2 gold coins, human!
Come back later.

steps.player: But... that means I'm stuck here.

steps.npc: Hmm. I suppose I could make an exception for you this time.

steps.text: If the player has exactly 1 coin:

steps.npc: Here, let me just relieve you of that one coin you have there and I'll take you across.

steps.player: Thanks a lot!

steps.text: The dwarf ferries you across the river.

steps.player: No thanks.

options.text: [Charm] I don't have any money on me.
options.condition: If the player has the Ring of Charos equipped:

steps.player: I don't have any money on me, now I'm stuck here forever!

steps.npc: Oh, we wouldn't want that to happen. Come along, you can go for free this time.

steps.text: The dwarf ferries you across the river.

standard-dialogue-south-ferryman.npc: Want to cross the river? It's just 2 gold pieces!

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.text: If the player has 2 coins:
The dwarf ferries you across the river.
If the player doesn't have 2 coins:

steps.player: No thanks.

options.text: [Charm] I don't have any money on me.
options.condition: If the player has the Ring of Charos equipped:

steps.player: I don't have any money on me, is that alright?

steps.npc: I... guess.

steps.text: The dwarf ferries you across the river.

historical-dialogue-south-ferryman-stand.npc: Across the river, across the river! It's just a short ride!

historical-dialogue-south-ferryman-stand.player: How much will that cost me?

historical-dialogue-south-ferryman-stand.npc: Haha, you understand us dwarves well, human!
It's just 2 gold pieces! Want to go?

options.text: I'd like to go further downstream.

steps.player: I'd like to go further downstream.

steps.npc: You mean to the city of Keldagrim?

steps.player: Ehm, yes, I think so.

steps.npc: Sorry, I'm just a simple ferryman, I only go across.
But talk to my friend here, he sometimes goes to the city in his ship.

steps.player: Thanks.

Player is transported across the river
If the player has fewer than 2 coins:

steps.player: No thanks.

bringing-over-the-outfit-to-nickolaus-go.text: I already have a golden feather like that.

bringing-over-the-outfit-to-nickolaus-in.text: The door seems to be locked in place. There is an engraving of an eagle on the door. Three of the feathers illustrated in the engraving seem to be cut deeper than the others. It looks like they may once have contained some sort of decoration.
Unfortunately this metal feather doesn't seem to match any of the indentations in the engraving.

There doesn't seem to be any way of attaching this feather to the engraving. The indentations look like they probably contained some sort of decoration rather than real feathers, although there is no sign of their whereabouts now.
You insert the metallic feather into one of the feather-shaped indentations in the engravings.
As you insert the metallic feather into the final indentation you hear a low grinding as if stone blocks were moving against one another.
The engraving is already complete. There is nowhere left to put this feather.
You must have completed the Eagles' Peak quest before you can try to lasso a giant eagle.

saving-nickolaus-passing-the-eagle.text: You edge cautiously past the eagle; it doesn't seem to object.

saving-nickolaus-with-eagle-outfit.player: Hello Nickolaus, how are you getting on with your discoveries?

saving-nickolaus-with-eagle-outfit.text: If the player is wearing the eagle disguise:

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: What's this, a young hatchling?  Oh no, I hope it doesn't think I'm its dinner!

steps.player: No, Nickolaus, it's me!  I'm just in disguise!

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: You're sure...you're sure you're not going to eat me?

steps.player: No of course not. You sent me to get you an eagle outfit remember?  So you could get out of this nest?

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Wow, that really is a very convincing disguise.  Have you got one for me too?

saving-nickolaus-with-eagle-outfit.text: If the player has a disguise for Nickolaus:

steps.player: Yes, I have one right here.

steps.text: You give Nickolaus a fake beak and an eagle feather cape.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Excellent, now there is no way the eagle will be able to tell me from one of its own.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Now you run off, and I'll meet you back down at the camp site.

saving-nickolaus-with-eagle-outfit.text: If the player does not have a disguise for Nickolaus:

saving-nickolaus-talking-to-nickolaus-ag.player: I've given you the disguise you needed, can we go now?

saving-nickolaus-talking-to-nickolaus-ag.speaker: Nickolaus
saving-nickolaus-talking-to-nickolaus-ag.text: Calm down.  You must realise I can't leave just like that, this is far too amazing an opportunity.  Just go down to the camp site and I'll meet you there.

saving-nickolaus-talking-to-nickolaus-by.speaker: Nickolaus
saving-nickolaus-talking-to-nickolaus-by.text: Ah, hello again.  Can I help at all?

options.text: Well I was originally sent to find you because of a ferret.

steps.player: Well I was originally sent to find you because of a ferret.  Can you get me one at all?

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: I'll do better than that.  I'll teach you how to capture one yourself.

steps.player: That sounds good to me.  What do I do.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Come with me and I'll show you.
Cutscene starts.

steps.player: Okay, so we've baited the trap with meat, now what?

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: And now...we wait. Quietly!

steps.player: But what if I don't like waiting for things?

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Did I mention we wait quietly?

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Shhh, here comes something.
A ferret goes into the box trap.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Ha ha, there you go! One gift-wrapped ferret ready for delivery.
Cutscene ends.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: See, it's all just a matter of patience.

steps.player: Great, thanks!

options.text: I've not got the time right now.

steps.player: I've not got the time right now.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Ah you don't get out of it that easily. When you've got the time come back and see me.

options.text: I was just wondering how you got on with those eagles.

steps.player: I was just wondering how you got on with those eagles.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: Ah wonderfully.  They're actually most cooperative creatures once they get used to you.  With some rope I'm sure you could find some way to tame them... maybe even fly on them.

options.text: No thanks.  I was just dropping by.

steps.player: No thanks.  I was just dropping by, wanted to make sure you hadn't been abducted again.

steps.speaker: Nickolaus
steps.text: No such luck I'm afraid, but I'm sure I'll make another discovery soon enough.  I always seem to.

finishing-up.speaker: Charlie
finishing-up.text: Ah, hello again. Have you had any luck finding a clue as to Nickolaus' whereabouts yet?

finishing-up.player: Yes I have actually. He'd been abducted by giant eagles, but I managed to rescue him. He's now gotten back to his hunting.

finishing-up.speaker: Charlie
finishing-up.text: Giant eagles? What a strange notion. Well, regardless, if you've found him can you tell him to hurry up with that ferret.

finishing-up.player: Even better, I have a ferret right here for you.

finishing-up.speaker: Charlie
finishing-up.text: You do? Ah, yes, wonderful, I never doubted you for a second. That'll make an excellent addition to the zoo.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

gcO__d.player: Well, I'll let you get on with your work then.

gcO__d.speaker: Nickolaus
gcO__d.text: It's always a pleasure to discuss my discoveries.

z_tgdP.speaker: Nickolaus
z_tgdP.text: Well like I said, the Varrock fancy dress shop is a good bet if you have the materials, and there are plenty of feathers around here.

z_tgdP.speaker: Nickolaus
z_tgdP.text: And while you're working on that, I'll get back to studying these incredible winged wonders.

steps.player: Hi.

steps.player: I would love to help you mix up some more fuel.

steps.npc: Thanks for eggreeing to help me.

The first ingredient is Dried cocoa. During any other time of year this ingredient would be eggceptionally hard to get.
But if I'm spot on with my information, there should be a merchant rolling into Al Kharid soon. He should sell you some.
Try not to bring me camel dung, they do look similar.
The second ingredient is really high quality milk.
The most eggceptional milk around has got to be milk from Hosidius, I'm sure Duke Horacio's cook can help you out.
The third ingredient is some cracking spices, very special ones. Can't go into detail, trade secret and all.
I'm sure if you talk to Martin in Draynor, he'll be a good egg and help you out if you ask for Special spices.

steps.npc: See you soon!

options.text: Where do I get the bottle of Hosidius milk?

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: Easter Bunny! I knew I would find you here.

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: Easter Bunny... Now there's a name I haven't heard in a long time...

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: Do you think perhaps they weren't talking to you?

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: Who could blame them? I'm a failure!

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: Oh come on now, what do you mean?

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: You call me the Easter Bunny? What right do I have to that name?
I don't feel the spirit of Easter within me.
I'm just a big dumb rabbit!

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.text: The Easter Bunny is clearly very upset and needs cheering up. Perhaps the other people in the Rabbit Hole have some ideas?

when-spoken-to-a-second-time.player: Hello Easter Bunny, how are you feeling?

when-spoken-to-a-second-time.npc: Maybe I'll make my way through this sorry old world as a clown...

cheering-up-easter-bunny-with-bowley-mol.speaker: Bowley Moley
cheering-up-easter-bunny-with-bowley-mol.text: Hello! Have you come to take part in the festivities?

options.text: The Easter Bunny is looking awfully glum this year.

steps.player: The Easter Bunny is looking awfully glum this year.
Perhaps we can help raise the Easter spirits?

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: You want to do some necromancy... To cheer up the Easter Bunny?

steps.player: No no no! It's just a figure of speech.
I just wonder if we could do anything to help.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Leave it to me boss.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I happen to know the E.B. is a big fan of bowling. In fact, he used to be a wizard on the lanes. A champion!

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I also happen to have the ability to...

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: ...Rig the game in his favour.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Which is handy, he's very out of practise nowadays.

steps.player: Won't he suspect something?

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Oh no! You see, I have these gears set up just here.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Wait, are you just trying to get my trade secrets?

steps.player: This is strictly a humanitarian effort!
Bun-itarian..?
Look, I just want to get Easter back on track.
You can keep your hustle going, I just want to help the Easter Bunny.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Oh alright, since I do owe the big softie. But I've got my whiskers on you!
Small cutscene ensues...

steps.npc: So, what is it you wanted to show me, [player name]?

steps.player: Well, Bowley here let me in on your secret. Bowling champion three years in a row.

steps.npc: Oh. Those were the days, I haven't partaken for while now though...
I just haven't had the spring in my step with my egg responsibilities.

steps.player: Well, here's your chance!

steps.npc: What do you mean? It's hardly fun without decent competition.
And nobody here quite likes bowling.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: They what now?

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I've only just gone and spent ages digging out this place and installing the machinery!

steps.player: Nothing to worry about I'm sure!

steps.npc: Ah Bowley, it is good to see you again.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Long Ears Johnson. Come to terrorise me pins again?

steps.player: We'll see about that.

steps.npc: Oh yes, [player name] is apparently quite good.
It's been so long since I've had a decent set with a worthy opponent.

steps.player: Chin up bucko, I'm here and ready to challenge your rule of these alleys!

steps.npc: Well, I suppose I'm not doing anything else. Why not?

steps.npc: A fine shot, but not quite enough!
Watch this!

steps.text: Thunk
The Easter Bunny bowls a strike.

steps.player: A lucky strike?
I'd better shape up or this will be quite one sided.
And that would be no fun at all.

steps.text: Clang
The player bowls down the middle 6 pins.

steps.npc: Ah, so you have some fight in you.

steps.player: I could do this all day.

steps.npc: That's exactly what I wanted to hear!

steps.text: The screen fades black with the text "Some time later..."

steps.npc: I'm surprised I hadn't heard about your prowess before, [player name].

steps.player: Ah you know me, the most modest adventurer in Gielinor.

steps.npc: Ah, well I suppose I should pack it in while I'm ahead.
But we should do this again.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Aye we should! Also if you could get the word out about my establishment, I'll be raking it in!

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I mean... The Rabbit Hole will enjoy all the visitors?

steps.player: Well, anyway...
It was a close match. How are you feeling now?

steps.npc: Oh it was fun but I think I'm just going to sit in the Rabbit Hole a bit longer.
I should be off. Always a pleasure, Bowley.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Aye, till next time.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.player: Here, it's an Easter bun. Fresh out of the oven.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.npc: An Easter bun? I like those!

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.player: You are most welcome. Do you feel a bit more Easter- ey now?

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.npc: Oh, I'm starting to remember now! Easter is great! But I just... Hmm, I don't know...
I feel like I need one more little treat before I do anything to help with Easter.

magic of our god. This heirloom will help you with the speed of your spell- casting.

steps.npc: Hi there. I'm Ektheme, an expert on the Xerician era.

steps.player: Who was Xeric?

steps.npc: Xeric was a dark mage who ruled Great Kourend for at least ten decades. A time period that is sometimes known as the Age of Strife.

steps.player: At least? Do you not know how long he was in power for?

steps.npc: We do have records of course. However, while Xeric was indeed ruler of the kingdom from the 37th to the 47th decades, some believe that he actually ruled for longer.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: It is often speculated that Xeric and his predecessor, King Shayzien VII, were in fact the same person.

steps.player: How could that be?

steps.npc: Like Xeric, King Shayzien VII was fascinated with the Dark Altar.
The King was killed at the Battle of the Concourse during the 37th decade. We have many accounts of this, yet his body was never recovered.
Just days after his death, we have the first recorded mention of Xeric, an incredibly powerful mage who resembled the King.
It is written that Xeric killed the rulers of Kourend's five cities and claimed the kingdom as his own.

steps.player: So King Shayzien VII was resurrected as Xeric using the Dark Altar?

steps.npc: It's possible. I am no expert on necromancy but we know the Dark Altar has the power to resurrect beasts. We also know that it can extend life. It's how the people of Arceuus are immortal.
King Shayzien VII may have found a way to combine these powers.

options.text: How did Xeric have so much power?

steps.player: How did Xeric have so much power?

steps.npc: Xeric drew much of his power from the Dark Altar, but he asserted his authority as ruler through his personal army of creatures, the lizardmen.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.player: Xeric created the lizardmen!?

steps.npc: Sadly so, though we're not exactly sure how he did so. Xeric used the citizens of Kourend for many experiments, as well as for his own sadistic pleasures.
We have little written record of the experiments, but we believe they might have led to the creation of the lizardmen.

steps.player: Do you know why he created the lizardmen?

steps.text: If the player has completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.npc: Originally, we believed that Xeric created the lizardmen. However, recent discovieres suggest they were actually created during the time of King Shayzien VII.

steps.player: Do you know why Xeric needed the lizardmen?

steps.npc: Xeric was undoubtedly powerful, but he couldn't rule the people singlehandedly, nor could he rely on human informants. He needed an army he could control.
Lizardmen are loyal creatures and would do as he commanded without question. With them at his disposal, the people were powerless to resist his authority.

options.text: What happened to the lizardmen after Xeric's reign?

steps.player: What happened to the lizardmen after Xeric's reign?

steps.npc: They remain loyal to Xeric. Even to this day they continue to attack the kingdom, as you may have seen.
Fortunately, the Shayzien Army keeps them under control.

steps.player: Why do they keep fighting? Surely after a thousand years they must know Xeric is gone?

steps.npc: Without examining their minds, we will never know for sure. However, we assume Xeric genetically altered them to enforce that their duty is to serve him.

steps.player: But if they are serving Xeric, why do they attack the kingdom?

steps.npc: A good question. One that I'm afraid I do not know the answer to.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.player: What happened to Xeric?

steps.npc: During the 47th decade, after ten decades of oppression, the people revolted against Xeric and his army of lizardmen.

steps.player: Why did the people suffer for so long?

steps.npc: The events were triggered through the courage of one man, Byrne. He was not a man of particular stature of nobility, though he did proceed to become king.

steps.player: What happened?

steps.npc: 'Twas the 312th day of decade 47. Byrne, a farmer by trade, is said to have witnessed a lizardman guard murder a child whilst working his farm.
Outraged at what he had just seen, Byrne grabbed his pitchfork and sprinted towards the guard.
Blinded by fury, Byrne attacked the guard, slaughtering the lizardman in plain sight of all around.
Legend has it Byrne then gave a galvanizing speech, standing over the butchered guard with his bloodied pitchfork held aloft in the air, urging the people to fight back.

steps.player: Do you know what he said?

steps.npc: Sadly no. While we have many witness accounts, they all differ, so we can not verify it at all.

steps.player: Ah, so what happened next?

steps.npc: Whatever Byrne said, the people responded. Together, the citizens of Kourend revolted, grabbing whatever they could use as a weapon. They fought the lizardmen.
The lizardmen, while strong and powerful, were simply outnumbered. In a matter of days, they had been driven back into the Kebos Lowlands.

steps.player: So what happened to Xeric?

steps.npc: During the battle, the temple surrounding the Dark Altar was destroyed, weakening Xeric's power. We believe he fled to Quidamortem.
Some say Xeric was actually killed during the revolt, but we have no record of his remains being discovered.

steps.player: So no one knows what really happened to him?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.

There are seven main Farming areas - Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius, Alan's area in the Farming Guild and
Oswallt's area in Prifddinas.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
If you need to be rid of your fruit trees for any reason, all you have to do is chop them down and then dig up the stump.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're a good enough craftsman, that is.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're a good enough craftsman, that is.

steps.player: Where is this place?

steps.npc: The fairies call it Puro-Puro. It seems to be the home plane of the implings.
I don't think these creatures have a name for it. As you can see there isn't a lot else here other than wheat.

steps.player: How did you get here?

steps.npc: The same way you did, I suspect. Through a portal in a wheat field. I followed one back.

steps.player: I haven't noticed them do that.

steps.npc: That's why I'm the investigator and you're the adventurer.

steps.player: So, what are these implings?

steps.npc: That's a very interesting question. My best guess is that they are relatives to imps, which is why there are imps here as well.
Implings do appear to like collecting objects and, as my clients have noted, have no concept of ownership. However, I do not sense any malicious intent.
It is my observation that they collect things that other creatures want, rather than they want them themselves. It seems to provide them with sustenance.

steps.player: So they feed off our desire for things?

steps.npc: Possibly. Either way, it seems that they almost exclusively collect things that people want, except their younglings who I infer haven't learnt the best things to collect yet.

steps.player: So the more experienced implings have the more desirable items?

steps.npc: That is my observation. Yes.

options.text: Can I catch these implings then?

steps.player: Can I catch these implings, then?

steps.npc: Indeed you may. In fact I encourage it. You will, however, require some equipment.
Firstly you will need a butterfly net in which to catch them and at least one special impling jar to store an impling.

You will also require some experience as a Hunter since these creatures are elusive. The more immature implings require less experience, but some of the rarer implings are extraordinarily hard to find and catch.

Once you have caught one, you may break the jar open and obtain the object the impling is carrying. Alternatively, you may exchange certain combinations of jars with me. I will return the jars to my clients. In
exchange I will be able to provide you with some equipment that may help you hunt butterflies more effectively.
Also, beware. Those imps walking around the maze do not like the fact that their kindred spirits are being captured and will attempt to steal any full jars you have on you, setting the implings free.

options.text: I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

steps.player: I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

steps.npc: Have you indeed? Well, that may well be true, though bear in mind that implings are quite small so they are unlikely to be lugging a sizeable shield around with them. However, since it seems that dragon items are
very desirable to humans then it certainly is possible that the most expert implings may try to obtain such equipment.

steps.player: So, it's true then? Cool!

steps.npc: I should warn you, though, if the impling is strong enough to collect dragon equipment, then you will have to be very skilled at hunting implings in order to catch them.

steps.npc: Certainly.

You will also require some experience as a Hunter since these creatures are elusive. The more immature implings require less experience, but some of the rarer implings are extraordinarily hard to find and catch.

Once you have caught one, you may break the jar open and obtain the object the impling is carrying. Alternatively, you may exchange certain combinations of jars with me. I will return the jars to my clients. In
exchange I will be able to provide you with some equipment that may help you hunt butterflies more effectively.
Also, beware. Those imps walking around the maze do not like the fact that their kindred spirits are being captured and will attempt to steal any full jars you have on you, setting the implings free.

options.text: Tell me more about these jars.

steps.npc: You cannot use an ordinary butterfly jar as a container as the implings will escape from them with ease. However, I have done some investigation and have come up with a solution - if a butterfly jar is coated
with a thin layer of a substance noxious to them they become incapable of escape.

steps.player: What substance is that, then?

steps.npc: I have tried a few experiments with the help of a friend back home, and it turns out that a combination of anchovy oil and flowers - marigolds, rosemary or nasturtiums - will work.

steps.player: How do you make anchovy oil then?

steps.npc: I'd grind up some cooked anchovies and pass them through a sieve.

steps.player: Where do I make these jars?

steps.npc: Well, I believe there is a chemist in Rimmington that has a small still that you could use.

steps.player: Is there anywhere I can buy these jars?

steps.npc: Well I may be able to let you have a few - if it means you will start hunting these implings - although I do not have an infinite supply.

options.text: Tell me more about these thieving imps.

steps.player: Tell me more about these thieving imps.

steps.npc: Imps and implings appear to be related, and the imps here are quite protective of their smaller relations. If you allow them to get too close then they will attempt to steal jarred implings from your pack, if you have them.
They will then set them free, dropping your jar on the floor. So, if you're quick, you may be able to catch it again.
I have some impling deterrent which I may trade if you prove that you can catch implings well.

options.text: So what's this equipment you can give me then?

steps.player: So what's this equipment you can give me, then?

steps.npc: I have been given permission by my clients to give three pieces of equipment to able hunters.

Firstly, I have some imp deterrent. If you bring me three baby implings, two young implings and one gourmet impling already jarred, I will give you a vial. Imps don't like the smell, so they will be less likely to
steal jarred implings from you.

Secondly, I have magical butterfly nets. If you bring me three gourmet implings, two earth implings and one essence impling I will give you a new net. It will help you catch both implings and butterflies.

Lastly, I have magical jar generators. If you bring me three essence implings, two eclectic implings and one nature impling I will give you a jar generator. This object will create either butterfly or impling jars (up to
a limited number of charges) without having to carry a pack full of them.

steps.npc: Well, dearie, I'm probably not the best person to ask about money, but I think the best thing would be for you to get a good trade. If you've got a trade you can earn your way, that's what my old father told me,
Saradomin rest his soul. I hear people try to get rich by fighting in the Wilderness north of here, but that's no way for honest folks to earn a living! So get yourself a good trade, and keep

steps.npc: Ahh, there's nothing like a nice cuppa tea. I know what, I'll tell you a story to thank you for the lovely tea...

A long time ago, when I was a little girl, there was a handsome young man living in Varrock. I saw him here in the church quite often. Everyone said he was going to become a priest, and we girls were so sad about that.

But young Dissy - that was the young man's nickname - he was a wild young thing. One night he gathered some lads together, and after the evening prayer- meeting they all put on masks and sneaked down to the
evil temple in the south of the city, the evil one. The next day, there was quite a hubbub. The guards told us that someone had painted 'Saradomin pwns' on the wall of the Zamorakian temple!

Now, we'd always been taught to keep well away from that dreadful place, but it really did us all good to see someone wasn't afraid of the scum who live at that end of town. Old Father Packett was furious, but Dissy just
laughed it off.
Dissy left town after that, saying he wanted to see the world. It was such a shame, he had the most handsome shoulders...

A young man came here looking for stories about Dissy - of course, that's not his proper name, but his friends called him Dissy - and I told him that one. He said Dissy had become a really famous man and there was

going to be a book about him. Well, that's all good, but I do wish Dissy had just come back to Varrock. I did miss him so much... well, until I met my Freddie and we got married, but that's another story.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Not that it makes much difference but my name's Emilia. Like all the other survivors here, I just try to make do and get through each day at a time.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: My name's Emilia. I do a bit of this, a bit of that. Plenty that needs sorting now that the vampyres aren't out to get us.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: It's a sorry tale. I was once an accomplished sculptor, you see.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: I made statues for the kings, queens and rulers of Gielinor. But then there was the accident...

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: After that, I could never hold a chisel again.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: But I have been struck by my muse while travelling the desert, and want nothing more than to build a statue in this area.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: The desert's plain and full of sand, and needs more decoration.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.player: So, what would you need my help with?

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: As I said, I can't hold a chisel, but I can guide you in crafting the statue for me.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: I'd need you to quarry the stone for it, as well.

starting-out-talking-to-lazim.speaker: Lazim
starting-out-talking-to-lazim.text: Well, will you help me with my art?

steps.player: Of course!
You'll have to explain it to me as you go along, but count me in.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Excellent.

steps.player: What should I be doing to make your statue?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: There is a stone quarry nearby; I require several blocks of sandstone in order to make the statue.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Each of these blocks should be around... well, let's say thirty two kilograms for the first one.

steps.player: I can't mine a block that big!

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Well, then, bring me enough smaller blocks to make thirty two kilograms, and I will deal with it.

options.text: So, how much do different blocks of sandstone weigh?

steps.player: So, how much do different blocks of sandstone weigh?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: From what the last adventurer told me, there are tiny blocks that weigh 1 kg, small blocks that weigh 2 kg, and medium-sized blocks that weigh 5 kg.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: There are also large blocks that weigh 10 kg, but I doubt a weedy adventurer like you could even carry one, let alone mine one cleanly.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Apparently, the more skilled you are at mining, the larger the blocks you can chip off the rock.

options.text: Okay, I'll get on with it.

steps.player: Okay, I'll get on with it.

options.text: I don't know, that sounds like a lot of work.
