middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Oh, you may look human, but I know you're not. I've heard stories.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: How you Mahjarrat can take on any form, and use magic to inflict pain without any weapons.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: I, er... what?
I have no idea what you're talking about, but I'm just as human as you are.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: You'll never get what you want from me. I'm a soldier of Avarrocka, and will stand strong!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Look, I'm not going to hurt you!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Besides, I am already wounded, and have been so for many years, thanks to this spell you cast on me. And hungry. So very, very hungry.

steps.player: I've got some food you can have. It's quite tasty.
Here, try this. It should fill you up.
Have some of this food. It's really good, I promise!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: My daughter was learning to cook this when I left.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered her in so long... thank you for reminding me of her.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: My son loved this dish. He would have eaten it every day if we had let him.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered him in so long... thank you for reminding me of him.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: A cake? There's nothing to celebrate, is there?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: So many years gone by. My children must have grown up and left home.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered them in so long... thank you for reminding me of them.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives a baked potato:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Did you just dig that up and throw it into an oven?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: It doesn't look good at all.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd prefer it with some sort of topping...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives a baked potato with toppings:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: That doesn't look too bad at all.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: It could almost be my wife's wonderful cooking.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I haven't remembered her in so long... thank you for reminding me of her.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What do you take me for? A rabbit?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives a vegetable:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What's this? Did you just dig it out of the ground?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives cooked meat or fish:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What do you think I am, a bear? It's not even seasoned!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm a civilised man, not a barbarian gnawing on his kill!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Oh, how pleasant. I'm surprised you remembered to cook it after you killed it!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives something half-eaten:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm hungry, but not so hungry that I'll eat your leftovers.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: That's revolting! Why would you give people food you've already eaten half of?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm not touching that!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I might have enjoyed that food if you hadn't already eaten part of it.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: So, you're throwing scraps of food to me like I'm a dog, are you?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: If only you could feel the bite of my sword!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives gnome food:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Do you think I'm a gnome, or something? I'm not going to eat that!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives anything else he doesn't like:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What are you trying to feed me? I don't want that!

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Are you just trying to feed me everything you have?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What do you take me for? A goat who'll eat whatever's in front of him?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If the player gives something inedible:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: What are you trying to do, kill me?

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Oh, I get it, you're experimenting on me with different things to see what I'll eat.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'm not going to eat something your cat dragged in!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: After giving him something he rejected:

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd rather have some good human home baking.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Some fresh home baking would be delicious.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd like something that's had some care put into making it.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd like to have a hearty meal fresh from the oven.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: The food you gave me healed my wounds, and it also reminded me of my family; that helped me to remember who I was.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: I'm afraid that I'm trapped here, but I still remember something of this floor of the temple.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.speaker: Pentyn
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-f.text: If you need any hints about the rooms nearby, I can give you some help.

options.text: Tell me about the room with the fountain.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: When we came to the temple, that fountain was frosted with ice.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: Even chipping at it with swords or lighting fires under it didn't do anything.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: My guess is that some sort of magic is keeping it that way.

options.text: Tell me about the room with the furnace.

steps.player: Tell me about the room with the furnace.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I tried to go in there, but the smoke was so thick I could barely see the furnace.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: It may be that it's blocked, in which case you'll have to clear it out.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: A good breeze should do the trick.

options.text: Tell me about the dark room.

steps.player: Tell me about the dark room.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I never went in there myself, but I peered through the door.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: There seemed to be fires of some sort all around the room, but they were burning low.

steps.speaker: Pentyn
steps.text: I'd imagine they've gone out by now.

options.text: It's okay, I don't need any help.

steps.player: It's okay, I don't need any help.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-cast-fi.text: With a hiss of steam, the ice melts away from the fountain.

steps.text: It looks like there was once a maple log fire burning here.
It looks like there was once a normal log fire burning here.
It looks like there was once an oak fire burning here.
It looks like there was once a candle burning here.
It looks like there was once a coal fire burning here.
It looks like there was once a willow log fire burning here.
You place the maple logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.
You place the logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.
You place the oak logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.
You place the lit candle carefully in the brazier.
You place the coal in the brazier, and carefully light it.
You place the willow logs in the brazier, and carefully light them.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.text: Wind rushes through the furnace, clearing away what's blocking it.
The smoke clears from the room.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-pass-th.text: You walk through the barrier easily.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: The treasure's up ahead, adventurer. Be careful of the traps.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What traps?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Oh, I don't know. Perhaps, say, huge skeletons that'll tear your arms and legs off?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Nothing, adventurer, nothing. You just trot along and get that treasure, now.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Leave this temple at once, or I shall be forced to attack!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I will defend this door until I am released from this prison of bone...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: You shall not pass me, unless I crumble into dust!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: These bones that trap me will block your path!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Now, flee before I attack you!
The Boneguard attacks the player.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.speaker: Freed Spirit
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.text: Thank you, kind [sir/lady]... now I am free from my imprisonment.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.speaker: Freed Spirit
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-casting.text: I no longer need these bones - take them, please, and bury what you can.
The spirit disappears with a soft sigh.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Don't interrupt me, human! I have to concentrate.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What are you doing?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: I'm keeping a weapon under control. If my attention wavers...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: ...then it tries to escape me. I must keep it safe for my lord Zamorak.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talk-to.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talk-to.text: Leave this place, before I am forced to attack!
If the player does not have protect from melee enabled:

steps.text: The Boneguard attacks the player once.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Someone so easy to hit isn't worth my time!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talk-to.text: If the player has protect from melee enabled:

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: If you value your life, young [man/woman/one], then flee!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: You should not be here! This is a dangerous place for beings such as you!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I am impressed, young [man/woman/one]. You seem to have more resilience than those I have fought off before.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Perhaps, then, you could help me with my predicament?

steps.player: Why, what's wrong?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I am trapped in this form against my will... it has been a long and painful struggle to even regain control over my own mind.

options.text: Who's trapped you in this form?

steps.text: Same as below from "Who's trapped you in this form?"

steps.player: Why did you attack me?
I didn't do anything to deserve it!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: As I said, I am trapped like this against my will.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I am forced to defend the one who enslaved me from any harm, even though it disgusts me to do so!

steps.player: Who's trapped you in this form?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: SHE has. She was my rival before we came to this world, and supported that upstart Zamorak in his quest to be a god.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: It angers me to think at how she tricked me into slavery...

steps.player: Yes, I understand, but who is 'she'?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Her name is Enakhra, and she is the one who made this accursed temple and this boneguard that I am trapped in.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Now, since you show some interest in my situation, will you help me?

steps.player: Of course, I'll help you out. But first of all, do you have any treasure?
I, er, was just wondering...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Certainly, young [man/woman/one]. If you help me, I will give you a valuable amulet, and some of my knowledge.

steps.player: That's good enough for me. What do I have to do?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Enakhra keeps me trapped in this form with magic.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Her hold over me grew weaker over the years, and I began to build a wall to keep her trapped in her own temple forever.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Unfortunately, she has strengthened her spells lately, and I can no longer will myself to continue building.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I want you to finish building this wall, that we might seal her in this temple forever, where she cannot taint the world with her creations again.

steps.player: About this wall...

options.text: Where do I get the stone?

steps.player: Where do I get the stone?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: There is a pile of rubble nearby, made of blocks that have fallen from the walls and the ceiling over time.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I have been trapped here for several thousand years, after all...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: How do I build the wall?

steps.player: How do I build the wall?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Since the blocks are heavy, you will need to be quite strong in order to lift them up to the wall.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Once you have placed the stones up on the wall, you must trim them with a chisel so that they do not fall off when you place the next layer.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

steps.player: How long will it take?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I was not far from finishing, I must say. It will most likely only take you three loads to finish building it.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: Could you tell me more about Enakhra?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Enakhra?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: She is a coward, and a despicable traitor. She even supported Zamorak when he tried to become a god.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Of course, even though she built a temple for him, he didn't care, and she's been hiding here ever since.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: Could you tell me more about yourself?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about yourself?

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I was once a proud mage, and now look at me. Trapped inside a bone skeleton and forced to defend my rival's temple.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: To think I believed her when she said she wanted to become allies and make amends for our rivalry!

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: That two-faced, conniving, backstabbing wretch...

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: I suppose it is our nature, after all.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

steps.player: Okay, I'll start building.

steps.speaker: Boneguard
steps.text: Thank you. Once you are finished, the wall itself will shield me from most of her magic, and I will be free to move once more.

options.text: Of course, I'll help you out.

steps.text: Same as above from "Of course, I'll help you out. But first of all, do you have any treasure?"

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: So, you're determined to meddle in other people's business?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: What do you mean?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: That weapon has suddenly become a lot harder to control.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: And I know it's your doing. He's tried to get you to help, hasn't he?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: If you're talking about Akthanakos, then yes!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Of course, I don't suppose he's told you who he's trying to support, has he?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Er, no. But if you hate him so much, I suppose he doesn't support Zamorak...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: How dare you throw around his name so casually?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: No, Akthanakos never supported Zamorak. Not even after these thousands of years...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: He has pledged his allegiance to someone much more foul.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Who?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: ...There are some names it is wiser not to mention, human.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Such as the name of my lord Zamorak, that you seem so fond of throwing around.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: But you said 'Zamorak' first!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Out of my sight, you unworthy scum, before I rend your flesh from your bones.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Never dishonour his name again.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Okay...

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Well, adventurer, do you have the treasure yet?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: There doesn't seem to be any treasure there.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: None at all?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Hmm... the big skeleton promised to give me something if I helped him.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Lazim
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Ah ha! So, it's not attacking you? Well done, adventurer. Your second brain cell must be working overtime today.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-s.text: You add the stone to the wall.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-using-c.text: You trim the stone that was added to the wall.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: The wall's finally built!

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for all your help.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Boneguard
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: I can feel Enakhra's control over me fading. Finally, I can be free from this imprisonment...
The Boneguard turns into Akthanakos.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: After thousands of years... finally, I am no longer her slave.
If the player has no inventory space:

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: As thanks for your help, young [man/woman/one], please take this amulet of mine.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Wow. Er, what does it do?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It allows you to understand the speech of the Ugthanki, my patron animals, and other camels.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It is also bound to the desert, and can thus transport you back to this temple if you wish.
Continues with Enakhra cutscene.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: After thousands of years... finally, I am no longer her slave.
If the player has no inventory space:

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: As thanks for your help, young [man/woman/one], please take this amulet of mine.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.player: Wow. Er, what does it do?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It allows you to understand the speech of the Ugthanki, my patron animals, and other camels.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-talking.text: It is also bound to the desert, and can thus transport you back to this temple if you wish.
Continues with Enakhra cutscene.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: After so many years, why didn't you just give up?

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: Now my lord will punish you for destroying his weapon.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: Ha ha... in that case, I'm sure lord Zaros will be happy to intervene.
Akthanakos and Enakhra transform into skeleton forms.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Enakhra
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: I'll be waiting for you in the north, Akthanakos.

middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.speaker: Akthanakos
middle-floor-of-enakhra-s-temple-enakhra.text: It'll be a pleasure to fight you once more...

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: Well, thank you, adventurer. You've just deprived me of a wonderful chance to learn from one of Zamorak's first followers.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.player: What? What about that treasure you were looking for?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: You utter imbecile! Did you think I was looking for gold?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: sigh* I might as well stay to study this temple. It has some interesting magical properties.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.player: Ooh, you're a mage? Can you teach me any spells?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: I'm sure I've dropped hints the size of Varrock, but you might not have noticed. I'm a Zamorakian mage.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-after-the-qu.text: If you really want to learn my spells, you'll have to dedicate yourself to Zamorak.

steps.player: I couldn't do that!

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Then you won't be learning any of my spells.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Ha ha ha ha!

steps.player: You're not very nice, are you?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: What did you expect from a Zamorakian mage?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: You really thought I would teach you my secrets just like that? Ha ha ha! You are a naive fool.

steps.player: That's not very nice of you.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: I'm a mage of Zamorak, after all. What else do you expect?

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: How are you and your defective brain doing nowadays, adventurer?
If the player lost the camulet:

steps.player: I've lost the amulet that Akthanakos gave me.

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.speaker: Lazim
post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: About that amulet - I might be able to improve it for you, for a fee. Have you got it with you?
If the player has the amulet in the bank:

steps.player: No, I don't have it on me at the moment. I must have stored it somewhere.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Of course you did. I bet you spend your life collecting junk, storing it, then complaining you've run out of storage space. Fetch the amulet if you want my help.

post-quest-talking-to-lazim-again-after-.text: If the player has the amulet:

steps.player: Yes, I've got it here.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Yes, it's what I thought. This amulet will run out of charges all the time, if you keep using it. For one million coins I can give it unlimited charges.

options.text: Why do you need so much money for it?

steps.player: Why do you need so much money for it?

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Three reasons. Firstly, I'm a Zamorakian mage - we're not big on charity work. Secondly, I want the money. Finally, in case you need reminding, I hate you.
If the player doesn't have the coins:

steps.player: Right. Well, I haven't got that kind of money on me.
Okay, here's one million coins.
I'm not interested.

steps.speaker: Lazim
steps.text: Your loss.

steps.player: Maybe another time.

hkR5tY.speaker: Lazim

hkR5tY.speaker: Lazim

s_fS9w.text: Honour demands that I reward you... and yet you have no room to carry my reward. Please, return when you can take it from me.

standard-dialogue.npc: Greetings young one. How can I enlighten you?

options.text: What do I have to do in this room?

steps.player: What do I have to do in this room?

steps.npc: In this chamber you will see various piles of shapes. You can pick up these shapes and enchant them using the enchant jewelry spells. By enchanting these shapes, you'll be converting them into orbs which you can be placed in the hole in the centre. You will get Enchantment Pizazz Points for every ten shapes that you convert and the points you get depends on the level of enchantment spell you cast. You will get a bonus Pizazz Point for enchanting a certain shape at a certain time, which I will periodically shout out. You will also be rewarded with an item for every so many orbs you deposit into the hole.

steps.player: What are the rewards?

steps.npc: As well as the magic experience from casting your enchantment spells, you will get Enchantment Pizazz Points for converting so many shapes, plus a bonus point for converting a shape of the correct type. You should also note that you will occasionally be rewarded with items when you put one of the enchanted orbs in the floor.

options.text: Got any tips that may help me?

steps.player: Got any tips that may help me?

steps.npc: Try to guess or keep track of the time between the changes of the best shape to enchant. This means you can be ready to run to a different shape when you know it is about to change. Look out for the dragon gems, as these will get you more Pizazz Points!

steps.player: I see.

steps.speaker: Graveyard Guardian
steps.text: Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.

steps.player: Thanks, bye!

standard-dialogue.npc: Well met, fellow adventurer! How can I help you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: How frightfully rude of me, my dear [chap/lady]. My name is Eniola and I work for that most excellent enterprise, the Bank of Gielinor.

options.text: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?

steps.player: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?

steps.npc: My presence here is the start of a new enterprise of travelling banks.
I, and others like me, will provide you with the convenience of having banking facilities where they will be of optimum use to you.

steps.player: So...what are you doing here?

steps.npc: The Z.M.I., that is, the Zamorakian Magical Institute, requested my services upon discovery of this altar. We at the Bank of Gielinor are a neutral party and are willing to offer our services regardless of affiliation.
So that is why I am here.

steps.player: Can I access my bank account by speaking to you?

steps.npc: Of course, dear [sir/lady].
However, I must inform you that because the Z.M.I. are paying for my services, they require anyone not part of the Institute to pay an access fee to open their bank account.

But, as our goal as travelling bankers is to make our customers' lives more convenient, we have accomodated to your needs. We know you will be busy creating runes and do not wish to carry money with you. The
charge to open your account is the small amount of twenty of one type of rune. The type of rune is up to you.
Would you like to pay the price of twenty runes to open your bank account?

steps.player: Yes please.

options.text: Let me open my account and then I'll give you the runes.

steps.player: I don't have the runes on me. Let me open my account and then I'll give them to you.

steps.npc: It's not that I don't trust you, old [chap/girl], but as the old adage goes: 'Payment comes before friends.'

options.text: No way! I'm not paying to withdraw my own money.

steps.player: That's preposterous! I'm not paying runes to withdraw my own stuff.

steps.npc: I'm sorry to hear that, [sir/madam]. If you should reconsider, because I believe this service offers excellent value for money, do not hesitate to contact me.

options.text: I'd like to talk to you about quick payment deals.

steps.text: If the player has not yet set up a quick payment plan:

steps.npc: Oh that is most wonderful you know. Let me know which rune you would like to set up a quick payment with.

steps.text: Player selects chosen rune type.

steps.npc: Very well! Whenever you use my services in future, I will take twenty of your lovely [selected type] runes! Assuming you have enough of course!

steps.player: What if I don't have enough, and how do I cancel this deal?

steps.npc: I will simply ask you to select a payment the old fashioned way my dear [sir/lady]. To cancel, simply come talk to me again!

options.text: I would like to cancel our quick payment deal.

steps.player: I would like to cancel our quick payment deal.

steps.npc: Very well, if you would like to set up another deal, just come ask me again.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Greetings!

steps.player: What are you doing?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Ah, it's a secret I'm afraid.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Enlightened Journey quest.

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: Greetings! Would you like to be my number one accomplice? I mean, assistant?

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: I am Auguste. I am going to be the first balloonist in all of Gielinor!

starting-off.player: Balloo-what? I thought only monks lived on Entrana.

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: Well, they do... I was a monk. But I'm so sick of living on this island! I want to explore new frontiers!

starting-off.player: And go where no man has gone before?

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: Maybe! That sounds good. I was thinking just over to Taverley, though.

starting-off.player: Why not take the boat then?

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: Ugh! Ocean! Don't talk to me about the ocean...oh dear...I feel ill.

starting-off.player: Whoa, ok, no ocean. How exactly are you going to get off the island, then?

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: I have devised a new way to travel. But I need an assistant balloonist to help me build my design.

starting-off.speaker: Auguste
starting-off.text: Are you an experienced adventurer willing to help me?

steps.player: Yes! Sign me up.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Wonderful! Let's get started.

steps.player: Wait, I still don't know exactly what we're doing.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Of course, of course, how foolish of me. Well, we are going to make a balloon.

steps.player: Which is what exactly?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Let me show you!

steps.player: I don't think so.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Oh, never mind then.

talking-to-auguste-a-second-time.player: How exactly do you plan to get to Taverley in that? How will it work?

talking-to-auguste-a-second-time.speaker: Auguste
talking-to-auguste-a-second-time.text: Have you noticed how ashes float above fires for long periods of time?

steps.player: What's your point?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Don't you see? It's the hot air! It rises, taking the ashes with it.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: I had this epiphany while I was at the glass blower's house. If we pump hot air into an envelope it will rise because it is lighter than the cold air around it.

steps.player: Come again?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: We are going to sew a big sack and light a fire under it. Once the sack fills with hot air it will begin to rise, taking us along with it in the basket.

steps.player: You seem pretty confident about this. Have you tested it?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Well, no. You see, I don't have the materials here to make any test balloons.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: That's where you come in!

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: You are going to collect materials for two test runs of the balloon.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: You will need to get three sheets of papyrus, one ball of wool, one full sack of potatoes, and one unlit candle.

steps.player: What am I supposed to do with all of that junk?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: When you have all of it, bring it to me and I'll explain what to do next. Any questions?

steps.player: Where do I get all this stuff?

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: You're the adventurer, you should know! Think of logical places, like, churches; they have tons of candles.

options.text: Err, no. I can't see that kind of detail.

steps.player: Err, no. I can't see that kind of detail.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: You don't? Oh...well...it's just, they rise, you know, from the fire...Maybe you should pay more attention to things!

steps.player: What's your point?
Yes.

steps.text: First, use the papyrus on the ball of wool. The papyrus is folded into an origami box and the yarn will support the heat source.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Next, add the unlit candle to the balloon structure. It will act as the heat source.

steps.speaker: Auguste
steps.text: Once you have done that let me know and we will begin our experiment.

before-learning-about-mage-training-aren.npc: Greetings. What wisdom do you seek?

options.text: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

steps.player: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

steps.npc: Well young one, you have entered the Magic Training Arena. It was built at the start of the Fifth Age, when runestones were first discovered. It was made because of the many pointless accidents caused by inexperienced
mages.

steps.player: Who created it?

steps.npc: Good question. It was originally made by the ancestors of the wizards in the Wizards Tower. However, it was destroyed by melee and ranged warriors who took offence at the use of this new 'Magic Art'. Recently,
the current denizens of the Wizards Tower have resurrected the arena including various Guardians you will see as you look around. We are here to help and to ensure things run smoothly.

steps.player: Interesting. So what can I do here?

steps.npc: You may train up your skill in the magic arts by travelling through one of the portals at the back of this entrance hall. By training up in one of these areas you will be awarded special Pizazz Points unique to
each room. With these points you may claim a variety of items from my fellow guardian up the stairs.

steps.player: How do you record the points I have earned?

steps.npc: You really are full of questions! You will need a special Pizazz Progress Hat! I can give you one if you so wish to train here.

steps.player: Yes please!

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.npc: Ah, I'm afraid I can't give it to you as you don't have room to carry it!

steps.text: If the player has inventory space:
Progress hat

steps.npc: Here you go. Talk to the hat to find out your current Pizazz Point totals.

steps.player: Talk to it?

steps.npc: Well of course, it's a magic Pizazz Progress Hat! Mind your manners though, hats have feelings too!

steps.player: Er... if you insist.

steps.npc: Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave the rooms by any method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.

steps.player: Can you explain the different portals?

steps.npc: They lead to four areas to train your magic: The Telekinetic Theatre, The Alchemists' Playground, The Enchanting Chamber, and The Creature Graveyard.

steps.player: What's the Telekinetic Theatre?

steps.npc: In there you can earn Telekinetic Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.

steps.player: What will I be doing in there?

steps.npc: That depends on how much of a time-waster you are! You are required to use the Telekinetic Grab spell in order to move a statue through a maze. Casting the spell will move the statue towards you until it reaches
a wall. So by standing on the different sides of the maze you can move the statue North, East, South or West. You will be rewarded Pizazz Points for each maze successfully solved.

It will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. There's a book you can buy from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.

steps.player: What's the Alchemists' Playground?

steps.npc: In the playground you can earn Alchemist Pizazz Points for trading with the rewards guardian upstairs.

steps.player: What's in there?

steps.npc: You'll find eight cupboards containing items you can turn to gold using the low and high alchemy spells. The money you earn will be taken from you upon leaving the playground to pay for the upkeep of this training

arena and to help fund magic shops around Gielinor. You will be rewarded with 1 Pizazz Point for every 100 coins deposited and a percentage of the money you create. Keep in mind that you will not be able to take
more than 1000 coins back out with you.

steps.player: Sounds simple.

steps.npc: I am afraid not, for the cost of the items varies, as does their locations in the cupboards. You'll see a list of item costs that will help you decide what you should be converting to gold.

Fear not, it will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.

steps.player: What's the Enchanting Chamber?

steps.npc: In here you will be able to earn Enchantment Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.

steps.player: What will I have to do?

steps.npc: You will find yourself amongst various piles of shapes. You can pick up these shapes and use one of your enchanting spells upon it to morph it into an orb. You'll also see a hole in the centre of the room; put the orbs
in here and for every 20 we will credit you with a gift. You will get Pizazz Points for every 10 shapes that you convert and the amount of points depends on the spell you use.

steps.player: What's the difference between the shapes?

steps.npc: Ah, you will be notified of a different shape that will give you a bonus Pizazz Point when you convert that shape. You should also look out for dragon stones, as these will give you more Pizazz Points when you
convert them.
It will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.

steps.player: What's the Creature Graveyard?

steps.npc: In here you will be able to earn Graveyard Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.

steps.player: But what do I have to do in there?

steps.npc: Patience young one. A great many creatures die in this world and much of their remains can cause clutter. We have taken it upon ourselves to teleport many bones from these creatures into this graveyard for a

use. It's up to you to practice your bones to bananas spell in order to put these bones into immediate use - nutritious food for monsters! Just convert the bones and put them in the holes in the walls. There is a

drawback to this room however, the bones often fall on people so you may want to eat some of those bananas to stay alive. When people die we confiscate Pizazz Points for the effort of teleporting incompetent mages.

steps.player: What else do I get from this besides bruises?

steps.npc: As well as the Pizazz Points for giving us the bananas, you will be credited with runestones for your efforts, and you may be able to save up for a new kind of spell to use in the graveyard!

It will be clearer when you arrive and one of my fellow guardians through the portal will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.

steps.player: Thanks, bye!

steps.npc: Use what you have learned.

steps.npc: You won't gain with that attitude.

steps.npc: Are you here to fight the cold?

steps.player: Umm... I guess?

steps.npc: Great! Ask me anything you like about the Bruma tree, I'm an expert.

steps.player: Tell me about the Wintertodt.

steps.npc: Some would say that ice preserves while fire destroys, but no amount of fire is destroying the Wintertodt. That's a cold that will freeze the air in your lungs.

steps.player: Looks like an angry snow storm to me...

options.text: Tell me about the Bruma tree.

steps.player: Tell me about the Bruma tree.

steps.npc: The Bruma tree is what keeps the Wintertodt weak. The prison was built here by Dinh because of its usefulness against the Wintertodt.
Some legends say that Xeric is the cause for the Doors weakening, or maybe he made the Wintertodt stronger?

steps.player: Is Xeric really such a bad guy?

steps.npc: It's a known fact that he was interested in the Bruma tree. For what purpose... there are only rumours.
Regardless, the Bruma tree definitely contains powerful magic. I've been studying the sap for years and it has truly astounding properties.
There's not many fires that burn green now, are there?

steps.player: What about gnomish fire lighters?
Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: Me? I'm a member of the Woodcutting Guild. More of a researcher though... I'm currently tasked with growing a new Bruma tree.

steps.player: How's that going?

steps.npc: Poorly. I believe the Bruma tree can only be grown in a freezing cold climate.

steps.player: Well, isn't that here?

steps.npc: It's just an idea really. For all I know, it could be magic way beyond me, beyond even the Pyromancers.

steps.player: See you later.

steps.npc: Goodbye!

in-varrock-museum-talking-to-curator-hai.text: Welcome to the museum of Varrock.

steps.player: I found Xerna's Diadem...

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Ah...

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: So you found the diadem? That's... Er... That's wonderful news!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I'm sure that the Grand Museum will be thrilled to hear it.

steps.player: Do you know where I found it?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I... No, why would I?

steps.player: Be honest with me, curator!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I don't know what you're talking about!

steps.player: You can't just steal artefacts and claim them as your own for the museum!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Steal?! I would never! You need to get your facts straight!

steps.player: The other museums will never trust you again!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: They'd understand my actions... I'm just trying to preserve history.

options.text: How would you feel if someone came in here and stole all your stuff?

steps.player: How would you feel if someone came in here and stole all your stuff?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Well, I'd feel terrible! Wait...

steps.player: You've ruined Varlamore's museum.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Well, as soon as they're ready to display it again, they can have it back!

steps.player: Just give it back already!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: No! You have no idea what you're asking me!

options.text: What if Varlamore finds out what you've done?

steps.player: What if Varlamore finds out what you've done?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: They will find out! As soon as you stop bothering me, I plan to tell them myself.

options.text: How do you sleep at night?

steps.player: How do you sleep at night?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Much better knowing that this valuable artefact is safe and sound!

options.text: I thought archaeology was cool. I didn't realise it was just thieving!

steps.player: I thought archaeology was cool. I didn't realise it was just thieving!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Archaeology is cool! This was just an exceptional circumstance...

options.text: You should be ashamed of yourself.

steps.player: You should be ashamed of yourself.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: There's nothing for me to be ashamed of! I merely did the best I could in a tough situation.

options.text: A real historian would never steal!

steps.player: A real historian would never steal!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Believe me, 'real' historians have done far worse.

options.text: If you're looking for stolen goods, I can get my hands on plenty.

steps.player: If you're looking for stolen goods, I can get my hands on plenty.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: What? Is this really how people see us?

options.text: Do your colleagues know what you've done? What do they think?

steps.player: Do your colleagues know what you've done? What do they think?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I... haven't had time to inform them yet. But I will! I just have to get my story straight...

options.text: So can anyone just go around stealing and call it archaeology?

steps.player: So can anyone just go around stealing and call it archaeology?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: No, but this really is archaeology! I promise!

options.text: You're supposed to protect history, not steal it!

steps.player: You're supposed to protect history, not steal it!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Sometimes protecting history means taking... unconventional measures.

options.text: Nobody wants to see stolen goods on display!

steps.player: Nobody wants to see stolen goods on display!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: That's why I put it in storage! No, wait, that's not what I meant!

options.text: You should give Varlamore a chance before stealing their stuff.

steps.player: You should give Varlamore a chance before stealing their stuff.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Maybe, but I know what I saw, and I wasn't impressed!

options.text: Do you even have room to display this artefact?

steps.player: Do you even have room to display this artefact?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: No, but our duties go well beyond putting artefacts on display for adventurers to gawk at!

options.text: Don't you have enough artefacts of your own?

steps.player: Don't you have enough artefacts of your own?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: If everyone cared only for their own town's history, we'd have a pretty boring world.

options.text: Do you really think you did the right thing?

steps.player: Do you really think you did the right thing?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I had no other choice. I couldn't just stand by!

options.text: Did you know Varlamore sends thieves to the Colosseum?

steps.player: Did you know Varlamore sends thieves to the Colosseum?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: But I'm no thief! Give me a chance to explain...

options.text: What if I came into your house and stole your stuff?

steps.player: What if I came into your house and stole your stuff?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Then you'd be a thief! This is nothing like that!

steps.player: You've committed a crime.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I have not! Just give me a chance to explain!

options.text: How will Varlamorians learn their history now?

steps.player: How will Varlamorians learn their history now?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Well, they can always come visit. Or perhaps we can arrange a loan?

options.text: Varlamore might never let you and your colleagues visit again!

steps.player: Varlamore might never let you and your colleagues visit again!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I've done Varlamore a great service! They just don't know it yet...

options.text: You should return all these artefacts. It's the only right thing to do.

steps.player: You should return all these artefacts. It's the only right thing to do.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I'll return them as soon as I know they'll be safe. Until then, they'll stay right here!

options.text: You're a disgrace to your entire profession!

steps.player: You're a disgrace to your entire profession!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: How dare you! I've never once failed to follow the proper procedures. Well, except this one time. But this is different!

options.text: Varlamore might close their lands again after this.

steps.player: Varlamore might close their lands again after this.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Better that than the loss of a priceless artefact! It's not my fault they didn't look after it.

options.text: How do you explain the other stolen artefacts you have in storage?

steps.player: How do you explain the other stolen artefacts you have in storage?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I didn't steal them! The museum simply borrowed them for further study.

options.text: You could have damaged the artefact!

steps.player: You could have damaged the artefact!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Had I not done something, it could well have been damaged anyway!

options.text: Why don't you just cooperate with Varlamore?

steps.player: Why don't you just cooperate with Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Believe me, I've been trying!

options.text: Why should you decide who gets to keep their artefacts?

steps.player: Why should you get to decide who gets to keep their artefacts?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Because I'm the only one willing to protect them!

steps.player: You're setting a terrible example.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Oh dear... Children! Pay no attention to this loud, dramatic argument!

options.text: Is everything here stolen from other museums?

steps.player: Is everything here stolen from other museums?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Nothing here is stolen from other museums! Er... I mean, nothing is stolen at all!

options.text: You can't justify theft by saying it's for preservation.

steps.player: You can't justify theft by saying it's for preservation.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Well that's the reality. Sometimes you have to make tough choices.

steps.player: I'm sick of your excuses!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I'm sick of your shouting!

options.text: You're not above the law! You stole this stuff!

steps.player: You're not above the law! You stole this stuff!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: It's more complicated than that!

options.text: What makes you think you know better?

steps.player: What makes you think you know better?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: The fact that I had to save this artefact at all says enough. It needs to be kept safe!

options.text: What if it's cursed?! It could be dangerous!

steps.player: What if it's cursed?! It could be dangerous!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Are you quite serious? Just because an artefact is from another culture doesn't mean it's cursed. Adventurers these days...

options.text: Stealing is stealing, no matter how you try to justify it.

steps.player: Stealing is stealing, no matter how you try to justify it.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Normally I'd agree, but this one situation is a little more nuanced than that...

options.text: Is the artefact really safer here?

steps.player: Is the artefact really safer here?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Absolutely! We're the greatest, most well-equipped museum in the world!

options.text: Look me in the eye and tell me you did the right thing.

steps.player: Look me in the eye and tell me you did the right thing.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I... I did the right... Stop staring at me like that!

options.text: You're hoarding artefacts, but you should be sharing them!

steps.player: You're hoarding artefacts, but you should be sharing them!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: We don't have enough room to show everything in our collections. If only we had the funding...

steps.player: You're a loose cannon.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: A loose cannon? A wild card maybe. Or a lone ranger. But a loose cannon?! Surely not...

options.text: Hand that artefact back this instant!

steps.player: Hand that artefact back this instant!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: There's no need to take that tone with me!

options.text: I guess you were just in it for the glory, were you?

steps.player: I guess you were just in it for the glory, were you?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: That's not true! I mean, I am better than this. I mean... oh, I'm all mixed up.

options.text: This is stealing! Thieving! Taking what's not yours!

steps.player: This is stealing! Thieving! Taking what's not yours!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Please stop telling everyone I'm a thief...

options.text: You've stolen from several other museums, too!

steps.player: You've stolen from several other museums, too!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Not every museum has the resources to keep their artefacts safe. We're just taking care of them for now.

options.text: This artefact doesn't belong to you! It belongs to Varlamore!

steps.player: This artefact doesn't belong to you! It belongs to Varlamore!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I believe artefacts like this belong to all of us. That's why it's so important for me to preserve them.

options.text: Have you no respect for your colleagues in Varlamore?

steps.player: Have you no respect for your colleagues in Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: They had the choice to take better care with this artefact! That's not on me.

options.text: Aren't you embarrassed to have stolen items in your collection?

steps.player: Aren't you embarrassed to have stolen items in your collection?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: I'm not embarrassed! I just put it in storage for... for normal reasons!

options.text: You're nothing but a common thief!

steps.player: You're nothing but a common thief!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: How dare you? I'm a well-renowned professional, not a thief!

steps.player: Stealing is against the law!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Well, sometimes the law is wrong!

steps.player: You ought to be ashamed.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: For what? I'm only doing my job!

options.text: This could destroy your reputation! Everyone will think you're a thief!

steps.player: This could destroy your reputation! Everyone will think you're a thief!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Oh, nonsense! Any real historian would see I'm only trying to preserve vital historical knowledge.

options.text: You've betrayed the trust of Varlamore.

steps.player: You've betrayed the trust of Varlamore.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: It's not my fault they couldn't look after their own history. Better that I took it than some thief!

options.text: Are you even a real historian, or just a petty criminal?

steps.player: Are you even a real historian, or just a petty criminal?

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Of course I'm a real historian! This just isn't my finest moment...

options.text: You don't even have room to display it! It's just sitting in storage!

steps.player: You don't even have room to display it! It's just sitting in storage!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Artefacts aren't just for gawking at! We keep things in storage so they can be studied and taken care of.

options.text: You're not preserving anything. You're just a thief.

steps.player: You're not preserving anything. You're just a thief.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Pish-posh! I haven't dedicated my life to this museum for you to slander my good name!

options.text: Think of the Varlamorian children who won't get to see this artefact.

steps.player: Think of the Varlamorian children who won't get to see this artefact.

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Now that's not true! They can see it any time they visit Varrock, for free!

steps.player: You can't just keep claiming these stolen goods as your own!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: This was a priceless artefact, and it was at risk! I knew it had to be protected, and there was nowhere better than in Varrock...

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
steps.text: Now I don't know what to do...

steps.player: You can't just be taking these things as your own!

steps.speaker: Curator Haig Halen

steps.player: Nice basement!

steps.player: I mean, evil!

steps.npc: Yeah! I'm going to use it to summon DEMONS to DO MY BIDDING, or raise an ARMY OF THE UNDEAD! And then I'm going to totally, like, take over the world!

options.text: So have you had any luck with the demon-summoning?

steps.player: So have you had any luck with the demon-summoning?

steps.npc: Well, I thought I should start small, so I asked Wizard Grayzag for some help with summoning imps...

steps.player: And did you manage to summon any?

steps.npc: Well, not imps, exactly. It turns out they're not the lowest form of demon after all. I got these hell-rats.

options.text: Weren't you going to give up evil?

steps.player: See you later!

steps.npc: If my ARMY OF DARKNESS doesn't get you first!

If you can find your way out of my BASEMENT OF DOOM!

Of course you will return! There is no escape from my DARK POWER!

options.text: Weren't you going to give up evil?

steps.player: Weren't you going to give up evil?

steps.npc: Yeah, well...
I did try. I wore this bright red jumper and I got up in the morning and spent the day outside in the sunshine...
But I couldn't keep it up. I just didn't find anything good very interesting, you know?
Sometimes I worry about the consequences of evil. I don't really want anyone to get hurt, not like what happened with Denath.
But I can't not be evil! It's just who I am!
Ah-ha-ha-ha-ha-haa!

options.text: Let me try to explain the time travel thing again...

steps.player: Let me try to explain the time travel thing again...

options.text: Although you're here, you're also still in the time freeze.

steps.player: Although you're here, you're also still in the time freeze.

steps.npc: What?

steps.player: I mean, the whole room was frozen in time at the moment the culinomancer cast his spell, right?

steps.npc: What? I didn't notice anything.

steps.player: Of course you didn't! You were frozen!

steps.npc: So how can I be there and also here? Which one is me?
I mean, I feel like I'm me, but what if I'm not me?
That would be terrible!

steps.player: They're both you!

steps.npc: How does that work?

options.text: From YOUR point of view I've saved you, but from MINE I haven't.

steps.player: From YOUR point of view I've saved you, but from MINE I haven't.

steps.npc: Well that's all right, as long as I'm saved from my point of view!

steps.player: But I have to save you, otherwise you won't be saved!

steps.npc: But I'm here so you must already have saved me!

steps.player: That's what I meant, from your point of view I've saved you but from mine I haven't!

steps.npc: What?

options.text: I've got to take the food back in time to give it to you.

steps.player: I've to take the food back in time to give it to you.

steps.npc: Why?

steps.player: Because otherwise you won't be saved from the culinomancer's spell.

steps.npc: But I was saved from the spell! I remember it!

steps.player: Exactly! That's why I know I have to go back and save you!

steps.npc: What will happen if you don't?

options.text: I can't not, I already have!

steps.player: I can't not, because I already have!

steps.npc: What?

steps.player: The fact that you're here means I already did save you, which means that you have to tell me the correct recipe. It's logically impossible for you not to!

steps.npc: I don't understand this at all.

options.text: There will be a temporal paradox and the universe will implode!

steps.player: There will be a temporal paradox and the universe will implode!

steps.npc: Oh no! That would be bad, and not even in an evil way!

steps.player: Exactly! So you've got to tell me the recipe!

steps.npc: But I still don't understand why you need the recipe when you've already saved me!

steps.player: I don't know.

steps.npc: That's not very helpful. I don't even understand why you need the recipe anyway.

options.text: You've got to tell me because the magic requires it!

steps.player: You've got to tell me because the magic requires it!

steps.npc: That's what you said before! Honestly, why make it more complicated than it needs to be?

steps.player: Oh, never mind.

options.condition: If the player has completed The Final Dawn

steps.player: I wanted to ask you about your masters.

steps.npc: What do you wish to know?

steps.player: I guess anything really. I still know so little about them.

steps.npc: If your hope is that I can tell you about a whole race, then I am likely to disappoint you, iknil. The masters were secretive individuals. They rarely divulged information that I did not require.
All I can tell you about are the three individuals that I knew personally.

steps.player: That's still something. What were they like?

steps.npc: They were kind, but filled with sadness. As you know, they summoned me after another of their kind unleashed the Moons of Peril.
It was a dark time. Their people had suffered great calamity years earlier and their extinction was inevitable.
It seems that many, such as the shaman who summoned the Moons, felt that the only salvation left was destruction.
My masters, however, felt differently. They fought for a world that was no longer their own. They believed in preserving these lands for those who would inhabit them afterwards.

steps.player: Us?

steps.npc: Yes. Humans and dwarves were recent arrivals here, but the masters saw you as inheritors. I believe in some ways, you offered them hope in a time filled with pain.

steps.player: I see. Than you for sharing that with me.

steps.npc: It is not a problem, iknil.

options.text: Do you ever get tired of guarding this place?

steps.player: Do you ever get tired of guarding this place?

steps.npc: No.

steps.player: Care to explain further?

steps.npc: Does the stream tire of eroding the earth? Does the earth tire of forming the mountain?

steps.player: Not that I can tell.

steps.npc: I have more in common with them than I do with most of your kind, iknil. Think of me as you do them.

options.text: This place is beautiful. I thought it was supposed to be a prison?

steps.player: This place is beautiful. I thought it was supposed to be a prison?

steps.npc: It is a prison. Everything around us serves that purpose.

steps.player: Even the plants and the streams?

steps.npc: I am a nagua of earth and stream. Being close to both empowers me to do my task.
Just as being far from moonlight weakens the Moons of Peril.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.player: Hello!

steps.npc: Nilsal. I'm afraid I must ask not to be disturbed. There are many things that one in my position must contemplate. If you seek conversation, I'm sure my companion would be willing.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

steps.npc: Well hello there; welcome to our little village. Pray, stay awhile.

options.text: You know, you sound just like the mayor?

steps.player: You know, you sound just like the mayor?

steps.npc: Really? That's the nicest thing anyone has ever said.
I admire him a great deal. He works so hard for this town.

steps.player: You look like him as well?

steps.npc: Hmm, I don't think I do.

steps.player: No really, what with the unhealthy skin tone and bulging eyes. The resemblance is uncanny.

steps.npc: Well, I haven't spoken to him in a while.  I don't get out much.

steps.player: I can see why.

steps.npc: Maybe the Mayor has finally seen how much I admire him and has grown to admire me?

steps.player: Anything's possible I suppose. Wait a minute, you mean you've always looked that odd?

steps.npc: Hey, I resent that!

steps.player: I'm sorry, it's just...  Nevermind.
What do you do here?

steps.npc: I supply the local fishermen with the tools and bait they need to do their job.

steps.player: Interesting. Have you been doing it long?

steps.npc: Why yes, all of my life.  I took over from my father, who inherited the business from his father and so on.
In fact, there have been Lovecraft's selling bait for over ten generations.

steps.player: Wow, that's some lineage.

steps.npc: Oh yes, we have a long and interesting family history. For one reason or another the Lovecraft's have always been bait sellers or writers.

steps.player: Hmm, yes well. I'm sure it's all fascinating, but I...

steps.npc: Oh very, very fascinating, for instance my great grandfather Howard...

steps.player: Yawn. Oh, I'm sorry but I really must be getting on. I think my giraffe needs feeding.

steps.npc: Your?

steps.player: Giraffe. Sorry, but he gets cranky without enough sugar. Bye now!

steps.npc: Oh right, goodbye.

options.text: Can I buy some fishing supplies please?

steps.player: Can I buy some fishing supplies please?

options.text: You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.

steps.player: You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.

steps.npc: Sniff. Yes, everyone says that.
Hello there, traveller.

steps.player: What's going on here? Where is everyone?

steps.npc: Most are in the city. As for the rest, hopefully somewhere nicer than this place.

steps.player: In the city?

steps.npc: Yes. When we heard they were going to lock Menaphos down and shut the gates, most people here decided they'd be better off behind the walls than outside them.

steps.player: But you stayed?

steps.npc: We didn't get much warning. People had to rush to gather whatever they could. Some things had to be left behind, along with some people...

steps.player: That's horrible!

steps.npc: It could have been worse. Had we been in Sophanem, we'd have had no warning at all. I just hope it won't be long before things are back to normal.

steps.player: I hope so too.

steps.npc: Thank you, traveller. Stay safe out there. These are troubling times.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: I can't belive Xilo hasn't shown up.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Were you expecting to meet someone here?

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: My... friend, Xilo. I told her to meet me by the magic trees of the rainforest. We don't often have a chance to meet without a crowd of people around.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Why? Is she not particularly local to you?

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: Unfortunately not. I'm from Aldarin, but she lives in Tal Teklan. It usually takes a special event being hosted for us both to be in the same place.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: So you never really get any privacy?
Not at all. Sorry if it seemed like I was.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: It's okay... Sorry... I just miss her.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: If the player has not already talked to Xilo:

steps.player: Do you think she's just running a little late?

steps.npc: It's possible.

steps.player: Could she maybe have considered another tree magical?

steps.npc: I suppose she may be where we first met... but this is where we shared our first... you know...

steps.player: Well, I'll keep my fingers crossed for you. I'm sure you'll be able to find one another soon!

steps.npc: Thank you, iknami.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: If the player has already talked to Xilo:

steps.player: Hang on... I think I might have met this Xilo.

steps.npc: You have? Where is she?

steps.player: By a tree to the north of here.

steps.npc: Oh, Xilo! She's gone to where we first met instead! Thank you, iknami. I'll head over there at once!

steps.text: Fabia departs.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.speaker: Xilo
standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: Hello again, iknami! Thank you for helping us find each other!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: To think we were waiting by different trees! It was so silly of us!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Well, I'm happy to see you together again. Now, I'm sure you have a lot of catching up to do. I'll leave you to it.

steps.npc: Don't bother me, can't you see I'm busy?

steps.player: No, I can't... can I go into the factory?

steps.npc: You can go in. The Consortium, in their infinite wisdom, has decided to open up the factory to all and sundry.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: We've built a new blast furnace and always have a shortage of people to work on it.

steps.player: I'll have a look, thanks.

steps.npc: Just don't go causing any trouble, I still run this factory!

unsectioned.player: I'm sorry, I'm looking for the blast furnace?

unsectioned.npc: Do I look like a guide to you?

unsectioned.player: No, you look like a hard-working dwarf, but can you please tell me where the blast furnace is?

unsectioned.npc: Alright, just head down the stairs, it's easy to find.

unsectioned.player: If you were any shorter you wouldn't exist.
What are you dwarves doing in this factory?

unsectioned.npc: Working of course, can't you see that?
Refining the ore that is being brought into the factory, of course.
It means you should stop asking so many questions and get back to work!

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Me?! I am-a da Fairy Godfather.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: I see-a by your face dat you have-a not-a heard of-a me. Irrispettoso, eet iz of no eemportance. You weesh-a to know sometheeng else or no?

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Ah, a tragedy to be-a struck-a down so young.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: How-a much do ya know about-a da fairy folk, my beeg friend?

steps.player: Not actually a whole deal, I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Well, let-a me enlighten yous. Zanaris iz-a a nexus of-a da worlds. Da Queen Bee, she iz-a da guardian of-a all da folk dat live-a in Zanaris.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: So when-a thees Tanglefoot arrives, da Queen Bee she-a goes to da Cosmic Temple area to kill-a eet, but someting goes-a wrong. Da Queen Bee, she gets-a hurt and is-a now inna da magic sleep.

steps.player: Thanks, I'll go see her then. Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Ciao. Oh, and [player name]...

steps.player: Yes?

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: A word-a of advice. You be-a careful not to cause da trouble for da folk while you are Zanaris. Ciao.

steps.player: What's going on here?

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Hmm, an eenteresting question, my friend. I am-a trying to run-a da fairy kingdom, and youz iz-a being da irritating adventurer.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: An eenteresting place to start... I am-a here, ze Queen Bee iz not. So my chair - eet iz-a here, her throne - eet iz- a not. Eez there anytheeng else? I ama a bizy fairy.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Eef there iz anytheeng I can-a help you weeth whilst you are-a veesiting Zanaris, plsi, do not-a trouble to bother me.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: I did, he said I should come and talk to you!
Actually it's more a case of what I can help you with? I told the Fairy Godfather that I would help you find a cure for the Queen.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Oh, thank you! I really need help, I have no idea what ails the Queen. You must be a mighty healer!

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Yes, I heard. It's just not what I was expecting to hear.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: But hang on, you might be just the sort of person I need to help me!

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: I'm sure the Godfather told you that the Queen is in an enchanted sleep?

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: Well sort of, I couldn't really understand everything he was talking about.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Shhh, somebody might hear. Look you're a visitor, so I'll tell you this much; it doesn't pay to talk about the Godfather behind his back.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: But back to the problem at hand - the Fairy Queen. She was brought here after her battle with the Tanglefoot in a terrible state, extremely weak and barely able to fly!

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: When the Queen got back here, she was clearly weakening fast. It appears as if the magic force that is her life essence is slowly unravelling.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Now, what I need you to do is find a mage by the name of Zandar Horfyre. He has spent many years studying magical illness. Take the list to him and ask him if he knows what ails the Queen, please.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: That doesn't sound too difficult, where will I find him.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: I believe he now resides in the Dark Wizard's tower near Falador, and [player name], please hurry. I fear the Queen doesn't have much time left!

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: You're back soon! Did you find out what ails the Fairy Queen?

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.player: No, I'm afraid I've lost the list of symptoms you gave me.

entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.speaker: Fairy Nuff
entering-zanaris-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: Well not to worry, I have a copy of it here.

at-the-dark-wizard-s-tower-talking-to-za.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
at-the-dark-wizard-s-tower-talking-to-za.text: And why should I help you, fool? You attack my brethren and I, and then you demand my help! I think not!

at-the-dark-wizard-s-tower-talking-to-za.player: But Fairy Nuff said you would help me!
The Fairy Queen is extremely ill. She was in a battle with a Tanglefoot and her injuries have resulted in her being in a coma.

at-the-dark-wizard-s-tower-talking-to-za.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
at-the-dark-wizard-s-tower-talking-to-za.text: You think the Tanglefoot is responsible? I don't see how that could be. A Tanglefoot will normally kill its victim outright...unless...hmmmm...I wonder...
If the player has the symptoms list:

steps.player: Fairy Nuff gave me a list of her symptoms. Here, have a look at it.

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: Hmm...yes...slow discorporation of ethreal body, eh? Hmm...I think I know what the problem might be.

steps.player: You do? That's great! What is it?

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: From what I know about fairies, their basic lifeforce is pure magic. Much as we humans would refer to our souls as our life essence, so too does a fairy have a life essence of pure magic.

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: You could actually refer to fairies as magic embodied and not be wrong.

steps.player: Yes, but about the Fairy Queen?

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: Patience, I'm getting to that. It appears the Fairy Queen has lost a large part, indeed the majority, of her life essence. Either it was drained from her by the Tanglefoot or she did it voluntarily.

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: Although why she would do that is beyond me.

steps.player: So I guess I need to go and kill this Tanglefoot and get back her magic essence if I am to help her?

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: Yes, but if I were you I would seek out a necromancer by the name of Malignus Mortifer. I believe that he once fought a Tanglefoot, many years ago.

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: He's rumoured to have been seen near Port Sarim with his followers recently. Rumour has it that he's working on a spell that has something to do with fungus!

steps.player: Ok, thanks very much.

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: Don't mention it, and give my regards to Nuff, when you see her next.

steps.player: Fairy Nuff gave me a list of her symptoms, but I don't have it with me.

steps.speaker: Zandar Horfyre
steps.text: Well, I can't diagnose the problem without knowing the symptoms. You'd better go and find that list, or get Fairy Nuff to give you another one.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Almost certainly, I am a great practitioner of the magic arts, after all.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Right then, to business. A Tanglefoot can not be harmed by might nor magic. The only weapon that can damage them are a pair of enchanted secateurs!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You will have to make them... listen carefully and I'll tell you how.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Obviously you will need a pair of secateurs, you will also need to gather [item 1], [item 2] and [item 3].

in-the-nature-grotto-talking-to-the-natu.speaker: Nature Spirit
in-the-nature-grotto-talking-to-the-natu.text: Ah, a Tanglefoot! Your information is correct, secateurs that have been blessed by a Nature Spirit are the only weapons that can harm such a terrible creature.
