steps.speaker: Martin the Master Gardener
steps.text: person who said that everything would be all right, so you're the person who they'll get angry with!

starting-off-talking-to-martin-again-aft.player: Don't worry, I'm working on it.

starting-off-talking-to-martin-again-aft.speaker: Martin the Master Gardener

steps.player: We must go after them!

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Yes! We must-a, but most-a of da folk are away from Zanaris atta the momento.

steps.player: Well tell me what to do and I'll go myself.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Ye-es, dat izza good idea. Hokay, you may use-a da fairyreengs. Talk-a to da co-ordinator, she will-a explain-a to you how to use-a da reengs, but you must-a promees me dat you weel come-a back-a here, eef you

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: find-a her. Whoever keednapped her must-a be very powerful. You find-a da Queen Bee and den-a yous come right back here and we will-a rescue her together. Hokay?

steps.player: Yes, okay.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Good. Now-a yous talk-a to da co-ordinator. She will-a tell you how-a da fairyreengs work.

steps.player: No, I'll rescue her myself.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Oh no, dat eet eez no good. Yous wanna to be da hero, but what-a about me? She izza my queen! No, no. You cannot-a use-a da fairyreengs

options.text: Where have all the fairies gone?

steps.player: Where have all the fairies gone?

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Da people are mostly out-a and about-a tryeeng to keep-a theengs working. Eet izza not easy weeth da Queen Bee notta here!

starting-off-talking-to-fairy-godfather-.speaker: Fairy Godfather
starting-off-talking-to-fairy-godfather-.text: Ah, [player name], yous hassa changed your mind? Yous weel-a come and getta me before yous rescue da Queen Bee? Only den can-a I geev yous permission to use-a da reengs.

steps.player: Oh, okay then.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Good, I knew-a you would change-a your mind. Now I just-a need you to sign-a dis scroll before I geev-a yous da permission to use-a da fairyreengs.
(Contract scroll interface pops up.)

steps.player: I am not signing this! It says I am indebted to you until you release me!

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Eet does? Oh, sorry, must-a geeven yous da wrong-a scroll. Tell-a yous what, yous hazza da honest face, so I'll trust-a yous. Go ahead, use-a da fairyreengs, but just-a make sure dat yous come-a back here and tell-a

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: me when-a yous finda da Queen Bee, like-a yous promised. Now go-a and talk-a to da co-ordinator. She-a weel tell-a yous how da fairyreengs work.

options.text: No, there's no chance of that happening.

steps.player: No, there's no chance of that happening.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Yous weel change-a your mind. Come and talk-a to me me yous do.

starting-off-co-ordinator.prompt: What do you want to ask about?

steps.player: Hi, the Godfather said I should ask you to explain how the fairy rings work.

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: Goodness! As if I don't have enough to do already without giving every adventurer that comes along a history lesson! Let's get this over with quickly. Zanaris is an extremely old place, it was here long before we

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: fairyfolk came to live here. In fact it is rumoured to be the nexus of all planes. When we arrived here we found many of the magical properties of this place to be dormant. One of these was the ability to jump between

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: planes using a powerful portal that had been sealed for centuries. The Fairy Queen harnessed that magic and created the fairy rings, these are not as powerful as the original portal would have been, but are very effective

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: nonetheless. There are 3 fairy rings in Zanaris, the one in the market and the one near the evil chicken's shrine will only take users to one specific place. However the third fairy ring, near the fountains, is a major portal.

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: Anybody who activates that fairy ring will find themselves able to dial in a 3 digit code. These codes will all take the user to different locations. Some of the codes no longer work and other codes go to extremely

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: dangerous places, so be careful. Fortunately the fairy rings are imbued with a powerful protective magic and as long as you stand in the middle of them nothing will be able to attack you. Remember, because you are a

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: human, you will need to be holding your dramen staff to activate the rings. Now I must get back to work, there is so much to do and so few fairies left to do it.

starting-off-fairy-fixit.speaker: Fairy Fixit
starting-off-fairy-fixit.text: What is it, human? Busy busy busy!

options.text: Why are you carrying that toolbox?

steps.player: Why are you carrying that toolbox?

steps.speaker: Fairy Fixit
steps.text: It's the fizgog! It's picking up cable again!

steps.player: Uh, right. So is it safe to use the fairy rings then?

steps.speaker: Fairy Fixit
steps.text: Sure, as long as you have been given permission to use them. You should just be aware that using the fairy rings sometimes has strange results, the locations that you have been to may affect the locations you are

steps.speaker: Fairy Fixit
steps.text: trying to reach. I could fix it by replacing the fizgog and the whosprangit, I've put in a request for some new parts but they're pretty hard to get hold of, it seems.

steps.player: I'm okay, thanks.

starting-off-talking-to-the-fairy-godfat.speaker: Fairy Godfather
starting-off-talking-to-the-fairy-godfat.text: [player name], you are-a back! Have-a you found da Queen Bee?

starting-off-talking-to-the-fairy-godfat.speaker: Fairy Godfather
starting-off-talking-to-the-fairy-godfat.text: Den whatta are you doing-a back here? Go and-a search for her!

steps.text: You don't find anything useful, just some glass from a broken vial.

locating-the-hideout-searching-for-fairy.text: Searching the right shelves with a free inventory space:

steps.text: Hidden inside a vial you find a copy of Fairy Nuff's certificate.

locating-the-hideout-searching-for-fairy.text: Searching the right shelves without a free inventory space:

steps.text: Hidden inside a vial you find a copy of Fairy Nuff's certificate, but you don't have space to take it.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: For why you show-a me dat? I-a busy fairy! I donn-a have time for nonsense!
You show the certificate to the Godfather.

steps.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: For why you show-a me dat? Eez very nice to see yous learning to draw! Bravo!

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.text: You show the certificate to the cow.

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.speaker: Cow
locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.text: Can't the human take a hint? I've been ignoring you! Do you think I would ignore you if I wanted to discuss your Rorschach ink-blots ?
Once again, the cow is ignoring you.
You show the certificate to the sheep.

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.speaker: Sheep
locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.text: The human found some symbols And doesn't know what they mean So now it's cross-examining me And spoiling my routine!

steps.speaker: Fairy chef
steps.text: Very nice, dearie, but that belongs to Fairy Nuff. I should put it back on her wall before she misses it if I were you. You wouldn't want her to think you stole it now, would you?
You show the certificate to the Fairy chef.

steps.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

steps.speaker: Fairy chef
steps.text: Sorry dearie, no, but I have seen a sign with similar marks near the mysterious ruins. You know, the ones that lead you to the Cosmic Rune Altar.
You show the certificate to the Gate Keeper.

steps.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

steps.speaker: Gatekeeper
steps.text: That you've been doodelling? If you don't mind I have a job to do, please stop distracting me.
You show the certificate to the Gate Keeper.

steps.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

steps.speaker: Gatekeeper
steps.text: No I don't and I'm trying to work here. Please stop distracting me!

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: Fairy Nuff is very proud of that certificate, it's her most prized possession. She won't like you taking it.
You show the certificate to the Fairy Coordinator.

steps.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

steps.speaker: Co-ordinator
steps.text: They look familiar, but I can't think where I've seen marks like that. Try asking around, maybe someone else will recognise them.

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.text: You show the certificate to the Fairy Nuff.

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.speaker: Fairy Nuff
locating-the-hideout-using-the-certifica.text: Thank you, [player name] but you'd better keep hold of it. You can't get to this hideout without it.

locating-the-hideout-trying-to-enter-the.text: Maybe you should bring that certificate with you.

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: I don't want to go back! That orc tried to kill me!

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: We must find a way to fight back! To throw those villains out of our homes.

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: I can't believe that there are orcs in Zanaris.

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: Have you heard? The Godfather has allowed orcs into Zanaris!

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: Those fairies that side with the Godfather are all traitors! The Queen is the true ruler of Zanaris!

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: Have you seen Fairy Cake? She went to talk to the Godfather and I haven't seen her since.

steps.speaker: Fairy
steps.text: How is the Queen? Has she woken up yet?

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: [player name]! You found us! I'm so glad, I was afraid you wouldn't get my message.

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: After you brought back the Queen's enchanted secateurs and gave them to the Fairy Godfather, I went to him to ask for them so that I could wake Her Majesty up, but he refused to give them to me. Then I

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: noticed that lots of my friends were missing, when I asked him about them he said they were off working for him and then he threatened to have his bodyguards pull my wings off! I was scared for the Queen, and so I

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: When I returned to Zanaris I found my cave ransacked! There were other fairies that had been attacked by the Godfather and so we fled the city and came here. I managed to hide a note that I hoped you

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: But why would the Godfather do this?

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Isn't it obvious? He wants to rule Zanaris instead of the Fairy Queen. The latest fairies to arrive have even reported that he has invited all sorts of monsters to the Lost City.

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: So what should we do about it do you think?

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: I've got terrible news! One of our spies has just returned from Zanaris and has reported that the Godfather has enlisted an army of orcs! Apparently they are wandering freely around our homes!

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: I'm sorry, but who are you?

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Oh, how rude of me! [player name] this is Fairy Very Wise, advisor to the Queen. Fairy Very Wise, this is [player name].

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Oh, I've heard of you. You're the young adventurer that defeated the Tanglefoot.

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: So you're also the idiot who gave that Godfather maniac the Fairy Queen's magic secateurs!

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: But that was a mistake! I thought he was trying to help the Fairy Queen!

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: So you're not evil, you're just not too bright. Well I'm glad you found this place, although if you can find it it's obviously not much of a hiding place, now you can help fix the damage that you've done!

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: Alright, what do I need to do?

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: The first thing we have to do is wake up the Fairy Queen. You will have to go back to Zanaris and find a way to get those magical secateurs back from the Godfather!

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.player: That's easy I'll just pickpocket them off of him, I'm really good at that.

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff.text: Ok, just be careful, his henchmen have keen eyes and will be watching out for him.

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-very-wis.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-very-wis.text: I'm so worried about the Queen, without her the fairy people may be chased out of Gielinor completely! You must wake her, for all our sakes!

in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff-aga.speaker: Fairy Nuff
in-the-hideout-talking-to-fairy-nuff-aga.text: What are you doing? You need to get those secateurs back very urgently!

in-the-hideout-pickpocketing-the-secateu.text: You attempt to pickpocket the Fairy Godfather.

steps.text: You pick-pocket the Fairy Godfather and get the Queen's enchanted secateurs!
You already have the Queen's secateurs. You don't need to risk getting caught in the Godfather's pockets again.

steps.speaker: Fairy Godfather
steps.text: Rocco, teach-a thees thief a lesson!
You slowly wake up in an unknown place.

curing-the-queen-returning-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-returning-to-fairy-nuff.text: Oh, [player name], you're back! I'm so glad. Did you manage to get the secateurs?

curing-the-queen-returning-to-fairy-nuff.player: Yes, but I seem to have lost them somewhere.

curing-the-queen-returning-to-fairy-nuff.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-returning-to-fairy-nuff.text: I can't believe you did that! You know how important it is that I get those secateurs as soon as possible! Please go and find them immediately!

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: Oh, [player name], you're back! I'm so glad. Did you manage to get the secateurs?

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.player: You should have seen me! The Godfather didn't even know I was going through his pockets! Here they are.

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: Fantastic! Let's just hope that it's not too late ...
You hand fairy Nuff the Queen's enchanted secateurs.

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: Oh no! It didn't work! She's been asleep too long!

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.player: Calm down! There's got to be something that we can do. After all, we've given her back her magical essence, right?

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: Yes, we have. There is one small chance that we might be able to wake her up still, but I'd need a potion of Magic Essence.

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.player: Well that doesn't seem too bad, what do I need to do to make one?

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: A potion of magic essence is made in the same way as any other potion, first you mix a vial of water with a base herb, in this case a Star Flower. Star Flowers are rich in magic essence and are excellent for curing

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: poisons and that's what the Queen is suffering from - a poisoning of her life essence. Then we need to add the catalyst ingredient; a powdered Gorak's claw. Goraks drain the life from their prey, so by using one of their

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: claws we are hoping to draw the Queen's life essence back.

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.player: Thanks for the lecture, but where do I get one of these Star Flowers and where can I find a Gorak?

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: Star Flowers only grow on the higher planes and even there they are extremely rare. You should be able to access some of the higher planes by using the fairy rings. Goraks also live on a different plane. They are

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: vicious creatures that draw the life essence from any living thing they find. It seems that in drawing the life force from the world that they live on they have trapped themselves on a small plane, as far as I am aware, the

curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-bringing-fairy-nuff-the.text: only way onto or off of their world is through the fairy rings.

curing-the-queen-talking-to-the-cosmic-b.speaker: Cosmic Being
curing-the-queen-talking-to-the-cosmic-b.text: Salutations traveller! It is unusual for one of the creatures called 'humans' to visit this plane. How can I assist you?

options.text: I'm looking for a Star Flower.

steps.player: I'm looking for a Star Flower.

steps.speaker: Cosmic Being
steps.text: Then you've come to the right place. Star Flower, which is much prized for its magical properties, only grows on this plane. It has a very short life-span; plants grow, flower and die in the space of minutes! If you search

steps.speaker: Cosmic Being
steps.text: around you might find some growing somewhere.

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: A potion of magic essence is made in the same way as any other potion, first you mix a vial of water with a base herb, in this case a Star Flower. Star Flowers are rich in magic essence and are excellent for curing

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: poisons and that's what the Queen is suffering from - a poisoning of her life essence. Then we need to add the catalyst ingredient; a powdered Gorak's claw. Goraks drain the life from their prey, so by using one of their

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: claws we are hoping to draw the Queen's life essence back.

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.player: Thanks for the lecture. Fortunately I think I know where to get all of the ingredients you need.

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: That's great news! Well what are you waiting for? We need that potion as soon as possible!

steps.speaker: Fairy Nuff
steps.text: Hello [player name]. How are you getting on with making that potion?

steps.player: I haven't found a Star Flower yet.

steps.speaker: Fairy Nuff
steps.text: I don't have to tell you again how important it is that you hurry!

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-nuff-a.text: After making an unfinished magic essence potion:

steps.speaker: Fairy Nuff
steps.text: How's that potion of Magic Essence coming along, [player name]?

steps.player: I've half made it, I found a Starflower on this really wierd plane.

steps.speaker: Fairy Nuff
steps.text: That's nice for you, but please stop wasting time. You need to finish the potion with a Gorak's claw.

steps.player: I've got it, I've made a potion of magic essence!

steps.speaker: Fairy Nuff
steps.text: Oh, [player name] that's fantastic! Please give it to Her Majesty immediately.

curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-very-w.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-talking-to-fairy-very-w.text: Thank you for your great service to the fairy people, we are indebted to you!

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: ...Urgh! Wh... what happened? ...Why do I feel so awful?

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Nuff
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: Your majesty! You're awake!

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: Wh... what happened? The last thing I remember was confronting that Tanglefoot with the aid of the Godfather.

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: Yes, that's what I said... oh, hello [player name]. Please excuse me for not having noticed you earlier, I'm not feeling quite myself. Why did you shout about the Godfather?

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.player: I'm not really sure how to tell you this, your majesty... It seems as though you've fallen foul of a clever scheme of the Godfather's...

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: That's absurd, why would the Godfather want to hurt me?

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: I'm afraid it's true your majesty. You see nobody knew that the Godfather was with you when you fought the Tanglefoot...

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: But that's the point, I didn't fight the Tanglefoot. We had only just entered its lair and sensing the danger to itself, the Tanglefoot fled down a passage, then... blackness!

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: Then your majesty, I think it may be worse than I imagined. I suspect the Fairy Godfather attacked you from behind and left you for dead. He has taken over control of Zanaris whilst you were...er, ...sleeping. He

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: has enlisted the aid of orcs and other assorted ruffians, if any of your subjects dared to question him, they were assaulted. I very much suspect that if it wasn't for the quick thinking of Fairy Nuff here, you would be

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: dead! She fled here with you and as many of your loyal fairies as she could gather. We've been in hiding ever since, until this brave adventurer managed to awaken you.

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: I can't believe it!

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: He shan't get away with this, how do I get back to Zanaris? The Godfather shall answer for his crimes!

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: No! Stop your majesty!

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: Why, old friend?

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: The Godfather has recruited an army of villains, whilst we just have the few fairies who escaped and although they would gladly follow you into battle, many are still wounded from their treatment at the tyrant's hands. I

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Very Wise
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: must counsel caution, lest this brave hero's efforts are all wasted and the godfather captures you. He won't let you survive a second time.

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: There is wisdom in what you say. I shall ponder your words before I act rashly. As for you, [player name], how can I reward you? You have done the fairy people a great favour that shall not be forgotten. I'm afraid

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.speaker: Fairy Queen
curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: you find us in trying times, but please accept this magic lamp as a sign of our thanks.
If the player has no room in their inventory:

steps.player: Thanks, but I don't have any space to carry it.

steps.speaker: Fairy Queen
steps.text: That's alright, come back and get it when you can.

curing-the-queen-after-using-the-magic-e.text: With free inventory space:

steps.text: The Fairy Queen gives you an XP lamp.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Not often we get one like you 'round these parts. Wind push you ashore?

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Apologies, not much one for the formalities. Name's Cormac. I'm the mayor of this place.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.player: Likewise. So what's with the others around here? Getting a sense they're not fans of... well, anyone.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Oh, pay 'em no mind. They're just a little wary of outsiders. Tend not t' get many through here, what with the isolated location and all.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.player: I'd expect more curiosity if outsiders are uncommon, if I'm honest...

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Our history's a complicated one... As I say, best put it out ya mind. That said, if you be wantin' to get in their good books, you could make yourself useful.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Well, if you're feeling brave, we've had one of the villagers, Keenan, go missing. We know he's not much of a sailor, so he'll be somewhere on the island.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.player: Couldn't you find him yourselves? The island doesn't seem like too much ground to cover.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Aye, we've tried, but this island... she has more than a few secrets... Were things different...

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.text: Ah, don't be worrying yourself about it. The point is, an outsider like yourself might be endin' up having better luck than we've had, if you're willing to help?

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac.prompt: Start the Fallen From Grace quest?

steps.player: Alright, I'll help you find Keenan. Any ideas on where to start?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: I'd check in with his mother, Muriel. She'd know more than most. Their house is the one just t' north east of here.

steps.player: I'll head over there right away.
Actually, I've got something I need to do right now. Sorry about that.

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: That's okay. I'll still be here if you end up feelin' otherwise.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac-a-s.player: You said there might be a way for me to get in people's good books?

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac-aft.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac-aft.text: Any luck on your hunt for Keenan yet?

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac-aft.speaker: Cormac
starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac-aft.text: I'd start by checking in with his mother, Muriel. She'd know more than most. Their house is the one just t' north east of here.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-cormac-aft.player: I'll head over there right away.

starting-the-quest-trying-to-dock-in-the.text: You can't see any good reason to try to dock in this dangerous looking cavern.

starting-the-quest-trying-to-disembark-i.text: You can't see any good reason to try to disembark in this dangerous looking cavern.

talking-to-the-villagers-oisin.speaker: Oisin
talking-to-the-villagers-oisin.text: Always knew he'd get into trouble.

talking-to-the-villagers-oisin.player: Was he that kind of person?

talking-to-the-villagers-oisin.speaker: Oisin
talking-to-the-villagers-oisin.text: A troublemaker? No, not necessarily. Had a habit of being in his own world a lot, wandering about unaware of a lot of things. Not a lick of survival instinct in him.

talking-to-the-villagers-angus.speaker: Angus
talking-to-the-villagers-angus.text: You'll go the way of the last one: wyrm food.

talking-to-the-villagers-baldwin.speaker: Baldwin
talking-to-the-villagers-baldwin.text: Well, you won't find him. No one who disappears on this island ever shows up again.

talking-to-the-villagers-baldwin.speaker: Baldwin
talking-to-the-villagers-baldwin.text: None of your business. You'd be better off staying out of things. Now go away.

talking-to-the-villagers-catriona.player: Hello to you as well. I was wondering if you knew anything about Keenan's disappearance?

talking-to-the-villagers-rian.speaker: Rian
talking-to-the-villagers-rian.text: Outsider, you better not be causing trouble.

talking-to-the-villagers-rian.speaker: Rian
talking-to-the-villagers-rian.text: Heh. Makes you better than the last one then. Keep that up.

talking-to-the-villagers-rian.player: What did the last one do?

talking-to-the-villagers-rian.speaker: Rian
talking-to-the-villagers-rian.text: Acted up a storm about how their boat had been wrecked on the rocks and they needed help, only to then go and get themselves killed in the caverns after we'd patched them up.

talking-to-the-villagers-rian.speaker: Rian
talking-to-the-villagers-rian.text: A damn shame to waste what limited resources we have.

talking-to-the-villagers-ffion.player: Excuse me, you didn't happen to know Keenan did you?

talking-to-the-villagers-ffion.speaker: Ffion
talking-to-the-villagers-ffion.text: Sure did. Strange lad that one. Spent hours going on about sun energy, or something like that.

talking-to-the-villagers-ffion.speaker: Ffion
talking-to-the-villagers-ffion.text: That's right, though I must admit, I didn't fully pay attention, so I may have misunderstood.

options.text: What am I meant to be doing here?
I'm looking for Keenan. You haven't seen him, have you?

steps.player: I'm looking for Keenan. You haven't seen him, have you?

steps.speaker: Geoff
steps.text: Aye, I heard t'lad went missin', but I can nay tell ye if he's been 'ere or not. These bleedin' goats be far too distractin'.

steps.player: I see. Thanks anyway.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.text: Ah... the outsider. I'm sorry, but I'm not really in the mood for visitors.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.player: I understand, but I'm actually here in the hopes that I can help you. Cormac has asked me to look for your son.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.text: Oh... well, what do you need from me?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.player: Did Keenan give you any idea where he might be going?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.text: No, no. It was a usual day. He ran about town doing everything he needed, then he grabbed his hat and went to sit and stare at the sunstone. I could never convince him to do something more productive...

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.text: That big rock over in the mine. He's been obsessed with it. Always going on about how it has some secret to be discovered...

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel.player: I see. I'll go over there and see if I can find anything of note.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.text: You're back. Have you had any luck finding Keenan?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.player: Not yet. Where did you say I should be looking?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.text: The sunstone over in the mine. He's been obsessed with it. Always going on about how it has some secret to be discovered...

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.player: Alright, I'll head over there and see what I can find.

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.speaker: Cormac
following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.text: Any luck on your hunt for Keenan yet?

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.player: Not yet, no, but Muriel's given me something to go on. I'll see if it leads me anywhere.

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.speaker: Cormac
following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.text: Let's hope it does. There be something out there that gives us a clue, I'm sure of it.

following-the-trail-inspecting-the-sunst.text: You look upon the large rock and feel a strange energy pulsing around you. You then notice a book amidst some nearby rocks, which you take. You also notice a trail of dust leading away from the rock...
If the player has a full inventory:

steps.text: You look upon the large rock and feel a strange energy pulsing around you. As you look upon it, you notice a book amidst some nearby rocks. However, you don't have enough room to take it.

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.speaker: Cormac
following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.text: Any luck on your hunt for Keenan yet?

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.player: I've found what I'm guessing is his notebook over in the mine.
I wouldn't call it all nonsense. He apparently felt like he was being watched whilst he was at the sunstone. That's something.

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.speaker: Cormac
following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.text: Watched? I mean, none of us really kept too close an eye on the lad. Why would he feel like someone was watching him?

following-the-trail-talking-to-cormac-af.player: Well, if I keep following the trail, maybe I'll find out.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.text: You're back. Have you had any luck finding Keenan?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.player: Not yet, but I've found a trail over in the mine that might lead me somewhere. Speaking of which, I'd better get back to it.

following-the-trail-investigating-the-la.text: You find a hat hooked onto a rock in the shadow of a large cathedral... Could the hat be Keenan's?
The camera slowly pans from the hat to the cathedral.
The hat appears to be hooked onto a rock. Could it be Keenan's?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.player: Does Keenan have a habit of losing his hat?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.text: Not particularly, no. He always takes good care of it. Why do you ask?

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.player: I found a hat caught up on some rocks to the south. I wondered if it might have been his.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.speaker: Muriel
following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-af.text: No, he'd not just leave it there like that. At least, not of his own volition...
Muriel begins to sob, preventing any further questioning.

following-the-trail-talking-to-muriel-ag.text: Muriel seems too upset to talk to you right now.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: Well, I found a hat that might belong to Keenan.
Down amongst the rocks beneath that big cathedral.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: The cathedral? No... No that can't be right...

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: What do you mean? What is that cathedral?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Ardeaglais. It be the home of the Mad Angel.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: I get the feeling you haven't been totally honest with me.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: It wasn't my wish to mislead, I just did nay want to waste your time with local superstitions...

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: It sounds like we might be dealing with more than superstitions.
I think it's time you explained. What is this Mad Angel?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Old. Vicious. At least, that's what some of the stories say. Others though... they call her our protector. The only thing keepin' us safe from horrors o' the deep sea.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: No. The stories... they be sayin' that she'll keep us safe in exchange for tribute, but if we fail to keep her happy, she'll take one o' ours instead.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: And you didn't think to mention this earlier?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: I thought they was just tales! That the cathedral was long abandoned! So many of the others get 'emselves proper worked up about the Angel, but my job is to keep things calm.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: Well, whatever the truth is, it seems I'm going to need to enter that cathedral. How do I get inside?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Well, I wouldn't even try the front... but maybe you'll have some luck getting in from beneath.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: The stories say that some o' the first settlers here apparently sailed into the caverns on the south side of the island, but between the rocks and the tides, their ships never be havin' a chance at coming back out.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Instead, they found another way t' get out, up onto the cliffs. The same one where they eventually built Ardeaglais.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: So I'm going to have to sail into those caverns myself?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Aye, but don't make the same mistake they did. Make sure t' use something on the smaller side, else you'll get into trouble on the rocks.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: And be careful down there. Some say the Mad Angel ain't the only danger on this island, and it ain't the wyrms they're talking about. They reckon there be other evils lurking in them caverns...

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: Wonderful. I'll be sure to take care then.

options.text: Do you know where the Mad Angel came from?

steps.player: Do you know where the Mad Angel came from?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: The tales say she led the first settlers here. She be the one to help 'em build this town and she kept them safe from all the dangers that come with such an out t' way location.

steps.player: And was she always mad?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: No. That happened slowly. To start with she was able t' live among the people, but eventually they had to build Ardeaglais for her.

steps.player: Which is where she's stayed ever since?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Supposedly. But no one's seen her in my lifetime, though I s'pose it's not like anyone be fancying going into Ardeaglais to check.

options.text: What tributes are you meant to give to the Mad Angel?

steps.player: What tributes are you meant to give to the Mad Angel?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Blood.

steps.player: Blood?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Aye, a tithe of human blood. No other blood will do.

steps.player: And people here have still been doing that?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Well, a lot of us dismissed her as a myth, but there be plenty of superstitious folk here who were keen to make sure the tributes continued.

steps.player: So they just deliver some blood up to the cathedral?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Pretty much. They leave it nearby and make sure not to be around when it gets taken.

steps.player: And it does get taken?

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Aye, but hard to say if it's actually the Mad Angel doing it. Could be it's just the wildlife.

steps.player: I'd best get going.

steps.speaker: Cormac
steps.text: Good luck, friend.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: Where was it you said I should go to get to the cathedral?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: You'll need to sail through the caverns that run beneath us. Should be able to get into them if you sail around to the south side of the island.

options.text: Do you know where the Mad Angel came from?
What tributes are you meant to give to the Mad Angel?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-muri.text: Muriel seems too upset to talk to you right now.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.text: Hey you! Get over here, quickly!

the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.text: It's dangerous here. What are you doing?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.player: A talking skeleton? What is this?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.text: That is a question that is not currently relevant, given our present situation. Help me with this blockage, and maybe then you'll get your answers.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.player: Fair enough... What do you need?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-meeting-mortime.text: It was those three nearby trolls that caused this, and they've not been happy about my attempts to sort it. Deal with them for me while I work on clearing the way.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: How are you doing with those trolls?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.player: I'm not quite done with them yet.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: Remember, I just need you to handle the three nearby ones.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-upon-killing-th.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-upon-killing-th.text: Hey! Come give me a hand over here.
You notice the skeleton calling you over.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: Perfect. I've pretty much got things cleared here. Give me a hand with the last few bits...
You help get the remaining rocks cleared...

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: Well, well, well, would you look at that! An adventurer who isn't just skin and bones! You did well handling those trolls.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.player: Thanks, but you look like you'd have been capable of handling them yourself.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: I would've done, if they hadn't trapped me on the other side of that rockfall.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.player: Fair point. So, who are you? And... what are you?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: The name's Mortimer, and I'm the oldest Slayer Master across all of the seas of Gielinor.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: Well noted. Now, what is it you're actually doing down here?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.player: I'm trying to find a missing villager. He may be up in the cathedral.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.speaker: Mortimer
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-mort.text: Hmm... a noble cause. I'm afraid I've not seen him myself. Good luck on your search though.

options.text: So you say you're a Slayer Master?

steps.player: So you say you're a Slayer Master?

steps.speaker: Mortimer
steps.text: Indeed. Perhaps you'd be up for one of my special slayer assignments?

steps.player: Maybe... What's so special about these assignments?

steps.speaker: Mortimer
steps.text: Well, back in my day there was a lot more freedom and less bureaucracy about what adventurers were assigned to slay... as long as it was in need of slaying.

steps.speaker: Mortimer
steps.text: If you slay for me, I will give you the choice of two different creatures to be assigned. If you continue to prove your worth to me, I could be convinced to offer three choices instead of two.

steps.player: What's the catch?

steps.speaker: Mortimer
steps.text: I'll only assign you options from creatures which have superior variants, regardless of whether you have that perk unlocked. My tasks also won't naturally offer any slayer points.

steps.speaker: Mortimer
steps.text: This is purely slaying for the love of slaying.

steps.speaker: Mortimer
steps.text: As an added bonus, some of my assignments include creatures which are more lucrative than they normally would be. I'll point this out when offering your assignments, so keep your eyes peeled.

options.text: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?
Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

steps.player: Thanks.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Any luck gettin' into the caverns?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: I've managed to get into them, yes. Still no sign of Keenan though.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Best we hope it isn't too late.

options.text: Do you know where the Mad Angel came from?
What tributes are you meant to give to the Mad Angel?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-searching-the-g.text: It's a broken down golem made from sunstone. You begin to inspect it closer...
If the player's inventory is full:

steps.text: You find a dulled golem core within its chest, but you leave it behind as you have nowhere to put it.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-searching-the-g.text: If the player's inventory is not full:

steps.text: You find a dulled golem core within its chest.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-inspecting-the-.text: This sunstone core was presumably once used to power a golem, but it looks to be lifeless now.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-searching-the-g.text: It appears to be a broken down golem made from sunstone with a large hole in its chest. You might be able to get it to move if you can power it up.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-attempting-to-o.text: The door is firmly locked. If you want to enter the cathedral, you're going to need to find another way inside.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Any luck gettin' into the caverns?

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.player: I've managed to get into them, yes, but the way forward is blocked by some sort of golem. I think it's made of sunstone.

the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.speaker: Cormac
the-way-under-ardeaglais-talking-to-corm.text: Sunstone? I do nay know much about that stuff. Ironically, Keenan would 'ave been the best person t' ask. I remember Muriel sayin' he was fascinated by the stuff.

options.text: Do you know where the Mad Angel came from?
What tributes are you meant to give to the Mad Angel?

entering-ardeaglais-putting-a-new-core-i.text: You place the sunstone core into the golem. It provides just enough energy for the golem to move aside, letting you get past it...

entering-ardeaglais-attempting-to-climb-.text: If the player has a full inventory:

steps.text: You go to climb the stairs, but notice a locked hatch at the top of them.

entering-ardeaglais-attempting-to-climb-.text: You go to climb the stairs, but notice a locked hatch at the top of them. You also spot a note on the floor next to them.

entering-ardeaglais-reading-the-note-the.prompt: You notice something written on the back of the note...

entering-ardeaglais-reading-the-note-aga.prompt: Something is written on both the front and back of the note.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-af.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-af.text: Any luck gettin' into the caverns?

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-af.player: Yes, and I've found a way through them and into the basement of the cathedral. Still no sign of Keenan though.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-af.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-af.text: It's startin' to feel like we've taken t' long...

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-af.player: Well, we can't give up on him yet.

entering-ardeaglais-unlocking-the-chest.text: If the player has a full inventory:

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-be.player: I've managed to find a way into the cathedral, but it's not looking good... Best I get back there right away.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.player: Cormac, I was too late. I managed to enter the cathedral, but I found Keenan dead inside.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.text: I see... Well, I had been hopin' for better news, but I s'pose this was probably inevitable... Was there anything you could bring back? A body?

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.player: There was, but it's not something that Muriel should have to see.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.text: And the Angel? Did you deal with her?

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.player: She wasn't there. I think whatever was left of her mind felt guilt over Keenan's death. It seems she's left the island.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.text: Is that it? She just gets t' leave us fendin' for ourselves?

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.player: She's built a golem to replace herself. It put up quite the fight. It needs some battle hardening, but if you're worried for your security, I'm certain it'll be able to help.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.text: Well, in a day we've gone from wonderin' if the Mad Angel is even real, to learnin' she was, but that she's now gone an' left for good. I s'pose that makes it a new era for us 'ere.

entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.speaker: Cormac
entering-ardeaglais-talking-to-cormac-an.text: First up though, I'd best be tellin' Muriel the bad news. Until next time, [player name]... and I hope there will be a next time. Would be good for you t' stick around.

steps.npc: Hi there [Fremennik name]. I am Falo the bard! Like my brother Olaf, who lives in Rellekka, I also write music.

standard-dialogue.player: Do you write about anything in particular?

standard-dialogue.npc: Oh most certainly! I write about all the objects in the lands. From weapons and armour to palm trees and sands. That's why I wander far from Rellekka to seek inspiration.
I have one problem though. I am very forgetful, I can never remember which particular object a song was about.

standard-dialogue.player: Surely the lyrics for such a song would be enough to help you remember?

standard-dialogue.npc: I am afraid not. It saddens me deeply, so I often send out messages to adventurers to help me discreetly.

standard-dialogue.player: I'll keep a look out for them! Goodbye Falo.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.npc: Get away! I do not speak to outlanders.

treasure-trails-master.npc: Thank you for coming [Fremennik name], I need your help.
I have one of my old songs stuck in my head, but I cannot remember what the object it refers to is. I am so forgetful. I'll sing it to you.
Here goes... [one of his random songs]
You have very kind words. I would be extremely grateful if you could remind me which object the song was about.

treasure-trails-master-when-talked-to-ag.npc: I really hope you can help me. Please show me the object my song is about!

treasure-trails-master-when-talked-to-ag.player: Can you sing me the song again?

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.text: You show your object to Falo.

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.npc: Yes yes yes! That is it, thank you so much [Fremennik name]. The memories have come flooding back. I get why the lyrics are what they are now.

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.text: You've been given a new clue!

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.player: I'm glad to have helped, hopefully you'll never forget again!

Falo's eyes fail to light up.

treasure-trails-master-when-an-incorrect.npc: No no no! That's not it. Please have another think about it, [Fremennik name].

starting-off-dimintheis.speaker: Dimintheis
starting-off-dimintheis.text: Hello. My name is Dimintheis, of the noble family Fitzharmon.

options.text: Why would a nobleman live in a dump like this?

steps.player: Why would a nobleman live in a dump like this?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: The King has taken my estate from me until such time as I can show my family crest to him.

steps.player: Why would he do that?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Well, there is a long standing rule of chivalry amongst the Varrockian aristocracy, where each noble family is in possession of a unique crest, which signifies the honour and lineage of the family. More than this

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: however, it also represents the lawful rights of each family to prove their ownership of their wealth and lands. If the family crest is lost, then the family's estate is handed over to the current monarch until the crest is

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: restored.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: This dates back to the times when there was much in-fighting amongst the noble families and their clans, and was introduced as a way of reducing the bloodshed that was devestating the ranks of the ruling classes at that

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: time. When you captured a rival family's clan, you also captured their lands and wealth.
Continues from "So where is this crest?"

steps.player: So where is this crest?

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Well, my three sons took it with them many years ago when they rode out to fight in the war against the undead necromancer and his army in the battle to save Varrock.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: For many years I had assumed them all dead, as I had heard no word from them, but recently I heard word that my son Caleb is alive and well, and trying to earn his fortune as a great chef in the lands beyond White

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Wolf Mountain, although I know not where.
If the player lacks one or more requirements of the quest and has a combat level lower than 55:
Before starting this quest, be aware that one or more of your skill levels are lower than what is required to fully complete it. Your combat level is also lower than the recommended level of 55.

steps.prompt: Start the Family Crest quest?

steps.player: Ok, I will help you.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: I thank you greatly adventurer! Also... if you find Caleb... please... let him know his father still loves him...

steps.player: I'm not interested in that adventure right now.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: I realise it was a lot to ask of a stranger.

steps.speaker: Dimintheis
steps.text: Gah! Lousy beggar! Your sort is what's ruining this great land! Why don't you just go and get a job if you need money so badly?

starting-off-dimintheis-talking-to-dimin.speaker: Dimintheis
starting-off-dimintheis-talking-to-dimin.text: Have you any news on my crest yet?

caleb.speaker: Caleb
caleb.text: Who are you? What are you after?

steps.player: Are you Caleb Fitzharmon?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Why... yes I am, but I don't believe I know you... how did you know my name?

steps.player: I have been sent by your father. He wishes the Fitzharmon Crest be restored.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Ah... well... hmmm... yes... I do have a piece of it anyway...

options.text: Uh... what happened to the rest of it?

steps.player: Uh... what happened to the rest of it?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Well... my brothers and I had a slight disagreement about it... we all wanted to be heir to my fathers' lands, and we each ended up with a piece of the crest.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: None of us wanted to give up our rights to our brothers, so we didn't want to give up our pieces of the crest, but none of us wanted to face our father by

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: returning to him with an incomplete crest... We each went our seperate ways many years past, none of us seeing our father or willing to give up our fragments.

options.text: So can I have your bit?

steps.player: So can I have your bit?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Well, I am the oldest son, so by the rules of chivalry, I am most entitled to be rightful bearer of the crest.

steps.player: It's not really much use without the other fragments is it though?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Well that is true... perhaps it is time to put my pride aside... I'll tell you what: I'm struggling to complete this fish salad of mine,

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: so if you will assist me in my search for the ingredients, then I will let you take my piece as reward for your assistance.

steps.player: So what ingredients are you missing?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: I require the following cooked fish: Swordfish, Bass, Tuna, Salmon and Shrimp.

steps.player: Ok, I will get those.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: You will? It would help me a lot!

options.text: Why don't you just give me the crest?

steps.player: Why don't you just give me the crest?

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: It's a valuable family heirloom. I think the least you can do is prove you're worthy of it before I hand it over.

options.text: Nothing, I will be on my way.

steps.text: Well, we haven't really kept in touch... what with the dispute over the crest and all... I did hear from my brother Avan a while ago though.

steps.text: He said he was on some kind of search for treasure, or gold, or something out in the desert east of Lumbridge. You might want to ask the traders there about him.

steps.text: Avan always did have expensive tastes however. You may find he is not prepared to hand over his crest piece to you as easily as I have.

steps.player: Thank you very much.

steps.text: You're welcome.

steps.speaker: Caleb
steps.text: Last I heard he was on some stupid hunt for gold or treasure, somewhere out in the desert east of Lumbridge. You might want to ask the traders there about him.

steps.speaker: Gem trader
steps.text: Fitzharmon eh? Hmmm.... If I'm not mistaken that's the family name of a member of the Varrockian nobility. You know, I HAVE seen someone of that

steps.speaker: Gem trader
steps.text: persuasion around here recently... Wearing a poncey yellow cape he was! Came in here all la-di-dah, high and mighty, asking for jewelry made

steps.speaker: Gem trader
steps.text: from 'perfect gold' - whatever that is - like 'normal' golds just not good enough for little lord fancy pants there! I told him to head to the desert

steps.speaker: Gem trader
steps.text: 'Cos I know theres gold out there, in them there sand dunes... and if it's not up to his lordships high standards of 'gold perfection'...

steps.speaker: Gem trader
steps.text: Maybe we'll all get lucky and the scorpions will deal with him.

options.text: I'm looking for a man named Avan Fitzharmon

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Then you have found him. My name is Avan Fitzharmon.

steps.player: You have a part of your family crest. I am on a quest to retrieve all of the fragmented pieces and restore the crest.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Ha! I suppose one of my worthless brothers has sent you on this quest then?

steps.player: No, it was your father who has asked me to do this for him.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: My... my father wishes this? Then that is a different matter. I will let you have my crest shard, adventurer, but you must first do something for me.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: There is a certain lady I am trying to impress. As a man of noble birth, I can not give her just any old trinket to show my devotion. What I intend to give her, is a golden ring, embedded with the finest precious red

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: stone available, and a necklace to match this ring.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: The problem however for me, is that not just any old gold will be suitable. I seek only the purest, the most high quality of gold - what I seek, if you will, is perfect gold.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: None of the gold around here is even remotely suitable in terms of quality. I have searched far and wide for the perfect gold I desire, but have had no success so in finding it.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: If you can find me my perfect gold, make a ring and necklace from it, and add rubies to them, I will gladly hand over my fragment of the family crest to you.

steps.player: Can you give me any help on finding this 'perfect gold'?

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: I thought I had found a solid lead on its whereabouts when I heard of a dwarf who is an expert on gold who goes by the name of 'Boot'.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Unfortunately he has apparently returned to his home, somewhere under Ice Mountain, and I have no idea how to find him.

steps.player: Well, I'll see what I can do.

avan-talking-to-avan-talking-to-avan-aga.speaker: Avan
avan-talking-to-avan-talking-to-avan-aga.text: His name was Boot. Unfortunately for me, he has apparently returned to his home under Ice Mountain, and I cannot find him.

options.text: Hello. I'm in search of very high quality gold.

steps.speaker: Boot

avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.speaker: Avan

avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.player: I have spoken to Boot the dwarf about the location of 'perfect gold', but haven't managed to make you your jewellery yet.

avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.speaker: Avan
avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.text: Well, I won't entrust you with my piece of the crest until you have brought me a necklace of perfect gold with a red precious stone, and a perfect gold ring to match.

avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.speaker: Avan

avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.text: Now, I suppose you will be wanting to find my brother Johnathon who is in possession of the final piece of the family's crest?

avan-talking-to-avan-after-talking-to-bo.text: Unsurprisingly, I do not believe he is doing a particularly good job of things.

steps.npc: A little while ago we had some real problems getting rum to the island, hence the two stills.
However, after a little misunderstanding involving San's still and a barrel of gunpowder our relationship seems to have become a little strained.
Apparently it is perfectly within the pirate code to burn each others stills, so long as nobody directly attacks the other person's crew, so rum production has taken a slight dip of late.

steps.player: Can I help out?

steps.npc: Yes, probably. I have a bunch of jobs that need doing, if you feel up to it.

steps.player: How do I help you brew 'Rum'?

steps.npc: Well the stills we have set up are based on the ones on Braindeath island... well roughly at any rate.
All you have to do is help put the ingredients into the hoppers and keep the boilers burning.
If you add enough ingredients to the hoppers then you have the ability to pick up a single bottle of rum when it brews.

So, if ye add 5 buckets of water to the hoppers, then ye get access to one bottle. If you add 3 bowls of coloured water you get access to one bottle, and if you add one of anything else you get access to one bottle.
This is cumulative, meaning that if you add (for example) 10 buckets of water, 3 sweetgrubs and 6 bowls of coloured water, then you have a chance to collect 7 bottles of rum for the team.
The boilers are easy as pie to sort out. You just put some logs in, light them with a tinderbox, and then keep putting logs in until they are good and hot.
Three logs should do it, but it's best to keep heaping them in just in case.
The ingredients are; Bitternuts, Scrapey Tree Bark, Sweetgrubs, Buckets of Water and some Coloured Water.

steps.player: Where can I get Bitternuts?

steps.npc: There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.

steps.npc: Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.

steps.player: Wait a second, dye?

steps.npc: Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs too.

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me and item, and I'll tell you if it's super-compostable or not.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You don't have tp buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can fill plantpots with soil from  any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
That depends on whether I have it to sell. What is it that you're looking for?

standard-dialogue-monologue-1.npc: So there I was, minding my own business on the boat, when I feel us slow to a halt.
This man walks over to me and says that it's my stop, absurd though that is.
So they all sort of... toss me onto this island with a meagre amount of survival objects.
I think they were laughing whilst they did it.
Either way, there I was. Alone. On this island.
I'd paid quite handsomely for my passage too!
A tour to the rainforest, and then dinner in Tal Teklan.
This crew were all so very willing to get me where I wanted to go.
Very helpful as they collected my belongings. Eager, even.
It felt exclusive. I was the only passenger they took aboard.
I do see now that I was perhaps foolish.
Drawn in by their charms, throwing money around.
I just really wanted that dinner in Tal Teklan, you know?
Now I'm going to die alone on an island, bereft of my worldly possessions.
Perhaps the bards of Temptestus will write of my sorrow, should they hear my tale.

standard-dialogue-monologue-2.npc: Excuse me! Hello! I appear to have found myself in a situation here.
Can you see any way for me to... defamiliarise myself with this island?
I'm getting rather bored being stuck here waiting for the tide to swallow me.
Though, that is reliant on me not throwing myself into the dark sea first.
But fear not! I shan't do that, for it would be improper.
Though if it rains again, I may be tempted.
Observe how I have nothing here on this island.
There's myself and the occasional crab, but I've been left here... Abandoned! Forgotten!
I don't suppose you could send for a boat to retrieve me?
Yes, this predicament needs excessive force to be resolved peacefully.
Maybe I should pack a flag next time. Claim this land for myself.

standard-dialogue-monologue-3.npc: No! I can't be stuck here! It's far too small.
Are you finding the air just chokes you here? It is the air, isn't it?
Gosh, it feels as if my skin is just crawling.
Nobody's going to find me here... I'm going to rot on this island alone.
My regular baker will realise I've not come by in a day. He will send a search party!
They will send a search party, won't they?
This island is too small though... They won't be able to see it.
I'd start a fire, if only I had the tools to do so.
This isn't how I was meant to die!
I was meant to go down gloriously in the Colosseum!

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Hello, the face said that you were looking to talk with me.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Indeed, word has gotten to me from our other ratcatcher chapters that you are quite a talent.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Well I can't take all the credit, I've had more than a little help from my cat.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Modesty, a trait seldom displayed by adventurers these days.
Too many more like you and I'll lose half of my business.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Why is that?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Epic poems of bravery and heroics aren't usually commissioned by the shy and retiring.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Smokin' Joe said that you know lots about training wily cats.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Indeed I do. It's for this very reason that I requested to talk to you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: So you will show me how to turn my cat into a wily cat?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: No, not yet.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Sighs.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: No I need you to carry out just one task for me.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Well experience has taught me to expect as much, what must I do?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Nothing too difficult, just rid the port of every single rat, with just one action.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: What?
Are you serious?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Deadly.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: You see a manic glint in her eye which you had previously missed.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: But why? Why one stroke, why not a slow eradication?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I want to write a new poem.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: But...
I am touched that you want to write an epic poem about me, but why can't you write the poem about seagulls or daffodils or something?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Well seagulls rarely make good central characters. They're a bit too ... uhm.... flighty.
Besides the poem is about me not you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Sorry I don't follow.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I myself carried out the very same feat once upon a time.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: So why do you need me to repeat your most heroic of feats?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: It's all about objectivity and integrity. I need to be utterly divorced from the process.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Umm... ok, I suppose.
So can you tell me how you went about achieving this?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: No. Therein lies the challenge.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Sigh* Why does it always have to be like this?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.npc: You haven't completed the task yet.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.player: What do I have to do again?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.npc: Rid the port of all its rats with one action.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.player: I'd better get to it then.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: I think I know how to carry out the task.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Has the face being telling tall tales again?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Oh no, she didn't say a word.
Really she didn't.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-o.player: Ha! I did it. Did you see me?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-o.npc: Yes I saw that, now what can I do for you? Don't keep me overly long, I'm trying to complete my poem.

talking-to-fernahei-before-completing-sh.npc: I'm getting out of here Bwana, the place is infested with zombies.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: You're surrounded by a relic of a long lost kingdom.

steps.player: What happened here?

steps.npc: Oh, I couldn't really tell you that.
This place has sat in ruin for an age, slowly destroyed by the harsh climate of the Wilderness.

steps.player: If it's a ruin, what's the point in being here?

steps.npc: I search for knowledge. I want to know what happened to this part of the world.
Whilst looking for answers, I slowly turned this broken town into a safe haven for travellers. Welcome to Ferox Enclave.

steps.player: Quite a dangerous place for a town, don't you think?

steps.npc: It is, but that's why it's needed! Look around, you can see how many others share my opinion.
You'll find yourself quite safe inside my enclave - the protective barriers should keep any troublemakers out.
I will warn you though, if you've had Teleblock cast upon you, I will not allow you back into the Enclave. You'd be a danger to the others gathered here.

options.text: What can you do for me?

steps.player: Thanks for the information! I'll take a look around.

steps.npc: Tread carefully my friend.

options.text: What can you do for me?

steps.player: What can you do for me?

steps.npc: Well, if you'd like, I can make it so you respawn in our Enclave. It'll put you right in the heart of all the chaos that surrounds us.

steps.player: Tell me more.

steps.npc: This is how it'll work: When you die, you'll respawn right here in Ferox Enclave, just outside the pub we've set up. You will lose your items as normal of course.
I won't be able to do anything if you die somewhere like Castle Wars or the Emir's Arena; they have their own magic to keep you safe.
It'll cost you though! Transporting you here is no easy task. 5 million coins should do it, that'd be a one time fee of course.

steps.text: Without at least five million coins in the inventory:

steps.player: I don't have that much money on me.

steps.npc: Understandable, you'd have to be a brave [man/woman] to be carrying that much gold out here.

steps.text: With at least five million coins in the inventory:

options.text: Okay, switch my respawn to Ferox Enclave.

steps.text: 5 million coins

steps.npc: Thank you, you'll respawn in the Enclave from here on out.

steps.player: I'm not interested.

steps.npc: Can't say I blame you, this wouldn't be my choice either.

steps.player: That doesn't interest me.

steps.npc: Come find me if you change your mind.

steps.player: Never mind, I'm just looking around.

steps.npc: So be it.

steps.player: Your family? Can I help?

steps.text: You'd be willing to?

steps.player: Of course. Tell me what happened.

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: Well, I'm Lady Servil. I was travelling to Ardougne with my husband, Justin, and son, Sammy, when our cart broke on some rocks.

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: Some of General Khazard's men spotted us and offered to help, but they demanded my husband and son fight in their arena first! We said no, but they took them anyway!

steps.player: General Khazard?

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: He's a menace! This entire area is under the control of him and his mercenary group, the Khazard Army. They prey on the weak and vulnerable, making them fight in that arena of theirs, all for entertainment!

steps.player: That's horrible! How are they able to get away with it?

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: The authorities don't care. Khazard's men just pay them off if they ever come to investigate.

steps.player: Well they won't stop me. I'm going to try my best to find your family.

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: Thank you. They'll be somewhere inside the arena. I'll be waiting here for you.

steps.player: Well I hope it works out. Good luck.
