steps.speaker: Spectator
steps.text: Hello there. I hear Khazard's got some great fights lined up today. I can't wait!

the-battles-talking-to-a-spectator.text: If the player doesn't have the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.speaker: Spectator
steps.text: Hello, stranger. I hear Khazard's got some great fights lined up today. I can't wait!

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.player: Lady Servil, I freed your son, but he went to help your husband.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: No! Please, you have to help them!

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: Well, well, well, you seem to be in quite the rush. Do you have somewhere else to be?

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: You presume correct. I must say, I sense a great air of defiance to you. Does my appearance not fill you with fear?

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: How arrogant. No matter though, you will come to learn.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: Now, despite your entertaining show, the two individuals you are attempting to leave with are my property.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: Ha! Well if their freedom is so valuable to you, how about a trade? Fight in my arena, and if you win, I'll let them go.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.player: And what if I refuse your offer?

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: Well... I wasn't actually giving you a choice. Guards, take [him/her/them] to the cells.
The player is taken to a jail cell.

the-battles-talking-to-a-spectator-after.speaker: Spectator
the-battles-talking-to-a-spectator-after.text: Hey, you're the one from the arena! That was some great fighting!

the-battles-talking-to-a-spectator-after.speaker: Door Guard
the-battles-talking-to-a-spectator-after.text: So you're back for more are you? General Khazard will be pleased.
The player is taken back to the jail.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Hello there. So Khazard got his hands on you too?

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Well if you're lucky, you might last as long as me.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.player: How long have you been here?

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: As long as I can remember. I was a child when his men kidnapped me. My whole life has been spent killing and fighting, all in the hope that one day I might escape.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Thanks, friend.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Wait... sounds like the guard is coming. Looks like you'll be going back into the arena. Good luck, friend.
The player is brought into the arena.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Now watch closely, friends. I fear this may be where your protector dies.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Ignore him! You can do it!

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: I don't know how you managed to escape, but you may not be as lucky next time. Get out of here while you can.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-scorpion.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-scorpion.text: Impressive, but now for a proper challenge. Time for my puppy. Bring on Bouncer!

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: You monster! You'll pay for what you've done!

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.player: I only did what you asked. I fought in your arena. Now let the Servils go.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: Fine! I am not a coward who makes false promises. I have no need of them anyway. You on the other hand, won't be going anywhere.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: Guard, escort the Servils out. I'll take great pleasure in dealing with this one myself!

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: Don't try to fight him! Just run!

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer-opening.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer-opening.text: You! You're the one who killed Bouncer.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer-talking.speaker: Spectator
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer-talking.text: Hey, you're the one who beat Bouncer! Amazing!

the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.text: Ha! Arrogant fool! You think you can kill me? I am General Khazard! My power is absolute!

the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.text: Now, part of me would very much like to kill you for what you've done today, but let it be known that I am not without generosity.

the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.text: You proved yourself in battle against me. That is something few can boast of. For that, you may leave. However, if you ever oppose me again, I won't hesitate to wipe you from existence!

the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-defeating-general-khaza.text: Now go. I have business to attend to elsewhere that is far more important than you.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: You're alive! I feared General Khazard would have killed you!

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Thank goodness. I'd have never forgiven myself if you'd have died saving my family.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Now, you'll be pleased to know that my son and husband are safe and recovering at home. Without you they would certainly be dead. Thank you, for everything.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Please, take this payment. It's the least you deserve.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: You're alive! I feared General Khazard would have killed you!

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.player: He tried, but I was able to defeat him.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: You killed General Khazard?

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.player: I thought I had at first, but it seems he is not that easy to kill.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Well, at least you're alive.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Now, you'll be pleased to know that my son and husband are safe and recovering at home. Without you they would certainly be dead. Thank you, for everything.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Please, take this payment. It's the least you deserve.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

getting-started.speaker: Khazard Guard
getting-started.text: This area is restricted, leave now!

getting-started.speaker: Khazard Guard
getting-started.text: OUT! And don't come back.

getting-started.speaker: Khazard Guard
getting-started.text: I don't know you stranger. Get off our land.

getting-started-talking-to-local.speaker: Local
getting-started-talking-to-local.text: Hello stranger, are you new to these parts? You look lost.

getting-started-talking-to-local.speaker: Local
getting-started-talking-to-local.text: I suppose you're here for the fight arena? There are some rich folk fighting tomorrow. Should be entertaining.

getting-started-talking-to-lady-servil.player: Hi there. Looks like you're in some trouble.

getting-started-talking-to-lady-servil.speaker: Lady Servil
getting-started-talking-to-lady-servil.text: Oh I wish this broken cart was my only problem... I've got to find my family...

steps.player: Can I help you?

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: Would you? Please?

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: I'm Lady Servil, my husband is Sir Servil. We were travelling north together with our son Sammy when we were ambushed by General Khazard's men.

steps.player: General Khazard?

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: He's been after me ever since I declined his hand in marriage.

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: Now he's kidnapped my husband and son to fight in his battle arena to the south of here. I hate to think what he'll do to them. He's a sick and twisted man.

steps.player: I'll try my best to return your family.

steps.speaker: Lady Servil
steps.text: Please do. My family is wealthy and can reward you handsomely. I'll be waiting here for you.

steps.player: I hope you can, good luck.

getting-started-talking-to-lady-servil-a.speaker: Lady Servil
getting-started-talking-to-lady-servil-a.text: Brave traveller, please... bring back my family.

entering-the-arena.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena.text: I don't know who you are. Get out of my house stranger.

entering-the-arena-searching-the-armour-.text: If the player has neither helmet nor armour:
If the player does not have the armour:

steps.text: You search the chest, and find the armour of a Khazard guard.

entering-the-arena-searching-the-armour-.text: If the player does not have the helmet:

steps.text: You search the chest, and find the helmet of a Khazard guard.

entering-the-arena-searching-the-armour-.text: If the player has both helmt and armour:

steps.text: You search the chest, but find nothing.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.speaker: Lady Servil
entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.text: Have you had any luck with freeing my family?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.player: I've managed to get a guard's uniform, hopefully I can infiltrate the arena.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.text: Despicable thieving scum, that was good armour. Did you see anyone around here soldier?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.text: Oh, you're a guard as well. That's ok then. We don't like strangers around here.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.speaker: Local
entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.text: I heard the Servil family are fighting soon. Should be very entertaining.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.speaker: Local
entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.text: Hello stranger, are you new to these parts?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.player: Just visiting friends in the cells.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.speaker: Local
entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.text: Only Khazard guards are allowed to see prisoners. Unless you know where to get some Khazard armour, you won't be visiting anyone.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard barman
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Hi, what can I get you? We have a range of quality brews.

steps.player: I'll have a beer please.

steps.speaker: Khazard barman
steps.text: That'll be two gold coins please.
If the player doesn't have 2 coins:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.text: If the player has 2 coins:

steps.speaker: Khazard barman
steps.text: There you go, that's two gold coins.{{^|Drops to ground with full inventory.}}

steps.player: Got any news?

steps.speaker: Khazard barman
steps.text: If you want to see the action around here you should visit the famous Khazard fight arena. I've seen some grand battles in my time. Ogres, goblins, even dragons have fought there.

steps.speaker: Khazard barman
steps.text: Although you have to feel sorry for some of the slaves sent in there.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: I've never seen you around here before!

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Erm.. yes.. soldier, I take it you're new around here?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Khazard died two hundred years ago. However his dark spirit remains in the form of the undead maniac General Khazard. Remember he is your master, always watching.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.player: Undead, maniac, master. Got it, loud and clear.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-while-a-.player: This door appears to be locked.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-while-a-.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-opening-door-while-a-.text: Nice observation guard. You could have just asked to be let in like a normal person.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-joe.text: If the player has the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.player: Do either of you know a Justin or Sammy Servil?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: If we did, why would we tell you guard?

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.text: Until our last breath, our every action will be against Khazard. Never will we help you.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: I spit on Khazard's grave, and all who do his bidding.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-joe.text: If the player does not have the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.player: Do either of you know a Justin or Sammy Servil?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: I have heard of those of whom you speak. But I fear it may be too late.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.text: It is said that Khazard has a personal vendetta against those two, their time is therefore short.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: You're a brave [man/woman]. If the guards get you, you'll be in here next.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-kelvin.text: If the player has the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.player: Do either of you know a Justin or Sammy Servil?

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.text: If we did, why would we tell you guard?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Until our last breath, our every action will be against Khazard. Never will we help you.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.text: I spit on Khazard's grave, and all who do his bidding.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-kelvin.text: If the player does not have the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.text: I have heard of those of whom you speak. But I fear it may be too late.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It is said that Khazard has a personal vendetta against those two, their time is therefore short.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.text: You're a brave [man/woman]. If the guards get you, you'll be in here next.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-fightslave.player: Do you know of a Justin or Sammy Servil in this arena?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-fightslave.text: If the player has the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.speaker: Fightslave
steps.text: Please leave me alone.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-fightslave.text: If the player does not have the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.speaker: Fightslave
steps.text: I've not met anybody in here by that name.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-hengrad.player: Do you know a Justin or Sammy Servil?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-hengrad.speaker: Hengrad
entering-the-arena-talking-to-hengrad.text: You're not a real guard. I've been in here long enough to know that. What's your business?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-hengrad.player: I've been sent to rescue Sir Servil and his son.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-hengrad.speaker: Hengrad
entering-the-arena-talking-to-hengrad.text: I've seen them in here, although they don't look up to much. My advice to you is to leave before you end up in a cell too.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.text: If the nearby guards are alive:

steps.speaker: Khazard Guard
steps.text: And where do you think you're going? Only General Khazard decides who fights in the arena. Get out of here.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.text: If the nearby guards are dead:

steps.text: This door appears to be locked.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.text: Have you come to laugh at the fight slaves? I used to really enjoy it, but after a while they become quite boring.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.text: Now I just want a decent drink. Mind you, too much Khali brew and I'll fall asleep.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.text: Bored, bored, bored. You'd think the slaves would be more entertaining. Selfish the lot of them.

entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-opening-door-to-the-a.text: I used to enjoy this job, but now all I want is a decent drink.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.text: If the player has the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.player: Sshh. This uniform is a disguise, I'm here to help. Where do they keep the keys?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.text: If the player does not have the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.player: Sshh. I'm here to help. Where do they keep the keys?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.speaker: Sammy Servil
entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.text: The guard always keeps hold of them.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.player: Don't lose heart, I'll be back.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-lady-servi.player: Lady Servil, I have managed to infiltrate General Khazard's arena.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard barman
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Hi, what can I get you? We have a range of quality brews.

options.text: I'd like a Khali brew please.

steps.player: I'd like a Khali brew please.

steps.speaker: Khazard barman
steps.text: That'll be five gold coins please.
If the player doesn't have 5 coins:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.speaker: Khazard barman
steps.text: There you go, that's five gold coins. I suggest lying down before you drink it. That way you have less distance to collapse.{{^|Drops to ground with full inventory.}}

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Bored, bored, bored. You'd think the slaves would be more entertaining. Selfish the lot of them.* Player: Do you still fancy a drink?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: I really shouldn't... oh... ok then just the one.
You hand a bottle of Khali brew to the guard. He takes a mouthful of the drink.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Blimey this stuff is pretty good. It's not too strong is it?

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.player: No, not at all. You'll be fine.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: The guard quickly finishes the rest of the bottle and begins to sway slightly.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: That is some gooood stuff... yeah... wooh yeah!

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Yeesshh, hiccup! Oooh, maybe I sshould relax for a while.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.player: Good idea. I'll look after the prisoners.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.text: Yeesh, yes that shounds reasonable. Here, 'hiccup', take the keysch. Any trouble, you give... you givem a good beating.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-khazard-ba.player: No problem, I'll keep them in line.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.text: Please, leave me alone. I'm sure the walls never used to sway that much.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.player: Hi, er.. I lost the keys.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.text: ...and I'm drunk. Here, take my spare set.{{^|Drops to floor with full inventory.}}

entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.speaker: Khazard Guard
entering-the-arena-talking-to-drunk-khaz.text: Go away. Thish areash resh... restricted! We don't like strangersh, 'specially ones who sway. Oooh!

entering-the-arena-using-keys-on-a-cell-.player: The gate is locked, but Sammy's not in there anyway.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.player: Sammy look, I have the keys.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.speaker: Sammy Servil
entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.text: Wow! Please set me free, then we can find my dad. I overheard a guard talking. I think they've taken him to the arena.

entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.speaker: Sammy Servil
entering-the-arena-talking-to-sammy-serv.text: Quick, help him! That beast will kill him. He's too old to fight.
A cutscene plays of a Khazard Ogre exiting a cell toward Justin Servil.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-in-t.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-in-t.text: Quick, help him! That beast will kill him. He's too old to fight.

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard.text: If the player has the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.player: General Khazard?

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: What do you want guard? I'm a busy man.

steps.player: Of course sir.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: In the last two hundred years, I have survived all horrors imaginable. Now it is my turn to cover this land in darkness. One day you shall see, all will quake on hearing my name.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Now leave me.

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard.text: If the player does not have the Khazard armour equipped:

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Who dares enter my home? You? A feeble traveller?

steps.player: Feeble?!

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Get out!  Whoever let you in shall be severely punished for this.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil.player: Lady Servil sent me to rescue you and your son. Come on, we have to get out of here.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil.text: I'm too old to fight. I'm afraid you'll have to kill that ogre by yourself.

the-battles-trying-to-exit-the-arena-thr.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-trying-to-exit-the-arena-thr.text: Please don't go, you must help us. We'll never survive in here alone.

the-battles-trying-to-exit-the-arena-thr.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-trying-to-exit-the-arena-thr.text: Quick, help him! That beast will kill him. He's too old to fight.

the-battles-attacking-general-khazard.text: I don't have time. I'm here to rescue Sir Servil and Sammy.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.player: Lady Servil. I freed your son, however he has returned to the arena to help your husband.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: Oh no, they won't stand a chance. Please go back and help.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: You saved my life and my son's, I am eternally in your debt brave traveller.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: Haha, well done, well done that was rather entertaining. I am the great General Khazard, and the two men you just 'saved' are my property.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: Well, I suppose we could find some arrangement for their freedom... hmmm?

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: I'll let them go, but you must stay and fight for me. You'll make me double the gold if you manage to last a few fights.
The player is taken to a jail cell.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-khazard-ogr.text: The General seems to have taken a liking to you. He'd normally kill imposters like you without a second thought.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.text: You saved my life and my son's. I am eternally in your debt brave traveller.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.player: Come on Sammy, we have to get out of here.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.text: Thank you for saving my father.

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.player: I have come to demand the release of Sir Servil and his son.

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.text: Why would I give them up, those two men are my property now.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-in-the-jail.text: Sammy is in the arena with his father now.

steps.speaker: Fightslave

steps.speaker: Fightslave
steps.text: What did I do to deserve this?

steps.speaker: Fightslave
steps.text: Please help me.

the-battles-talking-to-fightslave-after-.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-talking-to-fightslave-after-.text: General Khazard doesn't tolerate the lazy. If you're not keeping busy I'll practice my combat skills on your hide.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Get away, get away. One day I'll have my revenge, and I'll have all your heads.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Spare me your fake pity. I spit on Khazard's grave, and all who do his bidding.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: You're not safe here traveller. Leave while you still can

steps.text: You're a brave person. If the guards get you, you'll be in here next.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: I'm fine thanks.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: So Khazard got his hands on you too?

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: If you're lucky you may last as long as me.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.player: How long have you been here?

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: I've been in Khazard's prisons ever since I can remember. I was a child when his men kidnapped me. My whole life has been spent killing and fighting, all in the hope that one day I might escape.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Thanks friend.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Wait.. sshh, the guard is coming. Looks like you'll be going into the arena. Good luck friend.
The guard walks up and unlocks the cell.

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-in-the-ja.text: Right you, move it.
The player is brought into the arena.
From above you hear a voice.....  'Ladies and gentlemen! Let today's first fight between the outsider and everyone's favourite scorpion commence.'
The scorpion exits the cell and attacks the player.

the-battles-entering-the-building-after-.player: This door appears to be locked.

the-battles-entering-the-building-after-.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-entering-the-building-after-.text: So you're back for more are you? General Khazard will be pleased.
(The player is taken directly to the arena.)

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-in-t.player: Don't worry, I'll get us out of here.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-in-t.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-in-t.text: Thanks traveller. I'm sorry that you too are now a subject of this arena.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-in-.player: Don't worry, I'll get us out of here.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-in-.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-in-.text: You've incurred the anger of Khazard yourself now. He won't let any of us go easily.

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-d.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-d.text: How dare you speak to me, you are a slave of this arena now.

the-battles-trying-to-exit-the-arena-dur.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-trying-to-exit-the-arena-dur.text: It would be impolite to leave now. The General insists you stay a little longer.

the-battles-upon-killing-the-scorpion.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-the-scorpion.text: Not bad, not bad at all. I think you need a tougher challenge. Time for my puppy. Guards! Guards! Bring on Bouncer!
From above you hear a voice.....  'Ladies and gentlemen! Today's second round of battle is between the outsider and Bouncer.'

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-dur.player: Come on, we only have to fight a creature called bouncer now.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-dur.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-dur.text: You may laugh, but the name of the General's 'pet' is feared by many in this land.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-dur.player: Don't worry, I'll get us out of here.

the-battles-talking-to-the-local-during-.speaker: Local
the-battles-talking-to-the-local-during-.text: Hey you're the guy from the arena! How'd you get out!

the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-during-th.speaker: Hengrad
the-battles-talking-to-hengrad-during-th.text: I don't know how you managed to escape the arena, but you may not be as lucky next time. Get out of here while you can.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: Nooooo! Bouncer! How dare you? You've taken the life of my only friend. Now you'll suffer traveller, prepare to meet your maker.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.player: You agreed to let the Servils go if I stayed to fight.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: Indeed. I obviously underestimated you, although you still pale in comparison to the might of General Khazard.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: You shall see that I am not cowardly enough to make false promises. They may go.

the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-upon-killing-bouncer.text: You however have caused me much trouble today. You must remain here so that I may at least have the pleasure of killing you myself.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.player: What does Khazard want with us now?

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.text: I don't know, but I can't imagine he'll be happy with you now.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.text: The agreement was that the Servils may leave if you won a few fights, and indeed they are now free to do so.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.player: What does Khazard want with us now?

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.text: I don't know, but he won't be happy that you've killed his so called pet.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.text: The agreement was that the Servils may leave if you won a few fights, and indeed they are now free to do so.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.player: You can run, Khazard's interest is in me now.

the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.speaker: Justin Servil
the-battles-talking-to-justin-servil-aft.text: My thanks, we'll be ok now. I suggest you run too, General Khazard is mighty and his anger fearsome.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.player: You and your father should run, Khazard's interest is in me now.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.speaker: Sammy Servil
the-battles-talking-to-sammy-servil-afte.text: I'm sorry to have gotten you into so much trouble. You should run as well, Khazard is too dangerous.

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.text: You killed my pet, and yet still you dare to speak to me?

the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.speaker: General Khazard
the-battles-talking-to-general-khazard-a.text: You shall die for your insolence.

the-battles-entering-the-door-to-the-bui.player: This door appears to be locked.

the-battles-entering-the-door-to-the-bui.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-entering-the-door-to-the-bui.text: You're [him/her]. The one who murdered the General's pet.

the-battles-opening-the-door-to-the-aren.speaker: Khazard Guard
the-battles-opening-the-door-to-the-aren.text: You're the one who killed Bouncer.

the-battles-talking-to-sammy-in-the-cell.text: You've already rescued Sammy from the fight arena.

the-battles-talking-to-the-local-after-k.speaker: Local
the-battles-talking-to-the-local-after-k.text: You're the guy who beat Bouncer, amazing!

the-battles-talking-to-the-local-after-k.speaker: Local
the-battles-talking-to-the-local-after-k.text: That makes you a champion to many, but you'd better get out of here while you still can. General Khazard liked that brute.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: You're alive, I thought Khazard's men had taken you.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: My son and husband are safe and recovering at home. Without you they would certainly be dead. I am truly grateful for your service.

the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.speaker: Lady Servil
the-battles-talking-to-lady-servil-after.text: All I can offer in return is material wealth. Please take these coins as a sign of my gratitude.

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.npc: There's no rain or wind down here.
Some of the dwarves say that there's water in the other caves, and one of them says he's seen monsters in there.

steps.player: Monsters? What sort of monsters?

steps.npc: I don't know, sorry. You'd better ask one of the dwarves about it.
Hello, human.

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: How are you finding the Conch so far?

steps.player: Very nice, thank you. It's a remarkable island you have here.

steps.npc: It is, isn't it? Still, I must admit, I'm keen to get out into the wider world. Coco and Torgan say it won't be long now until it's time for my Trial by Water.

steps.player: Well, in that case, I wish you good luck.

steps.npc: Thank you, human.

steps.npc: Relaxing after a long day at the factory.
If I keep up this winning streak, I mightn't have to go into work tomorrow.

steps.player: Do you mind me asking how much you have won?

steps.npc: Not at all, I'm up 10 coins so far.

steps.player: Umm ok.
So how do these rat pits work?

steps.npc: The Keldagrim pits cater for those with the larger variety of cats.
If you have an overgrown cat and a couple of coins you can challenge someone else who also has an overgrown cat and some spare change.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 9 rats first wins.

steps.player: That sounds vile and cruel.

steps.npc: It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Each to their own, I say.

options.text: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.player: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.npc: I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.

steps.player: Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?

steps.npc: Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.

steps.player: Oh that sounds quite wise.

steps.npc: That depends on how you value your cat.

steps.player: Sorry, I don't follow.

steps.npc: Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.

steps.player: Wow that sounds like fun!

steps.npc: I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.

options.text: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.player: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.npc: Hmmm... let me think. I don't think that's ever arisen but I think it's 20,000.

steps.player: Hmm, that sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.

steps.npc: You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.

steps.npc: I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.

steps.player: Thanks for your help.
Hello!

steps.npc: Ahoy there! Here for a drink? You've picked the right place for it. Steve is thankfully a much better bartender than he was a sailor.

steps.player: Sounds like there's a story here?

steps.npc: Indeed there is. Steve fancied himself a pirate, but on his first proper voyage he managed to crash his ship, the Pandemonium, right here.

steps.player: He crashed? How?

steps.npc: He claims it was an unavoidable accident caused by the Storm Tempor, but I heard it was actually because he got distracted by a large flock of angry parrots.

steps.player: So he crashed the boat and then decided to open a bar?

steps.npc: Pretty much.

steps.player: I see. Fair enough.

standard-dialogue.npc: What do you need, adventurer? There is a battle to fight!

steps.player: How do I help?

steps.npc: Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

steps.player: Aye aye!

options.text: What should I watch out for?

steps.player: What should I watch out for?

steps.npc: If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

steps.player: Aye aye!
I want to leave.

steps.npc: Really? You will receive no reward if you do.

options.text: Yes, I really want to leave.
No, I don't want to leave.
I'll get on with the fighting.

steps.player: I'll get on with the fighting.

standard-dialogue-after-subduing-temporo.npc: We did it! Tempoross has been sudbued once again. Well done!
Take a well deserved rest but don't get too comfy, it'll regain its energy soon enough!

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.npc: We usually find some debris washed up near the docks back at Unkah. Feel free t' have a look. Ya might find somethin' useful!
It won't be long before Tempoross regains enough energy to be a problem and we'll have to wrangle it again. Hopefully we can count on you to 'elp!

steps.player: I'm ready to leave.

steps.npc: Aye aye!

steps.text: The player returns to the Ruins of Unkah.

steps.player: Goodbye.

We must find...

steps.player: Wow, are you okay? What happend to you?

steps.npc: Ugh... Well met, adventurer. I wouldn't go down there if I were you. That trap is an absolute nightmare! The one who created it must be a sadist. I don't know of anyone who has cleared it.

steps.player: Oh? I've cleared it.

steps.npc: Oh? Are you pulling my leg, adventurer?

steps.player: I'm fairly certain that if I did that, it would fall off!

steps.npc: No need to add salt in the wound.
Although I am curious, how did you beat the trap?

steps.player: I just made sure to prioritise looking out for the arrows. The fire was fairly easy to get through if I just made sure to take one step at a time.

steps.npc: I see, you're clearly more skillful than I. I'm not sure if I'd be agile enough to do that. Do tell, what was on the next floor?

steps.player: The place looked magnificent, gold lion statues, coffins untouched by anyone else and plenty of Hallowed marks compared to these floors. Although, the traps were significantly harder than the one below.

steps.npc: I see. Well, I guess I'd better brush up on my skills if I want to see it for myself. Nothing worth having in life comes easy right?

steps.player: That's very true, I wish you the best of luck!

options.text: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

steps.player: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

steps.npc: Well, unlike the rest of the traps I've seen so far, you have to deal with both an arrow trap and a fire trap at the same time.

steps.player: Wow, that does sound hard. Do you have any tips for me?

steps.npc: Well, individually they aren't that hard to do. The fires are always swapping between on and off. I think that if you run to where the fire just was you should be safe.
The hardest part for me is the arrows. You have to look forward to watch the fire trap whilst also looking over your shoulder to see where the arrows are.
I certainly wish there was a way to see both at once. Perhaps it would help if a fellow adventurer was looking down from above to call out where the arrows are.

steps.player: Yeah... I'd imagine having an aerial view of the situation would be pretty helpful.

steps.npc: Of course, but we both know that's impossible for one person! Ouch! Sorry, it hurts to laugh. I wish you luck adventurer!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Well met! My name's Florin, I do a bit of this, a bit of that. Just try to survive really, there's nothing much else we can do.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Oh, my name's Florin. I just help out around here, you know, gathering food and so on.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.player: But you do realise that the vampyres in Morytania are immune to everything except silver?

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.player: Hi there, Veldaban! Have you got any new quests for me?

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.text: Not at the moment, no, [player name].

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.player: That's too bad, I'm starting to get a little bored.

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.text: Then perhaps you should try your hand at the Hemenster Fishing Contest.

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.player: Er, that's a bit of a random suggestion. Why would I go on a fishing contest?

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.text: We dwarves don't know much about fishing, but a couple of our brothers at White Wolf Mountain want to win the competition.

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.player: Why would they want to do that if they don't know much about fishing?

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.text: Ah, you see, the trophy is made of pure gold. And these dwarves in particular love gold.

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.player: Alright, sounds interesting, I'll check it out. White Wolf mountain, you said?

starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-without-fishing-contest-com.text: Yes, you can speak to a dwarf at either side of the mountain.

starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.player: You mean, half the world has suddenly become a sailor?

starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.text: No, not that. It's the Red Axe!

starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.player: What have those grumpy little guys done now?

starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.text: They've left the city! They were already boycotting the trade floor, but now they've completely left the city.

starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.text: It's never happened before! At the moment it's unclear yet if they've left the Consortium as well. The directors are in turmoil!

starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-out-talking-to-commander-veldab.text: Well... I may require your services again. Are you interested in hearing more?

steps.player: Very interested!

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: We need some more information about what the Red Axe is up to.

steps.player: Are you asking me to... spy on them? Isn't that treason?

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: The other directors of the Consortium don't think so and are likely to expel the Red Axe completely anyway.

steps.player: So where would you like me to go?

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: That's the problem. We don't know where they moved their headquarters to. But we may have one lead...

steps.player: Yes?

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: There is a dwarf, all the way to the northeast in Keldagrim-East. He talks about kebabs a lot. Don't suppose you've met him?

steps.player: Yes, I do believe I have. Smashed glasses, wrecked house? Poor personal hygiene standards? Brother or cousin to that other drunken dwarf?

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: That's him, poor fellow. He didn't always used to be like that.
Continues below at "But he seems to know something about the Red Axe for some odd reason."

steps.player: No, I don't believe so.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: He lives in his brother's house.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Or was it his cousin?

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: In any case, he's a bit of a drunk these days. Well, when I say a bit, he's actually smashed all the time.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: But he seems to know something about the Red Axe for some odd reason. He speaks of them sometimes in one of his many rants.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Problem is, no one believes him. Everyone thinks he's completely mad. And perhaps they're right.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: But if he does indeed know something about the Red Axe or where their headquarters may be, we need to find out.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: What do you say then, [player name]? Do you want to help the Black Guard with this?

steps.prompt: Start the Forgettable Tale... quest?

steps.player: Sounds like just the job for me!

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Excellent, good luck to you in your quest! May Guthix protect you!

A cutscene plays, showing the statue from The Giant Dwarf. "Rise of the Red Axe, Part II, Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf" appears on the screen, and the camera pans to the drunken dwarf's house. The player ends up in front of the house after the cutscene.

steps.player: Well, here I am... at the drunken dwarf's relative's residence, who is also drunken. I wonder what drunken tales he can tell me.
No, I try to stay away from drunken dwarves.
Although I wish they would try to stay away from me too...

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Very well. Come back when you change your mind.

steps.player: Some other time, perhaps.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Very well.

steps.text: The Red Axe? You want to know about them, do you? Then let me tell you my tale. It is long and quite unforgettable...

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: A long time ago, quite a while ago, yes... I resigned from my mining company, the Magenta Accordion.

steps.player: The what? The Magenta Accordion? That's not a mining company!

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: It is, it is! It's one of the many minor companies, not part of the Consortium.

steps.player: Alright, if you say so...

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: Right, so I had just left my company. I'd had enough of slaving away in the mines and decided to become an explorer. Oh yes, like my cousin.

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: I explored this old mine, you know, just south of Keldagrim. I think it's boarded up now. Some amazing things I saw there.

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: First of all...
Screen fades.

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: ...and then I nearly fell into the Abyss! But I...
Screen fades.

steps.text: ...so I had to run for my life, but then...
Screen fades.

steps.speaker: Drunken Dwarf
steps.text: ...pink dragons...
Screen fades.

I must tell you about... about...

steps.npc: I'm extremely pleased to hear that! I've always wanted an apprentice. Let me talk you through the secrets of glassblowing.

Glass is made from soda ash and silica. We get our soda ash by collecting seaweed from the rocks - the prevailing currents make the north-west corner of the island the best place to find it, it can also be found in

your nets sometimes when you're fishing, on Karamja island or at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony in the nets there. To turn seaweed into soda ash, all you need to do is burn it on a fire. Feel free to use the range in
my house for that; it's the one directly west of here. Next we collect sand from the sandpit that you'll also find just west of here, there are others located in Yanille and Shilo Village.
You'll need a bucket to carry it in. Tell you what, you can have this old one of mine.

steps.npc: Bring the sand and the soda ash back here and melt them together in the furnace, and there you have it - molten glass!

the fine art of glassblowing you can use my spare glassblowing pipe. I think I left it on the chest of drawers in my house this morning.
Alternatively I am always happy to buy the molten glass from you, saves me running about making it for myself.

steps.npc: Well, I am very busy at the moment, but I guess I can take 5 minutes off for my favourite student.

Glass is made from soda ash and silica. We get our soda ash by collecting seaweed from the rocks - the prevailing currents make the north-west corner of the island the best place to find it, it can also be found in

your nets sometimes when you're fishing, on Karamja island or at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony in the nets there. To turn seaweed into soda ash, all you need to do is burn it on a fire. Feel free to use the range in

Fritz the Glassblower: my house for that; it's the one directly west of here. Next we collect sand from the sandpit that you'll also find just west of here, there are others located in Yanille and Shilo Village.
You can use the bucket I gave you earlier.

options.condition: If the player has asked Gabooty what he does in Tai Bwo Wannai:

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Not much really... I run a local shop which earns me a few trading sticks, but that's about it. I keep myself to myself really.

steps.player: What are trading sticks?

steps.npc: They're the local currency Bwana, it's used in Tai Bwo Wannai, there's usually some odd jobs that need doing around the village which you could do to earn some trading sticks.
Or, if you have something which the local villagers might like, you could sell it to me and I'll pay you for it in trading sticks.

options.text: What sort of things do the local villagers like?

steps.player: What sort of things do the local villagers like?

steps.npc: Gnome cocktails! It's amazing but we all just love them! Luckily I've managed to get stocks of the gnome made cocktails and I supply those to my favourite customers. However, many of the customers really like the cocktails
made by the adventurers passing through this way. If you ever happen to have any, bring them my way! I'll give you a good deal on it that's for sure!

steps.player: How did the villagers ever get to try any gnome cocktails?

steps.npc: I think it was that gnome pilot who crashed his glider, perhaps he had a little mini-bar on board? Come to think about it, you'd expect the little guy to get his stuff together and move on out of here wouldn't you? He
must love the jungle to have stayed here so long!

options.text: I want to ask another question.

steps.player: You run a shop?

steps.npc: Yes, it's the Tai Bwo cooperative... catchy name huh! We sell a few local village trinkets and tools. Also, there are a few items that we're actually looking to stock for the locals' sake.
If you happen across any of them please bring them to me, I'll pay a good price for them. I'm sure you'll find the prices very reasonable.

options.text: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?

steps.player: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?

steps.npc: Sure you can...which shop would you like to see? The Cooperative or Drinks store?

steps.target: Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Drinky Store.

steps.player: None thanks...

options.text: Why do you only take one sort of Gnome cocktail?

steps.player: Why do you only take one sort of Gnome cocktail?

steps.npc: It's funny that actually. I've managed to get a good deal with the pilot of that gnome glider. He can supply me directly now. However, it's really interesting that the local villagers really like the gnome cocktails made by the
adventurers passing through this way.

steps.player: Why, what's the difference?

steps.npc: I think it may just be that they're made fresher, or there is a slight twist in the flavour of the drink, you know, a little more of this, a little less of that, it all adds up and makes for an interesting tipple!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Gabriela, I'm looking after my husband who isn't feeling too well!

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Gabriela. I'm looking after my husband who isn't feeling too well!

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

steps.npc: Welcome to the Mining Guild. My name's Gadrin and I'm the Guildmaster. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: What have you got in the guild?

steps.npc: All sorts of things! There's plenty of coal rocks along with some iron, mithril and adamantite as well.
Deeper in the guild you'll find even more rocks including some runite! The best bit though is our amethyst mine, the only one in the land!
There's no better mining site anywhere!

options.text: What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?
What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?

steps.player: What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?

steps.npc: What do you think? We smelt it into bars, smith the metal to make armour and weapons, then we exchange them for goods and services.

steps.player: I don't see many dwarves selling armour or weapons here.

steps.npc: No, this is only a mining outpost. We dwarves don't much like to settle in human cities. Most of the ore is carted off to Keldagrim, the great dwarven city. They've got a special blast furnace up there - it makes
smelting the ore so much easier. There are plenty of dwarven traders working in Keldagrim. Anyway, can I help you with anything else?
