Hi.

steps.npc: Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?

steps.player: Indeed.
Hi.

steps.npc: What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

steps.player: Nothing.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...

steps.player: Strange how?

steps.npc: Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome to the vinery. Can I help you?

steps.player: How do I farm here?

steps.npc: Let's see... First, you'll need to treat the soil with saltpetre. Dig it into the patch with a trowel. The minerals are good for the fruit.
Then plant a grape seed, and just let it grow. I'll look after it, so it won't get diseased.
When your grapes are ready, pick them and clear the patch so you can grow a new vine.
Does that seem clear, or would you like help with something else?

steps.player: What do you do?

steps.text: If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I'm the vintner. I helped Lord Hosidius to develop this land as a vinery, and now it's complete he's put me in charge of production while he works on a new project.
His son, young Pandur, works here too. Pandur checks the wine I produce. But if you've got any questions about the farming, don't ask Pandur. Ask me instead. He checks the wine too much.

steps.text: If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I'm the vintner. I helped the late Lord Hosidius develop this land as a vinery. He put me in charge of production once it was completed.
The new Lord Hosidius used to work here as well. He has new duties of course, but that hasn't stopped him coming down to check the wine I produce.
So can I help you with anything?

steps.player: Why are you called Gallow?

steps.npc: It's short for 'Gallows'. When I was young, a boy made some improper suggestions to me, so I grabbed him by his neck and held him in the air until he learnt some manners.
Now, dear, do you need help with the vinery? I'm enjoying the chat, but I have work to do.

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

treasure-trails.npc: I have a question for you.

treasure-trails.text: Gallow has given you a challenge scroll!

treasure-trails-talking-to-her-with-the-.npc: Please enter the answer to the question.

steps.npc: No, try again.
Correct!

steps.text: a medium clue scroll or medium reward casket
If the reward is another clue scroll:
Gallow has given you another clue scroll!
If the reward is a casket:
You've obtained a casket!

steps.player: Hello there. How's it going?

steps.npc: Another human? Do what you need to and then be gone from here.
Every day they let more of your kind in.
Hmph!
I don't talk to you lot.
Not interested!

standard-dialogue-man-in-leather-body.npc: I'm ruined, all because of that stupid cat! It has ruined me.
Why did it have to get itself killed? Why?

standard-dialogue-man-in-leather-body.player: Aside* I think I should leave him alone. He seems a little upset right now.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.npc: Trying to win my shirt back. I lost it last night in a silly bet.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.player: Well I hope your luck improves. I doubt it can get any worse.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.npc: Well I've little left to lose, maybe some more hair and my trousers.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.player: I really think you should try hold on to them.

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.player: I was just wondering what you were doing here?

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.npc: I ask myself the same question often.
What am I doing down here in these pits along with these filthy dregs of society?

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.player: And do you ever come up with an answer?

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.npc: I'm here taking their money, that's what.

standard-dialogue-man-with-feathered-hat.npc: Just a bit of drinking, a bit of fighting and a few people trying to win big.

standard-dialogue-man-with-feathered-hat.player: Nothing but good clean family fun.

standard-dialogue-woman-in-green.npc: Nothing much. Just keeping myself occupied, placing a couple of wagers here and there.
Yes in the sense that I'm not as bored as I was and no in terms of the number of coins in my purse.

standard-dialogue-woman-in-grey.npc: Trying to win back some money.
In every bet there is a fool and a thief and I'm beginning to think that I'm not much of a thief.

standard-dialogue-woman-with-pink-beret.npc: Having fun. It's such a blast I've already won 5 thousand gold coins today, my cat just keeps winning.

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.player: So how do these rat pits work?

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.text: If in the Ardougne rat pit:

steps.npc: Things work simply in the Ardougne ratpits.
If you have a kitten and at least 100 coins you can challenge someone else who also has a kitten and some spare change.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 5 rats first wins.

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.text: If in the Varrock rat pit:

steps.npc: It's simple.
In Varrock if you have a grown cat and a couple of coins you can challenge someone else who also has a grown cat and some spare change.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 7 rats first wins.

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.text: If in the Port Sarim rat pit:

steps.npc: The Port Sarim pits are quite fussy, no lazy cats allowed in here.

steps.player: Lazy cats?

steps.npc: You know if you neglect a wily cat, it gets fat and lazy? Well, they're not allowed to fight in here, only wily cats.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 11 rats first wins.

steps.player: That sounds vile and cruel.

steps.npc: It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Each to their own, I say.

steps.player: Thanks for your help.

options.text: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.player: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.npc: I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.

steps.player: Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?

steps.npc: Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.

steps.player: Oh that sounds quite wise.

steps.npc: That depends on how you value your cat.

steps.player: Sorry, I don't follow.

steps.npc: Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.

steps.player: Wow that sounds like fun!

steps.npc: I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.

options.text: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.player: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.npc: Hmmm... let me think. I don't think that's ever arisen but I think it's 20,000.

steps.player: Hmm, that sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.

steps.npc: You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.
There is a minimum bet of 100 coins too.

options.text: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.player: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.npc: No, not now, we don't really bet with outsiders.

steps.player: But I'm not an outsider, am I not inside in the pits now?

steps.npc: I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.

steps.player: Can it be bought?

steps.npc: What?

steps.player: Your trust.

steps.npc: No. Regular townsfolk don't like us, which leads us to distrust them and anyone else.

standard-dialogue.npc: Ello there. I'm Gamfred, the engineer in this here guild. Have you seen my catapult?

options.text: That's not a catapult, it's a large crossbow.

steps.player: That's not a catapult, it's a large crossbow.

steps.npc: WHAT!? I'll have you know that is the finest piece of dwarven engineering for miles around! How DARE you insult my work!

steps.player: Yes, beautiful piece of engineering.

steps.npc: Nice to meet someone who appreciates fine work, have you tried it out yet?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: What did you think?

steps.player: It was ok I guess.

steps.npc: Well I guess not everyone will like it.

steps.player: It was fun!

steps.npc: Glad ta hear it. Try it again sometime. We have more tests to run.

steps.player: I didn't like it.

steps.npc: Well I guess not everyone will like it. But give it another chance before you go.

options.text: May I have a shield please?

steps.player: May I have a shield please?

steps.text: If the player has a defensive shield:

steps.npc: Silly muffin, you have one already!

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.npc: I'd be happy ta give you a shield but you've no space for it.

steps.text: If the player does not have a defensive shield:

steps.npc: Of course!

steps.text: The dwarf hands you a large shield.
Defensive shield

options.text: No, how do I do that?

steps.player: No, how do I do that?

steps.npc: Well ye take the big defence shield in both hands and watch the catapult. My assistant will fire different things at you and you need to defend against them.

options.text: May I have a shield please?

steps.player: Sounds boring.

steps.npc: Your loss...

steps.player: No, where is it?

steps.npc: Are ye blind [lad/lass]? Tis over there in the next room with me assistant working it!

options.text: May I claim my tokens please?

steps.player: May I claim my tokens please?

steps.text: If the player has earned Warrior guild tokens, but has no inventory space:

steps.npc: You don't have space to carry them.

steps.text: If the player has earned Warrior guild tokens:

steps.npc: Of course! Here you go, you've earned [number] token[s]!

steps.text: Warrior guild tokens

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.text: If the player has not earned Warrior guild tokens:

steps.npc: I'm afraid you have not earned any tokens yet. Try some of the activities around the guild to earn some.

steps.player: Ok, I'll go see what I can find.
Bye!

steps.npc: Come back soon! My catapult needs more test subjects.

claim-tokens-dialogue.player: May I claim my tokens please?

claim-shield-dialogue.player: May I have a shield please?

standing-on-the-marker-without-a-shield.npc: Watch out! You'll need to equip the shield as soon as you're on the target spot else you could get hit! Speak to me to get one, and make sure both your hands are free to equip it.

steps.npc: Bring some of the heavy squad to carry the crates.
Get this right and I'll see you're well paid.
Handle the explosives carefully.
If the shopkeeper won't cooperate, kill his wife.
If the soldiers try to interfere, kill them.
Make sure the captain knows not to talk.
Our ship is due with the evening tide.
Pay attention or I'll rip your throat out.
The boxes marked with a cross are ours.
Weigh the gold carefully in case he double-crosses us.
Got it, boss.
Okay, boss.
Sure thing, boss.
We're on it, boss.
Yes, boss.
You're the boss.

before-spirits-of-the-elid.npc: And a good day to you too.

after-spirits-of-the-elid.player: How's life now the curse has been lifted?

after-spirits-of-the-elid.npc: It's been lifted? I hadn't realised. I've still been buying water from Ali the Carter!

standard-dialogue.npc: Be warned human. The Wyrms here are under my protection. I will not let you kill them unless you have permission.

when-attempting-to-kill-wyrms-outside-of.npc: Human! To attack these creatures would be a threat to the balance. Only those with permission may fight them!

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: What's going on here? I see a lot of farming patches with nothing growing in them.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: No, one has just had them installed. One has had the most marvellous idea to bring renewed happiness to one's own dearest husband.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: One? I'm not sure I understand you-

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: Oh dear - the common classes, oh how they fill one with intolerable levels of exasperation, I swear to be most true.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: Ri-ight ... if you say so, my lady. I'll be off then, if you don't mind-

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: Yes, be off with you, before I call the guards.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: No problem, sorry to have bothered you.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: Who else would I be speaking to, you funny little fool? Of course you.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: Well for a moment there I thought there was a dog around here somewhere...

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: Oh yes, sarcasm - how amusing. No, no, peasant - I have a question to ask of you, and you are required to answer.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: Well, seeing as you put it so nicely...

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: Do you know of anyone who might have some degree of horticultural experience?
If the player does not meet all of the requirements to start the quest:

steps.player: Not really.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Well, hurry off then. You are of no use to me.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Garden of Tranquillity quest.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: If the player meets all of the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh, marvellous! Peasant, I hereby order you to assist me with a little project I have planned.

steps.player: You'll have to ask me nicely first.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh, what I have to deal with these days - to think this is what being a Queen has become. Very well then: would you ... good sir help me with a little project of mine?

steps.prompt: Start the Garden of Tranquillity quest?

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh dear, what a pathetic creature you are. One would give you a list, but you do not appear to have room enough to carry it.
If the player has one free inventory space:
a List

steps.player: I would be happy to help someone who is so in touch with the people.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Ah, more sarcasm - wonderful. Well, it is nice to have a master of the fine art of gardening to assist me; in the absence of any such person, I gladly accept your service.

steps.player: I'm not sure if that's a compliment or not. Anyway, what would you like me to do, and what do I get out of it?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: To answer your first question, you have noticed the new farming patches that we have had installed around us. We wish to grow many varied and exotic plants in them, to bring happiness back to my husband.

steps.player: King Roald?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: The very same, and that's 'His Most Royal Majesty' to you. Now we come to the plants that one wishes you to grow in these patches. I would tell you all at once, but I fear that your small mind would not cope.

steps.player: Thanks, I'm sure. So tell me Queeny, how do I know which plants I am to get for you?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: I have given you a list of the items that I need in each patch. One is sure that you will know how to use the list with each patch to find out what needs to go in each one. There is one more thing, though.

steps.player: One listens with bated breath...

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Obtaining the seeds may prove difficult if you go about it by hacking and slashing everything that moves. No, to gather these items you will need to employ a finer tactic; the art of persuasion.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: You must go at once and converse with the wise old man who is said to dwell in Draynor Village; he may guide you in mastering this delicate and sophisticated ability.

steps.player: I'd rather jump off the docks at Port Sarim.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Well don't allow one to delay you - it is probably the most constructive thing you could do with your life, to be honest.

starting-off-talking-to-queen-ellamaria-.text: If the player does not have a list:

steps.player: Can I have another list?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Take better care with this one.
another List

options.text: How am I supposed to move statues all the way here?

steps.player: How am I supposed to move statues all the way here?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: You use the dormant object that lies between your ears, that's how. A statue may be far too heavy to carry, but simplicity itself to push.

steps.player: Push?

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes peasant, push. One would give you something to help with this task, but you do not appear to have room enough to carry it.
If the player has one free space:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes peasant, push. Here - take this trolley. You can use it to push the statues here.
a Trolley

options.text: What I am supposed to be getting again?

steps.player: What I am supposed to be getting again?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Haven't you got that list I gave you?
If the player does not have the list:

steps.player: Err ... no ... I seem to have lost it.

steps.text: If the player does not have one free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh dear, what a pathetic creature you are. One would give you another list, but you do not appear to have room enough to carry it.
If the player has one free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh dear, what a pathetic creature you are. Here, have another one.
another List

options.text: Will these patches need much in the way of watering?

steps.player: Will these patches need much in the way of watering?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Well, you are supposed to be the gardener here, but I would say not. One had the soil imported from an extremely fertile area at great cost - watering should not be necessary one would have thought.

starting-off-talking-to-queen-ellamaria-.text: If the player uses the list or the trolley on Queen Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Very good peasant, thank you for showing one that, but one has given you a job to do. Do it.

starting-off-inspecting-the-statue-plint.text: If the player searches the southern plinth:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: I want you to place a statue of Saradomin there.

starting-off-inspecting-the-statue-plint.text: If the player searches the northern plinth:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: I want you to place a statue of a Misthalin king there.

starting-off-inspecting-the-plantpots.text: If the player inspects the eastern plantpot:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: I want you to grow yellow orchids there.

starting-off-inspecting-the-plantpots.text: If the player inspects the western plantpot:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: I want you to grow pink orchids there.

options.text: Queen Ellamaria has sent me to seek your guidance.

steps.player: Queen Ellamaria has sent me to seek your guidance.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ellamaria? Well, if you're in her service my guidance is this: do the fastest run that you can off the shortest pier you can find.

steps.player: You know Queen Ellamaria?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh yes, we go way back, long before she married that fool the King of Varrock. She wasn't always royal you know.

steps.player: Really?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, in her youth she was a barmaid at the Blue Moon inn. All that fancy talk, that's just for show. No, the Ellamaria I knew was as common as muck, until she lucked onto good King Roald.

steps.player: I'll certainly look at her in a different light when I return to Varrock.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So what sort of guidance has Little-Miss-Hoity-Toity sent you to seek?

steps.player: I am supposed to gain some knowledge of diplomacy and persuasion from you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That is an area that - luckily for you, young [player name] - I have studied. Have you heard of the diplomat known as Charos?

steps.player: Charos? I must say the name rings a bell...
Charos...
Yes, I remember! Once, during my travels to Morytania, I came upon an item of magical jewellery called the Ring of Charos.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You have found the Ring of Charos?!? Tell me - do you still have it in your possession?
If the player is wearing the Ring of Charos:

steps.player: Yes, I'm wearing it at the moment. Is it important, then?

steps.text: If the Ring of Charos is in the player's inventory:

steps.player: Yes, I have it in my bag. Is it important, then?

steps.text: If the Ring of Charos is in the player's bank, grave, in death's office or any item retrieval service:

steps.player: Yes, I have it stored somewhere. Is it important, then?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Important?!? This ring possesses hidden power beyond belief! Go and get it, and I will tell you its secrets.
If the player is not wearing the ring or in their inventory:

steps.player: No, I'm afraid that I lost it at some point.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Lost the Ring of Charos?!? That is indeed a disastrous turn of events. This ring that you have so casually thrown away possesses hidden power beyond belief.

steps.player: How can I re-obtain the Ring of Charos?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If everything I have heard about Charos's ring is true, it will not stay lost forever. Where did you originally find it?

steps.player: I ... um ... 'borrowed' it from a rather shady character called Fenkenstrain.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: In order to find the ring it may be wise to return to Fenkenstrain - he may have found a way to regain it. If you manage to reobtain the ring, return to me and I will reveal its secrets to you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Charos rose to power under the rule of Lord Drakan of Morytania, his only living servant. The Vampyre Lord suffered the existence of Charos because of the talents that this sophisticated diplomat had to offer.

steps.player: The art of persuasion?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed. Charos had many uses - spy, assassin, negotiator - because he could convince anyone to do his wishes. These talents were in some part Charos's own, but greatly enhanced by the ring that he fashioned.

steps.player: The Ring of Charos.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Exactly. One who wears the ring must possess some innate ability of their own, which the ring enhances so that the wearer can convince all but the most strong- minded to do their bidding.

steps.player: What happened to Charos? And why did Fenkenstrain have the ring?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Charos had a castle built on the northern coast of Morytania, where he dwelt for many years in service to Drakan. None really know what became of him, but some say that he became too certain of his abilities,

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: and turned them on his master. This would have been his ultimate downfall, for the ring's power would have had little or no effect upon Drakan.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Fenkenstrain probably found the ring many years later, buried somewhere within the depths of Charos's castle.

steps.player: So what you are telling me is that nobody really knows what happened to Charos? That he could still be alive? And if he is still alive...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ...he would naturally come looking for the ring that is his by right. But I don't believe that you should worry about that - it has been many years since his disappearance, and the likelyhood is that he is dead.

steps.player: Still - it doesn't inspire me with much confidence.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I could activate the power within this ring for you, but for me to do that I must know that you will use it wisely. To do that I must ask you a few questions, to see how good a diplomat you can be.

steps.player: Okay, go ahead...

steps.text: Note that the answers are randomly shuffled; Answer A may switch to C/B if retaking the test.

1/7: Two goblins are fighting over the colour of their armour. What do you do?[A] Kill them both and steal their bronze spears.[B] Leave them to it. Armour's not going to help - any noob could take them.[C] Show them a range of colours so that they can come to a compromise.

2/7: A Drunken dwarf offers you a kebab. What do you do?[A] Take his generous gift even though you have no need for it.[B] Run away leaving the lonely dwarf on his own.[C] Stand there until he gets annoyed and attacks you.
3/7: Are you enjoying your experience of Farming?[A] Definitely.[B] Yes.[C] It's absolutely, unquestionably the most interesting thing I've ever done!

4/7: A dwarf asks you to put on a silly golden helmet so that you can be fired from a cannon into a wall. What do you do?[A] Refuse this crazy request blankly.[B] Put on the silly helmet and jump into the cannon.[C] Put the helmet on the dwarf and fire him into the wall.

5/7: You meet Pkmaster0036 in the wilderness who asks you who is the greatest player killer in the world. How do you answer?[A] Cower in fear and quickly cast teleport to Varrock.[B] You of course Pkmaster0036, no one could ever challenge your greatness![C] I am, prepare to meet your doom Pkmaster0036!

6/7: Queen Ellamaria orders you to go on a foolish quest without any offer of reward. What do you say?[A] I'll do whatever you ask - I just love the monarchy![B] Ask me nicely and I might consider it.[C] Stop ordering me about and get behind the bar where you belong!

steps.text: I wouldn't call my livelihood 'nothing' if I were you. Very well, I shall find someone else to assist me.

talking-to-bernald.text: If the player uses the plant cure on the diseased grapevines:

steps.text: You treat the diseased grapevines with plant cure ...
... but it doesn't seem to make any difference.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: Plant cure not doing the trick, eh?

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.player: I don't understand - it's worked with everything else.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: That grapevine disease must be much stronger than the usual. You'll need something a bit more potent to cut out that infection.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.player: Do you know of any stronger cures?

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: No, I don't - but I know of a man who might. Not far from here there's a druid gardener who goes by the name of Alain. He's an expert on things like this, so they tell me.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.player: Why didn't you just go and ask him yourself?

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: These vines are very precious indeed. I could not hazard the risk that someone would steal my grapes while I was away - they may be diseased, but they still contain Burthorpe Vine seeds.

options.text: I need to ask you about strong plant cures.

steps.player: I need to ask you about strong plant cures.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: Well, you have come to the right person, then - I researched exotic plant diseases as part of my druidic training. What is the affliction that you need to cure?

steps.player: Bernald up in Burthorpe has got some seriously diseased grapevines. I tried plant cure on them, but it didn't seem to have any positive effect.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: Ah, so is this the famous Burthorpe Vine?

steps.player: The very one.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: I'm afraid that my researches did not extend to Burthorpe Vine. Bernald and his ancestors have always closely guarded their heritage, that vine. In fact, I'm surprised that he has involved you.

steps.player: Er, I did have some ... assistance there.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: I see. Well, if it involves some unnatural power I would rather not know. I prefer the use of power that can be brought forth from the plants around us.

options.text: Are you sure there's nothing you can suggest?

steps.player: Are you sure there's nothing you can suggest?

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: Well...

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: There is one thing you could try. One of the most potent cures I have discovered involves using the natural power held within a very special mineral, but it is a very closely guarded secret.

steps.player: Do you mean the rune essence?

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: You know of that?!? Then I can do no further harm here. You can make a potent plant cure by mixing some crumbled rune essence into a normal plant cure. This may possibly cure Bernald's vines.

steps.player: Thank you Alain, I will try it out immediately!
You're hiding something from me.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: This is the power you are abusing!! I feel it now - it emanates from the ring you wear, a festering fountain of corruption that appalls my very soul!!!

steps.player: Oh, sorry. I forgot that it only works on the weak- minded.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: You, [player name], are the one who must be weak- minded, if you consider using such a dreadful weapon. Beware - it may one day be your downfall.

options.text: Would you look after my crops for me?
Can you give me any farming advice?

talking-to-alain-making-a-stronger-plant.text: If the player uses the pestle mortar on the rune/pure essence:

steps.text: The [rune/pure] essence is too big to grind. You might want to break it up into shards first.

talking-to-alain-making-a-stronger-plant.text: If the player uses a hammer on the rune/pure essence:

steps.text: You break up the [rune/pure] essence into shards.
some rune/pure essence shards

talking-to-alain-making-a-stronger-plant.text: If the player uses the rune/pure essence with the pestle and mortar:

steps.text: You break up the [rune/pure essence] shards into dust.
some rune dust

talking-to-alain-making-a-stronger-plant.text: If the player uses the rune dust with the plant cure:

steps.text: You mix the rune dust into the plant cure.
a stronger plant cure

talking-to-alain-talking-to-bernald-with.text: If the player has not gotten the plant cure in their inventory yet:

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: Have you spoken to Alain yet?

steps.player: Yes. He has given me some knowledge so that I can make a more potent plant cure.

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: Let's hope that it does the job, then.

talking-to-alain-talking-to-bernald-with.text: If the player uses the stronger plant cure on the vines:

steps.text: You treat the diseased grapevines with strong plant cure ...
... and they blossom with new found life!

talking-to-alain-talking-to-bernald-with.text: If the player talks to Bernald after curing the vines:

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: My vines are cured! You have worked a wonder here, [player name]! Here, you can have those seeds like I promised.
If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: I would give you some, but you don't appear to have room to carry them.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: Yes, here you go - I hope they grow for you.
Bernald gives you some Burthorpe Vine seeds.
4 Burthorpe Vine seeds

talking-to-alain-subsequent-dialogue-wit.text: If the player is missing vine seeds:

steps.player: Do you have any more Burthorpe Vine seeds?

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: What did you do with the ones I gave you?

steps.player: Erm...

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: Yes, here you go - I hope they grow for you.
Bernald gives you some Burthorpe Vine seeds.
4 Burthorpe Vine seeds

talking-to-alain-subsequent-dialogue-wit.text: If the player has the vine seeds in their inventory or bank:

steps.player: How are your grapes coming along?

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: Marvellously, thanks to your help, [player name]!

options.text: Do you know how I could grow a White Tree?

steps.player: Do you know how I could grow a White Tree?

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: There are no more White Trees left in the world - they have all been chopped down, and their beauty has forever left this world.
If the player is not wearing a Ring of Charos:

steps.player: Then my quest is over - I cannot grow a White Tree.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Even if there were a White Tree somewhere I would not tell you, for as soon as it would grow then it would be slaughtered in its prime. Man's hunger for fire is greater than his admiration of beauty.
If the player is wearing a Ring of Charos:

options.text: Then my quest is over - I cannot grow a White Tree.
[Charm] I think that there is something that you are not telling me.

steps.player: I think that there is something that you are not telling me.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Am I so transparent? You have seen through me; there is something I would rather not tell you.

options.text: You need to chill out and stop taking yourself so seriously.

steps.player: You need to chill out and stop taking yourself so seriously.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Leave me in peace then, if you are so unable to understand my grief.

options.text: [Charm] A secret is a dreadful burden to have to keep to yourself.

steps.player: A secret is a dreadful burden to have to keep to yourself.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: It is not hard to keep this secret - to give it away would cause me great sorrow.

steps.player: I don't see how. Tell me your secret, and I will keep it as well as you have done.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Very well - I feel deep trust in you for some reason. It is the White Tree, last survivor of a race of Trees that have disappeared from our landscape. Once they covered the land; now there is only one.

steps.player: What happened to them?

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Man desired the wood of the White Tree, because of its wood of pure white. Need I tell you more?

steps.player: I can fill in the rest. So where is the remaining White Tree?

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: She stands atop Ice Mountain, alone and sorrowful; and, I fear, that she is dying.

steps.player: If I took a cutting from ... her ... then I could grow another one.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Yes, but she only has life enough to produce one shoot. Cut this shoot, and she will die, last of her kind gone forever. If you failed to grow this shoot, there would be no more White Trees.

options.text: You should get out a bit more and quit worrying about trees.

steps.player: You should get out a bit more and quit worrying about trees.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: No, I am afraid I cannot do that. She is the last White Tree, and I am the last to care about her. I will not let her pass away alone and unloved.

options.text: [Charm] Unless you allow me to do this she will die anyway.

steps.player: Unless you allow me to do this she will die anyway.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: I know, but I try not to think about that. You speak truly - she does not have much time left.

steps.player: Then will you allow me to take this cutting?

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Do so with my blessing. I wish you good fortune, [player name]. Go now, and save the beauty of the White Tree.

options.text: Would you look after my crops for me?
Can you give me any farming advice?

talking-to-dantaera-getting-the-white-tr.text: If this is the first time the player cuts down the shoot:

steps.player: Here is the shoot that Dantaera spoke of. Everything she told me is true – this tree will die once I cut this shoot. Well, here goes...

steps.text: The player uses the secateurs from their inventory and cuts a shoot.
You cut a shoot from the White Tree.
a White tree shoot

talking-to-dantaera-getting-the-white-tr.text: If the player attempts to cut down the White tree after receiving a shoot in their inventory:

steps.player: I have already cut the shoot from the White Tree. I should quickly grow a new tree in Queen Ellamaria's garden.

talking-to-dantaera-getting-the-white-tr.text: If there are other subsequent attempts after losing the shoot:

steps.player: Ah, luckily there is another shoot here that I can cut. Better not lose this one...

talking-to-dantaera-getting-the-white-tr.text: If the player gets the white tree shoot and loses it after:

steps.player: I have lost the cutting from the White Tree.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: I do not believe what I am hearing, after everything you said to me before!

steps.player: Er, yes I know ... sorry ...

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Maybe - just maybe - there might be another shoot somewhere on the Tree that you can take as a cutting. Go and havea  look, before she dies without offspring!

talking-to-dantaera-getting-the-white-tr.text: If the player has the white tree shoot in their inventory without planting it:

steps.text: Shows general Farming dialogue.

talking-to-brother-althric.text: If the player talks to him without the Ring of Charos:

steps.player: Can I have some rosebush seeds, please?

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: No, I think not. These bushes are my pride and joy, and I will not give them away so cheaply.

talking-to-brother-althric.text: If the player talks to him whilst wearing the ring:

options.text: Can I have some rosebush seeds, please?
[Charm] These are the most beautiful rosebushes I've ever seen.

steps.player: These are the most beautiful rosebushes I've ever seen.

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Nice of you to say so, but I sense the use of some unnatural power underneath your fine words. You are concealing something of great evil, an evil that cannot touch someone of my purity.

steps.player: Oh ... no, that's not true ...

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Nonsense, you reek of this evil power! I suggest that you throw whatever dark talisman it is that you are using down the Edgeville well, and never think of it again! Either that or just simply destroy it!

talking-to-brother-althric-the-edgeville.text: If the player uses the ring on the well without talking to Brother Althric:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

talking-to-brother-althric-the-edgeville.text: If the player uses the fishing rod on the well without throwing the ring in first:

steps.player: Fish in a well? There can't be anything down there except water!! Perhaps I should try some place where I might expect to find fish - a fishing spot maybe?

talking-to-brother-althric-the-edgeville.text: If the player uses the ring on the well:

steps.text: You throw the Ring of Charos down the well.
You hear a splash from far below.

talking-to-brother-althric-the-edgeville.text: If the player uses the oily fishing rod or barbarian rod on the well:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

talking-to-brother-althric-the-edgeville.text: If the player uses the fishing rod (or the oily version) on the well:

steps.text: You cast out your line into the well...
The hook catches onto something...
The player will occasionally sing...

steps.player: la-de-da
dum-de-dum
Nice day for it.
(whistles a happy tune)

steps.text: If the player is successful:
... and you retrieve the Ring of Charos.
If the player is unsuccessful:
...but it drops back into the water with a splash.

talking-to-brother-althric-talking-to-br.text: If the player did or did not throw the ring in the well:

steps.player: Very nice rosebushes you have here.

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Yes, it has taken me many long hours in this garden to bring them to this state of near-perfection.

talking-to-brother-althric-talking-to-br.text: If the player attempts to pick some seeds whilst still having the ring:

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Are you messing about with my rosebushes again?

steps.player: Er ... no ... I was just admiring them.

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Nonsense, you reek of this evil power! I suggest that you throw whatever dark talisman it is that you are using down the Edgeville well, and never think of it again! Either that or just simply destroy it!

talking-to-brother-althric-talking-to-br.text: If the player attempts to pick some seeds after throwing the ring in the well:

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Are you messing about with my rosebushes again?

steps.player: Er ... no ... I was just admiring them.

steps.speaker: Brother Althric
steps.text: Ah, I sense that you speak so without the use of the evil power you carried before. That is good. As you have taken the road back towards the light, you may take any seeds that you wish.

talking-to-brother-althric-talking-to-br.text: If the player takes some seeds from the red bush:

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:
You don't have enough inventory space to do that.
If the player has enough inventory space:
You take some seeds from the pink rosebush.
4 Pink rose seeds

talking-to-brother-althric-talking-to-br.text: If the player takes some seeds from the white bush:

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:
If the player has enough inventory space:
You take some seeds from the white rosebush.
4 White rose seeds

talking-to-brother-althric-talking-to-br.text: If the player takes some seeds from the pink bush:

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:
If the player has enough inventory space:
You take some seeds from the yellow rosebush.
4 Pink rose seeds

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player uses the trolley on the statue of Saradomin north of Falador:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player uses the trolley on the statue of Saradomin at the centre of Falador:

steps.text: A cutscene starts with two Falador guards...

steps.player: (Hmmm ... better not let those guards see me...)

steps.text: Meanwhile, Billy - a new recruit of the Falador Guard - has just arrived for his first shift, guarding the Northern Falador gates...

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: So what are you doing this weekend?

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: This weekend?

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: You haven't been here long I take it.

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: Do you know the life expectancy of a Falador guard?

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: No...

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: About thirty seconds, I reckon.

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: Thirty seconds???

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: They didn't tell me that when I signed up!!!

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: Any second now someone is going to try and kill us, for no apparent reason, completely unprovoked.

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: But why, Bob???

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: What have we ever done to them?

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: I don't know, Billy.

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: But I'm not wasting my final seconds worrying about it.
Meanwhile...

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: Uh-oh, someone's coming...

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: Bob???

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: Steady, Billy - remember you are a guard of Falador.

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: But...
Note: Due to a bug, the following part of the cutscene does not occur:

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: See you in the next world...
PKMaster0036 walks up to Bob and attacks him, instantly killing him.

steps.speaker: Bob, another guard of Falador
steps.text: Aaarrrgghhh!!!!

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: NOOOOO!!!!!!!!!

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: Why are you doing this?!?
PKMaster0036 then walks up to Billy and attacks him, instantly killing him.

steps.speaker: Billy, a guard of Falador
steps.text: Aaarrrgghhh!!!!
The camera pans out, showing the northern Falador entrance being unguarded as PKMaster0036 buries the bones of the guards and walks into the city.

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player pushes the trolley:

steps.text: If nothing is blocking the trolley:
The trolley moves one square away from the player.
If something is blocking the trolley:
The statue doesn't move.

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player pulls the trolley:

steps.text: If nothing is blocking the trolley:
The player pulls the trolley one square back towards the player's direction.
If something is blocking the trolley:
The statue doesn't move.

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player pushes big on the trolley:

steps.text: If nothing is in the way:
The trolley moves 4 spaces away from the player.
If something is blocking the trolley:
The statue doesn't move.

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player takes longer than two minutes to push the trolley:

steps.text: The guards have recaptured the statue of Saradomin, and placed it back in Falador.
The guards also take the player's trolley.

pushing-the-statues-statue-of-saradomin-.text: If the player pushes/pulls the trolley toward the northern Falador gates:

steps.text: Much huffing and panting later...
The player finally pushes the statue to the back of Varrock Castle.
If the player takes too long to push/pull the trolley from the back of the Castle to Ellamaria's garden:
The guards have recaptured the state of Saradomin, and placed it back in Falador.
If the player attempts to place the statue more than one square from a plinth:
You need to move the trolley next to a plinth before you can place the statue - it's too heavy to carry very far.
If the player attempts to place the statue on the incorrect plinth:
This statue needs to go on the other plinth.
If the player attempts to place the statue on the correct plinth:
You place the state of Saradomin on the plinth.
back the Trolley

pushing-the-statues-lumbridge-king.text: If the player attempts to use the trolley on the Queen statue:

steps.player: I'm supposed to be getting a statue of a KING from Lumbridge. I'm no expert, but that looks like a QUEEN to me.

pushing-the-statues-lumbridge-king.text: If the player attempts to use the trolley on the King statue:

steps.text: All of the (big) push, pull, and place mechanics are identical as mentioned above.

pushing-the-statues-lumbridge-king.text: If the player attempts to place the statue more than one square from a plinth:

steps.text: You need to move the trolley next to a plinth before you can place the statue - it's too heavy to carry very far.

pushing-the-statues-lumbridge-king.text: If the player attempts to place the statue on the incorrect plinth:

steps.text: This statue needs to go on the other plinth.

pushing-the-statues-lumbridge-king.text: If the player attempts to place the statue on the correct plinth:

steps.text: You place the statue of the king on a plinth.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the white tree sapling on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Very good peasant, thank you for showing one that, but one has given you a job to do. Do it.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the delphinium seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's delphiniums that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the delphinium patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses either the pink or yellow orchid seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's orchids that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the orchid patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the vine seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's Burthorpe vine that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the Burthorpe vine patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the red/white/yellow rose seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's a [red/white/yellow] rosebush that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the [red/white/yellow] rosebush patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the snowdrop seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's snowdrops that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the snowdrop patch, and let it grow.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player plants the seeds in the correct patch:

steps.text: You plant [3-4] seeds in the [grapevine/delphinium/snowdrop/[white/red/yellow] rosebush/white tree] patch.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player plants the seeds in the wrong patch:

steps.text: You can only plant those in the Varrock Palace garden.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use a watering can on the patches:

steps.text: These don't really need watering - the soil seems to be extremely fertile.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use regular/super/ultracompost on the patches:

steps.text: This patch doesn't really need treating with compost - the soil seems to be extremely fertile.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use a spade on a planted patch:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Hey, why are you digging that up? Leave it alone!

steps.player: Oh, sorry, didn't mean to...

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use a soil-filled plant pot on the plantpot:

steps.text: You need to fill it with compost rather than soil.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use the seeds on the plantpot before adding compost first:

steps.text: This plantpot needs some compost in it first.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use the wrong seeds on the plantpots:

steps.text: These seeds need to be planted in the other plantpot.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: One finds that hard to believe. Out of my way, let me see for myself.
If a patch hasn't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: One was right not to trust your word, common as it is. The garden is not yet complete.

steps.player: Really? What haven't I finished yet?

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: I see that the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If two patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Also, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If three patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Thirdly, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If four patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh look, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If five patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: To add to that, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If six patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: And what a surprise, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If seven patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh you are doing so well, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If eight patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: To add insult to injury, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If nine patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: And finally, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: One suggest you learn a little patience. These plants should not take long to grow - these patches have been filled with extremely fertile soil that was very expensive to import.

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh yes, very nice, if a little yobbish. Rollie will be so pleased–

steps.player: Rollie?!?

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: You will address my husband by his proper title!!!!! Speaking of whom, I think it is time that we brought him to see his new garden. And when one says we, one means you.

steps.player: Oh, you want me to go and get Roald – sorry ... King Roald ... and bring him here. Fair enough, wait here then, I'll be back in a mo.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: So are you going to get Rollie then?

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.player: No, I haven't spoken to Roll ... King Roald ... yet.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: Well hurry along peasant. This garden will be such a wonderful surprise!

talking-to-king-roald.speaker: King Roald
talking-to-king-roald.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

options.text: Would you like to follow me for a minute?

steps.player: Would you like to follow me for a minute?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Follow you?!? I am the King! I am the followed, not the follower!!
If the player is not wearing the Ring of Charos:

steps.player: Well, if you can't be bothered then neither can I.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.player: No, you suit yourself.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You're quite argumentative for a peasant.

steps.player: I'm not the one who's arguing, you are.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Then why do you keep answering me back?

steps.player: No, you're answering me back.
Well, stop talking and I'll stop answering.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: No, you stop talking.

steps.player: I have stopped talking.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: No you haven't, you're doing it now.

steps.player: No, I'm just answering what you're saying.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Okay, so if I don't say anything, you won't answer me back.

steps.player: Suits me.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Go on, then.

steps.player: No, you first.

steps.text: King Roald doesn't say anything to you.
You don't say anything back.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: See, that's better.

steps.player: Yes, much better.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: What were you saying about me following you somewhere?

steps.player: I can't remember, it was such a long time ago.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Ah, that's a shame - I could have done with a breath of fresh air.

steps.player: Oh well.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, never mind.

steps.player: See you around.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, see you later.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I thought you were going.

steps.player: I was until you spoke to me again.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'll stop speaking to you then.

steps.player: See you around.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, see you later.
If the player is wearing the Ring of Charos:

options.text: Well, if you can't be bothered then neither can I.
[Charm] Of course, your majesty - please forgive me.

steps.player: Of course, your majesty - please forgive me.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Forgiveness is something that cannot be earned so easily. And I'm certainly not following you off on some wild goose chase when I have important matters of state to attend to.

options.text: That's it - I've had it with royalty.

steps.player: That's it - I've had it with royalty.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: And I've had enough of peasantry! Get out of my castle!

options.text: [Charm] The Queen asked me to bring you.

steps.player: The Queen asked me to bring you.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Ellie?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Now that's a different matter. Lead on, peasant - let's see what my darling wife has been up to now.

steps.player: Not really.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You will have to excuse me then. I am very busy as I have a kingdom to run!

the-garden-of-tranquillity.speaker: Queen Ellamaria

the-garden-of-tranquillity.text: Well? Are you going to thank one, Rollie?

the-garden-of-tranquillity.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
the-garden-of-tranquillity.text: Much better. Now get back to the castle and rule our kingdom.

the-garden-of-tranquillity.speaker: King Roald
the-garden-of-tranquillity.text: Yes pumpkin.

the-garden-of-tranquillity.speaker: Queen Ellamaria

the-garden-of-tranquillity.speaker: Queen Ellamaria

steps.npc: Hello there. Don't see many people around here. The name's Garl.

steps.player: Hey. What are you doing here?

steps.npc: Exploring. Until that Nomad chap opened things up, this island was abandoned. Who knows what could be hiding here.

steps.player: Found anything good so far?

steps.npc: Well there's a dungeon on the east side of the island. I haven't gone too far in though. There's also a tower to the north west, near my camp.
There's no shortage of resources either. Though there's not really any way to process them. I tried to build a spinning wheel and a pottery wheel myself, but they broke.

steps.player: You could really live off the land here. I can think of worse places to do so.

steps.npc: Indeed. It's all very peaceful. And yet...

steps.player: What is it?

steps.npc: I don't know. Something just seems amiss. There's something sinister about this place. I just don't really know what.

steps.player: I'm sure it's nothing.

steps.npc: You're probably right. Anyway, I'll let you get on. All the best.
Hello there.

options.text: Can you tell me about this castle?

steps.player: Can you tell me about this castle?

steps.npc: It's called Ver Sinhaza. They say it was once the home of a Saradominist queen. Now it belongs to Verzik Vitur, a vampyre noble.
Beneath the castle you'll find the Theatre of Blood. Every day, citizens of Meiyerditch take on various challenges set up by Verzik, all the provide entertainment for the vampyres.
The citizens don't need to be forced though. Anyone who survives the Theatre is promised freedom from the vampyres. It provides a little bit of hope in this dark place.

options.text: Do you know anything about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know anything about the Myreque?

steps.text: Before completing Sins of the Father:

steps.npc: I do. I'd rather not talk about them though. Those kinds of conversations get you in trouble.
Old Man Ral might be willing to talk to you about them though. He lives in sector one of Meiyerditch, directly west of here.

steps.text: After completing Sins of the Father:

steps.npc: There's no such thing. You'd do well not to mention that name around here again.

options.text: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.npc: Yep, that's where we are at the moment. The region is split into two cities, Meiyerditch in the south and Darkmeyer in the north.
Meiyerditch is just one large ghetto. The city is split into sectors so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill everyone off in one go.
Darkmeyer is the vampyre capital. Humans aren't allowed there unless they're a personal slave of some lord or lady. They say the vampyres there live very luxurious lifestyles.

options.text: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.player: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.npc: Not much really. There seems to be three main types, juveniles, juvinates and vyres.
Juveniles seem to be the lowest form of the vampyre. No one around here knows for sure but the general consensus is that they're former humans who've been converted in some way.
Juvinates are initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to gain some powers.
Then you have the vyres. Very nasty and very powerful. I wouldn't get on the wrong side of one if I were you.

options.text: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.player: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.npc: No one had seen anything of him for years. They say he's back now though. But we shouldn't talk of him. The vyrewatch might not like it.

steps.player: I need to get going.

steps.npc: Hello. What do you want?

steps.player: Can I go in there?

steps.npc: No. In there is private.

steps.player: I want for nothing!

Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: I am Gelin, the greatest assassin ever to train in Al Kharid. If you have not heard of me, that is because my victims never live to speak of me.
In my years as a warrior of fortune, I have fought in many lands, meeting fighters of all calibres, and I found they all had something in common:
Every single one had a soul-gripping fear that they would suffer a humiliating defeat at the hands of their foes.
They did not fear the pain, you understand. They feared the diminishment that comes with defeat.

steps.player: Diminishment?

steps.npc: To see one's wealth in the hands of another. To see one's skills decrease, as the hard-earned experience is lost. That is what they all feared.
Thus I was inspired to create this life insurance brokerage. I can protect your Hitpoints experience, so that you will not lose so much of it when you are defeated.
I cannot protect other skills, and I have no intention whatsoever of protecting anyone's items - a victor deserves their spoils.

options.text: Why do you sell life insurance in a graveyard?

steps.player: Why do you sell life insurance in a graveyard?

steps.npc: There is no more fitting place! The graves of the dead remind the living that their lives are fragile, and that death is the inescapable fate of all mortals.
That is exactly the frame of mind that encourages people to buy life insurance from me.

options.text: Can I ever get a refund on this insurance?

steps.player: Can I ever get a refund on this insurance?

steps.npc: No, my life insurance policies are for life. Similarly, when a customer upgrades their policy to a better one, I charge the full price of the new policy. They may take it or leave it.

I like to think of myself more as an evil and scary sort of genie, who people talk about in hushed and fearful tones.

steps.npc: Two reasons really. Firstly, I can see in the dark, so light or dark makes little difference to me.

steps.npc: Why do I get the sense that I'm not being taken seriously here? Please try to remember I am very dangerous and not to be trifled with.

first-interaction.text: If the player has never trapped goats before:

steps.npc: Ah, what'm'ah gonna do with these damn goats...

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.npc: Hrm... ye are an outsider... but ye do have a look about ye. Tell me, d'y'ave experience herdin' goats?

steps.text: If the player has not yet completed Sheep Herder:

steps.player: Uh... no?

steps.npc: Ah, a damn shame. If ye get some experience under yer belt, come back, but these goats aren't for the weak handed.

steps.text: You need to have completed the Sheep Herder quest to hunt goats.
If the player has completed Sheep Herder:

steps.player: I have experience herding sheep, if that counts for anything?

steps.npc: Aye? Well, I s'pose I should take what I can get. Feel like helpin' out with the goat problem?

steps.player: How can goats be a problem?

steps.npc: When there's too bleedin' many of 'em!

As yer can see, on this hill, there's a... large goat herd. We think the wyrms used to eat 'em and keep the numbers down, but since we moved in, we think they've just kept spawnin' and... well, you can see what happens.
Best plan o' action we came up with is the goat pit. It ain't pretty, but the goats are dumb enough for it t'work.

steps.player: So how does goat herding come into this?

steps.npc: You herd the goats into the pit and they're dumb enough t' jump right in.
There's a pile o' spikes right 'ere. You'll wanna grab yerself a set of them and line the pit with 'em first.
The other pile 'ere is a bunch o' cattleprods. You can use one of them, or if ye fancy yerself one of them mages, me pal Jeff reckons ye might be able to pull 'em around wit' a spell or two.
Telly knee rectric grab? Dark le hure? I don't remember. If those names mean anything to ye, don't tell me. I'm better off not knowing.

steps.player: So I just prod the goats into the pit?

steps.npc: Aye, but the pit can only hold so many goats at a time. I reckon ye could fit more in if ye get better at animal handlin', but ye'd need to inspect the pit to tell, I reckon.
Once ye've got goats in t'pit, ye'll need t'sort out the carcasses. Feel free t'keep any horns or fur ye can salvage. Just remember t'line the pit with spikes again once yer done.

steps.player: So, line the pit with spikes, herd the goats into the pit, sort the carcasses and repeat. Got it, thank you!

steps.npc: Aye, ye could reduce me speech into a single line, ye bloody outsider...

first-interaction.text: If the player has trapped goats before first speaking to Geoff:

steps.npc: Have ye been pittin me goats without permission?!

steps.player: Sorry, I didn't realise that I-

steps.npc: Ha! I'm just pullin' yer leg, outsider. Ye've got nothin' t'worry 'bout!
Glad t'see ye've figured out how t'use the pit, at least. If ye need help with anythin' else, we can talk later, else I'll leave ye to it.

subsequent-conversations.player: What am I meant to be doing here?

subsequent-conversations.npc: Ye wanna grab a set of spikes from this pile o'er 'ere and line the pit wit' 'em.
Then take a prod and shove the goats in t'pit. Me pal reckons you could use a 'telly knee rectric grab' or a 'dark le hure' to do it, but I don't go fer that magic nonsense.
Ye can probably fit more goats in t'pit if ye get better at herdin' animals, but eventually it'll get full regardless.
Once it is, ye'll need to sort the carcasses. Ye can keep any furs or horns ye salvage as ye clear 'em out. Then ye can just re-line the pit and keep at it.

steps.npc: Can I help you?

options.text: What can you tell me about the people here?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the people here?

steps.npc: Let's see... We currently have Herman & Franklin Caranos, Arnold Lydspor, Devin Mendelberg and Ramara du Croissant. And me, of course.

Herman and Franklin are brothers, as you'll know. Herman's always been a fishing nut. Franklin's not all that bothered about fishing, but he does like tinkering with machinery. They're originally from East Ardougne.
Arnold's a bit more of a mystery. We think he might be from one of the barbarian tribes, but he never talks about that. He's always up for a chat, if you can understand his accent.
Devin Mendelberg comes from some town in Morytania - ghastly place! I'm not surprised he moved about as far west as he could go! He helps Franklin with the machinery, among other things.

Ramara's another Ardougnian. Her father's a baker there, but she didn't want to spend her whole life baking and doing his accounts. Also, you probably know what Ardougne's crime rate is like - it can't be easy running
a market stall in that city! I went there once, and some wannabe adventurer started following me around trying to pick my pockets! I kept hitting him, but he kept coming back again and again!

steps.player: You haven't told me about yourself yet.

steps.npc: Oh, I used to work with my sister, Emily, in the Rising Sun in Falador, but I wanted an outdoor job. The pay's better out here too, and the work's not too bad.

options.text: What is there for me to do here?

steps.player: What is there for me to do here?

steps.npc: You can fish! But I'd be very glad if you could go and do something about the skeletal magi in the dormitories. They've kept appearing there ever since the trolls left.
Also, if you're into glassbowing, you'll probably want a bit of seaweed. It catches in our nets all the time, so you'll usually find some in the machinery down by the shore.

steps.player: Thanks.
No thanks, I'm fine.

steps.npc: Ok, but come and talk to me anytime.
If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...

steps.player: Strange how?

steps.npc: Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

before-waterfall-quest.npc: Good day to you traveller, are you here to fish or just looking around? I've caught some beauties down here.
The last one was this big!

after-learning-about-the-treasure-during.npc: Hello traveller. Are you here to fish or to hunt for treasure?
Adventurers pass through here every week, they never find anything though.

For completely charting the Unquiet Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a burned key?
For completely charting the Shrouded Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a weird black orb?
For completely charting the Ardent Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a bedsheet?

steps.player: ... What am I meant to do with these?

steps.npc: I'm not sure, but you seem like a smart person. I'm sure you'll figure something out.

options.text: Do you have any spare trinkets?

steps.npc: Well, I do have plenty of trinkets, but I suspect you've gotten all the use out of anything I could give you.

steps.text: If the player is missing any items they haven't used to get paint:

steps.npc: Of course!

steps.text: Gerardus hands you another book about lighthouses. You get the feeling he might have had too many of them in the first place.

steps.player: What's in it for me?

steps.npc: Well, over the years, while out mapping the world, I have amassed a collection of.... rare and valuable items.
My maps are now only a few seas from completion. If you're able to help me, I will make sure you are well rewarded for your troubles. So, what do you say?

steps.player: No, goodbye.

steps.npc: Oh.

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome! You can buy fishing equipment at my store. We'll also buy anything you catch off you.

options.text: Let's see what you've got then.
