finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.text: Hello. How's it going? Any luck?

finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.speaker: Gertrude
finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.text: Well well, you are clever! Did you bring her back?

finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.player: Well, that's the thing, she refuses to leave.

finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.speaker: Gertrude
finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.text: Oh dear, oh dear! Maybe she's just hungry. She loves doogle sardines but I'm all out.

finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.speaker: Gertrude
finding-fluffs-talking-to-gertrude-again.text: Yes, raw sardines seasoned with doogle leaves. Unfortunately I've used all my doogle leaves, but you may find some in the woods out back.

making-seasoned-sardines.text: You rub the doogle leaves all over the sardines.

making-seasoned-sardines-pick-up-fluffs.text: The cat seems afraid to leave. In the distance you can hear kittens mewing...

making-seasoned-sardines-talking-to-gert.speaker: Gertrude
making-seasoned-sardines-talking-to-gert.text: Hey traveller, did Fluffs eat the sardines?

making-seasoned-sardines-talking-to-gert.player: Yeah, she loved them, but she still won't leave.

making-seasoned-sardines-talking-to-gert.speaker: Gertrude
making-seasoned-sardines-talking-to-gert.text: Well that is strange, there must be a reason.

making-seasoned-sardines-searching-crate.text: You find a kitten! You carefully place it in your backpack.

making-seasoned-sardines-returning-the-k.text: Fluffs has run off home with her offsping.

finishing-up.player: Hello Gertrude. Fluffs ran off with her kitten.

finishing-up.speaker: Gertrude
finishing-up.text: You're back! Thank you! Thank you! Fluffs just came back! I think she was just upset as she couldn't find her kitten.
Gertrude gives you a hug

finishing-up.speaker: Gertrude
finishing-up.text: If you hadn't found her kitten it would have died out there!

finishing-up.player: That's okay, I like to do my bit.

finishing-up.speaker: Gertrude
finishing-up.text: I don't know how to thank you. I have no real material possessions. I do have kittens! I can only really look after one.

finishing-up.player: Well, if it needs a home.

finishing-up.speaker: Gertrude
finishing-up.text: I would sell it to my cousin in West Ardougne. I hear there's a rat epidemic there. But it's too far.

finishing-up.speaker: Gertrude
finishing-up.text: Here you go, look after her and thank you again!

finishing-up.speaker: Gertrude
finishing-up.text: Oh by the way, the kitten can live in your backpack, but to make it grow you must take it out and feed and stroke it often.
Gertrude gives you a kitten.
kitten
...and some food!
Congratulations! Quest complete!

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.npc: Purrrrr! So you can talk to cats now?

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.player: Yes, I got this amulet from a Sphinx.

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.npc: Well, I should thank you for finding my kitten that time. I have a terrible time keeping track of them, and I never know how many Gertrude has managed to sell.

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.text: The player's cat is removed from the inventory and begins to follow the player

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.npc: Is [player name] looking after you well?
Good, good. That's what I like to hear.
Purrrrr! So you can talk to cats now?

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.player: Yes, I got this amulet from a Sphinx.

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.npc: Well, I should thank you for finding my kitten that time. I have a terrible time keeping track of them, and I never know how many Gertrude has managed to sell.

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.player: They're cute little creatures, aren't they?

standard-dialogue-in-the-lumberyard-afte.npc: My children have always been popular with adventurers. They inherit their father's adventurous spirit. He's always travelling the world, when he can find some kind person to help him open doors!

standard-dialogue-in-varrock-ratpits-wit.player: Well seeing as I've had to go off and fetch you for Gertrude already...

standard-dialogue-in-varrock-ratpits-wit.npc: Oh would you ever quit worrying, I come down here to watch the fights all the time.
Oh yes, it's a great place for catching a bit of tail.

standard-dialogue-in-varrock-ratpits-wit.player: Ummm, ok. I'll leave you to it then.

steps.npc: Can I help you at all?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?

steps.player: No thanks.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.text: The name's Gordon. Good day to you.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.player: It's a nice farm you've got here.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.text: Thank you. We built it ourselves.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.player: Really? So you haven't been here long?

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.text: Nope. Not too long ago you couldn't safely travel around these parts. Too many lizardmen. But then some Hosidius explorers discovered how fertile this land was.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.text: Lord Hosidius made a deal with Lord Shayzien and the lizardmen were cleared out to make room for the Farming Guild.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon.text: When we heard, we decided to come up here and start up our own farm.

steps.player: Need a hand with anything?

steps.text: If the player does not have the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: I think we're good. Thank you for the offer though.
If the player has the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: Well actually, there is something we've been having a problem with.

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: Recently, some strange beast has been stealing our livestock at night. The soldiers are too busy dealing with the lizardmen to help, so we haven't been able to stop it.

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: You look like you know your way around a weapon. If you can kill the beast and bring me its head as proof, I'll ensure you are compensated for your trouble.

steps.prompt: Start the Getting Ahead quest?

steps.player: Bring back the head? I can do that. I'm good at killing things. Do you know where the beast is?

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: Well it can't be living too far from here, but I don't know exactly where. You might want to check with my wife, Mary. Perhaps she's seen something I haven't.

steps.player: Very well. I'll return once I have the head of this beast!
Not something I can help with I'm afraid. Good luck though.

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: I understand. I'm sure someone else will be able to help.

options.text: Very nice. Well I hope it goes well for you.

steps.player: Very nice. Well I hope it goes well for you.

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: Thank you friend. See you later.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.text: Hello there. Not too bad, thanks.

options.text: Great to hear. All the best.

steps.player: Great to hear. All the best.

steps.speaker: Gordon
steps.text: Thank you friend. See you later.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.text: Hello again. Any luck finding that beast?

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.player: I've been trying, but I haven't made much progress yet.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-talkin.text: Well it can't be living too far from here. You might want to check with my wife, Mary. Perhaps she's seen something I haven't.

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.player: I'm [player name]. Your husband told me that some beast has been causing you both trouble. I've agreed to kill it and bring back its head!

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.text: Ah, that's good to hear. We've already lost a lot of livestock to it.

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.player: Well fear not. I'm sure I'll make short work of it. I do have one issue, however.
I don't yet know where to find this beast. I was wondering if you'd seen anything?

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.text: I'm afraid not. It only ever comes in the night, so we haven't been able to get a proper look at it.

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.text: Oh! I have an idea! If this beast ended up getting coated in flour, it wouldn't be hard for you to track it back to its home.

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.player: But how would I get it coated in flour?

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.text: Oh come on now! You're the adventurer here! Why don't you use your head?

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.player: Use my head? Wait... Did you just...?

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary.text: I don't know what you mean.

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary-talking-.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary-talking-.text: Hello there. How goes the headhunt?

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary-talking-.player: I'm still trying to come up with a way to cover the beast in flour.

a-strange-event-talking-to-mary-talking-.speaker: Mary
a-strange-event-talking-to-mary-talking-.text: Well I'm sure you'll think of something. Just remember to use your head.

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.player: Hello. Do you know anything about the beast causing trouble around here?

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.speaker: Sergeant
a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.text: The farmers mentioned it. We haven't seen anything though. Our focus is on the lizardmen.

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.player: Surely you'd notice a big beast wondering around though?

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.speaker: Sergeant
a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.text: The farmers said it came at night. We're not on shift then.

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.player: But then who's guarding the farm at night?

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.speaker: Sergeant
a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.text: That's not our problem. We're just here to follow orders.

a-strange-event-talking-to-the-sergeant.player: Fine. I'll find the beast myself.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Hello again. Any luck finding that beast?

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-after-.player: I've been trying, but I haven't made much progress yet.
Just one question. You said this beast has been going for your livestock. Which animals has it been targeting?

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: It's mainly been going for the cattle. I fixed up a new gate which has kept it out the past couple of nights. Not sure how long it will hold though.

a-strange-event-talking-to-gordon-after-.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

a-strange-event-pouring-the-flour-on-the.text: You pour some flour over the gate.

a-strange-event-pouring-the-flour-on-the.player: There we go. Anything that touches this gate will end up coated in flour. Now just to wait for the beast to come...

a-strange-event-pouring-the-flour-on-the.text: You head off for the night and come back the next day.

a-strange-event-pouring-the-flour-on-the.player: Looks like the beast tried to get in again. Now to see if the flour plan worked...

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Hello again. Any luck finding that beast?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.player: Your wife gave me a good idea to help track it down. I'll have its head soon enough!

a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-po.speaker: Mary
a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-po.text: Hello there. How goes the headhunt?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-po.player: The flour idea worked great. Now I just need to find the beast's home.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-po.speaker: Mary
a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-po.text: Well keep your head up. I'm sure you'll manage it.

a-strange-beast-upon-killing-the-headles.player: Ah... a headless beast. Can't really bring back the head if there isn't one. Let's hope Gordon is still happy to reward me...

a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-ki.speaker: Mary
a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-ki.text: Hello there. How goes the headhunt?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-ki.player: I've run into a little issue. The beast is dead, but it didn't have a head.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-ki.speaker: Mary
a-strange-beast-talking-to-mary-after-ki.text: Oh dear. You should probably talk to Gordon about this.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Hello again. Any luck finding that beast?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Wonderful! Do you have the head?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.player: So it didn't actually have a head.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: I'm sorry, but no. I agreed to pay you for a head and you don't have one.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.player: Well actually I do have a head. Quite a good looking one in fact. It was the beast that didn't.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: That's not what I meant. Look, it's nothing personal, but I can't be seen paying someone if they didn't do the job.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.player: But I did the job... How am I meant to bring you the head of a beast with no head?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Maybe you killed the wrong beast? It doesn't make sense that a headless beast would be taking cattle. How would it eat them?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Well if you manage to get hold of the beast's head, let me know. Until then, I can't pay you.

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Hello again. Do you have the head of that beast yet?

a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-talking-to-gordon-after-.text: Well I can't pay you if you don't have the head.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.text: You show the journal to Gordon.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.player: I don't have the head of the beast. I do have proof it was headless though.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.text: Proof? This doesn't seem like proof to me. Anyone could have written this. Maybe you wrote it?

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.player: You assume I can read and write.
Well.. yes. I promise I didn't write this though.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-ne.text: Well you would say that. I'm sorry but I'm not having this. Come back when you have the head of the beast.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.text: You show the bones to Gordon.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.player: I don't have the head of the beast. I do have the bones though!

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.text: Bones? I don't want bones! I want the beast's head!

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.player: Have you considered that you might be being too picky?

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-bi.text: Of course not! Besides, these bones could be from anywhere.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.text: You show the ensouled head to Gordon.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof!
This is literally the head of a dead bear. What is wrong with you?

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.text: I can see this is the head of a bear! This beast we're dealing with is more than a mere bear though!

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.player: What? You said you'd never seen the beast! How do you know it wasn't just a bear?

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-en.text: We've dealt with bears before! This is clearly something more! Now, go and find the real beast!

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.text: You show the fake bearhead to Gordon.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof!

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.text: What? But this is clearly just part of a costume!

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.player: Maybe it didn't have any brains.

a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-beast-using-items-on-gordon-be.text: The only thing without brains is you! Come back once you have the actual head!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.text: Hello there. How goes the headhunt?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.player: I've run into a little issue. The beast is dead, but it didn't have a head. Your husband says he won't pay me until I bring him one.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.text: Oh dear. I'm afraid Gordon can be quite picky sometimes.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.player: But what do I do now? I can't bring him a head if there isn't one.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.text: Well, between you and me, Gordon is a good farmer but I wouldn't say he's a genius by any means. He also doesn't actually know what the beast looks like.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.player: So I make him a fake head! Great idea!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.text: That's the spirit! I've tried my hand at clay modelling in the past. You can make all sorts of things. Just get some soft clay and a knife and I'm sure you'll be able to make a lovely head.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-kil.text: Keep at it! I've tried my hand at clay modelling in the past. You can make all sorts of things. Just get some soft clay and a knife and I'm sure you'll be able to make a lovely head.

a-strange-fake-making-the-clay-head.text: You sculpt the clay into the shape of a head.

a-strange-fake-making-the-clay-head.player: Still, maybe it will be enough to convince Gordon.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.player: I've made a head out of clay.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.text: Wonderful! You should show it to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-using-the-clay-head-on-go.text: You show the clay head to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-using-the-clay-head-on-go.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Hello again. Do you have the head of that beast yet?
You show the clay head to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Its head? This is its head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: But this just looks like clay... It feels like clay...
As you talk to Gordon, part of the clay falls off.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: It's falling apart... What creature is this?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: Ah yes! A good question! A very good question! A good question in need of a good answer I'm sure!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Okay... So what is the answer?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: Yes... well... This is the head of a... a claybear!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Claybear? There's no such thing!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Quite rare because they don't exist! I'm no fool, this is clearly a pretend head! It doesn't even have any fur!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Come back once you have the real head of the beast!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Do you have the head of that beast yet? Or do you just have more clay?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: No head, no pay.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.player: I made a head out of clay. Gordon didn't buy it though.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.text: Oh dear. Keep trying. I'm sure with a few tweaks you can make a head that will convince him.

a-strange-fake-making-the-fur-head.text: You attach the fur to the clay head.

a-strange-fake-making-the-fur-head.player: It somehow looks even worse than before!
Gordon said it needed fur though. Maybe he'll be happy with this one.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.player: I made a head out of clay. Gordon didn't buy it though, so I've now added some fur.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.text: Wonderful! You should show it to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-using-the-fur-head-on-gor.text: You show the fur head to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-using-the-fur-head-on-gor.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof! For real this time!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Do you have the head of that beast yet? Or do you just have more clay?
You show the fur head to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof! For real this time!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Well there's fur this time. It does look like an actual head, I have to admit.
It really doesn't, but you let Gordon continue.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Yes, I think this is the head of a beast.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Well hang on just a moment...

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Where's the blood? If this is a fresh kill, the head should have blood on.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: Ah... Yes... Well the thing about this head is that this is the head of a...

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Yes?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Bloodbear? What's a bloodbear?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: It's a rare type of bear. One that doesn't have any blood.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: It's called a bloodbear but it doesn't have blood? Did a fool name it?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: Well actually the one that named it is quite the intellectual... Very cool as well... not that I know them or anything.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: You must take me for an idiot! This is some head you bought from a taxidermist or something. It's clearly not a fresh kill!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Come back once you have the real head!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Do you have the head of that beast yet? Or do you just have more fakes?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: No head, no reward. Come back once you have it!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.player: Gordon didn't buy the clay head so I tried adding some fur. He still wasn't convinced though.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.text: Well I'm sure you're not far off. Keep it up!

a-strange-fake-using-a-vial-of-blood-or-.text: That would be a terrible waste. Perhaps there's something better you can use.

a-strange-fake-making-the-bloody-head.text: You dye the fur head red.

a-strange-fake-making-the-bloody-head.player: Well... it doesn't. It actually looks like someone tried to dye a fur covered clay monstrosity red.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.player: Gordon didn't buy the clay head so I tried adding some fur. He still wasn't convinced so I've dyed it red to make it look bloody.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mak.text: Wonderful! I'm sure this will convince him. You should show him what you've got.

a-strange-fake-using-the-bloody-head-on-.text: You show the bloody head to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-using-the-bloody-head-on-.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof... Again!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Do you have the head of that beast yet? Or do you just have more fakes?
You show the bloody head to Gordon.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.player: I have bested the beast and I bring you its head as proof... Again!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Hmm...

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Hmm...

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: It's...

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: It's wonderful! This is clearly the head of the beast! Well done adventurer!

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: There's just one thing though...

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: A head like this deserves a place of honour! My friend, please could you mount it in our home?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Have you mounted the head of the beast in our home yet?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Well let me know once you have and I'll give you your reward.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.text: Hello there. Any luck with that head?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.player: Yes. Gordon was happy with the head I made. In fact, he was so happy that he wants it mounting in your home.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-sho.text: Oh dear. Well if it keeps him happy, I suppose. There should be a good spot near the stairs.

a-strange-fake-mounting-the-bloody-head.player: What a work of art! I've really outdone myself this time! I guess I should let Gordon know.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mou.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mou.text: Well I have to say that mounted head looks awful.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mou.speaker: Mary
a-strange-fake-talking-to-mary-after-mou.text: Not to worry. If it keeps Gordon happy, so be it. Anyway, you should go and let him know it's all done.

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: Have you mounted the head of the beast yet?

a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.speaker: Gordon
a-strange-fake-talking-to-gordon-after-m.text: That's great! I'd say it's about time for your reward. But first, let's have a look at this head...
A cutscene plays in which Gordon cheers and laughs at his new mounted head. Meanwhile, Mary comes next to the player. Both wipe the sweat off their forehead, happy that Gordon has been fooled.
Congratulations, you've completed a quest: Getting Ahead
Congratulations! Quest complete!

standard-dialogue-after-spirits-of-the-e.npc: Good day to you young lady.
I'm happy that we have our water back, thanks for your help.

standard-dialogue-after-spirits-of-the-e.player: Well it's good to see you happy.

standard-dialogue-after-spirits-of-the-e.npc: Mostly happy, but young people have no respect for their elders, theres too many confusing newfangled magic carpets and snake charmers around these days. I remember when this used to be fields.
Well no admittedly it used to be sand, just like it is now, but let an old man have his grumble.

standard-dialogue.npc: Can I help you?

options.text: What are you doing out here?

steps.player: What are you doing out here?

steps.npc: This here is the Warrior's Guild, a place where the strong may train. I'm the one who decides if you are allowed in or not.

steps.player: Am I qualified to enter?

steps.text: If the player meets the requirements to enter the Warrior's Guild:

steps.npc: Yes you are. Welcome to the Warrior's Guild!

steps.player: Thank you!

steps.text: If the player does not meet the requirements to enter the Warrior's Guild:

steps.npc: You may not enter the Warrior's Guild as you are right now.

steps.player: What? But I'm a warrior!

steps.npc: While you may consider yourself a warrior, I do not.

steps.player: Go on, let me in, you know you want to. I could... make it worth your while...

steps.npc: Go away and train small one. I do not take bribes.

steps.player: Why not?

steps.npc: The Warrior's Guild has a code of honour, a code that I respect. Move along.

options.text: I'm here to talk about Combat Achievements.

steps.player: I'm here to talk about Combat Achievements.

options.text: Could you explain what they are?

steps.player: Could you explain what they are?

steps.npc: Combat Achievements are a set of tasks for all adventurers to try and accomplish. They range from simple missions to kill various creatures, to challenges that will push you to your limits.
The purpose of these tasks is for you to grow and improve, experience all that Gielinor has to offer, and become stronger in the process.
Is this something that sounds interesting to you?

options.text: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

steps.player: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

steps.npc: Combat Achievements are broken down into six tiers: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, Master and Grandmaster.
As you complete tasks, you'll earn points. Tasks in higher tiers give more points than easier tasks. Your rank depends on how many points you've earned.
Whenever new tasks are added to the list, there are more points available to earn, so the threshold needed for each rank will increase. Keep completing tasks to maintain your rank!

steps.text: This is the icon for the summary panel. Within it there is a section for Combat Achievements.
Clicking on the section will open the Combat Achievements interface, where you can browse tasks, bosses and rewards.
Some tasks will require numerous criteria to be completed, so make sure you read them carefully.

steps.npc: I'd recommend you go kill some monsters. Come back to me when you've completed a tier or two. I'll reward you for your efforts.

steps.player: Thanks a lot, I'll get going.
Not at the moment, no.
I have to go.
No, I'm alright thanks.

steps.player: Yes please!

steps.npc: I can see that. Nice job. You'll be expecting your medium rewards?

steps.player: Yes please!

from the Warrior guild and two extra commendation points from each Pest Control game. Additionally, equipping one of my sword hilts at the Barrows will prevent your prayer points from being drained and
your Dwarf multicannon can hold five extra cannonballs.

steps.npc: I can see that. Nice job. You'll be expecting your hard rewards?

steps.npc: You have come very far. You have earned these rewards.

even fewer God Wars minions to access the generals. Plus of course, you'll get even more common ecumenical keys and access to even cheaper private God Wars rooms. And yes, I can also customize your

I do wonder what you will do now. Good luck, adventurer.

steps.player: Thank you so much!

steps.npc: We are waiting for you to join us.

steps.text: The ghost attacks the player

steps.npc: Woooo... Woooooo...

steps.text: You cannot understand the ghost.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: You see me? You understand me?

steps.player: Yes. Who are you?

steps.npc: Me Hopespear of Narogoshuun tribe. Who you?

steps.player: I'm [player name].

steps.npc: You not goblin. What you want here?

steps.player: Why are you here?

steps.npc: Me dead, but me not go. Long ago, me have vision of Big High War God. Me chosen prophet of Big High War God.
Me think, when me die, Big High War God take me to reward in Yu'biusk. Every day great battle, every night great victory with feasting.
Big High War God not come, but me have faith. Someday Big High War God come for me, take me to him. Until then me hang on, not let go into death.

steps.player: I visited Yu'biusk.

steps.npc: You go to Yu'biusk? What you see?

steps.player: It was a wasteland.

steps.npc: Wasteland? No goblins fighting glorious battles?

steps.player: No one. It was all empty.

steps.npc: You lie!

steps.player: I'm not lying. It's what I saw.

steps.npc: Even so... Yu'biusk is place of Big High War God. Land of Goblins. It where goblins should go.
Will you do me favour?

steps.player: What favour?

steps.npc: High priests in this tomb, when they die they believe they go to Yu'biusk. But their spirits still here.
If you can go to Yu'biusk, you can take their bones and bury them there. Will you do this for me?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Thank you!

steps.player: How can I get the bones? When I defeated them before, the high priests just spoke to me and then went back into the ground.

steps.npc: Normally, undead goblin high priests cannot be destroyed, but there is ancient goblin combat ritual.
You must defeat high priests without using any weapons, armour or spells. Once you have bones, take them to Yu'biusk and bury them there.

steps.player: I'll do that.

steps.npc: Thank you, human.

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Me should know better than to ask human to do favour for dead goblin.

options.text: It was everything you hope for.

steps.player: It was everything you hope for.

steps.npc: Thank you! I know Big High War God still care for us! I wait for him here. Someday he take me to Yu'biusk to live with him.
In meantime, will you do me favour?

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.

steps.player: I should go.

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.

steps.player: Tell me about the Big High War God.

steps.npc: Big High War God greatest of all gods! He take puny goblins from Yu'biusk and make them mighty warriors for great war of gods!
When gods go to war, goblin soldiers so good that Big High War God sell tribes to fight for different gods. Big High War God fight with other gods, sometimes for one, sometimes another.
Other gods fight for their own reasons, but Big High War God fight for war itself!

steps.player: Tell me more about yourself.

steps.npc: Me chosen prophet of Big High War God. Before I have prophecy, goblin tribes fight one another very much.
Long ago we fight other people: beardy-short-people, pointy-hat-short-people, tall people with keen blades. Other people build cities with walls, and we not able to attack them any more.
There not enough food for all tribes, so tribes with no food attack tribes who have food. Goblin war last many many years. Finally all tribes meet at this place, where temple is now.
It rain many days. But rain not stop goblins. Goblin feet churn up ground with rain and goblin blood. All ground turn to mud. That why it called Battle of Plain of Mud.
Battle last many days. Both sides same size, none win, none lose. Goblin bodies everywhere. Many dead.
Me not important general, not mighty sergeant. Me just normal goblin. But one night, me have dream.
Me see throne of Big High War God. He shine with light so bright me cannot see him, but me hear his voice.
He say, 'Stop the fighting!' He say, 'Fighting good, but not if all my followers die! You must not fight one another so much you all die!'
Then he say, 'Today I cannot lead you, but some day I will send Chosen Commander to lead you.'
I see Chosen Commander in dream. He wear shining armour and stand at front of army of goblins. Behind Chosen Commander, goblins stretch to horizon. Many goblins, too many to count.
I see banners of every tribe. Banners of all tribes, even Dorgesh tribe.
Other races, they run away from mighty goblin army! Chosen Commander make goblins build siege machines and they break down walls of cities. Then goblins march in and kill everyone!
And when all dead, Big High War God himself appear and sit on great throne of bronze and rule over all, with Chosen Commander beside him.
Then I wake from dream. I know it true vision from Big High War God. I run to general of my tribe, and he call other generals for emergency meeting.
I tell all generals what I see. They decide to stop fighting so goblins not all die. By this time, so many had died that there enough food for all.
Then generals set goblins to work building temple on site of battle. It sink into mud, so they turn it into underground temple, and keep it secret from others.
Goblins write my vision down in goblin holy book, along with history of goblins and commandments of Big High War God.

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.
Tell me more about the Chosen Commander.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Chosen Commander.

steps.npc: Me not know much more. In vision, Chosen Commander wear heavy armour and big helmet that cover face. Me not know what he look like. I see him give orders, but he far away so me not hear his voice.
Me think Chosen Commander will be great goblin general, but Big High War God chose me to have vision, not great general, so Chosen Commander could be anyone.

steps.player: Nothing. I should go.

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.

steps.npc: Aaaah!
Children, run quickly!
Oh my gods, the dragon is coming back!
Quickly, run!
Aaaah!
Get the women and children to the boats!
On the horizon! Do you see it?
Put that fire out!
Eeeek!
EIEEEEE!
Mummy, are we safe now?
Mummy! Where are you?
Aaaah!
I don't want to die like this!
Oh no!
Someone help me! I'm trapped!
AAARGH!
Come on, you monster! Just finish me!

We're all doomed.

standard-dialogue-with-a-ghostspeak-amul.npc: Don't send me back to that library!
It took me too long to get out of there... Just don't send me back!

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-barronite.npc: You there! Seek out the centurion at once. Inform him that the enemy leader has been identified and the Carnifex Maximus himself has been dispatched to bring back his head!
Did you not hear me? Do I need to spell it out for you?

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-barronite.player: If you could that would be great.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-barronite.npc: Goodness you are a fool! Their leader is named Yonrith Lovakengj. He has fled to the west with his closest allies, but much of his army still remains. Carnifex Maximus Vardorvis is in pursuit of him.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-barronite.player: Yeah... I still have no idea what you're on about.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-barronite.npc: Useless! Perhaps the headsman needs to take your head as well. I will find the centurion myself!

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-bank-area.npc: Ah, there you are. Dire news I'm afraid. We've lost all contact with the capital. Worse, another dwarven clan has joined the Saradominists. They march upon the fortress as we speak.
Is everything all right my friend? You don't seem to be yourself.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-bank-area.player: I don't think I'm who you believe I am.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-bank-area.npc: Hmm. You're clearly confused. The lack of sleep is getting to you. Go and have a lie down and we will discuss this later.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.npc: I've been doing some research into our new foes. Rumour has it they once lived in a great city in the far north. The city fell and now they are homeless.
It seems they have been promised a new home here in return for wiping us out. We must take great care. We may be fighting for our home, but it seems they are as well.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.player: Right... And err, how's the fight going so far?

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.npc: You tell me, I'm no warrior. That said, I did hear that they'd managed to turn some of our own golems against us. If they can do that, I fear what else they may do.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.player: Oh my... That doesn't sound good...

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.npc: Indeed. We have increased our offerings tenfold, but I fear they fall on empty ears. Perhaps our lord really has gone.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.player: Hmm. Well I hope it all works out.

dialogue-with-a-ghostspeak-amulet-equipp.player: I fought a really big ghost dog in here - is he gone now?

steps.text: If the player has a Shadow Sword:

steps.npc: You were well rewarded for you effort. But you should leave this place, for it is not wise to tarry.

standard-dialogue.npc: At the moment, nowhere. The mini-Ectofuntus that powers the Ghostship is in major need of repair, and until it gets it, this ship is going nowhere.
This is the Ectofuntus, the most marvellous creation of Necrovarus, our glorious leader.

steps.player: What is the Ectofuntus for?

steps.npc: It provides the power to keep us ghosts from passing over into the next plane of existence.

steps.player: And how does it work?

steps.npc: You have to pour a bucket of ectoplasm into the fountain, a pot of ground bones, and then worship at the Ectofuntus. A unit of unholy power will then be created.

steps.player: Can you do it yourself?

steps.npc: No, we must rely upon the living, as the worship of the undead no longer holds any inherent power.

steps.player: Why would people waste their time helping you out?

steps.npc: For every unit of power produced we will give you five Ectotokens. These tokens can be used in Port Phasmatys to purchase various services, not least of which includes access through the main toll gates.

options.text: Where do I get ectoplasm from?

steps.player: Where do I get ectoplasm from?

steps.npc: Necrovarus sensed the power bubbling beneath our feet, and we delved long and deep beneath Port Phasmatys, until we found a pool of natural ectoplasm. You may find it by using the trapdoor over there.

steps.player: How do I grind bones?

steps.npc: There is a bone grinding machine upstairs. Put bones of any type into the machine's hopper, and then turn the handle to grind them. You will need a pot to empty the machine of ground up bones.

steps.player: How do I receive Ectotokens?

steps.npc: We disciples keep track of how many units of power have been produced. Just talk to us once you have generated some and we will reimburse you with the correct amount of Ectotokens.

steps.player: How do I generate units of power?

steps.npc: You have to pour a bucket of ectoplasm into the fountain and then worship at the Ectofuntus with a pot of ground bones. This will create a unit of unholy power.

steps.player: Thanks for your time.

standard-dialogue.npc: Greetings, traveller. Welcome to 'The Green Ghost' Tavern. What can I do you for?

steps.player: Can I buy a beer?

steps.npc: Sorry, but our pumps dried up over half a century ago. We of this village do not have much of a thirst these days.

steps.player: Can I hear some gossip?

steps.npc: I suppose, as long as you keep it to yourself...
You see Gravingas out there in the marketplace? He speaks for the silent majority of Port Phasmatys, for those of us who would prefer to pass over into the next world.

options.text: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.player: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.npc: That's a long story, my friend, but you look like you have the time...
Do you know why ghosts exist?

steps.player: A ghost is a soul left in limbo, unable to pass over to the next world; they might have something left to do in this world that torments them, or they might just have died in a state of confusion.

steps.npc: Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!

steps.player: Why on earth would you do such a thing?

steps.npc: It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands of Gielinor. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.
We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.
He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.
As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands. Then, Necrovarus came to us.

He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.
Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.
Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm. He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.
Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.
Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.
The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.
We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.
We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.

steps.player: What is your name?

steps.text: Yes, and proud of it.

options.text: Can I have the key to the chest?

If the model ship is fixed and correctly recoloured:

steps.speaker: Old man

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: My name Ak-Haranu. I am trader, come from many far across sea in east.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: You come from the lands of the East? Do you have anything that can help me translate a book that is scribed in your language?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ak-Haranu not want money for this book, as is such small thing. But there may be something you could do for me. I am big admirer of Robin, Master Bowman. He staying in village inn.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: What would you like me to do?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Please get Master Bowman sign an oak longbow for me, so Ak-Haranu can show family and friends when returning home and become much admired. Then I give you book in exchange.

options.text: Yes, I'll give you a game.

steps.text: Er ... we'll deal with that when we come to it.

options.text: Yes, I'll give you a game.

steps.player: How do you play Runedraw?

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: Two players take turns to draw a rune from a bag, which contains ten runes in total. Each rune has a different value: an air rune is worth one point, up to a Nature rune which is worth nine points.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: If a player draws the Death rune then the game is over, and they have lost.

steps.speaker: Robin
steps.text: A player can choose to hold if they wish and not draw any more runes, but this runs the risk of the other player drawing more runes until they have a greater points total and win.

steps.player: No, that doesn't sound fun.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Do you want another game of Runedraw?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ah, can it be true? You have obtained bow from Master Bowman?

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.player: He was more than happy to oblige (cough). Here you are.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: Ak-Haranu gives you a translation manual in return for the signed oak longbow.

something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.speaker: Ak-Haranu
something-to-translate-the-book-of-haric.text: May honour be bestowed upon you and your family!

robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
robes-of-necrovarus-talking-to-the-ghost.text: Greetings, traveller. Welcome to 'The Green Ghost' Tavern. What can I do you for?

steps.player: Can I buy a beer?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Sorry, but our pumps dried up over half a century ago. We of this village do not have much of a thirst these days.

steps.player: Can I hear some gossip?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: I suppose, as long as you keep it to yourself...

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: You see Gravingas out there in the marketplace? He speaks for the silent majority of Port Phasmatys, for those of us who would prefer to pass over into the next world.

options.text: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.player: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: That's a long story, my friend, but you look like you have the time...

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Do you know why ghosts exist?

steps.player: A ghost is a soul left in limbo, unable to pass over to the next world; they might have something left to do in this world that torments them, or they might just have died in a state of confusion.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!

steps.player: Why on earth would you do such a thing?

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands of Gielinor. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands. Then, Necrovarus came to us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm. He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper
steps.text: Yes, actually, I do. We have a very famous Master Bowman named Robin staying with us at the moment. Could you take him some clean bed linen for me?

steps.player: Yes, I'd be delighted.

steps.speaker: Ghost innkeeper

initial-dialogue.npc: Hello, welcome to Aluft Aloft, the gnome food delivery service. We deliver gnome foods to customers all over Gielinor. Do you want a job? We are always looking for new staff.

steps.player: Yes, tell me more.

steps.npc: First of all you will need some basic Gnome Cooking and Cocktail making training. Go and talk to my Father, Aluft Gianne snr. and Blurberry, if you haven't already, and they'll tell you what you need to do.
Once you have got recommendations from both of them I'd be happy to take you on at Aluft Aloft!

Once you are working for us, I will give you a choice of either an easy or hard job. I will then ask you to make a piece of Gnome Cuisine, and tell you who ordered it, with some information about how to find him
or her. Don't take too long, the order is only valid for a short period of time.
If you complete the delivery successfully, you will be given a tip by the customer and credit towards your own 'free delivery token'.

options.text: What's the difference between an easy and a hard job?

steps.player: What's the difference between an easy and a hard job?

steps.npc: The foods that you need to cook for the easy jobs are more straight forward than the hard ones, and the customers will be within the Gnome Stronghold, or one of the Gnome Glider Pilots on duty. You will get one
credit for completing a delivery, and the tips you get will be a small amount of cash.

The hard jobs could require you to cook any piece of gnome cuisine or cocktail. The customers could be anywhere in Gielinor, If you are going to complete the delivery in time, you'll probably have to use some form
of transport. Gnome gliders are especially useful here.

For the hard jobs you will be given more time to complete the delivery though. You get three credits for completing it, and the tips you get tend to be useful objects, and even a few unusual items, that you won't
be able to get hold of anywhere else!

options.text: What are these free delivery tokens?

steps.player: What are these free delivery tokens?

steps.npc: I'll give you a free delivery token when you earn 12 credits. You can then use the token to make a food order yourself! This is a great privilege, we normally only deliver to gnomes. You may only have one token
at a time, and they are non-transferrable.

If you gain more credits then for every 12 extra credits you earn, you will receive an extra item of food or drink per delivery, up to a maximum of ten items. You can continue to make deliveries after this, but you
will not get any more credits - just the normal tip and cooking training.
Once you call for a delivery your token will be used up, and you'll have to earn another one, if you want another delivery.

options.text: Will this help me with my cooking?

steps.player: Will this help me with my cooking?

steps.npc: You will be able to develop your cooking skills during deliveries - you'll get the normal training for making the items, but also a bonus for successfully delivering the goods.

standard-dialogue.npc: My name is Gnosi. I am here to assist the Varrock Museum in their research.

standard-dialogue.player: I didn't know the Varrock Museum was familiar with this continent. What research are you conducting?

standard-dialogue.npc: We're studying the history of the region, origins of the lizardmen and how it all connects to Xeric.
We've wanted to study this place for a while, but haven't been able to explore due to lizardmen blocking the way.
But now that the Shayzien Army have cleared the path and discovered the Chambers of Xeric in the process, there is much to explore!

steps.player: Who is Xeric?

steps.npc: Xeric was an incredibly powerful dark mage. He ruled Great Kourend for ten decades.
If you'd like to find out more you should visit the Historical Archive at the Grand Library.

options.text: What are the Chambers of Xeric?

steps.player: What are the Chambers of Xeric?

steps.npc: At the summit of this mountain we've found an ancient temple and a vast network of caves that we believe were formed by Xeric and his followers.
The discovery of the Chambers tells us Xeric invested significant time and resources here, yet it was never documented.
While much of Kourend's history under Xeric remains unknown, it is very surprising to discover such a huge area that was previously undiscovered to us.

steps.player: Can I explore the Chambers?

steps.npc: Of course, though be careful. The dangers of the Chambers of Xeric are as yet unknown. You should take a strong group of companions with you.

options.text: What do you think Xeric used this area for?

steps.player: What do you think Xeric used this area for?

steps.npc: When he ruled Kourend, we know Xeric performed experiments on the living, using power drawn from the Dark Altar. After he was overthrown, he would have needed a new source of power.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.npc: We believe he came here to seek it. Xeric would also have required a source of many creatures for these experiments, and the Chambers certainly contain many of those!
He must have also had some form of teleportation in order to reach the temple unnoticed.
With time and careful study we will uncover these secrets and be able to answer these questions.

steps.text: If the player has completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.npc: We believe this altar is that source. It seems to act as an amplifier for the Dark Altar.
As for what he used the Chambers for, that we still don't know. There's a lot of creatures in the Chambers. Maybe he used them in his experiments.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.text: If goblin scribe previously thought the goblins worshiped an unknown god:

steps.npc: Before Dorgesh-Kaan, the Dorgeshuun lived on the surface with many other goblin tribes. All goblins were ruled over by an evil god whose name has been forgotten.

steps.text: If the goblin scribe thinks the war was for the gods' own entertainment:

steps.npc: The gods became bored and decided to make the mortal races fight for their amusement. The goblins were sent to fight in many bloody battles against each other and other races.
The war lasted for thousands of years, and millions of goblins died. Eventually, the evil god sent the Dorgeshuun tribe to fight a battle that they could not win.
But General Bloodfist of the Dorgeshuun refused to fight in this battle. Instead, he commanded the Dorgeshuun army to march down into a fissure in the ground.
General Bloodfist stood at the mouth of the fissure and defied the might of the evil god.
The evil god smote him with a mighty blast that shook the earth, but that blast also closed the fissure, sealing the Dorgeshuun away from the reach of the gods.
Lieutenant Strongaxe, now the leader of the Dorgeshuun, led the tribe deeper into the caves. They found this cavern, and here they founded Dorgesh-Kaan, city of the Dorgeshuun.

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Dorgeshuun civil war?

steps.npc: Certainly!  *Ahem*
At first, Dorgesh-Kaan was ruled over by generals, just as the tribe had been when it was on the surface. Each general succeeded the last by defeating him in combat.
The generals were advised by a council of elders, but the Dorgeshuun were no longer an army, and many of the people felt that the Council should have authority.
The people voted to become a republic, but General Bonehelm refused to give up power, and so the Dorgeshuun Civil War began.
The republican faction was larger, but the military faction contained most of the trained warriors and controlled the magical equipment that the tribe had brought from the surface.
General Bonehelm was driven from the city, but dug his own base out of the caves nearby.
General Bonehelm's army attacked the city using archers mounted on giant frogs. There was a bloody battle, and General Bonehelm was driven back again into his base.
But General Bonehelm's mining had weakened the stone around his base, and the retreating army's footsteps caused the roof to collapse, crushing his army.
That was the last time one Dorgeshuun has raised arms against another. Since then, the city has been ruled peacefully by an elected council.

steps.player: Can you tell me about recent years?

steps.npc: Ah, this is where you come in!  *Ahem*

In the twenty-ninth century since the founding of the city, one of the miners broke through a wall into the cellar of a surface dwelling. The miners blocked up the tunnel and went back into their mines.

steps.player: How do I use the Grand Exchange?

steps.npc: My colleague and I can let you set up trade offers. You can offer to Sell items or Buy items.
When you want to sell something, you give us the items and tell us how much money you want for them.
We'll look for someone who wants to buy those items at your price, and we'll perform the trade. You can then collect the cash here, or at any bank.
When you want to buy something, you tell us what you want, and give us the cash you're willing to spend on it.
We'll look for someone who's selling those items at your price, and we'll perform the trade. You can then collect the items here, or at any bank, along with any left-over cash.
Sometimes it takes a while to find a matching trade offer. If you change your mind, we'll let you cancel your trade offer, and we'll return your unused items and cash.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.player: Are you the grave digger this entry mentions?

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.npc: It seems likely, but I've no recollection of this conversation.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.player: That's odd. Did you forget a lot when you...

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.npc: Died? I guess some memories have faded, but my death still lingers within me.
I was minding my own business while digging a grave when suddenly there was a loud metallic sound.
I was dead... I recall seeing a man a few yards from me, speaking out loud, yet nobody else was around...
I thought I could hear a woman's voice respond, but it was likely just the wind.
I wouldn't think on it too long. I'd just died, my emotions were unbearable.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.player: I'll let you know if I figure anything out. What's your name?

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.npc: Please do. My name? It's um... Sander.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-or-book-of-the-.player: Pleased to meet you Sander, I'll see you around.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Greetings young one. What knowledge do you seek?

options.text: What do I have to do in this room?

steps.player: What do I have to do in this room?

steps.npc: Have you noticed all the bones around the room? These are teleported here from all over Gielinor to help clean up the landscape of countless bones left behind from combat. What better use for these bones than to convert them to nutritious fruit to be eaten by you mortals? You have to use your Bones to Bananas spell to convert the bones and then place them in the holes on the walls to earn Graveyard Pizazz Points. Unluckily for you, your health will constantly decrease from getting hit by these dropping bones so you will probably want to eat some of the bananas yourself to increase your stay here.

steps.player: What are the rewards?

steps.npc: You will get experience from casting your bones to bananas spell and you will get Graveyard Pizazz Points when you put the bananas through the wall. Occasionally you will also be credited with a runestone to help you in your future spell casting.

options.text: Got any tips that may help me?

steps.player: Got any tips that may help me?

steps.npc: Different bones will provide you with different numbers of bananas, so try to find the best type. Collect enough points and you will be able to buy a 'Bones to Peaches' spell from my fellow guardian above the entrance hall. This spell can be used here just like the bones to bananas spell, except this spell will give you even more experience and the peaches will restore more health!

steps.player: I see.

steps.npc: Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.

steps.player: Thanks, bye!

steps.npc: See those traders out there, just out the door? They're all standing in the Trade Octagon. There's an awful lot of trade going on in the palace, you know.

steps.npc: You will have to find that out on your own, I'm afraid. I do have more work to do.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-is-not-d.npc: Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Well met! My name's Grigore, I do a bit of this, a bit of that. Just try to survive really, there's nothing much else we can do.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Oh, my name's Grigore. I just help out around here, you know, gathering food and so on.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

getting-started.text: If the player does not have the requirements to begin the quest:

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Ahhh, good day young adventurer. I can't stop to talk right now I'm afraid.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Grim Tales quest.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Ahhh, good day young adventurer. A good day indeed! Sylas is the name. It is lucky for you that you met me.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Well it just so happens, [player name], that I have something you simply must have!

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Beans, my friend! Beans!

getting-started.player: Why would I want beans exactly? I mean, beans are good, of course, but I'm pretty sure I can get them anywhere.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Ahhh, but not beans like this, young [player name]. No, not at all! These are 'magic' beans.

getting-started.player: Ok then. So what do they do exactly?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: An excellent question! Excellent indeed! What do they do? What do they do? Yes, yes! A most excellent question!

getting-started.player: O...kay. So, are you going to tell me what they do?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: You must plant them in the ground. Water them well. Then the magic will work, it's...er...magic...yes! Plant them, [player name].

getting-started.player: So, can I have the beans then?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: All in good time, my excitable young friend. All in good time.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Few things in this world are free, you know, and beans - magical or otherwise - are no exception!

getting-started.player: So, how much gold do you want for the beans, if I decide to buy them?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Ah, well you see now I am a collector of rare and unusual trinkets and objects. Not much in value, but very important to me.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Right, well I think that for magic beans, I will need something magical back and I know of just the right items that would help my collection.

getting-started.player: Ok, so if I get these items, you will trade them for the beans. Is that right?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Yes! Excellent! You do catch on quick! I can see that we will become great business partners indeed. Oh, yes. Yes indeed! Hmm-ha! Yes.

getting-started.player: What items do you need me to find then - assuming I still want those beans of course. Not that I do, but I might.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Well, there are two. The first item should be nice and simple for you to get for me. I want a griffin feather. Now, this is not just any feather, this one is special.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: There is a griffin named Grimgnash who lives in a nest on one of the peaks of White Wolf Mountain. It is one of his feathers that I want.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: But although this task should be easy, you must be careful [player name]. Grimgnash has a very bad temper and even sharper claws!

options.text: What do you need the feather for?

steps.player: What do you need the feather for?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: I told you, [player name]. It is for my collection of magical items and trinkets, weird and wonderful thereof.

steps.player: Thereof?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Yes, I was quite happy with that word. I think it went rather well in that last sentence, don't you?

steps.player: I guess. If you say so.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Yes. Excellent! Yes. Now...er...was there anything else?

options.text: How do I find Grimgnash again?

steps.player: How do I find Grimgnash again?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: When he's not chewing on some poor soul's bones or raining terror on an unsuspecting village, he can be found in his nest, atop White Wolf Mountain.

steps.player: Excuse me...say what now? He chews people's bones? I thought you said this was an easy task?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Oh, I daresay he has to eat sometimes. But I don't think he'd take too much fancy for you. Not much meat on you at all. Oh dear me, no!

steps.player: You know, I'm not sure that was even a compliment.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: I'm sure it was meant to be! Don't worry, [player name], you'll be fine. Now was there anything else?

options.text: What's the other item I need to find?

steps.player: What's the other item I need to find?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Right, well, the second item is this. I know of a dwarf named Rupert the Beard who has a very fine dwarven helmet. I'd like you to see if you can obtain it for me.

steps.player: Ok. Where can I find him?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Travel north-east from here and between the Goblin Village and Ice Mountain you will find Rupert in a tower there.

steps.player: Ok, that seems simple enough. I'll get the helmet for you as well.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Excellent! Yes, yes. Now was there anything else?

options.text: Do you have any weird items in your collection?

steps.player: Do you have any weird items in your collection?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Haha! Weird items? Oh yes. Yes indeed! Yes. Many items. Many items. Yes.

steps.player: Umm...I see. Well, can you tell me about any of them?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Hmm. Well let's see now. I have the second eye of a mutant two-eyed cyclops. That was a rare find indeed! And at a tidy price too!

steps.player: A two-eyed cyclops? Uh...wouldn't that be a normal giant perhaps?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Whatever do you mean? How many mutant two-eyed cyclops do you think there are out there? Not many, I'd wager!

steps.player: Umm...no, I guess not. Well, what else do you have?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Ah, well I'm glad you asked. My most prized possession to date: Through my connections, I managed to acquire a horn-less Unicorn!

steps.player: Really? That's amazing! A unicorn without a horn?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Yes. Yes indeed! Indeed yes! And I'm very proud of it, too! It was an exceptionally lucky find, I must say!

steps.player: I expect so. Well, on to other things for now then, I guess.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Of course. Was there anything else you wanted?

options.text: I should be off, I think.

steps.player: I should be off, I think.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Excellent, excellent! Best of luck then, my friend. I'll be right here waiting for you to return.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-initial-co.text: Human? Human come to Grimgnash? Grimgnash pleased! Grimgnash hungry!

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-initial-co.player: No, wait! I didn't come to be eaten!

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-initial-co.speaker: Grimgnash
obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-initial-co.text: What human come for then? Grimgnash tired and hungry. Be quick, human. Answer Grimgnash before Grimgnash eats your legs!

options.text: I heard you were a great and mighty Griffin!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Hah! Human hears right about Grimgnash! Grimgnash great and mighty griffin!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Now what human want? Grimgnash tired and can't sleep. Wolves make awful howling racket. Keep Grimgnash up all night.

steps.player: Perhaps I can help you get to sleep in some way. Is there anything I can do?

options.text: I have come for your magic feather!

steps.player: I have come for your magic feather!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Grimgnash's feather? Human come to steal feather? How dare human! Puny, scrawny little morsel! Grimgnash should eat human where human stands!
(Grimgnash attacks the player, and does a large amount of damage.)
Grimgnash lashes out at you and you recoil backwards in pain. You must be more careful what you say. Grimgnash could eat you at any moment!

options.text: Do you have any quests for me?

steps.player: Do you have any quests for me?

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Quests? Quests? Human morsel wants a quest from Grimgnash? Human think Grimgnash is drunken dwarf or lazy ork? Grimgnash not gives quests!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Grimgnash tired and hungry and will eat little bite-size human!

steps.player: Argh!
