standard-dialogue.speaker: Group Iron tutor
standard-dialogue.text: Hail, Group Iron Man! My name is Tony, and I'm here to teach you everything you need to know about Group Iron Men. What can I do for you?

options.text: What is a Group Iron Man?

steps.player: What is a Group Iron Man?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Group Iron Man is a game mode where you do everything as a group. You can only trade items with player's in your group, take their items and accept their help.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: This means if your friend in the group has something you want to borrow, you can - assuming you have Individual Prestige status or are a Hardcore Group Iron player! But don't confuse Individual and Group

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: What is Individual Prestige?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Individual Prestige is automatically awarded to you the very first time you create a group. It is proof that you were one of the original members of that group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: This proof is displayed as a gold star next to your name on the group sidepanel. Note that if you join an existing group, you will not be considered an original member.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: The limits are gold and items worth up to 1,000,000 coins for the 1st week, 20,000,000 coins for the 2nd week, 50,000,000 coins for the 3rd week and 100,000,000 coins for the 4th week.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: During these 5 weeks you will also have restrictions to what you can equip: certain items will require you to have killed the monster that drops them.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: What is Group Prestige?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Non-Hardcore groups can show their dedication to the group through Group Prestige. This status can be viewed on the group's sidepanel, just below the group's name.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Group Prestige is lost upon inviting new members into the group, or upon doing certain activities with players outside of your group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?

steps.player: What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Hardcore Group Iron mode is a more challenging version of the regular mode, in which you have only a set number of lives for the entire group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: If you die in an unsafe area, you will lose one of your group's lives. When your shared lives hit 0, you will all be downgraded to regular Group Iron players.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: I'd like to manage my group.

steps.player: I'd like to manage my group status.

options.text: I'd like to leave the group.

steps.player: I'd like to leave the group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: We can start the process for you to leave. The process will take 7 days to complete.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Are you sure you want to leave your group?

steps.player: No, I changed my mind.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: I'd like to change my group's name.

steps.text: If the player is the group's leader:
If the player is not the group's leader:

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Only the group leader can do that.

options.text: How do I leave a group?

steps.player: How do I leave a group?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: You can leave your group by talking to me about group management. However, know that there will then be a 7 day grace period before it takes effect. In this time you can come back to cancel the request if you've

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: changed your mind.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: You could also be kicked from the group. If you are kicked from the group, you also have a 7 day grace period before you are removed. Only the leader of a group can kick other people. The leader must talk to me

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: in person about group management so I can confirm that they're really the leader before I let them kick anyone.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: The leader can come back to me at any point during those 7 days to cancel the request if they have changed their minds about kicking someone.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: Can I change my Group Iron mode?

steps.player: Can I change my Group Iron mode?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Unfortunately, Group Iron players who are not new to the island can't change their Group Iron mode.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

standard-dialogue-using-the-armour-right.speaker: Group Iron tutor
standard-dialogue-using-the-armour-right.text: There you go. Wear it with pride.

standard-dialogue-using-the-armour-right.speaker: Group Iron tutor
standard-dialogue-using-the-armour-right.text: I think you've already got the whole set.

standard-dialogue-interacting-with-the-n.speaker: Group Iron tutor
standard-dialogue-interacting-with-the-n.text: You can only change your Group Iron mode if you haven't been to the mainland.

steps.npc: Good day! I'm here to to teach you about group storage, and to let you access your personal bank. You can call me Maggie. How may I help you?

options.text: How do I use the group storage?

steps.player: How do I use the group storage?

steps.npc: You can access the group storage via the button in the top-left of your bank interface. Only one member of the group may access the storage at one time.
You will then be able to deposit and withdraw items from the group storage. You can't deposit untradeable items.
When you have finished, click the 'Save' button to confirm the transaction.
Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: I'd like to access my bank account please.

steps.player: I'd like to access my bank account please.

steps.npc: This bank is for new adventurers only, you cannot access it as you've already started your Group Ironman journey.

options.text: I'd like to check my PIN settings.

steps.player: I'd like to check my PIN settings.
I'd like to collect items.
Goodbye.

steps.npc: Farewell.
Me lonely.

steps.player: Why?

steps.npc: Other goblins in village follow either General Wartface or General Bentnoze. Me try to follow both but then me get left out of both groups.

steps.speaker: General Wartface/Bentnoze
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

steps.npc: Don't talk to me!

steps.player: Why not?

steps.npc: Me not allowed to talk. Generals will tell me to shut up whenever I talk.

steps.speaker: General Wartface/Bentnoze
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

steps.npc: Grubfoot do this! Grubfoot do that! They always want different things and they never satisfied!

steps.speaker: General Wartface/Bentnoze
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

steps.npc: Me wish generals wouldn't tell me to shut up.
Sometimes they tell me to shut up when me not even say anything!

steps.speaker: General Wartface/Bentnoze
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

steps.npc: Me wish me weren't so small. Other goblins all pick on me and make me do all hard work for generals.

steps.speaker: General Wartface/Bentnoze
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

standard-dialogue-after-land-of-the-gobl.npc: Did you go to Land of Goblins?

standard-dialogue-after-land-of-the-gobl.player: Yes, but it wasn't how you'd dreamed. It was a devastated wasteland.

standard-dialogue-after-land-of-the-gobl.npc: Yu'biusk... Land of Goblins... All gone?

standard-dialogue-after-land-of-the-gobl.player: I'm afraid so. And that's not all. Zanik vanished there.
Yes. A bright white light picked her up and then she was gone.

standard-dialogue-after-land-of-the-gobl.npc: She not gone. I sure of it. Someday she return.

options.text: Would you like your hedges trimming?

steps.player: Would you like your hedges trimming?

steps.npc: Eh? Don't be daft! We don't even HAVE any hedges!

steps.player: I want to come in.

steps.npc: No, go away.

steps.player: Do you want to trade?

steps.npc: No, I'm busy.

standard-dialogue-in-the-house.npc: Hi. I'm a little busy right now.

steps.npc: Ukk...I's dun fer...me's don't feel legsies anymore!
Yous creature doesn't stick mee's chompy, else mee's squeeze creature till yous a deadun!
Yous creatures too weedy for da ogre stabby chucker, yous best stick wiv da cluks-cluks.
Chompy is bestest yumms...
Me'se can't wait for da chompy yumms...I's dribbling all down me's for da tasty chompy.
Da fatsy toadies geddin' all messy...
Me's gonna ged da pridy chompy hatsies...an looks like a good-un wiv da laydies.
Mee's scared of Jiggig and da zogries, deyz is not da right dead-uns.
Mee's got no stabbers no more...gonna go home wiv no chompy...
I's stickin' da chompy...
De'se stabbers are worser dan a dead dog....
Would you like to buy or sell some gold jewellery?

steps.player: No, I'm not that rich.

steps.npc: Get out then! We don't want any riff-raff in here.

standard-dialogue-before-delivering-thei.npc: Bored, bored, bored. These Fremenniks are taking ages.

standard-dialogue-before-delivering-thei.player: Hey, they're doing their best. You arrived early.

standard-dialogue-before-delivering-thei.npc: Hey, we arrived precisely when we told your representatives. Lack of planning on your part does not constitute an emergency on my part.

standard-dialogue-before-delivering-thei.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
standard-dialogue-before-delivering-thei.text: Please, someone get these guys their ore quickly. They are eating all the good food on the island, and complaining about it!

standard-dialogue-before-delivering-thei.player: I'd better get a move on!

standard-dialogue-after-delivering-their.npc: Ah, yes. Now that's what I call a meal.

standard-dialogue-after-delivering-their.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
standard-dialogue-after-delivering-their.text: That's funny, I called it fourteen meals yesterday.

steps.npc: Ho! Outlander.

steps.player: What's down the scary-looking staircase?

steps.npc: These are the stairs down to the mining caves. There are rich veins of many types down there, and miners too. Though be careful; some of the trolls occasionally sneak into the far end of the cave.

steps.player: Thanks. I'll look out for them.

steps.npc: Party! Party!
Something's happening in the party room!
Everyone get to the party room!
What's happening in the party room?
Someone's having a big party!
Get to the party room NOW!
Get to the party room!
Get to the party room quick!
Big value items in the party room now!
Quick! Get to the party room!
Be on your way.
You don't want to mess with me, human.
If you're thinking of trying anything, you'll quickly find yourself regretting it.
I'm watching you, human.
Move along.

squeezing-through-door.npc: What do you think you're doing, human?

squeezing-through-door.player: Oh... I was just going to check out the inside of this house.

squeezing-through-door.npc: This isn't a house, it's a... Actually, human, it's none of your business!

squeezing-through-door.player: Well now you've just made me curious. What's in there?
Is it a really large anvil?

options.text: Is it a dwarf with a really long beard?

steps.player: Is it a dwarf with a really long beard?

steps.text: (Player takes damage.)

steps.npc: Why don't you ask me again?!

steps.player: If you insist...
Is it a dwarf with a really long beard?

steps.text: (Player takes damage.)

steps.npc: Ask me another question! I dare you!

steps.player: Okay, okay! I'm leaving.

before-hazeel-cult.npc: Hello there. I haven't seen you around here before. If you've come to admire the Carnillean family home, I must warn you not to cause any trouble.
Due to recent criminal activities against such prominent Ardougnians, I have been sent here on special guard duty to ensure the Carnilleans' security.
Anyone caught interfering with the person or possessions of any Carnilleans will be taken to jail so quickly that their feet won't even touch the floor!

before-hazeel-cult.player: Well, I wasn't actually planning on doing anything like that...

after-hazeel-cult-sided-with-carnillean.npc: Well look who it is! Good to see you managed to clear your name. I always had faith in you!

after-hazeel-cult-sided-with-carnillean.player: Thanks! So is everything all quiet around here now?

after-hazeel-cult-sided-with-carnillean.npc: Indeed! For now at least, everything is back to normal.

after-hazeel-cult-sided-with-hazeel.npc: Hello, adventurer. It's a shame you never found that cult. We have a horrible suspicion that there's been another burglary.
Yes, it is. The thing is, we can't even work out what they've taken! It's all very odd.

after-hazeel-cult-sided-with-hazeel.player: Is there anything more I can do to help?

after-hazeel-cult-sided-with-hazeel.npc: I don't think so. Sir Ceril says you've done enough.

steps.npc: Don't you try anything, surface-dweller. I'm keeping an eye on you.
Welcome, surface-dweller, to the hidden city of Dorgesh-Kaan!
Surface-dweller!

steps.player: What?

steps.npc: Have a nice day!
I don't want to be unfriendly, but I can't help noticing that since surface-dwellers started coming into the city there has been an increase in CRIME!
Surface-dweller! I don't know how you got into the city, but you will never escape!

steps.player: But... I thought I was allowed into the city!

steps.npc: You are. I just wanted to say that. And now that you're allowed into the city, I'll never be able to!

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-th.npc: This is a restricted area. You can only enter under the authority of King Lathas.

standard-dialogue-crossbow-guard-normal.player: I'm more of an adventurer really.

standard-dialogue-crossbow-guard-normal.npc: In this day and age we're all soldiers. No time to waste gassing, Fight! Fight! Fight!

standard-dialogue-crossbow-guard-three-g.npc: Well hello brave warrior. These ogres have been terrorising the area, they've eaten four children this week alone.
So we decided to use them for target practice. A fair punishment.

standard-dialogue-mace-guard.npc: What do you want? Leave us be!

standard-dialogue-guard-1.npc: Welcome to the Seers' Village courthouse. Court is not in session today, so you're not allowed downstairs.

standard-dialogue-guard-2.npc: The Seers' Village courthouse. We give all criminals a fair trial, by a jury of their peers. Or whoever we can round up from the pub.

steps.npc: What are you looking at?

steps.player: You're a long way out from the city.

steps.npc: I know. We guards usually stay by banks and shops, but I got sent all the way out here to keep an eye on the brigands loitering just south of here.

steps.player: It sounds more exciting than standing around guarding banks and shops.

steps.npc: It's not too bad. At least I don't get attacked so often out here. Guards in the cities get killed all the time.

steps.player: Honestly, people these days just don't know how to behave!

steps.npc: Please don't disturb me, I've got to keep any eye out for suspicious individuals.

standard-dialogue-before-royal-trouble.npc: The area under the palace is going to be excavated soon, and I'm guarding the entrance to it.

standard-dialogue-before-royal-trouble.player: Oh, I see. Can I go down there?

standard-dialogue-before-royal-trouble.npc: There's not even a rope to let you down there. You'd break both your legs if you tried it.

standard-dialogue-after-royal-trouble.npc: I'm surprised you managed to get out of there without breaking any bones.
Still, the Queen says it should be safe, and I'm to let you go back down if you want.

steps.npc: Stand back. This area is restricted.

steps.player: What's so special about it?

steps.npc: That's none of your business.

steps.player: I think I've left some of my loot in there. Can I get it quick?

steps.npc: Nice try, [Colosseum rank].

steps.player: What if I share some of it with you?

steps.npc: I do not care for wealth. Now move along.

steps.player: May I pass?

steps.npc: You shall not... *cough*
No one is allowed past I'm afraid.

steps.player: How suspicious...

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

standard-dialogue.npc: I'M ON SHOUTING DUTY!
I'M SORRY I'VE BEEN SHOUTING INSULTS SO LONG I CAN'T HELP IT!
THE TOWER IN NEITIZNOT. THEY SHOUT INSULTS BACK.
THE KING TELLS US TO.

standard-dialogue.player: Your King is a strange person.

steps.player: Can I watch? I'm curious.

steps.npc: IF YOU LIKE!

steps.text: Continues below at Watching the shouting

options.text: Oh well, I'd better get going

steps.player: Oh well, I'd better get going

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: YOU WOULDN'T KNOW HOW TO KILL A TROLL IF IT CAME UP AND BIT YER ARM OFF!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Neitiznot tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: YOU WOULDN'T KNOW HOW TO SHAVE A YAK IF YOUR LIFE DEPENDED ON IT!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: YAK LOVERS!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Neitiznot tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: MISERABLE LOSERS!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: CALL THAT A TOWN, I'VE SEEN BETTER HAMLETS!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Neitiznot tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: YOUR MOTHER WAS A HAMSTER.

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: AND YOUR FATHER SMELLED OF WINTERBERRIES.

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Neitiznot tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: AT LEAST WE HAVE SOMETHING OTHER THAN SMELLY FISH!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: WOODEN BRIDGES ARE RUBBISH!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Neitiznot tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: AT LEAST WE CAN COOK!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: OUR KING'S BETTER THAN YOUR BURGHER!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Jatizso tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: JATIZSO!

watching-the-shouting.speaker: Guard (Neitiznot tower)
watching-the-shouting.text: NEITIZNOT!

standard-dialogue-speaking-to-the-guard-.text: If the player has completed The Fremennik Isles:

steps.npc: Welcome, [Fremennik name].

standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.speaker: Rightie
standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.text: Only from your perspective. Someone entering the gate should call you Rightie, right Leftie?

standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.speaker: Leftie
standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.text: Right, Rightie. So you'd be Leftie not Rightie, right?

standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.speaker: Leftie
standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.text: Rightie-oh Rightie, or should I call you Leftie?

standard-dialogue-speaking-to-a-guard-in.player: Aaagh! Enough! If either of you mention left or right in my presence I'll have to scream! Can I come through the gate?
You said it! You said it! ARRRRRRRRGGH!

standard-dialogue-before-throne-of-misce.player: My name is [Fremennik name], will you not let me through?

standard-dialogue-before-throne-of-misce.npc: I'm afraid the King won't give an audience to anyone except a worthy hero.

standard-dialogue-before-throne-of-misce.text: If the player has not completed Heroes' quest:

steps.npc: If you become a member of the Heroes' Guild, he will definitely grant you an audience.

standard-dialogue-before-throne-of-misce.player: I am a member of the Heroes' Guild; does that not show my worth?

standard-dialogue-before-royal-trouble.npc: Sorry, but nobody's allowed down there by order of the King.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-royal.npc: You're free to go into the dungeons, your Highness.
Try not to get eaten by those monsters.

steps.npc: Be on your way.
You don't want to mess with me, human.
If you're thinking of trying anything, you'll quickly find yourself regretting it.
I'm watching you, human.
Move along.
Halt! Are you here to sabotage the Motherlode Mine?

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.player: What's the Motherlode Mine?

steps.npc: Prospector Percy discovered unusual mineral veins in this cave. Now he's built a machine to let us extract useful ores.
Percy calls it the Motherlode. I don't know why, and I'm not asking - that's between him and his mother.
Dwarves don't normally let humans claim areas of the mine like this, but Percy's machine is really useful, so we struck a deal.

steps.player: No, I'm not.

steps.npc: That's a relief. Have a nice day.

options.text: What would you do if I said 'yes'?

steps.player: What would you do if I said 'yes'?

steps.npc: I'd ask you not to.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-climb.text: If the player has done The Fremennik Trials:

steps.player: Don't worry, I'm not an outerlander, I am [Fremennik name], a Fremennik!

steps.npc: I said stay there, outerlander! You are not welcome in our camp.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-climb.text: If the player has not done The Fremennik Trials:

steps.player: Why, what's beyond here?

steps.npc: Our camp, outerlander, and we don't want any trouble there.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-climb.npc: I suppose I might as well let you pass now, since I can't seem to stop you anyway.
Just remember that I'm watching you.
Go, outerlander, and do not hurry back.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-talki.npc: Hey, how did you get here?

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-talki.player: Can you come and help me? The chieftain's daughter -

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-talki.npc: No, outerlander, I'm guarding this mountain pass from trolls and inquisitive people like you.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-talki.player: Doesn't look like you were very successful in the last regard.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-talki.npc: If the chieftain would let me, I would correct that oversight.

guard-at-entrance-to-mountain-camp-talki.player: Thanks... and try to lighten up a bit, alright?

guard-in-the-mountain-camp.npc: Feel free to come in and see the highlight of our culture, outerlander.

standard-dialogue.npc: Ah, this is a strange ritual that has been going on for generations.
One of our clan stands on this tower and shouts insults at the other side.

standard-dialogue.player: I'm surprised your Burgher approves of this sort of thing.

standard-dialogue.npc: He suggested stopping it, but there was resistance from the rest of the village. We find it therapeutic.

options.text: Can I watch? I like odd rituals.

steps.player: Can I watch? I like odd rituals.

steps.npc: Certainly.

steps.npc: HALT! Who goes there?

options.text: Don't worry, I'm not going to cause trouble.

steps.player: Don't worry, I'm not going to cause trouble.

steps.npc: But you shouldn't be here - be off with you!

steps.player: I was going anyway.
I am [player name] the Mighty!

steps.npc: Mighty? You look like another of those silly adventurers who thinks they're the bee's knees just because they've done a few lousy quests!

steps.player: Well it sounds better than sitting on this rooftop all day looking at trees!

steps.npc: I'll have you know it's a very important job guarding this jail!
If anyone comes sneaking in here to mess around with the prisoners, the lads downstairs will make mincemeat of them, and I'll be here to pick them off if they try to escape.

steps.player: You mean people aren't meant to be able to shoot the prisoners in the cells?

steps.npc: Yes, that's right.

steps.player: Okay, it's been nice talking to you.
No-one, there's no-one here.

steps.npc: What? I can see you!

steps.player: No, you're just imagining it. Perhaps you've been up here in the sun for too long?

steps.npc: So who am I talking to?

steps.player: Oh dear, you've started talking to yourself. That's a common sign that you're going mad!

steps.npc: But... but... you're standing right there...

steps.text: Maybe you should leave him alone now.

steps.npc: Guh... mwww... zzzzz...
Hmph... heh heh heh...
Mmmm... big pint of beer... kebab...
Mmmmmm... donuts...

steps.player: Maybe I should let him sleep.

before-song-of-the-elves.npc: I'm afraid not. The city is on lockdown until the rebel elves are dealt with.

before-song-of-the-elves.player: Please, I won't cause any trouble.

before-song-of-the-elves.npc: Rules are rules. No one enters until the criminals are gone.

before-song-of-the-elves.player: Fine, doesn't look very exciting anyway, it's just an empty field.

before-song-of-the-elves.npc: Mind your tongue human. Our great city may be lost to us but that doesn't give you an excuse to talk like that.

overhead-dialogue-catching-players-attem.speaker: Market Guard
overhead-dialogue-catching-players-attem.text: Hey! Get your hands off there!

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Greetings, traveller. Enjoy your time at the Ranging Guild.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

overhead-dialogue-catching-the-player-at.npc: Hey! Get your hands off there!

standard-dialogue-after-king-s-ransom.npc: The Sinclairs are under house arrest for crimes against a crown, and it's all thanks to you.

standard-dialogue-after-king-s-ransom.player: It's more luxury than they deserve.

standard-dialogue.text: The guard stares at you suspiciously.

outside-the-courthouse.npc: Welcome to the Seers' Village courthouse. Court is not in session today, so you're not allowed downstairs.

inside-the-courthouse.npc: The Seers' Village courthouse. We give all criminals a fair trial, by a jury of their peers. Or whoever we can round up from the pub.

inside-the-courthouse-trying-to-go-down-.text: Court is not in session today.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Don't distract me while I'm on duty! This mine has to be protected!

steps.player: What's going to attack a mine?

steps.npc: Goblins! They wander everywhere, attacking anyone they think is small enough to be an easy victim. We need more cannons to fight them off properly.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Dwarf Cannon:

steps.player: Cannons? Those sound expensive.

steps.npc: A new cannon can cost 750,000 coins, and the ammo isn't easy to get, but they do up to 30 hitpoints of damage with each shot. When you've got an important mine like this one to protect, it's worth the expense.

steps.player: Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: You're welcome. Now please let me get on with my guard duties.

steps.text: If the player has completed Dwarf Cannon:

steps.player: What should I do?

steps.npc: You have five minutes to explore the treasure rooms and collect as many artefacts as you can.
The artefacts are in the urns, chests and sarcophagi found in each room.
There are eight treasure rooms, each subsequent room requires higher thieving skills to both enter the room and thieve from the urns and other containers.
The rewards also become more lucrative the further into the tomb you go.
You will also have to deactivate a trap in order to enter the main part of each room.
When you want to move onto the next room you need to find the correct door first.
There are four possible exits, you must open the door before finding out whether it is the exit or not.
Opening the doors require picking their locks. Having a lockpick will make this easier.

first-time-talking.npc: Oh, hello there newcomer. I'm Guild Scribe Verity. Do you need me to explain the work we do here?
So it's nice and simple. Just chat to any of the hunters in here to help them out. They're all following reports that I've split up amongst them.
Indeed. There are all sorts of interesting creatures to hunt out there. Sometimes we get reports of a particularly unique example. When that happens, one of the hunters will set out to find it.
If you do decide to take a job from any of the hunters, they'll tell you what type of creature they're looking into. Hunt that creature until you encounter the unique specimen.
Once you've caught it, bring some proof back to the hunter that sent you out in the first place. I'm sure they'll reward you for your time.

steps.npc: I'm the primary record-keeper here. I organise all of our reports and write up anything important to be sent back to the city.

steps.npc: I wouldn't know what to do with myself out there, so I like to stay back here with my scrolls.

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome to the woodcutting guild. How may I help you?

steps.player: Tell me about the guild.

steps.npc: I founded the woodcutting guild when I retired from the Shayzien military. I spotted the ancient redwood trees in the hills many years ago from the Shayzien camp, and decided to construct the guild around them.
You can find them to the West, just follow the path.

However, if you're skilled in combat, or simply afraid of heights, the ent cavern may be more suited for you. The ents dwell deep beneath the ancient redwoods, and can be accessed through the cave to the North-West.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: That's all, thanks.
Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: My name is Lars, and I am the founder of the woodcutting guild. I originally grew up in a Shayzien camp, and was raised on the battlefield.
As I grew older, I found peace in Hosidius, and the joys of skilled labour. I turned in my battleaxe for a hatchet, and set up a guild for those also talented in the skill of woodcutting.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Hello Buoy and Gurl!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Hello sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: How do you know our names?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I had a chat with your dad. He's super busy, so he's asked me to help you build a snowman!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Really? We get to make a snowman?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes! And I'm going to build whatever snowman you want!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yay! Can it be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: But I want it to be five tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Five is a bad number, it should be three tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You're a bad number. Five is so much better.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait a second. Why don't we meet in the middle. How about four snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl think for a second.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Fine, it can be four tall.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yes, four tall is okay.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Great. Now, we need to pick what size snowballs we want for each tier. Why don't you take it in turns? You can do two each.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: The bottom one should be a huge snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The next one should be big!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: This is working nicely, we're half way! What about the top two parts?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: The next one should be a small snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: No, it should be little!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: But it needs to be small, little would look bad.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: It wouldn't look bad. Small is better for decorations.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: My decorations will fit on a little one.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Why do you always ruin everything?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You ruin everything with your silly ideas!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait. This clearly isn't working, and I don't want you two to fall out. It's Christmas, we shouldn't be arguing!
How about I make you both a snowman? It can be whatever height and size you like. One each!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: So mine can be five snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: And mine can be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes, I'll make you both whatever snowman you like!
What would you both like?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I'd like mine to be three snowballs tall please! And I want the bottom one to be small, the middle one big, and the top one huge!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: I'd like mine to be five snowballs tall please! I want the bottom one to be humongous, then large, then normal, then big, and then a little one for the top!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: That's two very different snowmen, I see why this didn't work before!
What do all these different sizes mean? Humongous? Normal? Little? How big are those?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You silly billy! Humongous is the biggest snowball of course!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Normal is the normal size that you get when you make a snowball normally. It's easy!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Right, thank you for clearing that up. I'll figure something out.
What are you two going to do for decorations?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I already know what I want mine to look like!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Me too!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Why don't you guys find some decorations while I build the snowmen? Then you can add them once I'm done.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Okay sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: We will do that!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl go back to playing in the snow.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, that seems sorted. I should speak to Larry again, and see if he has any advice about building the snowmen.
Hello there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Have you started making the snowmen yet?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You should talk to dad if you need some help, he knows how to make snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yeah, he always used to make really big ones with us!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Maybe I'll go talk to him and see what advice he has.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: He'll say, make them really tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: He'll say make them shorter, because that's better!
Buoy and Gurl wander off, arguing about what size snowman is the best.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I should go and speak to Larry. I'm sure he has some handy advice for me!

2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.speaker: Buoy/Gurl
2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.text: That looks good! It needs a [size] snowball next!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.npc: Yay! Can we decorate them now?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Yes! Can we decorate them now please [player name]?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: Of course you can. Are they what you wanted?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Mine too. It's just how I wanted it.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I am happy to hear that. It was harder work than I thought.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.npc: You did a good job. Thank you very much [sir/madam].

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: It was no problem. Merry Christmas to you both!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Buoy and Gurl go to their snowmen to start decorating.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I should go and speak to Larry. Hopefully he has that festive white wine ready for me.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Those snowmen look amazing!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Thank you! Decorating them was quite hard!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Yeah, they took ages to do! Do you like mine?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: It's really good! Reminds me of something actually.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: What about mine? Do you like it?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I like yours too. They both remind me of something!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Mine is Thermy! My favourite monster! She's so big and scary, makes me go woah!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Mine is Tempy! My favourite monster! He lives in the water, a huge mass of angry wet!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: They're both amazing! I didn't know you guys would be so good at decorating.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Dad lets us decorate every year. We get a lot of practice!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Last year we made them into the Fragment of Seren and the King Black Dragon!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: What... really??? I'd like to have seen that. Those sound even more difficult than these two!
How do you know all these monsters anyway? There is no way your dad would let you anywhere near them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Dad reads us lots of stories, and we hear about them from passing adventurers, like you.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: You must meet some interesting and cool adventurers!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Not as cool as you though; none of them helped us make our snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yes, you're the first to help us make them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, you're welcome. I really enjoyed it. What are you guys going to do now you're finished?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: We're going to go and play! And maybe visit the festival. Will you be there?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I sure will be. Maybe see you there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Bye sir, Merry Christmas.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Merry Christmas, have fun!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Look, here come 'nother wan'be jubbly chaser.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Be nice, Gurt, or you'll scare off another one!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Another what? What are you two doing here?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Me's big boss of of dis boatsie skill test. Call it Jubbly Jive. Only best wiv boatsies can hunt da jubblies.
Gurtob is da bestest jubbly hunter in all of da seas. No one surpass Gurtob.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Boatsies? Jubblies? Skill test? What's going on here.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: I'll take it from here, Gurt.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Dis... Sorry, this corner of the Shrouded Ocean is where we Barracudas like to challenge ourselves to a fun Barracuda Trial called the Jubbly Jive.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: While he may not look it, Gurtob here is actually an expert sailor and trial master for the Barracudas.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: An ogre is a trial master for the Barracudas? That's surprising.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Not at all! He may be rough around the edges and difficult to understand at times, but he's a fantastic sailor and that's the only thing us Barracudas care about.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. So what do I do here? What's the challenge?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Creatures talk... talk... long. Go da fastest, grab da toadies, throw da toadies, trick da jubblies, eat da jubblies. Dat's it.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I'm not sure I follow.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If the player does not have 55 Sailing:

steps.npc: Weak creature needs more boatsie skills first.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Yes, you'd probably benefit from testing your sailing skills elsewhere before attempting this trial.

steps.player: Thanks for the advice. I'll bear that in mind.

steps.text: You require a Sailing level of 55 to take on the Jubbly Jive.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: The goal of this trial is to use balloon toads to lure jubblies. First up, you'll want to sail west to collect da... sorry, collect the balloon toads from a boat of ours.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: On your way, keep an eye out for any lost supplies. You'll need to collect all of them to complete the trial.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Sailing over rapids will give you a burst of speed! Try to go over as many as you can. The more rapids you go through in quick succession, the faster you'll go!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: As you continue sailing west, keep an eye out for the jubblies. Remembering where they are will help you later in the trial. They tend to be perched on top of rocky outcrops or trees growing out of the water.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: The total number of them will depend on the rank you're going for. They're also fairly consistent, so your experience should be the same during each trial attempt.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Once you've sailed far enough west, you should be able to spot the boat where you can collect the balloon toads from. The maximum amount you can collect depends on the rank you're going for.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Once you've collected some balloon toads, you'll want to start sailing back this way so you can begin luring the jubblies.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: As you sail, watch out for the extra thick stagnant patches of water. They'll slow down any boat, so do your best to avoid them.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: As you keep making your way back, you'll want to start luring the jubblies back with you. The goal is to lure all of them back to us here.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: To lure a jubbly, look out for empty outcrops similar to the ones they like to perch on. If you throw a balloon toad at one of these outcrops, a nearby jubbly will move to it.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: It's worth noting that jubblies will only travel to the closest outcrop to them, so you'll need to lure them one outcrop at a time. Make sure to keep track of where you've thrown toads and where the jubblies started.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: When attempting higher ranks, you may want to set up balloon toads at multiple outcrops ahead of time!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: While the jubblies are important, don't forget to keep collecting the lost supplies as you come back as well.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If you can lure all the jubblies and collect all the lost supplies in the time given, you'll be awarded a Barracuda rank! Each trial has three ranks: Swordfish, Shark or Marlin. Each rank is harder than the last.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: For this trial, you'll be asked to lure additional jubblies and collect even more lost supplies as the rank increases.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: You can't attempt the next rank until you beat the one before it. You can also try unranked if you'd like to warm up beforehand.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: See, is like Gurtob said so. Go da fastest, grab da toadies, throw da toadies, trick da jubblies, eat da jubblies. Dat's it.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Of course!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: First up, you're going to need a boat with at least a mithril helm in order to withstand the strong rapids here, but don't forget, provided you can withstand them, they'll give you a burst of speed!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Secondly, you really want to try to avoid the fetid pools around us. They won't harm you or your boat, but they will completely kill all momentum you've built up.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: The only way to get across them is by using a wind catcher, but even then the timing is tricky, so we only give those out to sailors who have achieved at least Shark rank here.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Thirdly, trim your sails frequently to build up even more speed, but be careful! While it's important to go fast, doing so can make it harder to navigate around the fetid pools.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If I were you, I'd consider briefly lowering your speed for those tricky turns to avoid getting your boat stuck.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Hah! Gurtob sail never go down. Only go fastest.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Finally, and you probably don't need to be told, but watch out for those rocks, hitting them will put a stop to all of your momentum, just like the pools.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Thanks for the advice. I'll bear that in mind.

options.text: I'd like to attempt the Jubbly Jive.

steps.player: I'd like to attempt the Jubbly Jive.

steps.text: If the player is manning the helm:
If the player is not manning the helm:

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: You should make sure your helm is manned before starting the trial.
If the player has crewmates on their ship:

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: For this Barracuda Trial you are not allowed to bring any crewmates.

options.text: Can you help me transfer my crew away?

steps.player: Can you help me transfer my crew away?

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Yes, I suppose so.

steps.player: I'll come back another time.

options.text: Can you tell me about the Jubbly Jive?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Jubbly Jive?

steps.npc: Dis wat Gurtob best at! Dancin' wif da jubblies.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: He's right, you know. Whilst exploring the ocean, a group of Barracudas saw Gurtob 'sailing' around this place on what could barely be described as a boat, hunting jubblies.

steps.npc: Dey join in and try steal Gurtob jub jubs! But creatures nice and give Gurtob strong boatsie. Now Gurtob friends.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Gurtob friends indeed! When the Barracudas tried it themselves, they realised how much fun it was sailing around these tight spaces. They worked with Gurtob to design this trial!

steps.npc: Gurtob make bestest trial back then! Now yous little creatures make it easier, but me think it still best.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: It's true that some claim the trial is easier now than before due to new pathways being carved through the fetid pools. Still, don't let that fool you! The course is still a tricky one!

steps.player: So what do I need to do during the trial?

steps.npc: Go da fastest, grab da toadies, throw da toadies, trick da jubblies, eat da jubblies. Dat's it.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Let me explain it in non-Gurtob terms...

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: The goal of this trial is to use balloon toads to lure jubblies. First up, you'll want to sail west to collect da... sorry, collect the balloon toads from a boat of ours.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Me's Gurtob. Da fastest jubbly hunter on boatsies and big boss of dis boatsie skill test.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: And I'm Ros. I'm fairly new to the Barracudas and I help Gurtob out with managing this trial.

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: He's not much of a speaker and is easily misunderstood, so I help translate and make sure that any up and coming prospective Barracudas understand exactly what they need to do.

steps.player: Why stay out here in this awful smelling place? Aren't there better places to be at sea?

steps.npc: Dis Gurtob home. Only funny smelly is you's scrawny creatures.
Gurtob find funny when you's creatures gets stucks in bubbly watery. Gurtob also likes when you's creatures bring da jubblies.

steps.player: I get what's in it for him, but what's in it for you, Ros?

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Well, after joining the Barracudas, I discovered a fascination for different cultures. This is just a small step in my personal journey to understand more about the world!

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Plus da jubblies do taste good!

steps.npc: Da jubblies do taste da bestest.

steps.player: Who are the Barracudas?

steps.npc: Dey like da creatures which sound like da fishies but no taste like da fishes but fast like da fastest fishies.

steps.player: Erm...

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Gurtob sure has a way with words!

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Us Barracudas are the fastest sailors across the entire ocean! Our motto is 'Anyone from anywhere as long as they can sail.'

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: We work together to help hone each other's skills and test our mettle through challenges called Barracuda Trials.

steps.player: Can I become a Barracuda?

steps.speaker: Ros
steps.text: Of course you can! There's a bunch of trial masters like Gurtob scattered across the seas. Best our trials and earn your spot in our ranks.

steps.player: I'd best be off.

subsequent-dialogue.npc: Look, here come 'nother wan'be jubbly chaser.

subsequent-dialogue.speaker: Ros

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: The objective of this trial is to imbue large crystals dedicated to the different elven clans. You do that by sailing through portals linked to them. To get started, head out into the course in search of the portals.
While you're out there, keep an eye out for any lost supplies. You'll need to collect all of them to complete the trial.
The portals you're looking for are found next to the large crystals. Once you find one, just sail right through it. As you do, the portal will teleport you elsewhere in the crystal-flecked waters.

After being teleported, you'll need to find a second portal to return to the trial area near me, ideally corresponding to the one you went through. The portal you choose to return through determines which crystal
is imbued.

As you sail around, you'll find crystal motes all across the crystal-flecked waters. If your boat is kitted out with an activated wind catcher, you'll be able to turn their energy into wind motes, allowing you to go even
faster.
In order to complete the trial, a specific number of crystals will need to be imbued. Each one is imbued in the same way - by traversing the portal linked to it.
The number of crystals that need imbuing will depend on the rank you're going for. The higher the rank, the more you'll need to imbue.
This course will truly test your capabilities as a sailor. You'll find yourself alternating between navigating narrow spaces and vast wide open ones with the required speed and grace.
While navigating the more narrow spaces, you should be wary of resonance crystals. These old ship defence systems can crystallise your helm, damaging those holding it.
If your helm does get crystallised, you should be able to break the crystals with three swift strikes.
When using the portals, you'll find that each crystal near me has a pair of them near it. Both will send you to the same location.

However, upon using a return portal, your arrival location will depend on which portal you first picked. Choosing which portals to use and planning ahead of time are critical for overcoming this trial.

If you can imbue all of the crystals and collect all the lost supplies in the time given, you'll be awarded a Barracuda rank. Each trial has three ranks: Swordfish, Shark or Marlin. Each rank is harder than the last.
For this trial you'll be asked to imbue additional crystals and collect even more lost supplies as the rank increases.
You can't attempt the next rank until you beat the one before it. You can also try unranked if you'd like to warm up beforehand.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Of course, that's why I'm here.
To start, traversing the portals will reward your boat with an incredible burst of speed, so use that to your advantage.
Additionally, be aware that the portals will both displace your boat and change which direction it is headed for.
Aligning yourself properly before going through is not required, but you should try to anticipate where you'll end up and react quickly.

Next, avoid the resonance crystals in the area. They will target the helm of your boat. If you do get hit by them, make sure to break the crystals rapidly. Doing so will grant your boat a small speed boost.
Another thing to look out for are the crystal motes. If you have a wind catcher or gale catcher activated on your boat, they will be converted into wind motes and charge it up for you.
If you don't have a wind catcher, I'd suggest attempting the Jubbly Jive trial over in Backwater.
Finally, keep your sails trimmed and try not to get lost out there. The portals can be disorientating at first, but I'm sure you'll learn the layout of the course over time.

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Gwenith Glide?

steps.npc: Certainly. The large crystals you see around us are actually remnants of large ships that were destroyed during the Siege of Prifddinas.
Elven ships are not constructed from wood and metal, but are instead sung and woven into life over many moons from extraordinarily rare crystal seeds.
The process is incredibly intimate and time consuming. Each ship created represents not just our goddess, but also the individual who brought it into existence.

Like all Barracuda Trials, the Gwenith Glide exists to push your sailing skills to the limit. However, it also acts as an opportunity to honour not just those that died here, but also the ships themselves.

steps.player: So what is it that I need to do within the trial?

steps.npc: The objective of this trial is to imbue large crystals dedicated to the different elven clans. You do that by sailing through portals linked to them. To get started, head out into the course in search of the portals.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Gwyna of the Hefin Clan. I'm a trial master for the Barracudas and I provide guidance and counsel to those who attempt this trial, the Gwenith Glide.
It is my job to see that those who died here are honoured and that the sanctity of the course is upheld.

steps.player: Do those goals ever conflict? I'm not sure how the sanctity of the course is upheld as sailors race around the place.

steps.npc: I appreciate your concern, but you need not worry. Respect for the dead can be upheld in many ways. All who take on the trial have my blessing to proceed as they wish.

steps.player: Who are the Barracudas?

steps.npc: The organisation is a collection of like-minded individuals interested in furthering their own expertise and knowledge of sailing.
We're open to all with the spirit and patience to learn this delicate and precise skill.

steps.player: Can I become a Barracuda?

steps.npc: Of course you can, but you'll have to prove yourself first. There are other trial masters like me across the seas. You'll need to overcome our trials to earn your place among us.

steps.player: Tell me more of Elidinis.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Elidinis is one of a group of gods, known as the Menaphite Pantheon. She is wife of their leader Tumeken. She is the Menaphite goddess of growth and fertility and goddess of the river.

options.text: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis?

steps.player: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis though? Why did you pick on Nardah specifically?

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: It is true many do not follow Elidinis, but there is more to the story than that. The answers

steps.npc: lie in the story of Nardarine. Wouldst thou likest to hear the telling of this tale? It is not a short one.

options.text: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.player: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: Nardarine came from a town towards the north side of the desert which does not exist today. This was in the third age in the time thou callest

steps.npc: the God Wars. Her town was once controlled by Saradomin, but there was a great battle there between Saradominist and Zamorakian forces which pretty much levelled the town

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: to the ground. Most of the human citizens perished. Nardarine had the wisdom to escape into the desert before the fighting got really serious and thus survived. However she found herself wandering lost and alone in

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: the desert. She prayed to Saradomin for help, but Saradomin was too concerned with the loss of a strategic outpost to worry about the fate of one small human. Nardarine had wandered towards the realm of

steps.npc: the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: homage to me and I grant this also unto thine descendents as long as they too will pay an oath of fealty and homage to me'. Nardarine said 'If you would grant me a safe home, with a

steps.npc: supply of food and water, then I would surely do this for it is more than any other God would seem to do for me'. Then Elidinis made

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: a spring of water appear at Nardarines feet and brought stone from below the sand so that she

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: might have something to build with. She called forth camels which have many uses and taste good in kebabs. She then provided Nardarine with a statuette in her image to worship. Nardarine built up her home. Over

steps.npc: time more refugees from the God Wars found Nardarine's home. Nardarine let them stay with her as long as they did make the same oath as her. Hence the town of Nardah was born and Nardarine lived the rest

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: of her days in the peacefulness that she craved. The oath was passed down the generations for many ages, but now seemeth to be forgotten. Now maybe thou canst see why we are not best pleased.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-more.npc: I'd rather not waste time in conversation with someone who can't pay for information.
You travelling types, all you have is questions.

options.text: I guess I'm a little curious about your companion.

steps.player: I guess I'm a little curious about your companion.

steps.npc: The jester? The journey has put him off performing, for the better, I'd say.

steps.text: The thief takes a handful of coins from your pack.

steps.player: That was hardly worth it.

steps.npc: I never promised worthwhile information.

options.text: Do you know much about the Painted One in the town center?

steps.player: Do you know much about the Painted One in the town center?

steps.npc: Oh yes, he came with us. He tends to find himself in strange situations, but he can handle himself.

steps.text: The thief takes a handful of coins from your pack.

steps.player: Do you care more for gold than you do your friend?

steps.npc: Apparently.

options.text: I'm not giving you my money.

steps.player: I'm not giving you my money.

steps.npc: Then we have nothing to discuss.

steps.player: Excuse me, Hannibal.
Hello, Hannibal.
Hello there, Hannibal.
Hi there, Hannibal.

standard-dialogue-without-a-catspeak-amu.text: He appears to be sleeping peacefully, so you decide to leave him be.

steps.player: Excuse me, Hannibal.
Hello, Hannibal.
Hello there, Hannibal.
Hi there, Hannibal.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: (Dialogue continues with the current response, starting with 1.)

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hi [player name]. You woke me up, I was fast asleep!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I'm sorry, I didn't realise you were sleeping. I just wanted to say hello.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hello then. Can I help you with anything?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: No, that's it. You can go back to sleep, sorry to have disturbed you.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: It's no problem.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal snuggles back down and is fast asleep in an instant.
(Future conversations with Hannibal will use response 2.)

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hello [player name]. Did you need something?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Nothing important. I'd like to ask you a question if that is okay?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Ask away.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Why did you pick the kitchen as your spot to sleep? It must get quite noisy sometimes?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: It does during meal times, but it's also lovely and warm near the fire, and look at all the food!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Good point. Now it seems like the best spot in the house!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: You catch on quickly, for a human! Now I am going to go back to sleep, unless there is something else I can help you with?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That was all I wanted to ask, thank you.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal curls up on the stool and goes back to sleep.
(Future conversations with Hannibal will use response 3.)

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Oh, hello [player name]. Did I hear a bark?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: A bark? Is there a dog here?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: There is, sometimes...
It always wakes me up with its barking.
It seems to come and go. I can't figure out why or how.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That is indeed strange. I'll keep an eye out for it.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: There it is again, did you hear it?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I can't say I did.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Maybe I'm imagining it.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal settles back down and is sleeping in moments.
(Future conversations with Hannibal will use response 4.)

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hi [player name].

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: How are you doing?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: I'm okay, thank you. I've been enjoying the piano playing. Was it you playing earlier?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Oh, that wasn't me.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Must have been Gem then. She often plays the piano when she thinks nobody is listening.
She's actually quite good.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I'll have to keep an ear out.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal stretches and goes back to sleep.
(Future conversations with Hannibal will use response 5.)

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hi there, [player name].

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I have another question for you, if that is okay?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Go ahead.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Do you ever leave the hall? I've only ever seen you in here.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: I do sometimes. If I do go out, it's normally at night.
I much prefer it in here though. Nice and warm with good food. There is even a bank, if I ever needed a bank for anything.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That's fair enough. The world can be a pretty scary place out there anyway.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Exactly. It's much nicer to relax here, even with the occasional adventurer disturbing me.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That'll be me! Sorry, I'll let you get back to sleep.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal goes back to sleep, enjoying the warmth of the fire.
(Future conversations with Hannibal will use response 1.)

steps.text: You pet Hannibal...
He lets out a quiet purr before going back to resting.
You scratch Hannibal behind the ears...
He purrs contentedly before going back to sleep.

feeding-hannibal-selecting-the-feed-opti.player: I should give him some fish from my inventory!

feeding-hannibal-using-raw-fish-on-hanni.text: Hannibal gobbles up the fish, then settles back down to rest.

feeding-hannibal-using-raw-fish-on-hanni.npc: Thank you [player name]. That's very tasty, though it would be even more tasty if it was cooked.
I do. Why do you think I'm in the kitchen? All this lovely food being cooked all the time!

feeding-hannibal-using-raw-fish-on-hanni.player: That is a good point. I will see if I can find you something cooked.

feeding-hannibal-using-raw-fish-on-hanni.npc: I look forward to it. You know where to find me.

feeding-hannibal-using-raw-fish-on-hanni.text: Hannibal settles back down to sleep.

feeding-hannibal-using-cooked-fish-on-ha.npc: Thank you [player name]. That was lovely! Do you have any more?

feeding-hannibal-using-cooked-fish-on-ha.player: You just ate the entire thing, and you're still hungry?
I do often wake up hungry, maybe you're on to something.
I'll see if I can find you something else.

feeding-hannibal-using-cooked-fish-on-ha.npc: Lovely, I'll be right here, working hard.

feeding-hannibal-using-cooked-fish-on-ha.text: Hannibal settles back down to sleep.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello. What are you doing here?

options.text: I'm looking for whoever is in charge of this place.

steps.player: I'm looking for whoever is in charge of this place.

steps.npc: Who, the Duke? He's in his study, on the first floor.

options.text: I have come to kill everyone in this castle!

steps.player: I have come to kill everyone in this castle!

steps.text: Hans runs away from the player screaming

steps.npc: Help! Help!

options.text: I don't know. I'm lost. Where am I?

steps.player: I don't know. I'm lost. Where am I?

steps.npc: You are in Lumbridge Castle, in the Kingdom of Misthalin. Across the river, the road leads north to Varrock, and to the west lies Draynor Village.

options.text: Can you tell me how long I've been here?

steps.player: Can you tell me how long I've been here?

steps.npc: Ahh, I see all the newcomers arriving in Lumbridge, fresh-faced and eager for adventure. I remember you...
You've spent [amount] days, [amount] hours, [amount] minutes in the world since you arrived [amount] days ago.

steps.player: Nothing.

standard-dialogue-contacting-through-ast.player: I'm a brave knight! I am coming to kill anyone in the vicinity of Lumbridge Castle!

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Hello.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Hari.

steps.player: And what are you doing here Hari?

steps.npc: Like most people who come to Edgeville, I am here to seek adventure in the Wilderness.
I found a secret underground river that will take me quite a long way north.

steps.player: Underground river? Where does it come out?

steps.npc: It comes out in a pond located deep in the Wilderness.
I had to find a very special type of canoe to get me up the river though, would you like to know more?

steps.player: Could you teach me about canoes?

steps.text: If the player has 1-11 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Well, you don't look like you have the skill to make a canoe.
You need to have at least level 12 woodcutting.
Once you are able to make a canoe it makes travel along the river much quicker!
It's really quite simple. Just walk down to that tree on the bank and chop it down.
When you have done that you can shape the log further with your axe to make a canoe.

steps.text: If the player has 12-26 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: I can sense you're still a novice woodcutter, you will only be able to make a log canoe at present.

steps.player: Is that good?

steps.npc: A log will take you one stop along the river. But you won't be able to travel into the Wilderness on it.

steps.text: If the player has 27-41 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: You are an average woodcutter. You should be able to make a Dugout canoe quite easily. It will take you 2 stops along the river.

steps.player: Can I take a dugout canoe to reach the Wilderness?

steps.npc: You would never make it there alive.

steps.player: Best not to try then.

steps.text: If the player has 42-56 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: You seem to be an accomplished woodcutter. You will easily be able to make a Stable Dugout
They are reliable enough to get you anywhere on this river, except to the Wilderness of course.
Only a Waka can take you there.

steps.player: A Waka? What's that?

steps.npc: Come and ask me when you have improved your skills as a woodcutter.

steps.text: If the player has 57-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Your skills rival mine friend. You will certainly be able to build a Waka.

steps.player: A Waka? What's that?

steps.npc: A Waka is an invention of my people, it's an incredible strong and fast canoe and will carry you safely to any destination on the river.

steps.player: Any destination?

steps.npc: Yes, you can take a waka north through the underground portion of this river.
It will bring you out at a pond in the heart of the Wilderness. Be careful up there, many have lost more than their lives in that dark and twisted place.

steps.player: No thanks, not right now.

options.text: Can you teach me about Canoeing?

steps.player: Could you teach me about canoes?

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome, Effendi!

steps.player: Can I go in?

steps.npc: Come now Effendi, to pass you must tell me a story, one of grand heroics!

steps.text: If the player has not completed Dragon Slayer:
You tell the tale of how you bested a goblin, it lacks heroics and sounds more like senseless murder.

steps.player: ...And then I pulled the goblin mail from the corpse, but it didn't fit, so I dropped it.

steps.npc: You thought that was a story of heroics?! Come back when you have something worth telling.

steps.text: To gain entrance to the resource area, you must first complete the quest 'Dragon Slayer'.
If the player has completed Dragon Slayer but have not spoken to Haris yet:
You tell the tale of how you bested the legendary dragon Elvarg in combat.

steps.player: ...And then I cut her head off, so as to make sure she was dead!

steps.npc: Amazing! A story well worth telling! Please Effendi, enter at your leisure.

steps.text: If the player has already obtained permission to enter area:

steps.npc: Of course Effendi! You have proved yourself worthy!

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Me? I am Haris! Owner of the area north of here, it is has great resources, I assure you.

steps.player: You own the land? Who did you buy it from?

steps.npc: Buy? Oh no no no. Do you see this sword, Effendi?

steps.player: I do.

steps.npc: Well then, that is why it is mine! Hahaha.

steps.player: Oh, so do I pay a toll? 10 coins should do, right?

steps.npc: Not quite, while gold can get you to many places, I seek stories of heroics, for my land is only for the worthy.

steps.player: Is the story behind your sword one of heroics?

steps.npc: I promise you, the monkey I took it from was big! Hahaha!

steps.player: Bye!

steps.npc: Farewell, Effendi!

if-the-player-tries-to-enter-the-corsair.npc: Hey! I didn't say you could go in there!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.npc: ... Wait a minute... you're that adventurer that has been taking on the Colosseum!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.text: If the player has achieved Champion rank but not Grand Champion rank:

steps.npc: The Champion!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.text: If the player has achieved Grand Champion rank:

steps.npc: The Grand Champion!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.npc: Wow, what are the chances you'd run into a simple farmer like me.
I suppose you might be needing a reliable herb supply if you're planning to continue fighting in the Colosseum?
I'll keep an eye on any herbs you plant here. It's the least I can do for someone like you.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.player: That's a really kind gesture, but aren't you meant to be focusing on growing your own food?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.npc: It's no trouble. The soil around here is very rich, so it won't need much attention at all. I might even get a reward from the palace for helping such a valiant contender!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.text: If the player has achieved Champion rank but not Grand Champion rank:

steps.npc: Best of luck on your journey, Champion!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-after.text: If the player has achieved Grand Champion rank:

steps.npc: Best of luck on your journey, Grand Champion!

standard-dialogue-after-death-plateau.player: Can I buy you a drink?

standard-dialogue-after-death-plateau.npc: Now you're talking! An Asgarnian Ale please!

standard-dialogue-after-death-plateau.text: If the player doesn't have an Asgarnian ale in their inventory:

steps.player: I'll go and get you one.

standard-dialogue-after-death-plateau.text: If the player has an Asgarnian ale in their inventory:

steps.text: You give Harold an Asgarnian ale.

steps.npc: burp*
I guess this will be my last day of blood tithes, one way or another.
It can't be that hard can it?
Soon I will be free!
I'm starting to think I made a mistake coming here.
Can't talk. I need to prepare myself.
I will survive the Theatre! Just like Serafina did!

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome to my humble guild [player name].

options.text: Quite a place you've got here.

steps.player: Quite a place you've got here.

steps.npc: Indeed we do. Would you like to know more about it?

options.text: Tell me about the strength training area.

steps.player: Tell me about the strength training area.

steps.npc: Ahh the mighty warrior Sloane guards the strength training area. This intriguing little area consists of two shotput lanes for different weights of shot. It's fairly simple, the Referee or Sloane can explain more. You
may find yourself panting for breath though.

steps.player: Oh? Why?

steps.npc: Well you see my dear [boy/lady], the games there really do sap your energy quite a bit. You can find it just up the stairs behind the bank.

options.text: Tell me about the attack training area.

steps.player: Tell me about the attack training area.

steps.npc: Ahhh, dummies.

steps.player: I'm no dummy, I just want to know what is there!

steps.npc: Oh no my dear [man/lady], I did not mean you at all! The training area has mechanical dummies which pop up out of holes in the floor. The noble dwarf Gamfred invented the mechanism and Ajjat can explain more about what
to do there.

steps.player: Oh, ok, I'll have to try it out!

steps.npc: You can find it just down the corridor and on your right.

options.text: Tell me about the defence training area.

steps.player: Tell me about the defence training area.

steps.npc: To polish your defensive skills to the very highest level we've employed a most inventive dwarf and a catapult.

steps.player: You're going to throw dwarves at me?

steps.npc: Oh my no! I think Gamfred would object to that most strongly.
He's an inventor you see and has built a marvellous contraption that can throw all sorts of things at you including magic missiles...

steps.player: Mmmm?

steps.npc: ....spiked iron balls.....

steps.player: Err....

steps.npc: ....spinning slashing blades....

steps.player: Ummm...

steps.npc: ... and even anvils.

steps.player: ANVILS!?

steps.npc: No need to be afraid, it's all under very controlled conditions! You can find it just up the stairs behind the bank.

options.text: Tell me about the combat training area.

steps.player: Tell me about the combat training area.

steps.npc: Ahh yes, our resident magician from foreign lands created a most amazing gadget which can turn your own armour against you! It's really quite intriguing.
