steps.player: That sounds dangerous. What if I'm wearing it at the time?

steps.npc: So far that's not happened. You need to speak to Shanomi about the specifics of the process, but as I understand it, putting a suit of armour in one of these devices will make it come to life some how. The better
the armour, the harder it is to 'kill'.

steps.player: Fighting my own armour, that sounds... weird. I could be killed by it...

steps.npc: Indeed we have had a few fatalities from warriors over stretching themselves and not knowing their limits. Start small and work up is my motto! That and go see Lidio for some food if you need it.

steps.player: Ok, thanks for the warning.
Tell me about tokens.

steps.npc: Ahh, yes, our token system is designed to allow you an appropriate amount of time with my discovery in the very top floor of the guild. I won't spoil the surprise as to what that is. Go up and see for yourself. Now, the
amount of tokens you collect from the various activities around the guild will dictate how long Kamfreena will allow you in the enclosure on the very top floor. More tokens equals more time.

steps.player: So what's up there?

steps.npc: If I told you it would spoil the surprise!

steps.player: Ok ok... so how do I earn and claim these tokens?

steps.npc: You can earn them simply by using the training exercises around the guild, the staff will then enter this into a ledger as you play. You can claim them by simply asking any of the staff at the training areas, or
myself.

steps.player: Sounds easy enough.

options.text: Tell me about the strength training area.
Tell me about the attack training area.
Tell me about the defence training area.
Tell me about the combat training area.
You any good with a sword?

steps.player: You any good with a sword?

steps.npc: Am I any good with....a sword... Have you any clue who I am?

steps.player: Not really... no.

steps.npc: Why I could best any person alive in a rapier duel!

steps.player: Try me then!

steps.npc: My dear [sir/lady], I couldn't possibly duel you, I might hurt you and then what would happen to my reputation! Besides, I have this wonderful guild to run. Why don't you take a look at the various activities we
have. You might even collect enough tokens to be allowed in to kill the strange beasts from the east!

steps.player: Bye!

steps.npc: Farewell [brave warrior/fair lady], I do hope you enjoy my guild.

after-completing-while-guthix-sleeps.npc: Welcome to my humble Guild [player name].

steps.player: How are you, Harrallak?

steps.npc: I've lost two of my dear friends, [player name]. This old place doesn't seem to be the same since they're gone.

steps.player: I feel responsible.

steps.npc: Nonsense, my friend! They both died bravely fighting against a great evil! There is no blame on you for that.
Remember them for who they were and what they stood for. Mourn their loss, but never bear the burden of their death, for that is not what they would want.

steps.player: And what about vengeance?

steps.npc: Ah, now that is a topic we could debate for many moons, my friend. Still, regardless of the reason, know that when the time comes, I will fight beside you against Lucien once more.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the Guild?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about the Guild?

steps.npc: Of course. What would you like to know about?
Welcome, you can buy fishing equipment at my store. We'll also give you a good price for any fish that you catch.

options.text: Let's see what you've got then.
Can I get a fish for this bowl?
options.condition: If the player has either a fishbowl filled with water or both water and seaweed in their inventory:

steps.player: Can I get a fish for this bowl?

steps.text: If the player has a fishbowl filled with only water in their inventory:

steps.npc: Sorry, you need to put some seaweed into the bowl first.

steps.player: Seaweed?

steps.npc: Yes, the fish seem to like it. Come and see me when you have put some in the bowl.

steps.text: If the player has a fishbowl filled with water and seaweed in their inventory:

steps.npc: Yes you can!
I can see that you have a nicely filled fishbowl there to use, and you can catch a fish from my aquarium if you want.
You will need a special net to do this though, and I sell them for 10 gold.

steps.player: I'll take it!

steps.text: If the player has 10 coins:
Tiny net

steps.npc: Here you go!

steps.text: If the player doesn't have has 10 coins:

steps.npc: Well, I'll be happy to give you the net once you have the cash, but not before!

steps.player: No thanks, later maybe.

options.condition: If the player has either a fishbowl filled with water or both water and seaweed in their inventory:

steps.player: Do you have any fishfood?

steps.npc: Sorry, I'm all out. I used up the last of it feeding the fish in the aquarium.
I have some empty boxes though, they have the ingredients written on the back. I'm sure if you pick up a pestle and mortar you will be able to make your own.

steps.text: An empty box

steps.npc: Here. I can hardly charge you for an empty box.

steps.player: Sorry, I'm not interested.

before-the-fremennik-trials.npc: I don't have time to talk to an outerlander.

after-the-fremennik-exiles-rellekka.npc: Good to see you [Fremennik name]. Wanting to go to the Island of Stone?

steps.text: Player is transported to the Island of Stone

steps.player: No thank you.

after-the-fremennik-exiles-island-of-sto.npc: Good to see you [Fremennik name]. Do you wish to return to Rellekka?

steps.text: Player is transported to Rellekka

steps.player: No thank you.
Can I have another ring?

steps.text: Hatius gives you another ring.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I am Hatius Cosaintus, the taskmaster for the Lumbridge & Draynor Achievement Diary.

steps.player: What is the Achievement Diary?

steps.npc: It's a diary that helps you keep track of particular achievements. In the Lumbridge and Draynor area it can help you discover some quite useful things. Eventually, with enough exploration, the inhabitants will
reward you.
You can see the list of tasks on the side-panel.

options.text: I have a question about my Achievement Diary

steps.player: I have a question about my Achievement diary.

steps.npc: Well, there are four different Explorer's rings, which match up with the four levels of difficulty. Each has the same rewards as the previous level and some additional benefits too... which tier of rewards would you like to
know more about?

steps.player: Tell me more about the Easy rewards please!

steps.npc: If you complete all of the easy tasks in Lumbridge and Draynor, your ring can recharge half of your run energy twice per day and cast low level alchemy without runes 30 times per day.

steps.player: Thanks!
Tell me more about the Medium rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy rewards, your ring can restore half of your run energy and teleport you to the Draynor cabbage patch three times per day.

steps.player: Thanks!
Tell me more about the Hard rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy and medium benefits, the ring will have unlimited cabbage teleports and four charges to restore half your run energy. Collecting Tears of Guthix will provide increased experience.

steps.player: Thanks!
Tell me more about the Elite rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the previous tiers of rewards, you can block an additional slayer target with slayer masters, recharge all of your run energy three times per day and cast high level alchemy thirty times per day. The
Culinaromancer's chest is 20% cheaper, you can use Fairy rings without needing a dramen or lunar staff and you'll receive double wire when thieving in Dorgesh-Kaan.

steps.player: Thanks!

options.text: How do I claim the rewards?

steps.player: How do I claim the rewards?

steps.npc: One should complete the tasks in Lumbridge and Draynor so they're ticked off, then speak to me to be rewarded.

steps.player: Bye!

steps.npc: Toodles.

easy-tasks-completed.player: I've completed all of the easy tasks in my Lumbridge & Draynor Achievement Diary!

easy-tasks-completed.npc: Quite... You'll be wanting a reward then.
This ring is a symbol of your exploration of Lumbridge and Draynor. It can recharge half of your run energy twice per day and cast low level alchemy without runes 30 times per day.
If you ever lose your ring, come back to me to reclaim it.

medium-tasks-completed.player: I've completed all of the medium tasks in my Lumbridge & Draynor achievement diary!

medium-tasks-completed.npc: Quite... You'll be wanting a reward then.

medium-tasks-completed.text: Explorer's ring 2

medium-tasks-completed.npc: I've upgraded your Explorer's ring for you. It can restore half of your run energy and teleport you to the Draynor cabbage patch three times per day.

hard-tasks-completed.player: I've completed all of the hard tasks in my Lumbridge & Draynor achievement diary!

hard-tasks-completed.npc: Quite... You'll be wanting a reward then.
I've upgraded your Explorer's ring for you. It now has unlimited cabbage teleports and four charges to restore half your run energy. Collecting Tears of Guthix will now provide increased experience.

elite-tasks-completed.player: I've completed all of the elite tasks in my Lumbridge & Draynor achievement diary!

elite-tasks-completed.npc: I can see that, well done! You've completed all of the tasks in the Lumbridge & Draynor diary! You've earned another reward.

I've upgraded your Explorer's ring for you. In addition to the previous benefits you can now block an additional slayer target with slayer masters, recharge all of your run energy three times per day and cast high
level alchemy thirty times per day. The Culinaromancer's chest is now 20% cheaper and you'll receive double wire when thieving in Dorgesh-Kaan.

options.text: Can I go for a ride?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride?

steps.text: If the player does not have 20 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Minecart rides are 20 coins.

steps.text: If the player has 20 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.text: (Lovakengj Minecart Network interface opens.)

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

options.text: Can I go for a ride?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride?

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.text: (Lovakengj Minecart Network interface opens.)

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

standard-dialogue-unlimited-ride-fee-ref.npc: As a loyal customer of the Lovakengj Minecart Network, you're entitled to this.
Now, can I help you today?

starting-out.player: Hello there. What are you doing here?

options.text: I follow the path of Saradomin.

steps.player: I follow the path of Saradomin. Strength through wisdom.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Ah, a wise choice my friend. But if you truly follow Saradomin, what brings you to these evil lands?

options.text: I come seeking challenges and quests.

steps.player: I come seeking challenges and quests.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: A noble cause indeed. One that I can sympathise with, for I myself am upon a quest.  One that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

steps.prompt: Start the Haunted Mine quest?

steps.player: What quest is that then?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Well, below the very ground you stand upon lies an intricate network of tunnels that make up the abandoned Mort Ridge mines. These mines used to be a valuable resource to the inhabitants of Morytania.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: As with many things, this changed when Misthalin was finally able to push the minions of Morytania back, and Saradomin himself blessed the river Salve.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: The mines are also the site where the legendary artefact, the salve amulet, was thought to have been carved from the crystals that grow in the lower levels of the mine.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: These crystals are thought to be formed by the blessed water of the river Salve as it percolates through the rocks to the lower levels of the mine.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: It is not known what happened to the salve amulet, but it is generally believed that by encapsulating within it some of the goodness of Saradomin himself, it afforded the bearer power over evil.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin has entrusted me alone with the task of regaining access to the mines, whatever the dangers.

steps.player: How can an abandoned mine be dangerous?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Because the mines are said to be haunted. The crystals and the ridge used to be protected by Zamorak's mage, Treus Dayth.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Dayth failed and fell during an incursion by Saradominists, who then made it into the mines and were able to remove a shard of crystal.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Zamorak, furious at his mage, condemned Dayth's soul indefinitely to an existence of turmoil in the mines. Dayth's soul is bound to prevent the crystals from ever being reached again.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Further, Zamorak's then ruler upon the land ordered the slaughter of anyone within the mines and that the mines be sealed.

options.text: Is there any other way into the mines?
How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?
Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered?

steps.player: I must be going now, good luck on your quest.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: You should believe not in luck, but in the protection of Saradomin. Farewell.

steps.player: I hope it goes well.  Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Goodbye, and may Saradomin give you strength through wisdom.

steps.player: Ok I lied, I don't support Saradomin. I'm only here for dastardly evil purposes.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Then leave me, I have no time to listen to your poisonous tongue.

options.text: I could ask the same of you.

steps.player: I could ask the same of you.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin has granted you wisdom. The evil creatures of this land are cunning and you are right to question anyone's purpose here.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am upon a quest. One that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

steps.player: I serve only Zamorak. Strength through chaos.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Then begone.  Normally I would strike you down in an instant, but for now I have no time. I am on a quest of the utmost importance.

options.text: What is this quest of which you speak?

steps.player: What is this quest of which you speak?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: It is no concern of yours, but rest assured it will help in crushing you and those others who serve your vile master.

steps.player: I doubt that.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I would expect nothing less of you, misguided as you already are.

options.text: Fine, I didn't want to talk to you either.

steps.player: Fine, I didn't want to talk to you either.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Fear not fiend, even though I may leave you be, you shall not escape justice at the hands of the righteous.

options.text: My beliefs are in accord with the teachings of Guthix.

steps.player: My beliefs are in accord with the teachings of Guthix. Balance is power.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: A wishy washy set of beliefs. You should follow Saradomin and find a real purpose in your life.

options.text: And what sort of purpose would that be?

steps.player: And what sort of purpose would that be?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: To further the glory of Saradomin of course.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Take myself, I am upon a quest that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

options.text: I can make my own choices.

steps.player: I can make my own choices, who are you to dispute them?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I look only to help those who are misguided.

steps.player: I have no particular allegiance.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Then your life is without reason or direction. I would talk to you further on the matter, but for now my attentions must be elsewhere.

options.text: Then I shall leave you to your business.

steps.player: Then I shall leave you to your business.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I shall pray that Saradomin grants you the wisdom to see through your folly.

steps.player: Why, what are you doing?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am upon a quest. One that will allow Saradomin to be glorified even in these dark lands.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-again.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-again.text: Hello again. I'm afraid I'm rather preoccupied. What was it you wanted?

options.text: Can you explain the history of these mines again?

steps.player: Can you explain the history of these mines again?

options.text: Is there any other way into the mines?
options.condition: Before asking if there is any other way in:

steps.player: Is there any other way into the mines?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Indeed I have found hope that this may be so. By making discreet inquiries I have been led to believe that a second entrance may exist into the mines.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Further, I have come into possession of a key that will apparently afford entrance to the lower levels of the mines once inside.

options.text: Where is the second entrance to the mines?

steps.player: Where is the second entrance to the mines?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Of this I am not yet sure. From what I have been able to gather, it was not originally built for humans to enter by. Where it may be, I am still endeavoring to find out.

options.text: How can you be discreet with THAT star emblazoned on your robes?

steps.player: How can you be discreet with THAT star emblazoned on your robes?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin watches over me, I am not troubled by those who are not meant to notice.

steps.player: Even so, you're not exactly keeping quiet about your allegiance are you?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin will protect me. Even if I should fall there are many behind me who would stand in my place.

steps.player: Is that much consolation when you get chopped up into little pieces?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I would rather be cut into little pieces whilst proclaiming the goodness of Saradomin than hiding my faith.

options.text: I can't see anyone behind you.

steps.player: I can't see anyone behind you.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Although you may not realise it, Saradomin works quietly in many people, such is the folly of looking with your eyes and not with your heart.

options.text: And I would be one of them. So, can I borrow that key?

steps.player: And I would be one of them. So, can I borrow that key?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am afraid my task can be entrusted to nobody else. Saradomin has asked me alone to do this. I cannot take the slightest risk of losing this key. The stakes are too high.

options.text: Please? I'll be very careful with it.
I didn't want that key anyway.
You're right, I was wrong to doubt Saradomin.

steps.player: You're right, I was wrong to doubt Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Let not your faith in Saradomin falter, for all else is insignificant.

steps.player: You're nuts, goodbye.
Can I borrow your key?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am afraid my task can be entrusted to nobody else. Saradomin has asked me alone to do this. I cannot take the slightest risk of losing this key. The stakes are too high.

options.text: Please? I'll be very careful with it.

steps.player: Please? I'll be very careful with it.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: You know not what you deal with. There is evil in that mine and, whatever your assurances, I cannot risk you falling to the creatures within.

options.text: And you think you'll be safer in the mine than me?

steps.player: And you think you'll be safer in the mine than me?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Of course I'll be safe, my faith in Saradomin protects me.

steps.player: I'll trade for it.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin provides for my every need. There is nothing you could offer me.

steps.player: Pretty pretty please?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Saradomin grant me patience. The answer is no.

options.text: I didn't want that key anyway.
I didn't want that key anyway.

steps.player: I didn't want that key anyway.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Witness the goodness of Saradomin, that he has granted you the wisdom to see our positions in perspective.

options.text: How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?
Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered?
Where is the second entrance to the mines?
options.condition: After asking if there is another way into the mines:

options.text: How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?

steps.player: How does a lost artefact that was only legendary help?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Although the amulet was lost, it is my hope that if I can make it into the mines I can craft another.

options.text: Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered?

steps.player: Why was everyone in the mines slaughtered? Surely it wasn't their fault that the crystals formed?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: It is said that some of the workers in the mines, merely from being in the presence of these crystals, found themselves bestowed with the love of Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: The advantage to our cause was considered too great by some within Morytania. They set about mercilessly and brutally killing everyone in the mines rather than risk losing them to us.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Such is the treachery of the servants of evil, that they even destroy their own kind without a moments thought.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: The mines are now rumoured to be haunted by the souls of all those brutally and needlessly killed.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.text: Hello again. I'm afraid I'm rather preoccupied. What was it you wanted?

options.text: Can you explain the history of these mines again?
I've found the second entrance to the mine.
options.condition: Before reaching the sixth level of the mine:

steps.player: I've found the second entrance to the mine, I've managed to make it inside.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: You are foolhardy indeed should you venture inside. The presence of evil is strong within the mines. If you take the risk I shall pray for your safety, although I hold little hope for your safe return.
After turning the water valve and before going down the lift:

steps.player: Unfortunately I need a key to use the lift that goes to the lower levels.  Can you help?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Indeed? My own inquiries have led me into possession of a key. I was informed that this key would apparently afford entrance to the lower levels. It therefore seems likely that this is the key which you seek.

steps.player: Yes, that sounds like the one. May I borrow it?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I am afraid my task can be entrusted to nobody else. Saradomin has asked me alone to do this. I cannot take the slightest risk of losing this key. The stakes are too high.

options.text: Please? I'll be very careful with it.
I didn't want that key anyway.
I've made it in to the mines.
options.condition: After reaching the sixth level of the mine:

steps.player: I've made it in to the mines. Unfortunately some parts are too dark to navigate.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Ah ye of little faith. Let Saradomin guide you even in the darkest places. By his light you may reach your goal.

steps.player: As much as I respect your fanaticism, that was spectacularly unhelpful.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.player: G... g... g... ghost!  Scary ghost! Machinery flying everywhere.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.text: I warned you not to enter those mines. It sounds like you've met Dayth.  You must not go back down there.

options.text: Who did you say Dayth was again?

steps.player: Who did you say Dayth was again?

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Treus Dayth was Zamorak's mage in charge of defending the ridge during the time of the orginal amulet.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Dayth failed and fell during an incursion by Saradominists, who then made it into the mines and were able to remove a shard of crystal.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: Zamorak, furious at his mage, condemned Dayth's soul indefinitely to an existence of turmoil in the mines. Dayth's soul is bound to prevent the crystals from ever being reached again.

options.text: Nonsense, he'll be no match for me.

steps.player: Nonsense, he'll be no match for me.

steps.speaker: Zealot
steps.text: I don't know if you think your persistance makes you heroic, but you must realise it's just going to get you killed.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.player: I met that Dayth character you talked about. He wasn't as tough as all that.

starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.speaker: Zealot
starting-out-talking-to-the-zealot-after.text: I was afraid this would happen. The fear you must have experienced within those mines has left you delusional. There's no way you could have survived had you actually fought Dayth.

inside-the-mine-attempting-to-enter-the-.text: You're not sure what's down there, perhaps it's safer to find another route.

inside-the-mine-picking-the-glowing-fung.text: You pull the fungus from the water. It is very cold to the touch.

inside-the-mine-dropping-the-glowing-fun.text: When you drop the fungus it crumbles mysteriously to dust.

inside-the-mine-exiting-the-mine-via-the.text: As you crawl out into the sunlight, the strange fungus you are carrying crumbles to dust.

inside-the-mine-teleporting-out-with-the.text: The strange fungus you are carrying crumbles to dust.

inside-the-mine-pulling-track-levers.text: You pull the lever. The old points creak into place.

inside-the-mine-after-moving-the-cart-wi.player: I wonder if that cart is anywhere useful now?

inside-the-mine-attempting-to-open-the-l.text: This door appears to be locked.

inside-the-mine-retrieving-the-glowing-f.player: I wonder if that cart is anywhere useful now?

inside-the-mine-retrieving-the-glowing-f.prompt: There's a glowing fungus I placed in here earlier.

steps.text: glowing fungus

inside-the-mine-retrieving-the-glowing-f.text: I just went to all the effort of getting this over here. I'm not sending it back.

inside-the-mine-turning-the-water-valve.text: If the player has not used the zealot's key on the valve:

steps.text: The valve seems to be locked in position. There is a small keyhole in the side.

inside-the-mine-turning-the-water-valve.text: If the player has used the zealot's key on the valve:

steps.text: The key unlocks the valve.
You open the valve. Water begins to flow through the lift mechanism.

inside-the-mine-turning-the-water-valve.text: If the mischievous ghost closes the valve:

steps.text: You hear the sound of a valve being turned.

inside-the-mine-mischievous-ghost-appear.text: You hear the sound of a valve being turned.

inside-the-mine-taking-the-lift.text: You get in the lift. Now powered, the lift descends further into the mines...
...plunging you straight into the middle of a flooded with water.
It's unlikely any of your light sources will dry off until you leave this dank cave.

steps.player: It's kind of dark down here. I should probably find a light source before going further.
Hey - my light source isn't working! I'd better find a more suitable one before trying to go any further.

inside-the-mine-taking-the-lift-attempti.text: This door appears to be locked.

inside-the-mine-attempting-to-take-the-i.text: The key floats away as the player tries to grab it before resting on the crate again.
You hear a disembodied voice laughing at you....Poor puny mortal. I'm going to have fun with you.
Treus appears, and strikes the player with the loading crane behind them.
I should deal with that ghost before trying to take the key again.

inside-the-mine-upon-killing-treus-dayth.text: As you make the killing strike, the machinery within the room falls silent.

inside-the-mine-taking-the-crystal-mine-.text: You take the key. It doesn't resist anymore.
You already have a key like that.
You should cut a shard from one of the crystals before leaving.

inside-the-mine-chiseling-a-crystal-outc.text: You cut a shard from the crystal.

starting-off.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
starting-off.text: Blooming, thieving cultists! Why don't they leave me alone? String them all up, that's what I say!

steps.player: What's wrong?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: It's those blooming cultists from the south! They keep breaking into my house!

steps.player: Have they taken much?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Well... no. They stole a suit of armour when they first broke in months ago, but they've been back four more times since then and taken nothing.

steps.player: I see. And you are?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: You don't know me? Why, I am Sir Ceril Carnillean! Mine is quite a famous bloodline, you know. We've played a vital role in the politics of Ardougne for many generations.

steps.player: Well I'm [player name]. Maybe I can help you with these cultists?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Interesting... I suppose the authorities haven't been much help so far. Yes, very well. If you return the stolen armour, I will provide you with a modest cash reward!
If the player is below level 10 combat:
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 10.

steps.prompt: Start the Hazeel Cult quest?

steps.player: Yes, of course, I'd be happy to help.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: That's very noble of you! Keep that attitude up and one day you might have the honour of working full-time for someone like me.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Now, I caught a glimpse of the thieves leaving, but due to... uh... my cold, I was unable to give chase.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: What I do know is that they belong to some sort of cult. They seem to be based in a cave just south of the city, near the Clock Tower.

steps.player: How do you know that?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: My old butler, Higson, once followed them there. Unfortunately, the next night he died in his sleep.

steps.player: That's awful!

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: No, it's okay. Jones, a replacement from the Servants' Guild, arrived the next day. He's been great - makes an excellent broth!

steps.player: Right... I'll see if I can find this cave.
No thanks. I've got other plans.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Well no wonder I'm the one with the big house and you're the one on the streets.

steps.player: You probably deserve it.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: And who are you to judge me? You look like a peasant anyway. I'm wasting my time talking to you.

options.text: You seem uptight, I'll leave you alone.

steps.player: You seem uptight. I'll leave you alone.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Yes, I doubt you could help anyway.

starting-off-talking-to-ceril-again.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
starting-off-talking-to-ceril-again.text: That's Sir Ceril to you, you impudent scamp. Show a bit of respect to your betters. Now, shouldn't you be recovering my armour?

starting-off-talking-to-ceril-again.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
starting-off-talking-to-ceril-again.text: Good. I suggest you start with that cave south of the city, near the Clock Tower. That is where the cult is based.

starting-off-talking-to-henryeta.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
starting-off-talking-to-henryeta.text: Oh, hello. I'm afraid I'm not very presentable at the moment. I've been under incredible stress of late! It's ruining my complexion!

starting-off-talking-to-henryeta.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
starting-off-talking-to-henryeta.text: It's those awful cultists! I just don't feel safe here anymore!

starting-off-talking-to-philipe.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
starting-off-talking-to-philipe.text: Mommy said you're here to kill all the nasty people that keep breaking in.

starting-off-talking-to-claus.speaker: Claus the Chef
starting-off-talking-to-claus.text: Sorry, can't stop to chat! You would be amazed at how many meals this family gets through daily!

starting-off-talking-to-claus-inspecting.text: A pot of soup is bubbling away on the range.

starting-off-talking-to-claus-using-any-.speaker: Claus the Chef
starting-off-talking-to-claus-using-any-.text: Oi - I don't want people messing around with my range!

starting-off-trying-to-use-the-raft.speaker: Clivet
starting-off-trying-to-use-the-raft.text: Hey! I don't remember saying you could use that raft!

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: You can call me Clivet. What do you want, adventurer?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: Carnilleans? Don't think I've ever heard of them.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.player: Look, I know you're lying. I know all about your cult.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: Is that so? In that case, I'd say you'd be wise to leave now.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.player: Unfortunately, I have a job to do. I'm not leaving until it's done.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: Ah, I see. That two-faced snob has made you fall for his propaganda, eh?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: The Carnillean home does not belong to them. It was built long ago by the great Lord Hazeel, who once ruled over this entire region.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: Many years ago, the Carnilleans led a rebellion against Lord Hazeel and all who followed him. Under the cover of darkness, they stormed his home in an angry mob, torturing and butchering everyone they found.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: The following morning, the Carnillean forefathers moved into the empty household and claimed it as their own. They have grown fat on the hard work of Lord Hazeel ever since.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.player: Right... And what happened to this Hazeel?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: The foolish Carnilleans believed him dead. Unluckily for them, being an all-powerful Mahjarrat gave him access to powers and enchantments they knew nothing of.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: As they stormed his home, Lord Hazeel made preparations for his eventual return. We, his faithful followers, have been working to bring that about ever since.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.player: What makes you think I care about the politics and histories of Ardougne?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: I could kill you right now and be done with it, but I don't think you're the fool that the Carnilleans believe you to be. Instead, I offer you a chance to join us.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: Help us bring about the return of Lord Hazeel, and you will be well rewarded. However, should you continue to try and prevent his return, you will suffer the wrath of Zamorak.

options.text: Before I decide, I have some questions for you.

steps.player: Before I decide, I have some questions for you.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Very well.

steps.player: Tell me more about Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Lord Hazeel is one of the great Mahjarrat who once fought alongside Zamorak himself. He ruled this region for many years, until the cowardly Carnilleans rebelled against him.

steps.player: But he survived?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Of course! The Mahjarrat know magic that others can only dream of. Lord Hazeel used his abilities to ensure that one day he'd eventually return. That day will soon be upon us.

options.text: Why did the Carnilleans rebel against Hazeel?

steps.player: Why did the Carnilleans rebel against Hazeel?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: The Carnilleans served the pathetic Saradomin. They considered it their duty to overthrow Hazeel due to his loyalties to Zamorak. They were fools, blinded by Saradominist propaganda!

steps.player: Saradominist propaganda?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Yes! Something even more prevalent today. Too many people now are fooled into believing that Saradomin is a god of good, while Zamorak is evil. Those lies couldn't be further from the truth!

options.text: Why do you keep breaking into the Carnillean Mansion?

steps.player: Why do you keep breaking into the Carnillean Mansion?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: There is something we need inside. I will say no more unless you agree to join us.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Mahjarrat?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Mahjarrat?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Surely you have heard of the Mahjarrat? Their race is the ultimate example of power! Each of them wields the strength of an entire army. To oppose any one of them, is to face your doom!

steps.player: And Hazeel is one of them?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: More than that! Hazeel is one of the greatest Mahjarrat to have ever lived!

steps.player: I see.
I have no more questions.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Then we have nothing more to discuss until you've made your choice.

steps.player: Alright, I've made my decision.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: And?

steps.player: I'll help you.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Good. Now, we are not the monsters that the Carnilleans would claim we are, so we were hoping to do this without violence. However, the fact they sent you here makes it clear that won't work now.

steps.player: Meaning?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: You must prove your loyalty to our cause, and Ceril Carnillean must die. Kill him for us, and we will know you are truly dedicated to Lord Hazeel.

options.text: Alright, how do I do it?

steps.player: Alright, how do I do it?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: I can already tell I was right about you. I can see you are of exactly the right character to join the followers of Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Here, take this poison and pour it into Ceril Carnillean's food. Once the deed is done, return here and speak to me once more.
If the player has a full inventory:
Clivet tries to give you some poison, but you don't have enough room to take it.
If the player inventory space:
Clivet gives you some poison.

options.text: I need some time to think on this.

steps.player: I won't help you.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Then you are a fool. Go back to your small-minded little life. You will never know the glories you could have tasted as one of us!

steps.player: You know I'm going to stop you, right?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: You'll try, but you'll never find us.
Clivet jumps onto the nearby raft and pushes off into the sewer system.

options.text: Actually, I need more time to think on this.

steps.player: Actually, I need more time to think on this.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Don't take too long.

options.text: I need some time to think on this.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.text: So, you've returned. I hope you're here because you've recognised the folly in serving the Carnilleans. Think about what you could achieve if you join us instead.

options.text: Before I decide, I have some questions for you.
I need some time to think on this.

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.speaker: Alomone
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.text: How did you get in here?

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.player: I've come for the Carnillean family armour. Hand it over, or face the consequences.

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.speaker: Alomone
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.text: I thought I made it clear to Jones that you could not be allowed to interfere with our mission. The incompetent fool must be going soft.

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.player: So the butler's part of your little cult? Why is it always the butler? I should have known...

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.speaker: Alomone
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-a.text: Well you won't live long enough to tell anyone! Die!

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-c.speaker: Clivet
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-c.text: You! Leave this place at once, before we're forced to make you!

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-h.speaker: Hazeel Cultist
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-h.text: You have no place here! Leave now, before someone makes you!

joining-the-carnillean-side-if-alomone-i.text: If the player has a full inventory:

steps.text: You find some armour in the chest, but you don't have enough room to take it.

joining-the-carnillean-side-if-alomone-i.text: If the player has enough space:

steps.text: You find some armour in the chest.

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.text: Hello, adventurer. How are you doing with your quest?

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.player: Drop the act, Jones. I know you're in league with the cultists.

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.text: Have you hit your head? That's a preposterous accusation!

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.player: Really? So you won't mind me telling Ceril then?

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-b.text: Oh, you think he'll take your word over mine? He trusts me completely!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: You're back. Have you had any luck yet?

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Well done! I must say I am very impressed! Come on, hand it over.
You give the armour to Ceril.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Before we send you on your way with your payment, I'll just get Jones to whip you up a batch of his special broth.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.player: I'd rather not if it's all the same to you. Apparently Jones is in league with the cultists.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: What? Right! You! We're going to blooming well sort this out right now, once and for all!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Jones! This commoner says you had something to do with the cultists that stole my armour. What do you have to say for yourself?

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Nothing to do with me, sir. I am, as you know, a loyal servant.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Humph. Quite right too. I cannot fathom why this scoundrel would accuse you of such a crime without evidence to back up the accusations.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Right, I have made a decision. I have given my word as a nobleman to reward you for your efforts in retrieving my armour, but I must also compensate Jones for this terrible slander.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Now take this and leave! And don't darken my doorstep again!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Don't worry, sir, he won't be bothering us any more.
Jones smirks at you. You are going to need more than words to prove his treachery.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: I owe you nothing you scoundrel! Now get out or I'll have Jones throw you out!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: You! Don't think you can go around insulting our trusted staff and then waltz up to me as though nothing has happened!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.player: Everything I said was the truth.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Ha! Don't be so ridiculous! Next you'll be trying to tell me that Jones murdered our old butler!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Daddy says you don't like Mr Jones. Mr Jones is nice. He brings me toys and sweets.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Well if you think that, I don't like you!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.player: Well I'll do my best to console myself over your feelings towards me.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: I believe you've been asked to leave, adventurer.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.player: You won't get away with this, Jones! I know who you really are!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: That's quite enough of that. All of us here are starting to tire of your theatrics.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.player: This isn't over! I will find proof!

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Claus the Chef
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Hello. How are you today?

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Claus the Chef
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Good good.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Guard
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: Hello, adventurer. I hear you accused Jones of being part of that cult. Is that true?

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.player: It is, but nobody believes me.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Guard
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: You have my utter faith, adventurer. I can't openly defy Sir Ceril, but I'd like you to know that I think you're on the right track with this.

joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.speaker: Guard
joining-the-carnillean-side-returning-th.text: I always found it suspicious that Jones would just show up on the doorstep the very day after the old butler died. Good luck in clearing your name

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: You search the cupboard and find a bottle of poison along with a mysterious amulet.

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.player: And what do we have here...

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: What do you want now you scoundrel?

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.player: Take a look at what I've found.

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: Right... but this amulet... I recognise this! Those cultists wore amulets like this!

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: Jones! We trusted you! We took you into our home!

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: You senile old fool... it was all too easy! I should have killed you and your pathetic family weeks ago!

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: This man is one of those cultists! Take him away!

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: Don't think this is over, Ceril! You will die at the hands of the Hazeel Cult! I promise you that!

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: Well... It looks like I am indebted to you!

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.player: No problem. We all make mistakes.

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: But if it weren't for you... my whole family... we could have been...

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: I apologise for my harshness before. The very least I can do is to reward you for your noble efforts, and to offer my sincerest apologies as a gentleman.

joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-accusing-the.text: No, no, thank you! Feel free to stop by anytime, adventurer!

after-quest-completion-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
after-quest-completion-talking-to-ceril.text: Hello again, adventurer! It's good to see you! If it wasn't for your quick thinking, the treacherous Jones would have probably poisoned my family and I by now! We are in your debt.

after-quest-completion-talking-to-ceril.player: Don't worry about it! A good deed is its own reward. And that money didn't hurt either.

after-quest-completion-talking-to-guard.speaker: Guard
after-quest-completion-talking-to-guard.text: Well look who it is! Good to see you managed to clear your name. I always had faith in you!

after-quest-completion-talking-to-guard.player: Thanks! So is everything all quiet around here now?

after-quest-completion-talking-to-guard.speaker: Guard
after-quest-completion-talking-to-guard.text: Indeed! For now at least, everything is back to normal.

after-quest-completion-talking-to-philip.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
after-quest-completion-talking-to-philip.text: What have you brought me? I want some more toys!

after-quest-completion-talking-to-philip.player: I'm afraid I don't have any toys.

after-quest-completion-talking-to-henrye.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
after-quest-completion-talking-to-henrye.text: Hello again, adventurer. Since you dealt with those horrible cultists, things have vastly improved for us around here!

after-quest-completion-talking-to-claus.speaker: Claus the Chef
after-quest-completion-talking-to-claus.text: Well hello there, adventurer! Are we fit and well?

joining-the-hazeel-side-obtaining-the-po.speaker: Clivet
joining-the-hazeel-side-obtaining-the-po.text: Here's that poison you need. Take it and pour it into Ceril Carnillean's food. Once the deed is done, return here and speak to me once more.
If the player has a full inventory:

steps.text: Clivet tries to give you some poison, but you don't have enough room to take it.
Clivet gives you some poison.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-clive.speaker: Clivet
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-clive.text: You have a mission for us, adventurer. Go to the Carnilliean household and poison Ceril Carnillean's meal to prove your loyalty.
If the player has poison in their inventory:
If the player has no poison in their inventory:

steps.player: I need some more poison.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Fool! Be more careful with it this time.
If the player has a full inventory:
Clivet tries to give you some poison, but you don't have enough room to take it.
If the player inventory space:
Clivet gives you some poison.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.text: Hello, adventurer. I hear your quest is going well.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.text: Oh yes. Do keep up the good work.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: You're back. Have you had any luck yet?

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: That's Sir Ceril you blooming scoundrel! Show respect when addressing someone of my rank! I must say, I am a bit disapointed you haven't made any progress. Maybe I was wrong about you.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.player: Yeah, well, just unlucky I guess.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.text: Oh, hello. I hope you've found those awful cultists! I simply cannot sleep at night knowing they're loose!

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.player: I'm afraid I haven't found them yet.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.text: Well you really are useless, aren't you?

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-phili.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-phili.text: Mommy said you're here to kill all the nasty people that keep breaking in.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-claus.speaker: Claus the Chef
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-claus.text: You're that adventurer the family asked to help deal with those weird cultists, right?

joining-the-hazeel-side-inspecting-the-r.text: A pot of soup is bubbling away on the range.

joining-the-hazeel-side-inspecting-the-r.prompt: Pour the poison into the pot?

steps.text: You pour the poison into the pot and it dissolves into the soup.

joining-the-hazeel-side-using-the-poison.text: You pour the poison into the pot and it dissolves into the soup.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-claus.speaker: Claus the Chef
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-claus.text: Hello there. Caught any of those weird cultists yet?

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.text: Those hooligans! They slaughtered my precious Scruffy! I shall never recover! I am emotionally scarred for life!

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-henry.player: Yeah... Hopefully someone finds them soon.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.text: Hello, adventurer. Such a terrible shame about Scruffy. I wonder if the family will ever fully recover.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.text: Anyway, I hear your quest is going well.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.speaker: Butler Jones
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-butle.text: Oh yes. Do keep up the good work.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: Oh the inhumanity... the cruelty... the misery... the pain...

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: My son is a good boy, really, but how could he give his dinner to Scruffy without having the servants test it for poison first? How? How could he be so thoughtless and careless? He knows we are all under threat!

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: He's been with our family for twenty years... that's 140 in dog years! The poor dog... What did he ever do to deserve such a fate?

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.player: Your dog got poisoned? That's not right.

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: I agree! I hope whichever evildoer is responsible gets the full weight of the law brought upon them!

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.text: Oh the misery... How could someone do something like this?

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-ceril.player: Uh... I'm sure they won't get away with it...

joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-the-g.speaker: Guard
joining-the-hazeel-side-talking-to-the-g.text: Today is a dark day. Those cultists have been back, and this time they've gone further than ever before! Murder! We can't afford to keep letting them get away with this.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.player: I poisoned the food as requested, but it didn't quite go to plan.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.text: Yes, we heard all about it from one of our sources. It's a shame that Ceril Carnillean survived, but that is no fault of yours. You have proven your loyalty to Hazeel.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.text: I would like you to meet with our leader, Alomone. You'll find him in our hideout, deeper in the sewers. You can use this raft to get there.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.text: However, be warned that reaching the hideout is impossible unless the flow of water down here is set correctly. You'll need to use the sewer valves above to do that.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.player: But how will I know how to set the valves?

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.text: If the player has a full inventory:

steps.text: Clivet tries to give you an amulet, but you don't have enough room to take it.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Clivet gives you an amulet.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Going from left to right, turn each of the five sewer valves above so that they follow the design of the amulet. Once you've done that, you'll be able to use the raft here to enter our hideout.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-if-the-play.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-if-the-play.text: Going from left to right, turn each of the five sewer valves above so that they follow the design of the amulet. Once you've done that, you'll be able to use the raft here to enter our hideout.

the-scroll-reclaiming-a-lost-amulet.player: I lost that amulet you gave me.

the-scroll-reclaiming-a-lost-amulet.text: If the player has a full inventory:

steps.text: Clivet tries to give you an amulet, but you don't have enough room to take it.

the-scroll-reclaiming-a-lost-amulet.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Clivet gives you an amulet.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.player: What am I meant to be doing?

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.text: Use the raft here to enter our hideout and meet with our leader, Alomone.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.text: Be warned, you'll need to ensure the flow of water down here is set correctly for you to be able to use the raft.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again.text: Going from left to right, turn each of the five sewer valves above so that they follow the design of the amulet I gave you.

the-scroll-using-the-raft.text: The current is flowing against the raft. It won't move.

the-scroll-inspecting-a-sewer-valve-that.prompt: The valve is currently turned to the right.

steps.text: You turn the valve to the left. Beneath your feet you hear the sudden sound of rushing water.

the-scroll-inspecting-a-sewer-valve-that.prompt: The valve is currently turned to the left.

steps.text: You turn the valve to the right. Beneath your feet you hear the sudden sound of rushing water.

the-scroll-one-valve-set-correctly.text: The raft washes up the sewer and stops at the first island. You'll need to find the right combination of the five sewer valves above if you want to go further.
The raft flows back to the cave entrance.

the-scroll-two-valves-set-correctly.text: The raft washes up the sewer and stops at the second island. You'll need to find the right combination of the five sewer valves above if you want to go further.
The raft flows back to the cave entrance.

the-scroll-three-valves-set-correctly.text: The raft washes up the sewer and stops at the fourth island. You'll need to find the right combination of the five sewer valves above if you want to go further.
The raft flows back to the cave entrance.

the-scroll-four-valves-set-correctly.text: The raft washes up the sewer and stops at the third island. You'll need to find the right combination of the five sewer valves above if you want to go further.
The raft flows back to the cave entrance.

the-scroll-sucessfully-using-the-raft-wi.text: The raft washes up the sewer until it reaches the end of the passage.

the-scroll-talking-to-a-hazeel-cultist.speaker: Hazeel Cultist
the-scroll-talking-to-a-hazeel-cultist.text: I cannot talk right now. Lord Hazeel will soon be back with us and I have many preparations to make.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.text: Well, well, well... we have a new recruit. Clivet told me of your desire to join us in our glorious task to resurrect the mighty Hazeel.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.text: Well if all goes well, you'll play a key role in just that. Before his defeat, Hazeel secured within his home a powerful magical scroll of restoration. It remains there still, hidden to even the foolish Carnilleans.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.text: Up to now, our attempts to recover this scroll have been met with disappointment. However, I know you will not fail us.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.player: So you want me to find this scroll?

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.text: That is correct. You must return to the Carnillean Mansion and find where it is hidden. We already have an agent in place to support you.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.text: Indeed. Their Butler Jones is in fact a faithful follower of Hazeel. He has been unsuccessful in locating the scroll himself, but together the two of you will find it.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone.text: Now, go with haste. Soon we will restore Hazeel to his true power and glory!

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone-again.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone-again.text: Hazeel has already waited far too long for his return. It is imperative that you find that scroll! It hides somewhere within the Carnillean Mansion.

the-scroll-taking-the-raft-back.text: The raft flows back to the cave entrance.

the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again-2.speaker: Clivet
the-scroll-talking-to-clivet-again-2.text: It is good to see you once more, adventurer. Glory to Hazeel!

the-scroll-talking-to-ceril.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
the-scroll-talking-to-ceril.text: Oh cruel world! Scruffy... I knew you well... I... just... don't think I can... go on without...
Sir Ceril breaks down into tears.

the-scroll-talking-to-ceril.player: Loosen up already. It was only a DOG.

the-scroll-talking-to-butler-jones.speaker: Butler Jones
the-scroll-talking-to-butler-jones.text: Hello, adventurer. I hear your quest is going well.

the-scroll-talking-to-butler-jones.player: I'm making progress. On that note, I hear you might be able to help me with my next task.

the-scroll-talking-to-butler-jones.speaker: Butler Jones
the-scroll-talking-to-butler-jones.text: Ah yes, the scroll. I'm afraid I've searched high and low, but have so far been unable to locate it. I'm sure it is somewhere within the house, hidden where even the family won't find it.

the-scroll-talking-to-butler-jones.player: Hmm... So it must be somewhere they'd have never stepped foot. I'll keep on looking.

the-scroll-using-the-knock-at-wall.text: You knock on the wall. It sounds like there's a hollow space on the other side.

steps.text: The player enters the wall.

the-scroll-chest-without-the-key.text: The chest is locked. It looks like it needs a key.

steps.text: You search the crate and find an old key hidden at the bottom, but you don't have enough room to take it.
You search the crate and find an old key hidden at the bottom.

the-scroll-searching-the-crate-in-the-ki.text: You search the crate but find nothing of interest.

steps.text: You unlock the chest and find a scroll inside, but you don't have enough room to take it.
You unlock the chest and find a scroll inside.

the-scroll-opening-the-chest-searching-t.text: You already have the scroll from this chest.

the-scroll-talking-to-jones-after-obtain.speaker: Butler Jones
the-scroll-talking-to-jones-after-obtain.text: Hello, adventurer. How is your quest going?
If the player does not have the scroll:

steps.player: I'm making progress.

steps.speaker: Butler Jones
steps.text: Good. Remember, the scroll must be somewhere within the house, hidden where even the family won't find it.

steps.player: Hmm... I'll keep on looking.

the-scroll-talking-to-jones-after-obtain.text: If the player has the scroll:

steps.player: I have the scroll!

steps.speaker: Butler Jones
steps.text: Then you should waste no time in returning to Alomone. The return of Hazeel will soon be upon us!

the-scroll-talking-to-hentryeta-after-ob.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
the-scroll-talking-to-hentryeta-after-ob.text: I'm sorry. I am far too upset to talk to anybody right now. Oh... poor Scruffy...

the-scroll-talking-to-the-guard-after-ob.speaker: Guard
the-scroll-talking-to-the-guard-after-ob.text: Hello, adventurer. I hope you find the cult soon. We have a horrible suspicion that there's been another burglary.

the-scroll-talking-to-the-guard-after-ob.speaker: Guard
the-scroll-talking-to-the-guard-after-ob.text: Yes, it is. The thing is, we can't even work out what they've taken! It's all very odd.

the-scroll-taking-the-raft.text: The raft washes up the sewer until it reaches the end of the passage.

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone-after-obta.speaker: Alomone
the-scroll-talking-to-alomone-after-obta.text: Have you brought the scroll of restoration?
If the player has the scroll in their inventory:

steps.player: Yes, I have it right here.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: At long last! With the words contained within this scroll, our lord shall finally return to us!

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Watch adventurer, and witness the glorious rebirth of Hazeel!
Alomone begins to revive Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Sentente sillaberi junque dithmento! Ia! Ia! Dextrimon encanto! Termando... Imcando... Solly enty rando... Sentente! Ia! Ia! Indenti zaggarati g'thxa!

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Dintenta! Sententa! Retenta! Q'exjta! Ia! Sottottott! Ia! Dysmenta junque fammatio svelken! Sottey! Sentey! Soloment!
Hazeel awakens from the coffin.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: My loyal followers, I have pride in you all. You have achieved a feat many would have considered impossible and returned me to this land.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Much time has passed and I have much to attend to, but first, I believe there is one here who deserves my gratitude.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Adventurer, I know that your efforts were essential in bringing about my return. You have my thanks. Know that I consider you an ally.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Now, I must leave you, loyal subjects, for time is short. My Mahjarrat kin will soon head northwards, and I have much to prepare.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Rest assured, when my work is done, I will return to you. Before long, the world will know of Hazeel once more!
Quest complete

the-scroll-talking-to-alomone-after-obta.text: If the player does not have the scroll in their inventory:

steps.player: Nope, sorry.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: You must find it and bring it to me! Hazeel has already waited far too long for his return.

C3CzKz.speaker: Guard
C3CzKz.text: Hello there. I hear you're after that cult who broke in the other night. It always gladdens me when civilians assist the law like this.

C3CzKz.player: I'm just happy to be of help.

x2-KnX.player: I need some time to think on this.

pnFVX0.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
pnFVX0.text: Someone killed Scruffy. I liked Scruffy. He never told me off.

C8J0t-.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
C8J0t-.text: Sir Ceril! Sir! And things are terrible! Our beloved dog is dead, and I fear it's only a matter of time before those cultists strike again!

C8J0t-.player: Don't worry, I'm sure it will all be okay in the end.

zGZzwo.speaker: Claus the Chef
zGZzwo.text: I just don't understand it! How? How could someone poison my delicious food without me even noticing? I... I just don't get it!

zGZzwo.speaker: Claus the Chef
zGZzwo.text: Oh man... I hope I don't lose my job over this... but how? How did they do it? And why would they want to kill poor Scruffy anyway? He was such a good dog...

starting-off.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
starting-off.text: Blooming, thieving, weirdo cultists! Why don't they leave me alone? String 'em all up, that's what I say!

steps.player: What's wrong?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: It's those blooming cultists from the forest! Those freaks keep breaking into my house!

steps.player: Have they taken much?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: They first broke in months ago and stole a suit of armour. The strange thing is that they've broken in four times since but taken nothing.

steps.player: And you are...?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Why, I am Sir Ceril Carnillean! We really are quite a famous bloodline... who've played a vital role in the politics of Ardougne for many generations.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Perhaps you would be able to assist me in returning the stolen armour? For a modest cash reward of course!

options.text: No thanks. I've got other plans.

steps.player: No thanks. I've got other plans.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: No wonder I'm the one with the big house, and you're the one on the streets.

options.text: Yes, of course, I'd be happy to help.

steps.player: Yes, of course, I'd be happy to help.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: That's very noble of you sirrah! I caught a glimpse of the thieves leaving but due to... uh.. yeah, my cold I was unable to give chase.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: They're some kind of crazy cult who dress all in black, and hang out near the cave entrance in the forest south of here.

steps.player: How do you know that?

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: My old butler, Higson, once followed them to their hideout there. Unfortunately the next night he died in his sleep.

steps.player: That's awful!

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: No, it's ok. A replacement arrived the next day. He's been great - cooks an excellent broth!

steps.player: Ok. I'll see what I can do.
You probably deserve it.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: And who are YOU to judge ME? Hmmm. You look like a peasant anyway. I'm wasting my time talking to you.

options.text: You seem uptight, I'll leave you alone.

steps.player: You seem uptight. I'll leave you alone.

steps.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
steps.text: Yes, I doubt you could help anyway.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones.speaker: Butler Jones
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones.text: This is the home of Sir Ceril Carnillean of the noble Carnillean family. You're welcome to look around, but I'm afraid I'll have to keep an eye on you.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones.speaker: Butler Jones
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones.text: Recently we've been having a real problem with thieves and strange cultists coming out of the forest for some reason.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones.speaker: Butler Jones
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones.text: Yes, well, these things are bound to happen when you're as wealthy as the Carnilleans.

options.text: Have you any more info on the Carnilleans?

steps.player: Have you any more info on the Carnilleans?

steps.speaker: Butler Jones
steps.text: There's a lot I could tell you about the Carnillean family history. However, I'm afraid if I did speak about such matters I would be at risk of losing my job.

options.text: How long have you worked here?

steps.player: Ok then, take care.

steps.speaker: Butler Jones
steps.text: You too.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones-usi.speaker: Claus Carnillean
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jones-usi.text: Oi - I don't want people messing around with my range!

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: You mind your business, I'll mind mine.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.player: Look, I KNOW you're hiding something. I've heard theres a cult hideout down here.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: If you want to stay healthy you'll leave now.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: So... that two faced cold hearted snob has made you fall for his propaganda eh?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.player: Sir Ceril Carnillean is a man of honour!

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: Is he now? Is he REALLY? There is a lot more to the Carnilleans than meets the eye you fool...

confronting-the-hazeel-cult.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult.text: And none of it is honourable.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: The Carnillean home does not belong to them. The builder of the house was Lord Hazeel, one of the Mahjarrat followers of Zamorak. Many years ago there was a civil war

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: in this land, and the hateful Saradominists declared war upon all Zamorakians who lived here. Lord Hazeel nobly would not repent his beliefs, and the Carnilleans harrassed

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Hazeel and his followers for many decades. One fateful night, under cover of darkness, they stormed his home in an angry mob torturing and butchering all loyal

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Zamorakians they encountered inside. The following morning, the Carnillean forefathers moved into the empty household and claimed it as their own.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: They have grown fat on the hard work of Lord Hazeel ever since. Unluckily for them Lord Hazeel as a Mahjarrat had access to powers and enchantments they knew nothing

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: about, and made preparations for his return when first they began to storm his home. Soon the day will come when he will return to wreak his vengeance upon the thieves!

steps.player: The politics and histories of Ardougne do not concern me. I have been given a job and intend to see it through to the end.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Well then friend, perhaps I can offer you a different job then? Sooner or later Our master WILL return to this land; those faithful to him will be well rewarded.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Join our cult and assist us in his restoration, and you will be well rewarded; try and prevent his return and suffer the wrath of Zamorak and the Mahjarrat.

options.text: You're crazy, I'd never help you.

steps.player: You're crazy, I'd never help you.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Then you are a fool. Go back to your small minded mundane little life; you will never know the glories you could have tasted as one of us!
The man jumps onto the raft and pushes off down into the sewer system.
Clivet: You'll never find us...

options.text: So what would I have to do?

steps.player: So what would I have to do?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: You must prove your loyalty to our cause. Killing one of the Carnillean household should be sufficient proof of your dedication to resurrecting our master Lord Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: So what say you adventurer? Join our side against the Carnillean thieves?

steps.player: No. I won't do it.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Then you are a fool. Go back to your small minded, mundane little life; you will never know the glories you could have tasted as one of us!

steps.player: Ok, count me in.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Excellent. It takes a rare character to see through the cursed Carnillean lies. I can tell you are a [man/lady] of exactly the right character to join the followers of Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Here. Take this poison. Pour it into their food, and once the deed is done, return here and speak to me once more.
Poison (item)

options.text: I've heard enough of your rubbish.

steps.player: I've heard enough of your rubbish!

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Then leave, fool!

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.speaker: Clivet
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.text: So. You've returned. Now do you want to know the truth about the 'honourable' Carnilleans?

options.text: I've heard enough of your rubbish.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-using-the-ra.text: The current is flowing against the raft. It will not move.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-turning-the-.text: You turn the large metal valve to the right. Beneath your feet you can hear the sudden sound of rushing water from the sewer.
You turn the large metal valve to the left. Beneath your feet you can hear the sudden sound of rushing water from the sewer.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-sucessfully-.text: The raft washes up the sewer, past the islands until it reaches the end of the sewer passage.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.speaker: Alomone
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.text: How did YOU get in here?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.player: I've come for the Carnillean family armour. Hand it over, or face the consequences.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.speaker: Alomone
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.text: I thought I made it clear to the butler you could not be allowed to interfere with our mission. The incompetent fool must be going soft.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.player: So the butler's part of your sordid little cult huh? Why is it ALWAYS the butler? I should have known...

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.speaker: Alomone
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.text: Well you won't live long enough to tell anyone! DIE!!!

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.speaker: Hazeel Cultist
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-a.text: What? Who are you and why did you come here? It doesn't matter, leave now adventurer. While you still can.

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.text: That's SIR Ceril to you, you impudent scamp. Show a bit of respect to your betters. And shouldn't you be recovering my armour?

confronting-the-hazeel-cult-talking-to-c.player: Yeah yeah, I'm on it, I'm ON it.

joining-the-carnillean-side.speaker: Clivet
joining-the-carnillean-side.text: You're more of a fool than you look if you think you will ever find it. When Lord Hazeel is revived you will be first to grovel for his mercy!

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-c.speaker: Ceril Carnillean
joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-c.text: Have you had any luck yet?

joining-the-carnillean-side-talking-to-c.player: Hello Ceril. Yes, I found their hideout.
