steps.player: Well, I infiltrated one of the gangs here in Varrock...

steps.npc: We have gangs?

steps.player: Erm, yes...anyway, I managed to get half the shield back.

steps.npc: Only half?

steps.player: Yes. The gangs had a bit of a tiff, you see. A friend helped me get the other half and I returned it here to get my reward.

steps.npc: Yes, yes, we were most pleased to have the shield returned - as was the King, I imagine. This is wonderful news, I shall make sure the display is updated at once! Display number 24, 5th Age, year 700-800.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.

steps.player: Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.

steps.npc: You're welcome!

steps.text: If the player has Rune Mysteries completed:

steps.player: I helped the Order of Wizards rediscover how to access the Rune Essence Mine.

steps.npc: Ah, I heard about that. Tell me more.

steps.player: Hmm. I can't tell you much, but I do know that this mine is hidden away. You can only get there by teleportation.

steps.npc: Sounds like magic to me! I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 21, the first display of the 5th Age.

steps.text: If the player has Observatory Quest completed:

steps.player: I helped to rebuild the Observatory near Ardougne. I had to fight to do it, and learn how to use the telescope too. I can draw you a diagram of the Observatory if it would help.

steps.npc: That would help immensely. Restored it, eh? And it works, you say? Excellent, perhaps we can get to some real stargazing now! Display number 17, 5th Age, year 70.

steps.text: If the player has Merlin's Crystal completed:

steps.player: I helped to free the wizard, Merlin, by using Excalibur...

steps.npc: Is that some kind of spell?

steps.player: No, it's a sword. King Arthur's sword.

steps.npc: What kingdom does he rule then?

steps.player: Britain...

steps.npc: Where on Gielinor is that?

steps.player: It's not! That's what I've been trying to tell you. I found that King Arthur and his knights are really biding their time here in Gielinor until they are called back to their own world, when they are needed!

steps.npc: That's amazing! So he's really from another world! Well, this is interesting, I'll make sure a display is put up immediately. Well done, [player name]! Display number 9, 5th Age, year 132.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.

steps.player: Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.

steps.npc: You're welcome!

steps.text: If the player has The Grand Tree completed:

steps.player: I helped to save the gnomes' Grand Tree!

steps.npc: Oh? You mean those little green fellows with their gliders?

steps.player: Yes. I uncovered this nasty character called Glough and ended up being ambushed by a black demon...

steps.npc: A black demon! How did you survive!?

steps.player: Oh, I was fine. After the demon it was downhill all the way, and King Narnode allowed me to use the mine under the Tree, and free passage on gnome gliders.

steps.npc: You mean that those flimsy things can fly with more than a gnome in? That is unexpected. I shall update the display immediately. Display number 10, upstairs in the middle of the room!

steps.text: If the player has Priest in Peril completed:

steps.player: Some disturbing and heroic news from Morytania, concerning the River Salve and the Temple Knights.

steps.npc: Ahh, the Temple Knights...little is known of them.

steps.player: Yes, it seems that these seven knights drove back the nasty things coming out of Morytania, and Saradomin blessed the Salve to stop them getting back.

steps.npc: Quite worrying that it's just a bit of water keeping them there, but Saradomin will protect us I've no doubt. Thank you for the information, I'll get a display put up. Display number 23, 4th Age, year 1100-1200.

steps.text: If the player has In Aid of the Myreque completed:

steps.player: Some disturbing and heroic news from Morytania concerning the River Salve and the seven priests.

steps.npc: Oh?

steps.player: Yes, it seems that these seven priests were also warriors and drove back the nasty things coming out of Morytania. Then Saradomin blessed the Salve to stop them getting back.

steps.npc: Quite worrying that it's just a bit of water keeping them there, but Saradomin will protect us, I've no doubt. Thank you for the information, I'll get a display put up. Display number 23, 4th Age, year 1100-1200.

steps.text: If the player has A Tail of Two Cats completed:

steps.player: You know Bob the Cat?

steps.npc: The little black cat that used to wander around sometimes? Sure, I remember him.

steps.player: I found out a lot about his background...turns out he was once human and helped to defeat a dragonkin once!

steps.npc: Dragonkin?
Tell me more!

steps.player: Well, you see, it started when Bob went missing...and involved a big sphinx in Sophanem, the City of the Dead, and me taking care of Unferth...

steps.npc: This is starting to sound familiar...

steps.player: It must...you know Reldo, the Varrock librarian - he knows all about Robert the Strong.

steps.npc: You mean that was Bob? Wow... I will get a display erected immediately about the history of this brave warrior. Display number 20, 4th Age, year 1-100.

steps.text: If the player has Making History completed:

steps.player: I found out more about King Lathas's ancestors.

steps.npc: Oh? I'd be interested to hear this, we have a painting of him upstairs.

steps.player: Indeed, it turns out that there was a big battle in the year 98 of the 5th Age. One of his ancestors became king because he survived it...

steps.npc: Ahh, is this relating to that small museum near Ardougne?

steps.player: Yes!

steps.npc: Ahh yes, we've been meaning to make a display on that for some time. They sent us some information, too; I'm glad you reminded me, I'll get that done now. Display number 46, 5th Age, year 98.

steps.text: If the player has Temple of Ikov completed:
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl:

steps.player: Well, I was asked to retrieve the Staff of Armadyl, from the Temple of Ikov, by Lucien, but instead, I helped the guardians of the staff and banished Lucien from this plane of existence, so that he could never again return.
I saw the staff and can describe it to you if you want?

steps.text: If the player sided with Lucien:

steps.player: Well, I was asked to retrieve the Staff of Armadyl, from the Temple of Ikov, by Lucien. When I returned it he grew in power unimaginably. I held the staff and can describe it to you if you want?

steps.npc: Yes! Please do!

steps.text: You describe the staff in detail while the historian takes notes.

steps.npc: That's excellent, I'll get a display put up straight away! Display number 28, end of the 2nd Age.

steps.text: If the player has Curse of the Empty Lord completed:

steps.player: Well, I found out more about the Staff of Armadyl from a ghost. It seems that Zamorak was a mortal when he got hold of the staff, and he used it to, well...spear Zaros, and somehow ended up becoming a god. It was
a bit confusing.

steps.npc: Now that is what you call a story. Tell me more so that I can put it up on the display.

steps.text: You recount the tale of the battle between Zaros and Zamorak as you heard it from the ghostly swordsman.

steps.npc: This is wonderful, I shall have a display made immediately to go with the staff model. Display number 28, end of the 2nd Age.

steps.text: If the player has Hazeel Cult completed:

steps.player: I discovered the truth behind the Carnillean family fortune!

steps.npc: Oh? Is that the family over near Ardougne?

steps.player: Yes. I got a bit involved in family business...

steps.npc: And?

steps.player: I found a secret cult in Ardougne and found that the Carnillean family started building the city of Ardougne from a house they'd captured from a Zamorkian lord.

steps.npc: How exciting, I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 7, 5th Age, year 7.

steps.text: If the player has What Lies Below completed:

steps.player: I discovered a tunnel and a cult of chaos mages here in Varrock!

steps.npc: Oh! Whatever can we do!

steps.player: Calm down, I have arrested the ringleader.

steps.npc: Oh, thank Saradomin for that. So, tell me the story!

steps.player: Well, I met Rat and he asked me to fill his folder, and I got mixed up with Surok....

steps.npc: A rat asked you to fill a folder?

steps.player: No, no, no - Rat Burgiss. But anyway, it turns out that this cult has been trying to get to the King, but I stopped them.

steps.text: If the player does not have the book Dagon'hai history in their inventory:
The historian looks a little overwhelmed, but also skeptical.

steps.npc: I don't suppose you have any evidence of this cult?

steps.player: Not with me, but there is a book I can get you from the library.

steps.npc: That sounds good - bring me that and we'll create a display.

steps.text: If the player has the book Dagon'hai history in their inventory:
The historian is scribbling furiously on his pad, and finally turns to you.

steps.player: Actually, to save you some writing, I have this book here that has lots of information. You can have it if you want...

steps.npc: Why, thank you... Yes, this is a bit of a revelation! I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 3, 5th Age, year 70.

steps.text: If the player has Defender of Varrock completed:

steps.player: Well, we got rid of the marauding zombies.

steps.npc: That's handy. Zombies do tend to leave horrible muddy footprints around the place. So what actually happened with them?

steps.player: Well, Zemouregal the Mahjarrat sent his zombie army against Varrock. However, we figured out how to stop him.
I found out that the descendant of the founder of Varrock could use the shield to stop the zombie army. It turns out that Dimintheis was that descendant, so he was able to defeat the zombies.

steps.npc: My, my, that is all very interesting. I shall make sure the display is updated at once! Display number 24, 4th Age, year 700-800.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around. Since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.

steps.player: Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.

steps.npc: You're welcome!

steps.text: You receive an old lamp.
If the player has no new quests to report:

steps.player: On second thoughts, you seem to have everything I know covered here!

steps.npc: No matter. I'm sure you'll find more. Look around the Museum, explore the city and maybe do some quests, and I'm sure you'll find out something worth telling.

steps.player: Yes, I'll go do some quests or something...

options.text: Tell me about other sections of the Museum.

steps.player: Tell me about other sections of the Museum.

steps.npc: I'd be delighted to; which areas are you interested in?

steps.player: Tell me about the Natural History exhibit.

steps.npc: Ahh, our newest expansion. The Natural History exhibit in the basement was set up to inform our citizens of the weird and wonderful diversity in our environment today. Indeed, I am sure you will recognise some of
the creatures down there. Hopefully, our lectures will teach you some things you didn't know about them!

steps.player: So where does the 'history' bit come in?

steps.npc: Ahh, I see. The 'history' refers to that of the species - it doesn't necessarily mean it's died out. After all, we have human history and we're still here!

steps.player: I guess that makes sense.
Tell me about the Dig Site exhibit.

steps.npc: Ahh, those. We're slowly filling them up with the help of people who have their Earth Sciences exams completed at the Dig Site. If you have, feel free to give us a hand. We'd appreciate it.

steps.player: Tell me about the Dig Site find cleaning area.

steps.npc: The cleaning area, yes. Well, we have some really good archaeologists on site right now. They're cleaning up the finds that are shipped over from the Dig Site to the east of here. If you have the right qualifications, you can help them clean the finds.

steps.player: What qualifications?

steps.npc: Level 3 Earth Science exams. You can take them over at the Exam Centre on the Dig Site.

steps.text: If the player has not passed the exams:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have those.

steps.npc: I'm sure you can get them easily enough. Just pop over to the Exam Centre on the Dig Site and speak to one of the examiners there.

steps.text: If the player has not yet taken the exams during The Dig Site quest:

steps.player: Oh, I'm already working towards those!

steps.npc: That's excellent. Keep up the good work and soon you'll be cleaning finds with the best of them.

steps.text: If the player has passed the exams:

steps.player: Oh, I already have those!

steps.npc: That's excellent. If you feel like helping us out, pop downstairs and clean up some finds for us.

steps.player: Tell me about the Timeline exhibit.

steps.npc: Ahh, my speciality. Being a historian, matters of the past are my passion. Collated on this floor and the one above are just part of my life's work. I am still working on updating and finding out more everyday, so if you find
any information on your travels that may be useful, please do let me know.
You can follow the timeline of the history of Gielinor from the creation of the world to the present day, simply by walking around this display. A wondrous journey, I think you'll agree!

steps.player: Wow, that's a lot of information. I'm sure in my travels and quests I'll pick up a few bits of information for you.

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.npc: Of course. I plan to assist the forces of Saradomin who will come to our aid, and fight against the legions of vampyres that infest this foul place. These brave mercenaries shall need a guide.
When a guide arrives, I will aid the mercenary by holding their wealth for their eventual return. The mercenary will repay the guide by giving [him/her/them] a token for items which I am holding.
I shall give such items to the guide as payment for their services once I'm handed the token.

steps.player: What items will you hold?

steps.npc: Oh, the range of items is very varied. Mercenaries tend to hold raw materials in high esteem and so will deposit those with me. They also seem to be good bartering items.
Generally, things like uncooked lobsters, coal, silver bars, bow strings. Things which are useful! Plus the odd tome of experience, which are considered incredibly useful.

steps.player: I'd best be off.

standard-dialogue-after-darkness-of-hall.npc: Hello friend. What can I do for you?

options.text: Could you exchange my tokens for me?
options.condition: If the player has a reward token (Burgh de Rott Ramble) in their inventory

steps.player: Could you exchange my tokens for me?

steps.npc: No need, friend. You can do that yourself.

options.text: Do you know what these nail beast nails are used for?
options.condition: If the player has nail beast nails in their inventory

steps.player: Do you know what these nail beast nails are used for?

steps.npc: Hmmm, not really sure. They do look disgusting though..oh, actually, I remember some other adventurers taking some of these to Sanfew now...something about being able to make a potion with them.

steps.player: Ok, so perhaps Sanfew knows then?

steps.npc: Maybe. It's worth a try. Next time you're in Taverley, pop in and ask him. I think I remember some adventurers saying something about a serum though, some sort of potion that can be made with them.

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.npc: Of course. These mercenaries are here waiting for someone to take them down to Burgh de Rott. They want to do their bit against the vampyres.
I hold some items for these good hearted souls so that the guide can be recompensed when the job is done.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

standard-dialogue-after-the-blood-moon-r.npc: Hello friend. What can I do for you?

options.text: Could you exchange my tokens for me?
options.condition: If the player has a reward token (Burgh de Rott Ramble) in their inventory

options.text: Do you know what these nail beast nails are used for?
options.condition: If the player has nail beast nails in their inventory

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.npc: Of course. Now that the vampyres are no longer a threat, these warriors are keen to test their mettle in the Theatre of Blood.
However, given they're not familiar with the area, they're waiting for someone to help guide them down to Burgh de Rott.
I hold some items for these good hearted souls so that the guide can be recompensed when the job is done.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.text: You show the priest the nail beast nails.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.player: Do you know what these are? Or what they're used for?

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.npc: Hmmm, not really sure. They do look disgusting though..oh, actually, I remember some other adventurers taking some of these to Sanfew now...something about being able to make a potion with them.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.player: Ok, so perhaps Sanfew knows then?

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.npc: Maybe? It's worth a try. Next time you're in Taverley, pop in and ask him. I think I remember some adventurers saying something about a serum though, some sort of potion that can be made with them.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-a-rewar.text: You show the priest the token.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-a-rewar.npc: Oh well done! Thank you for aiding our citizens.

standard-dialogue-before-murder-mystery.npc: This is private property! Please leave!

standard-dialogue-after-murder-mystery.npc: Thank you for all your help in solving the murder.

standard-dialogue.npc: What? Oh, hello. I was deep in thought. Did you want me to show you the prices of weapons and armour?

steps.player: You seem a bit flustered.

steps.npc: Sorry, I'm just deep in thought. I'm waiting for many deals to complete today.

steps.player: What sort of things are you selling?

steps.npc: Good old weapons and armour! My people - dwarves, you understand - are hoping I can trade with humans.

steps.player: It looks like you've come to the right place for that.

steps.npc: I have indeed, my friend. Now, can I help you?

options.text: Yes, show me the prices of weapons and armour.
Yes, show me the prices of weapons and armour.

steps.player: Yes, show me the prices of weapons and armour.

steps.text: Grand Exchange: Weapons and Armour opens

options.text: Can you tell me about the bank's auto-charging services?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the bank's auto-charging services?

steps.npc: Hm? Oh, yes. If you don't want to charge your items yourself, you can have the bank attendant do it for you on withdrawal.

steps.player: How do they know how many charges to add?

steps.npc: You can tell them how many you would like for each item. Or if you'd like, I can let them know a minimum threshold for all items.

steps.prompt: Set a global minimum charge threshold?
Are you sure? Some charging resources may not be retrievable.

steps.player: I don't think that's necessary, but thank you for offering.

steps.npc: Alright then. Where was I...?

steps.player: I'll leave you alone.

steps.npc: Thank you, I have much on my mind.
Wow, that's cheap.
Oh. That didn't sell so well.
Hmmm. If I spend twenty thousand on that, then...
Jackpot! I'm in the money now!
Hahaha! Trading the likes of which I have never seen.

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak-amulet.npc: Oh how splendid! Every time I come back here I try to talk to people, but no one seems to understand.
I was telling my friend Bob this the other day in the afterlife. At least he can relate to the struggle of people not understanding.

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak-amulet.text: If the player has not completed Dragon Slayer II:

steps.player: That must be frustrating.

steps.npc: Yes, it really is.

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak-amulet.text: If the player has completed Dragon Slayer II:

steps.player: Wait a second. Your friend Bob... does he happen to be a cat?

steps.npc: Why, yes, he is! Do you know Bob?

steps.player: I do! How is he doing?

steps.npc: He's alright, all things considered. He did speak of a human friend he misses though. I suspect that's you.

steps.player: I miss him too. Could you tell him I said hi? And tell him I'm sorry he got killed. I wish I could have saved him.

steps.npc: I will tell him that you miss him. Regarding his death, he said it was necessary, so please don't feel bad about it.

steps.player: Necessary? What do you mean?

steps.npc: He never explained why, only said that it had to be that way.

options.text: What can you tell me about Eve?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Eve?

steps.npc: Eve? One of the greatest witches I know. Also the oldest person I know. She's been around for practically forever.
It is said that when she was alive she was a hard working witch, mastering advanced spells at a very young age.
Unfortunately she died while still a young adult. That's why she looks so young now, despite being centuries old.

steps.player: How can she still be around after all these years?

steps.npc: Like I said, she mastered spells at a very young age. She took some of that magic with her into the afterlife.
The sad truth about Eve is that she spent all her life working and striving to achieve great things.
But she never got to relax and appreciate how far she had come. That is why she is so obsessed with partying now.

steps.player: I understand. That really makes you think, doesn't it.

steps.npc: Indeed. Enjoy the moment while you can, because you may not get another. Take it from me, I'm a ghost.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: Goodbye.

standard-dialogue-before-starting-the-se.npc: Well hello. Beautiful day isn't it.
Just smell that sea air... beautiful.

standard-dialogue-after-starting-the-slu.npc: I don't know what to do without my boat.

steps.npc: Oh, hello.

steps.player: Hello, what's in those boxes?

steps.npc: Crossbows, are you interested?

steps.player: Maybe, are they any good?

steps.npc: Are they any good?! They're dwarven engineering at its best!

options.text: How do I make one for myself?

steps.player: How do I make one for myself?

steps.npc: Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.

steps.player: Wood fletched into stock... check.

steps.npc: Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.

steps.player: Which goes with which?

steps.npc: Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.

steps.player: Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?

steps.npc: Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows. You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning
wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.

steps.player: What about magic logs?

steps.npc: Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable. I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want
anything to do with it!

steps.player: Thanks for telling me. Bye!

steps.npc: Take care, straight shooting.

steps.player: Thanks for telling me. Bye!

steps.npc: Take care, straight shooting.

steps.player: What about ammo?

steps.npc: You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though. You can poison any untipped bolt but there's also the option of tipping them with gems then
enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.

steps.player: Oh my poor bank, how will I store all those?!

steps.npc: Find Hirko in Keldagrim, he also sells crossbow parts and I'm sure he has something you can use to store bolts in.

steps.player: Thanks for the info.
Thanks for telling me. Bye!

steps.npc: Take care, straight shooting.

starting-off.player: Now I am a knight of the round table, do you have any more quests for me?

starting-off.speaker: King Arthur
starting-off.text: Aha! I'm glad you are here! I am sending out various knights on an important quest. I was wondering if you too would like to take up this quest?

steps.player: Tell me of this quest.

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: Well, we recently found out that the Holy Grail has passed into Gielinor.

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: This is most fortuitous!

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: None of my knights ever did return with it last time. Now we have the opportunity to give it another go, maybe this time we will have more luck!
If the player's combat level is less than 50:
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 50.
If the player's combat level is more than 50:

steps.prompt: Start the Holy Grail quest?

steps.player: I'd enjoy trying that.

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: Go speak to Merlin. He may be able to give a better clue as to where it is now you have freed him from that crystal.

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: He has set up his workshop in the room next to the library.

steps.player: I may come back and try that later.

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: Be sure that you come speak to me soon then.

options.text: I am weary of questing for the time being...

steps.player: I am weary of questing for the time being...

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: Maybe later then?

steps.player: Maybe so.

starting-off-subsequent-dialogue-with-ki.player: I am making progress, but I have not recovered the Grail yet.

starting-off-subsequent-dialogue-with-ki.speaker: King Arthur
starting-off-subsequent-dialogue-with-ki.text: Well, the Grail IS very elusive, it may take some perseverance.

starting-off-subsequent-dialogue-with-ki.speaker: King Arthur
starting-off-subsequent-dialogue-with-ki.text: As I said before, speak to Merlin in the workshop by the library.

talking-to-merlin.player: Hello. King Arthur has sent me on a quest for the Holy Grail. He thought you could offer some assistance.

talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
talking-to-merlin.text: That is a powerful artefact indeed. Returning it here would help Camelot a lot.

talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
talking-to-merlin.text: Due to its nature the Holy Grail is likely to reside in a holy place.

talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
talking-to-merlin.text: I believe there is a holy island somewhere not far away... I'm not entirely sure... I spent too long inside that crystal! Anyway, go and talk to someone over there.

talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
talking-to-merlin.text: I suppose you could also try speaking to Sir Galahad?

talking-to-merlin.speaker: Merlin
talking-to-merlin.text: He returned from the quest many years after everyone else. He seems to know something about it, but he can only speak about those experiences cryptically.

steps.player: Thank you for the advice.

options.text: Where can I find Sir Galahad?

steps.player: Where can I find Sir Galahad?

steps.speaker: Merlin
steps.text: Galahad now lives a life of religious contemplation. He lives somewhere west of McGrubor's Wood I think.

talking-to-merlin-updating-king-arthur.player: I am making progress, but I have not recovered the Grail yet.

talking-to-merlin-updating-king-arthur.speaker: King Arthur
talking-to-merlin-updating-king-arthur.text: Well, the Grail IS very elusive, it may take some perseverance.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Palomedes
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Hello there adventurer, what do you want of me?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: I'd like some advice on finding the Grail.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Palomedes
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Sorry, I cannot help you with that.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Lucan
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Hello there adventurer.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: I seek the Grail of legend!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Lucan
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: I'm afraid I don't have any suggestions...

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: Thanks. I'll try and find someone who does.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Gawain
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Good day to you!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: I seek the Grail in the name of Camelot!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Gawain
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: The Grail? That is truly a noble quest indeed. None but Galahad have come close.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Gawain
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: He used to be one of the Knights of the Round Table, but he mysteriously disappeared many years ago.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: Why would he quit being a Knight?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Gawain
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: That is a good question.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Gawain
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: I'm afraid I don't have the answer.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Kay
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Good morrow!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Kay
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: I hear you are questing for the Holy Grail?!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Kay
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Unfortunately not, Sirrah.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Tristram
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Hail Arthur, King of the Britons!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Tristram
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Good luck with that!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Pelleas
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Greetings to the court of King Arthur!

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: Any suggestions on finding the Grail?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Pelleas
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: My best guess would be some sort of spell. Merlin is our magic expert. Ask him?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Pelleas
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Although having said that, I believe Galahad found its location once...

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: Really? Know where I can find him?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Pelleas
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: I'm afraid not. He left here many moons ago and I know not where he went.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Bedivere
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: May I help you?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Bedivere
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: You are looking for the Grail now adventurer?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Bedivere
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: The best of luck to you! Make the name of Camelot proud, and bring it back to us.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Lancelot
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: Greetings! I am Sir Lancelot, the greatest Knight in the land! What do you want?

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.player: I am questing for the Holy Grail.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Lancelot
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: The Grail? Ha! Frankly, friend, you're not in that league.

asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.speaker: Sir Lancelot
asking-the-other-knights-talking-to-sir-.text: You got lucky with freeing Merlin but there's no way a puny wannabe like you is going to find the Holy Grail where so many others have failed.

talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.speaker: High Priest
talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.text: Many greetings. Welcome to our fair island.

talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.player: Hello, I am in search of the Holy Grail.

talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.speaker: High Priest
talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.text: The object of which you speak did once pass through holy Entrana. I know not where it is now however.

talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.speaker: Crone
talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.text: Did you say the Grail? You are a Grail knight, yes? Well you'd better hurry. A Fisher King is in pain.

talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.player: Well I would, but I don't know where I am going!

talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.speaker: Crone
talking-to-the-high-priest-of-entrana.text: Go to where the six heads face, blow the whistle and away you go!

steps.player: What are the six heads?

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: The six stone heads have appeared just recently in the world. They all face the point of realm crossing. Find where two of the heads face,

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: and you should be able to pinpoint where it is.

steps.player: What's a Fisher King?

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: The Fisher King is the owner and slave of the Grail...

steps.player: Ok, I will go searching.

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: Good luck with that.

options.text: What do you mean by the whistle?

steps.player: What do you mean by the whistle?

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: You don't know about the whistles yet? The whistles are easy.

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: You will need one to get to and from the Fisher King's realm. They reside in a haunted manor house in Misthalin, though you may not perceive them unless you carry something from the realm of the Fisher

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: King...

options.text: What do you mean by the whistle?

steps.player: The point of realm crossing?

steps.speaker: Crone
steps.text: The realm of the Fisher King is not quite of this reality. It is of a reality very close to ours though... Where it is easiest to cross, THAT is a point of realm crossing.

talking-to-sir-galahad.speaker: Galahad
talking-to-sir-galahad.text: Welcome to my home. It's rare for me to have guests! Would you like a cup of tea? I'll just put the kettle on.
Brother Galahad hangs a kettle over the fire.

options.text: Are you any relation to Sir Galahad?
I'm on a quest to find the Holy Grail!

steps.player: I'm on a quest to find the Holy Grail!

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: Ah... the Grail... yes... that did fill me with wonder! Oh, that I could have stayed forever! The spear, the food, the people...

options.text: So how can I find it?

steps.player: What are you talking about?

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: The Grail castle... It's... hard to describe with words. It mostly felt like a dream!

steps.player: Why did you leave?

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: Apparently the time is getting close when the world will need Arthur and his knights of the round table again.

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: And that includes me.

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: Leaving was tough for me, so I took this small cloth from the table as a keepsake.

options.text: Why didn't you bring the Grail with you?

steps.player: Why didn't you bring the Grail with you?

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: ...I'm not sure. Because... it seemed to be... NEEDED in the Grail castle? Half a moment, your cup of tea is ready.
Sir Galahad gives you a cup of tea.
a cup of tea

options.text: So how can I find it?

steps.player: So how can I find it?

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: I did not find it through looking - though admittedly I looked long and hard - eventually, it found me.

options.text: Well, I'd better be going then.

steps.player: Well, I'd better be going then.

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: Half a moment, your cup of tea is ready.
Sir Galahad gives you a cup of tea.
a cup of tea

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: If you do come across any particularily difficult obstacles on your quest, do not hesitate to ask my advice.

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: I know more about the realm of the Grail than many, and I have a feeling you may need to come back and speak to me anyway...

options.text: Do you get lonely here on your own?

talking-to-sir-galahad.text: If the player talked to the High Priest of Entrana first:

options.text: I seek an item from the realm of the Fisher King.

steps.player: I seek an item from the realm of the Fisher King.

steps.speaker: Galahad
steps.text: Funny you should mention that, but when I left there I took this small cloth from the table as a keepsake.

steps.player: I don't suppose I could borrow that? It could come in useful on my quest.

steps.text: Galahad reluctantly passes you a small cloth.
a Holy table napkin

talking-to-sir-galahad-blowing-on-the-ma.text: If the player blows the whistle anywhere besides between the four pillars at Brimhaven:

steps.text: The whistle makes no noise. It will not work in this location.

talking-to-sir-galahad-blowing-on-the-ma.text: If the player blows the whistle whilst inside the Fisher Realm:

steps.text: The player is teleported back to Brimhaven.

encountering-the-black-knight-titan.text: I am the Black Knight Titan! You must pass through me before you can continue in this realm!

options.text: Okay, have at ye oh evil knight!

steps.player: Okay, have at ye oh evil knight!

steps.text: If the player defeats the Black Knight Titan without the excalibur:
Puny mortal... You cannot defeat me...
Maybe you need something more to beat the titan?
The Black Knight Titan's regenerates back to full health.
If the player uses the excalibur to defeat the Black Knight Titan:
Well done! You have defeated the Black Knight Titan!

options.text: Actually I think I'll run away!

steps.player: Actually I think I'll run away!

talking-to-the-fisherman.speaker: Fisherman
talking-to-the-fisherman.text: Hi! I don't get many visitors here!

steps.player: How's the fishing?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Not amazing. Not many fish can live in this gungey stuff. I remember when this was a pleasant river teeming with every sort of fish...

options.text: Any idea how to get into the castle?

steps.player: Any idea how to get into the castle?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Why, that's easy!

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Just ring one of the bells outside.

steps.player: ...I didn't see any bells.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: You must be blind then. There's ALWAYS bells there when I go to the castle.

options.text: Yes, well, this place is a dump.

steps.player: Yes, well, this place is a dump!

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: This place used to be very beautiful, however, as our king grows old and weak, the land seems to be dying too.

talking-to-the-fisherman-peasant.speaker: Peasant
talking-to-the-fisherman-peasant.text: Woe is me! Our crops are all failing... how shall I feed myself this winter?

ringing-the-grail-bell.text: If the player rings the Grail bell but is not by the dismantled bricks:

steps.text: Ting-a-ling-a-ling!
Nothing happens.

ringing-the-grail-bell.text: If the player rings the Grail bell and is at least four tiles by the dismantled bricks:

steps.text: Ting-a-ling-a-ling!

steps.speaker: Grail Maiden
steps.text: Welcome to the Grail castle. You should come inside, it's cold out here.
Somehow you are now inside the castle.

ringing-the-grail-bell-taking-the-holy-g.text: You feel that the Grail shouldn't be moved. You must complete some task here before you are worthy.

talking-to-the-fisher-king.speaker: The Fisher King
talking-to-the-fisher-king.text: Ah! You got inside at last! You spent all that time fumbling around outside, I thought you'd never make it here.

options.text: How did you know what I have been doing?

steps.player: How did you know what I have been doing?

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: Oh, I can see what is happening in my realm. I have sent clues to help you get here, such as the fisherman, and the crone.

steps.player: I seek the Holy Grail.

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: Ah excellent. A knight come to seek the Holy Grail. Maybe our land can be restored to its former glory.

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: At the moment the Grail cannot be removed from the castle. Legend has it a questing knight will one day work out how to restore our land; then he will claim the Grail as his prize.

steps.player: Any ideas how I can restore the land?

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: None at all.

steps.player: You don't look too well.

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: Nope, I don't feel so good either.

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: I fear my life is running short... Alas, my son and heir is not here. I am waiting for my son to return to this castle.

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: If you could find my son, that would be a great weight off my shoulders.

steps.player: Who is your son?

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: He is known as Percival.

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: I believe he is a knight of the round table.

steps.player: I shall go and see if I can find him.

options.text: Do you mind if I have a look around?

steps.player: Do you mind if I have a look around?

steps.speaker: The Fisher King
steps.text: No, not at all. Please, be my guest.

talking-to-king-arthur.player: Hello, do you have a knight named Sir Percival?

talking-to-king-arthur.speaker: King Arthur
talking-to-king-arthur.text: Ah yes. I remember young Percival. He rode off on a quest a couple of months ago. We are getting a bit worried, he's not back yet...

talking-to-king-arthur.speaker: King Arthur
talking-to-king-arthur.text: He was going to try and recover the golden boots of Arkaneeses.

talking-to-king-arthur.player: Any idea which way that would be?

talking-to-king-arthur.speaker: King Arthur
talking-to-king-arthur.text: Not exactly. We discovered some magic golden feathers that are said to point the way to the boots...

talking-to-king-arthur.speaker: King Arthur
talking-to-king-arthur.text: Just blowing gently on them will supposedly show the way to go.
If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.speaker: King Arthur
steps.text: Free up some space and I'll give you a feather.

talking-to-king-arthur.text: If the player has one free inventory space:

steps.text: King Arthur gives you a feather.
a Magic gold feather

talking-to-king-arthur.text: If the player loses the feather:

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is directly to the west of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the east.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is directly to the east of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the west.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is directly to north of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the south.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is directly to the south of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the north.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is southeast of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the northwest.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is southwest of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the northeast.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is northeast of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the southwest.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is northwest of the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to the southeast.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player is within 5 tiles away from the boots:

steps.text: The feather points to somewhere nearby.

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player blows the feather whilst inside Scrubfoot's Cave or any dungeon:

steps.text: The feather doesn't seem to work here...

blowing-on-the-magic-gold-feather.text: If the player blows the feather whilst inside Sir Percival's house:

steps.text: The feather points at the sacks.

talking-to-sir-percival.text: If the player prods at the sacks:

steps.text: You hear a muffled groan. The sack wriggles slightly.

talking-to-sir-percival.text: If the player attempts to open the sack:

steps.text: You hear muffled noises from the sack. You open the sack.

talking-to-sir-percival.speaker: Sir Percival
talking-to-sir-percival.text: Wow, thank you! I could hardly breathe in there!

options.text: How did you end up in a sack?

steps.player: How did you end up in a sack?

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: It's a little embarrassing really.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: After going on a long and challenging quest to retrieve the boots of Arkaneeses, defeating many powerful enemies on the way, I fell into a goblin trap!

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: I've been kept as a slave here for the last 3 months!

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: A day or so ago, they decided it was a fun game to put me in this sack: then they forgot about me!

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: I'm now very hungry, and my bones feel very stiff.
inital

options.text: Come with me, I shall make you a king.

steps.player: Come with me, I shall make you a king.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: What are you talking about?

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: The king of where?

steps.player: Your father is apparently someone called the Fisher King. He is dying and wishes you to be his heir.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: I have been told that before.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: I have not been able to find that castle again though...

talking-to-sir-percival.text: If the player does not have the whistle:
If the player has the magic whistle:

steps.player: Well, I do have the means to get us there - a magic whistle!

steps.text: You give a whistle to Sir Percival. You tell sir Percival what to do with the whistle.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: Ok, I will see you there then!

options.text: Your father wishes to speak to you.

steps.player: Your father wishes to speak to you.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: My father? You have spoken to him recently?

steps.player: He is dying and wishes you to be his heir.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: I have been told that before.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: I have not been able to find that castle again though...

talking-to-sir-percival.text: If the player does not have the whistle:
If the player has the magic whistle:

steps.player: Well, I do have the means to get us there - a magic whistle!

steps.text: You give a whistle to Sir Percival. You tell sir Percival what to do with the whistle.

steps.speaker: Sir Percival
steps.text: Ok, I will see you there then!

talking-to-sir-percival-subsequent-dialo.speaker: Sir Percival
talking-to-sir-percival-subsequent-dialo.text: I said I will see you there then!

talking-to-sir-percival-talking-to-sir-p.speaker: King Percival
talking-to-sir-percival-talking-to-sir-p.text: I got here and agreed to take over duties as king here, then before my eyes the most miraculous changes occured here... grass and trees were growing outside before our very eyes!

talking-to-sir-percival-talking-to-sir-p.speaker: King Percival
talking-to-sir-percival-talking-to-sir-p.text: Thank you very much for showing me the way home.
If the player talks to him again:

talking-to-sir-percival-taking-more-than.text: You feel that taking more than one Holy Grail might be greedy...

talking-to-king-arthur-2.speaker: King Arthur
talking-to-king-arthur-2.text: Wow! Incredible! You truly are a splendid knight!

Ss216z.player: Well, I do have the means to get us there - wait, let me go get the magic whistle!

after-tower-of-life.player: Hi there, you mentioned something about creating monsters...?

after-tower-of-life.npc: Good! I gain know from alchemists and builders. Me make beings.

after-tower-of-life.player: Interesting. Tell me if I'm right. By the alchemists and builders creating you, you have inherited their combined knowledge in much the same way that a child might inherit the looks of their parents.
So what do you need me to do?

after-tower-of-life.npc: Inspect symbol of life altars around dungeon. You see item give. Use item on altar. Activate altar to create, you fight.

during-creature-creation.text: If the player does not have the correct ingredients:

steps.npc: You no haveee the two materials need.

during-creature-creation.text: If the player has the correct ingredients:

steps.npc: You haveee materials need. Here goes!

standard-dialogue.npc: You here for the...stuff?
Look [miss/pal] I got the goods if you have the cash.
We talkin' the same language yet?

options.text: Yes, I am here for the stuff.

steps.player: What stuff is this again?

steps.npc: The sort of stuff you use in brewing.
The sort of stuff the Cooking Guild banned last year.
The sort of stuff that (if added to a vat of brewing ingredients just before the hops) has a higher chance of producin' a mature batch of whatever ale you wanted to make.
That sort of stuff.

steps.player: What was that bit about adding it to something?

steps.npc: I said, it's the sort of Stuff you add to a brewing vat after you have put the water and barley malt in.
THEN you add the sort of stuff I'm talking about, followed by the hops and the yeast.
Then, when whatever you are making brews it will have a higher chance of being a mature batch of ale.
That clear enough for you or am I going to have to start drawin' pictures on the wall of the hut?

options.text: Yes, I am here for the stuff.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Then sling yer 'ook!

options.text: I hear you are the man to talk to about maps.

steps.player: I hear you are the man to talk to about maps.

steps.npc: I might be, you got something for me?

steps.player: Like what?

steps.npc: Like...5000 Pieces of Eight?

steps.text: If the player has 5,000 pieces of eight:

steps.player: I might have 5000 Pieces of Eight with your name on them if you have a map for me.

steps.npc: Look, I might have a little something for you for that amount of cash, but I'll have to check.
You sure you want in on this?
Ok, there you go, now try and keep this to yourself, ok?

steps.text: a medium clue scroll

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Then sling yer 'ook!

steps.text: If the player does not have 5,000 pieces of eight:

steps.player: Well, no but...

steps.npc: Look, you want something or not?

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: Then sling yer 'ook!

options.text: I have no idea what you mean.

steps.player: I have no idea what you are talking about.

steps.npc: Then sling yer 'ook!

standard-dialogue-right-click-trade-opti.npc: Are you here for the stuff?

options.text: Yes, I am here for the stuff.
I hear you are the man to talk to about maps.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If the player has something equipped in the helmet slot:

steps.npc: Sorry, no hats allowed. Shove it in the deposit box if you want to play.

steps.player: Why not?

steps.npc: Cos it's one of the rules, you got a problem with rules?

steps.player: Yes, I am sort of a pirate after all.

steps.npc: Good answer!
But still, no hats. They give you a hat to show what team you are on, and if you got a hat on, it might get nicked, see?

steps.player: Oh, ok.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If the player has items in their inventory:

steps.npc: Might want to dump that stuff yer holdin'.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: Well, if you are carrying anything in there, then it might get damaged. Burned up, that kind of thing.
You might want to put it in the bank, nice and safe like.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If the player has a cat following them:

steps.npc: No cats.

steps.player: Are you sure?

steps.npc: Yep, they might get into the brew, and I know a few pirates that are allergic to them.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If the player has a different follower out:

steps.text: You cannot take your follower into the game.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If the player is on a PvP world:

steps.npc: Hah!

steps.text: This minigame is unavailable on this world.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If the player has less than 40 cooking:

steps.npc: You a good cook?

steps.player: Well, not very...

steps.npc: Then you don't get in. Cooking 40 or over, Cooking Guild regulations, if you catch my drift.

when-using-the-right-click-join-team-opt.text: If none of the previous conditions apply:

steps.text: The player is teleported into one of the Trouble Brewing waiting rooms.

contacting-through-astral-contact.player: It's [player name]. I'm using my magic to communicate to you. Don't worry.

contacting-through-astral-contact.text: If the player has less than 40 cooking:

steps.npc: Well, I'm not sayin' anything to anyone unless they have decent cookin' skills.

contacting-through-astral-contact.text: If the player is near the Trouble Brewing distillery:

steps.npc: I figured, seeing as I can see you over there! I don't make deals like this.

starting-off.speaker: Larrissa
starting-off.text: Oh, thank Armadyl! I am in such a worry... please help me!

steps.player: With what?

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: Oh... it is terrible... horrible... My boyfriend lives here in this lighthouse, but I haven't seen him the last few days! I think something terrible has happened!

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: Look, you can see for yourself that the light has gone out, and the front door is locked up tight! He would NEVER do that!

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: With the light off this coastline is terribly dangerous to ships! And to lock the front door so that nobody can turn the light back on?

steps.player: Maybe he just went on holiday or something? Must be pretty boring living in a lighthouse.

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: That is terribly irresponsible! He is far too thoughtful for that! He would never leave it unattended! He would also never leave without telling me!

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: Please, I know something terrible has happened to him... I can sense it! Please... please help me adventurer!

steps.player: But how can I help?

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: Well, we have to do something to get the lighthouse working again! Also, as you may have noticed, the storm that knocked the bridge out

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: has trapped me on this causeway! You seem to have got here okay somehow, so if you could go and visit my cousin and get the spare key I left him,

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: as well as fix the bridge enough so that I can go and speak to my family in Rellekka and tell them whats happened, I will be eternally grateful!

steps.prompt: Start the Horror from the Deep quest?

steps.player: Okay, I'll help!

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: OH! THANK YOU SO MUCH! I know my darling would never have left with the lighthouse lights off and without even telling me where he's gone!

steps.player: Where is your cousin?

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: My cousin was always interested in agility. He left our home in Rellekka many moons ago, so that he could pursue this interest.

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: I don't exactly know where he has gone, but I am sure he went somewhere to practise his agility. If you see him, his name is Gunnjorn. Mention my name, he will recognise it.

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: Well, I am not just some helpless girl! I have pretty good agility, so you will only need to use two planks to make a ledge that I can balance along.

steps.speaker: Larrissa
steps.text: Just use a plank on each side of the bridge. You will need a hammer, and thirty steel nails for each plank you use as well. I believe there are some planks near here...

standard-dialogue.npc: What are you doing in our village, outlander?

steps.player: Nothing much.

steps.npc: Bah! Go down to the longhall, and there you will find excitement aplenty! Our finest warrior, Gunthor the Brave, will give you a rousing welcome!

I'm exploring.

steps.npc: Bah! You cannot hope to learn anything of us just by strolling through our village! We are an ancient tribe, our ways date back to the time before Avarrocka was founded!

steps.player: Would you care to tell me more?

steps.npc: Oh? You are not so ignorant as I thought. Very well, I shall speak of our tribe...

Our elders remember that about a century ago we were living in the lands far to the west. We were a large nomadic mountain tribe, settling wherever there was food, moving on when it had run out. As the tribe

grew larger, it was hard to find enough food for everyone, and we were forced to shift our camp more and more often. In time, a warrior called Gunnar took his friends and their families and left the larger tribe,
moving south in search of new places. They eventually settled here and built this village, finding that the old nomadic traditions were no longer needed.
Our current chieftain, Gunthor the Brave, is a direct- line descendent of Gunnar.

However, our ways have changed little in the last century. Although more and more people use magical powers, we do not believe it is wise to take upon oneself the power of the gods in this way. To this day, we fight

with the mighty sword, the vicious axe and the swift arrow on the wind. Some of our young, wishing to try so-called 'civilisation' and the softness of city life, abandon the tribe and move to the cities. It is sad to
see them go, but we do not prevent them; we live here in our village because we love this life - we do not force it on those whom it does not suit.
There, I have said enough.

steps.player: Thank you.

options.text: You look like a load of primitive savages.

steps.player: You look like a load of primitive savages.

steps.npc: And you look like an arrogant fool. And you smell like a raccoon's bottom.

steps.player: I'm bored.

steps.npc: Bah! Go down to the longhall, and there you will find excitement aplenty! Our finest warrior, Gunthor the Brave, will give you a rousing welcome!

steps.player: I'll bear it in mind.

beginner-clue.text: You've [found a new clue/obtained a casket]!

standard-dialogue-without-99-hunter.npc: Whoah there, stranger, careful where you're walking. I almost clobbered you there; thought you were a larupia or something.

steps.player: What are you doing here?

steps.npc: Me? Oh, I'm just having some fun, capturing wild animals, living on the edge, stuff like that.
Hey, want me to teach you how to catch the critters around here? Ain't come across anything yet that I couldn't capture.

options.text: Okay, where's a good place to start?

steps.player: Ok, where's a good place to start?

steps.npc: Your easiest bet around here is probably to go for some of the birds. Go for the crimson swifts; they're the bright red ones that hang around near the coast. They're as obliging as can be, or maybe they're just
plain dumb, but either way they just seem to throw themselves into traps half the time.

steps.player: What sort of traps should I use?

steps.npc: Just use a standard bird snare and you'll be fine. You can get them in any decent shop that sells Hunter gear.

steps.player: How do they work, then?

steps.npc: Well, they're kind of sneaky, really. You've got a tall post with what appears to be a little perch sticking out the side. Now, the bird will see this as somewhere to sit, but the perch is actually rigged such that when the bird
lands on it, it'll drop away.
Further, as the perch drops, it releases a noose that tightens around the bird's feet and captures it. Neat huh?
So, was there anything else you wanted to ask about?

options.text: What other sorts of things are there to catch around here?

steps.player: Thanks for your help.

steps.npc: Not a problem, any time.

options.text: What sort of things are there to catch around here?

steps.player: What sort of things are there to catch around here?

steps.npc: What're you interested in? You've got anything from birds for beginners up to larupias for the pros, not to mention weasels, butterflies, barb-tails and chinchompas.

options.text: How would I go about catching birds?

steps.player: How would I go about catching birds?

steps.npc: There are a couple of varieties that you can try your hand at catching around here, but the technique for both is essentially the same. You need to set up a bird snare.

steps.player: How do they work, then?

steps.npc: Well, they're kind of sneaky, really. You've got a tall post with what appears to be a little perch sticking out the side. Now, the bird will see this as somewhere to sit, but the perch is actually rigged such that when the bird
lands on it, it'll drop away.
Further, as the perch drops, it releases a noose that tightens around the bird's feet and captures it. Neat, huh?
So, was there anything else you wanted to ask about?

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
How do I get hold of a weasel?

steps.player: How do I get hold of a weasel?

steps.npc: Not with large quantities of rice and treacle as many people would have you believe. Besides, the Feldip weasel isn't technically a weasel, but, as is typical with any sort of colloquial name, it's been called that often enough
now that it's stuck.
Anyway, the Feldip weasel's main survival technique is in hiding; other than that, it's pretty stupid. So, if you can actually find one, then you've probably got a fairly good chance of catching one.

steps.player: And how would I actually go about finding one?

steps.npc: The best place to start would probably be just south of here. You'll find lots of kebbit burrows there. Take a close look at some of them, follow the trails and you can't go far wrong.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...

steps.player: Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...

steps.npc: Ah yes, yes, larupias are fun; just think of them as big kittens.

steps.player: Uh huh, big kittens that just want to rip your throat out!

steps.npc: Indeed, and you can use this to your advantage. If a larupia is keen to chase you then let it; that way you can happily lead it straight into your trap without any fuss or waiting around.

steps.player: Into what sort of trap should I lead it?

steps.npc: A pit trap should do you. There are some appropriate pits to the east of here that you can use. Cover one with a few logs and branches, tease the kitty and then lead it to the pit. Simple.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

steps.player: Barb-tails sound interesting.

steps.npc: They do sound interesting, don't they? Unfortunately, they're actually just another type of kebbit; those things get everywhere. Still, the tails of these particular kebbits can be useful for fishing.

steps.player: So, how would I go about catching one them?

steps.npc: Just squash them with a boulder, quick and simple.

steps.player: What, you mean just pick up some boulders and start throwing them at kebbits? That doesn't sound simple.

steps.npc: No silly, you let the creature squash itself. Just use some sticks to hold a boulder in a nice precarious position, place some bait underneath and let the creature knock itself out.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
What on earth is a chinchompa?

steps.player: What on earth is a chinchompa?

steps.npc: Awwww, chinchompas are great. They're highly volatile little balls of fluff. Cute as you like, but for some reason they do have this tendency to spontaneously combust.

steps.player: What? Why?

steps.npc: Probably something to do with the fact they'll eat anything and everything, especially spicy food.
Anyways, if you want to capture a chinchompa, I suggest using a box trap. That way, if the little fluffball does explode, then at least most of the blast will be contained within the box.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.

steps.player: Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.

steps.npc: Not really, but some people like them. The ones around here are at least vaguely interesting, though. The black ones are supposedly magical butterflies.

steps.player: Doesn't that make them harder to catch?

steps.npc: Not particularly; you can still catch them using an ordinary butterfly net. Oh, and you'll probably need some butterfly jars in which to keep them as well.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?

steps.player: How can I improve my chances of making a capture?

steps.npc: There are four key factors that will affect your chances: what bait you use, how close to the trap you are, your appearance and your smell.

steps.player: How does bait help?

steps.npc: Unfortunately, creatures don't just jump into traps for the fun of it nearly as often as we as Hunters might like. However, it is possible to improve those odds. If you can find the right bait to use on your trap,
something your prey really craves, then hunger overrides fear and the creature is just that little bit more likely to bounce to its furry little doom.

options.text: Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

steps.player: Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

steps.npc: However well you might be blending in, if you're standing with your nose pressed right up against your own trap, the poor little critters ain't going to go anywhere near it. So, you need to make sure you put
a sensible distance - I'd say at least four strides - between yourself and your trap.

options.text: Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

steps.player: Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

steps.npc: You're a human. From the point of view of a lot of creatures, you're big and scary. So, it'd be best if the furry little monsters didn't notice you. You need to blend in like the creatures themselves.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.npc: Easy, dress up like one of them. Even easier, dress up using the furs of the creatures themselves; then you're bound to get the colour right. And, I suppose, if you don't fancy just slinging a dead fur over your
shoulders, you can probably get them made into something more appealing. I hear there are tailors in Varrock who are good at that sort of thing.

steps.player: What's wrong with my smell!?

steps.npc: I'm sure there's nothing wrong with your smell...from a human point of view. But to your prey, any trap that you've set up will reek of human, and that's going to work against you if you don't do anything about it.

steps.player: So what should I do?

steps.npc: You need to mask that lovely human scent of yours with something else. Smoke works well. Take a lit torch and waft it around the trap a bit. You'll quickly overpower most of the other smells around the trap.

options.text: Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

steps.player: Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

steps.npc: Well, the equipment isn't too hard to get hold of. You've got specialist shops like Aleck's in Yanille that'll see you right. He's a bit pricey, mind, but it's pretty decent kit.
The clothing is a tad trickier to get hold of, the materials required being rather difficult to seperate from their reluctant owners.
But, if you can get the furs, there are shops like the tailor's in east Varrock that can help you.

options.text: I think I'll give it a miss right now.

steps.player: I think I'll give it a miss right now, thanks.

steps.npc: Suit yourself!

steps.player: What's a larupia?

steps.npc: What's a larupia? You don't know? You mean you really don't recognise the significance of these clothes I'm wearing?

steps.player: Well, they're certainly decorative...what about them?

steps.npc: Well, these are the furs from a larupia. Caught the creature myself I did, and these make me blend in better, see?
If you want to be successful as a hunter you've got to be as stealthy as a kyatt, as quiet as a mouse and blend in like a, well, like a larupia, I guess!

options.text: So, what's good to hunt around here?
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
What is that cool cape you're wearing?

steps.player: What is that cool cape you're wearing?

steps.npc: This? It's a Hunter's Skillcape. It shows that I am a true master of the art of Hunting and provides five daily teleports to either the Feldip Hills or Wilderness Hunter areas. If you ever manage to train your
Hunter skill to its maximum level then I could sell you one.

options.text: Ahh, leave me alone you crazy killing person.

steps.player: Ahh, leave me alone you crazy killing person.

steps.npc: Heh, well I guess it's not everyone's thing.

options.text: Can you give me some hunting traps?

steps.npc: I do have a spare Hunter kit lying around, you can have it for free.

steps.player: Thanks! I will put this to good use.

steps.npc: Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: If the player has already received a Hunter kit from a hunting expert:

steps.player: Can you give me some hunting traps?

steps.npc: I don't have any more Hunter kits lying around, sorry. Maybe you could try one of the many shops that sell hunting traps, you can find one in Yanille.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

standard-dialogue-with-99-hunter.prompt: What would you like to talk about?

steps.player: Can I buy a Hunter's Skillcape from you?

steps.npc: I would be delighted to recognise you as a master hunter, the cape provides five daily teleports to either the Feldip Hills or Wilderness Hunter areas. I will need 99000 coins to cover the expense of making such a
costly item!

steps.player: 99000! That seems a bit expensive.

steps.npc: Actually it's quite reasonable; it's made from the fur of the nearly extinct Raharni wildcat. Well, if you change your mind you know where to find me.

options.text: Certainly, I'm happy to pay that.

steps.player: Certainly, I'm happy to pay that.

steps.player: But it seems that I don't have enough money with me.

steps.npc: Well, come back and see me when you do.

a Hunter cape and hood

steps.npc: Now you look like a true hunter!

Come back when you have and I shall allow you entry.

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-th.npc: Sorry, but only those who've completed the hard set of the Western Provinces tasks may enter my private hunting ground.

steps.npc: Ah, this is a wonderful area for a spot of hunting, don't you think?

steps.player: I don't know, is it?

steps.npc: Oh absolutely; there's a huge variety of creatures to catch around here. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those piques your interest?

options.text: Where would I find polar kebbits?

steps.player: Where would I find polar kebbits?

steps.npc: Funnily enough, you've just put your finger right on the problem. With polar kebbits, finding them is the hardest part! You'll have to track them down.

steps.player: How would I go about doing that, then?

steps.npc: The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!
You'll be hard pressed to catch a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.
Good places to look for clues include hollow logs in which the kebbit may have hidden or vegetation which may have been chewed or damaged.
There are also tunnels running through the ice here that the kebbits use, so you should check those out as well.
What's more, these tunnels can often help to shelter a trail from further snow, making it even easier for you to pick them up again.
Eventually, of course, the kebbit will have probably hidden somewhere. Polar kebbits don't hang about in the open for long for fear of their natural predators.
If you suspect a kebbit is close by, try looking around for signs of disturbed snow. Polar kebbits will often bury themselves in snow drifts as a means of hiding.
If you think you've found a kebbit, use a noose wand to haul the creature out from the snow.

steps.player: Wow, that's quite a lot to remember.

steps.npc: Don't worry; if you find yourself struggling to follow a trail, just come and ask me and I'll see if I can help.
But remember, the best place to start is by searching around their burrows.

steps.player: Great, thanks.
How do you hunt birds?

steps.npc: Ah, you can get cunning little bird snares for just that. You should be able to find them in specialist Hunter shops. Try to lay them in fairly open areas with lots of birds.

steps.player: Do I need to place any bait on these traps?

steps.npc: No, that's not necessary. The idea is that the bird will see the trap as somewhere to perch. If the bird lands on the trigger stick, it should drop away and a small loop of wire should close around the bird's feet.
And remember, it's important to collect any captures from your traps fairly quickly; otherwise, you risk losing them to various wild scavengers.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.player: How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.npc: Ah, the key there is concealment, both of yourself and your traps.
The most obvious point is to stay out of sight of your own traps. If possible, hide around a wall, hedge or similar. Failing that, make sure you're a good few feet away from your trap.
You can hide yourself even better by wearing clothing appropriate to the area in which you are hunting.
Your best bet is to use the skins of creatures native to the area. There is a very good tailor in east Varrock who may be able to help you with making clothing out of such skins.
Finally, a lot of creatures may avoid your traps if they can smell a human scent on them. This is where smoking a trap can be useful.
It takes a bit of practice, but by using the smoke from a torch, you can mask any other scents that may surround a trap.

steps.player: Wow, thanks for your help.
Thanks for your help.

steps.npc: You're welcome, good luck with the hunting.

steps.player: What's so special about butterflies?

steps.npc: That depends entirely on the butterfly.
I'll admit that the activities of many butterflies may be of no interest at all. However, we are lucky in having around here some fine examples of rare thaumic butterflies.
These butterflies reputedly have magical powers that, when released, can make a person stronger or heal otherwise critical wounds.
At this point, I should offer a note of caution, however: it is also said that these powers will not manifest themselves if the butterflies are captured for selfish purposes.
Rather, they are gifts that must be used by one person to aid another. Of course, you'll have to catch them first.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.npc: Why, with a butterfly net of course! You should also carry some empty butterfly jars with you in which to keep the butterflies.
