How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

steps.player: How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

steps.npc: Ah, now for these creatures I would recommend using a deadfall trap. Deadfalls are quite easy to set up, and yet you can catch some very reasonably sized creatures with them.
Deadfall traps basically work by having a large dead weight, such as a boulder, positioned so as to be delicately balanced above some form of bait.
You will need to make sure you have a knife and some wood with you to create appropriate supports and a trigger for this sort trap.
In the case of sabre-toothed kebbits you should use some form of raw meat to bait your trap, but other animals may prefer other baits, such as fish or vegetables.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.player: Oooh, kyatts sounds interesting. I want to catch one of those.

steps.npc: Well, you've set your sights high, kyatts are incredibly fearsome creatures, but with determination like that I'm sure you'll make it.
Now, you're not going to be able to catch a kyatt with just a small box or a noose on a stick. You need a much bigger trap.
Pit traps are a good bet. You'd be best off finding a natural dip in the ground as the basis for your trap. If you dig a pit yourself, you risk creatures noticing the disturbed ground nearby.
Once you've found an appropriate spot, you'll need some logs and a knife. The logs serve two purposes.
Some can be carved into sharp skewers for the bottom of the pit; hopefully the kyatt will die when it falls onto these. Others can be used to conceal the trap.
Of course, even then the pit is going to look suspicious, so you're going to need to lure the kyatt onto the branches in some way. What actually tends to work best for this is, well, yourself!

steps.player: What? I don't like the sound of that.

steps.npc: Yes, that's the normal response, but I kid you not. If you really want a kyatt to follow you over that pit then just give it a good poke!
Of course, I suggest you use something long to poke it with. Poking a kyatt with your finger is likely to end in unfortunate limb loss.
Fortunately, you can get very good sticks for poking from most Hunter shops.

Once you have...got the creature's attention, try to lead it to one of your traps. Make sure to jump the branches when you reach the trap yourself, of course; it would be embarrassing to fall into your own trap.
Then, if the kyatt is giving you all of its attention, hopefully it won't notice the trap, and with any luck, it will stumble right into the pit.

steps.player: That sounds a bit hit or miss, and kind of suicidal too!

steps.npc: Well that's what makes it exciting, isn't it? But honestly, if you want to capture a kyatt, that's your best bet.

steps.player: How do I make one for myself?

steps.npc: Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.

steps.player: Wood fletched into stock... check.

steps.npc: Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.

steps.player: Which goes with which?

steps.npc: Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.

steps.player: Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?

steps.npc: Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows. You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning
wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.

anything to do with it!

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Too true, you didn't rob just anybody's grave. You managed to rob the grave of Klenter, the recently deceased High Priest of Icthlarin. Do you know what that means?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Icthlarin is the Menaphite god of the dead. By desecrating the tomb of one of his priests, you've made an enemy out of every person in this city.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: But I didn't desecrate any tomb! There's no proof!

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Really? Because if I'm not mistaken, that's Klenter's shade right over there. He definitely doesn't seem happy with you. There's also the burial jar in your possession. How do you explain that?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: How did you know about the burial jar?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: I can smell the rotting organs from here.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: Look, I don't know exactly what happened. All I know is that wanderer hypnotised me and had me steal something from this pyramid.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: The burial jar?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: I... I guess so. It's all still very unclear.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Interesting. I'm afraid I can't help you. I have my own concerns without involving myself with petty human affairs.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: However, I suggest you seek out the new High Priest of Icthlarin to the south east. He might be able to assist you. Of course, you'll need to convince him to talk to you first.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Here, I have a token that he will know is from me. Take that to him, and I'm sure he will speak with you.

steps.player: But you stole my last one!

steps.player: I lost that token you gave me. Could I have another please?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Ah, you humans.
The Sphinx gives you another token.

steps.player: Thanks.
Tell me about yourself.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I am an agent of neither good nor evil. I am unconcerned with the plight of mankind and their petty wars and beliefs.

steps.player: Well, now that you've told me what you're not, can you perhaps tell me what you are?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I am the guardian of feline kind.

steps.player: Why would they need a guardian?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Cats play a significant role in the religion of this area, particularly when it comes to guarding the dead from the Devourer.

steps.player: The Devourer?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: She's the very incarnation of destruction.

steps.player: I don't understand.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: What understanding do you have of the Menaphite gods?

steps.player: Little to none.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Well the Menaphite Pantheon is made up of four main deities.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: The two main gods of the pantheon are Tumeken, the god of light, and Elidinis, the goddess of fertility.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Tumeken and Elidinis also have two children. Icthlarin is one, and the Devourer is the other.

steps.player: They named her the Devourer? Not great at parenting, were they?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: She was not always called such. She is known by her deeds now, rather than her name.

steps.player: So if the Devourer is the bad sibling, does that make Icthlarin the good one?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: That is the common belief, but things are rarely that simple. In some ways, neither of them are good or bad.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Icthlarin is the god of the dead. He takes care of the passing of souls to their next life. The Devourer is the goddess of destruction, and that is what she craves.

steps.player: I thought you said she wasn't evil?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: That's not quite what I said. Still, is destruction enough to make one evil? Fire destroys, but is that evil?

steps.player: Um... no, but it also creates heat.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: We could have an overlong theological debate now, but let's instead get to my point. Destruction has a place, so maybe the Devourer does as well. However, she has taken it too far.

steps.player: How?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: The Devourer wishes to destroy every soul in existence, living or dead. As you can imagine, this has brought her into conflict with Icthlarin.

steps.player: Ah, I see where this is going. The cats are used to protect the dead from the Devourer, like you said earlier. But who protects the cats?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Well anticipated. The Devourer is terrified of cats for reasons I will not explain. However, her followers, although few in number, are not. I ensure the survival of cats. For this service, Icthlarin grants me eternal life.

steps.player: So, then, you are a follower of Icthlarin?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Nothing of the sort. As I've said before, I have no interest in humans and their gods. I look after my kind. For that, Icthlarin looks after me.

options.text: What's going on in this city?
This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

steps.player: This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

options.text: What's going on in this city?

steps.player: What's going on in this city?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I thought that would be pretty obvious.

steps.player: Well, I could benefit from your point of view. You seem the independent type.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Flattery, my adventurer, will get you everywhere. But to answer your question, Sophanem has been struck with plagues.

steps.player: More than one?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Quite a number. There's a plague of frogs to the west. In the east, you can also find locusts.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: The cows have only been producing sour milk since the outbreak, and the residents have been struck down by a rash of spots.

steps.player: The residents? There are a lot of living people here for a city of the dead.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Sophanem is called the city of the dead because the dead are brought here. Death plays a rather large role in the beliefs of the people and, as a result, the business.

options.text: This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

steps.player: This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

options.text: I'll go speak with the High Priest.

steps.player: I'll go speak with the High Priest.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: What do you want, cursed one?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: The Sphinx told me to find the High Priest of Icthlarin.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: A likely story. She would never reduce herself to talk to one as lowly as you, never mind help you!

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: High Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: You! I will have no dealings with those who plunder the houses of the dead.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: Wait! The Sphinx told me that I should talk to you.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: High Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: The Sphinx? Is it possible? That contrary old cat has never done anything to help us. Prove it!
If player does not have the token:

steps.player: She gave me a token to show you, but I lost it.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well then stop wasting my time! Can't you see I'm trying to put a stop to these plagues?
If the player has the token:
You hand the token to the High Priest.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well this is... unexpected...

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: So what do you want from me, thief?

steps.player: I appreciate it doesn't look great right now, but I'm not actually a bad person.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well you could have fooled me! Good people don't rob from the dead!

steps.player: It wasn't me! Well... it was, I guess. I didn't do it on purpose though. I was hypnotised!

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Hypnotised?

steps.player: Yes! There was this wanderer! She had me break into that pyramid to steal... a burial jar... I think. It's all still a bit confusing.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: This is all a disaster! The plagues were bad enough, but now we've got hypnotised adventurers plundering tombs! I've only just started this job as well!

steps.player: You do seem to be going through a rough patch. Do you know what caused the plagues?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: We fear they are a punishment sent by the gods. Perhaps we have displeased Icthlarin in some way. Maybe I am to blame. All this only started after I became High Priest.

steps.player: Well I'm not sure if I can help with your plagues, but I need to fix whatever mess I caused in that pyramid. Can you help me?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Oh, er... I suppose the burial jar you took must be returned as soon as possible. That will allow my predecessor to rest once more.

steps.player: I can do that. Do you have any advice for me when it comes to the pyramid?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I don't think so... No wait! There is something important.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: As with many of our tombs, the pyramid has magical seals to protect it from the Devourer, the goddess of destruction. The fact that you were able to get in before means that you must have a cat.

steps.player: Well... yes. But how did you know that?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Cats act as guardians against the Devourer. I'm surprised the Sphinx didn't tell you this. As such, only a cat can open the pyramid door.

steps.player: I see. I guess that makes sense.

options.text: Why is it so important that the jar be returned?
Can you tell me more about the plagues.
Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.
Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

putting-things-right-talking-to-the-high.text: If the player does not have the canopic jar:

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: One of my priests found this lying outside the pyramid. Please try to be more respectful of our dead.
The High Priest gives you a burial jar.

steps.player: Oops. I'll make sure I look after it this time. Sorry.

putting-things-right-talking-to-the-high.text: If the player has the jar:

steps.player: Hello.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Have you managed to return the jar yet?

steps.player: No, not yet.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Please hurry. The people are beginning to... well...

steps.player: What? Question your sanity?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: No, just my authority. Don't forget that to enter the pyramid, you'll need a cat.

options.text: Why is it so important that the jar be returned?

steps.player: Why is it so important that the jar be returned?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well those jars are a key part of our burial practices. To remove one is to directly insult not just Icthlarin, but all those that have passed on to the next life.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Not to mention, it wasn't just any jar you took. You stole a jar from the tomb of our former High Priest! Why do you think his ghost is now wandering the city once more?

steps.player: But what will happen if I don't return the jar?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Have you not noticed the plagues already filling our city? How long before Klenter calls upon Icthlarin to send a few more?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: For all we know, the plagues we already have could be punishment for your grave robbing!

steps.player: Hey, don't go blaming me for that. Those plagues were here before I even met that wanderer!

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Perhaps Icthlarin foresaw what would happen and sent the plagues as a pre-emptive punishment?

steps.player: You really think he'd do that?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I don't know... Icthlarin is a patient and forgiving god. It does not make sense to me that he would do this to us.

steps.player: Maybe he's not the one responsible.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Perhaps. Either way, that jar needs to be returned.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the plagues.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the plagues.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: They started a few days ago. We have locusts in the east of the city and frogs in the west. The cows have started to produce sour milk, and all of us have become infected with some sort of pox.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Once it became clear how bad it was, Menaphos, our neighbouring city, closed their gates to us and everyone else. We closed our own gates soon after.

steps.player: That can't have been an easy choice to make.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I didn't want to, but the other priests insisted. We had to stop the plagues from spreading. It seems that our choice was the right one. So far, the plagues have remained contained, but at a great cost.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Many of our citizens are trapped outside the city. Some are stuck in Menaphos, with more in other parts of the desert.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: However, that may well be for the best. Without trade from other settlements, we've been struggling to even feed the few of us left in the city.

steps.player: How much longer do you think you can last?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Not long. We need to find a way to stop the plagues soon.

options.text: Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Icthlarin is the son of Tumeken and Elidinis and brother to the Devourer. He is the Menaphite god of the dead. He is responsible for ensuring the safe passage of all souls from this life to the next.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Here in Sophanem, we support Icthlarin in his role by making sure the dead are suitably prepared for their journey.

steps.player: So is Icthlarin only responsible for those that die in the desert?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: No. While Icthlarin is only worshipped here, his responsibilities stretch across all of Gielinor. He cares not for an individual's beliefs. All who pass on, enter his care.

steps.player: I imagine there are plenty of people out there who have a different take on things.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Which they are welcome to. It does not change the facts.

steps.player: You seem very sure in these 'facts'.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: While most of the gods, Tumeken and Elidinis included, may be long gone from Gielinor, Icthlarin remains. His important role in caring for the dead means that he is still able to interact with us.

steps.player: So you've met him?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well... no. While he is able to walk among us if he desires, he chooses not to so as to respect our way of life. Not to mention, his role requires his constant attention.

steps.player: I see. Fair enough.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Long ago, back when Tumeken and Elidinis still walked these lands, they had two children. Icthlarin, god of the dead, was one. The other was Amascut, the goddess of rebirth.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: For a time, Icthlarin and Amascut worked together in harmony. Icthlarin would ensure most souls are safely guided to the next life, while Amascut would select a small number to be reborn.

steps.player: But something happened?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Yes. During a great war over these lands, Amascut became corrupted. She was warped into the Devourer, becoming the goddess of destruction.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Since then, her only goal has been to devour every soul in existence, both living and dead.

steps.player: The Sphinx told me something similar, but her interpretation was a bit different.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: We here have a lot of respect for the Sphinx. However, you should be careful of her words. She does not know the gods like we priests do.

steps.player: So is the Devourer still around?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Unfortunately so. Most gods have long since left this world. However, the Devourer was able to find a way to remain.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Luckily for us, some of her former priestesses were able to weaken her, but she still poses a great threat.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.player: I need to get the burial jar for the mistress...

putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.speaker: Apparition
putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.text: You will not defile this place!

putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.player: So I really did steal the jar. I need to return it as fast as I can.

putting-things-right-attempting-to-take-.player: I've already caused enough trouble over these jars. I'll just leave them alone.

putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.speaker: Priest
putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.text: Bother me not. I am preparing for the ceremony. I'm sure even you can curb your trivial demands until after that.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Have you managed to return the jar yet?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Wonderful! Now we can prepare for the ceremony.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: The ceremony to reconsecrate Klenter's tomb of course!

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: It would have been nice for you to mention this earlier.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Sorry, with all this plague business, it must have slipped my mind.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: You're the High Priest of Icthlarin, but you forgot a key ceremony?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Well if you want to try running a city with multiple plagues, you're welcome to take over.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: That's not what I... Never mind.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Good. Now, this ceremony is very dangerous, so we must ensure everything is done correctly.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Well the pyramid has these magical seals on it...

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: ... to protect it from the Devourer. Yes, you told me earlier.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Right! Of course I did. Well for us to properly reconsecrate the tomb, we must first remove those seals. That means that once we begin, the pyramid will be vulnerable until the ceremony is complete.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Now, we made many of the preparations while you were gone, but the carpenter and the embalmer could both use a hand. Could you go and speak with them?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: Why do I have to help?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Did you forget that this is all your fault?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: I guess I assumed that by returning the jar I stole, my job would be done.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: The job will be done when Klenter is at rest once more.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Besides, thanks to the plagues, we're not allowing people to leave the city. However, as you seem to be unaffected, I've told the guards to make an exception for you.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: And that means I'm best placed to help. Fine. The carpenter and the embalmer, did you say?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: That's right. We need the carpenter to create a new holy symbol for the ceremony. He lives over to the east. The embalmer also needs help gathering some supplies. He lives just south of here.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the plagues.
Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.
Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-hig.text: Have you helped the embalmer and the carpenter yet?

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-hig.text: The embalmer lives just south of here and the carpenter lives over to the east. Please hurry. We need to get this ceremony performed before some other bad thing happens.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the plagues.
Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.
Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-a-pries.player: Hello. Can I go through this gate?

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-a-pries.speaker: Priest
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-a-pries.text: Yes. The High Priest has given you permission to come and go as you please.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Oh, it's you. I hear you're helping us now. To be honest, I'm still not thrilled to have you around, but so be it.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.player: I guess that's probably the best I can ask for, given the situation. Anyway, the High Priest said you needed help gathering some supplies for the ceremony.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: That's right. I need three things, but the quarantine is making some of them hard to obtain.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: First, I need some salt. Normally I get mine from the salt lake just north of the city. Just fill a bucket from the lake and then use the suntrap outside to separate the salt from the water.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Next, I need some tree sap. You can use a knife to extract some from a tree, but make sure you have a bucket ready. Most coniferous evergreen trees should have some. They're the cone-shaped ones.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Finally, I need some linen. That one shouldn't be too hard. The local cloth salesman should have some.
If the player has a bucket of sap:

steps.text: You hand a bucket of sap to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has salt:

steps.text: You hand some salt to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has linen:

steps.text: You hand a sheet of linen to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player gave an item to the Embalmer:

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: Well that was unexpected. Thank you.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: You cut the tree and allow some sap to drip into your bucket.
If the player does not have a bucket of saltwater:

steps.text: You don't have anything suitable to use with the suntrap

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has a bucket of saltwater:

steps.text: You pour the water into the suntrap and it quickly evaporates, leaving you with a pile of salt.
pile of salt

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Raetul
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Good afternoon.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Raetul
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: It's hot and sunny, which is good enough for me. So can I help you with anything?

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.player: I've met with the town's embalmer and he mentioned that he needed a few things, linen being one of them.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player does not have 30 coins:

steps.speaker: Raetul
steps.text: Well I can sell you a sheet of linen for 30 coins.

steps.player: I don't have that much on me. I'll be back.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has 30 coins:

steps.speaker: Raetul
steps.text: Of course. That will be 30 coins please and thank you.
The merchant takes your money and hands you a sheet of linen before you realise that a transaction has been agreed.

steps.player: What the...

steps.speaker: Raetul
steps.text: Do come again.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Oh, it's you. Any luck obtaining those items?
If the player has a bucket of sap and the Embalmer still needs sap:

steps.text: You hand a bucket of sap to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has salt and the Embalmer still needs salt:

steps.text: You hand some salt to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has linen and the Embalmer still needs linen:

steps.text: You hand a sheet of linen to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the Embalmer now has all the items:

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: Thank you. I think that's everything I need.

steps.player: Great. I guess I should go and see how the carpenter is getting on.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player gave an item but the Embalmer still needs more:

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: Thank you.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player did not have any items the Embalmer needs:

steps.player: I'm still working on it.

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: Well you'd better get a move on.

options.text: Where do I get tree sap?

steps.speaker: Embalmer

options.condition: If the Embalmer still needs salt

steps.player: Where do I get salt?

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: Normally I get mine from the salt lake just north of the city. Just fill a bucket from the lake and then use the suntrap outside to separate the salt from the water.

options.condition: If the Embalmer still needs linen

steps.player: Where do I get linen?

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: The local cloth salesman should have some for sale.

steps.player: Okay, I'll get going.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Oh, it's you. You've already gathered everything I need. I'm sure you have plenty of other things to be doing.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.player: I guess I do still need to speak to the carpenter.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Hello, adventurer. The High Priest says that you're here to help us.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.player: That's right. He asked me to come and speak to you about a holy symbol for the ceremony.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Ah yes, it needs to be made from willow. Thing is, there's a small problem with that.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.player: Is this the part where you need me to get you something?

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Wow, you're quick. I'm all out of willow, and due to the quarantine, I'm unable to leave the city to get more. However, the High Priest mentioned that a special exception has been made for you.
If the player does not have willow logs:

steps.player: Meaning I can leave the city and get you some. Alright, I'll be back soon.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: If the player has willow logs:

steps.player: Well there's actually no need for me to go anywhere. I already have some willow logs here.

steps.text: You give the carpenter some willow logs.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: Thank you. Now, just give me a moment...

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: There we go. All done.
The carpenter gives you a holy symbol.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: I imagine the High Priest will be down in the pyramid by now. You should take that to him as soon as possible.

steps.player: Will do. Thanks.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Do you have that wood for me?
If the player has willow logs:

steps.text: You give the carpenter some willow logs.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: Thank you. Now, just give me a moment...

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: There we go. All done.
The carpenter gives you a holy symbol.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: I imagine the High Priest will be down in the pyramid by now. You should take that to him as soon as possible.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: If the player does not have willow logs:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: I'll be here when you do.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Hello, adventurer. I'm still working on that symbol. Do you have something else you can do in the meantime?

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.player: Yes, I need to help out the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Well you're probably best off doing that then. I'm sure I'll have it ready by the time you're done.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Hello, adventurer. The symbol is all finished now.
The carpenter gives you a holy symbol.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: I imagine the High Priest will be down in the pyramid by now. You should take that to him as soon as possible.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-emb.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-emb.text: Well I have lots to do, so good day.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-car.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-car.text: Hello. Have you given the symbol to the High Priest yet?
If the player still has the holy symbol:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: Well you should as soon as possible. He'll be down in the pyramid by now.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-car.text: If the player lost the holy symbol:

steps.player: Actually, there's a slight problem with the symbol.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: What? But I made it to exactly match the drawings from the High Priest. I can't believe this!

steps.player: Oh, I'm sure the symbol itself is fine. The problem is... I lost it.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: Agh, you fool! Is stupidity the newest plague in town?

steps.player: Can you please calm down? I gave you plenty of willow. I'm sure there's some left over for another symbol.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: Fine. Just give me a moment...

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: There we go. All done. Try not to lose this one.
The carpenter gives you a holy symbol.

steps.speaker: Carpenter
steps.text: Now you should take that to the High Priest as soon as possible. He'll be down in the pyramid by now.

steps.player: Will do.

reconsecrating-the-tomb-entering-klenter.text: If the player does not have a cat follower or in the inventory:
If the player has a cat follower or in the inventory:

steps.player: Hey puss! Think you can open this door again?

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Meeeow.
The player enters the pyramid

reconsecrating-the-tomb-flashback-3-jump.text: As you go to make the jump, another sense of deja-vu sweeps over you...
The player has a flashback of being at the other side of the pit inside the pyramid

reconsecrating-the-tomb-flashback-3-jump.player: I need to hide the mistress's symbol in the ceremonial room...
I need to hide the mistress's symbol in the ceremonial room...
No... It must be somewhere more secret...

reconsecrating-the-tomb-flashback-3-jump.text: You hide the unholy symbol in the sarcophagus.

reconsecrating-the-tomb-flashback-3-jump.player: Yes... Now the mistress can enter the pyramid whenever she pleases...
The wanderer! She's going to attack the ceremony! I need to warn them!

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: A cutscene begins of the ceremony

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: Ah there you are. Do you have the holy symbol?

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.player: Wait! We can't begin the ceremony!

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: Wanderer
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: You have done well, adventurer. All my brother's dogs in one place, with no one around to save them.

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: It can't be... It's the Devourer!

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.player: I'm not your slave any more!

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: Amascut
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: Shame. Not to worry though, I have plenty more.

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: Amascut
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: You! Priest of the dog lord. You are now mine. Kill your brethren!

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: Protect us, adventurer! We must complete the ceremony!

the-devourer-revealed-defeating-the-pose.text: The priest seems to recover from the Devourer's spell

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-a-pries.speaker: Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-a-pries.text: You have surprised me... I commend you for your efforts.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Thank you so much, adventurer. Thanks to you, we were able to complete the ceremony.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: Well it was the least I could do. After all, it was sort of my fault all this happened.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Well on that note, what exactly did happen there? That was the Devourer!

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: It seems the wanderer that hypnotised me was actually the Devourer all along.
I'm guessing the reason she had me steal that burial jar was because she knew you'd have to gather here to reconsecrate the tomb again.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: She wanted to kill us all in one go?

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: Yes, and she had me plant an unholy symbol here to allow her to teleport right in.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Well once again, thank you. Without you, the Devourer would have struck a devastating blow against Icthlarin.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: Here's that holy symbol, by the way.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: You give the holy symbol to the High Priest.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Thank you. We wouldn't have been able to complete the ceremony without that in our presence.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: We have a few things to finish here, but then we'll head back up into the city. Please join us there.

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: All of a sudden, a final sense of deja-vu sweeps over you...
The player has a flashback of meeting Icthlarin in the pyramid

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.speaker: Icthlarin
the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: And what do we have here?

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.player: I must do as the mistress commands...

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.speaker: Icthlarin
the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: Did my sister really think that I would not sense her presence here?

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.speaker: Icthlarin
the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: Amascut! Release your hold on this human!

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.player: Well I guess that explains why Amascut's control over me was broken. Not every day the god of the dead comes to your rescue.

finishing-up-speaking-with-the-high-prie.speaker: High Priest
finishing-up-speaking-with-the-high-prie.text: Ah, there you are. You were gone for quite a while. As a thank you for what you've done, I have a little trinket for you. I'm sure you'll get a huge amount of enjoyment out of it.

finishing-up-trying-to-enter-the-pyramid.player: I think it would be best if I stayed out of this tomb after what happened last time.

trpgum.speaker: Sphinx
trpgum.text: I have no interest in speaking with you. You should bring your cat to me again. The two of us have much to discuss.

46UaUb.player: I think the High Priest mentioned something about needing a cat to enter the pyramid.

standard-dialogue-post-quest.npc: You found those people who went missing! Did you see them? Did you see the night people?

standard-dialogue-post-quest.player: Sort of. I wouldn't call them people though.

standard-dialogue-post-quest.npc: But they're real! They're actually real! No one believed me, but I knew they were real!

steps.player: Hi.

steps.npc: You know, there are so many different ways to greet people. Hello, 'ello, hello there...

steps.player: That still only counts as one!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?

steps.player: I'm great, thank you!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?

steps.player: Indeed.
Hi.

steps.npc: What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

steps.player: Nothing.

steps.npc: Would you like to buy or sell anything?

steps.player: Yes, please.

steps.text: Ifaba's General Store

steps.player: No, thanks.

standard-dialogue-if-the-2021-halloween-.npc: Sorry, dearie, if I stop to chat I'll lose count. Talk to my sister instead; she likes to chat. You'll find her upstairs in the church.

steps.player: Hello Iffie, remember our adventure?

standard-dialogue-before-25-january-2022.npc: Sorry, dearie, if I stop to chat I'll lose count.

standard-dialogue.npc: Can I help you at all?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Ignatius Vulcan. Once I was - like you - an adventurer, but that was before I realised the beauty and power of flame! Just look at this...

steps.text: Ignatius makes a fire.

steps.player: Yeeouch!

steps.npc: Stare into the flame and witness the purity and power of fire! As my attraction to flame grew, so did my skills at firelighting. I began to neglect my combat skills, my Mining skills and my questing. Who needs such
mundane skills when one can harness the power of fire? After years of practice I am now the acknowledged Master of Flame! Everything must be purified by fire!

steps.player: Okaaaay! Err, I'll be going now. Umm, get better soon.

options.text: What is that cape you're wearing?

steps.player: What is that cape you're wearing?

steps.npc: This is a Skillcape of Firemaking, so bright that wearing it lights up caves! I was given it in recognition of my skill as the greatest firemaker in the lands! I AM the Master of Flame!

steps.player: Hmm, I'll be going now. Keep a sharp look out for those men with their white jackets!
No, thanks.

steps.npc: Okay, keep the fire burning.

options.text: Can I buy a Skillcape of Firemaking?

steps.player: Can I buy a Skillcape of Firemaking?

steps.npc: Of course you can. You are already a master of fire, you just need the cape to prove it. The cape is so bright that wearing it will light up dark caves. That'll be 99000 coins, please.

steps.player: No thanks, that's too much.

steps.npc: Sorry to hear that, I'll be here if you change your mind.

steps.player: Okay, that seems reasonable.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough money:

steps.player: But, unfortunately, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.npc: Well, come back and see me when you do.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins but not enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Unfortunately all Skillcapes are only available with a free hood, it's part of a skill promotion deal; buy one get one free, you know. So you'll need to free up some inventory space before I can sell you one.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins and enough inventory space:
99,000 coins
Firemaking cape and Firemaking hood

steps.npc: I'm sure you'll look hot in that cape.

with-a-firemaking-cape-but-no-hood.npc: Can I help you at all?

options.text: Can I buy a Skillcape of Firemaking?

steps.player: May I have another hood for my cape, please?

standard-dialogue.player: Hello. What do you do here?

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello. My name is Imerominia and I'm the library horologist.

steps.player: Horologist? What does that mean?

steps.npc: Horology is the study and measurement of time. Specifically, I study how time and dates have been historically recorded.
For example, the date convention in Great Kourend is to state the number of days and decades since the signing of the Royal Accord of Twill.

steps.player: Days and decades? That's a bit confusing.

steps.npc: Yes, it's an interesting convention. Truth be told, most in the kingdom prefer to use the same date format as you'll find used elsewhere.
However, as this is the Historical Archive, we stick to the dates used historically within Kourend.

options.text: Tell me more about the Royal Accord of Twill.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Royal Accord of Twill.

steps.npc: The Royal Accord of Twill was signed by the rulers of each of the houses 139 decades ago, following the great famine.
The Accord declared that each house will, in turn, rule the Kingdom of Great Kourend for one decade in rotation, based on lots drawn.

steps.text: If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: You may find a book in the Grand Library with further information. Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Is the Royal Accord of Twill still honoured today?

steps.player: Is the Royal Accord of Twill honoured today?

steps.npc: Our kingdom has advanced somewhat over the many decades since the Accord. Though some parts of the Accord remain intact, the Kourend Council now rules Great Kourend.

steps.player: Was the Accord ever breached?

steps.npc: Indeed it was. In the 13th decade, King Shayzien III seized control of Kourend using the military under his command.
The full set of laws within the Accord haven't been followed since. However, some of them were reinstated in the 47th decade, by King Byrne I.

steps.player: Fascinating. What happened during that time?

steps.npc: During the 20th decade, King Shayzien VI married the daughter of Lord Hosidius. Four decades later their son was crowned king.
He took the name King Hosidius IV in an attempt to distance the family from the breaking of the Royal Accord of Twill.
King Hosidius IV followed by his son, King Hosidius V ruled Kourend until the early days of the 33rd decade.
It was then that King Shayzien VII took control of the kingdom. His rule was a notably violent one.
King Shayzien VII was killed some five decades later during the Battle of the Concourse. He was succeeded by the dark mage, Xeric.
Xeric ruled Kourend for more than ten dark decades using an army of lizardmen. This time period was known as the Age of Strife.
Xeric was eventually killed during the 47th decade and succeeded by King Byrne I.

options.text: Can you tell me more about Xeric?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Xeric?

steps.npc: Ah, I do not have much more information on him. You should speak to Ektheme, our Xerician expert.

steps.player: Thanks.
No thanks.

steps.text: If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: The Royal Accord of Twill no longer plays much part in the rulership of Kourend. It was breached in the 13th decade when King Shayzien III seized control of the kingdom. It hasn't been honoured since.
That said, it was the basis for Rose's Accord, which sets out how the kingdom is currently ruled today. As decreed in Rose's Accord, the Hosidius family are now the royal family of Kourend.

We have the original Royal Accord of Twill safely stored here. Although it's not available for public viewing, there are copies available within the Grand Library. Is there anything else I can help you with?

standard-dialogue-jumping-1.npc: Hop! Hop! Take that you stupid rock!

standard-dialogue-jumping-2.npc: Me wrecky relic! Me wrecky relic! Hahaha!

standard-dialogue-jumping-overhead.npc: Oh no, is the relic starting to break? Oops!
I can jump higher than you all!

standard-dialogue-dying-in-yama-s-lair-f.npc: Gratz on your Nightmare Mode loss
Seriously, you died to a 1? Eat a cabbage next time, then you might survive. Yuck.

steps.player: Give me a quest please.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Well seeing as you asked nicely... I could do with some help.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: The wizard Grayzag next door decided he didn't like me so he enlisted an army of hundreds of imps.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: These imps stole all sorts of my things. Most of these things I don't really care about, just eggs and balls of string and things.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: But they stole my four magical beads. There was a red one, a yellow one, a black one, and a white one.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: These imps have now spread out all over the kingdom. Could you get my beads back for me?

steps.prompt: Start the Imp Catcher quest?

steps.text: If the player already has all four beads in their inventory:

steps.player: Well this is a surprising turn of events!

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: What?

steps.player: Well I just so happen to have all of those beads on me!

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Are you saying that you stole my beads all this time and I've been blaming these imps!?

steps.player: No, not at all! I just found them throughout my travels and presumed somebody would need them at some point.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Bah! Fine.
(Continues in Quest complete section.)
If the player does not have all four beads in their inventory:

steps.player: I'll try.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: That's great, thank you.

steps.player: I've better things to do than chase imps.

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Well if you're not interested in the quests I have to give you, don't waste my time by asking me for them.

options.text: Give me a quest or else!

steps.player: Give me a quest or else!

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Or else what? You'll attack me?

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Hahaha!

options.text: Just stop messing around and give me a quest!

steps.player: Just stop messing around and give me a quest!

steps.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
steps.text: Ah now you're assuming I have one to give.

finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.text: So how are you doing finding my beads?

finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.text: Well get on with it. I've lost a white bead, a red bead, a black bead, and a yellow bead. Go kill some imps!

finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.text: So how are you doing finding my beads?

finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.player: I have found some of your beads.

finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-miz.text: Come back when you have them all. The colour of the four beads that I need are red, yellow, black, and white. Go chase some imps!

finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-gra.speaker: Wizard Grayzag
finding-the-beads-speaking-to-wizard-gra.text: You're a fool, [player name]. Do you really think you'll find four imps out of thousands? Good luck. Ha!

finishing-up-giving-the-beads-to-wizard-.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
finishing-up-giving-the-beads-to-wizard-.text: So how are you doing finding my beads?

finishing-up-giving-the-beads-to-wizard-.player: I've got all four beads. It was hard work I can tell you.

finishing-up-quest-complete.speaker: Wizard Mizgog
finishing-up-quest-complete.text: Give them here and I'll check that they really are MY beads, before I give you your reward. You'll like it, it's an amulet of accuracy.
You give four coloured beads to Wizard Mizgog.
Wizard Mizgog places the four beads on the table and casts a spell on them.
The wizard hands you an amulet.

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-2.player: Hey imp, can you hear me?

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-2.text: Of course I can hear ya, ya great big ape. You know, 'veres not even enuf space to swing Bob about in 'ere. How about a breather? You know, stretch me pins for a bit?

options.text: No, I'm going to keep you in there.

steps.player: No, I'm going to keep you in there. I might keep you as a pet.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Pet!! Nah mate. I fink you'd find dat you'd be my pet!! We is not makin good pets.

steps.player: Really? Why not?

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Coz...errr...

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: We bite! Yeah we is biting and...and...er...

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: We is fire risk! Yeah dat's it! We be burning down your housey and stealin' all ya shiny gems. Oh, and da beads!! Mmmm, beads.

steps.player: Fire risk? How does that work?

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Is those wizzies. Dey don't like de imps so dey make us go BOOOM!!

steps.player: It's not that bad. You've got four big windows, charming company...er...

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Yeah, we's love tiny, crampt space. It be magical. But I is a busy imp, innit? Dragons needin' ticklin', shiny relics needin' stealin', you know how it goes.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: So, if you's know whas good for ya, you'd be lettin' me go, right?

steps.player: Don't I get three wishes?

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Nah, mate. Dunno what you're chirpin' about.

steps.player: Well, you're a magical creature aren't you? Surely I get some wishes for capturing you, or releasing you, or something?

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I'm finking dat you be a bit confoosed. I is an imp, not some namby-pamby genie or some kinda fairy. Ye can tell by the horns.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Sayin' dat, I don't fancy being cooped up like one of me uncle's pigeons. Tell you what, is there anything you need deliverin' to the bank? I may not be no cunjerer or sommink like dat, but I can get about nice

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: an quick like. If you let me scarper, I'll take a couple of fings to the bank for ya. You game?

steps.player: Okay, that sounds fair.

options.text: Surely it should be three items?

steps.player: Surely it should be three items? Then it's one item per wish.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I've already told ya, I ain't no bloomin' fairy. Besides, you know wot dey say, three's a crowd innit? I don't fink I can hop about carryin' more dan 2 fings.

options.text: I've got nothing I need banking right now.

steps.player: I've got nothing I need banking right now.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Great, just blinkin great, dat is. I'll just sit about countin' zombie sheep then. One...two...two and a bit...three and a bit more... I don't fink sheep 'ave dat many legs...

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-1.player: Hey imp, are you still there?

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-1.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-1.text: An who's fault is that, eh? EH? I got betta fings to do dan sit ere waitin' for ya. 'Ave ya made up ya mind what else I'm luggin about?

steps.player: Yes I have.

options.text: No, I'm afraid you're going to have to wait a bit longer.

steps.player: No, I'm afraid you're going to have to wait a bit longer.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Dat's alright guv'nor. I'll get back to me luvverly dream about beads. Big shiny beads. Love it!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit items while in the Mage Training Arena, Chambers of Xeric, Trouble Brewing, Soul Wars, or is teleblocked:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Sorry, guv'nor, I seem to 'ave caught meself; I can't do nuffink right now.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit items that cannot be taken out of a player-owned house:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: What use would that be in a bank? You'd be better off leaving it in yer house.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a light source:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Ow! That's hot! Put it in yer bank yerself!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a looting bag:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: No way, I can't bank your looting bag.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a bloated toad:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Nope, between me and you, that toad doesn't look stable.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a book of knowledge:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: What good is banking that book? Just read it or throw it away!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a glowing fungus:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I'm no expert, but when a mushroom glows that much, I'm guessing it's dangerous. Keep it away from me.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a gnomeball:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I'm not touching a gnome ball; that's a vicious game! I might die!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit Karamjan rum:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Don't you know? You can get into trouble for giving alcohol to minors, and I'm pretty small, it has to be said.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit skeletal gorilla bones:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: There's something weird about those bones; I ain't touching them.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a stick:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: It's a flipping stick; why bother banking that? You humans are crazy sometimes.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a lamp:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I know what lamps like that contain; I'm not touching it. I might get hurt.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit an unholy symbol:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Sorry, I'm not going to risk upsetting someone by bundling random holy symbols I don't recognise into bank vaults.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit Ana in a barrel:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Hey, if she wants to use the bank, why can't she use her own two legs? Besides, she's too big.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit an unbankable item that is not listed above:

steps.text: The imp seems uneasy about teleporting that.

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...

steps.player: Strange how?

steps.npc: Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
Down with rutabagas!
I may be a werewolf, but I do love the smell of frying onions.
Onion skins very thin, mild winter coming in. Onion skins very tough, coming winter very rough.

When you cut onions they release a gas that makes you cry.
Maybe I'll start an Onion Guild.
People are like onions. They have lots of layers and sometimes smell quite pungent.

Life is like an onion...well, sort of.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.text: You're back. Any luck in Canifis?

the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.player: I went back to the place where I first met Vanstrom. He was gone though.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.text: I feared as much. Worry not though. The day will come when we get our revenge on him and the rest of his kind.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.text: Anyway, now that you're back, there was something I was hoping you'd help us with.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-veliaf-hurtz.prompt: Start the In Aid of the Myreque quest?

steps.player: What do you need?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Now that our base of operations is no longer safe, we're going to need to relocate before the vyrewatch descend on us.

steps.player: Seems like a wise move. What part do I play?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: To the south of Mort'ton there's an old town known as Burgh de Rott. The place was abandoned but I hear some escapees from Meiyerditch have made their home there.

steps.player: And you want me to scout the place out?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Exactly. Head down to Burgh de Rott and see if you can find a suitable place for our new hideout. While you're there, do what you can to forge a good relationship with the townspeople.

steps.player: I'll get it done.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Be sure to take a weapon of silver with you. You'll find it of great use if vampyres attack. Good luck to you.

steps.player: Sorry. I'm not interested.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Very well. You know where we are if you change your mind.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Well met, [player name].

steps.player: What do I need to do again?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Head to Burgh de Rott and see if the town has a suitable location for our new hideout. While you're there, do what you can to forge a good relationship with the townspeople.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: You'll find the town just south of Mort'ton. Good luck.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-radigad-ponfit.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
the-myreque-s-job-offer-radigad-ponfit.text: Hello. I hear you're doing some important work for Veliaf. You'd best get to it.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-polmafi-ferdygri.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
the-myreque-s-job-offer-polmafi-ferdygri.text: Not so good. It's great to see you're helping us out though.

the-myreque-s-job-offer-ivan-strom.speaker: Ivan Strom
the-myreque-s-job-offer-ivan-strom.text: Is something new and exciting happening?

the-myreque-s-job-offer-ivan-strom.player: Maybe. Veliaf has asked me to do some work for him. Hopefully it will benefit you all.

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ope.text: The gate has been locked. Clearly the townspeople don't want visitors.

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ope.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ope.text: Get out of it! You're not having our food or our blood!

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.text: Get out of it! You ain't comming in here to get our blood or our food!

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.player: What on earth makes you think I want your food or your blood?

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.text: Hey! Don't try to sweet talk me. I know you want something! But we got nothing! Nothing!

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.text: What blood we've got, we're keeping for ourselves! You can tell that stinking Vanstrom to go suck a cow's udder!

entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-attempting-to-ent.text: And as for food, why we've barely got enough to feed ourselves. So you ain't having none!

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: This is our town! We live here. It's called Burgh de Rott, and you ain't coming in!

steps.player: Where did you all come from?

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: We escaped from the vampyres. They had us trapped in Meiyerditch to drink our blood! Yuck!

steps.player: What's Meiyerditch?

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: As if you don't know! It's that dark city to the east where humans are kept like animals to feed those greedy evil vampyres!

steps.player: Sounds like an awful place! Let me in and I'll help you!

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: Yeah, okay then eh! No way! You can't trick me like that!

options.text: Why would I want your blood?

steps.player: Why would I want your blood?

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: Your probably one of them stinking vampyres in disguise! You ain't coming in!

steps.player: I don't want your blood!

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: We don't care. You probably want our food then, so you ain't coming in!

options.text: Why would I want your food?

steps.player: Why would I want your food?

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: You probably want to eat it all and we ain't gonna let you!

steps.player: But I don't want to eat your food. I'm plenty healthy enough!

steps.speaker: Florin
steps.text: Well, that's as maybe, but yous probably wants to drink ours blood! And you aint having it and you aint coming in!

steps.player: Okay, goodbye.

entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-t.text: If you placed food here, it would just get ruined. You decide against it.

entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-s.text: The chest contains some empty packages. It looks like they were used to hold food.

entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-u.text: You gingerly place the food into the chest.

entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-u.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-u.text: Blimey, did you see that? [He/She] put some food in the chest for us! [He/She]'s probably not after anything!

entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-s.speaker: Florin
entering-burgh-de-rott-depositing-food-s.text: Hey, what did you put in that chest? Is it something tasty, like a nice cooked snail? Or perhaps a well matured piece of cheese with some fresh bread? Ohhh, I bet it's dead tasty...

entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.text: Dialogue is the same between citizens unless specified, names are changed

options.text: How come you have no food?

steps.player: How come you have no food?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Well obviously we just don't seem to get out to the shops like we used to!

steps.player: How come you have no food?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: We can only stay in the village and there's precious little food in here, just rats to live on! Not very appetising.

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: There's also nowhere to store any food around here, the town is incredibly run down.

steps.player: How come you have no food?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: We dare not leave the town for fear that the vampyres might spot us and force us to pay a blood tithe.

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: We're all very weak and would most likely die if they took more blood from us.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: This is our town! We's live here. It's called Burgh de Rott. It aint much to look at, but it's our home.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.text: If speaking to one of Florin, Luscion, Sergiu, Sorin, Ileana, Radu, Valeria, Grigore, Emilia:

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: My name's [citizen name]. I do a bit of this, a bit of that. Just try to survive really, there's nothing much else we can do.

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Oh, my name's [citizen name]. I just help out around here, you know, gathering food and so on.

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Not that it makes much difference but my name's [citizen name]. Like all the other survivors here, I just try to make do and get through each day at a time.
If speaking to one of Vasile, Razvan, Luminata:

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Oh hi. I'm [citizen name]. I hunt rats mostly. Speaking of which, this rat tastes awful, but it's the only food we have!

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Huh? I'm [citizen name]. Ravaging after food is what I mostly do. Ocasionally I'll happen across a rat, and that's a good day, just like today!

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Oh, hello. [Citizen name] is the name and I help to keep the village clear of rat infestations. Clearly I love my work, as I bring it home with me... On a stick!
If speaking to one of Simona, Calin, Nicoleta, Mihail:

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: I'm [citizen name]. I'm just trying to stay warm.
If speaking to Elisabeta:

steps.speaker: Elisabeta
steps.text: I'm Elisabeta, the village leader.
If speaking to Teodor:

steps.speaker: Teodor
steps.text: I'm Teodor. I'm a farmer. Not that there's much to grow here.
If speaking to Aurel:

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Aurel
steps.text: I'm Aurel, the village store owner.

steps.player: Can you open the shop for me please?

steps.speaker: Aurel
steps.text: I'm sorry my friend, but I cannot open a store which has no stock.
If speaking to Cornelius:

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Cornelius
steps.text: I'm Cornelius. I don't really do anything here.
If speaking to Gabriela:

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Gabriela
steps.text: I'm Gabriela. I'm looking after my husband who isn't feeling too well!

options.text: Are there any 'out of the way' places here?

steps.player: Are there any 'out of the way' places here?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: How do you mean, 'out of the way'?

steps.player: Somewhere where myself and a couple of friends could hold up for a while without attracting any vampyre attention?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Ah, right, I know what you mean. Hmm, let's think now...

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Well, there's the inn. You could look there I suppose. The cellar would have been useful, but the trapdoor down to it is covered with rubble from a broken wall.

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: The cellar itself is probably filled with rubble as well. But you may be able to do something with it.

steps.player: That could work. Thanks.

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: Listen, if you do decide to join us here, we'll expect you to contribute. You know, help to fix things up a bit.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.text: Dialogue is the same between Ivan, Catalina, Victor, Helena, names are changed

entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.speaker: Child Citizen
entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.text: Sorry. I shouldn't talk to strangers.
The man is too ill to talk.

steps.text: You manage to mine the rubble to pieces.

entering-burgh-de-rott-cleaning-the-inn-.text: Upon clearing the first piece of rubble:

steps.text: You manage to mine the rubble to pieces. You should be able to move what's left out of the cellar now. Though you'll need something to carry it in.
With a pot:
You use a pot to scoop the rubble into a bucket.
With a spade:
You use a spade to scoop the rubble into a bucket.

entering-burgh-de-rott-cleaning-the-inn-.text: Upon clearing a piece of rubble and receiving items:

If inventory is not full:
You find a piece of plaster with some interesting inscriptions on it.

entering-burgh-de-rott-cleaning-the-inn-.text: Upon clearing a piece of rubble and receiving a dusty scroll:

If inventory is not full:
You find a scroll with some interesting writing on it.

entering-burgh-de-rott-cleaning-the-inn-.text: Upon clearing the last piece of rubble:

steps.text: You clear out the last of the rubble.
Camera points at a wall with a plaque and zooms in.
As you clear away the last of the rubble, you notice a dusty looking wall plaque which you hadn't spotted before.

entering-burgh-de-rott-cleaning-the-inn-.text: Trying to drop/empty when in the basement:

steps.text: You'll just fill the room up with rubble again if you [drop/empty] the bucket here.

entering-burgh-de-rott-cleaning-the-inn-.text: Trying to drop/empty when in Burgh de Rott:

steps.text: The people of Burgh de Rott would not be happy if you dumped the rubble here.

entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.speaker: Citizen
entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.text: Hey there. So you're looking to clear out the cellar at the inn? How's it going?

entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.player: Not so bad, but it's a lot of hard work to be honest.

entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.speaker: Citizen
entering-burgh-de-rott-speaking-to-citiz.text: Oh well, I'm sure you can manage.

at-castle-drakan.text: My lord... We've finished our latest round of tithing. I'm afraid we haven't been able to collect the desired amount.

at-castle-drakan.text: I saw your wife today, Gadderanks. She's well.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
at-castle-drakan.text: I hope she stays that way.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Gadderanks
at-castle-drakan.text: My lord Vanstrom, there are precious few human settlements left worth collecting tithes from.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Gadderanks
at-castle-drakan.text: Mort'ton is just a dead town, full of afflicted. Lord Malak was so ill when he drank of them last time.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Gadderanks
at-castle-drakan.text: Canifis is delivering more than expected but that still isn't sufficient.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Gadderanks
at-castle-drakan.text: Please, where should I get the remainder from?

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
at-castle-drakan.text: I couldn't care less for your problems Gadderanks. Just do the job you've been appointed to do.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
at-castle-drakan.text: Wait... Do you smell that? Smoke. It's coming from Burgh de Rott.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Gadderanks
at-castle-drakan.text: But Burgh de Rott is abandoned.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
at-castle-drakan.text: No. Burgh de Rott was abandoned. That is clearly no longer the case.

at-castle-drakan.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
at-castle-drakan.text: It seems you have a fresh appointment, Gadderanks. I hope there will be no more delay.

steps.player: Who's Gadderanks?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: He's some human lackie for the vampyres. His job is to collect blood tithes from all the villages around here. He goes around with his juvinate bodyguards because he's too weak to defend himself.

steps.player: What's a juvinate?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: A form of vampyre. They're stronger than juveniles but not as bad as a full-blown vyre. Still, no one that I've seen has ever gotten the better of one.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: Citizen
steps.text: If I were you, I'd get out of town. Now that Gadderanks is here, I doubt many people will stay around!

steps.player: Maybe I can stop him.

steps.speaker: Citizen

steps.speaker: Gadderanks
steps.text: Oh happy days! It's so good we found all these specimens here! If it hadn't been for some good soul lighting that furnace, we'd have never come down here!

steps.speaker: Gadderanks
steps.text: Now I should be able to make my blood tithe quota... especially after you pay your tithe. You look like an incredibly fit specimen!

steps.speaker: Gadderanks
steps.text: I bet you could pay twice as much as the others before passing out!

steps.speaker: Gadderanks
steps.text: Ha! We'll see about that!

steps.speaker: Gadderanks
steps.text: Do I need to explain it all again? Stand in line ready to pay your blood tithe!

steps.speaker: Vampyre Juvinate
steps.text: We're getting some delicious blood tithes from these sacks of food. Yum!

steps.speaker: Vampyre Juvinate
steps.text: You deaf? We're getting some delicious blood tithes from these sacks of food.

gadderanks-arrives-at-burgh-de-rott-at-t.text: They're draining my blood, that's what they're doing!

gadderanks-arrives-at-burgh-de-rott-at-t.speaker: Gadderanks
gadderanks-arrives-at-burgh-de-rott-at-t.text: I've had enough of you poking your nose in here! If you think you can stop us, go ahead!
