myreque-hideout-when-first-entering-the-.text: Hey! Who are you and why are you here?

myreque-hideout-when-first-entering-the-.player: It's okay. I'm a friend. I'm here to deliver some weapons to you.

myreque-hideout-when-first-entering-the-.speaker: Harold Evans
myreque-hideout-when-first-entering-the-.text: Weapons? You'd better talk to Veliaf then. I'll be keeping an eye on you though, so don't go trying anything.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Harold Evans
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: I'm keeping my eye on you. Nothing personal. We just need to be careful with newcomers. Anyway, Veliaf will want to speak to you.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Greetings! Good to see some new blood. You'd better speak with Veliaf. He's in charge here.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Hello there. Here to help the cause are you? Speak to Veliaf. He'll sort you out.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Sani Piliu
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Hi there. You're new here aren't you? You'd best go and talk with Veliaf.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Ivan Strom
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Oh... Hello. Sorry, but I'm not sure if I'm supposed to be talking to you. You'd better speak to Veliaf.

myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.text: You... I saw you come in. Harold didn't kill you though so I'm guessing you're no enemy. Who are you?

myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.player: I'm [player name]. Don't worry, I'm a friend. I was asked to bring you some weapons.

myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.text: It's true that we could do with some supplies. Thank you for bringing them here. I'll have a proper look over them in a moment but there's something I must finish first.

myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf.text: Feel free to introduce yourself to the others in the meantime.

myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf-talkin.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
myreque-hideout-talking-to-veliaf-talkin.text: Ah, well met. We'll discuss those weapons shortly. I need to finish something first though. Feel free to introduce yourself to the others in the meantime.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If first time speaking:

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: Hello there. Forgive me if I seem cautious of you. We just need to be careful with newcomers.

steps.player: It's fine. Do you mind if I ask a few questions?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If speaking again:

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: Hello there. What can I do for you?

steps.player: I'd like to ask a few questions if that's okay?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Harold Evans
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Sure. I'll do my best to answer them.

steps.player: What's your job here?

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: Cheating death seems to be my main role. I'm the main fighter for the group so I'm always in the thick of it. It's gone okay for me so far though.

options.text: What can you tell me about this group?

steps.player: What can you tell me about this group?

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: We're a good team, though many of the others haven't had any proper training before. I used to be in a militia so I've been trying to share my knowledge as best I can.

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: In most cases we end up having to improvise though. Thankfully, this lot are good at that. Ivan over there, he saved our bacon in a recent run in with some juves.

steps.player: Juves? What are they?

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: Juveniles, the lowest form of vampyre. We come across them quite often around here. They may be the weakest vampyres but they're still very dangerous.

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: They're stronger and faster than many well trained soldiers, and twice as bloodthirsty.

options.text: What's your grasp of the situation?

steps.player: What's your grasp of the situation?

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: The situation is grave. It would be dangerous to think differently.

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: We're really up against it, but we have no choice. This is a battle for our very existence and we need to employ any tactics to achieve our goal.

steps.player: Have you heard any rumours?

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: Yes, I hear them all the time. I don't pay any attention to them though.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

options.condition: If the player has asked a question (replaces 'I'll be back later'):

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If first time speaking:

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: Ah, I see you've introduced yourself to Veliaf. Are you planning to join the fray against the Drakans?

steps.player: Maybe. I'd like to ask a few questions if that's okay?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If speaking again:

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: Hello again! How can I be of service to you?

steps.player: I'd like to ask you few questions.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Sure, go ahead. I'll answer as best I can.

steps.player: What's your job here?

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: I help with anything I can. I used to be a mercenary before joining the Myreque so I know my way around a blade. I've relied on Veliaf's sword arm many a time. I like to think that he can rely on mine.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: We're the only resistance against the vampyres. We're seriously outnumbered though. Veliaf doesn't like to hear us saying 'hopeless' but that's our situation at the minute.

options.text: What're your plans for the future?

steps.player: What're your plans for the future?

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: That's more a question for Veliaf. Ultimately though, our goal is to rid Morytania of the vampyres so that we might reclaim our right to exist.

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: For me personally, I hope that more people will join our ranks soon. Strengh comes in numbers after all.

steps.player: Have you heard any rumours?

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: I have. Something you might find interesting is that Safalaan Hallow, the leader of another Myreque group, has apparently managed to sneak one of his people into the vampyre capital, Darkmeyer.

steps.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
steps.text: I'm not sure how true that is. It would be great though!

steps.player: I'll be back later.

options.condition: If the player has asked a question (replaces 'I'll be back later'):

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If first time speaking:

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: Ah, I see you've introduced yourself to Veliaf. Now, what can I do for you?

steps.player: Do you mind if I ask a few questions?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If speaking again:

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: Salutations! How are you?

steps.player: Fine thanks. I'd like to ask a few questions if that's okay?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Not at all. I'm sure I'll be able to help.

steps.player: What are you doing here?

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: I'm a key advisor to Veliaf. He seeks my council on many issues before we engage the enemy. Not that we do that very often. Our foes heavily outnumber us.

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: We don't give up though. After all, all that is required for evil to survive is for good people to do nothing.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: Well there's multiple groups of us. Even we don't know exactly how many. The less we know about our allies, the less we can reveal to the vampyres if captured.

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: Veliaf leads this group. We operate throughout Mort Myre and the surrounding villages. He reports to Calsidiu who is the head of our resistance.

options.text: What do you know about Morytania?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.player: What do you know about Morytania?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: All the land on this side of the Salve is known as Morytania. Humans and vampyres are the main occupants of the region, though other races also live out here.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: The humans here live like cattle with the vampyres taking regular blood tithes to keep themselves fed. All in all, it's a dire place. Though we hope to change that.

steps.player: Have you heard any rumours?

steps.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
steps.text: Yes, I hear them all the time. They're neither correct or even all that interesting though.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

options.condition: If the player has asked a question (replaces 'I'll be back later'):

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If first time speaking:

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: Hello. Very nice to meet you! The name's Sani Piliu. What's yours?

steps.player: I'm [player name]. Nice to meet you Sani.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: The pleasure's all mine! I've got a good feeling about you. I reckon you're going to do great things for us! You have a powerful aura. Sorry, that must seem really strange.

steps.player: Well, perhaps a little. It's nice of you to say so in any case though. I'd like to ask a few questions if that's okay?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If speaking again:

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: Oh, hello [player name]. Nice to see you again! How's things?

steps.player: Fine thanks. Do you mind if I ask a few questions?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Sani Piliu
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: Sure, go ahead. I'll answer as best I can.

options.text: Tell me a bit about yourself.

steps.player: Tell me a bit about yourself.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: There's not much to tell really. I was nine years old when my family was ripped to pieces by a vampyre.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: One moment I was a happy member of a loving family, the next I was an orphan living a hand to mouth existence.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: Somehow I managed to get by, eking out a living wherever I could. People took pity on me and I earnt food by helping them out.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: I quickly found I had a very useful set of skills and there were plenty of people willing to pay for them.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: I bumped into Veliaf in Canifis. He saw that I would be an asset to the Myreque and invited me to join. I said yes of course. I couldn't turn down the chance to fight against those who took away my family.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: Well Veliaf is the leader of our group. We're not the only ones in Morytania though. Veliaf reports to someone called Calsidiu who's in charge of all the Myreque. I've never met any of the others though.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: Our hope is to one day bring an end to the reign of Lowerniel Drakan and his vampyres.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: For now though, we're just trying to find any weaknesses we can take advantage of. We need to know how to kill them before we take the war to them!

steps.player: You make it sound easy!

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: With determination you can achieve great things. However, Veliaf always tells us not to underestimate the enemy. I've made that mistake before. I won't be making it again.

steps.player: What's going on in Morytania?

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: The entire region is ruled over by Lowerniel Drakan and his family. Everyone living here must pay blood tithes to the vampyres. The tithes keep the vampyres fed and ensure that people are too weak to oppose them.

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: That's where we come in. We won't just offer our family members to the Drakans as a weekly snack. We're going to fight back!

steps.player: Is this your main camp?

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: It's our only camp! At least, for our group. I know there's more Myreque in other parts of Morytania but I don't know exactly where.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

options.condition: If the player has asked a question (replaces 'I'll be back later'):

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If first time speaking:

steps.player: Hi there. Veliaf said that I should introduce myself to everyone.

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: Okay. Well my name is Ivan. It's nice to meet you.

steps.player: Would you mind if I asked you a few questions?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: If speaking again:

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: Oh, hello again. How are you?

steps.player: Fine thanks. Would you mind if I asked you a few questions?

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.speaker: Ivan Strom
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-myreque-memb.text: That's fine. I don't know how much I can help though.

steps.player: What are you doing here?

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: Me personally? I shouldn't be here really. I'm training to be a priest and I was meant to travel to Paterdomus to learn from Drezel. The trip's too dangerous at the moment though.

steps.player: Is it really important for you to train as a priest? I'd have thought there'd be more pressing issues.

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: Veliaf thinks it would be useful to have a priest to advise him. I think he also wants me further away from harm until I'm more experienced.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Myreque?

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: We're the only ones brave enough to put up a fight against the Drakans. I'm proud to be one of them.

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: I do worry that I might let the others down though. I'm not as skilled as they are.

options.text: What do you know about Morytania?

steps.player: What do you know about Morytania?

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: It's a lost land. The evil Drakan family rule all of the region. People cling to each other in fear when the blood tithes are to be paid. It's horrible!

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: It won't be like this forever though. The Myreque will bring light back to this dark place.

steps.player: Have you heard any rumours?

steps.speaker: Ivan Strom
steps.text: Sorry, but I haven't heard anything notable recently.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

options.condition: If the player has asked a question (replaces 'I'll be back later'):

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

myreque-hideout-speaking-to-veliaf-after.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
myreque-hideout-speaking-to-veliaf-after.text: Well met. I see you've introduced yourself to everyone. Shall we discuss those weapons now? Or was there something else you wanted to talk about?

steps.player: Let's talk about the weapons.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Let's see what you have for us.
If the player does have the weapons:
You give the weapons to Veliaf.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: These weapons look great! Many thanks.
Cutscene begins

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: What the...

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Vampyre!

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: It's Vanstrom!

steps.player: Wait... What?

steps.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
steps.text: Well done adventurer! You led me right to them. The little dears are going to wonder which side you're on!

steps.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
steps.text: The Drakans have been wanting you lot dealt with for a while now. We wouldn't want to disappoint them, would we?

steps.speaker: Sani Piliu
steps.text: We're dead!
Vanstrom casts blood barrage hitting and killing Sani for 30 HP

steps.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
steps.text: Quite right.

steps.speaker: Harold Evans
steps.text: No!

steps.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
steps.text: Sorry Harold, you too!
Vanstrom casts blood barrage hitting and killing Harold for 40 HP

steps.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
steps.text: And now... A little gift for the rest of you.
Vanstrom summons a Skeleton Hellhound; Cutscene ends
If the player does not have the weapons:

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Ah. I'm afraid you don't have suitable weapons for us. Sorry friend.

steps.player: What weapons do you need?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Well we all have our own specialisms. We could do with a longsword, two shortswords, a dagger, a mace and a warhammer, all made from steel.

steps.player: Okay. I'll come back once I have them.
I'll be back later.

options.text: So you're the leader of this group?

steps.player: So you're the leader of this group?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: That's right. I can't say I particularly asked for it. The others look up to me though, so they decided I was the best man for the job.

options.text: Can you tell me about your organisation?

steps.player: Can you tell me about your organisation?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Well I wouldn't say we're an organisation. We're really not that organised.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Anyway though, we're a group of Myreque freedom fighters. We're dedicated to mounting a resistance against the Drakan family and their vampyre kin.

options.text: What can you tell me about Morytania?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Morytania?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: If legend is to be believed, it was once a beautiful place. But then Lowerniel Drakan and his vampyres arrived.

steps.player: Who is Lowerniel Drakan?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan is his full name. He's the vampyre that heads up the Drakan family. Helped by his brother Ranis and his sister Vanescula, he rules over all of Morytania.

steps.player: You sound very bitter.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: So would you if you lost everyone dear to you at the hands of such monsters.

options.text: What are your plans for the future?

steps.player: What are your plans for the future?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: At the moment we're maintaining a low profile here at our hideout. We were recently spotted while out on a scouting mission so we're playing it safe and lying low.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Looking further ahead, we need to build more support if we have any hope of taking on the vampyres. We also need to learn more about their weaknesses, so we can take advantage of them.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

options.condition: If the player has asked a question (replaces 'I'll be back later'):

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Sani... Harold... That murderer killed them!

steps.player: I'm so sorry. This is all my fault.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: I don't understand though. He said you led him here. How?

steps.player: He was the one that asked me to bring the weapons to you. He looked like a human though.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: I'm sorry friend, but he clearly took advantage of you. Vampyres can shapeshift to look like humans. Someone from around here might have realised. You were not to know though.

steps.player: No. I'm still responsible though.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: The burden of what happened here is for your conscience to bear. That said, you managed to kill that pet of his. We might all be dead if not for you.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: I imagine you now see why we fight for our freedom.

steps.player: Yes. I think I understand. Is there anything I can do to help now? I first met Vanstrom in Canifis. I could go back and see if he's still there?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: I suspect he will have moved on now. You're welcome to try though. I know a shortcut that you might find useful.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: If you head back into the main cave and go north you'll reach a wall. There's a hidden door in that wall that leads right into the basement of the Hair of the Dog Tavern.

steps.player: That's very useful. Thanks.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Once you are done, I'd appreciate you coming back here to discuss a few things. You held your own against that creature. We could use someone like you.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Need something?

options.text: I want to join your organisation.

steps.player: I want to join your organisation.

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: Well we could definitely use someone like you. You should go and see if Vanstrom is still in Canifis though. Come back once you're done, and we'll talk.

options.text: What do you plan to do now?

steps.player: What do you plan to do now?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: We won't be able to stay here now that Vanstrom knows where we've been hiding. We have some time though. He'll expect that we're all dead. We'll use that time to form a plan of action.

options.text: How do I get out of here again?

steps.player: How do I get out of here again?

steps.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
steps.text: If you head back into the main cave and go north you'll reach a wall. There's a hidden door in that wall that leads right into the basement of the Hair of the Dog Tavern.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.speaker: Radigad Ponfit
myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.text: That monster! He killed them! We'll make them all pay!

myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.text: This is a dark day for the Myreque.

myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.player: I'm so sorry for your loss.

myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.speaker: Polmafi Ferdygris
myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.text: Don't worry. No one blames you. You were tricked and that's that. It serves no useful purpose to blame any of ourselves for this.

myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.speaker: Ivan Strom
myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.text: Thank Saradomin you managed to kill that awful beast! I just wish we could have done more.

myreque-hideout-after-defeating-the-skel.player: I'm so sorry for your loss. If there's anything I can do, please let me know.

myreque-hideout-finishing-up.speaker: Stranger
myreque-hideout-finishing-up.text: Hello friend. What can I do for you?

myreque-hideout-finishing-up.player: Oh, sorry. I thought you were someone else.

myreque-hideout-finishing-up.speaker: Stranger
myreque-hideout-finishing-up.text: Who did you think I was?

myreque-hideout-finishing-up.player: I thought you were that dirty murderer Vanstrom.

myreque-hideout-finishing-up.speaker: Stranger
myreque-hideout-finishing-up.text: Woah! It sounds like you've got a score to settle!

steps.player: Hi.

steps.npc: You know, there are so many different ways to greet people. Hello, 'ello, hello there...

steps.player: That still only counts as one!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?

steps.player: I'm great, thank you!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?

steps.player: Indeed.
Hi.

steps.npc: What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

steps.player: Nothing.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

standard-dialogue.text: If the information clerk has rewards for the player:

steps.npc: Ohh, hello there, I see from our records that you've helped us out a bit, and I'd love to give you a bit of a reward for that.
My father knew a lot about Prayer, Mining, Crafting, Smithing, Slayer and Hunter, and I learnt some of his tricks... would you like me to share a little of my knowledge?

options.text: Yes, teach me something in those skills.

steps.player: Yes, teach me something in those skills.

steps.text: If the player has between 51-100 Kudos:
You feel more knowledgeable in the Mining skill.
If the player has between 101-150 Kudos:
You feel more knowledgeable in the skills Mining and Crafting
If the player has over 150 Kudos, and has claimed the previous rewards:
You feel more knowledgeable in the skills Crafting, Smithing, Slayer, Prayer and Hunter.
If the player has over 150 Kudos, but has not claimed any of the previous rewards:
You feel more knowledgeable in the skills Mining, Crafting, Smithing, Slayer, Prayer and Hunter.

steps.player: Wow, thanks.

steps.npc: You're most welcome. Now, is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: No.
I'll come back later.

steps.npc: Okay!

standard-dialogue.text: If the information clerk does not have any rewards for the player:

steps.npc: Welcome to Varrock Museum. How can I help you today?

options.text: Take a map of the Museum

steps.text: You reach and take a map of the Museum.
museum map

options.text: Find out about the Dig Site exhibit.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Dig Site exhibit please?

steps.npc: Of course. The Dig Site exhibit has several display cases of finds discovered on the Dig Site to the east of Varrock.

steps.text: If the player has not completed The Dig Site quest:

steps.npc: Unfortunately, you haven't passed your Earth Science exams, so you aren't qualified to help us on the dig. If you're interested, visit the Education Centre on the Dig Site to the east and talk to the examiners there.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site quest, but has not helped with the exhibit:

steps.npc: As you've passed your Earth Science exams at the Dig Site, you can go through into the cleaning area and clean off some finds. This will help our Dig Site display floor to give a more accurate view of life back in the
3rd and 4th Ages, as well as earning you Kudos. If you'd like to know more about cleaning finds, just ask the archaeologists.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site quest, and has partially completed the exhibit:

steps.npc: I see you've already helped out in the Dig Site exhibit. Our picture of life back in the 3rd and 4th Ages in that old city is really becoming clearer. There are still a few displays that need updating, though. If you'd like to
know more about cleaning finds, just ask the archaeologists.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site quest, and has completed the exhibit:

steps.npc: You have really helped out a lot. I see all the nice clean finds with their information are in the once empty cases. I'm sure we'll get some more cases in soon for you to fill. For now, perhaps you should investigate the
rest of the Museum.

steps.player: Bye.

steps.npc: Have a good day!

options.text: Find out about the Timeline exhibit.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Timeline exhibit please?

steps.npc: Why, yes. The Timeline exhibit has lots of display cases showing things from the beginning of time right up to the present day.

steps.text: If the player has not contributed to the timeline exhibit:

steps.npc: You could help out in the Timeline exhibit upstairs. By providing information you may have gathered on your travels around the world, you can help to make our displays more comprehensive and earn yourself Kudos
too.

steps.text: If the player has contributed to the timeline exhibit:

steps.npc: I know you've helped out a bit in the Timeline exhibit upstairs, but I'm sure you can help more. When you're out on your travels being a brave adventurer, remember that you can come back to the Museum
after some quests to let us know important historical facts. This will help us to update the displays and make the Museum a more informative place! You'll earn yourself Kudos too.

steps.text: If the player has completed timeline exhibit:

steps.npc: I see you have filled up the display cases we have, and given us large amounts of information for the Timeline exhibit. At the moment, you have left us nothing to do ourselves, but I'm sure we'll be getting some new cases
in soon for you to help us out with! For now, perhaps you should investigate the rest of the Museum.

steps.player: Okay, thanks. One more question: why are the display numbers all out of sequence?

steps.npc: Ahh, that's due to the numbering being done as we were constructing the cases and putting the displays in them, then shuffling them into the right places. We thought rather than renumbering them all - such a
boring job, writing labels - we'd leave it. They all have unique numbers and future displays would mess up the consecutive numbering anyway.

steps.player: Ahhh, I see.

options.text: Find out about the Natural History exhibit.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Natural History exhibit please?

steps.npc: Why, yes. The Natural History exhibit has displays of various creatures you can find around Gielinor.

steps.text: If the player has not corrected any of the display cases:

steps.npc: Downstairs, in the Natural History exhibit, you can answer quizzes about animals to show us your knowledge and earn Kudos at the same time. Talk to Orlando, I'm sure he'd appreciate your knowledge.

steps.text: If the player has completed at least one display case:

steps.npc: I see you have already demonstrated some of your knowledge of the natural world in the Natural History exhibit, so why not pop down and do some more quizzes with Orlando! You can earn Kudos at the same time.

steps.text: If the player has corrected all of the display cases:

steps.npc: You really know your stuff when it comes to animals, don't you! Orlando tells me you have exceeded his teachings. For now, perhaps you should investigate the rest of the Museum.

options.text: But what's Natural History got to do with existing animals?

steps.player: But what's natural history got to do with existing animals?

steps.npc: The study of natural history is simply the study of the history of the species. The species doesn't necessarily need to be an extinct one.

steps.player: What is Kudos?

steps.npc: Kudos is a measure of how much you've assisted the Museum. The more information you give us, Dig Site finds that you clean and quizzes you solve, the higher your Kudos.

steps.player: But what's it for?

steps.npc: Well, recently we found a rather interesting island to the north of Morytania. We believe that it may be of archaeological significance. I suspect we'll be looking for qualified archaeologists once we have constructed our
canal and barge. So, we're using Kudos as a measure of who is willing and able to help us here at the Museum, so they can then be invited on our dig on the new island.

steps.player: Would I qualify, then?

steps.text: If the player does not have enough Kudos:

steps.npc: Unfortunately, you haven't earned enough Kudos yet, so you aren't qualified to help us on the dig. If you're interested in helping us out and getting that Kudos, simply help out around the Museum.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

steps.text: If the player has enough Kudos:

steps.npc: Why yes! You've helped us so much around the Museum and you have the necessary qualifications from the Earth Sciences exams you took. When the canal is ready, we'll let you know.

steps.player: Thank you, I'll look forward to it!

crack-the-clue-iii.npc: Well done! I have new information to share with you.

crack-the-clue-iii.text: You've found a new special clue! However, a magical force prevents you from putting this item in your inventory!
Interface showing the next clue opens.

before-the-fremennik-trials.npc: I cannot speak to you outerlander! Talk to Brundt, the Chieftain!

before-the-fremennik-trials-attempting-t.npc: You stay away from me outerlander!

before-the-fremennik-trials-attempting-t.text: They are too suspicious of you for you to get close enough to steal from them.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Hello again [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. What need you of me this day? You can always rely on my assistance!

steps.player: Nothing thanks. I just fancied a chat.

steps.npc: My door is always open should you ever need my help [Fremennik name].

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: [Fremennik name]... It has been too long since last we met!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Welcome back [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. It is always a pleasure to see you here!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: My apologies [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]! I have not time to tarry here with you!

steps.player: That's okay, I didn't really want anything.
Hello.

steps.npc: How are you [Fremennik name]? I hope all fares well with you this day!

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks, how are you?

steps.npc: All is well with me also!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Hello to you, too!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Hello. Did you want something [Fremennik name]?

steps.player: No, not really.

steps.npc: Well... okay then!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Always good to see you [brother/sister] [Fremennik name].
You shame us, [Fremennik name]!
How can you steal from me, [Fremennik name]?
You have betrayed your heritage, [Fremennik name]!
Why would you try to steal from me, [Fremennik name]?
I think the locals are taking a liking to us! One of them hasn't stopped wearing those clothes Arnkel sold her. Much better than those piddly little things she was wearing before!

steps.player: I think they're piddly because of how warm it is here...

steps.npc: Bah! A bit of heat never hurt anyone.

steps.player: I don't think that's true.

steps.text: If the player has not completed The Fremennik Trials:

steps.npc: Oh stop your whining, traveller! Now, I think it's time for a drink.

steps.text: If player has completed The Fremennik Trials:

steps.npc: Oh stop your whining, [Fremennik name]! Now, I think it's time for a drink.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Good day, your Royal Highness.

before-and-during-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Outlander, I have work to be getting on with... Please stop bothering me.

after-the-fremennik-trials-but-before-ol.npc: Good afternoon! How do you like our village?

after-the-fremennik-trials-but-before-ol.player: It's lovely. You have a fine collection of goats.

standard-dialogue.player: Hey, what do you do here?

standard-dialogue.npc: I help the main man over there. He can get a bit cantankerous. Every now and then he'll just start attacking people without warning. I act as a sort of home help...

standard-dialogue.npc: Well, sometimes he'll fly right off the handle and just start, you know, 'raising the dead' to do his 'bidding'. That kind of activity is just so anti-social, so it tends to attract a lot of hero types, you know!

standard-dialogue.player: What, you graze your knees a lot?

standard-dialogue.npc: I was going to say that you soon get fed-up with it. I guess it's one of those perks of the job though, ability to raise yourself from the dead.
You'd think he'd do better things with a gift like that, but all he tends to do is get angry at people who come into his house without being invited and then he's off again 'raising the dead'.

options.text: What can you tell me about Mount Quidamortem?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Mount Quidamortem?

steps.npc: Our first records of the mountain date back to the 36th decade where a Shayzien patrol discovered the mountain during a survey of the Kebos Lowlands.
King Shayzien VII was keen on conquering more land for Kourend and demanded his people explore suitable territories.
The mountain became known as Mount Quidamortem after it was realised venturing towards the summit resulted in certain death.

Gnosi is our expert on Mount Quidamortem, but I'm afraid she's currently on an expedition to the temple near the summit of the mountain. However, we do have some texts available detailing the great expedition.
Is there something else I can help you with?

Unfortunately, the expedition was a failure and the entire party was killed. The king himself died a few years later and was succeeded by the tyrant Xeric. No more expeditions were ordered under his rule.

I've visited Safalaan a few times as well. He always seems pretty upbeat, but I do worry about him... Having to live as a vampyre... It must be horrible!

steps.player: At least he has Efaritay now.

steps.npc: I don't rightly understand your speech outerlander, but my loyalty is with Chieftain Brundt.

steps.player: So what are you doing here?

steps.npc: This should not concern you, outerlander. I am awaiting other Fremenniks to join me on an expedition to Waterbirth Island.
It is a small crescent-shaped island just north-west of here, outerlander.
We have many legends about it, such as the tale of the broken sky, and the day of the green seas.
The reason I am travelling there is more serious Fremennik business, however. I doubt an outerlander would be interested.

steps.player: Can I come?

steps.npc: An outerlander join us on an honoured hunt???

steps.player: Oh, pleeeeease? I really LOVE killing stuff!

steps.npc: Well... I remain unconvinced that it would be wise to allow an outerlander to join us in such dangerous battle, but your enthusiasm seems genuine enough...
I will allow you to escort us, but you must pay me a sum of money first.

steps.player: What? That's outrageous, why charge me money? And, uh, how much does it cost me?

steps.npc: Ah, the outerlanders have stolen from my people for many years, in this way you can help my community with a small amount of money...
Let us say... 1,000 coins. Payable in advance, of course.
For this I will take you to Waterbirth Island on my boat, and will bring you back here when you have had your fill of the hunt. Assuming you are still alive to wish to leave, of course.
So do you have the 1,000 coins for my service, and are you ready to leave now?

steps.npc: When the Kurasks finded new treasures, many humans come to the Slayer cave to hunt them... No Kurasks left for Jelly to train on, so Jelly makes a private area just for training. These be Jelly's very own Kurask!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello there. Welcome to the Temple of the Lesser Gods.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.npc: Of course. The lesser gods, or avatars as some call them, were born from the dreams of Tumeken. They are Apmeken, Het, Crondis and Scabaras.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Apmeken?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Apmeken?

steps.npc: Apmeken is the goddess of companionship. She is known to be the most mischievous, playful and unpredictable of the minor deities. I'd say she's my personal favourite.

steps.player: So I shouldn't trust you then?

steps.npc: Apmeken can appeal to the most erudite scholar or the most barefaced liar. I'd like to be considered amongst the former category.

steps.player: I see. What does she look like?

steps.npc: She has the head of a monkey, or sometimes an ape. It changes depending upon what nature she is displaying. For example, the orangutan represents wisdom, while the baboon represents mischief.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Het?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Het?

steps.npc: Het is the least strange of our deities to foreign eyes, for he looks just like us. I suspect this is why his shrines are particularly targeted by thieves like that infamous Templeton.

steps.player: What does he represent?

steps.npc: Het is the god of health, both in mind and body. He is quite popular amongst soldiers as a result, especially up in Al Kharid.

steps.player: Just soldiers?

steps.npc: Not at all! Like I said, the wellbeing of the mind is also key to Het. Many great orators also look to him for guidance. I imagine his teachings help with some of their strenuous speeches.

steps.player: How did his followers react to the plagues here?

steps.npc: With many arguments. They really couldn't decide whether it was a punishment from Het, or an affront to him. I stayed out of that debate.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Crondis?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Crondis?

steps.npc: Crondis is a ferocious lady with the head of a mighty crocodile.

steps.player: That must be awkward when buying helmets.

steps.npc: Luckily for her, I don't think deities have much need for them.

steps.player: So what is she the goddess of?

steps.npc: Resourcefulness. A word which seems to be open to large interpretation.

steps.player: How so?

steps.npc: Most consider her to be a teacher of modesty. They say we should be resourceful by only taking and using that which we absolutely need.

steps.player: But there's others with a different interpretation?

steps.npc: Some believe she is actually the goddess of pleasure. They claim that the idea of modesty came from a misinterpretation, and that to be resourceful is to take all that you can.

steps.player: That doesn't sound right.

steps.npc: No. It is a more recent take that I suspect was born in Menaphos. There are many in that city with more wealth than they'll ever need. Modesty is not an ideal they'll ever embody.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Scabaras?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Scabaras?

steps.npc: There are many opinions out there on Scabaras, but general knowledge isn't always the most accurate.

steps.player: Well what are the absolute facts then?

steps.npc: Scabaras is the god of isolation. He takes on the appearance of a man with the head of a scarab. Both he and his followers were driven into hiding long ago.

steps.player: And?

steps.npc: And that's it. You asked for the absolute facts. Anything beyond that is just speculation.

steps.player: But there must be more. The High Priest told me that Scabaras tried to conquer these lands.

steps.npc: So it is said, but the written accounts that exist contain many inconsistencies when it comes to what role Scabaras actually played. Of course, most would not know that.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: Many of the writings are only available to us priests. That does of course include the new High Priest, but perhaps he is yet to read them. They are definitely... illuminating.

steps.player: Interesting...
Interesting. Thanks for the information.
I'd better get going.

steps.npc: Mum says I not to talk to strangers.

steps.player: Okay then.

steps.npc: We's be new here, on the bana plantion.

steps.npc: Yeah, we's be new here. Anyway, I gonna go play now.

steps.npc: Yes, that's me.

steps.player: Okay then.

steps.npc: We play here.

steps.player: That must be fun.

steps.npc: Yeah, it's fun. Bye.
No, I not say. You have to guess.

steps.player: Okay. Is it Jill?

steps.npc: How d'ya know that? Are you magic?

steps.player: Not really - just call it a gift.

steps.npc: If you were magic, you would know why the sea is blue... are you magic?

steps.player: Nope, I'm not magic, and I have no clue why the sea is blue.

steps.npc: Oh, well. That's a bit sad. I was hoping you were magic and could magic me some sweets. But you can't, so I go find someone else who's magic. Bye.

after-the-event.npc: Thanks so much for saving us from those stinky gublinch. They were awful! I hope Shanty gave you somefing cool for your efforts.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Hello?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Ah... Another wayward traveller.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Excuse me?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: You are not the first to make your way down here. Undoubtedly, you will not be the last.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: My aeternal name, given to me long ago, is Jimp.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Jimp the imp?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Yes, though my many centuries upon this realm have taught me that the newer tongues struggle with its pronounciation.
So you may call me Jim.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Okay...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I see you still have questions. Before I answer them, I will need you to swear to secrecy.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Hang on... why would I do that?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I believe you will find my cooperation helpful. Perhaps I shall find yours helpful one day too.

options.text: I've already entered one dubious contract.

steps.player: I've already entered one dubious contract.
I'm not sure I should be signing any others.

steps.npc: You will find the nature of my contracts refreshing, then. My terms are simple: do not endanger me or take what is mine, and I shall do what I can to help you.

steps.player: Okay then, why not.
Okay then, why not.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: You sign the crumpled looking document.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Excellent. It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, [player name].

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Wait, how do you know my name? Was this a trick?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: No, friend, you signed it right here.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Oh, right.

steps.player: Who are you really?

steps.npc: I suppose since you already know my name, you are asking who I am in the context of history and society.

steps.player: Yes, let's go with that.

steps.npc: I am afraid other agreements bar me from telling you much of my past. Nowadays, I am a humble servant of Yama, existing only to do as he pleases.

steps.player: And what is that?

steps.npc: Mostly fetching records, and dying. When I am not doing that, I rest here. The features of this isle remind me of those I once knew.

steps.player: Who do you mean by 'those'?

steps.npc: I already skirt as closely as I can to what I am disallowed from sharing. I apologise, but I cannot answer further.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This isle is a small wonder. The rock formations here bear a slight resemblance to those from my own realm.

steps.player: The rock looks like it's crumbling.

steps.npc: Yes, infernal shale is kept together largely by the pressure from above. Once a piece is broken off, it can easily be broken down with a hammer and chisel.

steps.player: That's good to know. What about the smithy?

steps.npc: I can say nothing more than that it was not here when I arrived.

steps.player: So you brought it here?

steps.npc: I cannot say.

steps.player: It's rather hot here.

steps.text: If the player has never received Jim's wet cloth:

steps.npc: Yes, the unique composition of this chasm does create a warm environment.

steps.player: I can see my sweat turning to vapour as soon as it appears.

steps.npc: Yes, water is an ineffective coolant at this temperature. Perhaps I could offer an alternative.

steps.player: That would be handy.

steps.text: Jim hands you a cloth dripping with blackened liquid.

steps.npc: The liquid will only offer a brief respite from the heat, but I find it can help to apply it frequently between bursts of exertion.

steps.player: I see, thanks. I'll give that a try.

steps.npc: I can see you eyeing the liquid. It is best you do not ask.

steps.text: If the player has previously received Jim's wet cloth:

steps.player: It's rather hot here.

steps.npc: Have another cloth. Remember, it only offers a brief respite from the heat. You'll want to time bursts of exertion right after using it.

options.text: Why is there a smithy down here?

steps.player: Why is there a smithy down here?

steps.npc: I cannot speak to the purpose the smithy has, but I might be able to shed some light on the purposes it could be given.

steps.player: Go on.

steps.npc: The furnace is capable of extremely high temperatures. Whilst not very helpful for your ores, it can melt metal from our realm.

steps.player: Like the rocks on this isle?

steps.npc: Not quite, though they are necessary to power the furnace. Nobody but Yama has access to the kinds of ores it was designed for.

steps.player: But if I were to get my hands on some, I could work them here?

steps.npc: Yes. The process is quite involved. Smaller shards must be melted into nuggets for stability, and then combined into chunks.

steps.player: I see. Maybe I can give that a go.

options.text: You're very friendly for a demon.

steps.player: You're very friendly for a demon.

steps.npc: I am not alone in this amongst my kind, but I understand that I am rare. I have my reasons for being this way.

steps.player: Well, if there is anything I can do for you, let me know.

steps.npc: Thank you. There is little I can ask of you given the nature of my other agreements, but watching you work on this isle does bring me some comfort.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: Safe travels, [player name].
Welcome to the Jungle Store. Can I help you at all?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling

No thanks.

steps.player: Tell me about this room?

Thish here'sh a shtore room right?

steps.player: A store room you mean?

steps.npc: That'sh what I shaid! *HIC* A shtore room.... Now technic'ly shpeaking, I should be outshide guarding it...

steps.player: But you just nipped in to have a quick drink?

steps.npc: Yep... and to practish.

steps.player: Practish? I mean.. practise what?

steps.npc: Keg balancin. I'm the besht.

options.text: Tell me how to balance kegs.

But you couldn't ever balansh ash many ash meee!

steps.npc: Nah... hic.... I'm a wizsh at copyin' signaturesh! Jus' ashk an offishal mem'er of shtaff like Shloane fer yer tokensh.

steps.npc: The Third Age of the world was a time of great conflict, of destruction never seen before or since, when all the gods save Guthix warred for control.

The colossal Wyrms, of whom today's dragons are a pale reflection, turned all the sky to fire, while on the ground armies of foot soldiers, goblins and trolls and humans, filled the valleys and plains with blood.

In time the noise of the conflict woke Guthix from His deep slumber, and He rose and stood in the centre of the battlefield so that the splendour of His wrath filled the world, and He called for the conflict to cease!
Silence fell, for the gods knew that none could challenge the power of the mighty Guthix -- for His power is that of nature itself, to which all other things are subject, in the end.
Guthix reclaimed that which had been stolen from Him, and went back underground to return to His sleep and continue to draw the world's power into Himself.
But on His way into the depths of the earth He sat and rested in this cave; and, thinking of the battle-scarred desert that now stretched from one side of His world to the other, He wept.
And so great was His sorrow, and so great was His life- giving power, that the rocks themselves began to weep with Him.
Later, Guthix noticed that the rocks continued to weep, and that their tears were infused with a small part of His power.
So He set me, His servant, to guard the cave, and He entrusted to me the task of judging who was and was not worthy to access the tears.

steps.npc: I will tell you the story of the light-creatures.
Myriad and beautiful were the creatures and civilizations of the early ages of the world. Gielinor was a work of art, shaped lovingly over the millennia by the creative mind of Guthix.

Only the sturdiest races survived the Godwars, and even then only by abandoning their high culture and gearing their societies towards war. Of the more delicate races there is now no trace, and almost no memory.
One such race had bodies as fragile as snowflakes, yet they built crystal cities that stood for a thousand years.

The wind would whisper through the spires and fill them with sweet harmonies, and the rising sun would shine through the precious gems that studded the towers and create inter plays of light as if rainbows were dancing.

Indeed, so marvellous was this light-show at its height that the patterns of light themselves became alive, and great flocks of luminous creatures rode along the gem- cast beams, each drawn to its own colour.
The creatures you see floating in this chasm are the last sorry remnants of that age. I do not know how they made their way here and survived to this time, but I am grateful for their company.

steps.npc: Not long after the start of my vigil a party of goblins happened on my cave. These were the ugly brutes of the gods' armies, but their armour bore a faded patch where the symbol of a god had been removed.
They looked around hesitantly, squinting in the light of crude torches, but as soon as they saw me they raised their spears and charged.
No one may access the Tears of Guthix by force. I sent them tumbling into the chasm.
Two hundred years later another goblin found me. This one was unarmed, and although she was very wary I succeeded in engaging her in conversation.
Since then I have had many more visits from the descendants of those lost warriors, and over the centuries I have seen them change.
They have become timid rather than aggressive, and I have seen the light of intelligence grow in their bulging eyes.
Their stories are repetitive and grim, of scraping a living out of the harsh rock and through ingenuity and toil shaping it into a home.
I have followed the progress of their race, but their individual stories hold little interest for me.

steps.text: Junior Jim gives you a log book.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.npc: Not a problem. Don't forget to see Charles down in the cave on the island if you need more help with charting.

steps.player: Actually, never mind.

steps.npc: No worries, mate.

options.text: Do you have any tips on how I can become a better sailor?

steps.player: Do you have any tips on how I can become a better sailor?

steps.npc: To be frank, mate, I'd say you're already at the top of your game. Still, I guess I can probably chuck a few pointers your way. Let's have a butchers...
Yeah, I reckon I can probably chuck a few pointers your way. Let's have a butchers...

Right, you've got all sorts of ways you can buff up your sailing skills. There's port tasks, sea charting, shipwreck salvaging, Barracuda Trials, deep sea trawling, and probably loads more I've gone and forgotten about.

options.text: Can you tell me more about port tasks?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about port tasks?

steps.npc: Sure thing, mate. You'll find that a lot of ports will have a notice board where folks have gone and stuck up some ads for jobs they want sorting.
Might be they want some cargo lugging about, or maybe they're after someone to pop out and do a bit of killing for them.

steps.player: And is there anything I should keep in mind while doing these tasks?

steps.npc: Well, after you've gone and accepted a task or two, you'll want to keep your captain's log handy. It's good for keeping tabs on what jobs you're currently grafting away at.

Also, if you're doing a bit of courier work, you might find it handy to get a couple of crewmates on board. They can help you shift the goods about so you're not knackering yourself by carrying one crate at a time.

steps.player: Makes sense. Thanks, Jim.

steps.npc: No worries, mate. Wanting any other tips?

options.text: Can you tell me more about sea charting?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about sea charting?

steps.npc: Well, mate, sea charting is all about heading out and improving your own knowledge of the sea itself. Your captain's log has all sorts of cracking tips on how to do so.
If you want to know more, your best shout's going to be heading down into the cave on the island for a chinwag with Charles. He's the local expert on this sort of stuff.

steps.player: I might just do that. Thanks, Jim.

steps.npc: Not a problem, mate. Do you need any more tips?

options.text: Can you tell me more about shipwreck salvaging?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about shipwreck salvaging?

steps.npc: Well, as the name suggests, mate, it's all about salvaging old shipwrecks from the sea. Keeps the place nice and tidy, and allows you to snag some swag from those that don't need it anymore.
To get started, you're going to want to head over to the shipyard and sort yourself out with a proper nice salvaging hook. The flashier the hook, the quicker you'll be able to salvage.

Once you've got your hook all nicely set up, it's time to head out and find a shipwreck. You've got plenty of different types to pick from. Once you spot a good one, just use the hook to get stuck in.
You'll want to keep salvaging until you're feeling chuffed with your haul. Then you just need to use a salvaging station to sort through it all. Any half-decent port's going to have one.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Always a pleasure, mate. Wanting any other tips?

options.text: Can you tell me more about Barracuda Trials?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Barracuda Trials?

steps.npc: Sure can, mate. The Barracudas are a top group of daredevils, but they're also proper show-offs. They like to head out in their fancy boats, giving it proper beans and pushing them right to the limit.
If you're a bit of a cheeky sod yourself, you might want to get involved in one of their trials. All of them are about speeding around and clocking the best time possible.

Anyway, if you fancy it, the nearest one is just south of here in the Storm Tempor. Just don't go being a lemon and jumping in without a boat that's up to the task. Last thing you want is to go and sink!

steps.player: I'll be sure to keep that in mind. Thanks, Jim.

steps.npc: No worries, mate. Need any other tips?

options.text: Can you tell me more about deep sea trawling?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about deep sea trawling?

steps.npc: To be honest, mate, it's not something I'm properly clued up on. The basic gist though is that it's all about heading out in your boat to snag some fish that you wouldn't normally be able to get your mitts on.
Still, you don't need to worry, mate. I may not be able to help you, but word is there's a geezer who can over in Port Roberts. Kellan is his name apparently.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Not a problem, mate. Do you need any more tips?

options.text: Is there anything else I should keep in mind?

steps.player: Is there anything else I should keep in mind?

steps.npc: Well, mate, you're going to want to keep taking full advantage of the shipyard. If you don't keep regularly upgrading your boat and the facilities on it, you're just holding yourself back for no good reason.

Speaking of which, don't be afraid to sort yourself out with more than one boat. That way you can have different ones with different facilities on them. Do that, and you'll be golden regardless of what you're up to.
Another thing to remember is that you don't need to go it alone. Get yourself a proper bang up crew, mate. They'll be able to help you with all sorts of things on your boat.
Just speak to the Crew Registrar down the docks and she'll get you properly sorted out.
Finally, mate, while self-betterment is ace and all that, don't forget to kick back, chill out, and enjoy yourself! Sometimes it ain't about the destination, it's about the journey!

steps.player: Very true. Thanks, Jim.

steps.npc: Always a pleasure, mate. Need any other tips?

options.text: Actually, let's talk about something else.

steps.player: Actually, let's talk about something else.

steps.npc: No worries, mate.

steps.player: Nothing, thanks.

steps.npc: No worries, mate.

limbo-dialogue.npc: Calm down, mate. You seem cheery for someone out in the middle of nowhere.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: Well, mate. Some people like to call it Limbo... But I always thought that was the game with the stick.

steps.player: Sure, but... Where are we?

steps.npc: Somewhere out at sea. What does it matter? All the same, now you're here, isn't it?.

steps.npc: Good luck with that, mate!

steps.npc: Well, I thought it'd be nice to go on a little vacation. Get away from all the rabble.
Didn't account for the rabble showing up here, did I?

steps.player: Vacation? Is life on the Pandemonium all that taxing?

steps.npc: Don't you go getting sarky with me, mate! Not like you ever work a hard day, is it?

standard-dialogue.npc: It's called the Rogue's outfit. I got it from the Rogue's Den in Burthorpe. I've found it helps me blend in when pickpocketing people, allowing me to steal more coins from them.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Leave us.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Your presence is not desired.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: But I need your help! I was sent by Asteros Arceuus, son of Lord Trobin Arceuus.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Arceuus.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: The name of a liar.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: They came to us. Two of them.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: The brother and the husband.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Her time was running out. They wanted to give her more.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: We granted them knowledge. To give her more time.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: But they misused it. And the world suffered.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: In a way. But it was not meant for that.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Time was what it was meant for. But time still runs out.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: They put an end to time. They endangered the balance.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: For every death, there must be life.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: For every life, there must be death.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Perfectly balanced.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: As all things should be.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: For without balance, the world burns.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: You're very confusing, you know that right?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Perhaps.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Perhaps our knowledge is beyond your understanding.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Well thankfully I didn't come here for knowledge. I came here for help. The Dark Altar is failing and the people of Arceuus are in danger. I need you to help me find the cause.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: The people of Arceuus have had their time.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Why should we help them?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: sigh* It can never be easy can it.
Fine. If you help me save the people of Arceuus, then I will help you.
I've done this enough times to know that everyone wants something, even the masters of life and death.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Interesting. Maybe the human is not as stupid as it looks.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Well I've been known to have my moments.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Very well human.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: We admit, the Arceuus people do have their uses.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Their work with souls has been useful in helping to maintain the balance.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: We will help them. But first, you will serve us.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Excellent. What do you need from me?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: To the south lies a battlefront.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: There is a grave there. Within it lies a soul, trapped inside a corpse.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Free this soul. In return, we will provide our help.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: So you just want me to kill a zombie?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: A zombie is soulless. An empty shell, reanimated by magic.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: This is a soul. Trapped in this world, when it should have long departed.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Its existence is an affront to the balance.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Which is why it falls to you.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Consider it a test.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: We may have further use for you.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Hmmm. Very well, I'll go and free this soul.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.player: I've dealt with the trapped soul.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.npc: And now we shall help you.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.text: While you were busy, so were we.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.text: We have found the cause of your problem.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.npc: You said the Altar was failing.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.text: The Altar is fine, but its power has been redirected.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.text: To a construct built by a mortal.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.player: So I just have to go to the Dark Altar, find this device and then destroy it. Sounds easy enough.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-after-freei.text: Then you have what you need.

steps.player: Tell me about yourselves.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: We are the Tasakaal.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: We serve the balance.

steps.npc: Between life.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: And death.

steps.player: Balance? So you serve Guthix?

steps.npc: A pretender.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: We serve another power.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: A higher power.

steps.player: What power?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: One beyond your understanding.

steps.player: Why do you serve this power?

steps.npc: The anima of this world, it is fed by life.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: Without life, there is no anima.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: But life can also destroy. It can endanger the anima.

steps.npc: So life must be kept in check.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: This is our purpose.

steps.player: And you were given this purpose?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: Yes.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: And no.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: Our purpose was to wait. But we saw the world burn.

steps.npc: We could not stand by and watch.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: So we left our people. Left our home.

steps.npc: And took on a new purpose.

steps.player: I'm still not sure I understand.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: Maybe you never will.

options.text: Why did that soul need freeing?

steps.player: Why did that soul need freeing?

steps.npc: Upon death, a soul should leave this world.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: And move to the one beyond.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: This soul remained.

steps.npc: It endangered the balance.

steps.player: Was it always there?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: No.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: The body was of one who died a long time ago.

steps.npc: But the soul was of one who died more recently.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: It possessed this body.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: We know not why.

steps.player: Is this something that often happens?

steps.npc: No.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: It is a concerning occurrence.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: We believe a mortal to be involved.

steps.npc: Meddling.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: Where one should not meddle.

steps.player: Interesting...

options.text: You said you might have further use for me?

steps.player: You said you might have further use for me?

steps.npc: We did.

steps.player: What did you mean by that?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: The task you performed.

steps.npc: It was a menial one.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: Another could have filled your role.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: But you showed promise.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: So we tested you.

steps.npc: You passed.

steps.player: You said it was an important task. Now you say it's a menial one. Which is it?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: An important task can still be menial.

steps.npc: There is no contradiction here.

steps.player: Hmmm... If you say so.
So why was it only a small task? Surely saving the Arceuus people was worth more than that.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: You assume it was a trade.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: You assume wrong.

steps.player: But you said I had to do it to save them?

steps.npc: Incorrect.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: We had already committed to saving Arceuus.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: But we needed time to determine the problem.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: While we worked, you needed purpose.

steps.npc: So we gave you one.

steps.player: I feel a little bit used.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: Then you should have paid more attention.

steps.player: So what is the further use you have for me?

steps.npc: None.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: For now.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: But we will call on you again.

steps.npc: That, we can guarantee.

options.text: Why do you hate Lord Arceuus?

steps.player: Why do you hate Lord Arceuus?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
steps.text: We granted them knowledge.

steps.npc: For a specific purpose.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: But they misused it.

steps.player: Them? Who else was there?

steps.npc: Another.

steps.player: Another?

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
steps.text: Another.

steps.player: I can see we're not going to get anywhere here.
Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San

options.text: Can you explain the fundamentals again?

steps.player: Can you explain the fundamentals again?

steps.npc: Indeed I will...
Herblore is the skill of working with herbs and other ingredients, to make useful potions and poison.
First you will need a vial, which can be found or made with the crafting skill.
Then you must gather the herbs needed to make the potion you want.
You must fill your vial with water and add the ingredients you need. There are normally 2 ingredients to each type of potion.
Bear in mind, you must first clean each herb before you can use it.
You may also have to grind some ingredients before you can use them. You will need a pestle and mortar in order to do this.
Herbs can be found on the ground, and are also dropped by some monsters when you kill them.
Let's try an example Attack potion: The first ingredient is Guam leaf; the next is Eye of Newt.
Mix these in your water-filled vial, and you will produce an Attack potion. Drink this potion to increase your Attack level.
Different potions also require different Herblore levels before you can make them.
Good luck with your Herblore practices, and a good day to you.

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: Me? I'm a cook. Fish dishes a speciality. I hate fish. But fish is about all we have. Except for yak. But we're not allowed to eat yak.

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: Why not, is yak meat bad for you?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: Certainly not! Yak meat is both sweet and delicately flavoured. Yak is juicier than buffalo and elk - but never gamey. It goes wonderfully well with a glass of red wine, and it's healthy too!

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: So why aren't you allowed to eat it?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: King's orders. They breed and eat yaks on Neitiznot, so WE'RE not allowed to. It's unjust I tell you! I had a dream last night about a juicy fillet of yak, served on a bed of deep-fried seaweed and topped with a garnish

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: That's a little sad. So do you have any cooked food I could buy?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: No. It would only be fish anyway. Why would you want to eat fish?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: Well, I wouldn't mind a few shark and swordfish steaks as back-up you know.

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: If you insist. Sorry the stock is so low, but I just can't be bothered to cook any more.

steps.player: What do you mean they changed you?

steps.npc: I was once a free man, powerful and wealthy. I owned several apothecaries across Kourend and sold the tastiest potions in the land.

steps.player: What happened?

steps.npc: One of my greatest inventions, it was going so well. I spent days finding the right herbs, I travelled across all of Kourend to find the most exotic weeds. Once I had gathered them all, I put them in a potion and mixed in
the final ingredient.

steps.text: If the player has not travelled to Great Kourend:

steps.player: Kourend? Interesting...

steps.text: If the player has travelled to Great Kourend:

steps.player: Kourend? Oh yeah, I've been there.

steps.npc: Yes, yes... The potion tasted delicious but it was missing a tiny something so I added Magic roots to the potion. It started to pulsate and glow! I took a sip and I felt like a million gold! A few seconds later my eye sight
began to blur, my brain was throbbing. I fell and hit my head on my worktop, then it all went black.

steps.player: Ouch! But, you still haven't said who changed you?

steps.npc: Will you let me finish?

I woke up screaming in pain. Blue foam streaming out of my mouth, my eye sight worse than before, the only things I could make out were 3 tall figures with green banners - they were of the Arceuus Elders. They

muttered to each other in Archaic Language after trying to get up several times. I lost hope and stared at the sky. I had given up when the tallest of the figures bent over and brought his face right to mine and spoke
very softly 'We can save you, but it will come at a cost'.

steps.player: So they saved you?

steps.npc: Yes of course they saved me but look at the cost! I have horns coming out of my head and I'm still blind and stuck here... forever alone.

steps.player: What was the curse?

steps.npc: I have been charged to stay here to prevent the Monstrosity from escaping. Those gates and the winches that operate them are the only thing that stops it breaking free.

steps.player: What monstrosity? What's behind those gates?

steps.npc: You really do not want to know. Leave this place human.

steps.player: Hey now, I'm no wimp. What's to stop me from just turning the winch to open the gate and going in?

steps.npc: Me. And of course your quick demise at the mercy of Cerberus, guardian of the river of souls.

steps.player: But I can do it!

steps.npc: You are obviously passionate at trying. But only those with great skill at slaying these types of beast may enter.
