overhead-dialogue-song.text: We're Knights of the Party Room

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Knights
overhead-dialogue-song.text: We dance round and round like a loon

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Knights
overhead-dialogue-song.text: Quite often we like to sing

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Knights
overhead-dialogue-song.text: We're Knights of the Party Room

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Knights
overhead-dialogue-song.text: Do you like our helmet plumes?

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Knights
overhead-dialogue-song.text: Everyone's happy now we can move

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Knights
overhead-dialogue-song.text: Like a party animal in the groove

overhead-dialogue-song.speaker: Party Pete
overhead-dialogue-song.text: The party room is a silly place!

standard-dialogue.player: Who are you? What are you doing here in the snow?

standard-dialogue.npc: My name is...Sir Gerry. I am...a member of a secret...society of knights. My time is short and I need...your help.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has not completed Recruitment Drive:

steps.player: A secret society of knights? What a surprise! Is there an old charter or decree that says if you're a knight you have to belong to a secret order?

steps.npc: I'm sorry, my friend... I do not understand your meaning. Please, time is short... Take this scroll to Sir Tiffy. You will find him in Falador park... You should not...read it... It contains information for his eyes only.

steps.text: The knight hands you a scroll.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has completed Recruitment Drive:

steps.player: A secret society of knights? You don't mean the Temple Knights, do you?

steps.npc: Yes! Praise Saradomin! You...have been sent in...my hour of need. Please, take...this scroll to Sir Tiffy in Falador park... You should not...read it.

steps.text: The knight hands you a scroll.

standard-dialogue-trying-to-talk-to-the-.text: He's still alive, but in no condition to talk. He appears to be almost comatose.

standard-dialogue-upstairs.npc: Hello there citizen. What can I do for you?
These stairs lead to the Ardougne Prison. It's home to thieves, murderers and everything in between.

standard-dialogue-upstairs.player: Sounds lovely. Can I go in?

standard-dialogue-upstairs.npc: I'm afraid not citizen. Only the Knights of Ardougne are allowed into the prison and I can see that you are no knight.

standard-dialogue-trying-to-go-downstair.npc: Sorry citizen. Only Knights of Ardougne are allowed in the prison.

standard-dialogue-when-wearing-ardougne-.npc: Hello there fellow knight. Isn't today a wonderful day to be a Knight of Ardougne?

standard-dialogue-when-wearing-ardougne-.player: I mean it's okay I suppose. The constant fear of some random adventurer murdering you and the fact that people are constantly picking your pockets isn't great. But hey ho, at least the benefits are good.

standard-dialogue-when-wearing-ardougne-.npc: That they are fellow knight, that they are.

standard-dialogue-when-wearing-ardougne-.player: Anyway, can I go down these stairs?

standard-dialogue-when-wearing-ardougne-.npc: Of course you can! You're a Knight of Ardougne! There is no place where you can't go.

standard-dialogue-downstairs.npc: Hmm... Is your head working okay today [Tim/Sue]?

standard-dialogue-downstairs.player: Of course, my head has never been better.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has not spoken to him before:

steps.npc: Ah, nilsal! Hello!

standard-dialogue.text: If the player has spoken to him before:

steps.npc: Ah, hello again!

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: I'm a Knight of Varlamore, the Kingdom of Sun. I venture to Kourend on a mission, one I can say very little of.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: I'm afraid you must accept my secrecy adventurer, for who knows what the future holds.

options.text: I found an ancient sun temple.
options.condition: If the player completed In Search of Knowledge:

steps.player: I found an ancient sun temple.

steps.npc: Oh, pray tell, where is this temple?

steps.player: In a place called the Forthos Ruin to the south east of here. I was exploring there and I discovered symbology for an entity called Ralos.

steps.npc: I see. I think I shall check out this ruin. Thank you for letting me know adventurer.

steps.player: No problem... Oh, I don't know your name.

steps.npc: Call me Astra! Now, I must see this discovery for myself. It may well help with my mission here. May the light shine upon you!

steps.text: Astra leaves the castle, and moves to the Altar of the Sun.

options.condition: If the player has never been to Varlamore:

steps.player: Where's the Kingdom of Varlamore?

steps.npc: To the south, beyond Mount Quidamortem. It's a glorious land where the sun forever shines.

steps.player: Sounds wonderful!
I have to go.

steps.npc: Stay vigilant, friend.

steps.player: How are you, Astra?

steps.npc: Not great... Can you believe what they've done?

steps.player: Done what?

steps.npc: Are you blind? Look what they've done to the altar of Ralos!

steps.player: Oh... I guess it has seen better days.

steps.npc: It was those others! Those undead druids. Blind moon worshippers...
Do you see what they've become? That's what turning your back on the light does. Even as I stand here in this desecrated temple, I feel the light fading from me.

steps.player: I suppose it is quite spooky down here.

steps.npc: So you feel it too? A shadow hangs over this place.

steps.player: What will you do now?

steps.npc: My mission is still a secret, adventurer. Perhaps I'll share it with you one day.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Don't you know? I am a proud Knight of the Lion, serving under the Justiciar of the Lion.
And you are the adventurer who disturbed my rest!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Yeah... I'm not really all that sorry about that. I was searching for Hallowed marks. Although I didn't actually intend to disturb you if that's any consolation.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Hallowed marks? That currency is reserved only for the devout followers of holy Saradomin. Are you a follower, adventurer?

steps.player: Yes, I follow Saradomin.

steps.text: If the player has at least one Saradomin item equipped:

steps.npc: I see! Yes, I can sense that you at least carry some items bearing his symbol. Well met fellow follower! Do tell, what is the Justiciar of the Lion up to these days?

steps.player: The Justiciar of the Lion? I've never heard of them.

steps.npc: By Saradomin's mercy! Are you serious adventurer? You've never heard of her glory?
The statue in the south east bears her resemblance. I remember the day it was built in her honour.
The Justiciar of the Lion is a title bestowed upon the most powerful wizard of our order. She was capable of wiping out an entire army of Zamorakian demons with a single spell!
I lament that I could not learn more from her in life but I do not regret for a single instant following her to my grave.

steps.player: I see, she sounds like an inspirational figure indeed. Do you know where I can find her?

steps.npc: I was hoping that you could tell me. Last I heard, she was residing in the college here in Hallowvale.

steps.player: Oh dear...

steps.npc: Is something wrong adventurer?

steps.player: Never mind, you don't want to know.

steps.text: If the player has no Saradomin items equipped:

steps.npc: You lie adventurer. I do not sense a single item of holy Saradomin on your person.
To think that our currency is being handled by non- followers. It's a disgrace! If I weren't dead, I'd incinerate you where you stand for your impudence!

steps.player: Yeah well, you are dead and I have your currency so you're going to have to... live with that!

steps.npc: I don't appreciate your attempts at humour, non- follower.

steps.player: No, I follow another god.

steps.npc: To think that our currency is being handled by non- followers. It's a disgrace! If I weren't dead, I'd incinerate you where you stand for your impudence!

steps.player: Yeah well, you are dead and I have your currency so you're going to have to... live with that!

steps.npc: I don't appreciate your attempts at humour, non- follower.

upon-opening-a-coffin-in-the-hallowed-se.npc: You dare defile this sacred place? That treasure doesn't belong to you!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Who indeed? I am a wise Knight of the Owl. I serve the Justiciar of the Owl.

options.text: Who's this Justiciar of the Owl?

steps.player: Who's this Justiciar of the Owl?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Mage Arena II:

steps.npc: Saradomin's wisest of servants. It surprises me that you've not heard of his many feats.

steps.player: Do you know any?

steps.npc: I know them all.

steps.player: Care to share?

steps.npc: Of course. Do you see the foliage around you, adventurer?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: For it to be in such a state means that there is unimaginable evil nearby. These plants were grown personally by Zachariah, the Justiciar of the Owl.
Anything he plants blossoms with unimaginable vigour. You may have noticed that he has a love for lilies. Perhaps he knew they'd serve multiple purposes in a place like this.

steps.player: Hmm. Hopefully I'll meet him one day.

steps.npc: If you do, send my regards.

steps.player: Do you have a name?

steps.npc: I'm but a loyal watcher, that is all.
So, was there anything else?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena II:

steps.player: Wait...
Your helmet looks familiar. I defeated a knight who wore one with a similar design.

steps.npc: This helmet? It is based on the one worn by the Justiciar of the Owl. You mean to say you fought the great Zachariah and lived to tell the tale?

steps.player: Well, I suppose so.

steps.npc: This can't be... You killed the great Zachariah?

steps.player: Hmm, he didn't really die. He just sort of faded away and left behind a glowing magical hand.

steps.npc: Strange, when I saw him last he had no magical hand to speak of... I suppose time has changed the world above beyond my recollection...

steps.player: Yep, it probably has.
What's with the owls?

steps.npc: They are a symbol of the wise. You see, owls can see the light in the darkest of places. Their presence within the sepulchre is one of grave importance.

steps.player: Yes, I saw some down there. They seemed incorporeal in some way, as if they were ghosts...

steps.npc: Indeed. These creatures have the blessing of Saradomin and the wisdom of ages long past. They are the watchers of the Hallowed Sepulchre. The last defence against unseen evils.

steps.player: Err... past the wolves?

steps.npc: The third floor... Home.
Thank you for freeing me, adventurer. If the owls have already retreated that far back, it's best that I reside here. From this position I can more effectively watch for evil.

steps.player: Hmm... Perhaps I should steal from graves more often?

steps.npc: Excuse me?

steps.player: Oh, nothing.
I'm off now, goodbye.

steps.npc: Stay watchful.

upon-opening-a-coffin-in-the-hallowed-se.npc: You dare defile this sacred place? That treasure doesn't belong to you!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I am a holy Knight of the Unicorn. I served under the Archpriest of this place who himself served under the Justiciar of the Unicorn.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: You don't look like a knight... Don't knights wear plate armour and wield swords and lances and stuff?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: The title of knight perhaps has a different meaning to you adventurer. In fact, all of the knights of my order are priests who serve under Saradomin.
During my life, I spent my time here consecrating the fallen followers of holy Saradomin. I would perform their final rites before laying them to rest within this place.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: I see. So does this place only contain the bodies of these 'knights' who followed Saradomin?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Not at all. We also provided these rites for all the citizens of Hallowvale. They were mostly laid to rest on the first two floors.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Interesting. So who is this Justiciar of the Unicorn you spoke of?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: The Justiciar of the Unicorn? Why this title is only bestowed upon the holiest priest of Saradomin.
The justiciar I followed would spread the teachings of Saradomin everywhere he went, converting the masses to our religion.
The statue in the north east of this room was created in his likeness when the place was built. I must say though, it does concern me that this is the first you've heard of him and his feats.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Well I've certainly heard of the word justiciar, but nothing about the Justiciar of the Unicorn.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: That saddens me greatly. I do hope that he is still carrying out Saradomin's will.
Anyway, do tell me adventurer, what brings you to the Hallowed Sepulchre?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: I found this place within the city of Darkmeyer and that mysterious stranger over there asked me to acquire some Hallowed marks which you and your bretheren were buried with.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I see. Did you say Darkmeyer? An interesting name, especially when this region is so bright and full of life.
When I was alive this place was known as Hallowvale. Do you know why the queen decided to change the name?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Erm, simply put, the land here is... under new management.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Hmm, interesting. I wish I could see for myself but unfortunately, I am unable to leave this place. I do wonder if this new 'management' is the reason my spirit did not pass on to the afterlife.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Perhaps so. However, it's probably best that you can't leave this place. I'm not sure you'd like what you'd find.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I fear you may be right adventurer. The last instruction I was given was to help protect this place from invaders by placing magical enchantments on the statues within.
I admit, I never dared ask who or what we were protecting it from.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: If it's any consolation, the enchantments you placed did prevent the 'invaders' from entering. It's only us human adventurers who enter the Sepulchre.
Although we have been stealing some of your stuff... Sorry about that.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: It's not like I have any use for my stuff anymore. Thanks adventurer, your words do lighten my spirits somewhat.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Aren't you all spirit?

upon-opening-a-coffin-in-the-hallowed-se.npc: You dare defile this sacred place? That treasure doesn't belong to you!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Me? I am a Knight of the Wolf. I serve the fierce Justiciar of the Wolf!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Of the Wolf?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Aye, the most loyal and fiercest of Saradomin's followers! We are the bastion against all that is evil.

options.text: Who's this Justiciar of the Wolf?

steps.player: Who's this Justiciar of the Wolf?

steps.npc: You haven't heard of...

steps.player: What happened to her?

steps.npc: I was hoping you could tell me... Ah, the white wolf we called her... For she had the brightest hair you'd ever seen. A silver so bright it could blind. Some said she had icyene blood, but those close to her knew better.

steps.player: I take it you were close?

steps.npc: Close enough. The white wolf was but a mere human, albeit with astounding prowess on the battlefield... She vied for Saradomin's attention the most out of all the justiciars.

steps.player: Hmm... Why do you think that was?

steps.npc: Ah, well... She always wanted to be stronger and never seemed happy with what she had. There was always more.
Was there anything else you wanted?

options.text: Any great battles to speak of?

steps.player: Any great battles to speak of?

steps.npc: There was this time a great evil swept over Hallowvale...

steps.player: Ah! The vampyres?

steps.npc: The what?

steps.player: Y'know? The ones with the wings and all the blood sucking?

steps.npc: No, don't be so ridiculous. As I was saying... A great evil...
The common folk called it the Egregore. They said it could shift and change shape at a moments notice into creatures from the deepest abyss...

steps.player: Sounds terrifying.

steps.npc: These folk, they tend to exaggerate. It wasn't until the nobles started spreading word of its ghoulish features, each more horrible than the last...
Talons as sharp as runite, fire-breath, mind reading abilities... Worst of all though, they said it couldn't be killed!
That was when we took an interest in killing the thing. We are Knights of the Wolf after all! Our duty is to eradicate all evil.

steps.player: Woah! How does one vanquish such a foe?

steps.npc: Well, we made short work of it. That is what we do.

steps.player: But, how?

steps.npc: With a big sword of course!

steps.text: If the player has Attack, Strength, or Defence as their highest combat skill:

steps.player: Ah... A favorite method of mine.

steps.text: If the player has Ranged as their highest combat skill:

steps.player: Ah... I prefer a carefully placed arrow myself. Each to their own though.

steps.npc: It does the job! Once we had shown the head of the beast to the masses, talk of the Egregore soon died down. At least... for a while.

steps.player: It returned?

steps.npc: Yes. It was strange... As soon as the small folk had forgotten about the Egregore, rumours started to arise that it had returned. And so it had! That was the nature of this beast.

steps.player: So it was truly undying?

steps.npc: Does the Egregore still haunt these lands, human?

steps.player: Hmm, I can't say I've seen it...

steps.npc: Then you must assume we were quite successful! At least by the time of my passing, the beast hadn't returned. Although, who knows? It could have taken any form by now.

steps.player: Well I can't say for certain, but you look pretty old.

steps.npc: Your humour is wasted on me.

steps.player: I'm off now, goodbye.

steps.npc: May the light of Saradomin guide you, adventurer.

upon-opening-a-coffin-in-the-hallowed-se.npc: You dare defile this sacred place? That treasure doesn't belong to you!

before-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-leve.npc: Sorry my friend, the Skipper has been grindin' me up the wrong way lately. If ye need anythin', talk t' Cap'ain Pudi over by the dock.

after-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-level.npc: That ungrateful Skipper. How dare he blame me for that freak storm?

options.text: Why are you angry at the Skipper?

steps.player: Why are you angry at the Skipper?

steps.npc: It be a long story.

steps.player: I've got time. I would love to hear it.

steps.npc: Fine, 'ere be me tale of misfortune.
About a half moon ago, we set sail on our fortnightly fishin' trip. 'Twas smooth sailin' all the way t' our spot.
Caught a load of manta ray an' snappers.

steps.player: What's a snapper?

steps.npc: Ah, I should'a realised you were a landlubber. We on the ship call them snappers, but you lot call 'em lobsters.
Anyway, back to me tale.
After a couple o' days, we pulled up the anchor an' sailed closer t' the Karamjan coast. There is where the big'ns are.

steps.player: What's a big'n?

steps.npc: You landlubbers... It be a shark.

steps.player: Oh, how was I supposed to know?

steps.npc: CAN YOU STOP INTERRUPTIN' ME TALE?

steps.player: Ok...

steps.npc: Good, now where was I...
When we arrived at the spot, the Skipper saw a lack of fish swimmin' in the waters.
I looked yonder onto the horizon an' noticed a storm was a brewin', so we adjusted our course accordin'.
As if by magic, winds started a blowin' an' the storm started movin' in our direction.
Lightnin' struck the boat, an' a piece of wood holdin' up the sail fell an' struck me on the 'ead.
I woke up in a bed an' the Skipper started on me, tellin' me I ruined his ship an' I need t' pay him back.

steps.player: That's awful. He does not sound like a nice man.

steps.npc: Nay, he usually is. He be upset about his ship, is all.
Can I help ye with anythin' else?

options.text: Got any tips for fighting Tempoross?

steps.player: Got any tips for fighting Tempoross?

steps.npc: Watch out for the waves. If ye get hit by that you could end up lost at sea.
Ye might find tying yourself t' somethin' using a rope t' be a life saver.
Or if ye manage to get yer hands on one of them there fancy Spirity Angler outfits, it comes with a built- in rope harness.
Can I help ye with anythin' else?

steps.player: I have to go.

steps.npc: Have a good'n. I know I won't.

using-items-on-her-damp-egg.player: Would you care for an egg in this difficult time?

using-items-on-her-damp-egg.npc: Oh, a damp egg! Yes, please!
Aye, I'll add it t' me collection!

using-items-on-her-damp-egg.player: You know there's a crate of them you could just help yourself t'...

using-items-on-her-damp-egg.npc: Hush! Don't let Timallus hear ye speak o' the damp egg crate. It'll set 'im off!

using-items-on-her-damp-egg.text: You give Koanee the damp egg.

using-items-on-her-egg.player: Would you care for an egg in this difficult time?

using-items-on-her-egg.npc: This is some comfort to be sure.

standard-dialogue.npc: What you do here, human? Get out of my sight!

standard-dialogue-after-monkey-madness-i.npc: You are a brave one, human!
You win, I will call off the attack.

standard-dialogue-before-underground-pas.player: Hello. What are you up to?

standard-dialogue-before-underground-pas.npc: Nothing exciting, just keeping an eye out.

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-th.npc: I wouldn't go in there if I were you. Only death awaits those who enter that place.

after-underground-pass.npc: I'm good... just keeping an eye out.

after-underground-pass-after-underground.player: These traps don't get any easier. But I'm alright, thanks.

without-level-60-magic.player: Hello there. What is this place?

without-level-60-magic.npc: Do not waste my time with trivial questions. I am the Great Kolodion, master of battle magic. I have an arena to run.
Hah! A wizard of your level? Don't be absurd.

after-mage-arena-i.npc: Hey there, how are you? Are you enjoying the bloodshed?

options.text: I think I've had enough for now.

steps.player: I think I've had enough for now.

steps.npc: A shame. You're a good battle mage. I hope to see you soon.

steps.player: Good stuff.

steps.npc: Not so good for the citizens; they won't stand a chance.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at-l.text: If this is the first time talking to Konar:

steps.npc: I see we have a new arrival. A bringer of death. Tell me, have you come to serve the balance?

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

steps.player: Tell me about the Saviours of Kourend.

steps.npc: For many years I used my position to fight against the crime and corruption in this city. No matter what I did it was never enough though. I realised that to defeat my enemies I needed to act as they do.
That's why I formed the Saviours of Kourend. We take the laws into our own hands and fight against all who would damage this city, no matter who they are.
What else do you want?

steps.player: Tell me about Port Piscarilius.

steps.npc: You've been here how long? You should know what we do by now.
Port Piscarilius is home to Kourend's fishermen and traders. We are the first port of call for any visitors to Kourend which means Port Piscarilius is home to a wide variety of individuals.
All people and goods coming to or from Kourend go through Port Piscarilius. This unfortunatly means that we are a centre point for the majority of crime within the city.
For many years I appealed to the Kourend Council for help in fighting this crime, but they cared little for us. Instead, I decided to beat them at their own game and fight fire with fire.
What else do you want?

steps.player: Tell me about your plans.

steps.npc: No.
What else do you want?

steps.player: Nothing.

steps.npc: How about you go away then?

steps.npc: Good to see you [player name]. You're very brave to come see me.

steps.npc: Most of the elves around here give me a wide berth. They seem to find me intimidating. How ironic that an old woman is more of a threat to them than the entire Iorwerth clan.

steps.player: You must have seen a fair bit in your time.

steps.npc: Oh yes, I'm the oldest elf still alive. You can thank this exoskeleton for that, one of our finer inventions.

steps.player: You must have plenty of stories to tell.

steps.npc: Yes, but not the time to tell them. They have plenty of books in the Tower of Voices if you want stories, most of them are from our Grand Library.
I'd personally recommend the one about Zalcano, a fun tale about how we trapped her beneath the city. She's still here now in fact, feel free to go give her a poke.

steps.player: I'll see about paying her a visit. See you later.

Lovakengj is a city of dwarves. It's the only non-human city in Kourend.
Lovakengj is very important you know. The resources mined here are used throughout the kingdom. Weapons, armour, tools, buildings...
All sorts of things come out of Lovakengj.

options.text: I'm here to talk about Combat Achievements.

options.text: Could you explain what they are?

steps.player: Could you explain what they are?

steps.npc: Combat Achievements are a set of tasks for all adventurers to try and accomplish. They range from simple missions to kill various creatures, to challenges that will push you to your limits.
The purpose of these tasks is for you to grow and improve, experience all that Gielinor has to offer, and become stronger in the process.
Is this something that sounds interesting to you?

options.text: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

steps.player: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

steps.npc: Combat Achievements are broken down into six tiers: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, Master and Grandmaster.
As you complete tasks, you'll earn points. Tasks in higher tiers give more points than easier tasks. Your rank depends on how many points you've earned.
Whenever new tasks are added to the list, there are more points available to earn, so the threshold needed for each rank will increase. Keep completing tasks to maintain your rank!

steps.text: This is the icon for the summary panel. Within it there is a section for Combat Achievements.
Clicking on the section will open the Combat Achievements interface, where you can browse tasks, bosses and rewards.
Some tasks will require numerous criteria to be completed, so make sure you read them carefully.

steps.npc: I'd recommend you go kill some monsters. Come back to me when you've completed a tier or two. I'll reward you for your efforts.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.player: Mistag said that Grubfoot could come into the city as long as he stayed with me.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.speaker: Ur-tag
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.text: That is somewhat irregular, but I suppose it is reasonable. Welcome to the city, surface goblin! What brings you to Dorgesh-Kaan?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.text: I looking for Chosen Commander.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.speaker: Ur-tag
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-cave-goblins.text: Ah yes, of course. I think she has been helping Oldak with his experiments recently. You should check Oldak's lab.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.player: Hello, Zanik! There's someone here to see you.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.text: Remarkable! You must be a goblin from the surface, correct?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.text: I recognize you. You were in Goblin Village, weren't you? You said you had a dream about me.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak.text: Yes. You Chosen Commander. Other goblins not believe, but I believe.

steps.player: Why don't other goblins believe?

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: They say Zanik not true goblin. She cannot be Chosen Commander because she not worship Big High War God. Because she not think war good.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: I certainly don't!

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: But does that mean she have no destiny? Perhaps her destiny to lead goblins into new age of peace.

options.text: That's an unusual sentiment for a goblin.

steps.player: That's an unusual sentiment for a goblin.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Yes. I thought all surface goblins thought war was good.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: Most do, but not me. I see goblins kill goblins, humans kill goblins. I think, is this really best thing in life?

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: I not say that to other goblins. They kill me if they think I not like war.

options.text: So why have you come to talk to Zanik?
So why have you come to talk to Zanik?

steps.player: What is the Chosen Commander?

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: Goblin legend. Hopespear, long ago goblin, he have dream. He say someday Chosen Commander come, lead all goblins to new age.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: Most goblins, they think Chosen Commander lead goblins to war and fight other races. But I think maybe not.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: I have dreams that Zanik is Chosen Commander. Before you visit Goblin Village I dream about Zanik. And now, last night I have new dream.

options.text: So why have you come to talk to Zanik?

steps.player: So why have you come to talk to Zanik?

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: To tell Chosen Commander about new dream I have.

steps.player: What was this new dream?

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Yes, what was it?
Cutscene begins, showing a distant, lush, foreign land with goblins.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: I have dream of far-off land. It like no land I ever see, but somehow I know it.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: It cool and wet. Ground is soft, big plants everywhere, red water bubbling.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: I see goblins, many goblins. Goblins of all tribes, but they not fight. They have no weapons. They live in peace.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: Then I see Chosen Commander. She stand at entrance to new land, she show way in. She lead all goblins on long journey to new land.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: I never see land before. I see it only in dream. But somehow I know what it is. It Yu'biusk, Land of the Goblins.
Cutscene ends.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: That goblin legend. Land of Goblins. Legend say long ago, even before war of gods, goblins come from Yu'biusk. Big High War God find them in Yu'biusk and take them to other lands.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: Most goblins forget legend. Think only of war. But I think, if Zanik lead us back to Yu'biusk, maybe we have peace. Maybe we be safe from people who want to kill us.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.player: How do you know your dream was true?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: Yes, how do you know? Dorgeshuun scientists and philosophers generally believe that dreams are a way for the mind to sort through memories. There is no known mechanism by which they can predict the future.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: This dream not like other dream. It so real.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: What do you think, [player name]?

options.text: It's just a dream. It doesn't mean anything.

steps.player: It's just a dream. It doesn't mean anything.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: It not just dream! It true! I know in heart!

steps.speaker: Oldak
steps.text: I'm sorry, Grubfoot, but wanting something badly doesn't make it true.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Even so... if there's any chance there might be something in it, we have to investigate.

options.text: I think it must mean something.

steps.player: I think it must mean something.

steps.speaker: Grubfoot
steps.text: Thank you, [player name]! I know you believe me!

steps.player: I don't know.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: It's probably nothing, but if there's even a small chance there's something in it, we have to investigate.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: So where is this promised land, Grubfoot?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I not know. Not know any goblin who know. But...

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: But what?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I should not tell! Not in front of non-goblin!

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: [player name] is a friend. You can tell [him/her/them].

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I suppose...

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: There secret place. Secret temple to Big High War God. No one know of it but goblins. Priests in secret temple, I bet they know way to Yu'biusk.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: But before I tell you where temple is, you must make promise. Promise not to tell any other non-goblins where temple is. If humans find out, maybe they attack, kill all goblins in temple.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I promise, Grubfoot. I won't tell anyone where the temple is.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: If that is what is required to keep your temple safe, then I promise too.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: [player name], you must promise as well. That very important.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.player: I promise not to tell anyone where the temple is.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I trust you, [player name]. You save village from H.A.M. attack. Now I tell you where temple is.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: It built long ago, on Plain of Mud. It sink into mud and now it underground in muddy caves. It far west of here, near place where many humans catch fish.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: Hmm... I've heard of a cave system to the west where many goblins live. That must be where this temple is hidden. I can make teleport spheres to take you there.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I can't go. I must get back to village before generals miss me.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: Oh, that's a pity. Just a minute...

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: Here, break this sphere on the ground. It will take you back to the Goblin Village.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: Thank you. I go now, but you must go to temple and find way to Yu'biusk.
Grubfoot teleports away.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: [player name], Zanik, are you ready to leave?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.speaker: Zanik
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-zanik-oldak-.text: I'm ready!

steps.player: I'm ready.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Then let's go!
Zanik and the player teleport to the Goblin Cave.

steps.player: I'm not ready.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: I'll wait until you are, [player name].

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-oldak-again-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-oldak-again-.text: Hello, [player name]. What did you find in the Goblin Temple?

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-oldak-again-.speaker: Oldak
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-oldak-again-.text: Ah, well you'd better get back there then.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the temple again?
Can I buy a teleport sphere please?

steps.player: I'll see you later.

grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-grubfoot-bef.speaker: Grubfoot
grubfoot-s-dream-talking-to-grubfoot-bef.text: Did you go to Land of Goblins?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Shut up Grubfoot!

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-zanik.speaker: Zanik
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-zanik.text: The entrance to the secret temple must be around here somewhere, [player name].

steps.player: Follow me.

options.text: I need to do something else.

steps.player: I need to do something else.

steps.speaker: Zanik
steps.text: Okay, [player name]. I'll meet you back at the cave entrance.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (1)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: Me hear Dorgesh tribe return from below ground.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (2)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: You want get into temple, Dorgesh-goblin?

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (2)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: Human! Where you think you going?

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.player: But you said we could go in!

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (1)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: No, we say Dorgesh-goblin go in. You human, you go away!

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (2)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: Humans not allowed! Only goblins allowed!

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (2)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: Go away, human! We already tell you not to come in!

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.speaker: Goblin guard (1)
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-goblin.text: Only goblins allowed in. If you goblin, you come in. But you not goblin, you stupid stinky puny human.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.text: Hello, [player name]. What did you find in the Goblin Temple?

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.player: Humans aren't allowed inside. They let Zanik in, but not me.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.text: Hmm... that is an interesting problem. But I think there is a way to get you in.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.player: How can I get into the temple without being a goblin?
What? But you said you had a way.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.text: Yes, I think you can get into the temple, but not without being a goblin. I have been in correspondence with some of the wizards who live on the surface. I know of one who might be able to help you.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak.text: They are known as the Makeover Mage. You should go and talk to them. I believe they live south west of the human city of Falador.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the temple again?

steps.player: Can you teleport me to the temple again?

steps.speaker: Oldak
steps.text: I can, but I can't afford to keep doing it for free. If you get me two law runes and a piece of molten glass, I'll make a sphere to take you there.
If the player does not have the materials:

steps.player: I'll have to go get some law runes and molten glass then.

steps.text: If the player has the materials:
The player is teleported to the Goblin Cave.

steps.player: Never mind, I'll walk.

options.text: Can I buy a teleport sphere please?
I'll go and see this mage.

steps.player: I'll go and see this mage.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.text: Hello, [player name]. Did you speak to the Makeover Mage?

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.text: You really should. I believe they live south west of the human city of Falador.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the temple again?
Can I buy a teleport sphere please?
I'll go and see this mage.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.text: You shouldn't just go picking berries from bushes that don't belong to you.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-the-ma.speaker: Makeover Mage
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-the-ma.text: Hello there! I am known as the Makeover Mage! I have spent many years researching magics that can change your physical appearance!

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-the-ma.speaker: Makeover Mage
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-the-ma.text: I can alter your physical form with my magic, there's no fee. Would you like me to perform my magics upon you?

options.text: Cool amulet! Can I have one?
Can you turn me into a goblin?

steps.player: Can you turn me into a goblin?

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: Into a goblin? What do you want to turn into a goblin for?

options.text: I need to slip past some goblin guards.

steps.player: I need to slip past some goblin guards.

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: Really? What are they guarding?

options.text: I promised not to tell anyone.

steps.player: I promised not to tell anyone.

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: Okay, okay, sorry I asked.

options.text: Can you turn me into a goblin or not?

steps.player: Can you turn me into a goblin or not?

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: I think I know how, but I've never deliberately transmogrified someone into another species before. It's a very risky procedure, and I don't want to be held responsible if it goes wrong.

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: How about I tell you the recipe so you can make the potion yourself. It's not too complex. You'll just need to take a toadflax potion and add some pharmakos berries.

steps.player: Pharmakos berries?

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: That's right. They're quite rare, but have wonderful properties that help with transmogrification. Luckily, I grow plenty right outside. Feel free to take some.

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: Now, once you've made the potion, remember that the transformation is very delicate. It will reverse itself if you are in direct sunlight or if you perform a strenuous activity like fighting.

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: For that reason, you should only drink it in the area where you're going to need it. I'd also suggest you take off any pieces of armour or similar before drinking it, just in case the transformation damages them.

steps.player: Okay. Thanks for the help.

options.text: Actually, I don't want to be a goblin.
Can you turn me into a goblin or not?
Actually, I don't want to be a goblin.

steps.player: I just like goblins.

steps.speaker: Makeover Mage
steps.text: What a strange thing to want to turn into.

options.text: I need to slip past some goblin guards.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.text: Hello, [player name]. Any luck getting into the Goblin Temple?

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.player: Not yet, but I spoke to the Makeover Mage. They told me how to make a potion to turn myself into a goblin.

imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.speaker: Oldak
imposter-among-goblins-talking-to-oldak-.text: Excellent! You'd better head back to the temple and try this potion out.

Can I buy a teleport sphere please?

steps.player: I'll see you later.

options.text: I'd like to get into the temple please.

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: This is what Big High War God say:

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: Slay enemies of Big High War God!

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: Not to doubt Big High War God!

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: Big High War God make us strong!

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: In beginning, goblins have no commander.

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: Big High War God send commander!

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: He send commander to lead us.

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: But some day he send new commander!

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: New commander leads goblins to victory!

the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.speaker: Preacher
the-temple-of-tribes-preacher-s-sermon.text: Then Big High War God return!

steps.speaker: Goblin
steps.text: Me hear Dorgesh tribe come back from underground. Maybe now all tribes united, prophecy will come true! Chosen Commander come and lead all tribes to victory over world!

steps.speaker: Goblin
steps.text: Me hear there ghost in temple crypt! No one see it, but sometimes they hear it. 'Wooo... wooo...' it say.

steps.speaker: Goblin
steps.text: Me mighty warrior of Big High War God! Me find farmer working in field, and me attack! He so scared he run off! Then me trample on crops! This deeds of great warrior of Big High War God!

steps.speaker: Goblin
steps.text: Me glad me finally get to secret goblin temple! Me walk long way to get here, always in danger of humans. But now me here, me safe! There no humans here!

steps.speaker: Goblin
steps.text: Me hate humans! When me leave temple, me go and kill many human children!

steps.speaker: Goblin

She Chosen Commander.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead

steps.player: Oh... well she Dorgeshuun goblin.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: Yes, there was goblin who say she Dorgesh-goblin. She have big eyes and she speak in strange accent. She ask about Yu'biusk, but she not pass test.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: She not just not know answers. Lots of goblins not know answers. She start shouting crazy ideas about how war is bad and we not need gods.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: Huzamogaarb guards, they grab her and they put her in prison in Huzamogaarb enclave.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: Only Huzamogaarb tribe allowed in the enclave. That not you. You wearing wrong armour. The Huzamogaarb tribe wear black armour.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: They use dye to make armour black. Other tribes do similar, but in own tribe colour instead.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: High Priest Bighead says a line of random dialog shown above.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.player: Me want to know about Yu'biusk.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: That knowledge not for ordinary goblin. Only those who understand ways of Big High War God may learn of Yu'biusk.

options.text: I understand Big High War God.

steps.player: I understand Big High War God.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Then you answer my questions, and we will see.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: True or false: Those who do not believe in Big High War God, whether they goblins or other races, must die.

steps.player: True.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Oh? Why?

options.text: Big High War God commands it.

steps.player: Big High War God commands it.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That right! It in commandments.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: 'Not to doubt Big High War God! Doubters must die!' This mean we slay goblins who not believe.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: 'Always to slay enemies of Big High War God!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Second question. True or false: Big High War God chose goblins to be his race because goblins mighty warriors.

steps.player: True.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Really? Then how we come to be mighty warriors, before Big High War God find us?

options.text: We taught selves to be mighty!

steps.player: We taught selves to be mighty!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Fool! Heretic! You guilty of sin of pride! Goblins teach selves nothing. All good we have come from Big High War God!

steps.player: Other god made us mighty.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: You confused. Yes, in time of great war, some goblins serve other gods. But no one make us mighty but Big High War God.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Look around at how mighty we are! How we proud of war. How we never flinch from battle or pain or death. How we never surrender or show mercy or pity!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: How could any other god but Big High War God do this?

steps.player: We naturally mighty warriors.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Naturally? Let me tell you what goblins are naturally! We tiny, we weak, we cowardly, we love peace and not war!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: All that is good, that is strong, that is powerful, we get from Big High War God! Go away and remember this!

steps.player: False.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Oh? Why you say that?

options.text: He chose us for other quality.

steps.player: He chose us for other quality.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: What other quality important, except that we great warriors? Get away, silly goblin! Too much drink muddle brain and give you strange thoughts!

options.text: Goblins not mighty warriors before he chose us.

steps.player: Goblins not mighty warriors before he chose us.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That good! Goblins mighty warriors now, but that only because Big High War God make us so! Without Big High War God we nothing! Remember that.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Third question. True or false: Goblin leaders should be good at planning in order to win battles.

steps.player: True.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Oh? Why you say that?

options.text: Big High War God rewards victory.

steps.player: Big High War God rewards victory.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Even victory that comes through clever dirty tricks? Even victory that comes through breaking Big High War God's commandments? No. Not all victory honour Big High War God.

options.text: Big High War God teaches us to think for selves.

steps.player: Big High War God teaches us to think for selves.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: What? Where you hear that? You think for yourself, you maybe think stupid, dangerous thoughts. You maybe think war not good, or Big High War God not best god.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: No. Do not think for self. Think only thoughts of Big High War God. His thoughts perfect, so if you think different thoughts, those thoughts bad.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That why Big High War God command, 'Not to make own plans. Thinkers must die.'

options.text: Planning is part of war, and all parts of war are good.

steps.player: Planning is part of war, and all parts of war are good.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: You confused. It true all parts of war are good, but not all parts of war are for goblins.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Big High War God not make us commanders. He make us soldiers, and send commanders to lead us. They make plans for us. We not have commander now, but still we must not make own plans.

steps.player: False.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Why not?

steps.player: That one of the commandments.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That right. 'Not to make own plans. Thinkers must die.'

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Last question. Prophecy say someday Big High War God send Chosen Commander. What Chosen Commander do?

options.text: Lead goblins to promied land of Yu'biusk.

steps.player: Lead goblins to promised land of Yu'biusk.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Yu'biusk? You have story wrong way round! Yu'biusk land all goblins come from. But there no prophecy that we go back there.

options.text: Lead goblins to victory over whole world.

steps.player: Lead goblins to victory over whole world.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That right! And war will end in victory and victory last forever!
Dialogue continues as below after answering questions.

steps.player: Destroy world.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Destroy world? Why Big High War God want to do that? Then there be no goblins to fight for him!

steps.player: Make goblins fight each other.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Ha ha ha! Big High War God not need send commander to do that! Only reason goblins not fight more is prophet Hopespear say not.

options.text: Big High War God controls outcome of the battle.

steps.player: Big High War God controls outcome of the battle.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That true. But it true whether goblin leaders make plans or not. So it not answer question.

options.text: Goblins stupid and would make poor plans.

steps.player: Goblins stupid and would make poor plans.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: You call me stupid? Big High War God make goblins perfect! Big High War God tell us not make plans, but if we make plans, they be best plans ever!

steps.player: Goblins not mighty warriors.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: How dare you? You insult goblin race in holy temple! We mighty warriors because we worship Big High War God!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Goblins like you, who say we not strong, you are thing that make us weak! Never doubt, never question, never think! That way of Big High War God.

steps.player: They might lead us astray.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That wrong! No true goblin be lead astray by those who not believe. If goblin led astray, that goblin deserve to die!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: I think you weak in faith, if you think you be led astray. You go now, think on this. Be stronger in faith.

steps.player: False.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Oh? Why not?

options.text: Big High War God commands it.

steps.player: Big High War God commands it.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Big High War God command we not kill enemies?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: You not understand Big High War God at all! You like filthy stinking cave goblin! Go away and think on how stupid you are!

steps.player: Goblin should not fight goblin.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: It true that prophet Hopespear tell us goblin should not fight against goblin. But Big High War God, he command that those who not believe must die.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: To little mind, weak mind, this seem to contradict. But only if you not have faith. In Big High War God, there no contradiction.

options.text: We try to convert them instead.

steps.player: We try to convert them instead.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Convert them? You stupid goblin! You not even know name of god. He Big High WAR God! We kill enemies, not convert!

steps.player: I not know.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That good. True goblin not want to understand. Fight and die for glory of Big High War God. Never ask question or have thought.

steps.player: Is not for me then.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That good. True goblin not want to understand. Fight and die for glory of Big High War God. Never ask question or have thought.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: High Priest Bighead says a line of random dialog shown above.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.player: Me want to know about Yu'biusk.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.speaker: High Priest Bighead
the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: You ready to answer questions?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.text: Same as above

steps.player: No.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That good. True goblin not want to understand. Fight and die for glory of Big High War God. Never ask question or have thought.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: High Priest Bighead says a line of random dialog shown above.

options.text: Me want to know about Yu'biusk.

steps.player: Me want to know about Yu'biusk.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Yu'biusk is goblin legend. Very old legend, from before this temple built. From before Hopespear the prophet. Even before great war.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Legend say that goblins come from land of Yu'biusk. Big High War God find goblins in Yu'biusk and bring them to other lands to train them as warriors!

steps.player: Will goblins return to Yu'biusk?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Why we want to return to Yu'biusk? In Yu'biusk we weak. Big High War God take us from Yu'biusk and make us strong.

steps.player: Where is Yu'biusk?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Me not know. Me think Snothead maybe know.

steps.player: Where can I find him?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: He old high priest in temple crypt behind me! He dead!

steps.player: Oh.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Maybe me ask him next time me see him.

steps.player: What? But you said he dead!

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Ha ha! You not know, but since you pass test, me tell you.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: When goblin high priest die, they buried in temple crypt in special magic way.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: This mean next high priest can ask them questions, even though they dead. I just say name of high priest over grave, and he appear and answer questions.

options.text: Can I talk to old high priests?

steps.player: Can I talk to old high priests?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: No. Temple crypt is holy place. Only high priest allowed into crypt, and that me. No other goblin ever go in.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Crypt door locked by six keys, kept by six tribal priests. Priests only give keys to me. They never give them to normal goblin like you.

options.text: What Big High War God's real name?
Why there only six tribes in temple?
What Big High War God's real name?
Why there only six tribes in temple?
What Big High War God's real name?

steps.player: What Big High War God's real name?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: You ask big question. Big High War God's true name not for normal goblin minds, but since you pass test, I tell you. His true name Bandos.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: That name that ogres call him, that orks call him. That name that goblin priests call him on holy days. But normal goblins, you must show respect. You only call him Big High War God.

options.text: Why there only six tribes in temple?

steps.player: Why there only six tribes in temple?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Goblin tribes are thing of past. Long ago, all goblins divided into twelve tribes. Dorgeshuun tribe rebel, so Big High War God punish them. Then there eleven tribes.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: No other tribes disappear like Dorgeshuun, but over ages, tribes merge. Now most goblins, they not know what tribe they come from.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Sometimes, goblins who know what tribe they come from, they come here and make tribal enclaves. They colour armour different colours to show what tribe they in. But not all tribes here.

options.text: How me get into tribal enclaves?

steps.player: How me get into tribal enclaves?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Goblins show tribe by dying armour special tribe colour. Yellow for Yurkolgokh, white for Saragorgak, purple for Horogothgar, orange for Narogoshuun, blue for Ekeleshuun and black for Huzamogaarb.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: You not wearing colour, you not entering the enclave.

steps.player: Where they get dye?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Some goblins say they go to witch-lady in Draynor for it. Me hope they beat up witch-lady and take dye! That way of Big High War God!

options.text: Me want to know about Yu'biusk.
What Big High War God's real name?

steps.player: Me have no questions.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Good. Goblins should not ask questions. Fight and die for glory of Big High War God. Never ask question or have thought.

the-temple-of-tribes-talking-to-high-pri.text: High Priest Bighead says a line of random dialog shown above.

options.text: Me want to take test again.

steps.player: Me want to take test again.

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Good. Goblins must always remember faith to Big High War God.

options.text: Me want to know about Yu'biusk.
What Big High War God's real name?
Why there only six tribes in temple?

steps.speaker: High Priest Bighead
steps.text: Then bring glory to Big High War God.

keys-to-the-crypt-talking-to-aggie.speaker: Aggie
keys-to-the-crypt-talking-to-aggie.text: What can I help you with?

options.text: What could you make for me?
Cool, do you turn people into frogs?
You mad old witch, you can't help me.
Can you make dyes for me please?

steps.player: Can you make dyes for me please?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: What sort of dye would you like? Red, yellow or blue?

options.text: What do you need to make red dye?
What do you need to make yellow dye?
What do you need to make blue dye?
Can you make black or white dye?

steps.player: Can you make black or white dye?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Black dye can be made by grinding up black mushrooms. That's dead easy. The mushrooms grow in some old caves and ruins.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: But white dye? There's no such thing!

steps.player: Then how can you colour clothes white?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Usually you can't, but with poorly-made clothes, it's possible to remove the dye. Even then, it's a very tricky process involving a special ingredient found in the gut of the Hemenster Whitefish.

steps.player: Hemenster Whitefish?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Yes, found only at Hemenster, oddly enough. It's the place where they have those fishing contests.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: If you fancy catching some, you should know that very specific bait is needed. Only slimy eels will work. I hear you can catch those in the caves below Lumbridge Swamp.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Anyway, if you do have something you want the dye removing from, just bring me a Hemenster Whitefish and five coins.

options.text: What other colours can you make?

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: You're welcome!

options.text: Actually, I am happy the colour I am.
