steps.player: He didn't want to prove himself?

steps.npc: Ugh, of course not. The fool says he won't fight a woman. That demon thinks he's a pillar of chivalry.

steps.player: That is a little suspicious.

steps.npc: Yes. Anyway, to fully answer your initial question, I found demons here to the north and some lesser demons to the east.

steps.player: What are they doing here?

steps.npc: Demons tend to stay where they were summoned. You see, once they're done eating the stupid wizard that thought it could control a demon, they're pretty much stuck until someone else decides to summon them.

steps.player: Summoning, aye? Sounds like a dangerous skill to practise.

steps.npc: Be even warier of the imps. They'll steal the boots from your feet if you give 'em the chance.

steps.player: I don't see how that's worse than being eaten, but thanks, I'll keep an eye out.
Bye!

steps.npc: See you 'round, human.
Nilsal, my child. I hope you are enjoying your time in the valley.

options.text: Can you heal me? I'm injured.

steps.player: Can you heal me? I'm injured.

steps.text: If the player is on a PvP world:

steps.npc: Sorry, but I cannot.

steps.text: If the player has full hitpoints:

steps.npc: I could, but you don't appear to actually need healing right now.
Of course.

steps.text: The teoki whispers a prayer and you suddenly feel a bit better.
2 + 20% of the player's hitpoints are restored.

options.text: What's the giant tree stump all about?

steps.player: What's the giant tree stump all about?

steps.npc: Ah, it is quite a sad story I'm afraid. You should speak to my counterpart if you wish to hear it. He tells it better than I.

steps.player: I'd better be off.

steps.npc: May the sun light your way, my child.

investigating-livius.player: A few cuts and scrapes... No stab wound... Poison perhaps?

steps.player: Hi.

steps.npc: Hey! What can I do for ya' today?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm Lleidr, a simple forest dweller.

steps.player: It's nice to meet you Lleidr, I'm [player name].

steps.npc: Great.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Currently, I'm fishing.

steps.player: Anything else?

steps.npc: Avoid idle chit-chat.

steps.player: Alright, I get the hint.

steps.npc: That's nice to hear, see you around.

steps.player: ...Bye.
Bye!

steps.npc: Farewell, adventurer.
You look like someone that could use an overly expensive crown. Finest clothes around! Want to take a look?

steps.player: Yes, please.
No thanks.

steps.npc: Your loss, I suppose.
Can I interest you in any herbal equipment? Any supplies, perhaps?

steps.player: Let's see what you've got.
No thanks.

steps.npc: Well whenever you're looking to mix a potion or two, I've got what you need!

before-tree-gnome-village.npc: Hee hee, lardi da, lardi dee. (The gnome appears to be singing.)

standard-dialogue.npc: You're the best!
Well I'm better. Hee hee.
Get out of my way, you fool! Can't you see I'm busy?
Monkeys these days... you'll be acting like one of those awful Gnomes next...

standard-dialogue-undisguised-with-monke.npc: You're one of those humans that everybody has been talking about! The Marimbo Guard will kill you on the spot!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello, can I help you?

steps.player: Let's trade.
Where am I?

steps.npc: This is the marketplace of Hosidius. To the north west there's my sister's pub, and in the south is my grandfather's fruit farm. Do you need to buy anything while you're here?

steps.player: No, I'm okay.

standard-dialogue-interacting-with-logav.npc: Hey! You're that thief! Get away from my stall.

steps.player: Hello. What are you doing here?

steps.npc: I'm studying the Invasion of the Wintertodt.

options.text: Tell me more about the Wintertodt.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Wintertodt.

steps.npc: The Wintertodt is a fiercely cold being, capable of freezing entire areas with its mere presence. We do not know what exactly the Wintertodt is, nor where it came from.
When the Wintertodt first attacked, it was feared that all of Kourend would be lost. Fortunately, the Order of the Sacred Flame and Dinh the Master Smith were able to stop it.

options.text: How did they stop the Wintertodt?

steps.player: How did they stop the Wintertodt?

steps.npc: Dinh was a great smith and engineer. He uncovered the power of the Bruma tree. Using bark from the tree and various metal compounds, Dinh forged the doors of the prison that hold the Wintertodt.
In addition, the Order of the Sacred Flame utilised the Bruma tree in firemaking. They heated the environment to subdue Wintertodt.

options.text: Tell me more about the invasion.
Tell me more about the invasion.

steps.player: Tell me more about the invasion.

steps.npc: More than 137 decades ago, seemingly from nowhere, the Wintertodt began terrorising the lands north of Kourend, freezing everything within its path.
After five decades of this terror, the people of Kourend were able to quell the beast, containing it in an icy prison.
The Wintertodt remained subdued until very recently, when it began to threaten Kourend once more.
Fortunately, the Order of the Sacred Flame is able to contain the Wintertodt and prevent another attack.

steps.player: Goodbye.

options.text: I'm going to stop looking for temple, sun and moon pages.
options.condition: If the player is currently looking for more tome pages:

steps.player: I'm going to stop looking for temple, sun and moon pages.

steps.npc: As you wish adventurer.

steps.text: You will no longer have a chance to receive temple, sun and moon pages from creatures in the Forthos Dungeon.

steps.npc: Now shhhh!

options.text: I'm going to start looking for temple, sun and moon pages.
options.condition: If the player is currently not looking for more tome pages:

steps.player: I'm going to start looking for temple, sun and moon pages.

steps.npc: As you wish adventurer.

steps.text: You will now have a chance to receive temple, sun and moon pages from creatures in the Forthos Dungeon.

steps.npc: Now shhhh!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.npc: Shhhh!

steps.player: Tell me about the Library.

steps.npc: Shhhh!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

options.text: Do you help people find books?

steps.player: Do you help people find books?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

steps.player: Can you stop shushing me?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

options.text: Do you do anything useful at all?

steps.player: Do you do anything useful at all?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

steps.player: What is wrong with you?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

options.text: What is the point in you being here?

steps.player: What is the point in you being here?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

options.text: How can I get a job like yours?

steps.player: How can I get a job like yours?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

steps.player: You're an utterly useless person.

steps.npc: Shhhh!

options.text: HOW ABOUT I SHOUT REALLY LOUD THEN.

steps.player: HOW ABOUT I SHOUT REALLY LOUD THEN?

steps.npc: Shhhh!

steps.player: Sorry.

steps.npc: That's better.

using-a-forthos-tome-on-logosia.text: If the player has not handed in all three tomes:

steps.npc: I have not seen this before. Your donation to the library is appreciated.

using-a-forthos-tome-on-logosia.text: If the player has one other tome in their inventory:

steps.player: You can have this tome which I discovered aswell.

steps.text: You hand Logosia the tome.

using-a-forthos-tome-on-logosia.text: If the player has the two other tomes in their inventory.

steps.player: You can have these tomes which I discovered aswell.

steps.text: You hand Logosia the tomes.

steps.npc: Again, your donation to the library is appreciated

using-a-forthos-tome-on-logosia.text: If the player has not handed in all three tomes.
If the player has handed in all three tomes.

steps.npc: Your contributions to the library have been noticed. We would like to reward you for your assistance.

steps.text: You receive an experience lamp as a reward.

steps.npc: If you find any spare pages for these books I would be willing to give you 1,000 gold for each one. Duplicate sources of information are always useful.

steps.player: I'll keep an eye out.

steps.npc: Enough talk now, Shhhh!

treasure-trails-master.text: With a full inventory:

steps.npc: Hey, I have something for you but you don't have any space for it!

treasure-trails-master.text: a torn part of a clue scroll.
You are handed a torn part of a clue scroll.

options.text: Can I go for a ride?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride?

steps.text: If the player does not have 20 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Minecart rides are 20 coins.

steps.text: If the player has 20 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.text: (Lovakengj Minecart Network interface opens.)

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

options.text: Can I go for a ride?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride?

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.text: (Lovakengj Minecart Network interface opens.)

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

standard-dialogue-unlimited-ride-fee-ref.npc: As a loyal customer of the Lovakengj Minecart Network, you're entitled to this.
Now, can I help you today?

before-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Don't talk to me! I don't have time for the likes of you!

before-the-fremennik-trials.text: You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Lunar Diplomacy quest.

standard-dialogue-rellekka-without-a-sea.npc: You won't make many friends on Lunar Isle without your Seal of Passage.

options.text: That's fine, I'm just going to Pirates' Cove.

steps.player: That's fine, I'm just going to Pirates' Cove.

steps.text: Player is transported to Pirates' cove

options.text: Oh, I'd better go back and get it.

steps.player: Oh, I'd better go back and get it.

standard-dialogue-rellekka-with-a-seal-o.player: Hi Lokar, can you take me back to your ship?

standard-dialogue-rellekka-with-a-seal-o.npc: Sheesh, make your mind up [pal/lady], I'm not a taxi service!

steps.text: Player is transported to Pirates' cove

steps.player: Actually, I've changed my mind. Again. I don't want to go.

steps.npc: You are possibly the most indecisive person I have ever met...

steps.player: Well, 'bye then.

standard-dialogue-pirates-cove.npc: Hi again [Fremennik name]! What can I do for you?

standard-dialogue-pirates-cove.text: If the player doesn't have a Seal of Passage:

steps.player: Do I still need the Seal of Passage?

steps.npc: Yeah, why?

steps.player: I lost it.

steps.npc: Silly you. You'll have to go back to Brundt the Chieftain to get another before you can go on to Lunar Isle.

options.text: Can you take me back to Rellekka?

steps.player: Can you take me back to Rellekka please?

steps.npc: Hey, if you want to go back to loserville with all the losers, who am I to stop you?

steps.text: Player is transported to Rellekka

steps.player: Nothing thanks! I just saw you here and thought I'd say hello!

steps.npc: Hey, I knew you seemed cool when I met you [Fremennik name]!
Greetings human.

steps.player: Hello, who are you?

steps.npc: Lokraa quo Sihar. I am one of the mystics of the Kahlith. Are you here to serve the balance?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.npc: Then you should speak to Konar quo Maten. She will guide you.

steps.player: No.

steps.npc: A shame. You are a bringer of death, you could be of great use to the balance.

steps.player: I'm not sure.

steps.npc: Then you should speak with Xorrah quo Sihar. He will show you the way.

standard-dialogue.npc: Arrr, matey!

standard-dialogue.text: Before completing Pirate's Treasure:

steps.player: I'm looking for Redbeard Frank.

steps.npc: Redbeard Frank ye say? He be outside. Says he likes the feel of the wind on his cheeks.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: Why are you called Longbow Ben?

steps.player: Why are you called Longbow Ben?

steps.npc: Arrr, that's a strange yarn.
I was to be marooned, ye see. A scurvy troublemaker had taken my ship, and he put me ashore on a little island.

steps.player: Gosh, how did you escape?

steps.npc: Arrr, ye see, he made one mistake! Before he sailed away, he gave me a bow and one arrow so that I wouldn't have to die slowly.
So I shot him and took my ship back.

steps.player: Right...

options.text: Have you got any quests I could do?

steps.player: Have you got any quests I could do?

steps.text: Before completing Pirate's Treasure and Goblin Diplomacy:

steps.npc: Nay, but the barkeep hears most of the news around here. Or Redbeard Frank, he's often spoken of buried treasure. Perhaps ye should be asking them for quests.

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.text: Before completing Pirate's Treasure:

steps.npc: Nay, but Redbeard Frank has often spoken of buried treasure. Perhaps ye should be asking him for a quest.

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.text: Before completing Goblin Diplomacy:

steps.npc: Nay, but the barkeep hears most of the news around here. Perhaps ye should be asking him for a quest.

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.text: After completing Pirate's Treasure and Goblin Diplomacy:

steps.npc: Nay, I've nothing for ye to do. But I hear there's an old landlubber in Draynor Village who's always a-looking for a lively [lad/lass] to do him a favour.

steps.player: Thanks.

alternate-dialogue.npc: Nay, always ye say it wrong! Tis 'we are', not 'we be'.

alternate-dialogue.speaker: Jack Seagull
alternate-dialogue.text: I be a pirate, not a scurvy schoolmaster!

alternate-dialogue.npc: Ye be a fool, and a disgrace to piracy.

alternate-dialogue.player: I think I'll leave you two to sort it out.

before-the-fremennik-trials-talking-to-h.speaker: Longhall bouncer
before-the-fremennik-trials-talking-to-h.text: Hey, outerlander. You can't go through there. Talent only, backstage.

after-completing-the-bard-s-trial.npc: You can't go through there. Talent only, backstage.
No you're not. I saw your performance. I was paid well to keep you from ever setting foot on stage here again.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello there.

standard-dialogue.player: Hello, Longramble. How goes the hunt for the edge of the world?

standard-dialogue.npc: Truth be told, I've found myself getting a bit side- tracked. The potential discovery of Arposandra is quite an exciting one!
Yes, that's why I've not dared go inside again. It's much safer out here. Slightly less smelly as well.

standard-dialogue.player: Slightly being the key word there.

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Hello there. How goes the hunt for Arposandra?

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.player: I think I've found an entrance to the city, but it's too well defended. There's all these traps, and some talking terrorbird guards!

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Talking terrorbirds? There must be some strange magic being practised in there. What do you plan to do?

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.player: I don't know. I think I've hit a dead end for now.

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: That's a shame. Still, you've made a big discovery. It will be quite the tale to tell... assuming anyone believes a story about talking terrorbirds, that is.

standard-dialogue-when-delivering-a-tang.text: You hand over the tangled toads' legs to the very grateful-looking gnome. He stuffs them straight into his mouth and hands you a mint cake in return.
Longramble continues into his standard dialogue.

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.player: I appear to have misplaced the grappling equipment I need to cross the river.

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.npc: That wasn't very clever, was it?
Well, it's a good job explorers like me know how to use their surroundings. I have an idea!

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.text: Longramble explains, in huge detail, a wildly complicated plan to get you across the river. It involves using various items scrounged from the local flora and fauna.

Before you know it, you find yourself on the other side of the river with a bump on your head and no recollection of how you got across. You wonder what Longramble's plan was. It must have been very clever.

steps.npc: What do you want?

steps.player: What are you guarding?

steps.npc: This path leads to the Doors of Dinh. You should be careful if you wish to travel any further.

options.text: Tell me about the Doors of Dinh.

steps.player: Tell me about the Doors of Dinh.

steps.npc: They're to keep the Wintertodt at bay. No-one knows what it really is, but centuries ago it came out of the northern wastes to terrorise the kingdom.
The Doors were created by Dinh, a master smither, to imprison the Wintertodt.
Now we keep a watch on the pass, so that the armies can be summoned if the Wintertodt ever escapes.

steps.player: Okay, thanks for the warning.
Okay, thanks for the warning.
Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm the duty look-out on the northern pass. It's the worst assignment there is.
As if the cold weren't bad enough, the snooty Arceuus magi always look down their noses at the Shayzien armies, just because we use muscle and steel rather than fancy magicks.

steps.player: I'll leave you alone now.

standard-dialogue-after-sins-of-the-fath.npc: You! You're the one that lost me my tithes. Get out before I have you killed!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-is-not-d.npc: Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!

standard-dialogue-after-the-blood-moon-r.npc: Then be on your way. I have a meeting with Lord Vitur soon and I don't need any distractions.

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.npc: Tell me, [player vampyre name], what blood tastes the best?
You misunderstand me, I mean what kind of human?
What? I mean, yes. But what else?

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.player: I don't know... What's the actual answer?

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.npc: Love. Blood tastes best when it comes from one who loves.
Too many around here treat their tithes with discontentment. When they do, they miss out on the full potential blood has to offer.
Treat your tithes with respect instead. They will come to love you, and their blood becomes so much better as a result.

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.player: I see. I'll keep that in mind.

after-song-of-the-elves.npc: The city is flourishing, largely thanks to you. There's still some mistrust for the Iorwerth clan, but overall I'd say it's been over a thousand years since our people were doing this well.

after-song-of-the-elves.player: That's great to hear. What about you though?

after-song-of-the-elves.npc: I still mourn Glarial every day, until the end of time a part of me will be missing, never to be replaced.
But I know now that I can't let that impact the elves here. Many of them never even knew their former queen. My grief is mine alone, they need not bear it.

To them, I'm trying my best to be a leader they deserve, to correct the mistakes of the past. Lord Iorwerth believed we were nothing without Seren. We need to prove that we have a future with her gone.
Thankfully I have the other elders to help this time. Ruling is not as hard when you share out the responsiblities.

after-song-of-the-elves.player: Well I'm glad to hear things are going well.

after-song-of-the-elves.npc: And we are glad to have you here with us. None of this would have been possible without you.

steps.player: Are you alright?

steps.speaker: Damien Leucurte
steps.text: You may speak.

steps.npc: Oh, yes yes, I'm fine.

steps.player: You look a little beat up.

steps.npc: These scratches? Don't worry, just a disagreement with a thorn bush.

steps.player: Sure...

steps.speaker: Damien Leucurte
steps.text: Is there something you wanted, bloodbag?

steps.player: Just looking around.

steps.speaker: Damien Leucurte
steps.text: Well, I'd prefer you did it elsewhere, Crombwick is busy entertaining his guests.

steps.player: Strange bunch of guests...
Hello.

steps.npc: What want you, with the Lord of the Kinshra? Speak!

steps.player: Erm, nothing actually.

steps.npc: Then begone knave, before I have my Knights put you to the sword!
Greetings [player name].

steps.player: Hey Iestin. So they made you the new Lord Iorwerth?

steps.npc: Indeed. Apart from Morvran, I am the closest living relative of the previous Lord Iorwerth.

steps.player: Did Morvran not want the role?

steps.npc: No. That's probably for the best though. Morvran was very close to my predecessor. It would have made many uncomfortable if he had taken on the role.

steps.player: How have things been since the city was reformed?

steps.npc: The others still hold a lot of mistrust for our clan. It will take a long time for those rifts to be repaired. We are on the right path though.

steps.player: That's good to hear. All the best.

steps.npc: Likewise.
Good day [player name]. Have you come to hear the song of the elves?

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: Do you not hear it? The sounds of a city in harmony. It is the song of the elves, the story of our people.
The last few verses were dark and quiet, but now our city is restored, we find ourselves singing a new verse, one of joy and light.

steps.player: I see. I guess I've never been the type to reflect on that sort of thing.

steps.npc: More of a fighter? We have a song for that too. If you wish to sing it, head to the Gauntlet and put yourself to the test.

steps.player: I might just give it a shot. Thanks.
Good day.

steps.npc: Sorry, can't stop to talk. So much to do, so little time.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello there.

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: I am Kandur Hosidius and I am the lord of Hosidius, the city of farmers and chefs. I live here with my wife, Elena, and my two sons, Artur and Pandur.
My family and I have a peaceful existence here. That's mainly because I care not for the politics of the other houses. I instead devote my time to more meaningful pursuits.

steps.player: Such as?

steps.npc: Ensuring that Kourend is well fed. We may live in gentle times now but who knows how long it will be that way. Sooner or later another war or long winter will hit us. History has proven that.
Anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: Tell me about Hosidius.

steps.npc: Hosidius is home to the farmers and chefs of Kourend. We are the main food supplier to the kingdom and we ensure that her people are fed.
We also own more land than the other Kourend houses. We need the extra space for all of our crops.

steps.player: Do the other houses not get annoyed at how much land you have?

steps.npc: Sometimes. They know it is necessary though. There was once a time when the land was shared equally. But then the great famine came, and Kourend did not have the food to last through it.
After that, more space was given to Hosidius. We've had the most land ever since.
Anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: Tell me about your plans.

steps.npc: Plans? My only plan is to keep providing food to this kingdom.

steps.player: But what of the Royal Accord of Twill? You must have kept it for a reason.

steps.npc: I did. The Accord has the potential to be a powerful weapon, for words cut deeper than a blade ever can. However, I have no need to use this weapon, not unless the other houses give me reason to.
Anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: Until next time.

if-the-player-lost-the-memoir-page-befor.npc: I assume you're after that reward I promised you. Here you go.

steps.player: Good day!

steps.npc: Isn't it just!

steps.player: What brings you down here?

steps.npc: This and that... But mostly, I'm looking for a good place to mobilise my army.

steps.player: That's awfully specific, you sure this is a good place for it?

steps.npc: I don't see why not!

steps.player: I'm not sure there's enough land, to be honest.

steps.npc: Tish tosh! I'm importing sand from Al Kharid, there'll be a base camp here in no time, do not fret!

steps.player: Oh. Okay then.

standard-dialogue.npc: The tithes are growing weak. That werewolf needs to do a better job of keeping them fed.
There's no shortage of corpses around here. The dead can still have some uses.

standard-dialogue.player: You're feeding them corpses? No wonder they're becoming weak. That meat must have all sorts of problems.

standard-dialogue.npc: What else would you have me feed them? If I give them nicer food, I'm wasting more money than if I were to just kill them and buy some more.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-is-not-d.npc: Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Hello there young one. Interested in getting your hands dirty?

steps.player: Err... maybe?

steps.npc: Ah don't worry, it's nothing sinister. We leave that kind of thing to clan Iorwerth. I speak in a more literal sense, of the ground beneath us and the trees over us.

steps.player: Oh, I see. So it's your clan that looks after the plants of the city?

steps.npc: Indeed. We maintain the farms and manage the trees. The produce we grow goes to the Meilyr clan to feed the city and the wood we provide is used by the Ithell clan in construction.
Feel free to join us. Our farming patches are open to you, as is our sawmill.

steps.player: Awesome, thank you.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I stole the Ring of Charos from Fenkenstrain.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Rologarth
after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: I saw him climb up into the Tower to hide it. It doesn't matter - soon the werewolves will come for him, and his experiments will be forever ceased.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: Do you want the ring back? It is yours after all.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Rologarth
after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: No, you keep it, my friend. Werewolves hunger for the scent of live flesh - I have no need for the ring. I have my castle back, if not my soul.

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: Well citizen, you are speaking to Lord Shiro Shayzien. I am the ruler of Shayzien and the commander-in-chief of the Shayzien Army.

steps.player: How long have you held this position?

steps.npc: Since my father passed away four years ago. He was a good man who took the defence of Kourend very seriously. I have been working hard to continue his legacy.
Anything else I can help you with citizen?

steps.player: Tell me about Shayzien.

steps.npc: Most citizens of Shayzien are part of the Shayzien Army in some form or other. We are responsible for defending Kourend against external and internal threats.

steps.player: What are the current threats against Kourend?

steps.npc: Externally, we have recently being dealing with increased lizardman activity. We've also been keeping a close eye on Varlamore to the south, just in case they try anything.
Internally, we have seen a rise in gang crime across the kingdom. It seems to be especially prevalent in Port Piscarilius.

steps.player: How do you tackle these issues?

steps.npc: By doing what we do best citizen. There's no threat that can't be defeated by a Shayzien soldier with a sword in their hand.

steps.player: Is that going well?

if-the-player-lost-the-memoir-page-befor.npc: Here citizen. Your reward for helping with the expedition.

standard-dialogue.npc: Good day friend.

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: I am Trobin Arceuus, lord of Arceuus. It's a position I've held for a thousand years, ever since the Ascent of Arceuus.

steps.player: That's a long time. I guess you've seen quite a bit.

steps.npc: Indeed. I've been present at some of the most notable moments in Kourend's history.
I was there when King Agata IV was deposed, I was there when Kharedst the Builder opened Kourend Castle and I was there when Emperor Imafore was executed.
I tend to keep out of public affairs these days though. My presence is often more of a distraction than a benefit. It also means I can focus on my work in peace.

steps.player: Your work?

steps.npc: The freeing of souls. There are many souls that find themselves trapped here after death. My people and I do our best to release them.

steps.player: Tell me about Arceuus.

steps.npc: If you find something magical in Kourend, chances are it came from Arceuus. Our people have lived for a thousand years. The knowledge we've gained in that time has resulted in many a magical discovery.
Most of our discoveries start with the Dark Altar. It is the source of our immortality and our people dedicate their lives to studying it.
Our people also serves an important role in the wider world. We work to free trapped souls so that they may pass on to the next world. It is a crucial task that the Dark Altar helps us to perform.

steps.player: Was the Dark Altar always here?

steps.npc: Impossible to say. The Dark Altar has been mentioned in records dating back to the earliest days of Kourend. Before then, who knows.

steps.player: You weren't around back then?

steps.npc: No. The Ascent of Arceuus didn't occur until after Xeric's Age of Strife, hundreds of years after Kourend was formed.

options.text: Tell me about the Ascent of Arceuus.

steps.player: Tell me about the Ascent of Arceuus.

steps.npc: It was a thousand years ago, during the time of King Byrne II. I went to my people and shared the secrets of immortality with them.
Not all of them accepted this gift of course, as was their right. Those that did, were granted new bodies to house their souls. These bodies are sustained by the Dark Altar.

steps.player: It wasn't you that discovered this secret though was it?

steps.npc: No. It was granted to us by the Tasakaal. They are ancient beings, ones that make us seem like mere children.
Their age and experience have granted them knowledge over life and death that we can only dream of.

steps.player: The Tasakaal don't like you very much. They called you a liar and claimed you misused the knowledge.

steps.npc: The events that led to the Ascent of Arceuus are more complicated than even the Tasakaal know. But that is a story for another day.

steps.player: Tell me about your plans.

steps.text: If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I had one of my people recover the remains of that device. The one that was absorbing the Dark Altars power.
We're performing tests to see if we can learn more about it. We haven't made any meaningful progress yet though.
Once we've learnt more about it, we'll be in a better position to determine our next move.
I admit, the idea of someone sabotaging the Altar is more than a bit concerning. I hope we can make some progress soon.

steps.text: If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: Now that we know Xamphur was responsible for the device that was absorbing power from the Dark Altar, we're hoping we can use it to help locate him.
Alas, so far we've had no luck. We're also scanning for energy that matches what we observed during that earthquake he caused, but again, nothing has been discovered so far.
It seems this work will take time. I assure you though, we will find him and his master.

steps.player: What about that Pyromancer?

steps.npc: We've begun an investigation into their order, but we have little to go on. Hopefully we find a good lead soon.

steps.player: Well just let me know if you need my help.

steps.npc: I will, thank you.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: Farewell.

steps.player: How do I brew ales?

steps.npc: Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.player: How do I brew cider?

steps.npc: First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush. Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.player: I'd like to know more about security.

steps.npc: First I must warn you to take every precaution to keep your RuneScape password and PIN secure. The most important thing to remember is to never give your password to, or share your account with, anyone.

I can also tell you about password security, avoiding item scamming and in-game moderation. I can also tell you about a place called the Stronghold of Security, where you can learn more about account security and
have a bit of an adventure at the same time.

options.text: I'd like to know about password security.

steps.player: I'd like to know about password security.

steps.npc: Well, the first thing to remember with password security, which I can't stress enough, is to never tell your password, bank PIN or authenticator details to anyone, not even if they claim to be Jagex staff. Real

Jagex staff will NEVER ask for your password. Sharing your account is a very bad idea, even if you think that you know and trust the person you are sharing with. Players have lost items and even their
account this way. Sharing accounts is also against the rules.

steps.player: Is there anything else to be aware of?

steps.npc: Yes, also be careful where you enter your password. Be aware that fake Old School RuneScape websites exist. These are sites that claim to give things such as item/stat upgrades, free items, beta testing and
moderator applications. Jagex do not offer any of these services.

Also be aware of trojans and keyloggers. These nasty programs can send everything you type into your device back to the computers of malicious people, so you can lose more than just your Old School RuneScape

password in this way. To avoid getting these on your device, be very wary of what you download, especially when it comes to downloading third party software. Also be very wary of email attachments and instant
messenger file transfers, which can contain such things.
Finally, remember the game doesn't censor your password or bank PIN when you type them; anyone who tells you otherwise is probably trying to steal your character or items.
Is there anything else you need help with?

steps.player: I'd like to know more about security.

steps.npc: First I must warn you to take every precaution to keep your RuneScape password and PIN secure. The most important thing to remember is to never give your password to, or share your account with, anyone.

I can also tell you about password security, avoiding item scamming and in-game moderation. I can also tell you about a place called the Stronghold of Security, where you can learn more about account security and
have a bit of an adventure at the same time.

options.text: I'd like to know about password security.
I'd like to know more about avoiding item scamming.
I'd like to know more about in-game moderation.

options.text: I'd like to know more about avoiding item scamming.

steps.player: I'd like to know more about avoiding item scamming.

steps.npc: There are many nice and helpful players in Old School RuneScape; unfortunately, as in real life, there are some who aren't so honest. Some people may try to trick you out of your items. Try not to fall for this as

Jagex policy is to never return lost items to players that have been scammed. Doing so just encourages users to claim they lost items they never had to gain an unfair advantage. However, people carrying out such
scams will get banned as it is against the rules.

When trading, you have a second trade confirmation screen. Always double check that you are getting the items you expect on this page as some people may try and change what they are trading at the last minute on
the first trade screen. Remember when you have clicked accept on the second trade screen, the trade is not reversible.

Try and find out from someone else what an item is before spending a lot of money on it. Not all merchants are honest about the rarity or the uses of their wares. For example, some people try to pass off spinach rolls as
rare when in fact they're as common as cabbages!

Be wary of people offering to improve your items. For example, some people will claim they can add a trim to your armour or upgrade your sword to a more powerful one. This is not possible and they are trying
to steal your hard-earned equipment.
Is there anything else you need help with?

options.text: I'd like to know about something else.

steps.player: I'd like to know about something else.

steps.npc: Well, what would you like to know?

steps.player: No thank you.

options.text: I'd like to know more about in-game moderation.

steps.player: I'd like to know more about in-game moderation.

steps.npc: You will, from time to time, see moderator characters in game. Remember: a real staff member will never ask for your password or any other personal information. There are two types of moderator. You may see Jagex

staff characters in game - these can be identified by a gold crown next to their name and are the people who work in the Jagex offices. They might be from Customer Support, or they might be a tester or a

programmer. You may also see player moderators - these can be identified by a silver crown next to their name. Player moderators are trusted players of Old School RuneScape that help keep in-game behaviour in
line with the Old School RuneScape rules.

steps.player: How do I become a player moderator?

steps.npc: The only way to become a player moderator is to know and play by the rules laid down by Jagex. Report those who break the rules, help players who need it and one day you might find an invite to become a moderator in
your Old School RuneScape inbox. Note that Jagex will never contact you in game or by email to become a player moderator.
Is there anything else you need help with?

steps.player: No thank you.
Yes please.

steps.npc: An exciting new discovery has been made in the Barbarian Village. Soon after they started mining in the middle of the village, one of the miners got caught in a cave.

steps.player: Sounds painful, did he fall on his head?

steps.npc: No, but it turned out that he had discovered a place unlike any other.

steps.player: How so?

steps.npc: Well an explorer went to look down there, it's full of new and exciting creatures and other surprises on top of that. It turns out this place can also help you to secure your account more effectively.

steps.player: Wow, that sounds good. Where can I find the explorer to learn more?

steps.npc: Sadly the explorer went missing and has not been found. However, here is some information to get you started on securing your account. You can find the Barbarian Village north of Falador and west of Varrock.

contacting-through-astral-contacts-rando.npc: What? No I haven't!

giving-him-the-tarnished-locket-first-ti.player: Does the name 'Philly' mean anything to you by chance?

giving-him-the-tarnished-locket-first-ti.text: You present the locket to the Lumbridge Guide.

giving-him-the-tarnished-locket-first-ti.npc: That locket! Where did you get it?

giving-him-the-tarnished-locket-first-ti.player: I found it in a magical rift. Does it belong to you?

giving-him-the-tarnished-locket-first-ti.npc: Not exactly... It's a long and sad story.

options.text: It's okay, I have time to listen.

steps.player: It's okay, I have time to listen.

steps.npc: Well, if you're sure then.
It all started in my youth when I was part of the Order of Wizards. I frequently spent time travelling across Gielinor, which kept me away from my beloved who worked here in Lumbridge.
Due to being apart, I would often send her gifts. This locket was one of them.

steps.player: I see... I'm not sure I like where this story is going. How come I found the locket in a magic rift then?

steps.npc: As I said, my research often kept me away from home. During one of my trips away, our house was robbed. My dear Thenia tried to stop them, but they took her life in return. The locket was taken in the robbery.

steps.player: Oh my... I'm so sorry for your loss.

steps.npc: I appreciate your kind words, but this was a long time ago. The pain of losing a loved one never fades, but in time you come to live with it.
Anyway, after that I stepped down from the Order of Wizards. I now spend my days offering guidance to those who come through Lumbridge.

steps.player: I'm still curious to know how it ended up in some rift. Do you have any theories?

steps.npc: Well... where was this rift?

steps.player: In an ancient temple. Most things in the rift came from the Abyss.

steps.npc: The Abyss? I wasn't aware anyone had ever been to the Abyss.

steps.player: They hadn't until recently, but the Z.M.I. found a way there.

steps.npc: The Z.M.I.? But could that mean...

steps.player: What?

steps.npc: Oh, nothing to worry about. Just me being a silly old man. Tell me more about this temple.

steps.player: It's called the Temple of the Eye. It was built by Saradominist wizards long ago to house a powerful artefact.

steps.npc: The Eye?

steps.player: You've heard of it?

steps.npc: Only stories, of which there are very few. Still, I always believed them to be real. After all, why else would an eye be the symbol of the Order of Wizards?
Ah, but that reminds me, I was not the first in my family to join the order. This amulet was passed down from generation to generation.

steps.text: Phileas shows you an amulet.

steps.player: That looks just like the amulet that led us to the temple!

steps.npc: As soon as you mentioned it, I wondered if there might be a connection.
The origin of this amulet was something I spent much time puzzling over when I was younger. I'm glad you have answered the question I couldn't.
I'd be happy to give you this amulet in return for that locket. I have no use for it, but that locket is something which holds a lot of sentimental value to me.

options.text: Of course you can have the locket.

steps.player: Of course you can have the locket.

steps.text: You exchange the locket for the amulet.

steps.npc: Thank you for returning this to me. I wish you the best of luck on the rest of your adventures.

steps.player: Thanks, Phileas. I wish you luck also.

options.text: I'd rather keep the locket for myself.

steps.npc: Oh, I see. I guess I can't really force you to hand it over. The offer still stands if you ever change your mind.

options.text: Never mind then. I have to go.

steps.player: Never mind then. I have to go.

giving-him-the-tarnished-locket-after-no.npc: You're back. Would you consider giving me that locket? It holds a lot of sentimental value to me. I'll give you that amulet in return.

options.text: Of course you can have the locket.
I'd rather keep the locket for myself.

contacting-through-astral-contacts-rando.npc: Baaaa.
Baaa?

on-ape-atoll.player: Can you take me back to Crash Island?

on-crash-island.player: Can you take me back to Ape Atoll?

steps.player: Hi!
Who are you?

steps.npc: I am...
...Lumiere.

steps.player: It's nice to meet you, Lumiere.

steps.npc: ...It is?

steps.player: Yeah?
Why are you here?

steps.npc: I... light the candles...

steps.player: Oh, I've always wondered who did that. It doesn't sound like much fun...

steps.npc: I... did not choose this fate...

steps.player: Punishment?

steps.npc: Yes... for my sins.

steps.player: Tough break.

steps.npc: It is not too bad... There has been plenty of blood... Although stocks are frighteningly low...

steps.player: Good thing the sanctuary was unsealed. Plenty of adventurer folk you could grab some blo-

steps.npc: You are... not imaginary?

steps.player: Oh... no... I'd better go.

steps.npc: Stay... we have so much to discuss.

steps.player: Bye!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Oh hi, I'm Luminata, I hunt mostly...rats...Speaking of which, this rat tastes awful - but it's the only food we have!

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Oh, hello. Luminata is the name and I help to keep the village clear of rat infestations. Clearly I love my work, as I bring it home with me... On a stick!

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.text: Don't talk to me outerlander! I don't have time for the likes of you!

getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.player: Hey! Don't call me outerlander! I'm known as the mighty [Fremennik name]!

getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.text: Can't say I've heard of you. So they let your sort into the clan nowadays? Wow. Things have really changed since I've been gone...

options.text: You don't look like a Fremennik yourself...

steps.player: You don't look like a Fremennik yourself...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Yes, I suppose that's true... I have been gone such a long time...

options.text: You've been away from these parts a while?

steps.player: You've been away from these parts a while?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Oh, you haven't heard of the infamous Lokar, scourge of the northern seas?

steps.player: Erm... no... That's you then, is it?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Forgotten already? Tch! I have no regrets about why I left!

steps.player: Why did you leave?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: As a young man, I learnt that the Fremennik way of life was too slow for me...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Oh, sure, every so often we got to go on big raiding parties, looting and pillaging the weaker islands around here for food and profit, but...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Well, after a while, that was all I looked forward to doing.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Growing crops, milking cows, catching and cooking food, the day to day activities of our life...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: THEY'RE SO BORING!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: No, I knew what I wanted to do, and that was attack innocent people going about their daily business, steal all their money, then spend it on wine, women and song!

steps.player: Oh.... Kaaaaay....

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: So I ran away from Rellekka to become a PIRATE! It's way more fun. Plus you get to see the world!

steps.player: Was the world good then? Only, you seem to have returned to Rellekka after all.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Yes, I have returned here, but that's only because we're short on supplies.

steps.player: I see. So where are you and your scurvy sea-dogs headed to next? Arrr shiver-me timbers!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: You're trying my patience...

steps.player: Sorry, got caught up in the moment.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Indeed. Well, the rest of the group are at Lunar Isle at the moment. It's where the Moon Clan live.

steps.player: The Moon Clan... I think I've heard of them...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: I'd be surprised if you hadn't, they're the Fremenniks' most hated enemy!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: They've been at war with them for hundreds of years!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Hmmm. Actually, that might be a problem for you then.

steps.player: A problem?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Yeah, they're a really powerful race of mages. They'd read your mind and see that you're a Fremennik straight away, then probably turn you inside out and feed you to the birds.

steps.player: Cosmic.
But you went there okay?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Yeah, but I think the Fremenniks are a bunch of losers. They probably picked up on that.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Look, I know a way you'll be able to travel there without, you know, getting killed and that, if you fancy a trip!

steps.prompt: Start the Lunar Diplomacy quest?

steps.player: Why not, I've always wondered what the state of my innards are!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: That's the spirit!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Well, what you want to do is go and talk to Brundt the Chieftain and get a Seal of Passage from him.

steps.player: A Seal of Passage? What's that?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Well, it shows that you're a diplomat for the Fremennik, so you'll have immunity from being killed and stuff.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: It's an ancient tradition not to attack anyone bearing a Seal of Passage, because they're probably on a diplomatic mission. Or well connected with powerful allies. Either way, killing them is usually a bad idea.

steps.player: So I have to try and bring peace to two warring nations who have been fighting for centuries?!?!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: What? I never said you had to bother trying to do that, you just have to pretend like you might.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: No skin off my nose if those losers want to get slaughtered by the Moon Clan, just more stuff for me to loot when they're all dead.

steps.player: Well I will try. I am the mighty [Fremennik name] after all!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Yes....

steps.player: So I just have to go talk to Brundt the Chieftain and tell him I want a Seal of Passage?
That's it? Because in my experience simple tasks like that always seem to take longer than I expect...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Yeah, just go over and talk to the chief loser. You might have to tell him some rubbish he wants to hear, but that's it.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Come back here when you got it, my supplies are loaded and I'm good to head back to our ship.

steps.player: Okay, I'll be right back.
No thanks, I'd like to live.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Oh, so you're a loser like the rest of the Fremenniks then? See ya around, loser.

steps.player: Well, 'bye then.
Well, 'bye then.

getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.text: Hey there [Fremennik name]. So you get that seal thingy off of the Brundt the Chieftain yet?

getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-talking-to-lokar-searunn.text: Well hurry it up, okay? I'm sick of this dump of a town, I want to go back to the ship!

options.text: Ask about a Seal of Passage.

steps.player: Hi there Brundt the Chieftain. Could you help me out with a Seal of Passage?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: A Seal of Passage? Whatever for?

steps.player: Well, I've heard that there have been great troubles between your people and that of the Moon Clan. I was hoping to help. And so I need the Seal of Passage to show my intentions.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Ah [Fremennik name], many have tried, but The Moon Clan are by no means a sharing group of people. They do everything by magic, something we never use. But they are so secretive about it. If only they would share, we

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: wouldn't have to kill them all the time!

steps.player: I will see what I can do.
Can I have that seal then?

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Yes, but you have no room to carry it. You should have thought of that before, [Fremennik name]!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: If you are to bring peace to our two warring clans, then perhaps it is best that you do...
a seal of passage

options.text: Ask about a Seal of Passage.

steps.player: Well... I would if I had space to carry one.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Oh dear...

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Then you had better take a replacement and be less careless in future.

options.text: Ask about a Seal of Passage.

steps.player: Hi there.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Yes?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Ah, [Fremennik name]. How goes the peace talks with the accursed Moon Clan?

steps.player: Oh, you know. Ongoing negotiations.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: I see. Well, I don't hold out for much hope!

steps.player: I'm glad you're confident in my abilities.

getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.text: So you got that seal yet from Brundt the Chieftain? Can I leave this dump of a town?

getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.player: Uh... yeah... Well, Brundt the Chieftain gave me a seal, but I think I lost it somewhere along the way...

getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.text: What are you? Useless? Go get another one from Brundt the Chieftain, and hurry it up, I don't want to be here any longer than I have to be!

getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.text: So you got that seal yet from Brundt the Chieftain? Can I leave this dump of a town?

getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.player: Yup, I've got it right here!

getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.speaker: Lokar Searunner
getting-started-returning-to-lokar-searu.text: Great! Then let's head back to my ship! You ready to go now?

options.text: Arrr! Yar! Let's be on our way, yar!

steps.player: Arrr! Yar! Let's be on our way, yar!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: ...Why are you talking like that?

steps.player: Um... isn't that how pirates talk?

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Only the very stupid ones...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: I suggest you DON'T talk like that to my crew. They will probably assume you are mocking them and kill you.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: So let's start again: Are you ready to go?

steps.player: Why yes! Tally-ho!

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: I suppose that will have to do.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Here we are at the Pirates' Cove! You'll find the captain already on board.

steps.player: Not just yet...

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: Well hurry it up okay? This place is a dump, and I'm a vicious blood-thirsty pirate, not your personal travel agent.
