pirates-cove-talking-to-lokar-searunner-.speaker: Lokar Searunner
pirates-cove-talking-to-lokar-searunner-.text: Sheesh, make your mind pal, I'm not a taxi service!

steps.player: Actually, I've changed my mind. Again. I don't want to go.

steps.speaker: Lokar Searunner
steps.text: You are possibly the most indecisive person I have ever met...

steps.player: Well, 'bye then.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Hey, how you doing? You a stowaway?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: (sigh) NO, I am NOT a stowaway...
And to be honest, I don't know why everybody seems to think I am...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Hey, I'm not here to judge you, if you're a stowaway you picked a good ship for it!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: There's lots of convenient hiding places around here - I should know, whenever I'm in trouble with the Captain I find myself a good barrel to hide in, until the fuss dies down.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: What exactly is it that a 'cabin boy' actually does on a pirate ship anyway?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Mostly make coffee. Occasionally I have to swab the decks, but pirates aren't exactly known for cleanliness, you know?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: Hello. See anything good through your telescope there?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Not really, just those creatures on the island. Don't worry, we sent some men out there to deal with them.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: The captain said we might have a barbecue out there later...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: You seem unhappy about that... Wouldn't a barbecue on the beach be fun?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: You obviously haven't met the cook yet...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: It is customary when stowing away on a vessel to not introduce yourself to the Captains First Mate, oh foolish one.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: That Lokar guy invited me aboard...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: I see. Well, don't distract me as I'm making preparations for departure.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Try not to distract any of the crew either, Zamorak knows it's hard enough to get them to do any work around here without strangers wandering round the ship asking them inane questions.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Hi.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Me? I'm the navigator. My job is to ensure the ship travels where it's supposed to go once it's moving by constantly checking our

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: bearings against our plotted course, using charts and a sextant.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: People often think that we just sail off when we feel like it, but its actually far more complicated than that!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Why, when you think of just how much sea there is out there, ANYTHING could happen if there wasn't a competent navigator on board ensuring that we reach our destination safely and in the shortest possible time!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: Okay. So... What are you doing?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: As I say, being a navigator is a real skill - you really have to think on your feet!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Yesiree, once we get sailing, it's all up to me to make sure we don't run into trouble or go off course!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Yep, as the rest of the crew basically stand around not doing much, I'll be the one in the cabin, comparing wind speeds, landmarks and charts with my sextant, making sure that we get to the destination on time, and on

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: course!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: You could almost say that I'm the linchpin of the entire operation! Why, if it wasn't for me, the rest of the guys might be sailing for, oooh, hours, and be slightly off course and

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: never even known it!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: They might even be a few hours late for their destination! Or a few miles down the road from it!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: And then where would they be?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: A few hours late or a few miles down the road?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Exactly!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: Great. So... What are you doing?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Oh, just relaxing while I wait for the ship to cast off.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Birds-Eye' Jack
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: When we're sailing I'll be very busy you know! I'm probably the single most important person on board when we're sailing!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Beefy' Burns
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: The galley ain't open fer food yet whipper-snapper, ye'll hafta come back later if'n ye be wanting food.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.player: Uh... something something open, something something food?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.speaker: 'Beefy' Burns
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-before-.text: Aye, ter be sure, yer yella-bellied land-lizard!

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: Hmmmm? I don't recognise you as one of my men, what are you doing aboard my ship?

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Parrot
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: Stowaway! Stowaway! *Squark*

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.player: Oh, Lokar offered me a journey. He said you could take me to the island of the Moon Clan.

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: Oh he DID, did he? (sigh) I sometimes regret ever allowing that vagabond to join the crew.

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: He has a very bad work ethic, and I have to say his attitude can be very confrontational.

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Parrot
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: Lokar's a loser! *Brakawk*!

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.player: So... You won't take me to Lunar Isle?

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: Well now, I didn't say that.

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: We are returning there again soon anyway, as our last visit was most profitable.

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: In fact as soon as our boys are finished loading stocks we should be ready to depart!

pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-captain-bentley-.text: Now, as captain of this ship I feel I must play host, even if you aren't exactly a welcome guest, so was there anything you wished to know?

options.text: Can you tell me something about the Moon Clan?

steps.player: So... What can you tell me about this 'Moon Clan'? It all seems very mysterious I must say...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: The Moon Clan? Oh, very fine people. Very hospitable.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: We had heard that they are very wary of strangers, and dislike people just showing up on their island, but when we sent a landing party aboard they all seemed more than happy to see us.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, they even threw a big festival in our honour!

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Anyway, they had a large supply of items that we felt we could use on the high seas, so we made a few trades with them, and were on our way.

steps.player: What kinds of items?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, I'm not sure how much you've heard about them, but they are magical experts.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: They sold us many rune-stones, as well as a few good luck charms and talismans and such to help us on our voyage.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Yes, they might have been a little secretive about that strange temple, and the old lodge of theirs in town, and I must say they certainly have the strangest house I have ever seen in my life in their little village, but it was

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: a pleasant trip all round, and I look forward to trading there again in the future.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: After all, it's not everywhere that a pirate captain and his crew can rest ashore without having to worry about the authorities catching them, is it?

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Fight the law! *Squawk*

steps.player: No, I guess it isn't.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Was there anything else you wished to ask me about while I'm not busy?

options.text: What were you doing at Lunar Isle?

steps.player: What were you doing at Lunar Isle anyway? I always thought pirates would be... You know. Out pirating.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, obviously the actual pirating is a big part of our agenda, but we like to think of ourselves as non- regulated merchants.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: What good is plunder if you have nothing to spend it on, hmmmm?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Likewise, I am a forward thinking captain, and endeavour to invest much of my plunder back into the ship and its crew, so that we can be a better and more efficient force for theft upon the seas.

steps.player: So you went to Lunar Isle for supplies?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, obviously not initially. Obviously, our first thought was to show up, rob them blind, then take off again with the plunder spilling from our decks.

steps.player: So what made you change your mind?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, firstly there were the monsters.

steps.player: M-monsters?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Oh yes, hundreds of the things. The island's swarming with them you know.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Dirty smelly beasts, as big as a wolf! Yes, you'd certainly better be either handy with a blade or quick on your toes if you wanted to spend much time outside of their village with those things around

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: everywhere.

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Squawk* Run fer yer lives lads, it's a monster! *Squawk*

steps.player: So you didn't attack the Moon Clan because you were worried you would yourself be attacked by these monsters trying to make your escape?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Oh yes, absolutely. That and the next reason.

steps.player: The next reason?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Yes, the next reason being that the Moon Clan are quite stupendously powerful magicians.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: You'll notice it as soon as you look at them, really quite, quite powerful indeed.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: As soon as we saw them we lost any thoughts about trying to attack or steal from them.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Which as it turned out was lucky for us.

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Bunch of blooming loonies! *Brakawk*

steps.player: It was?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Oh yes. They can read minds, you see. If we'd shown up there thinking about robbing them they would have just killed us all on the spot.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I did mention that they are extraordinarily powerful magicians, didn't I?

steps.player: Yes, yes you did.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Ah, I'm glad I did. Because they really, really are. And mind-readers.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Yes, all in all I'm glad we didn't try any funny business in the end after all.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Plus there's that other good reason.

steps.player: That reason being?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, when you are a crew of successful pirates, it becomes more and more difficult to ever moor somewhere and spend your loot.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: People are far too quick to call the guards on a troublemaker nowadays.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: So finding a village where people are more than happy to trade with you regardless of who you may have just stolen from and killed.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I like that non-judgemental attitude of theirs!

steps.player: Okay then...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Anything else you wanted to know before we set sail?

options.text: Can you tell me something about your ship?

steps.player: I was hoping you could tell me a little bit about your ship. I must say, it's really very impressive.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Ah, a connoisseur! Yes, she's named the Lady Zay, and may I say, is one of the finest ships to ever sail the seas!

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: It was a steal from the Karamjan shipyards.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: And when I say it was a steal, I mean to say that myself and some of the lads broke in and stole it one night.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I don't know who they were building these warships for, but whoever it was seemed to be a little on the short side.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: We had to do a little remodelling of the doors and rooms so that we didn't have to crouch around everywhere, but I've finally got her just how I want her, and we have enough cannons down below decks to

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: bombard a small town I'd wager!

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Brawwwwwwk* I want guns, lots of guns! I want guns, lots of guns!

steps.player: I used to own my own ship you know...
It was called the Lady Lumbridge if I remember correctly...
I wonder whatever happened to it...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Interesting. You never struck me as being Captain material, but I guess there's a ship out there for everyone...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: The Lady Zay is certainly a big step up from my last ship anyway.

steps.player: Your last ship? Why, what was wrong with it?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, it just wasn't sturdy enough!

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I was on a perfectly routine raiding expedition to the east of here, when we ran into a squall, that pushed us towards the rocky shore.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: A few select men and myself managed to escape with our lives intact on a small row boat, but the rest of my crew were washed ashore as the ship was wrecked on those jagged rocks.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Ah yes, it was a tragedy...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: To lose such a fine ship in such an insulting manner...

steps.player: And of course the rest of your crew...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Who? Oh. Yes. The crew. Yes, it was a tragedy.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I'd paid them in advance you know, I'll never see that money again!

steps.player: Um... no, I actually meant it was a shame that so many of your crew must have died in the shipwreck.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Was it? Well, if you say so.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Actually, the last I had heard quite a few of them had survived, and had set up a little hideaway next to the remains of the shipwreck.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: If you're particularly worried about them, perhaps you might like to go and pay them a visit someday, and make sure to bring a lot of easily transferable wealth with you.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: They love people visiting with easily transferable wealth.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Now, was there something you wished to talk to me about? Time is pressing on, and we really need to set sail soon if we want to make the most of the winds.

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Squawk* Move it or lose it, move it or lose it.

options.text: Can we sail to Lunar Isle now?

steps.text: If the player does not have the seal of passage:

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well, I would be more than happy to take you, unfortunately the Moon Clan are, frankly, very scary people, and I believe they would not take kindly to us bringing a Fremennik there.{{^|No line from the player in this case.}}

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: They are at war with them after all.

steps.player: But I thought Lokar had already been there?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Yes. Yes he has. I'm talking about you.

steps.player: Oh. Oh yeah, I'm a Fremennik aren't I?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Yes, yes you are.

steps.player: I probably should have kept that Seal Of Passage Brundt the Chieftain gave me with me, shouldn't I?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Yes, yes you should have. Honestly, you're going to need it with you.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I'm afraid I can't let you travel with us without it.

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Brakawk* Don't drop quest items half way through a quest! *Squawk*

steps.player: Okay, I'll go and get it again then.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: You do that.
If the player has the seal of passage:

steps.player: Can we sail to Lunar Isle now? I must say, it all sounds very intriguing over there...

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: As long as you keep your Seal Of Passage with you at all times while you are on the island you should be okay, even if you are a Fremennik.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: I'm not kidding, they are a very dangerous people, and it would NOT be wise for you to travel there without your Seal Of Passage marking you as a diplomat.

steps.player: Okay, keep my Seal with me at all times, check. Can we go now?

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Ah, yes indeed! The winds seem good, so let's make a move!

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: She's blowing a storm, cap'n! *Brarrrrrk*
Cutscene of boat circling island on map plays.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Well... THAT was deuced strange!

steps.player: Um... Way to sail a boat?

steps.speaker: Parrot
steps.text: Squawk* Way to sail a boat! Way to sail a boat! *Brarrrk*

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: This... This is VERY strange!

steps.player: No, actually, I don't really want to know anything that you can tell me.
In fact, I don't even know why I began talking to you in the first place!

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Hmmmm. You could perhaps be more grateful to someone offering you free transport, but then I suppose you are a friend of Lokar's, and a Fremennik, so I suppose the

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: rudeness is natural.

steps.speaker: Captain Bentley
steps.text: Make sure you are ready for departure, I will be issuing orders to set sail shortly.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: What happened to the ship?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Lecherous' Lee
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: I have no idea! It doesn't normally do that!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Weird.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Lecherous' Lee
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Yup.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: So the Captain's a very bad sailor I take it?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: No... Usually he's one of the best around, I don't know why we didn't reach our destination like we were supposed to, and it CERTAINLY wasn't anything to do with me

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: or anything I have done!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Alright, calm down I wasn't accusing you of anything!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Good, because it has NOTHING to do with me!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Cabin boy
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: IT'S NOT MY FAULT!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: I think you should lay off the coffee for a bit, youngster...
Do you know what's wrong with the ship? I've never seen a ship sail in a big circle like that before...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Sticky' Sanders
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: I can't say for sure, but it must be either the Captain or the Navigator to blame.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Sticky' Sanders
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: They're the only ones who control the actual sailing of the ship.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: I see... Thank you, that's very helpful.
So you reckon it's the navigator or the Captain's fault?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Sticky' Sanders
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Yeah, stands to reason, dunnit?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Did you just see that?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: See what?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: The ship sailing. Or not sailing. Or sailing in a big circle and coming back here.
I don't know, I'm not a sailor! But whatever it was, it was very odd!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Can't say that I did, no. Sorry, I was keeping an eye out.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: An eye out? For what?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Um... Sorry, I can't really say, but I'll know it when I see it!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Okay then...
Was the ship supposed to go in a big loop like that?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Jack Sails
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Pretty sure it wasn't, no...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Any idea what caused it?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Jack Sails
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Absolutely none at all...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Pretty crazy sailing you guys got here!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Murky Pat
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Weird, the ships never done that before...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Jenny Blade

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-about-t.text: I remember Beefy the cook was being a bit of a killjoy and had stayed on board the ship, and the Captain was having some fancy meal with the Moon Clan toffs, but I'm pretty sure the rest of us were all at the meal...

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-about-t.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-about-t.text: Anyway, spirits got a little high later on after we'd finished eating, and I remember Tommy Two-times got out his old fiddle, and we sang and danced all through the night until daybreak when we made our way back

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-about-t.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-about-t.player: When you say there were high spirits... You don't think perhaps you accidentally offended the Moon Clan somehow do you?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-about-t.speaker: 'Eagle-eye' Shultz

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Oh, what on Gielinor are you on about now?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: I know your SECRET Mr first mate! I know that you are a PHONY!
I know that you were NOT where you claimed to be on the night in question!

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Night in question? Phony? Secret?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: What ARE you blathering about now?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: Oh, come come, Davey-boy! It is too late to weasel your way out of this one!

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: I have absolutely no idea what on earth you are talking about.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: Oh, you know... your ALIBI?!?!

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Alibi?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: YOU know. How you told me that you were at that feast on Lunar Isle ALL night?
Well, let me tell YOU that you are a LIAR!
I have an eyewitness that SAW you leave the feast, and go off and do who-knows-what for a good TWENTY MINUTES!
I think it is time to come clean, Davey-boy. I think we should hear the truth.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: What? Well of COURSE I was at that feast all ni...

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: ...Hmmm. You know, now that you come to mention it, you are correct, I did leave the feast.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: AH-HA! I KNEW IT!

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Oh, do calm down, it was nothing particularly interesting.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: I merely had to inspect the rigging was secure before the ship was docked securely for the night.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: It's one of those things you have to do, in case a storm blows up while we're asleep and yanks the ship off to sea unattended.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: So why didn't you tell me this before?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Well, clearly it slipped my mind.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: It's not one of my usual responsibilities, so obviously I didn't think much of it.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: Wait, what do you mean it's not one of your usual responsibilities?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: It's the cabin boys' job to ensure that the rigging and the sails have been safely secured before disembarking the ship.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Pirates Regulations #445-328.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: So why didn't he?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: I have no idea. I couldn't find him at the feast, so I left to secure them myself.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: Wait, so he wasn't even at the feast?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: Not that I could see, no. And I do recall I spent some good time looking for him.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: So the cabin boy wasn't at the feast at all? WHY DIDN'T YOU TELL ME EARLIER?!?!

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: I suppose it slipped my mind. Surely it can't be of any importance, a runt like that?

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: It's only the single most important thing you've said to me since I've met you!

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'
pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.text: If you say so.

pirates-cove-talking-to-first-mate-davey.player: Well, I guess this explains why the Cabin Boy's been acting so suspiciously... I'd better go and have a word with him!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: No, I meant, 'Captain? Can I have a word with you?'

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: You just did didn't you?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: (sigh) Let's start again...
Captain, I need to speak to you.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Speak away. How goes the search for the jinx?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Well, I think I may have found who was responsible for upsetting the Moon Clan.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: Hmmm? Who would that be then?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Well, I'm pretty sure it was the Cabin Boy.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Well he seems to be the only member of the crew who was absent without a good reason to be so.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: I see. And have you spoken to him about this?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: It is very possible he has a valid reason to have not been present.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: As I understand it Pirate Regulation number 445-328 required him to have been checking the sails.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Yes, but the First Mate was doing that instead of him.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley
pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.text: That's very strange. So what does he have to say for himself... Have you asked him?

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Erm... Not yet, no.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Captain Bentley

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: I'm pretty sure now that it was the Cabin Boy that has caused all this.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Well if I did accuse everyone, eventually I would be right.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Bird's-Eye' Jack

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: I feel a bit sick.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Murky Pat

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Murky Pat

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: I can't say anything right with you Pirates.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: Jenny Blade

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: First mate 'Davey-boy'

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Oh HA HA. Thanks for the help!

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Bird's-Eye' Jack

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: I was being sarcastic.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Bird's-Eye' Jack

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.player: Wow! I pity your wife.

pirates-cove-talking-to-the-crew-after-s.speaker: 'Beefy' Burns

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Hello.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Why hello, how are you today?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Fine. Yes I know.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: What? How'd you...

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: By reading your mind. But that's not important. We have some important things to discuss.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: We do? This is going to take some time getting used to.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Of course! I can see that you come bearing great promise.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Great promise?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Please. Just tell me why you have come to our island.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Well, I'm seeking some kind of settlement between your clan and the Fremenniks. I understand there has been a dispute for a great many years and being a member of the Fremennik clan I wanted to come as a
representative to see if something couldn't be sorted out.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: A very honourable objective, but how do you suppose this will be possible?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: That's what I was hoping you may be able to help me out with.
Can you tell me more of why you don't feel your people get on with the Fremenniks?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: We are very in tune with magic as you have no doubt observed, but we have yet to meet one Fremennik with the perspective that this is of any value. They are always picking at us to reveal our secrets, but why

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: should we when they view us so.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: I think you'd be surprised at how flexible they could be. I think they just feel like you put yourselves on a higher pedestal to look down at them. They don't like that and can't see what is so special about you and
your ways.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Hmmm. Well you are one of them. Perhaps if you can understand our ways, that will at least be a start. How does that sound to you?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Fine. I am always eager to learn.
What sort of thing had you in mind?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Well, we have a ritual called 'The View of Self Dream'. It is a ritual that we all have to go through. You see the path to understanding magic is through understanding ourselves. It is a power innate to every

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: living creature, but it takes a great understanding of self to tap into. One of the best ways to understand ourselves is through our dreams. These are a demonstration of our subconscious, our subconscious

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: being raw and true. But it takes many years to get into a situation where you are ready to attempt it.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: I'm not so sure I want to wait years to solve this... Is there any way I can just attempt this ritual now?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: I don't mind you trying, but I really doubt you'll achieve anything. There are also a fair few preparations you'll have to make first too.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: That's OK. What do I have to do?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: You are going to need to do a few things. You'll need a waking sleep potion, a Lunar staff, and ceremonial traveling clothes. Start with the potion, I suggest you have a word with Baba Yaga in her chicken house,

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: she will be able to help you with the making of the potion.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Chicken house?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Yes, you can't miss it, it's walking around the north of the town.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Hi, what was I supposed to be doing again?

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.text: Seek Baba Yaga, she is in her chicken house to the north of our island. She should be able to help you out with the potion of waking sleep.

obtaining-the-waking-sleep-potion-talkin.player: Thanks.
Hi.

options.text: Have you got anything to trade?

obtaining-the-lunar-staff-talking-to-the.text: Have you got the potion to give me?

obtaining-the-lunar-staff-talking-to-the.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-lunar-staff-talking-to-the.text: Well done, I'll take that for safe keeping.

obtaining-the-lunar-staff-talking-to-the.speaker: Oneiromancer
obtaining-the-lunar-staff-talking-to-the.text: Next we will sort you out with the staff before the clothes. You are going to have to get hold of a Dramen staff first. You will need to take it to the air, fire, water and earth altars to imbue it with power to convert it

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.player: I'm on the lookout for ceremonial clothing so I can visit my dreams. I don't suppose you could help me out?

steps.player: Pauline

steps.player: Oh no. Can't you give me some kind of clue?

steps.text: Let's see...

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.speaker: Pauline Polaris
obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.text: Ah, a stranger to our island. What brings you here?

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.player: Well, I've actually come here on a diplomatic mission. I want to try and settle some of the disputes between the Fremenniks and your clan.

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.speaker: Pauline Polaris
obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.text: The Fremenniks? Pah! They are just too ignorant and stubborn to listen to anything we have to say - how can we possibly associate with a race that won't listen?

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.player: I think they are very eager to listen, but they feel like you are keeping secrets from them.

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.speaker: Pauline Polaris
obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.text: Secrets?

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.player: Yes, as in your magic ways. To be honest, I think it is fear of the unknown.

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.speaker: Pauline Polaris
obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.text: Well, when the day comes that a Fremennik can prove they have the patience and interest in learning our ways, then we will perhaps share our secrets.

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.player: I'm hoping I might be able to achieve that.

obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.speaker: Pauline Polaris
obtaining-the-lunar-clothing-talking-to-.text: Good luck. It's far from simple.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: Ok. Like what?

steps.player: How about the values of the Moon clan!

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: Let me see...  We value knowledge of self because it is this that gives us our strength! It is most important!

steps.player: Well... I know things about myself. I know I like hot chocolate!

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: I was meaning something a little deeper than that.  We also like to see someone listen. You know how they say a wise man listens?

steps.text: Did you hear me?

steps.player: .... I'm listening.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: Most wise.

steps.player: Huh?
I'm looking for a ring.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: Well there are a great many rings darling, try to be more specific.

steps.player: It's to go with the ceremonial clothes I need for visiting the dream land.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: Ah, I see. I'm afraid to say I don't have one of those. But... I do know that my grandfather had such a ring, but he passed away a long time ago.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: There is a chance he buried it though.

steps.player: Buried it? Why would he do a thing like that?

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: He was an archaeologist. Well, more of a treasure hunter. When I was little he always used to bury items around the island and give me clues and maps to find them. If you're lucky you

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: might find one of those rings.

steps.player: It's worth a shot.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: I remember those days fondly, hours of digging around, dodging boulders, pits of snakes...

steps.player: About that ring...

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: Ah, yes.

steps.speaker: Selene
steps.text: The clue I have written down here says: From water's source you should follow, crossing the western-most bridge and travelling further south- westerly to a bloom of blue.

steps.player: Thanks... I hope.

steps.player: You know the ceremonial clothes?

steps.speaker: Rimae Sirsalis
steps.text: I certainly do! A real tricky set of garments to make.

steps.player: Well that's unfortunate, because I was going to ask you how I might go about getting some.

steps.speaker: Rimae Sirsalis
steps.text: All I can really help you out with is the tanning of the hides.

steps.player: Sorry?

steps.speaker: Rimae Sirsalis
steps.text: The ceremonial clothes are made from the hides of the Suqah monsters. Bring them to me and I will tan them for you. You can then craft them into the top, trousers, gloves and boots.

steps.player: Ok.

steps.speaker: Rimae Sirsalis
steps.text: It's an interesting creature the Suqah. You see, they have been indigenous to this island since we arrived. They seem to thrive of eating the minerals that exist in the mines below the town. We try our best to live in

steps.speaker: Rimae Sirsalis
steps.text: harmony with them, because they provide us with a great many materials when they die, and in turn we have given them magic to help protect themselves.

steps.player: Interesting.

options.text: It's a very interesting island you have here.

steps.player: How can I sell food?

steps.npc: Most of the people wandering around the market want to buy food. Since the passage to the surface opened up there's been a craze in exotic food from up there.
To sell something, simply use a piece of food on one of the gourmets in the market, then name your price, and the gourmet will tell you how many they are interested in buying for that price.
If you want a rough idea of how much something will sell for, show it to me and I'll try to estimate.
But you should also take into account the gourmet's reactions when naming your price. If someone likes the look of a food, they will pay more for it.
Also remember that the novelty of new foods quickly wears off. If people have been eating a lot of something lately, then they won't pay as much for it.
If someone especially likes your food then you might even start a craze for it! If there's a food that's in fashion like that, then the gourmets will pay more for it.
If you want to sell food in the market, you'll need to renew your permission from the council first. The councillor in charge of giving permission at the moment is [councillor].

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Oh, my name's Luscion. I just help out around here, you know, gathering food and so on.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Well, friend, I'm Arls Lutwidge of the Moonlight Broadsword! Renowned all over Gielinor!

steps.npc: Very good, young one! Very good indeed!

steps.player: So... where's this famous sword of yours?

steps.npc: Gone. I gave it to a fledgling when I retired and the damned fool went and died fighting some great monster in a far off land.

options.text: What grand feats are you known for?

steps.player: What grand feats are you known for?

steps.npc: I peaked rather early and most know me for my first act of heroism when I defeated the Moonfly. It may sound cute, but it killed many of the smallfolk and their livestock, for it was a vile creature.

steps.player: Where'd it come from?

steps.npc: It was I that discovered the creature. I pulled it from the Lum during a fishing trip of mine.
As young and foolish as I was, I dropped it down a dried up well and went for help. However, upon my return, the creature was gone.

steps.player: And then what happened?

steps.npc: Many years passed until suddenly there were sightings of a winged demon around the River Lum. Some claimed it was an overly large heron and that it was nothing to be worried about.
As time went on, folk started to go missing and I knew I had to return home and face this demon.

steps.player: You left?

steps.npc: I had wars to fight, glory to be won and all that rubbish. Upon my return I spoke to an old crone who lived in the swamps and she gave me some advice.
She told me to spike my armour and described how to lure the creature toward me.

steps.player: And you defeated it? The Moonfly?

steps.npc: Some bard wrote a poem of the events. The telling of the battle is a little embellished and rife with errors. The poem can be found in this library somewhere, providing it has been returned.
And did I defeat the creature? I wouldn't be here if I hadn't!

steps.player: I'll be sure to keep an eye out.

steps.npc: Please do! And come to me if you have any burning questions about it.

steps.player: Sure thing.
Why are you here?

steps.npc: I've grown old, friend. Heroes need to know when to throw in the towel, so they say. I've always enjoyed a good book, so it seemed fitting to stay here as librarian for the guild.

steps.player: Hmm... the books are very interesting. I thought there would be more though...

steps.npc: Well, that's why I'm here! So many of you adventurers help yourself to any old book and never return the damn things!
If I could have it my way, you wouldn't be allowed to wander off with them, but I'm not the guildmaster, as Alec likes to remind me.

steps.player: Certainly sounds like you have a problem.

steps.npc: Well fear not. I'm working on it!

steps.player: Bye!

steps.npc: I'll see you around.

steps.npc: Hey there! Do you have a grapple I can borrow?

steps.player: I might have one, but I need it myself. Why do you need a grapple?

steps.npc: I need it to grapple to that pillar over there and get some treasure of course. What else could I need it for?

steps.player: I mean that makes sense I suppose. How did you end up here?

steps.npc: Well, I made my way to Morytania in search of a place called the Ba... Barlows? I've heard it's a great way to earn gold.

steps.player: Barrows.

steps.npc: Yeah, that's what I said!
Anyways, I got lost on the way here and was abducted by some vampyres! However, I'm so sneaky I managed to escape and find this place.
The weird hooded guy at the top said that if I get him some hollow marks, he'll help me escape.

steps.player: You mean Hallowed marks.

steps.npc: Yeah, that's what I said. Don't you listen?

steps.player: sigh*

steps.npc: So, can I borrow a grapple?

steps.text: If the player does not have a grapple:

steps.player: No, I don't have a grapple on me.

steps.npc: Well, you're clearly a noob then.

steps.text: If the player has a mithril grapple:

steps.player: Yes, I do have a spare grapple. I'm not sure you'd be able to use it to get across that gap though, what is your Ranged level?

steps.npc: Pfft, I'm level 50 Ranged. Over half-way to 99, getting over there will be a breeze.

steps.player: You need 62 Ranged to make it across that gap.

steps.npc: Maybe you do with that attitude.

steps.text: If the player has a hallowed grapple:

steps.player: Yes, I do have a spare grapple, although I spent a lot of Hallowed marks to obtain it so you can't have it.

steps.npc: Keep your grapple then noob. I can make that jump without it anyway.

steps.player: Oh yeah? What's your agility level?

steps.npc: None of your business.

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-wa.npc: You be on your way, then.

standard-dialogue.npc: Ah, greetings. What can I do for you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm Madam Sikaro.

steps.player: ...Is that it?

steps.npc: Why shouldn't it be? You asked who I was, and I answered.

steps.player: I was hoping to learn something about you, like what you were doing here...!

steps.npc: Well, perhaps next time you'll ask a more direct question.

steps.player: What are you doing here?

steps.npc: Making a wizard hideout.

steps.player: A wizard... hideout?

steps.npc: A wizard hideout! You know how some wizards have their own towers? Think that but underground.

steps.player: So why not just get a tower?

steps.npc: Land price. Kingdoms want you to pay an extortionate amount of money to build on 'their' land, it turns out.

steps.player: So instead you ended up in the basement of a tavern.

steps.npc: Yep. Camarst said I could have it as long as I don't hurt any of his customers too badly.
Not that I actually plan to hurt any of his customers.

options.text: I have this part that looks like it's from a weapon...
options.condition: If the player has a part of the Voidwaker:

steps.text: If the player has less than three parts of the Voidwaker:

steps.player: I have this part that looks like it's from a weapon...

steps.npc: Ah yes, that does look like a part of a particularly powerful weapon.

steps.player: Can I do anything with it?

steps.npc: You? Perhaps not, though if you could bring me all three pieces, I suspect I could put it back together for you.
There should be a hilt, a blade and a conduit gemstone. Oh, and I'll want 500,000 coins as payment as well. Good hunting!

steps.player: Do you know where I could find the other parts?

steps.npc: I suspect the Wilderness would be a good place to start. There are monsters out there that have grown immense over time.
Seeking out the strongest of them is where I'd start, anyway.

steps.text: If the player has all three parts of the Voidwaker:

steps.player: I have these parts of a weapon, do you think you could assemble it for me?

steps.npc: Hmm... yes, these are the parts of a particularly powerful weapon indeed. I can reassemble it... for a fee, of course. 500,000 coins, no less.

steps.text: If the player has less than 500,000 coins:

steps.player: I don't have that much on me...

steps.npc: Well, if you come across some more, come find me again.

steps.text: If the player has at least 500,000 coins:

steps.prompt: Have Madam Sikaro assemble the Voidwaker for 500,000 coins?

steps.text: Madam Sikaro takes the components off you and, in a flash of white light, fuses them together to form the Voidwaker.

steps.player: Actually, I've changed my mind.

steps.npc: Curious, you come to me with all of the parts and the coin, yet you change your mind at the last second.
I do rather get the feeling you're toying with me. Very well, I shall do my part in playing with you.

steps.text: You feel the contents of your inventory shift slightly.

steps.npc: Now, do talk to me again if you'd like to proceed more sensibly.

options.text: What are you doing with the money?
options.condition: If the player has had Madam Sikaro assemble the Voidwaker:

steps.player: What are you doing with the money from combining the Voidwaker?

steps.npc: I'll spend some of it improving the hideout. The rest on general expenses.

steps.player: What kind of expenses?

steps.npc: Living isn't free, you know? A woman my age has expenses. Food, clothing, protection... It all adds up.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: You walked up to me just to say goodbye? Ok, sure, goodbye.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: So what exactly is this sword, anyway?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Well, that largely depends on who you ask and when you ask it. The sword is not unique, but many like it have been referenced in folktales.
Some tell of great and prideful warriors roaming the lands, cutting down all who oppose them in great crashes of lightning.
Others tell of lovers, one bound by oath, the other free as the wind, cruely torn apart by fate.
Others still tell of three great beasts that alone were powerful, but combined could destroy Gielinor.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: Are we still talking about the sword?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Amazingly, yes. In all of these tales, the sword is there, potential shining through the metal, thunder rolling in its wake.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: Are any of these tales... true?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Oh, I'm sure there are elements of the truth buried in there, but folklore being what it is, I'm inclined to not believe any of it.
Aside from the bit where it can summon lightning. It can absolutely do that.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: What about the name? You called it Voidwaker?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Well, in a lot of these tales, it's only ever reffered to as someone's sword. Like, [player name]'s sword.
So, I chose a name for it.
There are multiple reasons. I suppose you could say the sword is so powerful that it leaves a void in its wake.

standard-dialogue-using-any-other-item-o.npc: No thank you, I'm currently on a diet.

standard-dialogue.npc: Good morrow, adventurer.

steps.player: I guess so.

steps.npc: You guess? The sun is shining, the sea breeze is salty, what's not to enjoy?

steps.player: I don't know... The sand? It's coarse and rough and irritating, and it gets everywhere.

steps.npc: Hmm, well my spa isn't quite ready yet, but when it is, I'm sure that'll solve all of your sand related issues!

steps.player: Okay.
Who are you?

steps.npc: I am Madame Caldarium! A pirate's life was for me, but lately I've been looking to expand my business, I'm getting old, ya see.

steps.player: A spa business? Do you really think these Corsairs are the washing type?

steps.npc: Ha! That's what the Rum is for!
I'm more concerned of their laziness, 'Can't work today Madame, I'm cursed!'. Bunch of idiots, the lot of 'em.

steps.player: Surely you never expected this lot to be any different... They're either stealing, killing or both!

steps.npc: Yes... I have plans adventurer, the local cave dwelling population are... Let's say, sorting something out.

steps.player: Interesting, I'm sure that'll be an entertaining turn of events.

steps.npc: We'll see...

steps.player: Goodbye!

steps.npc: Farewell, adventurer.

treasure-trails-medium.npc: I have a question for you.

treasure-trails-medium-when-talked-to-ag.npc: Please enter the answer to the question.

steps.npc: No, try again.
Correct!

steps.text: You have obtained [another clue/a casket]!

steps.npc: Is he still out there?

steps.player: Who?

steps.npc: That angry captain. His boat got damaged and he blames my husband for not providing a weather report. The thing is, my husband's missing!

steps.player: I'm sorry to hear that. Maybe I could help try and find him?

steps.npc: Thank you for the offer, but there's already plenty of people looking for him. I'm sure they'll find him soon. I'm sure he'll be fine.

steps.player: I'm sure he will be as well, and if they need more help, I'm always happy to get involved.

steps.npc: Thank you.

steps.player: Hi.

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?

steps.player: I'm great, thank you!

steps.npc: Isn't it wonderful? So many books, so much knowledge to be absorbed!

steps.player: You're right, it is.

steps.npc: Where did I see that book? It can't be far...

steps.player: Uh... Hello?

steps.npc: I'm sure it was around here somewhere...

steps.player: Okay... Maybe later...

steps.npc: What can I do for ya?

options.text: Got any good books to recommend?

steps.player: Got any good books to recommend?

steps.npc: I've always found Prifddinas' History to be fascinating!
I've always found The Journal of Randas to be fascinating!
I've always found Big Book of Bangs to be fascinating!
I've always found The Great Divide to be fascinating!
I've always found Ode to Eternity to be fascinating!

steps.player: Thanks!
Nothing.
Hi.

steps.npc: You know, there are so many different ways to greet people. Hello, 'ello, hello there...

steps.player: That still only counts as one!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?

steps.player: I'm great, thank you!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?

steps.player: Indeed.
Hi.

steps.npc: What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

steps.player: Nothing.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

steps.npc: Welcome to Elder Raley's Herblore Stall. Would you like to buy some herblore supplies?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.text: Elder Raley's Herblore Stall opens.

steps.player: So this isn't your stall?

steps.npc: No. Elder Raley's teaching me to become a herbalist myself, but he's always quite busy, so I normally look after the stall for him.

steps.player: I see. Fair enough.

steps.npc: So, would you like to buy some herblore supplies?

steps.player: No thanks.

steps.npc: Okay, well, you know where to find me if you change your mind.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello friend. I wish to slay evil and avail them of their loot! Take me to Burgh de Rott!

options.text: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.player: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.npc: I think so? At least my heart knows courage and that should be sufficient for the meantime. I expect that when we get to Burgh de Rott, we'll be able to purchase suitable provisions.

steps.player: But you do realise that the vampyres in Morytania are immune to everything except silver?

steps.npc: Er...well, I've not heard mention of that fact, but I have faith that Saradomin will provide the means to furnish me with suitable weapons when I reach Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: And if we happen to run into some vampyres on the journey down there?

steps.npc: I trust that you will help us to avoid them. You are a guide after all, aren't you? Anyway, you look like you can handle yourself. I presume you've fought such creatures before and won? How hard can it be?

steps.player: It can be pretty difficult, actually. But you're right, I'll be your guide so I should be able to handle the situation.

options.text: Why do you want to go to Burgh de Rott?

steps.player: Why do you want to go to Burgh de Rott?

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I'm going down there to teach those vampyres a lesson or two. I've heard about the terrible conditions down there and I intend to put a stop to it.

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I want to have a go at this Theatre of Blood everyone keeps talking about!

options.text: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies...?

steps.player: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies on the route to Burgh de Rott?

steps.npc: Let's just say that I'm somewhat experienced and I'm happy to take on my fair share of enemies. You don't need to worry about that.

options.text: I can take you to Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: I can take you to Burgh de Rott.

steps.text: If the player has a follower:

steps.npc: Hmmm, it seems that you have a follower. I think it may get lost on this journey if it's left to wander on its own. Let's leave when your follower is safe.
Oh really? That would be great! I'll give you a small reward once we reach our destination.

steps.text: Burgh de Rott Ramble begins

steps.npc: Ok, which route should we take?

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

standard-dialogue-when-a-piece-of-accept.npc: Ah, so you want to give me some supplies, eh? Let me just open me backpack.

steps.npc: This place is a bit grim. How can people live here?
Do you visit Burgh de Rott often? You seem to know the route well.
When are we going to get to Burgh de Rott?
We don't have all day to stand around chatting; let's press on. I have loot to get.
Oh, I hate this trip, but it's better than the opulet life styles forced on us adventurer types. I'd much rather be up to my eyes in mud and having a good fight!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-during-com.npc: Can't you see I'm being attacked...

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-when-a-pie.npc: Thanks, I'll get this down my neck.

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-bridge-eve.npc: Blimey! Looks like we're going to have to go back to Paterdomus. We can't get over that bridge!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-bridge-eve.player: Oh, I'm sure we can find a way!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-bog-event.npc: Well that's torn it... Looks like we can't get over this bog. We'll have to go back to Paterdomus.

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-bog-event.player: Oh, I'm sure we can find a way!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-bog-event.npc: Hey...that's great...you did a great job...I'll follow you.
Whahay...that was great!
But we really should be heading off now.

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-river-even.npc: Well that's torn it... Looks like we can't get over this bog. We'll have to go back to Paterdomus.

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-river-even.player: Oh, I'm sure we can find a way through!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-river-even.npc: That's amazing! I'll have to do the same.
Whahay! That was great! But we really should be heading off now.

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-tentacle-e.npc: Ahhh, that would be a tentacle...
I think I'm going to faint!
Blimey! Look at that beast! You're gonna have to sort that thing out on your own!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-finishing-.npc: Many thanks for getting me safely to the Burgh de Rott. Here's your reward.

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-finishing-.text: The Mage gives you a reward token!

starting-off.speaker: Kolodion
starting-off.text: Hey there, how are you? Are you enjoying the bloodshed?

options.text: I think I've had enough for now.

steps.player: I think I've had enough for now.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: A shame. You're a good battle mage. I hope to see you soon.

options.text: How can I use my new spells outside of the arena?

steps.player: How can I use my new spells outside of the arena?

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Experience, my friend, experience. Once you've used the spell enough times in the arena, you'll be able to use them in the rest of Gielinor.

steps.player: Good stuff.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Not so good for the citizens; they won't stand a chance.

steps.player: How am I doing so far?

steps.speaker: Kolodion

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You are almost ready to use the strike spell outside of the arena.
If player has cast Saradomin Strike at least 100 times:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You're experienced enough to use the strike spell anywhere.
If player has cast Claws of Guthix less than 51 times:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You still need to train with the claw spell inside the arena before you can use it outside.
If player has cast Claws of Guthix at least 51 times:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You have completed over half of the training needed to use the claw spell outside of the arena.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You are almost ready to use the claw spell outside of the arena.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You're experienced enough to use the claw spell anywhere.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You still need to train with the flame spell inside the arena before you can use it outside.

steps.text: You have completed over half of the training needed to use the flame spell outside of the arena.

steps.text: You're experienced enough to use the flame spell anywhere.

options.text: Are there any more challenges available?

steps.player: Are there any more challenges available?

steps.text: If player hasn't mastered all the god spells yet:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You still need to learn how to cast all god spells outside of the arena.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I've made a note of the spells you still need to learn in your journal.
If player doesn't have 75 Magic:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You have indeed shown potential, [player name].

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: However, a wizard of your level wouldn't stand a chance.
If player has mastered all the god spells and is 75 Magic:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I am one of the most powerful mages in existence. But even my power has limitations. There are some beings however that have power exceeding even my own.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I have detected three life forces within the Wilderness, each of them giving out a strange magical power, one unlike any I have ever felt before.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: If we could harness the power of these beings, I could imbue your god cape with that power, greatly increasing its potential.

options.text: Great, I've been waiting for an improvement!

steps.player: Great, I've been waiting for an improvement!
What do you need me to do?

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I will need you to kill these three beings and bring me their remains. Even in death, their power should be great enough for me to harness it for our own uses.

steps.player: Where am I supposed to find these beings?

steps.text: If the player has room in their inventory for the symbol:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Here, take this enchanted symbol of the gods. It will guide you to the creatures.
Kolodion hands you an enchanted symbol.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Bring me the remains of all three magical beings. Do this and I will imbue their combined power into a single god cape of your choice.

options.text: Where can I find these beings?
Any advice on fighting the beings?
Tell me more about these beings.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have room in their inventory for the symbol:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You'll need to free up an inventory space before we continue.

options.text: Actually, my current cape is fine.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I see... If you ever change your mind, you know where to find me.

starting-off-talking-to-kolodion-again.text: If the player doesn't have an enchanted symbol:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Here, take this enchanted symbol of the gods. It will guide you to the creatures.
Kolodion hands you an enchanted symbol.

starting-off-talking-to-kolodion-again.text: If the player doesn't have an enchanted symbol and their inventory is full:

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: You'll need to free up an inventory space before we continue.

starting-off-talking-to-kolodion-again.speaker: Kolodion
starting-off-talking-to-kolodion-again.text: Bring me the remains of all three magical beings. Do this and I will imbue their combined power into a single god cape of your choice.

options.text: Where can I find these beings?

steps.player: Where can I find these beings?

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: They can all be found in the Wilderness. The enchanted symbol can track their unique magical energies, leading you to their exact locations.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Be warned though, the symbol will take a blood sacrifice every time it's used.

options.text: Any advice on fighting the beings?

steps.player: Any advice on fighting the beings?

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: They can't be harmed by normal magic, melee or ranged attacks, you will need to use the god combat spell corresponding to the creature you are fighting.

options.text: Tell me more about these beings.

steps.player: Tell me more about these beings.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: One is a justiciar. According to legend, the justiciars were the elite of Saradomin's forces. Some worked alone, operating as assassins behind enemy lines. Others led entire armies in Saradomin's name.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I couldn't tell you why this one wanders the Wilderness, but I suspect he has good reason.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: The second is a Demon of Zamorak. From what I can tell, he is completely mad. He roams the Wilderness, killing all who he comes across without mercy. Even his own kind do not escape his fury.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: He's known to battle the justiciar quite regularly, perhaps they are old enemies.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: The final being is a Guthixian Ent. Like most followers of Guthix, he will avoid combat if possible. Make no mistake though, he is deadly when threatened.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: He seems to take great interest in the other two creatures. Maybe he is trying to keep a balance between them.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: All three of them give off a unique magical energy, one unlike any I have ever felt before. The fact that the three of them are so different, yet possess powers so similar, is very odd indeed.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: I'd be very interested in learning more about the source of their power.

steps.player: Thanks, bye.

steps.speaker: Kolodion
steps.text: Farewell, [player name].
It appears the creatures have moved locations, the symbol glows slightly as it locates their new positions.

standard-dialogue-wilderness.npc: This isn't the place to talk. Visit me in Varrock's Chaos Temple if you have something to discuss. Unless you're here to teleport or buy something?

steps.player: Let's see what you're selling.

options.text: Could you teleport me to the Abyss?

steps.player: Could you teleport me to the Abyss?

steps.npc: Veniens! Sallakar! Rinnesset!

steps.text: Player is teleported to the Abyss.

steps.player: Alright, I'll go.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-enter.npc: Ah, you again. What do you want?

options.text: About that incantation your initiate gave me...
options.condition: After Temple of the Eye:

steps.player: About that incantation your initiate gave me...

steps.text: If this is the first time using this option:

steps.npc: Ah yes, the one to trace that amulet. Don't think I didn't notice that you modified the transmission spell I put on it. Next time you need help, we might not be so willing.

steps.player: Well maybe you should have asked first! Besides, you wouldn't have got anything useful out of it. In tracing that amulet, we accidently managed to open an uncontrollable rift to the Abyss.

steps.npc: And does this 'we' include the Order of Wizards?

steps.player: Maybe...

steps.npc: I knew it! It's just like them to play with magic they don't understand. First they burnt down the Wizards' Tower, now they're opening uncontrollable abyssal rifts!
Perhaps the fools should leave the dangerous magic to us next time!

steps.player: Oh, that reminds me. That incantation didn't appear to be written on parchment. What was it?

steps.npc: Hmm... probably the flesh of an abyssal creature. Why do you ask?

steps.player: Oh, I just thought it might be human flesh. I'm relieved it wasn't!

steps.npc: You've been spending too much time with your friends in the Order of Wizards! I know that we Zamorakians have a bad reputation, but do you really think we'd be so barbaric?

steps.text: If this is not the first time using this option:

steps.npc: Ah yes, the one that led those fools in the Order of Wizards to open an uncontrollable abyssal rift! Perhaps they should leave the dangerous magic to us next time!
Not to mention that they tried to convince you that we wrote that incantation on human flesh! Their lies never cease to amaze me!

steps.player: Right...

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Abyss?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Abyss?

steps.npc: It is a hard place to describe. We often refer to it as another plane, but that isn't quite accurate. If anything, it is more like a plane that sits between all other planes.

steps.player: Right... And what does it have to do with runecrafting?

steps.npc: In truth, nothing at all. However, it has everything to do with teleportation. You see, time and space work differently in the Abyss.

For example, you can travel to the Abyss, walk a few steps and then exit, only to find yourself somewhere completely different from where you entered. You might even find yourself on a different plane.
You can also enter the Abyss and spend days there, but on your return, only moments have passed.
This is why the Abyss is so useful. It can be used as an effective hub for teleportation. In fact, all teleportation that we know of uses the Abyss, you just don't realise it.

steps.player: Wait... So when I teleport, I'm actually travelling through the Abyss?

steps.npc: In some ways, I suppose you are. Whenever you use a teleport spell, that spell is actually travelling through the Abyss and using it to link two places together.

steps.player: So did you discover the Abyss?

steps.npc: No. Knowledge of the Abyss has existed for a long time, hence it being used for teleportation. However, we believe we may be the first to have properly gained access in centuries.

steps.player: How did you manage it?

steps.npc: By complete accident. One of our initiates was performing a routine teleportation experiment when something went wrong. Instead of ending up at their destination, they found themselves in the Abyss.
Now, did you want something else?

options.text: Can you tell me more about your group?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about your group?

steps.npc: I suppose you have proven yourself trustworthy. We are a group of mages in service to Zamorak. Our group is called the Zamorak Magical Institute, or Z.M.I. for short.
Few actually know of us. Saradominist groups like the Order of Wizards hold sway over these lands, so we are forced to work in the shadows. However, make no mistake, our power far exceeds theirs.

steps.player: You don't seem to like the Order of Wizards very much.

steps.npc: And why would we? Did you know that the Order of Wizards wasn't always a Saradominist group? Once they allowed mages of all faiths to study with them, but they became greedy.

steps.player: What happened?

steps.npc: They started to desire more control. They banned Zamorakian wizards from certain areas of study, claiming them to be too dangerous. In reality, they just wanted that knowledge for themselves.
It all went wrong for them, of course. A Zamorakian wizard made a great breakthrough in teleportation magic, but the Saradominists stole his research.
They used it to perform a ritual, but their lack of understanding caused it to go wrong. The entire Wizards' Tower burnt down. Many were killed, and years of research was destroyed.
Naturally, they blamed the Zamorakians. Claimed we intentionally burnt the tower down. After the tower was rebuilt, we were banished from the Order of Wizards and forced underground.

steps.player: And that's how the Z.M.I. was formed?

steps.npc: Exactly.
Now, did you want something else?

steps.player: Nothing. I'm just looking around.

steps.npc: Very well.

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-god-item.npc: How dare you wear such disrespectful attire in this holy place? Remove those immediately if you wish to speak to me.
I don't speak to Saradominist filth.

treasure-trails-master.text: a torn part of a clue scroll
