after-talking-to-the-last-person.speaker: Jorral
after-talking-to-the-last-person.text: It all makes sense now, I never realised there was quite so much history to this place, it was more than I could have hoped.

after-talking-to-the-last-person.player: I'm glad to hear. What's the whole story?

after-talking-to-the-last-person.speaker: Jorral
after-talking-to-the-last-person.text: Many years ago, there were two friends who fell out over their difference of opinion in religion. One decided to dedicate his life to Saradomin, the other to Zamorak. Years passed and the follower of Zamorak moved into

after-talking-to-the-last-person.speaker: Jorral
after-talking-to-the-last-person.text: this outpost with a group of others to cause havoc for the city of Ardougne. The people of the city called upon some Saradomin followers, who happened to be led by the other friend. A battle ensued that ended with the

after-talking-to-the-last-person.speaker: Jorral
after-talking-to-the-last-person.text: two ex-friends at the top of the outpost as the sole survivors. Realising their mistakes they made friends again. One decided to become King and spread the word of equality, and the other chose to start up a

after-talking-to-the-last-person.speaker: Jorral
after-talking-to-the-last-person.text: market where all could trade their wares equally and fairly. The one that became king is the great grandfather of the King Lathas that we know!

after-talking-to-the-last-person.player: So what should I do now?

after-talking-to-the-last-person.speaker: Jorral
after-talking-to-the-last-person.text: Well, what I'll do is write down the details you have provided in a more easy to digest manner, along with my plans for using this building as a museum.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

options.text: Who are you and what are you doing here?

steps.player: Who are you and what are you doing here?

steps.npc: I am the great Malignius Mortifer, wielder of strange and terrible powers. These lowly followers of mine are dedicated students of the magical arts. Their business is to follow me and learn all they can.

steps.player: They don't look very tough.

steps.npc: You may believe that, but even if you strike one down, another will rise up within minutes.

steps.player: Yeah, right.

steps.npc: Each of my followers is a master of his chosen element. His life becomes bound to that element in a way you could not hope to understand.

steps.player: And what do you do?

steps.npc: I am mastering a branch of magic that few dare to attempt: Necromancy! The fools in the Guild of Wizards shun anyone who practices this art, but there are a few in this land who know the rudiments.

steps.text: If Zogre Flesh Eaters has been completed:

steps.npc: Grayzag, Invrigar, Sithik... Even Melzar studied the methods of necromancy, until an accident affected his mind. Now his spells tend to result in...

steps.text: If Zogre Flesh Eaters hasn't been completed:

steps.npc: Grayzag and Invrigar... Even Melzar studied the methods of necromancy, until an accident affected his mind. Now his spells tend to result in...
... well, let us simply say that he does NOT raise armies of undead minions.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.player: Is this like Summoning? Can you teach me?

steps.npc: The obscure magical art of necromancy has nothing to do with Summoning.
Through necromancy, I may resurrect the bodies of those who have fallen, and bend them to my will, and even command them to tell me hidden knowledge.
I shall not pass on my secrets lightly to any passer-by!

steps.player: Even a mighty hero like me?

steps.text: If the player isn't wearing equipment aligned with Guthix, Saradomin, or Zamorak:

steps.npc: Perhaps one day you shall learn ways to summon creatures to your side, but my own work is of a different sort.

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Guthix:

steps.npc: Deluded lover of Guthix, you will get no secrets from me!

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Saradomin:

steps.npc: Saradominist fool, you will get no secrets from me!

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Zamorak:

steps.npc: Although I note your respect for our Lord Zamorak, I am afraid the subtle secrets of necromancy must remain beyond your grasp.

steps.player: What happened to Melzar?

steps.npc: The forces required to wield power over the dead are very difficult to control. Melzar's concentration slipped, and his spell rebounded upon him.
Although he did not die, his mind broke. Now he dwells amidst the beasts that fill his strange home, and when he attempts to do magic he gets... amusing results.

options.text: Why do you keep making fungi appear?

steps.player: Why do you keep making fungi appear?

steps.npc: Necromancy is... still not fully understood. So few people dare to study it. Although my spells usually raise whichever undead creature I desire, they sometimes misfire. As Melzar has learnt!

steps.player: Thanks, I'll be off now.

steps.npc: I am sure your curiosity will eventually draw you to speak to me again, [player name].

options.text: Can you teach me something about magic?

steps.player: Can you teach me something about magic?

steps.text: If Rune Mysteries hasn't been completed:

steps.npc: I see no glimmer of understanding in your eyes; my time would be wasted trying to teach you of the subtle arts.
If you are truly interested in magic, perhaps you should go and speak to the Duke of Lumbridge, who lives east of this place. Perchance he will have a mission for you that will teach you something.

steps.text: If Rune Mysteries has been completed:

steps.npc: Ah, you are an inquisitive fellow. I shall speak of the great Wizards' Tower, destroyed by fire many years ago...
Many say it was the greatest building in the history of Gielinor, a magnificent monument to human ingenuity.
Yet when humans are offered great power, they so often buy it at the cost of their principles.
Wizards who claimed allegiance to Saradomin began to insist that magic be restricted to the few they deemed 'worthy' of such powers.
Before long, those who did not share their fatuous obsession with Saradomin were excluded from the Tower completely. This state of affairs could not continue.
One dark night, a brave band of magi loyal to the great Lord Zamorak stormed the Tower. Despite heavy losses, they fought their way up the levels until they reached the Great Library.

Alas, they were trapped and could not steal the precious records. But before they could be defeated, the bravest of them took it upon himself to blast the writings into nothingness, destroying the library.
The ensuing fire raced through the tower, and none escaped its fury. Some say that Lord Zamorak himself fanned the flames to ensure the destruction of his enemies!

steps.text: If Enter the Abyss has been completed:

steps.npc: Much of that knowledge was lost, and some has never yet been rediscovered. Still, your efforts on behalf of my colleagues have not been wasted! Once again, the forces of Zamorak can create unlimited runestones!
May the world cower in its boots!

steps.player: I see...

steps.npc: I bid you farewell for now.

steps.text: If Enter the Abyss hasn't been completed:

steps.npc: Much of that knowledge was lost, and some has never yet been rediscovered. Still, the power of magic remains in the world, and we who dedicate our lives to its study may yet perform great works...

steps.player: Thanks, I'll be going now.

steps.npc: As you wish.

steps.player: Tell me more about Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Well now, the history of the isles is a bloody tale. When told in its intended form it takes 9 days and 9 nights. However, I will give you the abridged version.

steps.player: Phew!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Four generations ago there was a mighty king who ruled wisely and was loved by all.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: He had many sons, most of whom proved themselves in the usual Fremennik ways of fighting, sailing, drinking and so on.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: His youngest two sons, however, were a problem. Ever since they were old enough to hit one another they had bickered and fought.

steps.npc: Their names were Jatizso and Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Hey! Who's telling this story?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Ahem. At the time it was customary for the Kings' sons to claim a prize from his treasury when they came of age.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Each brother rallied support and strode out to confront the other on the field of battle to claim the same prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The brothers met on the field, limbs were bruised, bones were crushed and heads clashed.

steps.npc: They probably didn't notice the head-clashing bit. Too thick skulled!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Can I finish the story without interruptions?

steps.npc: Carry on dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, long into the night they fought, until they stood alone, facing each other.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: On the second day the old king, whose patience was exhausted, strode out onto the field and demanded to know who had claimed his prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso looked at his father and told him yes, it was his, to which the other called out 'No! It's not'.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so, the argument continued through to the third day, with the sounds of 'Jah! 'tis so!', 'Ne! It's not!' echoing over the field, becoming more hoarse as the darkness enveloped the brothers.

steps.npc: Bah! What they needed was a good clip round the ear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At the end of the third day, when the brothers lay unable to move, let alone stand, the King stood between them in shame.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: As punishment for their squabbling he banished his sons from his realm, ordering that neither should return until they had conquered lands of their own.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso set sail with a band of loyal followers, sailing into the east, while Neitiznot went west.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso ventured far into uncharted oceans, his crew dwindling as the trials of sailing and sea monsters took them.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso's ship limped through the frozen wastes, in need of repairs, fighting off pirates who thought them easy pickings.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At last a promising land was sighted, a land rich in minerals, deep fjords and sweeping mountains.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso claimed the land and named it after himself.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: A mighty citadel was constructed to protect his land; then Jatizso set forth to explore his new kingdom.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Crossing a few fjords, Jatizso spied an island which remained green and fertile, even at such latitude.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: With a mighty cheer Jatizso and his men marched on the island. Upon reaching the island, however, they discovered a wooden stockade.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Determined to be master of all the land, Jatizso stood in front of the gates. He looked up and demanded that those within the stockade surrendered.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso was horrified when his brother appeared on the battlements and cried 'This is my land! Go find yer own'. To which his brother replied 'No it's not!', throwing some rocks for good measure.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so the blood feud continued.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The fighting between the towns has continued for generations with little sign of improvement.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Quite recently a massive troll army seized one of the islands to the north, while our townships' militias were busy fighting one another.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: They marched down and razed Neitiznot to the ground while Neitiznot's troops laid siege to Jatizso.

steps.npc: The smoke damage was atrocious, I had to replace my entire wardrobe.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Yes, dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, a hasty sort of peace has been agreed until the trolls are dealt with.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: But you can still see the bitter rivalry as guards hurl insults between the towns.

options.text: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.player: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.npc: Well Burgher Mawnis Burowgar is a gentle soul at heart. His kinsfolk are happy and content with their lot.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: 'Soft' is the word we use in Jatizso.

steps.npc: Well a soft Burgher is better than a stupid King.
Anyway, there was a time when Burgher Burowgar was similar to King Sorvott.
Argumentative, short tempered; I am sure you know what I mean.
The change happened when the trolls came and razed Neitiznot to the ground.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: You mean while Neitiznot's militias were assaulting Jatizso.

steps.npc: Yes, well our tribes have been at war for nearly four generations now.
Anyway, the Burgher lost his wife and youngest son in the trolls' raid and has been a changed man since.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: May their journey to our ancestors' halls be swift.

steps.npc: Personally, I am much happier with the considerate Burgher we have now.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.npc: Let's set sail then.

steps.text: Leaving Rellekka for Neitiznot.

steps.player: I just stopped to say hello.

steps.npc: Thanks, and good luck with the Burgher's tasks.

steps.player: I may be back later.

steps.npc: Bye

talking-to-maria-gunnars-on-neitiznot.npc: Hi, [Fremennik name], you should speak with Burgher Mawnis Burowgar in the main chambers. Do you have any questions?

talking-to-maria-gunnars-on-neitiznot.prompt: What do you want to know about?

steps.player: Tell me about your husband.

steps.npc: My husband is a typical Fremennik, being both headstrong and brave.
We fell in love when we were young, but as there was a war between our isles, we were ordered to stop seeing each other by our parents.
This didn't stop Mord climbing the wailing tower, on his side of the channel between our isles, to sing to me every night.
After Mord's voice broke, his singing voice was lost, but I still listened to his terrible sonnets each and every night.
Until one night there was no singing! Then, far below me, I heard a gentle voice calling my name.
Mord had stolen his father's boat to come and fetch me from my prison
and from that day forth we have lived in Rellekka.

steps.player: Tell me about Jatizso.

steps.npc: My husband does not speak of the inhabitants of the isle of Jatizso much.
He has little positive to say about his parents, so he chooses not to speak of them in my presence. The only thing I've noticed is that everyone on that island seems very sad...

steps.prompt: Who do you want to know about?

options.text: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.player: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.npc: King Sorvott IV follows in the footsteps of a line of kings who have reigned since Jatizso himself passed away. It is rumoured that the King has no heir and is seeking a bride to bear him children. Given his
personality I'm not surprised he hasn't found a bride yet!

steps.player: Tell me about Neitiznot.

steps.npc: To be honest with you, I do not keep up to date with all the goings on here now that I have a home in Rellekka.
However, Neitiznot seems a happy place! The Burgher seems a wiser rule than King Sorvott, although I believe he is worried about the trolls at the moment. They seem to be a big threat.

steps.npc: Sure.

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're a good enough [craftsman/craftswoman], that is.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're a good enough [craftsman/craftswoman], that is.

standard-dialogue.npc: Ah, hello and welcome. I'm Martin Holt, leader of Kourend's Royal Society. This is our little protest against the Kourend Council.

standard-dialogue.player: Pleased to meet you. I'm [player name]. So, what's wrong with the Council?

standard-dialogue.npc: Now there's a question! I have a better one. What's right with the Council?
I bet you didn't know that the Council was originally only temporary. After the last King died, they were only supposed to rule until his daughter came of age.
However, according to the Council, the King's daughter went mad. Such a wonderful convenience for them of course. With her out of the picture, the Council became permanent.

standard-dialogue.player: Interesting. What else don't you like about the Council?

standard-dialogue.npc: Democracy! That's meant to be the big thing for the Council. Funny thing is, although they're meant to be elected by the people, the same four people have won every single election. Little odd, no?

standard-dialogue.player: That is a bit suspicious, I suppose.

standard-dialogue.npc: Indeed it is. So, do you want to join our protest?

standard-dialogue.player: Not right now. But thanks for the information.

standard-dialogue.text: You do not meet all of the requirements to start the A Kingdom Divided quest.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: Hello Martin. Now here's somewhere I wouldn't have expected to find you.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.npc: Indeed. I never thought I'd be back here.
We won! The Council are out, and we have what Kourend really needed. We have a king!
Of course, King Artur ended up taking the throne from his father a little faster than anyone expected, so he needs plenty of guidance. That's where I come in!

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: So you're helping to advise the King?

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.npc: Exactly! When the people voted on Rose's Accord, they voted for the Hosidius family to become the new royal family. From a technical standpoint that means they voted for King Artur.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: But in reality it was his father they expected to rule.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.npc: Precisely. My job is to advise King Artur and ensure his actions have a positive impact on the people that he now rules.
Not too bad. While he lacks experience, the King has a good heart. He wants to do the right thing, and he has the support needed to do it.
Mind you, he could do with listening to his mother less. She's always whispering things in his ear. She forgets that he's the one in charge, not her.
Still, I'm sure he just needs time to adjust. I have no doubt that under King Artur, Kourend will prosper like never before.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: I'm sure you're right. See you around Martin.

steps.npc: Only a king can right the wrongs of the Council! And only you can make that happen!
How long will you keep your eyes closed? Their corruption surrounds you!
This kingdom will never be safe while the Council rule!
You deserve the truth! They won't give it to you!
The Council have wronged you! It's time to make things right!
Together, we can bring an end to the treachery of the Council!
The Council care only for themselves! It's time for a ruler who cares for you!
Kourend is a kingdom! A kingdom needs a king, not a council!
Democracy? What democracy? It's all a façade!
People of Kourend, you have been lied to!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey newbie! I'm the Master Navigator - let's teach you how to get around.
Ha. You've worked your way around to me, but this island is bigger than you think! I will show you by teaching you how to use the world map. First things first, you will need to open your world map.
You can find this in the top right side of the screen, look for the flashing globe icon.

standard-dialogue-after-looking-at-the-w.npc: Well done, you have found your world map.
The world map can show where you are in the world, as well as where other places are. You can find where you are by looking for the yellow X icon.
You may have noticed all the icons on the map, these icons have a meaning behind each one. You can find out what the icon means by looking at the map key.
To open or close the map key you will have to click the scroll looking icon in the bottom left part of the map.
Once opened, you will see a list of all the different icons on the map, as well as some text next to the icon telling you what the icon is. You can click on an icon in the key.
Every icon that is the same as the one you just selected, will start to flash.
Lastly, next to the key you will see there is a search bar. You can click on the search bar and type in a location. You can then press enter and the map will move to the specified location.
Now you know the basics of the world map, I am going to task you with making your way to the Quest Guide. You can find him just north of here. Go out the door to the west and follow the path.

Remember that your world map is just a larger version of your mininmap, with the difference that you can click on your minimap to navigate around. You will also see icons on your minimap as well, just like the world map.

To open or close the map key you will have to click the scroll looking icon in the bottom left part of the map.
Once opened, you will see a list of all the different icons on the map, as well as some text next to the icon telling you what the icon is. You can click on an icon in the key.
Every icon that is the same as the one you just selected, will start to flash.
Lastly, next to the key you will see there is a search bar. You can click on the search bar and type in a location. You can then press enter and the map will move to the specified location.

steps.text: If the player has level 1-20 Smithing:

steps.npc: You're going to need to get your hand on some metal bars. You could do this by mining your own ores and smelting them at a furnace.
There is a furnace located in Lumbridge, just north of the castle opposite the general store.
If you are looking for some ore, there is a mine east of Varrock. There you can find some copper and tin ore. Don't forget to bring a pickaxe.
When you have your bars, bring them to an anvil to open the smithing interface. If the item name is in black, this means you do not have the level to smith the item.
If the item name is in white, this means you do have the level to smith the item. You will see the bars required to smith the item underneath the name of the item.
If the number of bars is in orange, this means you do not have enough bars to smith the item. If it is in green, this means you have enough bars for the item.

steps.npc: Cor blimey, I don't think there is anything I can teach you, but I'll do my best.

It may be worth you stockpiling coal for a while before attempting these difficult metals or even sticking to good old reliable iron by the bucket load.
If you want to stop yourself from failing to smith iron, I suggest purchasing some rings of forging. Be aware that they will break after a certain number of bars are smelted.
If you want to save on coal, you could try smithing your bars over at the Blast Furnace in Keldagrim.

steps.npc: There are many things you can make, from weapons to your good old fashioned armour.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-agai.speaker: Lelia
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-agai.text: Ready to go back in? If you don't deal with that minotaur, no one will want to buy those kebabs of yours.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-emilio-aft.speaker: Emelio
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-emilio-aft.text: Nilsal, friend. Have you taken those kebabs to Lelia at the Colosseum yet?

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-emilio-aft.player: I have. She set me up with a slot to promote them to the crowd, but there's been a bit of an issue.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-emilio-aft.speaker: Emelio
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-emilio-aft.text: Well, then you'd better get back there and sort it out.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.speaker: Lelia
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.text: You put on a good performance in there. The crowd seemed very impressed.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.speaker: Lelia
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.text: What about it? It got out of control and you killed it. Saves the beastmaster a job.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.player: But it could have killed me! You said it would be safe.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.speaker: Lelia
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.text: You survived, didn't you? I don't see the problem.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.speaker: Lelia
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-afte.text: Now, I need to get things ready for the next slot. Why don't you go and tell Emelio about the good impression his kebabs made.

guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-agai.speaker: Lelia
guerilla-marketing-talking-to-lelia-agai.text: I don't think you need anything else, do you? Why don't you go and tell Emelio about the good impression his kebabs made.

wrapping-up.speaker: Emelio
wrapping-up.text: Nilsal, friend. Given that I've already served our first customers, I take it your trip to the Colosseum was a success?

wrapping-up.player: Well I did run into a slight complication, but apart from that, it went very well.

wrapping-up.speaker: Emelio
wrapping-up.text: You have done a great service to Varlamore, friend. Thanks to you, all here will be able to indulge in the joy that is kebabs. As thanks, I will offer you a special price for any kebabs you buy!

wrapping-up.player: Do I not get to share in any of the profits, given I helped set it all up?

wrapping-up.speaker: Emelio
wrapping-up.text: Sorry, friend, but I must prepare some more kebabs for our next customers! Until next time.

first-time-after-completing-beneath-curs.npc: I sense that the Devourer's corruption has been lessened. I trust you were successful?

first-time-after-completing-beneath-curs.npc: Continue your fight against the Devourer. Only with her defeat, will we finally find freedom.

options.text: What do you know about Amascut?
Tell me more about the war you mentioned.

steps.npc: It can't be that hard can it?
I guess this will be my last day of blood tithes, one way or another.
I will survive the Theatre! Just like Serafina did!
Soon I will be free!
I'm starting to think I made a mistake coming here.
Can't talk. I need to prepare myself.
What? What's wrong?

steps.player: Nothing, I just need to ask a couple of questions.

steps.npc: Oh, hello. How's everything?

steps.player: Not too bad thanks, but I wanted to ask a question.

steps.npc: Hello?

steps.player: Hello, I wonder if I could ask some questions.

steps.npc: Hey, don't sneak up on me like that!

steps.player: Sorry, didn't mean to scare you. I just wanted to ask a question.

steps.npc: Well, I guess so.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm barely surviving...
When I'm not being drained of blood, the vyrewatch force me to repair the walls.
When I'm not being drained of blood I'm fixing up the ghetto.
I just try to make a living the best way I can. You haven't got some food have you?
Like everyone else, I just survive here. Just try to keep alive till after the next blood tithe. That's when they feed us.
Why do you wanna know?

steps.player: Just curious, that's all.

steps.npc: I dunno. I don't know if I can trust you...

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.player: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.npc: Well, you're in sector [one/two/three/four/five/six], but if you were hoping for any other help then I'm very sorry. I find it hard enough to help myself.
Life's so very hard here. Before too long they'll be wanting to have another blood tithing and then I'll feel just awful again.

steps.player: What's a blood tithing?

steps.npc: You must be new here, else you'd know for sure. It's where we have to give a blood tithe to the vampyres. They do it on a weekly basis, a different sector each week so they don't kill us all off.

options.text: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.npc: It's probably best not to talk about that, friend.

steps.player: I need to make contact with them. Please don't worry - I'm on their side.

steps.npc: As are we all, but I really can't talk about them. It's not a subject easily broached here.

steps.text: After completing Sins of the Father:

steps.npc: The Myreque are gone. Do not speak of them, it will do you no good.

options.text: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.npc: Yep, that's where we are at the moment. This place, Meiyerditch, is just one large ghetto.
The city is sectioned off so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill us all off in one go.

options.text: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.player: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.npc: They're monsters, I know that much. I've never known anything else, but I have a feeling it might be nice to not have to live in fear the whole time. Worrying if I'm going to make the next blood tithe quota.
I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres. Apparently they were human once, converted by the vampyres.
Then you have juvinates. They're initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to get some powers.
After that you have the vyres. They're nasty... really nasty.

options.text: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.player: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.text: Before completing A Taste of Hope:

steps.npc: Drakan? Which one: Ranis or Vanescula?

steps.player: Well, I was referring to the main Drakan, you know, the overlord of Morytania.

steps.npc: Hmm, nothing has been seen of him for many years now. Some people say they occasionally see Ranis or Vanescula flying about, but it's not too often.

steps.text: After completing A Taste of Hope:

steps.npc: Vanescula?

steps.player: Well, I was referring to the main Drakan, you know, the overlord of Morytania.

steps.npc: Hmm, nothing has been seen of him for many years now. Some people say they occasionally see Vanescula flying about, but it's not too often.

steps.text: After completing Sins of the Father:

steps.npc: No one had seen anything of him for years, they say he's back now though. We shouldn't talk of him any more though, the vyrewatch might not like it.

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: To do? Around here? Survive! Eke out an existence and just live for another day, that's it really.

The juvinates organise work crews to mine the daeyalt, fix the walls, the castles and so on. If we refuse to do the work, they put us on double tithes and you can't do that for long before you dry up.
If you want to escape, there's only one way. Anyone who survives in the theatre gets to leave. It's pointless though. No one survives.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.npc: It's very nice of you to offer, my friend, but I shouldn't expect that you could do anything. The vampyres are just too powerful to overcome.
They say this place once had a Saradominist Queen. Even she could not withstand the vampyres. Anyone who has challenged their power in the past has come undone.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.
What do you do here?

steps.npc: I've been working on getting some things fixed up around here. Hopefully we can eventually make a proper home out of this city.
Just trying to make a living really. Things are a lot better now the vampyres aren't taking our blood, but it's still going to be a long time before we get this place in a good state.

steps.player: How are things here?

steps.npc: Well, the vampyres aren't taking our blood anymore, and they've promised to help us rebuild the city. Still, it's going to take a long time to fix this place up. Most people have chosen to leave instead.

steps.player: I'd best be off.

steps.npc: I often thought about trying out the Theatre myself before Drakan was dealt with. Glad I never ended up doing that!
It's nice that they let us watch the performances in the Theatre now. It's fun seeing how good some of those warriors from Misthalin are!
Going to give the Theatre a go? You look like you've got what it takes.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: We're miners, perhaps that might give you a clue! We're forced to mine for those stinking vyres. Once we've filled the cart, they sometimes let us go back to Meiyerditch, but then we get tithed. Don't know if I

Work work work, that's all I ever do.
I can't think strait, I'm so tired.
Ohh, my arms.
Ohh, my back.
I'm rich in experience, poor in wealth.
I'm so tired, I could sleep standing up.
What I wouldn't give for a good night's rest.
Good to see you safe friend.

steps.npc: The vyrewatch are getting more ferocious by the day. You're doing well if you can get from one side of Meiyerditch to the other without getting attacked!

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Hi. Welcome to the general store. How might I help you?

steps.npc: About magic of course.

steps.npc: I said about magic of course. You know, in response to your question.

steps.npc: It's quite simple, everyone has a resonance that is responded to by the moon. This resonance changes depending on what we are thinking. You can tune yourself in to listen to this resonance with practice - it's
a life long quest for the members of the Moon Clan, but its especially easy to read with outsiders like yourself, as you are far louder and unguarded.

steps.npc: That's disgusting!

standard-dialogue.npc: Greetings adventurer, I am the Melee combat tutor. Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.player: Tell me about melee combat.

steps.npc: Well adventurer, the first thing you will need is a sword and a shield appropriate for your level.
Make sure to equip your sword and shield. Click on them in your inventory, they will disappear from your inventory and move to your worn items. You can see your worn items in the worn items tab here.
When you are wielding your sword you will then be able to see the correct options in the combat interface.
There are four different melee styles. Accurate, aggressive, defensive and controlled. Not all weapons will have all four styles though.

steps.player: Interesting, what does each style do?

steps.npc: Well I am glad you asked. The accurate style will give you experience points in your Attack skill, you will also find you will deal damage more frequently as a result of being, well, more accurate.
Next we have the aggressive style. This style will give you experience points in your Strength skill. When using this style you will notice that your attacks will hit a little harder.
Now for the defensive style, this style will give you experience points in your Defensive skill. When using this style you will notice that you get hit less often.
Finally, we have the controlled style. This style will give you the same amount of experience as the other styles would but shared across all three of the combat skills.
If you were using the training sword for example, there are four different attack types. Stab, lunge, slash and block.
Each type uses one of the attack styles. Stab uses accurate, lunge and slash use aggressive and block uses defensive.
To find out which style an attack type uses, hover your mouse cursor over the style button.

steps.text: If the player is eligible for Adventure paths:

steps.npc: If you need some more advice, you should talk to Adventurer Jon about Adventure paths. He may even have a handy starter kit you can use.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

options.text: What if I wanted to fight something a bit more... human.

steps.player: What if I wanted to fight something a bit more... human.

steps.npc: Well adventurer, there are a few places you might be able to do this.
You could try your luck at castle wars. Here, two teams fight each other to defend their respective flags. To win the game you will need to get the other team's flag and return it to your flag stand.

steps.player: Capture the flag, sounds like a lot of fun.

steps.npc: If you are in a clan, you should gather some clan members and try out clan wars. There you can see which clan is better than the other by fighting each other in an arena.
Both activities are safe minigame, which means if you die you will not loose any of your items. You can get to them by using the teleport option in your minigames tab.
There is also the wilderness. The wilderness is north of Varrock and you can fight other players there. But bare in mind if you die to another player in the wilderness you will lose your stuff.
But this also means that if you kill another player you will be able to take their stuff too.
Only go into the wilderness with items you are willing to lose and pay attention to the wilderness level you are in. The higher the level you go, more player will be able to attack you.
You can find which player can attack you by checking your combat level.
Minus the wilderness level from your combat level to find the lowest level that you can attack, then add the wilderness level to your combat level to find the highest level that you can attack.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

options.text: Tell me about different weapon types I can use.
I'd like a training sword and shield.
Tell me about different weapon types I can use.

steps.player: Tell me about different weapon types I can use

steps.npc: Well let me see now...There are stabbing type weapons such as daggers, then you have swords which are slashing, maces that have great crushing abilities, battle axes which are powerful.
It depends a lot on how you want to fight. Experiment and find out what is best for you. Never be scared to try out a new weapon; you never know, you might like it!
While I tried all of them for a while, I settled on this rather good sword.
You might also find that different weapon types are more accurate against different monsters.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.player: Tell me about skillcapes.

steps.npc: Of course. Skillcapes are a symbol of achievement. Only people who have mastered a skill and reached level 99 can get their hands on them and gain the benefits they carry.
The Cape of Defence will act as ring of life, saving you from combat if your hitpoints become low.

steps.player: How do I play board games?

steps.npc: You can challenge someone to a game anywhere in the Games Zone (except on a PvP or Deadman world) by using the right click option.
Choose the type of game and then choose the options you want such as time per move.
If your opponent accepts the challenge you will be taken to one of the tables around where you will play your game of choice.
Once you have finished your game you will come back here where you can challenge again! We also have tables in a few pubs around the world!

steps.player: What games can I play?

steps.npc: Currently we offer Draughts, Runelink, Runesquares, and Runeversi.

steps.player: Draughts?

steps.npc: Draughts uses standard rules, apart from: a draw is declared if no piece has been taken or promoted for forty moves.

steps.player: Runelink?

steps.npc: Yup, you have to get four runes in row.

steps.player: Runesquares?

steps.npc: Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn.

steps.player: Runeversi?

steps.npc: Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own.

steps.player: Is that your ship?

options.text: Do you deliver to the fort just down the coast?
Do you deliver to the fort just down the coast?

steps.player: Do you deliver to the fort just down the coast?

steps.speaker: Arhein
steps.text: Yes, I do have orders to deliver there from time to time. I think I may have some bits and pieces for them when I leave here next actually.

options.text: Can you drop me off on the way down please?

steps.player: Can you drop me off on the way down please?

steps.speaker: Arhein
steps.text: I don't think Sir Mordred would like that. He wants as few outsiders visiting as possible. I wouldn't want to lose his business.

options.text: Aren't you worried about supplying evil knights?

steps.player: Aren't you worried about supplying evil knights?

steps.speaker: Arhein
steps.text: Hey, you gotta take business where you can find it these days! Besides, if I didn't supply them, someone else would.

steps.player: Where do you deliver to?

steps.speaker: Arhein

options.text: I don't suppose I could get a lift anywhere?

steps.player: I don't suppose I could get a lift anywhere?

steps.speaker: Arhein
steps.text: Sorry pal, but I'm afraid I'm not quite ready to sail yet.

options.text: Well, good luck with your business.

steps.player: Well, good luck with your business.

steps.speaker: Arhein
steps.text: Thanks buddy!

steps.player: Are you rich then?

steps.speaker: Arhein
steps.text: Business is going reasonably well... I wouldn't say I was the richest of merchants ever, but I'm doing fairly well all things considered.

infiltrating-the-keep-trying-to-board-ar.speaker: Arhein
infiltrating-the-keep-trying-to-board-ar.text: Hey buddy! Get away from my ship alright?

infiltrating-the-keep-hiding-in-arhein-s.text: The crate is empty. It's just about big enough to hide inside.

infiltrating-the-keep-hiding-in-arhein-s.prompt: Would you like to hide inside the crate?

steps.text: You climb inside the crate and wait.
And wait...
You hear voices outside the crate. Is this your crate, Arhein?
Yeah, I think so. Pack it aboard soon as you can. I'm on a tight schedule for deliveries!
You feel the crate being lifted. Oof. Wow, this is pretty heavy! I never knew candles weighed so much!
Quit your whining, and stow it in the hold.
You feel the crate being put down inside the ship.
You wait...
And wait...
Casting off!
You feel the ship start to move.
Feels like you're now out at sea.
The ship comes to a stop.
Unload Mordred's deliveries onto the jetty. Aye-aye cap'n!
You feel the crate being lifted.
You can hear someone mumbling outside the crate. ...stupid Arhein... making me... candles... never weigh THIS much....hurts....union about this!...
...if....MY ship be different!... stupid Arhein...
You feel the crate being put down.

steps.prompt: Would you like to get back out of the crate?

steps.text: You climb out of the crate.
You wait.
And wait...
And wait...

steps.prompt: Would you like to get back out of the crate?

inside-keep-le-faye-encountering-sir-mor.speaker: Sir Mordred
inside-keep-le-faye-encountering-sir-mor.text: You DARE to invade MY stronghold?!?! Have at thee knave!!!

options.text: Tell me how to untrap Merlin and I might.

steps.player: Tell me how to untrap Merlin and I might.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: You have guessed correctly that I'm responsible for that.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: I suppose I can live with that fool Merlin being loose for the sake of my son.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: Setting him free won't be easy though.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: You will need to find a magic symbol as close to the crystal as you can find.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: You will then need to drop some bats' bones on the magic symbol while holding a lit black candle.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: This will summon a mighty spirit named Thrantax.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: You will need to bind him with magic words.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: Then you will need the sword Excalibur with which the spell was bound in order to shatter the crystal.

options.text: So where can I find Excalibur?

steps.player: So where can I find Excalibur?

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye
steps.text: The lady of the lake has it. I don't know if she'll give it to you though, she can be rather temperamental.

options.text: OK I will do all that.

steps.player: Ok, I will go do all that.

steps.text: Morgan Le Faye vanishes.

steps.speaker: Morgan Le Faye

steps.player: No. He deserves to die.

searching-for-excalibur-asking-the-knigh.speaker: Sir Palomedes

searching-for-excalibur-asking-the-knigh.speaker: Sir Pelleas
searching-for-excalibur-asking-the-knigh.text: My best guess would be some sort of spell. Unfortunately Merlin is our magic expert.

searching-for-excalibur-asking-the-knigh.speaker: Sir Tristram
searching-for-excalibur-asking-the-knigh.text: Hail Arthur, King of the Britons!

steps.player: I seek the sword Excalibur.

steps.speaker: The Lady of the Lake

steps.text: 'Tis very valuable, and not an artefact to be given away lightly.

steps.text: I would want to give it away only to one who is worthy and good.

searching-for-excalibur-attempting-to-en.speaker: Beggar
searching-for-excalibur-attempting-to-en.text: Please, stranger... my family and I are starving...

Termtrick!

Thrantax the Mighty destroys the black candle and attacks

Candtrick...
Termanto!

steps.text: GRAAAAAARGH!

steps.speaker: Thrantax the Mighty
steps.text: Thou hast me in thine control. So that I mayst return from whence I came, I must grant thee a boon. What dost thou wish of me?

steps.speaker: Thrantax the Mighty
steps.text: GRAAAAAARGH!

standard-dialogue-after-spirits-of-the-e.npc: Much better thanks to you. We're all very impressed.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.npc: Look, you can destroy that letter as many times as you want, but it won't change anything. The sender isn't the kind of individual who takes no for an answer, so for both of our sakes, please just read it.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.text: The messenger has given you a letter... again.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.npc: Please... don't keep doing this. You don't know who you're dealing with...

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.text: The messenger has given you a letter... again.

without-ghostspeak.player: Hello, I wonder if you could help me on this whole brewing thing...

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak.player: Hello, I wonder if you could help me on this whole brewing thing...

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak.npc: I might be able to - what do you need to know?

steps.player: How do I brew ales?

steps.npc: Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.player: How do I brew cider?

steps.npc: First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush. Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

options.text: What do I do once my ale has matured?

steps.player: What do I do once my ale has matured?

steps.npc: Well, once you've got a full vat of the good stuff, just turn the valve and your barrel will fill up with eight pints of whatever your chosen tipple is. Mind it's an empty barrel, though.

options.text: Do you have any spare ale yeast?

steps.player: Do you have any spare ale yeast?

steps.npc: Well, as a matter of fact I do, although I wouldn't describe it as spare. This ale yeast I've got is the best you can get - if you've got a pot I'll fill it for you for 5 ectotokens. Coins are of no use to me.

steps.text: Without an empty pot or 5 ectotokens:

steps.player: I don't have an empty pot, or enough ectotokens I'm afraid.

options.text: That's all I need to know, thanks.

steps.player: That's all I need to know, thanks.
Take me to your leader.

steps.npc: Wot?

steps.player: Isn't that what you're supposed to say when you meet a new race of people?

steps.npc: Well, mate, we don't av no leader, so I ain't gonna take ya to um. We auw av eqwuw right's un stuff, yeah? But if ya wont an intro go live it up wiv da Onerimancer.

steps.player: OK. Is he rich and powerful?

steps.npc: No man, SHE, is dead-wise yeah? She is responsible for initiation wituals an stuff.

steps.player: Great. Thanks. And where is she?

steps.npc: She angs out int souf east of ouw island.

steps.player: Okey dokey....yeah.

steps.npc: Huh?
Yeah? Need something?

steps.player: What do you have?

steps.npc: Rock. Lots of it.

steps.player: What brings you here?

steps.npc: Rock. This here is Stonecutter Outpost. We get rock, cut it, then sell it.

steps.player: So you're pretty far from home then?

steps.npc: What? No. We go back to Cam Torum sometimes, but this is home.

steps.player: Fair enough.

steps.npc: Need something else?

steps.player: I'm good.

steps.npc: Then why you keep staring? Get gone!
Oh... Nilsal. Unusual to see someone up here. What can I do for you?

options.text: What do you do around here?

steps.player: What do you do around here?

steps.npc: I used to work downstairs... but I started using the lab after hours for my own projects and the supervisor found out. Now I've been assigned to rooftop duty to look after the plants.

steps.player: Sorry to hear that. At least the view is good!

options.text: Do you have any tips for potion production?

steps.player: Do you have any tips for potion production?

steps.text: If the player has not joined the Alchemical Society:

steps.npc: I do, but only for fellow members of the Alchemical Society. Perhaps you should join up if you're interested in Herblore.

steps.player: Interesting... Perhaps I should.

steps.text: If the player has joined the Alchemical Society:

steps.npc: Yes... Make good use of the digweed once they're ready to pick. Choose which potion you use it on wisely!
Oh, and the processing tables can be sped up a bit if you use them correctly. You might need to do some experimenting to figure that out.

steps.player: Interesting...

options.text: Thanks! I'd better be going now.

steps.player: Thanks! I'd better be going now.
Hello, you look worried.

steps.npc: My husband is serving near the Lizardman Canyon. I'm worried that something might happen to him.
And I lost my job last week. I need to find another one before my savings run out.

steps.player: Oh, that is bad. I'm sorry to hear that.

steps.npc: Well, it's a difficult time for a lot of people I guess. The war with the lizardmen never ends.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.npc: Thanks so much for saving me from being a vampyre. Here, take this certificate, I'm sorry but it's all I can offer as a reward.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.text: You're handed a certificate of treasure as a reward.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-them-again.npc: Thanks for changing me back, it must have been hard for you. I must be off now.

standard-dialogue-before-talking-to-rupe.npc: Oh, hello there. I'm afraid I don't have time to talk right now. I'm rather busy. Come back some other time please.

standard-dialogue-after-talking-to-ruper.npc: Who am I? Why, how impertinent! I am a princess and I will be spoken to like one. Now be off with you. I have no time for scruffy adventurers like yourself!

standard-dialogue-after-talking-to-ruper.player: I notice there is a dwarf up in the tower there. Why is he up there?

standard-dialogue-after-talking-to-ruper.npc: I do believe that is none of your business, young scallyrumpit! Now kindly leave.

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-gr.npc: Thanks again for finding my pendant. I felt so lost without it.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Mihail, I'm trying to stay warm by this fire.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Mihail. I'm just trying to stay warm.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.npc: Arr? Be ye wantin' te go on account with our gang o' fillibusters?
The powder monkey be takin' a caulk after gettin' rowdy on bumboo, so there be plenty of room for ye.

standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.player: I'll just be over here if you need me.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy.npc: Wanna buy some clothes? Good quality, none of yer rags.

steps.player: I'll take a look.
No thanks.

steps.npc: Then what are you doin' in my shop? Move along.

options.text: Why does that shirt have a hole in it?

steps.player: Why does that shirt have a hole in it?

steps.npc: It's to put your head through.

steps.player: In the stomach? Isn't that an odd place for a neck hole?

steps.npc: Oh! It seems as if I must have slipped while cleaning it and put a bit of a hole in the front.

steps.npc: Making flour is pretty easy. First of all you need to get some grain. You can pick some from wheat fields. There is one just outside the Mill, but there are many others scattered across Gielinor. Feel free to pick wheat
from our field! There always seems to be plenty of wheat there.

steps.npc: Yes, or one of the other mills in Gielinor. They all work the same way. Just take your grain to the top floor of the mill (up two ladders, there are three floors including this one) and then place some grain into the hopper.
Then you need to start the grinding process by pulling the hopper lever. You can add more grain, but each time you add grain you have to pull the hopper lever again.

steps.player: So where does the flour go then?

steps.npc: The flour appears in this room here, you'll need a pot to put the flour into. One pot will hold the flour made by one load of grain

steps.text: Clay can be mined in many places. Try south west of Varrock or the crafting guild. See the crafting tutor upstairs in Lumbridge Castle for more information on what you can make with clay.
Rune Essence can only be mined at secret places... I don't know where these are but you can speak to the Duke of Lumbridge to find out more.

steps.npc: You can make all sorts of things from clay, if you have the crafting skill. Rune Essence is used for magic to cast spells.

steps.text: Rocks which yield copper ore can be found around here, and other places such as Al Kharid, Rimmington or Varrock mines. They're quite common.
Tin ore is much the same as copper. It can be found around this area as well as Varrock, Al Kharid and the Barbarian Village.
Iron can be mined around Rimmington, Al Kharid and Varrock. It's tricky to smelt though - see the boy at the furnace in Lumbridge for tips.
Look for this icon on your minimap to find the furnace.
You'll need to be a fairly good miner before you can start mining coal. You can find it in the Dwarf mine, Al Kharid and quite a few other places.
Silver can be mined to help you with your crafting. You can find it in the Crafting guild, Al Kharid and many other mines.
Gold requires quite a lot of experience in mining before you can successfully extract it from the rocks. It can be found in Al Kharid, the Crafting guild, Rimmington and other places.
Mithril and Adamantite rocks are fairly rare and require great skill to mine. You can find them in Al Kharid, the Dwarven mines, Lumbridge Swamps and other places.
Runite is the most prized of ores and is very rare. I'll leave you to find where to mine it.

The Bronze Pick is your basic tool of the trade. You can buy one from Bob's Axe shop very cheaply, that's north of here in Lumbridge, I also heard that exploring the castle walls may yield a surprise or two.
The Iron and Steel Picks are faster than the bronze pickaxe, but you will need to progress with your mining a little before you can use them. You can buy them from Nurmof in the Dwarven mines.
Mithril, Adamantite, and Rune Picks may be used as you progress with your skill of mining. They can be obtained from Nurmof in the Dwarven mines.

steps.text: Keldagrim, our home!

steps.player: Can you take me there?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh no, we can't do that.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: We're far too busy.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: You have to keep busy, you see.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Always keep busy, is what our good father used to say.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Besides, there's been some weird going ons in the city.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't tell [him/her] that! None of [his/her] business!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Only fair if [he/she] wants to go into the city.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, they only just cleaned up the mess from the last little incident.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: So watch out if you ever do manage to travel to the city! Weird things could happen!

options.text: Any good spots to fish around here?

steps.player: Any good spots to fish around here?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Fish?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Fish?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What are fish?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: No fish around here.
After Fishing Contest:

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Say, you're the Fishing Champion, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That must be why you were talking about fish then...

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What are fish?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: But this water here, you see, it comes dripping down from above.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Molten snow, you see.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What are fish?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, they're these small wriggly things that live in the water.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: But they're not all small! Some can be large!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: And they don't breathe air.
After Fishing Contest:

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: But [player name] could tell you all about it! After all, [he's/she's] the Fishing Champion!

steps.player: Maybe later...

options.text: What are these mines used for?

steps.player: What are these mines used for?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: What does it look like they're used for?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Isn't it obvious?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: For mining of course!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: These mines are actually the territory of one of the eight major companies of the mining Consortium.
Before The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: Mining companies? Where are they at then?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, they all have their headquarters in the city.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: First floor of the palace.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: No need to give [him/her] directions.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: We haul all our goods to the city by ship, you see.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Since the mine carts don't come here.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: But because the river goes right to the city, this is just as easy.

options.text: Can you help me with this rock?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Can you help me with this rock down in the mines?
It seems to be unbreakable. I need to know why.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Say, is that Dondakan's rock?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: That big unbreakable rock?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That's what [he/she] said, isn't? Pay more attention!

steps.player: Yes, yes, that's the one.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Oh, you're not going to get through there I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: It's unbreakable, you see.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Dondakan's been there for...

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: How long would you say he's been there, Miotvednir?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Eighteen years, Derni, and not a year shorter!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: That's some dedication!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: But look at what it got him.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Nothing, that's what.

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: What material would break that rock?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: What material would break that rock? You know, the impenetrable one?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Well... have you tried a rune pickaxe?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: An adamantite tool?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What about a bronze pickaxe?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: A bronze pickaxe??

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: What good would that do?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Well, you never know...

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't you think that's the first thing they tried?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Hey, it was just a suggestion!

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: Do you know anyone named Rolad?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Do you know anyone named Rolad? Some kind of a dwarven scholar?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Sorry, doesn't ring a bell.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, I know Rolad!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, stop winding up the human, Dernu!

steps.player: Do you know where he is right now?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: No idea, why?

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: Dondakan wants to shoot me out of a cannon!
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Dondakan wants to shoot me out of a cannon!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Oh dear!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: How awful!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That's terrible!

steps.player: He thinks I'm actually going to fly through it and land on the other side.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That sounds a bit daft.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: How would that work?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: I think you're going to hurt your head.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Old Dondakan might have finally lost it.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: He was always obsessed with that rock.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: And gold.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Right, and gold.

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: Any tips on how to defeat an evil demon?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Any tips on how to defeat an evil demon?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: An evil demon, you say?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: I'd run away if I ever ran into an evil demon.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't be such a coward, Dernu!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Well, what would you do then?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I don't know, I've never encountered an evil demon.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: I once met a good demon though.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, what did he say?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: He gave me a puzzle box and then went off again.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I think you must have had too much dwarven stout in you.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Could be, could be, but there's no telling, is there?

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: I defeated the spirit of the rock!
options.condition: First time after Between a Rock...:

steps.player: I defeated the spirit of the rock!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: That's amazing!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That's fantastic!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What rock was that again?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Pay attention for once, Dernu! It's Dondakan's rock!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: That's quite impressive, Player. How did you manage to do that?

steps.player: Well, you see, I just-

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: What kind of question is that to ask? With [his/her/their] great might of course!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Or vast magical skills!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: No, you're more a ranger, aren't you Player?

steps.player: Actually, I-

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Anyway, this calls for a celebration.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, we should go down into Keldagrim to celebrate.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Tonight, of course, not now. We're on duty now.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Right... and I'm sure traffic here will pick up soon with that rock broken.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: I heard there's vast amount of gold inside!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: The company is going to be rich!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Now don't you go and discuss company business in front of this human, Dernu.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Right. Let's get back to work.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Anything else you wanted, Player?

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: I need some help with this statue...
options.condition: During The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: I need some help with this statue... King Alvis' statue, to be precise.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, what's the problem then?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: It was knocked down, remember? Parts of it nearly landed on our heads?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: A terrible noise it made too!
Before helping Blasidar:

steps.player: Never mind.

steps.text: While helping Blasidar:

steps.player: This sculptor has got me looking for a lot of items, you see.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Items eh?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: We love items.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Can't get enough of them.

steps.player: Well, can you he-

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: I got this puzzle box once, you know.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, not that story again.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: You have told that story before, Dernu.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Well forget about it then. I'll shut up if you don't want to hear about it.

steps.player: Never mind.

steps.text: After helping Blasidar:

steps.player: Well, the sculptor only needs to build the head now. But I need to get the Consortium to help me with that.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: The Consortium, you say?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: You're going to talk to the Consortium?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: My, you're certainly moving up in the dwarven world, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: What do you need us for then?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: We are but simple dwarves.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Especially you, Dernu.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Now now, Derni, there was no need for that.

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: I have rebuilt the statue for the [company name]!
options.condition: First time after The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: I have rebuilt the statue for the [company name]!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What, really?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Of course, really! Player wouldn't have said it otherwise, would [he/she/they]?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: And didn't you see Blasidar working on the statue?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, he was out there for quite a while.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That must have been a huge task.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Nothing's too difficult for old Blasidar.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: He truly is a master builder.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: We can all take an example to his hard work and dedication.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Speaking of, shouldn't we get back to work ourselves?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Quite right. Anything else you wanted, Player?

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: Do you know about this drunken dwarf...?
options.condition: During Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf:

steps.player: Do you know about this drunken dwarf...?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Drunken dwarf?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Yeah, we know a drunken dwarf!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: In fact we know plenty!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: There's this one really annoying dwarf though, he sometimes throws rocks at me for no reason.

steps.player: Yeah, tell me about it.
The one I mean is his relative, living in the northeast of Keldagrim. I wonder if you could help me with him.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Ah yes, him.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Such a sad case, poor fellow.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Who is he?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't you know anything?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Now now, there's no reason to get angry.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I suppose you're right. Well, he's a drunk dwarf that talks about kebabs a lot.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Has some pretty odd tales to tell too.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: And I understand he's the relative of that dwarf I mentioned earlier.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I hope that helped, Player?

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: I have this unforgettable tale to tell you!
options.condition: First time after Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf:

steps.player: I have this unforgettable tale to tell you!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: A tale!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: We love tales!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: We live for tales!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Like, there was this one time when I lost my spanner in the mines...

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Player wants to tell a tale!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: But my spanner... it's a very interesting tale you know.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: I think we've heard it before.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: It was pretty forgettable.

steps.player: Excuse me, do you want to hear my tale or not?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Happy to.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Would love to hear it.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: As long as it's better than my spanner story.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: So, what's your tale like?

steps.player: Ah, I errrr...
I seem to have forgotten.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Must have been pretty forgettable as well then.

steps.player: Never mind.
I must be off now, thanks for the chat.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: No problem!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Glad to be of service!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Come back any time!

options.text: Can I go for a ride?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride?

steps.text: If the player does not have 20 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Minecart rides are 20 coins.

steps.text: If the player has 20 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.text: (Lovakengj Minecart Network interface opens.)

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

options.text: Can I go for a ride?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride?

steps.npc: Of course.

steps.text: (Lovakengj Minecart Network interface opens.)

steps.player: I'm fine, thanks.

standard-dialogue-unlimited-ride-fee-ref.npc: As a loyal customer of the Lovakengj Minecart Network, you're entitled to this.
Now, can I help you today?

historical-dialogue-before-setting-up-th.npc: Hello, human. Can I help you?

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is the principal station of the Lovakengj Minecart Network. Once it's running, our people will be able to travel rapidly all across the city.

steps.player: Can I ride your minecart?

steps.text: If the player has a full inventory:

steps.npc: The network is for the citizens of Lovakengj only, though I'll let you use it if you help me first. Free up some inventory space if you're interested.

steps.text: Otherwise:

steps.npc: The network is for the citizens of Lovakengj only, though I'll let you use it if you help me first.

options.text: Alright, what do you need me to do?

steps.player: Alright, what do you need me to do?

steps.npc: The workers at the other stations got incorrect versions of the control scrolls, so they can't operate the minecarts. Please take these updated scrolls to them.

steps.text: Miriam gives you some control scrolls.

steps.npc: That's one scroll each for the Arceuus station, the Shayzien station, the Hosidius station, the Piscarilius station and the Quidamortem station.

options.text: Where do I need to go?

steps.player: Where do I need to go?

steps.npc: The Arceuus station is just next to the Arceuus Library, in the north of the city.
The Shayzien station is east of the Shayzien Encampment.
The Hosidius station is north of the Woodcutting Guild.
The Piscarilius station is south of the city, next to a small mine.
The Quidamortem station is at the peak of the mountain, deep in the Kebos Lowlands.

options.text: Can I go for a ride now?

steps.player: Can I go for a ride now?

steps.npc: No, you haven't unlocked any of the other stations yet.

options.text: Do I have to pay every time I use the carts?

steps.player: Do I have to pay every time I use the carts?

steps.npc: Hmmm... We normally charge 50 coins per ride. For 100,000 coins, you'll never have to pay again.

steps.player: 100,000 coins is a rip-off!

steps.npc: Take it or leave it, human! You may enjoy being about to ride our carts without having to carry coins every time.

steps.player: I'd rather not, thanks.

steps.npc: Can I do anything else for you, human?

steps.player: I'll get on with it.
I'm not interested.
I'm fine, thanks.

historical-dialogue-while-setting-up-the.npc: Some of my stations still require control scrolls.

options.text: Have you got any more scrolls?

steps.player: Have you got any more scrolls?

steps.text: Otherwise:

steps.npc: Here you go, human.

steps.npc: The Shayzien station is east of the Shayzien Encampment.

steps.text: If the player has not delivered a scroll to the Hosidius station:

steps.npc: The Hosidius station is north of the Woodcutting Guild.

steps.text: If the player has not delivered a scroll to the Piscarilius station:

steps.npc: The Piscarilius station is south of the city, next to a small mine.

steps.text: If the player has not delivered a scroll to the Quidamortem station:

options.text: Do I have to pay every time I use the carts?

steps.player: I'll get on with it.

historical-dialogue-while-setting-up-the.npc: No thanks, I don't want it back.

historical-dialogue-after-setting-up-the.npc: Thanks for delivering those control scrolls, human. What can I do for you today?
