Here, have this one. Just look after it this time.
Go on, use the soul fragment on the Obelisk.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-chargin.text: You charge the Soul Obelisk and weaken the enemy avatar.
Player starts running towards Nomad and talks to Nomad automatically.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Good job! Now that you have charged the Obelisk, the enemy avatar will have been weakened.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.text: Note the display in the top-left of the screen. See how the red avatar's strength has decreased.
The number shown here represents the percentage of your damage that the avatar will block.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.player: So, once I've charged the Obelisk, can I just kick back and wait for the end of the game?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Ha! I think not! I'm not about to reward those who don't put the effort in!

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.text: Note the orange bar in the top-left of the screen. This bar represents how active you have been during the game.
Over the course of the battle, the bar will slowly drain. Should the bar drain completely you will be removed from the game due to your inactivity.
You can refill the bar by performing actions in the game, such as dealing damage or charging the Obelisk.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.player: Oh well. Say, do you think the enemy avatar minds us weakening it like this?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Hmm, why don't we go find out?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.text: The screen fades to black. The player and Nomad are now by the red team's avatar area.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: So, here we are in the enemy base.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.player: Is that the enemy avatar over there?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Yeah, and it looks like you made it pretty mad.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.player: What? You're the one that told me to weaken it!

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Ha! Don't worry - I won't let it kill you.
Of course, that doesn't mean I won't kill you.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.text: Nomad casts a slow projectile Iban's Blast spell without an Iban's staff at the player, with the sound of a trident of the swamp spell cast, instantly killing the player, taking the player back to the blue team's base in the form of a ghost.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-ghost.text: If the player doesn't do anything for 15 seconds:

steps.text: The player returns to life.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.text: When you die in Soul Wars, you become a ghost.
After 15 seconds as a ghost, you return to life and can carry on with the fight.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.npc: At least it wasn't permanent! Think of it as an opportunity to learn.
The other team will be after you and any soul fragments you have collected, after all.
I needed to show you what happens when you fall in battle.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.player: Did you turn me into a ghost?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.npc: Not exactly. The Soul Obelisk tried to claim your soul, as it does with all who perish in the battleground.
Only my power brought you here, and returned you to life.
You're more useful to me alive... for now.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.player: Are there any other painful things to learn about this place?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.npc: There is much more to this place, but you don't need to know about it yet.
If you want to learn more, I can give you a Soul Wars guide upon our return to the waiting area.
Use the large blue portal at the back of this graveyard to return to the waiting area. Why not sign up for a battle while you're there?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-leaving.npc: Use the portal over there to return to the waiting area. I'll see you on the other side!

They say that an object of great power was once stored in this very cave. Apparently, the presence of this object created the daeyalt deposits.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-if-th.player: I see. What is the daeyalt used for?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-if-th.npc: Its main use is as a key component in the vampyrification process. There's other uses though. It can be used to create runes, for example.
The essence mined by the slaves is reserved. If you want some, you'll have to mine your own.
If you do choose to mine the deposits, you should know that the daeyalt shards you'll get are useless on their own. They'll need converting into essence to be used.
Luckily for you, I can provide that service.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: Quickly, tell me - is it still there?
The THING, the THING! It was just outside my house! Has it gone away yet? Or is it still lurking out there, waiting for me to go outside?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: I didn't see any THING out there, just a couple of guards. What did it look like?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: Ohhhh, it was HORRIBLE! It was an enormous THING, with TEETH and EYES and... and... and THINGS!

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: Um... would you care to be more specific?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: I can't. I only saw it in the dark.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: You only saw this THING in the dark?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: I was sleeping peacefully one night, when suddenly I woke up and saw it through the window. It was LOOKING at me! I haven't dared go out since then. It's had me trapped in here for days! I've packed my
bags so I can escape, but the THING's still out there waiting for me to come out! If I have to stay in here much longer I'll go mad! MAD!! MAD!!!

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: There's no THING outside. Just come out and get some fresh air before you go funny in the head.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: You want me to go outside?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: I think you might just have dreamed about the THING.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: You want me to believe that it's not real?
No! No! I know what you are! You're in league with the THING! It keeps sending people in here to trick me into going outside! They keep stealing from me too! GO AWAY!

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: I'm not trying to trick you!

steps.player: What's that board for?

steps.npc: The one behind me? We use it to keep track of fallen stars and those that find them.

steps.text: If the player hasn't found a fallen star before:

steps.player: Fallen stars?

steps.npc: That's right. From time to time, stars fall from the sky and land somewhere in Gielinor.
Whenever one does, we make a note on the board. If someone finds it, we note their name as well.

steps.player: I see. And how do people find them?

steps.npc: There's a lot of amateur astronomers out there. Many of them have small telescopes in their homes. They use them to work out when a star is going to fall.

steps.player: Could I do that?

steps.npc: I imagine so. Just get yourself a telescope and look out for stars.

steps.player: Awesome. I might just give it a go.

steps.npc: Good luck. If you're interested, I hear there's a dwarf at the Mining Guild who's keen on gathering stardust. If you find some, he might be willing to trade with you.

steps.player: Good to know. Thanks.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.player: Where does the blood come from?

steps.npc: Throughout the generations, countless people of this land have perished in times of strife, with their bodies left to rot where they fell.
Some were slain by the deadly creatures that roam the land; others perished at the hands of their fellow citizens during the wars of this land.
Their blood flowed into the soil, pooling and percolating unseen in the dark, as the power of the Altar drew it to this sacred place to form the River.

steps.player: Why are you here?

steps.npc: The blood is the blood of Kourend's citizens. It is fitting that we honour their memory.
Also, it smells so good.

options.text: I'll leave you to enjoy the view.

steps.player: I'll leave you to enjoy the view.

historical-dialogue-as-enoch.speaker: Enoch
historical-dialogue-as-enoch.text: I see the river foaming with much blood.

options.text: Where does the blood come from?
I'll leave you to enjoy the view.

before-the-fremennik-trials.player: Hello there. So you're a bard?

before-the-fremennik-trials.npc: I am afraid I cannot speak to outerlanders. Besides, I am busy composing an epic.

after-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Hello again to you [Fremennik name]. Us bards should stick together, what?

steps.player: About the Music Cape...

steps.text: If the player has unlocked all the songs:

steps.player: I believe you are the person to talk to if I want to get a Music Cape?

steps.npc: That's right! If you know that then you'll also know that they cost 99000 coins.

steps.player: No, I hadn't heard that.

steps.npc: Well, they do.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: Have fun with it.

steps.text: Player receives a Music cape and Music hood in exchange for 99,000 coins.
If the player does not have at least 99,000 coins in their inventory:

steps.player: I don't have that much at the moment.

steps.npc: Save up some more then!

steps.player: Yes, I know.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins in their inventory:
If the player does not have at least 99,000 coins in their inventory:

steps.player: May I have another hood for my cape, please?

steps.npc: Most certainly, and free of charge!

steps.text: The bard hands you another hood for your cape.
If the player has not unlocked all songs:

steps.player: I believe you are the person to talk to if I want to get a Music Cape?

steps.npc: Yes, but you don't know all of the music in the land.

options.text: Do you know any great stories about Basilisk Jaws?
options.condition: If the player has a basilisk jaw in their inventory and has not learned about the story yet:

steps.player: Do you know any great stories about Basilisk Jaws?

steps.npc: Why do you ask?

steps.text: You show the Basilisk Jaw to Olaf.

steps.npc: Oh my! This must be the jaw of a legendary Basilisk Knight. There's a great song about how the Fremennik warriors of old would use these jaws to enhance their helmets.

steps.player: I see. I have a nice helmet that Neitiznot's Burgher gave to me. I bet it would work well with that.

steps.text: (The player can now create Neitiznot faceguards.)

steps.npc: I'm sure it would, [Fremennik name]. Now, do you want to hear the song?

steps.player: Err... I think I'll pass. Thanks for the help though.

options.text: Can I learn to play my lyre again?

steps.player: I was wondering... Can I learn to play my lyre again?

steps.npc: Well, that is an interesting question. Let me let you into a little secret. If you make another offering to Fossegrimen you will learn a secret melody.

steps.player: What kind of melody?

steps.npc: It is the song of Rellekka. When you play it, it will bring you back to this town wherever you are in this world.
We often go adventuring with bards for precisely this reason; No matter where we have ended up we can return safe and sound to home.

steps.player: Thanks Olaf!

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: Get lost, outlander! I've no time for you!

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.player: It's me, [player name]. What are you doing out here?

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: Nothing... Just carving these horribly broken pieces of driftwood.

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: Wait! Would you do me a favour?

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: Look, you see that heap of driftwood over there? That is my ship, and all that is left of my one shot at making my ancestors proud of me.

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: My family have always been great explorers and seafarers, and I recently set off on my maiden voyage.

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: However, a big storm - yes, a huge storm in fact - blew my ship onto the rocks. Three times.

talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-if-the-fremennik-trials-.text: I've been sitting here ever since, trying to think of a way to make my family proud, and if you will help me...I think I have a way.

steps.player: Okay, I'll help you out.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Thank you! I don't have much apart from my carvings, some driftwood and the map that I was following when I had my little...

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: ...accident.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: If you help me out, then I'll gladly hand it over.

steps.player: So, what is your plan?

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Well, I have a little food left, although it's a little briny.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: If you take a couple of carvings to my wife and son in the village over the hill and tell them that I sent you with them from a distant island, then I can wait out here for a week or so before returning.

steps.player: Alright, hand me over the carvings and I'll be on my way.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Well, none of these are any good. I'll need some fresh wood from a decent tree.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: When I was swimming for my life I saw an odd-looking windswept tree to the east of here, up that cliff.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Could you bring me some of that wood so I can work it?

steps.player: Wow, you must have pretty good eyes to be able to see a single tree from the water during a heavy storm.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Yes...great eyes...they run in the family.

steps.player: Possibly later, when you don't smell so damp.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Bah! Well, if you aren't going to help, do me a favour and jump off that cliff!

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-again-wi.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-again-wi.text: So... Got the logs for me yet?

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-again-wi.player: Not yet. I just popped back to see how you were doing.

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-again-wi.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-again-wi.text: Still cold. Still damp. 'Bout average, really.

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.player: Olaf, I cut some logs from the tree. Here's the wood.

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.text: Wonderful! I'll carve them up now.

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.text: This is for my wife, Ingrid. I'm sure she will love it. Tell her it's tribal or something.

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.text: And this one is for my son, Volf. Kids love planks in my experience. Tell him I said hello.

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.player: Alright. They live in Rellekka, right?

talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-talking-to-olaf-with-the.text: Yes. Hurry back! And don't forget the story: I'm not here, I'm someplace far away.

delivering-the-presents-talking-to-olaf-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
delivering-the-presents-talking-to-olaf-.text: So, how did my wife like her carving?
If Ingrid's present has not been delivered yet:

steps.player: I don't know... I've still got it.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Well, hurry up and give it to her then!

delivering-the-presents-talking-to-olaf-.text: If Ingrid's present has been delivered:

steps.player: She was very happy with it!

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Wonderful!

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: I wish i could see her again...

steps.player: Well, if this plan works out you will be able too, right?

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Yes, you're right.

delivering-the-presents-talking-to-olaf-.text: If Volf's present has not been delivered yet:

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Did my son like his present? I'll bet he was thrilled.

steps.player: I'll bet he will be... but I've still got it.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Well, take your time over it, why don't you.

delivering-the-presents-talking-to-olaf-.text: If Volf's present has been delivered:

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Did my son like his present? I'll bet he was thrilled.

steps.player: Yes, he was thrilled with it!

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: I'll bet he's grown since I left, those many, many, many...hours ago.

steps.player: That's doubtful, unless magic is involved.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: You have a good point. I can't wait to get back.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.player: Excuse me, but are you Ingrid? The same Ingrid that is married to Olaf Hradson?

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.speaker: Ingrid Hradson
delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.text: Yes I am. Why do you ask?

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.player: I am a friend of your husband. He sent me here with a gift for you.
An expensive, exotic gift from the far-flung and tropical shores of the Island of Obscurity.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.speaker: Ingrid Hradson
delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.text: How wonderful! I assumed from the way the big oaf always referred to the rigging as 'big strings' that he couldn't navigate his way out of a soggy paper bag. So, can I see the gift he sent?

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.player: Certainly! Here it is. He sends his best wishes along with it.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.speaker: Ingrid Hradson
delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.text: I see. It looks like a log with 'Olaf was here' carved in it.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.player: It's tribal! Very tribal! I watched the natives carve it myself.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.speaker: Ingrid Hradson
delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.text: Well, since you have come such a long way, you can have this. I baked it this morning, so it's still nice and fresh.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.player: Oh, thank you! Enjoy your Obscurian Tribal Artefact(tm). It has a million-and-one uses!

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.speaker: Ingrid Hradson
delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.text: Hello again! Have you any word from my husband?

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.player: Err, no, not yet. It takes a while for the messages to reach me, you know.

delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.speaker: Ingrid Hradson
delivering-the-presents-ingrid-s-present.text: Well, when you do, tell him we'll be more than happy to see him again.

delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present.player: No, but I do know your father. He sent me with a present for you from, err...

delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present.speaker: Volf Olafson
delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present.text: Oh! That was fast! He only set off recently, and I was wondering how he was doing. So, where is this gift?

delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present.player: Very valuable. Have a nice time!

delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present.speaker: Volf Olafson
delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present.text: Wait! Here, take this. I was going to have it for my lunch, but I suppose you can have it in payment.

delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present-t.speaker: Volf Olafson
delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present-t.text: Hello again! Does my father send any word...or treasures like before?

delivering-the-presents-volf-s-present-t.player: Not today, but if he does, you will be the first to know.

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.player: I delivered your carvings as you asked. Your family would like to see you again.
Here, let me get you to the village before you freeze to death.

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.text: I won't...go...anywhere. I don't...care if I...freeze.

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.player: Well, at least give me the map like you promised!

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.text: So...very...cold. Almost cold enough to tear up an old map with my fevered shivering. Cough, cough.
You managed to get the fire going!

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.player: Well, I'm glad you're happy. Can I have that map now?

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.text: Well, okay...but could I have a little of that food first? I've had nothing but seaweed and biscuits for the past week.

options.text: Alright, here, have some food. Now give me the map.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Oh... That was a banquet compared to the stuff I've been living off.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Look, I have a bit of a confession. I think that the map may well be cursed.

steps.player: What? All this running about for a cursed map! Couldn't you have made this little revelation before I fed you?

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Look, I'm sorry, okay. Remember that I followed this map and ended up on the rocks.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: It may be nothing, after all, but I think you should be very careful if you go looking for the treasure.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Well, regardless, you've more than earned this map. It was the last one my grandfather, Sven the Helmsman, ever made.

steps.player: Not a chance.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Okay, okay, I was only asking.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: Well, regardless, you've more than earned this map. It was the last one my grandfather, Sven the Helmsman, ever made.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: It is supposed to show the location of one of his stashes of treasure, but I have never been able to decipher the strange, runic inscriptions that point the way.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: I wish you luck!

steps.player: Well, thanks. What will you do now?

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: I'll sit here and practice carving.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: If you pass this way again, I'll be glad if you drop my next load of work off with my family.

steps.speaker: Olaf Hradson
steps.text: That or bring me some food before I starve. Whichever.
Olaf hands you the map.

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.text: Hey! I'm trying to carve and you're standing in my light! Move it!

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.player: Olaf, I seem to have lost your map, can I have another?

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.text: You lost the treasured map of Sven the Helmsman? How dare you!

talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.speaker: Olaf Hradson
talking-to-olaf-after-the-presents-have-.text: You'd best take better care of this one, or else!

entering-the-brine-rat-cavern-when-diggi.text: ...and fall into a dark and slimy pit!

entering-the-brine-rat-cavern-attempting.text: This 'wall' has some disks set into it showing a picture and some levers. I should try pulling the levers to see what happens.

entering-the-brine-rat-cavern-opening-th.text: You open the chest and the vengeful spirit of a fremennik captain appears!
You find a note in the chest...

while-possessed.npc: It's mine. You can't have it, we found it!

steps.player: What have you found?

steps.npc: Not dragonstones. I like dragonstones, that's why I came here. However, I found a valuable coin instead, it speaks to me... but you can't have it! It's precious to me!

options.text: I don't want it, I have something better.

steps.player: I don't want it, I have something better.

steps.npc: What is it? Is it dragonstones? I like dragonstones!

steps.speaker: Olbertus (possessed)
steps.text: Ask it for five! It looks rich!

steps.npc: Five? Will it give us five?

steps.text: If the player has less than five dragonstones:

steps.player: No. I don't have five dragonstones.

steps.npc: Well then we are not interested!

steps.text: If the player has five dragonstones:

steps.player: Yes. I have five dragonstones, tell you what, I'll trade you them for that coin you found.

steps.npc: Yes! Yes! We'll trade it for the dragonstones.

steps.speaker: Olbertus (possessed)
steps.text: No we will not! It is too precious!

steps.npc: But why? I like dragonstones...

steps.speaker: Olbertus (possessed)
steps.text: It is trying to trick us! Evil, nasty creature it is. Do not listen to it!

steps.npc: But it seems nice enough...

steps.player: I am standing right here, you know? You really are crazy. Yes, I'll give you five! Do we have a deal or not?

steps.npc: Yes! Yes!

steps.text: You give Olbertus a dragonstone and receive a very worn coin in return.

steps.npc: Thanks for helping me, I'm not sure what would have happened if I had continued to listen to the voices in my head.
I took that coin from the Stone Relief in the Crypt of the Moon and trapped my friend Eodan in a secret room behind the relief. Could you return the coin to the relief and set him free?

options.text: No, don't give him your dragonstones.

steps.player: On second thoughts, I'll keep it for myself.

options.text: Since it's valuable, I think I'll just just kill you for it.

steps.player: Since it's valuable, I think I'll just just kill you for it.

steps.npc: Please! No!

steps.text: This is a dangerous fight, you will lose your items on death.

steps.npc: Foolish decision!

steps.text: Olbertus transforms into a Shaeded Beast, and curses the Altar, rendering it unusable.

steps.speaker: Shaeded Beast
steps.text: I require this one alive human!

steps.player: Just kidding!
You're crazy!

after-being-freed-from-possession-if-the.npc: Thanks for helping me, I'm not sure what would have happened if I had continued to listen to the voices in my head.
I took that coin from the Stone Relief in the Crypt of the Moon and trapped my friend Eodan in a secret room behind the relief. Could you return the coin to the relief and set him free?
It appears that when I stole the coin, the creature possessed me.
I took that coin from the Stone Relief in the Crypt of the Moon and trapped my friend Eodan in a secret room behind the relief. Could you return the coin to the relief and set him free?

reclaiming-the-coin-if-the-player-traded.npc: I'm glad I no longer have that coin. I'm not sure what would have happened if I had continued to listen to the voices in my head.
For some reason the coin returned to me. Here, take it before it corrupts me again!
I took that coin from the Stone Relief in the Crypt of the Moon and trapped my friend Eodan in a secret room behind the relief. Could you return the coin to the relief and set him free?

reclaiming-the-coin-if-the-player-chose-.npc: It appears that when I stole the coin, the creature possessed me.
For some reason the coin returned to me. Here, take it before it corrupts me again!
I took that coin from the Stone Relief in the Crypt of the Moon and trapped my friend Eodan in a secret room behind the relief. Could you return the coin to the relief and set him free?

after-speaking-to-eodan.npc: I'm glad I no longer have that coin. I'm not sure what would have happened if I had continued to listen the voices in my head.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Hmph! Why? What do I know? I'm just an old man; what would anyone want with an old man?

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.player: I'm lost... Can you help me?

steps.npc: Hmph! Who says I'm not lost, eh? Ever think of that, did you?
In a rush to find out all the answers, not thinking for a second that someone else might be just as lost, if not more lost, than you! And what do you care about them, huh?

options.text: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.npc: Hmph! Why should I know about the Myreque, eh? What use have they ever been to me, huh? I ask you!

steps.player: Can you help me?

steps.npc: Hmph! What makes you think that I can help you, eh? Do I look like a fountain of knowledge, eh? Do I?

steps.player: Well, you've helped me before! You said something about symbols? To find the Myreque!

steps.npc: Hmph! Yes of course, that's how to get to them. Follow the symbols.

steps.player: Which symbols?

steps.npc: The symbol of the Myreque - the silver sickle!

steps.player: Oh, and where would that be then?

steps.npc: Around and about; it should be an aid.

steps.player: Okay, thanks

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?
Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.npc: Hmph! Why should I know about the Myreque, eh? What use have they ever been to me, huh? I ask you!

steps.player: But they live right under your house?

steps.npc: Hmph! Suppose they do. Stupid Myreque...

steps.player: Can you help me?

steps.npc: Hmph! What makes you think that I can help you, eh? Do I look like a fountain of knowledge, eh? Do I?

steps.player: Well, you've helped me before! You helped me find the Myreque!

steps.npc: Hmph! Yes of course, follow the symbols and all that. Pointless now though, they're right below us. Hmph!

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: I'm lost... Can you help me?
Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.player: Do you know about the Myreque?

steps.npc: Hmph! Dead! That's what I know about the Myreque. You're lucky to not be dead as well. Don't talk about them any more!

steps.player: Can you help me?

steps.npc: Hmph! What makes you think that I can help you, eh? Do I look like a fountain of knowledge, eh? Do I?

steps.player: Well, you've helped me before! You helped me find the Myreque!

steps.npc: Hmph! Yes of course, follow the symbols and all that. Pointless now though, they're all dead! Hmph!

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

standard-dialogue-after-ivan-leaves-the-.text: If the player has no tomes to reclaim:

steps.player: Hello again!

standard-dialogue-after-ivan-leaves-the-.text: If the player has a tome to reclaim:

steps.npc: Oh, it's you. That lad left a tome here for you. Take them with you so I don't have to keep looking after them like some librarian.

steps.player: Thank you.

standard-dialogue-after-ivan-leaves-the-.text: If the player has multiple tomes to reclaim:

steps.npc: Oh, it's you. That lad left some tomes here for you. Take them with you so I don't have to keep looking after them like some librarian.

steps.player: Thank you.
I need some equipment.

steps.npc: Well, you're not having it for free. Cough up.

steps.player: I need another Drakan's Medallion.

steps.text: With a full inventory:

steps.npc: Hmph! And where do you plan to put it? Make some room first!
Oh, you need one do you? Wouldn't hurt you to think about what I might need, would it? Hmph! Still, s'pose I promised the lad I'd help you out.

steps.text: If the player reclaims one medallion:
Old Man Ral gives you another medallion.
If the player reclaims multiple medallions:
Old Man Ral gives you [number] medallions.

steps.player: I'd better be off.

steps.npc: Hmph!

treasure-trails-master.text: Old Man Ral hands you a puzzlebox!

treasure-trails-master-if-inventory-is-f.npc: Please make yourself some space, I have something for you.

steps.npc: That doesn't look solved to me.
Well done [player name]. Here you go.

steps.text: You've obtained [another clue scroll/a casket]!

standard-dialogue.npc: What brings you here, young [man/lady/one]?

steps.player: I'm just wandering around.

steps.npc: Oh, that's nice. I used to wander around, back when my legs were better. So long ago.

steps.player: Nothing, really.

steps.npc: That's the trouble with young people these days. Not my boy, though. He's a good boy, always working. That's why he never visits. Run along now, young [man/lady/one].

talking-to-old-man-yarlo-after-the-quest.npc: Hello again, young [man/lady/one]. You really did wonders for my little home. I feel so much happier living here now.

options.text: That's good to hear. Goodbye now.

steps.player: That's good to hear. Goodbye now.

standard-dialogue.npc: I've been better...

steps.player: What happened to your foot?

steps.npc: I was minding my own business in that abandoned shack for the night and suddenly I could hear...

steps.player: A g-g-g-ghost?!

steps.npc: No... Don't interrupt!
Where was I?
That was it... a faint sound... wind chimes...

steps.player: Please don't tell me you were attacked by the wind.

steps.npc: What did I say about interruptions?

steps.player: Sorry.

steps.npc: The chiming grew louder and started to sound like the knocking of bones. I was in the bed hiding under the moth-eaten sheet - ignorance is bliss, y'know? - and suddenly the sheet was pulled off of me and there was
a-

steps.player: A skeleton!

steps.npc: I SAID NO INTER- Oh yes, that's correct... Skeletons. Two of the blighters.

steps.player: Well, you seem to have got away in one piece!

steps.npc: One piece?! Do you not-
THE BONEY BLIGHTER BIT MY FOOT!

steps.player: Sorry... You didn't leave anything behind did you? I'm a brave adventurer! I'm sure I can pry whatever it is from their malicious mitts.

steps.npc: A few pots, but without my tools they won'y do me any good.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Me? Just a tinker with nothing to trade.

steps.player: What happened to your wares?

steps.npc: A tinker doesn't get the respect that they used to... Gah! A thief took my bag in the night, they took everything.

steps.player: Sorry to hear you've had some bad luck of late, did you lose much?

steps.npc: Bits and pieces, nothing too important I s'pose... An old pan flute, a dirty book and a charred skull.

steps.player: Hmm.

steps.npc: That's all in the past now, anyway... I'm afraid I can't help you.

steps.player: That's alright, I need no help.

steps.npc: Didn't someone send you for the pots?

steps.player: Nope, just exploring...

steps.npc: Well, if anyone asks... I'm dead!

steps.player: Bye.

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.player: Are you the tinker this entry mentions?

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.npc: Oh, me? Oh my... Goodness gracious what...
Well, I s'pose that was me...
How did you find me!? Was it you?

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.player: Was it me what? I just found this journal... I didn't write it.

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.npc: I remember this day... How could I forget.
Are you saying the man I sold those trinkets to was the king?!
Those were dark objects, corrupted with powerful magic. Dark magic.

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.player: Well, it's all in the past now. I don't think there's any reason to worry about it.

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.npc: No, no, no... this ain't good. They'll find me.

using-items-on-him-kharedst-s-memoirs-wi.player: Well if I find out anything useful, I'll come let you know, alright?

using-items-on-him-any-item-worth-one-mi.player: No, I didn't mean for you to keep it.

using-items-on-him-any-item-worth-one-mi.npc: Then why are you handing it to me?

steps.player: Existential Crisis?

steps.npc: It'll pass! Anyhow, I'll be seeing you.

steps.player: Yeah...

standard-dialogue-before-ghosts-ahoy.player: Don't be silly - half the ship's missing!

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Hello traveller, do you know what this is?

steps.player: It looks like a monument.

steps.npc: Yes. I served in the military for 30 years. This monument always reminds me of my days in the army.

standard-dialogue.npc: Oh, hello! I was just trying to discover the properties of these magical stones you call 'runes', and trying to make some devices to harness their power.

steps.player: What have you discovered?

steps.npc: Oh, it's terribly exciting! Let me explain...

steps.player: What have you made?

steps.npc: The only thing I've been able to make so far is this. I call it the moving-over-distance sphere.

steps.player: What is it?

steps.npc: Well, I was experimenting with these blue runes, the ones you call 'law' runes. They have a strange property of being able to move instantly from one place to another.
I know; I couldn't believe it either!
I found that whenever I prepared powdered law runes in a certain way and then threw them on the ground, I would appear somewhere else in the city.

steps.text: So, I made this sphere. It's a glass ball coated with powdered law runes, prepared in a special way.

steps.npc: I asked Zanik to test it, and she said that wherever she was in the caves, even if she went to the surface, whenever she smashed the sphere on the ground she would appear back in the city!
I can see how it might be useful, but I wish I knew more about how it worked...

steps.player: Can I buy one?

steps.npc: Oh, I can make one for you if you like. You'll need to give me two law runes and a piece of molten glass.

steps.player: I'll have to go and get some then.
Goodbye!

steps.npc: Oh, er, goodbye. Now, where was I...
