lacking-the-requirements-for-rum-deal.npc: I may have a quest, but you don't look like you'd be able to handle the kind of monsters I have problems with.

starting-rum-deal.npc: Yeah, I do, as a matter of fact!
I am a poor, dispossessed nobleman, forced by circumstance to lurk in the middle of nowhere, soliciting help from passers-by.
You see, my fiendish half-brother has seized my estates and forced me into exile.
The simple lemon farmers suffer under his tyrannous yoke, and only a brave adventurer can lift his iron boot from the neck of the poor.
To reclaim my lands I will need to have my family sword returned to me so that I may present it as proof of my rulership.
Will you help me find my family sword?

steps.player: No, I don't think I'll help you out this time.

steps.npc: Look, I think I'll wait here for someone a little more... you know...
...heroic.

starting-rum-deal-talking-to-pirate-pete.player: Had any luck finding someone to slay the demon?

starting-rum-deal-talking-to-pirate-pete.npc: Oh! Yes! The demon, with the oppression and stuff!

starting-rum-deal-talking-to-pirate-afte.npc: So, what brings you down here today?

options.text: I've decided to help you for free.

steps.player: I've decided to help you for free! I will dispose of this evil half-brother of yours and leave you what little money is left to feed your family.

steps.npc: Wonderful! Just pick up your diversion and we'll leave!

steps.player: What diversion?

standard-dialogue.npc: Yes, you owe me some money.

standard-dialogue.text: If the player is on the dock north of Port Phasmatys:

steps.npc: Want a lift to Braindeath Island?

steps.player: Well, possibly, but could I go to Mos Le'Harmless instead?

steps.npc: Nope. It's Braindeath island or nothing. Interested?

standard-dialogue.text: If player is on Braindeath Island:

steps.npc: Want a lift to Port Phasmatys?

steps.player: Okay!

steps.npc: All right. I'll need to use my Magical Teleporting Bottle.

steps.player: Magical Teleporting Bottle?

steps.npc: Yes. Just turn around three times, then clap your hands and say the place you want to go.

steps.player: This I have to see.
Oh well, here goes.
One...

steps.npc: Would you like a hand with your stuff? You seemed to have dropped something.

steps.player: Where?

steps.npc: All right. You know that it's going to cost extra to take your friend as well, right?

steps.player: What friend?

steps.npc: Certainly. By the way, you have a spider in your hair.

steps.player: Oh no! Get it out, get it out!

steps.npc: Sure, turn around and I'll get it for you.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.npc: Well I'll be more than happy to...
Egad! Did you see that?

steps.player: What? Where?

steps.text: Pirate Pete hits the player on the head.

steps.player: OW!

steps.text: Fades to black, player appears on Braindeath Island.

steps.player: Ooooh... my head...

steps.npc: Are you ok? You, errr...
...missed your mouth while drinking from a bottle. Hence the bottle-shaped bruises.
...slipped and slid into a brick wall.
...managed to fall onto my boot while I was practicing kicking.
...hit your head on my oars while I was rowing over.
Twice.

steps.player: Wow... I'm lucky I wasn't seriously hurt!
Not now.
I'm getting an awful headache talking to you. Any idea why?

steps.npc: No idea whatsoever.

options.text: Why do I get a headache every time I see you?

steps.player: Why do I get a headache every time I see you?

steps.npc: Well, it's possibly the weight of all of your expensive items giving you a sore back.
As a doctor I can tell you that sometimes a bad back can manifest as a headache.

steps.player: You're a doctor?

steps.npc: I'm on a break.
Regardless, I can tell you that if you hand me your most expensive items, then the pain will disappear.
CoughonceyouturnaroundagainCough!

steps.player: What was that last bit?

steps.npc: Nothing...

options.text: Are you any relation to Party Pete?

steps.player: Are you any relation to Party Pete?

steps.npc: Yes I am, he's my cousin.

steps.player: Well, you don't sound too happy about it. What happened?

steps.npc: Well, I arranged with all my friends to have a party at his place.
But then I humiliated myself by trying to dance with the knights.
All of them collapsed on me in a horrific, jangling pile.
I tried to salvage the night by having all the balloons come down...

steps.player: So what happened?

steps.npc: I didn't know that someone had swapped the balloons with cannonballs!
The casualties were horrific...
That was the worst fifth birthday party in the history of the world.

steps.player: I'm sure it wasn't that bad.

steps.npc: Not according to the Official History of Gielinor!
Every edition... the pictures bring it all back...

steps.player: Ouch...

treasure-trails-hard.npc: Please solve this for me. I have other things to be thinking about.

steps.speaker: Redbeard Frank
steps.text: Arr, that's the spirit!

steps.player: Not right now.

steps.speaker: Redbeard Frank
steps.text: Fair enough. I'll still be here and thirsty whenever you feel like helpin' out.

visiting-karamja-talking-to-luthas.speaker: Luthas
visiting-karamja-talking-to-luthas.text: Hello I'm Luthas, I run the banana plantation here.

options.text: Could you offer me employment on your plantation?

steps.player: Could you offer me employment on your plantation?

steps.speaker: Luthas
steps.text: Yes, I can sort something out. There's a crate ready to be loaded onto the ship.

steps.speaker: Luthas
steps.text: You wouldn't believe the demand for bananas from Wydin's shop over in Port Sarim. I think this is the third crate I've shipped him this month..

steps.speaker: Luthas
steps.text: If you could fill it up with bananas, I'll pay you 30 gold.

options.text: That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

steps.player: That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

steps.speaker: Luthas
steps.text: Well I know her pretty well. She doesn't cause me any trouble any more.

steps.speaker: Luthas
steps.text: She doesn't even search my export crates any more. She knows they only contain bananas.

steps.player: Really? How interesting. Whereabouts do you send those to?

steps.speaker: Luthas
steps.text: There is a little shop over in Port Sarim that buys them up by the crate. I believe it is run by a man called Wydin.

steps.text: You pack a banana into the crate.

steps.text: You pack all your bananas into the crate.

steps.text: The crate is already full.

steps.text: You stash the rum in the crate.

steps.text: There's already some rum in here...

steps.text: There is also some rum stashed in here too.

visiting-karamja-talking-to-luthas-after.player: I've filled a crate with bananas.

options.text: Will you pay me for another crate full?

options.text: Thank you, I'll be on my way

options.text: So where are these bananas going to be delivered to?

options.text: That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

options.text: Search away. I have nothing to hide.

steps.player: Search away. I have nothing to hide.

steps.text: Aha, trying to smuggle rum are we?

steps.text: This is not the Karamja rum we are looking for.

steps.player: Drat...

steps.text: You will need to try again.

steps.text: Well you've got some odd stuff, but it's all legal. Now you need to pay a boarding charge of 30 coins.

steps.player: Okay.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have 30 coins:

options.text: You're not putting your hands on my things!

steps.text: You're not getting on this ship then.

options.text: Does Karamja have unusual customs then?

steps.speaker: Wydin

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond.speaker: Edmond
starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond.text: Sorry, I can't stop to talk...

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond.speaker: Edmond
starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond.text: I've got to find my daughter. I pray that she is still alive...

steps.player: What's happened to her?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Elena's a healer. Three weeks ago she managed to cross the wall into West Ardougne. No one's allowed to cross the wall in case they spread the plague.

steps.player: Plague?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Not that long ago, West Ardougne was hit by a deadly plague. They had the wall built to try and keep it contained. No one is allowed to enter the city now apart from the mourners.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: They say the plague is a horrible way to go... That's why Elena felt she had to go help. She said she'd be gone for a few days but we've heard nothing since.

steps.player: Maybe I could help find her?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Really, would you? I've been working on a plan to get into West Ardougne, but I'm too old and tired to carry it through. But you on the other hand, you should have no problem.

steps.prompt: Start the Plague City quest?

steps.player: Where should I start?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: If you're going into West Ardougne you'll need protection from the plague. My wife made a special gas mask for Elena with dwellberries rubbed into it.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: They help to repel the plague apparently. We need some more though...

steps.player: Where can I find these dwellberries?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: The only place I know of is McGrubor's Wood, just west of Seers' Village. The berries are bright blue so they're easy to spot.

steps.player: Okay, I'll go and get some.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: The foresters keep a close eye on it, but there is a back way in.

steps.player: On second thoughts, I'd better not.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Well if you hear anything about Elena please tell me.

steps.player: I will. Goodbye.
Well, good luck finding her.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.speaker: Alrena

Alrena has given you a gas mask.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.text: I'll make a spare mask for you in case you lose that one. I'll hide it in the cupboard in case the mourners come looking.

starting-the-quest-searching-the-cupboar.text: If the player does not have the gas mask:

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.speaker: Alrena
starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.text: Hello darling, I think Edmond had a good idea of how to get into West Ardougne, you should hear his idea.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.player: Alright, I'll go and see him now.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.player: Hi Edmond, I've got the gas mask now.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.speaker: Edmond
starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.text: Good stuff, now for the digging. Beneath us are the Ardougne sewers. I've done some research, and I reckon you can use them to enter West Ardougne.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.speaker: Edmond
starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.text: I've already tried digging down to them but the soil is rock hard. You'll need to pour on several buckets of water to soften it up. I reckon four buckets should do it.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-bef.player: I still need to pour four more buckets of water on the soil.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-bef.speaker: Alrena
starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-bef.text: Hello darling, how's that tunnel coming along?

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-bef.player: I just need to soften the soil and then we'll start digging.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-bef.speaker: Alrena

You climb down into the hole.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-mourner-ou.speaker: Mourner

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.player: I still need to pour three more buckets of water on the soil.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.speaker: Alrena

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.player: I just need to soften the soil a little more and then we'll start digging.

I still need to pour one more bucket of water on the soil.
I've soaked the soil with water.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.speaker: Edmond
starting-the-quest-talking-to-edmond-aft.text: That's great, it should be soft enough to dig through now. There should be a spade nearby that you can use.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-alrena-aft.speaker: Alrena

starting-the-quest-talking-to-mourner-ou.speaker: Mourner

starting-the-quest-talking-to-mourner-ou.text: Funny, you don't look like the gardening type.

starting-the-quest-talking-to-mourner-ou.player: Oh no, I love gardening! It's my favorite pastime.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-men-an.speaker: Woman
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-men-an.text: Bah, those mourners... they're meant to be helping us, but I think they're doing more harm here than good. They won't even let me send a letter out to my family.

options.text: Have you seen a lady called Elena around here?

steps.player: Have you seen a lady called Elena around here?

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: Yes, I've seen her. Very helpful person.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: Not for the last few days though... I thought maybe she'd gone home.

options.text: You should stand up to them more.

steps.player: You should stand up to them more.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: Oh I'm not one to cause a fuss.

options.text: Yes, living in a plague city must be hard.

steps.player: Yes, living in a plague city must be hard.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: Plague? Pah, that's no excuse for the treatment we've received. It's obvious pretty quickly if someone has the plague.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: I'm thinking about making a break for it. I'm perfectly healthy, not gonna infect anyone.

steps.player: I'm sorry to hear that.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: Well, ain't much either you or me can do about it.

options.text: I'm looking for a lady called Elena.

steps.player: I'm looking for a lady called Elena.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: I've not heard of her. Old Jethick knows a lot of people, maybe he'll know where you can find her.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-men-an.speaker: Woman
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-men-an.text: We don't have good days here anymore. Curse King Tyras.

steps.player: Oh okay, bad day then.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: His army curses our city with this plague then wanders off again, leaving us to clear up the pieces.

options.text: I'm looking for a woman called Elena.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.text: Not heard of her.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-men-an.player: Sorry, that's not what I'm here to do.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-men-an.speaker: Man

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-mourne.speaker: Mourner
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-mourne.text: Hmmm, how did you get over here? You're not one of this rabble. Ah well, you'll have to stay. Can't risk you going back now.

steps.player: So what's a mourner?

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: We're working for King Lathas of East Ardougne. He has tasked us with containing the accursed plague sweeping West Ardougne.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: We also do our best to ease these people's suffering. We're nicknamed mourners because we spend a lot of time at plague victim funerals, no one else is allowed to risk attending.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: It's a demanding job, and we get little thanks from the people here.

options.text: I haven't got the plague though...

steps.player: I haven't got the plague though...

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Can't risk you being a carrier. That protective clothing you have isn't regulation issue. It won't meet safety standards.

options.text: I'm looking for a woman named Elena.

steps.player: I'm looking for a woman named Elena.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Ah yes, I've heard of her. A healer I believe. She must be mad coming over here voluntarily.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: I hear rumours she has probably caught the plague now. Very tragic, a stupid waste of life.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-ted-re.speaker: Ted Rehnison
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-ted-re.text: Go away. We don't want any.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: Hello, I don't recognise you. We don't get many newcomers around here.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: The plague of course. Not many people want to come to a place like this and the few that do normally get stopped by the mourners.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: All you'll find here now are the dead and the dying. Even our own king has abandoned us.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: Yes, King Tyras of West Ardougne. He's the brother of King Lathas, the ruler of East Ardougne.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: Well he's always been a bit of an explorer. He's led multiple expeditions into the uncharted lands to the west.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: The plague first started when he came back from one of these expeditions. More than a few suspect that some of his men caught it out there and brought it back with them.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: The king didn't care though. He just left on another expedition to the west. He hasn't been seen since. He left the city warder Bravek in charge but he's no better.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: Anyway, you clearly didn't come here to talk about kings. So tell me, what brings you to West Ardougne?

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.player: I'm looking for a woman from East Ardougne called Elena.

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: East Ardougnian women are easier to find in East Ardougne. Not many would come to West Ardougne to find one. Although the name is familiar, what does she look like?

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.player: Um... brown hair... in her twenties...

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.speaker: Jethick
entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-jethic.text: Hmmm, that doesn't narrow it down a huge amount... I'll need to know more than that, or see a picture?

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-edmond.speaker: Edmond

entering-west-ardougne-talking-to-alrena.speaker: Alrena

steps.player: Hey there, is this where you live?

steps.npc: Yes it is! Don't look down your nose at me. I have to put up with an awful lot to earn my living, life is a daily struggle.

steps.player: Sorry, I am just curious. Why is life so difficult here?

steps.npc: Just look at the place, rats, flies and all sorts just swarming the area. Doesn't help that I stink but ain't no one who likes using those tin baths right in public view.
It is difficult to make ends meet. There are just so many skilled fishermen here that the competition is too much! Leaves no room for someone like me.
Thieves! Thieves everywhere. Come to think of it, they always look remarkably like you! Adventurers running about stealing our things, get out of my sight.
Look, this is none of your business, I'd appreciate it if you left me to it. I don't want to see another fancy adventurer again!

steps.player: Okay okay! I'll be off now.

steps.npc: Gang crime is everywhere! I see them sometimes... it makes me very uneasy. It becomes difficult to sleep at night, never mind the draft in here.

steps.player: I've heard about those gangs! The Shayzien soldiers do a lot of work to put an end to it.

steps.npc: Don't talk to me about those soldiers, all they ever do is blitz onto these docks with not a care in the world for us folk.

standard-dialogue.npc: Greetings adventurer, what can I do for you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: The name's Porkai, I look after the village canoe station.

steps.player: Interesting, why does the village have a canoe station?

steps.npc: So that adventurers, such as yourself, can travel the river. Want to know more about canoes?

steps.player: No thanks...

steps.npc: No problem, come back anytime.

options.text: Can you teach me about canoes?

steps.player: Could you teach me about canoes?

steps.text: With 1-11 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Well you do not look like you have the right skills to make a canoe at the moment. Try using your axe a bit more first.

steps.text: With 12-26 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
Unfortunately, you will not be able to carve it into a more reliable canoe right now.

steps.player: Why not?

steps.npc: By looking at you and your posture holding your axe, you don't have the right skills for that. You will only be able to go to the next stop.

steps.text: With 27-41 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
By the looks of it, you can make a reasonable canoe with your skills. You'll be able to make a dugout!

steps.player: How far will I be able to go in a dugout canoe?

steps.npc: Two stops sounds about right before it sinks.

steps.text: With 42-56 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
I see, you seem like the type of adventurer who could make a very nice canoe.

steps.player: Really, how far will I be able to go?

steps.npc: A decent distance, but not the whole river.

steps.text: With 57-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
Wow, you seem knowledgeable about the woods, are you a gnome yourself? All joking aside, you will be able to craft the best canoes to go anywhere down the river!

steps.player: Amazing, thank you.

options.text: Can you hold onto my axe?

steps.text: If they're not already holding onto an axe:

steps.player: Can you hold onto my axe?

steps.npc: I sure can, you can even use the axe to make a canoe while I hold onto it for you.

steps.text: If they're already holding onto an axe:

steps.npc: I already have you're axe, would you like it back?

steps.player: Yes, I would like my axe back.

steps.npc: Here's your axe.

steps.player: No, hold onto it for me.

steps.text: If you don't have a valid axe to give:

steps.npc: I could, but you don't have an axe that you have the Woodcutting level to use.

store-axe.text: If they're not already holding onto an axe:

steps.npc: I'll hold onto that axe for you.

store-axe.text: If they're already holding onto an axe:

steps.npc: Here's your axe.

steps.player: Hello! What are you doing here?

steps.npc: Hello, I'm keeping this berth free for the return of Lady Piscarilius.

steps.player: Lady Piscarilius is out at sea?

steps.npc: Indeed, As a keen seafarer Lady Piscarilius often leads voyages herself.

steps.player: Is she expected to return soon?

steps.npc: Lady Piscarilius did not reveal how long she may be at sea for nor where she intended to explore.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

steps.npc: Another recovery? This won't take long...
Need a recovery? One moment please...

talking-to-the-port-master-after-complet.npc: Hi, sailor. How can I help you?

options.text: I'd like to claim my port task rewards.

steps.player: I'd like to claim my port task rewards.

steps.text: If the player has a completed port task:

steps.npc: Thanks, sailor. Here's your payment.

steps.text: If the player has no completed port tasks:

steps.npc: According to my records, you don't have any port task rewards to claim.

options.text: I'd like to cancel a port task.

steps.player: I'd like to cancel a port task.

steps.text: If the player has no active tasks:

steps.npc: I'm afraid you don't have any assigned tasks for me to cancel.

steps.text: If the player has one or more active tasks:

steps.prompt: Select a port task to cancel.

steps.npc: There you go. That's all sorted for you.

steps.player: I'm good, thanks.

talking-to-the-port-master-before-comple.npc: Hi there. How can I help you?

talking-to-the-port-master-before-comple.player: What do you do around here?

talking-to-the-port-master-before-comple.npc: I'm the port master. It's my job to keep everything around here running nice and smoothly for all the vessels coming and going.

options.text: So could you tell me how I could get my own vessel?
options.condition: If the player has not yet sailed with Will and Anne during the quest:

steps.player: So could you tell me how I could get my own vessel?

steps.npc: I'm afraid not, but maybe someone else around here could help. I saw a couple of people further north on the docks. I think I heard them saying they were looking for help on their boat.

options.text: Sounds like quite a challenging job. I'd best not distract you.

steps.player: Sounds like quite a challenging job. I'd best not distract you.

claim-rewards-or-cancel-task-before-comp.npc: I'm afraid I can't help you with that at the moment. You'll have to come back later.

claim-rewards-or-cancel-task-before-comp.text: You need to complete the Pandemonium quest to fully access the Sailing skill.

claim-rewards-or-cancel-task-before-sail.npc: I'm afraid I can't help you with that at the moment. You'll have to come back later.

claim-rewards-or-cancel-task-before-sail.text: The Sailing skill will release on the 19th November.

steps.npc: Go away, I'm busy!

standard-dialogue-varrock-library.player: HEY PETE, WHAT ARE YOU DOING HERE?

standard-dialogue-varrock-library.npc: Shhhh! It's a library you know!

Not much, just doing some research on Dwarvern Culture. Did you know that Keldagrim was originally constructed by a long lost clan who embraced the power of magic, and used it to aid with glorious buildings like
Yes. They even stayed down there for 1000 years or more, in a time they call 'The age of Kings'.
Shhhh! That's enough history for one day I think!

standard-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.player: Pete, what are you doing out here in the deep wilderness?

standard-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.npc: Shhh!! Don't let the others see me here! I'm on a top secret mission for the Burth..., no, nothing. Never mind. Oooo, look, the chaos elemental!! Quick, run!!

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: Hey Postie. Hows tricks? Who are you interviewing here?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: Everyone deserves a hic break you know. It gets pretty tiring lugging burp letters about all day.

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: I see. Can I join you?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: Why, am I hic coming apart?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: You've been here a while, haven't you?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: Maybe I haves, maybe I haves. It all goes straight to my head you see.

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: Yes... I can see that. Bye Pete!

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.player: Hey Pete what you doing here?

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: Just doing a quick survey on famous people and their favourite colour. It's a special feature for 'West Wyverns Women's Weekly'.
Here! Are you mad? No, 'fraid I can't do that. Could cause all sorts of trouble.

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.player: You're a bit mad really aren't you?

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: So would you be if you could speak over 1000 languages. I bet it's bliss being ignorant of this world's trouble! I'm off!

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: Just chatting to my big brother Pete. Hee heee!!
Just a joke that he told me. Care to hear it?
2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'? Hee heheee he ho ho.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: And so what did the other one say?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: Sigh. 2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'? Hee heheee he ho ho.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: I see. So... what did the other one say?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: You're serious aren't you. Listen again. 2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: Fish, right. So, what was the reply?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: ARGH!! 2 PARROTS. ON A PERCH. SMELLS FISHY.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: No, still lost. Is one of them a penguin?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: You're doing it on purpose now aren't you? Please leave me alone!

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.player: Hey Pete, what you doing here?

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Just chatting to my brother Pete. He keeps Parrots.

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.player: Doesn't sound too tough. What's the pay like?

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Not very good I'm afraid. His bosses are pretty cheep.

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.player: Groan. Don't give up the day job Pete.

standard-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.player: Hey Pete what you doing here?

standard-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: Arrrr. Avast shipmate. Arrr. I Likes the cut of your gibb. Arrr. That it be.

standard-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.player: I have a strange feeling of Deja Vu. I must go now.

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.player: Hey Postie! What you doing all the way up here?

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: I was just trying to get some wise words of wisdom from the Oracle. You know, she's been here a long, long time.

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.player: Yes, I thought as much. What did she have to say?

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: First she said 'I am the Oracle, And when I open my lips, let no dog bark!'
I didn't know she was familiar with the works of Shakespeare. So I said 'Et tu, brute?'
Well, she started leaping about and pointing to Ardougne, shouting something about betrayal. She was really angry.

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.player: Cripes! What do you think it means?

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: Who knows. Always cryptic to the last. See you around.

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.npc: Reldo, have you found that book I was looking for yet?

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.speaker: Reldo
overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.text: No, not yet... but I know I have seen it somewhere...

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.npc: Sure, no problems. See you later.

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.speaker: Reldo
overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.text: Bye! Say hi to the other Petes for me.

overhead-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.npc: Psssst! How is the plan going?
Great. Now don't forget - nobody does anything until I give the word! OK?

overhead-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.speaker: Noterazzo
overhead-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.text: Sure no problem. We'll be waiting.

overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.speaker: Barmaid
overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.text: 4 Pints coming right up. Are you expecting guests?

overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.speaker: Barmaid
overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.text: You want me to put it on your tab?

overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: That would be great, thanks. Oh cripes! I've left a fire burning! I'll be back in a mo.

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.speaker: Lanthus
overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.text: Easy Pete, calm down. Don't lose your head!

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: Cheeky!! If you're not careful I'll get you cursed too!

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.speaker: Lanthus
overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.text: You wouldn't catch me double-crossing a witch!

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: But which witch is which! Anyway, I'm late for an appointment with the oracle.

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.speaker: Lanthus
overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.text: Take care and say hi to the kids for me.

overhead-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: Hey, bro! How's the party business?
Nice. Well, I'm here to talk to some White Knights.

overhead-dialogue-falador-party-room.speaker: Party Pete
overhead-dialogue-falador-party-room.text: Want to take some cake with you?

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Mum wants to know if you're coming round for tea.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.speaker: Parroty Pete
overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.text: No, I've got another late night here.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.speaker: Parroty  Pete
overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.text: Ol' bluebeak's got the flu again!

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Oh dear. Nothing too serious I hope.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.speaker: Parroty  Pete
overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.text: Well, as long as he hasn't caught anything from that evil chicken.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Got a taste for parrots now too has he?
Sigh.* Will nothing sacred be safe?

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: Hey Pete. Any news from the fleet?

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.speaker: Pirate Pete
overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.text: 'Tis all quiet on the eastern front.

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: Well, you know what to do if something goes wrong.

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.speaker: Pirate Pete
overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.text: Holler like a bosun without a bottle.

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: That's it brother, and we'll come a running!

overhead-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: Well, I'm back. And he said no. Again.
Lemons? What are you talking about?
I swear you get stranger every time.

overhead-dialogue-upon-changing-location.npc: Now, how's this thing work again...?

evil-twin-random-event-standard-dialogue.npc: Hello [player name]. I've got a message for you from Molly. She needs your help urgently. Will you assist her now?

steps.player: Sure, anything for Molly.

steps.text: Player is teleported to the Evil twin claw machine place

steps.player: Tell her to get stuffed.

evil-twin-random-event-if-postie-pete-is.npc: Sorry, I don't have any messages for you.

evil-twin-random-event-overhead-dialogue.text: Upon spawning in for the player:

steps.npc: Message for you, [player name]!

evil-twin-random-event-overhead-dialogue.text: While waiting for a response by the player:

steps.npc: Hello, [player name]?
Urgent message for you, [player name]?
Someone needs your help, [player name]!
Will you accept the message, [player name]?

evil-twin-random-event-overhead-dialogue.text: If the player does not respond in time:

steps.npc: Maybe later.

standard-dialogue-before-starting-ratcat.npc: I think I'll go hunting soon, there's a warehouse with some rats in it nearby.

standard-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-whi.text: The cat is too sick to respond.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-ratcat.npc: Still a bit below purrrr. Thank you for fetching the medicine for me.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-ratcat.player: No problem, I hope you get better soon.

high-prayer-level.npc: Greetings, [player name]. Can I help you with anything, today?

options.text: How can I train my prayer?

steps.player: How can I train my prayer?

steps.text: If the player has 99 prayer:

steps.npc: I think you should be teaching me a thing or two, shouldn't you?
Well, if you really want my advice...
The most common way to train prayer is by either burying bones, or offering them to the gods at some kind of an altar.
Lots of adventurers build such altars in their own homes, or there are a few frequent places of worship around the world.
Different kinds of bones will help you to train faster. Generally speaking, the bigger they are and the more frightening a creature they come from, the better they are for it.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.player: What is prayer useful for?

steps.npc: The gods look kindly upon their devout followers. There are all kinds of benefits they may provide, if you pray for them!

steps.player: Really? What kind of benefits?

steps.npc: They could help you in combat, help your wounds to heal more quickly, protect your belongings... There's a lot they can do for you!

steps.text: The prayer tab opens.

steps.npc: You can find out more by looking in your prayer book.

steps.player: Wow! That sounds great.

steps.npc: You need to be careful that your prayers don't run out, though. You can get prayer potions to help you recharge, or you can pray at an altar whenever one's nearby.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.player: No, thank you.

steps.npc: Very well. Saradomin be with you!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello! Glad to see you're okay. I was worried you might have gone and got stuck down that hole.

standard-dialogue.player: No need to worry. I'm mostly quite capable when it comes to these kinds of things!

standard-dialogue.npc: Good to hear!

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.text: If the player never spoke to Ramarno after completion of Below Ice Mountain:

steps.npc: Hello there. Did you see that dwarf by the big forge? I think he wanted to talk to you.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.text: If the player spoke to Ramarno after completion of Below Ice Mountain:

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Hello! Look at this place. Isn't it amazing?

steps.player: It sure is! Not every day you find yourself in a lost city.

steps.npc: So what can I do for you?

steps.player: Does the name Lassar mean anything to you? It was an old fortress that once existed here, long before Camdozaal. I'm wondering if there might still be some traces left down here.

steps.npc: A ruin within a ruin? How exciting! We have found the odd thing that doesn't seem to be dwarven in origin, but it's still early days for us here, so we haven't been able to learn much yet.
One that was particularly interesting was this strange icon I found in the mine.

steps.text: The archaeologist shows you an unusual icon.

steps.npc: Could be a lot more to find over there, but I must admit, I haven't been back since... well...

steps.player: Since what?

steps.npc: It's probably nothing, but there's this big sinkhole on the other side of the mine. I'm probably just being silly, but I'm sure I heard a voice coming from inside.

steps.player: Interesting... And if I wanted to go down this hole?

steps.npc: Go down the hole?! You're far braver than I am! There's plenty of rocks around there. I'm sure you could tie a rope to one of them. You'd need a pretty long rope though. Here, you can use mine.

steps.text: The archaeologist gives you some rope.

steps.player: Thanks!
Hi.

steps.npc: Hello! What can I do for you today?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm Preswylwyr.

steps.player: It's nice to meet you Preswylwyr, I'm [player name].

steps.npc: And it's great to meet you, [player name].

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I'm Gwerin's partner, he runs the mill while it's my job to use up all the flour he produces.

steps.player: You bake? So that's what the wonderful smell is.

steps.npc: Ha ha! Would you care for some bread? There should be some on the table.

steps.player: Really? That's very nice of you, thanks!

steps.npc: No problem! Was there anything else you wanted?

steps.player: Bye!

steps.npc: Farewell, adventurer.

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Peace be with you, friend.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-a-priest-at.npc: Greetings. May the blessings of Icthlarin rest on your tired shoulders and set you at ease during these strange times.

options.text: What's that place to the south?

steps.player: What's that place to the south?

steps.npc: That's the old necropolis. It's been abandoned for a long time. In fact, you couldn't even access most of it until fairly recently.

steps.player: How come?

steps.npc: It was mostly buried under the sand until a storm came in from the south.

steps.player: Interesting... I bet the place is a hotspot for grave robbers.

steps.npc: Not as many as you'd think. There's a lot of superstition about the place. People say that even the sand is marked by death.

steps.player: You sound like you don't believe them.

steps.npc: Not really. The sand is probably that colour due to the amount of salt in it. Still, if it keeps people from robbing the dead, that's no bad thing.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Any time, adventurer.

steps.player: Good day.

using-a-potion-on-him.npc: Hey, hey, hey! What in the name of sweet suffering Icthlarin are you doing?

using-a-potion-on-him.player: I thought this acne potion might clear up your spots.

using-a-potion-on-him.npc: All that you'll achieve by pouring that potion on me is to ruin my lovely robes.

using-a-potion-on-him.player: Sorry, I was just trying to help.

standard-dialogue.npc: I wish there was more I could do for these people.

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.npc: It's going to take a lot of work to fix the damage done to this city.

pre-quest-attempting-to-attack-the-templ.text: You have no reason to do that!

starting-the-quest.speaker: King Roald
starting-the-quest.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

steps.player: I'm looking for a quest!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: A quest you say? Hmm... What an odd request to make of the King. It's funny you should mention it though, as there is something you can do for me.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Are you aware of Paterdomus? It's a temple east of here. It stands on the holy River Salve and guards the only passage into the deadly vampyre-infested lands of Morytania.

options.text: Yes, I think I've heard of it.

steps.player: Yes, I think I've heard of it.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Very good. Well, it has been some days since last I heard from Drezel, the priest who lives there. Be a sport and go check in on the silly old codger for me, would you?
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 15.

steps.prompt: Start the Priest in Peril quest?

steps.player: Sure. I don't have anything better to do right now.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Many thanks, adventurer! I would have sent one of the squires, but they wanted payment for it!

options.text: Why do you care about Drezel anyway?
Do I get a reward for this?

steps.player: I'll get going.
No. That sounds boring.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, I dare say it does. I wouldn't even have mentioned it had you not seemed to be looking for something to do anyway.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You will have to excuse me then. I am very busy as I have a kingdom to run!

starting-the-quest-talking-to-king-roald.speaker: King Roald
starting-the-quest-talking-to-king-roald.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

steps.player: About that job I'm doing...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You have news of Drezel for me?

options.text: Where am I supposed to go again?

steps.player: Where am I supposed to go again?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: The temple of Paterdomus where Drezel lives. It is but a short journey east from here. It lies at the source of the River Salve. Don't worry, you can't miss it.

options.text: Why do you care about Drezel anyway?

steps.player: Why do you care about Drezel anyway?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Well, that is a slightly impertinent question to ask of your King, but I shall overlook it this time.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: As you are no doubt aware, this kingdom worships Saradomin, the god of wisdom and order. As such, it is a peaceful place to live and prosper.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Paterdomus, the temple where Drezel lives, stands on the eastern border of Misthalin. It guards the only passage into the evil lands of Morytania.

steps.player: Evil?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Oh yes. Morytania is a fearful place, filled to the brim with accursed servants of the chaos god Zamorak. All of them are terrible, but none more so than the rulers of the region, the vampyres.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Thankfully, the sacred River Salve marks a natural border between Misthalin and Morytania. The waters of the river have been blessed with Saradomin's almighty power, preventing any invasion by the vampyres.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Drezel is descended from one of the original Saradominist priests who first blessed the river. His job is to ensure nothing happens to the river that might allow the evil of Morytania to invade this land.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This is the reason why the lack of communication from him bothers me somewhat, although I am sure it's nothing too serious. Nobody would dare to try and attack our kingdom!

options.text: Do I get a reward for this?

steps.player: Do I get a reward for this?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You will be rewarded with the knowledge that you have done the right thing and assisted the King of Misthalin.

steps.player: So... that would be a 'no' then?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: That is correct.

steps.player: I have to go.

at-the-temple.speaker: Mysterious Voice
at-the-temple.text: Who are you and what do you want?

options.text: King Roald sent me to check on Drezel.

steps.player: King Roald sent me to check on Drezel.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Drezel? Right... I, er... Just give me a moment.
You hear someone moving around followed by what sounds like panicked muttering.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Okay, he's just coming! Wait a second!

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: Hello, my name is Drevil.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Drezel!

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: I mean Drezel. How can I help?

steps.player: Er... Is everything okay in there?

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: Yes, totally fine. Now, what can I do for you?

steps.player: Well, the King hadn't heard from you for a few days. He sent me to make sure everything's okay.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: I see... And, uh, what would you do if everything wasn't okay?

steps.player: I'm not sure. Ask you what help you need I suppose.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: Ah, good, well, I don't think...

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Hey... The dog!

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: Ah, actually there is something I could use some help with. Will you do me a favour, adventurer?

steps.player: What kind of favour?

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: Well, there's this horrible big... dog-like thing that's moved into the mausoleum outside. It's causing all kinds of problems. Could you get rid of it for me?

steps.player: I don't know... Something about all this seems a bit suspicious... I think I'd better go and check in with the King.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: No, no, there's no need for that. He's a very busy man! Besides, you said yourself that he sent you here to help me, right?

steps.player: Right...

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
steps.text: Then please, deal with that dog for me.

steps.player: Hmm...

options.text: Hi, I just moved in next door.

steps.player: Hi, I just moved in next door.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: What?

steps.player: Yeah, and I was just wondering if I could borrow a cup of coffee?

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Next door? Coffee? What are you on about? Who are you?

options.text: I hear this place is of historic interest.

steps.player: I hear this place is of historic interest.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Right... And?

steps.player: Can I come in and have a wander around? Possibly look at some antiques or buy something from your gift shop?

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Gift shop? What are you on about? This isn't a museum! Clear off!

options.text: The council sent me to check your pipes.

steps.player: The council sent me to check your pipes.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Voice
steps.text: Pipes? We don't have any pipes! Now get lost!

options.condition: Before selecting any of the other options:

steps.player: Nothing. Never mind.

options.condition: After selecting any of the other options:

steps.player: Actually, never mind.

at-the-temple-knocking-on-the-door-after.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
at-the-temple-knocking-on-the-door-after.text: Hello? Is that you again, adventurer? Have you dealt with that dog yet?

at-the-temple-knocking-on-the-door-after.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
at-the-temple-knocking-on-the-door-after.text: But you're going to, right? For good old Delzig?

at-the-temple-knocking-on-the-door-after.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
at-the-temple-knocking-on-the-door-after.text: Sorry, for good old Drezel, right?

at-the-temple-attacking-the-temple-guard.text: If the player attempts to use Magic spells on the guardian:

steps.text: Your spells do not seem to affect it.

at-the-temple-talking-to-king-roald-afte.speaker: King Roald
at-the-temple-talking-to-king-roald-afte.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

steps.player: About that job I'm doing...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You have news of Drezel for me?

steps.player: Well... I went to the temple like you asked me to... and I spoke to someone inside...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Ah, well that must have been Drezel then. What did he say?

steps.player: Well... he seemed to be having some kind of trouble. He asked for my help.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Well, I expect you to offer him your full assistance in whatever he needs.

steps.player: But-

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Now, run along. I have a lot to do and it sounds like Drezel needs you.

steps.player: Well... okay then.

you-killed-a-dog.player: There we go, one dead dog. I should go and tell Drezel.

you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.text: Is that you, adventurer? Have you dealt with that dog?

you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.text: Really? Well... thank you! That's really... quite something.

you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.player: Don't mention it... Is there anything else you need?

you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.text: I think it's safe to say that you've done more than enough, adventurer.

you-killed-a-dog-letting-the-monks-know-.player: Okay... I guess I'd better go and let the King know.

you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-the-monks-ag.speaker: Mysterious Voice 2
you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-the-monks-ag.text: Is that you, adventurer? Once again, thank you so much for dealing with that dog. It's really... quite something.

you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-the-monks-ag.player: Don't mention it... Now, I guess I'd better report back to the King.

you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-king-roald-a.speaker: King Roald
you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-king-roald-a.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

steps.player: About that job I'm doing...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You have news of Drezel for me?

steps.player: Well, I went to the temple and spoke to... Drezel. He asked me to kill a dog in the mausoleum.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: A dog? Tell me you didn't do it?!

steps.player: Well...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Are you a complete imbecile?

steps.player: I tried to tell you it was a bit suspicious, but you told me to help Drezel!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Do you even realise what you've done? That mausoleum contains the only passage between Morytania and Misthalin! Not only that, it's built right over the source of the River Salve!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: That 'dog' was responsible for guarding the entrance to the mausoleum! With it gone, there's nothing to stop someone from sabotaging the blessings on the river. Thanks to you, all of Misthalin is now at risk!

steps.player: But Drezel...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Do you not see what's happened here, you absolute cretin! Obviously some fiend has done something to Drezel and tricked your feeble intellect into helping them!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Now you get back there and get this mess sorted out. If you don't do whatever is necessary to safeguard this kingdom from attack, I will see you beheaded for high treason!

steps.player: Y-yes, your highness.

you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-him-again.speaker: King Roald
you-killed-a-dog-talking-to-him-again.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

steps.player: About that job I'm doing...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Why haven't you ensured the border with Morytania is secure yet?

steps.player: Okay, okay... I'm going, I'm going... There's no need to shout...

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: No need to shout?! Listen, and listen well, and see if your puny mind can comprehend this: if the border is not protected, then we are all at the mercy of the vampyres!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I would say that me shouting at you for your incompetence is the least of your worries right now. Now get yourself back to Paterdomus! At once!

saving-drezel-and-the-world-attempting-t.player: It sounds like there's something alive inside it. I don't think it would be a very good idea to open it...

saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.speaker: Drezel
saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.text: Oh! You do not appear to be one of those Zamorakians who imprisoned me! Who are you and why are you here?

saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.player: My name's [player name]. King Roald sent me to find out what was going on at the temple. I take it you're Drezel?

saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.speaker: Drezel
saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.text: That's right! Oh, praise be to Saradomin! I feared that when those Zamorakians attacked this place, Misthalin would be doomed!

saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.player: Why? What are they planning to do?

saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.speaker: Drezel
saving-drezel-and-the-world-meeting-drez.text: I believe they aim to desecrate the blessings placed upon the holy River Salve by the Seven Priestly Warriors themselves! We'd be left defenceless against the vampyres of Morytania!

steps.player: Seven Priestly Warriors?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Indeed. While this isn't the... ideal time for a history lesson, this knowledge may help you with our next steps, so allow me to explain...

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It is said that many years ago, the land that is now Morytania was a peaceful Saradominist kingdom. Alas, all that ended when the vampyres invaded, claiming the land as their own.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Morytania wasn't enough for them though. Soon, they set their sights on these lands as well. Misthalin would have quickly fallen to the vampyres, were it not for the bravery of the Seven Priestly Warriors.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: They led the armies of Misthalin against the vampyres, with the war culminating in a great battle that took place right where this temple stands.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: For ten days and nights they fought, never sleeping, never eating, fuelled only by their faith in Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: On the eleventh day, reinforcements arrived, but when they did, they found the Seven Priestly Warriors had been slain by the vampyres, along with most of their forces.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: However, their sacrifice was not in vain. Before they were defeated, the Seven Priestly Warriors managed to bless the Salve with the holy power of Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Those blessings remain to this day, ensuring no vampyre can cross the river. The temple here was built soon after. It guards the source of the River Salve, and acts as the only passage into Morytania.

steps.player: And what about the mausoleum below?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: That is the most important part of the temple, for it is where the passage into Morytania is found. It is also the final resting place of the Seven Priestly Warriors.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Their tombs are built around the well that provides direct access to the source of the Salve, with a golden gift placed upon each of the tombs as a mark of respect.

steps.player: I see. And you think those Zamorakians are going to try and remove the blessings on the river?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: I fear that is almost certainly their goal.

steps.player: So what do we do?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: First, we need to get me out of this cell. The leader of those Zamorakians probably has the key. I believe he's the one in the hood.

steps.player: So I need to go and find this key. Anything else I should be aware of?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: I'm afraid so. When the Salve was first blessed, a small number of vampyres were left trapped on this side of it. They were heavily weakened, but still posed a dangerous threat.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Even with them weakened, the brave Saradominists who built this temple were unable to kill them. Instead, they trapped them in coffins and buried them outside the temple.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: This coffin here contains one of those vampyres. The Zamorakians must have dug it up and brought it in here with them.

steps.player: But why?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well, as those fiends pointed out to me with delight, as I am the descendant of one of the Seven Priestly Warriors who blessed the river, it will likely recognise the smell of my blood.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: If I get too close, it will probably wake up and kill me, very slowly and painfully.

steps.player: Maybe I could kill it somehow?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: I would not risk waking it. Even now, it could pose a huge threat. The priests of old would incapacitate trapped vampyres with the blessings of Saradomin. Perhaps there's a way for you do the same.

steps.player: Right. So, I need to find the key to your cell and do something about the vampyre. Got it.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Good luck.
Continues above from "So what do we do?"

saving-drezel-and-the-world-talking-to-d.speaker: Drezel
saving-drezel-and-the-world-talking-to-d.text: How goes it, adventurer? Any luck in finding the key to the cell or a way of stopping the vampyre yet?

saving-drezel-and-the-world-talking-to-d.speaker: Drezel
saving-drezel-and-the-world-talking-to-d.text: Well, don't give up adventurer! The key must be nearby. Most likely the leader of those Zamorakians has it. I believe he's the one in the hood.

saving-drezel-and-the-world-talking-to-d.speaker: Drezel
saving-drezel-and-the-world-talking-to-d.text: As for the vampyre, the priests of old would incapacitate the ones they'd trapped with the blessings of Saradomin. Perhaps there's a way for you do the same.

options.text: Could you tell me more about this temple?
