starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Greetings! I am Hassan, Chancellor to the Emir of Al Kharid.

options.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.player: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
steps.text: Well... we do currently have a very urgent issue we need to resolve, and I suppose you look like someone who knows how to get a job done. Are you definitely interested in helping?

steps.prompt: Start the Prince Ali Rescue quest?

steps.player: Of course.

steps.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
steps.text: You'll find our Spymaster, Osman, just outside the palace. Go to him and tell him I sent you. He will fill you in on the details of our problem.

steps.player: Alright, I'll get to it.
Actually, I've changed my mind.

steps.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
steps.text: I see. Well you know where to find me if you do wish to help us.

options.text: It's just too hot here. How can you stand it?
Do you mind if I just kill your warriors?

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Hello again. Have you spoken to Osman yet? He should be just outside the palace.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.player: Not yet. I'll go and see him.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Hello again. I hear you have agreed to help rescue Prince Ali. On behalf of the Emir, I will have a reward ready for you upon your success.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Osman? I was told by the Chancellor to come and speak to you. Apparently you have an issue that I can help with.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: That would be an apt description. However, I find you to be an interesting choice by the Chancellor. Why has he chosen to trust you with this task over one of our own?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Er... I just asked if he needed help and he said yes.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: That man is far too trusting at a time when we must take extra care. However, if he has made his decision, I will not question it. Still, you should know that I will be keeping a close eye on you.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Fair enough. So what is this issue?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Prince Ali, heir to the Emir of Al Kharid, has been taken. My spies have already discovered where he is being held, but we need someone to make the rescue.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Well I'm sure I can manage that. How do I go about rescuing him?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: The Prince has been taken by a group of bandits led by the self-proclaimed 'Lady' Keli. They are holding him in the abandoned jail just east of Draynor Village.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: According to our information, Keli is the only one able to freely move around the area. For you to get the Prince out, you will need to disguise him as her. She will of course need dealing with first.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Why can't I just go in and kill her and her bandits?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: And endanger the life of the Prince in the process? No. There will be no unnecessary risks. We need to do this with as little bloodshed as possible.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: You make a fair point. Do you know what Keli looks like?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: She has blonde hair and wears pink clothes. My daughter, Leela, one of my spies, is currently in Draynor Village keeping an eye on the jail. I'm sure she can help you with the specifics.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Before you go, there is one more thing. You'll need a key to get the Prince out of his cell. Keli has the only one. You could steal it, but that seems like a risk we should avoid.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: But if she has the only copy, and I can't just steal it, how do I get the key?

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: If you bring me an imprint of the key along with a bronze bar, I can show you how to make a copy. You should be able to make an imprint of the key using some soft clay.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Of course, you'll need to find a way to get Keli to show you the key without causing suspicion. I'm sure Leela can help you with that.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: Sounds like I should head on over to Draynor Village and see Leela then.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Indeed. Do you have any further questions before you go?

options.text: Do you know why they've taken the Prince?

steps.player: Do you know why they've taken the Prince?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: No, but we have our theories.

steps.player: Care to share them?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: No. You have not yet proven yourself enough to be trusted with that information.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Now, do you have any further questions?

options.text: Where abouts in Draynor is Leela?

steps.player: Where abouts in Draynor is Leela?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: She will be somewhere near the abandoned jail that the bandits are using. It's just east of the village.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Do you have any further questions?

options.text: No. I think I know everything I need to.

steps.player: No. I think I know everything I need to.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Then you should get going.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: You again. How are things going in Draynor?
If the player has the key imprint but no bronze bar:

steps.player: I have an imprint of the key.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Good. Bring me a bronze bar, and I'll get a copy made.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has the key imprint and a bronze bar:

steps.player: I have an imprint of the key.

steps.text: You give Osman the imprint along with a bronze bar.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I'll use this to have a copy of the key made. I'll send it to Leela once it's ready.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has not acquired the key imprint:

steps.player: I'm still working on gathering all the items I need.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Well if you need help, just talk to Leela.

options.text: Do you know why they've taken the Prince?
Where abouts in Draynor is Leela?

steps.player: I'll get going.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.player: You must be Leela. Your father sent me to help rescue Prince Ali.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela.text: Yes, he sent word ahead that you'd be coming. Are you aware of the plan?

starting-out-talking-to-leela.player: I need to obtain a copy of the key to the Prince's cell, create a disguise for him that makes him look like Keli and then break him out of the jail.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela.text: I'd say that's a good summary. Now, do you have any questions for me about any part of the plan?

steps.player: Any ideas for the key?

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Keli keeps it on her at all times, on a chain around her neck. If you can convince her to show it to you, you might be able to use some soft clay to take an imprint.
If the player hasn't obtained the key print yet:

steps.player: That doesn't sound easy.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: My suggestion is that you pretend to be interested in joining her bandits. From there, you should be able to steer the conversation towards the key.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Once you have the imprint, take it to my father along with a bronze bar. He'll then be able to make us a copy.
If the player has the key print in their inventory:

steps.player: I already have the imprint!

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Then you should take it to my father along with a bronze bar. He'll then be able to make us a copy.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Do you have any other questions about the plan?

steps.player: Any ideas for the disguise?

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: To make the Prince look like Keli, you'll need a blonde wig and a pink skirt. You'll also want some skin paste to hide the black eye he got when they captured him.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: There's an old sailor in the village who makes rope. Perhaps he could make you a wig. Don't forget to dye it once you have one.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: For the skin paste, there's a local witch who's apparently an expert on all sorts of potions. I'm sure she could make you some. I hear she also sells dye, if you need some for the wig.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Finally there's the skirt. I imagine you could just buy one from any clothes shop. Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock is probably the closest.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Do you have any other questions about the plan?

options.text: Don't think so. I'll go and prepare.

steps.player: Don't think so. I'll go and prepare.

starting-out-talking-to-leela-talking-to.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela-talking-to.text: You're back. Do you have everything needed yet?

options.text: Not yet. I'll go and prepare.

steps.player: Not yet. I'll go and prepare.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-ned.speaker: Ned
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-ned.text: Why, hello there, [lad/lass/kid]. Me friends call me Ned. I was a man of the sea, but it's past me now. Could I be making or selling you some rope?

options.text: Could you make other things apart from rope?

steps.player: Could you make other things apart from rope?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: I'm sure I can. What are you thinking of?

options.text: Could you knit me a sweater?

steps.player: Could you knit me a sweater?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Do I look like a member of a sewing circle? Be off wi' you. I have fought monsters that would turn your hair blue.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: I don't need to be laughed at just 'cos I'm getting a bit old.

options.text: How about some sort of wig?

steps.player: How about some sort of wig?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Well... that's an interesting thought. Yes, I think I could do something. Give me three balls of wool and I might be able to do it.
If the player does not have three balls of wool:

steps.player: Great, I will get some. I think a wig would be useful.

steps.text: If the player has three balls of wool:

options.text: I have them here. Please make me a wig.

steps.player: I have them here. Please make me a wig.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Okay, I'll have a go.
Ned gives you a pretty good wig.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Here you go. How's that for a quick effort? Not bad I think!

steps.player: Thanks Ned. There's more to you than meets the eye.

options.text: Actually, I don't need one right now.

steps.player: Actually, I don't need one right now.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Fair enough.

options.text: Could you repair the arrow holes in the back of my shirt?

steps.player: Could you repair the arrow holes in the back of my shirt?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Ah yes, it's a tough world these days. There's a few brave enough to attack from ten metres away.
Ned pulls out a needle and attacks your shirt.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: There you go, good as new.

steps.player: Thanks Ned. Maybe next time they will attack me face to face.
Actually, I don't need anything.

options.text: Yes, I would like some rope.
No thanks, Ned. I don't need any.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-aggie.speaker: Aggie
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-aggie.text: What can I help you with?

options.text: What could you make for me?

steps.player: Can you make skin paste?

steps.text: If the player does not have all the required items:

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Why, it's one of my most popular potions! Lots of people around here like to pretty their faces up a bit. I can make it for you if you get me what's needed.

steps.player: What do you need?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Well dearie, you need a base for the paste. That's a mix of ash, flour and water. Then you need redberries to colour it as you want. Bring me those four items and I will make you some.
If the player has all the required items:

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Yes I can. I see you already have the ingredients. Would you like me to mix some for you now?

options.text: Yes please. Mix me some skin paste.

steps.player: Yes please. Mix me some skin paste.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: That should be simple. Hand the things to Aggie then.
You hand the ash, flour, water and redberries to Aggie. She tips the ingredients into a cauldron and mutters some words.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Tourniquet, Fenderbaum, Tottenham, Marshmallow, Marblearch.
Aggie hands you the skin paste.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: There you go dearie. That will make you look good at the Varrock dances.

options.text: No thank you. I don't need any skin paste right now.

steps.player: No thank you. I don't need any skin paste right now.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Okay dearie, that's always your choice.

options.text: Cool, do you turn people into frogs?
You mad old witch, you can't help me.
Can you make dyes for me please?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.player: Are you the famous Lady Keli? Leader of the toughest gang of bandits around?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: Yes, I am Keli. You've heard of me then?

options.text: Heard of you? You're famous in Gielinor!

steps.player: Heard of you? You're famous in Gielinor!

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: That's very kind of you to say. Reputations are not easily earned. I have managed to succeed where many fail.

options.text: I think Katrine is still tougher.
options.condition: If Shield of Arrav has been completed:

steps.player: I think Katrine is still tougher.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well you can think that all you like! Those cowards dare not leave Varrock. Out here, I'm toughest. You can tell them that! Now get out of my sight, before I call my guards.

steps.player: What's your latest plan then?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Why do you want to know?

steps.player: Well I was actually hoping to join your group.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Join us? Interesting... I suppose you do look the type.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You'll of course need to properly prove yourself before we let you join us. However, what I can tell you is that we currently have a very valuable prisoner. If all goes well, he will make us very rich.

options.text: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.

steps.player: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: To catch him? Oh yes. We had to grab him without his bodyguards noticing. It was a stroke of genius. Mostly my doing, of course.

options.text: How do you know someone won't try to free him?
How do you know someone won't try to free him?

steps.player: How do you know someone won't try to free him?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There is no way to release him. The only key to his cell is on a chain around my neck, and the locksmith who made it died very suddenly.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There isn't another key like this in the world.

options.text: Could I see the key please?

steps.player: Could I see the key please?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Why?

steps.player: It will be something I can tell my grandchildren, when you are even more famous than you are now.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well I suppose there's no harm in letting you see it. After all, you have no hope of stealing it.
Keli shows you a small key on a strong looking chain.
If the player doesn't have soft clay or already has the key print:

steps.player: Thank you. I'd better go now.

options.text: Could I touch the key for a moment please?

steps.player: Could I touch the key for a moment please?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well... only for a moment then.
As you touch the key, you take an imprint of it using your soft clay.

steps.player: Thank you so much! You are too kind.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You are welcome, but run along now. I will need some time to consider your request to join us.

options.text: Thank you. I'd better go now.

steps.player: Thank you. I'd better go now.

options.text: That is a good way to keep secrets.

steps.player: That is a good way to keep secrets.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: It is the best way I know. Dead men tell no tales.

options.text: Well I'll be off. Good luck.

steps.player: Well I'll be off. Good luck.
Well good luck with it.

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.

steps.player: You must have trained a lot for this work.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: I have used a sword since I was a girl. My first kill was before I was even six years old.

options.text: I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.

steps.player: I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Yes, I am very busy. Goodbye.

options.text: I've heard a little, but I think Katrine is tougher.
options.condition: If Shield of Arrav has been completed:

options.text: I've heard rumours that you kill people.

steps.player: I've heard rumours that you kill people.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There's always someone ready to spread rumours. I hear all sort of ridiculous things these days.

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.
No, I've never really heard of you.

steps.player: No, I've never really heard of you.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You must be new around here then. Everyone knows of Lady Keli and her prowess with a sword.

options.text: No, still doesn't ring a bell.

steps.player: No, still doesn't ring a bell.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well, you know of me now. You should also know that I will wring your neck if you don't show some respect.

options.text: I don't show respect to killers and hoodlums.

steps.player: I don't show respect to killers and hoodlums.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You should, you really should. I am wealthy enough to place a bounty on your head, or I could just remove your head myself. Luckily, I am too busy to deal with the likes of you, so clear off!

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.
Actually, I have heard of you. You're famous in Gielinor!

steps.player: Actually, I have heard of you. You're famous in Gielinor!

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.
I shouldn't disturb someone as tough as you.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: Oh, it's you. What do you want?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.player: I was hoping we could talk more about your prisoner.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: Until you join us, I can say little. What I can tell you is that he is very valuable. If all goes well, he will make us very rich.

options.text: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.
How do you know someone won't try to free him?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.player: Hi. Who are you guarding here?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.speaker: Joe
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.text: Can't say. It's all very secret. You should get out of here. I am not supposed to talk while I guard.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: You're back. Do you have everything needed yet?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: Good work. Now, before breaking the Prince out, you'll need to find a way to deal with his personal guard. He's talkative, so try to find a weakness. Remember, we don't want any unneeded violence.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.player: Alright. I'll go have a chat to this guard.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: You're back. How are things going?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.player: I'm afraid I lost that key you gave me.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: Well that was foolish. I can sort you out with another, but it will cost you 15 coins.
If the player does not have 15 coins:

steps.player: I haven't got that much.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Then come back to me when you do.

steps.player: Here, I have 15 coins.

steps.text: Leela gives you a key.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Now, how are things going with that guard?

steps.player: I haven't spoken to him yet.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Well you'd better get on it then. We need him out of the way.

options.text: I have some beer here. Fancy one?

steps.player: I have some beer here. Fancy one?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Ah, that would be lovely. Only one though, just to wet my throat.

steps.player: Of course. It must be tough being here without a drink.

steps.text: You hand a beer to the guard. He drinks it in seconds.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: That was perfect! I can't thank you enough.

steps.player: How are you? Still okay? Not too drunk?

steps.text: If the player has less than three beers:

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: No, I don't get drunk from only one drink. I reckon I'd need at least two more for that. Still, thanks for the beer.
If the player has two more beers:

steps.player: Would you care for another beer, my friend?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: I'd better not. I don't want to be drunk on duty.

steps.player: Here, just keep these for later. I hate to see a thirsty guard.

steps.text: You hand two more beers to the guard. He takes a sip of one, and then he quickly drinks them both.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Franksh! That wash jusht what I need to shtay on guard. No more beersh, I don't want to get drunk.

options.text: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.player: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Well, the hours are good, but most of those hours are a drag.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Sometimes I wonder if I should have spent more time learning when I was a young boy. Maybe I wouldn't be here now, scared of Keli.

options.text: What did you want to be when you were a boy?
What did you want to be when you were a boy?

steps.player: What did you want to be when you were a boy?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Well, I loved to sit by the lake, with my toes in the water. I'd shoot the fish with my bow and arrow.

steps.player: That's a strange hobby for a boy.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It kept us from goblin hunting, which was what most boys did.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Hang on... Why do you ask? What do you want?

options.text: Hey, chill out. I won't cause you trouble.

steps.player: Hey, chill out. I won't cause you trouble.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Sorry, it's hard to relax when I'm on duty. Stress of the job, and all.

steps.player: So why do you do it?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: There's good money in it, and some of the shouting I rather like.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: RESISTANCE IS USELESS!

options.text: So what do you buy with your great wages?

steps.player: So what do you buy with your great wages?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Really, after working here, there's only time for a drink or three. All us guards go to the same pub and drink ourselves stupid.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It's what I enjoy these days. I can't resist the sight of a really cold beer.

options.text: I have some beer here. Fancy one?
Tell me about the life of a guard.
What did you want to be when you were a boy?
Tell me about the life of a guard.
Would you be interested in making a little more money?

steps.player: Would you be interested in making a little more money?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: What? Are you trying to bribe me? I may not be a great guard, but I am loyal. How dare you try to bribe me!

steps.player: No, no, you've got the wrong idea, totally. I just wondered if you wanted some part-time bodyguard work.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Oh... sorry. No, I don't need money. As long as you were not offering me a bribe.

options.text: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.player: I'd better go.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Thanks, I appreciate that. Talking on duty can be punished by having your mouth stitched up. These are tough people, make no mistake.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.player: Hello friend. I'm just here to rescue the Prince, if thats okay?

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.speaker: Joe
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.text: Thatsh a funny joke. You are lucky I'm shober. Go in peace, friend.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-ag.speaker: Leela
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-ag.text: You're back. How are things going with that guard?

steps.player: I could attack him.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: I don't think that's a good idea. Any violence could put the Prince at risk.

options.text: I might be able to get him drunk.
Maybe I could bribe him to leave.

steps.player: I'll keep thinking.

options.text: I might be able to get him drunk.

steps.player: I might be able to get him drunk.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Yes, that could work. I'd imagine three beers would do it. Why don't you give it a try?

options.text: Maybe I could bribe him to leave.

steps.player: Maybe I could bribe him to leave.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: It would take a lot of gold to convince him to betray Keli. She's not known to be kind to those she believes to be traitors. Perhaps there's something else you could try.

steps.player: I'm not sure yet.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You should try talking to him. He might give away some sort of weakness.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-on.speaker: Leela
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-on.text: You're back. How are things going with that guard?

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-on.speaker: Leela
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-leela-on.text: Great! I think that means we're ready. Go in and use some rope to tie Keli up. Once she's dealt with, use the key to free the Prince. Don't forget to give him his disguise so the guards outside don't spot him.

executing-the-rescue-dealing-with-lady-k.text: If the player is not ready:

steps.text: You cannot tie Keli up until you have all equipment and disabled the guard!
You'll need to deal with Lady Keli before freeing the Prince.

executing-the-rescue-dealing-with-lady-k.text: If the player used rope on Lady Keli:

steps.text: You overpower Keli, tie her up, and put her in a cupboard.

executing-the-rescue-dealing-with-lady-k.text: If the player is ready and talks to Lady Keli:

steps.player: Hello! I'm here to tie you up!

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: What?
You overpower Keli, tie her up, and put her in a cupboard.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-prince-a.player: Prince Ali? I'm here to rescue you.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-prince-a.speaker: Prince Ali
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-prince-a.text: Oh thank goodness! What's your plan?
If the player does not have a complete disguise and key:

steps.player: I've already dealt with Lady Keli and the guard. I'm going to get you a disguise so the guards outside don't spot you leaving. I'll be back once I have it.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-prince-a.text: If the player has a complete disguise and key:

steps.player: Take this disguise. You can use it to get past the guards outside.

steps.speaker: Prince Ali
steps.text: Thank you, my friend. I must leave you now, but my father will pay you well for this.
Prince Ali puts on the disguise and uses it to escape.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-afte.speaker: Joe
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-afte.text: Did yoush say something about shome Prince?

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-leela.text: You did it! Prince Ali is now safe again. You should head back to Al Kharid. I expect you will be well rewarded for your work.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-osman.text: Prince Ali is safe once more. Chancellor Hassan has your payment.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.speaker: Prince Ali
prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.text: Good to see you, friend. I am forever in your debt for what you did, as is all of Al Kharid.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.speaker: Prince Ali
prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.text: I know my father is very grateful as well. If he were in better health, he would have thanked you personally. However, at his age, it is best that he spends his time resting.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-prince-ali.player: I'm just happy to have helped. All the best.

prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-chancellor.speaker: Chancellor Hassan
prince-ali-rescued-talking-to-chancellor.text: Prince Ali is home safe. You have the eternal gratitude of the Emir for rescuing his son. Please, take this payment as a thank you.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Greetings I am Hassan, Chancellor to the Emir of Al- Kharid.

options.text: Can I help you? You must need some help here in the desert.

steps.speaker: Hassan
steps.text: I need the services of someone, yes. If you are interested, see the spymaster, Osman. I manage the finances here. Come to me when you need payment.

options.text: It's just too hot here. How can you stand it?
Do you mind if I just kill your warriors?

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: Have you found the spymaster, Osman, yet? You cannot proceed in your task without reporting to him.

starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.speaker: Hassan
starting-out-talking-to-chancellor-hassa.text: I understand the Spymaster has hired you. I will pay the reward only when the Prince is rescued.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.player: The chancellor trusts me. I have come for instructions.

starting-out-talking-to-osman.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman.text: Our prince is captive by the Lady Keli. We just need to make the rescue. There are two things we need you to do.

options.text: What is the first thing I must do?

steps.player: What is the first thing I must do?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: The prince is guarded by some stupid guards and a clever woman. The woman is our only way to get the prince out. Only she can walk freely about the area.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I think you will need to tie her up. One coil of rope should do for that. Then, disguise the prince as her to get him out without suspicion.

steps.player: How good must the disguise be?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Only enough to fool the guards at a distance. Get a skirt like hers. Same colour, same style. We will only have a short time.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Get a blonde wig, too. That is up to you to make or find. Something to colour the skin of the prince.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: My daughter and top spy, Leela, can help you. She has sent word that she has discovered where they are keeping the prince.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: It's near Draynor Village. She is lurking somewhere near there now.

options.text: What is the second thing you need?
Okay, I better go find some things.
What is the second thing you need?

steps.player: What is the second thing you need?

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: We need the key, or we need a copy made. If you can get some soft clay then you can copy the key...

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: ...If you can convince Lady Keli to show it to you for a moment. She is very boastful. It should not be too hard.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Bring the imprint to me, with a bar of bronze.

options.text: What is the first thing I must do?
What exactly is the second thing you need?
Okay, I better go find some things.
Okay, I better go find some things.

steps.player: Okay, I had better go find some things.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: May good luck travel with you. Don't forget to find Leela. It can't be done without her help.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.player: Can you tell me what I still need to get?

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has not obtained the key print:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: A print of the key in soft clay and a bronze bar. Then, collect the key from Leela.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has given Osman the key print and not picked up the bronze key:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You can collect the key from Leela.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has obtained the bronze key from Leela:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: The key you already have. Good.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has not obtained the blonde wig:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You need to make a blonde wig somehow. Leela may help.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has obtained the blonde wig:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: The wig you have got; well done.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player does not have a pink skirt in your inventory:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You will need a skirt that looks the same as Keli's.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player have a pink skirt in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You have the skirt. Good.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player does not have the skin paste in your inventory:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Something to make the prince's skin appear lighter.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has a skin paste in your inventory:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: You have the skin paint; well done. I thought you would struggle to make that.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player has a rope in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Yes, you have the rope.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: If the player does not have a rope in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: A rope with which to tie Keli up.

starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.speaker: Osman
starting-out-talking-to-osman-talking-to.text: Once you have everything, go to Leela. She must be ready to get the prince away.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.player: I am here to help you free the prince.

starting-out-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
starting-out-talking-to-leela.text: Your employment is known to me. Now, do you know all that we need to make the break?

options.text: I must make a disguise. What do you suggest?

steps.player: I must make a disguise. What do you suggest?

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Only the lady Keli, can wander about outside the jail. The guards will shoot to kill if they see the prince out so we need a disguise good enough to fool them at a distance.
If the player does not have a blonde wig:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You need a wig, maybe made from wool. If you find someone who can work with wool ask them about it. There's a witch nearby may be able to help you dye it.
If the player has a blonde wig:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: The wig you have got, well done.
If the player does not have a pink skirt:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You will need to get a pink skirt, same as Keli's.
If the player has a pink skirt:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You have got the skirt, good.
If the player does not have the skin paste:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: We still need something to colour the Prince's skin lighter. There's a witch close to here. She knows about many things. She may know some way to make the skin lighter.
If the player has the skin paste:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You have the skin paint, well done. I thought you would struggle to make that.
If the player does not have a rope:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You will still need some rope to tie up Keli, of course. I heard that there's a good rope maker around here.
If the player has a rope:

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: You have rope I see, to tie up Keli. That will be the most dangerous part of the plan.

options.text: I need to get the key made.

steps.player: I need to get the key made.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Yes, that is most important. There is no way you can get the real key. It is on a chain around Keli's neck. Almost impossible to steal.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Get some soft clay and get her to show you the key somehow. Then take the print, with bronze, to my father.

options.text: What can I do with the guards?

steps.player: What can I do with the guards?

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Most of the guards will be easy. The disguise will get past them. The only guard who will be a problem will be the one at the door.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: We can discuss this more when you have the rest of the escape kit.

options.text: I will go and get the rest of the escape equipment.

steps.player: I will go and get the rest of the escape equipment.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Good, I shall await your return with everything.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-ned.speaker: Ned
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-ned.text: Why, hello there, [lad/lass]. Me friends call me Ned. I was a man of the sea, but it's past me now. Could I be making or selling you some rope?

options.text: Could you make other things apart from rope?

steps.player: Could you make other things apart from rope?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: I'm sure I can. What are you thinking of?

options.text: Could you knit me a sweater?

steps.player: Could you knit me a sweater?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Do I look like a member of a sewing circle? Be off wi' you. I have fought monsters that would turn your hair blue.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: I don't need to be laughed at just 'cos I'm getting a bit old.

options.text: How about some sort of wig?

steps.player: How about some sort of wig?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Well... That's an interesting thought. Yes, I think I could do something. Give me 3 balls of wool and I might be able to do it.
If the player does not have three balls of wool:

steps.player: Great, I will get some. I think a wig would be useful.

steps.text: If the player has three balls of wool:

options.text: I have that now. Please, make me a wig.

steps.player: I have that now. Please, make me a wig.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Okay, I will have a go.
Ned gives you a pretty good wig.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Here you go. How's that for a quick effort? Not bad I think!

steps.player: Thanks Ned. There's more to you than meets the eye.

options.text: I will come back when I need you to make me one.

steps.player: I will come back when I need you to make me one.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Well, it sounds like a challenge. Come to me if you need one.

options.text: Could you repair the arrow holes in the back of my shirt?

steps.player: Could you repair the arrow holes in the back of my shirt?

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: Ah yes, it's a tough world these days. There's a few brave enough to attack from ten metres away.
Ned pulls out a needle and attacks your shirt.

steps.speaker: Ned
steps.text: There you go, good as new.

steps.player: Thanks Ned. Maybe next time they will attack me face to face.
Actually, I don't need anything.

options.text: Yes, I would like some rope.
No thanks, Ned. I don't need any.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-aggie.speaker: Aggie
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-aggie.text: What can I help you with?

options.text: What could you make for me?
Could you think of a way to make skin paste?

steps.player: Could you think of a way to make skin paste?

steps.text: If the player does not have all the required items:

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Why, it's one of my most popular potions. The women here, they like to have smooth looking skin. And I must admit, some of the men buy it as well.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: I can make it for you, just get me what's needed.

steps.player: What do you need to make it?

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Well dearie, you need a base for the paste. That's a mix of ash, flour and water. Then you need redberries to colour it as you want. Bring me those four items and I will make you some.
If the player has all the required items:

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Yes I can, I see you already have the ingredients. Would you like me to mix some for you now?

options.text: Yes please. Mix me some skin paste.

steps.player: Yes please. Mix me some skin paste.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: That should be simple. Hand the things to Aggie then.
You hand the ash, flour, water and redberries to Aggie. Aggie tips the ingredients into a cauldron and mutters some words.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Tourniquet, Fenderbaum, Tottenham, Marshmallow, MarbleArch.
Aggie hands you the Skin Paste.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: There you go dearie, your skin potion. That will make you look good at the Varrock dances.

options.text: No thank you, I don't need any skin paste right now.

steps.player: No thank you, I don't need any skin paste right now.

steps.speaker: Aggie
steps.text: Okay dearie, that's always your choice.

options.text: Cool, do you turn people into frogs?
You mad old witch, you can't help me.
Can you make dyes for me please?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.player: Are you the famous Lady Keli? Leader of the toughest gang of mercenary killers around?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.speaker: Lady Keli
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-lady-.text: I am Keli, you have heard of me then?

options.text: Heard of you? You are famous in Gielinor!

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: That's very kind of you to say. Reputations are not easily earned. I have managed to succeed where many fail.

options.text: I have heard a little, but I think Katrine is tougher.

steps.player: I think Katrine is still tougher.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well you can think that all you like. I know those blackarm cowards dare not leave the city. Out here, I am toughest. You can tell them that! Now get out of my sight, before I call my guards.

options.text: I have heard rumours that you kill people.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There's always someone ready to spread rumours. I hear all sort of ridiculous things these days.

options.text: I think Katrine is still tougher.
What is your latest plan then?

steps.player: Of course, you need not go into specific details.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well, I can tell you I have a valuable prisoner here in my cells. I can expect a high reward to be paid very soon for this guy. I can't tell you who he is, but he is a lot colder now.

options.text: Ah, I see. You must have been very skillful.

steps.player: You must have been very skillful.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Yes, I did most of the work. We had to grab the Pr...

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Er, we had to grab him without his ten bodyguards noticing. It was a stroke of genius.

options.text: Are you sure they will pay?
Can you be sure they will not try to get him out?
I should not disturb someone as tough as you.
That's great, are you sure they will pay?

steps.player: Are you sure they will pay?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: They will pay, or we will cut his hair off and send it to them.

steps.player: How about trying something tougher? Maybe cut his finger off?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: That's a good idea, I could use talented people like you. I may call on you if I need work doing.

options.text: You must have been very skillful.
Can you be sure they will not try to get him out?
I should not disturb someone as tough as you.
Can you be sure they will not try to get him out?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There is no way to release him. The only key to the door is on a chain around my neck and the locksmith who made the lock died suddenly when he had finished.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: There is not another key like this in the world.

options.text: Could I see the key please?

steps.player: Could I see the key please? Just for a moment. It would be something I can tell my grandchildren. When you are even more famous than you are now.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: As you put it that way I am sure you can see it. You cannot steal the key, it is on a Runite chain.
Keli shows you a small key on a strong looking chain.

options.text: Could I touch the key for a moment please?

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Only for a moment then.
You put a piece of your soft clay in your hand. As you touch the key, you take an imprint of it.

steps.player: Thank you so much, you are too kind, o great Keli.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You are welcome, run along now, I am very busy.

options.text: I should not disturb someone as tough as you.
That is a good way to keep secrets.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: It is the best way I know. Dead men tell no tales.

steps.player: I am glad I know none of your secrets, Keli.

options.text: I should not disturb someone as tough as you.
I should not disturb someone as tough as you.
You must have trained a lot for this work.
I should not disturb someone as tough as you.
No I have never really heard of you.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You must be new to this land then. EVERYONE knows of Lady Keli and her prowess with the sword.

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: I have used a sword since I was a small girl. I stabbed three people before I was 6 years old.

options.text: I should not disturb someone as tough as you, great lady.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: I need to do a lot of work, goodbye. When you get a little tougher, maybe I will give you a job.

options.text: No, still doesn't ring a bell.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: Well, you know of me now. I will wring your neck if you do not show respect.

options.text: I do not show respect to killers and hoodlums.

steps.player: I do not show respect to killers and hoodlums.

steps.speaker: Lady Keli
steps.text: You should, you really should. I am wealthy enough to place a bounty on your head. Or just remove your head myself. Now go, I am busy, too busy to fight a would-be hoodlum.

options.text: You must have trained a lot for this work.
I should not disturb someone as tough as you, great lady.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.speaker: Joe
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.text: Hi, I'm Joe, door guard for Lady Keli.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.player: Hi, who are you guarding here?

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.speaker: Joe
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-joe.text: Can't say, all very secret. You should get out of here. I am not supposed to talk while I guard.

preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.speaker: Osman
preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.text: Well done; we can make the key now.
Osman takes the key imprint and the bronze bar.

preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.speaker: Osman
preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.text: Pick the key up from Leela.

preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.player: Thank you. I will try to find the other items.
I'm afraid I lost that key you gave me.

preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.speaker: Osman
preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.text: Foolish [man/woman]! A new key will cost 15gp.

steps.player: Here, I have 15gp

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: That is good. I will have another key made. You may collect it from Leela.

preparations-for-rescue-bringing-the-imp.text: If the player does not have 15 coins:

steps.player: I haven't got 15 coins with me.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: Then come back to me when you do.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: My father sent this key for you. Be careful not to lose it.
Leela gives you a copy of the key to the prince's door.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: Good, you have all the basic equipment. Next to deal with the guard on the door. He is talkative, try to find a weakness in him.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.player: I'm afraid I lost that key you gave me.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.speaker: Leela
preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: Foolish [man/woman]! A new key will cost 15 coins.
If the player does not have 15 coins:

steps.player: I haven't got 15 coins with me.

steps.speaker: Leela
steps.text: Then come back to me when you do.

preparations-for-rescue-talking-to-leela.text: If the player does has 15 coins:

steps.text: Leela gives you another key.

options.text: I have some beer here. Fancy one?

steps.player: I have some beer here, fancy one?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Ah, that would be lovely, just one now, just to wet my throat.

steps.player: Of course, it must be tough being here without a drink.

steps.text: You hand a beer to the guard, he drinks it in seconds.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: That was perfect, I can't thank you enough.

steps.player: How are you? Still ok? Not too drunk?

steps.text: If the player has less than three beers:

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: No, I don't get drunk with only one drink. You would need a few to do that. But thanks for the beer.
If the player has two more beers:

steps.player: Would you care for another beer, my friend?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: I better not, I don't want to be drunk on duty.

steps.player: Here, just keep these for later, I hate to see a thirsty guard.

steps.text: You hand two more beers to the guard. He takes a sip of one, and then he drinks them both.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Franksh, that wash just what I need to shtay on guard. No more beersh, I don't want to get drunk.
The guard is drunk, and no longer a problem.

options.text: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.player: Tell me about the life of a guard.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Well, the hours are good.....

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: .... But most of those hours are a drag. If only I had spent more time in Knight school when I was a young boy. Maybe I wouldn't be here now, scared of Keli.

options.text: Hey, chill out, I won't cause you trouble.

steps.player: Hey, chill out, I won't cause you trouble. I was just wondering what you do to relax.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: You never relax with these people, but it's a good career for a young man and some of the shouting I rather like.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: RESISTANCE IS USELESS!

options.text: So what do you buy with these great wages?

steps.player: So what do you buy with these great wages?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Really, after working here, there's only time for a drink or three. All us guards go to the same bar and drink ourselves stupid.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It's what I enjoy these days, that fade into unconciousness. I can't resist the sight of a really cold beer.
(Shows initial options without the option to offer beer)

options.text: Tell me about the life of a guard.
Would you be interested in making a little more money?
I had better leave, I don't want trouble.
What did you want to be when you were a boy?
I had better leave, I don't want trouble.
What did you want to be when you were a boy?

steps.player: What did you want to be when you were a boy?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Well, I loved to sit by the lake, with my toes in the water and shoot the fish with my bow and arrow.

steps.player: That was a strange hobby for a little boy.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: It kept us from goblin hunting, which was what most boys did. What are you here for?

options.text: Chill out, I won't cause you trouble.

steps.player: Hey, chill out, I won't cause you trouble. I was just wondering what you do to relax.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: You never relax with these people, but it's a good career for a young man and some of the shouting I rather like.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: RESISTANCE IS USELESS!

options.text: So what do you buy with these great wages?
Tell me about the life of a guard.
Would you be interested in making a little more money?

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: WHAT?! Are you trying to bribe me? I may not be a great guard, but I am loyal. How DARE you try to bribe me!

steps.player: No, no, you got the wrong idea, totally. I just wondered if you wanted some part-time bodyguard work.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Oh. Sorry. No, I don't need money. As long as you were not offering me a bribe.
(Shows initial options without the option to offer beer)

options.text: I had better leave, I don't want trouble.
Tell me about the life of a guard.
I had better leave, I don't want trouble.
I had better leave, I don't want trouble.

steps.player: I had better leave, I don't want trouble.

steps.speaker: Joe
steps.text: Thanks, I appreciate that. Talking on duty can be punishable by having your mouth stitched up. These are tough people, no mistake.

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.player: Hello friend, I am just rescuing the prince, is that ok?

executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.speaker: Joe
executing-the-rescue-talking-to-joe-talk.text: Thatsh a funny joke. You are lucky I am shober. Go in peace, friend.

steps.player: Prince Brand, will you marry me?

steps.npc: Oh, my darling, you've made me the happiest person alive.

steps.player: Is that a yes?

steps.npc: Yes! We'll have to put off the actual ceremony until we can find a priest, but I will tell my father I have agreed to marry you.

standard-dialogue-after-royal-trouble-wh.npc: I hear you made peace between our kingdom and Etceteria once more. Well done, darling.

options.text: Have you found a priest for our marriage yet?

steps.player: Have you found a priest for our marriage yet?

steps.npc: I'm afraid not, darling. I don't think there is one to be had on these islands for love nor money...
Do not fear, though; I shall call for you as soon as one is found.

options.text: I'm having second thoughts about the wedding.

steps.player: I'm having second thoughts about the wedding. This marriage would change things, with an increase in responsibilities and duties you were keen to avoid.
While I want to support the kingdom, I don't want that to end up impacting your life negatively. Maybe it's too soon to make this kind of decision.

steps.npc: You're right, I am not interested in more responsibilities. I would have less time for poetry! Is that your final decision?

options.text: Yes, I think it's for the best.

steps.player: Yes, I think it's for the best.

steps.npc: I think you'll make a great Thane for our kingdom.

before-starting-the-heart-of-darkness.player: Hey, Itzla. How are things going?

before-starting-the-heart-of-darkness.npc: Father should make a full recovery, though given that his would-be killers are still out there, that's not anywhere near as much comfort as it should be.

before-starting-the-heart-of-darkness.text: If the player does not meet all of the requirements:

steps.player: In that case, I'll make sure to keep checking in.

steps.text: You do not meet all of the requirements to start The Heart of Darkness quest.

steps.npc: I've sent word to mother about what happened here, but I've not heard back yet. However, in the meantime, I've devised a little plan for how we might go about dealing with our cultist problem.

steps.prompt: Start The Heart of Darkness quest?

steps.player: What is it?

steps.npc: We're going to go... undercover!

steps.player: Undercover? What do you mean?

steps.npc: The Twilight Emissaries of course! If they are the ones responsible for what is now two attempts on my father's life, their deaths will be swift and brutal.
However, given we're somewhat civilised people, we can't exactly start executing cultists without definitive proof. How do we get that? By joining up of course!

steps.player: You want us to join the cult?

steps.npc: Exactly! Quite a clever plan, if I do say so myself.

steps.player: Right...

steps.text: Prepare for the arrival of Queen Zyanyi Arkan!

steps.player: I'd love to hear it, but I have some things I need to do first.

steps.npc: Very well. I'll be here when you're ready.

standard-dialogue.npc: Nilsal, [player name].

steps.npc: Well, now that the local cult of murderers is no longer trying to kill me or my father, I'd say things are looking up.
I'm also finding I've got a bit more time on my hands now that things are all sorted. I suggested to mother I spend that time in the Colosseum. I don't know if she was totally convinced.

steps.player: I can't imagine why...

steps.player: Yeah... definitely...

steps.npc: Anyway, I had to pay 250,000 coins to buy this one, so if you want it, that's how much I'll have to charge you.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-prison-pete.npc: Don't mind me, I was just leaving...

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome to the pet insurance bureau. How can I help you?

options.text: Can you tell me about pets and pet insurance?

steps.player: Can you tell me about pets and pet insurance?

steps.npc: Certainly! You can find pets while out on your adventures. They're very rare, but you may be lucky enough to find one.
You have a chance to find them when defeating bosses, playing minigames, and taking part in skilling activities.
If you do find one, they will be automatically insured against loss, for free!
If you then somehow lose your pet, you can reclaim it here for free also. The service used to cost Reclaim tokens worth 1,000,000 coins each. If you have any of those, I can refund you.

steps.player: I see, thank you.

options.text: I've lost a pet. Have you got it?

steps.player: I've lost a pet. Have you got it?

steps.npc: If you've lost your pet, it will be reclaimable here!
Let's have a look...

options.text: I have a pet that I'd like to insure.

steps.player: I have a pet that I'd like to insure.

steps.npc: You don't need to pay to insure your pet with me. They're automatically insured for free as soon as you find them!

If you lose a pet somehow, you can come here and reclaim them. It used to cost reclaim tokens, although we're now subsidised by the Grand Exchange and the service is free. If you have any reclaim tokens left, let
us know and we will buy them back.

steps.player: What pets have I insured?

steps.npc: Every pet you've ever found is automatically insured here!
Here, take a look...

options.text: My pet is still lost. Could you look again?

steps.player: My pet is still lost. Could you look again?

steps.npc: It's possible there was an error in our records. Let me check again for you.

steps.text: If you believe you have some pets that are not showing on your insurance record, please visit Probita with your pets and she will automatically insure them for you.

using-items-on-probita-any-other-item.npc: This is a pet insurance bureau. I'm not insuring that.

steps.npc: You can challenge someone to a game anywhere in the Games Zone (except on a PvP or Deadman world) by using the right click option.

steps.npc: Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn.

steps.npc: Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own.

initial-dialogue.npc: Ah, [player name]. You made it.

initial-dialogue.player: So, tell me about this proposal of yours.

initial-dialogue.npc: Camdozaal is a shadow of what it once was. We Imcando Dwarves were the finest artisans in the world, but now I am all that remains. Today, you'll only find echoes of our once great city.
But that which was once great can still be great again! We Imcando Dwarves know that better than most. There is hope for the future of Camdozaal. But I need help.
We have a Sacred Forge. You will find none other like it in all the world. Some of the greatest weapons of legend started life here.
The Forge could be the key to Camdozaal's future, but it's going out. If it does, I fear it will never be lit again. I can no longer gather the fuel it needs. But perhaps you can?
Barronite. You'll only find it in these ruins. If you can gather some for me, I can use it to keep the Forge lit. In return, I'll let you take what you want from our Great Vault.
I no longer have use for anything in the Vault. Besides, material possessions mean nothing compared to the fire of the Sacred Forge.

initial-dialogue.player: So I find barronite in the ruins and bring it to you? Doesn't sound too difficult. Where should I start?

initial-dialogue.npc: Anywhere you like. The ruins are filled with barronite, so anything you do here should yield some. If you need more information on specific things you can do, just let me know.

options.text: I have something I'd like you to examine.
options.condition: If the player has found an item within the Ruins of Camdozaal:

options.text: What happened to the other Imcando Dwarves?

steps.player: What happened to the other Imcando Dwarves?

steps.npc: Ah... It's a tough tale to tell. Even though it's been many years since the last of my kin died out, the memory is still fresh.

steps.player: You don't have to tell me if the memory hurts too much.

steps.npc: No, I will. The legacy of my kin must live on.
As you can see around you, Camdozaal was once a great city. Alive with the hum of activity. We dug deep into the mountain and reaped the rewards.
Our methods would often differ from other dwarves. Whereas they just used traditional smithing techniques, we would combine them with magic as well.
Alas, that was ultimately our undoing. We learned of a horde of barbarians pillaging across the land, hunting down and killing anyone who dared use magic.
We underestimated them. We believed our weapons would be enough to keep us safe. We were wrong.
The barbarians brought ruin upon Camdozaal. Most of my kind died as the city collapsed around them. Only a few of us survived until the end. Now, only I remain.

steps.player: The world has changed a lot, Ramarno. Magic is practiced freely. Those barbarians failed to wipe it from Gielinor.

steps.npc: I'm glad they didn't win, I suppose. But it doesn't change much for me. I am still the last Imcando Dwarf.

steps.player: I'm sorry Ramarno. I will do my best to help ensure the legacy of your kin lives on.

steps.npc: Thank you, [player name]. That gives me some hope. If you have any more questions, do not hesitate to ask.

steps.player: I'll see you later.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-me.npc: Ah [player name]. I'm sure you have plenty of questions. I will do my best to answer them.

steps.player: What can I do here?

steps.npc: As you can see, Camdozaal isn't the city it once was. That said, there are still a few things around here that might interest you. There's the golem workshop, the barronite mine and the offering altar.

options.text: Tell me more about the golem workshop.

steps.player: Tell me more about the golem workshop.

steps.npc: You'll find it to the east. It was once the forefront of our technological advances. Sadly, it was also one of the major factors that led to our doom.

steps.player: What were you doing there?

steps.npc: Camdozaal was built upon the ruins of an older civilization. Little trace of them remained by the time we arrived. However, when building the city, ancient golems were discovered.
These golems were very crude. They were mostly made from clay, of all things. We used our advanced Smithing knowledge to improve their form. Eventually, we were able to get them working again.
We kept pushing with the golems. Many of them we imbued with magical energies. We started with mind and body energy, but eventually moved on to chaos as well.
Alas, the influence of chaos had grave results. We lost control of many. Those that became corrupt had to be locked away, but by then it was already too late.
The barbarians had learnt of our experimentation, and were determined to destroy all traces of it.
Ironically, locking them away meant the golems were among the few things to survive the barbarians. If you fancy a bit of combat, you might want to go take a look.
They're largely made of barronite now, so they're a good source of the stuff.
Their cores are also very interesting. Apparently, the dwarves of the golem workshop once used old cores to craft runes. Maybe you could do the same.

options.text: Tell me more about the barronite mine.

steps.player: Tell me more about the barronite mine.

steps.npc: You'll find it to the north west. Unsurprisingly, it's the best place to find barronite in the city.
At one time, our miners would work all through the day there to gather the barronite needed to power the Sacred Forge. That was a long time ago.
If you're lucky, you might find other things while mining there. We were not the first to build a home beneath this mountain. Sometimes traces of an older civilization can be found.

steps.player: What kind of traces?

steps.npc: You might find some ancient relics encased within barronite. If you do, you can use the anvils here to crack open the deposits.
The relics are of no interest to me. Maybe some of your race would find them interesting.

options.text: Tell me more about the offering altar.

steps.player: Tell me more about the offering altar.

steps.npc: You'll find it to the south west. It's not something that ever interested me, but most of my kind were followers of Saradomin - the god of order and wisdom.
Many of my kin would visit the altar to make offerings in his name.
First, they'd catch fish from the nearby reservoir. Next, they'd ritually prepare them at tables by the altar. Finally, they'd use the altar to offer the fish.
There's plenty of barronite to be found within the reservoir, so it might be worth checking out. Be warned though: worshipping gods never did my kind any good.

steps.player: Let's talk about something else.

steps.npc: Very well.

steps.npc: What do you mean?

steps.npc: An Imcando Dwarf survived outside the city?

steps.player: Yes. He looks to be doing quite well for himself. In fact, he seems to be a master of Smithing.

steps.npc: I can't believe it. I hope to meet him one day. He must be a truly amazing smith to reach such heights.

steps.player: Well he's certainly an interesting dwarf.

steps.npc: Thank you, [player name]! You've given me hope that my kin can live on. If you need help with anything else, let me know.

steps.player: Can I use the Forge?

steps.npc: I'm afraid not. The Sacred Forge is like none other in existence. Only an Imcando Dwarf could use it correctly.

steps.player: What makes it so special?

steps.npc: Truth be told, I don't fully know. It's far older than I am. It was supposedly built in the earliest days of the city.
What I do know is that it's been imbued with powerful magic - some said that of the gods themselves. The Forge powers the entire city, or what's left of it at least.
I've been doing my best to keep it lit over the years. It's not a job I'm capable of any more though. That's why I'm hoping you can help.
Bring me any barronite you find. In return, I can channel enough power from the Forge into the city or even open the Great Vault.

options.text: What will powering the city do?

steps.player: What will powering the city do?

steps.npc: From what I can tell, my ancestors linked the Forge to the entire city.
It truly is the heart of this place. From it, I can channel any barronite you have into empowering different aspects of the city.

steps.player: What will that do?

steps.npc: The Sacred Forge is a strange beast, but with its arcane power, you'll see an improvement to the various activities you can do in the city.
Would you like to take a look?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.npc: Very well. Anything else you'd like to talk about?

steps.player: What is the Great Vault?

steps.npc: It's one of the many marvels of this city. We used it to store our greatest creations, along with our most interesting finds.
Of course, I have no use for those treasures myself. I'd happily give them up to keep the Sacred Forge alive.
Now be warned - I won't be able to channel much power into the Vault. I can't afford to waste too much barronite. You'll only have a limited amount of time in there.
Not only that, there's an automatic security system that activates if power to the Vault is lost. If that happens, you'll be removed. I imagine any treasures would be lost as well.

steps.player: How much barronite do you need to power it?

steps.npc: Hmm, for a minute, I suppose 750 barronite shards should do the trick.
If you do go in, I'd suggest heading to the back first. That's where the most valuable things are kept.

options.text: How can I train my Ranged?

steps.player: How can I train my Ranged?

steps.text: If the player's Ranged level is below X {{tmissing}} :

steps.npc: To start with you'll need a bow and arrows, you were given a Shortbow and some arrows when you arrived here from Tutorial island.
Alternatively, you can claim a training bow and some arrows from me.
Mikasi, the Magic Combat tutor and I both give out items every 30 minutes, however you must choose whether you want runes or ranged equipment.
To claim the Training bow and arrows, right-click on me and choose Claim, to claim runes right-click on the Magic Combat tutor and select Claim.
Not all bows can use every type of arrow, most bows have a limit. You can find out your bows limit by checking the Ranged skill guide.
If you do decide to use the Training bow, you will only be able to use the Training arrows with it. Remember to pick up your arrows, re-use them and come back when you need more.
Once you have your bow and arrows, equip them by selecting their Wield option in your inventory.
You can change the way you attack by going to the combat options tab. There are three attack styles for bows. Those styles are Accurate, Rapid and Longrange.
Accurate increases your bows attack accuracy. Rapid will increase your attack speed with the bow. Longrange will let you attack your enemies from a greater distance.

steps.text: If the player is eligible for Adventure paths:

steps.npc: If you need some more advice, you should talk to Adventurer Jon about Adventure paths. He may even have a handy starter kit you can use.

steps.text: If the player's Ranged level is above Y {{tmissing}}:

steps.npc: My word, I think you should be the one giving me advice instead, but I will do my best.
You should know the basics of ranged combat by now, but if you are looking for somewhere to test your skills and make some money, you should try hunting Moss giants in Varrock sewers.

If you are lucky you might find a Mossy key, with this key you will be able to enter Bryophyta's lair. Make sure to bring plenty of food and good armour and weapons when you fight her as you will need it.
If your lucky you might snag some goodies that you can sell for a decent profit.
If you are looking to do something different, visit the ranging guild over near Hemenster, there you can practice your archery and earn tickets for it at the same time.
You can then hand those tickets in for a variety of goods you can use to train your Ranged skill.
If you are ever in the market for a new bow or some arrows, you should head on over to Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock. I can show you where the shop is if you like.

options.text: How do I create a bow and arrows?

steps.npc: Ahh the art of fletching. Fletching is used to create your own bow and arrows.

steps.text: If the player is on a free-to-play world:

steps.npc: To create your bow and arrows you would need to gather some wood, feathers, arrow heads and bow string. The wood would be to make arrow shafts which can be turned into unstrung bows and arrow shafts.
Unfortunately, Fletching is a member only skill so you will have to get your ranging supplies from shops or other players.
Is there anything else you want to know?

steps.text: If the player is on a members' world:

steps.npc: It's quite simple really. You'll need an axe to cut some logs from trees and a knife. Knives can be found in and around the Lumbridge castle and in the Varrock General store upstairs.
Use your knife on the logs. This will bring up a menu listing items you can fletch.
For arrows you will need to smith some arrow heads and kill some chickens for feathers.
Add the feathers to your Arrow shafts to make Headless arrows, then use your chosen arrow heads on the Headless arrows to make your arrows.
Now for making bows. When accessing the fletching menu, instead of choosing Arrows shafts, you can make an unstrung bow instead.
To complete the bow you will need to get your hands on a Bow string.
First you will need to get some flax from a flax field. There's one south of Seers' Village. Gather flax, then spin it on a spinning wheel, there's one in Seers' Village too.
This makes bow strings which you can then use on the unstrung bows to make a working bow!
