standard-dialogue-if-the-player-does-not.player: Hmm, I wonder if there's something I could use to communicate with him.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-gh.npc: Aaah! What are you doing down here!?

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-gh.player: Hey, keep it down! I've come to slay the monsters down here.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-gh.npc: Oh, that's ok then. These vile creatures do make an awful racket.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-gh.player: You should hear it upstairs! Those Aberrant Spectres are just the worst.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-gh.npc: I'm Raulyn. Once servant to the great Viggora who built this place centuries ago.
This was, of course, before the building started to sink into the swamp...
Oh, and the darn Zamorakian mages. They didn't help matters. Always making a mess.
I've been here ever since. You're the first person I've spoken to in over 200 years.
Sometimes, but it's not all that bad. I hope you stop by more often!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-gh.player: Hopefully! I should be going now, speak to you later.

when-attempting-to-kill-monsters-that-ar.npc: I don't think that's what you're meant to be slaying.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-the-f.npc: Oh, hello again. Want to buy some armour?

steps.player: I'll have a look.
Not right now.
Oh, look! A raven!

steps.npc: Nope, we're not doing that again!

steps.player: Wait... What? Doing what?

before-shades-of-mort-ton-as-an-afflicte.npc: The serum works...but it's not too fresh, make some yourself and then it might work for longer.

after-shades-of-mort-ton.npc: Ah, it's you, how's it going?

after-shades-of-mort-ton.player: Can you open a store for me?

after-shades-of-mort-ton.npc: Sure, which store do you wanna see?

options.text: Can I see the general store please?
Can I see the building store please?

steps.player: Ok, thanks

using-serum-208-on-him.npc: Well done...I feel this serum is really working on me. I think you've cracked it my friend!  I'd like to give you something for your trouble!
Ah, it's you, how's it going?

using-serum-208-on-him.player: Can you open a store for me?

using-serum-208-on-him.npc: Sure, which store do you wanna see?

options.text: Can I see the general store please?
Can I see the building store please?

using-serum-208-on-him-using-serum-208-o.npc: You've already used the permanent serum on me, you don't need to use that any more.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Huh! I'm Razvan, ravaging after food is what I mostly do...occasionally I'll happen across a rat...and that's a good day...just like today!

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Huh? I'm Razvan. Ravaging after food is what I mostly do. Ocasionally I'll happen across a rat, and that's a good day, just like today!

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

standard-dialogue-prior-to-the-release-o.player: Just wondering what you're up to?

standard-dialogue-prior-to-the-release-o.npc: Right now, not a lot. I'm just here for a drink or two.

steps.npc: Hello again! I'm so glad to hear that you decided to join our family. Unfortunately, I'm all out of personal welcome packages, but I'm sure I'll have more soon.

steps.player: Personal welcome packages?

steps.npc: That's right! They contain all the details on our Pillars of Progress, and also include a company branded mug!
As I say, I unfortunately don't have any available right now, but do let me know if there's anything else I can help you with.

steps.player: Will do, thanks.

starting-out.speaker: Cook
starting-out.text: How is the adventuring going, my friend?

options.text: Do you have any other quests for me?

steps.player: Do you have any other quests for me? That last one of yours was so much fun, I was hoping you would!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ooooh dear, I might have, but it's all very embarrassing...

steps.player: Embarrassing? How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Weeellll... You know I told you that it was the Duke's birthday?

steps.player: Yup, that's why I had to go and collect you things to make a cake with wasn't it?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yeeeesssss... Weeeelllll...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: It isn't. I don't even know when his birthday is!

steps.prompt: How does that make you feel?

steps.player: GRRRR! Why did you have me running around finding ingredients for you then?!?!

options.text: I don't really care to be honest.

steps.player: So you lied to me to get me to do you a favour?
Fair enough, you're not the first, but why lie? You could have just asked me, I'd have been happy to help.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I needed to test you and see if I could trust you...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I am in a terrible pickle, and I desperately need somebody trustworthy to help me out!

options.text: What seems to be the problem?

steps.player: You need help AGAIN? Well, what seems to be the problem?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, you're obviously trustworthy, I guess I could tell you...

steps.player: Please do. The suffering of others always seems to turn out very profitable for me.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well... It's like this...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you ever hear of Franizzard Van Lumbcook?

steps.player: Erm... Can't say I have.
And with a name like that, I'm sure I would remember.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, he was a great chef, and also my ancestor.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: One hundred years ago there was a very important meeting held here in Lumbridge Castle, and he cooked a banquet for the meeting, which was so stupendously amazing that he was offered a job for life, along with all

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: of his descendants.

steps.player: So you have your job because a hundred years ago your ancestor was a very good cook.
I don't see how that's much of a problem for you...
In fact I would say you are a VERY LUCKY man indeed. Frankly, I'd have fired you by now if you worked for me.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oooooh no.... You don't understand...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: This big important secret meeting that Franizzard cooked for is held here in Lumbridge castle every 10 years, and tonight will be the tenth anniversary of it!

steps.player: Still not seeing the problem...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, I have always felt like a failure as a cook, and that my job here is down to the skills of my ancestor.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I want to prove to the world that I am a great cook too!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: But to do that... (sigh) No, it just won't work...

steps.player: What won't? Come on man, pull yourself together and speak to me!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: (sniff) Weeeeelll... I thought that I would recreate the meal Franizzard cooked all of those years ago, the one that impressed

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: everybody so much... There's just this small problem though...

steps.player: Let me take a wild guess: You have the recipe but you don't have any of the ingredients, and OBVIOUSLY you can't just go and get them yourself?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes! However did you know?

steps.player: Call it a hunch.
Okay, tell me what you're after and then I'll decide if I want to help you or not.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, they are common enough ingredients, although I must admit the recipe I am following is very strange indeed...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I will pay you upfront for any expenses you may incur while obtaining them, and of course you may keep the change for being so helpful to me.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Please can you help me? The feast is scheduled to start very soon, and I simply cannot leave!

steps.prompt: Start the Recipe for Disaster quest?

steps.player: I would love to help you! What do I have to do?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, I have an incredibly important banquet that I have to prepare for, and I am using an ancient cookbook to recreate the meal my famous ancestor made a hundred years ago.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Most of the ingredients I was able to obtain fairly easily, but there were some... oddities... that I have been unable to lay my hands on.

steps.player: Like what?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I need the following ingredients as soon as possible!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: One Eye Of NewtA freshly made 'Dirty Blast'A rotten tomato

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: And a glass of greenman's ale.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I have given you 100 coins to cover any expenses you may incur, feel free to keep the change.

steps.player: I'll go look for those for you then!
To be honest... I just can't be bothered.
Sorry about that.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh nooooo... What am I going to do now?

steps.player: Dunno. Maybe I'll change my mind and come back later and help you.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oooohhh... I really hope you do...

options.text: No thanks, I don't want to help.

steps.player: You know... Thinking about it...
I just can't be bothered to help you out. You'll have to find some other adventurer to do your little quest for you.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I guess I don't have anything more to say to you then.

steps.player: I guess you don't.

options.text: How do you still have a job?

steps.player: I'm curious... How exactly do you still have a job?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm sorry? How do you mean?

steps.player: It's just surprising that you would still have employment as head cook of Lumbridge castle, given how obviously bad at your job you are.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: WHAT?

steps.player: Well, things you would expect every kitchen to have... Eggs, milk, flour... You know... But you don't.
And what is worse, you don't even go off and get them yourself, you expect people like me to run around after you!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I know I'm such a failure... I bring shame to my honourable ancestor, and now I need help again...

steps.player: Help again?
You need help AGAIN? Well, what seems to be the problem?

options.text: I am getting strong and mighty.

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.player: About those ingredients you wanted for the banquet...

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.text: Did you bring them? Remember, I need an eye of newt, a glass of greenman's ale, a rotten tomato, and a 'Dirty Blast'!
If the player has none of the ingredients:

steps.player: Erm... Sorry, I don't have any of that with me...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well come back when you have all of them! And hurry! It is a VERY important meeting!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.text: If the player has some of the ingredients:

steps.player: Weeelll... I have some of that stuff with me, but not all of it...

steps.text: If the player has only one of the ingredients:

steps.player: I'm afraid I only have [a/an] [item name] with me...

steps.text: If the player has only two of the ingredients:

steps.player: I'm afraid I only have [a/an] [item 1] and [a/an] [item 2] with me...

steps.text: If the player is missing only the eye of newt:

steps.player: I've got a 'Dirty Blast', a Greenman's ale and a rotten tomato, I just need to get the eye of newt!

steps.text: If the player is missing only the rotten tomato:

steps.player: I've got the 'Dirty Blast', a Greenman's ale and the eye of newt, I just have to find myself a rotten tomato...

steps.text: If the player is missing only the greenman's ale:

steps.player: I managed to find a 'Dirty Blast', a rotten tomato and an eye of newt, but I didn't manage to get a hold of a Greenman's ale yet...

steps.text: If the player is missing only the dirty blast:

steps.player: I've got you a Greenman's ale, the rotten tomato and the eye of newt, but haven't had any luck on the 'Dirty Blast' yet...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Come back and see me when you've got everything I need!

steps.player: Okay then. I'll get on it.

options.text: Where do I get an eye of newt?

steps.player: Where would I find an eye of newt?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I don't know. A newt's face?

steps.player: Thank you so much for that help.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah, I don't know where they get them, they usually have them at herblore and magic shops.

options.text: Where do I get a rotten tomato?

steps.player: Where would I find a rotten tomato?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm not entirely sure, but I hear they're sold for public spectacles.

steps.player: Public spectacles?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yeah. Pre-arranged combats, caught thieves on show, that sort of thing.

options.text: Where do I get a greenman's ale?

steps.player: Where would I find a greenman's ale?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, as the official sponsored drink of Castle Wars it might be worth looking around there.

options.text: Where do I get a 'Dirty Blast'?

steps.player: Where would I find a 'Dirty Blast'? I've never heard of it before.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes, I must admit I had never heard of it either until reading through my ancestor's cookbook.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Tell me, do you know how to make a Fruit Blast?

steps.player: A Fruit Blast? Sure, like they sell at Blurberry's Bar, right?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah, so you've heard of it then? But for this recipe I'd need a fresh one; you can't just buy me one from a shop or from your friends.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, a 'Dirty Blast' is a freshly made Fruit Blast, but then for some reason you add ash at the end!

steps.player: Freshly made? Why did you specify that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Apparently the ash reacts with the freshly squeezed juice in the glass. It means you can't just buy one Blurberry made earlier, you'll have to make it yourself.

steps.player: Oh. Well, it shouldn't take that long.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: That's the spirit!

steps.player: A Fruit Blast? Can't say I've ever heard of it...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah, well, they're a popular Gnomic delicacy served at the Blurberry bar. But for this recipe I'd need a fresh one; you can't just buy me one from a shop or from your friends.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Basically, what you do is juice a pineapple, an orange and a lemon, then put them all into a cocktail shaker.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Pour that into a glass, then top with a slice of lemon.

steps.player: Okaaaay... So what's a 'Dirty Blast'?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, apparently after you have done the above then by adding ashes you create a unique new drink.

steps.player: Sounds horrible..

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I agree, but it's what the recipe specifically needs.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Bear in mind it will only work with very fresh ingredients, so you will have to make your own cocktail, not rely on one of the pre made ones Blurberry sells.

d-j-vu-using-ashes-on-a-fruit-blast.player: That looks disgusting, but it's what the cook asked for...

d-j-vu-attempting-to-drink-the-dirty-bla.player: No thanks, that looks DISGUSTING! I won't drink that!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.player: About those ingredients you wanted for the banquet...

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.text: Did you bring them? Remember, I need an eye of newt, a glass of greenman's ale, a rotten tomato, and a 'Dirty Blast'!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.player: You will be happy to know... I have all of that with me!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.text: You absolutely MUST go through into the dining room just there and see the feast I have prepared.

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.text: I simply won't take no for an answer!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.text: Why haven't you gone and looked at the feast I have prepared yet? Trust me, it will be a sight the likes of which you will never see again!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.player: I don't know... I'm just... quite busy, I guess...

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.text: No, honestly, you MUST go in there!

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Screen fades out and in as the player enters the dining hall. Cutscene begins, zooming in on Duke Horacio.
If Beneath Cursed Sands hasn't been completed:

steps.text: Camera switches to Osman.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I welcome Osman, Spymaster for the Emir of Al Kharid.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I thank you for your hospitality.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: If Beneath Cursed Sands has been completed:

steps.text: Camera switches to Selim.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I welcome Selim, acting Spymaster for the Emir of Al Kharid.

steps.speaker: Selim
steps.text: I thank you for your hospitality.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome the chief guard of the White Wolf Mountain dwarves.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome Pirate Pete from Braindeath Island.
Camera switches to Wartface and Bentnoze.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome the chief of the Goblin Village.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome Skrach Uglogwee of the Feldip Hills ogres.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Skrach Uglogwee
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Der ogres, dey call me Bone Cruncher.
Camera switches to the Lumbridge Guide.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome my neighbour, Phileas the Lumbridge Guide.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Lumbridge Guide
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I didn't have far to travel!

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: From the town of Edgeville, I welcome Evil Dave.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Evil Dave
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: These secret meetings are SOOO EVIL!
Camera pans to Sir Amik Varze.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: A hearty welcome to Sir Amik Varze, leader of the White Knights...
Camera switches to an empty chair.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: ...and finally, I welcome the ruler of Ape Atoll, Awowogei.
Horacio kicks Awowogei who moves back several spaces.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Lumbridge Guide
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I think he's lost his Amulet of Manspeak.
The mysterious old man suddenly teleports next to Horacio, and takes a bow.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Mysterious Old Man
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Here you go Horacio, it's all yours!
The mysterious old man teleports away.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Excuse me while I deal with this...

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Osman/Selim
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: We should do something about that old man.
Evil Bob suddenly teleports next to Osman/Selim.
The door opens and the player walks in.
The Culinaromancer suddenly teleports into the room, at the head of the table.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Culinaromancer
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Hah! Your chef did! And now I'll kill you!
The Culinaromancer launches a spell at each side of the table. The spells go through every attendee who is seated.
The door opens and Aris walks in.
The Culinaromancer launches a spell at Aris.
Aris conducts a time freezing spell.
The screen flashes white, then fades back in, showing that all the attendees except Aris and the player have been frozen in time.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Aris
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: [player name], you must help me defeat this evil!
Screen fades to black as cutscene ends.

chef-surprise-talking-to-aris.speaker: Aris
chef-surprise-talking-to-aris.text: Hello there adventurer. How can I assist you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I am the fortune-teller. My friends call me Aris.

steps.player: Okay then Aris...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Was there something you wanted to ask me about?

steps.player: I do have a question. A very GOOD question.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Oh yes? What's that then?

steps.player: Just what in the flipping hippo is going on?!?!?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: ...flipping hippo?

steps.player: Yeeeess.... You've never heard that phrase?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: No, no I'm quite sure that I never have.

steps.player: Well, that's not the point!
Please, tell me what just happened!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Certainly. That fellow over there in the chef's hat is called the Culinaromancer.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: A hundred years ago, he threatened the secret council with death, but was foiled by the quick thinking of his assistant, who managed to trap him in another dimension.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: As a result of that action, the assistant was offered a job for life as head cook of Lumbridge, for himself and all his future descendants.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Now, apparently the current head cook of Lumbridge decided to recreate his ancestors greatest achievement, not realising that his achievement was not a meal but a powerful food-magic, and by recreating the spell he has

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: inadvertently freed the evil Culinaromancer from his prison, to wreak havoc upon this world once more.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Naturally, when I saw what was happening, I intervened with a simple Tempus Cessit spell, so that we would have time to immunise the secret council from his attack, and so that we can defeat the Culinaromancer

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: once and for all.

steps.player: Um... what?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: You want me to explain it again?

steps.player: Yes please. But slower. And more understandable.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: (sigh) Okay then: 100 years ago, the evil food magician was defeated and banished.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Because of you and the Lumbridge cook, he is now free.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: He was about to slaughter all of these people, but I stopped time so that you could protect them.

steps.player: You stopped time? And... wait, I have to protect them? Why me?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes I stopped time. And YOU have to do it partly because you helped release him by getting those ingredients, and partly because I am stuck here keeping the spell intact.

steps.player: Isn't stopping time kind of... You know, dangerous?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Oh, unbelievably so. This is why I have limited the time bubble to this room and this room alone.

steps.player: Huh? How does that work?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Everything outside this room continues to flow through time. This is why outside of this room you have already defeated the Culinaromancer, and protected the

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: members of the secret council.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Inside this room however you have not.

steps.player: Uh... what?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Where time has been frozen in this room, outside it continues to flow, so this room is now currently in what we would call 'the past', meaning events inside here have already happened, and the longer time continues to flow

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: outside, the more removed from normal time this room becomes.

steps.player: Wait... so I've already saved all of these council members and defeated the Culinaromancer?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. But only outside. What you need to do now is save them in here as well, so that time can resume its normal ebb and flow.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Otherwise there will be increasing temporal pressure, and the entire universe might explode!

steps.player: Not the whole universe! That's where I keep my stuff!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. That is why it is so important that you protect them all.

steps.player: But... You said I already had...?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. You have. In the future, which is also the present, but not in the present, which is also the past.

steps.player: My brain hurts...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, time travel tends to do that to people.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I suggest you don't worry about it too much, just make sure you protect each council member and then defeat the Culinaromancer.

steps.player: How would I do that?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Each council member will have their own unique dish that will serve to counteract the Culinaromancer's spell.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Inspect the one you wish to save, and I will offer any advice I have.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Was there anything else you wanted to ask me about?

steps.player: Who's that guy over there? Seemed like you knew each other.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: He calls himself the Culinaromancer. He is an extremely evil man, with incredibly powerful magics.

steps.player: Culinaromancer?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, that's correct. Just as an Oneiromancer draws their magical powers from dreams, or a  necromancer draws their strength from the energies of the dead, a Culinaromancer uses

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: food as his source of magical power.

steps.player: Food? What's so dangerous about food?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Do not underestimate the latent power of foodstuffs as a source of magical energy.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Not only are they a fundamental life-force, but they often evoke great emotional attachment.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Do not underestimate him, part of his strength lies in the fact his unique type of magical power is quite obscure, I have seen many fall before him.

steps.player: Okay, so he's powerful, but I don't get why he's here!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ah, it is a very old story indeed.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: A hundred years ago, he worked here in Lumbridge castle for the then Duke as a cook.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: This was all a pretence, of course. As part of his duties he was allowed access to many exotic and esoteric foodstuffs. These allowed him to experiment with his magic and increase his power exponentially.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Building his power was just the first step however.

steps.player: How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Knowing of the regular meetings of the secret council here in Lumbridge, the Culinaromancer decided that he would eliminate all of them as the first step to his plans for world domination.

steps.player: Would that have worked?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Possibly, we might never know. As his plans were coming to fruition his assistant discovered them, and used his own magic against him, to trap him in another dimension where his powers would

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: be useless.

steps.player: Then how did he escape?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Well, the current cook of Lumbridge obviously discovered an ancient manuscript of his ancestors, and believing it to be a recipe decided to recreate the spell that banished him.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Which obviously seems to have opened the portal enough for him to escape back to this dimension. So this is partly your fault.

steps.player: Oh. Those ingredients?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, those ingredients. So I hold you responsible for assisting me in ridding him of this dimension once and for all.

steps.player: Yeah... I had a feeling you were going to say that...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Are you clear on what you have to do, or was there something you wished me to explain?

steps.player: Who are these people? Seems like quite the random selection in here!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: The people you see assembled here are the self-styled secret council of Gielinor.

steps.player: 'Self-styled' council? What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Many centuries ago, a small group from around the world of Gielinor decided that these lands needed to be directed, that it was too risky to leave the fates of this land to luck and the gods.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: They decided that every 10 years they would meet to discuss current events, and shape how the world might then develop.

steps.player: So they're pretty influential people?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: No, not really. For all of their grand schemes and ideas, nothing ever gets done except every ten years they have a bit of a posh meal together and a bit of a gossip.

steps.player: I see... But this evil cook guy that just appeared thinks they might be important?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I don't really know what he thinks.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Either way I'm not prepared to let him get away with a brazen attack on anybody while I have the power to stop him.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: And given that this is partly your fault, I fully expect your assistance in saving them.

steps.player: MY fault??

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. You were the one who provided the cook with the ingredients that he needed to allow the Culinaromancer to return to this dimension.

steps.player: I just don't understand any of this...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: What exactly is it that you don't understand?

steps.player: Uh... Is it me, or did this room just get much bigger?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ah, that would be the time dilation effect.

steps.player: The... time dilation... effect?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. As time has stopped flowing in the normal way, your eyes are playing tricks on you, as the pictures absorbed by your eyes take slightly longer to reach your brain

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: than normal.

steps.player: Erm... what?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: As everybody knows, time flows from north to south, so my freezing time means that this room has apparently stretched slightly along its horizontal axis.

steps.player: Um... does that even make sense?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Don't let it worry you too much. It's just an optical illusion, the room is exactly the same size as it always has been, it just appears to be a tiny bit bigger.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Anything else you wanted to know?

steps.player: Ah, forget it, I don't want to talk to you now.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, I'm sure you have far more important things to do than SAVING THE ENTIRE UNIVERSE!

steps.player: They're both you!

steps.text: What will happen if you don't?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: I don't understand this at all.

ape-atoll-snake-dungeon-leaving-the-dung.text: You climb up the rope and out of the pit.

It looks like you'll need to find a way to bring the bananas within reach.

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-using-rope-on-.text: You are not monkey enough to bend that tree!
You're just not that great an ape!

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-no-bananas.text: There are no bananas on the tree right now.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nuts.text: You scamper through the vine choked hole...
...and find yourself in front of a magnificent Monkey Nut bush.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nuts-nutless-bush.text: There are no nuts on the bush right now.

You don't understand a word. Maybe you've forgotten to wear something...

ape-atoll-entering-exiting-the-cave-to-c.text: The hot rocks burn your feet.
The snake isn't ready for cooking yet.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: (Iwazaru is hysterically trying to get your attention)

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: I think Iwazaru is trying to say something.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: mmmh!! (He quickly makes some signs at Kikazaru)

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Iwazaru says that you have the wrong kind of monkey nuts.  Ordinary Monkeys nuts just won't do.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: There is a special type of monkey nut that grows on the island and has a subtle and distinctive flavour that is highly valued by all monkeys with a sophisticated palate.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: They are called Tchiki monkey nuts and require a very particular combination of soil and climate.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: They need the minerals and dampness found in hill caves, but they also cannot grow without sunlight.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Myth and Legend shrouds the History of the Tchiki Monkey Nut.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Some say that it is the nut that gave monkeys their superior intelligence!

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Others say Tchiki Monkey nuts are the food of the Monkey Gods.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Either way, you will have to find a path through treacherous undergrowth to harvest the Nut of Kings.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: I never realised monkey sign language was so...concise. Anyway, where do I find this plant then?

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Look to the hills, south of here.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: Right! I'd better start looking for this Tchiki Monkey Nut Bush then...

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Mizaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: This feels like the banana, this should do the job.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: (Iwazaru Jumps up and down waving his arms and legs about wildly)

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: I think your friend wants to tell me something.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: (Iwazaru makes what you suspect was a very rude gesture to Mizaru)

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: (Iwazaru waves his arms about yet more)

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Iwazaru says that you have the wrong type of banana.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: (sigh), I should have guessed that it wouldn't be that easy. A red banana. Don't all bananas taste the same?

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: How can a monkey say such a thing!

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: Oh, you mean RED bananas, yes, of course, I've heard that they are the tastiest. Much tastier than blue bananas. How could I forget. Bah, only a fake monkey wouldn't know that. Ahem.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Blue bananas? There's no such thing. Hey, wait a second where did you say you came from?

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: Errm I'm not from round here, anyway, moving quickly on, is there a red banana tree nearby?

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Mizaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Iwazaru says that there is a tree in the West of the Island.

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.player: Right! I'd better start looking for a red banana tree.
Where's this tchiki monkey nut bush again?

ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.speaker: Mizaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-wise-monkeys-the-w.text: Iwazaru says that there is a bush in a cave somewhere in the hills just south of the village.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-trying-to-ente.text: Only the stealthiest and most agile monkey can use this!

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-entering-as-a-.text: You slip climbing down the hole and land hard on the floor.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-no-inventory-r.text: You do not have space in your inventory for that item.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-taking-nuts.text: You take some Tchiki Nuts from the bush.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-taking-nuts-af.text: You take some Tchiki Nuts from the bush.
I hope Mizaru doesn't find this one!

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-trying-to-take.text: You already have one Tchiki Monkey Nut, better not take another.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-grinding-nuts.text: You grind the tchiki monkey nuts into a smooth sticky paste.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-eating-nuts.text: You eat the Tchiki monkey nuts. They taste nutty.

ape-atoll-tchiki-nut-bush-eating-nut-pas.text: You eat the tchiki nut paste. It sticks to the roof of your mouth.

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.player: I think I've got some Tchiki monkey nuts.

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.text: Mizaru snatches the nuts from your grasp in an eye blink.

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.speaker: Mizaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.text: Mmm these are very tasty. Tchiki Monkey nuts really are the best nuts I've ever tasted.

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.speaker: Kikazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.text: But I'm afraid you're going to have to get some more.

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.player: So these are definitely Tchiki Monkey nuts then?

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.text: Mizaru tries to snatch the nuts from your grip.  You slap his wrists.

ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-tchiki-monkey-nuts.text: Iwazaru nods and gives you the thumbs up.

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-taking-banana-.text: I hope Mizaru doesn't find this one!

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-trying-to-take.text: You already have one Red Banana, better not take another.

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-eating-the-red.text: You eat the red banana. They're tastier than your average banana.

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-cutting-the-re.text: You deftly chop the red banana into slices.

ape-atoll-red-banana-tree-eating-sliced-.text: You eat the sliced red banana. Yum.

ape-atoll-showing-the-red-banana-to-the-.player: Is this the red banana I'm looking for?

ape-atoll-showing-the-red-banana-to-the-.text: Mizaru grabs the banana surprisingly quickly for a blind monkey.

ape-atoll-showing-the-red-banana-to-the-.player: Wait! I need that, you don't have to eat...
Well... is that the right one?

ape-atoll-showing-the-red-banana-to-the-.speaker: Mizaru
ape-atoll-showing-the-red-banana-to-the-.text: Oh yes, I'd recognise the taste of red anywhere.

ape-atoll-showing-the-red-banana-to-the-.player: Really... I suppose I'd better get another one now.

ape-atoll-showing-them-a-red-banana-agai.text: You hold on to the red banana tightly.

ape-atoll-showing-them-a-red-banana-agai.speaker: Iwazaru
ape-atoll-showing-them-a-red-banana-agai.text: Iwazaru nods and gives you the thumbs up.
You carefully stuff the ingredients into the snake corpse. Ewww!

ape-atoll-talking-to-the-wise-monkeys-wi.text: Have you cooked the snake yet?

steps.player: I'm afraid I've lost it.

steps.speaker: Mizaru
steps.text: That was a bit careless wasn't it? You'd better go and make another one then.

steps.player: Err what am I doing again?

steps.speaker: Mizaru
steps.text: Get a red banana, some tchiki monkey nuts, and the snake corpse.  Prepare the ingredients and stuff them into the snake. Simple.  Even Kikazaru could do it.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: So how do I cook it again?

steps.player: How do I cook this thing, it's huge! It's not going to fit in an oven or on a spit?

steps.speaker: Mizaru
steps.text: A very good question. Anyone know?

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: (Iwazaru nods) He looks at Kikazaru to translate for him.

steps.speaker: Kikazaru
steps.text: Zzzzzzzzzzzzzzz

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: (Iwazaru prods Kikazaru)

steps.speaker: Kikazaru
steps.text: Zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: (Iwazaru sighs, and then points to the floor directly beneath him, then acts like a zombie.

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: He then points at you and falls over and plays dead, gets up and then shrugs.)

steps.player: Hmmm, somewhere underneath here, with zombies?

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: (Iwazaru nods)

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: (He then wipes his forehead as if it were hot and points at the sacrificial pyre in the east of the temple.)

steps.player: Somewhere hot, nearby? What's this business about me dying though - that's not so cool.

steps.speaker: Iwazaru
steps.text: (Iwazaru shrugs)

steps.player: Well, I suppose I'd better have a look.

ape-atoll-cooking-the-snake-eating-stuff.prompt: Are you sure you want to eat the cooked snake?

steps.text: You eat the stuffed snake - it's quite a meal! It tastes like chicken.

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-aft.speaker: Mizaru
finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-aft.text: You still here? You haven't lost the royal dish have you?

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-aft.speaker: Mizaru
finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-aft.text: You'd better make another one then... You know what to do.

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.player: Yup, it's all cooked and ready to go, or at least I think it is.

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.speaker: Mizaru
finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.text: Maybe the King wouldn't notice if we had a little bit?

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.speaker: Iwazaru
finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.text: Iwazaru slaps both of the other monkeys on the back of the head!

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.player: Yeah, listen to Iwazaru - stay away from my stuffed snake! I'm not making another one.  There was more than enough monkey business involved in making this one.

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.speaker: Mizaru
finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.text: Take that thing away from us.  It will only fill us with unfulfilled longing...

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.player: Thanks for your help guys! I've had more fun than a barrel of monkeys doing this.
Though I wish I'd realised earlier on that Iwazaru was the monkey with brains...

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.speaker: Iwazaru
finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.text: (Iwazaru mimes a crown on his head.)

finishing-up-talking-to-wise-monkeys-wit.player: Heh, time to serve this to the king...

finishing-up-trying-to-feed-king-awowoge.text: Maybe you should wear your amulet of Monkeyspeak before talking to the Monkey King...

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Err Where am I? Ooh! Roasted Stuffed Snake, lovely.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Mmmm, I'm sure I can detect the delicate aroma of Tchiki Monkey nuts, and the sweet perfume of Red Bananas, all slowly caramelised on hot rocks.
King Awowogei tucks into his roasted snake.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: I'm just a wandering chef, travelling from town to town saving peoples lives.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: gorge* You're a bit odd, aren't you?

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: Yet again, my heroic work goes unappreciated, I suppose that is the fate of a true hero.
So ... I've heard that this dish makes you more cooperative.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: stuff* That's a lie, no definitely not. Well maybe.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: Well, getting to Ape Atoll is quite a pain.  Do you have a way of making it easier to get there?

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: N,   Nnnnn..... nghghghnmnmn ... Yes there is a spell.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: Will you let me know how to cast it?

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Absolutely No... Nerrrrnnnn...Oh, go on then.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: So, what do I need to know?

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Well, it will take a while to explain...

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: Ah I see, so the banana actually has the crucial effect on the teleportation matrix.
I'm sorry I forced you to tell me the spell.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Oh that's alright - it could have been worse - you could have asked me to marry you.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: Yes - that would have been a lot worse.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: King Awowogei
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Anyway, it seems you have done me a favour. Though I'm a bit confused about what went on here.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.player: You're confused? Get a ticket and join the queue, Your Monkeyness.

finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-feeding-king-awowogei.text: Good work adventurer, I've teleported them away to safety! You only have [X] council member[s] left to protect!

finishing-up-trying-to-get-more-red-bana.text: You have already made the King's meal, you dont need any more of these.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-wise-old-mon.speaker: Mizaru
finishing-up-talking-to-the-wise-old-mon.text: The punkiest Monkey that ever popped,

finishing-up-talking-to-the-wise-old-mon.speaker: Mizaru
finishing-up-talking-to-the-wise-old-mon.text: All monkey stories are fun. Maybe I'll tell it to you some time...

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.text: Ah yes. To immunise him from the culinaromancer's attack, you will need to feed him fishcakes.

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.player: Fishcakes? What, like chocolate cake with fish instead of chocolate?

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.text: No... Like small bread crumbed fishy delicacies.

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.player: Um... So how would I make those then?

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.text: I don't know. I am a fortune-teller, not a cook.

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.text: I don't suppose it occurred to you to ask the actual cook in the room right next door to us?

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete.player: Ooooh yeah... I'll be right back!

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.text: No... Like small bread crumbed fishy delicacies.

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.player: Um... So how would I make those then?

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.text: I don't know. I am a fortune-teller, not a cook.

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.text: I don't suppose it occurred to you to ask the actual cook in the room right next door to us?

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.player: Ooooh yeah... I'll be right back!

starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-pirate-pete-agai.text: And try not to forget this time!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: Can we talk about what happened in the dining room?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Wow! You were incredible! The way you defeated the Culinaromancer, you made it seem so easy!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: With the foods, and that big portal thingy, and everything!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: I'm just glad you were around, who knows WHAT could have happened if you weren't able to help us!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: I'm sorry, I don't have any clue what you...
Oh. Oh, right. This must be part of that whole time-bubble thing that Aris told me about.
So the cook outside of the bubble remembers me having already saved the council members even though I haven't actually gone and done it yet...
Gah! This time travel stuff makes my head hurt!
So... I don't suppose you can remember exactly how I defeated him can you?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Of course! Which bit can't you remember doing?

steps.player: I can't quite remember how I managed to save that pirate...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: The pirate? Yes, you used fishcakes didn't you?

steps.player: I did? Er... I mean I did.
Out of interest, could you just help me quickly with that?
Can you tell me how to make fishcakes?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Fishcakes? As in with fish eggs and fish milk?

steps.player: Don't be silly, that would never work.
Can you check to see if there is a recipe for them?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Of course.
The Chef checks one of his cookbooks.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Found it!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Apparently you need Ground Cod, Ground Kelp, Ground Giant Crab Meat and Breadcrumbs.

options.text: Where do I get Ground Cod?

steps.player: Where do I get Ground Cod?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, if you use a pestle and mortar on a raw cod that will grind it up nicely.

options.text: Where do I get Ground Kelp?

steps.player: Where do I get Ground kelp?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: There are apparently some kelp patches off the coast near Rimmington. Murphy knows more about that.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: As for the grinding part, all you have to do is use a pestle and mortar on it, that ought to get it sorted.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Murphy also used to bring in Giant Crabs occasionally. He hasn't had any of them in for a while though.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: You had best go and have a word with him to see if he can tell you what happened.

options.text: Where do I get Ground Giant Crab Meat?

steps.player: Where do I get Ground Giant Crab meat?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, Murphy used to bring in Giant Crabs occasionally. He hasn't had any of them in for a while though.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: You had best go and have a word with him to see if he can tell you what happened.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh, and  there are apparently some kelp patches off the coast near Rimmington. Murphy knows about that too.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: As for the grinding part, all you have to do is use a pestle and mortar on it, that ought to get it sorted.

steps.player: Where do I get Breadcrumbs?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: That's easy, all you do is use a knife to slice the bread up into tiny, tiny chunks.

options.text: What do I do with all of it?

steps.player: What did I do with all of it?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm not entirely sure. What am I, an encyclopedia?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'll have a look through my cookbook while I wait for the ingredients.

steps.player: Ok, I'll go out and get all of the stuff and bring it to you.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ok.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

options.condition: If the player has asked at least one question

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: No problem!

steps.player: Murphy, what can you tell me about giant crabs?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Giant Crabs? Why, I used to haul up a few of those whenever I set my nets around Rimmington.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Why the interest?

steps.player: I need to get some Giant Crab Meat and Kelp. Can you tell me where I can get some?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, the only thing I can think to do is to go down there and look to see if there are any left.

steps.player: Go down there? What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: As in under the water!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Tell me, can you get your hands on a fishbowl?

steps.player: I'm sure I will be able to if I put my mind to it, why do you ask?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, I know how to rig up a handy set of breathing gear that can allow you to keep air inside the fishbowl.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: You just put the barrel of air on your back, with the fishbowl over your head, and then dive over the side.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: It should hold enough air to keep you alive for quite some time.

steps.player: That sounds pretty dangerous...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Not at all. I'll even weigh anchor with the chain somewhere easy to reach so you can climb out easily enough if you run into trouble.

steps.player: I'm still not happy about this...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, I can't think of any other way to check. If you come up with a better plan then feel free to tell me.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: In the meantime I'll wait, and if you want me to take you diving I'll be ready.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: By the way, why are you so interested in crabs all of a sudden?

steps.player: I can't tell you I'm afraid. The very fabric of space and time could collapse!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, I guess some people will do anything for a bit of fresh seafood.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Ahoy there! Up for a bit of a swim?
If the player doesn't have a fishbowl:

steps.player: Not just yet.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, whenever you want me to get you some diving gear, just come and see me with a fishbowl.
If the player has a fishbowl:

steps.player: I certainly am.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Great! I'll sort that fishbowl out for you.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: There you go.

steps.player: Are you sure this is safe?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Sure! It's as sound as my ship!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Want me to take you out now?

steps.player: Yes, Let's go diving.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well I can't take you out until you are properly geared up.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: We lost three diving parties that way!

steps.player: Ok, well I'll just put my diving helmet and diving backpack on.

steps.text: If the player has lost their diving helmet:

steps.player: Murphy, can I get another diving helmet?

steps.text: If the player has a full inventory:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well sure, just as soon as you have some spare space for it.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Sure, here you go. Try not to lose this one, I'm not a very good glassblower.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, the bowls I make tend to shatter under pressure into razor-sharp shards of lethal, face shredding shrapnel.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Don't let it bother you, I think I know what I'm doing wrong now.
If the player has lost their diving apparatus:

steps.player: Hello Murphy. Do you have a spare diving backpack?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Sure, I have plenty after the...little incident.

steps.player: What 'little incident'?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Nothing to worry yourself about.
If the player has a full inventory:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, I have plenty of them under the tap, getting sluiced off. When you have space for one come and see me.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Here, have this one. Only dropped once!

steps.player: Is that blood?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: No, no.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, yes.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: But seriously, what are the chances of getting a jellyfish jammed in there again?
If the player has all their equipment:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Ahoy there! All set for a dive?

steps.player: Yes, Let's go diving.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have the diving equipment on:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well I can't take you out until you are properly geared up.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: We lost three diving parties that way!

steps.player: Ok, well I'll just put my diving helmet and diving backpack on.

steps.text: If the player weighs more than 27kg:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well that's the sort of spirit I like to see. However you are far too heavy to go diving right now.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, I can't take you diving if you are carrying more than 27kg worth of equipment.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: We arrived at that number through trial and error, and the errors were not pretty let me assure you.

steps.player: So what can I do?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Well, if you pop over to a bank and leave all your heavy equipment behind then I'll take you out.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: See you then!
If the player has any pet other than a cat following them:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: I'm not taking you out for a dive with that pet following you. It'll get wet.
If the player has a cat following them:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: You want that cat of yours to drown or something?

steps.player: You mean you can't make them an adorable set of tiny diving gear?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: No. Just...no.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: I'm not taking you out for a dive with that cat following you.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: I'm not a cat person, and it'd have to stay on the ship while you were down.
If the player has a cat in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: You know, I can see your cat right there.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: I'm looking right at it. See, it's just there in your bag!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: I'm not taking you out with that cat. I'm not some sort of cat-sitter, so go and put it somewhere safe, then come back.

steps.player: O'kay...
I still think I should get some cat-sized diving gear...

steps.text: If the player is properly equipped:

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Ok, let's be off then.
(Cutscene plays of Murphy taking the player out on a boat.)

steps.player: Ok, see you soon Murphy!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.text: Good luck, I'll weigh anchor. Climb up the chain to get aboard.

underwater-trying-to-enter-the-underwate.text: You have no idea what is in there, best leave it for the time being.

underwater-talking-to-a-mogre-guard.speaker: Mogre Guard
underwater-talking-to-a-mogre-guard.text: Silly fishy! You lookin' like likkle Mogre wid your likkle arms an' wid your likkle legs!

underwater-talking-to-a-mogre-guard.speaker: Mogre Guard
underwater-talking-to-a-mogre-guard.text: Swim along silly round head fishy!

underwater-talking-to-a-mogre-guard.speaker: Mogre Guard
underwater-talking-to-a-mogre-guard.text: Dont let dem big skippies eat you!

underwater-trying-to-open-the-pen-door-e.speaker: Mogre Guard
underwater-trying-to-open-the-pen-door-e.text: Hey! Nung says no fishies in da big crunchy claws!

underwater-trying-to-open-the-pen-door-e.speaker: Mogre Guard
underwater-trying-to-open-the-pen-door-e.text: You want crunchies, you talk to him, an' hope he not hungry!

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Hey, silly fishy wit da round head!

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Ya! What kinda fishy you's tinkin you are?

underwater-talking-to-nung.player: I'm not any kind of fishy, err, fish.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Well what you doin' here if you's no a fishy?

underwater-talking-to-nung.player: Well I'm trying to get some Giant Crab meat.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Dis fishy is a funny fishy!

underwater-talking-to-nung.player: You see those big crabs? I want one of those.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: You's here to stealin' my big crunchy claws?

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Nung should smash your stoopid round head!

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Always the big nettings was taking my big crunchy claws, I put them in the cages, and now you's come to get them.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Swim away little fishy or I eat you till you's dead!

underwater-talking-to-nung.player: Wait, could I buy some of the crab meat?

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Silly round head fishy want to swaps big crunchy claws?

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Naaah...you no real deal. I bet you no do Nung big favour.

underwater-talking-to-nung.player: Seriously, I need to get that meat. I'll do your big favour if you want.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Hah! Silly round head fishy! If you get Nung 5 big skippy skins, den maybe Nung thinking you ok.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: Ya, da big skippies live over dere.
(Cutscene highlighting the Underwater Cavern Entrance plays.)

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: You need lotsa big big stones to get down dere. Den you kill da big skippies and bring da skins to Nung.

underwater-talking-to-nung.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung.text: You do dis, den maybe Nung let you swaps da big crunchy claws.

underwater-talking-to-nung-again.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-again.text: Hey fishy! You gots da skippy skins?

underwater-talking-to-nung-again.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-again.text: Den no crunchy claws for you!

underwater-picking-up-rocks.text: If the player is holding less than 5 rocks:

steps.text: You pick up a rock and put it in your pocket.

underwater-picking-up-rocks.text: If the player picks up a 6th rock:

steps.text: You have enough rocks to stand on the sea bed if you need to.

underwater-entering-the-underwater-caver.text: If the player hasn't collected 5 rocks:

steps.text: You need to collect 5 rocks to get into the pen.

underwater-entering-the-underwater-caver.text: If the player has enough rocks:

steps.text: You enter the cave...

underwater-exit-the-underwater-cavern-en.text: You kick off the sea bed and begin swimming again.

underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.player: Nung, I have your giant Mudskipper Skins.

underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.speaker: Nung
underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.text: What you say? Has da silly round headed fishy got da big skippy skins?

underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.player: Yes, I have the big skippy skins.

underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.speaker: Nung
underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.text: Silly round head fishy done good!  Gimme!
If the player has given Nung fewer than 5 hides:

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Ya, dis fishy is a good fishy, but it no count good like Nung! Nung say dere are dis many hides left for da fishy to get.
Nung holds up [number] of his fingers.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Go get me da hides little fishy!

underwater-bringing-nung-the-mudskipper-.text: If the player has given Nung 5 hides:

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Ya, da round head fishy does a good big favour for Nung.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: I am thinkin you's ok enough to swaps the giant crunchy claws now.

steps.player: Great! How much do you want for them?

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: You's gotta get me somefing to make dese hides to a cloak and flippers and hat, den I lets you have all the big crunchy claws you can get.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: But it not be easy

steps.player: Well I'll do it. What do I need? An item of ancient power? Something from the deepest, darkest dungeon in the world?
What sort of monsters will I need to fight? I'd best grab myself some potions too.
Will there be traps? Should I bring cakes?

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Ya, it real dangerous for a fishy.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: You's gotta go up to da topsies, and your gotta get a needly-thing and some wirey stuff.

steps.player: A needle.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Ya.

steps.player: And bronze wire.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Ya. Tree wirey stuffs.

steps.player: So, all I have to do is bring you three rolls of bronze wire and a needle, and I can have all the Giant Crabs I can kill?

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: Ya, but be a sneaky round head fishy. Da topsies has not water for a little fishy like you to breathing.

steps.speaker: Nung
steps.text: It REAL dangerous.

steps.player: Yeah, sounds it.

underwater-talking-to-nung-without-the-w.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-without-the-w.text: Has da fish brung Nung the wiry stuff and the needly thing?

underwater-talking-to-nung-without-the-w.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-without-the-w.text: Nung not supprised, the upsies is real scaredy for da little fishies like you.

underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.player: Nung, I have the needle and wire.

underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.text: Nung thinks this is a useful fishy he finds. Gimme!

underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.text: Nung have all da wiry stuff and needly things he needs to make da biggestest skippy skin hat ever!

underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.text: You's a good little fishy, you eat as many big crunchy claws as you want.

underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-with-the-wire.text: Maybe you get big and strong like Nung!

underwater-talking-to-nung-again-2.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-again-2.text: Hey fishy. If you's a good fishy I might sell yous bitses of skippy skin clothes.

underwater-talking-to-nung-again-2.speaker: Nung
underwater-talking-to-nung-again-2.text: But Nung needs time to makes them first.

underwater-trying-to-enter-the-crab-pen.player: I just spoke to Nung, he said it was ok.

underwater-trying-to-enter-the-crab-pen.speaker: Mogre Guard
underwater-trying-to-enter-the-crab-pen.text: Well...if Nung say it ok, den go ahead.
If the player does not have enough rocks:

steps.text: You try to enter the pen, but the current is too strong.
You need to collect 5 rocks to get into the pen.

underwater-trying-to-enter-the-crab-pen.text: With the rocks in your pocket you can quite easily land on the sea bed.
It is a little slippery, but you should be able to fight normally.

underwater-exiting-the-crab-pen.text: You kick off from the sea bed and begin swimming again.

underwater-climbing-the-anchor.text: If the player is holding any rocks:

steps.text: You have to drop all of your rocks to surface.

underwater-climbing-the-anchor.speaker: Murphy
underwater-climbing-the-anchor.text: Great, I'll take us back in.

finishing-up-using-raw-cod-on-a-pestle-a.text: You grind the Cod into a paste.

finishing-up-using-crab-meat-on-a-pestle.text: You grind the Giant Crab meat into a paste.

finishing-up-using-a-knife-on-bread.text: You slice the bread into breadcrumbs.

finishing-up-using-kelp-on-a-pestle-and-.text: You grind the Kelp into flakes.

finishing-up-trying-to-combine-the-ingre.text: You do not yet know how to make fishcakes.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cook.player: Can we talk about what happened in the dining room?

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
finishing-up-talking-to-the-cook.text: Wow! You were incredible! The way you defeated the Culinaromancer, you made it seem so easy!

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cook.player: So... I don't suppose you can remember exactly how I defeated him can you?

finishing-up-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
finishing-up-talking-to-the-cook.text: Of course! Which bit can't you remember doing?

steps.player: I can't quite remember how I managed to save that pirate...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: The pirate? Yes, you used fishcakes didn't you?

steps.player: I did? Er... I mean I did.
Out of interest, could you just help me quickly with that?
I have all the ingredients for fishcakes!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Great! Just like before! I've been reading the recipe and I know how to make the fishcakes now.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: It's pretty simple actually. All you have to do is use the ingredients on each other and then cook the fishcakes on a range.

steps.player: That's it?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes. I thought that there was a page missing from the cookbook because it seemed so easy, but it turns out it really IS that easy!

finishing-up-combining-the-ingredients.text: You mix all the ingredients together to make an uncooked fishcake.

finishing-up-cooking-a-fishcake.text: You manage to cook a fishcake.

finishing-up-inspecting-pirate-pete-whil.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-inspecting-pirate-pete-whil.text: Stop messing about and use the fishcakes on him!

finishing-up-using-the-fishcake-on-pirat.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-using-the-fishcake-on-pirat.text: Good work adventurer, I've teleported them away to safety! You only have [number] council members left to protect!

sdRxJ4.speaker: Murphy
sdRxJ4.text: Ok, well I'll be here if you change your mind.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: To protect this noble knight from the magic of the culinaromancer, you will have to give him a creme brulee.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: Not just any creme brulee mind you, but a creme brulee supreme!

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.player: Well that doesn't sound too hard. What's so supreme about a creme brulee supreme?

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: Are you going to constantly ask me questions?

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: I am a fortune-teller, not a cook, and again I would suggest you speak to the cook next door who will be much more helpful on such culinary matters.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: Although I happen to know that one of the ingredients is the egg of the evil chicken.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.player: The evil chicken? Great. He only ever seems to show up when I don't want him to.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: I believe the wise old man in Draynor has studied the Evil Chicken.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: I would suggest you speak to him to get you on the right track. And tell him Bubbykins says hi.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.text: That is not important right now. Go! Protect Sir Amik from the magic that threatens his life, my spell will only hold so long!

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze.player: Just give me 5 minutes and I'll be back!

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.player: Could you give me that recipe again, please?

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.text: To protect this noble knight from the magic of the culinaromancer, you will have to give him a creme brulee.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.player: Well that doesn't sound too hard. What's so supreme about a creme brulee supreme?

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.text: Are you going to constantly ask me questions?

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.text: I am a fortune-teller, not a cook, and again I would suggest you speak to the cook next door who will be much more helpful on such culinary matters.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.player: The evil chicken? Great. He only ever seems to show up when I don't want him to.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.text: I believe the wise old man in Draynor has studied the Evil Chicken.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.text: I would suggest you speak to him to get you on the right track. And tell him Bubbykins says hi.

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.text: That is not important right now. Go! Protect Sir Amik from the magic that threatens his life, my spell will only hold so long!

starting-out-inspecting-sir-amik-varze-a.player: Just give me 5 minutes and I'll be back!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: Can we talk about what happened in the dining room?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Wow! You were incredible! The way you defeated the Culinaromancer, you made it seem so easy!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: So... I don't suppose you can remember exactly how I defeated him can you?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Of course! Which bit can't you remember doing?

steps.player: That white knight... Sir Amik Varze... I can't quite remember how I saved him...
but it was something to do with creme brulee supreme...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah yes! Why, I was so impressed with that recipe you created that I memorised it!

steps.player: Ah, you did, did you? I don't suppose you could refresh my memory about that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: But of course! It was an unusual dish, an unusual dish indeed! First you blend together, in a pot, some milk and some cream. Then add cornflour to the mixture.

steps.player: Cornflour? How do I... er, how DID I make that then?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh, you told me you used sweetcorn in a mill!

steps.player: Really? Weird. Okay, what did I do then?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Then you travelled to the Kharazi Jungle and searched the plants there until you found a vanilla stick, which was then added to the mixture.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: After that you told me that you sought out and killed the fearsome Evil Chicken, to get one of his eggs, which was then mixed with the other ingredients.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Finally you made some cinnamon by grinding the branch of a Dramen Tree and sprinkled it on top of the creme brulee.

steps.player: Sounds easy enough so far. Er, I mean it was easy enough up to that point.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes, but then came the impressive part!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Apparently, a creme brulee supreme needs to be flambed at exactly the right temperature, and the only fire that is hot enough to do this is the breath of a dragon. Luckily, while killing black dragons near the Evil

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Chicken's lair, you came across a method of forcing a dragon to your will so that it would complete the dish, which you then used to protect Sir Amik!

steps.player: I definitely said that I had to kill some black dragons to do that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh yes. You were quite adamant about it. Specifically black dragons. Specifically near the Evil Chicken's lair.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?
