steps.player: Could you tell me about the Evil Chicken, please?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The Evil Chicken! Many are the myths and legends surrounding this foul bird. Some say that it is the result of a mad mage's attempt to summon a demon, others say that it was once a

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: normal chicken that realised how limited its farmyard life was. It threw off its chains and attempted to unite the other chickens in revenge against their human captors.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: When that failed the Evil Chicken grew angry with its brethren and swore to kill any human or chicken that it ever encountered again!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It is whispered that there is a coven of witches that meet, on the night of the full moon in the fabled fairy kingdom, to worship this bird and that they can summon it to do their twisted will!

steps.player: Right, so if you were looking for the chicken where would you go?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I would start in the lands of the fairies, possibly there is some truth in the rumours of summoning the chicken there. Actually, I've done further research, it may be around

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: here somewhere, if you're really thinking of going there you should be extremely careful, it's claimed that the chicken has forced some very powerful creatures to guard his lair.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.prompt: Pick a topic

starting-out-inspecting-the-goblin-gener.text: Well you could try asking some of the other goblins in their village for ideas. You should be able to find it just to the North of Falador, unless they've decided the sky is the wrong colour there or something.

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Wow! You were incredible! The way you defeated the Culinaromancer, you made it seem so easy!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: So... I don't suppose you can remember how I defeated him can you?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Of course! Which bit can't you remember doing?

steps.player: Those bickering goblins... How did I protect them again?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, that was a weird one alright, you told me that they couldn't agree on what food they liked, so you ended up just mushing a bunch of stuff together somehow which seemed to do the trick.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook

options.text: Can I ask about what food you like?

options.text: I need to save you from the Culinaromancer's spell.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: From who's what?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Lumbridge...?

steps.text: Oh yeah. Me remember. Me was goblin representy thingy.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No you weren't! That was me!

steps.player: Never mind that, don't you remember the spell?

steps.text: All me remember is Wartface stealin' chair!

steps.text: Weren't your chair. You shouldn' even've been there!

steps.player: But...

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: I there before you were. So I get chair...

steps.player: Never mind.
Market research.

steps.text: But us never use your markets.

steps.player: Exactly. That's why we need to find out what goblins eat, so we can better cater to your needs.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Go away human, we busy.

steps.player: But it'll only take a minute of your time.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: I said we busy!

steps.player: Erm... no particular reason.

steps.speaker: General Wartface

options.text: So how is life for the goblins?

asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.player: Hey, I need your help. Wartface and Bentnoze have been cursed!

asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.speaker: Goblin
asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.text: What that got to do with me?

asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.player: I need to find a meal they'd both eat.

asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.speaker: Goblin
asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.text: Me no chef, ask village cook instead.

asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.speaker: Goblin Cook
asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.text: Go away human, me's busy here!

asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.speaker: Goblin Cook
asking-around-goblin-village-talking-to-.text: Me's working on new way of cooking. Will be most famous-est goblin cook ever.

options.text: What is this new way of cooking?

steps.player: What is this new way of cooking?

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Got the idea from the dwarves. Saw them playing with something. They called it a malty canned nun or summat. Used lotsa heat and bright light.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Wouldn't tell Mudknuckles how it worked of course. But I figured it out. Mudknuckles is smarter than them. Now I'm gonna be able to cook better'n anyone. And faster too, yes.

steps.player: Well, good luck with that.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: No luck. Will work cos Mudknuckles destined for great things.

steps.player: I need your help. Wartface and Bentnoze have been trapped by a terrible curse!

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Oh, maybe that why Mudknuckles not been shouted at recently.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Hmmm, s'pose me should help. But first Mudknuckles must finish experiment. Unfortunately is missing one vital ingredient.

options.text: What do you need? Maybe I can get it for you.

steps.player: What do you need? Maybe I can get it for you.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Is called charcoal. Mudknuckles hear you can get it from shops on Karamja, but the customs officers, they no like goblins any more.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Burnt trees, they good too. Smash 'em up with axes. But Mudknuckles only knows of burnt trees in the wilderness, and Mudknuckles too afraid to go there.

steps.player: Ok, I'll see what I can do.

options.text: I guess I'll come back later then.

steps.player: I guess I'll come back later then.

options.text: Well, I guess I'll leave you to it.

steps.text: Yes, Mudknuckles too busy to talk.

steps.text: Really? Then no time to lose. Mudknuckles already have everything else. Sulphur 'n stuff.

steps.player: Sulphur? Er...

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: It fine, it...

steps.text: What that noise?

steps.speaker: Goblin 1
steps.text: You just hear that?

steps.text: Hear what?

steps.player: Mudknuckles?

discovering-the-recipe-talking-to-the-bu.text: I thinking of calling it fast food, 'cos of how fast it goes from raw to burnt, see?

steps.text: Can't see why. Not like you gonna get food poisoning. Food is very well cooked.

options.text: Do you think that will sell?

steps.player: Do you think that will sell? Like you said, it's burnt.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: So maybe some imperfections, but fast food will sell. People buy anything when in hurry, even if does taste like sawdust.

steps.player: I need your help...

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Yes, yes, Mudknuckles very grateful, how can I help?

steps.player: Your leaders, Wartface and Bentnoze, have been trapped by a terrible curse!

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: So that's why Mudknuckles not been shouted at recently. But how can I be helping? Cooking and magic no mix.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Oh...

steps.player: What?

steps.text: Is impossible. Mudknuckles try it before, but their requests, they make no sense.

steps.player: Why, what did they want?

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Well Bentnoze wanted fruit in the dish. But Wartface, only fruit he eat is sliced oranges.

steps.player: That doesn't sound too bad.

steps.text: Maybe, but Bentnoze objects to the colour.

steps.player: Anything else?

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Wartface, he want some nice juicy maggots.

steps.text: Humans use them all the time for fishing. Mudknuckles think this a crazy waste of maggots mind, but each to their own.

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Bentnoze not like maggots, say they're too bland. Would only eat them if they spicier.

steps.player: Ok, is there anything other than orange slices and maggots?

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Bentnoze asked for some bread in the mix.

steps.player: Let me guess, Wartface complained right?

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Yep, Wartface think bread too crunchy. He prefer slimier soggier food, like the maggots.

steps.player: So let me get this straight. I need orange slices which aren't orange, maggots that aren't bland, and bread which isn't crunchy?

steps.speaker: Goblin Cook
steps.text: Yep, 'bout sums it up. Bring 'em all to me and Mudknuckles will make suitable dish.

steps.player: Wonderful. Well, I guess I'll have to see what I can do.

steps.player: Hi. I was wondering if you could help me?

steps.player: Erm. No I don't think I did. I need to make that cake for the Lumbridge Guide. He's been frozen in time and needs help.

steps.speaker: Wizard Traiborn

steps.speaker: Wizard Traiborn
steps.text: What would you do without me? I can give you another...

steps.player: Thank you.

options.text: Ask about helping the Lumbridge Guide.

steps.text: If the player still has the cake

steps.player: I made the cake. Just need to go use it now! Thanks for your help!

steps.speaker: Wizard Traiborn
steps.text: Wah hey! Good work Bill.

steps.player: Who's Bill?

steps.speaker: Wizard Traiborn
steps.text: Who knows!?
If the player has lost the cake

steps.player: I made the cake... but I lost it.

steps.speaker: Wizard Traiborn
steps.text: Oopsy daisy! You'll have to make another one!

steps.player: I lost the [ingredient]!

finishing-up-inspecting-the-lumbridge-gu.text: If the player still has the cake

finishing-up-inspecting-the-lumbridge-gu.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-inspecting-the-lumbridge-gu.text: What do you want? A prize? Use it on the Lumbridge Guide already!
If the player has lost the cake

finishing-up-inspecting-the-lumbridge-gu.player: I made the cake... but I lost it.

finishing-up-inspecting-the-lumbridge-gu.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-inspecting-the-lumbridge-gu.text: Best you go see Traiborn again then and see if he can help you.

finishing-up-freeing-the-lumbridge-guide.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-freeing-the-lumbridge-guide.text: Good work adventurer, I've teleported them away to safety! You only have [number] council members left to protect!

starting-out-inspecting-the-dwarf.player: How do I protect you I wonder....

starting-out-inspecting-the-dwarf.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-the-dwarf.text: To protect our short angry friend from the culinaromancer's magics, I suggest that you seek out his father within the mountain tunnel that he guards.

starting-out-inspecting-the-dwarf.speaker: Aris
starting-out-inspecting-the-dwarf.text: His fondness for rock cakes could prove key in freeing him.

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: Can we talk about what happened in the dining room?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Wow! You were incredible! The way you defeated the Culinaromancer, you made it seem so easy!

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.player: So... I don't suppose you can remember how I defeated him can you?

starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.speaker: Cook
starting-out-talking-to-the-cook.text: Of course! Which bit can't you remember doing?

steps.player: That dwarf... I somehow can't remember how I managed to save him...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: The dwarf? Oh, yeah, I think that was an easy one, didn't you say?

steps.player: I did? Er, I did.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: You went to see his dad in the tunnels under white wolf mountain, and then got some rock cakes, if I remember rightly.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.speaker: An old Dwarf
below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.text: I have absolutely no clue what you are on about. Sit down, catch your breath and explain please!

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.player: Ok. Your son, the one who guards the tunnel entrance?

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.speaker: An old Dwarf
below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.text: Oh aye. Good lad he is.

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.player: Well he's at a special meeting and he's frozen by the culinaromancer!

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.speaker: An old Dwarf
below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.text: Ok... you lost me again. I just got back from visitin' him up top, he's fine.

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.speaker: An old Dwarf
below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.text: Oh that. No no, he's quite ok. That was last week.

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.player: I need your rock cakes to free him from it.

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.speaker: Rohak
below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-an-.text: You're delusional. Never would old Rohak give away his special recipe, not for all the golden nectar from the Rising Sun!

below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-roh.speaker: Rohak
below-white-wolf-mountain-talking-to-roh.text: I would never give away me special rock cake recipe, not for all the golden nectar from the Rising Sun!

the-golden-nectar-talking-to-emily.speaker: Emily
the-golden-nectar-talking-to-emily.text: Heya! What can I get you?

options.text: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

steps.player: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Erm... they like it?

steps.player: No no no... I mean what kind of ale do they drink?

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Well I know for sure that they enjoy my special recipe.

steps.player: Oh? Would you tell me?

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: And lose money? I think not!

options.text: I could offer you some in return, how about 100 gold?

steps.player: I could offer you some in return, how about 100 gold?

steps.text: If the player does not have a chocolate bar or a plain pizza in backpack:

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Sorry, no deal, that wouldn't even cover my expenses.
If the player has a chocolate bar in their backpack:

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: You have CHOCOLATE in your pack, I can smell it! 50 gold and chocolate and the secret is yours!!
If the player does not have enough money:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have enough money on me.

steps.text: If the player has enough money:

steps.player: You have a deal. Here you go...

steps.text: You hand over the chocolate and money.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Mmmmm... the secret is in the gold. Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love, I think they're genetically attracted to gold.

steps.player: Sorry, no deal.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Your loss! Next customer please!
If the player has a plain pizza in their backpack:

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Welll... maybe... look.. I'm on duty here at the bar so I can't get anything to eat, I could murder a pizza.

steps.player: I just happen to have some on me.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Pizza and 100 gold and the secret is yours!
If the player does not have enough money:

steps.player: Oh, I don't have enough money on me.

steps.text: If the player has enough money:

steps.player: You have a deal. Here you go...

steps.text: You hand over the pizza and money.

steps.player: Sorry, no deal.

options.text: I could offer you some in return, how about 200 gold?

steps.text: If the player does not have enough money:

steps.player: But I don't have the money on me. I'll have to come back.

steps.text: If the player has enough money and does not have the Ring of Charos(a) equipped:

steps.player: I could offer you some in return, how about 200 gold?

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: You sure you haven't got anymore?

steps.player: Just 200... honest!

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Hand it over then and I'll tell you the secret.
You hand over 200 gold.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Mmmmm... the secret is in the gold. Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love, I think they're genetically attracted to gold.
If the player has enough money and the Ring of Charos(a) equipped:

steps.player: I could offer you some in return, how about 200 gold?

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: You're a good person... for you, 150 and you have a deal.
You hand over 150 gold.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Mmmmm... the secret is in the gold. Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love, I think they're genetically attracted to gold.

options.text: (Persuade)I'm really quite trustworthy once you get to know me.
options.condition: With a Ring of Charos(a) equipped

steps.player: Oh go on, I'm really quite trustworthy once you get to know me.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Mmmmm... the secret is in the gold. Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love. I think they're genetically attracted to gold.

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: What...what am I saying? I just gave you the secret!

the-golden-nectar-talking-to-kaylee.speaker: Kaylee
the-golden-nectar-talking-to-kaylee.text: Heya! What can I get you?

options.text: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

the-golden-nectar-talking-to-tina.speaker: Tina
the-golden-nectar-talking-to-tina.text: Heya! What can I get you?

options.text: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

the-golden-nectar-talking-to-emily-again.speaker: Emily
the-golden-nectar-talking-to-emily-again.text: Heya! What can I get you?

options.text: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

steps.player: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Oh it's you again. Forgotten the secret already?

steps.player: No... I just... misplaced it.

steps.speaker: Emily
steps.text: Mmmmm... the secret is in the gold. Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love, I think they're genetically attracted to gold.

steps.player: Thanks, I won't forg...err... misplace it, this time.

the-golden-nectar-talking-to-kaylee-agai.speaker: Kaylee
the-golden-nectar-talking-to-kaylee-agai.text: Heya! What can I get you?

options.text: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

the-golden-nectar-talking-to-tina-again.speaker: Tina
the-golden-nectar-talking-to-tina-again.text: Heya! What can I get you?

options.text: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.text: You hand the ale to the dwarf who slurps it with a noise of a thousand seals celebrating a rain of fish.

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.text: Is that what I think it is?

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.text: That's from the Rising Sun, the barmaid there will never tell me the recipe she uses. It's divine!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.text: No! I shwears I'll never tell...
The dwarf nurses the very last drops of the pint as if he'd really like more.

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-with.player: I think you deserve another pint.
I'm sure another pint will go down nicely.

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.text: Ahhh, yer me besht mate... mate.

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.player: You're a good friend Rohak, do you think you could do me a favour?

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.text: Fer you [player name]? Fer you I'd... I'd... shlide down a shlope of thishtlesh wif no 'elmet on!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.player: I don't need you to do that ... friend. Just something as simple as baking me some of your wonderful rock cakes. Hmm? For your good friend?

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.text: Fer you! Anyfin'! Fer a price of course!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.player: Good. I'm sure I have some gold somewhere!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-a-sober-ro.player: How much gold do you want to make the cake?

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-a-sober-ro.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-a-sober-ro.text: WHAT?! That wasn't a dream? Oh my aching head...

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-a-sober-ro.player: No, not a dream, you agreed to make me your special rock cake, for a fee.

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-a-sober-ro.text: If the player doesn't have enough money

steps.player: Maybe I should have some more money with me, he did say he'd want payment...

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-a-sober-ro.text: If the player has enough money

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: Also... you'll need to get the ingredients too. Milk, flour, egg and bowl of water, mind it's a bowl and not a dirty bucket.
You hand over 100 gold.

steps.player: You didn't say I'd have to run around... but ok! Milk, flour, egg, bowl of water....I'll be back!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.text: If the player has none of the items
If the player only has some of the items

steps.player: I have found some of the things you asked for:

steps.text: The following dialogue will change depending on what items the player has:

steps.player: [I have the egg/I don't have an egg, I'll look for some chickens], [I have a pot of flour/I don't have a pot of flour, but I'll investigate the windmills], [I have the bucket of milk/I don't have any milk but I'll check out the cows], [I have the bowl of water!/I don't have a bowl of water].

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: That's all well and good...but come back when you have all the ingredients. You're lucky Dwarves stick to their word else I might not make these cakes for you.

steps.player: Okay okay I'll get right on it! Keep your beard on!

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.player: N..n...nothing honest!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-agai.text: If the player has all the items

steps.player: I have all the items you asked for...is that it? I could make these!

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: No you couldn't, there's a special ingredient, but I'm not going to tell you what it is!

steps.player: Well... here's the ingredients anyway.

steps.text: You hand over the ingredients and watch the dwarf make the cake.
Rohak places the cake on the table.

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: There, as good as my word. Hot rock cakes to my special recipe.

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-afte.speaker: Rohak
getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-afte.text: Got any use out of that rock cake I made you [player name]?
If the player still has the rock cake

steps.player: Not yet but I will. I'm going to save your son.

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: I keep tellin you, he's fine!

getting-the-recipe-talking-to-rohak-afte.text: If the player has lost the rock cake

steps.player: I appear to have lost it somewhere, can you make me another?

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: I suppose so, but you'll need all the ingredients like last time.
If the player has none of the items
If the player only has some of the items

steps.player: I have found some of the things you asked for:

steps.text: If the player has all the items

steps.player: I lost the rock cake! But I have more ingredients, will you make me some more please?

steps.speaker: Rohak
steps.text: Oh... I suppose so. Give me the ingredients.
You hand over the ingredients and watch the dwarf make the cake.

getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.speaker: Aris
getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.text: STOP! What do you think you're doing!

getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.speaker: Aris
getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.text: You can't feed him red hot rock cakes! You'll kill him! Find a way to cool them down.

getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.player: Oh, ok, I'll find a way to cool them down then.

getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.speaker: Aris
getting-the-recipe-attempting-to-free-th.text: I hear there's a rather chilly reception on top of a rather icey mountain.

getting-the-recipe-cooling-the-rock-cake.text: The dying breath of the icefiend cools your hot rock cake.
Your ice gloves cool the hot rock cake as you pick it up.

finishing-up-freeing-the-dwarf.speaker: Aris
finishing-up-freeing-the-dwarf.text: Good work adventurer, I've teleported them away to safety! You only have [number] council members left to protect!

jhrwBw.speaker: Rohak
jhrwBw.text: Have you forgotten the ingredients list? I'll need an egg, a pot of flour, a bucket of milk and a bowl of water to make these cakes for you.

jhrwBw.player: Ok, I'll see about getting them.

steps.npc: Citizens of West Ardougne! King Tyras needs you for his Royal Army! Who will join this noble cause?

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Plague bringer!

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: King Tyras is scum!

steps.npc: Tyras will be informed of these words of treason!

steps.text: Someone throws a tomato at the recruiter.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.player: Do you have any other quests for me to do?

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: Nothing I can think of at the moment...
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Recruitment Drive quest.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.text: Quests, eh? Well, I don't have anything on the go at the moment, but there is an organisation that is always looking for capable adventurers to assist them.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.text: Your excellent work sorting out those Black Knights means I will happily write you a letter of recommendation.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.text: Would you like me to put your name forwards to them?

steps.player: Sure thing Sir Amik, sign me up!

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: Erm, well, this is a little embarrassing, I already HAVE put you forward as a potential member.

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: They are called the Temple Knights, and you are to meet Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador park for testing immediately.

steps.player: Okey dokey, I'll go do that then.
No thanks, that doesn't sound like the kind of thing that would interest me...

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: As you wish adventurer, let's say no more about it.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze-t.player: Do you have any other quests for me to do?

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze-t.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze-t.text: No, I am afraid not. I suggest you go meet Sir Tiffy in Falador Park, he will be expecting you.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.player: Sir Amik Varze sent me to meet you here for some sort of testing...?

starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Ah, [player name]! Amik told me all about you, dontchaknow! Spiffing job you did with the old Black Knights there, absolutely first class.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Well, a top-notch fellow like yourself is just the right sort we've been seeking for our organisation.

steps.player: ...testing? What exactly do you mean by testing?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Jolly bad show! Varze was supposed to have informed you about all this before sending you here!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, not your fault I suppose, what? Anywho, our organisation is looking for a certain specific type of person to join.

steps.player: So... You want me to go kill some monster or something for you?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Not at all, old bean. There's plenty of warriors around should we require dumb muscle.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: That's really not the kind of thing our organisation is after, what?

steps.player: So you want me to go and fetch you some kind of common item, and then take it for delivery somewhere on the other side of the country?
Because I really hate doing that!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Haw haw haw What a dull thing to ask of someone, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: I know what you mean though, I did my fair share of running errands when I was a young adventurer, myself!

steps.player: So what exactly will this test consist of?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Can't let just any old riff-raff in, what? The mindless thugs and bully boys are best left in the White Knights or the Guards, we look for the top-shelf brains to join us.

steps.player: So you want to test my brains?  Will it hurt?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Haw Haw Haw That's a good one!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Not in the slightest... Well, maybe a bit, but we all have to make sacrifices occasionally, what?

steps.player: What do you want me to do then?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: It's a test of wits, what? I'll take you to our secret training grounds, and you will have to pass through a series of five separate intelligence tests to prove you're our sort of

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: adventurer.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Standard puzzle room rules will apply.

steps.player: Erm... what are 'standard  puzzle room rules' exactly?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Never done this sort of thing before, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: The simple rules are: No items or equipment to be brought with you. Each room is a self contained puzzle. You may quit at any time.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Of course, if you quit a room, then all your progress up to that point will be cleared, and you'll have to start again from scratch.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Our organisation manages to filter all the top-notch adventurers this way. So, are you ready to go?

steps.player: This organisation you keep mentioning... Perhaps you could tell me a little about it?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Oh, that Amik! Jolly bad form, did he not tell you anything that he was supposed to?

steps.player: No... He didn't really tell me anything except to come here and meet you...

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well now old sport, let me give you the heads up and the low down, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: I represent the Temple Knights. We are the premier order of Knights in Asgarnia, if not the world. Saradomin himself personally founded our order

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: centuries ago, and we answer only to him.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Only the very best of the best are permitted to join, and the powers we command are formidable indeed.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: You might say that we are the front line of defence for the entire kingdom!

steps.player: So what's the difference between you and the White Knights?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, in simple terms, we're better! Any fool with a sword can manage to get into the White Knights, which is mostly the reason they are so very, very incompetent, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: The Temple Knights on the other hand have to be smarter, stronger, better than all others. We are the elite. No man controls us for our orders come directly from

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Saradomin himself!

steps.player: Cool, you mean I get to meet Saradomin?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, uh, not exactly... Sir Vey Lance, our head of operations, is the only one of our order who has ever personally met Saradomin, but everything he tells us to do is done with

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Saradomin's implicit permission.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: It's not every job where you have more authority than the king, now is it?

steps.player: Wait... You can order the King around?!?!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, not me personally, I'm only in the recruitment side of things dontchaknow, but the higher ranking members of the organisation have almost absolute power over this kingdom.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Plus a few others, so I hear....

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Anyway, this is why we keep our organisation shrouded in secrecy, and why we demand such rigorous testing for all potential recruits. Speaking of which, are you ready to begin your

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: testing?

steps.player: Yeah, this sounds right up my street. Let's go!

steps.text: If the player does not have an empty inventory or has equipped items:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, bad luck old [boy/gal/bean], you'll need to have a completely empty inventory and you can't be wearing any equipment before we can accurately test you.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Don't want people cheating by smuggling stuff in, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Come and see me again after you've been to the old bank to drop your stuff off, what?
If the player has an empty inventory and no equipped items:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Jolly good show! Now, the training grounds location is a secret so...

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Here we go! Mind your head!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Oops, ignore the smell! Nearly there!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: And... Here we are! Best of luck!

steps.player: Well... I don't know... This doesn't really sound like my kind of thing...
To be honest, I'd rather go kill stuff for loot than use my mind to work things out...

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, it takes all sorts to make the world spin, what? Maybe you'll find a nice job with the Guards sometime.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Sad though, your intelligence file seemed quite promising. Should you change your mind, you come back and let me know, what?

the-tests-upon-failing-a-test.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien

steps.player: Let's see what you've got.
Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Regath, traveller.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This place is a union of the mystical and the mundane, where the magical realm reaches out to touch the humdrum world of commerce.
Or, in terms that you may understand more easily, this place is a shop that sells magic stuff for money. Though I also trade in various other items.

steps.player: I don't need anything.

treasure-trails-elite.npc: I have a question for you.

treasure-trails-elite-after-solving-the-.text: You've [been given a new clue/obtained a casket]!

starting-off-message-from-the-king.speaker: King's Messenger
starting-off-message-from-the-king.text: I take it you are [player name]? King Lathas sent this message for you. He's not a man you'd want to keep waiting.
The messenger gives you a scroll.

starting-off-talking-to-king-lathas.player: I received your message my liege. How may I serve the kingdom?

starting-off-talking-to-king-lathas.speaker: King Lathas
starting-off-talking-to-king-lathas.text: Ahh... adventurer. The repair work on the Well of Voyage has been completed. We're finally ready to move against my brother.

options.text: I assume you have a plan?

steps.player: I assume you have a plan?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: I do indeed. I recently managed to make contact with the elves that inhabit the western lands.

steps.player: Elves? I've never seen an elf before.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Well that may well change soon. Apparently, my brother has been causing them quite a bit of trouble. As such, they've agreed to help us get rid of him once and for all.

steps.player: So what do I need to do?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: You are to head into the Underground Pass and through the Well of Voyage. Lord Iorwerth, the leader of the elves, will send some representatives to meet you on the other side.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: With their help, you are to find my brother and kill him. Once that's done, return to me.

steps.prompt: Start the Regicide quest?

steps.player: Very well. Anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: My brother may not be the only threat you face. I hear the elves are currently dealing with a rebellion. The rebels likely won't take kindly to you working with their enemy so be on the look out.

steps.player: I see. I'll be careful.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Good luck adventurer.

steps.player: Actually, I don't think I'm ready for this yet.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: As you wish. Return to me when you are ready and we will begin.

options.text: What's the deal with your brother again?

steps.player: What's the deal with your brother again?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: My brother, King Tyras, was always a bit of an explorer. He went on numerous expeditions to the lands west of here. On one of these expeditions, he was captured by the forces of the Dark Lord.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: The Dark Lord agreed to spare his life, but only on one condition... That he would drink from the Chalice of Eternity. The chalice corrupted him. He joined forces with the Dark Lord, the embodiment of pure evil...

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: As a result, I had a wall built around West Ardougne to act as a barrier between him and the rest of the world. Tyras is king of West Ardougne, sealing off the city was the only way to stop him and the Dark Lord.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: I knew people would never believe the truth, so I had the plague made up as an excuse for the cordon. I'm not proud of it, but it was the only way to keep people safe.

steps.player: But now we're ready to stop him.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Indeed we are. My brother has been gathering strength in the west, preparing to move against us. But now that we have a way through, we can move against him first.

options.text: Excellent. Do you have a plan in place?

steps.player: Excellent. Do you have a plan in place?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: I do indeed. I recently managed to make contact with the elves that inhabit the western lands.

steps.player: Sounds good. See you later.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Farewell adventurer. Return to me once you are ready to begin.

starting-off-talking-to-lathas-again.player: My liege. What must I do again?

starting-off-talking-to-lathas-again.speaker: King Lathas
starting-off-talking-to-lathas-again.text: You are to head into the Underground Pass and through the Well of Voyage. Lord Iorwerth, the leader of the elves, will send some representatives to meet you on the other side.

starting-off-talking-to-lathas-again.speaker: King Lathas
starting-off-talking-to-lathas-again.text: With their help, you are to find my brother and kill him. Once that's done, return to me.

entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.speaker: Idris
entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.text: Halt human! What are you doing here?

entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.speaker: Idris
entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.text: Wait! What was that? What the...
Morvran and Essyllt appear and kill Idris, then head towards the player.

entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.speaker: Morvran
entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.text: Are you the human by the name of [player name]?

entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.speaker: Essyllt
entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.text: Good... We've been expecting you. King Lathas sent word of your coming.

entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.speaker: Essyllt
entering-isafdar-encountering-idris-morv.text: You should speak with Lord Iorwerth. He will help you track down that brigand Tyras. You'll find his camp in the north west of the forest.

entering-isafdar-talking-to-the-elf-trac.speaker: Elf Tracker
entering-isafdar-talking-to-the-elf-trac.text: Human! You must be one of Tyras's men. I have no time for brigands or outlaws.

entering-isafdar-talking-to-the-elf-trac.speaker: Elf Tracker
entering-isafdar-talking-to-the-elf-trac.text: Leave me be. I have no time for brigands or outlaws.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.player: Hello there, I'm [player name]. Your scouts said that I should come and see you.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.text: Ahh... [player name]. Welcome to Tirannwn. I understand you've been sent here to rid us of that criminal Tyras. I offer my full support.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.text: Unfortunately, most of my troops are currently dealing with a group of renegade elves. That does mean we're a bit more limited than we otherwise would be.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.player: I see. I'll need to play this smart then.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.text: Indeed. Now, Tyras and his forces moved camp recently so your first step will be to find their new camp. I have a tracker currently working in that area. I suggest you join up with him.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.text: You'll find him at Tyras's old camp. It's south east of here, just north of that poisoned lake. Once you've found the camp, come and let me know.

entering-isafdar-speaking-with-lord-iorw.player: Thank you. I shall return when my task is complete.

entering-isafdar-talking-to-iorwerth-aga.player: Where can I find that tracker again?

entering-isafdar-talking-to-iorwerth-aga.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
entering-isafdar-talking-to-iorwerth-aga.text: He should be at Tyras's old camp. It's south east of here, just north of that poisoned lake. Once you've found the camp, come and let me know.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.text: Human! You must be one of Tyras's men...

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.player: No I'm [player name]! Lord Iorwerth said you might be able to help me.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.text: And you have something to prove this?

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.text: As I was saying... I have no time for brigands or outlaws.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.text: Good day [player name]. How may I help you now?

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.player: Your scout refused to help. He asked for proof that you sent me.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.text: Bless his loyalty but curse his suspicion. Here he will recognise this.
If the player doesn't have enough inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth tries to give you a crystal pendant but you don't have enough room for it.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.text: If the player has enough inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth gives you a crystal pendant.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: Human! You must be one of Tyras's men...

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.player: No I'm [player name]! Lord Iorwerth said you might be able to help me.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: And you have something to prove this?
You show the tracker the crystal pendant.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: That's Lord Iorwerth's pendant. He must have a lot of faith in you. Now, what is it I can help you with?

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.player: I need to find Tyras and kill him. Do you know where his camp is?

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: Well this was his old camp. After the battle a few days ago they moved. We're yet to find them again.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: As it goes I'm not actually tracking them at the moment. I'm currently trying to trace our renegade brethren instead. This here is the best lead we've found so far.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: Ahh I guess you can't see it with those human eyes.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: I tell you what. Now that you're here I may as well give you a hand. I'll search here on the east side. You check out the west end of the camp. Come and tell me if you find anything.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.text: [player name], how goes your search? Any luck hunting down that brigand?

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.player: I've found no trace of him as yet.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.text: I'm sure you will find something at his old camp that can help you.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.player: I'll take a look and see what I can find.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-lord-i.text: Good. Come find me when you've located the camp.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.player: What should I be doing again?

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.text: Check out the west end of the camp and see if you can find anything. I'll keep looking here. Let me know if you find anything.

tracking-tyras-camp-finding-the-tracks.text: You try to follow the footprints but they lead into impassable woodland.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.player: I've found tracks leading off to the west. But they trail off into the trees. Beyond that I am unable to follow.

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.text: These forests aren't always as dense as you'd think. If you look closer, you might see ways that you can get through. With that in mind, why don't you give it another go?

tracking-tyras-camp-speaking-with-the-el.player: Thanks... I'll see what I can find.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: How goes the hunt for that bandit camp?

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.player: I found it a short distance west of here.

tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.speaker: Elf Tracker
tracking-tyras-camp-returning-to-the-elf.text: I'm sure Lord Iorwerth will be pleased to hear that. You should let him know.

tracking-tyras-camp-fighting-the-tyras-g.speaker: Tyras Guard
tracking-tyras-camp-fighting-the-tyras-g.text: I see you making friends with that elf, traitor!

tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.speaker: General Hining
tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.text: Yes, is there anything I can help with? I'm General of what's left of this army and I'm rather busy.

tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.player: If you're a General can you help me meet the king?

tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.speaker: General Hining
tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.text: The king will see no one. He can trust no one!

tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.player: Is there no way I can see him?

tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.speaker: General Hining
tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.text: In the coming battle he will stand between us and the end. Then you will see him.

tracking-tyras-camp-talking-to-general-h.player: Not quite what I had in mind.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.text: [player name] how goes your search... Any luck hunting down that brigand?

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.player: I've finally tracked the brute down. His camp is in a secluded bit of forest, almost directly south of here.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.text: Good job. As we don't have the troops available to take on his forces directly, I suggest we try some alternative tactics.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.text: I have this book here which details an explosive reaction. We should be able to use it to create a bomb.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.player: Well that should make short work of Tyras.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.text: Indeed. Have a read through and see what you think. Once you have, let me know if you have any questions.
If the player doesn't have any inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth tries to give you a book but you don't have enough room for it.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth gives you a book.

making-a-bomb-losing-the-book.player: I lost my copy of The Big Book of Bangs.

making-a-bomb-losing-the-book.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
making-a-bomb-losing-the-book.text: Its lucky I had a scribe make a few copies then, is it not?
If the player doesn't have any inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth tries to give you a book but you don't have enough room for it.

making-a-bomb-losing-the-book.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth gives you a book.

steps.player: Thank you.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
making-a-bomb-speaking-with-lord-iorwert.text: Good day [player name]. Have you had any luck with that book?

steps.player: I need some quicklime.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Quicklime?

steps.player: Apparently it's made by heating limestone.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Ah, I see. There's a mine directly east of here where you can mine limestone.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help with?

steps.player: I need some sulphur.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Check the shore south of the old camp you were at earlier. I've seen sulphur there in the past, it comes from that poisoned lake.

steps.player: Sounds good, thanks.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help with?

steps.player: I need some naphtha.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Naphtha?

steps.player: According to the book, you get it through the fractional distillation of coal tar.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Well you should be able to get some coal tar from that poisoned lake to the south. As for the rest, I'm afraid I don't have the chemistry knowledge to understand it.

steps.player: Hmm... I know someone from Ardougne who might be able to help. She knows a thing or two about chemistry.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Perfect! Take the book to her and see if she can help. Just don't tell her what it's for. Even if she's trustworthy, we can't take any risks.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Anyway, is there anything else I can help with?

steps.player: I need a barrel.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Have a look around the camp, there should be some empty barrels lying around.

steps.player: Will do, thanks.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help with?

steps.player: I need a fuse.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Some sort of fabric should work. You can use the loom here if needed.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help with?

steps.player: That's all thanks.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: Let me know if you need anything else.

making-a-bomb-speaking-with-the-chemist.prompt: What do you want to talk about?

steps.player: Good day. I was hoping you could help me with something. I have a book which mentions the fractional distillation of coal tar. I don't know how to do that though.

steps.speaker: Chemist
steps.text: Ah, you'll be wanting to use the still then. It's just outside.

steps.player: How do I use it?

steps.speaker: Chemist
steps.text: It's quite simple really. You have to get the still heat up very high for it to work. However, if it gets too hot it will burn out and you will have to start over.

steps.speaker: Chemist
steps.text: You must also watch the pressure, if it gets too high you will also have to start over. There are valves to control pressure and tar flow. These will also affect the heat of the still.

steps.player: Is that all?

steps.speaker: Chemist
steps.text: You'll also need plenty of coal to keep the still hot.

steps.player: I see, thanks for the information.

committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.text: Good day [player.] Have you had any luck with that book?

committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.text: Excellent work. Now we can finally deal with Tyras.

committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.player: So what should I do? Plant it in his camp?

committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.text: No, you'll be spotted by the guards if you try that. You'll need to get it in from outside.

committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.text: Tyras and his men have used catapults against us in the past. Maybe you can turn one of them against him.

committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-returning-to-lord-io.text: Now you'd better get going. Don't forget, you'll need a tinderbox to light that fuse. Return to me once the deed is done.

committing-regicide-bribing-the-guard.player: I was wondering what you were doing out here?

committing-regicide-bribing-the-guard.speaker: Tyras guard
committing-regicide-bribing-the-guard.text: I was just wondering what I was doing here too. I'm meant to be looking after this catapult but I can't keep my mind on the job. We've been living off field rations for almost a year now.

committing-regicide-bribing-the-guard.speaker: Tyras guard
committing-regicide-bribing-the-guard.text: I keep seeing rabbits in this forest. What I wouldn't give to eat one, but I'm not quick enough to kill any and I'm no good with a bow.

steps.player: I can see how that would be distracting.
Well I have one here for you.

steps.speaker: Tyras guard
steps.text: You cooked me a rabbit! Thanks a lot. You don't mind watching things while I take five to eat it, do you?

committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.speaker: Tyras guard
committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.text: They say the king died from a flying fire ball. Are you certain no one messed with the catapult while I was eating?

committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.player: I was the only one here. I was watching the whole time.

committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.speaker: Tyras guard
committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.text: These are dark times, I must prepare for the coming darkness.

committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.speaker: General Hining
committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.text: This is not a good place to be, go and prepare for the coming darkness.

committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.speaker: General Hining
committing-regicide-talking-to-tyras-for.text: There is no great hero left to fight back the forces that face us now... Go, leave, prepare for the darkness. While you still have time!

committing-regicide-talking-to-the-elf-t.speaker: Elf Tracker
committing-regicide-talking-to-the-elf-t.text: I take it that the huge explosion I just heard was you?

committing-regicide-talking-to-the-elf-t.player: Yes, I've finally dealt with Tyras, he should cause you no more problems.

committing-regicide-talking-to-the-elf-t.speaker: Elf Tracker
committing-regicide-talking-to-the-elf-t.text: This is good news indeed. Lord Iorwerth will be very happy. You should go and let him know.

committing-regicide-reporting-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-reporting-to-lord-io.text: Good good... One of my scouts reported that they saw his tent in a ball of flames. You have done well.

committing-regicide-reporting-to-lord-io.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-reporting-to-lord-io.text: I'm sure you will want to get back to your king and tell him. He will undoubtedly want some proof. He should trust me enough in this matter, Give him this letter, it verifies that the job is done.
If the player doesn't have any inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth tries to give you a scroll but you don't have enough room for it.

committing-regicide-reporting-to-lord-io.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth gives you a scroll.

steps.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
steps.text: As a token of my own thanks, I give you access to the pass through Arandar. You'll find the start of the trail in the far north east of the woods.

steps.player: Thank you my lord.

committing-regicide-losing-the-scroll.player: Lord Iorwerth, I have lost the message for King Lathas.

committing-regicide-losing-the-scroll.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-losing-the-scroll.text: Here have another copy, but don't let it fall into the wrong hands.
If the player doesn't have any inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth tries to give you a scroll but you don't have enough room for it.

committing-regicide-losing-the-scroll.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Lord Iorwerth gives you a scroll.

steps.player: Thank you my lord.

committing-regicide-talking-to-lord-iorw.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-talking-to-lord-iorw.text: Have you delivered the message to King Lathas yet?

committing-regicide-talking-to-lord-iorw.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
committing-regicide-talking-to-lord-iorw.text: There is no time for delay, he'll need to see it.

reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.text: Are you the human by the name [player name]?

reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.text: Thank Seren, maybe all is not yet lost.

reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.text: I am Arianwyn, leader of the Elven Resistance. We've been watching you since you arrived in Tirannwn. We know it was you that murdered King Tyras.

reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.text: There is much to explain and little time. You carry a message from Lord Iorwerth, do you not?

reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.player: Well you seem to know everything else so I'll not lie. Yes.

reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.speaker: Arianwyn
reporting-to-king-lathas-meeting-arianwy.text: Good, we understand each other well. Now hand it here and find the truth of who your real employer is.
You show the message to the elf, he moves his lips silently and the seal on the message is parted.

steps.npc: The Imcando dwarves, you say? Let's see...

Unfortunately, about a century ago, the once thriving group was wiped out during the barbarian invasions of that time.
I believe a few of them survived, but with the bulk of their population destroyed, their numbers dwindled even further. If any are left now, they'll no doubt keep to themselves.

'Not much is known about the hero called Robert the Strong. Most folk tales describe him as being taller than the tallest human and far stronger than the strongest warrior.'
'He wields a six foot tall longbow and travels with his faithful panther, Odysseus. He is said to have had a personal crusade against the dragonkin...'

'The stories tell of the dragonkin being an intelligent race of bird-like creatures that walked rather than using their wings. They are said to be immortal, but cannot reproduce.'
'Because of this, they became very afraid of death and shunned all other races.'
'Some even say the dragonkin made corrupted versions of themselves for protection, what we now know as dragons. However, this has never been proven.'

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is the prison of Zalcano.

steps.player: Zalcano?

steps.npc: That's right. She's a powerful demon, one bearing an ancient curse.

steps.player: A curse? That doesn't sound good.

steps.npc: Don't worry, the curse only affects her. Because of it, her entire body has been turned to stone.

steps.player: I see. So why is she here?

steps.npc: She came to our lands long ago, before the curse had fully taken hold. We imprisoned her here for study, so that we might learn more about her affliction.
If you want to learn more, you should be able to find a book in the Grand Library about her.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: What can I do here?

steps.npc: Well we could always use some help in keeping Zalcano under control.

steps.player: How would I do that?

steps.npc: Zalcano is formed completely from stone. Because of this, normal weapons won't work on her.
That said, when she's vulnerable, you can still do some damage to her if you use a pickaxe.

steps.player: When she's vulnerable? How do I make her vulnerable?

steps.npc: The ore found within these caverns can be rather volatile, especially when heated. We've found that when imbued, this ore can damage her armour.
You'll want to head on in and mine the ore from the rocks around the prison. Once you have some, you can heat it using the furnace and then imbue it using the altar.
Once you've got some imbued ore, just give it a throw her way and she'll definitely feel it.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: What do I get for helping out here?

steps.player: What do I get for helping out here?

steps.npc: Well assuming you are successful of subdueing Zalcano, she has accumulated a lot of ores and magical runes from her time as a demon.

steps.npc: Well we would always appreciate these resources, in exchange we could bestow upon you our elven knowledge for mining.
We wouldn't be asking for anything special though, just the common resources are what we require.

options.text: Could you tell me about Barnacle Barnaby?

steps.player: Could you tell me about Barnacle Barnaby?

steps.npc: He was a cruel and vicious pirate. Orchestrator of the Driftwood Massacre and unleasher of the Plague of Black Mists. He believed himself untouchable, but his arrogance was his undoing.
Despite the warnings of many, Barnacle Barnaby attempted to plunder the Skullhorde, but his only reward was a deadly curse. It destroyed the Crimson Kraken, condemning all on board to a watery grave.

steps.player: And you had a map leading to the wreck of the Kraken?

steps.npc: Aye! I purchased the map from Ulrich the Unfortunate, the sole survivor of the Kraken, but I had no intention of using it. I knew that no good would ever come from seeking the Kraken.

steps.player: Then why not destroy the map?

steps.npc: And risk the wrath of Barnaby's ghost? No. I thought it better the map be locked away, so that neither it nor the curse could harm anyone else, but those young fools put an end to that.
Now we can only hope that someone puts a stop to them before it's too late. Who knows, perhaps it will be you who does so.

steps.player: Well, on that note, I'd best be getting off. Until next time, Ribs.

options.text: It's a very interesting island you have here.

steps.player: It's a very interesting island you have here.

steps.npc: Why thank you. It's been our haven for a great many generations.

steps.player: Everything seems to have a magical feel to it.

steps.npc: Of course. We integrate magic into all areas of our lives. It is a part of everyone, so why deny it? It's best to make the most of this innate gift we have all been given.

steps.player: What sort of things do you use your magic for?

steps.npc: Take a look around. We use it in our day to day lives, from making a cup of tea, to travelling around the island. You see our ancestors were the ones that found the first rune essence and put it to use! The various
factions were eventually created, with people having different ideas on how the essence should be used (or not in some cases!)

steps.player: What has kept you so secluded on this island?

steps.npc: It may be a bit beyond you, but although magic comes from within, we are all very strongly linked to the moon and the effects it has on us cannot be denied!

steps.player: It can't?

steps.npc: Of course not. This very island has a great link to our moon, which helps us understand ourselves - especially our dreams, which is the path to understanding magic.

steps.player: I think I will just have to take your word on that.
I'm good thanks, bye.

steps.npc: Come to visit my garden then, have you, human?

steps.player: This is your garden?

steps.npc: No no, not quite. But I do look after it. It's the palace garden, you see. I keep it tidy, keep it living.
It's hard to grow much on these hard rocks deep beneath these mountains, you know.

steps.player: I can imagine. Where do you get all your food from? Or even the soil for this garden?

steps.npc: We can grow a little food underground, but most of it comes from the extensive steamcart network that runs beneath the earth.
In the Era of Kings, many centuries ago, it was harder of course. Our steam technology was not developed as far yet and getting fresh supplies of food was always a problem.
Oh, I'm not boring you, am I?

steps.player: Not at all! Please, go on!

steps.npc: Oh yes, as I was saying, it was difficult to make a decent living here. I'm afraid this garden was rather neglected during that time.

steps.player: Why did you dwarves stay so deep under ground, then? Why not simply go above ground?

steps.npc: What, with the wars raging up there?
We dwarves went underground a long time ago, see. For a while the city of Keldagrim was completely cut off from the rest of Gielinor simply waiting out the wars of the humans and the gods.
This made it hard, though, to determine when the wars above the ground were over. Perhaps Keldagrim had remained hidden for far too long.
Only when King Alvis heroically defended the city against an invasion of trolls did we dare to venture out and see how much the world had changed.
Of course, after that...
Ah well, enough history lessons I should say. I must really get back to my gardening.

steps.player: Thanks for the info!

steps.player: Not really, no.

I hear he has all these crazy followers who say things like we shouldn't kill people and eat them! What's up with that?

options.text: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

steps.player: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...

steps.player: That doesn't seem likely...

steps.npc: No? The Saradominists hate us. It's only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands are kept safe.

steps.player: Lord Drakan? Who is that?

steps.npc: Ahhh... you must be new to these parts if you haven't heard of Lord Drakan! He's the lord of this land, and we all pledge allegiance to him.
In return for our allegiance, and the tithe of course, he keeps our land safe from any invaders and the Saradominists who want to kill us all.

steps.player: Tithe? What do you mean?

steps.npc: Ah, well, in return for his protection, we have to give Lord Drakan a share of blood every week. If we don't have any to spare from our hunts, then we need to pick a member of the village to give their life in return
for the blood so that the tithe is fulfilled.

steps.player: You mean you kill someone you know in order to meet the tithe???

steps.npc: That's right, but only if we haven't managed to get enough spare blood from our hunts. It's kind of severe if you look at it that way, but frankly, I think the price is fair in return for his protection and his tolerance of
our village. He could probably kill us all if he wanted us gone, so keeping on his good side is worth the sacrifice to us. Lucky we're not human really!

steps.player: Why's that?

steps.text: If Vampyre Slayer is completed:

steps.npc: He hates humans! Apparently long ago his brother Draynor was trapped in Misthalin and lost much of his powers, and was recently killed by some human!

steps.text: If Vampyre Slayer is not completed:

steps.npc: He hates humans! Apparently his brother Draynor is trapped in Misthalin, and adventurous little human wannabe-heroes keep trying to kill him!
Man, I'd hate to be a human around here, that's for sure. Drakan would really enjoy hunting them down and killing them!

steps.player: Uh... thanks for the info...

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...

steps.player: That doesn't seem likely...

steps.npc: No? The Saradominists hate us. It was only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands were kept safe, but now he's gone and we've got some new overlord who apparently wants us to all be friends! Like that's ever
going to happen!

steps.player: So... Are you going to do something about that?

steps.npc: Me? Of course not! Someone really should though...

steps.player: Okay...

options.text: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

steps.player: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

steps.npc: Hmmm? Why, who did you want to hear the gossip about?

steps.player: Tell me what you know about Sbott the Tanner.

steps.npc: Hey, I won't hear a word said bad about that guy! He's an honest and hard-working wolf if I ever met one! He charges a lot for his job, but he's one of the best tanners I've ever seen - and I'm over four hundred
years old! You need stuff tanning, I recommend him!

steps.player: Know anything interesting about Rufus the food seller?

steps.npc: Ah yeah... good old Rufus... He's kind of getting on in years and doesn't like to come out of his wolf form so often, but let me tell you this: that guy is a hunter through and through. You seen how much food he

catches a day? That takes real dedication! Some of the young pups think just because a wolf has a bit of grey in his fur then he's past it, but I've seen him put those pups to shame in a hunt! He's a real inspiration to us
all!

steps.player: Got anything to share about Barker the clothes seller?

steps.npc: Eh, I don't like the guy much, but you can't knock the quality of his stock. They're some fine quality threads you can get yourself there.

steps.player: What's wrong with him?

steps.npc: Eh... I can't really tell you to be honest. Something about the guy just gets my hackles up everytime he opens his yap, know what I mean?

steps.player: No, not really.

steps.npc: Lucky for you. I can't really explain it, I just don't like the guy. Does great clothes though, you got to give him that.

steps.player: I bet you have some juicy gossip about Fidelio the general store owner.

steps.npc: That nut job? Oh sure, we all know about him. He was a real firebrand daredevil when he was younger, always taking risks to make himself a quick buck... he got himself caught up in the smuggling trade, sneaking over
the border into Misthalin and pretending to be a human so he could buy exotic items to sell.

steps.player: Exotic items? From Misthalin? Like what?

steps.npc: Oh man, you name it! Flour... buckets... tinderboxes... chisels... he could get the lot! He's been doing it so long now though, his nerves are shot.
Nowadays he's a disgrace, he can barely string a sentence together and jumps at his own shadow. Makes you feel ashamed to be a werewolf.

options.text: Tell me about the temple to the West.

steps.player: Tell me about the temple to the west.

steps.npc: Well, I'm not old enough to remember the full story behind it, but it was a terrible day for these lands when it was built there.
Apparently, Morytania was once a strong and mighty kingdom, with lands spreading far further west than they do today, and south into the desert as well.

That was all until the day when a sneak attack by the hated human forces who worship Saradomin burned our villages and slaughtered our peoples in mass. To rub salt into the wound, they then cursed the river as well!
Luckily they seem to have calmed down somewhat recently, and tend to stay on their side of the river... but the wrong they have done my people will never be forgotten, and will never be forgiven!

steps.player: So you hate humans?

steps.npc: Absolutely! If I ever met one I would gobble him up where he stands! And then chew the bones for dessert!

steps.player: Um, okay, thanks, bye.
Can I hear a story?

steps.npc: A story??? Heh, well the only one I can think of right now is one my dear old mammy told me as a pup...
Now how did it go... Ah yes!

Once upon a time a brave young wolf was walking through a forest, when he came upon a human dressed all in red. 'Aha!' he thought to himself, 'Here's a nice easy meal!' But the human talked to him, and as he was
always taught to be a polite wolf, he spoke back to it.

Well, this cunning human told him that there was a better meal that would not run away in a house in the woods. As the brave young wolf could see that this human was not fully grown, he figured maybe he'd

better get a better meal at this house, so he ran as fast as his paws could carry him to the house the human told him about... inside he found an old human lying in bed, and although the meat was a little tough, as the

human was older than he thought, he had a good meal and decided to sleep it off in the house for awhile. He had not been asleep long though, when he was woken by a knocking at the door. The human in red had followed

him to the house! Suspecting a human trap, the brave young wolf put on the old humans clothes and jumped into the bed, so that he could pretend to be human and escape from this terrible trap! Well now, this human

dressed in red came into the house, and pretended to believe the brave wolf was really a human, and began to talk to him. But then the human started asking strange questions of the wolf, because the human knew that it

was not a human at all! The brave young wolf decided to try and escape, for it was only a young human, and not very strong, so the brave young wolf said he would eat the human if they did not let him escape! As he said

this however, the human in red shouted out at him: 'Aha! You are a wolf!' and as the human shouted this another bigger human ran into the room from outside! This bigger human was much stronger and was
carrying an axe, and the poor young wolf died in this terrible trap made for him by the humans.
And do you know what the moral of this story is?

steps.player: Um... no, not really.

steps.npc: It's 'Never trust humans' of course! My dear old mammy told me that story when I was a pup, and I'm still alive and well to tell it to you today!
Pretty good story huh?

steps.player: Um... yeah. It was great. Really.
Nothing thanks.
