steps.text: They've not been used to keep prisoners for a long time. But since the war ended, we've had more people visiting the island.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Some of them decided they wanted to stay, so we've had to find somewhere for them to live...

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Only the weather on Miscellania is terrible, and nobody could build houses that would stand up to a strong wind. Etceteria is just the same.

steps.player: So you decided to live in the dungeons instead?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Well, of course, they had to be enlarged first. There are still some dwarves working there, making more of the dungeons inhabitable before they move over to work in Etceteria.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: If you're looking for those kids from Rellekka, you'll find them in those dungeons.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Why are you surprised about this, though? I thought you'd become the Regent.

steps.player: I'm still an adventurer, and I can't be everywhere in Gielinor...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: Sorry, but nobody's allowed down there by order of the King.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.player: But I'm the Regent! I order you to let me go down there.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: You're the Regent? Well, I didn't vote for you.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: Sorry, 'Regent', nobody can go into the dungeons without the King's say-so.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.player: What'll it take to convince you that I'm really the Regent?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: If the King came and told me, then I'd believe it.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: Or, if he can't come here himself, I suppose a royal proclamation would be fine.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.player: Does he have to shout it from the battlements, or something like that?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: No, just his signature and a statement saying you're really the Regent would do.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.player: Your Majesty, how do I get into the dungeons?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Of course, how could I have forgotten?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: I'm surprised I didn't tell you when you were appointed Regent.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.player: It's okay, the sailor explained it to me.
He said that the only new arrivals on the island were some teenagers, who came from Rellekka to visit their relatives.
Those relatives were living in the houses in the dungeons.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Ah, so you wish to look in the dungeons in case these new arrivals are to blame?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: I doubt that anyone with Miscellanian relatives would be at fault. However...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: There is something I need you to do in the dungeons.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: They are still being excavated, and the dwarven architects are finding new caves as they go. There have been reports of odd sightings in these new caves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Perhaps they are monsters, waiting to devour unwary Miscellanians...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Whatever they are, I want you to look into it.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: You are a member of the royal family, after all, so I know I can rely on your help.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: The guard by the dungeon entrance may not recognise you, since he was only hired recently. Here, take this scroll to show that you have access to the dungeons.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: You'll find the entrance by the south-east corner of the palace.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: Have you given that scroll to the guard yet?
If the player still has the scroll:

steps.player: Not yet, your Majesty.

steps.text: (Continues with Changing heirs dialogue.)

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: If the player lost the scroll:

steps.player: I seem to have lost it.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Honestly... very well, I'll write you another one.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Try not to lose it this time.
(Continues with Changing heirs dialogue.)

options.text: How do I manage the kingdom?
What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Showing the dungeon guard that you have permission to enter, Your Royal Highness.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Sorry, but nobody's allowed down there by order of the King.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.player: But I'm the Regent! I order you to let me go down there.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: You're the Regent? Well, I didn't vote for you.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Sorry, 'Regent', nobody can go into the dungeons without the King's say-so.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.player: Look, the King gave me a scroll saying I have access to the dungeons. I have it right here.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Hmm... all seems to be in order.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: All right, your Highness, you're free to go down there.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Try not to be eaten by monsters.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.speaker: Halla
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.text: Welcome to Miscellania's first clothing store! We sell clothing made especially for Fremenniks and Dwarves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.speaker: Halla
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.text: Can I help you with anything, Your Royal Highness?

options.text: I'd like to look at what you have for sale.
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Halla
steps.text: It's very spacious. One of the dwarves said that the caves go on for miles!

steps.speaker: Halla
steps.text: I don't like these rumours I've heard about the other caves, though.

steps.player: What rumours?

steps.speaker: Halla
steps.text: They say there might be monsters in there. You'd best talk to the dwarves who are excavating - they'd know about these stories.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.speaker: Osvald
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.text: Welcome to the Miscellania food store. We've only opened recently.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.speaker: Osvald
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.text: Would you like to buy anything, your Royal Highness?

options.text: Could you show me what you have for sale?
No thank you, I don't need food just now.
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: The town's growing larger, and business is doing well.

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: I'm worried about the stories I've heard about monsters, though.

steps.player: What stories about monsters?

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: I heard that one of the dwarves saw monsters in the other caves!

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: I don't know more than that, so you'd have to ask the dwarves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-finn.speaker: Finn
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-finn.text: Can I help you, your Royal Highness?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Finn
steps.text: There's no rain or wind down here.

steps.speaker: Finn
steps.text: Some of the dwarves say that there's water in the other caves, and one of them says he's seen monsters in there.

steps.player: Monsters? What sort of monsters?

steps.speaker: Finn
steps.text: I don't know, sorry. You'd better ask one of the dwarves about it.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.speaker: Runa
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.text: Would you like to try some fine Miscellanian ale, Your Royal Highness?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.speaker: Runa
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.text: Well, I say Miscellanian, but it's actually brewed on the mainland.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.speaker: Runa
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.text: Would you like to try some anyway?

options.text: What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Runa
steps.text: The dwarves living down here spend a lot of time and money in my inn.

steps.speaker: Runa
steps.text: One of them's been in here all day, and only bought one pint.

steps.speaker: Runa
steps.text: Could you ask him to at least order another drink?

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: I'm waiting for my shift. I'm supposed to be digging once the others have finished.

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: I don't like the sound of these monsters, though.

steps.player: Monsters?

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: I heard that Donal went exploring in the caves, and saw a huge monster.

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: If you want to know more about it, ask Thorodin - he's working on the excavation right now.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: I'm working on the digging, of course.

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: It's a small excavation, so only two of us can work on it at a time.

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: Thorodin and Donal were working on it earlier, but I hear Donal's run off to hide in the inn.

steps.player: Why is that?

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: Apparently he saw a monster when he was in the caves.

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: I'm not scared of monsters - I won't let them stop me from digging!

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: I'm waiting to work on the digging.

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: It's the first excavation I've worked on, and I'm looking forward to it.

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: I heard there were monsters in the other caves, though. I don't really want to meet them.

steps.player: Monsters?

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: Donal saw them when he explored the caves. He's been in the inn ever since.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.

steps.player: ...such as?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: You don't get rained on, for example.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Of course, there are some problems, like the monsters Donal saw...

steps.player: Someone saw a monster?
Could you tell me more? The King asked me to investigate.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: One of the other dwarves who was working with us saw it. His name's Donal.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: He went further into the caves to plan our excavations, and a while later he came out shaking.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: He's been in the inn ever since.

steps.player: Good day.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.

steps.player: ...such as?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: You don't get rained on, for example.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Have you spoken to Donal?

steps.player: Not yet, no.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Well, if you want to hear stories about monsters, he's the best one to ask.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.

steps.player: ...such as?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Not getting rained on, for example.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Have you spoken to Donal?

steps.player: I have. The monster he talked about could be in the caves nearby.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: You'd better get in there and do something about it, then.

steps.player: It's not safe. I need to shore up the walls before I can go through.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.player: What are you doing down in these caves?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: I'm waiting to work on the excavations...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: ...though I don't really want to start digging again.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.player: Why not? I thought digging was something dwarves were good at.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: Not with monsters like that one in those caves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: It had huge teeth and flaming red eyes, and was almost the size of the tunnel!

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: Are you an adventurer, by any chance?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: In that case, could you go and deal with that monster?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: I don't want to have to face it again if it attacks the town.

options.text: Of course. Dealing with monsters is what I do best!

steps.player: Of course. Dealing with monsters is what I do best!

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: You'll need to get into the other caves first, of course.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: There's a crack in the wall where the others are digging, but the rocks are loose, and can fall on you if you're not careful.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: I can give you a mining prop to keep them from falling, if you give me a minute to find it...

steps.player: Okay, so all I have to do is get through that wall?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: No, after that the only way you can get further is climbing up onto a high ledge, then crawling through a tunnel.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: But the walls are slippery...

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: ...and I think I might have broken the lift when I fell off it on my way back.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: You'll probably need to fix the lift - I doubt you'd be able to climb.

steps.player: And the monster's behind that tunnel?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Somewhere behind it. I couldn't get very far, what with the flooding in the tunnel.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: There's some rope and some planks near the broken lift - those would probably come in handy.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Ah, here's that mining prop. I knew I had it somewhere.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Here you go. Good luck with fighting that monster.
mining prop

options.text: Why bother? It can't get through solid rock.

steps.player: Why bother? It can't get through solid rock.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: That's what I thought, until I saw the sheer size of it. This thing probably MADE the tunnels!

steps.player: And you're sending me in to deal with it alone?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: I've heard stories from the Miscellanians. If you're the Regent, you must be quite a strong hero.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: So what are you worried about? You probably eat monsters like that for breakfast!

steps.player: I wouldn't put it quite like that...
But I'll help you after all. Now, how do I find this monster?

steps.text: Continues above at "You'll need to get into the other caves first, of course."

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.player: Just wondering if you were still here.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: I'm not going near that crack in the wall again.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: Rock falls and so on are fine, but sea monsters in caves - never!
If the player lost the mining prop:

steps.player: I've lost that mining prop you gave me...

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Lucky I have a spare, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Here you go. Good luck with fighting that monster.

repairing-the-lift-attempting-to-squeeze.player: It's not safe. I need to shore up the walls before I can go through.

repairing-the-lift-putting-the-prop-in-p.text: You approach the crack in the wall...
You wedge the prop in the wall to stop the rocks falling.

repairing-the-lift-taking-a-pulley-beam.text: ...and pull out a beam with a pulley on it.

repairing-the-lift-adding-the-pulley-bea.text: You add the plank to the scaffold as a crossbeam.

repairing-the-lift-creating-a-long-pulle.text: You attach the beams together to form a longer beam.

repairing-the-lift-creating-a-longer-pul.text: You attach the beams together to form a very long beam.

repairing-the-lift-adding-the-longer-pul.text: You carefully add the top beam to the scaffold.

repairing-the-lift-adding-the-rope.text: You carefully add the top beam to the scaffold.

repairing-the-lift-adding-a-beam-to-the-.text: You repair the platform with the beam.

repairing-the-lift-adding-coal-to-the-en.text: You put the coal into the engine.

repairing-the-lift-attempting-to-overfil.text: The engine seems to be full of coal already.

repairing-the-lift-adding-the-engine.text: You put the coal engine onto the scaffold. It appears to fit perfectly.

repairing-the-lift-using-items-on-the-li.text: The lift seems to be working now. It doesn't need further repair.

the-burnt-diary-using-a-rope-on-the-rock.text: You throw the rope up and lash it around the rock formation.

the-burnt-diary-approaching-the-first-fi.player: I can see the embers of a fire up ahead. Has someone else been in these caves?

the-burnt-diary-searching-the-first-fire.text: You find a burnt diary with one page in the embers.

the-burnt-diary-look-at-rocks.text: The water's making the rocks too slippery to walk on.
Maybe if you had a board or plank...

the-burnt-diary-using-a-plank-on-the-roc.text: You place the board across the slippery rocks...

the-burnt-diary-getting-hit-by-steam-ven.text: As you walk over a steam vent, a plume of steam shoots up and hits you!

the-burnt-diary-getting-hit-by-rocks.text: Rocks tumble from the cave walls as you walk under them!

the-burnt-diary-searching-the-second-thi.text: You find some diary pages in the embers.
You add them to the diary you have.

the-burnt-diary-searching-fire-remains-y.text: You don't find any more diary pages in the embers.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-enter-the-.player: I should explore this cave more before I jump through any more cracks in the walls...

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Cutscene begins.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What do we do now?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If you hadn't got drunk in that inn, Signy, we could have stayed there for longer.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It wasn't just me who got drunk. You looked like you were about to puke all over the barmaid.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Reinn threw up anyway.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I can't help it, I just have a weak stomach.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You're no better, Hild. You said you knew where we were, and now look at us!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We're cold, we're hungry and now we're LOST!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We wouldn't have been so cold if Armod had more diary pages he'd let us use!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Hey! I have to write down what's happened.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Otherwise father won't believe me when I tell him.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If your father listened to what you say, we wouldn't BE here.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We'd have passed the trials and we'd be proper adults!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Besides, it's not like he'll even look at the rubbish you've written in your diary.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If only my father would come and save us.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If only SOMEONE would come and save us.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Someone's coming!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Quick, let's hide!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What if it's the monster again? What if it's one of the townspeople?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What if my father's found out what we've been doing?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: H-hey! Where am I going to hide?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Shhhh! Just pretend you're part of the scenery, or something!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You're almost smart enough to make a good rock.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You want me to hit you?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Just act normal, Armod! And hurry!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: O-okay.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Don't bother me!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I said, don't bother me!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I'm being a rock at the moment.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: You can't be a rock. I heard you talking to people earlier.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What did you hear?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Your name's Armod, isn't it? I found your diary.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What? How did you get it? Give it back!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Not until you tell me what's going on.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Why should I tell you? We're going to do really well and show my father that we're true adults!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What the-

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Did you read my diary?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What are you even doing in these caves anyway? Everyone else was scared to come down here.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Well, I'm the Regent of Miscellania. The King asked me to take a look-

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You're the REGENT?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Um, you four, I think you'd better come out now. We're in big trouble.
Cutscene ends.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Nice impression of a rock you did there, Armod.
If the player married Brand/Astrid:

steps.speaker: Signy
steps.text: So you're the adventurer we heard about, then. The one who married the [prince/princess].

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If the player did not marry Brand/Astrid:

steps.speaker: Signy
steps.text: So you're the adventurer we heard about, then. The one who gained the trust of the [prince/princess].

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: And you five are the people mentioned in Armod's diary, right?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Beigarth
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Armod, you should have burnt it all.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Did you steal those goods from the Etceterians and the Miscellanians?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It was Beigarth's idea, not mine!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: He said that if we disguised ourselves as soldiers, we could convince both the King and Queen that they were under attack. And it almost worked, too.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It would have worked, if it hadn't been for that huge snake!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We put the things we'd taken somewhere safe, so we could get them back when we made peace again.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Everything was going well, until we got back to that place, and a giant sea snake had moved in!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It's made a nest out of all the boxes and barrels.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I don't care about the plan. If you can get rid of that sea snake, we'll be really grateful to you.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We can't even get out of these dungeons while it's there.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I agree with him. I want to go back home.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It's cold here, we've got no food, and we can't go back to the town.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Not after we got drunk and then didn't pay our bill.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: So, will you get rid of that sea snake?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Of course. I was going to do that anyway.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Thank you so much. You've saved us from the brink of death.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Could I ask you for one more thing?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: PLEASE don't tell my father how badly we messed up.

those-meddling-kids-upon-killing-the-gia.text: A box of Etceterian items tumbles from the sea snake's nest.

those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.text: Hello down there! Are you all right?

those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.text: I'm up here, above this hole.

those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.text: I've thrown down a rope - you sounded like you were trapped in there.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-the-guard.text: If you still have the heavy box:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I'm surprised you managed to get out of there without breaking any bones.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Still, I can't let you go back down there until the Queen says it's safe.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-the-guard.text: If you lost the heavy box:

steps.player: I don't suppose you've seen a large box around here, have you?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh, so this is yours? You must have dropped it around here.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Seems rather heavy. Take better care of it this time.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.text: Wait a minute! You can't go down there.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.player: Why not? I came up through that hole...

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.text: Yes, and I'm surprised you managed to get out of there without breaking any bones.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.text: Still, I can't let you go back down there until the Queen says it's safe.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: I've talked to the Miscellanian citizens as well as the Etceterians.
The Etceterian citizens said that Miscellanian soldiers came to their houses and demanded tribute...

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Just as I suspected! Vargas, you treacherous snake!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: ...and the Miscellanian citizens said that the Etceterian army marched into their fields and demanded tithes!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Now I see his plan! Vargas isn't content with simply arguing; he wants to start a war even if it means swindling his own citizens!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Etceterian army? There hasn't been one for centuries! These Miscellanian soldiers of his must have disguised themselves.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: If he wants an Etceterian army, then we'll have to raise one!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: I've found out what caused all these problems.
A group of teenagers from Rellekka came to Etceteria to prove themselves as adults.
They said they tried to start a war, which they'd then stop, and be hailed as peacemakers.
They were the ones who disguised themselves as soldiers!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: That explains what the citizens said about armies, I suppose.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: But what about the items that went missing?

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: Well, there was a minor problem involving a sea snake...
But I dealt with it, and got the items back.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Finally, a ruler of Miscellania who's willing to do something for his neighbours.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Do you have the items with you?
If you lost the heavy box:

steps.player: ...I must have dropped the box on my way out of the dungeons.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: sigh* Well, if you ask the guard at the entrance to the dungeon, he might have picked it up.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Of course, he won't know what it's for, so you'd better bring it back here once you find it.

steps.player: I shall do, your Majesty.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: If you still have the heavy box:

steps.player: Yes, I have them here.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Thank you, [Fremennik name]. You've shown yourself to be an excellent diplomat and warrior - not a combination that comes naturally to many.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: My citizens would like their items back, of course. One of my guards will deal with the items for you, and you will be provided with a suitable reward.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Finally... I have a letter that I would like you to give to Vargas. This war was a mistake, and I've made a formal apology.

steps.player: I'll make sure to give it to him, your Majesty.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Thank you for all your help, [Fremennik name]. To show our gratitude, the woodcutters and other workers of Etceteria have pledged to add a proportion of what they produce to your treasury.
Letter (Royal Trouble)
20,000 coins

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Now that you've finished giving these items back, please give my letter to Vargas.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-sigrid-ag.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-sigrid-ag.text: I'm glad you've found my citizens' missing items, Dalkar. Have you had a chance to give Vargas my letter?
If you still have the letter:

steps.player: Not yet, your Majesty.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Oh, that's a pity.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Hurry up and give it to him, please. It means we can formally declare peace again.

steps.player: I'm afraid I've lost it.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Very well, I'll write another. Try to take better care of this one.

at-peace-once-again-reading-the-letter-q.player: I'm not sure I should be reading this...

options.text: I shouldn't read other people's letters.

steps.player: I won't read that letter. It's for the King, not for me.
I'm not sure I should be reading this...

options.text: Go ahead and read it anyway.

steps.player: Oh, why not. I'm the Regent, after all.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: How are your investigations going, [Fremennik name]?

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.player: I've found the people who took the goods from your citizens!
They weren't Etceterian soldiers after all.
They were teenagers from Rellekka who were trying to prove themselves as adults, by starting a war and then bringing about peace.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Why didn't they just go through the trials as usual?

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Unless they're the ones that the Council warned me about.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Still, I can't believe they'd start a war between Miscellania and Etceteria, just to show they were adults...

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: But at least you've found the missing goods. Do you have them with you?

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.player: I'm afraid not, your Majesty. There were far too many for me to carry.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: We'll have to send people down to collect them later, then.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.player: And I also spoke to Queen Sigrid of Etceteria.
She gave me a letter for you, which she said was a formal apology.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Oh? Do you have this letter with you?

steps.player: Er, I had it, but I seem to have lost it.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You'd better ask Sigrid to write you another one, then.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I'd like to see what she has to say.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: If you still have the letter:

steps.player: Of course, your Majesty. Here you are.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Let me see...

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You defeated that sea snake? Sigrid seems rather impressed with that.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: And the caverns underneath her palace are joined to ours, I see.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: She thinks we should join forces to develop them for more houses.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Finally... hmm. That's not what I'd have expected from Sigrid.

steps.player: What is it, your Majesty?

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: She, erm, says if I weren't a yeti, she might want to get to know me better.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Since we're both warmongering fools, she thinks we'd get on well.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I suppose she has a point there.

steps.player: Brand's suggestion worked, and I didn't even do anything.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: What was that?

steps.player: Nothing, your Majesty.
Do you want me to give a reply to Queen Sigrid?

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: No, no. I'll think about it for a while.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Though I'd like to tell her I'm sorry for calling her a warmongering harpy.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: In the meantime, [Fremennik name], you have managed to avert a war and bring the culprits to light.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: The kingdom of Miscellania will have to reward you for this.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I hear that the Etceterians are also grateful for your help, and have pledged some of their resources.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You can talk to Ghrim to deal with those, just as before.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Thank you for your work in bringing peace back to these islands, [Fremennik name].

post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.text: I hear that the Etceterians have also pledged to give you some of their resources, as thanks for preventing war once again.

post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Remember, speak to Ghrim if you require assistance.

steps.text: (Continues with Changing heirs dialogue.)

post-quest-talking-to-prince-brand.speaker: Prince Brand
post-quest-talking-to-prince-brand.text: I hear you made peace between our kingdom and Etceteria once more. Well done, [dear/[Fremennik name]].

post-quest-talking-to-princess-astrid.speaker: Princess Astrid
post-quest-talking-to-princess-astrid.text: I hear you made peace between our kingdom and Etceteria once more. Well done, [dear/[Fremennik name]].

post-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid.speaker: Queen Sigrid
post-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid.text: Thank you for all your help, [Fremennik name]. It's good to know that the Regent of Miscellania is willing to help his neighbours.

initial-dialogue.npc: Good day!

initial-dialogue.player: Hello there! What are you doing out here?

initial-dialogue.npc: I've been tracking gemstones, and I think I've found a potential source for them!
Yes! A large crab!

initial-dialogue.text: The gemstone crab is nearby:

steps.player: Right...

steps.npc: It moves around a bit, but look! It's right here with us at the moment!

initial-dialogue.text: If the gemstone crab is not nearby:

steps.player: Right... And where is this crab?

steps.text: The gemstone crab is north:
The gemstone crab is north east:
The gemstone crab is north west:
The gemstone crab is south:

steps.npc: It moves around a bit, but I believe it's currently to the south!

steps.text: The gemstone crab is south east:
The gemstone crab is south west:
While the gemstone crab is moving:

steps.npc: Hello again! Look! That large crab is here!

subsequent-dialogue.text: If the gemstone crab is not nearby:

steps.npc: Hello again!

steps.player: Do you happen to know where that large crab is?

steps.text: The gemstone crab is north:

steps.npc: I believe it's currently to the north!

steps.text: The gemstone crab is north east:

steps.npc: I believe it's currently to the north east!

steps.text: The gemstone crab is north west:

steps.npc: I believe it's currently to the north west!

steps.text: The gemstone crab is south:

steps.npc: I believe it's currently to the south!

steps.text: The gemstone crab is south east:

steps.npc: I believe it's currently to the south east!

steps.text: The gemstone crab is south west:

steps.npc: I believe it's currently to the south west!

steps.text: While the gemstone crab is moving:

steps.npc: Strange... I've lost track of it. I'm sure I'll pick up the trail shortly.

I believe the crab is currently to the [direction]!

subsequent-dialogue-directions-option.text: While the gemstone crab is moving:

steps.npc: It seems the crab is burrowing at the moment, but I believe it's heading [direction]!

historical-dialogue-avium-savannah-first.npc: Come on... Something here has to work...
Absolutely! I can't seem to find a way into that crevice to continue my scientific endeavour. I don't suppose you could have a dig around?

historical-dialogue-avium-savannah-first.player: A scientific dig... Where have I heard of that before?

historical-dialogue-avium-savannah-first.npc: Don't dwell on it too long. There are things I must learn about our world!

historical-dialogue-avium-savannah-after.player: I found a ruby in the ground.

historical-dialogue-avium-savannah-after.npc: Wondrous! A good sign to be sure! You may keep it, while I will keep the knowledge of what may be here.

historical-dialogue-south-of-fortis-colo.npc: So I'm here... That's there... Then how do we get down there?
Ah, hello there! I'm just pondering on the wonders of geography.

historical-dialogue-south-of-fortis-colo.player: Anything I can help you out with?

historical-dialogue-south-of-fortis-colo.npc: Most certainly. Perhaps you could dig around near the mouth of that nearby cave and elucidate its nature for me.

historical-dialogue-south-of-fortis-colo.player: Will I get anything for helping?

historical-dialogue-south-of-fortis-colo.npc: The feeling of satisfaction after helping a scientist in need?
Outstanding! This can only be seen as a positive! I shall add the knowledge to my reserves. You may keep the gem.

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.npc: No, my good friend, but I am in a bit of a pickle.
Perhaps a jam... Those bandits over there are in the way of scientific discovery!

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.player: Would you like me to deal with them?

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.npc: Well, I'm not averse to a little academic collaboration. I just need some proof that there's something strange here.
Is there any chance you could dig near the mouth of that cave for me? Let me know if you find anything.

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.player: What should I do with the bandits?

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.npc: I have no qualms with you doing what you must on that front.

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.player: I found an emerald in the earth.

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.npc: Stupendous! Combined with the other locations, I suspect there may be more to this than meets the eye.
Keep the gem for yourself, as payment for your assistance.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: You ssshould not be down here...

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: My name isss unimportant... I live only to ssserve my massster.

steps.player: Um... Okay then.
Why are you down here?

steps.npc: Thisss isss where I belong... Beingsss sssuch as myssself cannot abide in the light... It is in the darknesss where we find our homesss...

steps.player: Uh... Okay then.
Can I use your anvil?

steps.npc: Of courssse you may... I have very little ussse for it nowadaysss...

steps.player: Uh... Thanks, I guess.
Hi!

steps.npc: Grrreetings frrriend! Welcome to my worrrld famous food emporrrium! All my meats are so frrresh you'd swear you killed them yourrrself!

options.text: Why do you only sell meats?

steps.player: Why do you only sell meats?

steps.npc: What? Why, what else would you want to eat? What kind of lycanthrrrope are you anyway?

steps.player: ...A vegetarian one?

steps.npc: Vegetarrrian...?

steps.player: Never mind.
Do you sell cooked food?

steps.npc: Cooked food? Who would want that? You lose all the flavourrr of the meat when you can't taste the blood!

steps.player: Can I buy some food?

steps.npc: Cerrrtainly!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: What are you doing out here on your own?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I'm not alone! Me and my mates run these streets. You'd better watch your pockets, stranger.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: What do you mean you run the streets?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: You see those fancy houses?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: I think so?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: We keep a lookout to see when the owners leave and come back. Once they're out, we can break in and steal all their stuff!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: That sounds risky don't you think? There are guards everywhere.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: No one suspects us street urchins. Hidden in plain sight, as they say.
I can give you some info on which houses are free if you like...

steps.player: I'm alright for now.

steps.npc: Suit yourself.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-dialogue.text: If the player has not spoken to the "Dodgy Character" (Oriana):

steps.npc: Hello. Have you met our crew leader yet?

steps.player: I don't think I have...

steps.npc: Go chat to them! They should be near the bank... naturally.

steps.player: I'll head over there soon.

steps.npc: Happy thieving, stranger.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-dialogue.text: If the player has already spoken to Oriana:

steps.player: Hello there.

steps.npc: Hello. A fine day for stealing, wouldn't you say?

steps.player: I suppose so, just as long as you're not planning to steal from me.

options.text: I could do with some information on houses.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have any house keys in their inventory:

steps.npc: You don't have any house keys, do you? You won't find yourself getting very far without any. Maybe come back later?

steps.text: If the player has at least one house key but less than 15 valuables in their inventory:

steps.npc: You don't have any valuables worth my time. Come back when you do!

steps.text: If the player has at least one house key and at least 15 valuables in their inventory but there is no house available for thieving:

steps.npc: Looks like [Caius/Lavinia/Victor] is returning to [his/her] house. You'll have to wait a moment until we get word of the next house.

steps.text: If the player has at least one house key and at least 15 valuables in their inventory and a house is or will soon be available for thieving:
If it is the player's first time asking (does not require 15 valuables in inventory):

steps.npc: You're new around here. Normally I'd charge 15 valuables for information, but I'm feeling generous.

steps.prompt: Pay 15 valuables for information?

steps.text: If the homeowner is about to leave:

steps.npc: I hear that [Caius/Lavinia/Victor] might be leaving [his/her] house soon.

steps.text: If this is the first time the player is receiving intel on the current targeted house:

steps.npc: Looks like [Caius/Lavinia/Victor] isn't home right now. Go quickly!

steps.text: If the player has already received intel on the current targeted hosue:

steps.npc: Already forgotten? Head over to [Caius/Lavinia/Victor]'s house.

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.text: If Caius's or Victor's house is available for thieving:

steps.npc: His house is north of here.

steps.text: If Lavinia's house is available for thieving:

steps.npc: Her house is east of here.

steps.player: I'll find my own way.

steps.npc: Do you want me to point you in the right direction? {{Anchor|below}}

steps.player: I'll pass for now.

steps.npc: Suit yourself.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Greetings, desert traveller. Do you require the services of Ali Morrisane's flying carpet fleet?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.text: From the Shantay Pass:

steps.npc: From here you can travel to Uzer, to the Bedabin camp or to the North of Pollnivneach.
The second major carpet hub station, to the south of Pollnivneach is in easy walking distance from there.

options.text: I want to travel to Uzer.

steps.player: I want to travel to Uzer.

options.text: I want to travel to the Bedabin Camp.

steps.player: I want to travel to the Bedabin Camp.

options.text: I want to travel to Pollnivneach.

steps.player: I want to travel to Pollnivneach.

options.text: I don't want to travel to any of those places.

steps.player: I don't want to travel to any of those places.

steps.npc: Fair enough, magic carpet travel isn't for everyone. Enjoy the walk.

steps.text: From Uzer:

steps.npc: You can travel from here back to the Shantay Pass.

options.text: That sounds good, take me there.

steps.player: I want to travel to Uzer.

options.text: I don't want to travel there.

steps.player: I don't want to travel there.

steps.npc: Fair enough, magic carpet travel isn't for everyone. Enjoy the walk.

steps.text: From the Bedabin Camp:

steps.npc: From here you can travel to the Shantay Pass.

steps.player: Take me there.

options.text: I don't want to travel there.

steps.text: From the north Pollnivneach station:

steps.npc: From here you can travel to the Shantay Pass - the Southern gate of Al Kharid.

options.text: Take me to the Pass then.

steps.player: Take me to the Pass then.

options.text: I don't want to travel there.

steps.text: From the south Pollnivneach station:

steps.npc: From here you can travel to Nardah and the Menaphite cities of Sophanem and Menaphos.

options.text: I want to travel to Nardah.

steps.player: I want to travel to Nardah.

options.text: I want to travel to Menaphos.

steps.player: I want to travel to Menaphos.

options.text: I want to travel to Sophanem.

steps.player: I want to travel to Sophanem.

options.text: I don't want to travel to any of those places.

steps.text: From Nardah or Menaphos:

steps.npc: The carpets here will take you to the south of Pollnivneach.

steps.player: Let's go then.

options.text: I don't want to travel there.

steps.text: From Sophanem:

steps.npc: The carpets here will take you to the south of Pollnivneach. Do you want to take a lift?

steps.player: Pollnivneach will do.

options.text: I don't want to travel there.

steps.player: Tell me about Ali Morrisane.

steps.npc: What, you haven't heard of Ali M? Possibly the greatest salesman of the Kharidian empire if not all Gielinor?

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed The Feud:

steps.player: I can't say that I have, but he must be the ambitious type to try and set up his own airline.

steps.npc: You know something, I reckon that he's trying to take on those gnomes at their own game and I'd bet good money that he'll probably win.

steps.player: Hah? I think you've gone and lost me now.

steps.npc: You know those small little guys, not the dwarves now mind.

steps.player: Ya... gnomes, I'm with you that far.

steps.npc: Well they have already established an Airline, Gnome Air...

steps.player: Go on...

steps.npc: Anyway I think that Ali M's setup here will prove really successful and maybe once we're properly established we could try compete with those gnomes.

steps.player: I'll watch this space.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Feud:

steps.player: Ah yes I remember him now, I went on a wild goose chase looking for his nephew.

steps.npc: Ha! No doubt old Ali M instigated the whole thing.

steps.player: I had a bit of fun though, The whole job was quite diverting.

steps.npc: There's never a dull moment around that man, he's always looking for a way to make a quick coin or two.

options.text: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.

steps.player: Tell me about this Magic Carpet fleet.

steps.npc: The latest idea from the great Ali Morrisane. Desert travel will never be the same again.

steps.player: So how does it work?

steps.npc: The carpet or the whole enterprise?

options.text: Tell me about how the carpet works.

steps.player: Tell me about how the carpet works.

steps.npc: I'm not really too sure, it's just an enchanted rug really, made out of special Ugthanki hair. It flies to whatever destination its owner commands.

steps.player: Are they for sale then?

steps.npc: Do you think I'm mad? Do you think that Ali Morrisane would throw his magic carpet monopoly away?

steps.player: Well perhaps if I offered the right price?

steps.npc: Not a hope. Could you imagine the mess there'd be if people were constantly zooming through Al Kharid and Pollnivneach? It would be chaos. This way, we can keep the carpet traffic outside towns and other busy places.

steps.player: I suppose getting stuck in a carpet jam could get a bit tiresome.

steps.npc: Just think of the friction burns you would get if you were in a carpet crash.

options.text: Tell me about the enterprise then.

steps.player: Tell me about the enterprise then.

steps.npc: It's quite simple really, Ali Morrisane has hired myself and a few others to set up carpet stations at some of the desert's more populated places and run flights between the stations.

steps.player: So why has he limited the service to just the desert?

steps.npc: I don't think Ali is prepared to take on Gnome Air just yet, their gliders are much faster than our carpets, besides that I think we are in the short haul business, something that would only work in harsh conditions like
the desert.

steps.player: Why is that?

steps.npc: I suppose because people would just walk. Getting lost isn't too much of a problem generally, but it's a different matter when you're in the middle of the Kharidian desert with a dry waterskin and no idea
which direction to go in.

steps.player: You're right I guess. How's the business going then?

steps.npc: Not too bad, the hubs are generally quite busy. But the stations in Uzer and the Bedabin camp could do with a bit more traffic.

steps.player: A growth market I guess.
I have some questions.

steps.npc: I'll try to help you as much as I can.

steps.player: What are you doing here?

steps.text: At the Shantay Pass:

steps.npc: Well this is a good position for desert traffic. Shantay seems to have a nice little money spinner setup, but I reckon, this could turn out even better.

steps.text: At Uzer:

steps.npc: You mightn't realise it, but this is quite a busy station.

steps.player: Who would want to come here?

steps.npc: Well you for one, and besides that we get quite a few archaeologists from the dig site passing through to examine the golem.

steps.text: At the Bedabin Camp:

steps.npc: Well besides the obvious - looking after this station, I'm trying to figure out how these Tentis manage to cultivate such delicious pineapples.

steps.text: At the north Pollnivneach station:

steps.npc: Well Pollnivneach is the ideal location for setting up a carpet station.

steps.player: Why's that?

steps.npc: You see it's located halfway between Al Kharid, and the Menaphite cities and close enough to Nardah too, so we get more than enough traffic to keep the business running.

steps.text: At the south Pollnivneach station:

steps.npc: I work here renting out magic carpets. I'm from Pollnivneach so it is a handy job, I don't have to commute too far to work every day.

steps.player: Why's that?

steps.npc: You see it's located halfway between Al Kharid, and the Menaphite cities and close enough to Nardah too, so we get more than enough traffic to keep the business running.

steps.player: So I suppose you're called Ali then.

steps.npc: Not the most remarkable of names, not that it matters, you see everyone in town knows me as Flash.

steps.player: Really?

steps.npc: No.

steps.player: Oh right.

steps.text: At Nardah:

steps.npc: Well I'd preferred to have been running one of the carpet stations at a hub such as Pollnivneach. I was a bit slow off the mark to get that gig though. Still business in Nardah isn't bad for a terminal. At least
people come here for the bank and to see the herbalist.

steps.text: At Sophanem:

steps.npc: I look after the carpet station here. The place is a bit dead though. Ha! I'm just too much.

steps.player: What?

steps.npc: You know, Sophanem, city of the dead and all that?
Aw come on, the joke wasn't that bad.

steps.text: At Menaphos:

steps.npc: Until recently I was looking after one of the busiest carpet stations. But that all changed since Menaphos closed its gates.
Right now I have to fill my day trying to come up with reasons why Ali M should keep this place open.

steps.player: So have you come up with any good ideas then?

steps.npc: Not really. The only reason I have come up with to date is that by keeping the station open, people become familiar with it.
Maybe once Menaphos opens her gates again, the station will make a fortune once more.

options.text: Is that your pet monkey nearby?

steps.player: Is that your pet monkey nearby?

steps.npc: He's his own monkey, he does whatever suits him, a total nuisance.

steps.player: I detect a degree of hostility being directed towards the monkey.

steps.npc: I shouldn't say this really, but sometimes I begin to question some of Ali Morrisane's ideas, he says that associating a monkey with any product will increase sales. I just don't know, what will be next?

steps.player: Frogs?

steps.npc: I doubt it, amphibians don't have the same cutesy factor as monkeys.

steps.player: I'm confused. I thought you didn't like monkeys.

steps.npc: I don't dislike monkeys, it's just that monkey. I don't know, I might just be paranoid but I think he's... well... evil.

steps.player: Hmmm... Interesting.

steps.text: If the player has a monkeyspeak amulet in their bank:

steps.player: Hang on a minute, I think I have an amulet of monkeyspeak stored somewhere. Perhaps I could get it and see what it has to say for itself.

steps.npc: Would you? It sometimes gives me these stares... ~A visible shiver runs down his back.
I would be really grateful if you could get that monkey off my back.

steps.text: If the player has a monkeyspeak amulet in their inventory:

steps.player: Hang on a second, I have an amulet of monkeyspeak in my bag, perhaps I could have a word with him.

steps.npc: Would you? It sometimes gives me these stares... ~A visible shiver runs down his back.
I would be really grateful if you could get that monkey off my back.

options.text: Where did you get that hat?

steps.player: Where did you get that hat?

steps.npc: My fez? I got it from Ali Morrisane, it's a uniform of sorts, apparently it makes us more visible, but I'm not too sure about it.

steps.player: Well it is quite distinctive.

steps.npc: Do you like it? I haven't really made my mind up about it yet. You see it's not all that practical for desert conditions.

steps.player: How so?

steps.npc: Well it doesn't keep the sun out of my eyes and after a while sitting out in the desert they really begin to burn.
Come back anytime.

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.text: Yeah, I do, as a matter of fact!

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.text: I am a poor, dispossessed nobleman, forced by circumstance to lurk in the middle of nowhere, soliciting help from passers-by.

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.text: You see, my fiendish half-brother has seized my estates and forced me into exile.

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.text: The simple lemon farmers suffer under his tyrannous yoke, and only a brave adventurer can lift his iron boot from the neck of the poor.

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.text: To reclaim my lands I will need to have my family sword returned to me so that I may present it as proof of my rulership.

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete.text: Will you help me find my family sword?
If the player has one or more levels less than the requirement:

steps.text: Before starting this quest, be aware that one or more of your skill levels are lower than what is required to fully complete it.

steps.player: Yes! Your uncorroborated sob story has touched my heart. When do we set off?

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: You'll help! Wonderful!

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: But, alas, my half brother has a powerful ally, the mighty demon...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Err...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Err...Barrelor!

steps.player: Barrelor?

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: That's what I said!

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Barrelor is an awesome opponent, and to reclaim my family sword you will need to defeat him, for he guards it within the deadly Trapped Pit of Barrelor.

options.text: Of course, I fear no demon!

steps.player: Of course, I fear no demon!

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Atta [boy/girl]!

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: When I am reinstated in my rightful place, I will not be a very wealthy man, as my half-brother has squandered my family fortune.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: However, I will gladly give you every bent penny of what is left, and starve in the gutter with my many, many adorable children, if you say you will help me.

steps.player: Nonsense! Keep the money! I will dispose of this evil half-brother of yours and leave you what little money is left to feed your family.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Wonderful! Just pick up your diversion and we'll leave!

steps.player: What diversion?

steps.text: Pirate Pete catches the player off guard and knocks them out with a bottle.

steps.player: Ow!

steps.text: (Cutscene 1 begins.)

options.text: Great, I'll take the cash in used coins please.

steps.player: Great, I'll take the cash in used coins please.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Er...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Look, I think I'll wait here for someone a little more... you know...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: ...heroic.

options.text: Not a chance, this sounds too dangerous.

steps.player: Not a chance, this sounds too dangerous.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Look, I think I'll wait here for someone a little more... you know...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: ...heroic.

steps.player: No, I don't think I'll help you out this time.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Look, I think I'll wait here for someone a little more... you know...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: ...heroic.

setting-out-talking-to-pirate-pete-talki.text: If talking to Pirate Pete with having second thoughts after accepting the quest:

steps.player: Had any luck finding someone to slay the demon?

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Oh! Yes! The demon, with the oppression and stuff!

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: No, not yet. Why?

options.text: Because I came to offer to help.

steps.player: Because I came to offer to help.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: That's the spirit!

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: When I am reinstated in my rightful place, I will not be a very wealthy man, as my half-brother has squandered my family fortune.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: However, I will gladly give you every bent penny of what is left, and starve in the gutter with my many adorable children if you say you will help me.

options.text: Great, I'll take the cash in used coins please.

steps.player: No reason. I was just in the area and I thought I would ask.

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: I see...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: Look, I think I'll wait here for someone a little more... you know...

steps.speaker: Pirate Pete
steps.text: ...heroic.

setting-out-cutscene-1.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-cutscene-1.text: I found us a hero down by the docks!

setting-out-cutscene-1.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-cutscene-1.text: Be they heroic, brave and true?

setting-out-cutscene-1.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-cutscene-1.text: Aye! They also be gullible, tied up and unconscious!

setting-out-cutscene-1.speaker: Pirate Pete
setting-out-cutscene-1.text: They were willing to help out some random stranger with a good enough sob story, so I smacked them with a bottle and rowed them over.

setting-out-cutscene-1.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-cutscene-1.text: Brilliant! The island's location will remain a secret!

setting-out-cutscene-1.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-cutscene-1.text: We may make it through this yet...

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Are ye alright, [lad/lass]?

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.player: It feels like someone has smacked me one with a bottle...

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Arr... Those devils gave ye a nasty knock when ye came to aid us.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: But now yer here we'll run those evil brain-eatin' dogs off the island fer good!

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.player: What? What is going on here?
I can't seem to remember anything beyond chatting to a man at the docks.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Arr. Well, [lad/lass], that would be Pete, one of my men.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: He's been out lookin' fer heroes like yerself to aid us in our peril.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.player: Okay... I'll buy that. It sounds like something I would do.
So where am I, and what is going on?

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Yer on Braindeath Island!

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Where it lies is a secret, because ye are standin' in the brewery of Cap'n Braindeath, purveyor of the most vitriolic alcoholic beverages in the world!

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: I am the notorious alchemist Cap'n Braindeath, and this whole operation be my idea!

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: With my crew of sturdy, upright pirate brewers, we sail the seven seas, distributing cheap 'alcohol' to all and sundry.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: These be dark times, though, [lad/lass]. See, a week ago we awoke to find ourselves beseiged.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: The lads and I have held them off so far, but 'tis only a matter of time before they sweep through the buildin' and put us all to the sword.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Them!
Cutscene begins
The captian points out of the window....
Cutscene ends

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Arr, [lad/lass]! That they are!

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Day and night they seek to break our will with their chantin', and their singin' and their passive resistance!

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.player: So, what do you want me to do?

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Well, me and the lads got our heads together and decided that if we can get their Cap'n drunk enough, perhaps they'll stop protestin'.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: If that happens, we'll slip out the back and set up shop somewhere else.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Well, first of all, we need someone to go out the front and grow us some Blindweed.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: 'Tis one of the ingredients of our 'rum'.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: The only problem is that those rottin' fiends have torn up and destroyed all but one of the Blindweed Patches.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Here, [lad/lass]. I'll give ye the seed you'll need fer growin' the herb. Help yerself to the gardenin' equipment in the basement.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: I'll warn ye again that those devils are sat right on top of the patch.

setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.speaker: Captain Braindeath
setting-out-meeting-captain-braindeath.text: Try hecklin' 'em from a distance. Those Swabs may talk a good fight, but if ye can put a scare in 'em they'll keep out of yer way!

options.text: What exactly do you want me to do?

steps.player: What exactly do you want me to do?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Arr, well I want ye to get outside and grow some Blindweed.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Best be careful, [lad/lass], fer them pirates will skin ye alive if they catch ye.
If the player has lost the Blindweed seed:

steps.player: And what happens if I lose the seed?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Then I'll have ye flogged, hung, slapped with a haddock and sent back out there to fight the zombie hordes with little more than harsh language!
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Come back and see me when ye ain't loaded down with stuff, and I'll give ye another.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Arr... Here, [lad/lass]. Just take this and get goin'!
(The player is handed another seed.)

options.text: Why do you talk like a pirate?

steps.player: Why do you talk like a pirate? Didn't you tell me you were an alchemist?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Arr, [lad/lass], 'tis true.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: However, 'tis also true that I stumbled across the basic recipe fer my most potent of brews in a terrible alchemical accident.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: See, 'twas a dark and stormy night, and the wind was howlin' around the trees as I worked late into the night.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Steppin' too close to a candle with my flask in my hand, I was suddenly swept up in a terrible, yet potently alcoholic, explosion.

steps.player: And?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Well' [lad/lass], it seems the fumes from that first batch of me 'rum' did strange things to me brain.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: I don't remember the exact words the healers used, but apparently the stuff burned out the tiny, specialised part of me brain that tells me not to talk like a pirate.

steps.player: That... that... that sounds utterly impossible!

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Arr! That be what I told them!

options.text: So what do you make here anyway?

steps.player: So what do you make here anyway?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: 'Rum', [lad/lass]!

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: The finest, most potent, most flammable and most debilitatin' 'rum' in the whole of Gielinor!

steps.player: Rum, eh?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: No, [lad/lass], 'rum'!

steps.player: What's the difference?

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Well, see, it's like this.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: If we called the stuff we make 'rum' without makin' the little quote gestures every time, then the Cookin' Guild has promised to do entertaininly painful things to us with whisks.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: See, technically -

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: And by that I mean technically according to the Disposal of Hazardous Waste Act and the Health and Safety Laws -

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: technically, what we're brewin' here is Artificially Produced Hyper Condensed Sweetened 'Rum' Flavour Distillate.

steps.player: Riiiiiiiight...

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: So ye see, [lad/lass], we just call it 'rum' because the real name be a bit of a mouthful.

steps.speaker: Captain Braindeath
steps.text: Want a drop?

steps.player: No thanks... I think I'll skip it for now.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-captai.text: Best be careful, lad, fer them pirates will skin ye alive if they catch ye.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-brewer.player: So... how are you holding up?

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-brewer.player: Wow... I always thought pirates were tough...

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.player: Why are you not helping out the others?

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: Well you see, guv, I've got these unshakable religious convictions.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: Well, it's like this, see. I used to do a bit of the old priestin' on the side.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: You know, collectin' for repairs to the church roof, passing the collection plate, jumble sales, nicking the lead off the temple roof so they needed repairing again.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: You are, in fact, what we refer to in layman's terms as a punter.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: But anyway, all that priestin' left me with an unshakable faith in three things.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: The power of good over evil.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: The true glory of the human spirit.

getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.speaker: Davey
getting-your-beer-ings-talking-to-davey.text: And that I ain't goin out there with those things runnin' around.
