before-finishing-pandemonium.npc: Ahoy there, sailor! Can't stop to talk right now, I'm afraid. You'll need to come back later.

before-finishing-pandemonium.text: You need to complete the Pandemonium quest to fully access the Sailing skill.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Ahoy there, sailor, and welcome to the Storm Tempor!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Welcome? This place doesn't look very welcoming to me.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: What do you mean? We've got the fresh sea breeze, the spray of the ocean water, a supply of the finest rum around, and one of the fiercest storms in Gielinor to contend with.
What's not to love?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Yeah, it's contending with that storm that worries me.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Aye, it's true that the storm's bested many a sailor around these parts. Still, that's what makes things so exciting! We Barracudas live for the rush, and we trust that our skills will save us from a trip to the locker.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: But why? Could you not just take the safer route around the storm?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Well, you see, there's value in sailors with skills like ours. Most common folk would think like you and avoid the storm, but that takes time, and as them merchants say, 'time is money.'
But that's where we come in! Those merchant folk sail up to the south end of the storm, drop off their shipments to one of our boats down there and we make sure it gets up to the Pandemonium!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. That does make sense, but what's in it for you guys?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Why, the thrill of the sport! Sailing isn't just about going places, it's about mastery of the boat, the pull of the sails, the feeling of the helm in your hand and the taste of rum in your mouth!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Sailing as a sport? How does that work? What are the rules?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Fancy getting involved, do you? Well, we Barracudas have trials set up all across the sea where you can test your mettle against the clock. I'm in charge of this here trial, the Tempor Tantrum.
The objective of this trial is to collect rum shipments and bring them here. To do so, work your way around Tempoross Cove, towards our boat to the south.
While you're out there, keep an eye out for any lost supplies. You'll need to collect all of them to complete the trial.
Sailing over rapids will give you a burst of speed! Try to go over as many as you can. The more rapids you go through in quick succession, the faster you'll go!
The storm isn't going to make it easy for you. Those storm clouds are a nasty piece of work and they'll slow your boat down if they hit you.
Keep a close eye on them. If they are growing in size, that means they are about to strike. However, don't let your guard down once they do, as they always strike twice!
As you make your way around, don't forget your objective. You need to keep picking up lost supplies on route to our southern boat.
Once you reach the boat, collect a shipment of rum from it and then make your way back here.
Make sure you come back the opposite side of Tempoross Cove to the way you went, otherwise you're going to end up missing some lost supplies.
If you can deliver all the rum shipments and collect all the lost supplies in the time given, you'll be awarded a Barracuda rank!
Each trial has three ranks: Swordfish, Shark or Marlin. Each rank is harder than the last.
For this trial, you'll be asked to fetch additional rum shipments and collect even more lost supplies as the rank increases.
You can't attempt the next rank until you beat the one before it. You can also try unranked if you'd like to warm up beforehand.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If below 30 sailing

steps.npc: That said, with your Sailing experience I'd suggest sailing elsewhere for now and coming back when you've learned a thing or two.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If 30+ sailing

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Sure do, sailor!
First up, you're going to need a boat with at least an oak mast built in order to withstand the storm. Your boat's as good as a goner without that.
Second, your boat will also need to have at least an iron helm to withstand the rapids, but provided you can withstand them, they'll provide a burst of speed to your boat.
Third, avoid them lightning clouds! Even with a strong mast they'll still slow you down.
Fourth, keep your sails trimmed to gain even more speed. This aint no shipwreck salvaging. Go fast or go home!
Finally, watch out for those rocks. Hitting them will kill all of your boats momentum immediately.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Thanks for the advice. I'll bear that in mind.

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Tempor Tantrum?

steps.npc: Well, you see, there's value in sailors with skills like ours. Most common folk would avoid the storm, but that takes time, and as them merchants say, 'time is money.'
That's where we come in! Those merchant folk sail up to the south end of the storm, drop off their shipments to one of our boats down there and we make sure it gets up to the Pandemonium!

steps.player: And what do I need to do during the trial?

steps.npc: The objective of this trial is to collect rum shipments and bring them here. To do so, work your way around Tempoross Cove, towards our boat to the south.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: The name's Ralph, Rum-Dashed Ralph. I'm a trial master for the Barracudas and I've been tasked with overseeing our operation over here by Storm Tempor.

steps.player: Are there any benefits to being a trial master?

steps.npc: Plenty! Nothing brings a smile to my face quite like seeing a young budding sailor work at their skills and prove themselves capable of overcoming the storm.
Not to mention, the free rum recovered while doing the trial doesn't go amiss either!

steps.player: What about those that fail?

steps.npc: I wish them a safe journey to the locker.

steps.player: Who are the Barracudas?

steps.npc: We're only the fastest, most competent, most skilled and good looking sailors to sail the seas! Our motto is 'Anyone from anywhere as long as they can sail.'
Our goal is to work together and teach anyone willing the skills required to be a master sailor capable of overcoming anything.

steps.player: Can I become a Barracuda?

steps.npc: Haha! That's the spirit! Of course you can, but only once you prove yourself in our trials. There's a bunch of trial masters like me scattered across the seas. Best our trials and earn your spot in our ranks.

steps.player: I'd best be off.

subsequent-dialogue.npc: Ahoy there, sailor, and welcome to the Storm Tempor!

options.text: I'd like to attempt the Tempor Tantrum.
Can you tell me about the Tempor Tantrum?
Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

steps.player: Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

steps.npc: Sure do, sailor!
First up, you're going to need a boat with at least an oak mast built in order to withstand the storm. Your boat's as good as a goner without that.
Second, your boat will also need to have at least an iron helm to withstand the rapids, but provided you can withstand them, they'll provide a burst of speed to your boat.
Third, avoid them lightning clouds! Even with a strong mast they'll still slow you down.
Fourth, keep your sails trimmed to gain even more speed. This aint no shipwreck salvaging. Go fast or go home!
Finally, watch out for those rocks. Hitting them will kill all of your boats momentum immediately.

steps.player: Thanks for the advice. I'll bear that in mind.

steps.player: Do I have any rewards to claim?

Rum-dashed Ralph hands you a trial reward: Barrel stand.
If the player lost Ralph's fabric roll:
Rum-dashed Ralph hands you a trial reward: Ralph's fabric roll.

steps.npc: That's everything I have for you. Good luck in future trials!

steps.text: Upon reaching Shark rank at the Tempor Tantrum for the first time:

steps.npc: Woah, look at you go out there! You really surprised me with your mastery! A shark rank well earned.

steps.player: Thanks! I wasn't sure I was going to make it in time.

steps.npc: It's not often I see a sailor come through here with such promise. Here, I'll treat you to a drink on me. My speciality, the whirlpool surprise!
It's made from rum, fresh bananas, more rum, some sugar cane, and here's the surprise... even more rum!

steps.text: Ralph hands you two glasses of alcohol from below the deck of his boat.

steps.npc: If you fancy some more, have a word with Steve Beanie over at the Pandemonium. I'll send word to let you have access to his premium selection, for a price of course.

steps.player: Thanks! Do I have any more rewards to claim?

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.text: Welcome adventurer, to the world renowned Wizards' Tower, home to the Order of Wizards. We are the oldest and most prestigious group of wizards around. Now, how may I help you?

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.text: Sedridor? What is it you want with him?

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.player: The Duke of Lumbridge sent me to find him. I have this talisman he found. He said Sedridor would be interested in it.

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-archm.text: Did he now? Well hand it over then, and we'll see what all the hubbub is about.

steps.player: Okay, here you are.

steps.text: If the player has the talisman:
You hand the talisman to Sedridor.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Hmm... Doesn't seem to be anything too special. Just a normal air talisman by the looks of things. Still, looks can be deceiving. Let me take a closer look...
Sedridor murmurs some sort of incantation and the talisman glows slightly.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: How interesting... It would appear I spoke too soon. There's more to this talisman than meets the eye. In fact, it may well be the last piece of the puzzle.

steps.player: Puzzle?

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Indeed! The lost legacy of the first tower. This talisman may in fact be key to finding the forgotten essence mine!

steps.player: First tower? Forgotten essence mine? What are you on about?

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Ah, my apologies, adventurer. Allow me to fill you in.

steps.player: Go ahead.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: As you are likely aware, when we cast spells, we do so using the power of runes.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: These runes are crafted from a highly unique material, and then imbued with magical power from various runic altars. Different altars create different runes with different magical effects.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: The process of imbuing runes is called runecrafting. Legend has it that this was once a common art, but the secrets of how to do it were lost until just under two hundred years ago.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: The rediscovery of runecrafting had such a large impact on the world, that it marked the dawn of the Fifth Age. It also resulted in the birth of our order, and the construction of the first Wizards' Tower.

steps.player: If it was the first tower, I'm guessing it doesn't exist anymore? What happened?

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: It was burnt down by traitorous members of our own order. They followed the evil god of chaos, Zamorak, and they wished to claim our magical discoveries in his name.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: When the tower burnt down, much was lost, including an important incantation. A spell that could be used to teleport to a hidden essence mine.

steps.player: The essence mine you mentioned earlier, I assume?

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Precisely. Rune essence is the material used to make runes, but it is incredibly rare. That essence mine was the only place it could be found that our order knew of.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Since the incantation was lost, we have struggled to maintain our stocks of rune essence.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: There are seemingly those out there that still know where to find some, but while they have been willing to sell essence to us, they have refused to share knowledge on how to find it ourselves.

steps.player: I'm starting to see why this is so important. So you think this talisman can help you rediscover that incantation?

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: I do! All magic leaves traces, and from what I can tell, this talisman was used heavily during the time of the first tower.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: It would have been taken to the essence mine many times, and the magical energies there will have left an imprint on it. To think that it was hidden in Lumbridge all this time!

steps.player: So what happens now?

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: It is critical I share this discovery with my associate, Aubury, as soon as possible. He's not much of a wizard, but he's an expert on runecrafting, and his insight will be essential.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Would you be willing to visit him for me? I would go myself, but I wish to study this talisman some more.

steps.player: Yes, certainly.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: He runs a rune shop in the south east of Varrock. Please, take this package of research notes to him. If all goes well, the secrets of the essence mine may soon be ours once more!
Sedridor hands you a package.

steps.speaker: Archmage Sedridor
steps.text: Best of luck, [player name].

steps.text: Well, it is a long story from the past... Many years ago, this Wizards' Tower was a focus of great learning, as we mages studied together to try and learn the secrets behind

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: the Rune Stones that allow us to use Magic. Who makes them? Where do they come from? How many types are there? What spells can they produce? All these questions and more are still unknown to us,

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: but were once known to our ancestors. Legends tell us that in the past the mages who lived here could fashion Rune Stones almost at will, and as many as they desired.

steps.player: But they cannot anymore?

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: No, unfortunately not. Many years past, the Wizards who follow Zamorak, the god of chaos, burned this Tower to the ground, and all who were inside.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: To this day we do not fully know why they did this terrible act, but all our research, all of our greatest magical minds were destroyed in one fell swoop.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: This is why I spend my time searching through these few remains we have left from the glorious old Tower. I hope someday to find something that will tell us once more of the mysteries of

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: the runes that we use daily, which dwindle in supply with each use. Someday I hope we may once more create our own runes, and the Wizards' Tower will once more be a place of glory!

steps.player: Ok, well I'll leave you to it.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Perhaps I will see you later [player name].

steps.player: How did you know my name???

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Well, I AM the head wizard here...

options.text: I'm looking for the head wizard.

steps.player: I'm looking for the head wizard.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Oh, you are, are you? And just why would you be doing that?

steps.player: The Duke of Lumbridge sent me to find him. I have this weird talisman he found. He said the head wizard would be very interested in it.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Did he now? HmmmMMMMMmmmmm. Well that IS interesting. Hand it over then adventurer, let me see what all the hubbub about it is. Just some amulet I'll wager.

steps.player: Ok, here you are.

steps.text: If the player has the talisman:
You hand the talisman to Sedridor.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Wow! This is... incredible!

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Th-this talisman you brought me...! It is the last piece of the puzzle, I think! Finally! The legacy of our ancestors... it will return to us once more!

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: I need time to study this, [player name]. Can you please do me this task while I study this talisman you have brought me? In the mighty town of Varrock, which

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: is located North East of here, there is a certain shop that sells magical runes. I have in this package all of the research I have done relating to the Rune Stones, and

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: require somebody to take them to the shopkeeper so that he may share my research and offer me his insights. Do this thing for me, and bring back what he gives you,

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: and if my suspicions are correct, I will let you into the knowledge of one of the greatest secrets this world has ever known! A secret so powerful that it destroyed the

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: original Wizards' Tower all of those centuries ago! My research, combined with this mysterious talisman... I cannot believe the answer to the mysteries is so close now!

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Do this thing for me [player name]. Be rewarded in a way you can never imagine.

steps.player: Yes, certainly.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Take this package, and head directly North from here, through Draynor village, until you reach the Barbarian Village. Then head East from there until you reach Varrock.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Once in Varrock, take this package to the owner of the rune shop. His name is Aubury. You may find it helpful to ask one of Varrock's citizens for directions,

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: as Varrock can be a confusing place for the first time visitor. He will give you a special item - bring it back to me, and I shall show you the mystery of the runes...
The wizard gives you a package.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Best of luck with your quest, [player name].

steps.player: No, I'm busy.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: As you wish adventurer. I will continue to study this talisman you have brought me. Return here if you find yourself with some spare time to help me.
If the player doesn't have the talisman:

steps.player: ...except I don't have it with me...

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Hmmm? You are a very odd person. Come back again when you have found it.

options.text: No, I'll only give it to the head wizard.

steps.player: No, I'll only give it to the head wizard.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: HA HA HA HA HA! I can tell you are new to this land, for I AM the head wizard! Hand it over and let me have a proper look at it, hmmm?

options.text: No, I don't think you are the head wizard.

steps.player: No, I don't think you are the head wizard.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Hmmm. Well, I admire your caution adventurer, perhaps I can prove myself? I will use my mental powers to discover...

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Your name is... [player name]!

steps.player: You're right!

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Well I am head wizard you know! You don't get to my position without learning a few tricks along the way!

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: So now I have proved myself to you why don't you hand over that talisman, hmm?

steps.player: Ok, here you are.

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-sedri.speaker: Sedridor
delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-sedri.text: Welcome adventurer, to the world renowned Wizards' Tower. How may I help you?

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-sedri.speaker: Sedridor
delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-sedri.text: Ah, [player name]. How goes your quest? Have you delivered the research notes to my friend Aubury yet?
If the player lost the package:

steps.player: ...I lost the package you gave me.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: You WHAT?

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Tch, that was really very careless of you. Luckily as head wizard I have great powers, and will be able to teleport it back here without too much effort.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Ok, I have retrieved it. Luckily it doesn't appear to have been damaged. Now please take it to Aubury, and try not to lose it again.
The wizard gives you a package.

delivering-the-talisman-talking-to-sedri.text: If the player has the package:

steps.player: Not yet...

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Well, please do so as soon as possible. Remember: to get to Varrock, head due North, through Draynor Village, around Draynor Manor, and then head East when

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: you get to the Barbarian village. The man you seek is named Aubury, and he owns the rune shop there. It is vital he receives this package.

delivering-the-research-package-talking-.speaker: Aubury
delivering-the-research-package-talking-.text: Do you want to buy some runes?

options.text: Oh, it's a rune shop. No thank you, then.
I have been sent here with a package for you.

steps.player: I have been sent here with a package for you. It's from the head wizard at the Wizards' Tower.

steps.speaker: Aubury
steps.text: Really? But... surely he can't have..? Please, let me have it, it must be extremely important for him to have sent a stranger.
If the player has the package:
You hand Aubury the research package.

steps.speaker: Aubury
steps.text: This... this is incredible. Please, give me a few moments to quickly look over this, and then talk to me again.
If the player does not have the package:

steps.player: Uh... yeah... about that... I kind of don't have it with me...

steps.speaker: Aubury
steps.text: What kind of person tells me they have a delivery for me, but not with them? Honestly.

steps.speaker: Aubury
steps.text: Come back when you do.

delivering-the-research-package-talking-.speaker: Aubury
delivering-the-research-package-talking-.text: My gratitude to you adventurer for bringing me these research notes. I notice that you brought the head wizard a special talisman that was the key to our finally unlocking the puzzle.

delivering-the-research-package-talking-.speaker: Aubury
delivering-the-research-package-talking-.text: Combined with the information I had already collated regarding the Rune Essence, I think we have finally unlocked the power to

delivering-the-research-package-talking-.speaker: Aubury
delivering-the-research-package-talking-.text: ...no. I am getting ahead of myself. Please take this summary of my research back to the head wizard at the Wizards' Tower. I trust his judgement on whether to let you in on our little secret or not.
Aubury gives you his research notes.

delivering-the-research-package-talking-.speaker: Aubury
delivering-the-research-package-talking-.text: I suggest you take those research notes of mine back to the head wizard at the Wizards' Tower.
If the player lost the notes:

steps.player: I can't... I lost them...

steps.speaker: Aubury
steps.text: Well, luckily I have duplicates. It's a good thing they are written in code, I would not want the wrong kind of person to get access to the information contained within.
Aubury gives you his research notes.

delivering-the-research-package-talking-.text: If the player has the notes:

steps.player: Ok then, I will do that.

steps.speaker: Aubury
steps.text: Unless you were talking to me because you wished to buy some runes?

options.text: Oh, it's a rune shop. No thank you, then.

delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.speaker: Sedridor
delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.text: Welcome adventurer, to the world renowned Wizards' Tower. How may I help you?

delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.speaker: Sedridor
delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.text: Ah, [player name]. How goes your quest? Have you delivered the research notes to my friend Aubury yet?

delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.player: Yes, I have. He gave me some research notes to pass on to you.

delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.speaker: Sedridor
delivering-the-research-notes-talking-to.text: May I have his notes then?
If the player has the notes:

steps.text: You hand the notes to Sedridor.

steps.player: Sure. I have them here.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Well, before you hand them over to me, as you have been nothing but truthful with me to this point, and I admire that in an adventurer, I will let you into the secret of our research.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Now as you may or may not know, many centuries ago, the wizards at this Tower learnt the secret of creating Rune Stones, which allowed us to cast Magic very easily.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: When this Tower was burnt down the secret of creating runes was lost to us for all time... except it wasn't. Some months ago, while searching these ruins for information from the old days,

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: I came upon a scroll, almost destroyed, that detailed a magical rock deep in the icefields of the North, closed off from access by anything other than magical means.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: This rock was called the 'Rune Essence' by the magicians who studied its powers. Apparently, by simply breaking a chunk from it, a Rune Stone could be fashioned very quickly and easily at certain

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: elemental altars that were scattered across the land back then. Now, this is an interesting little piece of history, but not much use to us as modern wizards without access to the Rune Essence,

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: or these elemental altars. This is where you and Aubury come into this story. A few weeks back, Aubury discovered in a standard delivery of runes to his store, a parchment detailing a

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: teleportation spell that he had never come across before. To his shock, when cast it took him to a strange rock he had never encountered before... yet that felt strangely familiar...

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: As I'm sure you have now guessed, he had discovered a portal leading to the mythical Rune Essence. As soon as he told me of this spell, I saw the importance of his find,

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: for if we could but find the elemental altars spoken of in the ancient texts, we would once more be able to create runes as our ancestors had done! It would be the saviour of the wizards' art!

steps.player: I'm still not sure how I fit into this little story of yours...

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: You haven't guessed? This talisman you brought me... it is the key to the elemental altar of air! When you hold it next, it will direct you towards

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: the entrance to the long forgotten Air Altar! By bringing pieces of the Rune Essence to the Air Temple, you will be able to fashion your own Air Runes!

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: And this is not all! By finding other talismans similar to this one, you will eventually be able to craft every rune that is available on this world! Just

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: as our ancestors did! I cannot stress enough what a find this is! Now, due to the risks involved of letting this mighty power fall into the wrong hands

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: I will keep the teleport skill to the Rune Essence a closely guarded secret, shared only by myself and those Magic users around the world whom I trust enough to keep it.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: This means that if any evil power should discover the talismans required to enter the elemental temples, we will be able to prevent their access to the Rune Essence and prevent

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: tragedy befalling this world. I know not where the temples are located, nor do I know where the talismans have been scattered to in this land, but I now

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: return your Air Talisman to you. Find the Air Temple, and you will be able to charge your Rune Essences to become Air Runes at will. Any time

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: you wish to visit the Rune Essence, speak to me or Aubury and we will open a portal to that mystical place for you to visit.

steps.player: So only you and Aubury know the teleport spell to the Rune Essence?

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: No... there are others... whom I will tell of your authorisation to visit that place. When you speak to them, they will know you, and grant you access to that place when asked.

steps.speaker: Sedridor
steps.text: Use the Air Talisman to locate the air temple, and use any further talismans you find to locate the other missing elemental temples. Now... my research notes please?
You hand the head wizard the research notes.He hands you back the Air Talisman.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

steps.speaker: Sedridor

standard-dialogue.npc: Good day, your Royal Highness.

steps.npc: Oh, leave an old dwarf in peace will you?

steps.player: Why, what's wrong?

steps.npc: Ninenty years down in the mines, and this is all I got out of it. All my life wasted away.

steps.player: You've still got a nice house, don't you?

steps.npc: A crummy old house in East, that's all my life amounts to.

steps.player: I'll leave you alone then.

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: I say! Where on Gielinor did that voice come from?

before-grim-tales.player: Uh...hello there! Can you hear me?

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Why yes. Yes I can. My word. Is that...is that one of the gods? Guthix perhaps? Saradomin?

before-grim-tales.player: No, no. I'm not either of them.

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Egad! You're not...Zamorak...are you? I mean, uh...begging your pardon of course, my Lord. No offence intended!

before-grim-tales.player: Ha ha! No, I'm speaking to you through the pipe here! I'm at the bottom of your tower.

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Oh. Oh I see! Oh, yes. How clever! Remarkable idea! How ever did you think of that? Good show, old bean!

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Rupert the Beard. At your service, old fruit.

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Yes, old turnip. On account of my wonderfully long bearded chin, you see.

before-grim-tales.player: So what are you doing up there exactly? And how come you talk so strangely?

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: What am I doing? Well, I guess I'm stuck in a matter of speaking. Dear me, yes! I'm stuck. And I speak in the King's speech, I'll have you know.

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Which K...? Why, THE King old spud! THE King! Only one worth mentioning in my opinion.

before-grim-tales.player: Hey, you're not related to Sir Tiffy by any chance are you?

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: What? That namby pamby nincompoop? Not on your nelly! More fluff in the ears than sense, that man!

before-grim-tales.player: I see. Well is there anything I can do to help you up there?

before-grim-tales.speaker: Drain pipe
before-grim-tales.text: Hmmm. No, no, I can't think of anything at the moment. I'm a bit stuck. Let me know if you get any ideas though.

after-grim-tales.npc: Hello again, old cheesecake! Wonderful to see you.

steps.player: How are the investigations going?

steps.npc: Thanks to you freeing me, very well! I have much more to do of course, but now I am free, I can continue where I left off.

steps.player: That's great news!

options.text: Have you another helmet like the one you gave me?

steps.player: Have you another helmet like the one you gave me?

steps.npc: You might be in luck, old bellybutton fluff - I have made replacements. You could have one for 60,000 coins - for the materials, you understand.

steps.text: If the player has less than 60,000 coins:

steps.player: I don't think I can afford that, sorry.

steps.npc: No problem! Come back and see me any time, old garters.

options.text: I don't think I can afford that, sorry.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hiya. Are you carrying anything valuable?
Um... It's a quiz. I'm asking everyone I meet if they're carrying anything valuable.

standard-dialogue.player: What would you do if I said I had loads of expensive items with me?

standard-dialogue.npc: Ooh, do you? It's been ages since anyone said they'd got anything worth stealing.
Um... Not that I'd dream of stealing anything!

standard-dialogue.player: Well, I'll say I'm not carrying anything valuable at all.

standard-dialogue.npc: Oh, what a shame.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Safalaan.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: It's strange, this place. From the plants, to the creatures... even the land itself. It's all undeniably horrifying, and yet... there's a certain feeling of peace here.
I wonder if it's the simplicity. There are no politics here. No debates. You don't need to care about good or evil, because there isn't any. Here you can just... be.
Or of course, maybe that's just the monster within me talking.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: You're no monster, Safalaan.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Are you sure? How do you know I'm not about to try and eat you right now?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Er... You are joking right?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Probably... Or am I? Hard to say for sure... You never know when the urge to feed will take hold...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Safalaan!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Come on, [player name], look at me. Even other vampyres consider me an abomination... At least let me find some humour in all of this.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: hmph* Like you'd be able to eat me anyway. You do remember that I'm the one that finally killed Drakan, right?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: In truth, I can still barely believe it. All those years fighting him, and now it's finally all over... It almost doesn't feel real.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Well, you were a bit out of it for a fair chunk.
Oh, so the humour is only okay when you do it?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Just seems a bit unfair to kick me while I'm down... Maybe I should eat you...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: It's good to see you haven't changed, Safalaan.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: And for as long as I have friends like you, [player name], I hope I never will. Thank you... truly.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Like I told you, Safalaan, we're in this together. Anyway, I'll leave you to it, but we'll talk more soon.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Until next time, [player name].

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: [player name]. I must admit, things are very tiring at the moment. Even with help from mother, controlling this... condition takes a lot of work.
That's before we even get onto the work I've been doing to help Sugadinti with the blood shortages.
As a wyrd, I hunger far more than a normal vampyre. It... disgusts me, to be honest. However, it does mean I am a perfect test subject for Sugadinti.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.player: You're not doing too much, are you?

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: Perhaps, but I'd prefer to be useful. I find it easier, keeping myself busy. It helps me deal with things. Helps me come to terms with who I am now.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.player: Fair enough. You just make sure to let me know if anything gets too much.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: Oh I will. As you yourself reminded me, it would be unwise to get on the bad side of the one who finally killed Drakan.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.player: Shame I didn't do the same to his sister. If I had, you'd never have been in this position.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: Perhaps, or perhaps we'd just all be dead instead. Besides, Vanescula has already been well and truly punished for what she did.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.player: Not too eager to forgive her, are you?

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: Forgive her? Never. But with her in her state and me in mine, she'll fear me for the rest of her days.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.player: I suppose there is some justice in that.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-times.npc: Indeed. Now, you'll have to forgive me, [player name], but I believe Sugadinti will have need of me soon. I'll see you later.

If the player does not have the required materials:

steps.text: If the player has the required materials:
If the player does not have the required materials:

steps.player: Why do you need gems?

steps.npc: They're tougher than just metal on its own, plus it's the only such resource naturally available in this region.

options.text: Why do you need a gout plant tuber?

steps.player: Why do you need a gout plant tuber?

steps.npc: It's one of the harder to find resources which I mix with other ingredients in order to bind the ground down gem dust to the surface of the metal bladed machete.
You can sometimes, if you're lucky, find the plant if you hack away at the jungle around here. You'll need to find a way to dig up the tubers though, they're the important part of the plant.

steps.player: Why is it so expensive?

steps.npc: Expensive bwana, it's quite reasonably priced if you ask me. I can make it cheaper than Gabooty charges for it, that's for sure. And after all, I have to earn a living around here as well you know, I have children to feed!

options.text: Let me see the machetes again.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

options.text: No thanks, but I'd like to ask another question.
No thanks, I have to go.

steps.player: No thanks, I have to go.

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.player: Is there anything interesting to do around here?

steps.npc: Not that I'm aware of, just sit back and enjoy the sunshine bwana!
Bwana, if anyone else asks me that question today, I'll explode! Go and ask someone else!
It's just village life as normal around here Bwana, always something interesting to find to occupy your time if you look hard enough.
Sorry Bwana, I'm already busy, why not go and talk to Murcaily! He's around the village somewhere.
Well, I think that there's some work to be done...perhaps Murcaily can help you. He usually tends to the hardwood grove to the east of Trufitus's hut.

steps.npc: I yearn for the Sage to defy master Yama, I shall feast on their broken body!
HAHAHAHAHA! What sweet meats there are to be torn from them!
Oh the energies I will devour...

steps.player: Woah there, clearly you didn't have anything for breakfast today.

steps.npc: I am much more ferocious when I am hungry.

steps.player: Hey, me too!

steps.npc: Don't make me laugh. You are puny, barely a morsel.

steps.player: I wasn't planning on it. I can't reach up there anyway.

steps.npc: An answer for everything. Typical human.

steps.npc: You are far from many things in this place. Watch your tongue.

steps.player: I'm going to speak to the Sage now since you're intent on being rude.

steps.npc: I don't care what you do as long as you do not interfere. Proceed.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Hi, can I help you with something?

steps.player: You're not from around here are you?

steps.npc: Why do you say that?

steps.player: Well your accent for one sounds a little funny, and you seem to have a little more colour than most dwarves.

steps.npc: Living under a mountain isn't the best way to get a tan. No I'm not from around here. I was born and worked most my life in the desert.
Just even thinking of the place makes me thirsty. Now can I help you with anything?

steps.player: So how do these rat pits work?

steps.npc: The Keldagrim pits cater for those with the larger variety of cats.
If you have an overgrown cat and a couple of coins you can challenge someone else who also has an overgrown cat and some spare change.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 9 rats first wins.

steps.player: That sounds vile and cruel.

steps.npc: It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Each to their own, I say.

steps.player: Thanks for your help.

options.text: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.player: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.npc: I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.

steps.player: Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?

steps.npc: Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.

steps.player: Oh that sounds quite wise.

steps.npc: That depends on how you value your cat.

steps.player: Sorry, I don't follow.

steps.npc: Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.

steps.player: Wow that sounds like fun!

steps.npc: I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.

options.text: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.player: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.npc: Hmmm... let me think. I don't think that's ever arisen but I think it's 20,000.

steps.player: Hmm, that sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.

steps.npc: You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.
There is a minimum bet of 100 coins too.

options.text: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.npc: No, not now, we don't really bet with outsiders.

steps.player: But I'm not an outsider, am I not inside in the pits now?

steps.npc: I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.

steps.player: Can it be bought?

steps.npc: What?

steps.player: Your trust.

steps.npc: No. Regular townsfolk don't like us, which leads us to distrust them and anyone else.

options.text: How do I play board games?

steps.player: How do I play board games?

steps.npc: You can challenge someone to a game anywhere in the Games Zone (except on a PvP or Deadman world) by using the right click option.
Choose the type of game and then choose the options you want such as time per move.
If your opponent accepts the challenge you will be taken to one of the tables around where you will play your game of choice.
Once you have finished your game you will come back here where you can challenge again! We also have tables in a few pubs around the world!

steps.player: What games can I play?

steps.npc: Currently we offer Draughts, Runelink, Runesquares, and Runeversi.

steps.player: Draughts?

steps.npc: Draughts uses standard rules, apart from: a draw is declared if no piece has been taken or promoted for forty moves.

steps.player: Runelink?

steps.npc: Yup, you have to get four runes in row.

steps.player: Runesquares?

steps.npc: Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn.

steps.player: Runeversi?

steps.npc: Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own.

from everyone else. They're very useful when out in the wilderness with friends or anyone else you don't want to harm.

steps.text: The player is teleported into the Trouble Brewing waiting room.

options.text: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.player: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.npc: Well, well, looks like someone is fresh off the boat and no mistake!
A little while ago we had some real problem shipping 'rum' in the island. The Braindeath crew said it had something to do with zombies and the like.
All the pirates on the island got together and decided to make our own still, but of course things got a little out of hand, and now we have two.

steps.player: So with two stills you have plenty of 'rum' right?

steps.npc: Well we would do, if that scurvy, whelk-eating foppish dog wouldn't keep trying to burn our still to the ground!

steps.player: I say!

steps.npc: Neither of us can really corner the 'rum' market at the moment, but we are giving it our best shot.
The code of the island says that we can't attack each other, but after consulting with our fearsome pirate lawyers, we have discovered that destroying each other's property is fine.
Hence, that sniveling, hat-wearing cur keeps trying to burn down my still.
Of course he claims I started this whole thing, but who would trust him anyway?

steps.player: Can I help out?

steps.npc: Yes, probably. I have a bunch of jobs that need doing, if you feel up to it.
What would you like to know about?

steps.player: How do I help you brew 'Rum'?

steps.npc: Well the stills we have set up are based on the ones on Braindeath island... well roughly at any rate.
All you have to do is help put the ingredients into the hoppers and keep the boilers burning.
If you add enough ingredients to the hoppers then you have the ability to pick up a single bottle of rum when it brews.

So, if ye add 5 buckets of water to the hoppers, then ye get access to one bottle. If you add 3 bowls of coloured water you get access to one bottle, and if you add one of anything else you get access to one bottle.
This is cumulative, meaning that if you add (for example) 10 buckets of water, 3 sweetgrubs and 6 bowls of coloured water, then you have a chance to collect 7 bottles of rum for the team.
The boilers are easy as pie to sort out. You just put some logs in, light them with a tinderbox, and then keep putting logs in until they are good and hot.
Three logs should do it, but it's best to keep heaping them in just in case.
The ingredients are; Bitternuts, Scrapey Tree Bark, Sweetgrubs, Buckets of Water and some Coloured Water.

steps.player: Where can I get Bitternuts?

steps.npc: There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.

steps.player: Send it up the tree? How does that work?

steps.npc: Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.

steps.player: Wait a second, dye?

steps.npc: Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs too.

steps.player: That makes sense...I think...

steps.npc: Anything else?

options.text: Where can I get Scrapey Tree Bark?

steps.player: Where can I get Scrapey tree bark...and why do I get the feeling I won't like the answer?

steps.npc: Inside this walled area there are a few Scrapey trees. They are the big, ill looking ones, you can't miss them.
Basically, you cut them down and then carve the bark off with a knife.
It's pretty simple, except the sap tends so make people feel kind off ill if they get any on themselves.

steps.player: How ill?

steps.npc: Don't worry, we aren't talking deadly ill or anything.
It's more like you'll feel quite dizzy and weak for a bit.

steps.player: Joy...

steps.npc: Anything else?

steps.player: Sweetgrubs? What are they?

steps.npc: Well, lacking any sluglings in the area, we add these little grubs called Sweetgrubs. If you ignore the gag- inducing aftertaste, they are quite sweet.

steps.player: How... how can you drink this stuff?

steps.npc: Quite easily!
Pirates are renowned as being tough for a reason.

steps.player: So where do I get these grubs from anyway?

steps.npc: Well, there are a few sweetgrub mounds inside there. We have a handful of rat meat that you can use on the mounds to draw the grubs to the surface.
Mind your fingers though, they are voracious little things.

steps.player: And here was me thinking that nothing could be more disgusting than Braindeath 'Rum'.

steps.npc: There are a few lying about. Help yourself.

options.text: Where can I get coloured water?

steps.player: What sort of coloured water are we talking about here?

steps.npc: Well, the other still has an area of waste ground with a flower growing on it. If you go and grab one of the flowers and jam it in the kettle, the water will boil out the colour.
We use the colour to keep our rum easily identifiable.

steps.player: So I just empty the kettle into the hopper, right?

steps.npc: No, no, you'll need to take an empty bowl and fill it from the kettle.
That way you can use the stuff on a monkey if you need to.

steps.player: Use it on a monkey...of course.

steps.npc: Anything else?

options.text: Can I ask about something else?

steps.player: How do I repair the still?

steps.npc: Well, assuming those scurvy dogs have managed to set any of it on fire, then you'll need to tip a bucket of water on it before you can repair it.
Then, it all comes down to what part of it was damaged.

steps.player: How can I repair hoppers?

steps.npc: Well, assuming that they are not on fire, all you need to do is use the heavy lumber patches. They are big enough to cover most holes.

steps.player: Will I need a hammer?

steps.npc: No, just shove it into place and whack it until it lines up.
Anything else?

options.text: How do I repair Pipes and the pump?

steps.player: How do I repair pipes and the pump?

steps.npc: Well, if you use a pipe section on the damaged part you should be able to replace it easily.

steps.player: Will I need a hammer?

steps.npc: No, likely you'll just need to whack the old one out and slot the new one in with your hands.
Anything else?

steps.player: How do I repair bridges?

steps.npc: Well, we have these handy bridge sections you can use to repair the bridges.
The main problem is, while a still will keep working if a bit of it is only damaged, the bridges are completely out of commission if they are even slightly damaged.

steps.player: Is that going to be a problem? I mean, I can jump across I think.

steps.npc: Don't try that! Our lawyers tell us we aren't covered for injuries sustained while jumping over burned bridges.
Seriously, just keep off the bridges until they are fixed.
Anything else?

options.text: How do I get repair items

steps.player: Where do I get all this stuff anyway?

steps.npc: We have a load of items already on a table inside the still. You can also make new ones if you grab some logs.

steps.player: How does that work?

steps.npc: We have a work table set up in the still. If you use the logs in it you can craft up a handy replacement for part of the still.
Don't worry about them fitting, the things are held together by nails, replacement parts and soot by now.

steps.player: Well...how sanitary...

steps.npc: Anything else?

options.text: Ok, I think I've heard enough

steps.player: Ok, I think I've heard enough.

steps.npc: Fine. Glad I could help.

options.text: Can I ask about something else?

steps.player: So...how would I go about sabotaging the enemy still?

steps.npc: Ok, here's what you need to do.
The wood around here is really dry and flammable, so take one of the torches, light it up, and then go and attack the enemy still with it.

steps.player: That's it?

steps.npc: Most of their still is soaked in 'alcohol' and made from tinder dry wood.
Essentially, if it isn't ours, try using a torch on it and see what happens.

steps.player: Ok, I get you.

steps.npc: Anything else?

steps.player: So what will you give me for helping out?

steps.npc: Hahahaha! What a mercenary attitude! You'll do fine here.
Well, for each bottle that your team produces, I'll give you one piece of eight.
If you manage to set something on fire then I'll toss in another, same for repairing the still.

steps.npc: See Honest Jimmy there? He'll trade you some pretty nice stuff for them.

steps.player: Great!

options.text: Ok, I think I've heard enough

steps.player: Hey there, can you tell me something about this Sanfew Serum, like how do I make it, and what does it do?

steps.npc: Certainly. It was after all, my creation, and mine alone. If anyone should know how to make it, it should be me!

steps.player: Can't fault that logic!

steps.npc: Ok, essentially this potion is a mixture of a cure poison, cure disease and restore stats all rolled into one! Very handy for the adventurers with an eye on conserving inventory space.

steps.player: Ok, I'm sold... How do you make it?

steps.npc: Well, it's very easy really. You take a standard super stat restore potion. Add some ground unicorn horn. Then, add some snake weed from the island of Karamja. Finally, add some nail beast nails. You can
only get these from the area of Morytania, specifically, if you go deep in the Mort Myre swamp.

steps.player: How do you mean, deep into the Mort Myre swamp?

steps.npc: Well, most adventurers avoid the deep Mort Myre swamp, whereas the Paterdomus trek and the Burgh de Rott trek take you through the most interesting areas. These area's often allow the quickest, but potentially
more dangerous routes through Mort Myre. This is where you're likely to encounter a Nail beast.

steps.player: Are they very dangerous?

steps.npc: They can be pretty dangerous. They'll defend for a long time, then attack suddenly and seemingly without warning, landing three viscious attacks at once. This can be pretty lethal. However, the nail beasts themselves
are curiously wounded from the Sanfew Serum itself...very bizzare, that a potion made from their claws should have such a pronounced effect on them.

steps.player: Ok, yes that could work.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you wanted?

steps.player: Whereabouts were you attacked again?

steps.npc: Is there anything else you wanted?

steps.player: You mentioned that Rosie spooked the monster. Who's that?

steps.npc: Oh, that'll be our lady over there by the fire. She's such a good dog, always accompanies me on deliveries.
You can pet her if you like. She's very friendly.
Is there anything else you wanted?

options.text: I think that'll be all for now.

steps.player: I think that'll be all for now.

steps.npc: Excellent! Best of luck to you, I'll be waiting right here with your reward.

steps.player: That monster certainly won't be troubling you from now on.

steps.npc: Oh that's fantastic news! I'm so relie-
Wait, how do I know you're not just saying that to get the bounty?

steps.player: How about this as proof?

steps.text: You pull the foot out of your backpack and show it to Sarah.

steps.npc: Eugh! Yes, that certainly looks about right!

steps.player: Indeed, the smell is... something quite special.

steps.npc: I'll probably just give it to the dog.
I'm glad you made it back. Some strange woman in a hood came asking about the job shortly after you left. I didn't really want her back in here.
Anyway, thank you so much! Here's your reward.

steps.text: Sarah hands you a heavy pouch of 5,000 coins.

steps.player: Perhaps I should speak with Spria and tell her that the monster's been dealt with.

starting-off.text: Yes, yes... In fact, I've been getting rather used to life out here.

starting-off.player: I see... So, who are you, and how did you end up here?

starting-off.speaker: Alan
starting-off.text: Oh, I'm Alan. I was just visiting the area as a tourist, but I ended up straying from the pack a little.

starting-off.player: Do you need a hand getting back to civilization? I could maybe help you out if so.

starting-off.speaker: Alan
starting-off.text: Oh, no thank you. Like I say, I've actually come to quite like it here. Had I never got lost, I might never have met my best friend, Numpty Bumpty.

starting-off.speaker: Alan
starting-off.text: Still, it is nice for us to finally have a guest. In fact, you should stay for a while! I'll prepare a little feast for us all! What do you say?

steps.player: Well, I suppose I can't say no to that.

steps.speaker: Alan
steps.text: Wonderful! Would you mind staying here while I go out and gather the food? I may not have known you long, but I'm sure I can trust you to keep an eye on Wumty Scrumpty over there.

steps.player: Of course!

steps.text: A cutscene starts.

steps.speaker: Alan
steps.text: Right, time for me to get going. Don't worry, Hampty, our new friend here is going to take good care of you while I'm gone. Love you lots. Miss you already.

steps.player: Hello there, egg.

steps.text: The egg falls to the ground.
If the player has the profanity filter enabled:
If the player has the profanity filter disabled:

steps.player: Bollocks.

options.text: I've got something else to do first.

steps.player: I've got something else to do first.

steps.speaker: Alan
steps.text: Okay, I'll wait until you return. Just don't go getting lost out there!

steps.player: Thank you for the offer, but I really must get going... Maybe another time.

steps.player: This isn't good. I'd better head into town and try to find some help.

options.text: Can you heal me? I'm injured.

steps.player: We need to do something!

steps.player: I'm not giving up without at least trying first.

starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.text: Nilsal. What is it you need help with?

starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.player: This might sound a little strange... but Rumpty Bumpty fell off a wall.
He's an egg. I need to get him fixed up.

starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.speaker: Farmer
starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.text: You want to put a broken egg back together again?

starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.speaker: Farmer
starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.text: I don't think I can... but I might know of somebody who could help. You should speak to the local bartender. Her resourcefulness has earned her quite the reputation. Everyone calls her King.

starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.player: King? Okay, I'll try and find her. Thanks!

starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.speaker: King
starting-off-the-great-fall-talking-to-t.text: Welcome, iknami. What can I get you?

steps.player: Are you the king?

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: The king? No, no, you won't be finding anybody like that around these parts!

steps.player: Sorry, what I meant was... are you King?

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: Oh! That's me, yes. What can I do for you?

steps.player: It's about Pumpty Lumpty.

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: Scrumpty Lumpy?

steps.player: Yes, yes, the egg. He fell off a wall.

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: An egg fell off a wall?

steps.player: It was a disaster! He's everywhere! I was told that if anybody could help put him together again, it would be you.

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: Yes, I guess I have managed to gain a bit of a reputation when it comes to situations like this. After all, there's a reason everyone calls me King.

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: Still, putting a broken egg back together again... That does sound like quite the challenge. Unfortunately, I'm afraid I need to stay here and man the bar. However...

steps.player: Yes?

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: I have a plan, but it's going to take all my horses and all my men.

steps.player: What's a horse?

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: I have no idea.

steps.player: Oh... Well, what about these men?

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: They'll be up to the task, but you'll need to rally them up.

steps.player: Okay, where can I find your men?

steps.speaker: King
steps.text: Nezketi should be in the temple just south of here, Kauayotl will most likely be just outside the main entrance into town, and Acatzin is right here in the inn.

steps.player: Thanks! I'll have them gathered in no time.

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.text: I'm very busy, so you'll need to be quick! What do you need?

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.text: Sorry, I don't sell those! Move along!

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.player: I don't want to buy one! I'm here to pick up one that you're repairing.

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.speaker: Blacksmith
all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.text: Okay, yes, I can repair an axe for you. It won't be quick though as I have a lot of other work to get through first.

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.player: The axe is already here. I'm just here to pick it up.

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.speaker: Blacksmith
all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.text: Well, you can't. No repairs are getting done until the whetstone is fixed!

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.player: Well, what's wrong with the whetstone?

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.speaker: Blacksmith
all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.text: Yes, the whetstone! Are you going to get it fixed or are you just going to keep standing around like that?

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.player: Okay... I guess I can try and fix the whetstone.

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.speaker: Blacksmith
all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-the-blacks.text: Too slow! We need to speed things up! Let's come together and fix this whetstone!

steps.speaker: Kauayotl
steps.text: That would be appreciated. I reckon a couple of planks and some nails should be all you need to get it fixed. I'm sure you can find some around here somewhere. Oh, and don't forget your hammer and saw!

options.text: We have bigger problems right now!

steps.player: We have bigger problems right now!

steps.speaker: Kauayotl
steps.text: My friend, I know your plight, but the cart must be sorted before I can do anything else. I'm sorry.

all-the-king-s-men-talking-to-kauayotl-t.speaker: Kauayotl
