reading-the-book.prompt: Start the Shades of Mort'ton quest?

reading-the-book-curing-ulsquire.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
reading-the-book-curing-ulsquire.text: Ah, excellent, you've made your own serum and it seems to work well! Many thanks for using the Serum on me! But beware, I may start to change back soon!

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: My name is Ulsquire Shauncy, I'm the local teacher and priest around here. You've really come at a time when  Mort'ton is in a terrible state.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The emanations from the rest of Morytania affect the people here terribly turning them into mindless creatures. And, as if that wasn't enough, we get picked off by the evil Shades that exist in this area.

steps.player: Wow, you guys seem to be really at the bottom of the food chain around here.
What is this place?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: This sad and afflicted little town is called 'Mort'ton'. In it's heyday it was a busy and bustling market town with a speciality for interring the dead.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The vile emanations from the Sanguinesti area started to spread and the town hasn't been the same since. The serum you made was the one that Herbi Flax was working on. Unfortunately the serum isn't permanent.

steps.player: Do you know how I could make the serum permanent?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I remember Herbi Flax talking about the serum. He said it worked on what he called the 'biological' effects of the affliction but that some other secondary effect was at work which he didn't quite understand.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: He was interested in 'Flaemtaer', the ruined temple to the North. I found this odd. A man of science studying a structure dedicated to faith and the struggle of good verus evil, another concept he didn't understand.

steps.player: What's going on around here?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The people are affected by the emanations from  the rest of Morytania and the dead from the tombs  have manifested into shadow creatures.

options.text: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.player: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: They are the disturbed spirits of those interred in the earth beneath Mort'ton. Their eternal spirits have been poisoned by the close vicinity to the evil nature of the inhabitants of the Sanguinesti area.

options.text: Is there anyone else worth talking to around here?

steps.player: Is there anyone else worth talking to around here?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Well, there's my good friend Razmire Keelgan. He's a prominent shop owner in Mort'ton, at least he was before he was affected by the area.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I know he tried to gather the militia together to fight the shades. He might know something about the temple. Razmire lives in the building to the west just over there, go and talk to him.

reading-the-book-curing-ulsquire-talking.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
reading-the-book-curing-ulsquire-talking.text: Ah, hello again, what can I do for you now?

options.text: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: My name is Razmire Keelgan, I run a couple of shops in Mort'ton but don't get much custom these days.

steps.player: Which stores do you run?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: I run a general store with a few useful items, and I have a building supplies store, I'm hoping that when things get better down here, people will want to buy items to repair their buildings.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: This place is called Mort'ton, it used to be a quiet town with a specialism in death. That is to say that many burial tombs were created here in the naturally formed caves under this very village.

steps.player: What's going on around here?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Well, the people of the village, my usual customers... are all affected by the emanations from some place to the North East. Ulsquire can give you the name.

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Needless to say Herbi was working on a serum to help us and you stumbled across the recipe! I for one am grateful to you, but there's a lot left to do before Mort'ton is returned to it's former glory.

options.text: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.player: What are all these shadowy creatures?

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: Those disgusting entities are the filth that have ruined my life. They're the restless spirits of the dead who jealously guard their burial treasure yet feed on the  life force of the living.

steps.speaker: Razmire Keelgan
steps.text: I've heard that they jealously guard their tomb treasure and that it's worth plundering. I need you to kill five shades and bring me their remains so that I can conduct some experiments. Will you do it?

options.text: What did you find out about the remains?

steps.player: What did you find out about the remains.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The shade remains are made of a strange substance  which I've not come across before. I believe we should put these tormented spirits to rest.

steps.player: How can we do that? You can't even bury the remains!

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Quite right...I was thinking that a holy cremation would do the trick, but the funeral pyres need specially prepared 'pyre logs' - normal logs that have been  treated with 'sacred oil' to give it a nice holy touch.

steps.player: How would I make some sacred oil?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: You won't! It's a pagan secret lost a long time ago. Normally I would try to bless some commonly found vegetable oil, but I'm so weak from this illness that I know I just won't be able to do it.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Huh! I used to joke with Herbi Flax that if 'Flaemtaer temple' was still standing, we could practice some ancient pagan rituals and incite the sacred flame! Huh, I'm not surprised that he never took me seriously!

options.text: What can you tell me about that temple?

steps.player: What can you tell me about that temple?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: Hmm, interesting question. It is an ancient pagan  temple referred to as Flaemtaer. I've studied it quite    a lot, one day I hope to be able to rebuild it, who knows what ancient power it could unleash?

steps.player: How can you rebuild a totally destroyed temple?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I couldn't do it alone, I'd need a few expert artisans to help with the construction. I'd also need a good supply of limestone bricks, swamp paste and timber beams. Thankfully Razmire stocks all these items. (Sigh)

options.text: Do you know how I could make this serum permanent?

steps.player: Do you know how I could make this serum permanent?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The serum is a product of science. Herbi was a clever man to have made it, but he didn't integrate anything from the spiritual world into his work - and for all of his hard science there is still something missing.

steps.player: So, you don't know then!

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I'm a man of faith...that's all I know. Sometimes I feel that we should experiment with the sacred and the holy, not just the crude matter we find around us everyday.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: That's up to you my friend! I once heard someone say that making your own decisions is the only real freedom you have. Exercise your freedom my friend,  while you still can.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: I'm not surprised. The temple represents holiness. They may feel that it has power over them in some way. My advice is to carry on and finish the temple if you can, and see what happens. You may need help though!

steps.player: How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: You may need help building the temple or defending yourself against the Shades. I'm sure if you ask around nicely you would be able to get some help.

options.text: Tell me more about the Shades.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Shades.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: All undead hate mortal spirituality. It's a symbol of mortal hope in the face of death and the unknown. The temple represents the finality of true death where all ties to the mortal world are lost.

steps.speaker: Ulsquire Shauncy
steps.text: The Shades wish to forever possess the value of their tomb treasures and jealously guard them in death as they did in life. They are afraid of true death and so try to destroy anything which reminds them of it.

starting-off.text: Excuse me, I'm looking for [player name]. I have an urgent job for [him/her].

starting-off.prompt: Start the Shadow of the Storm quest?

steps.player: That's me!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Thank Saradomin I found you!
If the player still has Silverlight:

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: I believe you still have the magical sword Silverlight?

steps.player: The sword I used to defeat the demon Delrith? Yes, I still have it.

steps.text: If the player lost Silverlight:

steps.speaker: Father Reen

Reen hands you a shining silver sword.

steps.player: Silverlight! That's the sword I used to defeat the demon Delrith!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: There is an urgent task that only you can do - and only with Silverlight!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: My partner Badden and I have been observing the dark wizard Denath, who we believe has been preparing to summon the powerful demon Agrith-Naar.

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: A week ago he took a group of apprentice dark wizards and moved to Uzer, the lost city in the desert. We think he's going to use the city's ancient temple to summon the demon!

steps.player: So you want me to stop him?

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Stop him? No! We want you to wait until Agrith-Naar is summoned and then kill him once and for all!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Let me explain. Agrith-Naar is not an ordinary demon. He has immense magical powers, and he can use these powers to influence the mortal plane.

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: This summoning is our chance to rid the world of his evil influence!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: You should go to Uzer and find Badden at once. I'll follow once I've finished some business here.

steps.player: I'll let you know if I see [him/her].

starting-off-talking-to-father-reen-agai.text: If the player still has Silverlight:

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Did you go to Uzer to see Badden?

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: You must hurry!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: You idiot! You lost Silverlight! I found it on the sand!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: You need to take it with you and see Badden in Uzer.

to-uzer-talking-to-the-clay-golem.text: It is good to see a friendly face here. The priest has said nothing to me but 'Get ye away, foul construct!'

steps.player: Why does Badden hate you?

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: I do not know. I heard him say that Saradomin hates all artificial creatures.

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: It was not always so. When I was new, the priests of Saradomin praised the ingenuity of the golem-builders.

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: I paraded through the city with my siblings, all painted in bright colours, and they blessed us with holy water as we prepared for battle.

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: He should know that I could never hurt him. The first command in a golem's mind is that it cannot allow a human being to come to harm.

options.text: Do you know anything about the dark wizards who arrived here?

steps.player: Do you know anything about the dark wizards who arrived here?

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: Some of them were curious about me when they arrived, but since then they have ignored me.

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: As they passed me I felt a sense of dark foreboding, something I have not felt since the great enemy was nearby. I fear they are planning some great evil.

options.text: I want to go through the portal.

steps.player: I want to go through the portal.

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Go away! This is OUR portal now!

steps.player: Oh, nothing.

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Go away then!

options.text: Where did you get those robes?

steps.player: Where did you get those robes?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Yeah, evil, aren't they? One of the group made them. He said he found some mushrooms in the ruins that could dye things really black.

steps.player: Reen sent me.

steps.text: Saradomin be praised! And you have Silverlight! You're willing to help us, then?

steps.player: Tell me more about Agrith-Naar.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Agrith-Naar is not so much a demon as a force of nature. While he is in his own dimension his evil magics can reach everywhere in the world.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: No one knows how far his power extends, but Reen and I believe that much of the suffering in the world is due to him.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: The accident that cripples a man, the storm that sweeps a ship under the sea, the sudden fire in the blood that makes a wolf pack attack a town - all that is Agrith- Naar!

steps.player: Tell me more about Denath.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: We've been keeping an eye on Denath for some years now, but we've never been able to move against him.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: He was part of the group that summoned Delrith, but he left Varrock before you arrived and defeated the demon.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: He's been studying Agrith-Naar for years, but when he brought his group here we knew he was about to make his move.

options.text: Why has he come to Uzer?

steps.player: Why has he come to Uzer?

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: I'm not sure. This city is very ancient, and its builders were powerful workers of evil magic.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: As that foul construct over there proves.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Perhaps there's something here he needs. Do you know what happened here?

options.text: Foul construct? Do you mean the golem?

steps.player: Foul construct? Do you mean the golem?

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: The golem, yes! An abomination in the eyes of holy Saradomin! A mockery of life! Right now Denath is more important, but once he is dealt with I should find some way to destroy it.

steps.player: But the golem was created to fight a demon! You're on the same side!
Thousands of years ago a demon attacked this city, but the golem army drove it off.
When I last came here I opened the portal, and the demon was already dead - it had died of the wounds the golems inflicted.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: You opened a portal to a demon's realm? That must be why Denath is here!

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: It would be much easier to reach Agrith-Naar's realm from another demon's realm than from the mortal plane.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Denath must have heard that the portal here was open and decided to make his move!

options.text: Well I came here and opened a portal to a demon's realm.

steps.player: Well I came here and opened a portal to a demon's realm...

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: You opened a portal to a demon's realm? That must be why Denath is here!

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: It would be much easier to reach Agrith-Naar's realm from another demon's realm than from the mortal plane.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Denath must have heard that the portal here was open and decided to make his move!

options.text: So what do you want me to do?
So what do you want me to do?
So what do you want me to do?

steps.player: So what do you want me to do?

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: You have to be in position to kill Agrith-Naar as soon as he is summoned. The best way to do that is to infiltrate the group that is summoning him!

steps.player: How can I do that?

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: I don't know. You'll have to find some way to convince them you're one of them.

options.text: I'd never take part in a demonic ritual!

steps.player: I'd never take part in a demonic ritual!

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Oh, don't be so simple-minded! You'll be summoning a demon in order to kill it, to rid the world of great evil! You won't really be joining the group, just infiltrating it.

steps.player: How can I do that?

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: I don't know. You'll have to find some way to convince them you're one of them.
If the player lost Silverlight:

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Saradomin be praised!

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: But you will need Silverlight for this task. You should go back and get it.

steps.player: Just passing through.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Oh dear. I was hoping [player name] would arrive.

options.text: I haven't managed to infiltrate the group yet.

steps.player: I haven't managed to infiltrate the group yet.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Oh dear. Do try again. You must be in place when they summon the demon!

options.text: I'd never take part in a demonic ritual!

to-uzer-dyeing-silverlight-black.text: You slice the mushroom with Silverlight, and it stains the blade black.

options.text: I want to go through the portal.
I want to join your group.

steps.player: I want to join your group.

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Well we do need one more person now, since... um.

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: But we're an evil group! To join, you have to be evil!
While not wearing enough black items:

steps.player: I'm evil!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: You don't look evil. You certainly don't dress evil!

steps.player: I'm evil in disguise?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: There's no need for the disguise here! We're all evil!
While wearing 3 black items but Silverlight is undyed:

steps.player: I'm evil!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Yeah, I can see that. That outfit is totally evil!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: But what's that sword? It's far too shiny to be evil. We won't have any silver glowing swords in here!
While wearing 3 black items and having dyed Silverlight:

steps.player: I'm evil!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Yeah, I can see that. That outfit is totally evil!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Okay, I'll take you through to see Denath.
Evil Dave escorts you into the demonic throne room.

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Master! This person wants to join us!

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: Indeed? Well we are one wizard short since Josef ran away. Can you vouch for [him/her]?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Yeah! [He/She]'s totally evil!

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: Thank you, Dave.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: So you wish to join us? You have made a wise choice. When we summon the demon Agrith-Naar, he will grant all our worldly desires.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: An abyssal whip, a dragon chain mail? To conjure these items is trivial for Agrith-Naar.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: But you will not need such weapons or armour, for Agrith-Naar will grant you the power of life and death over all creatures!

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: You shall have every wish granted, and everyone who has ever wronged you will burn in a hell of your own devising!

steps.player: Isn't this, you know, wrong?

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: Right and wrong are for the weak! This is your chance to choose to be on the side of the strong, and have all your desires granted, while the weak are crushed beneath Agrith-Naar's demonic feet!

options.text: How do you know Agrith-Naar will do all this for us?

steps.player: How do you know Agrith-Naar will do all this for us?

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: My binding spells will make Agrith-Naar my slave! You would be wise not to question my powers again, lest I turn the same spells on you!

steps.player: Why did Josef run away?

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: Obviously he was a coward who did not have the strength to abandon his old-fashioned morality. I hope you will not be a similar disappointment.

options.text: What do I have to do?

steps.player: What do I have to do?

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: When I have finished preparing the magic circle, we will all recite the incantation that will summon Agrith-Naar.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: You must memorize the incantation carefully. It is Nahudu Camerinthum Caldar Agrith-Naar Tarren.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: You will also need to make yourself a demonic sigil to act as a focus of power. One of the group has the mould you need to make it.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: Now let me continue with my preparations!

steps.player: Never mind, I'm not evil.

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Well get out of our evil temple then!

options.text: Where did you get those robes?
I managed to get into the group.

steps.player: I managed to get into the group.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Oh, that is good! Make sure you are in place when they summon the demon!

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-fath.speaker: Father Reen
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-fath.text: Phew! It's too hot for me out here. But at least I found my way through the desert!

options.text: Why didn't you take the magic carpet?

steps.player: Why didn't you take the magic carpet?

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Oh dear no, you won't get me up in one of those things! What if the magic failed?

options.text: Why don't you change out of your heavy robes?

steps.player: Why don't you change out of your heavy robes?

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: But the rules of my order say I must wear them!

steps.player: Perhaps the rules were made in a colder place than this?

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Saradomin's rules are once and for all! It is not our place to question them!

options.text: Don't worry, soon I'll have killed the demon and we can all go home!

steps.player: Don't worry, soon I'll have killed the demon and we can all go home!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Summoning a demon! Those wizards make me sick! What kind of sad people would call on a supernatural being to solve their problems for them?

steps.player: Um, isn't that like what you do when you pray?

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: What? No, that's totally different, because... um... because we always give thanks to Saradomin, even when he doesn't do anything!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Not like those wizards! They're so full of themselves, with their fancy robes and their rituals!

steps.player: Um, isn't that like...

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: No, it's totally different!

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Anyway, there must be something wrong with the way they live in their little group and separate themselves from the rest of society. It can't be healthy.

steps.player: And that's *nothing* like you being a monk, of course.

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: No, nothing like that.

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Wait, are you being sarcastic? Because you should know that sarcasm is specifically forbidden in the holy book of Saradomin!

steps.player: Are you sure Saradomin was being serious about that bit?

steps.speaker: Father Reen
steps.text: Shut up!

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.speaker: Denath
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.text: Leave me alone! I am preparing for the summoning ritual. You should make yourself a demonic sigil and practice the incantation with the other wizards.

options.text: How do you know Agrith-Naar will do all this for us?

steps.player: I forgot the incantation.

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: Ignoramus! Are you incapable of even the simplest task? The incantation is Nahudu Camerinthum Caldar Agrith- Naar Tarren.

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.speaker: Evil Dave
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.text: Welcome, sister! Soon we'll summon the great demon! Aren't we evil?

steps.player: Yeah!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Yeah!
If the gems were removed from the throne:

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: And we've got such an evil throne room to do our ritual in!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: It's just a pity someone's removed the gems from the throne. That kind of vandalism is TOTALLY NOT EVIL.

steps.player: Um... Yeah, who would do a thing like that?

options.text: But isn't evil, you know, bad?

steps.player: But isn't evil, you know, bad?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: Yeah! We're BAD!

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: No. Last I heard, Matthew had it.

options.text: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.player: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: I didn't see anything. He left last night, and Denath only posted me here this morning.

steps.player: What?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: You don't understand.

steps.player: Understand what?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Nobody understands.

steps.player: What don't we understand?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Oh, it doesn't matter. You don't understand. Go away.

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?
Do you know what happened to Josef?
Do you have the demonic sigil mould?
Do you know what happened to Josef?
Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.text: Without already having it and while having free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Huh. So that's all you want. Here it is.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Huh.
Without already having it or free inventory space:

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Come back when you've got free space.
While already having the sigil mould:

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: I already gave that to you! Go away!

options.text: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.player: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: He didn't understand!

steps.player: No, I don't suppose he did.

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.speaker: Patrick
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.text: Agrith-Naar is going to make us all sooo rich!

steps.player: Yeah! We'll all be rich!

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: Yeah! I'm going to get myself a dragon longsword! And a million rune ores! And a small piece of coloured paper to put on my head!

steps.player: Um... if you like.

steps.text: If the gems haven't yet been taken from the throne:

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: Those gems on the demon's throne look valuable. I just wish I had some way to remove them.

options.text: Isn't it more satisfying to earn riches yourself?

steps.player: Isn't it more satisfying to earn riches yourself?

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: I don't want to be satisfied, I want to be rich!

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: Right now I don't have anything. But soon, I will have everything!

options.text: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.player: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: Denath says he ran away. I don't know why. Who would want to run away from what Agrith-Naar is going to do for us?

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.speaker: Eric
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.text: They won't ignore me for much longer!

steps.player: Who?

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: Everyone!

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: When I have demonic powers, they'll all have to pay attention to me!

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: And SHE won't ignore me then. I'll be able to show her how I feel.

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: I will make everyone like me!

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: No. I gave it to Matthew.

options.text: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.player: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: He went away and left us. He probably didn't like me.

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: Don't ignore me!

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.speaker: Tanya
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-the-.text: Soon, all will bow down before me!

steps.player: Oh?

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: Agrith-Naar will make us the rulers of the world! I shall be a dark queen over all Gielinor! All shall love me and despair!

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: Ha ha ha ha!

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: Ah ha ha ha ha ha!!

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: AAH HA HA HA HA HA HAAAAA!!!!

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: Look, we've told you not to do that. It makes everyone uncomfortable.

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: Sorry.

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: Hah! Carrying such humble implements is beneath me!

options.text: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.player: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: He was a fool who could not cope with power! When Agrith-Naar makes us rulers of continents, I will find him and crush him!

steps.player: Yes, I suppose I am.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: It just goes to show how little Denath values us.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Denath told us we would learn the secrets of demonic magic, but all we've done is memorize one incantation. And now he replaces poor Josef with the next person who comes along!

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.player: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: No, I think Jennifer has it.

options.text: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.player: Do you know what happened to Josef?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Shh! Listen, Denath doesn't know this...

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: When we joined him, Denath told us we were going to learn all the secrets of demonic magic, but we still don't know anything.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: The others, they just think they're terribly evil, with their sigils and the incantation they learned by rote. But Josef and I wanted more - we wanted to know how it worked.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Josef was more curious than me. Last night, he secretly read a book that Denath was keeping from us. He didn't know I was awake, but I saw what happened.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: I saw him read it, and then his face turned white, and he took the book and ran through the portal.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: But Denath was waking up, and when he saw Josef was gone he went through the portal to look for him. A bit later Denath returned, without Josef or the book.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Josef didn't have money for the magic carpet, and he can't have got far in the desert at night with that heavy book.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Josef must have hidden the book somewhere in the ruins, before Denath followed him. If you could find it, we'd know what it was that frightened him. We'd know what Denath is really up to!

options.text: Did you see anything happen here last night?

steps.player: Did you see anything happen last night?

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: I was sleeping last night. I'm only human after all!

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: But I had this odd dream, about fear and panic, and... fire...

infiltrating-the-wizards-asking-around-a.speaker: Clay golem
infiltrating-the-wizards-asking-around-a.text: It is good to see a friendly face here. The priest has said nothing to me but 'Get ye away, foul construct!'

options.text: Do you know anything about the dark wizards who arrived here?
Did you see anything happen last night?

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: I saw one of the men in dark robes run out of the temple. He looked very frightened and I feared for his safety.

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: He was carrying a large book. He started to head out into the desert, but then turned back and hid the book in one of the broken kilns in which my kind were created long ago.

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: Then another man came out of the temple. He said magical words and threw a fireball at the first man, turning him to dust!

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: I should have saved him, but I was not fast enough to throw myself in the path of the fireball.

steps.player: Which kiln did he hide the book in?

steps.speaker: Clay golem
steps.text: I cannot remember. The shock of seeing a human being killed wiped the details of the incident from my memory.
You look in the kiln but you see only sand and fragments of ancient golems.
You find a book in the kiln.

infiltrating-the-wizards-searching-kilns.text: Searching the correct kiln while already having the book:

steps.text: You have already found the book.

infiltrating-the-wizards-returning-to-ma.text: Without the book in your inventory:

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Did you find that book?

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: I really want to know what's in it. I think Denath is hiding something from us, but we won't know what unless we read that book!

options.text: Do you have the demonic sigil mould?

infiltrating-the-wizards-returning-to-ma.text: With the book in your inventory:

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Did you find that book?

steps.player: Yes. The golem saw Josef hide it in one of the broken kilns in the city.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Did the golem see what happened to Josef?

steps.player: It said Denath killed him.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Oh no!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: I knew Denath was a dark wizard but I didn't think he'd kill one of his disciples.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Let me look at the book then.
Matthew quickly reads the book then hands it back to you.

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: I don't understand. What's in here that Denath thought was worth killing over? Josef must have worked something out - but what?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: But look at the incantation in the book. The words are in the reverse order to the order that Denath taught us.

steps.player: The incantation in the book is backwards?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: More likely the book has the correct incantation and the one Denath taught us was backwards. But what does that mean?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: [player name], I'm not happy about this ritual. I don't think Agrith-Naar is going to grant all our wishes, I think he's going to kill us all. But if I try to stop it, Denath will kill me like he did Josef!

steps.player: Don't worry. I'm here to kill the demon!

steps.text: Without a dyed Silverlight in your inventory:

steps.player: But I need find a way to smuggle Silverlight in here. It's the only weapon that can defeat Agrith-Naar!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Thank goodness! I will try to stall the ritual until you have Silverlight. Hurry!
With a dyed Silverlight in your inventory:

steps.player: This is the demon-slaying sword Silverlight, the only weapon that can kill Agrith-Naar!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Thank goodness! I think Denath is nearly ready for the ritual. We must prepare!

infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-matt.speaker: Matthew
infiltrating-the-wizards-talking-to-matt.text: Are you prepared for the ritual? You must be ready to slay Agrith-Naar when he appears.

options.text: I don't think Denath is being honest with his wizards.

steps.player: I don't think Denath is being honest with his wizards.

steps.speaker: Father Badden
steps.text: Of course he isn't! You expect an evil sorcerer to be honest with anyone?

performing-the-ritual.speaker: Denath
performing-the-ritual.text: It is time for the ritual to commence!
Denath and the disciples assemble around the center of the room.

performing-the-ritual.speaker: Denath
performing-the-ritual.text: Player, please take your place in the circle!

performing-the-ritual-talking-to-evil-da.speaker: Evil Dave
performing-the-ritual-talking-to-evil-da.text: Our evil moment is at hand! You should get to your place in the circle so the ritual can start!

performing-the-ritual-talking-to-jennife.speaker: Jennifer
performing-the-ritual-talking-to-jennife.text: You ought to get to your place in the circle. Denath wants YOU to lead the ritual.

performing-the-ritual-talking-to-matthew.speaker: Matthew
performing-the-ritual-talking-to-matthew.text: This is it! Get to your place in the circle and say the words!

performing-the-ritual-talking-to-patrick.speaker: Patrick
performing-the-ritual-talking-to-patrick.text: Get to your place in the circle and lead the ritual! I'm so excited!

performing-the-ritual-talking-to-tanya.speaker: Tanya
performing-the-ritual-talking-to-tanya.text: Get to your place in the circle and lead the ritual! I'm so excited!

performing-the-ritual-getting-in-place.speaker: Denath
performing-the-ritual-getting-in-place.text: [player name] will lead us in the incantation.
If you got the incantation wrong:

steps.speaker: Denath
steps.text: You fool! Do it again, and get it right!

performing-the-ritual-getting-in-place.text: If you got the incantation correct:

steps.text: A magic circle appears in the floor...

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: Oh my gods!

steps.speaker: Eric
steps.text: He disappeared!

steps.speaker: Patrick
steps.text: Where'd he go?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Of course! How could we be so stupid?

steps.player: What happened?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: What do you get when you perform a summoning ritual backwards?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Denath was Agrith-Naar all along! We've just helped him return to his own dimension!

steps.speaker: Jennifer
steps.text: What was that?!

steps.speaker: Tanya
steps.text: Look! The portal's closing!

steps.speaker: Evil Dave
steps.text: I'm getting out of here!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: No, don't leave!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Who knows what Denath could do now?

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: We've got to perform the ritual again so you can kill Agrith-Naar. But we need eight people!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Quick, Snotra, you've got to get those three to come back! And you'd better take Denath's sigil and find one more person to help.

performing-the-ritual-talking-to-matthew.speaker: Matthew
performing-the-ritual-talking-to-matthew.text: We've got to perform the ritual again, forwards this time, so you can kill Agrith-Naar. I'll prepare for it here while you find four more people.

steps.player: Okay!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Hurry!

steps.player: I don't understand what happened!

steps.speaker: Matthew
steps.text: Denath must have been Agrith-Naar all along!

steps.speaker: Matthew

parents-anguish-talking-to-captain-ariad.speaker: Captain Ariadna
parents-anguish-talking-to-captain-ariad.text: No. As I said, we tried looking, but found nothing. Without a new lead, things are at a dead end.

parents-anguish-talking-to-captain-ariad.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.player: Excuse me. I'm looking into the-

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Turn around. Walk out.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Please... Nobody's looking into anything. Just leave us.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.player: But I'm trying to find the missing people!

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Prove it! What do you know?
The player has not talked to Ictus:

steps.player: Er...

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: Exactly! Now, go!

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: The player has talked to Ictus:

steps.player: Well, I know most of the town has given up on finding them. Most are just dismissing the disappearances, assuming them to have run away or had an accident.
However, there are some who think something more sinister is going on. If that's the case, I intend to find out. I'm [player name] and I promise I"m here to help.

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: You... You'll find our sons?

steps.player: I'm going to try.

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: Well... I suppose you do at least seem to somewhat care.

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: What do you need from us, [player name]?

steps.player: First up, what can you tell me about the disappearnce of your sons?

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: That's the thing... They just seemed to vanish! One moment they were playing upstairs, but the next they'd gone.

steps.player: And you didn't notice anything unusual at all?

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: Nothing really. The only thing that was a bit odd was the ents...

steps.player: The ents?

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: Yes. Their normal path takes them right past our house, but the night the boys disappeared, they took a different route. It's like they were avoiding something...

steps.player: I see. Can I look around the house a little and see if there's any clues as to where your sons went?

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: If you think it will help, then of course.

steps.player: Thank you.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: You again? We already told you to go away!

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Prove it! What do you know?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Have you found anything yet?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Please, help us find our sons.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Have you found anything yet?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.player: There are a few scratches on the wall outside along with this strange red substance.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Yes, I saw that, but I thought it was from the ents. Do you think something else left it?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.player: Possibly. It looks like there are puddles of the stuff leading away from your house. I'm going to follow them and see where they lead.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Thank you, [player name]. Please, help us find our sons.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Captain Ariadna
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Good day, traveller. Can I help you?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.player: Potentially. I was wondering if you have any clue what left these weird puddles through here?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Captain Ariadna
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Hmm... I hadn't noticed them before. I don't think the ents leave that sort of thing. My guess would be one of the woodland creatures.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.player: I see. Thank you for your help.

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-inspe.player: That's odd... There are some scratches going up the wall, along with a strange stick red substance. It's not blood... What is it?
What do we have here? More of that strange substance. I wonder where it leads...

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-inspe.text: It looks like there's some sort of fabric caught on the plank, but it's too far away for you to reach.

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-inspe.player: Hmm... A fishing rod might work...

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-using.text: It looks like there's some sort of fabric caught on the plank. You might be able to reach it with your fishing rod...
You use your fishing rod to hook a bit of fabric off the plank.

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-using.player: Interesting... I should see if this is from one of our missing people!

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-reins.player: I don't think this plank can offer me anything else. I should go and see if that fabric is from one of the missing people.

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-inspe.player: Could this be from one of the missing people?

parents-anguish-finding-the-fabric-destr.player: It could be evidence of something happening here... Surely it wouldn't be ethical to do this?
Then again, I wouldn't want to give false hope to those parents if it's actually nothing.
Yet I could still ask them about it, even if I don't have it to hand...

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Have you found anything yet?
The player has not found anything:

steps.player: I'm still looking.

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: Please, help us find our sons.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: The player has found the wet fabric scrap and kept it.

steps.player: Yes. Do you recognise this scrap of fabric? I followed a trail of... well, I'm not sure what it is. It led from your home to the river, and this was caught on a plank there.

steps.text: You show them the scrap of fabric you found.

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: One of our sons, Etz, often wears brown, and that looks like... Does that mean...

steps.player: It means I have a lead.

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: What direction was this trail going in?

steps.player: Up towards the mountains north west of here. It might be dangerous, but I think I can explore further.

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: If you're willing to, it would mean everything to us. You're the only one who's actually cared enough to find anything!

steps.player: It's the least I can do. I'll be back once I've discovered more.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: The player has found the wet fabric scrap and destroyed it:

steps.player: Yes. I followed a trail of... well, I'm not sure what it is. It led from your home to the river, and I found a scrap of fabric. Does one of your sons often wear brown clothes?

steps.speaker: Aemilia
steps.text: Yes, Etz does... What does it mean?

steps.player: It means I may have a lead.

steps.speaker: Francis

steps.player: Up towards the mountains north west of here. It might be dangerous, but I think I can explore further.

steps.player: It's the least I can do. I'll be back once I've discovered more.

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: You're back! Did you find anything in the mountains?

parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-aemilia-or-fr.text: Thank you for helping us. No one else seems to care...

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: Are you okay? Can you walk?

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Injured boy
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: I think so... I'm not sure if Etz can though...

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: That's okay. I should be able to carry him. Now, let's get out of here...

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: You take the two boys back to Auburnvale.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: I can't believe you found them!

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: I was very fortunate. They were in a cave in the mountains, but they weren't particularly far inside.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: Probably using the survival skills I taught them! That's my boys!

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: They're upstairs recovering. They need some rest, but they'll be okay.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: That's good to hear, though I am still worried as to how they ended up there. It's not really the kind of place someone visits, not to mention that strange substance I found...

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: You think they were taken by something?

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: I don't think we can rule it out.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: Well, they weren't the only ones to disappear. What if you're right? What if there are more people up there? And what if whatever took them comes back?

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: First things first, I need to find out exactly what happened to your sons. Do you think I could ask them about it?

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: Not yet. They need some rest first.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: In the meantime, you should go see Ariadna, the guard captain. People can't ignore this now. If something did take our boys, she needs to know about it. You'll find her by the main entrance into town.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: I'll go and see her. Is there anything else I can be doing to help as well?

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Aemilia
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: The boys were upstairs when they disappeared. What if whatever took them climbed our wall and came through the window? If that's the case, we need to stop it from happening again!

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: Let's see... I suppose I could take a look at the wall and see if it can be reinforced in some way?

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.speaker: Francis
parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.text: If it's not too much trouble, that would mean a lot to us.

parents-anguish-talking-to-etz.player: I'm sure it won't be too much to sort. Right, I'll be back once I've spoken to Captain Ariadna and sorted your wall out.

helping-around-town-attempting-to-climb-.speaker: Aemilia

helping-around-town-reinforcing-the-wall.player: Now then... How do we reinforce you? Perhaps some maple logs will do the trick!

Now then... How do we reinforce you? Perhaps some maple logs will do the trick! I reckon I'll need four sets in total.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: Good day! I'm here about those missing people.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: Yes, I saw you bringing those boys back to town. Where did you find them?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: In a cave up in the mountains.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: Did you see any sign of other missing people?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: I'm afraid not, but I intend to ask the boys about them once they've had some time to rest. I'm worried they didn't go up there on their own. There's a chance something might have taken them.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: Ah, wonderful. This is just what we need.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: Yes, I must admit, the town doesn't seem very well equipped to deal with this sort of thing. Is there anything I can do to help?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: Well, one of the people who went missing was the local fletcher. In his absence, our already light supply of longbows has become even lighter.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: I'm sure I can step in as your fletcher! New bows, was it?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: That's right. We typically use willow longbows. We've lost a few experienced archers over the years so we've tried to make things more approachable... and cheaper.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: Willow... Approachable... Got it! How many did you need?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: Four would keep us comfortable for the time being.
If the player does not have enough longbows:

steps.player: Alright, I'll be back soon.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: If the player happens to have enough longbows:

steps.player: I just so happen to have those on hand!

steps.speaker: Captain Ariadna
steps.text: Making the most of the woodlands around here, were you?

steps.player: Absolutely.

steps.text: You give Captain Ariadna four willow longbows.

steps.speaker: Captain Ariadna
steps.text: Thank you, traveller.

steps.player: So you've got the bows. What now?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: I have those bows you asked for!

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: You give Captain Ariadna four willow longbows.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: So you've got the bows. Now what?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: Well, not a lot really. We'll increase the number of guards posted at the entrances into town, but without knowing what we're looking for, we can't do much else.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: Right... Not quite the solution I was after, but it's a start. I guess I'd better go check in with those boys and see if I can find out more about how they ended up in that cave.

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.text: You're back. Have you sourced those willow longbows yet?

helping-around-town-talking-to-captain-a.player: Not quite. How many did you need?

helping-around-town-talking-to-marcus.speaker: Marcus
helping-around-town-talking-to-marcus.text: Ah, it's you. I hear you're still looking into the case of those missing people. Must say, you're the first person in a while to actually stick to it.

helping-around-town-talking-to-marcus.player: Well, I don't like leaving a mystery unsolved.

helping-around-town-talking-to-marcus.speaker: Marcus
helping-around-town-talking-to-marcus.text: Clearly. Anyway, good luck with it.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.speaker: Shas
rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.text: You're the one that saved us. Thank you.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.player: It's not a problem. I'm just glad you're both okay. If it's alright, I wanted to ask you how you ended up in that cave. I'm hoping it might help me track down the others who are missing.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.speaker: Etz
rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.text: We didn't see any others... It was just us and Antos...

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.speaker: Etz
rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.text: Yes! He makes bows for the guards. We'd see him sometimes when dad would go with him to the pub, but he wasn't in the pub! He was in the cave!

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.speaker: Shas
rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.text: He was deeper inside. Those... things... they dragged him away!

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas.player: This isn't good. I need to get back there!

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas-ta.speaker: Shas
rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas-ta.text: He was deeper inside that cave. Those... things... they dragged him away!

rescuing-antos-talking-to-etz-or-shas-ta.player: I'm going to head back there right now!

rescuing-antos-talking-to-aemilia-or-fra.speaker: Aemilia
rescuing-antos-talking-to-aemilia-or-fra.text: Have you spoken to the boys yet?
The player hasn't talked to the boys:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: They're just upstairs, but do be patient with them. They still have quite a bit of recovering to do.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-aemilia-or-fra.text: The player has talked to the boys:

steps.player: Yes, but I need to get back to the cave. Apparently someone called Antos is still in there!

steps.speaker: Francis
steps.text: Antos is up there? You'd better go and find him, iknami!

rescuing-antos-talking-to-captain-ariadn.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-captain-ariadn.text: Traveller. Did you find out more about what happened to those boys?
The player has not talked to the boys:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Captain Ariadna
steps.text: Well, without knowing what we're looking for, there's not much we can do.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-captain-ariadn.text: The player has talked to the boys:

steps.player: Yes, but I also found out someone called Antos is still in that cave! I need to go and find him!

steps.speaker: Captain Ariadna
steps.text: Antos? I'll get the guards ready, but that will take some time.

steps.player: We don't have time! I'm heading up there now!

steps.speaker: Captain Ariadna
steps.text: You're going alone?

steps.player: It's that or he dies!

steps.speaker: Captain Ariadna
steps.text: You're mad, traveller! Good luck up there.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: For now, but there could be more. We should get out of here.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Antos
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: Thank you, iknami. I thought I could find out where people were going... No one else seemed to care... I managed to track those boys here, but then those things...

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: It's okay, Antos. The boys are safe.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Antos
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: That's good... but everyone else... Look what they did to them...

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: I'm sorry, Antos. We can't help them now, but at least you and the boys are safe. Come on, let's get you home, before more of those things arrive...

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: You take Antos back to Auburnvale.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: You found Antos! I never thought we'd see him again. What happened?

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: That cave up in the mountains is full of some strange creatures. They were the ones responsible for the disappearances.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: I see... Did you find anyone else up there?

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: No. At least, no one alive, that is.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: That's... unfortunate. Still, from what you've said, I suppose we should be thankful that you found anyone still breathing.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: Right, time to get to work I guess. Now that we know about these creatures and where they're coming from, we can hopefully ensure they don't take anyone else.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: I suspect it's going to require us to establish a constant watch. Not ideal, but doable, especially with those new bows.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: Anything I can do to help?

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: Well, if you ever fancy heading up there and killing more of those creatures, you won't find me complaining. Apart from that though, I think you've done all you can.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.player: In that case, good luck with it all.

rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.speaker: Captain Ariadna
rescuing-antos-talking-to-antos-after-ki.text: Thank you. All the best, traveller.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-captain-a.text: Hello again, traveller. We've been keeping an eye on the mountain pass to make sure those creatures don't come back. We haven't had any more disappearances, so it seems to be working.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-captain-a.text: Still, we can't be too careful. If you ever fancy going up to that cave and killing a few of them for us, that would be appreciated.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-captain-a.speaker: Captain Ariadna
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-captain-a.text: Thank you, traveller. All the best.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-aemilia-o.speaker: Aemilia
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-aemilia-o.text: Thank you for finding our sons, iknami.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-aemilia-o.speaker: Francis
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-aemilia-o.text: Tetamo! You are too humble, friend. Without you, our boys would be dead. What you did means everything to us.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-shas-or-e.speaker: Etz
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-shas-or-e.text: And thank you for saving Antos as well!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: I's not doing a great deal now Bwana, as I'm no spring chicken. I do my fair share around the village bwana, though, I could tell you a thing or two about the jungle slashing.

options.text: Ok, tell me about jungle slashing!

steps.player: Ok, tell me about jungle slashing!

steps.npc: Ok Bwana, I will! To begin with you'll need a machete in order to hack your way through the jungle. There are some better gem edged weapons which you may be able to purchase from Gabooty.
Safta Doc makes them for him. You should be aware that hacking away at the jungle is not without its dangers though Bwana. Many times you may find some scary creatures lurking inside.

steps.player: What sort of creatures?

steps.npc: Ok, to start with there are spiders! These are pretty tough but if you defeat it, you can get a good meal from it, if you know how to cook it that is. My wife cooks them to a turn - Mmmm, delicious.

steps.player: Ok go on!

steps.npc: Yes Bwana, of course. Then there are snakes...these are dangerous because they're poisonous - so be prepared! However, they're not without their uses. A bush snake is large enough to have a useful hide.
Once the hide is tanned you get a snakeskin and you're able to make things from it, the same way that mainlanders use normal leather! However, it's actually still quite small.
You may need several skins in order to make something useful.

steps.player: Hmm, sounds interesting!

steps.npc: Then there are giant mosquitoes bwana, they're fast and agile. You'll need to be quick if you're to hit them at all! However, it certainly does train your reactions. They're not very tough, just difficult to hit.
I also believe that their proboscis is useful in someway, I believe Timfraku's sons sometimes use them for hunting.

steps.player: Ok, that sounds helpful...anything else?

steps.npc: Yes Bwana, much much more! What next...Oh yes, the tribesmen...you've probably seen them scouting around the village, sometimes sneaking inside the enclosure to steal our chickens!
They sometimes hide in the jungle bushes waiting for an opportunity to strike when we least expect it! Take care Bwana, these treacherous jungle natives use poison on their spears!

steps.player: Right Ok, good advice... 'poison on spears....' Anything else I should know about?

steps.npc: Yes Bwana... and this is serious... The jungle is very ancient and many unspeakable acts have been witnessed on these lands. Bizarre supernatural curses were placed on criminals and then they were buried alive!
These strange creatures have the curse of the Broodoo on them! They'll rise from their grave with their heads in their chests and move like crazy spirits of the afterlife.
If they're disturbed they will attack anything in the area with their magical abilities! They suffer little from being attacked as they seem to be protected by some form of defence.

However... it is said that the means of their death provides the clue to their destruction. So far three distinct Broodoo have been identified. The Broodoo with a green hued skin is said to have died from poison.
There is a broodoo of yellow hue and a pale skinned broodoo, but little is known of these two!

steps.player: Erk! Well that sounds pretty scary!

steps.npc: Yes Bwana...

steps.player: Ok, thanks a lot....

steps.npc: Wait Bwana, there's more!

steps.player: More... Blimey! Ok carry on...

steps.npc: Some of the local villagers have found strange plants which grow here-abouts. If you cut away at the jungle and find one, it's considered a blessing, though the useful part of the plant is usually buried underground.
And also, you may find an uncommon rock type which is impregnated with mineral wealth! Well that concludes all the help I can give you regarding the jungle in Tai Bwo Wannai!

steps.player: I have to say, that's quite a lot of information...thanks very much!

steps.npc: You're more than welcome bwana!

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.player: Is there anything interesting to do around here?

steps.npc: Bwana, if anyone else asks me that question today, I'll explode! Go and ask someone else!
Not that I'm aware of, just sit back and enjoy the sunshine bwana!
Sorry Bwana, I'm already busy, why not go and talk to Murcaily! He's around the village somewhere.
Well, I think that there's some work to be done...perhaps Murcaily can help you. He usually tends to the hardwood grove to the east of Trufitus's hut.
It's just village life as normal around here Bwana, always something interesting to find to occupy your time if you look hard enough.

options.text: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.player: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.player: What's wrong?

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: You may or may not be aware, but a plague has spread across West Ardougne. Now, so far, our efforts to contain it have been largely successful, for the most part.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: However, some sheep recently escaped from a farm near the city. When they were found, we noticed that they were strangely discoloured, so we asked the mourners to examine them.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: They believe that the sheep have become infected with the plague.

steps.player: Are you sure it's the plague?

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Well the mourners seemed convinced and they're the experts. Even if it's not though, the sheep are clearly diseased in some way.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: As the councillor responsible for public health and safety here in East Ardougne, I am in charge of dealing with this problem.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: We need someone to herd these sheep into a safe enclosure, kill them quickly and cleanly and then dispose of the remains hygienically in a special incinerator.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Unfortunately, nobody wants to risk catching the plague, and I am unable to find someone willing to undertake this mission for me.

steps.prompt: Start the Sheep Herder quest?

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: You will? That is excellent news! Head to the enclosure we have set up on Farmer Brumty's land to the north of the city; the four infected sheep should still be somewhere in that vicinity.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Before you will be allowed to enter the enclosure, however, you must ensure you have some kind of protective clothing to prevent contagion.

steps.text: If Client of Kourend has not been started:

steps.text: If The Queen of Thieves has not been started:

steps.npc: I hear that Lord Hosidius has misplaced one of his sons. The Hosidius family might pay a lot to see him returned safely.

steps.npc: It's very simple! First you'll need to be skilled in crafting and fletching, the exact details you can find in your skill guide.
For every shield, you'll require some tools! A knife for fletching the wood and a hammer for crafting the shield.
As for resources, you'll need 2 logs, 2 pieces of tanned leather and 15 nails.

steps.player: Where can I find out more information about the resources needed?

steps.npc: I have a flyer! It details all the shields and the resources needed for them.

steps.text: Well, truth be told, I would probably be here even if it wasn't where I worked. I very much like reading, not to mention sharing what I learn with all who are interested.

steps.speaker: Katrine
steps.text: We're fresh out of crossbows, but apparently they have plenty. If someone were to aquire a couple for us, it would be very much appreciated.

options.text: Hello. I am in search of a quest.

phoenix-gang-talking-to-straven-or-attem.speaker: Straven
phoenix-gang-talking-to-straven-or-attem.text: You can't go in there. Only authorised personnel of the VTAM Corporation are allowed beyond this point.

steps.player: I know who you are!

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Really? Well? Who are we then?

steps.player: This is the headquarters of one of the most dangerous crime syndicates this city has ever seen! The Phoenix Gang!

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: No, this is a legitimate business run by legitimate individuals. However... supposing we were this crime gang, what would you want with us?

options.text: I'd like to offer you my services.

steps.player: I'd like to offer you my services.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: You mean you'd like to join the Phoenix Gang? Well, obviously I can't speak for them, but the Phoenix Gang doesn't let people join just like that. First, you'd need to prove your loyalty.

steps.player: How would I go about doing that?

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Obviously, I would have no idea. Although, having said that, a rival gang of ours, er, theirs, called the Black Arm Gang is supposedly meeting a contact from Port Sarim today.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Apparently the meeting is going to take place in the Blue Moon Inn, and supposedly the contact is none other than the notorious mass murderer turned pirate captain, Jonny the Beard.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Now, obviously I know nothing about the dealings of the Phoenix Gang, but I bet if somebody were to arrange an accident for Jonny and bring back his intelligence report, the gang would be very pleased.

steps.player: I see... I'm sure I can help sort something out for them. I'll get right on it.

options.text: I want nothing. I was just making sure you were them.

steps.player: I want nothing. I was just making sure you were them.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Well then get lost and stop wasting my time.

options.text: How do I get a job with the VTAM corporation?

steps.player: How do I get a job with the VTAM corporation?

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Get a copy of the Varrock Herald. If we have any positions right now, they'll be advertised in there.

steps.player: Fair enough.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: How's your little mission going?

steps.player: I don't have it yet...

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Jonny the Beard is the person who has it. I imagine he will be in the Blue Moon Inn... Not that I'd know for sure, with me definitely not being a member of the Phoenix Gang and all.

phoenix-gang-talking-to-straven-or-openi.text: If the player has the intel report.

steps.player: I have the intelligence report!

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Let's see it then.

steps.player: Let me go get it from the bank.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: I'll wait here.
If the intel report is in the inventory.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Very good... Very good... Okay, I'm satisfied. Welcome to the Phoenix Gang! I'm Straven, one of the gang leaders.

steps.player: Nice to meet you. I'm [player name].

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: As a member of our gang, you now have access to our hideout and our weapons supply depot. The hideout is just through this door and the depot is two doors down from here. You'll need this key to get in.
Straven hands you a key.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Once again, welcome to the Phoenix Gang!

options.text: I've heard you've got some cool treasures in this place.

steps.player: I've heard you've got some cool treasures in this place.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Oh yeah, we've all stolen some stuff in our time. Our candlesticks down here, for example, were quite a challenge to get out of the palace.

steps.player: And the Shield of Arrav?

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Woah... that's a blast from the past! We stole that years and years ago!

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Truth be told, we don't even have the whole shield anymore. A few years ago there was a big fight within the gang and the shield got broken in half as a result.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: After the fight, some gang members split off and formed their own group. They took one half of the shield with them.

steps.player: This other group? The Black Arm Gang?

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Indeed.

options.text: Any suggestions for where I can go thieving?

steps.player: Any suggestions for where I can go thieving?

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: You could always try the marketplace over in Ardougne. Lots of opportunity there!

options.text: Where's the Black Arm Gang hideout?

steps.player: Where's the Black Arm Gang hideout?

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Interested in spying on the enemy, are you? It will be tricky. Their security is pretty good. Not as good as ours obviously, but still good.

steps.speaker: Straven
steps.text: Still, if you really want to go there, it's down an alleyway near the southern gate. One of our contacts, a tramp going by the name of Charlie, keeps an eye on it. He may be able to help you.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the help!
I'd better get going.

phoenix-gang-talking-to-straven-after-lo.speaker: Straven

phoenix-gang-talking-to-katrine-after-jo.text: You've got some guts coming here, Phoenix scum! Get lost, or I'll make sure you haven't got those guts anymore!

options.text: I've found half of the Shield of Arrav!

steps.speaker: Reldo

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.player: Hello there. I'm here about the Shield of Arrav.

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.text: The Shield of Arrav? The Museum has been searching for that for years! The late King Roald II offered a generous reward for its return!

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.player: Well, I'm here to claim it.

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.text: You've found the shield? Let's have a look!
You show the shield half to the curator.

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.text: This is incredible! But where's the other half?

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.player: I obtained this half from the [Phoenix Gang/Black Arm Gang]. The [Black Arm Gang/Phoenix Gang] might have the other half.

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.text: That does sound plausible. We will have to hope that another adventurer can recover that half.

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.player: So will I be rewarded for recovering half of the shield?

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.text: I'm afraid the reward is for the recovery of the full shield. However, what I'll do is write you out two half- certificates. If another adventurer returns the other shield half, I'll do the same for them.

finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-curator-haig-hal.text: The two of you can then swap one of the half- certificates to make a full one each. Take that to the King and he will grant you your reward.
The curator gives you two half-certificates.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.text: Welcome to the museum of Varrock.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.player: Hello there. I'm here about the Shield of Arrav.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.text: I gave you two half-certificates for the half you returned. If another adventurer returns the other shield half, I'll do the same for them.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.text: The two of you can then swap one of the half-certificates to make a full one each. Take that to the King and he will grant you your reward.

finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.player: Would it be okay to get more half-certificates?

finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
finishing-up-talking-to-the-curator-agai.text: I suppose so. It's not like you can do anything with them without the other half.

finishing-up-talking-to-king-roald-witho.speaker: King Roald
finishing-up-talking-to-king-roald-witho.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

options.text: I'm here about the Shield of Arrav.

steps.player: I'm here about the Shield of Arrav.

steps.text: If the player has a shield half:

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: The Shield of Arrav? Yes, I do recall my father put a reward out for that.

steps.player: Well, I've managed to find half the shield!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You have? Well, before we go any further, you'll need to get the authenticity of the shield verified by the curator at the museum.

steps.player: Okay. I'll head over there.

steps.text: If the player has a half-certificate:
