standard-dialogue-attempting-to-take-his.npc: Hey! What do you think you're doing? Leave my tea alone!

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-use-tele.npc: Hey! What do you think you're doing? Don't go casting that kind of spell anywhere near my tea!  Leave my tea alone you telegrabbing fiend!

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-zo.npc: Oh, so you're back then, come to gloat have you?

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-zo.player: Nope, I've just come to ask you a couple of questions.

options.text: How do I get rid of the undead ogres?

steps.player: How do I get rid of the undead ogres?

steps.npc: Haven't I already explained this to you once before?

steps.player: Humour me!

steps.npc: Ok, similar spells have been cast before and the only way to deal with the resulting creatures is to cordon off the area and not go in there again. The undead creatures usually manifest some sort of disease so it's
best to attack them from a distance with a ranged weapon.
Normal missiles like arrows and darts do very little damage to them because they're designed to destroy internal organs. This is a waste of time with undead creatures like undead ogres.

steps.player: Yeah, clearly so what should we use?

steps.npc: From my research it looks like a flat ended arrow was designed called a 'Brutal arrow'. This does large amounts of crushing damage to the creature.
You can make them by using larger arrows, I think some Ogre hunters make them. But instead of adding an arrow tip, you hammer a large nail into the end of the shaft.

options.text: How do I get rid of the disease?

steps.player: How do I get rid of the disease?

steps.npc: Haven't I already explained this disease thing to you once before?

steps.player: Just tell me again or else I'll turn you back into an ogre!

steps.npc: No...noo...please, I'll tell you.
My research shows that two jungle based herbs can be used, one is found near river tributaries and looks like a vine, the other is found in caves and grows on the wall.
It's quite well camouflaged so it's unlikely that you'll find it.

steps.player: We'll see about that!
Sorry, I have to go.

stat-reducing-attack.npc: I infect your body with rot...
I infect your body with rot...

before-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: Are you all right? You seem a little...incoherent.

before-skippy-and-the-mogres.npc: Inc'hearnt? Inc'herant! You...you...with yer fancy book- lernin' words. You'd be more than inc'herant if youd seen...

options.text: I'm sure I would as well.

steps.player: I'm sure I would as well.
I'm going over here to talk to non-crazy people now.

steps.npc: Yeah? Yeah? Well when THEY come floppin' into your house and eat your furniture you'll be sorry!

steps.player: Who are
(Dramatic pause)
THEY?

steps.npc: They! Those bloodthirsty, flesh-tearing devils! They are the reason I'm out here every day hurlin' bottles into the sea!
They are the reason I've lost everything, except the horrifying memory of what THEY look like...

steps.player: And what do THEY look like?

steps.npc: Mudskippers!

steps.player: Mudskippers?

steps.npc: Aye, Mudskippers! Those ferocious, ravening, evil, beady-eyed terrors of the deep!

steps.player: I...see...

steps.npc: I was ambushed by them way back, see. They got the drop on me...I can't remember where, somewhere around here though.

steps.player: These would be the mudskippers, right?

steps.npc: Aye! The mudskippers! Huge they were! Ten feet of glistening, muddy flesh floppin' towards me with white foam flying from their gnashing fangs!
I fought them up and down the beach, with the tide rising and more of them leaping towards me with cutlasses drawn!

steps.player: This is fascinating, but I have to be...

steps.npc: Shut yer' word-hole and listen! I can't remember all the details, as I'm sure they must have hit me quite hard, but the last thing I remember before it all went black...
...was one of those devils rearing over me, its eyes glowin' red with the fires of hell!

steps.player: Fires of hell...right. I believe you.

steps.npc: No you don't! You think I'm crazy, like all the rest! Well, if I'm crazy, how did I get these?

steps.player: Get what?

steps.text: Skippy shows you what appears to be massive bite scars on his legs. You're no expert, but they look like... giant mudskipper bites!

steps.player: Giant mudskipper bites! Where did you get those?

steps.npc: I can't remember... I've been drinking to forget the horror, and all I seem to have forgotten is where it all happened...

steps.player: Hmmm...I suppose if I sober you up you may well start to recall.

steps.npc: You'll have a job. I've been drinking this for a week.

steps.player: 'Captain Braindeath's Extra Strength Rum/Drain Cleaner. Now 50% more debilitating'?

steps.npc: It's the extra sheep tranquilizers that gives it that added kick!

steps.player: Stay here and I'll be right back. Try not to move. Or go near any open flames.

before-skippy-and-the-mogres-trying-to-s.player: You know, I could shock him out of it if I could find some cold water...

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: How do I annoy the Mogres again?

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.npc: Go south to Mudskipper Point and lob a Fishing Explosive into the sea. You can grab them from the Slayer masters.

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: Thanks! So, what are you going to do now?

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.npc: Well, I was planning on continuing my hobby of wandering up and down this bit of coastline, bellowing random threats and throwing bottles.

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: I was planning on wandering up and down the landscape, bugging people to see if they had mindblowingly dangerous quests for me to undertake.

after-skippy-and-the-mogres-when-using-t.player: I think he's sober enough. And I don't want to use another bucket of water.

steps.npc: Cutlasses! Think yer a pirate now [lad/lass/kid]?

steps.player: Well, yes.

steps.npc: Well, I have some cutlasses.
I have Brass Hand Harry's Cutlass. Well, a load of them to be honest.
Then there's Unlucky Jenkins' Lucky Cutlass. Lovely blade that.
I've also got Gentleman Mallard's Rapier. Not a cutlass I know, but the finest blade ever wielded by a privateer.
Now, which would ye like to hear about?

steps.player: Brass Hand Harry's Cutlass.

steps.npc: A good choice!
Ye may end up meeting Brass Hand Harry if ye hang around long enough.
He lost his left arm to a canister round, but that didn't stop him much.
Then he lost his right hand at the wrist fightin' the excise men off the coast of Karamja.
Not bein' the sort to lie about mopin', he asked me to make him a cutlass with a brass gauntlet fixed to the handle, and rig it up with a load of straps so he could keep fightin'.
He's a great man is Harry, but he keeps snappin' the straps while he's at sea, so he sells the cutlasses back to me in exchange for a new one.
It's quite a good blade, but the big, brass gauntlet is what makes it worthwhile. It's big enough to fit over even a real gauntlet, so ye get extra protection to yer sword hand.
I can sell ye one fer 1040 coins.
Interested?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 1040 coins:
If the player has at least 1040 coins:
Harry's cutlass

steps.npc: Here ye go. I've got a load of these left over if ye need more.

steps.player: Unlucky Jenkins' Lucky Cutlass.

steps.npc: Arr, tis a sad tale to this sword.
Jenkins was the lookout on the Jonah, a cursed vessel if there ever was one.

One day his ship were attacked by another group of pirates durin' a fierce storm. One of their bowmen took a shot at the Cap'n of the vessel, but it were deflected off his compass and hit Jenkins in the back.

steps.player: How unlucky!

steps.npc: That weren't the worst of it [lad/lass/kid]. He survived the fight, and the ship's surgeon was trying to get the arrow out when...
Are ye familiar with the spell bones to bananas?

steps.player: Yes, why?

steps.npc: Well, due to a blow to the head he took in the fight, the surgeon cast that spell, thinking it was some sort of new healing spell.
And he did so while touching Jenkins' ribs.

steps.player: And that killed him?

steps.npc: No [lad/lass/kid]!
See, he survived, his bones turned to bananas, as a huge storm blew up and the crew debated what to do with him.

But you see, the storm was actually the tail end of a hurricane that had swept the nearby jungle islands, and when it approached the ship it petered out, droppin' all manner of strange things onto the deck and into the
ocean.
The worst part was when the ship was bombarded with ravenous, hunger-crazed monkeys, the majority of which landed on Jenkins as he lay recoverin'.

steps.player: And that killed him?

steps.npc: No [lad/lass/kid]!
See, what happened next, after the monkeys had had their way with him was...

steps.player: Look, I don't want to hear any more. Why would I want to buy his cutlass?

steps.npc: Well, after the poor man passed on...
In a final, terrifying, mashed potato coated tragedy...
His shipmates found his cutlass was completely untouched.
See, having been exposed to all the bad luck that Jenkins went through, the thing is unlikely to ever see anything that bad again.
Hence, it must be lucky.
Ye can have it fer 2560 coins.
Interested?

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 2560 coins:

Lucky cutlass

steps.npc: Here ye go. I hope it brings you luck.

steps.player: Gentleman Mallard's Rapier.

steps.npc: Well, I'll tell ye the story, but it'll take a great deal of convincin' for me to sell you this rapier.
See, gentleman Mallard is a legend in these parts. His family had been rich, shipping all sorts of goods up and down the coast.
Then their rivals got together and had their ships sunk, one after the other, and his business partners were all either bought off or had...accidents.
With no money and only one ship left, he took to the life of a pirate, but no brigand was he.
He took only from those men that had brought about his downfall, was fair with his men, and generous with his loot.
Why, this island would have been wiped out by the shakes if he hadn't turned over his stash to buy medicine.
One day his ship was attacked by a huge sea creature that swept the decks of men with its tentacles.
The crew took to the lifeboats, and the last they saw of him the gentleman was stabbin' at the thing as it hauled the ship under the water.
A week later about ten foot of tentacle washed up on the beach, with his rapier embedded in it to the hilt.
I took it, cleaned it up, and I've been lookin' after it ever since.
I can't let it go for less than 25600 coins, and even then that's a bargain.
Ye think ye have what it takes to wield it?

rare-alternate-dialogue.npc: Mankind's variation frightens me.
The way they saw this universe, their modes of impression, differed so greatly from one another that to read their stories, to know their lives, is to wonder if they were not many species in one.
It was as if they had ranged across the actions of a thousand species and taken them for their own.
For nearly two thousand years they dreamed in a creative mania without antecedent.
They looked into the eyes and minds of other species and with their own intellect superseded them.
They destroyed many, coopted others, and in the space between necessity and carelessness, left some to grow as untended as any species could in the wake of their ubiquity.
They swarmed across the continents and oceans of a Gielinor they called their own, and shattered it into a billion imbricate worlds.
And they were, by the twisted jungles of their slaughterhouses, ruthless and aloof beyond measure.
The worst of us.
A superpredator.
A bringer of mass extinction.
All mountains move and all giants are mountains.
We rest upon their shoulders.
The world has grown older, senescent.
We are chimpanzee, we are gorilla, we are orangutan, and we are baboon and more.
We are, whether we like it or not, the blood legatees of humanity.
We are the children of men, but our mistakes will not be their mistakes.
We are telling a story.
We are telling a story of life, of what it means to live together in this universe, with vastly different modes of being, of seeing, of knowing.

Of sharing our own internal worlds with each other and making the universe we live in better for it. The empathy of a mind speaking to another mind, a vastly different mind, and yet each understanding each.
And if not, if the barriers seem too great, then striving to overcome them.
Sorrow in what humanity did to this world, in the horrors they unleashed, in their cataclysm of despair, in the tens of thousands of species that will never walk or swim or fly again.
Extinctions abounded in their wake, and yet look now at this sunbright land, at the joys we have brought to it, to have bound the chaotic climate to our will.
To have thought deeply of the future of this world, a sense of respect, of shared reverence for it and all who live within it.
We have strung the close sky with life.
Be proud.
And empathy, once limited only to mankind and some few species, now extends across all lands, across all time.

steps.player: I've lost my perfected whistle. Do you have any spares?

steps.npc: Someone found one just the other day and gave it to me in case someone came to claim it. Could it be yours?

steps.player: It's possible? Can I see it?

steps.npc: Of course!

steps.player: That notch in the tail, that scratch on the underside... Yes, it's mine! I can't believe it!

steps.npc: Here you go! I'm afraid it has no charges left, though.

steps.player: Thank you!

options.text: Can I get a whistle with unlimited charges?
options.condition: First time:

steps.player: Can I get a whistle with unlimited charges?

steps.npc: I see you already have a Perfected quetzal whistle, I can upgrade it for you at a cost.

steps.player: How much is this going to set me back.

steps.npc: I don't want your coins. Instead, I would like 10,000 charges worth of food for the birds here. You can give that to me piece by piece as well if need be.

steps.player: That sounds good to me, I have some food for the birds right here.

steps.prompt: Give Pitri food for the birds?

steps.npc: Thanks for the feed, you still need to give me another [number] charges worth of food for the birds.

steps.text: If the player has turned in 10,000 charges worth of meat:

steps.npc: Thanks for all the food, I'll be glad to give you a whistle with infinite charges. The first one is free of course, any more will cost you though.

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...

steps.player: Strange how?

steps.npc: Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard-dialogue-first-attempt.npc: By Ralos, we finally have a worthy challenger.
You've torn through multiple waves of combatants and you're still standing. I'm almost impressed.
Now let's see how you handle a real foe...

standard-dialogue-first-attempt.text: Sol Heredit jumps down from his seat...

standard-dialogue-second-attempt.npc: You're back so soon? A lesser combatant would've retired in shame after the show you put on last time...
But you're clearly different. Let's see what you have this time...

standard-dialogue-second-attempt.text: Sol Heredit jumps down from his seat...

standard-dialogue-third-attempt.npc: What is it they say? Third time's the charm? Let's see if that's true.

standard-dialogue-third-attempt.text: Sol Heredit jumps down from his seat...

standard-dialogue-subsequent-attempts-wi.npc: You might be an incapable fighter, but at least you're persistent. Shall we?

standard-dialogue-subsequent-attempts-wi.text: Sol Heredit jumps down from his seat...

steps.player: What?!
Huh?!
Er...
OK...
Are you insulting me in Latin?

steps.npc: Yes!

steps.player: Hmm...

standard-dialogue-warhammer.npc: I've been posted here to guard this chasm.
Not great. There's constant bursts of hot air, demon roars and strange lights coming from inside.
And then there's the cultists. They just climb out like it's normal to be down there. Try to talk to you like it's business as usual.

options.text: How long are you posted here?

steps.player: How long are you posted here?

steps.npc: Indefinitely. We don't know what the cult is up to and we don't want to be caught unprepared.

steps.player: Have you considered quitting?

steps.npc: No. I signed up to to protect Kourend, even if that means standing outside of a demon nest. Besides, it's not like any demons have come out of it yet.

steps.player: Well, good luck.

steps.npc: Thanks.

standard-dialogue-scimitar.npc: What do you want? Are you with those cultists?
Good. I've had enough of their games.
They start off polite, but before you know it, they're trying to get you to agree to something.
They're not fooling me though. The next one that crosses me is going to regret it!

steps.player: About the cultists... What sort of things do they ask you to agree to?

steps.npc: Usually they want you to follow them somewhere private. Some of the bolder ones try to get you to join them inside the chasm.
If it were up to me, we'd launch a sortie right now. See how they like it if we come down on our own terms.

steps.player: Aren't you worried about the demons?

steps.npc: You sound like the lieutenant.

steps.player: You sound eager to fight.

steps.npc: I am. If you ask me we should be out fighting lizardmen. That means we need to go on the offensive and wrap this chasm business up.

steps.player: I take it the rest of your squad aren't as keen.

steps.npc: You'd be right. The lieutenant is too cautious and the rest are too timid. The way some of them speak you'd think they had demon families.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: If you see any cultists lurking around, let me know.

standard-dialogue-dagger.npc: I might as well be if we're going to continue this performance.
There are no demons coming out of this chasm. If there were, we wouldn't last long.

options.text: You think the demons would overrun you?

steps.player: You think the demons would overrun you?

steps.npc: Demons don't die the same way we do. We could hold back a few of them, but not an endless stream.

steps.player: You seem to know a lot about them.

steps.npc: I do, which means I know that guarding the chasm is a pointless endeavour. Not that the lieutenant cares what I think.
Launching an attack into the chasm would also be pointless. That leaves us with only one other option.

steps.player: Fleeing?

steps.npc: No. We should talk to them. Try to reach an understanding.

steps.player: Somehow I don't think negotiating with demons will end well.

steps.npc: If you have a better idea, go ahead.

options.text: Aren't you a bit too calm about this?

steps.player: Aren't you a bit too calm about this?

steps.npc: No. If they wanted to, Yama and his demons could overrun this little squad.
The fact they haven't means they're probably not interested in doing so. As a matter of fact, they seem quite polite.

steps.player: You've spoken to them?

steps.npc: I didn't say that, But there's evidence to suggest that Yama and his cult can be reasoned with.
If Lord Shayzien is interested in diffusing the threat, he should consider trying to reach an agreement with them.

steps.player: I've met Lord Shayzien. He doesn't seem like the type to compromise.

steps.npc: You've met Lord Shiro Shayzien?

steps.player: Yes, I've met the leaders of all of the houses. Even King Artur Hosidius himself.

steps.npc: Interesting. You're quite the worldly fellow. Perhaps King Hosidius would make a more level headed negotiator. Maybe you could talk to him?

steps.player: I imagine he's quite busy at the moment.
Goodbye.
Are you OK?

steps.npc: Urrrgggh.....
I'll be OK, the trolls only leave the plateau at nightfall. The guys are bringing a stretcher shortly.

steps.player: As long as you're sure.

steps.npc: It's my own fault really, I was having a walk and wandered past the danger sign. The trolls throw rocks down at any one who goes up the path!
Don't go up there!

steps.player: OK, thanks for the warning.

standard-dialogue.npc: Are you here to fight the lizardmen? Be careful - they're fierce!

steps.player: Tell me about the lizardmen.

steps.npc: The lizardmen are the bane of Kourend. I'm not much for history, but the Shayzien Army have been fighting them off for as long as anyone can remember.
They can be aggressive, and they've got something nasty in their bite that can make you pretty ill.

options.text: Why are you up here instead of fighting?

steps.player: Why are you up here instead of fighting?

steps.npc: I got a bite from a lizardman. I'm all cured, but I'm not going down there again until I feel stronger, otherwise I'll be no use in the fight.

standard-dialogue.player: Oh, that's... interesting. Also rather disturbing...

standard-dialogue.npc: Try not to think about it.

options.condition: If the player has a Skull sceptre and either the Fancy boots, Fighting boots, or Fancier boots in their inventory:

steps.player: Could you imbue my sceptre?

steps.npc: Of course I can... But first, you must show me whatever treasure lies within that cradle and make sure that your account is safe.

steps.player: Is my account safe?

steps.text: If the player does not have the RuneScape Authenticator enabled on their account:

steps.npc: To make sure your account is secured, please turn on the authenticator. Simply visit the support link on the oldschool.runescape.com website.

steps.player: Oh, that sounds like a great idea, I'll go do that.

steps.text: If the player has the RuneScape Authenticator enabled on their account:

steps.npc: It seems you have the authenticator set up, that's perfect! Now just show me the treasure.

steps.player: Is this the treasure?

steps.text: If the player has Fancy boots in their inventory:
You show the fancy boots to Solztun.
If the player has Fighting boots in their inventory:
You show the fighter boots to Solztun.
If the player has Fancier boots in their inventory:
You show the fancier boots to Solztun.

steps.npc: Oh marvellous! If only I had corporeal form I'd be able to wear them, but alas...

steps.player: So could you imbue my sceptre?

steps.text: If the player does not have the RuneScape Authenticator enabled on their account:

steps.npc: It seems your account isn't as secure as it could be, I'm afraid I can't imbue your sceptre.

steps.player: Oh.

steps.text: If the player has the RuneScape Authenticator enabled on their account:

steps.npc: Of course, of course! In fact if you have more than one I'll imbue all of them!

steps.text: Solztun imbues any Skull sceptres the player has.

steps.npc: There you go, now that I've imbued all of your sceptres, once they run out of charges they will no longer break and they can be charged with any piece of the sceptre you find.

steps.player: Thank you very much! How many charges does each piece give?

steps.npc: Most of them give 3, although the left skull gives 5. Each completed tier of the Varrock achievement diary will get you one extra charge per piece and allow your sceptre to hold 4 more charges.
You can use a chisel to break a sceptre piece into fragments, then use those to charge the sceptre instead. More flexible if you ask me.
Finally, be warned that if you disable your authenticator, the imbue on the sceptre will be removed.

steps.player: Fantastic! It's best I keep my authenticator activated then. Good bye Solztun!

steps.npc: Stay safe, adventurer.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.text: If speaking for the first time:

steps.npc: I am Solztun, the greatest barbarian explorer!

steps.player: It's very nice to meet you, Solztun! I'm [player name].

steps.npc: I know.

steps.player: ... so, you were exploring this place?

steps.npc: Yes, my sister told me not to go, she said it was dangerous and that I'm no fighter. Unfortunately... she was correct.

steps.player: Oh! Your sister is Litara, the woman out on the surface? How come she was correct?

steps.npc: I died... Of course, I tried escaping, long before I'd made it to the treasure, but I was shot with arrows just as I approached the exit.

steps.text: If speaking again:

steps.npc: As I said, I am Solztun, the greatest barbarian explorer! I came to explore this place, but unfortunately I died long before I made it to the treasure.

steps.player: Nobody came to help?!

steps.npc: Oh no, they had no idea I was hurt, I guess they assumed I'd found the treasure and made a new life for myself.

steps.player: Were you not a fan of the barbarian life style?

steps.npc: It was all death and pillaging, I prefer the finer things in life, like exploration and discovery!

steps.player: Ah, I too enjoy those.
Why are you here?

steps.npc: I came for treasure!

steps.player: Oh right, you were looking for what's in that cradle?

steps.npc: Yes, but alas, I'm dead.

steps.player: I guess I could show you... for a price.

steps.npc: Hmm... I don't have much to offer, but if you happen upon a skull sceptre, I could make it stronger.

steps.player: Stronger you say... In what way?

steps.npc: Currently the sceptre is fragile, it breaks once all charges have been used. Show me the treasure and I could imbue it so it can be recharged with any sceptre piece.

steps.player: You, my dead friend, have a deal!
Bye!

steps.npc: Stay safe, adventurer.

using-a-skull-sceptre-on-him.npc: Of course I can... But first, you must show me whatever treasure lies within that cradle and make sure that your account is safe.

steps.player: Is my account safe?

steps.npc: To make sure your account is secured, please turn on the authenticator. Simply visit the support link on the oldschool.runescape.com website.

steps.player: Oh, that sounds like a great idea, I'll go do that.

steps.text: If the player has the RuneScape Authenticator enabled on their account:

steps.npc: It seems you have the authenticator set up, that's perfect! Now just show me the treasure.

steps.player: Is this the treasure?

steps.text: If the player has either the Fancy boots or the Fighting boots in their inventory or bank:
If the player does not have either the Fancy boots or the Fighting boots in their inventory or bank:

steps.npc: No, that's not it.

steps.player: But I didn't show you anything.

steps.npc: I sense that you don't have the treasure.

options.condition: If the player has either Fancy boots or Fighting boots in their inventory:

steps.npc: Hmm... You're not my usual kind of customer, but I reckon I can still make this work. What will it be? Haircut or a shave?

steps.player: I'd like a haircut please.

steps.npc: Then let's get to it.

steps.text: If the player is wearing an item on their head:
You should take off your hat if you want to get a haircut!
If the player is wearing nothing on their head:

steps.player: I'd like a shave please.

steps.npc: Then let's get to it.

You should take off your hat if you want to get a haircut!
If the player is wearing nothing on their head:

steps.player: I'm good, thanks.

steps.npc: Suit yourself.

starting-out-talking-to-edmond.speaker: Edmond
starting-out-talking-to-edmond.text: Not good at all my friend. It's Elena, she's been taken...

starting-out-talking-to-edmond.speaker: Edmond
starting-out-talking-to-edmond.text: The Knights of Ardougne. They claimed she was inciting rebellion against the king. Apparently she's been going around telling people that the plague isn't real...

starting-out-talking-to-edmond.player: Oh dear... This is a problem.

starting-out-talking-to-edmond.speaker: Edmond
starting-out-talking-to-edmond.text: Is there anything you can do to help us? It feels wrong to ask given what you've done for us before, but we're desperate.

starting-out-talking-to-edmond.prompt: Start the Song of the Elves quest?

steps.player: I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding. Let me try talking to the king.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Thank you friend.

steps.player: I can't help I'm afraid.

starting-out-talking-to-alrena.speaker: Alrena
starting-out-talking-to-alrena.text: Edmond tells me you're helping Elena again. Thank you so much.

talking-to-the-king.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king.text: Hello [player name]. What can I do for you?

talking-to-the-king.player: I'm here to talk about Elena, apparently she's been imprisoned.

talking-to-the-king.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king.text: That she has. She was making some heinous accusations.

talking-to-the-king.player: Right... But you and I both know that she's right, the plague is fake.

talking-to-the-king.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king.text: That's not the point. As I've explained to you before, the plague is a necessary evil. We can't have her exposing the truth and risking everything.

talking-to-the-king.player: But King Tyras is dead, what exactly are we risking?

talking-to-the-king.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king.text: My brother may be dead but the Dark Lord is still a threat. Until that threat is gone, the plague must remain.

talking-to-the-king.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king.text: No. I can't take any risks. Now I'm afraid I have business to attend to. You should be on your way.

talking-to-the-king.player: I see. I guess I should let her father know.

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-him-again.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king-talking-to-him-again.text: Hello [player name]. What can I do for you.

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-him-again.speaker: King Lathas
talking-to-the-king-talking-to-him-again.text: We've been through this already. I will not have the girl freed. She is a threat to Ardougne and will remain imprisoned.

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-him-again.player: I see. I guess I should let her father know.

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.text: Sorry citizen. Only Knights of Ardougne are allowed in the prison.

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.text: Hello there citizen. What can I do for you?

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.text: These stairs lead to the Ardougne Prison. It's home to thieves, murderers and everything in between.

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.player: Sounds lovely. Can I go in?

talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
talking-to-the-king-talking-to-the-knigh.text: I'm afraid not citizen. Only the Knights of Ardougne are allowed into the prison and I can see that you are no knight.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Hello there. Have you spoken to the king yet?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: I have.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: And?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: He won't be freeing her I'm afraid.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: But why? I know all this plague business has got her a bit emotional, but can't he see that she's just upset?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: He said she was a threat to Ardougne.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: A threat? But she's no danger to anyone. Why does he think that way?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Well the thing is...

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: What?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Well... She's right. The plague is a lie. That's why the king had her imprisoned. He was afraid she'd expose the truth.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: The plague is a lie? What do you mean the plague is a lie?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: I guess I have some explaining to do.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: You most certainly do.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Well, it all started after I freed Elena from West Ardougne. As you can imagine, she was still keen on helping the plague victims and asked me to help her find a cure.
We sent some samples to her old teacher, Guidor in Varrock. He ran some tests and found out that the plague isn't actually real. I confronted the king on this and he admitted it.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: But why?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: The king told me that his brother, King Tyras, was corrupted by the Dark Lord while exploring the lands to the west.
As Tyras was the king of West Ardougne, King Lathas decided to cordon the city off to keep the rest of the world safe.
The plague was the excuse he gave for the quarantine.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: But that doesn't make any sense. Why not just tell the truth? Why lie to everyone and make up a plague? Something doesn't seem right about it all.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Well you're right about that. Turns out King Lathas was lying about that as well. But I'll get to that in a minute.
After confronting the king, he recruited me and tasked me with helping him stop Tyras. He had me travel through the Underground Pass into the elven forests of Tirannwn.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Elves? I wasn't even sure they existed anymore.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Well Tirannwn is full of them. In fact, they're currently in the middle of a civil war.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: An elven civil war? I'm going to need a drink after all of this. So what happened next?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: I met with an ally of King Lathas, an elf called Lord Iorwerth. He's the leader of one of the elven factions. With his help, I was successful in assassinating King Tyras.
With the job done, I returned to Ardougne. However, on my way back, I was intercepted by an elf named Arianwyn, the leader of the rebel elves opposing Lord Iorwerth.
He revealed the truth to me, that King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth are in fact the evil ones. Together they intend to summon this Dark Lord.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Just when I thought this story couldn't get any worse. The king is evil? Why?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: From what I can tell, King Lathas hated how his father split the kingdom, giving half to him and half to his brother. He wanted his brother dead from the start.
Not only that, he also wants to reclaim Camelot from King Arthur. I think he's hoping that this Dark Lord will help him.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: All of this, just because Lathas wants more land? What about this Lord Iorwerth, what's in it for him?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: I think he wants to use the Dark Lord to defeat the rebel elves and end the civil war. Apparently, it's been going on for hundreds of years.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: I see, this still doesn't explain why the plague was made up though.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Well since I learnt the truth, I've been helping the rebel elves fight back against King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth.
I recently discovered that Lord Iorwerth believes the secrets to summoning the Dark Lord lie within the Temple of Light beneath Ardougne.
The plague was made up to hide their mining operation beneath the city.
All the mourners are actually Iorwerth elves in disguise and the people who they claim have died of the plague are actually getting sent into the mines.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Goodness me Elena, what have you gotten yourself into?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Thank you for telling me the truth [player name]. I just wish you had told me sooner.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: If even half of what you say about King Lathas is true, then my daughter is in great danger. We need to help her.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: Do you have something in mind?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: I do. They're holding Elena in the city prison beneath the castle. You'll need to disguise yourself as a Knight of Ardougne, infiltrate the prison and find a way to free her.

steps.player: Why me?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: As much as I hate to admit it, I'm far too old to pass as a knight. It will have to be you.

steps.player: How do I get this disguise?

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: You'll need to get a steel platebody, some steel platelegs and a steel full helm. The plume on the helm will need dying red and you'll need a tabard for the platebody.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: My wife should be able to help you with the tabard. You'll have to check with her to see what she needs for it. Come back to me once you have everything and we'll discuss what to do next.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.speaker: Alrena
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.text: Edmond tells me you're helping Elena again. Thank you so much.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.player: It's not a problem. Do you think you could give me a hand with something?
I need to make a Knight of Ardougne tabard.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.speaker: Alrena
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.text: Hmmm, well that shouldn't be too hard for me to do. Could you bring me some silk and some purple dye please?
If the player already has the required items:

steps.player: Luckily for us, I have them both right here.

steps.speaker: Alrena
steps.text: Hmm, that is lucky.

steps.prompt: Give Alrena the items?

steps.player: Here you go.

steps.text: You give Alrena the silk and purple dye.

steps.speaker: Alrena
steps.text: Here you go, one tabard.
Alrena gives you a Knight of Ardougne tabard.

steps.player: You can't have them.

steps.speaker: Alrena
steps.text: Well I can't make your tabard then.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.text: If the player doesn't have the required items:

steps.player: Will do.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.speaker: Alrena
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.text: Hello there. Do you have the silk and purple dye yet?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.player: Not yet. I'll go and get them.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.speaker: Alrena
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.text: Hello there. Do you have the silk and purple dye yet?

steps.player: Here you go.

steps.text: You give Alrena the silk and purple dye.

steps.speaker: Alrena
steps.text: Here you go, one tabard.
Alrena gives you a Knight of Ardougne tabard.

steps.player: You can't have them.

steps.speaker: Alrena
steps.text: Well I can't make your tabard then.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.speaker: Alrena
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-al.text: Thank you so much for helping Elena. It means so much to Edmond and I.

making-a-knightly-disguise-using-tabard-.text: You add the tabard to your platebody, making a Knight of Ardougne platebody.

making-a-knightly-disguise-dying-the-ste.text: You dye the plume of your helm red, making a Knight of Ardougne helm.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: I've finished the disguise.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: If the player is wearing the disguise:

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Well you definitely look the part. Those guards will be totally fooled. Now get yourself down to the prison and see if you can find a way to free Elena. You'll find it beneath the castle.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Excellent, let's have a look at it.
Edmond inspects your disguise.
If the player has a Defence level of 5 or above:

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Yes, this should be perfect. Those guards will be totally fooled. Now get yourself down to the prison and see if you can find a way to free Elena. You'll find it beneath the castle.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: If the player has a Defence level of less than 5:

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: Yes, this should be perfect. Those platelegs are a bit dirty though, let me give them a polish for you.

steps.speaker: Edmond
steps.text: There you go. Now get yourself down to the prison and see if you can find a way to free Elena. You'll find it beneath the castle.

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.player: What should I be doing?

making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.speaker: Edmond
making-a-knightly-disguise-talking-to-ed.text: Take your disguise and head down to the prison to see what you can find out. You'll find it beneath the castle.

freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.text: Hello there fellow knight. Isn't today a wonderful day to be a Knight of Ardougne?

freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.player: I mean it's okay I suppose. The constant fear of some random adventurer murdering you and the fact that people are constantly picking your pockets isn't great. But hey ho, at least the benefits are good.

freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.text: That they are fellow knight, that they are.

freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.player: Anyway, can I go down these stairs?

freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
freeing-elena-talking-to-the-knight-of-a.text: Of course you can! You're a Knight of Ardougne! There is no place where you can't go.

freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison.text: You don't look much like a [Tim/Sue/Sam].

freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison.text: Hmm... Very well. As you were... [Tim/Sue/Sam]...

freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison-t.speaker: Knight of Ardougne
freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison-t.text: Hmm... Is your head working okay today [Tim/Sue/Sam]?

freeing-elena-upon-entering-the-prison-t.player: Of course, my head has never been better.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.text: [player name]? What are you doing here?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.player: Rescuing you of course. Your father told me you were here.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.text: Oh thank goodness. It's awful in here. The smell from that mugger...

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.player: So what happened Elena? How did you end up here?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.text: Oh it's quite the tale, but let's save it for until I'm out of here. What's your plan?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.player: Well I err... I don't really have one.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.text: You don't have a plan? But aren't you meant to be an adventurer? How do you normally do this sort of thing?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.player: To be honest, I usually just make it up as I go along.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.text: Well luckily for us I have something in mind myself. There's an iron grate at the back of this cell that looks like it leads into the sewers. If I had some sulphuric acid, I could melt through it and escape.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.player: But where do we get the sulphuric acid?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena.text: Thankfully it's pretty much essential in my line of work. I have some at my home, opposite my parents' house. You'll need to get it from my cabinet and bring it here. It's the thick clear liquid.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena-again.player: It's okay Elena, it's me again.

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena-again.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena-again.text: Ah [player name], thank goodness. How's it going?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena-again.player: What do I need to do again?

freeing-elena-talking-to-elena-again.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-talking-to-elena-again.text: Go to the cabinet in my home, opposite my parents' house. Find some sulphuric acid and bring it back here. It's the thick clear liquid.

freeing-elena-searching-her-cabinet.player: Now what did Elena say it looked like?

steps.text: If the player doesn't have a chemical in their inventory:
You take the chemical from the cabinet.
If the player already has a chemical in their inventory:
You take the chemical from the cabinet and return your other chemical.

freeing-elena-returning-to-elena.player: It's okay Elena, it's me again.

freeing-elena-returning-to-elena.speaker: Elena
freeing-elena-returning-to-elena.text: Ah [player name], thank goodness. How's it going?
You show Elena the chemical you found.
If the player obtained the wrong chemical:

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: No that's not right at all. You need some sulphuric acid. It's the thick clear liquid.

steps.player: Sorry, I'll try again.

freeing-elena-returning-to-elena.text: If the player obtained the correct chemical:

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Yes that's it! Hand it over please.

steps.player: Here you go.

steps.text: You give Elena the chemical.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Right, probably best you're not here when I escape. You should head back to my father.

steps.player: Will do. Good luck Elena. I'll see you soon.
No.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Now's not the time for games [player name]!

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.player: Good news Edmond, Elena is free.

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.speaker: Edmond
freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.text: I know, she already came by to let us know. Thank you so much for your help.

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.speaker: Edmond
freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.text: She's had to go into hiding to avoid recapture. She asked me to pass on the location though. It's the Rehnison household in West Ardougne.

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.player: Thanks Edmond. I'll go and see how she's doing.
Hi Edmond. Do you know where Elena is?

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.speaker: Edmond
freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.text: She's had to go into hiding to avoid recapture. She's hiding out at the Rehnison household in West Ardougne.

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.player: Thanks Edmond. I'll go and see how she's doing.

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.text: (Non-quest dialogue.)

freeing-elena-telling-edmond-the-good-ne.text: If the player is not wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Hello [player name]. I'm afraid I can't talk right now. There's an issue with an escaped prisoner that I need to deal with.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.speaker: Milli Rehnison
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.text: Elena's come to visit! Elena's come to visit!

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.player: I heard. Do you know where she is?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.speaker: Milli Rehnison
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.text: She said she had some top secret work to do. Mummy and daddy will know.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.speaker: Martha Rehnison
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.text: Ah yes she said you'd be coming. They're all downstairs. The trapdoor is hidden under the bed.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.speaker: Martha Rehnison
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.text: You mean you don't know? The resistance of course! You'd better head down, Elena will fill you in.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.player: Hello. Could you remind me where Elena is?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.speaker: Ted Rehnison
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-the-rehniso.text: She's downstairs. The trapdoor is hidden under the bed.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: There's a trapdoor hidden under the bed.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: [player name]!

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Elena! It's good to see you safe.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: And you [player name]. Thank you so much for helping to get me out of there.

options.text: Well I couldn't just leave you to rot. I care about you, Elena.

steps.player: Well I couldn't just leave you to rot. I care about you, Elena.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I care about you as well, [player name]. Thank you for not forgetting about me.

options.text: It's all in a day's work.

steps.player: It's all in a day's work.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: So what's going on Elena? Why are all these people here?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: This, [player name], is the Ardougne Resistance!

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: The Ardougne Resistance?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Yes! It all started when you told me the truth about the king. I realised that it would take more than just us two to overthrow him, so I started to find allies for us.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: I see, when were you planning on telling me?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Well I knew you were busy infiltrating the mourners so I didn't want to trouble you until we were all set up. We're just about there now though.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: So is this how you ended up in that prison?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: It is. It happened while I was trying to gather more support for us. I was trying to convince some people of the truth behind the plague, but they didn't believe me. They reported me and I was arrested not long after.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Well you've clearly been quite busy. I've also made some progress since we last spoke.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: With the mourners? What did you find out?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: The mourners have been searching for a temple under West Ardougne. There's an altar there that they want to use to summon the Dark Lord.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: That doesn't sound good at all.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Don't worry, I restored the safeguards on the temple so they shouldn't be able to get in.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Ah, that's good to hear. Do you think we're safe now?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: For now, but we can't rule out King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth finding another way.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Well we can't do anything about Lord Iorwerth, your elf friends will have to sort him out. But if we get our way, Lathas might not be king for much longer.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: So what's your plan?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: You've met Councillor Halgrive before, right? He's been helping us put a plan together.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Good to see you [player name]. Allow me to run you through what we have so far.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: So unluckily for us, the king has total control over the Paladins and the Knights of Ardougne. With them, he has a large army at his disposal, one we cannot hope to stand against.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: But you're a councillor, can't you do anything about that?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: The council serves the king I'm afraid, we can't overrule his decisions. Nor can we take power from him. What we can do however, is step in if the king becomes unfit for rule.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: But the king is a traitor, surely that's enough reason.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: It is, but right now it's our word against his. And as you've already seen with Elena, he is keen to keep us silent.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Before I was arrested, we'd hoped to gather enough support among the people to be able to peacefully remove the king from power. Sadly, we've not been able to convince many of them.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: It's no surprise, really. The king has created a clever lie with the plague, one that's easy for people to believe.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Councillor Halgrive has come up with an alternative way to gather support. I can't pretend I totally approve of it, but it seems to be our only option.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: We need people to see the king for what he really is. They're clearly not going to believe us when it comes to the plague, so we'll have to resort to some dirtier tactics.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: When Elena told me about how you freed her from the prison, it gave me an idea...

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: With your disguise, you can appear to be working directly for the king. Any actions you perform in that disguise will seem like they were ordered by him.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: I see where this is going. If I upset people while dressed as a Knight of Ardougne, they'll blame the king.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: And once they are upset, they'll be far more likely to believe what we have to say.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: You can probably see why I'm not a fan now. If we're to remove the king, it should mark a new start for Ardougne. But if that's all built on a lie, are we any better than the king himself?

options.text: I agree, this is a dangerous path to follow.

steps.player: I agree, this is a dangerous path to follow.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: It is, and yet it seems to be the only path open to us. I fear the danger of inaction could harm the people far more than a few small lies.

options.text: It's not good, but it might be our only option.

steps.player: It's not good, but it might be our only option.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: I agree. I fear the danger of inaction could harm the people far more than a few small lies.

options.text: Who cares, it's for the good of the people.

steps.player: Who cares, it's for the good of the people.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: But who are we to decide that?

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: There is no perfect answer here. However, I fear the danger of inaction could harm the people far more than a few small lies.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: You're right, it just makes me feel uncomfortable, all of this.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: So, [player name], are you willing to help us?

steps.player: I am.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Excellent, let's get to work then. Wear your Knight of Ardougne disguise and use it to turn people against the king in East Ardougne.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: You'll want to build support in West Ardougne as well but the knights aren't allowed here. You can use your mourner disguise instead though.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: As you turn people against the king, we'll be on hand to convince them of our cause. If we aim to recruit 80 people from across both parts of Ardougne, we should have quite the army.

steps.player: What sort of things should I do?

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Anything that upsets people really. I suspect some of the others here will have a few suggestions for you. Just keep an eye out for suitable opportunities.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I'll keep track of how many people we've recruited, just let me know if you need an update.

steps.player: Right, I'd better get started then.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Good luck.

options.text: I need to think about this.

steps.player: I need to think about this.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Of course, it is a big ask. We'll be here once you have decided.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Carla/Jethick/Kilron/Omart
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: You'd better speak to Elena, she'll fill you in on what's happening here.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: What do I need to do again?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: We need to recruit people into our resistance so that we can overthrow the king. Elena can tell you how many people we've recruited.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Your role in this is to increase hatred for the king amongst the people. That will allow us to recruit them to our cause.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: What sort of things should I do?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Disguise yourself appropriately and perform any actions that cause upset with the citizens. With your disguise, people will think you are acting on the orders of the king.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: For East Ardougne, you'll need a Knight of Ardougne disguise. For West Ardougne, you'll want a mourner disguise.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: If you need any suggestions on what to do, ask the others here and see if they have anything for you.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Okay, thanks for the help.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Hey. We haven't recruited anyone into the resistance yet. You should speak to the others if you need help getting started.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Elena
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Hey. We've recruited [number] people into the resistance so far. We still need [number] more.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Hey there. Do you have any suggestions for this uprising of ours?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Carla
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: I bet people would get pretty angry if they had their food taken away. You could burn the food stores in West Ardougne and claim it's to protect people from the plague.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Won't people be willing to accept that though if they think it's preventing the plague spreading?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Carla
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Some will, but don't forget that it was the authorities that supplied the food in the first place. People will soon get angry if they think that not enough care is being taken with the food.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Ahh I see, that does make sense. I wonder if I can do something similar in East Ardougne as well.
Hey Jethick, got any ideas on how to increase hatred for the king?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Jethick
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: An increase in taxes would definitely cause some anger, especially if it seems that the king is making personal gain. No one likes the idea of the rich getting richer.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Good thinking, what's the best way to spread that sort of news?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Jethick
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: You could target the citizens themselves but that would be slow going. I'd recommend going for shopkeepers instead, that will impact more people in less time.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: Great, thanks for the help.
Hey, do you two know of any ways I can cause anger at the king?

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Omart
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: We did have an idea. With the plague, lots of people are worried for their health. We could take advantage of that.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Kilron
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: There's not many doctors and nurses around here. You've got Nurse Sarah in West Ardougne and Doctor Orbon in East Ardougne but that's about it.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.speaker: Omart
meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.text: Imagine if the king made a new law stating that all doctors and nurses in Ardougne had to retrain. They'd be out of action for months.

meet-the-ardougne-resistance-planning-a-.player: People wouldn't like that at all, thanks both.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.speaker: Priest
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.text: Taxes? Look at this place, do you think I can afford to pay any taxes?

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.player: Fighting the plague isn't cheap, the money needs to come from somewhere.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: As if life in this city couldn't get any worse. Where am I going to find the money?

steps.player: That's for you to work out. The first payment is to be collected soon.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: A knight wouldn't be telling me this, they're not allowed in West Ardougne. I don't know who you really are, but you should leave.

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: Citizens don't decide new taxes. You should leave.

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.text: You set fire to the food store.

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: What are you doing? The people need that food!

steps.player: Sorry, but we have reason to believe the food is contaminated. This is for the good of everyone.

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: But people will starve!

steps.player: I'm just doing my job. You should take it up with the king if you don't like it.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: If the player is not wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-re.player: I have some orders from the king for you.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-re.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Nurse Sarah
steps.text: Orders?

steps.player: Yes. The king is concerned about the plague spreading into East Ardougne. He has ordered that all doctors and nurses retrain to ensure they are capable of dealing with the plague.

steps.speaker: Nurse Sarah
steps.text: But I don't have time to retrain! The people here need me! Who will help them if I'm gone?

steps.player: I'm sure the king considered all of that before making his decision.

steps.speaker: Nurse Sarah
steps.text: Well he may be king but he clearly doesn't have a clue about health. This could be disasterous for the city!

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-re.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Nurse Sarah
steps.text: You knights aren't allowed in West Ardougne. You should leave.

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-re.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Nurse Sarah
steps.text: I don't take orders from citizens. Now I have work to be doing.

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: You set fire to the food store.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.speaker: Woman
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: You're burning the food! We need that food!

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.player: We believe the food is contaminated with the plague. This is for your own safety.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.speaker: Woman
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: We'll starve without it though! You can't do this!

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.speaker: Woman
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: I'll make sure everyone hears about this!

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.speaker: Chadwell
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-ta.text: Good day. What can I get you?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Chadwell
steps.text: New taxes? What are you talking about?

steps.player: The plague isn't easy to contain. New funds are needed to help the effort.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Chadwell
steps.text: But I barely make any money here. I can't afford to pay new taxes.

steps.player: Sorry, but the king himself gave the order. The first payment is due soon.

steps.speaker: Chadwell
steps.text: The people won't allow this to continue!
If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Chadwell
steps.text: Hang on, I know you knights aren't allowed in West Ardougne. You're an imposter! Get out!

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

steps.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Chadwell
steps.text: And why would a citizen be the one telling me this? Don't waste my time.

steps.player: I should probably wear my mourner disguise before doing that.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: You set fire to the food store.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.speaker: Clerk
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: What do you think you're doing?

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.player: The king has ordered us to burn this food. It could be contaminated with the plague.

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.speaker: Clerk
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: But that food is for the people. Without it they will starve!

causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.speaker: Clerk
causing-an-insurrection-west-ardougne-se.text: A lot of people are going to be angry about this!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Silk merchant
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: I buy silk. If you ever want to sell any silk, bring it here.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Silk merchant
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: New taxes? What new taxes?

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: Taxes on all market stalls. The order comes from the king himself.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Silk merchant
steps.text: Well I'll need to up my prices. A lot of people won't be happy about this.

steps.player: Probably not, but they'll just have to live with it. These taxes are needed for the good of the city. Someone will come to collect the tax from you soon.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Silk merchant
steps.text: The king wouldn't send a mourner to tell me this. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Silk merchant
steps.text: The king wouldn't send a citizen to tell me this. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Baker
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Good day [Sir/Madame]. Would you like some nice freshly baked bread? Or perhaps a nice piece of cake?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: What are you on about? New taxes?

steps.player: The plague isn't cheap to combat. The king has decreed that new taxes be introduced to help with the funding.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: I appreciate the need to combat the plague but this is a foolish move. My food feeds a lot of people, they'll be furious to hear about this.

steps.player: Better than getting the plague though. Your first payment is due soon, so you'd better be ready.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: You mourners may deal with the plague, but I know you have nothing to do with taxes. Now leave me alone!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: Citizens have nothing to do with taxes. Leave me alone!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Baker
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Good day [Sir/Madame]. Would you like some nice freshly baked bread? Or perhaps a nice piece of cake?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: New taxes? What new taxes?

steps.player: The king has ordered that new taxes be introduced to help fund the fight against the plague.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: The food I provide helps to feed this city! People won't be happy when I have to increase my prices!

steps.player: Sorry, it's needed though. The first payment is due soon, make sure you're ready.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: Just because you mourners handle the plague doesn't mean you get to make new taxes. Go away!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Baker
steps.text: Citizens don't deal with taxes. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Silver merchant
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Silver! Silver! Best prices for buying and selling in all Kandarin!

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Silver merchant
steps.text: New taxes? What are you on about?

steps.player: The king has called for a tax on luxury items. Your stall is included.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Silver merchant
steps.text: Well that is unacceptable! I will have to increase my prices. I've produced silver for the king himself before but don't expect me to do that again!

steps.player: As you wish, but you'll still need to pay. Your first instalment will be collected soon.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Silver merchant
steps.text: The king wouldn't send a mourner to tell me this. Clear off!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Silver merchant
steps.text: The king wouldn't send a citizen to tell me this. Clear off!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Gem merchant
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Here, look at my lovely gems.

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Gem merchant
steps.text: What new taxes?

steps.player: The king has called for a tax on luxury items like the ones you sell.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Gem merchant
steps.text: But the king is one of my biggest customers! I hope he realises that I'll have to increase my prices and he won't be exempt from that!

steps.player: I'm sure the king has good reason. I will return to collect your first payment soon.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Gem merchant
steps.text: I don't think the king would send a mourner to tell me this. Go away!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Gem merchant
steps.text: I don't think the king would send a citizen to tell me this. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Fur trader
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Would you like to trade in fur?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Fur trader
steps.text: What new taxes?

steps.player: By order of the king, all market stalls are to be taxed to help fund his new castle market.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Fur trader
steps.text: His new castle market? So he's taxing us to help him set up a competing market? This is outrageous!

steps.player: Well he's the king so he can do what he wants. Your first payment will be collected soon.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Fur trader
steps.text: And he sent a mourner to inform us? Go away!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Fur trader
steps.text: And he sent a citizen to inform us? Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Spice seller
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Are you interested in buying or selling spice?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Spice seller
steps.text: What are you on about?

steps.player: Taxes on all market stalls. It's to help fund a new market at the castle.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Spice seller
steps.text: A new market could put me out of business! Why should I help fund it?

steps.player: Because it's the law, refusing to pay is treason. Your first payment is due soon, so I suggest you prepare for it.

steps.speaker: Spice seller
steps.text: I will make sure the people hear about this!
If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Spice seller
steps.text: A mourner wouldn't be sent to tell me this. Go away!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Spice seller
steps.text: A citizen wouldn't be sent to tell me this. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Town Crier
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Hear ye! Hear ye! Player Moderators massive help to RuneSc-

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Town Crier
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Oh, hello citizen. Are you here to find out about Player Moderators? Or perhaps would you like to know about the laws of the land?

options.text: Tell me about the Rules of Conduct.
Could you help me tell people about some new taxes?

steps.player: Could you help me tell people about some new taxes?

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Town Crier
steps.text: New taxes? You know that people won't be happy about that, right?

steps.player: I know, it's the king's orders though. The castle is in need of repairs and more funds are required.

steps.speaker: Town Crier
steps.text: As you wish, I will make sure the people know. Just know that I'll be sending them right to the king if they get angry.
If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Town Crier
steps.text: New taxes? I know that mourners don't have anything to do with taxes. Please allow me to get on with my work.
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Town Crier
steps.text: New taxes? A citizen wouldn't have anything to do with taxes. Please allow me to get on with my work.

options.text: Can you give me a handy tip please?

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Zenesha
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Hello there! I sell plate mail bodies, are you interested?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Zenesha
steps.text: I'm already paying my taxes though?

steps.player: These are new ones. They are to help pay for the king's upcoming visit to Great Kourend.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Zenesha
