steps.text: Well I don't see why I have to pay for that! If the king can't afford the trip, then maybe he shouldn't be going!

steps.player: It's an important diplomatic trip I'm afraid so it has to go ahead. The first payment will be collected soon.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Zenesha
steps.text: And he's getting a mourner to tell me this? Nice try.
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Zenesha
steps.text: And he's getting a citizen to tell me this? Nice try.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Estate agent
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Hello. Welcome to the Gielinor Housing Agency! What can I do for you?

options.text: Can you move my house please?
Can you redecorate my house please?
I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Estate agent
steps.text: But the Gielinor Housing Agency doesn't pay taxes here! It's part of our business agreement with the king!

steps.player: These taxes are not included in that agreement. They're new emergency taxes related to the plague.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Estate agent
steps.text: Well this is just no good. If the king does not intend to honour his arrangement with us, we may well take our business elsewhere!

steps.player: You can do that, but while you're in Ardougne you must pay the tax. The first payment will be due soon.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Estate agent
steps.text: And a mourner is the one telling me this. I don't think so.
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Estate agent
steps.text: And a citizen is the one telling me this. I don't think so.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Probita
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Welcome to the pet insurance bureau. How can I help you?

options.text: I've lost a pet. Have you got it?
I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Probita
steps.text: What are you on about? I already pay my taxes.

steps.player: The king has ordered some new taxes to help fund his extensive collection of gnomish ornaments. Everyone has to contribute.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Probita
steps.text: Gnomish ornaments? Why can't the king pay for his own ornaments? He's got enough money as it is!

steps.player: The law has already been passed so it's not up for debate. Your first payment is expected soon.

steps.speaker: Probita
steps.text: I'll make sure people hear about this!
If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Probita
steps.text: And why would he send a mourner to tell me this? Stop lying and get out!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Probita
steps.text: And why would he send some random citizen to tell me this? Stop lying and get out!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Aemad/Kortan
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Hello there. You've come to the right place if you're looking for adventurer's equipment.

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.speaker: Aemad/Kortan
steps.text: New taxes? What new taxes?

steps.player: The castle is in dire need of repairs, the taxes are to help fund that. They've been ordered by the king himself.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Aemad/Kortan
steps.text: Ordered by the king? This is preposterous! We'll have to increase our prices to afford this, people will be furious!

steps.player: Sorry, but rules are rules. The first payment is due soon so make sure you're ready.

steps.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Aemad/Kortan
steps.text: Ordered by the king? What a load of rubbish! You mourners seem to think you own the place. Well you don't! Now clear off!
If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Aemad/Kortan
steps.text: Ordered by the king? What a load of rubbish! I can see you're not one of his people. Stop fooling around and get lost!

options.text: No, I've come to the wrong place.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Priest
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Peace be with you, friend.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Priest
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Taxes? But this is a holy church of Saradomin, we are exempt from taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: More funding is needed to hold back the plague. The church needs to help as well.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: We'll need to use the donations from the congregation. We were hoping to use that money to build an orphanage for those who lost their parents to the plague.

steps.player: Sorry, but the king has given the order. The first payment is due soon.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: It is not the job of a mourner to deal with taxes. Now, if there's nothing else, I must get to work.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: It is not the job of a citizen to deal with taxes. Now, if there's nothing else, I must get to work.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-re.speaker: Doctor Orbon
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-re.text: Hello there. Can't stop to talk I'm afraid, I'm very busy right now.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-re.player: I have some orders from the king for you.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-re.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Doctor Orbon
steps.text: What are you on about?

steps.player: The king is concerned about the plague spreading. He has ordered that all doctors and nurses in the city retrain to ensure they are capable of dealing with the plague.

steps.speaker: Doctor Orbon
steps.text: Retrain? But that will take months! Who will help the people if there are no doctors around? This is a foolish move!

steps.player: Well the king's word is law so there's little point arguing.

steps.speaker: Doctor Orbon
steps.text: Well don't blame me when there's no one to help the king if he falls ill!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-re.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Doctor Orbon
steps.text: I don't take orders from citizens. Now I really must get to work.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-re.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Bartender
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Would you like to buy a drink?

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Bartender
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: Taxes? What do you mean?

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: By order of the king, all establishments such as this must now pay an extra beer tax.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: Beer tax? My patrons work hard for the city of Ardougne! They come here to unwind after a long day. This is plain disrespect to the work they do!

steps.player: It's also plain disrespect to defy the king's laws so you'd better be ready to pay up. We'll be back to collect soon.

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: You haven't heard the last of this!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: And why would a mourner be telling me this? Clear off!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: You don't represent the king! Clear off!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Richard
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: New taxes? What for?

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: The king has ordered an increase in taxes on all farms in the area. It's due to a lack of care when it comes to the plague.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.text: Lack of care? This is about Farmer Brumty and his sheep isn't it? That has nothing to do with us here! Why should we pay for his mistakes?

steps.player: Sorry, it's the word of the king so you'll have to pay up. The first instalment will be collected soon.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit:

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.text: You mourners may serve the king, but you don't have the power to enforce that. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.text: You don't have the power to enforce that. Go away!

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.speaker: Banker
causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: New taxes?

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.player: Yes, they've been ordered by the king to help him buy a new throne.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing Knight of Ardougne armour:

steps.speaker: Banker
steps.text: No problem. However, we first need to tax you for your bank usage.

steps.player: Wait... what?

steps.speaker: Banker
steps.text: Well it's only fair right? You tax us so we tax you.

steps.player: On second thoughts... forget I said anything.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is wearing a mourner's outfit

steps.speaker: Banker
steps.text: Mourners don't deal with taxes. Nice try.

causing-an-insurrection-east-ardougne-ta.text: If the player is not wearing either:

steps.speaker: Banker
steps.text: Citizens don't deal with taxes. Nice try.

causing-an-insurrection-once-enough-peop.player: That should be enough people recruited, I'd better go and let Elena know.

vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-a.speaker: Carla/Jethick/Kilron/Omart
vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-a.text: Good work out there. You'd better speak to Elena and Councillor Halgrive, they'll go over the next steps with you.

vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.text: Welcome back [player name], and good work out there. Thanks to you we now have a force that can stand up to Lathas and his armies.

vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.text: Now comes the difficult part though. Before we move against the king, we need to deal with his allies, the mourners.

vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.text: We now significantly outnumber the mourners, we should be able to drive them out of the city. The main focus will be their headquarters. Without their leadership, they'll soon retreat.

vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.speaker: Elena
vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.text: We have the numbers, but the mourners are better trained and better equipped. You should make sure you're ready before we begin. There will be bloodshed, on both sides.

options.text: Are you sure you're okay with this Elena?

steps.player: Are you sure you're okay with this Elena?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I don't like it, but I know it's the only way. I appreciate the concern though, thank you friend.

steps.player: It's necessary bloodshed though.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: It is, it's just a shame there isn't another way.

options.text: A bit of blood doesn't scare me.

steps.player: A bit of blood doesn't scare me.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: No... But you're not the one I'm worried about.

vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
vive-la-ardougne-r-volution-talking-to-e.text: Are you ready to begin [player name]?
You are about to begin the Battle of West Ardougne. Any items left in the battle, including upon death, will be lost.

steps.player: I'm ready.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I will send word around to make sure our people are prepared. Good luck everyone.

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: This is it! The plague of West Ardougne has gone on for long enough, today is the day of plague's end!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-af.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-af.text: Good work! Let's head downstairs and deal with the rest of them!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-up.speaker: Essyllt
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-up.text: You! I knew you were trouble! Well don't worry, Lord Iorwerth will learn of your betrayal!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-af.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-af.text: We did it! Now we'd better get out of here!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: Excellent work with those mourners. I suspect the king might be getting a little worried now.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: We'll need to move fast. He's probably already planning his retaliation.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: He'll likely expect us to take some time to recuperate after that battle. He won't expect us to hit him right away.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.player: So let me guess, that's exactly what we're going to do?

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: Indeed, we hit the castle now before they have a proper chance to prepare for us.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.player: Even if they're not prepared, the castle will still be well defended.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: Yes, but thanks to our victory in West Ardougne, some of the knights are starting to question their loyalties. I've taken advantage of this and made arrangements to ensure the gates are open to us.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: Make no mistake, it will still be a tough fight, but it's a fight we should be able to win.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: We can afford to take a little bit of time to ensure everyone has resupplied so feel free to come back later if you're not ready yet. Just don't take too long.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-west-ardougne-re.text: Let me know when you are ready to begin [player name].
You are about to begin the Battle of East Ardougne. Any items left in the battle, including upon death, will be lost.

steps.player: I'm ready.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I never thought this day would come. We're finally going to deal with that traitor once and for all!

steps.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
steps.text: Let's show him what it means to cross the people of Ardougne!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-east-ardougne-af.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-east-ardougne-af.text: Look's like that's the last of them! Good work everyone!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Omart
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: Look who we found hiding in a wardrobe.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: So you're a coward as well as a traitor! What a pathetic excuse of a man you are.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: King Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: You call me a traitor? I am your king! The traitors here are the ones standing before me.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: Give it a rest, it's over. We know the truth.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: King Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: And what truth might that be?

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: You let an enemy into our city and covered it up by lying to your people.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: King Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: And I'm sure you'd never do something like that. Don't think I didn't hear about the lies you spread about me.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: There's also your brother. Murdered on your orders.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: King Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: You are aware that his killer stands with you, are you not?

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: [player name] is innocent in this. You manipulated them for your own gain.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: King Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: Oh don't you go pretending they're innocent! They're nothing more than a mercenary. All they care about is the big pot of gold at the end.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: King Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: They betrayed me! Before long, they'll betray you as well!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: Enough! You're finished Lathas. The people will decide your fate. I don't expect them to be kind.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-it-s-treason-the.text: [player name], do you have any questions for the king before we take him away? I suspect you won't get another chance to ask them.

options.text: Why were you helping Lord Iorwerth?

steps.player: Why were you helping Lord Iorwerth?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: My father, King Ulthas, once ruled over a united Kandarin. I was his eldest son, the kingdom was my birthright! But my fool of a father took that from me.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: When King Arthur and his knights arrived in our lands, my father granted them the castle of Camelot, ousting the loyal subjects that previously lived there.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Not only that, but he also declared that the kingdom be jointly ruled by my brother and I, rather than giving it to me as he should have.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: When I ascended to my half-throne, I promised myself that I would unite this kingdom again, no matter the cost.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: That's why I made the deal with Lord Iorwerth. In return for access to West Ardougne, he agreed to help me kill my brother and drive out King Arthur.

options.text: Did you know what the mourners were doing?

steps.player: Did you know what the mourners were doing?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: In West Ardougne? They were searching for some sort of temple. According to Lord Iorwerth, the power there would be essential in summoning Zamorak, the Dark Lord.

steps.player: So you knowingly allied with a group of Zamorakians?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Of course I did! I prayed to Saradomin that he would help unite my kingdom again. He chose not to reply. I turned to the Dark Lord instead.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: With Zamorak at my side, nothing would stand between me and Camelot!

options.text: Why did you kill your brother?

steps.player: Why did you kill your brother?

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Last I checked it was you that killed him, not me.

steps.player: You know what I mean.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: My brother was never meant to rule. The kingdom was mine by birthright! My father chose to give him half the kingdom, and he did a terrible job ruling it.

steps.speaker: King Lathas
steps.text: Have you seen West Ardougne? The city is a mess, and not because of the plague. That was my brother's doing. I may be a bad person, but make no mistake, my brother was no hero either.

options.text: We're done here, take him away.

steps.player: We're done here, take him away.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: Citizens of Ardougne! Before you stands Lathas Ardignas: a traitor, a murderer and a liar!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: He has been found guilty of numerous heinous crimes, and will now face judgement for his sins!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Elena
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: So this is it. After all this time, Lathas is finally going to pay for what he's done. It's like I should feel something, but I just feel empty.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: Lathas Ardignas, as decided by the people of Ardougne, you are hereby sentenced to death!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: Do you have any final words?

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: How dare you insult me like this! You can't kill me! I am the rightful king! Every person here is under my rule!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: The people have passed their judgement, you are not a king any more.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: Then you are all traitors, and you will all pay with your lives!

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Lathas
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: In the name of Zamorak I curse you, each and every one of you!
Lathas is killed by the executioner, and two Hooded Figures knock the player and Elena out.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: Well hello again adventurer! How are you today?

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: Councillor Halgrive
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: Not too bad, I've a lot to do though. King Lathas left plenty of things for us to clean up.

battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.speaker: King Thoros
battle-of-two-ardougnes-killing-of-a-kin.text: On behalf of everyone in Ardougne, I thank you for your help adventurer. I'm afraid I don't have time to talk, my predecessor has left me with a lot of work to do.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: So you finally decided to show your true colours, how disappointing.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Essyllt
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: We should have killed them both when we had the chance.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Hmm, perhaps.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: You know, after you killed King Tyras, I thought you might have some potential. Given time, we might have properly welcomed you into our ranks. You'd have been the first human among us.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.player: Well I'm glad to have disappointed you. I don't work with murderers.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: No? You seemed more than happy to kill King Tyras when it suited you. Burnt him alive in the middle of his own camp if I recall.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Elena
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: [player name] is innocent! You lied to them!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Lied? I told your friend here that King Tyras was an invader into our lands. Last time I checked, that was the truth.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.player: Maybe, but you conveniently missed out the part about you trying to summon the Dark Lord.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Ah, I see you have been led astray. You think we are the evil ones, but our cause is the true one. You think we are murderers, but we are in fact saviours.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: You think you're the hero of this story, but you're not...

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Elena
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: You're mad!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Essyllt
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Let me deal with them, my lord. They've caused us enough trouble.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: They may still be of use to us. Lock them away for now. Give them time to think on their choices.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Essyllt
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Hmm, as you wish.
Arianwyn and several Rebel Archers appear, killing some of the Iorwerth soldiers.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: That's enough Lord Iorwerth, let them go!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Brave of you to come here Arianwyn, but foolish. We have you outnumbered.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Don't be so sure. We fight with the strength of ten of your warriors.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Perhaps, but I don't believe you're the type to throw lives away without need. Instead, why don't we discuss this like reasonable people.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: We don't have anything to discuss with you, you Zamorakian scum!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Zamorakian? You don't really think we'd support that monster do you? I'm afraid to say that you're quite mistaken.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Don't try to manipulate us with your lies. We know all about your plot with King Lathas to summon the Dark Lord.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Ah, that. Well now that King Lathas is dead, I suppose there's no better time to reveal the truth.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: It was just a ruse I'm afraid. A lie we told King Lathas to get him on our side.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: What are you on about?

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: We needed access to West Ardougne so we needed the support of the king. Once we found out about his hidden worship of Zamorak, it seemed like an obvious lie to tell.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: I have no more love for Zamorak than you do. I've only ever served one god, the same one as you, Seren.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: You're lying! You wanted to use the Temple of Light to summon Zamorak!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: I can see why you'd think that, but you are mistaken. You're right to say that the temple is key to summoning a god, but that god is not Zamorak, it's Seren.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: That's impossible! Seren is dead!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: I thought the same once. That was until I managed to break one of the seals within the Grand Library.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: That's how I discovered the truth. A part of Seren lives on, trapped within the Temple of Light.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: I don't believe you!

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: A shame. You're better than this Arianwyn, I hope in time you will see that.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Morvran
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: What should we do with them, my lord.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Let them go. Let it be known that the Iorwerth clan is not without mercy.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Essyllt
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Are you sure about this?

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Yes. But make no mistake Arianwyn, if you and your rebels interfere with our affairs again, I will not be so forgiving.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Now, I suggest you leave, before I change my mind.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Arianwyn
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: This isn't over!
The player, Elena, Arianwyn and the rebels leave.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Essyllt
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: This is a bad idea.

face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
face-to-face-with-lord-iorwerth.text: Don't be so sure. They may not know it yet, but the rebels could be of great use to us...

retreating-to-lletya.speaker: Arianwyn
retreating-to-lletya.text: Ah [player name], there you are. We thought it best to let you rest for a bit after everything that happened earlier.

retreating-to-lletya.player: Thanks Arianwyn, I definitely needed it. And thank you for saving us back there, I don't know what we'd have done if you hadn't shown up.

retreating-to-lletya.speaker: Arianwyn
retreating-to-lletya.text: I suspect you wouldn't have been around to have this conversation. You played a dangerous game in Ardougne. I fear you may not have considered the outcome of that.

retreating-to-lletya.player: People were dying Arianwyn, we couldn't do nothing.

retreating-to-lletya.speaker: Arianwyn
retreating-to-lletya.text: Of course not, but we have no idea how Lord Iorwerth will respond to this. The things he said when we freed you were... concerning...

retreating-to-lletya.player: You can say that again. What do you think he meant by it all?

retreating-to-lletya.speaker: Arianwyn
retreating-to-lletya.text: I'm not sure. It's something that we should discuss with the others.

retreating-to-lletya.speaker: Arianwyn
retreating-to-lletya.text: Could you do me a favour and fetch Ysgawyn. He's probably on the upper platforms. You should bring your friend Elena as well. I'm not sure where she is I'm afraid, Ysgawyn might know though.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.text: I am, what of it human?

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.player: Arianwyn has called a meeting. He asked me to come fetch you.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.text: I see, so now I'm meant to follow the orders of a human.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.player: It wasn't an order, it was just...

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.text: Make no mistake human, you may have Arianwyn and the others fooled but I know what you are.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.player: I don't know what you mean...

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.text: You're a menace. You claim you're here to help, but everywhere you go you leave a trail of bodies behind.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.text: Anyway, I'll come to this meeting, I'm in no place to deny Arianwyn. Just stay out of my way from here on out.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.player: Fine. Before you go, do you know where Elena is?

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-ysgawyn.text: The other human? I think she's by the pond to the south west. Now if you'll excuse me...

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-elena.player: So how are you doing, Elena?

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-elena.speaker: Elena
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-elena.text: I'm okay. So much has happened so fast, it's a lot to take in.

options.text: It is. I'm here for you if you need me though.

steps.player: It is. I'm here for you if you need me though.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Thanks, that means a lot.

steps.player: You'll get used to it.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I guess... I just don't know if I want to.

steps.player: Yeah, it's no small thing.

retreating-to-lletya-fetching-elena.speaker: Elena
retreating-to-lletya-fetching-elena.text: Anyway, I wanted to ask you something.

steps.player: Go ahead.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: The people of Ardougne, the elves here, you've spent a lot of time helping them. Why? What drives you, [player name]?

steps.player: I care about helping people.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: So even if you knew that you'd get nothing out of it yourself, you'd still continue to help these elves?

steps.player: Of course.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I suspect not many people would feel that way.

steps.player: Well I'm not like other people.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Clearly. Thank you for answering, I realise it's a pretty pointless question. I was curious to know how you felt though.

options.text: Well a reward's always nice, but yes.

steps.player: Well a reward's always nice, but yes.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I guess it's always nice to be rewarded. It's good to know that isn't all that matters to you though. I suspect not many people would feel that way.

steps.player: Well I'm not like other people.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Clearly. Thank you for answering, I realise it's a pretty pointless question. I was curious to know how you felt though.

options.text: Actually, I think I'd want a reward.

steps.player: Actually, I think I'd want a reward.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I guess it's always nice to be rewarded. You should be careful not to let that drive you though. Money can't buy everything, [player name].

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Well I've rambled on enough. Was there something you needed?

steps.player: Arianwyn has called a meeting. He'd like you to attend.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I'd better head over there then.
Elena leaves for the meeting.

options.text: People reward me for helping them.

steps.player: People reward me for helping them.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: So if you didn't think you'd get a reward, you'd stop helping these elves?

options.text: Yes, the reward is what matters.

steps.player: Yes, the reward is what matters.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: You should be careful of letting that drive you. Money can't buy everything, [player name].

options.text: Actually, I think I'd still help.

steps.player: Actually, I think I'd still help.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: So it's not just about the reward after all. It's nice to know that isn't all that matters to you. I suspect not many people would feel that way.

steps.player: Well I'm not like other people.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Clearly. Thank you for answering, I realise it's a pretty pointless question. I was curious to know how you felt though.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Well I've rambled on enough. Was there something you needed?

steps.player: Arianwyn has called a meeting. He'd like you to attend.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I'd better head over there then.
Elena leaves for the meeting.

options.text: I need to fix my mistakes.

steps.player: I need to fix my mistakes.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: So it's about what happened with King Tyras? Do you think you'd still help these elves if that hadn't happened?

steps.player: I think so.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: So it's not just guilt that's driving you, that's good to know. What happened with King Tyras was awful but you can't take too much blame, Lathas manipulated you.

options.text: No, I don't think I would.

steps.player: No, I don't think I would.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: So the only thing driving you is guilt? That doesn't seem healthy. Be careful that you don't carry the world on your shoulders, [player name]. It's not your fault that Lathas manipulated you.

steps.player: I'm not sure.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Hmmm, not something you've had to think about I guess. Just make sure that you don't carry the world on your shoulders, [player name]. It's not your fault that Lathas manipulated you.

steps.player: I know, thanks Elena.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Anyway, I've rambled on enough. Was there something you needed?

steps.player: Arianwyn has called a meeting. He'd like you to attend.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I'd better head over there then. Thanks for the talk.
Elena leaves for the meeting.

options.text: It's my duty to help people.

steps.player: It's my duty to help people.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Be careful of hiding behind duty, it won't stop people holding you accountable for your actions.

steps.player: I'm not sure.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Hmmm, not something you've had to think about I guess. It's worth considering though. We should all have something to drive us.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Anyway, was there something you needed?

steps.player: Arianwyn has called a meeting. He'd like you to attend.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I'd better head over there then.
Elena leaves for the meeting.

steps.player: Maybe later.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Fair enough. Was there something you needed?

steps.player: Arianwyn has called a meeting. He'd like you to attend.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I'd better head over there then.
Elena leaves for the meeting.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena.text: Hey [player name]. You should talk to Arianwyn when you're ready to begin.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-ysgawyn.player: Hey, I wanted to ask you...

the-first-meeting-talking-to-ysgawyn.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-talking-to-ysgawyn.text: No. Go away and talk to Arianwyn instead.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-ilfeen.speaker: Ilfeen
the-first-meeting-talking-to-ilfeen.text: Hey there. You should let Arianwyn know once you're ready to get started.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-eluned.speaker: Eluned
the-first-meeting-talking-to-eluned.text: Hey there [player name]. Arianwyn's leading this meeting so you should let him know when you're ready to start.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-islwyn.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-talking-to-islwyn.text: Good to see you [player name]. You should speak to Arianwyn when you're ready to begin.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Right, now that we're all here, let's get started.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: So, as I'm sure you've all heard, King Lathas of Ardougne is dead. He was overthrown by his subjects and executed soon afterwards.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: That's not all though, the mourners of West Ardougne have been driven out of the city. Lord Iorwerth no longer has any presence in Ardougne.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Let's not ignore the obvious, Arianwyn. Our supposed ally, [player name], helped lead the uprising. His actions may well have endangered us all.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ilfeen
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: But surely this is a good thing? With Ardougne lost to him, Lord Iorwerth no longer has access to the Temple of Light. Without that, he has no way to summon the Dark Lord.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: The temple was already secure. All this uprising has achieved is to anger the enemy.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: You say that like it's a bad thing, Ysgawyn. Last time I checked, we didn't care about upsetting our foe.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: I care about keeping our people alive, Islwyn!

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: And what about our people? While you sat here in your secure little village, we took action! We saved lives! But I guess you're too selfish to care about us.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Selfish? How dare you! You know nothing of the plight of the elves, girl. You'd do well to keep your mouth shut!

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: That's enough Ysgawyn. We can debate what's happened for days and still reach no conclusion. That is not why I called you all here. Instead, we need to plan what happens next.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Now, while freeing [player name] and Elena from the Iorwerth camp, we were confronted by Lord Iorwerth. He could have killed us all, but he let us go.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Eluned
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: He let you go? Why?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: His reasoning was disturbing. For a long time now, we've believed that Lord Iorwerth has been trying to summon Zamorak, the Dark Lord. However, he claimed otherwise.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ilfeen
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: But if not Zamorak, then who?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Seren.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Eluned
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Seren? But that's impossible, Seren is gone.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: He seems to think otherwise. He claimed that a part of Seren still lives, trapped within the Temple of Light. Apparently, he discovered this by breaking one of the nine seals within the Grand Library.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: That's impossible. He must be lying.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Sorry, but I don't understand what you mean by all of this. Who's Seren? What library?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Eluned
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Seren was our goddess, our guardian and our teacher. Everything we have, we owe to her. She helped us build the great city of Prifddinas, a place where all elves could live in harmony.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ilfeen
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: At the end of the God Wars, the gods were banished from this world. Seren didn't want to leave us though, she couldn't. She shattered herself into thousands of crystals. Those crystals are all we have left of her now.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: I see, I'm sorry to hear that.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: As for the Grand Library, it was a great archive of knowledge beneath Prifddinas. Pretty much everything there was open to all of elven kind.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: There was an exception to that though, the nine seals of Seren. The seals guarded the forbidden knowledge, that which only Seren herself could access.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.player: And Lord Iorwerth managed to break one of these seals.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: So he claims...

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Is there no way we can check?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: No. Prifddinas was lost to us. When Lord Iorwerth first took control of the city, my grandfather, Baxtorian, led an army to try and stop him.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: When that failed, Baxtorian and the other clan elders made one final ditch attempt to save Prifddinas. They sung the song of inversion to revert the entire city to a crystal seed.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Their plan worked, and the city was lost to Lord Iorwerth. However, it was lost to the rest of us as well, the Grand Library with it.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: What happened to Baxtorian?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: While he was fighting Lord Iorwerth, invaders took control of our kingdom to the east. They kidnapped Glarial, Baxtorian's wife.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Unable to find her, he sealed himself beneath the waterfall where they lived, never to be seen again.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.player: Baxtorian was king of the elves back then. Do you think he had access to the forbidden knowledge?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: It's not impossible I suppose. If anyone, it would have been him. Baxtorian was closer to Seren than any other elf, it's one of the reasons he was chosen to become king.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Baxtorian is gone though, even if he knew something, he can't help us now.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Don't be so sure. I never knew my grandfather, but my mother always told me that he wasn't the type for taking chances. If he knew something important, he'd have made sure it wouldn't have been lost with him.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: We can't possibly make a plan without knowing Lord Iorwerth's intentions. While unlikely to be true, this stuff about the library is all we have to go on.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: If Baxtorian left behind anything that could help us, we should try to find it.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Baxtorian kept everything of importance to him at his home within Baxtorian Falls. If we're going to find anything, it's probably there.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: [player name], you've been to Baxtorian Falls multiple times. You're the best person to take the lead on this.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Ysgawyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: You trust the human with this?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Let go of your pride, Ysgawyn. [player name] has proven his worth to us.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: I'd like to accompany you on this one [player name], it might be useful to have an elf with you.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Islwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Before her death, my mother passed down a book to me. It was written by my grandfather for his wife. You should take it with you. It might contain something of use.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Thank you Islwyn. While we're gone, the rest of you should focus on Lord Iorwerth. See if you can get any idea on what he's planning now that he's lost Ardougne. Just be careful.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Eluned
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: We always are. Good luck to you both.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: And you. Let's get started.
The others leave the meeting.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Thank you for agreeing to help us, [player name]. We owe a lot to you, even if some of us don't show it very well.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.player: You mean Ysgawyn? He is a bit rude.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Try not to be too judgemental. Ysgawyn's husband was killed by Essyllt, one of Lord Iorwerth's henchmen. Ysgawyn's never really been the same since.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.player: I've met Essyllt, he was the one in charge of the mourners in West Ardougne.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: He's a nasty piece of work. If you try hard enough, you can find something redeemable about most elves, even those that serve Lord Iorwerth.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: But Essyllt... He seems to take joy in the suffering of others, especially those unable to defend themselves.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: Enough about him though, we need to focus on Baxtorian Falls. I suggest we travel seperately, we can't be too careful at the moment.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.player: Makes sense, will you be okay getting there on your own?

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.text: I'm no expert on your lands but I should be fine. I just have a few things to gather before I depart.

the-first-meeting-the-first-meeting-begi.player: Well in that case, I'll meet you there.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-arianwyn-af.speaker: Arianwyn
the-first-meeting-talking-to-arianwyn-af.text: I just have a few things to gather before I depart for Baxtorian Falls. I'll meet you there.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.text: Hey [player name]. Good to see you.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.text: Pretty good. I've been thinking about that elf, Ysgawyn.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.player: Bit of an angry guy isn't he?

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.text: That's one way to put it. I can't say I approve of his attitude, but I appreciate he's seen a lot in this war.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.text: It's interesting, the elves have such long lifespans, we're just children compared to them. And yet, even with all their experience, they're still just as fickle as we are.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.player: I find most races are the same to be honest.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.text: Anyway, had any luck with Baxtorian Falls?

the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.speaker: Elena
the-first-meeting-talking-to-elena-after.text: I'll let you crack on then. We'll talk more later.

the-first-meeting-talking-to-ysgawyn-aft.player: Hey, I wanted to ask you...

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: Hello there [player name], glad to see you made it here okay.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: I must say, it feels strange to be back here, especially after all of this time.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: I was one of the elves born in Baxtorian's new kingdom. My family were close relations of Baxtorian, he invited us here a few times.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: Those were simpler times, happier times. After Baxtorian left to try and retake Prifddinas, my parents were among those who joined him. They never returned. I was still just a child at the time, alone and afraid.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.player: I'm sorry to hear that Arianwyn.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: This war has taken so much... From my people, and from yours. I'd give anything to see peace, anything to finally see Prifddinas with my own eyes.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: Sorry, now's not the time for this. We need to see if Baxtorian left anything of use behind.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: Here's that book that Islwyn gave us. Hopefully it has something of use in it.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: Arianwyn tries to give you a book but you don't have enough room to take it.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.text: Arianwyn gives you a book.

options.text: Do you believe what Lord Iorwerth said about Seren?

steps.player: Do you believe what Lord Iorwerth said about Seren?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: To be honest... I really don't know. It seems impossible, and yet...

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: No. It's just me being wishful. He's lying, he has to be.

steps.player: Wishful?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: By the time I was born, Seren was already gone from this world. All I know of her is the stories my parents told me.

steps.player: You wish you could have met her?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: I do, but that doesn't mean I should fall for the lies of Lord Iorwerth. Seren is gone, nothing can ever bring her back.

options.text: Do you think we'll find anything to help us here?

steps.player: Do you think we'll find anything to help us here?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: I won't lie, we're clutching straws here. We have nothing else to go on though, so we have to try.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Baxtorian was once king of the elves, anything he left behind might be of use.

steps.player: I'll crack on.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-talking-to-aria.text: We need to see if Baxtorian left anything of use behind. Maybe that book will be of use.

options.text: Do you believe what Lord Iorwerth said about Seren?
Do you think we'll find anything to help us here?

visiting-baxtorian-falls-placing-the-ite.text: You place the Adamant chainbody on the pillar. It disappears in a puff of smoke.
You place the Wine of zamorak on the pillar. It disappears in a puff of smoke.
You place the Nature rune on the pillar. It disappears in a puff of smoke.
You place the Black dagger on the pillar. It disappears in a puff of smoke.
You place the Cabbage on the pillar. It disappears in a puff of smoke.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.player: I'm [player name] and this is Arianwyn.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: Arianwyn... I remember that name. You grew up in my kingdom... I'm sorry about your family.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: I appreciate the sentiment, but please, I am no king anymore.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: Now I must ask... Glarial... Is there any news?

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: I... I see... It was always a lot to hope for...

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: If it's any consolation, [player name] moved her remains here, to be closer to you.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: That... That means a lot. Thank you. It is good to see that some humans still see elves as friends.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: No... I feel I've spent long enough here.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: Then I can take you back to Lletya. Your grandson, Islwyn, is there.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: Grandson? So Eirlys had a child? Does she still live as well?

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: No father should outlive their child. Forgive me Eirlys.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Baxtorian
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: Please, let us leave now. There is too much sadness for me here, too much pain. Once we arrive, you must tell me everything that has happened in my absence.

visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.speaker: Arianwyn
visiting-baxtorian-falls-baxtorian-lives.text: Very well, I will teleport us back to Lletya. You'll have to make your own way back I'm afraid, [player name].
Arianwyn teleports himself and Baxtorian back to Lletya.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Oh... Hello there. You'd probably best talk to Arianwyn.

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

steps.player: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: I see... Go ahead.

options.text: Why did you seal yourself away?

steps.player: Why did you seal yourself away?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: My Glarial... She mattered more to me than anything else, but she was lost to me. The enemy took her, so I searched far and wide to find her again.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: At times I came close, but in the end, I was too weak to carry on. I knew there was a chance she may live though, so I sealed myself away, hoping she would be the one to wake me.

steps.player: I see. I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: I thank you friend, but please, don't be. The burden is mine to bear.

options.text: What happened between you and Lord Iorwerth?

steps.player: What happened between you and Lord Iorwerth?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: To be honest, even today I know little of him. When I left Prifddinas to expand our kingdom into the east, he was but a child, with the Iorwerth clan ruled by his mother.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The first time I properly met him was after I heard about his takeover of the city. I led my forces through the Underground Pass and confronted him at the city gates.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: I tried to reason with him, but he had already decided that I was his enemy. We had the numbers and our forces were better skilled, so we tried to besiege the city.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Iorwerth forces had the strength and safety of the city walls though. They slowly whittled us down until we were too weak to carry on. We had no choice but to retreat.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: We fell back into the Underground Pass, intending to return to our kingdom in the east. Lord Iorwerth sent his forces in after us, hoping to wipe us out.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: We no longer had the strength in numbers, but we still outmatched the Iorwerth troops in skill and experience. We fought back while we retreated. Both sides suffered huge losses.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Eventually we managed to make it through to the other side. By then, there were few of us left. Lord Iorwerth had failed to wipe us out, but he knew we were beaten.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: While we were gone, an uprising had occurred in the eastern kingdom. We took our best fighters to Prifddinas, those that remained were unable to hold back the enemy.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: My wife was taken and most of my people were slaughtered. I turned my attention to finding my wife and getting the rest of my people to safety.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Lord Iorwerth became the least of my problems. I suspect he didn't consider me much of a threat at that point anyway.

steps.player: What was Seren like?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: She... She was wonderful. She taught us to better ourselves in every way possible. Everything we know, everything we are, it all came from her.

steps.player: I wish I could have met her.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: I feel very blessed to have been able to. The love she had for us, it's unlike anything I've ever seen.

steps.player: Sounds like she was pretty much perfect.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Well... not quite. Many of the elves alive now were not around when Seren was still with us. They only know her through the stories passed down to them. The stories don't tell everything though.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Seren was remarkable, but under the surface, she hid a great pain. A sadness unlike any other. She never spoke of it, but when you looked hard enough, you could see the anguish.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: I guess we all have our demons, even the gods. Seren was a beacon of light in this grim world, but the brightest light casts the darkest shadow, and none shone brighter than her.

options.text: What do you think of the current elves?

steps.player: What do you think of the current elves?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Arianwyn and the rebels have done well to keep going for this long. They've been fighting this war for centuries, and yet they've never given up. I have much respect for them, they're far stronger than I ever was.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Most of them are still young though. They lack the wisdom of the older elves, the ones who were around when Seren still walked this earth. Many of them never saw Prifddinas before the song of inversion.

steps.player: Is that a bad thing?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Not necessarily, but it is something to be cautious of. That which they fight for, it's a mere dream to them. They should remember that dreams seldom come true.

steps.player: I'll be back later.
I'd better be off.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Welcome back [player name]. While you were gone, I filled Baxtorian in on everything that has happened. I also took the liberty of calling the others here, so that we can discuss our next move.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Eluned
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: You also missed out on Islwyn getting to meet his grandfather for the first time. I think he might have cried a little.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Islwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Cried? In your dreams Eluned.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: I appreciate we're all happy to have Baxtorian back with us, but let's not get distracted.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Eluned
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Apologies, Arianwyn.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Right, over to you Baxtorian.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Thank you, Arianwyn. I... Forgive me, it's been a long time since I last chaired a meeting like this. Much has changed since then as well.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Take your time.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Thank you friend.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Arianwyn has informed me of Lord Iorwerth's revelation...

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ysgawyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Do you believe his claims?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: About Seren? No. As for him breaking a seal in the Grand Library... I... do not know.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ysgawyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: You don't know? What do you mean you don't know?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Ysgawyn...

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: I know not what the seals hide. What I do know is that they could, in theory, be broken.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: I was lucky enough to be trusted by Seren. She confided in me many times. She never told me what knowledge the seals guard, but she did tell me that they could be destroyed.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: I don't know exactly. She said that those who follow the light would be able to access her knowledge.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ysgawyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: And that's it? This gives us nothing to go on.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Islwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Not nothing. We now know that the seals can be destroyed, which means Lord Iorwerth could have spoken the truth.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ysgawyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: But without access to the Grand Library, we have no way to be sure.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Well... we might still have a way.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Eluned
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: A way to access the library?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Yes... Prifddinas may have been reverted to seed, but it does still exist.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ysgawyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: You're not suggesting we restore the city are you? Even if we could, Lord Iorwerth would instantly take it.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: No. While Lord Iorwerth is at large, Prifddinas must remain as it is. However, there may be a way to still enter the city.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: You don't mean entering the crystal do you?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ysgawyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: That's not possible.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ilfeen
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Actually, I think it would be possible. The crystal seed that contains Prifddinas, it's not the same as the seeds we use to form weapons and armour.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ilfeen
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: The seed contains Prifddinas, but the seed itself is not the city.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: So it's like a box?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Ilfeen
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Exactly, and if we can enter the box...

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Islwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: We can enter Prifddinas!

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: That's the idea. It won't be straightforward though.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: We will need a special potion to be able to safely enter the crystal seed. We'll also need to be able to bypass the defences around it as well.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: A potion? Sounds like my area of expertise.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Perfect. Elena, if you could help create this potion, that would be greatly appreciated. The rest of us can work on those defences.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Right. [player name], meet me by the pond. I could use your help with this.
The others leave the meeting.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Oh... Hello there.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.player: What do I need to do now?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: I've given Elena the information she needs to make that potion. You should speak to her by the pond.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.player: What do I need to do now?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-the-second.text: Baxtorian has given Elena the information she needs to make this potion. You should speak to her by the pond.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: If you chose "Maybe later." when she wanted to ask you something before the first meeting:

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Hi.

steps.player: Hey Elena.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: If you chose "Go ahead." and picked the full options when she wanted to ask you something before the first meeting:

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Hey [player name]. Glad everything went okay at Baxtorian Falls.

steps.player: Thanks. Anything exciting happen while I was gone?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Nope, all nice and quiet for a change.

steps.player: Good to hear.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Baxtorian is an interesting one, isn't he?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Lost?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: He reminds me of a story my father once told me. A story of a broken man.

steps.player: What was the story?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: A long time ago, there were two brothers living in Avarrocka. They lived a simple life, farming the land and selling the produce to people in the city.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: When war came to the city, the king ordered that every able-bodied man take up arms against the enemy. The two brothers had to leave their home behind, to fight for a king they'd never met.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Like everyone else, they were given basic weapons and basic training. Enough to give them a chance, but not a big one. When the fighting started, they were poorly equipped and poorly prepared.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: They fought in many battles. Battles in strange places against strange people. As the war dragged on, they saw more and more horrors, from both sides. The only thing that kept them going was each other.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: As the war drew to a close, they were called to one final battle. The enemy knew they were losing, and they fought more ferociously than ever before.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: That was where it happened. One of the brothers was cut off and surrounded. He tried to fight back, but he didn't stand a chance.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Eventually the fighting stopped, and the war was over. The other brother could finally go home. But the truth is, he had nothing to go home to.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: It wasn't the farm that mattered, not really. The thing that mattered to him was gone.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: In a way, he'd died back on the battlefield alongside his brother. Left in his place was just a broken man, with nothing left to live for.

steps.player: Hmm. And you think Baxtorian is like this broken man?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: He lost his wife, his people and his kingdom. Now he's in a strange place, surrounded by strange people, helping to fight a war that he lost a long time ago.

options.text: Now's not the time for stories, Elena.

steps.player: Now's not the time for stories, Elena.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I guess you're right. The short of it is, Baxtorian has lost everything that he cared about. He's just an empty shell now, with nothing left to live for.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.player: Maybe he's not totally lost. He still has Islwyn, and we can still turn this war around.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Maybe. I guess only time will tell.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Right. Shall we get started with this potion?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Baxtorian gave me the details. To start with, we need an elder cadantine herb. We should be able to grow one from a normal cadantine seed, we just need to prepare the patch a little differently.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: The elves have said we can use this farming patch here. While I prepare the patch, could you go and fetch a cadantine seed and a seed dibber?
If the player already has a Cadantine seed:

steps.player: I already have the seed here.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Well it also happens that I've actually already prepared the patch, so you can get started right away.

steps.player: How convenient.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Indeed. When you're ready, go ahead and plant the seed.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: If the player doesn't have a Cadantine seed:

steps.player: Will do, I'll be back soon.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Hey [player name]. Do you have that seed yet?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: It's a cadantine seed that we need. Let me know once you have one. You'll want to get a seed dibber as well so we can plant it.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Hey [player name]. Do you have that seed yet?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Great. The patch is all prepared so just plant it when you're ready.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Elena
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Great. I'll keep an eye on the patch while it grows. You should check in with Arianwyn and Baxtorian in the meantime.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: Hello [player name], how's the potion going?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.player: We've planted the herb we need, now we have to wait for it to grow. Is there something I can do in the meantime?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: I suspect there is. Myself and Baxtorian have been looking over how we can get past the defences around the crystal seed.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: The crystal seed containing Prifddinas, it lies in the middle of the clearing where the city once stood. The only thing left of the city itself are the walls.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Baxtorian
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: These are no ordinary walls though. Long ago, they were reinforced by various enchantments to protect Prifddinas during the God Wars.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Arianwyn
preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.text: With Prifddinas gone, Lord Iorwerth has claimed the land where it once was. He's managed to manipulate the defences to only allow his allies to enter.

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.player: So how do we get past them?

preparing-to-enter-prifddinas-talking-to.speaker: Baxtorian
