attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I... I can't.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I see. I did hope it wouldn't come to this, but you've given me no choice. Morvran.
Morvran leaves, bringing Eoin in.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Eoin
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: What's going on? Where's mummy?

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I'll make this simple for you, Baxtorian. The life of the boy is now in your hands. Give me the orb, and no harm will come to him.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: You wouldn't...

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: No, I wouldn't. But the choice is not mine, it's yours. I will count to five.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: One.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Lord Iorwerth, please...

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Two.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Baxtorian, please. Just give him the orb.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Three.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Eoin
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I don't like this, I want mummy!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Four.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Stop!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Baxtorian
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: I'll give you the orb. Just please, don't hurt anyone else.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: A wise choice, must be a first for you.
Baxtorian gives Lord Iorwerth the orb.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Ysgawyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: No!
Ysgawyn attempts to stop them, but Essylt kills him in one hit.

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Ysgawyn!

attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.speaker: Islwyn
attack-on-lletya-lord-iorwerth-arrives.text: Get after them!

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: It wasn't meant to go like this. No one was meant to get hurt. I'm sorry.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: For so long I was led to believe that Lord Iorwerth was our enemy. I thought he'd turned his back on Seren, thought he'd betrayed her.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: But I was wrong. Everything we thought we were fighting for was a lie. He never betrayed her, everything he did was to free her.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: Whatever it is he's trying to free... it isn't her.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: How do you know? Because of what you found in the library? How do we know that was her? How do we know what's true anymore?

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: So that's why you turned to Lord Iorwerth? To find out the truth?

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: My whole life I've dreamed of her, dreamed of what it would be like to meet her. If there's even a chance that she's still alive, I have to know.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: And if she is alive? Then what?

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: Seren guided the elves for thousands of years. With her back, we'll finally be able to reform Prifddinas. We'll finally have peace again.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: Peace? Look around you Arianwyn. Look at what Lord Iorwerth has done to this village, your home. Does this look like the work of someone who wants peace?
It doesn't have to be this way. Step aside. Let me stop Lord Iorwerth and reclaim the orb. Once he's dealt with, we can find out the truth, our way.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: You... you know I can't do that.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: I'm sorry friend, but I've made my choice. Now please, walk away. No one else needs to die here.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.player: I can't let him get away.

attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.speaker: Arianwyn
attack-on-lletya-confronting-the-traitor.text: And I can't let you go after him.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Ysgawyn...

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: He wasn't a friend, to any of us. Everything he cared about he lost a long time ago.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: But he didn't give up. To the very end, he fought for a cause he believed in, our cause.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: And now he's gone. Along with the orb and that traitor, Arianwyn. Lord Iorwerth has everything he needs now. He'll be preparing to move on the temple as we speak.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Ilfeen
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: We can't give up Islwyn. If we do, then he died for nothing.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Oh I don't intend to give up, but make no mistake, this is a fight we're unlikely to win.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Eluned
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: So what do we do? Baxtorian?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I... I don't think there's anything we can do. Lord Iorwerth will destroy us if we try to stop him.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Maybe, but we have to try. What else is there?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: We'd be throwing lives away...

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Well Lord Iorwerth seemed to think you were no stranger to that. Why did he think that?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I don't know, probably just some lie he tells himself.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Hmm. I don't believe you.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: You'd trust Lord Iorwerth over me?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I wouldn't trust Lord Iorwerth if my life depended on it. I know a liar when I see one though, and I can tell you're not being honest about something.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: What happened? Tell us.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: It was after we were defeated by Lord Iorwerth. With Prifddinas lost to us, we returned to our kingdom in the east. We'd been gone for years by then, and in our absence, the kingdom had fallen to our other foes.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: So many dead... my people, the ones I was meant to protect. But that wasn't the worst of it. Glarial, my beloved, she was taken from me.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: We searched far and wide, desperate to find her. At times it felt like we were close, but the enemy always managed to elude us.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Eventually, we managed to track her captors to some caves south of our ruined kingdom. It was clearly a trap, but I was a fool. I was so blind in my desire to find her, I didn't consider the obvious.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I sent my soldiers in, the few that I still had. They fought the best they could, but it was hopeless. They were massacred.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: After that, I knew I couldn't carry on. I was alone and powerless. So I sealed myself away, in the hope that one day she would come back to me.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: You... you killed them? You killed them all?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: I did. But you don't understand, I loved my wife. If there was a chance of freeing her, I had to take it.

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: You think I don't understand love? I knew love, for Eirlys! My mother! Your daughter! She died in your war, while you hid away!

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Lord Iorwerth was right! You're just a coward!

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Eluned
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: Islwyn, where are you going?

after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.speaker: Islwyn
after-the-attack-a-rebellion-divided.text: The Underground Pass! I intend to fight for my people, even if their own king won't!
Islwyn leaves, and the funeral ends.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I used to think I was a good king, one that took care of his people. Thanks to me, they had roofs over their heads and food for their tables.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: And yet... I never loved them, not really. The only thing I loved was her, my Glarial.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: When they took her from me... I was torn apart. I vowed I would get her back no matter the cost. That vow destroyed my people... I destroyed my people. In the end... I became just like Lord Iorwerth.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Maybe you did fail your people, you didn't destroy them though.
You think this is over? Is that it? Lord Iorwerth beats us once so we just give up? If you truly think that then yes, you have destroyed your people!
Do you want to just rot here? Wallowing in your own self pity while you lose the little you still have?
We can fight! Lord Iorwerth doesn't win until he gets into the Temple of Light! We can still stop this!

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: But he outnumbers us ten to one... We'll all die.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Surely it's better to die trying than to live a life of regret? I'd have thought you'd know that better than anyone.

Oh for crying out loud! You have got to be the biggest waste of space I have ever met! I've met goblins with more of a spine than you! For once in your miserable life why don't you actually do something worthwhile?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: You... You're awful at pep talks.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: It wasn't meant to be a pep talk!
sigh* Look... Ask yourself this... What would she want?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: She... She'd want me to save them.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Then why are we still stood around talking? We've got work to do!

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I... You're right... We don't have a plan though.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Lord Iorwerth only has one way into the Temple of Light, the dwarf tunnel from the Underground Pass. We need to stop him getting through.
The dwarves should be able to seal the tunnel. We'll need to defend them while they do.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: But we don't have the strength to withstand Lord Iorwerth's forces.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: We have the clan elders, their combined power is an army in itself.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: Not all the clan elders. We're still missing two.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: Well have you deciphered their clues?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I have, but there's a problem. We should hopefully be able to find Lady Meilyr. But Lady Ithell, she died in the early days of the war.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: That's not good. Did she have any descendants?

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I had a look. Kelyn Ithell is her closest living relative. Problem is, we don't just need a Lady Ithell, we need the Lady Ithell.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: An illness of some sort, I never actually knew what it was. She'd had it for years.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: For years? So she'd have been ill when she gave you her clue. If she knew she was dying, maybe her clue reflects that.
Knowledge can be passed on. Maybe the clue will lead us to her knowledge.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I... I suppose you could be right.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.player: It's worth a shot at least. Leave it with me and I'll see what I can do. In the meantime, you should take the others to the dwarf camp in the Underground Pass.
See if you can get in contact with General Hining and the new king of Ardougne as well. Maybe they'll be willing to help us.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian.text: I'll see what I can do. We'll need to work quickly though, Lord Iorwerth will be preparing his forces as we speak. Now I guess you'll be wanting to hear those clues?

steps.player: What's Lady Ithell's clue?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Here is the clue she left behind: 'I'll put my soul into my greatest work.'

steps.player: I see, anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Ithell clan is a clan of builders and architects. Before her death, Lady Ithell was considered the finest architect of all the elves. This village was her final and finest contribution to our people.

steps.player: What's Lady Meilyr's clue?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Here is the clue she left behind: 'Follow the scrolls to find me.'

steps.player: I see, anything else I should know?

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: The Meilyr clan is a clan of scientists and explorers. You'll probably need to do some exploring yourself to find Lady Meilyr. You may also find this of use.
If the player has no inventory space:
Baxtorian tries to give you a scroll but you don't have enough room to take it.
If the player has inventory space:
Baxtorian has given you a scroll.

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian-ta.speaker: Baxtorian
after-the-attack-talking-to-baxtorian-ta.text: Do you need to hear one of the clues again?

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: Well I can't really go back to Lord Iorwerth now. He knows I betrayed him.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.player: No, but you don't have to stay here.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: I've made my decision and I intend to stick by it.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.player: So why follow him in the first place?

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: After we lost Seren, Baxtorian was chosen to lead us. Rather than looking after the city of Prifddinas, he chose to expand to the east, leaving us behind.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: With no ruler, Prifddinas fell into chaos. When Lord Iorwerth came to us and said he'd found a way to bring Seren back to us, you can understand why we turned to him.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.speaker: Iestin
after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.text: I wish things were as simple as good against evil, but that's rarely the case.

after-the-attack-talking-to-iestin.player: I suppose you're right. Anyway, I'd better get going.

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.player: Hey Elena. What are you up to?

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.text: Making sure I've got everything ready. I'll be leaving for the Underground Pass soon.

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.speaker: Elena
after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.text: Well I've stuck around for this long, it would feel wrong to leave now. Besides, I may not be much of a fighter, but I can help in other ways.

after-the-attack-talking-to-elena.player: Very true. I'll leave you to prepare.

after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.speaker: Mawrth
after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.text: I can't thank you enough for what you did. My children might be dead if not for you.

after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.speaker: Mawrth
after-the-attack-talking-to-mawrth.text: You're a hero and all of us here know it. Again, thank you.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-tou.text: You feel your mind fill with knowledge as the symbol vanishes before you. The knowledge is incomplete though.
The symbol vanishes before you as you gain the final piece of knowledge. The combined knowledge is a design for a statue to be built in the middle of Lletya, requiring 8 Limestone Bricks.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I... I see it! I see everything! All of her knowledge, I have it now!

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: Yes, I know everything that she knew! The statue, it must have given it to me somehow!

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.player: You're the closest living relative of Lady Ithell. Now you have her knowledge as well. I suppose that makes you the new Lady Ithell.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I... I suppose it does. Wow!

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I guess you'll be wanting me to help defend the Underground Pass then? Well don't worry, I was planning on joining you anyway. With this new knowledge, I can be an even bigger help.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
after-the-attack-finding-lady-ithell-her.text: I'll head there right away. Time is of the essence.
Lady Ithell departs for the Underground Pass.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.text: At last Baxtorian calls to me. I can't say I expected him to send a human, but I suppose nothing is as expected these days.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.player: We need your help. The final fight against Lord Iorwerth is nearly here.

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.text: I will join you in this darkest of hours. Where must I go?

after-the-attack-finding-lady-meilyr.player: The battle will take place in the Underground Pass. Head to Lletya first though, Baxtorian will meet you there.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Oh... Hello. Most of the others have departed for the Underground Pass. I'll be leaving with the rest soon.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Then I shall meet you there.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Don't take too long. We'll be at the dwarf camp.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: How are you Islwyn?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Islwyn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: As good as can be, all things considered. I idolised my grandfather for years. They always say you should never meet your heroes though, now I see why.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: He's still your family though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Islwyn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He is, he's the only family I have left. The rest of them died in his war. A war that will finally end today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Islwyn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Maybe if we both survive, I'll find it in my heart to forgive him. But for now, I have to focus elsewhere.

steps.player: I'll leave you to prepare.

steps.speaker: Islwyn
steps.text: Good luck [player name]. I'll see you on the other side.

options.text: Could I buy some crystal equipment?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Arianwyn is out there, walking alongside our greatest enemy.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He saved me once you know. Some of Lord Iorwerth's men found me in the forest. There were too many for me to fight off, I thought I was done for. Without Arianwyn, I wouldn't be here today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: But now he fights alongside them. This war has torn us apart, all of us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Well it ends today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Eluned
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Yes, today it ends... For better, or for worse.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I wonder if Essyllt will join the battle today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: What will you do if he does?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Me? Nothing. I'm not much of a fighter. I'll be helping with the wounded instead.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: You though... If you see him, don't show him mercy, for he will show you none. Instead, you should show him what happens to those who hurt us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: For Ysgawyn?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: No one liked him that much, but he was one of us, and he died trying to save us. He deserves justice.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: If I get the chance, I'll make sure he gets it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Ilfeen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Thank you friend.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

options.text: Could you enchant something for me?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Those are my people coming for us. My brothers and sisters.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: They were once, but not anymore. You're one of us now.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He's not evil you know, Lord Iorwerth. None of them are really, apart from Essyllt maybe.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Those that follow him, they do so because they believe in him, believe in what he's doing. For a long time, I believed in him as well.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: So why did you betray him?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: He became so obsessed with his cause, he forgot why we started following him in the first place. He became more extreme, more radical.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I tried to advise him as best I could, but over time he started listening more to Essyllt and less to me.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: After I lost my brother, who died following Lord Iorwerth's orders, I realised he needed to be stopped before it was too late.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You made the right choice.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Iestin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope so. But even now I find myself filled with doubt.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Kamen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Nothing like a *hic* bit of home brew before getting to work.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Are you sure you should be drinking? We can't afford to make mistakes here.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Kamen
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Argh, I work better with a bit of *hic* brew in me. Nothing for you to *hic* worry about.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: If you're sure.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Klank
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Didn't think I'd see you back down here [player name]. The elves are lucky to have you on their side.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: They're lucky to have you as well, you're our last hope.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Klank
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: What an awful thought. Four dwarves, one a drunk, are the final hope against this darkness. I hope we don't let you down.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You won't.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Klank
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope you're right friend.

steps.player: Take care Klank.

steps.speaker: Klank
steps.text: You too adventurer...

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Niloof
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: [player name]. We'll soon be ready to seal the tunnel, it's slow work I'm afraid.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: How come?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Niloof
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: If we do this wrong, we'll bring the entire cavern down upon all of us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Well that would definitely stop Lord Iorwerth.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Niloof
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: It would. I don't know about you though, but I intend to survive this day. Bringing the cavern down isn't a good way to achieve that.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: True that. I'll leave you to your work.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Thorgel
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Hey there [player name].

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: How's it going Thorgel?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Thorgel
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Apart from the army of elves about to descend on us, pretty good.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You'll be fine, you've got all of us to defend you.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Thorgel
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Well let's hope your better at fighting than Kamen is at brewing, or this will be a short battle.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Ieuan Amlodd
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: So here we are. At long last, the end is upon us. The only question that remains is who it's the end for.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You knew this day would come?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Ieuan Amlodd
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: No war lasts forever, not even this one. The darkest verse of the song of the elves is upon us. Who knows what the next verse will be.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Tangwen Trahaearn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Lord Iorwerth better show up soon! I can't wait forever!

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You seem keen.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Tangwen Trahaearn
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I've lived for thousands of years. If I'm going to die today, I'd rather just get on with it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Fair enough.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: This is a dark place we've come to. Fitting I suppose, for this is to be our darkest hour.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Do you think the fragment of Seren is the cause of the darkness?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lord Piquan Crwys
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Possibly, I suspect it was here long before her though. And whatever happens today, I'm sure it will remain for long after.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: The greatest battle of our time is almost upon us. We should take the time to reflect.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I've never really been one for looking backwards. I prefer to look ahead.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: You can still reflect on the future as well as the past. If we survive today, our future will be changed forever.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I suppose. I'll probably wait until we've won to think about that though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Carys Hefin
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: As you wish.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope we win today. It would be a bit embarrassing to be known as the shortest serving clan elder.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I bet. I'd also like to avoid death if possible. I suspect it's not very fun.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Not much is fun when Lord Iorwerth is involved. If all goes well though, he won't be a problem after today.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I've been on the run from Lord Iorwerth for centuries. I'll be glad to finally see peace.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: So you think we'll win?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Don't forget that death is a form of peace.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I guess. I'd rather avoid it if I can though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Lady Ffion Meilyr
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: There are worse things in this world than death. Never forget that.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Good to see you General.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: General Hining
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: And you friend. It will be an honour to fight against the darkness alongside you. Together, we can avenge King Tyras.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: You seem well prepared for the battle, compared to the rest of us at least.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: General Hining
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: We knew this battle would come, ever since the day our king died. We've been prepared for a long time.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I hope it's enough.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: General Hining
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: As do I. If it's not though, we'll make sure they remember us until the end of their days.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: That we will.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Ah... You made it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: That I did. I see you managed to gather some allies.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Yes, General Hining has given us the full support of the Tyras forces. Sadly though, the new king of Ardougne does not wish to assist us.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Typical, after all we did for them.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I suppose they've had enough of elves.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Hmmm. How are the defences looking?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: We've managed to fortify the area around the camp quite well. The dwarves have set up some cannons and General Hining's men have built some catapults.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Good. We may be outnumbered, but the defences will give us a fighting chance.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: I hope so... I fear it won't be enough to win though.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: We don't need to win, we just need to buy the dwarves enough time to seal that tunnel. Do we know how long they'll need?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: They haven't given us an exact time, it's a slow process apparently.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Well I suppose we don't want them to do it wrong, they could bring the entire cavern down on top of us. Do we know where Lord Iorwerth is?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: The scouts have reported that his forces are on the move as we speak. It won't be long.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Let's use the time wisely then. Is there anything I can do before the attack begins?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Elena said she had an idea that might help our defence. You could talk to her and see if she needs any help.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I'll get right on it.
What do I need to do again?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Speak with Elena. She said she had an idea that might help our defence.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: I'll get right on it.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Elena
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: Hey. I think Baxtorian wants to talk to you.

I'm not afraid.

options.text: I care about you Elena, you know that right?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Good luck today.

options.text: Baxtorian said you had an idea to help our defence.

steps.player: I'd better go.

steps.player: Baxtorian said you had an idea to help our defence.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: That's right. One of the dwarves here, Kamen, has brewed up some strange alcohol. Whatever it is, it's very flammable.

steps.player: Ah yes, I've made good use of it in the past.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Well I think we can make use of it again. I've combined the alcohol with some other chemicals. The result is quite explosive!

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: If we position some of these explosives on the approach to the camp, we can use them against the Iorwerth forces.

steps.player: Hmmm, that could work quite well. Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: I've dug some holes around the camp for the explosives to go in. Could you fill them in for me?

steps.player: Of course.

steps.speaker: Elena
steps.text: Here's the explosives. If you need more just let me know.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Elena
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.text: [player name], Lord Iorwerth's forces are approaching, you'd better go see Baxtorian.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.player: Will do, thanks Elena.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-talking-t.speaker: Elena

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.text: Good, because we're out of time. A message came into the camp, Lord Iorwerth wishes to meet.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.player: He wants to meet? Surely it's a trap?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.text: Maybe, but I don't think so. Even if nothing came of it, he was willing to meet me before the Siege of Prifddinas all those years ago.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.player: So what are you going to do?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.text: I will go. If there's a chance to avoid bloodshed, we should take it, no matter how slim the odds are. I would like you to join me.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.player: You think Lord Iorwerth will listen to me?

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.text: No, but maybe Arianwyn will. He considered you a friend, he may still care for what you have to say.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.player: I see. Then I will join you.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.text: Thank you friend. Now, Lord Iorwerth is unlikely to be patient, but we can spare a bit of time. If there's anyone you wish to talk to here, I suggest you do so before we depart. You may not get another chance.

preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.speaker: Baxtorian
preparations-at-the-dwarf-camp-a-final-m.text: Let me know when you're ready to go.

steps.player: I'm ready.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Then we will leave at once.

options.text: I'd like to ask you something about yourself.

steps.player: I'll be back soon.

steps.speaker: Baxtorian
steps.text: Don't take too long. I'll be here when you're ready.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Lord Iorwerth.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: King Baxtorian.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I'm not a king... not anymore.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: No. You never really were a king though were you? A king doesn't abandon his people like you did.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I did not come here to trade insults.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Really? So why did you come then?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.player: We came to put an end to this. To put aside our differences and stop this war before more people die needlessly.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: You talk sense human, and yet you stand beside the warmonger himself.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.player: You have a fair share of blood on your hands as well you know.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I do. I have done many unspeakable things, things that haunt me every day. But what I did, I did for the good of my people.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Whereas he, he only ever cared for himself.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Go on, deny it. Just like you always do.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I don't deny it. I failed my people, I failed you. I was never a worthy king, I know that now. But you can't use my failures as a mask to hide your own.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: We can stand here going around in circles all day, you won't change my mind.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.player: If you're not willing to change your mind, why even bother to meet us?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: In the hope that I might still change yours. I don't want anyone else to die in this war. I give you the chance to stand down.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: And what happens if we do?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: We enter the temple, free our goddess and with her by our side, reform the city of Prifddinas.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: And we all live happily ever after?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: In a manner of speaking.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.player: That temple, it doesn't contain your goddess. At best, it contains a shadow of what she once was.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Yes, Arianwyn told me what you discovered in the library. It matters not though, that is a part of our goddess in there, we have to free her.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: And if she's evil? What do you do then?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: My loyalty is to Seren, I will let her decide what is evil.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Arianwyn
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: That... that's not what we agreed.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: What?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Arianwyn
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: We agreed to enter the temple and free Seren. If that's not Seren in there, we shouldn't free her.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I will keep my promise to you Arianwyn, you should not doubt that.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.player: Why shouldn't he doubt that? You burnt his home, you killed his friends. You haven't given him much reason to trust you so far.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I did what I needed to do to save our goddess. No one would have needed to die had you not forced our hand.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.player: Listen to him Arianwyn, he'd sacrifice everything and everyone just to free whatever is in that temple. Is that really what you want?

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Enough of this! You can try to manipulate him all you want, he's made his choice.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: Now, I'm afraid I'll need to push you on a decision.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I'm sorry, but we can't let you enter that temple.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: A shame. As unlikely as it was, I did hope you might see reason.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: I think we're done here then. For what it's worth, I'm sorry it had to end this way.

sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.speaker: Baxtorian
sealing-the-underground-pass-meeting-wit.text: As am I.

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: The blockage is blown up, and Essylt arrives with two Iorwerth Warriors. Essylt immediately attacks Elena.

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Essyllt
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: Ha! Looks like you were too slow my friend.

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Essyllt
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: Or what? Will you murder me in cold blood like you did with King Tyras?

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Essyllt
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: You can lie to yourself all you want, I know what you are. You enjoy killing, just like I do.

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Essyllt
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: The satisfaction when I finally put an end to that fool Ysgawyn, it was beautiful. It was even better than when I dealt with that stupid lover of his.

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Essyllt
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: But if that wasn't enough, now I get to be the one to finally put an end to you and your pathetic girlfriend!

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Essyllt
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: Oh I'm going to enjoy this...
Lord Iorwerth and Arianwyn arrive, with two Iorwerth Warriors and Archers behind them.
Lord Iorwerth and Arianwyn proceed to enter the Temple of Light, with Baxtorian chasing after them.

sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.speaker: Eluned
sealing-the-underground-pass-attack-of-t.text: Don't worry, I'll take care of her.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: This is it, this is what we've spent the last thousand years fighting for. Today, it will finally all be worth it.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: Lord Iorwerth please, see reason. That thing is not Seren, it's not our goddess.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: I knew Seren, I'm the only one here that did, and I know that isn't her.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: Time can change a lot of things, perhaps Seren has changed as well.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Arianwyn
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: I... I don't think it's her.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: Of course it's her! Don't tell me you believe Baxtorian and his lies?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Arianwyn
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: I may not have met our goddess, but I heard enough stories to know what she looked like. This thing, it's not her.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: Well lucky for us, we have a way of finding out.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Arianwyn
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: Lord Iorwerth please, this isn't what we agreed.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-freed.text: I know what we agreed Arianwyn! We agreed to free our goddess, and that's what I'm going to do!
Arianwyn shoots Lord Iorwerth, critically injuring him, and the player is dragged into the Fragment of Seren's realm.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.text: You... you've come to free me?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.player: What's going on? Why's everything so dark?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.text: Dark? All I've ever known is darkness. It's all she gave me.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.text: You haven't come to free me at all have you? You're one of her servants!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.text: I loved her! She made me! But I couldn't be what she wanted, so she abandoned me! And now she can't bear to kill me herself, so she sends you instead!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.text: I won't let you! It's not fair! She doesn't get to do this! I don't want it!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-enrag.text: No! Get out! Get out! Get out!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: She acted like I was a monster! Come... look upon her monster!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: She left me, like I wasn't real! But I know what's real, do you?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: Did she think I would rot here? I am eternal, unlike you!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: She feared my power, and she was right to! Let me show you...

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: Look at me! Look at what she made me! Do you see?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: She treated me like I was less than her, but I'm so much more!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: I won't let her destroy me! She doesn't get to decide that!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: This power, she gave it to me! It's her power too! Feel it!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: I just wanted her to love me, but she wouldn't even look at me!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: She tried to forget me, but everywhere she looked she saw me!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: I have more power than she ever did! I will survive!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: Do you know pain? I do! She made sure of that! I'll show you...

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: Come! Come look upon her work, and despair!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: Do you think she cares? Maybe reality isn't what you think...

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: I am infinite! As hard as she tries, I can't be destroyed!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: The pain she caused me, let me give you a taste of it!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: Are you afraid? Too scared to even look at me?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: I'm better than her! I'm greater than her! That's what she hated!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: The things I've endured, do you think you could endure them?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.speaker: Fragment of Seren
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-battl.text: She didn't love me! She feared the strength of her own creation!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.text: She was confused, she was hurt. Yes, she was angry, but she was innocent!

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.text: How? With violence? That's all you know isn't it?

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.text: She just needed time, time to understand, time to overcome her pain. She was our goddess, the last hope for our people. And now, she's gone, because of you.

the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.speaker: Lord Iorwerth
the-fragment-of-seren-the-fragment-defea.text: I hope you can live with yourself...
Lord Iorwerth succumbs to his wounds, and dies.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: As well as can be expected. My guilt is a heavy load. A lot of people died because of me.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.player: A lot more might have died if you hadn't stopped Lord Iorwerth.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: He wasn't evil, not truly. He just became so obsessed with his goal that he forgot why he started fighting in the first place.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: As for the fragment of Seren... I wish there had been another way.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.player: She wasn't Seren, and she never would have been.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: No, and at least now her pain has ended. Still, I'll always wonder what could have been...

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: There's no place for me here anymore, not after what I've done.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: I wanted to stay long enough to help repair the damage of my actions, and to look upon Prifddinas for the first time. I've done that now. Lletya has been rebuilt and Prifddinas has been reformed.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: I don't know. There's a lot of places on this world that I've never seen. Maybe one of them will help me find redemption, and forgiveness.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: The elves here will do fine. Baxtorian has his own path of redemption to go on, and I imagine he'll struggle far more than me. He has the other elders to support him though. Under them, our people will prosper.

the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.speaker: Arianwyn
the-war-s-end-arianwyn-atones.text: Anyway, you should get going. Baxtorian will be waiting for you.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.player: Hey, good to see you both.
I thought the city had been restored, I don't see anything though.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: One of the security measures put in place during the God Wars, from the outside it seems like there's nothing there. Don't worry though, the restoration is complete.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: Speaking of which, myself and the other elders have come to an agreement. For too long, we've been afraid of outsiders, showing them mistrust while our own kind plot against us.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: After all that's happened, we've decided that from now on, that will no longer be the case. We will open our city up to the other races, letting them walk among us for the first time.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: As a thank you for all that you've done, we'd like the two of you to be the first to enter Prifddinas.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Elena
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: They've also agreed to let me move into the city. That tiny house in Ardougne was becoming a bit tiresome, and there's so much for me to learn from the Meilyr elves.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.player: Well I'll be sure to come and visit.
Now that the city has been reformed, are you going to become king of the elves again?

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: Oh I said my days as a king were done, and I meant it. From now on, the elves will be jointly ruled by the eight clan elders. No single elf will ever rule again. We've realised that we're not overly good at it.

the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.speaker: Baxtorian
the-war-s-end-prifddinas-reformed.text: But anyway, we can talk more later. For now, I'd say it's time for the two of you to see Prifddinas.

zWmqLP.text: Very well, return to us once you are ready.

Besides, Sophanem is my home. It will take a lot more than the threat of a few spots to keep me away.

steps.speaker: Councillor Hughes

standard-dialogue.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: Not that it makes much difference but my name's Sorin. Like all the other survivors here, I just try to make do and get through each day at a time.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.

steps.player: What's happening around here?

steps.npc: Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.npc: My name's Sorin. I'm just trying to make do I guess. The vampyres might not be a problem, but there's still no shortage of dangers around here.

steps.player: How are thing's here?

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind.
I'd best be off.

steps.npc: I hate this job. All the other staff are so happy all the time. It depresses me.

steps.player: Why don't you get a new job?

steps.npc: I can't find any other work. I wanted to be a Gnomeball player but I wasn't big enough.

steps.player: That's a shame. I'd better let you get on with your work.

steps.npc: OK, whatever.

steps.player: Aren't you going to wish me a nice day?

steps.npc: Have a day. It can be nice if you can be bothered. I know I can't.

steps.player: ... nice.

options.text: Can you tell me about the gods of the Menaphites?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the gods of the Menaphites?

steps.npc: If you wish to know about the lesser gods, you should speak with Jex at the Temple of the Lesser Gods. I suppose I could spare a moment or two to tell you about the main four though.

steps.player: Tell me about Tumeken.

steps.npc: Tumeken is the god of light and husband to Elidinis. He is the leading god of the Menaphite Pantheon.

steps.player: People don't seem to talk about him much. I'd have thought being the leading god would make him more popular.

steps.npc: A common saying about Tumeken is that you see him wherever you look, but never actually notice him.

steps.player: Okay... And what kind of god is he? The desert is a harsh place, so does that make him harsh as well?

steps.npc: In some ways. You humans sometimes say that 'you have to be cruel to be kind'. That seems a fitting way to describe Tumeken.

steps.player: So he's harsh, but for good reasons?

steps.npc: Indeed.

steps.player: Tell me about Elidinis.

steps.npc: Elidinis is the goddess of fertility. The River Elid is named in her honour, for it brings life to the whole region.
There are some who even believe the river to be Elidinis herself.

steps.player: That's an interesting take. I guess being a bringer of life makes her quite popular?

steps.npc: More so than many others in the pantheon, but not as much as she once was.

steps.player: Why not?

steps.npc: Humans are fickle. Perhaps they grew bored of her?

steps.player: That sounds unlikely.

steps.npc: Well if you're after the human take on things, you'd be better off asking a human.

steps.player: Tell me about Icthlarin.

steps.npc: Icthlarin is the god of the dead. He is the son of Tumeken and Elidinis, and brother to the Devourer. As this is the city of the dead, he's quite popular here.

steps.player: So are you a follower of Icthlarin?

steps.npc: Nothing of the sort. I have no interest in the gods or their followers. Instead, Icthlarin and I have an understanding.
Cats play a significant role when it comes to guarding the dead from the Devourer. As such, they are great allies to Icthlarin.
As a thank you for looking after them, Icthlarin grants me eternal life.

steps.player: Tell me about the Devourer.

steps.npc: I'd have thought you'd be more than familiar with her by now.

steps.player: I'm interested in hearing your take.

steps.npc: Very well. The Devourer is the goddess of destruction. As such, she is commonly considered an evil goddess, but this is an oversimplification.

steps.player: How so?

steps.npc: Not everything that destroys is evil. Destruction is often a necessity.

steps.player: Isn't that also an oversimplification? Amascut is doing far more than just destroying. She's a murderer!

steps.npc: Is causing death enough to make one evil? Icthlarin is the god of the dead. By your argument, surely he is the most evil of them all.

steps.player: Icthlarin doesn't actually kill people though. He just looks after those that have died.

steps.npc: You clearly know little of Icthlarin and his past. Are you aware of the Mahjarrat? They once served Icthlarin, before they left him for Zamorak.
Or was it the Empty Lord they left him for... I forget.
Regardless, they are a race that have regularly associated themselves with gods considered evil. Interesting company for one such as Icthlarin to keep.

steps.player: How does that make Amascut good though?

steps.npc: I never said it did. I'm just saying that things are often not as straightforward as they seem, especially when it comes to Icthlarin and the Devourer.

steps.player: If you say so...
Let's talk about something else.

steps.npc: Very well. What do you want to dicuss?

steps.player: Nothing. I should go.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Hmm, well that could be quite fortuitous. We really could do with some help here. Our town seems to have come under a curse, and we are desperate to get it removed.

steps.player: A curse? What sort of curse?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well first of all our fountain, which has served us for many years, suddenly dried up. We then started transporting water from the river, but what we carried would always have completely dried up by the time we

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: got it back to the village.

options.text: So what do you do for water now?

steps.player: So what do you do for water now?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well it's tough. There is a guy who calls himself Ali the carter down in the market. He's from Pollnivneach, so the curse doesn't seem to have affected him. He's got a cart full of water which he's selling to the people here.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Unfortunately in typical Pollnivneach style he's taking the opportunity to sell the water at outrageous prices because he knows we are desperate. Oh and Rokuh has developed something quite remarkable, called a choc ice

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: which is helping people stay cool.

options.text: Any idea how you got this curse?

steps.player: Any idea how you got this curse?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well we think it was because we were negligent in our duty to protect a priest of Saradomin. He came to us a few weeks ago from the north and we welcomed him into our town. He taught us much of the wisdom of

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Saradomin. Then about a week ago, we found him dead by the river. It seems unlikely that it is coincidence we were then cursed. If you look around the town you might be able to find out more.

steps.prompt: Start the Spirits of the Elid quest?

steps.player: Ok I will have a look around and see what I can do.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Good luck to you.

steps.player: I'm sorry to hear of your plight, but I must be going.

options.text: I'm sorry to hear of your plight, but I must be going.

steps.text: Well we've not fallen on the best of times here, but there are a few shops to look around and we have someone selling a marvelous new invention called a choc ice..

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Oh, and there's the old temple if you're interested in a bit of history.

options.text: What was I meant to do again?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Look around this town, see if you can uncover any information to why we were cursed and how the curse might be lifted. I suspect that it might be because a priest of Saradomin died while staying at our town, but

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: that isn't much help in getting the curse lifted and it is possible I'm wrong anyway.

options.text: I haven't really had the time to investigate.

steps.player: I haven't really had the time to investigate.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well I hope somebody can find the time soon, the despair of the people of this town increases daily.

starting-off-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elde.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
starting-off-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elde.text: Good day to you young man.

options.text: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.player: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Oh that's something which no one but the gods and the river spirits seem to know.

steps.player: River spirits, what are they?

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: They're the guardians of the source of the river Elid, they'll know of our curse, seeing as it's related to water we bring from the river. It's said that nothing happens on the river that they don't know about.

steps.player: So would it be possible for me to find these spirits and ask them what is going on?

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Ahh now the spirits are something which no one from here have seen in a good long time, certainly not in my lifetime, I don't think even in my own grandfather's lifetime.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Most the younger people of this town don't even remember that the spirits even exist.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Here I have something around here somewhere which may be of interest to you.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Aha yes here it is, the ballad of Jareesh. This tells of a previous quest to try and find the spirits.

How are things?

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Lousy, young people have no respect for their elders, there's too many confusing newfangled magic carpets and snake charmers around these days and now we don't even have any water.

steps.player: Well I hope things pick up for you.

options.text: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.text: Well with the moral standards of this town lately, I'm hardly surprised.

steps.text: Nothing someone like you would understand.

steps.player: Good day to you.

steps.text: Be Careful in here and don't touch anything! There's some old and valuable artefacts around here. Careless outsiders.. you're always coming in and making a mess of things!

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Yes, good don't.

steps.player: What is this building?

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: This is our local shrine to She.

steps.player: What do you mean by She?

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Such ignorance! I suppose I should come to expect it. People are forgetting the old ways of the desert around here. But then.. What do those bureaucratic fools in Menaphos expect! If they're going to take so long to

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: send us a new priestess of She. Do you know we haven't had one for five years now!

steps.player: Errm you still haven't told me what you mean by She.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: She! Otherwise know as Elidinis, Goddess of growth and fertility, Lady of the river, Wife of Tumeken, Flower of the desert, Mother of Icthlarin.

steps.player: That all sounds very confusing, I might just call her Elidinis for short.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: That's a very valuable artefact. Keep your hands off it.

steps.player: ..I just wanted to know what it did.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: hands off the key. People already meddle too much with the affairs of the shrine.

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: Nardarine came from a town towards the north side of the desert which does not exist today. This was in the third age in the time thou callest

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the God Wars. Her town was once controlled by Saradomin, but there was a great battle there between Saradominist and Zamorakian forces which pretty much levelled the town

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: to the ground. Most of the human citizens perished. Nardarine had the wisdom to escape into the desert before the fighting got really serious and thus survived. However she found herself wandering lost and alone in

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: the desert. She prayed to Saradomin for help, but Saradomin was too concerned with the loss of a strategic outpost to worry about the fate of one small human. Nardarine had wandered towards the realm of

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: homage to me and I grant this also unto thine descendents as long as they too will pay an oath of fealty and homage to me'. Nardarine said 'If you would grant me a safe home, with a

steps.speaker: Hallak

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: a spring of water appear at Nardarines feet and brought stone from below the sand so that she

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: might have something to build with. She called forth camels which have many uses and taste good in kebabs. She then provided Nardarine with a statuette in her image to worship. Nardarine built up her home. Over

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: time more refugees from the God Wars found Nardarine's home. Nardarine let them stay with her as long as they did make the same oath as her. Hence the town of Nardah was born and Nardarine lived the rest

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: of her days in the peacefulness that she craved. The oath was passed down the generations for many ages, but now seemeth to be forgotten. Now maybe thou canst see why we are not best pleased.
