steps.text: In a deep crevice to the west of this village.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.player: I'm told that a statuette was removed from this temple.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: Yes, that Saradominist priest brought a group of the villagers in here. Took it by force as far as I'm concerned. I'm not at all happy, standards have been slipping here for a while, but that was going too far.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: She! Elidinis! Goddess of growth and fertility! Lady of the River, Wife of Tumeken, Flower of the Desert. Mother of Icthlarin!

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.player: ..Ah yes, that She. Well you're right, that would be an insult to Elidinis. In fact it seems that affront is what has brought the curse upon this village.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: Well you know I suspected that all along, but does anyone listen to me anymore? No! Well I'm impressed you've come to the same conclusion as me, maybe I underestimated you.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.player: Er, why didn't you tell me about your suspicions when I was asking around about the curse then?

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: I have to apologise. We've already had one outsider around stirring trouble, which caused this whole mess in the first place. I feared that you were coming to force your ways on us.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: Well I'm grateful, anything you can do to find the statuette would be appreciated.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: Good day to you young man.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: Any progress on uncovering the town's curse yet?

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.player: Yes some actually. I managed to speak to the river spirits you told me about.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: You actually managed to find them? I'm impressed. As I say - no one has seen them in many many years.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.player: Yes the spirits told me that the town is cursed because you guys have thrown away a statuette to the goddess Elidinis.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: Ah yes I heard a group led by that Saradominist priest went into the shrine and removed the Statuette. It all seemed a bit unnecessary to me. Didn't realise it would curse us though.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: I have no idea what they did with it afterwards.

the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie.speaker: Genie
the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie.text: I am a mighty and powerful genie. Why do you come here? Speak now or I'll have to think of something exceedingly nasty to do to you.

options.text: You're a genie, grant me a wish.

steps.player: You're a genie, grant me a wish.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Not all genies are goody two shoes who go round granting wishes. It's something that my pathetic brother does to make people like him, but that's not my style.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: I like to think of myself more as an evil and scary sort of genie, who people talk about in hushed and fearful tones.

steps.player: Well you seem quite scary.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Why thank you, I put a lot of effort into my terrifyingness.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Wait! Did you say quite scary? I'll have you know I am VERY scary!

steps.player: Erm yes that's what I meant.

options.text: I'm after a statue that was thrown down here.
Why are you sitting here in the dark.
Well I must be off now.

steps.player: Well I must be off now.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Yes, run. Ruuuun in fear of.. The crevice genie of Nardah! Muhahaha!

options.text: Why are you sitting here in the dark?

steps.player: Why are you sitting here in the dark?

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Two reasons really. Firstly, I can see in the dark, so light or dark makes little difference to me.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Lastly, I gather it's normal for powerful terrifying creatures to lurk around in dark caves, so I found this one to lurk in myself, nice isn't it?

options.text: Very pleasant, the snakes are a nice touch.

steps.player: Very pleasant, the snakes are a nice touch.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Why do I get the sense that I'm not being taken seriously here? Please try to remember I am very dangerous and not to be trifled with.

options.text: I'm after a statue that was thrown down here.
You're a genie, grant me a wish.
Well I must be off now.

steps.player: I'm just looking around.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: I don't know about that. I can't have just anybody traipsing in here. I have a reputation to keep you see.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Actually I'll tell you what, you can hang around here for a bit, but be sure to spread the word about what a terrifying experience you had when you ran into... The crevice genie of Nardah!

steps.player: ...Ok I think I can manage that.

the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie-again-a.speaker: Genie
the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie-again-a.text: Do you have the sole of Awusah, so that we can make our trade?

options.text: How am I meant to remove someone's soul?

steps.player: I'm still working on it.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Well no rush, I quite like the statuette too.

options.text: No, it's not an easy thing to get.

steps.player: No, it's not an easy thing to get.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Haha, even a pathetic human should be able to manage to get another human's sole.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.text: Have you had any luck retrieving our statuette yet?

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.player: Err, well I have made some progress. I met a genie down the crevice. He told me that he would give me the statuette in exchange for your soul.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.text: What! That's just asking to much. So, he want's to have my soul when my time to die comes?

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.player: Well not exactly, he sort of basically said I should remove it with a knife.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.text: That's barbaric! I simply refuse. The price is too high. We'll just have to find other ways to get the town a good supply of water. Don't go bringing any knives near me.

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.text: What do you think you are doing?

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.player: Errm, I'm trying to remove your soul.

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.text: What, have you lost your mind?

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.player: It's for the good of the village. I met a genie down the crevice. He told me that he would give me the statuette in exchange for your sole.

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.text: That's barbaric! We'll just have to find other ways to get the town a good supply of water. Keep your knife away from me please.

sole-split-cutting-the-mayor-s-shoes.text: You remove the soles from the shoes.

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.speaker: Genie
sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.text: Do you have the sole of Awusah, so that we can make our trade?

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.speaker: Genie
sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.text: Ah excellent, here's the statuette then.
You trade the sole for the statuette.

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.player: So um, why do you need part of Awusah's footwear anyway? I hope you're not going to do some nasty magic on his feet or something.

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.speaker: Genie
sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.text: I hadn't thought of that. I just read that a lot of the most powerful beings are collecting soles these days. I haven't really got many yet though. You provided me with an opportunity to expand my collection.

sole-split-talking-to-the-genie-after-lo.speaker: Genie
sole-split-talking-to-the-genie-after-lo.text: Well fortunately for you, I am a mighty and powerful genie and managed to reacquire it. I will give it to you for another sole.
If the player has a sole:

steps.player: Yes I have one here.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Ah excellent here's the statuette then.
You trade the sole for the statuette.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: It's good doing business with you again.

sole-split-talking-to-the-genie-after-lo.text: If the player does not have a sole:

steps.player: I will go and get one then.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Great! Another one for my collection.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.text: Have you had any luck retrieving our statuette yet?

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.player: Yes I finally got it. I had to destroy a pair of your shoes though. A crazy genie wanted a sole off your shoe in return for the statuette. I think he got souls and soles confused.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.text: I suppose sacrificing a pair of shoes for the greater good of the town is reasonable. I don't begin to understand the ways of genies.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.player: Yes I thought it best not to correct him. He's somewhat less dangerous than he might be if he's a collector of shoe soles.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.text: Anyway thanks for getting the statue back. You should take it to our temple and then we can see if our fountain starts working again.

sole-split-talking-to-shiratti-with-the-.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
sole-split-talking-to-shiratti-with-the-.text: That is great news! I could kiss you, but they don't allow shrine custodians to engage in that sort of behaviour. You should put the statuette back on its plinth.

steps.player: That smells nice!

steps.npc: Mmm, yes. Some hunters caught it earlier today.

steps.player: Can I have some?

steps.npc: Oh, it's not cooked yet. But they sell frogburgers in the market!

overhead-dialogue-when-petting-a-spooky-.text: The spooky dog follows the player around.

before-completing-pandemonium.npc: I see you.

before-completing-pandemonium.player: You do?

before-completing-pandemonium.npc: Indeed! It's kind of what I do. The name's Virginia. I'm a lookout for the spirit anglers, as well as a six time eye spy world champion.

before-completing-pandemonium.player: And what are you on the lookout for at the moment?

before-completing-pandemonium.npc: To be honest, a new adventure. The anglers have been good to me, but after the chaos with Tempoross, I'd like a fresh start.

before-completing-pandemonium.player: Makes sense. Well, I hope one finds you soon.

before-completing-pandemonium.npc: I hope so too, but not before I find it first!

before-sailing-level-40.npc: Indeed! It's kind of what I do. The name's Virginia. I'm a lookout for the spirit anglers, as well as a six time eye spy world champion.

before-sailing-level-40.npc: To be honest, a new adventure. The angler's have been good to me, but after the chaos with Tempoross, I'd like a fresh start.

before-sailing-level-40.player: Well, at some point I plan to hire a crew of my own. I'm not ready for that sort of thing yet, but when I am, maybe you'd be interested?

before-sailing-level-40.npc: I think I might be! You just let me know once you start recruiting... provided I don't spot you first, of course!

before-sailing-level-40.text: You need a Sailing level of 40 to manage a crew.

before-sailing-level-40-again.player: Ah, hello again. How are things going?

before-sailing-level-40-again.npc: Pretty well, though I'm still on the lookout for a new adventure.

before-sailing-level-40-again.player: Well, at some point I plan to hire a crew of my own. I'm not ready for that sort of thing yet, but when I am, maybe you'd be interested?

after-sailing-level-40.npc: To be honest, a new adventure. The angler's have been good to me, but after the chaos with Tempoross, I'd like a fresh start.

options.text: How about you join my crew?

steps.text: If the player's Sailing level is under 90 or has less than 100 Tempoross subdues:

steps.player: Maybe I could help? How about you join my crew?

steps.npc: Sorry, but I can't see that happening right now. Maybe once you're more experienced.

steps.text: You require the following to recruit this crew member: Level 90 Sailing. Have subdued the Tempoross 100 times.
If the player's Sailing level is at least 90 and has at least 100 Tempoross subdues:

steps.player: Maybe I could help? How about you join my crew?

steps.npc: Sure! I can watch your back!

steps.text: You recruit Spotter Virginia as a crew member. She departs for the Pandemonium.

steps.player: Well, I hope one finds you soon.

steps.npc: I hope so too, but not before I find it first!

when-at-the-pandemonium.player: Hello there. How are things going?

when-at-the-pandemonium.npc: Pretty good. I'm very much enjoying seeing the sights.

when-at-the-pandemonium.player: Well, let me know if you spot anything worth looking into.

steps.npc: These sails are blocking my view.
I can't focus on being the lookout with all this work to do.

standard-dialogue-before-a-porcine-of-in.npc: I've only recently moved in and I'm still getting unpacked. Could you come back later?

standard-dialogue-after-a-porcine-of-int.npc: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

steps.player: I need another assignment.

steps.text: If the player has a high combat level:

steps.npc: You're actually very strong, are you sure you don't want Chaeldar in Zanaris to assign you a task?

options.text: No that's okay, I'll take a task from you.

steps.player: No that's okay, I'll take a task from you.

options.text: Oh okay then, I'll go talk to Chaeldar.

steps.player: Oh okay then, I'll go talk to Chaeldar.

steps.npc: Excellent, you're doing great. Your new task is to kill [amount] [task monster].

steps.text: If the player already has an assignment:

steps.npc: You're still hunting [task monster], you have [amount] to go.

steps.text: If the player already has an assignment, and they have become ineligible for this assignment:

steps.npc: You're still hunting [monster], with [amount] to go.
I don't think that's a suitable task for you. Shall I cancel it? This will not wipe your task streaks.

steps.player: Yes, please cancel it.

steps.npc: Alright, consider the task cancelled. You can now get a new assignment when you want one.

options.text: No, thanks, I want to try doing it.

steps.player: No, thanks, I want to try doing it.

steps.npc: Good luck with that.

options.text: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?

steps.player: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?

steps.npc: I have quite a few rewards you can earn, and a wide variety of Slayer equipment for sale.

options.text: Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

steps.player: Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

steps.text: If the player has disabled combat checking:

steps.npc: The Slayer Masters may currently assign you any task in our lists, regardless of your combat level.

options.text: That's fine - I can handle any task.

steps.npc: That's the spirit.

options.text: In future, please don't give anything too tough.

steps.player: About Turael...

steps.npc: It's nothing personal, but I'd prefer not to discuss what happened with my father.

steps.player: Of course. Sorry for bringing it up.
Er... Nothing...

standard-dialogue-after-the-knight-s-swo.npc: Hello friend! Many thanks for all of your help! Vyvin never even realised it was a different sword, and I still have my job!

standard-dialogue-after-the-knight-s-swo.player: I'm glad the new sword worked out alright.

standard-dialogue-before-king-s-ransom.npc: I'm sorry, my [lord/lady/liege], but you cannot enter this area.

standard-dialogue-before-king-s-ransom.text: You need to have completed the King's Ransom Quest to gain access to the Knight Waves.

before-completing-the-knight-waves.npc: That door leads to the training ground for the Knights of the Round Table.
Of course, my [lord/lady/liege]. But I must tell you the rules first. Would you like to hear them now?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.npc: The training ground is a melee combat area only. Merlin has cast a spell over the grounds to prevent anyone using Prayer, Ranged or Magic.

Upon entering the grounds, you will fight each of the Round Table Knights in turn. Each knight is more skilled than the last, but all have different attack styles that can be exploited. There are eight knights in all, and
each will do damage not only to your hitpoints, but also your combat stats. If you should die in the grounds, Merlin will teleport you back here. You will not lose any of your items.
If you feel you cannot complete the battle, you may exit the training grounds. However, if you exit or die, you will have to start over with the first knight the next time you enter.

If you are a great warrior and defeat Sir Lancelot, mightiest of all knights, you will receive great rewards. Two new prayers will become available to you and your respawn point will be set to Camelot, as well as 20,000
XP in to each of your combat stats.
If you do not want your respawn set to Camelot, Merlin can change it for you.
Would you like me to repeat any of that for you?

options.text: Tell me about the training ground

steps.player: Tell me about the training ground.

steps.npc: Only melee combat is allowed within the training grounds. Merlin will prevent the use of Prayer, Ranged and Magic.

steps.player: Why?

steps.npc: These grounds are for only the best knights of the land. It is not just testing your combat ability, but your honour and your chivalry. You must face your enemy head on, honourably and bravely.
Be watchful of your stats, as the Knights can do damage to your combat stats as well as your hitpoints.

options.text: Tell me about dying or leaving the grounds

steps.player: Tell me about dying or leaving the grounds.

steps.npc: As these are only training grounds, we keep our knights safe. If you should die, you will be teleported back to here and all of your items will be safe.
However, leaving the training grounds, in anyway, will mean you will have to start from the beginning the next time you enter. These grounds do not favour cowards.

steps.player: I have to start again? What do you mean?

steps.npc: You fight each knight of the Round Table, starting with Sir Bedivere and finishing with Sir Lancelot. Leaving means you will have to begin fighting Sir Bedivere again and work your way back up.

steps.player: What if I log out during the fights?

steps.npc: If you log out during a fight, upon logging back in you will fight the knight you were fighting when you logged out.

steps.player: Tell me about the rewards.

steps.npc: King Arthur believes in rewarding his knights for their chivalry. Having proven yourself in combat against his knights, and in your services rendered to Camelot, you will be rewarded with two new prayers, and a new
respawn at Camelot, as well as 20,000 XP in to each of your combat stats.

steps.player: What do the new prayers do?

steps.npc: Ah, patience is a virtue in knights, my [lord/lady/liege]. Fight in the training ground and earn your reward to find out!

steps.player: Then tell me about the respawn - how will it work?

steps.npc: Ah, Merlin has offered, as a reward for your help, to let your respawn in the safety of Camelot, should you befall misfortune elsewhere in the world. Should you wish to change your respawn back to Lumbridge, simply
speak to Merlin.

steps.player: No, thank you.
No, thank you.

after-completing-the-knight-waves.npc: Congratulations on succeeding in the Knight Waves, my [lord/lady/liege].

after-completing-the-knight-waves.player: Thank you. Can I go back inside?

after-completing-the-knight-waves.npc: I'm afraid not, my [lord/lady/liege]. Once you have won, you cannot re-enter.

steps.player: Hello there. How's it going?

steps.npc: Busy, busy, busy.
Sorry, but I'm busy right now.
Sorry, but I have lots of work to do.
Not too bad, but the work is definitely tiring.
Well I could do with a good rest, but fine otherwise.

options.text: Who are you and what are you doing?

steps.npc: I'm Vicks, squire to Sir Culler Flife. He's away on a surveillance mission to Burthorpe, so he sent me down here to do some cleaning.

options.text: You don't seem to be cleaning much.

steps.npc: Don't tell the knights, but I'm just not in the mood for it! I've served for years, and worked really hard, but they're not even thinking of making me a knight.
I don't know what the problem is. At my last review, I heard the examiner muttering something about my name, but I've no idea what he meant by that.

options.text: What's your master doing in Burthorpe?

steps.npc: Keeping an eye on those Imperial Guard. We can't trust 'em, you know. But I shouldn't talk about his mission.

options.text: What's with the glowing portal thing?
What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.player: Tell me about this place.

steps.npc: This place? It's the castle crypt. The greatest White Knights are buried here, after a lifetime in the service of Saradomin. At least, that's how it used to be.
When I was a new recruit, they brought me here and told me that if I served Saradomin faithfully, and with distinction, maybe I'd earn the honour of burial in this place too.
But if you think about it, that's never going to happen - there just isn't space for more tombs! Anyway, my plan is to avoid dying, and maybe marry one of the barmaids when I retire.

options.text: What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.player: What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.npc: It's because of something the Temple Knights have, called the Gaze of Saradomin. They get the option of being brought to Falador when they die, so Death has to maintain a presence in the area.
That portal takes you to Death's own realm. He's got portals in all the places where people go when they die - Lumbridge, Edgeville and the rest. I hate it - the thing's terrifying!

steps.player: I'll leave you alone.

steps.player: What's your master doing in Burthorpe?

steps.npc: Keeping an eye on those Imperial Guard, [sir/madam]. We can't trust 'em, you know. But I shouldn't talk about his mission, even with a knight such as yourself.

options.text: What's with the glowing portal thing?
What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.player: Tell me about this place.

steps.npc: This place? It's the castle crypt. The greatest White Knights are buried here, after a lifetime in the service of Saradomin. At least, that's how it used to be.
When I was a new recruit, they brought me here and told me that if I served Saradomin faithfully, and with distinction, maybe I'd earn the honour of burial in this place too.
But if you think about it, that's never going to happen - there just isn't space for more tombs! Anyway, my plan is to avoid dying, and maybe marry one of the barmaids when I retire.

options.text: What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.player: What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.npc: It's because of the Gaze of Saradomin. You Temple Knights get the option of being brought to Falador when you die, so Death has to maintain a presence in the area.
That portal takes you to Death's own realm. He's got portals in all the places where people go when they die - Lumbridge, Edgeville and the rest. I hate it - the thing's terrifying!

steps.player: I'll leave you alone.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hi, how can I help you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I'm a Squire for the Void Knights.

steps.player: The who?

steps.npc: The Void Knights, they are great warriors of balance who do Guthix's work here in Gielinor.

steps.player: Wow, can I join?

steps.npc: Entry is strictly invite only, however we do need help continuing Guthix's work.

steps.player: Good luck with that.
What kind of work?

steps.npc: Ah well you see we try to keep Gielinor as Guthix intended, it's very challenging. Actually we've been having some problems recently, maybe you could help us?

steps.player: Yeah ok, what's the problem?

steps.npc: Well the order has become quite diminished over the years, it's a very long process to learn the skills of a Void Knight. Recently there have been breaches into our realm from somewhere else, and strange creatures
have been pouring through. We can't let that happen, and we'd be very grateful if you'd help us.

steps.player: How can I help?

steps.npc: We send launchers from our outpost to the nearby islands. If you go and wait in the lander there that'd really help.

steps.player: Sorry, but I can't.
I'd rather not, sorry.
What's 'Gielinor'?

steps.npc: It is the name that Guthix gave to this world, so we honour him with its use.

steps.player: Uh huh, sure.
What's going on here?

steps.npc: This is where we launch our landers to combat the invasion of the nearby islands. You'll see three landers - one for novice, intermediate and veteran adventurers. Each has a different difficulty, but they therefore offer
varying rewards.

steps.player: And this lander is...?

steps.npc: The intermediate.

steps.player: So how do they work?

steps.npc: Simple. We send a lander out every few minutes, however we need at least 5 volunteers or it's a suicide mission. The lander can only hold a maximum of 25 people though, so we do send them out early if they get
full. If you'd be willing to help us then just wait in the lander and we'll launch it as soon as it's ready. However you will need a combat level of 70 to use this lander.

steps.player: I'm fine thanks.

steps.player: What's going on?

portals yourself.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: Not much to say. Came to Weiss with other trolls when we got kicked out of caves further south, but I was just young troll then.
Mostly been enjoying living round Weiss, 'cos wildlife is interesting here.

steps.player: Tell me about this place.

steps.npc: This here is Weiss. Trolls built it years ago, after we got kicked out from caves further south. Now Weiss is our home.
It great here, now Snowflake an' her husband troll taught us goutweed farming. Food so much better now.

steps.player: Do you like it here?

steps.npc: Eh, it kinda rough, but it getting better. Snowflake, she taught us goutweed farming. Goat, wolf, human all taste so much nicer with goutweed in.
So yeah, Weiss is good place to live, now Snowflake in charge. All trolls like Snowflake. Her husband troll kinda weird, but that not our problem.

steps.player: I'll be off.

steps.npc: Because I say so! My cousin Nieve thinks she's so great because she's got a big cave where she can boss people around. So I carved some steps out of the ice, and made myself a training area here.

steps.npc: No, I'm not. My cousin Nieve is a Slayer Master. There's nothing special about her, you know. All she does is tell people to kill stuff. That's Slayer Masters for you.

steps.player: Thanks, goodbye.

options.text: What kind of stone do you sell?

steps.player: What kind of stone do you sell?

steps.npc: A few kinds. Limestone, of course. Here in Keldagrim we're surrounded by the stuff so I can practically give it away! You'll be able to build some kinds of furniture out of that.
Marble is much better, of course, but it costs a lot for me to get hold of it. You can make some beautiful pieces of furniture out of that.
I also sell gold leaf, which can be used to decorate furniture made of marble or mahogany.
Then for the very special furniture I sell these magic stones. Only the most skilled builders can work them, but they can create a few amazing pieces of furniture with them.
So, do you want to buy anything?

standard-dialogue.player: Oh, that's a shame. Never mind then.

historical-dialogue.speaker: Stone mason

historical-dialogue.player: You know what would be brilliant?
Could you make some granite armour or alter granite armour to better fit me?

historical-dialogue.speaker: Stone mason
historical-dialogue.text: I'm afraid I can't do that, sorry. In the blazing desert sun, granite armour isn't very popular so I haven't had any experience of working with it.

historical-dialogue.speaker: Stone mason
historical-dialogue.text: Once the place is a bit less chaotic, however, I will try to think of ways you adventurers can help. Who knows what I'll come up with.

historical-dialogue.player: Should I come back soon, then?

historical-dialogue.speaker: Stone mason
historical-dialogue.text: I wouldn't hold my breath. I'm thinking it will be months before I have work for you rather than a few days.

his-faithful-servants-miniquest-dialogue.npc: Time to dig. To dig, dig, dig. But no normal dig. We now have new purpose!

his-faithful-servants-miniquest-dialogue.player: What do you mean? What purpose?

They made a pact you see! Strength in life for servitude in death.
Yes! They guard it for him! That was their purpose, but that time is up now. He wants it back! You can get it! You can dig!

his-faithful-servants-miniquest-dialogue.player: You want me to bring you something?

his-faithful-servants-miniquest-dialogue.npc: The icon! He needs it now! You must dig, dig dig. Slay the brothers six! It's okay, it won't hurt them... much. The icon will be in the chest!

his-faithful-servants-miniquest-dialogue.player: Right... So you want me to go and kill the six brothers and bring you back an icon?

his-faithful-servants-miniquest-dialogue.npc: Yes! Do this! Do this! Maybe little prize for you if you do. But first you must dig! Dig, dig, dig!

steps.npc: Welcome back, my child.

steps.player: How are things in Morytania?

steps.npc: Very good, my child. My disciples are providing a steady supply of their blood for the vampyres. As promised, the tithing of humans has been completely outlawed.

steps.player: And the vampyres are all happy with that?

steps.npc: Most are understanding of the fact that regardless of anything else, the days of tithing humans were running short. However, it is true that some found human blood to be more... appetising.

steps.player: I assume that won't be a problem?

steps.npc: You need not fear, my child. Any that attempt to take blood from a human will be dealt with harshly.

That said, my understanding is that some humans did willingly provide their blood to the Drakans. It is of course possible that could be explored again in future, albeit with very different arrangements.
However, I very much understand that will likely be a... difficult proposal for most to swallow.

steps.player: Yes, I can't see many being up for that sort of thing. Speaking of which, how are the humans of Morytania doing?

steps.npc: The fact that they are not being tithed is on its own a significant improvement to their quality of life. However, their homes are still ruins and these lands are still dangerous.
We are offering our help in building them new homes, but it will take many years, and most are still naturally distrusting of our kind.

steps.player: I'm guessing a lot will be more interested in starting new lives across the Salve.

steps.npc: You are correct, my child. However, while we have established somewhat of an... understanding with your human kingdoms to the west, it is their preference that we try to limit how many humans relocate over there.

They are not equipped to deal with a large number of refugees, and it is also our hope that many humans will realise they still have a place here. We will need their help restoring these lands to glory.

steps.player: That's not going to be an easy undertaking.

steps.npc: It will most certainly take many of your human lifetimes, but I have no doubt we will make it so.

options.text: I see you've opened a new portal to Vampyrium.

steps.player: I see you've opened a new portal to Vampyrium.

steps.npc: Yes... While my disciples are currently providing blood for the vampyres here, I do not consider that a suitable long-term solution. Haemalchemy, I believe, will be the true answer.

With us having outlawed the practice of vampyrification, we have started using the labs to explore the creation of artificial blood instead. Curiously, we've already had some luck with daeyalt of all things.
It seems that the very substance that is the key to making vampyres can also potentially contribute to feeding them. While it makes sense in many ways, it was also rather... unexpected.

steps.player: Interesting... And how does Vampyrium play into this?

steps.npc: Vampyrium is home to all manner of flora and fauna that cannot be found here. With the threat of Drakan dealt with, my disciples can freely travel to and from there, collecting samples to use in our experiments.

You are more than welcome to use the portal yourself, my child. Blood donations from Efaritay and my disciples keep it well powered, and it may be that you'll find Vampyrium to offer something of interest to you.

standard-dialogue-the-first-time-the-pla.npc: I've not seen your face before. Given they let you come down here, I'm assuming you've been allowed to join the Alchemical Society?
Well in that case, just through there is the lab we use to produce potions for the kingdom. However, before you head in and get started, there's a couple of things to note.
First, I can see you're not from around here, so I'll point out that Varlamorian Alchemy is a little different from the Druidic Herblore that you'll be familiar with.
We discovered that the majority of herbs in the world can be broken down into three alchemical reagents: Mox, Aga and Lye.
When mixed in the correct way, these three components produce drastically different results. As such, in the lab you will be using these components to create various potions.

standard-dialogue-the-first-time-the-pla.player: What potions do I need to make?

standard-dialogue-the-first-time-the-pla.npc: That depends. We get orders in from across the kingdom. You'll need to keep an eye out for what potions are currently desired and ensure you're making the right ones.

steps.player: Let's do that run through.

steps.npc: Very well... Listen closely.

steps.text: The scene cuts to each part of the laboratory as they are discussed

steps.npc: Start by breaking down herbs or unfinished potions over at the Refiner. This will give you your reagents: Mox, Aga, and Lye paste. The type you get will depend on the quality of what you put in.
Insert the paste into the Hopper and it will become available to use in the Mixer.
From here, you'll need to pull the Mixer Levers to create the right combination of reagents.

steps.player: But how do I know what the combinations are?

steps.text: If the player has mixology lab notes:

steps.npc: I see you've already found our book of lab notes. That'll give you the formulas for our various products.

steps.text: If the player does not have mixology lab notes:

steps.npc: Have a look on the bookshelf for a book of lab notes. That'll give you the formulas for our various products.
To know what needs making, you'll need to check the order list. There will always be three orders to choose from. You can work on just one or them, or multiple. It's up to you.
Just be aware that demand shifts fast here. Every time you fulfil one or more orders, a new set will come through.
Now, once you have set your desired combination of reagents, collect the unfinished mixture from the Mixing Vessel. This will then need to be processed on one of the three tables to finish it off.
The Alembic will Crystalise the mixture.
The Agitator will Homogenise the mixture.
And finally, the Retort will Concentrate the mixture.
After processing, place the finished mixture on the Conveyor Belt and move on to the next order.

steps.player: What if I get an order wrong, or am unable to fulfil any of the orders?

steps.npc: We always have need for spares, so fulfilling an incorrect order will still grant you a small reward and will refresh the orders.
One final thing to mention... We have some Digweed growing in the lab.
These rare herbs will occasionally come into maturity for a short period of time. Harvest them while you can!
Mixing some into your product will increase its potency and grant you bonus rewards.

steps.player: Bonus rewards?

steps.npc: That's right. As you produce potions, you'll find yourself collecting three types of Resin. The types obtained depend on what reagents are used, with the quantities being determined by the complexity of the
potion.
Potions using Digweed will reward additional Resin, as will handing in multiple potions in one go.

steps.player: Got it! So, refine herbs, deposit into the hopper, mix some products, process them, and then throw them on the conveyor. Seems easy enough!

steps.player: Can I have some rewards?

steps.npc: As you wish.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Alchemical Society?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Alchemical Society?

steps.npc: Can't imagine there's much to tell beyond what you already know. We exist to bring about advancements in Herblore, but in truth, a lot of what we produce doesn't directly contribute to that.
Instead, many of the potions we make here are simply to sell. Doing so is what provides the funding we need to further our true goals.

steps.player: Makes sense. So how did the society first get established?

steps.npc: For a long time, it was just a couple of us operating out of a makeshift lab we'd built in my garden. Our big break came when the Moonrise Brewery and Winery learnt about us.
They provided us with some initial funding to properly get things going, but more importantly, they provided this lab space. This was actually one of their old wine cellars before we moved in.

steps.player: Why were they so interested in your work?

steps.npc: They never properly said why, just that they were very keen to see us grow. Maybe they're hoping our work can help them create new beers and wines.

steps.player: I see. I suppose that makes sense.
Nothing, I'll be going now.

historical-dialogue-receiving-a-tutorial.npc: To know what needs making, you'll need to check the order list. There will always be three orders to choose from. Demand shifts fast here so every time you fulfil an order, a new set will come through.

steps.text: Before completing The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: How did you know about that?

steps.text: After completing The Giant Dwarf:

steps.npc: Veldaban told me about your involvement in the rebuilding of the statue. Congratulations.

steps.player: Thank you!
Who are you?

steps.npc: I am Bisi. I am the Supreme Commander of the Black Guard.

steps.player: I thought Veldaban was in command?

steps.npc: Only of our regiment in Keldagrim, and a most honourable position it is as well.
But the Black Guard has many regiments across the dwarven realm. All the Commanders of those regiments report to me.

steps.npc: That's good to hear.

steps.player: What news have you?

steps.text: Before completing The Giant Dwarf:

steps.npc: Apart from the statue of King Alvis falling down, you mean? I don't know. There is something suspicious about the whole case.

steps.player: How do you mean?

steps.npc: We've had several incidents recently. For a while we even closed off the city. And now this.

steps.text: After completing The Giant Dwarf:

steps.npc: The Red Axe has withdrawn from the city to some unknown location. I believe Commander Veldaban has asked you to assist him in finding their secret headquarters?

steps.player: Oh yes, you're right.

steps.text: After completing Forgettable Tale... (?):

steps.npc: Apart from you helping to rebuild the statue for the [company name]?
There seems to be some general unrest in the city. There is trouble brewing in Keldagrim.
But I'm sure Commander Veldaban is on top of it. He's a very capable officer, and I'm starting to get too old for this sort of thing.

steps.text: After completing Between a Rock... and Forgettable Tale... (?):

steps.npc: Well, I heard that you helped Veldaban's father in the mines to the south. That's caused quite a bit of an upset in the Consortium, so I understand.

steps.player: How so?

steps.npc: The amount of wealth that goldmine is generating might cause some distortion in the balance of power in the Consortium. But we'll see.
Apart from that there seems to be some general unrest in the city. Trouble is brewing in Keldagrim.
But I'm sure Commander Veldaban is on top of it. He's a very capable officer, and I'm starting to get too old for this sort of thing.

steps.player: I must go now.

steps.npc: Then I bid you farewell, human.

starting-out.speaker: Herman Caranos
starting-out.text: Lovely? Oh - er - if you say so. But please excuse me, I really don't have time to chat about the weather.

starting-out.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.player: What's the rush?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Trolls! They're attacking my fishing Colony!

steps.player: Gosh, I didn't know there were any trolls around here.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: These are a sort of sea-dwelling troll. They feed on the monkfish that live in this part of the sea, but just recently they've started invading my Colony!

steps.player: Do you need any help?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Well yes, I do. I've done some research about this, and I think our best hope is to get hold of an experienced adventurer.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: In all the legends I've read, brave adventurers have no trouble vanquishing whatever monsters are menacing the helpless settlement.

options.text: You've been... reading stories about adventurers?

steps.player: You've been... reading stories about adventurers?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Yes, I've done my research very carefully. I've always made important decisions based on careful analysis of whatever documents are available to me on the topic. For example, I chose this site for my Fishing Colony because

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: records show this part of the sea to be a prime site for catching monkfish. I don't just fumble along like an amateur!

steps.player: ... fair enough, I suppose! Anyway, you think you need an adventurer?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Yes, that's right. A brave adventurer with plenty of experience in this sort of work.

options.text: I'm a brave adventurer! Can I try?

steps.player: I'm a brave adventurer! Can I try?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: You? I hadn't thought of that... let's have a look at you...
If the player does not meet the quest requirements:

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: No, I'm sorry, but you simply do not have enough experience. I've got a LOT at stake here, and I can't afford to have an amateur getting in the way.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Hmmm... You're not what I'm looking for, but... [amount] Quest Points is really rather a lot...

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Ok, the Piscatoris Fishing Colony gratefully accepts your offer of help. When the Colony is safe you shall be handsomely rewarded.

steps.player: Oh goody, I love rewards! Now, how can I help?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Well, as qualified as you undoubtedly are, I believe we're going to need a truly expert adventurer if the Colony is to stand a chance.
If the player has not completed Legends' Quest:

steps.player: Expert adventurer? I'll wager I've had more adventures than you've had pickled gherkins!

steps.text: If the player has completed Legends' Quest:

steps.player: Expert adventurer? I'll have you know I'm in the Guild of Legends!

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: If you could just stop blowing your own trumpet for a minute...

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Excellent! Now, in far-away Misthalin there lives one of the greatest adventurers of all time.

steps.player: ... this better be good...

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: His name is lost in the mists of time, but you shouldn't have much trouble finding the Wise Old Man of Draynor Village.
If the player has either spoken to the Wise Old Man before or watched the Draynor bank robbery:

steps.player: Him? What in the heck do you want with HIM?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Oh, do you know him?
If the player does not know he robbed the bank:

steps.player: Well I've met him. Don't you think he's a bit old?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Maybe, but he's still an expert adventurer.
If the player knows he robbed the bank:

steps.player: Yes! He's mad! You know he smashed his way into a bank and stole a load of stuff?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Ah well, we must forgive him his little foibles.

options.text: You used to be a famous adventurer, didn't you?

steps.player: You used to be a famous adventurer, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Heh heh! Yes, I suppose you could say that. But that was all quite a long time ago. I haven't been on what you'd call a 'quest' for a while.

steps.player: Does that mean you'd be interested if someone asked for your help?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh? What exactly had you in mind?

steps.player: Herman Caranos of the Piscatoris Fishing Colony thinks he needs you to save his colony from a tribe of attacking sea trolls.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Hmmm... so I haven't been forgotten... and the world once again is calling for my aid...

steps.player: Well, it's just one man who smells of fish, not exactly the whole world...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ... yet this could be the opportunity I've been waiting for...

steps.player: ... yawn...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ... but I'm a lot older than I used to be, do I still have the strength? Should I retire now, or can I do just one more quest?

steps.player: If you're not feeling up to it, I'll leave you alone.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, I'll do it! This can be my final adventure, my last great quest. Saving this colony shall be my swan song.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Legend tells us that a swan, before it dies, sings a song of outstanding beauty as a fitting conclusion to its graceful life. This adventure will be my swan song.

steps.player: You're going to sing a song and then snuff it? Maybe I should tell Herman you've flipped...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, you ignoramus! I shall bring my adventuring days to a dramatic close by saving this colony!

steps.text: Ok, hand 'em over.

inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman.text: Excellent! You have no idea how grateful I am!

I'm sure my brother, Franklin, could do with a bit of help. Arnold, the storemaster, said he needed an extra pair of hands too. He's in one of the big storage sheds.

inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman.player: Ok, I help out, then I get a reward?

inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman.speaker: Herman Caranos
inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman.text: Yes, yes... now please excuse us.

inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman-agai.speaker: Herman Caranos
inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman-agai.text: [player name]? Have you helped Franklin and Arnold yet?
If the player hasn't helped either of them:

steps.player: No, I haven't.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Please do so!

inside-the-colony-talking-to-herman-agai.text: If the player has started helping either of them:

steps.player: I'm on the case, no problems.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: That's what I like to hear. Off you go...

helping-franklin.player: Herman said you wanted a hand with something.

helping-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin.text: Well, yes, I do. Are you any good at smithing?

helping-franklin.player: Oh yes, I'm quite an expert.

helping-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin.text: Ok, we'll see. Now, the trolls managed to smash part of our western wall earlier today. We need 5 sheets of iron to patch it.

helping-franklin.player: Won't iron go all rusty with all the salt water around here?

helping-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin.text: Yes, but it'll do for a few weeks, and we haven't the time or materials to do a proper job just now.

helping-franklin.player: Alrighty. So where do I get sheets of iron?

helping-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin.text: I've got a press in my shred. You can use it to heat up some iron bars and roll them into sheets. You'll need to fill its firebox first - stick some logs in it and light them.

helping-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin.text: When you've got 5 iron sheets, hammer them onto the damage wall.

helping-franklin.player: Why do I need to heat the bars? I've been cold- working metal all my life, and I've never bothered heating it.

helping-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin.text: How odd! I'd have expected all your products to be horribly brittle.
If the player is not carrying a tinderbox:

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Anyway, take this tinderbox and get to work.
Tinderbox

steps.player: Thanks.

helping-franklin.text: If the player has a tinderbox:

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Anyway, off you go.

helping-franklin-attempting-to-flatten-i.player: It's not hot enough to work at the moment.

helping-franklin-using-the-tinderbox-or-.player: The firebox is at the other end of the machine!

helping-franklin-using-the-iron-bars-on-.player: I should probably try putting metal bars into the OTHER end of the machine.

helping-franklin-using-the-logs-on-the-f.text: The firebox of the press is now filled with wood.

steps.player: I'm working on it.

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Good, good.

options.text: I can't remember what you wanted me to do.

steps.player: I can't remember what you wanted me to do.

steps.text: Put some logs into the metal press in my shed, and light them. Then feed 5 iron bars into the press to roll them into sheets. After that, you'll need to hammer them onto the damaged wall.

helping-franklin-using-an-iron-sheet-on-.text: The iron sheet is not changed in any way.

helping-franklin-using-any-other-item-on.player: I'm not putting that into the press! I don't want to break it!

helping-franklin-talking-to-franklin-aft.player: Well, the press is working now, but I still have to patch [the broken sections/[Amount] more bits of wall/the last piece of wall].

helping-franklin-talking-to-franklin-aft.text: With no sheets in inventory and no repaired walls:

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: I hope you don't have too much trouble with that press.
If the player doesn't have a hammer:

steps.player: Also I think I need a hammer.

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Hammer? Not a problem - here's mine.
Hammer

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos

helping-franklin-using-hammer-on-the-bro.text: You feel a lot calmer now, but it didn't achieve anything else. Maybe you should be using the iron sheet on the wall instead.

helping-franklin-using-any-other-item-on.player: I don't think that will help.

helping-franklin-using-iron-sheet-on-an-.player: This bit of wall is fine. I don't need to mess around with it now.

helping-franklin-using-hammer-on-an-alre.text: You feel a lot calmer now, but it didn't achieve anything else.

helping-franklin-using-iron-sheet-on-fra.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-franklin-using-iron-sheet-on-fra.text: You should be sticking the sheets to the wall, not to me!

helping-franklin-talking-to-franklin-aft.player: I've fixed all 5 bits of wall.

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Wonderful - thank you very much! Now you can turn your full attention to help Arnold...

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Oh, and if you've got any of those iron sheets left, I'll be happy to buy them off you once the Colony is safe.

steps.player: This is turning into a lot of work...

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Wonderful - thank you very much! You should return to my brother, Herman, and tell him you've finished helping me and Arnold.

steps.speaker: Franklin Caranos
steps.text: Oh, and if you've got any of those iron sheets left, I'll be happy to buy them off you once the Colony is safe.

steps.player: Oh good. Now maybe Herman will give me that reward he mentioned!

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: You come to speak to me, [player name]?

helping-arnold.player: Yes... Herman said you needed me to do something?

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: Ah, that is good. I the storemaster am for this Piscatoris Fishing Colony, and our stores are - ahah - not so good. Indeed, our stores contain not a bit of food!

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: This a catastrophe may become, as difficult it may be to fish while the trolls outside are waiting, and our bellies soon shall rumble loudly!

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: But now you come here to help Arnold! A good and sturdy warrior you must be indeed to have entered our Colony in these times! So you can the fishing do for us!

helping-arnold.player: You want me to catch fish?

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: Ja, this is so. But the fish must then be stored, or stinking rotten they become! So the fish you bring must be shiny fresh!

helping-arnold.player: Where do I get fresh fish?

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: The monkfish in these waters swim, this is why Herr Caranos build his Colony here.

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: You go catch 5 fresh monkfish from sea over in north- west corner. If you bring stinking old monkfish, Arnold know about it, and Arnold not take them!
If the player does not have a net:

steps.player: I'll need a net or something like that.

steps.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
steps.text: Ja, is not a problem.
Small fishing net

helping-arnold.player: Ok, five fresh monkfish coming up.

helping-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold.text: Big thanks, [player name]. When Colony safe, Herman reward you good.

helping-arnold-attempting-to-take-fish-f.player: I think I should maybe catch my own.

steps.player: No, I haven't got any.

steps.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
steps.text: Well, you go to sea at north-west corner of Colony and catch nice fresh monkfish for Arnold, ja?

steps.player: Ok.

helping-arnold-talking-to-arnold-again.text: With the wrong type of fish:

steps.player: I've got this fish...

steps.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
steps.text: That not monkfish! Go to sea at north-west corner of Colony and catch MONKFISH!

Your activity attracts an even bigger sea troll!

helping-arnold-talking-to-arnold-after-f.player: Arnold, I've got some monkfish for you.

steps.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
steps.text: This? This fresh, but it no good to me raw! You go use range in kitchen!

steps.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
steps.text: Ah, lovely fresh monkfish straight from the sea! Now you bring me [amount] more, ja?

steps.player: Right, right.

helping-arnold-talking-to-arnold-after-f.text: After giving Arnold all 5 cooked monkfish:

helping-arnold-talking-to-arnold-after-h.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
helping-arnold-talking-to-arnold-after-h.text: Now you done helping me and Frankie, you go see what Herr Caranos want next.

helping-arnold-talking-to-franklin-after.speaker: Franklin Caranos
helping-arnold-talking-to-franklin-after.text: Now you've finished helping me and Arnold, you should see if Herman's got anything else for you to do.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.player: I've finished helping Franklin and Arnold now.
Does this mean you're going to reward me now?

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Herman Caranos
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: There's something else I need you to do first.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Herman Caranos
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: Well, the Wise Old Man and I have discussed the situation, and he's come up with a plan...

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Wise Old Man
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: Yes, that's right. The sheer number of trolls means that the best hope for the Colony is to gather our forces and wipe out all the trolls at once.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.player: Well, that sounds like a nice plan. One big fight, no more trolls.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Wise Old Man
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: Yes, with the bit about gathering our forces.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.player: Let me guess - you haven't got any forces to gather!

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Herman Caranos
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: I sent most of the colonists away for their own safety when the trolls started attacking the Colony.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Wise Old Man
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: So what you need to do, [player name], is to fetch us an army!

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.speaker: Wise Old Man
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.text: In the Wizards' Guild in Yanille, Wizard Frumscone always seems to have a limitless supply of zombies and similar creatures. If you can persuade him to lend us an army, we should be able to defeat these trolls.

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman.player: Ok, so I just need to go see Wizard Frumscone in Yanille?

back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman-aga.speaker: Herman Caranos
back-to-herman-talking-to-the-herman-aga.text: [player name] - have you brought an army?

options.text: No, I'm afraid I haven't asked Wizard Frumscone yet.

steps.player: No, I'm afraid I haven't asked Wizard Frumscone yet.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Do get a move on, [player name]!

options.text: What was it you asked me to do?

steps.player: What was it you asked me to do?

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Go to the Wizards' Guild in Yanille and ask Wizard Frumscone to lend us an army to save the Colony!

steps.player: Right, I know it was something like that.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Do get a move on, [player name]!

back-to-herman-talking-to-franklin-again.speaker: Franklin Caranos
back-to-herman-talking-to-franklin-again.text: Thanks a lot for your help earlier, but I have a lot to do, so please excuse me...

back-to-herman-talking-to-arnold-again.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
back-to-herman-talking-to-arnold-again.text: It good to see you, [player name], but many things I have to do with lovely fresh monkfish you bring me earlier.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Do you like my magic Zombies? Feel free to kill them, there's plenty more where these came from!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: Hello. I need your help with something...

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Oho? Very well, young man, what can I do for you?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: The Piscatoris Fishing Colony, somewhere north of the Gnome Stronghold, is under attack by sea trolls, and they've sent me to ask for an army.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: An army, heh? But I haven't GOT an army!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: They said you might lend us some of your zombies.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: What? This is a combat training facility, not a library! My magic zombies are not for loan.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: So you can't help the Colony?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: I'm jolly well not lending them an army! If I did that for you, I'd have to do that for everyone, and I'd never get a moment's peace again!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: So what should I tell the Colony? They've got to give up all their work because you won't help?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Actually that does seem rather harsh...

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Now, you mustn't breathe a word of this to Zavistic or Disentor upstairs, but I know a man who could help you get an army.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: Great! Is he a Guild wizard too?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: No, his work is completely different. He's a necromancer.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: Necromancy? I don't want anything to do with that!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: He's not going to have you doing any of the actual spellcasting for it. You'll probably just have to collect some weird item from him and take it to the Colony.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: I don't know if I still want to do this.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: If you don't want to continue the quest, just walk away and think no more about it. But I'm sure you won't have to do anything evil or unnatural yourself.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.player: Enough of this - I'm off.

steps.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
steps.text: Understandable. But if you ever change your mind, just come and ask me.

options.text: I'll see what the necromancer needs me to do.

steps.player: I'll see what the necromancer needs me to do.

steps.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
steps.text: Excellent. His name's Malignius Mortifer. You'll find him somewhere south of Falador.

steps.player: Can't I ask a different necromancer? There's one not so far away.

steps.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
steps.text: Hah! Necromancers aren't helpful people. I don't know of many - most guild wizards won't have anything to do with their practices. I think Malignius will help only because he loves showing off his powers.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.player: You said you knew a man who could help me save the Piscatoris Fishing Colony.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: Oh yes. Now, you mustn't mention this to Zavistic or Distentor, but he's a necromancer.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.player: Necromancy? I don't want anything to do with that!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: Do you like my magic Zombies? Feel free to kill them, there's plenty more where these came from!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: [player name]? Have you spoken to Malignius Mortifer?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: He'll probably still be wandering around south of Falador whenever you do want to speak to him.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.speaker: Herman Caranos
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.text: [player name] - have you brought an army?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.player: Wizard Frumscone wouldn't help, but he told me where I could find a wizard who might help. I have to look for him just south of Falador.
By the way, where's the Wise Old Man gone?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.speaker: Herman Caranos
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.text: He said he'd be back in a minute. But never mind him - go to Falador and talk to this wizard!

talking-to-malignius-mortifer.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
talking-to-malignius-mortifer.text: So, [player name], your curiosity leads you to speak to me?

options.text: Who are you and what are you doing here?
I need help with saving a fishing colony.

steps.player: I need help with saving a fishing colony.

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Saradomin:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Not when you're dressed like that! I don't help Saradominist filth!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Hahaha! You want MY help? HAHAHA!

steps.player: ... um... The Piscatoris Fishing Colony needs an army to defend them against attacking trolls.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: And of all the people in the world, you came to ask ME? HAHAHA!

steps.player: ... um... pretty please?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Oh, I'll help! I'll give you GOOD help!

steps.player: ... um... thanks, I think...

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: An army, eh? I can raise you a lovely army of the undead skeletal magi! That'd be just right, wouldn't it?

steps.player: I'm not going to have to do anything... evil, am I?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: No, I'll keep the fun bits for myself. You'll just have to get a few things for me.

steps.player: Alright - what do you need?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Firstly, I need 7 bones, the normal sort you get from people and small monsters.
With no bones in inventory:
If the player already has the bones:

steps.player: I have some here!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Hah! And I thought only necromancers and jogres carried bones around with them! Very well, hand 'em over.

steps.player: What should I do now for the quest?

steps.text: (Continues below)

options.condition: After Fairytale I - Growing Pains:

options.text: Where can I get clothes like those?

options.condition: After Fairytale I - Growing Pains:

options.text: What was it you said you'd need to help me save the Colony?

steps.player: What was it you said you'd need to help me save the Colony?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Bones! I need bones, the normal sort you get from humans and small monsters. If you're having trouble, go to the highwaymen just north of here - they've got bones!

steps.player: Oh yes, how could I have forgotten?

options.text: Where can I get clothes like those?

talking-to-malignius-mortifer-giving-bon.player: I have some bones for you.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Good. Now I need [Amount] more.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Excellent!

steps.player: What should I do now for the quest?

steps.player: What had you in mind?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You must go to the Crafting Guild to ask the advice of the master crafters. There are quite a few of them there, and one of them's sure to help.
