steps.player: Thanks!

options.text: What am I meant to be doing for the Colony?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing for the Colony?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Is there something wrong with your memory? I told you to go to the Crafting Guild to ask the master crafters for advice on transporting bone seeds.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.text: Hello, and welcome to the Crafting Guild. Accomplished crafters from all over the land come here to use our top notch workshops.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.player: Can you tell me anything about transporting bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.text: Bone seeds? What are bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.player: A necromancer is going to bind the essence of an undead army into some bone seeds for me if I can get a container to carry them in.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: Can you tell me anything about transporting bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Woah dude! That's, like, some seriously maximum stuff you're talking.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: But do you know what I should carry them in?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Yeah, you just need a pot with a lid. Do you know how to make pot lids?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: Yes, a woman called Tassie taught me.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Tassie Slipcast? She's one groovy lady.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: Yes, yes, very nice. So if I get a pot with a lid, I'll be able to carry bone seeds safely in it?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Yeah, yeah. You need to chill out more, dude.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: What was it you said I needed for transporting bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: A pot with a lid. Nothing more, nothing less.

options.condition: After Fairytale I - Growing Pains:

options.text: I've spoken to the master crafter...

steps.player: I've spoken to the master crafter about a container for transporting bone seeds.

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Saradomin:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You can take that Saradominist attire off before you try speaking to me about your quest again!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Ah, excellent. HAHAHA! Have you got such a container?
If the player doesn't have a pot and pot lid:

steps.player: No, I haven't got one.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Then get one!
If the player has a pot and pot lid:

steps.player: Yes, I have it here.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I have raised you an army and bound them into bone seeds for you!

steps.player: ... um... Thanks!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Don't mention it, it was fun! HAHAHA!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Now I will seal the seeds into your pot.
Bone seeds

steps.player: Thank you. So what do I do with them?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Take the pot to the Colony and open it! HAHAHA! Just don't open it before you get there.

steps.player: Suppose I - ahem - need another one later?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Bring me another of these pots with a lid and I will give you more bone seeds.
Malignius unexpectedly casts a spell on you.
Malignius unexpectedly casts a spell on you!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: HAHAHA!
The player is teleported to the Fishing Colony

options.text: Where can I get clothes like those?

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Franklin Caranos
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: Herman tells me you've been fetching us an army.

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Franklin Caranos
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: Interesting. I didn't know magic could do that.

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.player: You learn something new every day.

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: [player name]! I hear you fetch mighty army for us!

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: You go take them to Herr Caranos quickly!

the-final-battle.speaker: Herman Caranos
the-final-battle.text: [player name] - have you brought an army?

the-final-battle.player: No, really, the wizard told me he'd put bone seeds in this pot, and when I opened it the army would come forth from the bone seeds.

the-final-battle.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle.text: Hmmmph. I don't much like the sound of this. I certainly won't be sending anyone to Frumscone for help again!

the-final-battle.speaker: Herman Caranos
the-final-battle.text: You can talk about that later! Now we've got an army we can get on with beating the trolls!

the-final-battle.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle.text: Well, I suppose so. [player name], this could be VERY dangerous. Do you feel ready to fight?

the-final-battle.player: Aren't you going to do the fighting?

the-final-battle.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle.text: Yes, of course. But you, my trusty sidekick, are in this adventure with me, and if I'm going forth into battle, you should make sure you're ready too.

steps.player: I'm ready. Let's fight!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Good. May this, my final adventure, end well!
Cutscene begins

options.text: I'd like to get some stuff together first.

steps.player: I'd like to get some stuff together first.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Come back to us as soon as you're ready.

the-final-battle-final-battle-cutscene.text: A cutscene opens by showing the player opening the jar, causing an army of skeleton magi to appear and fight off the incoming sea trolls.
A sea troll general appears from the ocean.
The Wise Old Man does battle with the sea troll general, deftly avoiding its strikes before finishing it off with his powerful magic.
A spell flies in from off-screen, hitting the Wise Old Man, knocking him to the ground. The Sea Troll Queen appears.

the-final-battle-final-battle-cutscene.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle-final-battle-cutscene.text: I... can't... move... [player name], you must fight this for me...

the-final-battle-entering-the-colony-wit.prompt: Do you need to see the battle again?

options.text: Yes, I missed it. Show me the battle again.
No, I'm ready to move on with the quest.

steps.text: The player is transported in front of the queen.

finishing-up-after-killing-the-sea-troll.player: Now I've killed that THING, Herman's sure to reward me!

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.text: You kick big troll queenie pretty hard, ja?

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.player: Yes, I don't think you'll have any more trouble with the trolls in future.

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.text: Piscatoris Colony owe you big-time for your help. You go see Hermie - maybe he got something for you.

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.text: Herr Herman Caranos. I call him 'Hermie' when him not listening. Sometimes I call him worse things, but not today.

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.text: I say, you certainly gave that Troll Queen a good thrashing!

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.player: Yes, no more trouble from her.

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.text: I think Herman would like to talk to you in his office. We all owe you so much.

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.player: Ok, I'll go and see Herman.

finishing-up-talking-to-ramara-du-croiss.speaker: Ramara du Croissant
finishing-up-talking-to-ramara-du-croiss.text: [player name]? Monsieur Caranos wishes to see you in 'is office. Please, go to 'im!

finishing-up-talking-to-everyone-else.speaker: Everyone else
finishing-up-talking-to-everyone-else.text: [player name]? Mr Caranos said he wanted to see you in his office. I wouldn't keep him waiting if I were you!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: I've defeated the Sea Troll Queen!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Your fight was truly magnificent, [player name]! Congratulations!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: [player name], how can I ever thank you? You have saved my Fishing Colony from utter destruction!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Well, you mentioned something about a reward?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Of course, of course!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: I think you've earned a little something from me, too.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Ooh, goody! Thanks, old man! Um... can I have your hat?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: 'Old man'... yes, I am old. That creature nearly killed me - I have never been so close to defeat.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Aww, cheer up - we won! But can I have your hat as my reward?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Yes, we won... YOU won... It is definitely time I retired.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: So that's the end of your adventuring? Also, how about that hat of yours?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Well, I'm sure I'll find some way to keep myself busy. But yes, this has been my last quest. My swan song.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: It's been... nice working with you! It'd be even nicer if you'd give me that hat...

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: It's been a pleasure working with you too. Do pop in to see me in Draynor soon! I leave you with my blessing...
The Wise Old Man teleports away.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Oh, he's gone. I hope he enjoys his retirement.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: HE DIDN'T GIVE ME HIS HAT!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Player performs the Cry emote.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: It's only a hat!
Player performs the Headbang emote.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Anyway, you were going to reward me too?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Oh yes, of course! You are hereby welcome to visit the Piscatoris Fishing Colony at any time and make full use of our fishing spots!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Why is it better to fish here than in Catherby or the Fishing Guild?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Ah, I'm glad you asked that! You see, this is the only known place where you can catch monkfish!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Ok, so I can catch monkfish. Um... thanks?!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Yes - there's good eating on a monkfish. They heal more health than the swordfish and lobsters most adventurers carry around, but they're easier to catch than sharks.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: I suppose that could be useful.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Indeed! I'm sure Arnold will help you send your monkfish to your bank account. Also, seaweed accumulates in the nets down by the shore, which you might find useful. Franklin says it's much quicker than trying to gather it on Entrana.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Maybe if I ever want to do glassblowing again...

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Finally, I'd like to give you a little token of my thanks.
25000 Coins

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: No, thank YOU!
Congratulations! Quest complete!

before-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Hello outerlander. This is my home, I would be grateful if you would leave.
I am sorry outerlander, I will not offer you hospitality until my Chieftain has vouched for your honesty. This is our way.

after-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Greetings to you [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]! How fare you today?

after-the-fremennik-trials.player: I am fine thanks Swensen. How are you doing?

after-the-fremennik-trials.npc: I am fine too!

after-grim-tales.npc: Ah, [player name]! Good to see you again.

after-grim-tales.player: How is the collection going now?

after-grim-tales.npc: Thanks to you finding the golden goblin for me, I am the envy of the collector's group. I can't thank you enough.

after-grim-tales.text: If the player doesn't have the dwarven helmet in their inventory:

steps.player: I think I've lost Rupert's helmet.

steps.npc: Not to worry, [player name] Go and speak to Rupert. These items have a strange way of returning to their owners sometimes!

steps.player: Ok, I will. Thanks.

steps.npc: No, no. Thanks for everything you've done!

after-grim-tales.player: I'm just happy that I could help. Goodbye!

steps.npc: Selling Magic Beans!
You there, you look like you could use some beans!
All beans must go!
Buy 1 bean get a bean free!
Selling bags of Magic Beans!

standard-dialogue-when-trying-to-climb-t.npc: Excuse me, human! Perhaps you shouldn't just go wandering through there without knowing what you're dealing with!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Hello! Are you the leader of this expedition?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Indeed I am, human! What's on your mind?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: What's going on here?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Well, the Hueycoatl has awoken.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: The Huey- what?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Huey-co-at... oh, I don't have time for this! The thing you need to know is that it's dangerous and it's coiled throughout this entire mountain!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Do you know where it came from?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: We're not sure. There are some records of our ancestors having dealings with it, but the details have been lost, assuming they were ever recorded.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So it's old?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Does it really matter how old it is?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: I suppose not. I guess I just want to get a better understanding of what this thing is.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: We don't know how old it is. It could be extremely old, or this could be just one in a lineage of them. Still, we haven't heard of any others so maybe it is some sort of ancient creature.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: And given that you're here, I assume it poses some sort of threat?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Now you're getting it! While it doesn't seem to be innately aggressive, our concern is the potential risk of it tunnelling into Cam Torum.
Oh, and given that it does lash out from time to time, I suppose it does pose a threat to your nearby human villages. A lesser priority for us, but maybe something for you to care about.
Anyway, for now, our only option is to keep it in check while we figure out what to do in the long term.
Unfortunately, that means recruiting all the help we can get, even from you humans...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: How can I help?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has not completed Perilous Moons:

steps.npc: Well, despite what some of us may think of your kind, we need all the help we can get.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has completed Perilous Moons:

steps.npc: Well, as you've already proven yourself useful to Cam Torum, I'd be glad to have you help here!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has a combat level below 85:

steps.npc: However, I'm not sure you have enough combat experience to face the Hueycoatl.

steps.text: To face the Hueycoatl, it's recommended you have a combat level of 85 and a Prayer level of 43.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has a combat level above 85:

steps.npc: We need to keep the Hueycoatl under control which, until we find a more permanent solution, means wearing it out through combat.
Don't go killing it, mind you! Not that I think you could, but such a magnificent creature doesn't deserve destruction.

steps.player: Do you have any tips for surviving?

steps.npc: We've found our prayers can protect us from its shards, so keep an eye out for those.
To reach the Hueycoatl's head, you'll need to get it to move its great body out of the way. We've found we can persuade it by giving the exposed parts a helpful nudge!
Once you reach its head, you'll need to work with your comrades and the seer to balance your prayers and weaken the beast.
But I'm sure you'll figure it out!

steps.player: Move the body, then attack the head while keeping prayers balanced. Got it!

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku.speaker: Timfraku
starting-off-talking-to-timfraku.text: I am the Chief of Tai Bwo Wannai Village! Who dares set foot in my hut?

steps.player: I am a roving adventurer.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then adventurer, you would do better to rove elsewhere.

steps.player: I am a travelling explorer.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then explorer, you would do better to travel elsewhere.

steps.player: I am a wandering wayfarer.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then wayfarer, you would do better to wander elsewhere.

options.text: Who me? Oh I'm just a nobody.

steps.player: Who me? Oh I'm just a nobody.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then NoBody, you would do better to go elsewhere.

steps.player: Why should I leave?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: This place has been cursed. Our people have angered the gods and have fled the village.

steps.player: Where is this place?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: You ask too many questions. Now begone!

steps.player: Who are the gods?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: You ask too many questions. Now begone!

options.text: Where have your people fled to?

steps.player: Where have your people fled to?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: You ask too many questions. Now begone!

steps.player: Right, I'm going then.
Trufitus sent me.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Trufitus Shakaya? What news does he send?

steps.player: Trufitus has communed with the gods. Your village was never cursed and your people are free to return.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Bwana, do you speak the truth?

steps.player: Yes, I helped Trufitus gather ingredients for a commune potion.

steps.text: Timfraku appears to concentrate very deeply.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Then it must be true.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I cannot thank you enough for what you have done so far.

options.text: Your gratitude is all I deserve.

steps.player: Your gratitude is all I deserve.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: No, Bwana, you deserve much more.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I now ask you to do one last thing for our village.

steps.player: And what is that?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I ask you to deliver the good news to my three sons Tamayu, Tinsay & Tiadeche, and then return them to the village.

steps.prompt: Start the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest?

steps.player: Ok, I'll do it.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Thank you very much. I shall reward you greatly if you succeed.

steps.player: If I succeed? How hard can it be?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: We shall see, Bwana.

steps.player: No, I've had quite enough of the jungle already.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Very well. Return when you are ready.

options.text: Well, some gold would be nice.

steps.player: So far??

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I now ask you to do one last thing for our village.

steps.player: What do you do here?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: It should be clear to anyone that I am the chief of Tai Bwo Wannai. I ensure that things run smoothly in this village.

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.player: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Yes Bwana, plenty of interesting things to do. Firstly you could make an effort to tidy the place up a little. Equip yourself with a machete and start cutting down the jungle that seems to be growing all around here.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Go and have a chat with Murcaily for information, he's tending the hardwood grove to the east of here.

options.text: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.player: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.text: If the player has not been doing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup tasks:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: That's good Bwana, I would hate to think that you were just being lazy while you're in my kingdom!
If the player has completed at least one task from the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup task list:

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.speaker: Timfraku
starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.text: Are you ready to help me?

starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.player: What do I have to do?

starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.speaker: Timfraku
starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.text: I ask you to deliver the good news to my three sons Tamayu, Tinsay & Tiadeche, and then return them to the village.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a roving adventurer:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, roving adventurer.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a travelling explorer:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, travelling explorer.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a wandering wayfarer:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, wandering wayfarer.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a "Nobody":

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, Nobody.

options.text: Can you tell me more about your sons?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about your sons?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: My first son is Tamayu. After him was born Tinsay. And after him was born Tiadeche.

options.text: Can you tell me more about Tamayu?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Tamayu?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Tamayu was a natural born hunter. He killed his first monkey at the age of three!
Shows initial brother queries

options.text: Can you tell me more about Tinsay?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Tinsay?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Tinsay was brought up to be a priest. Be careful with him - he has acted strange since the accident.

steps.player: What accident?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: It involved Jogres. We don't talk about it.
Shows initial brother queries

options.text: Can you tell me more about Tiadeche?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Tiadeche?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Tiadeche always wanted to hunt fish. However, he has not had much success.

steps.player: How come?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: He needs to improve his technique - but he does not heed my advice.
Shows initial brother queries

options.text: Where can I find your sons?

steps.player: Where can I find your sons?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: On our island of Karamja. They will not have fled far.

steps.player: Is there anything I need?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Patience, Bwana, patience.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: And good conversation skills.

steps.player: I'll be back later.

steps.text: Shows previous village questions.

starting-off-attempting-to-enter-any-of-.text: You do not have permission to enter here

talking-to-tiadeche.player: Tiadeche, I bring good news. Trufitus has communed with the gods -  your village is once again safe.
Your father requests that you return to the village.

talking-to-tiadeche.speaker: Tiadeche
talking-to-tiadeche.text: I will return only when I have caught a Karambwan.

steps.player: What is a Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: You don't know? The Karambwan is a species of octopus native to these waters.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: They have a monopoly on its sale in the pirate town of Brimhaven.

steps.player: When will you be finished?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: At this rate, it could take forever.

steps.player: We don't have forever.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Sometimes, oblivion is all I crave...

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I just don't know. You can try.

steps.player: What would you have me do?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Something ... helpful?

options.text: How are you fishing for the Karambwan?

steps.player: How are you fishing for the Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I'm trying to catch them with a net as they swim by.

steps.player: And ... ?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: They keep fighting loose of the twining.

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player uses a raw, cooked, or poisoned Karambwan on Tiadeche:

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I refuse to take your offerings. I must catch this Karambwan myself.

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player gives Tiadeche an empty Karambwan vessel:

steps.player: Tiadeche, instead of using your net, try using this vessel.

steps.text: You hand over the Karambwan vessel to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: What is it?

steps.player: It has been specially constructed to catch Karambwan. Once they enter it, they cannot return..

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: As you say, Bwana.
Tiadeche attempts to use the Karambwan vessel.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: This vessel is useless! The Karambwan are not even interested in entering it!
the Karambwan vessel back

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player gives Tiadeche a raw Karambwanji:

steps.player: I've been told that the Karambwan feed only on the Karambwanji. This will make good bait.

steps.text: You hand over a raw Karambwanji to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: The Holy Friend? Bwana, it is sacrilege to feed these fish to Karambwan!

steps.player: Just try it.

steps.text: Tiadeche hesitates, then loads the Karambwanji in his net.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: This attracts many more Karambwan, but they still break free of the net.

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player gives Tiadeche a Karambwan vessel with a raw Karambwanji inside:

steps.player: Tiadeche, instead of using your net, try using this vessel.

steps.text: You hand over the Karambwan vessel to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: What is it?

steps.player: It has been specially constructed to catch Karambwan. Once they enter it, they cannot return..
Also, it has been loaded with Karambwanji. The Karambwan will not be able to resist this bait.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: As you say, Bwana.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Bwana! I cannot believe my eyes!

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I, Tiadeche, who would never amount to anything, have managed to trap a Karambwan!

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Let me offer to you my first catch as a sign of gratitude.

steps.prompt: Accept Tiadeche's offer?

steps.text: Tiadeche hands you his first catch!
a Raw Karambwan (in the inventory or on the ground if no inventory space)

steps.player: Your father would be proud.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Hmph ... my father would not care.

steps.player: Speaking of your father, can we make way to the village? He awaits your return.

steps.text: Continues below

steps.player: I have no need for it, Tiadeche.
We must return to the village now.

steps.text: Continues below

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I cannot return just yet. We witness the change of a turning tide. The secrets of the Karambwan are to be unlocked!

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Before I return, I must ask you to do one thing.

steps.player: And that is?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Take a Karambwan vessel to my brother Tinsay. He is the academic amongst us. Tell him I have asked him to study it so that we may craft more of its type.

steps.player: Can I have the vessel back then?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I need this to practice with. Why don't you craft another one?

steps.player: I ... never mind.

talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.text: If the player has not received (another?) Karambwan

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I have caught another Karambwan! I think I ought to give it to you.
a raw Karambwan

talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.speaker: Tiadeche
talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.text: Have you taken the Karambwan vessel to Tinsay?
If the player has done so:

steps.player: Yes, I have.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Did you ask for crafting instructions as I said?
If the player does not have the crafting manual:

steps.player: I did, but I think I've lost them...

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Well go back and ask him to make another copy!
If the player has the crafting manual:

steps.player: Yes. He gave me this.

steps.text: You hand over the crafting manual to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Thank you so much. You cannot understand what all of this means to me and our people.

steps.player: Will you return to the village now?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Yes. I will do as I promised.

steps.player: I am glad to hear this. Let us go.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Not yet. I will stay here a while to catch more Karambwan.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I will meet you in the village once you have helped my brothers and spoken to my father.

talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.text: If the player has not done so:

steps.player: No, not yet.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Please hurry! Time is of the essence!

talking-to-tamayu.player: Tamayu, I bring good news. Trufitus has communed with the gods -  your village is once again safe.
Your father requests that you return to the village.

talking-to-tamayu.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu.text: I vow upon the blood of my fallen kin that I shall not set foot in that godforsaken village till I have slain the Shaikahan.

talking-to-tamayu.player: You could slay it after we return to the village.

talking-to-tamayu.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu.text: No! Your pitiful whining tires me. Now let me prepare.

options.text: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.

steps.player: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: A source of indescribable evil. A beast more foul than your dreams could imagine. It hunts the jungle for anything foolish enough to cross its path.

steps.player: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: It stands a full man's length in height. Its fore claws are sharp enough to rip through metal. In its eyes glow the embers of death.

options.text: How long have you been hunting the Shaikahan?

steps.player: How long have you been hunting the Shaikahan?

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Since before I was born, stranger. It is my destiny.

steps.player: When will you succeed?

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: When the gods bless me with success. You may join me on my next hunt, but you may not take part.

steps.prompt: Follow Tamayu on the next hunt?

steps.player: Lead the way.

steps.text: Tamayu attempts to defeat the Shaikahan with his bronze spear...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Shaikhan is at present far too agile for me!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I cannot do enough damage with this spear...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... and  it seems to be healing too quickly!

steps.player: Perhaps later, Tamayu, first son of Timfraku.

options.text: I could slay the Shaikahan for you.

steps.player: I could slay the Shaikahan for you.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: You offer to kill the beast for me? Stop this nonsense, lest I kill you first. It is I who must avenge the death of my kin.

options.text: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.
How long have you been hunting the Shaikahan?
Take me on your next hunt for the Shaikahan.

steps.player: Take me on your next hunt for the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Very well, but you must not interfere.

options.text: I could slay the Shaikahan for you.

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player uses the stuffed monkey or monkey corpse on Tamayu before he kills the Shaikahan:

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I'm not going to skin that! In the jungle, we help only those who help us.

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player hands a partially full agility potion on Tamayu before handing the better spear:

steps.player: I've noticed you commenting on the Shaikahan's agility. Try drinking this potion.

steps.text: If the Agility potion does not have four doses:
If the player asks to take them to his next battle:

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I am beginning to match Shaikahan's agility!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I cannot do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... and  it seems to be healing too quickly!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player uses an iron or better spear on Tamayu:

steps.player: Tamayu, try using this weapon.

steps.text: You hand the spear to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.
If the player asks to take them to their next hunt with the iron spear (or better):
A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Shaikhan is at present far too agile for me!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I can do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... but  it seems to be healing too quickly!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player hands a partially full agility potion on Tamayu after handing the better spear:

steps.player: I've noticed you commenting on the Shaikahan's agility. Try drinking this potion.

steps.text: If the Agility potion has one dose:
You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel much more agile, but I am not sure whether I can match the Shaikahan...
If the Agility potion has two doses:
You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel much more agile, but I am not sure whether I can match the Shaikahan...
If the Agility potion has three doses:
You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel much more agile, but I am not sure whether I can match the Shaikahan...
If the Agility potion has four doses:

steps.player: Tamayu, I have brought you more agility potion.

steps.text: You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel agile enough to finally match the Shaikahan!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player has brought a better spear and a four-dose Agility potion and wants to join the hunt again:

steps.text: A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I have matched the Shaikahan in agility! He can no longer avoid my strikes!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I can do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... but  it seems to be healing too quickly!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player brings a poisoned spear to Tamayu and joins the hunt:

steps.text: A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I have matched the Shaikahan in agility! He can no longer avoid my strikes!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I can do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... and  it does seem quite sick! Perhaps another poison would be more effective?

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player brings a poisoned Karambwan spear to Tamayu and joins the hunt:

steps.text: A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: The end approaches, Shaikahan!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Gods! Witness this triumph!
The cutscene ends as the Shaikahan is defeated.

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: I did it! I, Tamayu, first son of Timfraku, did slay the Shaikahan!

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: The deaths of my kin have been avenged. You are my witness.

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.player: Worry not - I am your witness. Shall we return to the village now?

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: Yes. Go on ahead without me. I have further matters to attend to here.

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: I will meet you in the village once you have helped my brothers and spoken to my father.
If the player uses the monkey corpse on Tamayu:

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Let me guess - you want me to skin that monkey. Very well: I shall, since you have assisted me.
You hand over the monkey corpse to Tamayu.
Tamayu hands you some monkey skin and bones.
Monkey skin and monkey bones

talking-to-lubufu.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu.text: Watch where you're going, young whippersnapper!

steps.player: I wasn't going anywhere...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well then go away from here!

steps.player: What's a whippersnapper?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: It's a whip. Which snaps. Like me. Now leave!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I am Lubufu - the only fisherman who knows the secret of the Karambwan!

steps.player: What's a Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: What a foolish question! Now leave!

talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.text: You again! I thought I told you to go away!

talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.text: So I see. What would a fool like you want with me?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I am Lubufu, son of Kedoaba, brother of Kedenda and second cousin twice removed of Ibeli!

steps.player: Who is Kedoaba?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Kedoaba is my father, the father of Kedenda and second uncle twice removed of Ibeli!

steps.player: Who is Kedenda?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Kedenda is the son of my father, my brother and second cousin twice removed of Ibeli!

steps.player: Who is Ibeli?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Ibeli is the second nephew twice removed of my father, and the second cousin twice removed of myself and my brother!

steps.player: Do you have any children?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Alas, no. Focussed and determined in my trade as I was, I never found a suitable wife.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: It is a great shame that the secret of the Karambwan has to die with me.

steps.player: You could tell me the secret...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Hah! What a stupid thought! The secret is mine and mine alone!

steps.player: Where are you from?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Our island of Karamja. Long ago, before you were even a thought in the back of a mind, I used to play on these beaches with the pebbles and stones.

steps.player: So you didn't have many friends then?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Silence!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: As I grew older the ways of the world became apparent to me, and my attention turned from the rocks of the land to the fish in the sea.

steps.player: And ... ?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Despite what you might hear, there are plenty of fish in the sea! Especially when they can only be caught by me!

steps.player: What do you do?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Nowadays I mostly fish for Karambwan and collect their bait. Collecting the bait has become increasingly tiresome, what with my age and health.

steps.player: How old are you?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: An order of magnitude older than you! What an impudent question! Collecting bait has become hard enough at this age as it is without having to endure the chiding of you young people!

options.text: Which other young people come by here?

steps.player: Which other young people come by here?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Hmm ... nobody I can recall right now.

options.text: What do you use for bait?

steps.player: What do you use for bait?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: That is part of the secret! Why would I tell you?

options.text: I could help collect the bait.

steps.player: I could help collect the bait.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: And why would you help me?

options.text: You sound like you could do with the help.

steps.player: You sound like you could do with the help.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well perhaps you're right. It's nigh time I could do with some help after all.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I have a fair amount of bait left over since last time I collected some, but I will be needing more shortly.

steps.player: Ok. Where can I find the bait? I don't even know what it is!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Patience. I have kept the nature of the Karambwan a closely guarded secret. There is nobody alive who knows more about them than I do. Furthermore, there is nobody alive who even knows how they feed.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You must therefore understand that what I am about to tell you is given in complete trust, and that you are to tell nobody else.

steps.player: I understand.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Very well. The Karambwan are a form of octopus native to our island of Karamja. They feed solely on Karambwanji, a brightly coloured fish which also inhabits the coastal waters surrounding the island.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Karambwanji congregate in coastal shoals near the Holy Lake. You will find it easiest to fish for them there.

steps.player: Where is the Holy Lake?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Just to the south of Tai Bwo Wannai Village. I'm sure you've met the locals already.

steps.player: And what do I use to fish for the bait?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Any small net will do. Return here as soon as you have caught 20 Karambwanji.

options.text: You sound like you need help.

steps.player: You sound like you need help.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: How dare you say such a thing! Be off with you!

options.text: I enjoy collecting meaningless items for people.

steps.player: I enjoy collecting meaningless items for people.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Meaningless? You know nothing of the Karambwan! Now leave!

options.text: You're right. I don't want to help.

steps.player: You're right. I don't want to help.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I didn't for one moment think you did.

steps.player: What is a Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: A species of octopus native to the island which I and I alone know how to catch.

options.text: What do you do with your Karambwan?

steps.player: What do you do with your Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I eat what I need and sell the rest to the Shrimp and Parrot restaurant.

steps.player: Where is the Shrimp and Parrot?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You don't know anything do you? Just north of here, in Brimhaven!

options.text: What do you use for bait?

steps.player: What do you use for bait?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: That is part of the secret! Why would I tell you?

steps.player: What does Karambwan taste like?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: That depends entirely on how it is cooked...

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Novicely cooked Karambwan is often poisonous to large mammals such as humans. If you buy some and cook it, be careful.

options.text: I have come for your soul.

steps.player: I have come for your soul.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well you've wasted your time. My soul is long gone, along with my compassion.

options.text: I'm with the Fishing Guild Anti-Monopoly Department.

steps.player: I'm from the Fishing Guild Anti-Monopoly Department.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: And I'm from the Island Karamja. What do you want?

steps.player: We demand that you hand over the secret of the Karambwan.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Erm ... no.

steps.player: Oh, ok then. It was worth a try.

options.text: Do you have any spare monkey skin lying around?

steps.player: Do you have any spare monkey skin lying around?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Funny you should say that...

steps.player: Why's that? Do you have any?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well, people have been asking me for monkey skins all day!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: But no, I'm out of monkey skin.

options.text: I've heard something about an accident.

steps.player: I've heard something about an accident.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You will want to ask one of the tribesmen. I don't usually talk about it.

talking-to-lubufu-delivering-raw-karambw.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-delivering-raw-karambw.text: Have you retrieved the Karambwanji yet?

steps.player: Yes, I have some here.

steps.text: If the player has all 20 raw Karambwanji:
You hand Lubufu 20 raw Karambwanji.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Thank you! This should tide me over for the next month.
If the player has some raw Karambwanji:
You hand Lubufu [#] raw Karambwanji.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Hurry along now. I still need [#] more.
If the player does not have 20 Karambwanji:

steps.player: No, I'm still fishing for them.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well hurry! My reserves are beginning to run low.
If the player has the rest of the Karambwanji:

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Have you retrieved the Karambwanji yet?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I still need [#] more.

steps.player: Yes, I have some here.

steps.text: You hand Lubufu [#] raw Karambwanji.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Thank you! This should tide me over for the next month.

steps.player: What is a Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: A species of octopus native to the island which I and I alone know how to catch.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You should really ought to know that by now.

options.text: What do you do with your Karambwan?
What do you use to catch Karambwan?

steps.player: What do you use to catch Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well ... since you ask, a specially constructed octopus pot. But don't tell anybody - that's part of the secret!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: My, you're keen aren't you?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: How would you feel about becoming my apprentice?

steps.player: That's a slight change in attitude...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: As much as I need to protect the secret, I should not carry it to the grave.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You seem a trustworthy type of person. Do you want to train as my apprentice?

steps.player: Yes!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I'm glad to hear it. I'm sure the secrets of the Karambwan will be safe with you.
Lubufu teaches you a new fishing technique.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: In our language, Karambwan literally means 'Friend of Karamja.' As a friend of mine I will now show you how to fish for them.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: There are two aspects to fishing for Karambwan. Firstly, you must have the correct bait. Secondly, you must have the correct equipment.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You already know of the Karambwanji, which shoal in the Holy Lake to the south. As I have explained, the Karambwan feed only on the Karambwanji, which are therefore the perfect bait.

steps.player: But what kind of equipment do you use?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: It is futile to attempt to catch Karambwan with something as basic as a net. They are too strong and vicious to be caught in such a fashion.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I have spent many years designing a specially shaped vessel, into which Karambwan may pass but from which they may not return.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: If this vessel is loaded with Karambwanji, and then repeatedly lowered into a Karambwan shoal, then you should shortly find a Karambwan octopus trapped inside.

steps.speaker: Lubufu

before-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-leve.npc: I not be in the mood t' talk, sorry. If ye need anythin', talk to Cap'ain Pudi over by the dock.

after-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-level.npc: I cannot believe that beast ruined me ship.

steps.player: What happened to your ship?

steps.npc: Was awful, me crew an' I were out on our fortnightly fishin' excursion. We set sail from Al Kharid t' the deep-sea fishin' spot we usually use.
Was nothin' but smooth sailin' all the way, we got t' the spot an' started fishin'.

steps.player: Sounds like a normal day of fishing to me.

steps.npc: Aye, I s'pose it was. After a few days, the crew an' I sailed further t' the Karamjan coast t' catch some sharks. More plunder from sellin' sharks.
While sailin', I noticed there was more debris than usual. Koanee said there must have been a storm recently.

steps.player: How did she know that?

steps.npc: Koanee is in charge of plottin' a course t' our destination an' watchin' the weather. I thought she was good at her job.
We got to our final fishin' spot an' Lauretta let down the net. Almost a whole day went by an' we still 'ad not caught any fish.
In fact, I could not see any fish in the waters at all. Such a strange sight.

steps.player: Not even bass?

steps.npc: Nothin'. We decided t' pack it in for the day an' I told Koanee t' leave the nets down, hoping we would catch some fish overnight.

steps.player: That sounds like a bad idea. What would have happened if your net got too full or your ship started drifting and the net got caught on some rocks?

steps.npc: 'Twas a risk we 'ad to take t' catch some fish.
The next day Koanee woke me up t' tell me a storm was on the horizon, so we lifted the anchor up an' adjusted our course.
Not sure what she was playing at with that decision, but out o' nowhere winds started t' change an' the storm was headin' in our direction, we couldn't outrun it.
'Twas also too dangerous to anchor down, so we 'ad to weather it.
Thick fog rolled in, giant waves crashin' against the ship's hull. So much lightnin', it felt like Saradomin was angry with us.
The lightnin' struck our sails, settin' them ablaze despite the 'eavy rain!
The last thing I see is glowin' fish an' a monster in the distance with a twisted face. Next thing I know, I'm lying on the shore just south of Al Kharid with Pudi waving a kebab in me face!

steps.player: That must have been awful. At least you and the crew survived.

steps.npc: Aye, we survived, but the same cannot be said for me poor ship! Koanee should 'o known better!
Once Pudi and the others helped us back on our feet, the Chancellor sent us 'ere t' setup shop and recruit others.
Not really my area of expertise, mind, but Pudi sorts most of it out!
Anythin' else I can help ye with?

options.text: Got any tips for fighting Tempoross?

steps.player: Got any tips for fighting Tempoross?

steps.npc: Always carry an 'ammer. That beast has a habit of destroyin' ships. You can fix it up by using said 'ammer.
The Spirit Anglers' ships you fight the beast from are kitted out with everythin' ye need.
Can I help ye with anythin' else?

steps.player: I found your ship's log.

steps.npc: Ye be stealin' me booty are ye?

steps.player: No, I jus...

steps.npc: I be yankin' ye chain, 'tis all good. I put that 'ere book on that shelf so I may spread me tale.

steps.player: It was a good tale. Is it true?

steps.npc: Of course 'tis true! Ye can ask me all about it.

steps.player: I have to go.

steps.npc: Be seein' ye.

using-items-on-him-damp-egg.player: Would you care for an egg in this difficult time?

steps.npc: Um... no, I don't want your damp egg, thanks...

steps.player: I'll take my eggs elsewhere then.

steps.npc: A damp egg? No thanks.

steps.player: I'll take my eggs elsewhere then.

steps.npc: I'd rather not. Thanks, though.

steps.player: I'll take my eggs elsewhere then.

using-items-on-him-egg.player: Would you care for an egg in this difficult time?

using-items-on-him-egg.npc: This is some comfort to be sure.

getting-started-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
getting-started-talking-to-phileas.text: Hello there. Not very often I get visitors. What brings you here?

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: The name's Phileas Rimor. I was once a soldier in the Shayzien Army but now I'm retired.

steps.player: Do you need help with anything?

options.text: Do you need help with anything?

steps.player: Do you need help with anything?

steps.text: If the player does not have the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: I'm fine thank you. Thanks for asking though.
If the player has the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: Well let me think...

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: You know, there is something I wouldn't mind some help with.

steps.player: Great! What is it?

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: When I was a boy, my grandfather would tell me the story of my ancestor, Magnus Rimor. He was a great explorer who lived a thousand years ago.

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: One day, Magnus was approached by none other than King Shayzien VII himself. The King asked him to lead an expedition to explore Mount Quidamortem in the Kebos Lowlands.

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: Alas, according to records, the party never returned and were declared to have perished in the field.

steps.player: That's very interesting and all but why are you telling me this?

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: A few days ago, I received a parcel. There was no name on it and I never saw the person that delivered it. Inside, I found something truly fascinating.

steps.player: What was it?

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: There was an old journal, along with a note. The note claims that the journal was stolen from the Tower of Magic during the uprising against Xeric.

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: But that's not all. Apparently the journal was written by King Shayzien VII himself!

steps.player: Again, really great and all but I still don't see where I come into this.

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: Most of the journal is illegible but I've still managed to find a few readable extracts. Listen to this one...

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: 'Quidamortem's creatures are compatible. The experimentation is proving successful and we will soon be ready to mass produce.'

steps.player: So?

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: That extract had a date in the 37th decade but the expedition was declared a failure in the 36th decade! If the expedition truly was a failure, why was the King writing about Quidamortem years later?

steps.player: Maybe there was another expedition.

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: Maybe. Or maybe someone wasn't telling the truth about that expedition. Regardless, I must find out what really happened. Can you help me?

steps.prompt: Start the Tale of the Righteous quest?

steps.player: What do you need?

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: We need to find out more about that expedition. The Library Historical Archive should have records on it. Talk to Archeio in the Arceuus Library. He can take you there.

steps.player: That doesn't sound too hard. Leave it with me.
I've got other things to do.

steps.speaker: Phileas Rimor
steps.text: Oh, okay then.

steps.player: Nothing.

getting-started-talking-to-phileas-talki.speaker: Phileas Rimor
getting-started-talking-to-phileas-talki.text: Hello again. How is your quest going?

getting-started-talking-to-phileas-talki.speaker: Phileas Rimor
getting-started-talking-to-phileas-talki.text: Well you need to find out more about that expedition. The Library Historical Archive should have records on it. Talk to Archeio in the Arceuus Library. He can take you there.

perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-talk.speaker: Archeio
perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-talk.text: Hello. Would you like to visit the Library Historical Archive? We've recently opened the archive to visitors.

perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-talk.speaker: Istoria
perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-talk.text: Welcome to the Library Historical Archive.

options.text: I have a question about King Shayzien VII.

steps.player: I have a question about King Shayzien VII.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: Well you've come to the right place. What would you like to know?

steps.player: I'm searching for information on an expedition to Mount Quidamortem during his reign.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: Ah yes, I know of that expedition. King Shayzien VII was one of Kourend's most notable rulers. According to the history books, his reign was defined by violence.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: The expedition to Quidamortem was part of his aggressive plans to expand Kourend's territory. Unfortunately, it was a failure. The entire party was killed.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: The King himself died a few years later and was succeeded by Xeric, a tyrannical mage who made the King seem meek in comparison. Though of course, many believe them to actually be the same person.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: But I digress. The key thing to note is that no more expeditions were ordered under King Shayzien VII's rule. Does that help you?

steps.player: No, not really. I have reason to believe that not everyone was killed on that expedition.

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: I'm afraid I can't help you there. All the evidence we have tells us that the expedition had no survivors.

steps.player: So I'm at a dead end?

steps.speaker: Istoria
steps.text: It would seem that way. However, if you do want to learn more about King Shayzien VII, it might be worth talking to Pagida. He's recently been investigating the King's additions to the Tower of Magic.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: How do I get out of here?

perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-talk.speaker: Pagida
perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-talk.text: Hello there, what can I do for you?

options.text: I don't know, what can you do for me?
I have a question about King Shayzien VII.

steps.player: I have a question about King Shayzien VII.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: What do you wish to know?

steps.player: I'm trying to find out more about the expedition he ordered to Mount Quidamortem.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: I'm afraid I don't have any information on that expedition. You're probably better off talking to one of the others.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: I could tell you about the King's work on the Tower of Magic though.

steps.player: Well it's not like I have anything better to do. Fire away.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: During the time of King Shayzien VII, the Tower of Magic was the seat of power in Kourend. The King spent a lot of his time at the Tower, more than any other ruler.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: In fact, he oversaw the construction of various new sections, most notably the prison.

steps.player: When was this?

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: Well now that I think about it, it was around the same time as the expedition you were asking about. That said, I doubt the two are connected.

steps.player: I see. Would it be possible to visit the prison?

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: Well the prison is abandoned and has been for many years, so I suppose there's no harm in letting you see it.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: Be aware that the magic in that part of the tower is a bit unstable, so any items left in the prison will be lost. Would you like me to teleport you there now?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: Very well, prepare yourself.

steps.player: No thanks.

steps.speaker: Pagida
steps.text: I'll be here if you change your mind.

perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-inve.text: You notice some writing carved into the floor beside the skeleton: 'Lizards on the mountain. Do not trust the King. The Altar is a lie.'

perhaps-the-archives-are-incomplete-inve.player: Hmm. I should tell Phileas about this.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: Hello again. How is your quest going?

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.player: So I went to the Library Historical Archive. I found out that King Shayzien VII ordered the construction of a prison there around the time the expedition was taking place.
I investigated the prison and in one of the cells I found a strange message.
'Lizards on the mountain. Do not trust the King. The Altar is a lie.'

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: Lizards on the mountain? So it was true! Someone did return from that expedition! Do you think it was Magnus?

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: That's a shame. I would have liked to have known what happened to him.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: That's one to dwell on later though. For now, we need to work out our next steps.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: Absolutely. We now know for sure that someone returned from that expedition, but we still don't really know why. We need to find out.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.player: But why does it matter? This all happened a thousand years ago. Anyone involved is long dead now.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: That doesn't mean it doesn't matter! This isn't just the chance to discover the truth about my ancestor. We also have the chance to expose the treachery of a former king!

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.player: Okay, I see you feel strongly about this. What do you need me to do?

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: If we're to find out what happened on that expedition, we're going to have to retrace its route. And by we, I mean you.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.player: Yeah, I had a feeling that would be the case.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.text: First things first, you'll need to talk to Lord Shayzien. He's ordered that any research work done on the mountain be approved by him first. You'll find him in the War Tent in the Shayzien Encampment to the

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas.player: I guess I'll be on my way then.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas-ta.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas-ta.text: Hello again. How is your quest going?

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas-ta.player: I still need to talk to Lord Shayzien.

another-expedition-talking-to-phileas-ta.speaker: Phileas Rimor
another-expedition-talking-to-phileas-ta.text: Well you'll find him in the War Tent in the Shayzien Encampment to the north.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.player: I'd like to perform some research on Mount Quidamortem, but I need your permission to do so.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: Quite right. Quidamortem is a dangerous place and I don't want to be ordering my troops on any unnecessary rescue missions.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: So, tell me about your research.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.player: Many years ago there was an expedition to Quidamortem ordered by King Shayzien VII. The expedition supposedly ended in failure.
But I have reason to believe that wasn't the case. I think something was discovered on that expedition. I want to find out what it was.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: Fair enough. I will approve your research, on one condition.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: If you discover anything, you will bring it to me first. King Shayzien VII was my ancestor and I want to be made aware of any discoveries that would present him in a bad light.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.player: But surely the library should be made aware of any important discoveries?

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: They will be made aware. But only after I have reviewed the discoveries first.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: Excellent. Consider your research approved. If you require assistance with your work, I'd recommend talking to Historian Duffy on Quidamortem. He's been researching the mountain for a while.

another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
another-expedition-talking-to-lord-shayz.text: Well if you require assistance, I'd recommend talking to Historian Duffy on Quidamortem. He's been researching the mountain for a while.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: That's me. Do you need something?

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.player: Lord Shayzien told me that you might be able to help with some research I'm doing.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: I'm rather busy with my own research.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.player: I'm trying to retrace the steps of an expedition ordered by King Shayzien VII. I believe something important was found on that expedition, but I don't know what.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: Interesting. So you don't know anything about what they found?

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.player: I have a quote which I believe is from someone on the expedition.
'Lizards on the mountain. Do not trust the King. The Altar is a lie.'

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: Fascinating. We've been researching the lizard creatures here for a while now. We have reason to believe they are not of natural origin and may in fact have been created by Xeric or his followers.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: But this quote of yours suggests the lizardmen may have existed during the time of King Shayzien VII, before Xeric's rule.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: Yes. This is definitely worth pursuing. In fact, I think I know where we should begin.

another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-historian-.text: We recently found a small crevice on the western face of the mountain. It seems to be manmade and appears to be older than the rest of the caves around here.

another-expedition-investigating-the-cre.player: This must be the crevice that Duffy mentioned. I'll need a rope to get in.

another-expedition-using-a-rope-on-the-c.text: You attach a rope to the crevice.
Do you want to enter the crevice? Any items left in there, including upon death, will be lost.

another-expedition-inspecting-the-unstab.text: As you approach the altar you hear a strange voice.

another-expedition-inspecting-the-unstab.speaker: Mysterious Voice
another-expedition-inspecting-the-unstab.text: Rickard! Turn away! Don't do this!

another-expedition-inspecting-the-unstab.player: Hmm, I wonder what that was about.
Oh well, I may as well go and tell Historian Duffy what I've found.

another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.text: If the player did not kill the Corrupt Lizardman:

steps.player: Hello.

steps.speaker: Historian Duffy
steps.text: Find anything in that cave?

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: Historian Duffy
steps.text: Well let us know when you do. It's on the western face of the mountain.

another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.text: If the player inspected the unstable altar:

another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.text: Hello. Did you find anything in that cave?

another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.player: I did. There was a weird looking lizardman along with a strange altar.
Don't worry, I took care of it.

another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-returning-to-duffy.text: Well in that case, we'll go take a look.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: This cave is quite fascinating. We could really be on to something big here.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: We've never come across lizards like the ones in this cave before. It would appear that they are a previously undiscovered species.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: That's nothing. The really interesting part is that these lizards appear to be directly related to the lizardmen that roam this region.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.player: So this is where the lizardmen came from?

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: It would appear so. That's not all though. This cave definitely predates Xeric, who we originally believed to be the creator of the lizardmen.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: Impossible to say for sure, but with what we've already learnt about King Shayzien VII, I do wonder if he was the one responsible.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.player: But if King Shayzien VII did create the lizardmen, why did they fight for Xeric?

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: There are some who believe that King Shayzien VII and Xeric were one and the same. They claim that after his death, the King was resurrected by his followers, taking on the name Xeric.

another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.speaker: Historian Duffy
another-expedition-talking-to-duffy-in-t.text: Anyway, I'm going to carry on with my research. I'd recommend you talk to Gnosi. She's made some interesting discoveries of her own.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.player: Hello. Duffy said you'd found something interesting.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: The Dark Altar was the key to Xeric's power. Because of it, he was able to rule Kourend unopposed for nearly a hundred years. His reign was so dark, it became known as the Age of Strife.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: Once he was finally defeated, Xeric came to Quidamortem and built the Chambers of Xeric deep below the mountain.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: For many years we've tried to work out how he managed to survive out here without the power of the Dark Altar. Thanks to this cave, I think we've found the answer.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: This altar, it seems to give off the same power as the Dark Altar.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.player: So this altar was how Xeric kept his power after he was defeated?

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: It appears to be manmade. I believe this altar was created to amplify the power of the Dark Altar, allowing it to reach areas it previously couldn't.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: This discovery does bring about an intriguing question though.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: The altar here is still giving out power. That means Xeric could have potentially used it to live for hundreds of years after his defeat. It's long been believed that Xeric eventually died here, but what if he didn't?

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: Indeed. I'm going to stay here and continue working. Do you mind heading to the library to let them know what we've discovered.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.player: Actually, Lord Shayzien asked me to go to him first with any discoveries.

another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.speaker: Gnosi
another-expedition-talking-to-gnosi.text: Hmm, I can see why he would take an interest. Very well, go let him know what we've found.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.text: How is your research going citizen?

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.player: We've discovered a small cave on the western face of Quidamortem. It's manmade and it predates the time of Xeric.
Inside, we found an altar. It seems to be giving off the same power as the Dark Altar.
We also discovered a unique lizard species, one that shares many similarities with the lizardmen.
It seems that this cave was the origin of the lizardmen. The fact that it predates Xeric suggests the lizardmen do as well.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.text: You believe they were the creation of my ancestor?

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.player: Hard to say for sure. It would make sense though.
From the evidence we have, I believe that King Shayzien VII ordered an expedition to Quidamortem, hoping to discover a suitable species for his lizardman project.
Once the expedition found one, he had them killed to keep the discovery a secret.
Not definitive, but there's a lot of evidence.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.text: So you claim. However, you never actually told me where this evidence came from.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.player: It started with a parcel delivered to Phileas Rimor. It contained a journal written by King Shayzien VII himself. The journal mentioned creatures on Quidamortem.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.text: A parcel? King Shayzien VII's journal was delivered in a parcel? Who sent it?

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.text: Well you need to find out. Go to Phileas Rimor and retrieve this parcel. I need to see it for myself.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien.player: Eugh, so much walking. Fine, I'll go see Phileas.

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien-.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien-.text: Do you have the parcel citizen?

finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien-.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-reporting-to-lord-shayzien-.text: Well go and fetch it then. I need to see it for myself.

finishing-up-entering-phileas-home.player: Err, this doesn't look good. I'd better tell Lord Shayzien.

finishing-up-returning-to-lord-shayzien.speaker: Lord Shiro Shayzien
finishing-up-returning-to-lord-shayzien.text: Do you have the parcel citizen?
