steps.text: I'm afraid it may be all my fault.

steps.player: Oh?

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Captain Tock had me exploring some caves, west of the cove. I'm a thief, see, like my brother Francois, and the Captain thought I could sneak past the monsters without being noticed.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Well, I climbed down the vines, and found a big cave filled with terrifying ogres!

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: I'd hoped I could use my amazing Thieving skills to avoid them seeing me, but I was out of luck. By the time I'd finished clambering down the ladder, they'd spotted me.

steps.player: So you were trying to explore that ogre cave, and the ogres saw you?

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Yes. I quickly grabbed some loot, so I wouldn't have to face the Captain empty-handed, and fled up the ladder before the ogres could kill me!

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: But a couple of days later we all fell ill. I think what I stole must have been some kind of sacred relic, and the shamans in the cave have cursed us for stealing it.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Maybe you could get the relic back from the Captain, and return it to the ogres? And tell them I'm very sorry. Then perhaps they'll lift the curse.

steps.player: I see.

options.text: Urgh to you too, with candy sprinkles on.

steps.player: Urgh to you too, with candy sprinkles on.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: A sympathetic soul you are. I'm in real pain here.

steps.player: Yes, I hear you've been cursed.

arsen-s-curse-talking-to-arsen-talking-t.speaker: Arsen the Thief
arsen-s-curse-talking-to-arsen-talking-t.text: Have you got that relic back from Captain Tock? Maybe if you return it to the ogres, they'll lift the curse.
If the player has not talked to Captain Tock yet:

steps.player: Nope, I've not done that.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Oh dear.

arsen-s-curse-talking-to-arsen-talking-t.text: If the player has not talked to Chief Tess:

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Please take it back to the ogres for me, and tell them I'm sorry.

arsen-s-curse-talking-to-captain-tock.speaker: Captain Tock
arsen-s-curse-talking-to-captain-tock.text: Have ye any idea about how to lift the curse?

options.text: Arsen says he gave you a sacred ogre relic.

steps.player: Arsen says he gave you a sacred ogre relic.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, that he did. I'd sent him to explore the caves west of the cove, an' he brings me back a bone lump, saying he stole it from the ogre chief.

steps.player: He thinks the ogres have cursed you all because he stole one of their sacred relics, and he wants me to take it back to them now.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, I've no use fer the silly thing. If it'll get the curse lifted, ye can take it right to that ogre chief an' give it back.
Captain Tock gives you the loot that Arsen stole from the ogre chief.

options.text: Please take me back to Rimmington.
A man called Arsen told me he'd visited your cave.

steps.player: A man called Arsen told me he'd visited your cave.

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Yah, skinny man climb down vine the other day. Little man, big idiot! Hahahaha...

steps.player: He says he's very sorry...

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: He very silly!

steps.player: Perhaps I should come back another time.

options.text: I've come to return what Arsen stole.

steps.player: I've come to return what Arsen stole.

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Arsen says he's very sorry for stealing from you. Here it is...
You present Tess with Arsen's loot.

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Yah, dat little man is big idiot. Climbed down vine, grabbed tooth-pick off Tess and ran away like scared kebbit.

steps.player: You're saying this is a tooth-pick? Not a sacred relic of the ogres? Did your shamans curse the Corsairs for stealing it?

steps.speaker: Chief Tess
steps.text: Dis is tooth-pick. Tess got plenty more. If skinny idiot man want Tess' old tooth-pick, maybe he sick in his head. But Tess not having shamans curse anyone.

steps.player: Oh. Well, I guess Arsen will be pleased to hear he didn't bring the curse upon the Corsairs.

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.speaker: Arsen the Thief
arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.text: Have you returned the sacred relic to the ogres? Will they forgive me and lift the curse?

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.player: Their chief, Tess, says that wasn't a sacred relic at all. It was her tooth-pick.

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.speaker: Arsen the Thief
arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.text: Are you telling me the ogres cursed us all because I stole their chief's tooth-pick?

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.player: She didn't care - she's got lots of tooth-picks, and she just thought you were some kind of weirdo when you stole one. They never cursed you at all.

arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.speaker: Arsen the Thief
arsen-s-curse-returning-to-arsen.text: Oh. That's a relief, I guess. Um... thank you for your help. But I do wonder where the curse really came from.

colin-s-curse-talking-to-colin.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
colin-s-curse-talking-to-colin.text: I'm sorry! Tell her I'm sorry! Then maybe she'll make the pain stop...

steps.player: I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Yes, that's what it must be. Ithoi, the navigator, always told us to beware of curses.

steps.player: I've met him. He definitely thinks it's a curse, but wasn't able to say exactly what caused it.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: This is all my fault. But I didn't mean to upset her. I just thought we could be friends. Now I must have upset her, and she's cursed us all!

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Ithoi always told us that bad things happen to sailors who get involved with mermaids, but I didn't believe him. I should have listened! But I'll tell you what happened...

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I was using Ithoi's telescope...

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Such a beautiful night!

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: What lands lie beyond the dim horizon, I wonder...
Colin uses the telescope at Ithoi's hut.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Eh?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: What was that? I'd better have another look.
Colin uses the telescope again.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Is that what I think it is?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: It's so dark out there, but I think... ... yes, I'm quite sure...

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: ... yes, it's a mermaid! She's beautiful!

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Hello?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Can you hear me?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: You're the most lovely person I've ever seen!
Colin uses the telescope again.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I can see you moving your arms, but it's very dark. Are you waving to me?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: kiss*

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Hello?
Colin uses the telescope again.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Oh, no, I think she's gone away. Did I put her off?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Maybe she doesn't like strangers shouting about her appearance and blowing kisses at her. That might have been rude of me.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I hope she's not angry. Ithoi says mermaids can be dangerous.
Cutscene ends.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Perhaps you can find the mermaid and tell her I'm very sorry I was rude to her. Then maybe she'll lift the curse.

options.text: Perhaps you can tell me about it another time.

colin-s-curse-talking-to-colin-talking-t.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin

options.text: Where did you find this mermaid?

steps.player: Where did you find this mermaid?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I was using Ithoi's telescope to look out at the sea, imagining the strange lands and fantastic creatures Ithoi's always telling us he's seen, and I saw her.

options.text: Nope, I've not seen any mermaids round here.

steps.player: Nope, I've not seen any mermaids round here.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Oh dear, oh dear. Maybe we'll be cursed forever!

colin-s-curse-using-ithoi-s-telescope.player: Let's see if I can find that mermaid he saw...

colin-s-curse-using-ithoi-s-telescope-ag.player: I've seen enough of that ogre already. Colin might be relieved to hear it wasn't a mermaid.

colin-s-curse-returning-to-colin.text: Have you found the mermaid yet? Will she forgive me?

colin-s-curse-returning-to-colin.text: If the player has not completed Big Chompy Bird Hunting:

steps.player: He's definitely not a mermaid.

colin-s-curse-returning-to-colin.text: If the player has completed Big Chompy Bird Hunting:

steps.player: I've met that ogre before. He lives with his dad in the Feldip Hills. He's definitely not a mermaid.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Oh. Oh, I see. Okay... I guess that means I didn't upset a mermaid after all. So the curse isn't my fault! Thank you!

steps.player: How are you feeling?

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: I still feel awful. But I'm glad you've proven it wasn't my fault that we got cursed. I hope you can work out what brought it on us.

steps.player: I'll be on the case.
I hear you've been cursed.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Yes, I think She did this to us. I should have left Her alone. Ithoi told us to beware of this kind of thing.

steps.player: I've met him. He definitely thinks it's a curse, but wasn't able to say exactly what caused it.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: It's all my fault, I know it is. I've awoken Her, and now She's done this to us!

steps.player: Who are you talking about?

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: I'll explain... See, I'm the cook, and I have to find the food as well as cooking it...

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: I was fishing...
A flashback to a few days ago...

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Let's see what I can find for the boys tonight.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: C'mon little lobsters, come to Gnocci!

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Obby-lobby obby-lobby oi oi oi!

steps.player: 'obby-lobby' - what?

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: It's a traditional lobster-fishing chant handed down by my ancestors. Don't interrupt.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: C'mon little lobsters. We don't want to keep the Captain waiting! He'll get angry with me again.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Ooh, what's this? This isn't a lobster.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Looks more like a child's toy. But - no, it can't be...

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Is it moving?

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: She's moving! SHE'S POSSESSED! HELP!

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: I buried Her in the sand, by that tree, to the west. But I still feel Her eyes staring into my soul. Please find Her, and kill the demon inside!

steps.player: My lower intestine!

options.text: Where did you say this happened?

steps.player: No, I've not.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Oh dear, I feel terrible. Please help us soon.

gnocci-s-curse-digging-for-her.player: Okay, he said he buried the possessed doll in the sand...

gnocci-s-curse-returning-to-gnocci.text: Have you tried to destroy Her yet? Her eyes, those terrible eyes!

gnocci-s-curse-returning-to-gnocci.player: Well, sort of. That doll wasn't possessed at all. It was a clockwork toy. They're supposed to move.

gnocci-s-curse-returning-to-gnocci.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
gnocci-s-curse-returning-to-gnocci.text: Clockwork? Oh, that would explain how it moved. Ahem. Well, I suppose the curse didn't come from Her.

gnocci-s-curse-returning-to-gnocci.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
gnocci-s-curse-returning-to-gnocci.text: I hope you can find the real cause soon.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.text: Arrr! That'll teach him to meddle with such folk. Colin should stick to what he's good at.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.player: Gnocci fished a doll out of the water, and he thought it might have been possessed by an evil spirit.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.text: Arrr chuckie chuckie chuckie! That'll teach him to play with dolls at his age. Dolls can be frightening.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.player: Arsen stole what he thought was a sacred relic from the ogre cave, and he said their shamans might have cursed you in revenge.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.text: Arrr! Ogre women be powerful, an' Arsen be a fool.

gnocci-s-curse-talking-to-ithoi-during-t.player: I'll carry on trying to solve the curse.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Ye can maybe solve the problem fer each victim, an' see if it lifts the curse.

options.text: Please take me back to Rimmington.

options.text: I've ruled out all the Corsairs' theories...

steps.player: I've ruled out all the Corsairs' theories...
Cabin-boy Colin thought he'd upset a mermaid, but there wasn't a mermaid, just a wet ogre.
Arsen the Thief thought he'd upset the ogre shamans by stealing a sacred ogre relic, but it was just a tooth-pick, and the ogres didn't care.
Ithoi the Navigator said there were lots of things that could bring a curse on a crew, and this could be any of them.
And Gnocci the Cook thought he'd awoken a demon in a possessed doll, but it wasn't possessed at all. It was clockwork.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, any sufficiently advanced technology be indistinguishable from demonic possession, that it be.

options.text: So what do I do now?

steps.player: So what do I do now?

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, I don't rightly know. It began when I'd gone away for a parlay with Ithoi; we came back ter find the crew all a-pukin' up their dinner. Then Ithoi felt ill too, though he'd not eaten with 'em, so it can't be the food.

steps.player: I see. You're saying it began after they'd all eaten, but Ithoi felt ill even though he'd not had any of the food.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr, that be right.

steps.player: That meal must have been interesting...

options.text: Can I give up and go home?

steps.player: Can I give up and go home?

steps.player: Maybe because the Captain's thinking of firing you - Arsen heard it from his brother. The Corsairs don't need a navigator anymore.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Arrr! Too clever ye be... I heard the Captain might kick me off the crew, so I poisoned the dinner, an' acted sick too. Now they think they're cursed, so they'll want me around, wi' my knowledge o' such things!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: But they all think I'm sick, so they'll never believe I'm behind it. Hahaha!

steps.player: We'll see what they have to say about that!

options.text: Maybe you're just a nasty person.

steps.player: Maybe you're just a nasty person.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Bah! Ye can't even think of a reason why I'd want to poison the crew, so don't bother me with yer accusations.

steps.player: I don't know your reason.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Bah! Ye can't even think of a reason why I'd want to poison the crew, so don't bother me with yer accusations.

steps.player: I'm still looking into it.

traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.text: Have you solved the curse yet?

options.text: Ithoi admits poisoning you all and faking the curse.

steps.player: Ithoi admits poisoning you all and faking the curse.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: If Ithoi's been afflicted by the curse as badly as I have, he might be half out of his mind with pain. I'm sure he doesn't know what he's saying.

steps.player: I'm still looking into it.

traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.text: Have you solved the curse yet?

options.text: Ithoi admits poisoning you all and faking the curse.

steps.player: Ithoi admits poisoning you all and faking the curse.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: That can't be right - he looks as sick as the rest of us. Maybe he's delerious and doesn't know what he's saying.

steps.player: I'm still looking into it.

traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.speaker: Arsen the Thief
traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.text: Do you know how we all got cursed?

options.text: Ithoi admits poisoning you all and faking the curse.

steps.player: Ithoi admits poisoning you all and faking the curse.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: He's had a lot to worry about, with losing his place on the crew, and now he's sick from the curse too. He must have gone mad and started babbling.

steps.player: I'm still looking into it.

traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.speaker: Captain Tock
traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-ithoi-af.text: Have ye any idea about how to lift the curse?

options.text: Ithoi admits he poisoned the crew!

steps.player: Ithoi admits he poisoned the crew! He's faked this whole curse!

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: That can't be! Ithoi's sick, an' he may be babbling madness from his fevered brain. Ye'll have to prove he's not really sick.

options.text: Please take me back to Rimmington.
I know you've faked the curse.

steps.player: I know you've faked the curse.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: The Corsairs all think I'm sick too, even though I never ate the food. An' ye'll never make me prove that I'm healthy - I ain't gettin' up! So they'll keep believing in the curse.

options.text: I bet I can prove you're well enough to get up.

steps.player: I bet I can prove you're well enough to get up.

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Ye'll never make me get up! I ain't afraid of cold, nor of wet, nor of anythin' ye can do in here.

steps.player: I'll be back.
Um... nothing, really.

traitor-in-the-midst-attempting-to-light.player: Maybe I should try to get more information out of him before trying to make his hut catch fire.

traitor-in-the-midst-using-any-abyssal-w.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator:
traitor-in-the-midst-using-any-abyssal-w.text: Arrr, Old School RuneScape isn't that sort of fantasy game, in case ye hadn't been told that a-fore today.

traitor-in-the-midst-attempting-to-light.text: Ithoi rushes out of the hut.
Ithoi casts Water Strike, extinguishing the fire, and returns to his hut.

traitor-in-the-midst-attempting-to-light.player: Well, I guess that proves he's well enough to get up! And apparently he knows some magic too.

options.text: I saw you running around! You're not sick!

steps.player: I saw you running around! You're not sick!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: So long as that old fool, Tock, believes it's a curse, I've nothing to fear from ye flapping yer mouth.

steps.player: We'll see what the Captain has to say about that.
Um... nothing, really.

traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-gnocci-a.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-gnocci-a.text: Can you tell me what's going on now?

options.text: Ithoi's faked the curse. I've seen him running around, healthy.

steps.player: Ithoi's faked the curse. I've seen him running around, healthy.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: Make sure he gets what's coming to him. No-one poisons my crew!

options.text: Ithoi's faked the curse. I've seen him running around, healthy.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: It sounds like there isn't a curse after all! Maybe I'll recover soon from whatever he did to me.

options.text: Ithoi's faked the curse. I've seen him running around, healthy.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: Give him what he deserves!

options.text: I've seen Ithoi running around. He's not sick at all.

steps.player: I've seen Ithoi running around. He's not sick at all.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Arrr! So he was never sick at all! An' here's me been feeling sorry for him. A trickster he be indeed! Kill him fer me.

options.text: Why don't you kill him yourself?

steps.player: Why don't you kill him yourself?

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: A captain shouldn't leave his ship in a time of crisis. Rule of the sea, that is. Even if the crisis ain't exactly on the ship.

options.text: I don't believe in capital punishment.

steps.player: I don't believe in capital punishment.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: I do.

steps.player: I'll be back.

options.text: Please take me back to Rimmington.

traitor-in-the-midst-killing-ithoi.text: One of the following will be said while hitting him:

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Ye'll pay!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Curse you!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Curse 'em all!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Arrr, land-lubber!

steps.speaker: Ithoi the Navigator
steps.text: Awww!

traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-gnocci-a.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
traitor-in-the-midst-talking-to-gnocci-a.text: Can you tell me what's going on now?

options.text: Ithoi faked the curse, and I've killed him.

steps.player: Ithoi faked the curse, and I've killed him.

steps.speaker: Gnocci the Cook
steps.text: You think you know a guy, and then he does a thing like this! Oh well, I hope I recover soon from whatever he did to me.

steps.player: Not much.

options.text: Ithoi faked the curse, and I've killed him.

steps.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
steps.text: Who'd have thought Ithoi would do such a thing? I guess if there isn't really a curse, I'll get better soon. In fact I feel better already.

steps.player: Not much.

options.text: Ithoi faked the curse, and I've killed him.

steps.player: Ithoi faked the curse, and I've killed him.

steps.speaker: Arsen the Thief
steps.text: I really didn't think he was like that. Still, if there isn't really a curse, I suppose we'll just get better from whatever he did to us. I don't feel so bad now.

steps.player: Not much.

options.text: I've killed Ithoi for poisoning your crew.

steps.player: I've killed Ithoi for poisoning your crew.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Thank ye fer dealing with that serpent. I suppose the rest of my crew will feel better now ye've proven there be no curse on them.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Most of them deleterious effects probably be psychosomatic anyway, arrr!

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Anyways, ye've been a mighty help, young [lad/lass]. Ye be brave in the heart, strong in the arm and full in the bowels, an' I be grateful to ye.

steps.speaker: Captain Tock
steps.text: Tell ye what, I'll have a word with Yusuf, in the bank. Ye've earned the right to use his services. An' thanks again, very much.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

options.text: Please take me back to Rimmington.

-7yaBI.player: Perhaps you can tell me about it another time.

-7yaBI.speaker: Cabin Boy Colin
-7yaBI.text: I'll be here. I'm not going anywhere while I feel so sick.

starting-the-quest.text: If the player speaks to Elias before receiving his message:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Ah, hello there, [player name]. Good to see you.

steps.player: And you, Elias. So what brings you all the way out here?

starting-the-quest.text: If the player speaks to Elias after reading his message:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Ah, hello there, [player name]. Good to see you. I take it you recived my message?

steps.player: I did indeed. So what brings us all the way out here?

starting-the-quest.speaker: Elias White
starting-the-quest.text: Well, it turns out the desert was the best place to begin my research into Arrav and his heart. Not too surprising of course, given the burial practices here.
If the player did not speak to Elias at the Uzer Oasis prior to 21 February 2024:

steps.player: And how's that going so far?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Pretty well. In fact, I think I'm getting close to something. It's related to that old mastaba up on the plateau. I reckon it might contain the knowledge we need to help old Arrav out.

starting-the-quest.text: If the player spoke to Elias at the Uzer Oasis before 21 February 2024:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: In fact, as you might recall, I was here before to look into that old mastaba up on the plateau.

steps.player: Yes, I remember. You said it might contain important information on the Mahjarrat.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed I did. And I reckon it might also contain the knowledge we need to help old Arrav out.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Elias White
starting-the-quest.text: And on that note, how do you feel about a bit of tomb raiding?

starting-the-quest.prompt: Start The Curse of Arrav quest?

steps.player: Sounds like a job for me! What do you need?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Well, without getting bogged down in all the details, my research led me to some information on a rare and unusual form of necromancy that was once practiced in these lands.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The key element of the process involved the removal and preservation of the heart, much in the same way that the priests of Icthlarin do so during their burial ceremonies.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The key difference: The process is performed while the victim is still alive!

steps.player: That's horrible!

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed. I have encountered many forms of dark magic in my time, but I must confess, few have filled me with the same anger that I felt upon discovering this vile form of necromancy.

steps.player: And you think this is what happened to Arrav?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Almost certainly. The end result of the process is an undead slave, bound to whoever possess their still-beating heart.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The victim must do whatever they are commanded, but unlike most other forms of necromancy, their mind, and indeed their very soul, remains intact. It all perfectly matches what you encountered with Arrav.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Now thankfully, as horrible as all this is, I believe this is a way for us to break Zemouregal's control over Arrav. To do so, we must recover Arrav's heart.

steps.player: But what does that have to do with the mastaba?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: If we are to recover the heart, we will need a way to not only keep it preserved, but to keep it beating as well.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Zemouregal must have a way of doing this, but I have a feeling he won't be willing to share the details on how.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: My hope is the mastaba contains the answers we need. It was built to house a Pharaoh who ruled the desert thousands of years ago.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: She was known for many feats, with one of them being her work in saving the victims of a Mahjarrat necromancer.

steps.player: Ah, I see. Well, if there's any information on heart preservation in there, I'm sure I can find it.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: I have no doubt you can. While you work on that, I will get started on our next issue: Finding where Zemouregal is keeping Arrav's heart. Hopefully I'll have something by the time you're done.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Oh, and a word of warning. When I was asking around about the mastaba, I was told about a group of... well they apparently called themselves explorers. They entered the mastaba, but never came back out.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: I'd say it's safe to assume that there are some sort of defensive measures in place to deter any would-be grave robbers.

steps.player: Thanks for the heads up. I'll be careful.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Good luck in there. I will meet you here once you are done.

steps.player: I'll have to pass right now. I have some other things I need to do.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Well, when you're ready, you know where to find me.

tomb-raiding-talking-to-elias-again.speaker: Elias White
tomb-raiding-talking-to-elias-again.text: Ah, hello again, [player name]. How goes the tomb raiding?
If the player has not entered the tomb:

steps.player: What do I need to be doing again?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: You need to head into that mastaba up on the plateau and see if you can find some information on how we can keep Arrav's heart preserved. Once you have something, meet me back here.

steps.player: Right. I'll get to it.

tomb-raiding-talking-to-elias-again.text: If the player has entered the tomb:

steps.player: I'm still working on it.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Well, keep at it. Once you have some information on how we can keep Arrav's heart preserved, meet me back here.

tomb-raiding-talking-to-elias-again.text: If the player has learned about canopic jars:

steps.player: I think I've discovered what we need. We should be able to preserve Arrav's heart using a specially prepared canopic jar.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Excellent stuff! So how do we prepare this jar?
If the player has not added anything to the canopic jar:

steps.player: We need to fill it with three dwellberries and a ring of life. I'll get started right away.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Sounds good. Let me know once it's ready and we can discuss our next steps.
If the player has added something to the canopic jar:

steps.player: We need to fill it with three dwellberries and a ring of life. I'm working on it right now.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Well, let me know once it's ready and we can discuss our next steps.

steps.player: Will do.

tomb-raiding-searching-the-skeleton-by-t.text: You search the skeleton and find an empty waterskin.
You search the skeleton and find some damaged armour.
You search the skeleton and find a key.

tomb-raiding-searching-the-south-skeleto.text: You search the skeleton and find a key.

tomb-raiding-searching-the-north-skeleto.text: You search the skeleton and find some worthless dust.

tomb-raiding-searching-the-skeleton-sout.text: You search the skeleton and find a vase.

tomb-raiding-pulling-the-lever.text: If the player does not have a key:

steps.text: You try to pull the lever, but it won't budge. However, you spot a small keyhole beneath it.

tomb-raiding-pulling-the-lever.text: If the player has the wrong key for the lever:

steps.text: You try to pull the lever, but it won't budge. You spot a small keyhole beneath it, but the key you are carrying doesn't fit in it.

tomb-raiding-pulling-the-lever.text: If the player has the right key for the lever:

steps.text: You try to pull the lever, but it won't budge. However, you spot a small keyhole beneath it that perfectly fits the key you are carrying. You turn the key in the lock and feel the lever loosen slightly.

steps.prompt: Pull the lever?

steps.text: If the player has not pulled a lever yet:
You pull the lever.
If the player has pulled one lever:
You pull the lever and hear a click coming from elsewhere in the mastaba.

tomb-raiding-pulling-the-lever.text: If the player has already used the key:

tomb-raiding-opening-the-imposing-stone-.text: The doors are securely locked. You can't see any obvious way to open them.

tomb-raiding-pulling-the-lever-after-the.text: You pull the lever and hear a rumbling coming from the floor grid.

tomb-raiding-searching-the-shelves.text: You search the shelves and find an oil-filled canopic jar.

tomb-raiding-inspecting-the-south-mural.text: Much of the mural is beyond your understanding, but you recognise a Pharaoh Queen preparing a canopic jar. A diagram seems to show the jar being filled with three dwellberries and a ring of life.

tomb-raiding-inspecting-the-west-mural.text: Much of the mural is beyond your understanding, but you recognise a Pharaoh Queen placing a heart into a canopic jar.

tomb-raiding-inspecting-the-east-mural.text: Much of the mural is beyond your understanding, but you recognise a Mahjarrat facing off against a Pharaoh Queen.

tomb-raiding-using-dwellberries-on-the-c.text: You put three dwellberries into the canopic jar.

tomb-raiding-using-a-ring-of-life-on-the.text: You put a ring of life into the canopic jar.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: Ah, hello again, [player name]. How goes the tomb raiding?
You show the canopic jar to Elias.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.player: This canopic jar should be able to preserve Arrav's heart!

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: Excellent stuff! I had no doubt you'd discover what we needed. You'll be pleased to hear that I've managed to make some good progress as well.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.player: Have you found where Arrav's heart is?

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: Not quite, but I have the next best thing. One of my contacts has been supporting my research by investigating Mahjarrat activity in the far north.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: He recently spotted Zemouregal entering an old fort near the mountain of Trollweiss.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.player: Ah, I know Trollweiss. I've been tobogganing there.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: Really? It hadn't struck me as a tourist area, what with it being a bit troll-ridden. Anyhow, you shouldn't need to be doing any tobogganing this time. Instead, you'll be heading underground.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: Yes. My contact located some tunnels that looked like they might lead right into the fort. Seems like a far better option than the front door.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.player: Well, then I'd best get going. Where can I find these tunnels?

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias.text: The entrance is right on the top of Trollweiss. I'd suggest you take a pickaxe with you. My contact mentioned that there had been a few cave-ins.

options.text: You seem to have a lot of contacts.

steps.player: You seem to have a lot of contacts.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Indeed. I've managed to make a few friends in my time.

steps.player: So are they all looking into Zemouregal for you?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Oh, not at all. Given recent events, Zemouregal is of particular interest of course, but Mahjarrat activity in general has been increasing recently, especially up north.

options.text: So how did you first end up researching the Mahjarrat?

steps.player: So how did you first end up researching the Mahjarrat?

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: You know, it's been so long that I can barely remember. As I recall, I first found mention of their kind right here in the desert.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: I was assisting some archologists in the south when I found an old tablet describing of a race of seemingly immortal shapeshifters wielding the power of gods. Naturally, I was immediately fascinated!

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Of course, I soon went on to find out that they are not only fascinating, but also very dangerous. I must admit that I see it as something of a duty to keep my research up to date.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: The events at Varrock showed that too many have forgotten the dangers of the Mahjarrat.

options.text: Alright. I'll be back once I've explored this fort.

steps.player: Alright. I'll be back soon.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Good luck.

options.condition: If the player has asked another question:

steps.player: I'd better get going.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Good luck out there.

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias-again.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias-again.text: Hello again, [player name]. Have you managed to explore those tunnels yet?

fort-invasion-talking-to-elias-again.speaker: Elias White
fort-invasion-talking-to-elias-again.text: You'll find the entrance atop Trollweiss Mountain. I'd suggest you take a pickaxe with you. My contact mentioned that there had been a few cave-ins.

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.text: If the player attempts to open the eastern door without speaking to Arrav:

steps.speaker: Arrav
steps.text: You...

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.speaker: Arrav
fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.text: You... You should not be here. Zemouregal could return at... urgh... at any time. If he does, I won't.... I won't be able to stop myself from... arrgh...

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.player: That's a risk I'm willing to take. I'm here to help you.

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.speaker: Arrav
fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.text: Why? You do not... do not know me. You do not know what I've... urgh... what I've done. Leave this place, and leave me. I am... forsaken.

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.player: Not if I have anything to say about it. Arrav, I need to find your heart. With it, I can free you!

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.speaker: Arrav
fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.text: It's not... here. Zemouregal did not want it too close to his... arrgh... his kin.

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.player: Do you know where it is?

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.speaker: Arrav
fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.text: In the next room... look behind the... urgh... the flame tapestry. You might be able to find something that can... arrgh... help.

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.speaker: Arrav
fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.text: My master calls me... Thank you... whoever you are. I... urgh... I don't even know your name.

fort-invasion-talking-to-arrav-in-the-fo.player: It's [player name], and I will save you Arrav, I promise.

fort-invasion-searching-the-tapestry.text: If the player does not have two free inventory spaces:

steps.text: You find some plans and a key behind the tapestry. However, you don't have enough room to take them.

fort-invasion-searching-the-tapestry.text: If the player has two free inventory spaces:

steps.text: You find some plans and a key behind the tapestry.

fort-invasion-studying-the-plans.text: These appear to be complex plans for Zemouregal's Base in Silvarea. Maybe Elias can help you interpret them.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Hello again, [player name]. Did you manage to find a way into that fort?

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.player: I did! The heart wasn't there, but I think I know where it is. I reckon it's in the base near Varrock.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Are you sure?

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.player: Well, take a look at these plans I found and see what you think.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: You give the plans to Elias.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Right then, let's see...

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Yes, there's a chamber here marked as containing a heart! It must be Arrav's!

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: However, reaching it is going to pose some significant problems...

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: It seems that the inner section of Zemouregal's Base has state of the art security. The corridor into the area is filled to the brim with human detection spells. These will set off an alarm.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Now, there is a sewage system running under some parts of the base that can be accessed from the nearby kitchen.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: These sewers could be used to bypass the spells. However, surges of energy are periodically sent through the water there.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: On the other side of the spells the vault door is found. This door is guarded by zombies. If they see an intruder, they will set off the alarm.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: If the alarm is sounded, a gas will be released, incapacitating all living things in the area.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: The vault door is made of five-inch thick runite-enforced steel, with a four digit access code. When the code is entered incorrectly more than twice, the alarm will be set off.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Inside the vault there is a criss-cross of special fire ray enchantments that Zemouregal has made. Touching any of these will do significant damage and set off the alarm.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Finally, at the back of the vault, we have the pedestal holding Arrav's heart.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.player: Well, that sounds an awful lot to get past. It sounds like an impossible mission!

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: It does appear to pose somewhat of a challenge, but if we engage in a bit of cunning, it may not be as impossible as you might think.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: First of all, we're going to need a distraction to lure some of those zombies out. I have no doubt that I'll be able to act as suitable bait. While I do that, you'll need to get through those sewers.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.player: But what about the energy surges? I don't really fancy getting fried!

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Understandable. I would suggest you invest in some kind of insulation to protect yourself from the surges.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Now, provided my distraction works, you should find the area on the other side of the sewers free of zombies. That will give you the time and space needed to get that vault door open.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Well, no great heist is complete without the use of a crossbow and a grappling hook.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.player: Okay, so to summarise, I need some sort of insulated protection along with a crossbow and grappling hook?

heart-heist-talking-to-elias.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-talking-to-elias.text: Precisely! Gather those items and then meet me outside Zemouregal's Base near Varrock. It's time to recover a heart!
Elias departs.

heart-heist-meeting-elias-at-the-base.text: If the player lost the canopic jar:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Hello again, [player name]. I found this earlier. I imagine you'll be needing it.
Elias gives you a canopic jar.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Now, are you ready to perform a heist? Remember, you'll need some sort of insulated protection along with a crossbow and grappling hook.

heart-heist-meeting-elias-at-the-base.text: If the player has the canopic jar:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Ah, there you are, [player name]. Ready to perform a heist? Remember, you'll need some sort of insulated protection along with a crossbow and grappling hook.

steps.player: Ready when you are.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Excellent. Once you head in, I'll arrange a distraction to lure some of those zombies away. I'll meet you back here once you've recovered the heart. Good luck.

options.text: I still need to do some preparation.

steps.player: I still need to do some preparation.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Very well. I will wait for you here.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias-again.text: If the player lost the canopic jar:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Hello again, [player name]. I found this earlier. I imagine you'll be needing it.
Elias gives you a canopic jar.

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: Now, once you head in, I'll arrange a distraction to lure some of those zombies away. I'll meet you back here once you've recovered the heart. Good luck.

heart-heist-talking-to-elias-again.text: If the player has the canopic jar:

steps.speaker: Elias White
steps.text: I'm ready when you are, [player name]. Once you head in, I'll arrange a distraction to lure some of those zombies away. I'll meet you back here once you've recovered the heart. Good luck.

heart-heist-searching-the-east-table.text: You search the table and find some interesting-looking notes.

heart-heist-searching-the-west-table.text: You search the table and find some strange pieces of paper with holes in.

heart-heist-searching-the-chest.text: You unlock the chest and find a code key inside.

heart-heist-taking-the-heart.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-taking-the-heart.text: Well, look what we have here...

heart-heist-taking-the-heart.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-taking-the-heart.text: Did you really think you had any hope of stealing that heart?

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Hmph!

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Arrav
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Urgh... [player name]...

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: What a miserable failure you are. Sharathteerk, get rid of him.
Sharathteerk casts a teleportation spell, but fails.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: What are you playing at?

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Sharathteerk
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Something's not right... Something's blocking my teleport!

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Impossible! Stop messing around and...

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Wait... I sense...
Elias White teleports in.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Zemouregal
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: You!

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: [player name]! Grab the heart, quickly!

Elias casts a powerful spell that binds both Zemouregal and Sharathteerk in chains, with the player taking Arrav's heart from its pedestal, causing it to glow red. Elias then teleports the player and himself.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: That's one way to put it. Good job I was keeping an eye on things.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.player: You can say that again, though that does leave me with some questions...

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: You're wondering how I managed to do it?

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.player: Teleporting directly into the room... Keeping a Mahjarrat at bay... Those aren't the kind of skills that just anyone possesses. Not to mention that Zemouregal knew you!

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: I have never kept it secret from you that I have a history with the Mahjarrat, although I may have chosen not to divulge some of the more... specific details.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: I hope you will not judge me too harshly for that. We are all entitled to our secrets, and even now I would prefer not to share them.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.player: I guess... It's just, you made out you were just researching the Mahjarrat. This is clearly a lot more than that.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: It is, and I apologise if you feel I have deceived you. My past with the Mahjarrat, and especially with Zemouregal is... complicated. Again, I would prefer we not discuss this further.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Now, why don't we instead focus this conversation on something far more positive than my history. We have successfully recovered Arrav's heart!

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.player: So does this mean we can free him now?

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Eventually, yes, but while the heart is key to Zemouregal's control over Arrav, merely possessing it won't be enough to break that control.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Doing so will require further research, not to mention the right opportunity.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: I will take the heart and begin working right away. Given that Zemouregal knows we have it, I intend to go to ground for this one.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: You might not hear from me for some time, but fear not, I will be in touch again once things are ready.

heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.speaker: Elias White
heart-heist-escaping-and-finishing-up.text: Stay safe out there, [player name]. Until we meet again.
Elias departs.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

starting-off.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
starting-off.text: Hello there.

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: I am Lord Kandur Hosidius, ruler of this city. Who are you?

steps.player: I'm [player name].

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Pleased to meet you [player name]. It is a shame we could not meet in better circumstances.

steps.player: Anything I can help you with?

options.text: Anything I can help you with?

steps.player: Anything I can help you with?

steps.text: If the player does not have the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Our family is in dire need of assistance. Alas, I do not feel I can trust you enough to involve you in this.
If the player has the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Our family is in dire need of assistance. My eldest son, Artur, has gone missing and we could desperately use some help in finding him.

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Would you be willing to assist us? You will be rewarded if you bring him home safe.

steps.prompt: Start The Depths of Despair quest?

steps.player: I can help. What do you need me to do?

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Thank you friend. I suggest you begin your search by talking to my family and servants. One of them might know where Artur has gone.

steps.player: No. I'm afraid I have other things to be doing.

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: I'm sorry to hear that. If you change your mind please return to me as soon as you can.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Until next time.

starting-off-talking-to-lord-hosidius-ag.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
starting-off-talking-to-lord-hosidius-ag.text: Hello there. Have you found my son yet?

starting-off-talking-to-lord-hosidius-ag.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
starting-off-talking-to-lord-hosidius-ag.text: I suggest you begin your search by talking to my family and servants. One of them might know where he's gone.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis.player: Hello. I'm helping Lord Hosidius find his missing son. I was wondering if you could help me.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis.speaker: Butler Jarvis
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis.text: I'm afraid I know not where Artur has gone. I do not speak to him much. He keeps himself to himself.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis.speaker: Butler Jarvis
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis.text: However, I've noticed him speaking to Olivia before. Maybe she can help.

starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis-ag.speaker: Butler Jarvis
starting-off-talking-to-butler-jarvis-ag.text: Good day [sir/madam]. I hope your quest is going well.

starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.speaker: Elena Hosidius
starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.text: You're the one helping to find our son.

starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.speaker: Elena Hosidius
starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.text: It's good that you're here to help. Artur is a good lad, but he does have a habit of biting off more than he can chew.

starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.speaker: Elena Hosidius
starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.text: He's meant for greatness you know. He'll be a king one day.

starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.speaker: Elena Hosidius
starting-off-talking-to-elena-hosidius.text: Lord. I meant to say lord. Now be on your way. Artur needs your help.

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.player: Hello, I'm helping Lord Hosidius find his missing son. I was wondering if you had any idea where he might have gone?

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.speaker: Chef Olivia
starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.text: I'm sorry, but I don't know anything.

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.speaker: Chef Olivia
starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.text: Oh this is awful. Please don't tell Lord Hosidius. He'll fire me if he finds out.

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.player: Calm down, you have nothing to fear from me. I just want to help find Artur. Do you know where he is?
Well don't worry, your secret is safe with me.

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.speaker: Chef Olivia
starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.text: Thank you. Before he went missing, Artur told me he was going to find the original copy of the Royal Accord of Twill. That's where he will have gone.

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.speaker: Chef Olivia
starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia.text: He's been spending a lot of time in the Arceuus Library recently, researching the Accord. He mentioned a librarian called Galana. Maybe she can help you.

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia-talk.player: Where should I be looking again?

starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia-talk.speaker: Chef Olivia
starting-off-talking-to-chef-olivia-talk.text: He's been spending a lot of time in the Arceuus Library. He mentioned a librarian called Galana. Maybe she can help you.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.player: I'm looking for information on the Royal Accord of Twill.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.speaker: Galana
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.text: The Royal Accord of Twill was signed by the heads of Kourend's five houses, known then as the Royal Lords. This was over a thousand years ago.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.speaker: Galana
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.text: The Accord declared that they would take over rulership of Great Kourend from the Council of Elders.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.speaker: Galana
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.text: For many years after the Accord was signed, the Royal Lords took it in turns to rule the kingdom. Each of them ruled for ten years in turn.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.speaker: Galana
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.text: Those practices have long since been abolished though and Kourend is now ruled by the Kourend Council. The original Accord has since been lost, but copies still exist in this library.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.player: What if I wanted to find the original?

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.speaker: Galana
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.text: Many have tried and failed. You would likely have no better luck. However, if it interests you, you might wish to read The Envoy to Varlamore, by Deryk Paulson.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.speaker: Galana
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.text: It details how the original Accord was lost.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-galana.player: Do you know where I can find the book?
Could you remind me where I can find that book on the Accord?

the-envoy-to-varlamore-searching-the-app.text: If the player already has the book:

steps.text: You find: The Envoy to Varlamore, by Deryk Paulson. You already have a copy.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-searching-the-app.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You find: The Envoy to Varlamore, by Deryk Paulson. You don't have room to take a copy.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-searching-the-app.text: You find: The Envoy to Varlamore, by Deryk Paulson. You take a copy.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-entering-the-cave.text: You climb down into the cave.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-crossing-the-step.text: You attempt to cross the stepping stones.

steps.text: You successfully make it to the other side.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-crossing-the-step.text: If the player does not succesfully cross:

steps.text: You slip and fall into the water.

steps.player: Crikey!

steps.text: You manage to swim back to the shore.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-climbing-the-rock.text: If the player successfully crosses the rocks:

steps.text: You climb over the rocks.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-climbing-the-rock.text: If the player does not successfully cross the rocks:

steps.player: Ouch!

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: Hello. I wasn't expecting to see anyone else down here.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.player: I'm [player name]. Your father sent me to find you. He's worried about you.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: He really shouldn't worry, I'm fine. I'll head home as soon as I've finished here.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.player: Well could I help speed things along in some way? I promised him I'd get you home.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: Now that you mention it, I could use some help. There's a chest in the next cave with something important in it. It's got a big snake guarding it though.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.player: By something important do you mean the Royal Accord of Twill?
How do you think I found you?

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: Oh. Well as you already seem to know, yes I'm here looking for the Royal Accord of Twill. I think it's in that chest, but the snake is in the way. Could you kill it for me?

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: I tried, but I'm not very good at fighting.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.player: Typical. Fine, I'll kill the snake. Just wait here.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: Have you killed that snake yet?

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: The sooner you kill it, the sooner I can head home.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-talking-to-artur-.text: Great. Now we just need to empty that chest. Would you mind?

the-envoy-to-varlamore-looting-the-chest.text: If the player already has the royal accord:

steps.text: You have already recovered the Accord.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-looting-the-chest.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You do not have enough inventory space to loot this chest.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-looting-the-chest.text: You search the chest and find the original Royal Accord of Twill.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-after-emptying-th.player: Not yet. You'll get it once you've returned home.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-after-emptying-th.speaker: Artur Hosidius
the-envoy-to-varlamore-after-emptying-th.text: Eugh. Fine, I'll go home. But you'd better not run off with the Accord.

options.text: Why do you want the Accord anyway?

steps.player: Why do you want the Accord anyway?

steps.speaker: Artur Hosidius
steps.text: Why wouldn't I want it? The signing of the Accord marked the start of a golden age. Once the Royal Lords replaced the Council of Elders, Kourend prospered like never before.

steps.player: But that was a long time ago. Why does it matter now?

steps.speaker: Artur Hosidius
steps.text: Because I think it's time for another golden age. The Kourend Council, like the Council of Elders before them, have failed to do a good job in running this kingdom.

steps.player: And you think the five houses would do a better job?

steps.speaker: Artur Hosidius
steps.text: Exactly.

options.text: What makes you say the Council have done a bad job?

steps.player: What makes you say the Council have done a bad job?

steps.speaker: Artur Hosidius
steps.text: More crime. Fewer homes. More illness. Loss of jobs. The list goes on.

steps.player: But aren't the five houses partially to blame as well? They rule the cities.

steps.speaker: Artur Hosidius
steps.text: The Council sets the laws and the Council sets the budgets. We have to do as they say, just like everyone else.

steps.player: Hmmm, fair enough. Anyway, we'd better get off.

options.text: Fair enough. Now let's be off.

steps.player: Fair enough. Now let's be off.

options.text: I won't. Now let's get going.

steps.player: I won't. Now let's get going.

the-envoy-to-varlamore-climbing-out-of-t.text: You climb up the sand pile.

finishing-up-talking-to-artur.speaker: Artur Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-artur.text: Hello [player name]. Thanks for your help in recovering the Accord.

finishing-up-talking-to-artur.speaker: Artur Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-artur.text: You should talk to my father. He will probably want to reward you.

finishing-up-talking-to-chef-olivia-afte.speaker: Chef Olivia
finishing-up-talking-to-chef-olivia-afte.text: Thank you for bringing Artur home safe.

finishing-up-talking-to-butler-jarvis-af.speaker: Butler Jarvis
finishing-up-talking-to-butler-jarvis-af.text: Good day [sir/madam]. On behalf of the Hosidius family, I thank you for bringing Artur home.

finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.speaker: Elena Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.text: Thank you for finding our son. You've done this kingdom a great service.

finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.speaker: Elena Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.text: I do wonder if his father could have done more though. My brother would have had the entire army out searching.

finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.speaker: Elena Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.text: My brother is Lord Shiro Shayzien. He commands the Shayzien Army. A luxury my husband doesn't have.

finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.speaker: Elena Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-elena-hosidius-a.text: Maybe it doesn't always have to be that way. Things may well soon be different. Now be on your way, I have things to do.

finishing-up-returning-to-lord-hosidius.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
finishing-up-returning-to-lord-hosidius.text: Hello there. Artur is safely back home again. I hear we have you to thank for that.

finishing-up-returning-to-lord-hosidius.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
finishing-up-returning-to-lord-hosidius.text: He also said that you managed to recover the original copy of the Royal Accord of Twill.
If the player doesn't have the accord in their inventory:

steps.player: I did. I don't have it with me though.

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Well go fetch it and bring it here.

finishing-up-returning-to-lord-hosidius.text: If the player has the accord in their inventory:

steps.player: I did. I assume you'll be wanting it.

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Yes. I'll make sure it's well looked after. Now as for that reward I promised.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

steps.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
steps.text: Is there anything else I can do for you?

finishing-up-talking-to-lord-hosidius-ag.speaker: Lord Kandur Hosidius
finishing-up-talking-to-lord-hosidius-ag.text: I assume you're after that reward I promised you. Here you go.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Examiner
starting-the-quest.text: Ah hello there! I am the resident lecturer on antiquities and artefacts. I also set the Earth Sciences exams.

starting-the-quest.speaker: Examiner

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: Unusual... This object doesn't appear right...

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: I wonder... Let me check my guide... Could it be? Surely not!

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: From the markings on it, it seems to be a ceremonial ornament to a god named...

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: ...Zaros? I haven't heard much about him before. This is a great discovery; we know very little of the pagan gods that people worshipped.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: There is some strange writing embossed upon it - it says, 'Zaros will return and wreak his vengeance upon Zamorak the pretender.'

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: I wonder what it means by that? Some silly superstition, probably.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: Still, I wonder what this is doing around here. I'll tell you what; as you have found this, I will allow you to use the private dig shafts.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-bala.text: You obviously have a keen eye. Take this letter and give it to one of the workmen, and they will allow you to use them.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.text: Good day to you. My name is Terry Balando; I am an expert on digsite finds.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.text: I am employed by the museum in Varrock to oversee all finds at this digsite. Anything you find must be reported to me.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.player: Oh, ok. If I find anything of interest I will bring it here.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.speaker: Terry Balando

options.text: I have something I need checking out.
Can you tell me anything about the digsite?

steps.speaker: Terry Balando

options.text: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

making-a-discovery-talking-to-terry-agai.speaker: Terry Balando

making-a-discovery-talking-to-doug-deepi.speaker: Doug Deeping
making-a-discovery-talking-to-doug-deepi.text: Well, well... I have a visitor. What are you doing here?

options.text: I have been invited to research here.

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: Indeed, you must be someone special to be allowed down here.

options.text: Do you know where to find a specimen jar?

steps.player: Do you know where to find a specimen jar?

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: Hmmm, let me think... Nope, can't help you there I'm afraid.

steps.player: I have things to do...

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: Of course, don't let me keep you.

steps.player: I am not sure really.

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: A miner without a clue - how funny!

options.text: I'm here to get rich, rich, rich!

steps.player: I'm here to get rich, rich, rich!

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: Oh, well, don't forget that wealth and riches aren't everything.

options.text: How could I move a large pile of rocks?

steps.player: How do you move a large pile of rocks?

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: There used to be this chap that worked in the other shaft. He was working on an explosive chemical mixture to be used for clearing blocked areas underground.

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: He left in a hurry one day; something in the shaft scared him to death, but he didn't say what.

steps.player: Oh?

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: Rumour has it he'd been writing a book on his chemical mixture. I'm not sure what goes in it but I'm sure you'll find the stuff he was using scattered around the digsite. He left so quickly he didn't take anything with

steps.speaker: Doug Deeping
steps.text: him. In fact, I still have a chest key he gave me to look after; perhaps it's more useful to you.

steps.player: It's ok, I already have one.

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.text: You find some unusual powder inside...

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.player: Mmmm... The lid is shut tight; I'll have to find something to lever it off.

I can't pick this up with my bare hands! I'll need something to put it in. It looks and smells rather dangerous though, so it'll need to be something small and capable of containing dangerous chemicals.

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.text: You fill the vial with the liquid.

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.player: I'm not sure what this stuff is. I had better be VERY careful with it; I had better not drop it either...

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.text: You put the lid back on the barrel just in case it's dangerous.

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.player: Do you know what this is?
From one of the barrels at the digsite.

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.text: This is a VERY dangerous liquid called nitroglycerin. Be careful how you handle it. Don't drop it or it will explode!

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.player: Do you know what this powder is?

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.text: Really, you do find the most unusual items. I know what this is, it's a strong chemical called ammonium nitrate. Why you want this I'll never know...

making-a-discovery-creating-the-explosiv.player: Now, what am I trying to achieve here?
That would be like cutting the lawn with nail scissors! It would take a year to chip away these rocks!
That was a good idea, but these blocks are huge. I' m going to need something much more powerful to shift these...

making-a-discovery-spreading-the-mixture.player: Okay, the mixture is all over the bricks. I need some way to ignite this compound.

making-a-discovery-lighting-the-mixture.player: Whoa! This is going to blow! I'd better run!

making-a-discovery-lighting-the-mixture.text: The player runs to the entrance of the dungeon.

making-a-discovery-lighting-the-mixture.player: Wow, that was a big explosion! What's that noise I can hear? Sounds like bones moving or something...

making-a-discovery-reading-the-stone-tab.player: It says: Tremble mortal, before the altar of our dread lord Zaros.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-the-resear.speaker: Researcher
making-a-discovery-talking-to-the-resear.text: I hear you've been given access to the private mining shafts. You're very lucky.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-the-resear.player: I managed to find something... interesting.
A talisman linked to Zaros, so Terry says.

making-a-discovery-talking-to-the-resear.speaker: Researcher
making-a-discovery-talking-to-the-resear.text: Wow! That's a serious find! Good luck in the lower digs.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.player: I found this in a hidden cavern beneath the digsite.
There is an altar down there. The place is crawling with skeletons!

making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.text: This is an amazing discovery! All this while we were convinced that no other race had lived here.

making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.text: It seems the followers of Saradomin have tried to cover up the evidence of the Zaros altar. This whole city must have been built over it!

making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.speaker: Terry Balando
making-a-discovery-turning-in-the-stone-.text: Thanks for your help; your sharp eyes have spotted what many have missed. Here, take this gold as your reward.
The expert gives you 2 gold bars as payment.

getting-started.speaker: Brimstail
getting-started.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: What's that cute creature wandering around?

steps.player: What's that cute creature wandering around?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh Izzie? He's my pet.

steps.player: What kind of creature is Izzie?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I'm not sure. He's very cute though don't you think? It's very restful having a pet, especially when you are stuck in a cave for as long as I am!

steps.player: So, what do you do down here anyway?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Isn't that obvious? I investigate Thaumaturgy, I research the Arcane, I attempt to explain the inexplicable.

steps.player: You study magic then, what kind of magic? I do a bit of magic myself you know.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Are you a budding mage? I can tell you more about my research if you'd like.

steps.player: Yes, that sounds fascinating...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Excellent, it's so rare I can find someone to discuss my researches, most gnomes seem to find it all very tedious.

steps.player: Never. How could they think that? Though, I suppose gnomes aren't known for their magic.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well that's true. These days, apart from a few combat spells most gnomes seem to be a bit suspicious of mages.

steps.player: Really? Why is that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well there is a bit of history there, do you want me to tell you about it?

options.text: Oh, yes I love a bit of History.

steps.player: Oh, yes I love a bit of History.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Very wise, a good knowledge of the History of Magic is crucial to understanding the Arcane.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, the most famous Gnomish Mage of all got into a bit of .... trouble.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Most gnomes don't really talk about him. Other than telling stories about him as if he was some sort of boogie-man.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ridiculous! He was a gnome like any other - he sounds like a fascinating character.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: He was one of King Healthorg the Great's advisors during the Grand Migration. But he was exiled after the Goblin Wars.

steps.player: Why was that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, I'm not really sure. This was all before I was born - and no-one talks about what happened to Glouphrie these days.

steps.player: He must have done something very bad then.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, maybe? I'm not so sure. As it happens I've been looking into that part of our History. All I've managed to establish was that he was particularly interested in optics and light magic.

steps.player: It's hard to see what he could misuse light in a way that would get him exiled.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, indeed. I have also found though he was generally disliked by other gnomes - his moniker was 'Glouphrie the Untrusted'.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oaknock the Engineer and Glouphrie didn't like each other either...

steps.player: Oaknock? I haven't heard of him before.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ah, Oaknock was an engineer and architect. Very famous. There are statues to him around the place - his reputation amongst gnomes is second only to King Healthorg himself. He built most of the Stronghold you know.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Are you really interested in all of this? Do you want to see something interesting?

steps.prompt: Start the The Eyes of Glouphrie quest?

steps.player: Errm, not right now. I'd better go.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Fine! Humans really do prefer to live their lives in ignorance...

options.text: I'm more interested in your researches right now.

steps.player: I'm more interested in your researches right now.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Gah! Young mages these days. No patience. No perseverance. Magic is not a toy or a shiny weapon you know! You cannot alter reality unless you understand it. And you cannot understand unless you search for the true causes of things. And history is a record of the causes of things.

steps.player: I stand corrected - tell me more.
Actually I'd better get going...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, I'd better carry on with my research then..

steps.player: Err, maybe some other time.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, I'd better carry on with my research then..

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

steps.player: We were discussing gnome magic...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ah, yes indeed. Well I do have a little mystery for you. Has your curiosity been piqued?

options.text: Actually, I'm a bit busy right now.
Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?
