steps.text: So? What did you find?

steps.player: There was a pit with a crystalline looking bowl in the centre.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Indeed, sadly I know very little about that, it looks elven to me though...

steps.player: There is also a large strange looking machine...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's right. It was built by Oaknock.

steps.player: How do you know that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That room used to be Oaknock's workshop. I'd also recognise his style anywhere.

steps.player: What does it do?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I have no idea. But I do know someone who might.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: There is one gnome left who knew Oaknock, and King Healthorg and Glouphrie for that matter...

steps.player: Who is that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have a guess.

steps.player: Errm....

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, King Narnode tells me you've already visited him...

steps.player: Err....
Oh I know, you're talking about Hazelmere aren't you?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Very good, young apprentice.

steps.player: Didn't he help create the Grand Tree?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's right. He was the third advisor to King Healthorg, he found and tended to the Grand Tree.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: If you are really interested in all of this, then could you do me a favour and visit Hazelmere for me? I've been meaning to go for a while, but I have responsibilities here - there's always someone who wants to use the Rune Essence mines.

steps.player: Of course, I'd love to!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Good! Good!

steps.player: Wait a minute, am I going to have to translate everything he says using that dictionary again?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ha! He's an old fashioned kind of gnome and doesn't like visitors much. But I'm sure he'll want to talk about the Old Days.

steps.player: But he only speaks Ancient Gnomish!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That may be true, though he may just be faking it to deter visitors. Either way - he is a wise old gnome. If he really wants to talk to you I'm sure he'll find a way.

steps.player: Well alright, if you say so. What do you want me to ask him?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well ask him if he knows anything about Oaknock's machine. And anything you can find about Glouphrie would be very interesting, wouldn't you agree?

steps.player: Right then. I'd better be on my way. I'll be back soon.

options.text: Actually, I'm a bit busy right now.
Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

investigating-the-next-room-talking-to-b.speaker: Brimstail
investigating-the-next-room-talking-to-b.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: So where do I find this Hazelmere chap then?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So haven't you managed to have a chat with Hazelmere yet?

steps.player: Not yet I'm afraid. Where do I find him again?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: He has a hut in a small island east of Yanille. It has a lovely sea-view, I'm jealous. I love my cave, but it's not very picturesque.

steps.player: Maybe you need some pictures. Though your pot plant adds something to ambiance of the place.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh, that's not my potplant. I think it was Oaknock's.

steps.player: Really? It's survived a long time. It must be a special pot plant.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I suppose it must be. It shakes every now and again you know... I don't know why.

steps.player: How very odd. Anyway, I'd better get on my way to Hazelmere... See you soon.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: The mage starts to speak but all you hear is:

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: Brimstail has sent me to ask you some questions.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Ha! Atarischeray! Blah blah mesi blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: I have some questions about the old days. Brimstail has been filling me in about Gnomish History.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Blah Brimstail blah blah human blah minahar!

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: It sounds like a fascinating time. It also sounds like some important things happened then. Events that we shouldn't forget.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Hmmph. Laquinay blah human. Blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: He has also found a machine - he says it was built by Oaknock...

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Oaknock! Ha blah blah minapor blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Blah blah blah blah Oaknock blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Blah blah blah blah Healthorg cinqo blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: Erm, I'm sorry I don't understand a word you're saying.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: The camera closes in as Hazelmere casts a mind spell on the player's head.
If the player doesn't have level 46 Magic:

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: ... ethereal link ... failed ... puny human mind ... insufficiently disciplined ... mental rigour required ... trained ... magical skills ...

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: If the player has level 46 Magic:

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Hmph. Not bad for a human.

steps.player: Weird! How are you doing this Hazelmere?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Old magicks beyond your skill human. You can stop flapping your big human lips as well. Just think.

steps.player: So how do I do this. Wow. That's impressive.  Brimstail was telling me that Gnomes don't trust Mages these days. Can you hear me? Glouphrie wasn't it? He did something bad and got exiled. Ooh, I'm feeling a little dizzy. You knew him didn't you? What can you tell me about him? And what's this machine that Oaknock built? Isn't that magical as well? Do you know what it does?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Stop wittering on [player name]. You're giving me a headache.  This mind speech is hard enough without having to listen to your incoherent babbling. Think about nothing. Clear your mind.

steps.player: Clear my mind? Hey, how did you know my name.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I'm reading your mind foolish human. How do you think?  Now CLEAR YOUR MIND...

steps.player: How do I think about nothing? I'll give it a go.
Hmm tasty lobster. Gah! I'm thinking about something. Stop thinking about Lobsters. Pink Lobsters. Big Lobsters. Lobsters with wings. Wings? Lobsters don't have wings. ARRGH. I can't do this.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Just shut up and listen! I have a story to tell you that will answer most of your questions.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Let us travel back in time, to the time you humans call the Fourth Age. King Healthorg had become King. The elves mysteriously decided to travel west, leaving most of Kandarin open for conquest. The humans weren't here yet, only King Healthorg and the gnomes to the north, and a collection of Goblin tribes to the south.
A map appears showing armies (flags) advancing towards each other

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Both armies moved to claim the lands, and were of course destined to meet in battle...
A flashback begins, visually showing the battle between gnomes and goblins.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And so it came to pass the Goblins and Gnome armies met at the battle of Atarisundri.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Both sides faced each other on the Battlefield. A bloody battle was in prospect, our gnomes were brave, but we were no match for the mass of brute goblin stupidity...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: ... but Glouphrie and King Healthorg had devised a plan...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: ... If you don't lead an invincible army - pretend you do...
Glouphrie begins casting a spell.

steps.speaker: Glouphrie
steps.text: Em Gal lauf rei!

steps.speaker: Glouphrie
steps.text: Emeto Laufolly egramentos umesco lamiten gan!
A large group of tortoises appear behind the gnomes.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And so, Glouphrie created an army of illusory Giant tortoises, knowing that goblins would be scared of anything bigger than they were.

steps.speaker: Goblin 1 (unnamed)
steps.text: Big Boss didn' say nuffin 'bout de nomiez havin' monsta tortisses!

steps.speaker: Goblin 2 (unnamed)
steps.text: Dey be huges! Tortisses too scary and pointy. We runz away!
The two goblins flee the battle, soon followed by others.

steps.speaker: Goblin 3 (unnamed)
steps.text: Scarey tortisses! Runz!

steps.speaker: Goblin 4 (unnamed)
steps.text: Runz away!
The flashback ends.

steps.player: Hey! Was that you next to the tortoise? You look so handsome!

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Handsome! Hmph! That was a long time ago...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Anyway, where was I? Oh yes...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Sadly, the golden times were not destined to last for long...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: There was once a very special Spirit Tree in the Stronghold. Silver as a birch, old and wise - I considered him a friend. I called him Argento, his true name was unpronouncable.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: He was the first Spirit Tree I had befriended, and the one I knew the best. I would sometimes travel, visiting and finding other Spirit trees, and during one such trip, I was filled with a great sense of foreboding...
Another flashback about Argento, the silver-coloured spirit tree, begins.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I felt a shadow pass over me, and a tingling in the air, even though the weather was fine and dry.
A large shadow appears and passes over the spirit tree.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Then I felt a sudden pain, as if the Anima Mundi was crying out with the loss of a favoured child...
A lightning bolt strikes Argento, splitting him in half.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And I knew that one of the Old Ones had died, and I had lost a friend.
The flashback ends.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I rushed straight back to the Grand Tree, only to find that no-one had noticed anything, and that Argento was still standing and seemed alive. But I knew something was wrong. He refused to talk to me and his aura was

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: no longer present.  Someone had hidden his death.  I talked to Oaknock and he was incensed.  He immediately blamed Glouphrie, and although Oaknock could be rather irrational when it came to Glouphrie -

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: they never saw eye to eye - I knew he was right this time.  Glouphrie had used his magicks to hide the truth from all of us.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Oaknock had made a machine - an anti-illusion machine, with some help from the elves.  He prepared it, and summoned the advisors to Argento..
A final flashback shows King Healthorg, Oaknock, Glouphrie and Hazelmere in front of an apparently intact Argento.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Why have you summoned us here?

steps.speaker: Oaknock the Engineer
steps.text: You'll see sire. Switch the machine on!
The anti-illusion machine is activated, revealing the true state of the Silver Spirit Tree.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: What is the meaning of this?

steps.speaker: Oaknock the Engineer
steps.text: The Silver Spirit Tree is dead!

steps.speaker: Oaknock the Engineer
steps.text: Glouphrie has been using his foul arts to mask the truth! What other secrets has he been keeping?
The King turns to Glouphrie.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Explain yourself!

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: I live to serve you sire. I work for the good of us all.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: How can lying to your fellow gnomes be 'Good'?

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Some things are best kept secret...

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Even from your King!?

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Occasionally.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Enough! How can I trust a gnome who hides things from me?

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: No gnome can blame you for what you do not know.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: That is NOT how I rule.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Glouphrie. You are no longer my advisor. Leave this place.

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Only the naive believe they can rule without someone like me.

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Your empire will crack and the gnomes will become but a joke.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Sarko!

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: So be it. I'll be watching.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And so Glouphrie left and travelled with some companions to a place they called Arposandra. We have heard nothing but rumours about them since...
The flashback ends.

steps.player: So where's this Arposandra place anyway?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Nobody knows for certain, somewhere rocky I suppose. The rumour is that after founding his new home, Glouphrie used his magicks to shroud the city in mist. Arposandra may not exist at all, however I suspect that

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Glouphrie is still around, one way or another.

steps.player: Why do you think that?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Just call it Gnomish intuition.

steps.player: So the machine that Brimstail has found is the one that Oaknock built to stop Glouphrie's illusions.  Do you know how it worked?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I never studied it, but I believe it used elven magic - So it must have used crystals of some sort. Crystal discs, yes that sounds familiar.  Actually come to think of it I think I may have one lying around.  Here take

steps.player: this, maybe it will help you.

steps.text: Violet pentagon

steps.player: Well, thank you, Hazelmere. You've told me a lot of things I need to ponder for a while.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Very well. Oh and when you see that lazy toad Brimstail, tell him next time he needs information to come himself.

steps.player: I'll do that. Farewell.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: The mage starts to speak but all you hear is:
The camera closes in as Hazelmere casts a mind spell on the player's head.

discussion-with-hazelmere-talking-to-haz.text: The mage starts to speak but all you hear is:
The camera closes in as Hazelmere casts a mind spell on the player's head.

discussion-with-hazelmere-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-talking-to-haz.text: What do you want now? Go and talk to Brimstail, that's why you came to see me in the first place...

the-anti-illusion-machine-returning-to-b.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-returning-to-b.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I've visited Hazelmere, he told me all sorts of interesting things.

steps.player: I've visited Hazelmere, he told me all sorts of interesting things.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ah, thank you my young apprentice. What did he tell you?

steps.player: Right. Well it starts during the Great Migration...

steps.text: You tell Brimstail everything Hazelmere told you - Brimstail takes lots of notes.
A cutscene shows a near-invisible gnome sneak by Brimstail and the player as they discuss.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So the machine emits an anti-illusion glamour?

steps.player: Glamour? What's that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Don't you know anything? *sigh* A glamour is a type of enchantment or magical effect.

steps.player: Oh yes it does have such a glamour. It seems to use crystal discs to work in some way.

steps.text: You show Brimstail the disc Hazelmere gave you.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh, crystal discs? I may have a few of those in a drawer somewhere.

steps.player: What's that? Something just moved behind you...

steps.text: The gnome destroys the machine.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Really? Wait - what's that banging noise?
Brimstail and the player hurry up to the other room

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: What's happened to the machine? It's broken!

steps.player: Hmm, something is afoot.  I sense sabotage....

steps.text: End of cutscene.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-speaking-to-br.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-speaking-to-br.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: The machine is broken, I suspect sabotage...!

steps.player: The machine is broken, I suspect sabotage...!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: This is intolerable! How could this happen?

steps.player: I'm confused, it must have happened while we were here talking!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: But we were just standing here, how could someone get past us?

steps.player: I did see something odd behind you...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Wait a minute, how did the saboteur know about the machine?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm ... You're the only person I've told about the machine...

steps.player: Hey! Don't look at me like that. The only person I've talked to is Hazelmere.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Surely this couldn't be the work of Hazelmere... That turncoat!!

steps.player: Wait! Wait! None of this makes any sense. There must be another explanation.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Alright. Someone snuck in here without us noticing. How?

steps.player: The intruder must have been invisible.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Right, and how does one make oneself invisible?
If the player has progressed far enough into Monkey Madness I:

steps.player: Of course! I've seen this before. Karam in the 10th squad used some sort of magic to make himself invisible.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Do you think the 10th squad did this?

steps.player: No, but I think our saboteur must have learnt the same magicks. Is Glouphrie still alive?

steps.text: If the player hasn't progressed far enough into Monkey Madness I:

steps.player: Illusion magic?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Invisibility is a form of illusion magic. So that makes sense...

steps.player: So this was done by Glouphrie? Is he still alive?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Who knows, but he may well have taught the skills to his gnomes.

steps.player: You mean the gnomes that went with Glouphrie to Arposandra?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Right. And why would they sabotage an anti-illusion device?

steps.player: Because there is an illusion that they want to remain hidden?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Of course. Which makes it imperative that we fix this machine and find out what it is!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have a look at the machine and assess the damage. I'll hunt around my boxes and see if I can find anything that might help.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: Something's happened to the machine! It's broken!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have you had a look at the damage yet?

steps.player: Not yet. I'll get right to it.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: You look at the damage done.   There are two main wooden parts that need to be repaired. It looks as if you'll need two types of wood; maple and oak, to complete the repairs. It also looks as if everything was stuck together by some sort of resin based glue that smells of pine, and contains flecks of grey powder that glint and sparkle in a
You think that you'll need some skill in construction (level 5) and the standard construction tools to repair the machine.
If the player doesn't have glue:

steps.text: You need something to stick all the bits together.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have oak logs:

steps.text: You need some oak logs to repair this.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have maple logs:

steps.text: You need some maple logs to repair this.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have a saw:

steps.text: You need a saw to repair this machine.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have a hammer:

steps.text: You need a hammer to repair this machine.

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I'm still a bit confused about how to fix Oaknock's machine.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So how are your investigations going?

steps.player: I'm not getting anywhere with these 'sticky runes'.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm, which runes would you think are sticky.

steps.player: Runes are runes! None of them are sticky! They're all round and disc-like and definitely non-adhesive.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Open your mind and think laterally. Thinking sideways is an important skill for a mage.

steps.player: Oh, all right. I'll give it a go. Well - air, water and fire and earth runes. There's nothing sticky about them.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I concur.

steps.player: Mind and body runes. Again distinctly non-glue-like in any way.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Keep going.

steps.player: Nature and Cosmic runes. Once more distinctly lacking in any gooeyness. Bah! This is a waste of time.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Patience young apprentice. You are on the right path - just think it through and I'm sure it will become obvious.

steps.player: Maybe. What do I do with the rune when I find it?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: What did Oaknock do?

steps.player: Well it looked powdered in the glue.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So there you go. What more do you need to know?
If the player doesn't have a bucket of sap:

steps.player: Well, I'm still a bit unsure about getting this glue.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So, what do you know so far?

steps.player: It looked ambery in colour and sticky, smelt of pine and had flecks of silvery stuff in it.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: It smelt of pine and was ambery in colour, that sounds like tree sap. From a coniferous tree probably.

steps.player: Tree sap?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have you never tried cutting a coniferous tree and watching the sap drip out?

steps.player: Err no.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well maybe if you had, you'd know something about tree sap!

steps.player: So where do I put the stuff?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm, use your head! What kind of substance is this tree sap?

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Is it a solid, a liquid or a gas?

steps.player: Oh, I see - a liquid I suppose.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So where do you put liquids?

steps.player: Some form of container?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Right! I think you know everything you need now...

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.text: If the player has a bucket of sap:

steps.player: Right. I'll go away and think about what you've said.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's right, use your noddle, exercise your noggin, employ your cranium. Think, think, think!

steps.player: Now you're just confusing me more...

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-making-magic-g.text: You mix the mud rune powder into the tree sap. It looks sticky.

the-anti-illusion-machine-repairing-the-.text: You've fixed it! It seems to be working now, though it does appear to be locked.

the-anti-illusion-machine-after-repairin.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-after-repairin.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I think I've fixed the machine now!

steps.player: I think I've fixed the machine now!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well done! You're almost as good at fixing things as a gnome! Who'd have thought?

steps.player: Though I still don't think it's actually activated. There appears to be some sort of lock on the front. I think I know what the discs are for though. There's a slot in the front that looks like it might fit a disc, and a
number.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So what do you think the number means?

steps.player: I'm not sure yet. Maybe I should put a disc into the slot and see what happens?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That reminds me, I found those crystal discs I mentioned before.
Red square and Yellow triangle

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: They are not quite the same as the one Hazelmere gave you, but they look similar in size and weight.

steps.player: They also look as if they might fit in the slots on both of the machines. Maybe I should try it out?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I wonder if the different sizes and shapes mean anything.

steps.player: I've been thinking that as well, I shall ponder it some more.. I'll work it out.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's the spirit! This is all good training for the mind...

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I can't work out what to do with these discs!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm. Maybe all of these discs all have different values and you have to choose the right one in order for it to work?

steps.player: Interesting. But how do I work out which discs are worth what value?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I'm not sure, but there will be some logic somewhere. Maybe if you look around the workshop you'll find some clues?

steps.player: I'll have a look.

steps.text: If the player has not received the three extra discs from Brimstail:

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh, I've been rooting through my drawers and I've found a few more discs that you might find useful.
three random discs

steps.player: Thanks, I'm sure they'll be very useful.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: The panel shows a diagram of boxes stacked on top of each other. The stacks are split into seven columns, with each column being taller than the previous. Each column is also a different colour. From left to right, the colours are: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

the-anti-illusion-machine-using-the-mach.text: You have not unlocked the machine yet...
You'll need to insert some discs and change them first.
You press the button. Not a lot happens...
Not a lot happens. Maybe you need to insert a disc first...
You cannot add more discs after you have exchanged.
The discs you put into the slot, clunk out into your hand.
You'll need to press either the exchange or cancel buttons to return discs.
You hear the machine make some whirring noises.
The discs shown in the window clunk out of the machine into your hands.
The front panel of the machine is unlocked! Well done.
The machine is still not fully operational.
The discs you have put in clunk out.

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I think Oaknock's machine is now unlocked, what do I do now?

steps.player: I seem to have opened some sort of control panel.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I wonder how it works? a similar way to the locking mechanism I'd guess.

steps.player: There seems to be more than one slot. Maybe I need more than one disc?

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.text: The machine is now fully operational. Congratulations!

the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.text: Well done [player name]! I knew you'd work it out. I'll make a mage out of you yet...
The machine removes the cute creature's illusion, revealing an evil creature.

the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.text: Izzie! No! There's something very wrong going on here...

the-anti-illusion-machine-attempting-to-.text: The machine is now working, you don't need to do anything to it any more.

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: Phew! I've got that machine working now. What do I need to do now?

steps.player: Phew! I've got that machine working now. What do I need to do now?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, it seems that Izzie was not so cute after all! How awful! How mysterious!

steps.player: So this was an illusion the Arposandrans went to so much effort to conceal? A pet. That wasn't cute enough.
Where did you find this one?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Izzie just wandered into my cave. He was cute and friendly so I kept him.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: He seemed very curious, and used to watch me do my researches. I liked the companionship – research is lonely work...

steps.player: So he's been keeping an eye on you while you do important magical research...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I suppose it has. I hadn't thought of it like that. I'm sure I've seen others of these creatures around the place...

steps.player: Where?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I think King Narnode has one, and I think I saw one by the gates. And I'm sure I've seen a few more wandering around.

steps.player: In other words all places to keep an eye on what's going in the Stronghold...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh my goodness. I think I'm beginning to understand where you are going with this.

steps.player: Yes, they must be spies. They are watching us with those creepy red eyes. And they must have told someone that we were working on the machine.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So that horrible thing was listening to us all along. You'd better tell the King what's going on.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-again.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-again.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: What should we do about these creatures?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So this horrible thing is listening to us right now... Aargh. Get rid of it! Don't forget to tell the king what's going on!

steps.player: I'll get on it now.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-killing-an-evil-creature.text: I've killed [number] spying creatures so far, maybe there are more to find...

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: What should we do about these creatures?

steps.player: What should we do about these creatures?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have you talked to the King yet?

steps.player: I'll get on it now.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-talking-to-narnode.player: Good day sire, I take it you've noticed that cute creature you had in here is looking rather different now.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Why yes! Do you know what's going on?

assassination-talking-to-narnode.player: I think I do. It's a long story but the short version is this. The Arposandran gnomes have planted these creatures as spies to watch what's going on in the Stronghold.
I have just reactivated a machine that was built by Oaknock that dispels illusions, and now these creatures true forms are revealed.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Glouphrie! Now we know what he has been up to all these years. Gah! Never trust a Mage.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.player: Well, I wouldn't go as far as that – it is only through Brimstail's and my researches that we have established this is going on.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Harumph! Well, all of these creatures must be removed, we cannot allow the Arposandrans to spy on us any more. How many of these things are there?

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Well find them all and dispatch them now.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again.text: Have you found all of those spies yet?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again.player: Not yet, I'm still looking for them.

assassination-killing-all-evil-creatures.text: You've killed all the creatures now, you'd better tell the King...

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I've killed all of the spies.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's a relief. Well, that's all good work, but I think you'd better inform the King now.

steps.player: I'll get on it now.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Have you found all of those spies yet?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: I think so. There were six in total.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Thank goodness. Thank you for your help. Brimstail also tells me that you helped him a lot finding out what was going on!

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: Help? I did all of the hard work!

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Aha! Getting others to do the donkey work seems to be a skill that Mages develop well.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: So what will you do now?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Well, I have many things to think about. Why are the Arposandrans spying on us, and what are they planning?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: It's certainly worrying, and whoever sabotaged the machine couldn't have been far from here. Are there gnomes here who are also spies?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Indeed, that is another thing that worries me...

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: If you find out more I'd be willing to help investigate.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: That may well be useful. Thank you – I may well call for your help again.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Oh, before you leave – I have something you might like.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: It was passed down to me from King to King. It belonged to Oaknock. He proclaimed that only a hero of the gnomes should have it. I think you count as a hero. Also since you have been looking into Oaknock you

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: might be able to work out what it is.
King Narnode gives you a small crystal seed.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: Hmm I wonder what it does?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Well, I'm sure that your magical research skills will help you there. Good luck!
Congratulations, you've completed a quest: The Eyes of Glouphrie

1675-y.speaker: Brimstail
1675-y.text: Well, have a careful look around at everything in the next cave and come back and tell me what you find.

DwqU9V.player: Actually, I'm a bit busy right now.

standard-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: That was an amazing performance! I've only seen one like it... as you know.

standard-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.player: Don't worry, Felkrash has no idea how I figured it out.

standard-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: And it had better stay that way!

steps.text: You've found another clue!

historical-dialogue-before-ratcatchers.text: She looks through you as if you don't exist.

historical-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-.npc: Step away from that manhole, you've no business down there.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Ah you, peasant. Felkrash wishes to speak with you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: 'The Face' comports herself in an air of haughtiness uncommon to those with appearances as ugly as hers.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Ok, where would I find her?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: You should find her below in the pits.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Hello.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh it's you again. She glances at you with barely disguised disdain.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* I wonder what her problem is?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Have you spoken with Felkrash yet?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Yes.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: You notice a rather unkempt looking cat nearby. Despite its bedraggled appearance it exudes power, strength and intelligence beyond that of a normal cat.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: That's an interesting looking cat.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Ah yes Belle. What a cat. Felkrash trained her for me shortly after she single handedly charmed all the rats of the Port and drowned them.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: I love that story. My favourite part is how she managed to get rid of all the rats. Would you tell it to me?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I don't know, I really shouldn't.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* I'll get the story out of her, a little sweet talking should do the trick.
Oh please tell me, I'm sure you'd tell the story wonderfully, you have such a pretty ...

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Yes..?
The face's face perks up at the mention of the word pretty.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: ...voice.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh. And just as quickly turns sour again.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* Dang!
... which compliments your radiant aura!
Aside* That should do the trick.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh you're too generous.
Do you know something, I think I'll tell you, mind you, don't tell Felkrash about this, she'd only get sore with me.
She's the story teller not me.
One day ......
One day ......

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: The camera fades briefly to black and back.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: And that is how she drowned the rats.
..and that is how she drowned the rats.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: You just about manage to stay awake through the long and turgid recital of the story.
The snakecharmer of Pollnivneach from what you gathered seemed to play a critical role in the story.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside*Perhaps I should pay this snake charmer a visit.
Hello.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh it's you again. She glances at you with barely disguised disdain.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* I wonder what her problem is?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Felkrash told me of the task she set you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Really?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I shouldn't have told that story. Shame on you for coaxing it out of me.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: I promise I won't tell her you helped me.

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: Oh it's you again. She glances at you with barely disguised disdain.*

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.player: Aside* I wonder what her problem is?

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: I must congratulate you on your performance, I have only ever seen one other display of musicality to match, as you should know.

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.player: Thank you, and don't worry, I won't tell Felkrash that you helped me.

getting-started.speaker: Ali Morrisane
getting-started.text: Good day and welcome back to Al Kharid.

getting-started.speaker: Ali Morrisane
getting-started.text: My name is Ali Morrisane - the greatest salesman in the world.

options.text: Are you really the greatest salesman in the world?

steps.player: If you're the greatest salesman in the world, why are you still selling goods from a stall?

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Well one can only do and sell so much. If I had more staff I'd be able to sell more, rather than wasting my time on menial things. I could get on with selling sand to the Bedabin and useless tourist trinkets to just about

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: everyone else.

options.text: I'm too busy to help. Adventuring is a full time job you know!

steps.player: I'm too busy to help. Adventuring is a full time job you know!

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: No problem my friend, perhaps another time.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Anyway, have a look at my wares.

options.text: I'd like to help you, but...

steps.player: I'd like to help you but...

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Yes, I know, I know - the life of a shop keeper isn't slaying dragons and wooing damsels, but it has its charms.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Although perhaps you can help me some other way. A nephew of mine lives not too far from here in a little town called Pollnivneach. He was supposed to become my assistant, but he hasn't shown up. If you fetch him

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: here I'll give you the first month of his salary!
If the player has a combat level less than 40:
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 40.

steps.prompt: Start The Feud quest?

steps.player: I'll find your nephew.
But you had better become the greatest merchant in Gielinor once I succeed!

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Ah, many thanks, my friend. My nephew's name is Ali and he lives to the south in a town called Pollnivneach.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Tell him his uncle Ali M needs his help up in Al Kharid.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: And while you're here, have a look at my wares.

steps.player: I'm too busy to help. Adventuring is a full time job you know!

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: No problem my friend, perhaps another time.

steps.speaker: Ali Morrisane
steps.text: Anyway, have a look at my wares.

options.text: So what are you selling then?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.speaker: Ali Morrisane
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.text: I sent you to learn the whereabouts of my nephew, Ali. Is there any word of him in Pollnivneach?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.speaker: Ali Morrisane
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.text: That's not really the news I was hoping for.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.speaker: Ali Morrisane
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-morrisa.text: But since you've been gone trade has gotten even busier. Will you have a look at my wares?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: Welcome, adventurer, to the town of Pollnivneach, the gateway to Menaphos and Al Kharid. My name is Ali and I'm the mayor of this town. I hope you enjoy your stay here.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.player: Thank you. That is one of the warmest welcomes I've ever had! People generally treat travelling adventurers with suspicion.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: All are welcome here. Now more than ever I suppose.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.player: What do you mean by that?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: There's trouble in town, and a lot of villagers have left as a result. Things are looking dire.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.player: I'm looking for someone called Ali.
I mean I'm looking for a specific Ali. He's Ali Morrisane's nephew.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.speaker: Ali the Mayor
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-may.text: Oh, that Ali! Well, er, your best bet is to ask around town. I'm sure someone will know what he's up to.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-cam.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
asking-the-locals-talking-to-ali-the-cam.text: Welcome to my discount camel store. Can I help you with anything?

steps.player: A discount camel store?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Yes - it's my great idea - selling camels at discounted prices so that the common man can experience the joys of owning a camel of their very own! They're not just a source of kebab meat you know!

options.text: So can I buy a camel then? I'm hungry!

steps.player: So can I buy a camel then? I'm hungry!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I would never sell one to the likes of you! They are beautiful, majestic creatures, not food! Get out of my shop.

steps.player: Yes, camels are beautiful creatures.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Ah, wondrous camels! Best of all Saradomin's creations. Ships of the desert, far more useful than any horse or donkey. Truly, they are a man's best friend.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Perhaps you'd like a camel of your own? You're in the right place, if so...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well yes, actually I would like to ask about something else.
No, but thanks for your time.

steps.player: No, but thanks for your time.

options.text: Why would I want a camel? All they do is spit and...

steps.player: Why would I want a camel? All they do is spit and...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Pah! I've seen mummies with more brains than you! If you treat camels badly then of course they're going to spit at you. May your robes never be clean again!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Actually, I think I was a camel in a previous life.

steps.player: Actually, I think I was a camel in a previous life.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: You're teasing me now! You rogue!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Everyone laughs at the poor Discount Camel Seller.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: So is the discount camel business good then?

steps.player: So is the discount camel business good then?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Business is booming! Pollnivneach has never seen this number of visitors.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: In fact I'm thinking of expanding and trying to break into the camel hire market.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: If only I could figure out how to get people to return the camels...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: Tell me about this town.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, Pollnivneach is a funny little place. It's a small town and you'd think it'd be nice and quiet.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: But those Menaphites and bandits are making the place quite unbearable.

steps.player: In what way?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, one group is as bad as the other! They steal, they fight, they cause trouble with us locals. Just yesterday one of those bandits came looking for protection money!

steps.player: Why don't the authorities stop this?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: We're a small town. We don't have the resources to keep the gangs off our backs! Menaphos and Al Kharid are no help either.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: To tell the truth we live in hope that an outsider, someone with no ties to either group, could broker a deal to halt the hostilities between them.

steps.player: Hmm...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well the weak will always be trodden on. Why not stand up to them?

steps.player: Well the weak will always be trodden on. Why not stand up to them?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: That's a little unfair, my friend. We can't all be brave adventurers. If we were, where would you purchase quality camels at discounted prices?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: You might think about that. Anyway, isn't it the job of the brave adventurer to protect the weak and innocent from evil and harm?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: Perhaps I could help.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Yes, perhaps you could.

steps.player: You know the politics better than I do. What do you recommend?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Me?! I am but a humble discount camel seller. You're the adventurer, don't you know what to do?

options.text: Of course I know what to do! I was just testing you!

steps.player: Of course I know what to do! I was just testing you!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: That is reassuring to hear. Too often one meets brainless adventurers whose solution to every problem is to hack, maim and murder.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I'm glad to know you're not of that ilk.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Perhaps I should know, but offered advice should never be shunned.

steps.player: Perhaps I should know, but offered advice should never be shunned.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: The state of adventurers today. They need everything spelled out for them.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: What, you want me to put a little note in your quest journal?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: But fine, I'll give you a hint. Try and see if you can get the gangs to agree to a truce by offering them each a token gift as an act of reconciliation.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: If that fails to work, you must consider trying to influence the gangs from within.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: It's a beautiful day today, but word has it that it will rain tomorrow.

steps.player: Really?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: No! When have you ever known it to rain here in Gielinor?

steps.player: Oh. Anyway...

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Are those camels around the side for sale?

steps.player: Are those camels around the side for sale?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Those two camels around the side are already sold.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I've got new stock coming very soon though. Come back later if you're still interested.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well yes, actually I would like to ask about something else.
No, but thanks for your time.

steps.player: No, but thanks for your time.

options.text: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.player: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, you've found your man.

steps.player: Really? Do you have an uncle called Ali?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Why yes - all my uncles are called Ali!

steps.player: Oh dear! Do any of them own a stall in the Al Kharid Bazaar?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well no, but one of them owns a moderately successful camel hire franchise.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Have you considered hiring a camel? Or perhaps purchasing one of your own? I can get you a discount.

steps.player: Never mind.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-rug-mer.speaker: Rug Merchant
asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-rug-mer.text: Greetings, desert traveller. Do you require the services of Ali Morrisane's flying carpet fleet?

steps.player: Tell me about Ali Morrisane.

steps.speaker: Rug Merchant
steps.text: What, you haven't heard of Ali M? Possibly the greatest salesman of the Kharidian empire if not all Gielinor?

steps.player: Hold on... yes I can place him now. He has me looking for his nephew Ali, I think he needs some help with his shop.

steps.speaker: Rug Merchant
steps.text: I wouldn't be surprised, he's mentioned to me on a few occasions that he is thinking of diversifying even further.

steps.player: You wouldn't have seen his nephew about then?

steps.speaker: Rug Merchant
steps.text: No it's been a quite a while since I last saw him.

options.text: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.speaker: Street urchin
asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.text: No one knows what's going on in the streets better than me. I live, sleep, eat and drink here. The fact that I'm so small means that people tend to ignore me which helps even more.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.speaker: Street urchin
asking-the-locals-talking-to-a-street-ur.text: Do you need any other information?

steps.player: Yes, tell me about...
Tell me about the Menaphites.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: They're a bad bunch, always starting fights down in the Asp and Snake. Word on the street is that they're led by some deranged priest. Nobody's ever seen them though - they do all their deals through Ali 'the

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Operator'. I reckon they're up to something, but they're such a close knit group that little ever slips out.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

steps.player: Tell me about the bandits.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: There's not much to say, really. They're just a group of local thugs led by the biggest and strongest amongst them. If they have any other plans, I don't know about it.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

steps.player: Tell me about the Mayor.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: The mayor is a spineless coward! He never stands up to anybody. That's why the Menaphites are so strong now! He let them stay, and then they started causing trouble. When he realised his mistake, he hired a band

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: of local thugs to drive them out, but they saw how weak he was and turned on us too. Now we've got bandits and Menaphites, and the mayor isn't doing anything!

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

steps.player: Tell me about Ali Morrisane's nephew.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: I know him! He used to kick us when he caught any of us stealing from his stall.

steps.player: Do you know where he is now then?

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: He disappeared a little while ago. All I know is it had something to do with the gangs. Probably he scammed them. You'd have to gain their trust to find out more, m'afraid - if I get too close, they might disappear me

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: too!

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

steps.player: Tell me about the town.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: It's boring! We're not as big as Menaphos or as powerful as Al Kharid, and we've got a really nasty crime problem. It's no wonder so many grown-ups have left.

steps.speaker: Street urchin
steps.text: Do you need any other information?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-ali-the.speaker: Ali the Barman
asking-the-locals-talking-to-the-ali-the.text: Good day. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, I'd like a drink please.

steps.player: Yes, I'd like a drink please.
What's going on in town?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Nothing much really. About what you'd expect from a sleepy little town like ours.

steps.player: What about those two gangs? That seems exciting.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: They're paying customers, so I won't rock the boat if you don't mind.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: No thanks, I'm ok. Thanks for your time.

options.text: Yes, I'd like to talk about something else.
I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.player: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Well, I'm called Ali and I'm from here. Are you looking for me?

steps.player: Do you have an uncle called Ali?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Yes! All my uncles are called Ali!

steps.player: Oh dear. Well do any of your uncles have a stall in the Bazaar in Al Kharid?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Um... no.

steps.player: Well do you know if anyone here does?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: That's a difficult question to answer. I don't know anyone else's uncles.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

steps.player: The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Maybe around these parts. Were you expecting it to have 'Ali' in the name?

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: I did think about calling it 'Ali's', but then it'd get confused with the Camel Shop, the Kebab House, the Mayor's residence...

steps.player: Yes, I get your point. It's a perfectly fine name.

steps.speaker: Ali the Barman
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Ahh, a kind stranger. Get this old man a drink so that he may wet his throat and tell you of the strange happenings in this town.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Now where were we? Ah yes, Ali Morrisane's wayward nephew.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: What?! How did you know that's who I was looking for?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Er... well, he's a real scamp, that lad! I can't imagine a stranger would be asking after anyone else.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Hmm. Well go on then, where is he?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: I'd tell you more, but my throat is drying up. This desert climate is an inhospitable one. Get me another beer so that I can continue my tale.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Get this poor, thirsty old man another drink so that he may wet his lips and continue.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: You are too kind, now what were we talking about?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Of course! I've known him since he was a wee lad. A right little mischievous beggar...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Yes, I can imagine. Do you have any more recent information about him? Where is he?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Well now, if you had just asked me that in the first place I would have told you directly!

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: You're right, I'm sorry for beating around the bush. Do you know where Ali's nephew is now, though?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: I'd tell you more, but my throat is drying up. This desert climate is an inhospitable one. Get me another beer so that I can continue my tale.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Alas, my throat has dried up, and I cannot speak... perhaps another drink would help?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Ahh, that hits the spot.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Now which of you two adventurers wanted to know where Ali's nephew is?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Is this a double? No wonder I feel sick...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Look, all I want to know is the whereabouts of Ali Morrisane's nephew.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Now is that his nephew from his side or his wife's? They have a huge family you see. I remember...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: No, no, no. Stop right there. You are not going to fool me into buying you another beer without first giving me some useful information.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: But my lips are so dry, how can I possibly continue?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: Well if your lips are dry, I'll have to wring you like a wet cloth and squeeze out enough booze to fill another tankard. I'd reckon it would hurt though.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: I see. Don't worry about me, I'll just have to soldier on. Now what do you want to know?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.player: For the last time, where is Ali Morrisane's nephew?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Oh, I don't know.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Wait, wait! The last I heard he was in trouble with those gangs hanging around town. You won't get any answers out of them, though, not while they're feuding. Maybe if you were to solve that little problem...

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Anyway, is there any chance of another beer?

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: What were we talking about again? Yes yes, when I was a boy... no, that's not it.

asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.speaker: Drunken Ali
asking-the-locals-talking-to-drunken-ali.text: Eh? What's this? I don't want that, get me a beer.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.player: I am trying to get to the bottom of this feud between you and the Menaphites.
I'm just trying to understand why thieves of your repute would stoop to their level.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.text: Well, if memory serves me correctly, I think the hostilities began when they robbed one of our camels. A heinous crime.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.player: So if they offered a camel back as a gesture of goodwill, would you and the rest of the bandits cease your hostilities?

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-bandit.text: Those Menaphites would never do that. They have no sense of honour.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.player: I am trying to figure out the feud that exists between you and the Bandits.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: Not much to figure out there, the problem is those thieving bandits.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: They are always stealing, starting fights and disrupting the lives of the townsfolk.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.player: Word has it that the Menaphites are also involved in unsavoury behaviour.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: Well, we also steal, start fights, and disrupt lives - but we do it with class! And the bandits definitely started it.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: I can scarcely remember, it's been so long.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: I think our leader once mentioned that they robbed one of our camels. A heinous crime around these parts.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.player: So if they offered a camel as a gesture of goodwill would you agree to cease hostilities?

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.speaker: Menaphite Thug
asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.text: Those bandits would never agree to that. They couldn't afford even the mangiest excuse for a camel, never mind the desert traversing, four legged beauty that we would demand.

asking-the-gangs-talking-to-a-menaphite-.player: Maybe if I got both gangs a camel, I could use the mutual good will to find out what happened to Ali's nephew.

acquiring-some-camels-talking-to-ali-the.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
acquiring-some-camels-talking-to-ali-the.text: Welcome to my discount camel store. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: Are those camels around the side for sale?

steps.player: Are those camels around the side for sale?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Those two camels around the side are already sold.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: But you are in luck - I have another two beautiful camels arriving soon from the best stable in all of Al Kharid.

steps.player: Excellent! Although another two ugly camels would have been fine, I think.

options.text: Can you tell me a little about them?

steps.player: Can you tell me a little about them?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well Sandy, the female camel, is a placid beast. At 20 years of age she comes from a prestigious line of camels - her mother was part of the Emir's baggage train!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Lumps, on the other hand, is a 15 year old male. He's a bit surly and prone to bouts of stubbornness. However, he more than makes up for this failing with his immense strength and stamina.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Both of them are of the 'Camelus Horribleus' family, a rare breed only found in this area of Gielinor. It is...

steps.player: Ok, ok, that's enough! They're camels, I get it.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Well yes, actually I would like to ask about something else.
No, but thanks for your time.

steps.player: No, but thanks for your time.

options.text: What price do you want for both of them?

steps.player: What price do you want for both of them?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: One cannot put a price on these beauties, they are precious beyond the worth of the crass value of gold coins!

options.text: So can I have them for free then?

steps.player: So can I have them for free then?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Are you trying to be funny?

steps.player: Perhaps I could make another offer?

options.text: Would 200 gold coins for the pair of them do?

steps.player: Would 200 gold coins for the pair of them do?

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Pah! That might buy you a mangy, flea-infested sheep if you're lucky. Don't insult me.

steps.player: Perhaps I could make another offer?

options.text: Would 500 gold coins for the pair of them do?

steps.player: Would 500 gold coins for the pair of them do?

steps.text: Without two empty inventory spaces:
Without enough gold:
Otherwise:

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I suppose I can silence my moral objections for that.
Ali the discount camel seller gives you a receipt for the camels in return for 500 gold coins.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Here are the receipts for the camels, so that you can pick them up as soon as I get them in.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Would 1000 gold coins for the pair of them do?

steps.player: Would 1,000 gold coins for the pair of them do?

steps.text: Without two empty inventory spaces:
Without enough gold:
Otherwise:

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: You are too generous. I would have sold them for half of that!
Ali the discount camel seller gives you a receipt for the camels in return for 1,000 gold coins.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Here are the receipts for the camels, so that you can pick them up as soon as I get them in.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

now-we-have-camels-talking-to-ali-the-ca.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
now-we-have-camels-talking-to-ali-the-ca.text: Hello! Welcome back to my discount camel store. How are those camels getting along?

options.text: About those camels. I've lost the receipt. Can I have another?

steps.player: About those camels. I've lost the receipt, can I have another?

steps.text: If the player has both receipts:

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: I think you're trying to con me into giving you an extra receipt.
If the player doesn't have enough inventory space:

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Come back to me when you're not so burdened.
Otherwise:

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: No problem, There you go.
Ali the Camel Man gives the player any missing receipts.

options.text: I decided to get rid of the camels.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Why? did they not please you?

options.text: No, they didn't. I sold them as Kebab meat!

steps.player: No, they didn't. I sold them as Kebab meat!

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Nooooo! Not Sandy and Lumps! You beast! Get out of my shop this instant!

options.text: I'm not really a camel person, so I gave them to a better owner.

steps.player: I'm not really a camel person, so I gave them to a better owner.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: That's very responsible of you. Too many people let their camels run feral through the desert, instead of sending them to happy homes.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: You want to watch out for those feral camels, you know.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: I decided to try and use them to end the hostilities between the two gangs.

steps.player: I decided to try and use them to end the hostilities between the two gangs.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: A noble purpose for two noble beasts! Did you succeed?

steps.player: Still working on that, I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Well, I wish you the best of luck.

steps.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
steps.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

now-we-have-camels-talking-to-a-menaphit.player: Good news, the bandits have agreed to give you a camel in order to restore peace.

now-we-have-camels-talking-to-a-menaphit.text: If the player does not have a receipt:

steps.speaker: Menaphite Thug
steps.text: So where's the camel?

steps.player: Um... I'll get back to you on that.

steps.text: You hand the doorman a sales receipt for the camel.

steps.speaker: Menaphite Thug
steps.text: A mere receipt? For a discount camel? I knew those bandits were cheap! Tell them that we have changed our minds and demand 10 camels in return for our

steps.speaker: Menaphite Thug
steps.text: mercy.

steps.player: Oh no... why do I bother?

now-we-have-camels-talking-to-a-bandit.player: Good news, the Menaphites have agreed to give you a camel in order to restore peace.

now-we-have-camels-talking-to-a-bandit.text: If the player does not have a receipt:

steps.speaker: Bandit
steps.text: So where's the camel?

steps.player: Um... I'll get back to you on that.

steps.text: You hand the guard a sales receipt for the camel.

steps.speaker: Bandit
steps.text: What's this? A mere promise of a camel? From a discount camel store? I knew those Menaphites were cowards. Tell them that we have changed our minds and demand 10 full-price camels in return for our

steps.speaker: Bandit
steps.text: mercy.

steps.player: Oh no... why do I bother?
The camel approach doesn't seem to be working. Perhaps I should be more direct and try to join one of the gangs.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.speaker: Ali the Mayor
joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-mayor.text: I really can't chat for very long, the recent escalation in crime has me run off my feet. There are muggings and burglaries happening in broad daylight! It's really not on.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-camel-.speaker: Ali the Camel Man
joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-camel-.text: Hello! Welcome back to my discount camel store. How are those camels getting along?

options.text: I decided to get rid of the camels.
I'm looking for Ali from Pollnivneach.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-bandit.text: Good day adventurer. Have you come with the Menaphite peace offering?

joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-bandit.player: Umm... no. Not yet. Actually I've come to ask about something else.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-bandit.speaker: Bandit
joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-bandit.text: We can talk once you bring back the Menaphites' full peace offering.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-menaphite-th.speaker: Menaphite Thug
joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-menaphite-th.text: Greetings Adventurer, Ali wants to have a word with you.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-menaphite-th.speaker: Menaphite Thug
joining-a-gang-talking-to-a-menaphite-th.text: Ali, our Chief of Operations. He should be somewhere nearby the tent.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-operat.speaker: Ali the Operator
joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-operat.text: You seem to be a man of action. We could do with more people like you to sort those despicable bandits out.

joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-operat.speaker: Ali the Operator
joining-a-gang-talking-to-ali-the-operat.text: So will you join us in our fight to wipe them out?

options.text: Yes, of course, those bandits should be taught a lesson.

steps.player: Yes, of course, those pesky bandits should be taught a lesson.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Good choice my friend, together we will crush them.

steps.player: So when do we start?

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Slow down, slow down. First you must prove yourself capable and trustworthy.

steps.player: How will I manage that?

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Don't worry about that, I'll just set you a few jobs to do.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: As you might have gathered we have a less-than- sparkling reputation around here.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: So I want you to foster this reputation and grow it.

steps.player: What exactly does that mean?

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: It means that I want you to go out into the town and pickpocket three villagers, then report back to me.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: If you have any problems don't be afraid to ask for some advice.

steps.player: Oh right, thanks.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: Yes I'd like to ask you about something else.

steps.player: Yes I'd like to ask you about something else.
Tell me about yourself.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: That information is available on a need to know basis and right now, you don't need to know.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: Tell me about the other people in the town.

steps.player: Tell me about the other people in the town.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Sheep, ready for the slau... hang on. I shouldn't be telling you that. Just forget I said anything.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: I'm looking for Ali.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Can you be a bit more specific? Everyone here is called Ali.

steps.player: So I noticed. Well, he has an uncle called Ali Morrisane, a market vendor in Al Kharid. That's all I really know about him.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Say no more. I know just the Ali you mean - that little snake robbed me too! If we work together perhaps we can catch him and teach him a lesson.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.player: No thanks.

options.text: Perhaps later, I'm quite busy at the moment.

steps.player: Perhaps later, I'm quite busy at the moment.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Tell me when you are ready. This deed should not be undertaken lightly.

steps.speaker: Ali the Operator
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

learning-to-steal-talking-to-ali-the-ope.player: I haven't started yet. I'm still psyching myself up to it.

learning-to-steal-talking-to-ali-the-ope.speaker: Ali the Operator
learning-to-steal-talking-to-ali-the-ope.text: Don't take all day, time is getting on and there are still plenty of foul deeds to be done.
