making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: Though I appreciate your efforts in our trials, I'm afraid I can't speak to you [Fremennik name].

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.player: Please, Seer! I'm on a mission for Brundt.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: Hmm... If the Chieftain can still trust you, so can I. How may I be of assistance?

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.player: It's a bit of a sensitive subject...

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: You can tell me anything, [Fremennik name]. What's the matter?

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.player: I can't bring myself to boil my pet rock!
I know, I'm a horrible person! Please help me, I can't bring myself to do it.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: Are you serious? I'm a busy man...

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.player: Please Seer, you're my only hope!

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: Very well. I'll clear your mind of any memories you have of your...

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: I won't be able to speak with you after this. The others might start to get suspicious.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.player: Thank you, Seer! I'll head back to the mountains now.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.speaker: Peer the Seer
making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.text: Now be gone with you, exile!

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-peer-th.player: I know it's just an act... but that hurt.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-large-g.text: You place the rock in the geyser.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-large-g.player: Well I don't think that will be bobbing up to the top anytime soon! I'll need to fish it out with something.
I'm not going to be able to get my rock back with just my bare hands! I'll need to get something to fish it out.
I've already dropped one rock in there. I should try fishing it out rather than throwing more away.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-large-g.text: If there is no pet rock inside the geyser:

steps.text: You wrap the rock around the fishing line and lower it into the geyser.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-large-g.text: If there is a pet rock inside the geyser:

steps.text: You cast your fishing line into the geyser.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-large-g.text: You reel the rock back up from the geyser...
If the player does not have the Ice gloves or Smiths gloves (i) equipped:

steps.player: Ow!

steps.text: You drop your rock into the geyser.
If the player does not have either the Ice gloves or Smiths gloves (i) in their inventory:

steps.player: Darn it! That rock was hot...
If only I had something that could keep my hands cold!

steps.text: If the player has the Ice gloves or Smiths gloves (i) in their inventory:

steps.player: Darn it! It would probably help if I actually wore my ice gloves.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-large-g.text: If the player has the Ice gloves or Smiths gloves (i) equipped:

steps.text: The geyser has heated your rock, giving you a Polishing Rock.
a Polishing rock

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-inspect.text: If the polishing rock is in the player's inventory:

steps.player: I already have a Polishing Rock. I think I'm done here.

making-v-s-shield-polishing-rock-inspect.text: If the polishing rock is in the player's bank:

steps.player: I already have a Polishing Rock in my bank. I think I'm done here.

making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-anvil.text: If the player has fewer than 3 lunar bars in their inventory:

steps.text: You require 3 Lunar bars to make a V sigil.

making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-anvil.text: If the player has at least 3 lunar bars in their inventory:

steps.prompt: Would you like to make a V Sigil?

steps.text: You hammer the three Lunar bars and make a V Sigil, exactly how Brundt described.
It will still need to be enchanted before it can be used for V's Shield.

making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-fossegrimen.speaker: Fossegrimen
making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-fossegrimen.text: What can I do for you?

making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-fossegrimen.player: I hear that I can present you with an offering and you will enchant my lyre for me.

making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-fossegrimen.speaker: Fossegrimen
making-v-s-shield-v-sigil-fossegrimen.text: This is true. For a simple enchantment, you may place an offering on my Altar. Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: Present offering of a single fish.
Ask about a permanent lyre enchantment.

steps.player: I'm currently trying to remake V's Shield. I was told I need his sigil enchanted by a powerful spirit.

steps.speaker: Fossegrimen
steps.text: V? Now that's a name I haven't heard in a long time...

steps.player: You know of V?

steps.speaker: Fossegrimen
steps.text: Oh yes. Were it not for V, this conversation might never had happened.

steps.speaker: Fossegrimen
steps.text: I owe V a debt that can never be repaid. It would be an honour to enchant his sigil.
If the player does not have the V sigil in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Fossegrimen
steps.text: Bring the unenchanted sigil to me and I'll provide you with what you need.
If the player has the V sigil in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Fossegrimen
steps.text: The Fossegrimen whispers an enchantment*

steps.speaker: Fossegrimen
steps.text: There you go! Go forth mighty warrior.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.player: I think I have everything needed to make V's Shield.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: Well what are you waiting for? Get it made and we'll have everything we need to put an end to your exile.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-usin.text: If the player does not have a glassblowing pipe:

steps.text: You need a Glassblowing Pipe to make V's Shield.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-usin.text: If the player has a glassblowing pipe:

steps.text: You meld the Lunar Glass to the Fremennik Shield. You then polish it with the Polishing Rock, which cools as you do so. Finally, you attach the V Sigil, finishing the shield.
V's shield

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-insp.player: This looks complete! I should head back to the Chieftain and see what he thinks.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.player: Oh, sorry. I simply left it in my bank. I'm such a ditzy person sometimes!

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: That's certainly one way to put it... Perhaps you should go and get it?
You hand V's Shield to Brundt the Chieftain.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: [Fremennik name]... This is incredible! It's as if you forged the shield from a picture. It's exactly how I imagined it from the stories!

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.player: Do you think this will be enough to convince the council?

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: I hope so [Fremennik name]. I do suspect some of them may never respect you though.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.player: Beggars can't be choosers, I suppose. Let's get going then...

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: The shield. It requires one last thing.

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: Return to me with two beers. No... Two kegs of beer! Quickly! There's not much time!

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: Have you got the two kegs of beer?

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: I'm litchrally abousht to go shtand uhp to the enshtire *hiccup* counshil for yooo...! I need thish!

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.player: That's a very good point. Carry on then.
I should probably head back to the longhall...

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: Return to me with two beers. No... Two kegs of beer! Quickly! There's not much time!

making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
making-v-s-shield-making-the-shield-brun.text: You're a bigger alcoholic than I am! Hand them over.
The chieftain takes both kegs and quickly drinks one.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.player: And you Brundt. You sobered up quickly.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: We Fremennik know how to handle a drink, [Fremennik name]. Anyway, I have some good news for you.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: Following your successful recreation of V's Shield, the council have agreed to end your exile. I hearby declare you a Fremennik again!

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: Not only that, but we would like you to be the one to carry V's legendary shield into battle.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: So you should be [Fremennik name]. V was our greatest hero. There is no greater honour than to bear his shield in battle.
Brundt the Chieftain gives you V's Shield.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: The basilisks intend to attack the town so they can keep us distracted while they free the Jormungand. Luckily for us, we know about this.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: Once the attack begins, the majority of our forces will stay here to hold the town. While they do, you and I will journey to the Island of Stone.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: There, we will ensure that the prison of the Jormungand remains sealed.

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Fremennik Warrior
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: Basilisks in the market! Basilisks in the market!

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: They've walked right through our defences!

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt.text: They've walked right through our defences!

basilisks-in-the-market-during-the-fight.text: Fremennik Warriors, Koschei the Deathless, Thorvald the Warrior and Brundt the Chieftain will say one of the phrases while in combat throughout the Market Fight.

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: This is Rellekka!

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: Kill the invaders!

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: You die here beast!

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: Die you foul beasts!

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: Death to the basilisks!

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: Kill them! Kill them all!

steps.speaker: NPC
steps.text: You will not take our home!

options.text: Ask about a Seal of Passage.

steps.speaker: Fremennik Warrior
steps.text: Basilisks in the market! Basilisks in the market!

basilisks-in-the-market-brundt-again-aft.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
basilisks-in-the-market-brundt-again-aft.text: [Fremennik name]! Get to the boat. It's time for us to go!

island-of-stone-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt.text: This isn't good [Fremennik name]. The prison has already been breached.

island-of-stone-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt.text: Not quite, but we'll have to act fast. If the Jormungand manages to leave the prison, the End of Things will be upon us.

island-of-stone-brundt.player: Well we'd better get in there and make sure that doesn't happen.

island-of-stone-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt.text: It looks like the basilisks resealed the door behind them. We'll have to get through it.

island-of-stone-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt.text: From what I can tell, the door uses a combination lock. You'll need to get the right combination to unlock it. Too many wrong attempts will reset the lock though.

island-of-stone-brundt.player: I'd better be careful then. I'll get to work.

island-of-stone-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt.text: Hurry [Fremennik name]. We can't afford to waste any time.

island-of-stone-brundt-brundt-again.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-brundt-again.text: Have you opened the door yet?

island-of-stone-brundt-brundt-again.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-brundt-again.text: Hurry [Fremennik name]. We need to get inside before it's too late.

island-of-stone-brundt-unlocking-the-doo.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-unlocking-the-doo.text: Good work [Fremennik name]. Let's get inside and see what's going on.

island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-unloc.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-unloc.text: Let's get inside and see what's going on.

island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-unloc.speaker: Bakuna
island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-unloc.text: Destroy them! Our king must be freed!

island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-unloc.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-unloc.text: With me [Fremennik name]! Let's kill these foul beasts!

island-of-stone-the-jormungand.speaker: The Jormungand
island-of-stone-the-jormungand.text: At long last, I have been granted freedom. You have done well Bakuna.

island-of-stone-the-jormungand.speaker: The Jormungand
island-of-stone-the-jormungand.text: Good, for I have one final use of you. My long rest has weakened me, you will grant me strength.
The Jormungand kills Bakuna in one hit

island-of-stone-the-jormungand.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-the-jormungand.text: This isn't over yet [Fremennik name], the Jormungand is weak from his imprisonment! We can still stop him!

island-of-stone-the-jormungand.speaker: The Jormungand
island-of-stone-the-jormungand.text: Humans, you have been bestowed with a great honour, for you are about to become the first of your kind in millennia to feed my power!

island-of-stone-the-jormungand.speaker: The Jormungand
island-of-stone-the-jormungand.text: Rejoice with me, for your miserable lives are finally at an end!

island-of-stone-the-jormungand.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-the-jormungand.text: You will not defeat us this day! Come [Fremennik name]!

island-of-stone-the-jormungand-in-combat.text: If The Jormungand uses his glare attack:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Turn away [Fremennik name]!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Don't look into his eyes!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Don't look at him [Fremennik name]!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: [Fremennik name]! Do not face him!

island-of-stone-the-jormungand-in-combat.text: If The Jormungand uses his binding attack:

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: The stone is weak! You can break it!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Try to break free [Fremennik name]!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: [Fremennik name]! You need to break loose!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: You can free yourself [Fremennik name]!

island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-leavi.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-again-after-leavi.text: Hurry [Fremennik name]! We need to get inside and stop those basilisks!

island-of-stone-attempting-to-enter-the-.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-attempting-to-enter-the-.text: Wait [Fremennik name]! I have some things for you!

steps.player: Do you have any of my items?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: I do have some of your items here [Fremennik name]. Do try to be careful with them.

steps.target: Brundt the Cheiftain's Item Retrieval Service

island-of-stone-brundt-s-right-click-col.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-brundt-s-right-click-col.text: I'm afraid I don't have anything for you [Fremennik name]. If I did have any of your items, but you died before collecting them, they'll now be lost.

island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.text: Ah, nothing like a glorious fight to make you feel alive!

island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.text: Now? We drink of course! The Jormungand has been defeated and the End of Things prevented!

island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.player: Are you sure? They did manage to free him. How do you know we weren't too late?

island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
island-of-stone-after-killing-the-jormun.text: You worry too much [Fremennik name]. If the end had begun, we'd have noticed by now. Come! Let us go and celebrate!

longhall-celebration.text: A cutscene starts with Olaf the Bard singing the Ballad of the Basilisk in the Rellekka longhall
After the first verse, the camera tilts down to reveal the adventurer standing amidst celebrating Fremenniks, leaving the bard to sing three more verses off-screen

longhall-celebration.speaker: Manni the Reveller
longhall-celebration.text: Another great victory for our people!

longhall-celebration.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
longhall-celebration.text: But it wouldn't have been possible without [Fremennik name]!

longhall-celebration.speaker: Agnar
longhall-celebration.text: You have truly proven yourself to be one of us, [Fremennik name]! I'm sorry we ever doubted you.

longhall-celebration.player: I'm just glad it all worked out in the end.

longhall-celebration.speaker: Manni the Reveller
longhall-celebration.text: And on that note, time for a drink! I want to see if [Fremennik name] can still drink me under the table!

the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.text: Where the king of the serpents,

the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.text: The storm it was a ragin',

the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.text: The bell rang with a tolling,

the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.text: From the fate of his quest,

the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-off-screen-segment-of-the-bard-s-bal.text: Winds tore through the main sail,

hsuZZR.player: It might have helped if I'd actually remembered to bring my pet rock.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Hello, are you [Fremennik name]?

steps.player: I am, but who are you?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: I am Maria Gunnars, Mord's wife.

steps.speaker: Maira Gunnars
steps.text: You should speak with my husband. He has been looking for you.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Hello, are you [Fremennik name]? by any chance?

steps.player: Well my name is [player name], but I am known as [Fremennik name] by the Fremennik. May I ask who you are?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Of course, I am Mord Gunnars, a humble ferryman.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: I come from an island north of here called Jatizso, while my wife Maria is from Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Maria
steps.text: Hello.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The King of Jatizso has requested that I take you to him, as he has an important task for you.

steps.prompt: Start The Fremennik Isles quest?

steps.text: (Show options below)

steps.player: Hello Mord.

options.text: Tell me more about Jatizso's history.

steps.player: Tell me more about Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Well now, the history of the isles is a bloody tale. When told in its intended form it takes 9 days and 9 nights. However, I will give you the abridged version.

steps.player: Phew!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Four generations ago there was a mighty king who ruled wisely and was loved by all.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: He had many sons, most of whom proved themselves in the usual Fremennik ways of fighting, sailing, drinking and so on.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: His youngest two sons, however, were a problem. Ever since they were old enough to hit one another they had bickered and fought.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Their names were Jatizso and Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Hey! Who's telling this story?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Ahem. At the time it was customary for the Kings' sons to claim a prize from his treasury when they came of age.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Each brother rallied support and strode out to confront the other on the field of battle to claim the same prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The brothers met on the field, limbs were bruised, bones were crushed and heads clashed.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: They probably didn't notice the head-clashing bit. Too thick skulled!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Can I finish the story without interruptions?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Carry on dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, long into the night they fought, until they stood alone, facing each other.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: On the second day the old king, whose patience was exhausted, strode out onto the field and demanded to know who had claimed his prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso looked at his father and told him yes, it was his, to which the other called out 'No! It's not'.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so, the argument continued through to the third day, with the sounds of 'Jah! 'tis so!', 'Ne! It's not!' echoing over the field, becoming more hoarse as the darkness enveloped the brothers.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Bah! What they needed was a good clip round the ear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At the end of the third day, when the brothers lay unable to move, let alone stand, the King stood between them in shame.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: As punishment for their squabbling he banished his sons from his realm, ordering that neither should return until they had conquered lands of their own.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso set sail with a band of loyal followers, sailing into the east, while Neitiznot went west.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso ventured far into uncharted oceans, his crew dwindling as the trials of sailing and sea monsters took them.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso's ship limped through the frozen wastes, in need of repairs, fighting off pirates who thought them easy pickings.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At last a promising land was sighted, a land rich in minerals, deep fjords and sweeping mountains.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso claimed the land and named it after himself.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: A mighty citadel was constructed to protect his land; then Jatizso set forth to explore his new kingdom.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Crossing a few fjords, Jatizso spied an island which remained green and fertile, even at such latitude.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: With a mighty cheer Jatizso and his men marched on the island. Upon reaching the island, however, they discovered a wooden stockade.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Determined to be master of all the land, Jatizso stood in front of the gates. He looked up and demanded that those within the stockade surrendered.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso was horrified when his brother appeared on the battlements and cried 'This is my land! Go find yer own'. To which his brother replied 'No it's not!', throwing some rocks for good measure.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so the blood feud continued.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The fighting between the towns has continued for generations with little sign of improvement.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Quite recently a massive troll army seized one of the islands to the north, while our townships' militias were busy fighting one another.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: They marched down and razed Neitiznot to the ground while Neitiznot's troops laid siege to Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: The smoke damage was atrocious, I had to replace my entire wardrobe.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Yes, dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, a hasty sort of peace has been agreed until the trolls are dealt with.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: But you can still see the bitter rivalry as guards hurl insults between the towns.

options.text: Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.

steps.player: Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Ha! Our benevolent King Gjuki Sorvott IV.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: He is short-tempered, arrogant and cares little about anything except outdoing Neitiznot's Burgher.

steps.speaker: Maria
steps.text: He's not at all like Burgher Burowgar.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: I'm surprised King Sorvott wishes to talk to you. Don't expect much in the way of gratitude.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Jatizso?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Jatizso?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Of course.
Leaving Rellekka for Jatizso.

options.text: I'm too busy to help your King.

steps.player: I'm too busy to help your King.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: I guess I won't be getting paid for finding you, then.

steps.player: I may be back later.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Bye

starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.speaker: Mord Gunnars
starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.text: Hi, [Fremennik name], you should speak with King Sorvott in the main chambers.

starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.speaker: Mord Gunnars
starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.text: The chambers have the town's banner erected outside.

starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.player: Thank you for bringing me here Mord.

starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.speaker: Mord Gunnars
starting-off-learning-about-jatizso-talk.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.player: Tell me more about Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso is a small Fremennik town, which is far less closed to the world than other Fremennik tribes.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: We maintain trade links with many powers in the world and have moved beyond some traditions to take advantage of modern advances.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: We do, however, continue to 'enlighten' our neighbours in Neitiznot. Unfortunately, some of the Islands are infested with trolls.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: We should really be trying to deal with the trolls, but the King tends to get a bit preoccupied with his cousin, the Burgher of Neitiznot.

options.text: I'm too busy to help your King.

steps.player: I'm too busy to help your King.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: I guess I won't be getting paid for finding you, then.

steps.player: I may be back later.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Bye!

options.text: Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.

steps.player: Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Ha! Our benevolent King Gjuki Sorvott IV. He doesn't have much of an opinion about anyone, apart from his cousin Mawnis who rules the other Island. He hates him with a passion that can occasionally be quite scary.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: You might be able to talk to him if you help out around Jatizso. Don't expect much in the way of gratitude though.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Sure.
Leaving Jatizso for Rellekka.

steps.player: No, I'm fine right now.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Oh, hello stranger. If you're new to town you should speak with our ruler, King Gjuki Sorvott IV. He'll want to meet you - he always wants to have a chat with any strangers in town. They could be spies you know.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Yes, spies from Neitiznot. They're everywhere. Apparently. That's what the King says anyway.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: So what do you do here?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Me? I'm a cook. Fish dishes a speciality. I hate fish. But fish is about all we have. Except for yak. But we're not allowed to eat yak.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Why not, is yak meat bad for you?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Certainly not! Yak meat is both sweet and delicately flavoured. Yak is juicier than buffalo and elk - but never gamey. It goes wonderfully well with a glass of red wine, and it's healthy too!

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: So why aren't you allowed to eat it?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: King's orders. They breed and eat yaks on Neitiznot, so WE'RE not allowed to. It's unjust I tell you! I had a dream last night about a juicy fillet of yak, served on a bed of deep-fried seaweed and topped with a garnish

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: That's a little sad. So do you have any cooked food I could buy?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: No. It would only be fish anyway. Why would you want to eat fish?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Well, I wouldn't mind a few shark and swordfish steaks as back-up you know.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: If you insist. Sorry the stock is so low, but I just can't be bothered to cook any more.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Hello. What's happening in town at the moment?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: These dwarves have arrived from Keldagrim - the Chancellor has asked me to look after them, but they are eating all of our food and drinking all of our booze.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: What are the dwarves doing here?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: They are organising some sort of trade agreement. I don't know what they are trading.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Brendt
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Hmm, interesting place this. It feels a little like Kelda, except without the good bits.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Bored, bored, bored. These Fremenniks are taking ages.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Hey, they're doing their best. You arrived early.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Hey, we arrived precisely when we told your representatives. Lack of planning on your part does not constitute an emergency on my part.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Please, someone get these guys their ore quickly. They are eating all the good food on the island, and complaining about it!

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: I'd better get a move on!

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Please introduce yourself to our ruler, His Royal Greatness King Gjuki Sorvott IV.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Guard, who is this outlander?

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Meeow? (An outlander, how unusual. Welcome.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Guard
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: This is [Fremennik name], your majesty.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Is this true? You are the outlander who has been given a Fremennik name?

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Miouw...meow. (You have a human Fremennik name, how unusual.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Excellent.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.player: How may I assist your Highness?

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Meouw! (Well, outlander, one requires a fish immediately.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Behave Hrafn!

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Meeeiouw! Mewwww! (Behave yourself human! One shall behave as one likes.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: I have a task that requires your unique-

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: MEEEEOOOUW!!!! (Will you stop interrupting one? For the last time one requires tuna immediately.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Not now, Hrafn.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Now where was I?

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.player: You mentioned a task requiring my unique-

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Ah, yes.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Your unique position among Fremennik-

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: MEEEIOOOOUW! MIOOOOOEW! YOOWLLL! (For goodness' sake! One might acquire the mistaken impression that the human rules this place. I command you to feed me.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Hrafn! Oh, alright, alright, I give in.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Purrr. (And about time too, insolent human-pet.)

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Look, could you fetch my cat some fish?

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Then we can finish our conversation in peace.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.player: Yes, that's probably a good idea.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Thank you.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Hrafn will only eat raw tuna.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: Yes, fussy though Hrafn is, he doesn't care where the tuna comes from.

starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-talking-to-king-sorvott-iv.text: If you don't already have any, you can catch some down by the docks, or you can buy some from my fishmonger, Flosi Dalksson.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.speaker: Guard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.text: Halt, in the name of King Gjuki Sorvott IV.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.text: Hello, [Fremennik name]. That cat really is a pain isn't he? Always interrupting the King.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.player: Oh, I've met worse. Still, I'd better get him his fish, otherwise he'll never keep quiet.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-th.text: Oh, go and talk to Flosi Dalksson in his shop. He'll have some tuna if you don't have any. You could also fish it from one of the spots round here, if you prefer.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.player: Here you go, enjoy your fish.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.text: What is the meaning of this serf? One specifically asked for RAW tuna, not fish defiled by human fire!

starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.player: Here you go. Enjoy your fish.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.text: What is the meaning of this serf? How is one supposed to eat a piece of paper?

starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.player: Here you go. enjoy your fish!

starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-tuna-delivery-giving-tuna-t.text: Purrrrrrrrrr (One is satisfied with the freshness of the tuna. The humans have acted satisfactorily in this matter.)

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Do you have a piece of raw tuna for Hrafn?
If the player doesn't have the raw tuna:

steps.player: Not yet, your Highness.

steps.speaker: Hrafn
steps.text: Miouw! (Then get a move on human!!)

steps.speaker: King Sorvott IV
steps.text: Well, what are you waiting for?

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.player: Yes, I have your pet's fish.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Meow. (Hmmm, one will lower oneself to eat the fish, despite the human's insult.)

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Hrafn
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Purrr. (One is satisfied with the freshness of the tuna. The humans have acted satisfactorily in this matter.)

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Ah, yes, so the Burgher of Neitiznot Island is an enemy of free-thinking Jatizso citizens. My informants tell me an increased number of trade ships have been seen docking at their ports. They must be preparing for something. Chancellor, fill in the details.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Sire, Sire! The Kelda merchants have arrived, they are three days early. We're not ready!

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: What? We cannot afford to offend the Red Axe traders. Where are they now?

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: They are in the hall, eating and drinking us out of food and beer. It's costing us a fortune.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Another good reason to get them their ore and get them out of town. Get all our miners on the job now!

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: I already have. They'll never get enough ore in time, the bunch of lazy no-good layabouts.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: Bah! Those miners haven't learned their lesson.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: It may be time for some extra incentives.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.player: Wait a minute! I'm fairly handy with a pick axe. Maybe I can help; what do you need?

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: We need [six/seven/eight] pieces of [tin/coal/mithril] for Keldagrim's merchants.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: The entrance to our mines are to the north-east of the western gatehouse, outside the walls.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.player: If I just happen to have the ore you need in the bank, do I need to go down to your mines?

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.text: If you bring us the ore, we won't ask where it came from. Don't worry we're discreet.

starting-off-tuna-delivery-talking-to-ki.player: Hmmm, interesting. I'll get the ore then.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-flo.player: Can you tell me where to find the nearest mines?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-flo.speaker: Flosi Dalksson
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-flo.text: Err, there are some mines just outside the western gatehouse. I don't know what the rocks contain there though, you'll have to have a look.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-flo.speaker: Flosi Dalksson
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-flo.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

options.text: Can I have a look at your stock please?

steps.player: Can I have a look at your stock please?
No, nothing just now thanks.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.text: If the player doesn't have the ore:

steps.player: Can you remind me of what those Dwarven traders need?

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: Of course. Please bring [six/seven/eight] pieces of [tin/coal/mithril] ore.

steps.player: And the mines are...

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: The entrance to the mines is outside the western gatehouse, on the north side of the town.

steps.player: Thanks.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.text: If the player has the ore noted:

steps.player: I have bank notes to the value of the ore here.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.text: If the player has the ore unnoted:

steps.player: I have the ore here.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.text: Excellent. This [man/woman] has gathered the [six/seven/eight] pieces of [tin/coal/mithril] ore needed by Keldagrim's merchants, sire.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-tho.text: Good, good. Please reward this [man/woman] for [his/her] efforts.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Hello again, [Fremennik name].

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Do you have all the ore my Chancellor requested?
If the player doesn't have the ore:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: King Sorvott IV
steps.text: Please hurry back with [six/seven/eight] [tin/coal/mithril], Keldagrim's traders are drinking my cellars dry.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: I have the ore here, sir.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: This [man/woman] has gathered the remaining ore needed by Keldagrim's merchants.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Excellent news, your majesty.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Please reward this [man/woman] for [his/her] efforts.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Of course, your majesty.
Thorkel Silkbeard takes [six/seven/eight] lumps of [tin/coal/mithril].
Thorkel Silkbeard hands you [amount] coins.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Thank you [Fremennik name]. If only our miners were as efficient as you.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Right. Now let us get down to business, young [Fremennik name]. Let us hope we have no more interruptions.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Neitiznot's Burgher, Mawnis Burowgar, is a simpleton and a fool.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: I have bested him before and will do so again!

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: He is surely plotting a new plan to defeat me.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: He's up to something, he's always up to something.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: I will not be kept in the dark about his plans any longer. I must know what underhand tricks he'll use to undermine me. He's out to get me! Get me I say!

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: Ahem, I see, sir. How may I help in this matter?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Well, I have heard that some call you 'bard' in Rellekka. Your lyre-playing reputation has carried this far.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: You want me to play the lyre? Well actually, I've been working on a few tunes in my spare time. I have this new song about-

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Silence! I do not wish to hear your wailing. All bards are charlatans and fools.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: However, a fool is exactly what I need right now.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: It's a great tune, very catching, you'll love-

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Bah! Bards are all the same, they never shut up! If I need to be entertained I'll hire a mime; maybe I'll get some rest then. Now if you'll listen, I'll explain what I need you to do.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: In the past I have sent my Spymaster to 'entertain' the Burgher, and to see what he can find out.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: You see, the Burgher of Neitiznot and his aides like a drink when they are being entertained, and their tongues are loose when they drink.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: However, yesterday my spy had an accident and could no longer help me in this task. However he is still stationed on Neitiznot.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: So this is a covert operation into Neitiznot? You need me to infiltrate the Burgher's hall, undercover, and uncover his evil plans?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Exactly, [Fremennik name]. So are you interested?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: Sounds like a task for an elite adventurer like myself. Mission accepted.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Excellent, [Fremennik name], you and I will get on very well.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: So what is the easiest way to get to Neitiznot?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: I suggest you catch Mord's ferry back to Rellekka and then catch a ferry from there.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: Are you sure that's the best way?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: You may find a way across the islands, but the bridges are almost certainly broken, and there are trolls which are a bit of a nuisance. The ferry is probably both quicker and safer.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Oh, there is one more thing. In order to gain an audience with the Burgher, you will need my Spymaster's, err, costume.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: The costume is in my chest. Don't forget to pick up all the pieces.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Then travel to Neitiznot and talk to my Spymaster. He is still over there. He will fill you in with the details, and you may report to him.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Oh, the Spymaster is a secretive kind of guy. He will require a password. The password is 'free stuff please'.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: What sort of password is that?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Don't ask me, it was his idea.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: His name is Slug Hemligssen, but don't expect him to answer to it.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: So how will I recognise him?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Don't worry, you'll find him.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.speaker: Brendt
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.text: Well it seemed rude not to finish the food they gave us.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.text: Feel free to leave it. Please leave.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.text: I'll just finish the roast off.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.text: Ah, yes. Now that's what I call a meal.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.text: That's funny, I called it fourteen meals yesterday.

jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.text: Have you finished the covert operation I asked you to complete?

jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.text: Well, what are you waiting for? Hop to it!

jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.text: Have you completed your undercover mission to Neitiznot yet?

jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.text: Then make sure you have your costume and go. There is no time to play around!

jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.speaker: Maria Gunnars
jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.text: I am Maria Gunnars. What can I do for you?

steps.player: Tell me about Neitiznot's geography.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Sure.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Well, as I have mentioned, I am from an island called Jatizso, while my wife is from another island called Neitiznot. Neitiznot is a far less sophisticated and successful island which will not see reason with Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Ne it iz not!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Ja it iz so!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Ahem, anyway, the islands are in a small volcanic archipelago north of here.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Along with the main isles there are numerous small islands and a frozen northern island that was recently overrun by trolls.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Jatizso is rich in minerals, and trades extensively, while Neitiznot has stolen all the decent arable land.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Only because Jatizso hogs all the wealth.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Well, that wealth is needed to buy the food from Neitiznot at extortionate rates!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Only because Jatizso hogs all the wealth!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Ok Maria, stop that!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Ok dear!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Where was I? Yup, that covers the layout of the islands.

options.text: Tell me about the islands' history.

steps.text: (Same as Mord Gunnars' "Tell me more about Jatizso's history" option)

options.text: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.player: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Well Burgher Mawnis Burowgar is a gentle soul at heart. His kinsfolk are happy and content with their lot.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: 'Soft' is the word we use in Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Well a soft Burgher is better than a stupid King.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, there was a time when Burgher Burowgar was similar to King Sorvott.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Argumentative, short tempered; I am sure you know what I mean.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: The change happened when the trolls came and razed Neitiznot to the ground.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: You mean while Neitiznot's militias were assaulting Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Yes, well our tribes have been at war for nearly four generations now.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, the Burgher lost his wife and youngest son in the trolls' raid and has been a changed man since.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: May their journey to our ancestors' halls be swift.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Personally, I am much happier with the considerate Burgher we have now.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Let's set sail then.
Leaving Rellekka for Neitiznot.

jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.speaker: Maria Gunnars
jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.text: Hi, [Fremennik name], you should speak with Burgher Mawnis Burowgar in the main chambers. Do you have any questions?

jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.prompt: What do you want to know about?

steps.player: Tell me about your husband.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: My husband is a typical Fremennik, being both headstrong and brave.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: We fell in love when we were young, but as there was a war between our isles, we were ordered to stop seeing each other by our parents.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: This didn't stop Mord climbing the wailing tower, on his side of the channel between our isles, to sing to me every night.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: After Mord's voice broke, his singing voice was lost, but I still listened to his terrible sonnets each and every night.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Until one night there was no singing! Then, far below me, I heard a gentle voice calling my name.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Mord had stolen his father's boat to come and fetch me from my prison

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: and from that day forth we have lived in Rellekka.

steps.player: Tell me about Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: My husband does not speak of the inhabitants of the isle of Jatizso much.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: He has little positive to say about his parents, so he chooses not to speak of them in my presence. The only thing I've noticed is that everyone on that island seems very sad...

steps.prompt: Who do you want to know about?

options.text: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.player: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: King Sorvott IV follows in the footsteps of a line of kings who have reigned since Jatizso himself passed away. It is rumoured that the King has no heir and is seeking a bride to bear him children. Given his

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: personality I'm not surprised he hasn't found a bride yet!

steps.player: Tell me about Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: To be honest with you, I do not keep up to date with all the goings on here now that I have a home in Rellekka.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: However, Neitiznot seems a happy place! The Burgher seems a wiser rule than King Sorvott, although I believe he is worried about the trolls at the moment. They seem to be a big threat.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Sure.
Leaving Neitiznot for Rellekka.

options.text: I have nothing to ask you right now.

steps.player: I have nothing to ask you right now.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Fare thee well.

jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.speaker: Kjedelig Uppsen/Trogen Konungarde

jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.text: Guards! Please escort this outlander to the docks. She is not welcome in my court.

jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.player: I am known as [Fremennik name] by those in Rellekka.

jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.text: Do you have me confused with the King of Jatizso? Guards!

jestering-around-first-meetings-in-neiti.player: I shall return to Rellekka. You have no need to call your guards.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson

steps.player: Thanks, Thakkrad.

options.text: The blue fish leap northwards at dawn.

steps.player: The blue fish leap northwards at dawn..

steps.text: Oranges are not the only fruit.

steps.player: The cabbages bloom in the spring.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen

steps.player: I bought an aardvark from Ardougne market.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen

steps.player: ...err...sprockets wangle burps in the forked flan.

steps.text: Ah, Operative Budgie. Welcome to the island.

steps.player: Budgie? That's not my name, you can call me-

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Shh!

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: No names! Names are unnecessary. Loose lives cost tongues.

steps.player: Shouldn't that be...never mind. So Mr Hemli-

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Shhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!

steps.player: Sorry, no names. I forgot.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Call me Operative Nighthawk.

steps.player: How come you get the cool name, and I get called Budgie? Can't I be called Operative Panther? Yeah I like that, panthers are cool. Rarrrr!

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: This is not a democracy, Operative! Panther already exists and he's working on a mission in Al Kharid. It's my way or the highway.

steps.player: Fine, whatever, I don't care anyway.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: To business. Here are the details of your operation. You will infiltrate Burgher Burowgar's hall, deep undercover as a travelling entertainer. Burgher Burowgar and his men are known to relax in the

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: presence of a jester - and a few barrels of beer. To get the information required from the court of Burgher Burowgar you must entertain him.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: While you are obeying the Burgher's instructions you should listen in on the conversations of his council and make note of what they discuss.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: When you return I shall ask you a few questions about what you have learned.

steps.player: Very well.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: You must wear all four pieces of the jester costume without anything in your hands, as the Burgher's guards will search you thoroughly.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Are you ready to begin?

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: Is your helmet chafing?

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: When do we assault the caves?

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: I can be ready in two days.

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: Good, my recruits are nearly ready

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: How many militia have you trained?

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: Seventeen, so far

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: More shields will be completed by noon.

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: And the armour?

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: I will finish their armour tomorrow

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: And the two bridges we need repaired?

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: I will fix them as soon as I can.

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: Useless fool! Return when you routine is more polished!

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: Well, thank you, that was much better than the last jester.

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.speaker: Kjedelig Uppsen/Trogen Konungarde
your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.text: Ha, more fool you! Ha Ha Ha!

your-mission-should-you-choose-to-accept.player: Your wit has no end. Or beginning or middle. I'd better talk to the Burgher and see if he wants to be entertained.

burgher-buddy-reporting-to-slug.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
burgher-buddy-reporting-to-slug.text: Have you obtained the information we require?

steps.player: Yes I have.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Now I will ask you some questions, but be warned I have other sources of information that will corroborate your answers.

steps.player: I am ready to answer your questions, Operative Nighthawk.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: How soon does Thakkrad think Neitiznot's troops can be ready?

options.text: They will be ready in two days.

steps.player: They will be ready in two days.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: How many militia have been trained?

steps.player: Seventeen militia have been trained.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: How many bridges does Thakkrad need repairing?

options.text: There are two bridges to repair.

steps.player: There are two bridges to repair.

steps.text: If all the correct options were picked:

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Hmmm. I believe you're telling me the truth.

steps.player: I would not lie to you.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Well done! I shall inform the King of your good work. I have been authorised to give you this...
Slug Hemligssen hands you 2500 coins.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Thanks to you, we know a little more about Neitiznot's plans.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: While you were deep undercover, I received instructions from 'Big Daddy'.

steps.player: 'Big Daddy'? Do you mean the K-

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Shhhh! Yes, I mean the head operative back at home-base. He has given me permission to follow up any leads based on your intelligence.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: It would be useful to know exactly when the Neitiznot engineers intend to repair the bridges. I'd do it myself but my injury stops me.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Curse this arm and my reckless bravery in the pursuit of intelligence!

steps.player: I heard you had an accident whilst juggling?

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: ahem* Misinformation my [boy/girl]. Misinformation and misdirection.

steps.player: Is that so?

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Anyway, enough chit-chat.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: You should gain the trust of the Burgher.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: You must not mention our arrangement.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Indeed, if you are offered tasks by Neitiznot's folk or Burgher, you should go along with them to avoid arousing suspicion.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Once you know that the bridges have been repaired then return to me.
If any of the incorrect options were picked:

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Do not think you can lie to me. Come back when you are more inclined to give me the information I require.

options.text: There are three bridges to repair.
There are four bridges to repair.
I need to make a fool of myself again.

steps.player: I need to make a fool of myself again.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: You'd better go back to the Burgher and get entertaining.

steps.player: I shall, Mr Nighthawk.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.player: What am I supposed to be doing again?

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Operative 'Big Daddy' requests that you gain the trust of Mawnis Burowgar, and determine whether they intend to repair the bridges that link their island to home-base. Mission understood?

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Oh, and stay away from me unless you need to contact me. It will begin to look suspicious.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.player: Right. Yes. You blend right in otherwise.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: With the full jester outfit equipped:

steps.speaker: Kjedelig Uppsen/Trogen Konungarde
steps.text: The Burgher does not require entertainment at the moment, jester.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Without the full jester outfit equipped:

steps.speaker: Kjedelig Uppsen/Trogen Konungarde
steps.text: Ho, outlander! Please introduce yourself to the Burgher.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: With the full jester outfit equipped:

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Please jester, we don't have time for entertainment right now.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Without the full jester outfit equipped:

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson/Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Ah! Are you the outlander called [Fremmenik name]?

steps.player: Yes I am. What can I do for you?

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson/Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: The Burgher would like to talk to you urgently. Please talk to him right away.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Maria Gunnars
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Welcome back [Fremennik name], how was your time on Jatizso?

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Maria Gunnars
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: I have been asked to ferry you to Neitiznot, as Burgher Mawnis Burowgar would like to make you an offer.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.prompt: What do you want to know about?

options.text: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Maria Gunnars
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Welcome to Neitiznot, [Fremennik name]; Mawnis Burowgar lives in the largest hut in the township.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Maria Gunnars
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: He is expecting you, so you should not keep him waiting for too long.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.player: Thank you for ferrying me here Maria. See you soon.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Maria Gunnars
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: If you have any questions I would be happy to answer them.

burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.speaker: Skuli Myrka/Raum Urda-Stein/Hring Hring
burgher-buddy-after-relaying-the-informa.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: With the full jester outfit equipped:

steps.text: After giving Slug the info but before being tasked with gaining the trust of Mawnis:

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Go away! I'm busy right now with important matters of state.
After giving Slug the info and tasked with gaining the trust of Mawnis:

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ah, jester. I am not currently in need of jest.
The Burgher gives you a hard stare.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Right now I need a Champion, not a jester.

steps.player: Ah yes.
The Burgher is both wise and perceptive.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ha! Fortunately for you he also has a sense of humour.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Hmmmm. Guard! Who is this outlander who has been brought before me?

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Fridleif
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Sire, this is the one who has been honoured with a Fremennik name. A rare honour indeed, for an outlander.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: You jest! [He/She] doesn't look that impressive to me.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.player: Ahem. I am indeed known as [Fremennik name] by those in Rellekka.
If I am the one you seek, then how may I assist you?

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Well, I have sought an audience with you for several days now.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: I have need for a courageous and valiant individual.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: One who will not flee at the sight of jest a few trolls.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.player: Ha! It is trolls that fear me! I am Fremennik!

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Ha! Well said! However, this is no jesting matter. Although a Fremennik name goes a great way towards gaining my trust, I must ask that you prove your loyalty to me and my kinsfolk.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Fridleif
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Sire, surely that isn't necessary! Anyone who has done the Fremennik Trials can be trusted.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Trust me Fridleif, I think in this case it is necessary. Anyway, there are many tasks that need to be done. Some of them are menial, and [Fremennik name] needs to show me that [he/she] can handle these as well as the ones that

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: simply require bravery. We on Neitiznot are warriors, but we are not just warriors.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Fridleif
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: I apologise for speaking out of turn. The Burgher is wise as always.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.player: I would be honoured to assist you and your tribe, Burgher Burowgar. Indeed I expected no less. This sort of thing seems to happen to me a lot.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Good.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Thakkrad, which tasks remain?

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: There are a few building projects that could do with a strong extra hand.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: Well then, [Fremennik name], are you willing to assist my engineer?

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: The bridges to the troll islands need repairing if we are to send a party over. First of all, we will need eight lengths of rope; maybe [Fremennik name] could assist me with this.
If the player doesn't have 8 ropes in the inventory or bank:

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: It's quite simple really. Gather some yak hair and take it to the spinning wheel in the south-east of the village.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: There you will be able to spin the yak hair you have gathered into strong lengths of rope.

steps.player: Is any rope fine for this?

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Of course not. Neitiznot rope is the best. Real men use yak rope. You need to make the rope yourself.

steps.player: Hmmm, the rope I've seen round here looks exactly the same as the rope I'm used to. It's exactly the same isn't it?

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well yes, of course it is. We supply rope to all of the rope traders in Gielinor. Its an excellent business.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Anyway, once you have obtained the rope we shall speak more about the quest I have for you. So get a move on!

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: If the player has at least 8 ropes in their bank:

steps.player: Right! I'll just go to the bank and get some rope.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Bank? Why do you need to go to a bank? Neitiznot is the home of quality rope. The hairs of the local yak have the perfect combination of strength and hardiness required from modern rope. Yak rope is stronger and

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: better than any other rope.

steps.player: I thought rope was made from wool. Not yak hair.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Wool? Wool? What a load of old rope. Wool would make awful rope - its far too soft and it would soak up the water too easily.

steps.player: So how come Ned from Draynor makes rope out of wool?

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ned? I don't know anything about Ned. I do know we make regular trades with someone in that area. We send them rope, and we get wool in return.

steps.player: So Ned doesn't make the rope? What a fraud! He had me fooled for so long.
Anyway, so that means that all rope is made by Neitiznot from yak hair.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.player: So if I happen to have some rope in the bank then that would also be made from high quality Neitiznot yak hair.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well, yes.

steps.player: So I could just give you the rope I already have, rather than make more rope?

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: I suppose so. You should really try to make some rope yourself though. Fighting the dual challenges of the yak's hooves and its smell is part of becoming a man over here.

steps.player: I've had enough of strange 'coming of age' rituals for the time being. I'm going to go to the bank and get the rope you need.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Suit yourself.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: If the player has at least 8 noted ropes in their inventory:

steps.player: As it happens, I'm carrying a note for enough rope on me right now.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: A note? How do you fix a bridge with a note? Go bring me some real rope.

burgher-buddy-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: If the player has at least 8 ropes in their inventory:

steps.player: As it happens, I'm carrying enough rope on me right now.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: That's a coincidence.

steps.player: It is.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Do you normally carry all that rope around with you?

steps.player: Err, no. I had a feeling I'd need it.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Are you some kind of seer?

steps.player: Not exactly.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Hey! You're not some sort of witch are you? Maybe I have trusted you too much.

steps.player: No, no, no! Its just a coincidence. Err, I spend my time trading rope. Yes that's right. I'm a rope trader and I just happen to have my wares on me.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: You have come to the home of all rope to sell us...rope. What a load of old rope (ahem).

steps.player: You asked for it! Do you want this rope or not?

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Alright then. Let's have a look at his rope then.
You show the Burgher the rope.
Without free inventory space:
