descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.speaker: [Innocent member]
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.text: Hey! No need for that. You found the failure among us already.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.text: Great work, [player name]. On to the final trial!

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.text: Are you ready to start the next trial?

steps.player: I'm ready!

steps.speaker: Forebearer Janus
steps.text: Well done, recruits. Victory is within your reach, but one more trial awaits...

steps.speaker: Forebearer Janus
steps.text: Face your opponent.

steps.player: Wait...

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.text: Er...

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.text: An Emissary must be prepared to sacrifice anything and everything. Only through sacrifice will we deliver Twilight's Promise. Only through sacrifice will we achieve the Final Dawn.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.text: Well, you heard the man, [player name]. Shall we dance?

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.player: I'm not sure if you should be so...

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-f.text: Ready yourselves! May the best warrior win!

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: You might want to dodge this one!

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Reckon you can dodge this?

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: I'd move if I were you!

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-d.text: Prince Itzla blocks the special attack with a protection prayer.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-d.player: You're not allowed to do that!

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: You and your companion will fit in nicely here. Let us head to the main chamber to discuss what happens next.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-a.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-a.text: You don't need to be going up there. You've already completed your trials.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: Well that was fun!

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.player: You know you're not meant to be enjoying yourself, right?

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: Don't be like that! Surely you must admit you enjoyed it a bit as well?

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.player: I suppose I liked the part where I beat you.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: Right, moving swiftly on. Let's see what Forebearer Janus has to say to us.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: Congratulations to you both on completing the trials. You will make fine Emissaries.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: Now the Augur herself will oversee your initiation. You may collect your new robes from that chest over there. Put them on and proceed into the temple.
If followed by Itzla:

steps.speaker: Forebearer Janus
steps.text: Congratulations on completing the trials. You will make fine Emissaries.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: If not followed by Itzla:

steps.speaker: Forebearer Janus
steps.text: Congratulations on completing the trials, [player name]. You will make a fine Emissary.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.text: We'd better change into those robes.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.text: Let's head over to the temple.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.speaker: Forebearer Janus
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-t.text: You should proceed to the temple. The Augur awaits.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: You search the chest and find some cultist robes for yourself and Itzla. Itzla puts his on.
You search the chest and find some cultist robes. However, you don't have enough room to take them.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-r.text: You search the chest and find some cultist robes.

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-s.text: You search the chest, but find nothing of interest

descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-a.speaker: Emissary Ascended
descending-into-the-tower-of-ascension-a.text: Hey! You don't have permission to go in there!

initiation.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation.text: Welcome, friends. You chosen few stand here because you have proven yourselves to be worthy. Here, you will not just find a home, you will find a family. Together, this family will bring about the Final Dawn.

initiation.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation.text: No doubt you are wondering how we will achieve our destiny. I call upon our glorious leader, the Augur, to explain our holy mission.
Augur Metzli walks onto the stage.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: This morning, you were nothing more than ants, scrambling to find purpose amongst the dirt. Now though... now you have achieved ascension.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Once, I was just the same. Like so many of you, I started my life with nothing. I would wake each morning and pray that I would find enough food to last through the day.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: All the while, those above me treated me worse than a common criminal. I was a villain to them! Why? Simply because they were born with privilege, and I was not.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Eventually, I looked to the Sect of Ranul for guidance. I thought they might have shown me my path, but I was wrong.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Before long, I was their leader and it was instead me who was being looked to for guidance, for purpose. In truth though, even then I had nothing I could offer. I was as blind as I had always been.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: But the day came when I finally saw my purpose, for I was blessed with a vision, granted to me by Ralos and Ranul themselves! I will share now with you what they shared with me.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Thirty one years ago, the moon eclipsed the sun and a false night fell across the land. That day marked a beginning, for it saw the birth of a pair of twins.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: To most, they were children like any other, but I was shown the truth of their birth, for as the sun and moon combined, Ralos and Ranul were born in mortal forms!

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Now, they seek Mokhaiotl. There, they will unite us all as one, and a new world will be born. My purpose, which I now share with you, is to lead them there.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Blasphemy! Deceit! That is what people cry when they hear the truth. The Church of Ralos teaches that our work is false, and our royal leaders lap up their every word!

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Perhaps you still harbour doubts yourselves. I do not judge you. We have all been lied to our entire lives, and in truth, even after I was blessed by our gods, I held many doubts myself.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: But you have all been chosen. You have all achieved ascension. I know that you are among the few who will understand. You are among the few who can see the truth!

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: And see it you will! You do not need to take the word of a mere herald. Instead, bask in the glory of our gods reborn!
Ennius and Furia Tullus walk onto the stage. The new Emissaries, including the player and Prince Itzla, kneel.

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: You may recognise these faces as Ennius and Furia Tullus, but now I give you the truth. Before you stand our gods! Ralos and Ranul!

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: Together, we will accompany them on their glorious journey! We will guide them to Mokhaiotl and bring about the Final Dawn! This is our purpose! This is our destiny! This is Twilight's Promise!

initiation.speaker: Augur Metzli
initiation.text: You all have a part to play in what is to come. Forebearer Fides will assign you your duties. Speak with her and then go forth. Go forth and serve our gods!

initiation-talking-to-fides-before-itzla.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-fides-before-itzla.text: Welcome, acolyte, and congratulations on your initiation. I am just making the final preparations on the duties for you and your companion. They will be ready shortly.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: Well that was a level of insanity that even I wasn't ready for.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.player: They think Ennius and Furia are Ralos and Ranul reborn...

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: Like I say, complete insanity! Metzli has twisted the minds of everyone here. They eagerly lap up her outlandish claims without ever stopping to consider how ludicrous they are.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: In some ways, I pity them, but alas, there is only one cure for this sort of thing. This cult must be eradicated, especially Metzli, Furia and Ennius.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.player: I'm still confused over what their plan is... They want to reach Mokhaiotl, but why would they need to kill Servius to do that? And why the whole set up with that Knight of Varlamore?
When Furia and Ennius set that knight up, it was so obvious. It's like they wanted us to know it was them.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: Hmm... A very good point. Could be this cult has just addled their brains, but it may be that they wanted us here.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: I guess we will find out soon enough.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.player: Should we not leave? We know the cult is guilty now, and we know Metzli, Furia and Ennius are part of it. We have everything we need.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: You said yourself, there are questions still unanswered. We must rectify that.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.player: So if there is a trap, you'd willingly spring it?

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: Well it would be the last thing they'd expect.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: Let's have a chat to this Forebearer Fides about our new duties. Whatever they are, hopefully they give us a chance to learn more.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-after.text: Let's see what duties this Forebearer Fides has for us.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: Welcome, acolytes. Congratulations on your initiation.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: Thank you! We're absolutely ecstatic to be here and we're ready to serve!

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: I am glad to see you are so eager. We have an essential task for you to help perform. The completion of this task may well be essential in us finding a route to Mokhaiotl.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.player: What would you have us do?

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: After the Augur was blessed with glorious purpose, she felt a calling to this place. She came to this fallen temple and built us a home. However, it was not the temple that called to her, but what lies below.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: This temple was built atop Tapoyauik, a ruined fortress of the Old Ones. They walked the world during the last cycle, and when the time came for their cycle to end, they embraced their destiny willingly.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: Of course! They basked in the glory of Ralos and Ranul and united with them as one, but before they did, they left behind the secrets needed to ensure that we too could fulfil our purpose.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: And the Augur? She found those secrets below?

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: She did, but there is more to be uncovered. That is where you come in. Tapoyauik is a hostile environment and the passage into the ruins has been blocked.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides.text: Head below and support the efforts in opening the path once more. Do this, and you will be rewarded by Ralos and Ranul themselves!

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-t.speaker: Forebearer Fides
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-t.text: Welcome back, acolytes. You should head below and support the efforts in opening the path into Tapoyauik. Do this, and you will be rewarded by Ralos and Ranul themselves!

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-t.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-t.text: Let's head down into these ruins.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-l.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-l.text: I'll wait for you inside the temple, [player name].

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-l.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-l.text: Nilsal, [player name]. Let's head down into these ruins.

steps.speaker: Emissary Ascended
steps.text: Yes?

steps.player: Can we go down there?

steps.speaker: Emissary Ascended
steps.text: You may. Now move along.

steps.speaker: Emissary Ascended
steps.text: Yes?

steps.player: Can I go down there?

steps.speaker: Emissary Ascended
steps.text: You may, but you should fetch your companion first.

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-t.speaker: Emissary Ascended
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-fides-t.text: Hey! You should go get your companion before going down there!

initiation-entering-tapoyauik.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-entering-tapoyauik.text: How are you with a pickaxe, iknami? I must confess, my own skills with one are rather poor.

initiation-entering-tapoyauik.player: Did they never teach you how to do a bit of hard labour back when you were young?

initiation-entering-tapoyauik.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-entering-tapoyauik.text: We all have different callings, my friend. Mining just wasn't mine.

initiation-entering-tapoyauik.player: Clearly combat wasn't either given that performance earlier.

initiation-entering-tapoyauik.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-entering-tapoyauik.text: Oh I see! You win one fight and you start thinking you're something special.

initiation-entering-tapoyauik.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-entering-tapoyauik.text: Well then a bit of mining shouldn't be any issue for you then. Get to it!

initiation-talking-to-forebearer-vulcan.speaker: Forebearer Vulcan
initiation-talking-to-forebearer-vulcan.text: That blockage won't clear itself! Grab a pickaxe and get to work!

initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.speaker: Forebearer Vulcan
initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.text: Excellent work! Ralos and Ranul have blessed us on this day!
The screen stops shaking as two frost nagua appear.
The two acolytes run away. The nagua both cast spells, killing Forebearer Vulcan and knocking Prince Itzla back across a chasm.

initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.text: Well... I'm alive, which I must be honest, I wasn't really expecting after that!

initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.player: I can't see any way over to you.

initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.text: Nor can I. I think we're just going to have to press on and hope that we can meet up again further ahead.

initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.text: Do you see any other options?

initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-after-clearing-the-rocks.text: Than I shall meet you up ahead. Good luck!

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-by-th.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-by-th.text: There you are! I was starting to worry you'd got lost.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-by-th.player: There were a few obstacles in my way.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-by-th.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-by-th.text: Well unfortunately it seems we have another before us. I can't see any way to open this door.

initiation-talking-to-prince-itzla-by-th.player: Hmm... I'll have a look around and see what I can find.

options.text: Could I ask you about some words I found carved into the wall?

steps.player: Could I ask you about some words I found carved into the wall?

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: I'll do my best.

steps.player: Oma.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Oma? If I remember right, that means the number 'two'.

steps.player: Thanks!
Yeya.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Yeya? That means...

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: I think it means 'three'.

steps.player: Thanks!
Naui.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Naui? Hmm...

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: I'm afraid I don't know what that one means.

steps.player: Not to worry. I'm sure I can still work it out.
Zema.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Zema? Let's see... That could mean a few things. 'Together', 'people' and 'one' are the ones I remember.

steps.player: Interesting... Thanks!

options.text: What do you think Metzli found down here?

steps.player: What do you think Metzli found down here?

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Nothing is my guess. The whole point of Ximoua is that it can't be, and shouldn't be, predicted. It's meant to teach us to live freely and not worry about that which we can't control.

steps.player: So she's lying?

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: That, or she herself was so desperate to find a greater meaning in something, that she misinterpreted what she did find.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: I suppose it doesn't matter though. This Final Dawn business is total nonsense, but if the Emissaries believe in it, then we need to work out what they consider so important about this place.

options.text: Could I ask you about some words I found carved into the wall?
On that note, I guess I should get back to the door.

steps.player: On that note, I guess I should get back to the door.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: Indeed. There must be some way to open it...

steps.player: Nothing yet.

steps.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
steps.text: There must be some way to open it...

initiation-if-prince-itzla-targets-an-ic.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-if-prince-itzla-targets-an-ic.text: Help me kill this thing, would you?

initiation-solving-the-puzzle-checking-t.text: The door seems to be frozen shut. There must be some way to open it.

initiation-solving-the-puzzle-interactin.text: The statue has [a water/a fire/an earth] symbol at the base. It looks like it's meant to be holding something.

steps.prompt: Place an icon on the statue?

steps.text: Water statue:
You place the icon on the statue.
Earth statue:
You place the icon on the statue.
Fire statue:
You place the icon on the statue.

initiation-solving-the-puzzle-interactin.text: If not holding the corresponding icon:
The statue has [an air/a water/a fire/an earth] symbol at the base. It's holding some sort of icon.

initiation-after-opening-the-door.text: The room shakes as the statues unleash their power on the locked door.

initiation-after-opening-the-door.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
initiation-after-opening-the-door.text: Great work opening the door, [player name]. Time to see what awaits us on the other side.

heart-of-the-ruins.text: Amoxliatl, a large ice nagua, appears.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Humans... You stand before Amoxliatl. State your intent.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: A greeting is not a statement of intent. State your intent.

heart-of-the-ruins.player: Er... Well we're looking for information. The cultists in the temple above apparently found something down here. We need to know what they found so we can stop them.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Your statement lacks specificity. Clarify. What information?

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
heart-of-the-ruins.text: On Mokhaiotl. The cultists are trying to get there.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Mokhaiotl? The Tlati archive? That place is not for your kind. You misused the gifts you were granted. You are unworthy.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Tlati? As in the rainforest? What do you mean? And what gifts?
Prince Itzla is teleported away. Metzli, Furia, Ennius, and two Emissaries enter the room.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Augur Metzli
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Itzla? He is no longer your concern.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Ennius Tullus
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Allow me to deal with this nuisance, Augur. The fire of Ralos is within me. He can be the first to bask in it.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Furia Tullus
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Save your fury, brother. This one is unworthy of it.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Human arrogance. Here in Tapoyauik, I decide who is worthy.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Ennius Tullus
heart-of-the-ruins.text: Silence, nagua! Do you not know who stands before you?

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: You? You are nothing. You defile this place. Now face the consequences.

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Augur Metzli
heart-of-the-ruins.text: There is nothing more for us here. If the nagua wants blood, our friend here will provide plenty...

heart-of-the-ruins.player: I need to get after them!

heart-of-the-ruins.speaker: Amoxliatl
heart-of-the-ruins.text: After them? No. You will not be going anywhere...

heart-of-the-ruins-after-defeating-amoxl.player: I'd better get to Fortis and let them know what happened!

heart-of-the-ruins-attempting-to-re-ente.player: I need to get over to Fortis rather than going in there again.

heart-of-the-ruins-attempting-to-climb-t.text: You've already completed the trials so have no need to go back up there.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: Ah, nilsal, my child. It is good to see you.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.player: Servius? I wasn't expecting you to be up so soon.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: Ralos still has need of me, my child. I will not bow down to a mere knife wound.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.player: Well I'm glad to see you're doing well, but I'm afraid I have some bad news. Itzla has been captured!
We infiltrated the Twilight Emissaries together. We discovered Metzli to be their new leader, with Ennius and Furia at her side. She's claiming the two of them are Ralos and Ranul reborn!

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: Blasphemy and betrayal in equal measure! They will all burn in the light of Ralos for this! And you say they have captured the Prince as well?

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.player: They have. I don't know where they've taken him.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: This is dire news. I must speak to the Queen at once. Is there anything else I should be aware of before doing so?

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.player: The cult are apparently trying to reach Mokhaiotl.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: Mokhaiotl is not a place that can be reached! These fools are truly lost!
If Perilous Moons has not been completed:

steps.player: I don't know... Something isn't right about all of this. We encountered a creature in some Old One ruins. The cultists called her a nagua. She referred to Mokhaiotl as the Tlati archive.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: If Perilous Moons has been completed:

steps.player: I don't know... Something isn't right about all of this. We encountered a nagua in some Old One ruins. She called Mokhaiotl the Tlati archive.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: You should be careful of trusting the words of a nagua. Still, I must seek the guidance of Ralos on this matter. First though, I will speak with the Queen.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: Fear not. I will ensure the Queen involves you in whatever plans are made for dealing with this cult. On that note, I'd best not delay. May the sun light your way, my child.

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.player: If you're going to speak to the Queen now, maybe I should join you?

heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.speaker: Servius, Teokan of Ralos
heart-of-the-ruins-talking-to-servius-te.text: Are you sure? It might be best for me to speak to her first. She will not take kindly to this development. I would hate for you to face her fire, my child.

t8gLJV.speaker: Prince Itzla Arkan
t8gLJV.text: But it seems we will have to ponder this mystery later. Pick up your follower and then let us head inside and see what tests await us.

uDj1Kv.speaker: Forebearer Janus
uDj1Kv.text: Then come back to me when you are.

s_fle1.speaker: Forebearer Janus
s_fle1.text: Recruit. Any luck finding the traitor yet?

s_fle1.speaker: Forebearer Janus
s_fle1.text: Remember, only one of the four before you is guilty of disloyalty. Question all four and determine who it is. I suggest you choose carefully.

starting-off.speaker: Cassius
starting-off.text: You!

starting-off.speaker: Cassius
starting-off.text: Yes you!

starting-off.speaker: Cassius
starting-off.text: That depends. Do you like making money?

starting-off.player: I'm not averse to making money.

starting-off.speaker: Cassius
starting-off.text: And do you enjoy... milk?

starting-off.speaker: Cassius
starting-off.text: Milk.
If the player is on a quest speedrunning world:

steps.player: I suppose it's okay.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Well, fair enough. If your passion for milk changes, let me know.
This quest is not available on Speedrunning Worlds.

starting-off.player: I can't say I've thought much about it.

starting-off.speaker: Cassius
starting-off.text: Would you like to think more about it?
Before starting this quest, be aware that your combat level is lower than the recommended level of 15.

starting-off.prompt: Start The Ides of Milk quest?

steps.player: What am I going to get from thinking more about... milk?

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Profit!

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Ten to fifteen percent, performance depending.

steps.player: How are we going to be making that profit? And who even are you anyway?

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Ah, my name is Cassius. I got carried away.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: But, we're going to construct an empire.

steps.player: Of milk?

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Of milk.

steps.player: How do you intend to make an empire of milk?

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: So, the first step is going to involve you doing a little... research.

steps.player: Right...

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: You're going to cross the River Lum, find Gillie and Seth Groats, and learn about animal husbandry.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Then... Then you're going to cross back to this side of the river, and tell me all about how they've made their animals so productive.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: It's a perfect plan!

steps.player: What use is it if I know everything and you don't? Couldn't I make my own... milk empire... with that information?
If anything I should be cutting you in at ten to fifteen percent.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Hey, I'm the one supplying the high-quality milk here.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: Not to mention, my associate Brutus is already embedded in the Groats operation to work a different angle. That will prove most lucrative.

steps.player: Right... I guess I'll go and see the Groatses then.
No, I'm not sure I would like that, thank you.

starting-off-attempting-to-release-the-b.player: Releasing the bull into the cow pen is a bad idea.

starting-off-attempting-to-release-the-b.text: You need to have completed The Ides of Milk quest to release this bull.

starting-off-talking-to-cassius-again-be.player: What was it you needed me to do again?

starting-off-talking-to-cassius-again-be.speaker: Cassius
starting-off-talking-to-cassius-again-be.text: I need you to speak to Gillie and Seth Groats. We need to learn everything we can.

starting-off-talking-to-cassius-again-be.speaker: Cassius
starting-off-talking-to-cassius-again-be.text: They live just across the River Lum. Head east from here and you should be able to find them.

starting-off-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
starting-off-talking-to-gillie.text: Hello, I'm Gillie the Milkmaid. What can I do for you?

options.text: Can you tell me how to milk a cow?
Can you share what makes your cows so productive?

steps.player: Can you share what makes your cows so productive?

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: Absolutely! The secret is happiness.

steps.player: Happiness?

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: The cows make the best milk when they're happy, and to be honest, they make too much!

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: I'm always glad that adventurers come by and help with milking them. I wouldn't be able to keep up otherwise.

steps.player: That can't be everything though, can it?

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: Come to think of it, I'm sure my father keeps a few tricks up his sleeve. Why don't you go and ask him?
If the player has not yet talked to Seth Groats:

steps.player: That would be Seth, wouldn't it?

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: It would be! I'm sure he'll he happy to share some information with you.

steps.player: I'll go and speak to him now, thank you!

steps.text: If the player has already talked to Seth Groats:

steps.player: I've already had a chance to talk to him. He did indeed have some tricks to share!

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: That's good. You must be ready to care for your own cows at this point!

steps.player: If you think so, then I must be. Thank you for your help, I'll make sure that knowledge is put to good use.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Well well, what can I do for you?

starting-off-talking-to-seth.player: I was wondering if you could teach me a little about how you're so successful with your animals.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Lookin' to get into the business, eh?

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Well, always happy to help another budding farmer out!

starting-off-talking-to-seth.player: Great! So where do I start?

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Would always recommend me Groats Principles as yer basics.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Aye. First one is that happy animals makes happy farmers.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Second of me principles is to never take more than you need. Greed'll stop you in your tracks.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: The last principle: never let the taxman know yer earnings. Money should be spent on the animals!
If the player is an ironman:

steps.player: I don't think I've ever paid any taxes.

steps.speaker: Seth Groats
steps.text: You're ahead of the game then!

starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: If the player is not an ironman:

steps.player: You've found a way to get around the taxes?

steps.speaker: Seth Groats
steps.text: A way or two.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth.text: Anyway, feel free to grab me book on the topic from the shelf over there.

starting-off-talking-to-seth.player: Okay, thank you for the help.

starting-off-searching-the-shelf.text: Before learning about the book or while having the book already:

steps.text: You find a bucket on the shelf, as you'd expect a farmer to have.
You find a loose egg on the shelf, and fortunately avoid knocking it to the floor.
Hidden behind the piles of junk on the shelf, you find a small farmer's hat with Gillie's name written on it.
You find Seth's book on the shelf, but don't have room to take it with you.
You find Seth's book of principles on the shelf.

starting-off-talking-to-seth-again.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth-again.text: Well well, what can I do for you?

starting-off-talking-to-seth-again.player: I was wondering if you could teach me a little about how you're so successful with your animals.

starting-off-talking-to-seth-again.speaker: Seth Groats
starting-off-talking-to-seth-again.text: Mmm we already had this talk. Go read me book on the shelf over there.
If the player doesn't have the book on them:

steps.player: I'll go grab it, thanks.

starting-off-talking-to-seth-again.text: If the player has the book on them:

steps.player: I've actually got it here, I'll take it away and give it a read somewhere a little more peaceful.

returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius.text: So, how did you get on?

returning-to-cassius.player: I've learned a lot about how the Groats family care for their animals. They say the secret is happiness!

returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius.text: Happiness?! That can't be the only trick they use! Surely you found something else?
If the player doesn't have the book on them:

steps.player: Now that you mention it, Seth did say he had a book that I... don't have on me right now.

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: The legendary Groats book on milk cultivation? I'm most interested! Go fetch it!

returning-to-cassius.player: I have this book from Seth. He claims it's got his principles of animal husbandry in it, if that's of any use?

returning-to-cassius.text: Cassius snatches the book from your hands.

returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius.text: The idea that a happy animal will do what you want is frankly absurd. What if they choose to not produce. Are you supposed to respect that?

returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius.text: However, the writings on the systems of taxation are fascinating. I couldn't imagine Seth was smart enough to put this together.

returning-to-cassius.player: So, do you think this is enough to start our milk empire?

returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius.text: No, no. Not quite yet. First of all, you haven't tried our milk yet, have you?

returning-to-cassius.player: I don't think I have, no. You already have some milk?

returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius.text: Don't look so worried. Here, have a try.
Cassius hands you a milk sample to try.

returning-to-cassius-destroying-the-milk.text: Why would you want to destroy such good milk? Do you not wish to taste it?

returning-to-cassius-reclaiming-the-milk.player: I've managed to lose that sample of milk...

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: I'll give you some more once you've got some space.
Cassius glares as he hands you another sample of milk.

returning-to-cassius-talking-to-cassius-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-talking-to-cassius-.text: Have you given that sample a try yet?

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.text: The player coughs and is damaged for 1 Hitpoints with a poison hitsplat.

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.text: So, what do you think? The milk is fantastic, isn't it?

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.player: It wasn't what I was expecting, certainly.

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.text: We're going to change the lactic landscape! Before we do though, I have another task for you.

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.player: Shouldn't you have got a permit before making milk?

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.text: The permit is to sell milk, not to make milk!

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.player: Fine, where are we going to get this permit?

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.text: From the Duke of Lumbridge! Where else? You need to bring him our milk and I'm sure he'll give us our permit without fuss.

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.player: Are you sure having the Duke drink our milk is a good idea?

returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-after-sampling-the-.text: Of course! Soon the whole of Lumbridge will be drinking my, I mean our milk!
Cassius hands you a milk sample.

returning-to-cassius-attempting-to-drink.player: I don't think I'm ready to drink another vial of this stuff.
I should find someone else to give it to.

returning-to-cassius-talking-to-cassius-.speaker: Cassius
returning-to-cassius-talking-to-cassius-.text: Has the Duke given us our permit yet?
If the player lost the second milk sample:

steps.player: Not yet, no. I could do with another sample of milk though, if you have one spare?

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: I should have one somewhere here. Just a moment.
Without free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Cassius
steps.text: It looks like you don't have space to carry this. You'll have to grab it from me when you have room.
With free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Cassius

returning-to-cassius-talking-to-cassius-.text: If the player still has the second milk sample:

steps.player: Not yet, no, but I am working on it!

talking-to-the-duke.player: Greetings. I come seeking a business permit.

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: Oh wonderful! What sort of business are you looking to start?

talking-to-the-duke.player: I'm looking to get into the milk trade!

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: Milk? Well, the Groats family still have their permit, and I can't start stepping on their toes.

talking-to-the-duke.player: If you'd just try this milk...

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: I really couldn't possibly give you a permit without their approval. This is really their territory.

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: Why not speak to Gillie Groats? She seems to handle the milk side of the business now. Maybe she'll get you set up under their permit.

talking-to-the-duke.player: You're the Duke. Couldn't you just grant a permit?

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: No, no. It's really quite important you speak to Gillie about this.

talking-to-the-duke.player: Aren't you the highest power in this land?

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: Don't go digging too deeply into that. Even I have some... commitments that I have to keep to.

talking-to-the-duke.player: But you're the Duke, you shouldn't need the approval of a business entity to grant a permit.
Not to mention, can't they just refuse to have any competitors?

talking-to-the-duke.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke.text: Well absolutely, but I'm sure you'll find they're more than reasonable about things.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-the-duke-.player: Hi, what did you want me to do for the permit again?

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-the-duke-.speaker: Duke Horacio
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-the-duke-.text: Go speak to Gillie Groats. She seems to handle the milk business in Lumbridge. Maybe she'll get you set up under their permit.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.text: Hiya, did you need something else from me?

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.player: I did. I've been trying to secure a business permit from the Duke, but he said that as it is a milk-related business venture, I should speak to you instead.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.text: The Duke is a good man, directing you to me! I've been running the milk side of our farm for a while now.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.text: Were you thinking of being a competitor to us then?
If the player doesn't have the second milk sample:

steps.player: I can prove we wouldn't be if you could just try this sample of...

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: Sample of?

steps.player: I seem to have misplaced my sample of milk. I'll be back when I have it.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie.text: If the player has the second milk sample:

steps.player: I think if you were to try this sample here you'd see we wouldn't be competing.

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: You want me to drink a vial of mysterious liquid?

steps.player: Well, it's not mysterious, it's milk!

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: No, I think you should drink it, I'll know the quality of it from your reaction.

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: It is just milk after all.

steps.player: Would it convince you to help me with my permit?

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: It definitely won't hurt your chances.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie-ag.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie-ag.text: Have you tried that milk sample yet?

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie-ag.player: Not yet. I really don't want to, but I guess I must.
I shouldn't drink this unless I have Gillie nearby.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.player: Oh, that's worse milk than before.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: That looked like a horrible experience.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: Where did you even get that milk?

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.player: My business partner, Cassius. I don't know where he gets it from originally though.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: Cassius... I don't recognise the name. He's not mentioned anything about its source?

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.player: Nothing, but he apparently has enough of a source to start a business. I'm mostly trying to be helpful.
If the milk's bad, you're not going to recommend us for a permit, are you?

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: With how bad it looks, you wouldn't be any competition to us.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: However, I wonder if I'd be doing a public service by protecting anyone else from it.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.player: Is there anything more I could do to convince you?

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: Now that you mention it, I've had an incredibly aggressive bull disrupting my herd lately. I've got him caught in the pen over there.

talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-drinking-the-second-.text: Perhaps you'd be interested in dealing with him? I'd owe you a fairly large favour.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie-ag.speaker: Gillie Groats
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie-ag.text: How are you getting on with the bull?

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-gillie-ag.player: I'm getting there! He looks quite tough though.

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-cassius.text: Has the Duke given us our permit yet?

talking-to-the-duke-talking-to-cassius.player: It's become rather complicated, but I am working it out!

steps.text: The bull enters. The cows scatter.
The bull enters. The cows scatter.

facing-the-bull-after-killing-brutus.text: You notice a strange tag float to the ground as the bull falls. It reads 'Brutus'.
You notice a strange tag float to the ground as the bull falls. It reads 'Brutus'.

facing-the-bull-attempting-to-open-the-g.player: Brutus has already been dealt with.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.text: You succeeded! I'll let the Duke know that you're all good to start a milk business.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.player: I don't think that's going to be necessary anymore.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.text: Oh? What happened in that field?

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.player: That bull was Cassius' other business partner, Brutus.
I'm sure he won't be feeling particularly friendly once I let him know.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.text: That bull was one of the business partners?

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.text: I wonder if his aggression is why Cassius' herd are producing such bad milk...

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.player: I'm starting to think Cassius doesn't even have his own herd.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.text: You think he's been stealing milk?

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.player: I'm not sure where else he would've been getting it from.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie.text: Why don't you go and talk to him about it! He may appreciate knowing the Brutus was bad for business.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie-again.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie-again.text: Thank you once again for handling Brutus, he was causing quite a problem for my herd.

facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie-again.speaker: Gillie Groats
facing-the-bull-talking-to-gillie-again.text: And, if you haven't yet spoken to Cassius, you should probably let him know what's transpired.

facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.player: Cassius, I don't think we'll be getting our business permit.
So the Duke asked me to... and then Gillie said that...

facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.text: Don't tell me you killed Brutus and ruined my- our, plan?

facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.player: In my defence, I had no idea that was Brutus! You made it sound like he was a business partner.
Not to mention, apparently his aggression was ruining Seth's herd's milk. This should be a good thing!

facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.text: Ruining the milk? The unique flavour was what I was trying to sell!

facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.speaker: Cassius
facing-the-bull-returning-to-cassius.text: You should leave. I can't even look at you.

post-quest-talking-to-cassius.text: Cassius makes a point of ignoring you.

post-quest-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
post-quest-talking-to-gillie.text: Oh, just the person I wanted to see! I have something for you.

post-quest-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
post-quest-talking-to-gillie.text: This is for helping out with that bull. Our cows are much happier these days.
Gillie hands you an amulet with a bell on it.

post-quest-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
post-quest-talking-to-gillie.text: One of our local milk enjoyers gave us some enchanted cow bells.

post-quest-talking-to-gillie.speaker: Gillie Groats
post-quest-talking-to-gillie.text: They seem to be quite versatile, enjoy!

post-quest-talking-to-gillie.player: Wow, thank you! I'll make sure to check it out.

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats

steps.speaker: Gillie Groats
steps.text: I also have this for you!
Gillie hands you a magical lamp.

steps.player: Oh, thank you!

options.text: Do you know where you lost it?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: The Imcando dwarves, you say? Let's see...

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Ah, yes... For many hundreds of years, they were the world's most skilled smiths. They used secret smithing knowledge passed down from generation to generation.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Unfortunately, about a century ago, the once thriving group was wiped out during the barbarian invasions of that time.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I believe a few of them survived, but with the bulk of their population destroyed, their numbers dwindled even further. If any are left now, they'll no doubt keep to themselves.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: However, I have heard tales of their love for redberry pie. Perhaps one of those could convince one to reveal their true heritage.

steps.player: So I just go around offering random dwarves redberry pie?

steps.speaker: Reldo

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Last night I was in the kitchen and I heard a noise from the cellar. I opened the trapdoor and saw a creature dart into a hole in the wall.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: It looked a bit like a goblin, but it had big bulging eyes. It wasn't wearing armour, but it had this odd helmet with a light on it.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: The tunnel was too dark for me to follow it, so I went to tell the Duke. But when we went down to the cellar the hole had been blocked up, and no one believes me.

steps.player: I believe you.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Thank you, [player name]! If you can convince the Duke I'm telling the truth then we can get to the bottom of this mystery.

options.text: Can you repair my items for me?

options.text: Can you repair my items for me?

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: Bob says he saw something in the cellar. Like a goblin with big eyes.

steps.speaker: Sigmund

steps.player: I dug through the rubble in the cellar and found a tunnel!

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: I dug through the rubble in the cellar and found a tunnel!
On the ground I found this brooch.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I've never seen anything like that before. It doesn't come from Lumbridge. What do you think, Sigmund?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: It is unknown to me, your grace. But the fact it is there is enough to prove Bob's story. It must have been dropped by a goblin as it fled.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I've never heard of a goblin wearing something so well-crafted.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: Then it must have been stolen!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: But it wasn't stolen from us. Where could it be from?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: That doesn't matter! You said yourself that goblins couldn't have made that, so they must have stolen it from somewhere.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: Horrible, thieving goblins have broken into our cellar! We must retaliate immediately!

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: First we should wipe out the goblins east of the river, then we can march on the goblin village to the north-west...

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I will not commit troops until I have proof that goblins are behind this.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: [player name], please find out what you can about this brooch. The librarian in Varrock might be able to help identify the symbol.

options.text: What can you tell me about this brooch?

steps.player: What can you tell me about this brooch?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I've never seen that symbol before. Where did you find it?

steps.player: In a cave beneath Lumbridge.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Very odd. Have you any idea how it got there?

steps.player: A goblin might have dropped it.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I've never heard of a goblin carrying a brooch like this. But just a minute...

steps.speaker: Reldo

options.text: Do you have anything to trade?

investigation-a-history-of-the-goblin-ra.text: You take the book from the bookcase.

investigation-a-history-of-the-goblin-ra.player: Hey... The symbol of the 'Dorgeshuun' tribe looks just like the symbol on the brooch I found.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: You see, your grace? I told you goblins were behind this!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I still find it surprising that such a well-crafted brooch would have a goblin symbol on it. Perhaps you should find out more about this ancient tribe.

options.text: I found out about the symbol...

steps.player: I found out about the symbol. It was the symbol of one of the ancient goblin tribes!

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: At last, proof that goblins are behind this! You should tell the Duke at once!

options.text: Have you ever heard of the Dorgeshuun?

steps.player: Have you ever heard of the Dorgeshuun?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Dorgeshuun? That old goblin legend. Lost tribe.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: In time of much-war there many tribes. Big High War-God send Dorgesh tribe to fight beardy-short-people in mountains.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No no, he send them to fight tall people with biting blades, that what I hear.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It was beardy-short-people, that how legend go.

steps.player: Make up your minds!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: It was tall people! That what old storyteller say!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: No, beardy-short-people. That how legend always go, stupid.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: You stupid!

options.text: Do you want me to decide for you again?

steps.player: Do you want me to decide for you again?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That most stupid idea yet. If it happen it either happen one way or the other. You can't just decide which.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Yeah even goblins know that.

steps.player: It doesn't really matter. What happened to them?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Well, they say, 'We not want to fight,' so god punish them.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That silly. No goblin ever say that.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: What happen then?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: They lose battle, that why god punish them.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Ha ha! If they lost battle they all be dead!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No no, they losing so they run away, and Big High War-God punish them for running away.

steps.player: Who were they fighting again?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It was beardy-short-people in mountains.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No no, it was tall people.

options.text: What kind of god would punish them for refusing to fight?

steps.player: What kind of god would punish them for refusing to fight?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Shh! Must not question Big High War-God!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: No, because he much bigger than us.

options.text: Well either way they refused to fight

steps.player: Well either way they refused to fight.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Yeah I suppose so.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Anyway then Big High War-God punish them. He turn their insides to stone.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Ha ha ha! That silly!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Not as silly as green armour! What happen then?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: He put them inside stone! Big hole open in ground and they all go into cave.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That not punishment! Caves nice and cool.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: But then he close cave so they not get out! You not want to stay in cave all the time.

steps.player: Why were there punished again?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It because they run away from fight.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No, it because they refuse to fight night before battle.

options.text: So do goblins make their own tunnels?

steps.player: So do goblins make their own tunnels?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: What? Make our own tunnels?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: We hadn't thought of that.

options.text: Well I found a brooch underground...

steps.player: Well I found a brooch underground, and I looked up the symbol and it was the symbol of the Dorgeshuun.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That not look like goblin brooch.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Goblins not wear jewellery.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Well if it Dorgeshuun tribe they not know who won big wars. You should greet them with goblin victory dance!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: No no, you greet them with goblin tribal bow.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Doing bow make you look like a wimp.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It how tribes greet each other in old days.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Only if they wimpy tribes! Goblin salute strong!

options.text: So why is the Dorgeshuun tribe underground?

steps.player: So why is the Dorgeshuun tribe underground?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: They punished by Big High War-God.

options.text: Wait, you say YOU won the big wars?

steps.player: Wait, you say YOU won the big wars?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Well we must have done! We goblins! Goblins always win!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Actually we not know who won.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: It was goblins I say!

options.text: Well why not show me both greetings?

steps.player: Well why not show me both greetings?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: That good idea. Watch.
The goblins show you the Goblin Victory Salute and Goblin Bow.

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Bye then.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Bye.

options.text: Wait, you say YOU won the big wars?
So why is the Dorgeshuun tribe underground?
So how is life for the goblins?

steps.player: I spoke to the goblin generals in the goblin village. They told me about an ancient goblin tribe that went to live underground.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: What more proof do we need? Nasty, smelly goblins have been living under our feet all this time! We must crush them at once!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Hmm, perhaps you are right. I will send word to the army to prepare for an underground assault.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: [player name], I would still like you to find out more about this tribe. It cannot hurt to know one's enemy.

options.text: I spoke to the generals in the Goblin Village...

steps.player: I spoke to the goblin generals in the Goblin Village. They told me about an ancient goblin tribe that went to live underground.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: I don't see how there can be any more doubt. You should tell the Duke at once!

meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.text: Who...who are you? How did you get in here?

meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.text: Help! A surface-dweller this deep in our mines? We will all be destroyed!
If the player performs the Goblin Bow emote:

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: A human knows ancient greeting?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Perhaps you are friend after all!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Greetings, friend. I am sorry I panicked when I saw you.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Our legends tell of the surface as a place of horror and violence, where the gods forced us to fight in terrible battles.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: When I saw a surface-dweller appear I was afraid it was a return to the old days!

steps.player: Did you break in to the castle cellar?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: It was an accident. We were following a seam of iron and suddenly we found ourselves in a room!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: We blocked up our tunnel behind us and ran back here. Then we did what cave goblins always do when there is a problem: we hid and hoped it would go away.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: We meant no harm! Please tell the ruler of the above- people that we want to make peace.

meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.text: If the player performs the Goblin Salute emote:

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Eeek! The war-dance!

options.text: May I mine the rocks here?

steps.player: May I mine the rocks here?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: No offence, but we will not let you mine here until there is peace between the humans and the Dorgeshuun.

options.text: Why do the Dorgeshuun live underground?
Can you show me the way out of the mines?

steps.player: Can you show me the way out of the mines?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Certainly. Please hurry, you must avert the war!

meeting-the-lost-tribe-using-mistag-s-br.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-using-mistag-s-br.text: We have more important things to think about than a brooch right now. We must prevent a war!

meeting-the-lost-tribe-trying-to-mine-th.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-trying-to-mine-th.text: We won't permit surface-dwellers to mine here until there is peace between our peoples.

steps.player: I've made contact with the cave goblins. They say they were following a seam and broke into the cellar by mistake.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: And I suppose you believe them, goblin-lover?

steps.player: Well, they seemed friendlier than most goblins, and nothing was taken from the cellar.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Actually, something was taken. Sigmund has informed me that some of the castle silverware is missing from the cellar.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Unless it is returned, I am afraid I will have no option but war.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: What was I doing again?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: We are preparing to go to war with the underground goblins over the missing silverware. If you think the cave goblins are innocent you should present evidence quickly!

options.text: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.player: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: The priceless Lumbridge Silverware! It comes out only on special occasions. It was kept in storage in the cellar, but now the goblins have stolen it.

steps.player: So why did no one notice earlier?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: That doesn't matter. You'll never find it, because the goblins took it. So you can't stop the war!

options.text: Some silverware has gone missing from the castle cellar...

steps.player: Some silverware has gone missing from the castle, and the Duke thinks you stole it!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Oh no! We would never do such a thing!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: I assure you we took nothing from the cellar. You must convince the Duke we are innocent!

options.text: Where is the silverware you stole from the castle cellar?

steps.player: Where's the silverware you stole from the castle cellar?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: What? We didn't take anything!

steps.player: You expect me to believe that? Perhaps Sigmund was right: you're just thieving little goblins!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Why would we want to steal silver? As you see we have much silver already in our mines!

steps.player: Well, the Duke says he will attack you unless the silverware is returned.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: The last thing we want is war! If we had anything of yours, we would return it at once. But we don't!

options.text: Can you show me the way out of the mines?

steps.player: You're a H.A.M member, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: Well, so what if I am? It's not a crime.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?
Did you know Sigmund is a member of HAM?

steps.player: Did you know Sigmund is a member of HAM?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Hmm, I had suspected it. But however much I disapprove of the HAM movement it's not actually illegal. I'll keep an eye on him though.

options.text: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.player: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: The priceless Lumbridge Silverware! It comes out only on special occasions. It was kept in storage in the cellar, but now the goblins have stolen it.

steps.player: So why did no one notice earlier?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: That doesn't matter. You'll never find it, because the goblins took it. So you can't stop the war!

steps.player: Actually I have found it! You put it in the H.A.M. cave!

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: I... I... You're lying! I don't know what you're talking about.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?
I found the missing silverware in the HAM cave!

steps.player: I found the missing silverware in the HAM cave!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Sigmund! Is this your doing?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: Of...of course not! The goblins must have, um, dropped the silverware as they ran away.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Don't lie to me! I knew you were a HAM member but I didn't think you would stoop to this. You are dismissed from my service.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: But don't you see it was for the best? For goblins to be living under our feet like this... ugh. It doesn't matter how civilized they are: all sub-human species must be wiped out!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: That's enough! Get out of my castle now!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I see I was ill-advised. Unless there is an act of aggression by the cave goblins there is no need for war.
The Duke writes a document and signs it.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: This peace treaty specifies the border between Lumbridge and the Cave Goblin realm. Please take it to the cave goblins and tell them I would like to meet with their leader to sign it.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: What was I doing again?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: You were taking the peace treaty to the cave goblins.
If the player doesn't have the peace treaty:

steps.player: I, er, lost the treaty.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: sigh* All right, here's another copy.

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.player: I have a peace treaty from the Duke of Lumbridge.

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.speaker: Mistag
resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.text: A peace treaty? Then you will not invade?

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.player: No. As long as you stick to the terms of this treaty there will be no conflict. The Duke of Lumbridge wants to meet your ruler to sign it.

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.speaker: Mistag
resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.text: I will summon Ur-tag, our headman, at once.
Fade to black and a cutscene starts

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: ~ The Signing of the Lumbridge-Dorgeshuun Treaty ~

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.player: Your grace, I present Ur-tag, headman of the Dorgeshuun.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: Welcome, Ur-tag. I am sorry that your race came under suspicion.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: I assure you that the warmongering element has been dealt with.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Ur-tag
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: I apologize for the damage to your cellar. I will send workers to repair the hole.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: No, let it stay. It can be a route of commerce between our lands.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: [player name], Lumbridge is in your debt. Please accept this ring as a token of my thanks.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: It is enchanted to save you in your hour of need.
The Duke hands the player a Ring of Life.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Ur-tag
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: I too thank you. Accept the freedom of the Dorgeshuun mines.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Ur-tag
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: These are strange times. I never dreamed that I would see the surface, still less that I would be on friendly terms with its people.
The camera pans out to reveal Sigmund eavesdropping beyond the doors.

if-the-player-is-spotted-without-a-disgu.npc: How dare you come near my farmhouse! Guards! Guards! Remove this human!

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello! What's a monkey like you doing here?
Fair enough then.

standard-dialogue-with-m-speak-amulet-eq.npc: What are you doing in my house?
Well I don't give a monkey's uncle!

initial-dialogue.npc: How curious? I have not seen a creature of your kind for many years. You have ventured into the Nexus human - I should warn you to be aware of the Abyssal Sires.

steps.player: Tell me about yourself.

steps.npc: Ah... Time does not pass in the Abyss at the same rate that it does in your realm, but nevertheless I have been in this place for aeons.
Indeed, when I was last in your realm, the armies of Zamorak were battling the other gods for control, and we sought reinforcements from any plane we could reach.
That was how I came here. We broke through to the Abyss, seeking allies for our cause, but instead I ended up a prisoner in this place, unable to leave, while the God Wars continued without me.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.player: What can I do here?

steps.npc: There is something you can do here, human. In fact it may perhaps benefit us both.
Bring me a spine, a claw and an axon from the Abyssal Sires, and I shall construct them into a mighty weapon for you. Yes, we shall both benefit from this.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.player: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.npc: The Sires are the engineers of this living pocket universe known to you and I as the Abyss.
At the hands of the 'Chaos God', Zamorak, like myself, they too were cast down and imprisoned in this living tomb.
They worked for centuries attempting to escape the pull of the Abyss but as food resources began to deplete they knew that their only chance for survival was to construct this Nexus.
They absorb flesh and bone of their demon kin, weaving it into the fabric of these very walls. Here they have remained in deep stasis, asleep.
If you succeed in awakening them, they will no doubt unleash their full fury upon you. Someone of your calibre should be able to deal with them though, especially with the shadows on your side...
If you succeed in killing a Sire, you may be fortunate enough to find one of its unsired offspring among its remains. Bring the Unsired here, to the Font of Consumption.
By placing the Unsired into the Font, I will be able to consume its flesh and perhaps you will receive something worth having.

steps.player: I'll be off for now.

initial-dialogue-if-the-player-brings-it.npc: I did not ask you to bring me anything, human.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-does-n.npc: Have you harvested any components for me?

steps.player: What's this stuff for?

steps.npc: I shall use the components to construct a mighty weapon for you. Rest assured, the process will be beneficial to both of us.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.player: No, sorry.

steps.npc: I still require [bludgeon component(s)] from an Abyssal Sire.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at.npc: Have you harvested any components for me?

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at.text: You hand over the component(s) to the Overseer.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at.npc: I still require [bludgeon component(s)] from an Abyssal Sire.

final-dialogue.npc: Have you harvested any components for me?

final-dialogue.text: You hand over the component(s) to the Overseer.

final-dialogue.npc: I now have all the components I require, so here is the weapon I promised you.

final-dialogue.text: The Overseer presents you with an Abyssal Bludgeon.

final-dialogue.npc: You have served me well, it is good to see that you humans are still as gullible as ever!
Bringing me those body parts from the Sires has now granted me enough teleportation energy to leave this living hell hole. Perhaps I will pay your realm a visit and there will be much to harvest!

final-dialogue.player: Yuck! This is disgusting. What use is this? It's unwieldly!

final-dialogue.npc: Have you not learned yet, appearances can be deceiving. You hold in your hands a living weapon whose power is rivalled by few weapons from your world, use it wisely.
Do not think that I am ungrateful for my freedom human. I will leave you this ancient tome that will instruct you in creating more of these weapons in future.
Just use the three components on the book, and it will do the rest. You can get spare copies here any time you need.

steps.player: Thank you.

steps.npc: Farewell...

steps.text: The Overseer teleports away.

options.text: Perhaps I shall use it to slay you, demon.

steps.player: Perhaps I shall use it to slay you, demon.

steps.npc: So be it... I will await you on the fields of blood!

steps.text: The Overseer teleports away.

final-dialogue-speaking-to-it-again-afte.npc: You have served me well, it is good to see that you humans are still as gullible as ever!

final-dialogue-using-bludgeon-pieces-on-.npc: I do not require anything further from you, human.

the-king-s-little-dumpling-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Bolren
the-king-s-little-dumpling-talking-to-ki.text: Hello there. It's good to see you again.

the-king-s-little-dumpling-talking-to-ki.player: I see you have a new pet.
Dumpling? I suppose it looks a little bit like a dumpling...

the-king-s-little-dumpling-talking-to-ki.speaker: King Bolren
the-king-s-little-dumpling-talking-to-ki.text: Hey! Dumpling isn't evil. She has cute ears and a little bobbly tail!

the-king-s-little-dumpling-talking-to-ki.prompt: Start The Path of Glouphrie quest?

steps.player: Look at it! It's clearly evil. It has six legs!
And those eyes... those black, black eyes... If you stare into them, you can see into its black soul!
Ahem, anyway, that's not how I know this creature is evil. I've seen one before, and I'm afraid I have some bad news.

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: What are you on about?

steps.player: I came across some creatures like Dumpling at the Gnome Stronghold. They're evil things created using dark magic.
If this is anything like the situation at the Gnome Stronghold, then Dumpling was sent by Glouphrie to wheedle itself into your affections and spy on you.

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: You can't be serious!

steps.player: I'm afraid so. The creature is shrouded by illusion magic to make it look like a cute pet, but in reality it's this horrible... black spiky thing.
It's watching you all the time, sending details of all your secret dealings back to Glouphrie.

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: You've been listening to too many gnomish children's stories! Glouphrie hasn't been seen since before I was King. He's almost certainly long-dead by now.

steps.player: Well, what if I were to prove it to you? I unmasked the creatures at the Gnome Stronghold using a machine created by Oaknock the Engineer. Maybe I could do it again.

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: It's going to need to be very solid proof for me to just cast Dumpling aside. She's become my constant companion!

steps.player: Oh it will be solid. I just need an anti-illusion device... I don't suppose you have one of those around here?

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: I don't think so. What does one look like?

steps.player: A big machine made out of wood and crystal.

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: Crystal? As in elven crystal? I haven't seen any elven crystal around here since...

steps.player: Since?

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: Since Yewnock came to visit!

steps.player: Yewnock?

steps.speaker: King Bolren
steps.text: Oaknock's son, of course! He visited a long time ago, before I was even King. I remember he brought all sorts of strange things with him, including some elven crystals!

steps.player: So perhaps there's a device nearby. When he was here, where did Yewnock spend a lot of his time?

steps.speaker: King Bolren
