on-red-rock-talking-to-the-receptionist.text: Fantastic! The display cases in this room should have all the details you need. You'll want to start with the one directly to the right of the entrance and then work your way around, ending with the ones behind me.

on-red-rock-talking-to-the-receptionist.player: I'll do just that. Thank you.

on-red-rock-before-looking-at-all-four-d.speaker: Receptionist
on-red-rock-before-looking-at-all-four-d.text: Mr Paxton will be with you shortly. While you wait, may I recommend you use the display cases to familiarise yourself with our company?

on-red-rock-before-looking-at-all-four-d.speaker: Receptionist
on-red-rock-before-looking-at-all-four-d.text: You'll want to start with the one directly behind you and then work your way around, ending with the ones behind me.

on-red-rock-before-looking-at-all-four-d.player: I'll take a look. Thank you.

on-red-rock-after-looking-at-all-four-di.speaker: Receptionist
on-red-rock-after-looking-at-all-four-di.text: Mr Paxton will see you now. He's waiting in his office.

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.speaker: Theodore Paxton
on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.text: So, I hear you're someone who can solve problems?

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.speaker: Theodore Paxton
on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.text: Good. A pirate captain by the name of Black Eye Bethel has been attacking our ships. Our understanding is that she has a hideout at Last Light to the south of here.

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.speaker: Theodore Paxton
on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.text: Sail over there and put an end to her and her ships.

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.speaker: Theodore Paxton
on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton.text: Yes. Do well here and I might have more work for you. Now, if you have no further questions, I have a lot of work to do, so please be on your way.

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton-a.player: What did you need me to do again?

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton-a.speaker: Theodore Paxton
on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton-a.text: Black Eye Bethel has a hideout at Last Light to the south of here. Sail over there and put an end to her and her ships.

on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton-a.speaker: Theodore Paxton
on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-paxton-a.text: Now, if that's everything, I have a lot of work to do, so please be on your way.

the-pirates-of-last-light-when-approachi.text: As you approach the island, you spot some pirate boats circling.

the-pirates-of-last-light-sailing-away-f.text: You manage to sail away from the pirates, ending up somewhere [north/east/south/west] of Last Light.

the-pirates-of-last-light-after-sinking-.text: With the pirate boats sunk, you can now deal with the pirates on Last Light.

the-pirates-of-last-light-when-reaching-.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
the-pirates-of-last-light-when-reaching-.text: Looks like we've got some fresh meat!

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: Dodge this!

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: It's slashin' time!

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: You're done!

the-pirates-of-last-light-the-battle-aga.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
the-pirates-of-last-light-the-battle-aga.text: Let's see if you can handle this!
If the player does not have a dragon scimitar equipped:

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: I stole this one from a monkey!

the-pirates-of-last-light-the-battle-aga.text: If the player has a dragon scimitar equipped:

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: Nice scimitar! I've got one too!

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: No god can save you from me!

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: Fight me properly, coward!

steps.speaker: Black Eye Bethel
steps.text: Even praying won't help you now!

the-pirates-of-last-light-the-battle-aga.text: Your protection prayers have been disabled!

the-pirates-of-last-light-freeing-the-pa.text: You open the cage and free the parrot. It flies away, squawking happily as it does.

back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.speaker: Theodore Paxton
back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.text: Good. It's nice to have someone around who can get things done. Consider me impressed.

back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.player: Does that mean you have more work for me?

back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.speaker: Theodore Paxton
back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.text: Me? No. However, the boss has an issue that has been proving tricky to solve. I think you might be just the kind of person he needs.

back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.speaker: Theodore Paxton
back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.text: I'll let him be the one to tell you that. He's out doing some work in the middle of the Red Reef at the moment. Sail out there and find his ship, the Zenith. It's easy to spot, so you shouldn't miss it.

back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.player: What did you need me to do again?

back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.speaker: Theodore Paxton
back-on-red-rock-talking-to-theodore-pax.text: You've got a meeting with the boss. He's out doing some work in the middle of the Red Reef at the moment. Sail out there and find his ship, the Zenith. It's easy to spot, so you shouldn't miss it.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: Hello! Welcome! You must be our friend who has a knack for solving problems.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.player: That's right. [player name]. Pleased to meet you.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: The pleasure is all mine. As you've probably already guessed, I'm Spencer Brentwood, and this is the Zenith.
If the player doesn't have diving equipment on them:

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: The best. Now, tell me, [player name], do you dive?

steps.player: Dive?

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: Underwater. I have some coral dredgers in need of repair.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: If the player has diving equipment or a medallion of the deep on them:

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: The best. Now, [player name], I see you have some diving equipment, so I'm assuming you dive?

steps.player: Why do you ask?

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: I'm about to go diving myself. I have some coral dredgers in need of repair.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: Of course. It would be a poor leader who left all the work to their subordinates.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: A trait that is far too rare these days. More and more I find our work to be a beacon of light in this dark world.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: The future of humanity, of course. I've long believed our salvation lies beneath the waves. Indeed, I myself feel far more alive below the sea than above it. I'd be very keen to show you.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.player: Well, I suppose I can't say no to that.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: If the player doesn't have diving equipment on them:

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: Excellent! I have some diving gear here that you can use. Put it on and then let me know when you're ready.
Spencer gives you some diving equipment.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: If the player has diving equipment or a medallion of the deep equipped or on them:

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: Excellent! Get your diving equipment on and then let me know when you're ready.

steps.player: Will do.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-bre.text: If the player has no diving equipment and not enough inventory space:

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.text: If the player doesn't have diving equipment:

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: I have some diving gear here that you can use. Put it on and then let me know when you're ready.
Spencer gives you some diving equipment.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.text: If the player has diving equipment or a medallion of the deep in their inventory:

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.text: Get your diving equipment on and then let me know when you're ready.

steps.player: Will do.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.text: If the player is wearing diving equipment or a medallion of the deep:

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: Are you ready to go diving?

steps.player: Let's go.

options.text: I just need to sort something else out first.

steps.player: I just need to sort something else out first.

steps.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
steps.text: Very well.

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.text: If the player has no diving equipment and not enough inventory space:

aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
aboard-the-zenith-talking-to-spencer-aga.text: Shall we return to the seabed?

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: Beautiful down here, isn't it? It's sad to think that most people will never see the wonders that exist here, but hopefully they can still benefit from them all the same.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: And right here we have one of those many wonders...
Spencer reaches into the coral dredger and takes out some red coral.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: The stuff of dreams... Quite literally. We're at the point now where my whole company is built on this stuff, though truth be told, I don't consider it anywhere near as big of a wonder as others do.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: The mages claim this stuff grants them dreams of the future. We've been supplying it to them for years, but despite that, all their dreams remain nothing more than that.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: I'm not here to be a mere dreamer. I'm here to turn dreams into reality.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: I find wealth to often be so distracting, and yet it is a sad necessity. Most simply hoard it, but for those of us lucky enough to find success, I believe it is our duty to use that wealth for good.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: Red coral is lucrative... Very lucrative. I need the money it makes to continue my work in other areas. Ironically, without red coral, my dreams will never come true.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.player: And that's why I'm here? To help realise your dreams?

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: I have a complicated issue that must be solved. It may be that you are the one capable of doing so.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: If money is all you care for, then rest assured you will be paid handsomely. However, my hope for you, as with everyone I work with, is that you will also share in my dream as well.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.player: I'm open to that, given time.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: Wonderful! Sadly, the same can't be said for the sea life here. They are rather insistant on damaging these dredgers.

underwater-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer.text: We will discuss the nitty-gritty of the work I have for you later. First, let's get these fixed. I'll get this one sorted and then deal with the one to the east. Do you mind fixing the northern one?
Spencer fixes the coral dredger before moving on to the next one.

underwater-talking-to-spencer-again-befo.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-talking-to-spencer-again-befo.text: Have you sorted that dredger out yet?

underwater-talking-to-spencer-again-befo.player: Not yet. I'll get to it now.

underwater-repairing-the-dredger.text: The dredger is mostly in good order, but some pieces have become detached. You put them back into place again.

underwater-returning-to-spencer.player: That dredger is all sorted now.

underwater-returning-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
underwater-returning-to-spencer.text: Excellent! I'll just get this one finished, and then we can head back to the surface...
Spencer fixes the coral dredger and the two of you return to the surface.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: Right, let's get down to brass tacks shall we?

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: The job. It's a delicate situation, and I must admit it has already led to some regrettable circumstances. However, this work is essential.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: The Red Reef isn't as red as the name suggests. Despite our best attempts, we've reached a point where it can no longer supply the amount of red coral we need. A new source is needed.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.player: And you want me to find this source?

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: No need! We already have one. After some extensive searches, we found a large reef in the Pearl Bank that should nicely suit our purposes. Our issue instead revolves around the inhabitants of that area...

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: How familiar are you with tortugans?

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: A remarkable race, but they are sadly very stubborn and stuck in their ways. There is an island in the Pearl Bank of great importance to them. They'd never allow an operation like ours so close to it.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: Our attempts to remove them from the island haven't produced results so far. My hope is that you will have better luck. I'd like you to come up with a plan for removing the tortugans from the area.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: If possible, I would appreciate it if you could minimise bloodshed, but make no mistake, nothing can be off the table. The Pearl Bank must be acquired for the company. There can be no compromises.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.player: I understand. I will get to work at once.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.speaker: Spencer Brentwood
back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.text: Wonderful! Report to me at Red Rock once you have something. Until then, I wish you good luck.

back-on-the-surface-talking-to-spencer.player: Thank you. I'd best be on my way.

back-on-the-surface-attempting-to-board-.text: You have no reason to reboard the Zenith. You should return to the Great Conch instead.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.player: I did. You were right Floopa, the Red Reef Trading Company were responsible for the attack on the Little Pearl.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: I don't understand. Why would these humans have a problem with us?

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.player: They've found a reef near the island. They want to start dredging it for red coral, but they need you gone from the Little Pearl first.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Floopa
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Red coral? Of course! Spencer talks the good talk, but all he really cares about is money. Trusting him was the biggest mistake I ever made.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: So what do we do? How can we stop him?

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.player: We don't need to rush. I've gained Spencer's trust and he has tasked me with coming up with a plan for getting you off the Little Pearl. That means time is on our side.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Ah, I see! Time for us to come up with a plan of our own. Very good, [player name]! Very good!

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Yes, yes, we'll start right away. Keep checking in, [player name]. We'll let you know once we've come up with something.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: In the meantime, Floopa had a suggestion for a little way to thank you for all you've done for us.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Do you remember the camphor trees in the Sacred Grove? I've made some arrangements, and you now have permission to chop their wood. It's a much better place to do so than anywhere else on the island.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Oh, don't mention it. It's really no problem at all. You've been a good friend to us, [player name]. It means everything.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Floopa
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Yes, thank you, [player name]. I know I've been a bit... difficult in all of this, but even though I'm terrible at showing it, I really do appreciate everything you've done.

back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.speaker: Elder Raley
back-on-the-great-conch-talking-to-floop.text: Now, before you go I had something to give you that you might find useful.
If the player doesn't have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Elder Raley
steps.text: You don't seem to have space for it, come back when you do.

starting-out.speaker: Father Aereck
starting-out.text: Welcome to the church of holy Saradomin.

steps.player: I'm looking for a quest.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: That's lucky, I need someone to do a quest for me.

steps.prompt: Start The Restless Ghost quest?

steps.player: Okay, let me help then.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: Thank you. The problem is, there is a ghost in the church graveyard. I would like you to get rid of it.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: If you need any help, my friend Father Urhney is an expert on ghosts.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: I believe he is currently living as a hermit in Lumbridge swamp. He has a little shack in the far west of the swamps.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: Exit the graveyard through the south gate to reach the swamp. I'm sure if you told him that I sent you he'd be willing to help.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: My name is Father Aereck by the way. Pleased to meet you.

steps.player: Likewise.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: Take care travelling through the swamps, I have heard they can be quite dangerous.

steps.player: I will, thanks.
Sorry, I don't have time right now.

steps.speaker: Father Aereck
steps.text: Oh well. If you do have some spare time on your hands, come back and talk to me.

starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.speaker: Father Aereck
starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.text: Have you got rid of the ghost yet?

starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.player: I can't find Father Urhney at the moment.

starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.speaker: Father Aereck
starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.text: Well, you can get to the swamp he lives in by going south through the cemetery.

starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.speaker: Father Aereck
starting-out-talking-to-father-aereck-ag.text: You'll have to go right into the far western depths of the swamp, near the coastline. That is where his house is.

steps.player: Well, that's friendly.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: I SAID go AWAY.

steps.player: Okay, okay... sheesh, what a grouch.

options.text: Father Aereck sent me to talk to you.

steps.player: Father Aereck sent me to talk to you.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: I suppose I'd better talk to you then. What problems has he got himself into this time?

options.text: He's got a ghost haunting his graveyard.

steps.player: He's got a ghost haunting his graveyard.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Oh, the silly fool.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: I leave town for just five months, and ALREADY he can't manage.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: (sigh)

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Well, I can't go back and exorcise it. I vowed not to leave this place. Until I had done a full two years of prayer and meditation.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Tell you what I can do though; take this amulet.
Father Urhney hands you an amulet.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: It is an Amulet of Ghostspeak.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: So called, because when you wear it you can speak to ghosts. A lot of ghosts are doomed to be ghosts because they have left some important task uncompleted.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Maybe if you know what this task is, you can get rid of the ghost. I'm not making any guarantees mind you, but it is the best I can do right now.

steps.player: Thank you. I'll give it a try!

options.text: You mean he gets himself into lots of problems?

steps.player: You mean he gets himself into lots of problems?

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Yeah. For example, when we were trainee priests he kept on getting stuck up bell ropes.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Anyway. I don't have time for chitchat. What's his problem THIS time?

steps.player: He's got a ghost haunting his graveyard.

options.text: I've come to repossess your house.

steps.player: I've come to repossess your house.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Under what grounds???

steps.player: Repeated failure on mortgage repayments.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: But... I don't have a mortgage! I built this house myself!

steps.player: Sorry. I must have got the wrong address. All the houses look the same around here.

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: What? What houses? What ARE you talking about???

steps.player: Never mind.

options.text: I don't know. I just wanted this house.

steps.player: I don't know. I just wanted this house...

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Oh... go away and stop wasting my time!

talking-to-father-urhney-talking-to-fath.speaker: Father Aereck
talking-to-father-urhney-talking-to-fath.text: Have you got rid of the ghost yet?

talking-to-father-urhney-talking-to-fath.player: I had a talk with Father Urhney. He has given me this funny amulet to talk to the ghost with.

talking-to-father-urhney-talking-to-fath.speaker: Father Aereck
talking-to-father-urhney-talking-to-fath.text: I always wondered what that amulet was... Well, I hope it's useful. Tell me when you get rid of the ghost!

options.text: I've lost the Amulet of Ghostspeak.

steps.player: I've lost the Amulet of Ghostspeak.

steps.text: Father Urhney signs.
If they player currently has it in their inventory:

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: What are you talking about? I can see you've got it with you!
If the amulet if stored in a bank, Death's Office, Item Retrieval Service:

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: You come here wasting my time... Has it even occurred to you that you've got it stored somewhere? Now GO AWAY!
If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: How careless can you get? Those things aren't easy to come by you know! Now clear some space in your inventory and I'll give you another one.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: How careless can you get? Those things aren't easy to come by you know! It's a good job I've got a spare.
Father Urhney hands you an amulet.
ghostspeak amulet

steps.speaker: Father Urhney
steps.text: Be more careful this time.

steps.player: Okay, I'll try to be.

options.text: I've come to repossess your house.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-opening-th.text: If the player opens the coffin:

steps.text: You open the coffin.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-opening-th.text: If the player attempts to search the coffin after opening it:

steps.text: There's a skeleton without a skull in here.

steps.player: Ooh, THAT'S interesting.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Woo wooo. Woooooooooooooooooo!

steps.player: Did he really?

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Woo.

options.text: My brother had EXACTLY the same problem.

steps.player: My brother had EXACTLY the same problem.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Woo Wooooo!

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Wooooo Woo woo woo!

options.text: You'll have to give me the recipe some time...

steps.player: You'll have to give me the recipe some time...

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Wooooooo woo woooooooo.

options.text: Hmm... I'm not so sure about that.

steps.player: Yeah, that's what I thought.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Wooo woooooooooooooo...

steps.player: Goodbye. Thanks for the chat.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Wooo wooo?

options.text: Hmm I'm not sure about that.
Any hints where I can find some treasure?

steps.player: Any hints where I can find some treasure?

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Wooooooo woo! Wooooo woo wooooo woowoowoo woo Woo wooo. Wooooo woo woo? Woooooooooooooooooo!

options.text: Thank you. You've been very helpful.

steps.player: Thank you. You've been very helpful.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Wooooooo.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-while-wear.speaker: Restless ghost
talking-to-the-restless-ghost-while-wear.text: Did you just understand what I said???

options.text: Yep, now tell me what the problem is.

steps.player: Yep, now tell me what the problem is.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: WOW! This is INCREDIBLE! I didn't expect anyone to ever understand me again!

steps.player: Ok, Ok, I can understand you!
But have you any idea WHY you're doomed to be a ghost?

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Well, to be honest... I'm not sure.

steps.player: I've been told a certain task may need to be completed so you can rest in peace.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: I should think it is probably because a warlock has come along and stolen my skull. If you look inside my coffin there, you'll find my corpse without a head on it.

steps.player: Do you know where this warlock might be now?

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: I think it was one of the warlocks who lives in the big tower by the sea south-west from here.

steps.player: Ok. I will try and get the skull back for you, then you can rest in peace.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Ooh, thank you. That would be such a great relief!

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: It is so dull being a ghost...

options.text: No, you sound like you're speaking nonsense to me.

steps.player: No, you sound like you're speaking nonsense to me.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Oh that's a pity. You got my hopes up there.

steps.player: Yeah, it is a pity. Sorry about that.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Hang on a second... you CAN understand me!

steps.player: No I can't.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Great. The first person I can speak to in ages...and they're a moron.

steps.player: Yep, clever aren't I?

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: I'm impressed. You must be very powerful. I don't suppose you can stop me being a ghost?

options.text: Yes, ok. Do you know WHY you're a ghost?

steps.player: Yes, ok. Do you know WHY you're a ghost?

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Nope. I just know I can't do much of anything like this!

steps.player: No, you're scary!

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Great.

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: The first person I can speak to in ages...

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: ..and they're an idiot.

steps.player: Wow, this amulet works!

steps.speaker: Restless ghost
steps.text: Oh! It's your amulet that's doing it! I did wonder. I don't suppose you can help me? I don't like being a ghost.

options.text: Yes, ok. Do you know why you're a ghost?

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.speaker: Restless ghost
talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.text: How are you doing finding my skull?

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.player: Sorry, I can't find it at the moment.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.speaker: Restless ghost
talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.text: I'm pretty sure it's somewhere in the tower south-west from here. There's a lot of levels to the tower, though. I suppose it might take a little while to find.

options.text: Any hints where I can find some treasure?

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-searching-.text: There's a skeleton without a skull in here.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.speaker: Father Aereck
talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.text: Have you got rid of the ghost yet?

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.player: I've found out that the ghost's corpse has lost its skull. If I can find the skull, the ghost should leave.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.speaker: Father Aereck
talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.text: Hmmmmm. Well, I haven't seen any skulls.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-talking-to.player: Yes, I think a warlock has stolen it.

talking-to-the-restless-ghost-searching-.text: The skeleton in the corner suddenly comes to life!

after-retrieving-the-skull-searching-the.text: You already have the Ghost's skull.

after-retrieving-the-skull-trying-to-dro.text: Dropping this skull here will destroy it!

after-retrieving-the-skull-trying-to-dro.prompt: Are you sure you want to drop the skull?

after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-fa.speaker: Father Aereck
after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-fa.text: Have you got rid of the ghost yet?

after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-fa.player: I've finally found the ghost's skull!

after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-fa.speaker: Father Aereck
after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-fa.text: Great! Put it in the ghost's coffin and see what happens!

after-retrieving-the-skull-inspecting-th.text: It's the skull of the ghost that is haunting Lumbridge graveyard. Maybe I should return this back to the ghost's coffin.

after-retrieving-the-skull-using-the-sku.text: Maybe I should open it first.

after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-th.speaker: Restless ghost
after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-th.text: How are you doing finding my skull?

after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-th.speaker: Restless ghost
after-retrieving-the-skull-talking-to-th.text: Hurrah! Now I can stop being a ghost! You just need to put it in my coffin there, then I'll be free!

after-retrieving-the-skull-using-the-sku.text: I can't give it to him. It goes right through him.

after-retrieving-the-skull-using-the-sku.speaker: Restless ghost
after-retrieving-the-skull-using-the-sku.text: If you just put it in my coffin that should do the trick...

after-retrieving-the-skull-searching-the.text: There's a nice and complete skeleton in here!
Surprisingly, this altar is empty. Probably because you took the skull off it earlier.

2NjIE_.player: Hmm... I'm not so sure about that.
Ah well, better be off now...

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.text: You! I bet you're with them!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.player: Frogs? What are you on about?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.text: Ah, I see. So you're going to play dumb are you? Well, be gone! I won't fall for your lies!
You do not meet all of the requirements to start The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute quest.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-without.text: Hey! I didn't say you could touch my farming patch, did I?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus.text: You! I bet you're with them!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus.prompt: Start The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute quest?

steps.player: Frogs? What are you on about?

steps.speaker: Marcellus
steps.text: Ah, I see. So you're going to play dumb are you? Well I won't fall for your lies!

steps.player: I promise I have no idea what you're on about. If you explain, maybe I can help you?

steps.speaker: Marcellus
steps.text: It's those frogs on the other side of the oasis! They're out to get us! All of us! If someone doesn't kill them all, we'll be living our lives as their slaves!

steps.player: I see... How about I head over there and take a look?

steps.speaker: Marcellus
steps.text: You want to go near them? Well then you're a fool! I will watch from a safe distance as they dine on your corpse!

steps.player: Okay then... Well provided that doesn't happen, I'll be back shortly to let you know what I've found.

options.quest: The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute

steps.player: I think I'm just going to go now. You clearly have some... issues that you need to get on top of.

steps.speaker: Marcellus
steps.text: That's it! You walk away! Just remember, I know the truth!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-talking.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-talking.text: You didn't go near those frogs yet, did you?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-talking.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-talking.text: I can tell. If you had, you'd be dead!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-talking.player: Okay then... Well assuming that I survive, I'll be back shortly to let you know what I've found.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Frog
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Oh, hello there.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Frog
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Well of course we can talk, silly. Why wouldn't we be able to?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: Well I guess I'd just never considered it before...

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Frog
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: We live in a world where giant lizards with wings fly around and expel highly combustible fluids from their throats, but you never considered a frog could talk?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: Well when you put it like that...

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Frog
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Well now that we've established our remarkable linguistic capabilities, how about some introductions. I'm Sue and this is Gary. Over there you have Dave and Jane, and good old Mr Lonesome over there is Cuthbert.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: Pleased to meet you. I'm [player name].

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Well, [player name], what can we do for you?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: Well there's a guy over there that thinks you're all evil.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Evil? We're not evil! We're just on strike.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: We're on strike. Fair work requires fair treatment, and we've had enough of his nonsense.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: But... What do you do? What are you striking from?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Oh... Well I can't really remember. It's been so long that I've gone and totally forgotten. Hey, Gary, why are we on strike?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Gary
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: No idea. I've been on strike my whole life, just like my pa, and his pa before him. At this point it's kind of a family tradition.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Gary
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: I know it's because of him though. That monster spends every day mistreating us. If he ever wants to see any work from us, he needs to start showing some basic respect.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Too right, Gary, too right. What reason does he have for thinking we're evil anyway?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Gary
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Well he's one of them capitalists, isn't he. They see a worker demanding fair rights and they go loopy. Can't have anything getting in the way of their profit margins!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: Actually, he never mentioned anything about work. He seems to think you're out to overthrow humanity.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Overthrow humanity? What a load of nonsense! We love humans! Gary here had one as a pet once.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Gary
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Ah, those were the days. I always loved my Sentia. Such a shame about the accident...

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: It wasn't your fault, Gary. It wasn't your fault. Anyway, if this chap thinks we're plotting to overthrow humanity, what's he planning to do about it?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: I'm not too sure. He did mention at one point something about killing you all...

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: He wants to what?!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Gary
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: He wants to kill us?! Well now I think we should overthrow humanity!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Yeah, we've been treated like second class citizens for too long. The revolution starts today!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Peace? Interesting... I suppose peace could be fun. There would need to be some assurances though. Wouldn't want the guy going back on his word.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.player: Right... Well how about I go and ask him what conditions he'd be willing to accept.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs.text: Well that just sounds swell!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.text: Hello again! Have you found out what peace conditions the grumpy guts has?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.speaker: Sue
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.text: Well don't go taking too long.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.speaker: Cuthbert
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.text: I hear you're the one handling the peace talks. You will fail. There is no peace to be had with that man.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.player: Well I'd still like to give it a good go.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.speaker: Dave
crazy-frogs-talking-to-the-blue-frogs-ta.text: Hello there! You're the one sorting out the peace talks, right?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: The frogs didn't kill you? This is unexpected.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Well I had a chat with them, and they're open to engaging in some peace talks.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Peace? The hypocrisy! After everything they've done they think peace is an option? Absolutely not!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Okay... But what exactly have they done that means peace isn't an option?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Look, I can't remember. But they must have done something!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Yes I'm starting to think that's where the problem lies as well.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: They must have taken my brain! That's why I can't remember! You tell them I want my brain back!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: So you'd be willing to negotiate peace in exchange for your... brain?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Negotiate? I don't negotiate with monsters!

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: I don't think they're monsters. They actually seem somewhat friendly.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Well do they have a leader?

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Well you go tell them that I'll only negotiate with their leader.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Every day I find myself further questioning my life choices. Fine. I'll go and ask them about their leader.

crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
crazy-frogs-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: I'm only going to negotiate with the leader of those monsters. You go tell them that!

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Hello again! Have you found out what peace conditions the grumpy guts has?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Sort of. He seems open to the idea of peace talks, but he will only negotiate with your leader. Do you have a leader?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Oh, well not really.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Nah, we're more about collective leadership. We did consider starting a union at one point, but Dave messed up the paperwork.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Well would you be interested in having a leader?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: A change to our political structure? That's quite the thing to undergo.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Yeah, especially in times of war. Still, maybe we need to mix things up. We've been saying for a while now that we've been stagnating. Perhaps this is just the thing we need.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: There would need to be an election of course.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Do you have a process for that sort of thing?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Absolutely! We use a first past the post system where everyone votes based on a candidate's hopping capabilities.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Oh it's all very simple. The candidates perform their finest hop and everyone else votes on which they thought was best. The one with the most votes wins!

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: I see. Well, I don't, but for the sake of my sanity, let's say I do. Shall we call an election then?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Sounds like a wonderful idea! There is just the small matter of Cuthbert...

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: That's right. You see, while you were gone, we told the others about this whole killing us all business. Now, I must admit, emotions did run a bit high, especially for Cuthbert.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Once he learns about the election, he will almost definitely want to put himself forward, and I'm afraid he has little interest in peace.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: I mean, can you blame the guy? Cuthbert was once the leader of the Frogs for Humanity society. The guy loved humans, but after what they did to his favourite plant...

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Some wounds never heal...

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: So you're saying Cuthbert can't win the election?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: The idea of rigging an election is one that fills my democracy-loving heart with terror, but yes, we will need to do that.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: It's okay if we're the ones to do it, right?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Not in the slightest, but I do love that positive attitude. Besides, the alternative is all-out war with humanity.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Which we very much need to avoid! So how do we ensure Cuthbert can't win the election?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: The hop-off will see the candidates hop from the shore to a lily pad. Now, if Cuthbert's lily pad had an unfortunate hole in it...

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Okay... I guess I'm off to sabotage a lily pad.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Just be careful of Dave and Jane. They're sticklers for the rules, I'm afraid. You can't let them see you.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Hello again! How are things going with that lily pad sabotage?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Just be careful of Dave and Jane. They're sticklers for the rules, I'm afraid. You can't let them see you.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-cuthbert.speaker: Cuthbert
democracy-at-work-talking-to-cuthbert.text: It seems we are to have an election. Know that once I win, our war with humanity will be unlike anything ever seen.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-cuthbert.speaker: Cuthbert
democracy-at-work-talking-to-cuthbert.text: You should go. Go and be with your loved ones. Hold them close while you can. Soon you will never have that luxury again.

democracy-at-work-attempting-to-sabotage.speaker: Jane
democracy-at-work-attempting-to-sabotage.text: Hey, don't be going near those lily pads. We've got them all set up ready for the hop-off.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Dave
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: Hello there! Have you heard about the election? Isn't it thrilling?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.player: That is definitely a word that could be used to describe this situation. Anyway, speaking of the election, I need to inspect the lily pads.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Jane
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: No can do. We've got them all set up nicely. Can't be letting anyone mess things up, can we?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.player: Of course not, but don't you think it would be wise for a third party just to give them a quick once over? Besides, the two of you deserve a break.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Dave
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: Well I really could do with a bit of a rest, not to mention the fact that I'm starving. Still, the lily pads are our duty. It would be wrong of us to let someone else touch them.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.player: Hmm... You said you were hungry? Out of interest, what would you fancy? For when the election is out of the way, of course.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Jane
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: Oh I'd kill for a nice tasty orange!

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.player: An orange? I didn't know frogs ate oranges...

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Dave
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: Yeah most people think we just eat flies. We do, and we love them, but sometimes you find that you've just had enough flies and fancy something more exotic.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.player: Where do you get your oranges?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Jane
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: They grow on trees around here, like this one right next to us. From time to time an orange will fall off, but the really good ones are the ones at the top.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Dave
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: Just a shame we can't reach those ones...

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.player: Remind me, where do you get your oranges?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Jane
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: They grow on trees around here, like this one right next to us. From time to time an orange will fall off, but the really good ones are the ones at the top.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.speaker: Dave
democracy-at-work-talking-to-dave-or-jan.text: Just a shame we can't reach those ones...

democracy-at-work-after-chopping-down-th.speaker: Dave
democracy-at-work-after-chopping-down-th.text: Can't stop to talk! There's oranges to be had!

democracy-at-work-sabotaging-the-lily-pa.text: You pick up a small stone from the shore and throw it at the lily pad. It leaves a barely noticeable hole in it.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Hello again! How are things going with that lily pad sabotage?

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: And just in time as well. The hop-off is about to begin.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Sue of course!

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Don't worry. Once I win, I'll make sure these peace talks go nice and smoothly.

democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
democracy-at-work-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Let's!

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.text: A cutscene starts. All the frogs and capybara gather by the water.

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.text: Welcome, one and all, to what is bound to be a thrilling frog hop-off! The stakes are high for this one, and indeed the future of our entire world may well be at stake.

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.text: Our first contender for today is Sue! Let's see what she's got!
Sue hops onto the lily pad.

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.text: What a corker of a hop! Excellent work!
Cuthbert hops onto the lily pad, but sinks into the water. A brief pause ensues.

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.text: Yeah, totally slipped my mind, but he never learnt how to swim!

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.player: A frog that never learnt to swim? Are you serious right now?!

democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.speaker: Gary
democracy-at-work-watching-the-frog-hop-.text: Afraid so! Cuthbert is now as dead as an Old One. With only one contender left standing, I can now announce that Sue is the winner!

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Well now that's all sorted, we can get these peace talks underway!

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: I can't believe we killed him...

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Ah, don't worry yourself. Something like this was bound to happen at some point. It's his fault really. Imagine never learning to swim!

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Exactly! So what does our foe want?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: He thinks you've stolen his brain and would like it back.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: His brain? But we don't have his brain...

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Well is there anything else you can offer him?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: It's not like we really do much. We're frogs. All we do is eat flies, along with the odd orange.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: Well maybe we can still work with that. I'm sure our friend doesn't like flies. Maybe you could deal with the flies around here for him?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Sounds like a job for us! Though we'd of course need something in return.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Fair pay for fair work, of course. If not, we'll go on strike! We're good at going on strike.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: And how would you like to be paid?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Well normally I'd say in flies, but it seems we've got that covered.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.text: Oh, and orange juice as well! Straight from the tap!

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue.player: From the tap? But orange juice doesn't...
Actually, never mind. Let's not complicate things further. I'll take these terms to him and see what he says.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.text: Hello! How go the peace talks?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.text: Remember, we kill flies, we get oranges. That's the deal.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.speaker: Dave
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.text: Can you believe Cuthbert died? Such a shame.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.speaker: Jane
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.text: Sue will be a great leader though. I can't wait to see what she does first!

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Have you found the leader of those frogs? I'm only going to negotiate with the leader!

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Yes, the frogs have selected a leader and she has sent me with her terms.
The frogs will kill the flies around the oasis and in return they'd like you to pay them in oranges.

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Flies? But what have the flies done wrong?

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Well don't they spread disease and eat your food?

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Yes, but so did my brother, and I never wanted him dead. What else have the flies been doing?

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: I don't know! You seemed convinced the frogs were out to get you before, maybe the flies are as well!

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: The flies are out to get me? Is it really true?

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: You know what, sure. The flies want you dead and they plan to do it tonight.
So are you willing to make this deal with the frogs?

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Not yet. First I must see proof of this horrific betrayal by the flies. Find this proof for me, and I will agree to the deal.

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.player: Maybe my whole life is just one big nightmare. Fine, I'll find this proof.

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: You're back. Do you have the proof?

peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-talking-to-marcellus-after-t.text: Then return to me once you have it.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.text: Hello! How go the peace talks?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.player: He's open to the proposals, but he wants proof that the flies are against him.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.text: He doesn't half complain, does he? Maybe it would have just been easier to kill him...

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.text: How about you steal a prized possession of his and plant it on the flies.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.player: Oh good, now we're adding theft to today's crimes.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.text: Well it could be worse. It could be murder!

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.text: Nah, that wasn't murder! Manslaughter at best! Or would that be frogslaughter...

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-2.text: It had to be done. Now, why don't you go and find something to steal.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.text: Hello! Did you find something to steal?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-talki.text: Keep looking. I'm sure you'll find something suitable.

peace-talks-searching-marcellus-bed.text: If the player is already holding the love letter:

steps.text: You search the bed, but find nothing of interest.

peace-talks-searching-marcellus-bed.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You search the bed and find a love letter, but you don't have enough room to take it.

peace-talks-searching-marcellus-bed.text: You search the bed and find a love letter.

peace-talks-unlocking-marcellus-chest.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You unlock the chest and find a plushy inside, but you don't have enough room to take it.

peace-talks-unlocking-marcellus-chest.text: You unlock the chest and find a plushy inside.

peace-talks-opening-the-chest-after-unlo.text: If the player already has the plushy:

steps.text: You already have the plushy from this chest.

peace-talks-opening-the-chest-after-unlo.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: You open the chest and find a plushy inside, but you don't have enough room to take it.

peace-talks-opening-the-chest-after-unlo.text: You open the chest and find a plushy inside.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-with-.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-with-.text: Hello! Did you find something to steal?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-with-.player: Yes, I have a plushy here of his.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-with-.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-with-.text: Perfect! Shove it in that big pile of dung the flies keep gathering around and then go and let him know.

peace-talks-planting-without-evidence.text: You don't have anything suitable to plant here.

peace-talks-attempting-to-plant-the-lett.text: While the letter has potential, you feel like you need something even better to plant here.

peace-talks-planting-the-plushy.text: You place the plushy right in the middle of the dung.

peace-talks-planting-the-plushy.speaker: Cuthbert, Lord of Dread
peace-talks-planting-the-plushy.text: You! Prepare to face the Lord of Dread!

peace-talks-opening-the-chest-after-plan.text: You search the chest, but find nothing of interest.

peace-talks-talking-to-dave-jane-or-marc.text: You should first deal with Cuthbert, Lord of Dread.

peace-talks-cuthbert-killing-the-player.speaker: Cuthbert
peace-talks-cuthbert-killing-the-player.text: I have come for you, [player name].

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-befor.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-befor.text: Hello! How goes the planting of evidence?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-befor.player: It's all done, but I do now have a little problem to deal with. I'll be back.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.text: Hello! How goes the planting of evidence?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.text: Well what are you waiting for? Time to go and let him know!

peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.text: You're back. Do you have the proof?

peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.player: I think I do. You see that big pile of dung the flies are gathered around? I'm sure I saw something belonging to you in it.

peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.text: It cannot be?! Wait here! I must check at once!
The screen briefly fades to black.
Marcellus goes to check on the dung...

peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.text: I see my worst fears have come to pass. This is dark day not just for me, but for all of humanity.

peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.text: Return to the frogs. Tell them we have a deal.

peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.speaker: Marcellus
peace-talks-telling-marcellus-of-the-evi.text: Leave me. I need time to contemplate this great loss. Return to the frogs. Tell them we have a deal.

peace-talks-talking-to-dave-or-jane.speaker: Dave
peace-talks-talking-to-dave-or-jane.text: I hear the peace talks are going well. We might be close to ending the conflict with that nasty human.

peace-talks-talking-to-dave-or-jane.speaker: Jane
peace-talks-talking-to-dave-or-jane.text: I do hope so. This war is starting to take a toll on all of us. We had to start rationing the oranges!

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.player: I have good news! The terms have been accepted.
Oh, and it turns out Cuthbert was still alive after all.
Er... no. He's now properly dead.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.text: War always has casualties. We will forever remember Cuthbert's sacrifice.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.text: Well said! Today will be a day remembered by all of frog-kind, and much of it is thanks to you, [player name].

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.player: Thanks. I only wish I had the ability to scrub the memories of all this from my brain, but as I can't, I guess I now have to carry them forever.

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.speaker: Gary
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.text: Have you tried soap and water?

peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.speaker: Sue
peace-talks-talking-to-gary-or-sue-after.text: Oh don't be so negative. You've done a good thing, [player name]! Now go. Go with the blessing of the frogs, and know that you really are a true hero!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-marcellus.speaker: Marcellus
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-marcellus.text: Hello again. You helped forge my alliance with the frogs against those disgusting flies. Please feel free to use my farming patch in return. It's the least I can do.

options.text: Would you look after my crops for me?
Can you give me any farming advice?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-gary-or-s.player: Hello again. How are things going?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-gary-or-s.speaker: Gary
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-gary-or-s.text: Amazing! We get paid to eat all day, and our payment is more food. Life has never been better!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-gary-or-s.speaker: Sue
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-gary-or-s.text: Too right, Gary! This is much better than being on strike!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dave-or-j.speaker: Dave
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dave-or-j.text: Today is a good day to be a frog!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dave-or-j.speaker: Jane
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dave-or-j.text: It sure is. Now that we have peace, life is at an all time high!

steps.player: Hello? Can you hear me up there?

steps.npc: I hear you, young one. Care to talk? I have a lot of time on my hands.

steps.player: What happened to you? Why are you trapped in a cage?

steps.npc: Hmm. I find myself ruminating on this very question. What happened to me?
Perhaps it is best to ask Yama this question. He will have a stronger opinion than I do.

steps.player: Do you not know?

steps.npc: I see the events from my perspective, but this does not guarantee truth or an accurate answer.
There is little value in tall tales.

steps.player: Are you okay in there?

steps.npc: Indeed. These bars keep me well away from those fiendish little imps.

steps.player: That's your biggest concern?

steps.npc: Not quite. The recent course of events has surprised me. This is not what I had planned for but I will make the best of it.

options.text: Can I help you at all?

steps.player: Can I help you at all?

steps.npc: Help me? You believe me in need of help? Do you think freedom is some precious thing to me? Vengeance perhaps?

steps.player: Well, do you want vengeance?

steps.npc: What I would like is for this league to proceed as outlined.
Go forth! Play your part.

steps.player: Aren't you worried about what will happen to you?

steps.npc: Of course, yet the games go on. Unpleasant circumstances and the volatile beasts that surround me are simply facts I must accept - for now.

steps.player: Goodbye.

steps.npc: Farewell.

steps.prompt: What would you like to ask about?

steps.player: So... what do I do here, in Grid Master?

steps.npc: Complete the Grid of course.

steps.text: Complete various challenges within the Grid Master interface.
To earn powerful rewards for Grid Master, and Grid Points for Main Game Cosmetics.
You can view the Grid Master interface by selecting it's Orb
If the player does not have any items to reclaim:

steps.npc: It doesn't look like you need any Grid Master items right now. I'll be here if you ever do.

steps.text: If the player has one items to reclaim:
You receive an item from the Sage.
If the player has multiple items to reclaim:
You receive some items from the Sage.

standard-dialogue.npc: Hello mortal. What do you seek?

options.text: What changes have been made for this League?

steps.player: What changes have been made for this League?

steps.npc: Much has happened since the last passage of the Trailblazers. This time, I have awakened the wrathful spirits of enemies across Gielinor.
Each region now contains a Raging Echo boss. These bosses are more powerful versions of their original self that drop unique rewards.
To help you overcome these new challenges, you may now gain power through Combat Masteries, which you can obtain access to by completing the Combat Mastery tasks.
As before, you'll initially be restricted to the Regions of Misthalin and Karamja. However, as you progress, you'll be able to unlock new areas of your choosing.
Be warned though - you won't be able to unlock every area, so choose wisely.
You must participate as an Ironman. This means you stand alone and cannot trade with other participants.
And that's not all. Training skills during the League will grant you substantially more experience than you'd normally expect.
These experience increases are known as passive effects, which get more generous the higher your Relic tier.
Finally, some quests have been completed for you automatically. Further quests and more will be completed as you unlock the relevant areas.
I think that covers the basics. Would you like to know more, [player name]?

steps.player: Yes, please.
Not right now.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Can you tell me about Combat Masteries?

steps.player: Can you tell me about Combat Masteries?

steps.npc: Combat Masteries are powerful boons granted by me that enhance your combat abilities for the entire League.
After all, it wouldn't be very interesting to ask you to defeat the enemies' raging echoes without allowing you to draw on your own.
You can obtain them by completing specific combat tasks to prove yourself to me.
Combat Masteries are split into the three combat styles: Ranged, Melee, and Mage. To unlock each mastery, you must have unlocked the previous mastery for that style.
There are 6 combat masteries for each style, but only 10 mastery points can be obtained. Once you have selected a mastery there is no going back, so choose your masteries wisely.
Now, would you like to take a look at the Combat Masteries available to you?

steps.player: Yes, please.
Not right now.

steps.npc: Fair enough. Is there anything else you need from me?

steps.player: How do tasks work?

steps.npc: In every League, there are a number of tasks for you to complete. Each task has a level of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.
Completing tasks allows you to access new areas. The more tasks you complete, the more areas become available to unlock.
Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.

steps.player: What do these points do?

steps.npc: Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Relic of mine. These are powerful artefacts to help you in this world.
League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.

steps.text: As we speak, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.player: So how many tasks are there?

steps.npc: More than you'll ever be able to complete, most likely. It's up to you which ones you attempt.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.npc: Now, would you like to take a look at the tasks for this League?

steps.player: Yes, please.
Not right now.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: How does the area system work?

steps.player: How does the area system work?

steps.npc: Currently, you are restricted to the Kingdom of Misthalin and the island of Karamja. However, as you progress, you can unlock more areas.
There are eleven different areas in total. However, you can only unlock a maximum of five, including the two you've started with. Choose wisely.
I give the first two area unlocks to everyone. You can unlock the other three by completing the tasks I've set.
The more tasks you complete, the more areas you can unlock.

steps.player: I see. Thanks!

steps.npc: Would you like to take a look at the available areas now?

steps.player: Yes, please.
Not right now.

steps.npc: Fair enough. Is there anything else you need from me?

steps.player: What are Relics?

steps.npc: Relics are powerful artefacts made by me that grant unique abilities for the entire League.
You may even recognise a few from Leagues past.
There are 23 separate Relics, split across 8 different tiers. You can only have one Relic from each tier, however.
The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points.
League Points are earned by completing tasks.
Once you have selected a Relic, your choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.
Would you like to take a look at the Relics for this League?

steps.player: Yes, please.
Not right now.

steps.npc: Very well. Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Can I claim some Combat rewards?

steps.player: Can I claim some combat achievement rewards?

steps.npc: You do not appear to have any combat achievement rewards available to claim.

options.text: Could I buy a max cape off you?
options.condition: If the player has a total level of 2,277:

steps.text: If the player does not have at least two free inventory spaces:

steps.npc: You don't have enough room.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have at least 2,277,000 coins in their inventory:

steps.npc: You don't have enough gold.

steps.text: If the player has at least 2,277,000 coins in their inventory and at least two free inventory spaces:

steps.prompt: Buy Max Cape for 2277000 gold?

steps.text: (Player loses 2,277,000 coins.)
a max cape and max hood

steps.npc: There you go. Congratulations, even if it may have been accelerated with my power, it's still a real accomplishment.

steps.player: I have some more questions.
Tell me about League rewards.

steps.npc: As well as letting you unlock new areas, completing tasks in the League will earn you League Points. The more League Points you have, the more Relic tiers you have available.
However, alongside allowing you to unlock Relics, League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.

steps.player: What rewards can I buy?

steps.npc: Oh, all sorts of things. New cosmetic kits, an alternative Home Teleport animation, some rather stylish outfits... and much more.
Many of these rewards can be traded with your fellow mortals, so if you wish, you can earn some money by selling them on. Of course, you might prefer to keep them for yourself instead.

steps.player: I see. That all sounds good to me.

steps.text: Currently, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be used to buy items on your main profile, although you can still browse the shop within the League.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.npc: You can use this shop to buy previous League rewards, too.
Alongside the rewards in the Leagues Reward Shop, there's also League Ranks.

steps.player: League Ranks? How do they work?

steps.npc: During the League as you gain more points you will gain a League Rank. This rank can be seen in the Ranks interface.
You currently have the rank: [rank].
As you get ranks you will gain access to trophies.

steps.player: Trophies?

steps.npc: That's right. Trophies are items that are awarded to you for competing in the League. You can use them to show off your League Rank.
Connected to League Ranks are the League to League rewards. These are unlocked in the next League based upon the League Rank you earn in this one.
League Starter Outfits and League Icons are some of things you can unlock for the next League. In addition, any pets you earn in this League will transfer over to the next one.
Finally, on top of the tasks for this League, there are some other activities for which I will recognise the first person who completes them.
You can view the entire list of activities, as well as whether or not someone has completed them, by reading the board beside me.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.npc: My pleasure. Now, is there anything else you need from me?

steps.player: Let's talk about pets.
Can you tell me how pets work in Leagues?

steps.npc: But of course. If you're lucky enough to obtain a pet during a League, it will automatically be insured for you.
This means that if you lose it somehow you can talk to me and I'll give it back to you. Insurance and reclaiming is all free of charge.
Additionally, each pet you obtain will be transferred to the next League. I'll take good care of it until you're ready to reclaim it.

steps.player: Okay! Thank you.

steps.npc: Come back to me once you have some pets and you can view your collection. Now, is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Do I have any League items to collect?
