steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: You need to what?

steps.player: I need to service your chest?

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: There's nothing wrong with the chest, it's fine, now get out!

options.text: I'm here to take your plans, hand them over now or I'll kill you!

steps.player: Prepare to die!

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: I'll teach you a lesson!

options.text: All the slaves have broken free!

steps.player: All the slaves have broken free!

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Don't talk rubbish, the warning siren isn't sounding. Now state your business before I have you thrown out.

options.text: I'm here to take your plans, hand them over now or I'll kill you!
The guard downstairs said you were lonely.
I need to service your chest.

steps.player: Fire! Fire!

steps.text: If Captain Siad is successfully distracted:
The captain seems distracted with what you just said. The captain looks out of the window to see if there is a fire.

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Where's the fire? I don't see any fire? Stop messing me around and state your business!

options.text: It's down in the lower mines, sound the alarm!

steps.player: It's down in the lower mines, sound the alarm!

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: You go and sound the alarm, I can't see anything wrong with the mine. Have you seen the fire yourself?

steps.player: Yes actually!

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Well, why didn't you raise the alarm?

options.text: I don't know where the alarm is.

steps.player: I don't know where the alarm is.

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: That's the most ridiculous thing I've heard. Who are you? Where do you come from? It doesn't matter... Guards! Show this person out!

options.text: I was so concerned for your safety that I rushed to save you.

steps.player: I was so concerned for your safety that I rushed to save you.

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Well, that's very good of you. But as you can see, I am very fine and well thanks! Now, please leave so that I can get back to my work.
The Captain goes back to his desk.

options.text: Er, no, one of the slaves told me.

steps.player: Er, no, one of the slaves told me.

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Well... you can't believe them, they're all a bunch of convicts. Anyway, it doesn't look as if there is a fire down there. So I'm going to get on with my work. Please remove yourself from my office.

options.text: Oh yes, you're right, they must have put it out!

steps.player: Oh yes, you're right, they must have put it out!

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Good, now perhaps you can leave me in peace? After all I do have some work to do.

steps.player: Er, yes okay then.

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: Good! Please remove yourself from my office.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-searching-captain-.text: You search the captains desk while he's not looking..
If the player already has all the keys:

steps.text: ...but you find nothing of interest.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-searching-captain-.text: If the player does not have the cell door key:

steps.text: You find a cell door key.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-searching-captain-.text: If the player does not have the metal key:

steps.text: You find the key to the main gate.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-searching-captain-.text: If the player does not have the wrought iron key:

the-quest-for-tenti-s-opening-chest-by-c.text: If Captain Siad is not distracted:

steps.text: The captain spots you before you manage to open the chest...

steps.speaker: Captain Siad
steps.text: What are you doing in here?

the-quest-for-tenti-s-opening-chest-by-c.text: If the player does not have the bedabin key:

steps.text: This chest needs a key to unlock it.
While the Captain's distracted, you quickly unlock the chest with the Bedabins' copy of the key. You take out the plans.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Hello Effendi!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Aha! I see you have the plans. This is great! However, these plans do indeed look very technical. My people have further need of your skills.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: If you can help us to manufacture this item, we will share its secret with you. Does this deal interest you effendi?

steps.player: Yes, I'm very interested.

steps.text: If the player is missing the bronze bar, feathers, and hammer:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, we need the following items: a bar of pure bronze, 10 feathers and a hammer. Bring them to me and we'll continue to make the item.
If the player is missing the bronze bar and feathers:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, we need the following items: a bar of pure bronze and 10 feathers. Bring them to me and we'll continue to make the item.
If the player is missing the feathers and hammer:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, I can see that you have a bar of bronze. Now we just need some feathers and a hammer before we can continue.
If the player is missing the bronze bar and hammer:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, I can see that you have some feathers. Now we just need a bar of bronze and a hammer before we can continue.
If the player is missing the feathers:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, I can see that you have a bar of bronze. Now we just need some feathers before we can continue.
If the player is missing the bronze bar:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, I can see that you have some feathers. Now we just need a bar of bronze before we can continue.
If the player is missing the hammer:

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, I can see that you have some feathers and a bar of Bronze, but you just need a hammer now.

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Great, I can see that you have some feathers, a bar of Bronze and a hammer. Are you still willing to help make the weapon?

steps.player: Yes, I'm kind of curious.

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Okay Effendi, you need to follow the plans. You will need some special tools for this... There is an anvil in the other tent. You have my permission to use it, but show the plans to the guard.

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: You have the plans and all the items needed. You should be able to complete the item on your own. Please bring me the item when it is finished.

steps.player: No, sorry.

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: As you wish Effendi!

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Come back if you change your mind!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-bedabin.speaker: Bedabin Nomad Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-bedabin.text: Sorry, but you can't use the tent without permission. Orders of Al Shabim.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-walk-through-tent-.speaker: Bedabin Nomad Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-walk-through-tent-.text: Sorry, this is a private tent, no one is allowed in. Orders of Al Shabim...

the-quest-for-tenti-s-walk-through-tent-.player: Al Shabim said I could enter, here are the plans!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-walk-through-tent-.text: You walk back out of the tent.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-experime.text: To forge items use the metal you wish to work with the anvil.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-bronze-bars-.text: Do you want to follow the technical plans ?

steps.text: You begin experimenting in forging the weapon...
If unsuccessful:
Through an unlucky accident you were not able to make the dart tip, but you think you know where you went wrong and perhaps next time you'll succeed.
If very unsuccessful:
You waste the bronze bar through an unlucky accident. But you think you know where you went wrong and perhaps next time you'll be successfull.
If successful:
You follow the plans carefully, and after some careful work, you finally manage to forge a sharp, pointed... dart tip.
You study the technical plans even more... You need to attach feathers to the tip to complete the weapon.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-feathers-on-.text: You try to attach feathers to the bronze dart tip.
Following the plans is tricky, but you persevere.
You successfully attach the feathers to the dart tip.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-trying-to-make-ano.text: You have already made the prototype dart. You don't need to make another one.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Hello Effendi!
You show Al Shabim the prototype dart.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: This is truly fantastic Effendi!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: We will take the technical plans for the weapon as well.
You hand over the technical plans for the weapon.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: We are forever grateful for this gift. My advisors have discovered some secrets which we will share with you.
Al Shabim's advisors show you some advanced techniques for making the new weapon.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Please accept this selection of six bronze throwing darts as a token of our appreciation.
You receive six bronze throwing darts from Al Shabim.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: I'll take that key off your hands as well effendi! Many thanks!
Dart Construction *** Congratulations! You can now construct darts.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Oh, and here is your pineapple!
You receive a tasty looking pineapple from Al Shabim

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Hello Effendi!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Many thanks with your help previously Effendi!

options.text: I am looking for a pineapple.

steps.player: I am looking for a pineapple.

steps.speaker: Al Shabim
steps.text: Here is another pineapple, try not to lose this one. {{^|Drops to ground with full inventory}}

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Hello Effendi!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.speaker: Al Shabim
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-al-shab.text: Many thanks with your help previously Effendi!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-a-regular-pi.text: The guard rolls his eyes in glee and takes a bite of the pineapple. His face turns from pleasure to pain as he spits the mouthful of pineapple out.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-a-regular-pi.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-a-regular-pi.text: Yeuch! That's awful! That's not Tenti pineapple! It's got no juice! Get me some Tenti pineapple if you know what's good for you. A whole one so I can see that it's good!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-a-pineapple-.text: Yeuch! That's awful! That's not Tenti pineapple! It's got no juice! Get me some Tenti pineapple if you know what's good for you. A whole one so I can see that it's good!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-pineapple-ch.text: The guard rolls his eyes in glee and takes a bite of the pineapple. His face turns from pleasure to pain as he spits the mouthful of pineapple out.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-pineapple-ch.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-pineapple-ch.text: Yeuch! That's awful! That's not Tenti pineapple! It's got no juice! Get me some Tenti pineapple if you know what's good for you. A whole one so I can see that it's good!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.player: Hey... I have something for you!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.text: You show the Tenti pineapple to the guard.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.text: Great! Just what I've been looking for! Mmmmmmm... Delicious!! This is soo nice! Mmmmm, *SLURP* Yummmm... Oh yes, this is great.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.player: So, can I go through now please?

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-the-tenti-pi.text: Yes, yes, of course... a deal's a deal!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-the-gua.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-the-gua.text: That pineapple was just delicious, many thanks. I don't suppose you could get me another? -- The guard looks at you pleadingly.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-the-gua.player: You must be joking! The last one I gave you cost me double shifts working copper ore! You should be grateful you got one at all.

the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-the-gua.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-talking-to-the-gua.text: Alright, alright, I was only asking!

the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-a-second-ten.speaker: Guard
the-quest-for-tenti-s-using-a-second-ten.text: Yeah, whaddya want... get out of here!

the-deeper-mine-walk-through-mine-cave.text: You walk into the darkness of the cavern...
... and emerge in a different part of this huge underground complex.

the-deeper-mine-look-in-full-barrel.text: You search the full barrel... It's full of rocks.

the-deeper-mine-search-full-barrel.text: This looks like a full mining barrel. Slaves use this to load up the rocks and stones that they're mining. This barrel is full of coal.

the-deeper-mine-look-in-empty-barrel.text: This looks like an empty mining barrel. Slaves use this to load up the rocks and stones that they're mining.

the-deeper-mine-search-empty-barrel.text: If the player is holding Ana in a barrel:

steps.text: You cannot carry another barrel while you're carrying Ana.

the-deeper-mine-search-empty-barrel.text: If the player already has a barrel:

steps.text: You can only manage one of these at a time.

the-deeper-mine-search-empty-barrel.text: This barrel is quite big, but you may be able to carry one. Would you like to take one?

the-deeper-mine-talking-to-the-guard-by-.text: This guard looks as if he's been in the sun for a while.

options.text: Nothing thanks - sorry for disturbing you.

steps.player: Nothing thanks - sorry for disturbing you.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well... I guess that's okay, get on your way though.

steps.player: Your head on a stick.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Why you ungrateful whelp.. I'll teach you some manners.
(Continues with getting jailed dialogue.)

the-deeper-mine-look-at-winch-bucket.text: This looks like a lift of some sort. You see barrels of rocks being placed on the lift and they're hauled up to the surface.

the-deeper-mine-using-the-winch-bucket.speaker: Guard
the-deeper-mine-using-the-winch-bucket.text: Hey there, what do you want?

steps.player: What is this thing?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: It is quite clearly a lift. Any fool can see that it's used to transport rock to the surface.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.
Can I use this?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Of course not, you'd be doing me out of a job. Anyway, you haven't got any barrels that need to go to the surface.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Now, move along and get some work done before you get a good beating.

the-deeper-mine-attacking-the-guard-by-t.text: This mercenary looks very fierce. Are you sure you want to attack him?

options.text: Yes, I can take him on!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh, want a fight do you!
(Continues with getting jailed dialogue.)

options.text: Er, no thanks, I've had second thoughts about it.

steps.text: You decide not to fight the Mercenary.

the-deeper-mine-look-at-mine-cart.text: This cart is being unloaded into this section of the mine. Before being sent back to another section for another load.

the-deeper-mine-searching-the-mine-cart.text: There may be just enough space to squeeze yourself into the cart. Would you like to try?

steps.text: If the player is holding Ana in a barrel:
If the player fails:
You fail to fit yourself into the cart in time before it starts its journey.
If the player bangs their head:
You bang your head on the cart as you try to jump in.
If the player falls off:
You jump onto the edge of the cart, but fall off.
You appear in a large open room with what looks like lots of miners working away. This is a very rough looking area, the miners look like they're on their last legs.

options.text: No thanks, it looks pretty dangerous.

steps.text: You decide not to get into the dangerous looking mine cart.

the-deeper-mine-look-at-mine-cart-in-the.text: This mine cart is being loaded up with new rocks and stone. It gets sent to a different section of the mine for unloading.

the-deeper-mine-searching-mine-cart-in-t.text: There may be just enough space to squeeze yourself into the cart. Would you like to try?

steps.text: If the player is holding Ana in a barrel:
If the player fails:
You fail to fit yourself into the cart in time before it starts its journey.
If the player bangs their head:
You bang your head on the cart as you try to jump in.
If the player falls off:
You jump onto the edge of the cart, but fall off.
You appear back in the barrel loading room. A nearby slave looks surprised to see you popping out of the cart.

options.text: No thanks, it looks pretty dangerous.

the-deeper-mine-search-gate-to-the-priso.text: You search the gates... yep, they're locked.
A nearby guard looks you over. He doesn't seem too impressed.
It looks as if this is where very difficult prisoners are sent as a punishment.

the-deeper-mine-open-gate-to-enter-the-p.text: The gate seems to be locked.
The nearby guard doesn't want to let you in.

the-deeper-mine-open-gate-to-enter-the-p.speaker: Guard
the-deeper-mine-open-gate-to-enter-the-p.text: Hey, move away from the gate. There's nothing interesting for you here.

the-deeper-mine-open-gate-to-leave-the-p.text: If the player does not have enough rocks:

steps.text: The gate seems to be locked.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Hey, move away from the gate. If you wanna get out you're gonna have to mine for it. You're gonna have to bring me 15 loads of rocks in one go!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: And then I'll let you out. You can go back to work with the other slaves then!

the-deeper-mine-open-gate-to-leave-the-p.text: If the player has enough rocks:

steps.player: Okay, I have all your rocks here, let me out now. -- The guard unlocks the gate. --

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Okay, okay, come on out.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Okay, you've got all the rocks, you can go now, but keep your nose clean in future.

the-deeper-mine-talking-to-ana.speaker: Ana
the-deeper-mine-talking-to-ana.text: Hello there, I don't think I've seen you before.

steps.player: No, I'm new here!

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: I thought so you know! How do you like the hospitality down here? Not exactly Al Kharid town style is it? Well, I guess I'd better get back to work.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Don't want to get into trouble with the guards again.

options.text: Do you get into trouble with guards often?

steps.player: Do you get into trouble with guards often?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: No, not really, because I'm usually working very hard. Come to think of it, I'd better get back to work.

options.text: Do you enjoy it down here?

steps.player: Do you enjoy it down here?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Of course not! I just don't have much choice about it a the moment.

options.text: I want to try and get you out of here.
Do you have any ideas about how we can get out of here?

steps.player: Do you have any ideas about how we can get out of here?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Hmmm, not really, I would have tried them already if I did. The guards seem to live in the compound. How did you get in there anyway?

options.text: I managed to sneak past the guards.
Huh, these guards are rubbish, it was easy to sneak past them!

steps.player: Okay, see ya!

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Goodbye and good luck!

options.text: I want to try and get you out of here.

steps.player: I want to try and get you out of here!

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Wow! You're brave. How do you propose we do that? In case you hadn't noticed, this place is quite well guarded.

options.text: We could try to sneak out.

steps.player: We could try to sneak out.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: That doesn't sound very likely. How did you get in here anyway? Did you deliberately hand yourself over to the guards? Ha, ha ha ha! Sorry, just kidding.

options.text: I managed to sneak past the guards.

steps.player: I managed to sneak past the guards.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Hmm, impressive, but can you so easily sneak out again? How did you manage to get through the gate?

steps.player: I have a key.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I heard that! So you used a key did you?!
If the player is holding the key:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Right, we'll have that key off you!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Guards! Guards!

steps.player: It's a trade secret!

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Oh, right, well, I guess you know what you're doing. Anyway, I have to get back to work. The guards will come along soon and give us some trouble else.

options.text: Huh, these guards are rubbish, it was easy to sneak past them!

steps.player: Huh, these guards are rubbish, it was easy to sneak past them!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I heard that! So you managed to sneak in did you!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Guards! Guards!

steps.player: Have you got any suggestions?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Hmmm, let me think...

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Hmmm.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: No, sorry...

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: The only thing that gets out of here is the rock that we mine.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Not even the dead get a decent funeral. Bodies are just thrown down disused mine holes. It's very disrespectful...

options.text: Okay, I'll check around for another way to try and get out.

steps.player: Okay, I'll check around for another way to try and get out.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Good luck!

options.text: How does the rock get out?

steps.player: How does the rock get out?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Well, we mine it in this section, then someone scoops it into a barrel. The barrels are loaded onto a mine cart. Then they're deposited near the surface lift.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: I have no idea where they go from there. But that's not going to help us, is it?

options.text: Maybe? I'll come back to you when I have a plan.

steps.player: Maybe? I'll come back to you when I have a plan.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Okay, well, I'm not going anywhere! -- Ana nods at a nearby guard!-- Unless he feels generous enough to let me go! -- The guard ignores the comment. --

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Oh well, I'd better get back to work, you take care!

options.text: Where would I get one of those barrels from?

steps.player: Where would I get one of those barrels from?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Well, you would get one from around by the lift area. But why would you want one of those?

steps.player: Er no reason! Just wondering.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Hmmm, just don't get any funny ideas... I am not going to get into one of those barrels! Okay, have you got that?

steps.player: Okay, yep, I've got that.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Good, just make sure you keep it in mind. Anyway, I have to get back to work. The guards will come along soon and give us some trouble else.

options.text: Well, we'll see, it might be the only way.

steps.player: Well, we'll see, it might be the only way.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: No, there has to be a better way! Anyway, I have to get back to work. The guards will come along soon and give us some trouble else.

options.text: I could try to sneak you out if you were in a barrel!

steps.player: I could try to sneak you out if you were in a barrel!

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: There is no way you are getting me into a barrel. No WAY! DO you understand?

options.text: Well, we'll see, it might be the only way.

steps.player: What's your name.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: My name? Oh, how sweet, my name is Ana. I come from Al Kharid though we've only recently moved there. I was born, and did most of my growing up, in Varrock. I thought the desert might be interesting.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: What a surprise I got!

options.text: What kind of surprise did you get?

steps.player: What kind of surprise did you get?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Well, I was just touring the desert looking for the nomad tribe to the West. And I was set upon by these armoured men.

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: I think that the guards think I am an escaped prisoner. They didn't understand that I was exploring the desert as an adventurer.

options.text: Do you want to go back to Al Kharid?

steps.player: Do you want to go back to Al Kharid?

steps.speaker: Ana
steps.text: Sure, I miss my Mum, her name is Irena and she is probably waiting for me. How do you propose we get out of here though?

steps.speaker: Ana

steps.npc: I see you have your equipment - well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.

steps.player: With what?

steps.npc: Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

steps.text: The archaeologist takes the necklace and turns it over in his hands, studying it closely.

The archaeologist shows you the techniques for this particular spell, which requires five fire runes arranged around one cosmic rune - and level 49 Magic - then casting the spell on a crafted ruby necklace of your
own.  You can make enchanted ruby necklaces.

steps.npc: Yes, indeed. Well done, youngster, thanks for helping us.

at which time, the city was known as Senntisten.

This is a most remarkable discovery, as we have other evidence indicating that Zarosian followers were resident before the Saradominists took over, but it also seems that Zamorakian forces used it during a battle of some
sort. Still, it allows us to roughly date when the city changed from following Zaros and Zamorak to following Saradomin. Put it in display case 44.

steps.player: Wow, thanks!

steps.player: Wow, thanks!

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.npc: We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.
These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.

steps.player: ...such as?

steps.npc: Not getting rained on, for example.
Did you do anything about that monster Donal was talking about?

steps.player: It's been taken care of.

steps.npc: Glad to hear it. Now we can get on with excavating.

before-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Leave me be, outerlander. I have nothing to say to the likes of you.

after-the-fremennik-trials.npc: And greetings to you too. It is good to see new blood entering the Fremennik; we gain our strength by bringing new warriors into the tribe.

standard-dialogue.npc: Welcome to the Realm of Memories, [player name].

steps.player: Who were you?

steps.npc: I am Thrander. Long ago, I used to live in Varrock, converting plate armour. For example, if you'd got a plate skirt, but you preferred leggings instead, I'd convert it, free of charge.

steps.player: Are you happy here?

steps.npc: Maybe retiring was a mistake. If the world ever wanted me again, I could come out of retirement and offer my services as before. Though people might fret about the economic impact if I did.

steps.player: Thanks.

using-platelegs-or-a-plateskirt-on-thran.npc: If you're hoping I'll convert your armour into a different item for you, I'm afraid I don't do that sort of thing now.

pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.speaker: Queen Sigrid
pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.text: Have you come for a particular reason? I am a busy Queen, you know. I had to attend the opening of a new orphanage this morning.

pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.speaker: Queen Sigrid
pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.text: And this afternoon I shall be receiving the Embassador of Karamja and accompanying him on his week-long tour of Etceteria.

pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.speaker: Queen Sigrid
pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.text: Then this evening we shall be putting on a grand ball! All of the kingdom's nobility will be present!

pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.speaker: Queen Sigrid
pre-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid-before.text: Oh, who am I kidding...nothing ever happens here. I always wanted to be a princess when I was a girl. If I'd been told it would be like this, I wouldn't have bothered.

pre-quest-talking-to-guard-at-door-to-th.player: My name is [Fremennik name], will you not let me through?

pre-quest-talking-to-guard-at-door-to-th.speaker: Guard
pre-quest-talking-to-guard-at-door-to-th.text: I'm afraid the King won't give an audience to anyone except a worthy hero.
If the player has not completed Heroes' Quest:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: If you become a member of the Heroes' Guild, he will definitely grant you an audience.

pre-quest-talking-to-guard-at-door-to-th.player: I am a member of the Heroes' Guild; does that not show my worth?

pre-quest-talking-to-advisor-ghrim-befor.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
pre-quest-talking-to-advisor-ghrim-befor.text: The King needs someone to take over the rule of the Kingdom. If I were you, I should consider the position.

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Who are you? Who seeks audience with the King of this fair land of Miscellania?

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.player: I am known in these lands as [Fremennik name], Your Majesty. I come in search of a quest.

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Ah, it pleases me to see such enthusiasm!

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.text: I was once an adventurer such as yourself; even while fulfilling my duties as King of Miscellania, I would roam the lands in search of adventure, and strike down mighty foes with a single blow!

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Unfortunately, I was a little too daring, and attempted to brave the icelands, where I finally met my match.

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.text: I survived, barely, but I was cursed for the rest of my life to stay in this form. Which leaves me incapable of performing my duties as ruler.

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.text: This is why I am looking for an exceptional soul to be regent of this fair kingdom of Miscellania.

getting-started-talking-to-king-vargas.prompt: Start the Throne of Miscellania quest?

steps.player: If I may be so bold, Your Majesty, I think Miscellania would rest in capable hands with me.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Hahaha! You are bold, [Fremennik name], but then I have yet to see a good ruler who was not.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You will first have to demonstrate your worth. You are a good warrior, that I do not doubt; however ruling also requires a good grasp of diplomacy.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: We have been at war with neighbouring Etceteria for hundreds of years; however, I think both of us have rather lost our appetite for hostilities.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Now may be an opportune time to make amends. If you manage to negotiate peace with them, then you will truly have shown your skill as a diplomat.

steps.player: Then do not stray far, Your Majesty, for I shall soon return.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Wait! There is one more matter to discuss... a mere formality, of course.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: By Miscellanious tradition, one may not become regent of the kingdom unless in the trust of the royal family.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: This includes that of the future king or queen. It is yet too early for me to decide which of my children should inherit the throne.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Until then, gaining the trust of one of them should suffice. Who knows? Your choice might help me make a decision later.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: So tell me! Which of my children will you attempt to gain the trust of?

options.text: I want to earn Prince Brand's approval.

steps.player: I would like to choose Prince Brand.
And you say this is a mere formality, Your Majesty?

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I am sure you can form a good working relationship with him. You can ask Ghrim for advice; that's what he's here for, after all.

options.text: I want to earn Princess Astrid's approval.

steps.player: I would like to choose Princess Astrid.
And you say this is a mere formality, Your Majesty?

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I am sure you can form a good working relationship with her. You can ask Ghrim for advice; that's what he's here for, after all.

steps.player: I'm afraid I must decline, Your Majesty. The call of adventure is too strong for me to accept a sedentary life.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I can assure you that I managed to heed that same call, and ruling this land was no hindrance to me. However, I understand your decision. Fare thee well!

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: King Vargas was once a brave and noble adventurer, well-loved by his subjects. Unfortunately, he was cursed while seeking a quest in the icelands to the north, and is now unable to reign.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Prince?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Prince?

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Prince Brand has always dreamed of becoming a famous bard; unfortunately, his musical and literary skills are somewhat lacking.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: He has no interest in ruling the kingdom, and seems to spend his time daydreaming or composing quite awful poems, and sagas of totally mundane events.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: He is rather vain, if you'll pardon my saying so; he will greatly appreciate any compliments on his poetry. He also has quite a sweet tooth.

options.text: What can you tell me about the Princess?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Princess?

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Princess Astrid thinks she'd be perfectly capable of ruling the kingdom, but her father doesn't trust her enough by herself.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Especially since she devotes herself to the - as the King sees it - cowardly skill of archery rather than the noble skill of melee combat...

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: She is fond of jewellery, and of course she collects bows. She is also quite the conversationalist.
If the player has not gained the trust of Princess Astrid:

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Many have tried to capture her attention, but she has yet to be impressed by any of them.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.

steps.player: I found something interesting.

steps.npc: Oh? Let's take a look...

steps.text: If the player has a Clean necklace in their inventory:

steps.player: I found this pretty necklace.

steps.npc: Interesting...yes...yes...hmmm.... It looks like it's enchanted.

steps.player: With what?

steps.npc: Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

steps.text: The archaeologist takes the necklace and turns it over in his hands, studying it closely.

The archaeologist shows you the techniques for this particular spell, which requires five fire runes arranged around one cosmic rune - and level 49 Magic - then casting the spell on a crafted ruby necklace of your
own.  You can make enchanted ruby necklaces.

steps.player: So I just make a ruby necklace and use five fire runes and one cosmic rune to enchant it.

steps.npc: Yes, indeed. Well done, youngster, thanks for helping us.

If the player is showing the Old coin for the first time:

steps.player: I've cleaned this old coin - is it of any use?

steps.npc: Oh my! What a wonderful find! If this is what I believe it to be, it would allow us to date the Dig Site city.
And look here, it has the name of the city too! Saranthium! That must be during the Saradominist occupation. This is a wonderful find. Please take it and place it in display case 45.

steps.player: Right, display case 45 it is...

steps.npc: You've already shown me one of those, but it was in better condition. It's in the display case over there. You can pop this one in the finds crate over in the corner.

If the player is showing the Ancient coin for the first time:

steps.player: I found this really old coin - is it of any use?

steps.npc: What have we here?

Oh! This is very interesting...and confusing at the same time. This coin means that the city that we're excavating on the Digsite - Saranthium - was actually inhabited much, much earlier by followers of Zamorak,
at which time, the city was known as Senntisten.

This is a most remarkable discovery, as we have other evidence indicating that Zarosian followers were resident before the Saradominists took over, but it also seems that Zamorakian forces used it during a battle of some
sort. Still, it allows us to roughly date when the city changed from following Zaros and Zamorak to following Saradomin. Put it in display case 44.

steps.player: Case 44 it is!

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are a gestalt entity. We each have our own body, but our minds

steps.npc: are united and we all think as one. Well except when Hallak doth leaveth

options.text: What manner of beings are you?

steps.player: What manner of beings are you?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are the spirits of the river Elid, many ages ago we used to be mindless wandering spirits, with little mind or purpose, we were here even in the first age. Then great Elidinis came to the desert and bound us to her

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: river, we've

steps.npc: become one with the river and over the centuries become full of the power of Elidinis that was in her river. We are now her trusted guardians of the Elid, we can control the river and anything which happens
near the river we know about.

options.text: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?

steps.player: Tell me more of Elidinis.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Elidinis is one of a group of gods, known as the Menaphite Pantheon. She is wife of their leader Tumeken. She is the Menaphite goddess of growth and fertility and goddess of the river.

options.text: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis?

steps.player: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis though? Why did you pick on Nardah specifically?

steps.npc: It is true many do not follow Elidinis, but there is more to the story than that. The answers

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: lie in the story of Nardarine. Wouldst thou likest to hear the telling of this tale? It is not a short one.

options.text: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.player: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.npc: Nardarine came from a town towards the north side of the desert which does not exist today. This was in the third age in the time thou callest

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the God Wars. Her town was once controlled by Saradomin, but there was a great battle there between Saradominist and Zamorakian forces which pretty much levelled the town

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: to the ground. Most of the human citizens perished. Nardarine had the wisdom to escape into the desert before the fighting got really serious and thus survived. However she found herself wandering lost and alone in

steps.npc: the desert. She prayed to Saradomin for help, but Saradomin was too concerned with the loss of a strategic outpost to worry about the fate of one small human. Nardarine had wandered towards the realm of

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

steps.npc: homage to me and I grant this also unto thine descendents as long as they too will pay an oath of fealty and homage to me'. Nardarine said 'If you would grant me a safe home, with a

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: supply of food and water, then I would surely do this for it is more than any other God would seem to do for me'. Then Elidinis made

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: a spring of water appear at Nardarines feet and brought stone from below the sand so that she

steps.npc: might have something to build with. She called forth camels which have many uses and taste good in kebabs. She then provided Nardarine with a statuette in her image to worship. Nardarine built up her home. Over

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: time more refugees from the God Wars found Nardarine's home. Nardarine let them stay with her as long as they did make the same oath as her. Hence the town of Nardah was born and Nardarine lived the rest

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: of her days in the peacefulness that she craved. The oath was passed down the generations for many ages, but now seemeth to be forgotten. Now maybe thou canst see why we are not best pleased.

steps.player: That does make some sense.
Maybe another day.

before-the-queen-of-thieves.npc: Greetings. What can I do for you?

steps.player: What are you doing here?

steps.npc: I'm conducting important business here for the Kourend Council.

steps.player: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.npc: There is something I could use some help with. I'm here on behalf of the Kourend Council to investigate some unusual happenings in Port Piscarilius.

steps.player: What are you investigating?

steps.npc: Port Piscarilius is home to various gangs. They're a nuisance, but up until now we haven't had much trouble in dealing with them.

steps.player: So what's the problem?

steps.npc: A new gang calling themselves the Saviours of Kourend has recently formed. That's not surprising as gangs come and go all of the time, but this one is different.

steps.player: How so?

steps.npc: The Saviours of Kourend have been absorbing many of the other gangs. Within a few weeks they've already become the largest gang in Kourend and more join them each day.
The talk amongst the people is that it's all down to their leader, a mysterious figure known only as the Queen of Thieves.

steps.player: Nice name. Why doesn't the ruler of Port Piscarilius do something about this?

steps.npc: Shauna Piscarilius is the ruler of Port Piscarilius, but she spends most of her time galavanting around in that boat of hers rather than looking after her home.

steps.player: Fair enough. So what do you need me for?

steps.npc: Well my original plan was to infiltrate the gang to get close to the Queen and capture her. However, I've been unable to make any progress. Apparently, I don't look the part.

steps.player: Yeah not sure what that's all about. You clearly fit right in here.

steps.npc: Quite right. They're quite insistent though, so someone else will need to give it a go. You look like you might be just the type they're after.

steps.player: What are you trying to say?

steps.npc: That you look poor.

steps.player: Oh...

steps.npc: Anyway if you're up for the task you'll need to infiltrate the Saviours of Kourend, find the Queen of Thieves, apprehend her and then bring her to me.
So are you up for it?

steps.text: The Queen of Thieves has been started.

steps.player: Absolutely.

steps.npc: Excellent. The Saviours of Kourend must have their headquarters somewhere nearby. You should ask around town and see if anyone knows where they are. Good luck.

steps.player: Nah.

steps.npc: Fair enough. I'll be here if you change your mind.

steps.player: What's the Kourend Council?

steps.npc: Although it's called a kingdom, Great Kourend hasn't actually had a king for many years. These days Kourend is a republic and it is ruled by the Kourend Council.
The Council consists of four councillors who are elected by the people every four years. The current councillors are Councillor Hughes, Councillor Unkar, Councillor Orson and Councillor Andrews.

steps.player: I see. So what are you investigating?

steps.npc: Port Piscarilius is home to various gangs. They're a nuisance, but up until now we haven't had much trouble in dealing with them.

steps.player: So what's the problem?
I'm looking for a quest.

steps.npc: Very well. Until next time.

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in
the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

getting-started-the-builders-on-strike-t.text: I wish. And I was, up until recently.

getting-started-the-builders-on-strike-t.speaker: 'Currency' The Alchemist
getting-started-the-builders-on-strike-t.text: This tower. Set me back a fair few million.

getting-started-the-builders-on-strike-t.player: I'll bet! It pleases you, then, to know that I have just become a builder and have been granted permission to go mess around inside.

getting-started-the-builders-on-strike-t.speaker: 'Currency' The Alchemist
getting-started-the-builders-on-strike-t.text: This is not a good day for me.

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.player: Are you Bonafido by any chance?

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.speaker: Bonafido
getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.text: How can I be of assistance?

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.player: Well, I've just spoken to Effigy about this tower. He tells me he hired you to work but you're on strike. Something about an extended tea break?

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.speaker: Bonafido
getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.text: Extended cup o' char? E's got it all wrong, mate. We know those alchemi-whatsits are up ta somefin' weird in building this tower, wot wiv all the machinery, and until we get some answers we're not movin a muscle.

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.player: Well, he wanted me to do something about it.
Is there no way I can convince you to continue?
Well, can I at least have a look inside the tower?

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.speaker: Bonafido
getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.text: Only builders are allowed in there, like. You don't look like much ov a builder to me.

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.player: I take offence at that! Give me a chance; you may be surprised.

getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.speaker: Bonafido
getting-started-speaking-with-bonafido-t.text: Okay. Come to me kitted out like a builder - hard hat, some boots, scruffy trousers and shirt - and I'll let ya try out ta be one ov us.

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-hard-hat.player: I was just wondering if you might be able to help me out with one?

steps.player: One?
Five?
Three?
Torn curtains?
8 clay pieces and 3 limestone bricks?
10 clay pieces?
Greener pastures?

steps.text: Hard hat
Try the beckon emote while wearing an item of builders' clothing!

steps.player: Wait a minute! Is there blood on this helmet?
Oh, okay. Thanks. Bye.
What?
10 limestone bricks?
A brown rug?
Opulent curtains?

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-hard-hat-t.speaker: 'Black-eye'
accessing-the-tower-obtaining-hard-hat-t.text: Why, thanks. Some would say as nice as the one you're wearing!

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.player: Hi, I'm looking to get some kit to look like one of you guys.
Anything you might be able to help me out with?
Hmmm. Has it been cleaned? I don't want some sweaty hand-me-down.
Well, that sounds good. Can I have it then?

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player doesn't have a beer:

steps.player: Sure. What's your 'usual'?
Simple, cheap beer. No problem.

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player has a beer in their inventory:

steps.player: Well, today's your lucky day!

steps.text: Builder's shirt
Try the beckon emote while wearing an item of builders' clothing!

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player attempts to give a beer again:

steps.player: Fancy another?

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player attempts to give a non-regular beer, such as Greenman's ale:

steps.player: Hi! How's this for some booze?

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player attempts to give a beer tankard or keg of beer:

steps.player: Fancy another?

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player attempts to give noted beer:

steps.player: Beer?
Oh, sorry.

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.player: What do you do when you're not lifting logs above your head?
I can honestly say you're a very original guy.
Ah, come on. You know you want to give me free stuff.
Likely story. Sure you weren't skinny dipping?

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the plant has the trousers:

steps.text: Aha! You find some trousers!
Builder's trousers
Try the beckon emote while wearing an item of builders' clothing!

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: If the player doesn't have the trousers:

steps.text: Nope, nothing here.

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.player: Hello. I was just wondering... I don't suppose you have any spare clothing you could lend me?
Oh, but why? I could pay you!

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.speaker: 'No fingers'
accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: Don't suppose you've seen any boots around here? Size nine, steel toed, brown leather...

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.player: Nope, not at all. I'd best be going. Have a nice day. Bye!

accessing-the-tower-obtaining-builder-s-.text: You attempt to pick the man's pocket.
You pick the man's pocket...and find some boots!
Try the beckon emote while wearing an item of builders' clothing!

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.speaker: Bonafido
accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.text: Well, if it ain't the wannabe builder!
If not wearing the full outfit:

steps.player: What clothes do I need?

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Ya don't seem to be able ta remember anyfin'... Dearie me.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Come back to me wearin' a hard hat, some scruffy trousers, a good top and some hard boots. Yow shud fand some around 'ere.

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.speaker: Bonafido
accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.text: Like a builder frew and frew! Good job - now it's time to test your skills.

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.player: Okay, what do you want me to build?

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.speaker: Bonafido
accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.text: Build? Hahaha, don't be a plonka!

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.speaker: Bonafido
accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.text: It's not building skills that makes a true builder, you have to have the right mental attitude, yeah?

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.speaker: Bonafido
accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.text: You've plenty of work to do, but you need a drink fast - what do you go for?

steps.player: Orange juice.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: What are you? A healthy builder? Of course, not juice!

steps.player: Tea.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Bingo! Ain't nufin' betta.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Now, let's hear you whistle!

options.text: Do a little dance and whistle as loud as you can

steps.text: Player performs the "dance" emote
You do a little dance and whistle as loud as you can.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: What on Gielinor are you doing? Get out of my sight.
You whistle a tune.
Player performs the "cheer" emote

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: You know, you have quite a talent there.

steps.player: Why thank you. Do you think I have what it takes to become a famous whistler?

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: No.

steps.player: Oh.

steps.text: (Player performs "Beckon (enhanced)" emote)
You whistle for attention.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Wahey! Nice one. Next question.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: What's a good sign that you need to replace your trousers?

options.text: Your legs are getting a bit cold

steps.player: Your legs are getting a bit cold?

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Exactamondo! Glad to see you are thinking like a builder.

steps.player: I am?

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Yes, obviously if your legs are cold, you lost your trousers altogether!

steps.player: That's just what I was thinking.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Now the last question - what do you do if you cut your finger?

steps.player: Cry.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: When was the last time you saw a builder cry?

steps.player: Carry on, it'll fix itself.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Yep, that's the one!

steps.player: Suppose it could get infected then, but that'll just impress the lads all the more.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Exactly, you're gettin the hang of this quickly!

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Cosmic! I canna see no reason why ya can't go in t'tower now. But be careful, there be some precarious situations in there.

steps.player: So, what's left to build?

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Well, there's a pipe system, a pressure machine and a strange cage up at the top that needs finishing off. The alchemists couldn't explain what they were for.

steps.player: Thanks!
Fetch a plaster and ointment.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Look, [player name], let me give you a bit of advice. If you want to look weak, that's the best way to go.

options.text: They're ripped and full of holes

steps.player: They're ripped and full of holes.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: No, no, no. That's the only way they should be!

options.text: The colour is starting to fade

steps.player: The colour is starting to fade?

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Oh no, you're really not getting the hang of this are you?

steps.player: Bottle of wine.

steps.speaker: Bonafido
steps.text: Ooh, get Mr Fancy Pants here and his posh wine! You're no builder.

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.speaker: Bonafido
accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.text: Hi, 'Kelsew the Builder'! Been into the tower yet?

accessing-the-tower-talking-to-bonafido-.player: Not yet, I'll go when I'm ready. I'm taking my time, may have a quick cup of tea first.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: Wow, this place looks special. Best I look around for something to fix.
Heya, Bona. I had a look at the building. There's some complex machinery in there! Going to cost someone.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: Bonafido
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: Yep, told ya so. Any idea what those alchemists are up ta?

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: Well, I agree now they're up to something. The question is what...? I don't think we're going to find out much from the alchmists, though.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: Bonafido
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: So what are you going to do?

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: I shall see if I can't fix it up and see for myself what is going on. Should be able to get a good reward from them. But don't worry, I'll make sure your efforts don't go unpaid.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: Bonafido
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: You're a star among builders, that ya are!

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: Hello again, Effigy. I've had a nose around the tower. There's a lot of work to do!

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: Effigy
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: I know, I know. But think of how fantastical it will be when it is finished!

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: Why fantastical? What are all those pipes and machines in there? What are you trying to do?

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: Effigy
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: The sun is shining... The birds are singing...

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: Effigy
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: Hehe. Just fix the tower. You'll soon see.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: You'd best pay me well for this.
I must say, the inside of the tower is really something to behold.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.speaker: 'Transmute' The Alchemist
unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.text: Why, thanks. You'll find various pieces of machinery to fix in there. You can no doubt find the materials in there, too.

unfinished-work-entering-the-tower-of-li.player: Hi, Currency. Got any spare cash?
I'm going to stop before this gets violent.

steps.text: You didn't find anything that time.
(Player performs the "No" emote)

4 coloured balls, 3 pieces of metal sheeting and 4 valve wheels.

steps.text: You need [materials] to fix the machine.
(The player builds the machine.)
You built the machine! It still needs calibrating, though.
The pressure seems to be affected by holes in the pipes. Perhaps you can block them up with the balls.

The machine is working!
The machine is working!
If this was the last part of the tower to fix:
The tower should be in working order now! Best go and tell Effigy!

6 rivets, 4 metal pipes and 5 metal rings.

steps.text: You need [materials] to fix the machine.

You built the machine! It still needs calibrating, though.
After connecting the pipes:
The machine is working!
The machine is working!
If this was the last part of the tower to fix:
The tower should be in working order now! Best go and tell Effigy!

5 metal bars and 4 bottles of binding fluid.

It's complete!
The cage is complete!
The cage is complete!
