steps.text: Meanwhile, a cutscene plays in the Lithkren Vault, with the camera slowly approaching the pool where Galvek once rested. The camera pans toward the strange tube to the east. A mysterious gas envelopes the dragonkin within, awakening it and breaking out. At the same time, the strange tube to the west also breaks, revealing two more dragonkin as they all convene by the pool.

steps.speaker: Sakirth
steps.text: Zorgoth?

steps.speaker: Sithaph
steps.text: Dead.

steps.speaker: Strisath
steps.text: Then we are free at last!

steps.speaker: Sakirth
steps.text: And a strength grows within us!

steps.speaker: Sithaph
steps.text: The Stone has been uncovered. The mortals try to claim its power.

steps.speaker: Sakirth
steps.text: Then let us bring terror and pain to them!

steps.speaker: Strisath
steps.text: Yes! The dragonkin will rise once more!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.player: Hey, Idria. How are things here?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.speaker: Idria
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.text: We're still trying to work out what Lucien's next move is, but so far everything has been quiet.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.player: What do you think he's doing?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.speaker: Idria
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.text: It's hard to say. He has the Stone of Jas and the Staff of Armadyl now. That should give him everything he needs to follow in Zamorak's footsteps, but for whatever reason, he's chosen not to act yet.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.player: Is there anything I can do?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.speaker: Idria
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.text: Not really at this point, but we'll be sure to let you know the moment he dares try anything. In the meantime, you might want to return to that temple beneath Lumbridge.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.speaker: Idria
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.text: It seems the magics Lucien used down there were far more than just a single summoning spell. The area has been permanently desecrated by those horrifying demons.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.speaker: Idria
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.text: If you were looking for some way of keeping Lucien and his forces in check, killing a few of those demons wouldn't be a bad idea.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-idria.player: I might just do that. Thanks, Idria.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.speaker: Akrisae
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.text: Saradomin be with you, [player name]. We have a lot to be grateful to you for.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.player: Thanks, but I'm not sure I feel the same way. I wasn't able to stop Lucien.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.speaker: Akrisae
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.text: But you came very close and you lived to tell the tale. Lucien may have gained the upper hand, but he's not safe by any means.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.speaker: Akrisae
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.text: He has people like you opposing him, not to mention an alliance between the Temple Knights, Crux Eqal and the Guardians of Armadyl!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-akrisae.player: You make a good point. Let's just hope it will be enough.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.speaker: Thaerisk
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.text: Ah, [player name], it's good to see you again.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.player: Hello there, Thaerisk. Any word on Lucien?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.speaker: Thaerisk
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.text: Nothing yet, but we're doing everything we can to find him. I hope he's ready for us, because once we do locate him, we're going to give him quite the bloody nose...

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.speaker: Thaerisk
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-thaerisk.text: ... or at least whatever passes for a nose on a Mahjarrat!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-silif.speaker: Silif
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-silif.text: Hello there, friend. I heard what happened with Lucien and the Stone. Don't worry, he'll pay for his crimes sooner or later.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-silif.speaker: Silif
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-silif.text: Have faith, friend. Evil never prospers for long.

options.text: I lost those robes I was using as a disguise.

steps.player: I lost those robes I was using as a disguise.

steps.speaker: Silif
steps.text: Not to worry. I have them here for you.
Silif gives you some Dark Squall robes.

steps.player: Thanks!
I'd better get going.

steps.speaker: Silif
steps.text: Until next time, friend.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-surok.player: How are you enjoying your cell, Surok?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-surok.speaker: Surok Magis
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-surok.text: You let me out of here! This isn't over...

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-surok.player: It's nice to see a little justice around here!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-sir-tiffy.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-sir-tiffy.text: Good day, Proselyte. I heard from Akrisae what happened with that Lucien business. Be sure to keep your chin up. We'll get the old boy sooner or later.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-sir-tiffy.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-sir-tiffy.text: Don't mention it, old bean. Now, is there anything I can do for you?

options.text: Do you have any jobs for me yet?
I have news on that assassin who attacked Entrana.
Can you explain the Gaze of Saradomin to me?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-aya.speaker: Aya
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-aya.text: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

options.text: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?
Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.
I'm here about blessed axes again.

steps.player: About Turael...

steps.speaker: Aya
steps.text: You need not share your condolences with me, adventurer. I've been prepared for this for a long time.

steps.player: You have?

steps.speaker: Aya
steps.text: My brother was a thrill-seeker his whole life. Even after he retired, I always knew something would come and pull him back in.

steps.player: And that something was me. I'm sorry...

steps.speaker: Aya
steps.text: Don't be. He died doing what he loved, and he died a hero. He wouldn't have had it any other way.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-spria.speaker: Aya
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-spria.text: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

options.text: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?
Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

steps.player: About Turael...

steps.speaker: Spria
steps.text: It's nothing personal, but I'd prefer not to discuss what happened with my father.

steps.player: Of course. Sorry for bringing it up.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-harrallak.speaker: Harrallak Menarous
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-harrallak.text: Welcome to my humble Guild, [player name].

steps.player: How are you, Harrallak?

steps.speaker: Harrallak Menarous
steps.text: I've lost two of my dear friends, [player name]. This old place doesn't seem to be the same since they're gone.

steps.player: I feel responsible.

steps.speaker: Harrallak Menarous
steps.text: Nonsense, my friend! They both died bravely fighting against a great evil! There is no blame on you for that.

steps.speaker: Harrallak Menarous
steps.text: Remember them for who they were and what they stood for. Mourn their loss, but never bear the burden of their death, for that is not what they would want.

steps.player: And what about vengeance?

steps.speaker: Harrallak Menarous
steps.text: Ah, now that is a topic we could debate for many moons, my friend. Still, regardless of the reason, know that when the time comes, I will fight beside you against Lucien once more.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the Guild?
Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?
Why are you wielding a tree branch?

steps.player: Why are you wielding a tree branch?

steps.speaker: Yadech Strongarm
steps.text: Well... there's a story to that. You see, I should have an axe but-

steps.player: Sloane's axe?

steps.speaker: Yadech Strongarm
steps.text: My axe. He won it because of a squirrel.

steps.player: A squirrel?

steps.speaker: Yadech Strongarm
steps.text: He bet me that I couldn't catch the squirrel while still holding my axe, but that he could... Thing is, he tricked me! When it was his turn, he just chopped the tree down!

steps.player: I see. That doesn't explain why you have a tree branch though.

steps.speaker: Yadech Strongarm
steps.text: A barbarian warrior is bound to his axe. I cannot take up another, so I use part of the tree that Sloane cut down as my weapon... It also reminds me of him.

steps.player: He was a great warrior.

steps.speaker: Yadech Strongarm
steps.text: Yes, and a good friend. Still, he would want us to be happy that he is now with his warrior brethren. Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: May I claim my tokens please?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-mazchna.speaker: Mazchna
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-mazchna.text: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

options.text: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?
Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

steps.player: About Lucien...

steps.speaker: Mazchna
steps.text: He will be made to pay, my friend, and I assure you, when the day of his reckoning comes, I will be there.

steps.player: So will I, Mazchna.

steps.speaker: Mazchna
steps.text: Then we will fight, side by side, my friend. We will fight in honour of Turael and Duradel, and we will see them avenged!

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-kuradal.speaker: Kuradal
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-kuradal.text: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

options.text: Have you any rewards for me, or anything to trade?
Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.
Tell me about your skillcape, please.

steps.player: About Duradel...

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: Are you here with news on Lucien?

steps.player: I'm afraid not.

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: The moment you find him, you must come to me. I will ensure my father is avenged!

steps.player: He wouldn't want you to get yourself killed as well!

steps.text: If the player has not yet received Duradel's notes:

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: I will not suffer the same fate as my father. I intend to be prepared. For a start, I have been researching my father's notes to find weaknesses in Lucien's demonic thralls.

steps.player: Those sound interesting. May I see them?

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: Of course. If we expect to defeat Lucien, we must work together.
If the player's inventory is full:

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: Return to me when you have space to carry them.
Kuradal hands you an old notebook.
If the player has received Duradel's notes:

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: I will not suffer the same fate as my father. That fate is reserved for Lucien!

steps.player: I hope you're right...

steps.text: If the player has not read Duradel's notes and it is not in their possession:

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: I will not suffer the same fate as my father. I intend to be prepared. For a start, I have been researching my father's notes to find weaknesses in Lucien's demonic thralls.

steps.player: Speaking of those notes, I seem to have misplaced them. Do you happen to have another copy?

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: Luckily for you, I made many.
If the player has sufficient inventory space:
If the player has no free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Kuradal
steps.text: Return to me when you have space to carry them.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-oneir.speaker: Oneiromancer
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-the-oneir.text: Hello there. What do you want to talk about?

steps.player: Hi.

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: Hello there. I hear that Cyrisus is no longer with us.

steps.player: He died fighting for a good cause. He'll be remembered as a great hero.

steps.speaker: Oneiromancer
steps.text: I suppose the good do die young.

post-quest-dialogue-attempting-to-contac.text: You take a moment of silence in honour of your fallen friend, Cyrisus.

steps.npc: I'm too important to talk to the likes of you, leave.
My secretary will deal with any inquiries you have about the White Chisel.
My secretary is sitting just over there, thank you.
I'm busy, please leave.
Today is not a good day, can you come back tomorrow?
If you're looking for the market, it's downstairs.
Do you mind? You're blocking my view.
How did you get in here? I don't have time to talk to you!
I can't help you, go and see my secretary.
Talk to my secretary, I don't have time to deal with you.
I said go!
I told you to leave, human!
What can I do for you, human?
Can I help you with anything?
Was there anything you wanted?
What did you need of the White Chisel?
Is there anything you need assistance with?
And what can I do for you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I am the head secretary of the White Chisel.

steps.player: The what?

steps.npc: The White Chisel. We are one of the most powerful companies in the whole of the dwarven realm, we are. We have grown so powerful that we are now part of the Consortium.

steps.player: Where am I?

steps.npc: These are the offices of the White Chisel.
This is the official residence of the White Chisel.
Why, you are in the headquarters of the White Chisel.
We share this floor of the palace with the other companies of the Consortium. And trade with them on the Trade Octagon.

steps.player: The Trade Octagon?

steps.npc: See those traders out there, just out the door? They're all standing in the Trade Octagon. There's an awful lot of trade going on in the palace, you know.

steps.player: Anything else of interest in the palace?

steps.npc: You will have to find that out on your own, I'm afraid. I do have more work to do.

options.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.text: The player is offered a task; see Transcript:The Giant Dwarf#Talking_to_a_company_secretary

steps.npc: Goodbye, human.
See you later.
Okay.

steps.player: Hi!

steps.npc: Hi!

steps.player: So, what you up to out here?

steps.npc: Oh...er...nothing!

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.speaker: Anne
standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.text: Ah, look what we have here, Will! This looks like someone who needs a good job!

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.player: What?

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.npc: Goodness, Anne, I think you're right! This one's clearly never worked an honest day in their life, and it's about time someone changed that!

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.player: But I don't need a...

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.speaker: Anne
standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.text: Alas! We are sadly not currently in a place where we can take on any more staff, but let us hope that changes soon!

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.player: Okay...

standard-dialogue-pre-sailing-release.text: The Sailing skill will release on the 19th November.

steps.npc: Hello there, are you interested in buying one of my special capes?

options.text: What's so special about your capes?

steps.player: What's so special about your capes?

steps.npc: Ahh well they make it less likely that you'll accidently attack anyone wearing the same cape as you and easier to attack everyone else. They also make it easier to distinguish people who're wearing the same cape as you
from everyone else. They're very useful when out in the wilderness with friends or anyone else you don't want to harm.
So would you like to buy one?

steps.player: No thanks.

standard-dialogue-near-the-dwarven-mine-.player: Hello there. What are you doing all the way out here?

standard-dialogue-near-the-dwarven-mine-.npc: Nothing you need to worry about.

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.player: So this is where you scampered off to after the monster awoke?

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.npc: Look [player name], it was a simple misunderstanding, that's all...

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.player: Oh really? You threatening to kill me was just a misunderstanding?

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.npc: Things got a little heated down there, but we all made it out alive, right?

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.player: Barely... I had to defeat that monster on my own!
What are you doing out here, anyway?

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.npc: We thought you'd rat us out to the authorities, so we came out here to hide.
Plus, we heard there are some sealed tombs in the desert that haven't been touched in hundreds of years...

standard-dialogue-at-nardah.player: Ah, of course... scoping out your next grave to rob.

standard-dialogue.npc: [I/We] don't talk to strange old people.

standard-dialogue.player: Hey who you calling old?! And strange?!

standard-dialogue-after-paying-him.npc: You think you're tough do you?

standard-dialogue-after-paying-him.text: The boy begins to jump around with his fists up. You decide it's best not to kill him just yet.

treasure-trails-hard.text: a puzzle box

treasure-trails-hard.npc: My brother reckons I can't solve this puzzle. I can't have him laughing at me! Do me a favour and solve it for me.

treasure-trails-hard.text: Wilough has given you a puzzle box!

treasure-trails-hard-while-holding-the-p.text: If the puzzle box is not solved:

steps.npc: Sorry but you haven't solved the puzzle yet.

treasure-trails-hard-while-holding-the-p.text: If the puzzle box is solved:

steps.npc: Thanks [mister/miss]!

steps.text: When given another clue scroll:
another clue scroll
Wilough has given you another clue scroll!
When given a reward casket:
a reward casket
You've obtained a casket!

standard-dialogue-after-temple-of-ikov.player: Hi again. Could you do the honours again please?

standard-dialogue-after-temple-of-ikov.npc: Certainly! We helps those that helps poor Winelda!

standard-dialogue-after-temple-of-ikov.text: A cutscene is shown where the player is teleported across the lava.

options.text: It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it?

steps.player: It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it? I thought you gnomes liked your home comforts.

steps.npc: Certainly I miss home cooking, but gnomes are also fundamentally curious people. I'm here exploring the furthest reaches of the world for the King.

steps.player: Found anything interesting?

steps.npc: Sophanem is a curious place, if you can get into the blighted place. There are several pyramids round here as well. Fascinating architecture, I've heard stories that some of them contain treasure tombs and mummies.
Cats seem to have considerable importance round here, they certainly seem tied into their religion. The Gods round here seem very alien to me - I've never heard of them before.

steps.player: Thanks.

options.text: What does this mint cake do?
options.condition: If the player has a Mint cake:

steps.player: What does this mint cake do?

steps.npc: Gnomish mint cake is a great source of energy for the gnome traveller. It will give you that extra bit of zip when you are running out of steam.

steps.player: Ooh, that might come in very handy. Do you have any spare?

steps.npc: I need all the mint cake I have, I'm afraid.

options.text: What does this seed pod do?
options.condition: If the player has a Grand seed pod:

steps.player: What does this seed pod do?

steps.npc: Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not
very pleasant...

steps.player: Wow, that's very interesting. Thanks.

treasure-trails-master.text: Wingstone hands you a [light box/puzzlebox]!

treasure-trails-master-while-holding-the.text: If the puzzle is not solved:

steps.npc: That doesn't look solved to me.
Well done [player name]. Here you go.

steps.text: You've obtained a [new clue/casket]!

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player doesn't have the correct item in their inventory:

steps.text: Although you have found your customer you don't appear to have brought the correct food with you! You need [a/some] [ordered gnome food/drink item]!

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player has a premade item in their inventory:

steps.text: Premade dishes will not do I'm afraid. Only hand made Gnome Cuisine is good enough for customers of Aluft Aloft.

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player has the correct item in their inventory:

steps.text: You hand over your delivery of [a/some] [ordered gnome food item] to Wingstone.

steps.npc: This will hit the spot. Oh yes. Thanks.

steps.text: If the reward is a mint cake:

steps.npc: Now that I have some proper food, I won't need this any more.

steps.text: You are given some mintcake as a tip.
If the reward is grand seed pods:

steps.npc: Here, take these Grand Seed pods. Very useful in emergencies!

steps.text: You are given some seed pods as a tip.
If the reward is a snake charm:

steps.npc: I was given this odd device, maybe you can do something with it.

steps.text: You are given a snake flute as a tip.
If the reward is anything else:

steps.npc: You must have had to travel a long way to get this to me. Here's a little something extra as a tip.

steps.text: You are given [a/some] [reward item(s)] as a tip.

gnome-restaurant-dialogue.text: If the player ran out of time:

steps.text: Your delivery is too late! Go back to Aluft jnr. to get another order. You discard your delivery box as you don't need it any more.

steps.player: Why are you in that cage?

steps.npc: That evil witch put me in here! She kidnapped me!

steps.player: That's awful! Why did she do that?

steps.npc: She wanted the secret of my ogleroots, so she did!

steps.player: Your ogleroots? I don't think I understand. What secret is that?

steps.npc: Well now, I have perfected a spell that would grow an ogleroot to an enormous size.

steps.player: That's amazing! But how do you move the ogleroot around if it's so big?

steps.npc: You know, I had the very same problem so I came up with a simple solution. I used a spell I learned from a chap called Larry to shrink 'em down really small so that I could carry whole bags filled with 'em to the
market place.
Then when I got there, I would use the growing spell once more to make 'em huge and sell 'em for a tidy sum.

steps.player: That's amazing! So how does the witch fit in to all this?

steps.npc: Well that old witch - she's a sly one, I tell you. She found out about my spell and kidnapped me along with my bag of ogleroots.
She wants the secret of the spell but I ain't talking! No sir! So she's been feeding my mini-ogleroots to those ugly...things over there.

steps.player: So she hasn't found out the spell yet?

steps.npc: Not yet, no. And I still ain't telling her. But from what I gather, she's started to use them ogleroots in some of her potions for something. I don't know what, though.

steps.player: I see. Can I get you out of there somehow?

steps.npc: No, it's ok. I want to keep an eye on what the witch is up to down here with these odd creatures.

steps.player: So, will you be alright?

steps.npc: Yes, I'll be fine for now. Good luck with your tasks!
This could be worse I guess. Oh wait... No it can't.
I'm hungry...
Sometimes I wish this thing would just escape. At least we'd have something to do then.
It's so cold...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Greetings, [player name].

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So you're a wise old man, huh?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Less of the 'old' man, if you please!
But yes, I suppose you could say that. I prefer to think of myself as a sage.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So what's a sage doing here?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I've spent most of my life studying this world in which we live. I've strode through the depths of the deadliest dungeons, roamed the murky jungles of Karamja, meditated on the glories of Saradomin on Entrana,
and read some dusty tomes in the Library of Varrock.
Now I'm not as young as I used to be, I'm settling here where it's peaceful.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has not completed Vampyre Slayer:

steps.npc: It's a pity about that vampyre that keeps attacking the village. At least Saradomin protects me.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: That's quite an exciting life you've had.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Exciting? Yes, I suppose so.
Now I'm here, perhaps I could offer you the benefit of my experience and wisdom?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Thanks! So you can help me?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Well, I imagine you've gathered up quite a lot of stuff on your travels. Things you used for quests a long time ago that you don't need now.
If you like, I can look through your bank and see if there's anything you can chuck away.
Alternatively, you can bring items here and show them to me. If I see that it's something you don't need, I'll let you know. I might even be willing to buy it.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So you'll help me clear junk out of my bank?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Yes, that's right. Or I'd be happy to chat with you about the wonders of this world!

options.text: Could I have some free stuff, please?

steps.player: Could I have some free stuff, please?

steps.npc: Deary deary me...

steps.text: If the player is in a F2P world:

steps.npc: I'm not giving out free money, but if you try again later I'd be glad to reward you if you'd do a little job for me.

steps.text: If the player is in a members world:

steps.npc: I'm not giving out free money, but I'd be happy to reward you if you'll do a little job for me.

options.text: Ok, what do you want me to do?

steps.player: Ok, what do you want me to do?

steps.npc: I'm sure I can think of a few little jobs. This won't be a quest, mind you, just a little favour...

steps.player: Thanks, maybe some other time.

options.text: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.player: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.npc: Please do!

steps.text: (See subsequent dialogue section down below)

options.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.npc: I'm sure I can think of a few little jobs. This won't be a quest, mind you, just a little favour...

steps.text: Continues to his tasks

options.text: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.player: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

steps.player: Thanks, maybe some other time.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-dialogue.npc: Greetings, [player name].

options.text: Can I get another hood for my Quest Point Cape?

steps.player: Can I get another hood for my Quest Point Cape?

steps.text: The Wise Old Man hands you a free hood.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-dialogue.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.npc: You don't appear to have enough space in your inventory. Come back and see me when you do.

options.text: Can I buy a Quest Point Cape, please?

steps.player: Can I buy a Quest Point Cape, please?

steps.npc: Gladly, though they cost 99,000 coins.

steps.player: Okay, 99,000 coins is fine.

steps.text: The Wise Old Man sells you a Quest Point Cape and a hood to wear with it.
If the player only has one or no inventory space open:

steps.npc: All skillcapes come with a hood - you're not going to be able to hold them now. Try again another time.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have enough coins:

steps.player: I'll have to come back another time.
Actually, no thanks.

options.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.text: If the player is in a F2P world:

steps.npc: Thanks, but I don't have anything I need doing right now.

steps.text: If the player is in a members world:
Continues to his tasks

options.text: What did you ask me to do?

steps.text: Continues to his tasks

options.text: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.player: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

options.text: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.player: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.npc: Please do!

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?

steps.npc: If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.
It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.
The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.
But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.
Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.
If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Yes please.
Thanks, maybe some other time.

steps.npc: As you wish. Farewell, [player name].

steps.player: What can you tell me about jungles?

steps.npc: If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.
Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.
There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.
Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!

steps.text: If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them.

steps.npc: Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.

steps.text: If the player has completed Shilo Village:

steps.player: I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.

steps.npc: The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Tell me about what's underground.

steps.npc: Oh, the dwarven realms?
Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.
Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.
If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley
dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What mystical realms can I visit?

steps.npc: Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.
Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!

steps.text: If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

steps.npc: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

steps.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What's the biggest monster in the world?

steps.npc: There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or
incinerate you where you stand.
But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.
Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.
Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.

steps.text: If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: Poison and how to survive it

steps.player: What does poison do?

steps.npc: Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.
Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.
Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.
Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What monsters drop good items?

steps.npc: As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.
If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.
You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?

steps.npc: Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and
attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Tell me about valiant heroes!

steps.npc: Ha ha ha... There are plenty of heroes. Always have been, always will be, until the fall of the world.

steps.text: If the player has less than 80 quest points:

steps.npc: If you'd do a few more quests, you'd soon become a fairly noted adventurer yourself.

steps.text: If the player has 80 or more quest points:

steps.npc: You're quite a noted adventurer yourself!
But I suppose I could tell you of a couple...

Yes, there was a man called Arrav. No-one knew where he came from, but he was a fearsome fighter, a skillful hunter and a remarkable farmer. He lived in the ancient settlement of Avarrocka, defending it from
goblins, until he went forth in search of some strange artefact long desired by the dreaded Mahjarrat.
Perhaps some day I shall be able to tell you what became of him.

But do not let your head be turned by heroics. Randas was another great man, but he let himself be beguiled into turning to serve Zamorak, and they say he is now a mindless creature deep in the Underground Pass that
leads to Isafdar.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Where did humans learn to use magic?

steps.npc: Ah, that was quite a discovery! It revolutionised our way of life and jolted us into this Fifth Age of the world.

They say a traveller in the north discovered the key, although no records state exactly what he found. From this he was able to summon the magic of the four elements, using magic as a tool and a weapon. He and
his followers learnt how to bind the power into little stones so that others could use it.
in the land south of here they constructed an immense tower where the power could be studied, but followers of Zamorak destroyed it with fire many years ago, and most of the knowledge was lost.

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.npc: Perhaps one day those lost secrets will be uncovered once more.

steps.text: If the player has completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.npc: I hear you've been very helpful to the wizards who are working on the mysteries of the rune stones.

steps.player: Well, I didn't do much...

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I suppose you'd know about the history of today's cities?

steps.npc: Yes, there are fairly good records of the formation of the cities from primitive settlements.
In the early part of the Fourth Age, of course, there were no permanent settlements. Tribes wandered the lands, staying where they could until the resources were exhausted.

This changed as people learnt to grow crops and breed animals, and now there are very few of the old nomadic tribes. There's at least one tribe roaming between the Troll Stronghold and Rellekka, though.

steps.text: If the player has completed Mountain Daughter:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them. They're all mad.

steps.npc: Truly, their faith in natural spirits is rather foolish, but they're a pleasant enough people.
Anyway, what was I saying? Ah, yes...
One settlement was Avarrocka, a popular trading centre.
In the west, Ardougne gradually formed under the leadership of the Carnillean family, despite the threat of the Mahjarrat warlord Hazeel who dwelt in that area until his downfall.

steps.text: If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: He'll be back, just you wait!

steps.npc: Oh dear, I hope you haven't done anything rash!

steps.text: If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.npc: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: The Wise Old Man of Draynor Village

steps.player: Tell me about yourself, old man.

steps.npc: Ah, so you want to know about me, eh?
Mmm... what could I say about myself? Let's see what I've done...
I've delved into the dungeon west of Brimhaven and heard the terrifying CRASH of the steel dragons battling each other for territory.
I spent some years on Entrana, where I learnt the techniques of pure meditation.
I've wandered through the vast desert that lies south of Al Kharid and seen the great walls of Menaphos and Sophanem.

steps.text: If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper:

steps.player: That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.

steps.npc: I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.

steps.player: So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?

steps.npc: Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!

steps.player: But I've met the Sph...

steps.npc: Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.
Even if such a creature were to exist...

steps.player: ... which it does...

steps.npc: EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.
I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.
Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!

steps.player: Hmmm?

steps.npc: So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...
Apart from all that, I've spent many a happy hour in dusty libraries, searching through ancient scrolls and texts for the wisdom of those who have passed on.
Plus plenty of other adventures, quests, journeys... Is there anything else you'd like to know?

steps.player: I heard that Gielinor has three gods.

steps.npc: Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.
Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.
Zamorak craves only death and destruction.
Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site:

steps.player: So who's Zaros?

steps.npc: What did you say?

steps.player: I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.

steps.npc: Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.

steps.player: So Zaros is real?

steps.npc: Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.

steps.text: If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

steps.npc: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!

steps.text: If the player has completed Temple of Ikov but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.

steps.npc: What is this of which you speak?

steps.player: A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.

steps.npc: And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?

steps.player: Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.

steps.npc: So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?

steps.player: Um... Yes, I suppose so.

steps.npc: I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.

steps.text: (If the player with the Guardians of Armadyl:)

steps.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

steps.npc: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.

steps.text: (If the player sided with Lucien:)

steps.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

steps.npc: YOU'VE DONE WHAT?
Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.

steps.text: If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?

steps.npc: What names are these?

steps.player: Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...

steps.npc: Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?

steps.player: But I've met Icthlarin! He'd got a jackal's head!

steps.npc: It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?

steps.player: Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.

steps.npc: So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?

steps.player: Umm...

steps.npc: Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!

steps.player: But...?

steps.npc: It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.

steps.player: But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?

steps.npc: Indeed, I have.

steps.player: So you'd know all about their gods?

steps.npc: I know what I know.
And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.

steps.player: I wanna know about the wars of the gods!

steps.npc: Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.

steps.text: If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.npc: You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.

steps.player: How did it all end?

steps.npc: Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are the Mahjarrat?

steps.npc: Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.
One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.
Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.

steps.text: If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!

steps.npc: Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!

steps.text: If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.npc: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.

steps.text: If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've defeated Lucien.

steps.npc: Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.

steps.text: If the player sided with Lucien in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.

steps.npc: Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.

steps.text: If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.

steps.npc: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.

options.text: Wielding the power of the gods

steps.player: Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena I:

steps.npc: I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed Mage Arena I:

steps.npc: If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I want to ask you about your hat.

steps.npc: Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.

steps.text: If the player has not yet seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

steps.player: Did you steal it from the bank?

steps.npc: Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?

steps.player: There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.

steps.npc: Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?

steps.player: Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!

steps.npc: Oh dear, oh dear...
So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?
I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?

steps.player: So you didn't rob the bank?

steps.npc: Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!

steps.player: Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.

steps.npc: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.text: If the player has seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

options.text: You stole it off that woman in the bank!

steps.player: You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!

steps.npc: Stole it? How could you possibly think I did such a thing?

steps.player: I saw you robbing the bank! You killed all those people!

steps.npc: Deary me, [player name], your imagination is running wild! What could make you think you saw me do that?

steps.player: I've seen a security recording that shows you robbing the bank. The bank's guard showed it to me.

steps.npc: You've seen the bank's security recording?
Tut tut tut... Oh well, at least you'll never be able to tell the bank about me. They'll never listen.

steps.player: So you're just going to get away with it?

steps.npc: That's my plan, yes.

steps.player: But that's... well, it's WRONG!

steps.npc: Wrong? WRONG? I'll tell you what's wrong!
I've spent my whole life travelling the world, doing quests for people, saving lives, saving villages from terrifying monsters and all that sort of thing.
Now I'm old, and where do I have to live? In this freezing old house next to a pig-sty, with a bunch of yobs outside who can't keep their hands off the market stalls! What sort of reward is that?
So don't talk to me about right and wrong!

steps.player: Maybe someone SHOULD talk to you about right and wrong...

steps.npc: Bah!

steps.player: Hmmph!

steps.npc: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

steps.player: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.npc: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.

steps.player: Can I buy your hat?

steps.npc: Ohhh no, I don't intend to part with this. Would you like to ask me about something else?

options.text: You should give it back, you know.
You should give it back, you know.

steps.player: You should give it back, you know.

steps.npc: No, I think I'll keep it.

steps.player: But...

steps.npc: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: That was quite an exciting quest we did together!

steps.npc: Oh yes, it was certainly a fitting end to my adventuring days. Your fight against the Sea Troll Queen was highly impressive!

steps.player: Are you tempted to go on another quest in the future?

steps.npc: No, I feel I am a bit old for that kind of thing now. New times need new heroes, and I'm sure you'll always be there to answer the call!

steps.player: I'll certainly see what I can do!

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: When we finished fighting those sea trolls, you said you'd finished with adventuring, didn't you?

steps.npc: Yes, that's right. I'm an old man, there's no denying it, and I need a nice quiet retirement.
Besides, I think you've proved that the new generation has its own heroes and adventurers - I should step back and let you get on with it!

steps.player: Does this mean you're not going to do any more big robberies?

steps.npc: Well, since you saved my life when we were fighting the Sea Troll Queen, I don't mind telling you... I trust you won't tell anyone about this?

steps.player: Go on...

steps.npc: I might just have something in mind. After all, that little bank incident went very smoothly.

steps.player: But you're retired!

steps.npc: I retired from adventuring and questing. The episode in the bank was hardly a quest, more like a shopping trip!

steps.player: Your shopping trip killed 3 bank staff and several innocent bystanders, not to mention the watchman!

steps.npc: I've saved countless villages from unspeakable terrors and slain innumerable evil monsters - surely I deserve some sort of reward in return? Yet what did I get? NOTHING!
You yourself would get pretty angry if you did a long and dangerous quest and didn't get any reward from it, eh? I'm sure you would!
Well imagine how I felt at the end of a long life of questing when was left penniless, and I had to move into this thief-infested village! This little shack was falling apart when I arrived!
You go speak to that hag who keeps looking through my window - she'll show you how it used to look before I could afford to redecorate it!
Being noble and virtuous simply doesn't put food on the table, and I don't intend to sit in banks begging like so many people do these days.

steps.player: So all those quests in the past, when you saved people from monsters and stuff like that... You only helped them because you wanted a reward?

steps.npc: No, it wasn't always like that. I used to be satisfied just knowing that I'd helped, and that was reward enough.

But eventually I realised that people forgot about me as soon as the danger was gone, and I wasn't even getting paid properly for my services. Sometimes they offered training in the various skills, but that's no use to me!
I eventually realised that the only way I could get a proper reward for my life's efforts is if I took the reward myself. So I took up my cape and staff and headed for the bank.

steps.player: And now you're planning to do another robbery? Didn't you get enough from the bank?

steps.npc: Perhaps not... But enough of this matter! Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

using-items-on-wise-old-man.text: If the player has not gone through the initial dialogue first:

steps.npc: Humph! You could at least say hello before waving your items in my face.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-of.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-of.npc: I suppose you could use that in combat.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-on.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-on.npc: I suppose you could use that for defense.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-low-value-ru.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-low-value-ru.npc: Runes are very useful things, but I'll take some of those off your hands for you.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-high-value-r.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-high-value-r.npc: Ooh, runes? Yes, they're quite valuable.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-coins.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-coins.npc: That's called 'money'. Money is fantastically important if you haven't got enough of it, but when you've got as much as I have, you realise that money doesn't matter.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-book-on-chic.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-book-on-chic.npc: That's mine. I'll take it back, thank you very much!

using-items-on-wise-old-man-the-banker-s.npc: How did you get your hands on that?!
Get out of here this instant.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-items-with-n.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-items-with-n.npc: Tell you what, rather than you showing me items individually, I'll look through all your possessions to see if I can find anything worth discarding.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-items-with-n.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

searching-through-his-bookcases-without-.npc: It'd be politer to come and talk to me before you start messing around with my possessions!

after-observing-his-telescope.player: I see you've got your telescope pointing at the Wizards' Tower.

after-observing-his-telescope.npc: Oh, do I? Well, why does that interest you?

standard-dialogue-after-the-completion-o.npc: Hello deary. Don't worry, I'm friendly.

standard-dialogue-after-the-completion-o.player: You look very familiar but I can't remember chatting to you before.

standard-dialogue-after-the-completion-o.npc: Well, my sisters used to live here but folk kept on killing them. A terrible affair, it was. I knew that no one would want to kill a chatty old dear like me, though.
We still have a problem with local louts, though. Poisoning my fish, spilling my compost all over the place and causing a nuisance for the dear count.
I'm sure a nice young sort like you won't be any trouble, though. In any case, the Professor will soon share the secret of chickenisation with me... Not that I'd use it these days of course.

steps.player: Right... and what kind of questions are you referring to?

steps.npc: Well, that's the thing. It's different for everyone! Why do trees grow from stumps substantially faster than from seeds? Where do meteorites come from? Why do we have to hold our arms out to teleport successfully?

steps.player: I don't know. What are the answers?

steps.npc: I don't know either!

steps.player: So you're in Al Kharid to work out how trees grow?

steps.npc: No, silly! I came here to buy something.

steps.player: Something?

steps.npc: That's right! Something! Tell me, what do you know of runecrafting?

steps.player: Not a lot really.

steps.npc: A shame. Unfortunately, this something requires some understanding in that area.

options.text: What's a wizard doing in Al Kharid?

steps.player: Er... good question. I guess I just haven't seen a wizard around here before.

steps.player: Pleased to meet you. I'm [player name].

steps.npc: Now as for your question, maybe you should start expecting the unexpected! That way you can spend less time worrying about why I'm here, and more time asking life's real questions.

steps.text: Continues above from "Right... and what kind of questions are you referring to?"

steps.player: See you around.

options.text: Err I'd better be off really.

steps.player: Tell me about different trees and axes.

steps.text: Almost every tree can be chopped down. Normal logs will be produced by chopping 'Trees' and Oak logs will come from chopping 'Oak Trees'. You can find Oak trees in amongst normal trees scattered about the lands.
Willow trees will yield willow logs. You'll find willows like to grow near water, you can find some south of Draynor.
Maple logs can be gleaned from Maple trees. You'll usually find Maple trees standing alone amongst other trees.
Yew trees are few and far between. We do our best to cultivate them. Look for the tree icon on your minimap to find rare trees. Try North of Port Sarim.

options.condition: If the player has level 29-98 Woodcutting

steps.text: Magic trees are... magic. A difficult wood to work with, but worth it for the rewards. Find them in the areas south of Seers village or on the East side of the Mage Arena.

steps.npc: Hollow trees can be found in the Haunted Woods east of Canifis, but be careful of the leeches.

steps.text: Bronze axes are easy to get, simply go visit Bob in his shop in Lumbridge, or talk to me if you have mislaid yours.

steps.npc: As you progress in your combat skill you will find you can wield your woodcutting axe as a weapon, it's not very effective, but it frees up a slot for another log.

steps.text: As your woodcutting skill increases you will find yourself able to use better axes to chop trees faster.... anything up to steel you can buy from Bob's axe shop.
Rune axes can be player made with very high level smithing and mining. They can also be obtained through killing one of the fearsome tree spirits, though this is very rare.

steps.player: I'm still working on it.

If the player talks to Veos in Port Sarim:

options.text: I could do with some extra help.

steps.speaker: Veos
