steps.player: I'm still working on it.

steps.text: If the player talks to Veos in Lumbridge:
If the player talks to Veos in Port Sarim:

digging-the-last-clue.text: You dig up an Ancient Casket. As you do, you hear a faint whispering. You can't make out what it says though...

digging-the-last-clue.player: Hmmmm... Must have been the wind.
Anyway, this must be the treasure that Veos is after. I should take it to him. If I remember right, he's docked at the northernmost pier in Port Sarim.

attempting-to-open-the-ancient-casket.player: I don't think Veos would want me to open his treasure. I should take it to him. If I remember right, it's docked at the northernmost pier in Port Sarim.

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: Hello there.

finishing-up.player: Hello Veos.

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: How's the treasure hunt going?

finishing-up.player: I found the treasure!

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: Excellent. I'll take it off your hands now.
You give Veos the Ancient Casket.

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: Brilliant. This is just what I was looking for. Thank you so much for your help.

finishing-up.player: No problem. So what is this treasure anyway?

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: Oh err... nothing important. Just something that might be of use to me back in Great Kourend.

finishing-up.player: If you say so...

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: Anyway, as promised, a reward for you.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: Anyway, I'd best be getting back to Great Kourend. I'm sure I'll be back here before long though, there's always more treasure to be found.

finishing-up.speaker: Veos
finishing-up.text: If you ever fancy visiting the kingdom, come find me here. I'm more than happy to take you there. Consider it an extra thank you for your help.

finishing-up.player: Sounds great, thanks Veos.

A8qY2A.speaker: Veos
A8qY2A.text: First you should go and make some room in your inventory. Once you've done that, you can have a look at this scroll.

2wx_K_.speaker: Veos
2wx_K_.text: Well keep at it. Once you've found the treasure, bring it to me.

gLxs8h.speaker: Veos
gLxs8h.text: Well keep at it. Once you've found the treasure, meet me at my ship. It's docked at the northernmost pier in Port Sarim.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: I can't believe she's done this.
Fabia! She asked me to meet her, and I quote, 'by the special tree'. You may notice that she isn't here! I've been waiting for hours!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Do you think she might just be delayed?

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: I know her too well. She wouldn't be delayed coming to see me.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Could you be at the wrong special tree?

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: No! This is the one, singular, special tree!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: If the player has not already talked to Fabia:

steps.player: Humour me for just a moment. What if, amongst this entire rainforest, there's a second very similar tree?

steps.npc: And Fabia would find herself at the wrong tree in this scenario?

steps.player: Or maybe it's you who is at the wrong one?

steps.npc: No, absolutely not! I know where to meet Fabia and I wouldn't miss any opportunity to do so!
This was the tree where we first met. It was a lovely day! A botanical tour of the rainforest, but the only thing I found myself looking at was her...

steps.player: Well, I'm sure the two of you will find each other soon. However, I do suspect that might happen sooner if you considered looking by some other trees...

steps.npc: Hmm... I'll think about it, but for now, I'll wait here a while longer.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: If the player has already talked to Fabia:

steps.player: Hang on... I think I might have met this Fabia.

steps.npc: You have? Where is she?

steps.player: South of here, by some magic trees.

steps.npc: The magic trees? Of course! How could I have been so stupid! Thank you, iknami. I'll head over right away!

steps.text: Xilo departs.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: Hello again, iknami! Thank you for helping us find each other!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.speaker: Fabia
standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: To think we were waiting by different trees! It was so silly of us!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Well, I'm happy to see you together again. Now, I'm sure you have a lot of catching up to do. I'll leave you to it.

steps.npc: Nilsal! Looking to buy some dyes?

steps.player: I'll have a look.
I'm good, thanks.

steps.npc: In that case, timoiva for now.
Nilsal, traveller.

options.text: Can you heal me? I'm injured.

steps.player: Can you heal me? I'm injured.

steps.text: If the player is on a PvP world:

steps.npc: Sorry, but I cannot.

steps.text: If the player has full hitpoints:

steps.npc: I could, but you don't appear to actually need healing right now.
Of course.

steps.text: The teoki whispers a prayer and you suddenly feel a bit better.
Up to 21{{fact}} of the player's hitpoints are restored.

steps.player: How are things here?

steps.npc: Very busy, my friend. We have a lot of repairs to be doing, not to mention that there will soon be a new Gathering taking place here.

steps.player: Any problems of note?

steps.npc: We did have a creature from down in the caverns try to come up here at one point. Presumably they've been disturbed by recent events. The warriors quickly dealt with it though.

steps.player: That's good to hear.
I'd better be off.

steps.npc: May the sun light your way, traveller.
Greetings human. Do you seek guidance?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.npc: I am Xorrah quo Sihar. I am one of the mystics of the Kahlith.

steps.player: Kahlith?

steps.npc: Yes. At one time we were like you, but then we met the Tasakaal. They taught us to have purpose. They taught us to serve the balance.
Our old lives were left behind. In their place, the Kahlith were born.

steps.player: Tasakaal?

steps.npc: Our teachers. They showed us the way and taught us to serve the balance.

steps.player: The balance?

steps.npc: For every death, there must be life. For every life, there must be a death. This is the balance.
Our purpose, as taught to us by the Tasakaal, is to keep this balance, no matter the cost.

steps.player: A mystic?

steps.npc: Yes. All Kahlith serve the balance. To do this, we take on one of four roles.
My role is that of a mystic. I learn from the Tasakaal and then pass on their teachings.

steps.player: That's all thanks.
What is this place?

steps.npc: This is our home. In your tongue, it is known as Mount Karuulm.

steps.player: My tongue?

steps.npc: Yes. You speak the language of humans but we Kahlith have our own language.
In the past, we have tried to teach our language to your kind. However, despite the simplicity of our tongue, success was limited.
We find that it is easier to just use your language when your kind are around.

steps.player: Can you give an example?

steps.npc: Of our language?

steps.player: Yes please.

steps.npc: Well you'll find our language is quite a simple one. Our names are a good example of how it is used.
I am Xorrah quo Sihar. The first word, 'Xorrah', is unique to me and it is how I can be identified.
The second word, 'quo', is a basic Kahlith word that translates to 'the' in your language.
The final word, 'Sihar', is my title. There are four possible titles, one for each role in Kahlith society. My title translates to 'Mystic' in your tongue.

steps.player: So in my language your name would be Xorrah the Mystic?

steps.npc: Exactly.

steps.player: Interesting. Thanks for the information.
I'm good thanks.

options.text: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?

steps.player: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?

steps.npc: Sure. You can buy a skillcape when you reach level 99 in a skill. Apart from boosting your statistics in that skill, they can also be used to perform some pretty amazing emotes!
The Cape of Strength also provides you with unlimited teleports to our guild. Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.player: What can I do here?

steps.npc: Ahh, the shot put is a great test of strength and can be quite rewarding. Mind you do it properly though, you might want to dust your hands with some powdery substance first. It'll give better grip.

steps.player: I'll remember that. What should I use?

steps.npc: I personally prefer ground ashes, it makes a nice fine powder and gives some really good grip.

steps.player: Ok, what else?

steps.npc: Basically you'll need to go in there, make sure you've got nothing cluttering up your hands, pick up a shot and throw it.... depending upon your technique, you can get quite long throws.

steps.player: What was your best?

steps.npc: Ahh that would be telling...

options.text: Why are you wielding a tree branch?

steps.player: Why are you wielding a tree branch?

steps.npc: Well...there's a story to that. You see, I should have an axe but-

steps.player: Sloane's axe?

steps.npc: My axe. He won it because of a squirrel.

steps.player: A squirrel?

steps.npc: He bet me that I couldn't catch the squirrel while still holding my axe, but that he could... Thing is, he tricked me! When it was his turn, he just chopped the tree down!

steps.player: I see. That doesn't explain why you have a tree branch though.

steps.npc: A barbarian warrior is bound to his axe. I cannot take up another, so I use part of the tree that Sloane cut down as my weapon... It also reminds me of him.

steps.player: He was a great warrior.

steps.npc: Yes, and a good friend, Still, he would want us to be happy that he is now with his warrior brethren. Can I help you with anything else?

options.text: May I claim my tokens please?

steps.player: May I claim my tokens please?

steps.text: If the player has no tokens to claim:

steps.npc: I'm afraid you have not earned any tokens yet. Try some of the activities around the guild to earn some.

steps.player: Ok, I'll go see what I can find.

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.npc: You don't have space to carry them.
Of course! Here you go, you've earned [amount] tokens!

steps.text: [amount] Warrior guild tokens

steps.player: Thanks!
Bye!

steps.text: (Yadech Strongarm bows.)

steps.npc: Be well, warrior [player name].

dialogue-with-99-strength.npc: Ah, but I can see you are already as strong as is possible! Perhaps you have come to me to purchase a Cape of Strength, and thus join the elite few who have mastered this exacting skill?
As an additional recognition of your achievement, the Cape of Strength can teleport you to our guild.

options.text: May I buy a Skillcape of Strength, please?

steps.text: If the player has already bought a skillcape before:

steps.player: May I have another hood for my cape, please?

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.npc: You don't appear to have enough space in your inventory, come back and see me when you do.
Most certainly, and free of charge!

steps.text: Sloane hands you another hood for your skillcape.

steps.player: May I buy a Skillcape of Strength, please?

steps.npc: Hmm, yes, you certainly look strong enough. That'll be 99000 gold coins, please.

options.text: Sorry, that's just too much to pay.

steps.player: Sorry, that's just too much to pay.

steps.npc: Not at all; there are many other adventurers who would love the opportunity to purchase such a prestigious item! You can find me here if you change your mind.

steps.player: Sure.

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 99,000 coins:

steps.player: But, unfortunately, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.npc: Well, come back and see me when you do.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Unfortunately all Skillcapes are only available with a free hood, it's part of a skill promotion deal; buy one get one free, you know. So you'll need to free up some inventory space before I can sell you one.

steps.text: a Strength cape and hood

steps.npc: Excellent! Wear that cape with pride my friend.

options.text: Why are you wielding a tree branch?
May I claim my tokens please?

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...

steps.player: Strange how?

steps.npc: Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: Ah... [player name], welcome. I would offer you some water, but we don't get much of it down here.
I take it you have questions.

options.text: You know why I'm here. Stop messing around.

steps.npc: I do, but it is important that it is you who is asking for information, not me that is offering it.

steps.player: Okay... How are you still communicating with your followers?

steps.text: Continues from "Why, through my voice, of course."

options.text: I take it you have answers.

steps.player: I take it you have answers.

steps.npc: I do, but I rarely share them umprompted.

steps.player: Okay, how are you still communicating with your followers?

steps.text: Continues from "Why, through my voice, of course."

options.text: Yes, a few of them actually.

steps.player: Yes, a few of them actually. How are you still communicating with your followers?

steps.npc: Why, through my voice, of course.

steps.player: You know what I mean. How are you still communicating with your voice?

steps.npc: The same way I always have.

steps.player: But the dark nullifier... I thought it was supposed to sever your connection.

steps.npc: Hmm... Yes, if anything could have done so, it would have been the power of the Dark Altar.
However, when your opponents have only one angle of approach, it makes them so predictable.

steps.player: You knew we would try to use it?

steps.npc: Yes. When I heard you would be hand delivering me a connection to the Dark Altar... Why, I was overjoyed.

steps.player: But... I remember planting it! The plan went off without a hitch!

steps.npc: I do not doubt that you remember it that way.

steps.player: What did you do?!

steps.npc: A simple transfiguration of the mind. My disciples granted you a memory of success. A fitting payment for your gratious service.

steps.text: If Icthlarin's Little Helper has been completed:

steps.player: You modified my memory?! That's only the second time someone has done that to me, and I wasn't very happy about it then either!

steps.text: If Icthlarin's Little Helper hasn't been completed:

steps.player: You modified my memory?!

steps.npc: Yes. And I have now answered five of your questions. I believe my generosity has been both demonstrated and exhausted.

steps.player: You call that gloating generosity? If you didn't want something from me, I wouldn't still be down here. Get to the point.

steps.npc: Hmm... Perhaps you are more astute than I thought. Very well, there is something that I want.

steps.player: Well you won't be getting it from me!

steps.npc: I am Yama. Every mortal desires something of mine. Ancient armaments? Hidden knowledge? Or perhaps a taste of revenge...
These things could be yours.
Face me in combat. If you win, you take it all. Armaments, knowledge, revenge.

steps.player: And if I lose?

steps.npc: I take your soul. For all of eternity.

steps.player: No thanks.

steps.npc: I see. Perhaps we could lower the stakes then.
I will face you in an inhibited form. I'll even allow you to bring an ally, provided they have entered the same contract.
If you win, I will give you a chance to gain some of my treasures, and of course, you will have sampled your revenge.

steps.player: And if I lose?

steps.npc: When you take your final rest, I shall take your soul for a year. A drop in the ocean compared to eternity.

steps.player: How can I know you'll keep your word?

steps.npc: The same way I will know you shall keep yours. A binding contract. As luck would have it, I had one of my scribes draft one up for just such an occasion.

steps.player: ...Okay.

steps.npc: Sign right here.

steps.prompt: Sign the contract?
Are you sure? A contract with Yama cannot be backed out of.

steps.npc: Excellent... Challenge me when you are ready, [player name]. I very much look forward to it.

steps.player: I'm not sure I want to...

steps.npc: Of course. There is no rush. Leave, with your tail tucked between your legs. If you grow a spine and wish to fulfil your revenge, I will be waiting.

standard-dialogue-after-backing-out-from.npc: You are back. Excellent. I have little time for cowards. If you are ready, I will retrieve the contract.

standard-dialogue-using-the-right-click-.npc: Ah... Yes, let us not get bogged down in the minutiae. Before we start, a quick contract. Nothing but a formality.

standard-dialogue-afterwards.npc: Welcome, [player name]. Have you come to challenge me?

steps.player: Yes. Let's do this.

steps.text: Yama snaps his fingers and teleports off his throne.

steps.player: Actually, I have some questions.

steps.npc: Of course.

options.text: There's something in our contract about additional contracts...

steps.player: There's something in our contract about additional contracts... Why would I want to sign any more of them?

steps.npc: As outlined in subsection C, if you wish for your revenge to feel more 'real', I am willing to lift some of the restrictions placed by the original contract.

steps.player: Why would I want that?

steps.text: If the player is an Ironman or Group Ironman:

steps.npc: You seem to enjoy self-imposed difficulty. I thought I would indulge you.

steps.text: If the player is not an Ironman:

steps.npc: You may not, in which case you can sell them to someone with greater respect for themselves. But if you do, the option is there.
And if you manage to claim victory, there is of course a reward for each contract.

steps.player: Okay, can I see the contracts?

steps.npc: No. For this, I require from you a service. My demons are... Lacking, of late. Unrefined.
They must fight, suffer and reform. If you deliver them specific ends during your 'tasks' in my domain, they may leave behind a contract.
And of course, if you defeat me, I may also reward you with one.

steps.player: What kinds of 'ends'?

steps.npc: Death by two-handed melee weapons, heavy ranged weapons, magic spells, special attacks, and defeating them whilst bound. Each kind may award a different contract.
If you find yourself eager to obtain any contract, I will use a glyph to indicate my preferred method, which you can utilise for a better chance to receive that contract.

steps.player: What kinds of contracts can I obtain?

steps.npc: Were you more adept at reading you would find the details in our original contract. Otherwise, bring any you obtain to me and I shall explain then.

options.text: Do you keep any record of our fights?

steps.player: Do you keep any record of our fights?

steps.npc: I do, I can have somebody retrieve your file. One moment.

steps.text: A mail-imp holding a scroll appears. Yama smites the imp.

steps.npc: For your reading pleasure.

steps.player: That's all.
No, I'd rather not.

steps.npc: I see. Perhaps you are just here to waste my time then? Return when you are not.
Your strike lacks bite.
A change of pace.
Colabi, infernus
Ven, estella infernus
Colabesur infernus
Ven, umbra eclipta
Umbra, proriumpse
Umbra apprerendehe
Begone
You bore me.
Enough.
Lacking.
Pathetic.
The price is paid.
Another day, perhaps.
Another day, another soul.
Your soul was always mine.
Fair is fair.
Your reward, as agreed.
A satisfying warmup. Collect your loot and let us continue.
A passing performance.
A close fight. Your nerve was well held.
A good risk, adequately rewarded.
Excellent performance. Again?
Effective, if a bit cowardly.
Risk averse, are we?

standard-dialogue-during-battle-attempti.npc: Missed the fine print, did we? Our contract forbids you from picking up stashed items.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-victoriou.text: One of the following is said before standard dialogue follows, after which the "In any case" section is played. This can appear as an overhead quote if Yama is challenged, which ignores the "In any case" section.

steps.npc: I hope you are finding the spoils from my treasury to your liking. There are plenty more for you to claim.
Your victories mount. You are getting better at this.
A victory earned. But there is room for improvement, is there not?
Here we go again. I suppose it is entertaining watching you desperately guzzle potions, at the very least.
I must once again commend your strategy. Employing tactics so boring that they put your opponents to sleep is very novel.
Back again I see. I can see how you find these bouts exhilarating, being such a feeble opponent.
Your willingness to wager your soul continues to surprise. I suppose you think of it even less worth than I do.
Honestly, I expected more. That it takes you as long as it does to defeat my inhibited form is rather embarrassing.
You look happy with yourself. How endearing.
You return once more. Excellent.
Ah, you have returned. Your competence matches only your greed.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-victoriou.npc: In any case, [player name], are you here to challenge me?

standard-dialogue-after-battle-defeated.text: One of the following is said before standard dialogue follows. This can appear as an overhead quote if Yama is challenged, which ignores the "In any case" section.

steps.npc: Don't let a single defeat set you back. You could have so many more.
My treasury remains over capacity. And here I was hoping to be relieved of some of its contents.
What a shame for our last bout to have ended that way! Maybe you will do better next time.
Back after being defeated so quickly? I suppose what you lack in skill you make up for with perseverance.
Some losses are unavoidable. Yours, of course, was not.
Your donation is greatly appreciated.
Defeat finds you. Of course, that is hardly unexpected.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-having-es.text: One of the following is said before standard dialogue follows, after which the "In any case" section is played. This can appear as an overhead quote if Yama is challenged, which ignores the "In any case" section.

steps.npc: If you are struggling to achieve victory, I suppose avoiding defeat is the best you can do.
You must be tired, having to run all the way back here.
Back for more? Well, you can always escape again I suppose.
Excellent work evading. Next time, try fighting back.
Our last bout was cut short. Perhaps the next will be more fruitful.
Back again? Watching you escape in such a hurry, I thought you might never return.
Ah, I see your legs have stopped quivering. Perhaps next time you will fight to the end.
I hear adventurers like to boast about their feats. I wonder if people realise how readily they run at the first sight of risk.
A well executed retreat. You must be very practiced.
There is no shame in defeat. There is plenty to be found in your cowardice, however.

options.condition: If the player has been victorious against Yama numerous times:

steps.npc: After all the confidence you demonstrated... still you lost your nerve. Perhaps I should have included in our contract a clause to cover your cowardly retreats.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-having-es.npc: In any case, [player name], have you come to challenge me?

using-items-on-yama-any-contract.npc: Why... Do my eyes deceive me? I see a glimmer of courage within you.

options.text: I've seen what you have to offer. It doesn't scare me.
options.condition: If Yama has been defeated at least 100 times:

steps.player: I've seen what you have to offer. It doesn't scare me.

steps.npc: Excellent! let us sign the contract and find out how long that feeling lasts.

steps.prompt: Sign the contract?

steps.text: If the player is signing a contract of oathplate acquisition:

steps.npc: The terms of this contract dictate that you are to make your choice of oathplate to receive known prior to the fight. Sign it here.

steps.prompt: Which piece of oathplate would you like to receive?

steps.text: You picked Oathplate Helm, are you sure?

options.text: Yes, I want the Oathplate helm.

steps.text: You picked Oathplate Chest, are you sure?

options.text: Yes, I want the Oathplate chest.

steps.text: You picked Oathplate Legs, are you sure?

options.text: Yes, I want the Oathplate legs.

steps.text: The [contract name] burns up and Yama breathes a contented sigh...

steps.npc: Good luck.

steps.text: Yama snaps his fingers and teleports off his throne.

steps.player: Actually, I think I may have forgotten to feed my kitten...

steps.npc: That's all it took? A vague threat to match your bravado? Get out of my sight.

options.text: I know what I'm doing, sign the contract.

steps.player: I know what I'm doing, sign the contract.

steps.npc: With pleasure.

steps.prompt: Sign the contract?

options.text: I want to know more about this contract.

steps.player: I want to know more about this contract.

steps.npc: Signing these contracts agrees us to a duel in which I am less inhibited. My powers will be greater than what you have experienced before.
Each one details unique rules and rewards, the details of which you can read on the contract itself.
But I'm sure you already have. Shall we?

steps.text: Yama presses a quill firmly into your hands.

steps.prompt: Sign the contract?

steps.player: No, I think I'd like to read over the terms again.

steps.npc: Very well. Return when you are ready.

options.text: Er... No, I thought you'd lost this.

steps.player: Er... No, I thought you'd lost this.

steps.npc: No, that contract was allowed to come into your possession quite deliberately. And I see you have bravely decided to make use of it.

steps.player: I'm not sure I...

steps.npc: I see that I had misjudged you, [player name]. Let us sign the contract and cement that assessment.

steps.text: Yama presses a quill firmly into your hands.

steps.prompt: Sign the contract?

steps.player: No, I think it might have been somebody else that dropped it. I should really go and find them...

steps.npc: Yes, perhaps it was. Perhaps it belonged to somebody else. Somebody with a semblance of pride or self respect.
If you find them, be sure to send them my way.

using-items-on-yama-plain-pizza.npc: Ah... The humble plain pizza. Unremarkable, yet powerful. Hand me it.

steps.text: Yama eats half of the pizza.

steps.npc: Yes... Delicious.

steps.text: Yama eats half of the pizza.

steps.npc: You think you can deny me pizza? Double check the fine print of our contract, [player name].

steps.player: What do you mean?! You can't just take my pizza!

steps.npc: Oh but I can. As per our contract, any pizza you present to me cannot be taken back. Right here.

steps.text: Yama points to a line on the contract that states that once a full pizza is shown to him, it cannot be taken back.

steps.player: Why am I here?

steps.npc: You are here for a number of reasons, [player name]. Chiefly because I deign to allow these petty games to play out.

steps.player: Petty games? You mean the League?

steps.npc: Yes, my League.
I confess my curiosity has finally won through. Long have I heard tales of these Leagues, and the lengths mortals like you will go to for a shred of favour from a superior being.
So now I offer you the same bargain that the 'mighty' Sage has struck time and time again. However, I present you with the chance of true power.

steps.player: True power, eh?

steps.npc: Does that intrigue you?

steps.player: Of course! Who wouldn't be interested in that?

steps.npc: Very good. In that case, complete the tasks you have been presented with and we can arrange some appropriate enhancements.

steps.player: Alright!

steps.npc: The League awaits you. Impress me.

options.text: What have you done to the Sage?

steps.player: Why have you imprisoned the Sage? They're usually quite pleasant.

steps.npc: I have seized the Sage just as I have claimed this League.
The Sage has well and truly earned their place in my domain. Such squandered potential...
More than that, do you understand what this League actually is? Where we are?

steps.player: Erm... Yes?

steps.npc: Hah! You do not. Nor did I before lengthy discussions with my guest.
It is enough to say that I require guarantees for the near future.

steps.player: What does that mean? Should I be concerned?

steps.npc: You are small. When the time comes you will slip through the net and leave this chapter without incident.

steps.player: Hmm... I'm not sure I like being called small, but I do like not having to worry!
So what exactly are you going to do with the Sage?

steps.npc: What am I going to do with them? Nothing. Unless they refuse my demands.
You cannot possibly fathom the potential futures I am conjuring for the contents of that cage should they fail me.
If I told you but one element of my intent, your mind would collapse, and your soul would scream with agony for a thousand years.
You simply would not comprehend.

steps.player: Try me.
